en: The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 213.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang under Imperial Decree.
Part 20, Chapter 34-20: The Section on Difficult-to-Believe Understanding.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the seer is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is that?"
If the seer is pure, if form is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the seer is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the seer, the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the seer is pure, the eye-base is pure; because the eye-base is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of the seer, the purity of the eye-base, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the sphere of the eye is pure, the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the seer, or the purity of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the seer is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is that?
If the seer is pure, if the sphere of form is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the seer is pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the seer, the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the seer is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is that?
Whether it be the purity of the seer, the purity of the eye-element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the seer is pure, the form element, the eye-consciousness element, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure; because the form element up to all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the seer, the purity of the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the seer is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the seer, the purity of the ear-element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the seer is pure, the sound element, the ear-consciousness element, and ear-contact, as well as all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, are pure; because the sound element up to all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the seer, the purity of the sound-element up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the seer is pure, the nose element is pure; because the nose element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the seer is pure, if the nose element is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not severed.

Because the seer is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the seer, the purity of the fragrance-element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the seer is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the seer is pure, if the tongue-element is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the seer is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because if the seer is pure, if the taste element and even the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the seer is pure, the body-element is pure; because the body-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the seer is pure, if the body-element is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the seer is pure, the sphere of tangibles, the sphere of body-consciousness, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure. Because the sphere of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the seer, the purity of the sense-field of tangibles up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the seer is pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the seer, the purity of the mental constituent (*manodhātu*), or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the visual faculty is pure, the dharma-element, the mental consciousness element, and mind-contact, as well as all sensations produced with mind-contact as a condition, are pure; because the dharma-element up to all sensations produced with mind-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the seer, or the purity of the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the seer is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the seer is pure, if the earth element is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the seer is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the seer, the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the seer is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of the seer, the purity of the absence of darkness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because seeing is pure, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the seer, the purity of everything from formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the seer is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the seer, the purity of the perfection of giving, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the seer is pure, the perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the seer, the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the seer is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is that?
If the seer is pure, if internal emptiness is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the seer is pure, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure. Because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the seer, the purity of external emptiness up to the purity of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the seer is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of the seer, the purity of suchness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the seer is pure, the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, the state of equality, the nature free from birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm are pure. Because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the seer, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the seer is pure, the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure; because the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the seer is pure, if the noble truth of suffering is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not separate.
Because the seer is pure, the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the seer, the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the seer is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the seer is pure, if the four dhyānas are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because the seer is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the seer, the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the seer is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the seer is pure, if the eight liberations are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the seer is pure, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because if the seer is pure, if the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten universal bases are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because the seer is pure, the four applications of mindfulness are pure; because the four applications of mindfulness are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is that?

If the seer is pure, if the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, this is because they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the seer is pure, the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eight branches of the noble path are pure; because the four right endeavors up to the eight branches of the noble path are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the seer, the purity of the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the seer is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the seer, the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the seer is pure, the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure; because the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the seer, the purity of the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the seer is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the seer, the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the seer is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of the seer, the purity of the five eyes, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
Because the seer is pure, the six supernormal powers are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the seer, the purity of the six supernormal powers, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the seer is pure, the ten powers of the Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of the Buddha are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure. Why is this?
If the seer is pure, if the ten powers of the Buddha are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the seer is pure, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the seer, the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not two, indivisible, and without distinction.
"Subhūti! Because the seer is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the seer, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the seer is pure, the state of constant abiding in equanimity is pure; because the state of constant abiding in equanimity is pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure. Why is this?

If the seer is pure, if the state of constant dwelling in equanimity is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, this is because they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the seer is pure, all-knowledge is pure; because all-knowledge is pure, the knowledge of all-knowledge is pure. Why is this?
If the seer is pure, if omniscience is pure, and if the knowledge of omniscience is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the seer is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, the knowledge of all-knowingness is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the seer, the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, or the purity of the knowledge of all-knowledge, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the seer is pure, all dhāraṇī-doors are pure; because all dhāraṇī-doors are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the seer, the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the seer is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure; because all doors of samādhi are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the seer, the purity of all doors of samādhi, or the purity of the knowledge of all-knowledge, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the seer is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is that?
If the seer is pure, if the fruit of stream-entry is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the vision is pure, the fruit of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship is pure; because the fruit of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship is pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the seer, the purity of the fruit of once-returning, non-returning, or arhatship, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the seer is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the seer, the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the seer is pure, all the practices of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure; because all the practices of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the seer, the purity of all the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the seer is pure, the unsurpassed perfect enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unsurpassed perfect enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the seer, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual; they are not two, not divided, not distinct, and not separate.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
The purity of desire is the purity of form; the purity of form is the purity of desire. Why is this?
This purity of desire and the purity of form are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of desire is itself the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness; the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is itself the purity of desire.

Why is this? Because the purity of this craving and the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of desire is the purity of the eye-base; the purity of the eye-base is the purity of desire. Why is this?
This purity of craving and the purity of the sense-base of the eye are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of craving is itself the purity of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind; the purity of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind is itself the purity of craving.
Why is this? Because the purity of this craving and the purity of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
"Subhūti! The purity of desire is the purity of the sense-field of form; the purity of the sense-field of form is the purity of desire. Why is this?
This purity of desire and the purity of the sense-base of form are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

The purity of desire is the purity of the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena; the purity of the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is the purity of desire.

Why is this? Because the purity of this craving and the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! The purity of desire is the purity of the eye-element; the purity of the eye-element is the purity of desire. Why is this?
This purity of desire and the purity of the eye-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of desire is itself the purity of the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and all sensations produced with eye-contact as a condition; the purity of the form-element up to all sensations produced with eye-contact as a condition is itself the purity of desire.

Why is this? Because the purity of this craving and the purity of the feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, up to and including the form realm, are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of desire is the purity of the ear-element; the purity of the ear-element is the purity of desire. Why is this?
This purity of craving and the purity of the ear-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of craving is the purity of the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, auditory contact, and all feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition; the purity of the sound-element up to all feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition is the purity of craving.

Why is this? Because the purity of this craving and the purity of all feelings produced with conditions ranging from the sound-element up to ear-contact are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! The purity of desire is the purity of the nose element; the purity of the nose element is the purity of desire. Why is this?
This purity of craving and the purity of the nose-element are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.

The purity of craving is itself the purity of the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition. The purity of the odor-element up to all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition is itself the purity of craving.

Why is this? Because the purity of this craving and the purity of the various feelings produced with the fragrance-element and so forth, up to those produced with nose-contact as a condition, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of desire is the purity of the tongue-element; the purity of the tongue-element is the purity of desire. Why is this?
This purity of craving and the purity of the tongue-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of craving is itself the purity of the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition; the purity of the taste-element up to all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition is itself the purity of craving.

Why is this? Because the purity of this craving and the purity of the various feelings produced with the taste-element and so forth, up to those produced with tongue-contact as a condition, are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of desire is the purity of the body element; the purity of the body element is the purity of desire. Why is this?
This purity of desire and the purity of the body-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of desire is the purity of the touch-element, the body-consciousness-element, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition; the purity of the touch-element up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition is the purity of desire.

Why is this? Because the purity of this craving and the purity of the various feelings produced with the sphere of touch, up to those produced with body-contact as a condition, are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of desire is the purity of the mind-element; the purity of the mind-element is the purity of desire. Why is this?
This purity of desire and the purity of the mind-element (*manodhātu*) are non-dual, undivided, distinctless, and uninterrupted.

The purity of desire is itself the purity of the dharma-element (*dharmadhātu*), the mind-consciousness-element (*manovijñānadhātu*), mental contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*), and all feelings (*vedanā*) produced with mental contact as condition. The purity of the dharma-element up to all feelings produced with mental contact as condition is itself the purity of desire.

Why is this? Because this purity of craving and the purity of everything from the dharma-realm up to the feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are non-dual, undivided, distinctless, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! The purity of desire is the purity of the earth element; the purity of the earth element is the purity of desire. Why is this?
This purity of desire and the purity of the earth element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
The purity of desire is the purity of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements; the purity of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements is the purity of desire.

Why is this? Because the purity of this craving and the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are without distinction, and they are not separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of desire is the purity of ignorance; the purity of ignorance is the purity of desire. Why is this?
This purity of craving and the purity of ignorance are non-dual; they are not two, they are not distinct, and they are not separate.

The purity of craving is the purity of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair; and the purity of volitional formations through to old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair is the purity of craving.

Why is this? Because the purity of this craving and the purity of conditioned formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not separate.
"Subhūti! The purity of desire is the purity of the perfection of giving; the purity of the perfection of giving is the purity of desire."
Why is this? Because the purity of this craving and the purity of the perfection of generosity (dānapāramitā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of desire is the purity of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; the purity of the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom is the purity of desire.
Why is this? Because this purity of desire and the purity of the precepts up to the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of desire is the purity of internal emptiness; the purity of internal emptiness is the purity of desire. Why is this?
This purity of desire and the purity of internal emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of desire is the purity of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature. The purity of external emptiness up to the purity of the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature is itself the purity of desire.

Why is this? Because this purity of desire and the purity of external emptiness, up to and including the purity of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
"Subhūti! The purity of desire is the purity of suchness; the purity of suchness is the purity of desire. Why is this?
This purity of craving and the purity of suchness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of craving is the purity of the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, the state of equality, the nature free from birth, the fixedness of dharma, the stability of dharma, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm; and the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm is the purity of craving.
Why is this? Because the purity of this craving and the purity of the dharma-realm, up to the inconceivable realm, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of desire is the purity of the noble truth of suffering; the purity of the noble truth of suffering is the purity of desire. Why is this?
This purity of craving and the purity of the Noble Truth of Suffering are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of craving is itself the purity of the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path; the purity of the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path is itself the purity of craving.
Why is this? Because the purity of this craving and the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
"Subhūti! The purity of desire is the purity of the four dhyānas; the purity of the four dhyānas is the purity of desire. Why is this?
This purity of desire and the purity of the four dhyānas are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of desire is itself the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments; the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is itself the purity of desire.
Why is this? Because the purity of this craving and the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not severed.
"Subhūti! The purity of desire is the purity of the eight liberations; the purity of the eight liberations is the purity of desire. Why is this?
The purity of this craving and the purity of the eight liberations are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of craving is itself the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities; the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities is itself the purity of craving.

Why is this? Because the purity of this craving and the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of desire is the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness; the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness is the purity of desire. Why is this?
This purity of craving and the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of craving is itself the purity of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path; the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path is itself the purity of craving.

Why is this? Because the purity of this craving and the purity of the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path, are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divisible, they are not distinct, and they are not separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of desire is the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness; the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness is the purity of desire. Why is this?
This purity of desire and the purity of the gate of liberation of emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of desire is itself the purity of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness; the purity of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness is itself the purity of desire.

Why is this? Because the purity of this craving and the purity of the gates of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of desire is the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva; the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva is the purity of desire. Why is this?
This purity of craving and the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva are non-dual; they are not two, they are not distinct, and they are not separate. "Subhūti!
The purity of desire is the purity of the five eyes; the purity of the five eyes is the purity of desire. Why is this?
Because this purity of desire and the purity of the five eyes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
The purity of desire is the purity of the six superknowledges; the purity of the six superknowledges is the purity of desire. Why is this?
Because this purity of desire and the purity of the six superknowledges are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not severed.
“Subhūti! The purity of desire is the purity of the ten powers of the Buddha; the purity of the ten powers of the Buddha is the purity of desire. Why is this?
This purity of desire and the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of desire is itself the purity of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is itself the purity of desire.

Why is this? Because the purity of this craving and the purity of the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of desire is the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness; the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness is the purity of desire. Why is this?
This purity of desire and the purity of the qualities of non-forgetfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
The purity of desire is itself the purity of the nature of constant equanimity; the purity of the nature of constant equanimity is itself the purity of desire.
Why is this? Because the purity of this greed and the purity of the nature of constant dwelling in equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
"Subhūti! The purity of desire is the purity of all-knowledge; the purity of all-knowledge is the purity of desire. Why is this?
This purity of desire and the purity of omniscience are non-dual, undivided, distinctless, and uninterrupted.

The purity of desire is itself the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects; the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects is itself the purity of desire.
Why is this? Because the purity of this craving and the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of desire is the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors; the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors is the purity of desire.”
Why is this? Because the purity of this craving and the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
The purity of desire is the purity of all gateways to samādhi; the purity of all gateways to samādhi is the purity of desire. Why is this?
This purity of craving and the purity of all doors of samādhi are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and inseparable. "Subhūti!
The purity of desire is the purity of the fruit of stream-entry; the purity of the fruit of stream-entry is the purity of desire. Why is this?
Because this purity of desire and the purity of the fruit of stream-entry are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

The purity of craving is the purity of the fruits of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat; the purity of the fruits of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat is the purity of craving.
Why is this? Because the purity of this greed and the purity of the fruits of the Once-returner, the Non-returner, and the Arhat are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of desire is the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha; the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is the purity of desire. Why is this?
This purity of craving and the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous. "Subhūti!
The purity of desire is the purity of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; the purity of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is the purity of desire.
Why is this? Because the purity of this craving and the purity of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! The purity of desire is the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas; the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is the purity of desire.”

Why is this? Because the purity of this craving and the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
The purity of hatred is the purity of form; the purity of form is the purity of hatred. Why is this?
This purity of hatred and the purity of form are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of hatred is itself the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness; the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is itself the purity of hatred.

Why is this? Because the purity of this anger and the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of hatred is the purity of the eye-base; the purity of the eye-base is the purity of hatred. Why is this?
This purity of hatred and the purity of the sense-base of the eye are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of hatred is itself the purity of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind; the purity of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind is itself the purity of hatred.
Why is this? Because the purity of this anger and the purity of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of hatred is the purity of the sphere of form; the purity of the sphere of form is the purity of hatred. Why is this?
This purity of hatred and the purity of the sense-base of form are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of hatred is the purity of the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena; the purity of the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is the purity of hatred.

Why is this? Because the purity of this anger and the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of hatred is the purity of the eye-element; the purity of the eye-element is the purity of hatred. Why is this?
This purity of hatred and the purity of the eye-element are non-dual; they are not two, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.

The purity of hatred is the purity of the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition. The purity of the form-element, up to and including all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, is the purity of hatred.

Why is this? Because the purity of this anger and the purity of the forms of the form realm, up to and including the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of hatred is the purity of the auditory element; the purity of the auditory element is the purity of hatred. Why is this?
This purity of hatred and the purity of the ear-element are non-dual, undivided, distinctless, and uninterrupted.

The purity of hatred is the purity of the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, and ear-contact, as well as all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition; the purity of the sound-element up to all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition is the purity of hatred.

Why is this? Because the purity of this anger and the purity of the various feelings produced with the sound-element and even the ear-contact as conditions are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! The purity of hatred is the purity of the nose element; the purity of the nose element is the purity of hatred. Why is this?
The purity of hatred and the purity of the nose-element are non-dual, undivided, distinctless, and inseparable.

The purity of hatred is the purity of the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, nose-contact, and all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition; the purity of the odor-element up to the purity of all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition is the purity of hatred.

Why is this? Because the purity of this anger and the purity of the various sensations produced with the fragrance-element and even the nose-contact as conditions are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
"Subhūti! The purity of hatred is the purity of the tongue-element; the purity of the tongue-element is the purity of hatred. Why is this?
The purity of hatred and the purity of the tongue element are non-dual, undivided, distinctless, and inseparable.

The purity of hatred is the purity of the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition; the purity of the taste element up to all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition is the purity of hatred.

Why is this? Because the purity of this anger and the purity of the various feelings produced with the taste element up to tongue-contact as conditions are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of hatred is the purity of the body element; the purity of the body element is the purity of hatred. Why is this?
This purity of hatred and the purity of the body element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of hatred is the purity of the touch element, the body-consciousness element, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition; the purity of the touch element up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition is the purity of hatred.

Why is this? Because the purity of this anger and the purity of the various feelings produced with the contact element—even up to those produced with body-contact as a condition—are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of hatred is the purity of the mind-element; the purity of the mind-element is the purity of hatred. Why is this?
This purity of hatred and the purity of the mind-element (manodhātu) are non-dual; they are not two, they are not distinct, and they are not separate.

The purity of hatred is itself the purity of the dharma-element (dharmadhātu), the mind-consciousness-element (manovijñānadhātu), mental contact (manaḥsaṃsparśa), and all feelings (vedanā) produced with mental contact as condition. The purity of the dharma-element up to all feelings produced with mental contact as condition is itself the purity of hatred.

Why is this? Because the purity of this anger and the purity of everything from the dharma-realm up to the various sensations produced with mental contact as a condition are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of hatred is the purity of the earth element; the purity of the earth element is the purity of hatred. Why is this?
This purity of anger and the purity of the earth element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
The purity of anger is the purity of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements; the purity of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements is the purity of anger.

Why is this? Because the purity of this anger and the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of hatred is the purity of ignorance; the purity of ignorance is the purity of hatred. Why is this?
The purity of hatred and the purity of ignorance are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of hatred is the purity of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair; and the purity of volitional formations through to old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair is the purity of hatred.

Why is this? Because the purity of this anger and the purity of conditioned formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

This purity of hatred and the purity of internal emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of hatred is itself the purity of the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path; the purity of the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path is itself the purity of hatred.

Why is this? Because the purity of this anger and the purity of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

The purity of hatred is itself the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments; the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is itself the purity of hatred.

Why is this? Because the purity of this anger and the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of hatred is the purity of the eight liberations; the purity of the eight liberations is the purity of hatred. Why is this?
This purity of hatred and the purity of the eight liberations are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of hatred is itself the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities; the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities is itself the purity of hatred.

Why is this? Because the purity of this anger and the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of hatred is the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness; the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness is the purity of hatred. Why is this?
This purity of hatred and the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.

The purity of hatred is the purity of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path; the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path is the purity of hatred.
Why is this? Because the purity of this anger and the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.
“Subhūti! The purity of hatred is the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness; the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness is the purity of hatred. Why is this?
This purity of hatred and the purity of the emptiness liberation door are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
The purity of hatred is itself the purity of the signless and wishless liberation doors; the purity of the signless and wishless liberation doors is itself the purity of hatred.

Why is this? Because the purity of this anger and the purity of the gates of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of hatred is the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva; the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva is the purity of hatred. Why is this?
This purity of anger and the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous. "Subhūti!..."

Because this purity of hatred and the purity of the five eyes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.

“Subhūti! The purity of hatred is the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha; the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha is the purity of hatred. Why is this?
This purity of hatred and the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

“Subhūti! The purity of hatred is the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness; the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness is the purity of hatred. Why is this?
The purity of hatred and the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and inseparable.
The purity of hatred is itself the purity of the nature of constant equanimity; the purity of the nature of constant equanimity is itself the purity of hatred.
Why is this? Because the purity of this anger and the purity of the nature of constant abiding in equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of hatred is the purity of all-knowledge; the purity of all-knowledge is the purity of hatred. Why is this?
This purity of hatred and the purity of omniscience are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

“Subhūti! The purity of aversion is the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors; the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors is the purity of aversion.”

The purity of hatred is the purity of all doors of samādhi; the purity of all doors of samādhi is the purity of hatred. Why is this?
This purity of anger and the purity of all doors of samādhi are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable. "Subhūti!..."

“Subhūti! The purity of hatred is the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha; the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is the purity of hatred. Why is this?

“Subhūti! The purity of hatred is the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas; the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is the purity of hatred.”
