"Furthermore, Subhūti!
The purity of ignorance is the purity of form; the purity of form is the purity of ignorance. Why is this?
This purity of ignorance and the purity of form are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
The purity of ignorance is the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness; the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is the purity of ignorance.

Why is this? Because the purity of ignorance and the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of ignorance is the purity of the eye-base; the purity of the eye-base is the purity of ignorance. Why is this?
This purity of ignorance and the purity of the sense base of the eye are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of ignorance is itself the purity of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind; and the purity of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind is itself the purity of ignorance.

Why is this? Because this purity of ignorance and the purity of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
"Subhūti! The purity of ignorance is the purity of the sphere of form; the purity of the sphere of form is the purity of ignorance. Why is this?
This purity of ignorance and the purity of the sense-base of form are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

The purity of ignorance is the purity of the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena; the purity of the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena is the purity of ignorance.
Why is this? Because this purity of ignorance and the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of ignorance is the purity of the eye-element; the purity of the eye-element is the purity of ignorance. Why is this?
This purity of ignorance and the purity of the eye-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of ignorance is the purity of the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, and eye-contact, as well as all sensations produced with eye-contact as a condition; the purity of the form-element up to all sensations produced with eye-contact as a condition is the purity of ignorance.

Why is this? Because the purity of this ignorance and the purity of the forms of the form realm, up to and including the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of ignorance is the purity of the ear-element; the purity of the ear-element is the purity of ignorance. Why is this?
This purity of ignorance and the purity of the ear-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of ignorance is itself the purity of the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and all sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition; the purity of the sound-element up to all sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition is itself the purity of ignorance.

Why is this? Because the purity of this ignorance and the purity of all feelings produced with conditions ranging from the sound-element up to ear-contact are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of ignorance is the purity of the nose element; the purity of the nose element is the purity of ignorance. Why is this?
This purity of ignorance and the purity of the nose-element are non-dual; they are not two, they are not distinct, and they are not separate.

The purity of ignorance is the purity of the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, nose-contact, and all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition. The purity of the odor-element up to all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition is the purity of ignorance.

Why is this? Because this purity of ignorance and the purity of the various feelings produced with the fragrance-element up to the nose-contact as condition are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
"Subhūti! The purity of ignorance is the purity of the tongue-element; the purity of the tongue-element is the purity of ignorance. Why is this?
This purity of ignorance and the purity of the tongue-element are non-dual; they are not two, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.

The purity of ignorance is the purity of the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition. The purity of the taste-element up to all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition is the purity of ignorance.

Why is this? Because the purity of this ignorance and the purity of the various feelings produced with the taste-element up to tongue-contact as conditions are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of ignorance is the purity of the body-element; the purity of the body-element is the purity of ignorance. Why is this?
This purity of ignorance and the purity of the body-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of ignorance is the purity of the contact-element, the body-consciousness-element, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition; the purity of the contact-element up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition is the purity of ignorance.

Why is this? Because this purity of ignorance and the purity of the various feelings produced with contact as a condition—up to those produced with body-contact as a condition—are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! The purity of delusion is the purity of the mind-element (manodhātu), and the purity of the mind-element is the purity of delusion. Why is this?
This purity of ignorance and the purity of the mind-element (*manodhātu*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of ignorance is itself the purity of the dharma-element (*dharmadhātu*), the mind-consciousness-element (*manovijñānadhātu*), mental contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*), and all feelings produced with mental contact as condition; conversely, the purity of the dharma-element up to all feelings produced with mental contact as condition is itself the purity of ignorance.

Why is this? Because this purity of ignorance and the purity of everything from the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of ignorance is the purity of the earth element; the purity of the earth element is the purity of ignorance. Why is this?
This purity of ignorance and the purity of the earth element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of ignorance is itself the purity of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements; the purity of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements is itself the purity of ignorance.

Why is this? Because this purity of ignorance and the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! The purity of delusion is the purity of ignorance; the purity of ignorance is the purity of delusion. Why is this?
This purity of ignorance and purity of non-arising are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of ignorance is the purity of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair; and the purity of volitional formations through to old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair is the purity of ignorance.

Why is this? Because the purity of ignorance and the purity of formations, up to and including old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, are non-dual; they are not two, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! The purity of delusion is the purity of the perfection of generosity; the purity of the perfection of generosity is the purity of delusion.”
Why is this? Because the purity of ignorance and the purity of the perfection of generosity are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
The purity of delusion is the purity of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
The purity of the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom is the purity of delusion.
Why is this? Because this purity of ignorance and the purity of the precepts up to the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.
“Subhūti! The purity of ignorance is the purity of internal emptiness; the purity of internal emptiness is the purity of ignorance. Why is this?
This purity of ignorance and the purity of internal emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of ignorance is the purity of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, emptiness of all phenomena, emptiness of the unapprehendable, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, and emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence. The purity of external emptiness up to the purity of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is itself the purity of ignorance.

Why is this? Because this purity of ignorance and the purity of external emptiness, up to the purity of the emptiness of the nature of non-existence, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of ignorance is the purity of suchness; the purity of suchness is the purity of ignorance. Why is this?
This purity of ignorance and the purity of *tathatā* (suchness) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of ignorance is the purity of the *dharmadhātu*, the *dharmatā*, the non-erroneous nature, the unchanging nature, the state of equality, the nature free from arising, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharma-niyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharma-sthititā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm. The purity of the *dharmadhātu* up to the inconceivable realm is itself the purity of ignorance.

Why is this? Because the purity of this ignorance and the purity of the dharma-realm, up to and including the inconceivable realm, are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! The purity of ignorance is the purity of the noble truth of suffering; the purity of the noble truth of suffering is the purity of ignorance. Why is this?
The purity of ignorance and the purity of the noble truth of suffering are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of ignorance is itself the purity of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path; the purity of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path is itself the purity of ignorance.
Why is this? Because the purity of ignorance and the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of ignorance is the purity of the four dhyānas; the purity of the four dhyānas is the purity of ignorance. Why is this?
The purity of ignorance and the purity of the four dhyānas are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
The purity of ignorance is the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments; the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is the purity of ignorance.

Why is this? Because the purity of this ignorance and the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of ignorance is the purity of the eight liberations; the purity of the eight liberations is the purity of ignorance. Why is this?
This purity of ignorance and the purity of the eight liberations are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of ignorance is itself the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities; the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities is itself the purity of ignorance.

Why is this? Because the purity of this ignorance and the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of ignorance is the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness; the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness is the purity of ignorance. Why is this?
This purity of ignorance and the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of ignorance is itself the purity of the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path; and the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path is itself the purity of ignorance.
Why is this? Because the purity of this ignorance and the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
"Subhūti! The purity of ignorance is the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness; the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness is the purity of ignorance. Why is this?
This purity of ignorance and the purity of the gate of liberation of emptiness are non-dual; they are not two, they are not distinct, and there is no separation between them.

The purity of ignorance is itself the purity of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness; the purity of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness is itself the purity of ignorance.
Why is this? Because the purity of this ignorance and the purity of the gates of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of delusion is the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva; the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva is the purity of delusion. Why is this?
This purity of delusion and the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate. "Subhūti!
The purity of ignorance is the purity of the five eyes; the purity of the five eyes is the purity of ignorance. Why is this?
Because this purity of ignorance and the purity of the five eyes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
The purity of ignorance is the purity of the six supernormal powers, and the purity of the six supernormal powers is the purity of ignorance. Why is this?
Because this purity of ignorance and the purity of the six supernormal powers are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of delusion is the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha; the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha is the purity of delusion. Why is this?
This purity of ignorance and the purity of the Buddha’s ten powers are non-dual, undivided, distinctless, and inseparable.

The purity of ignorance is the purity of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is itself the purity of ignorance.

Why is this? Because the purity of this ignorance and the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of delusion is the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness; the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness is the purity of delusion. Why is that?
This purity of ignorance and the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.
The purity of ignorance is the purity of the nature of constant equanimity, and the purity of the nature of constant equanimity is the purity of ignorance.
Why is this? Because the purity of this ignorance and the purity of the nature of constant equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! The purity of ignorance is the purity of all-knowledge; the purity of all-knowledge is the purity of ignorance. Why is this?
This purity of ignorance and the purity of all-knowledge are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of ignorance is the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects; the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects is the purity of ignorance.

Why is this? Because the purity of this ignorance and the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! The purity of delusion is the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors; the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors is the purity of delusion.”
Why is this? Because the purity of this ignorance and the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
The purity of delusion is the purity of all gateways to samādhi; the purity of all gateways to samādhi is the purity of delusion. Why is this?
This purity of delusion and the purity of all gateways to samādhi are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are not distinct, and they are not separate. "Subhūti!
The purity of ignorance is the purity of the fruit of stream-entry; the purity of the fruit of stream-entry is the purity of ignorance. Why is this?
Because this purity of ignorance and the purity of the fruit of stream-entry are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

The purity of ignorance is the purity of the fruits of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat; the purity of the fruits of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat is the purity of ignorance.

Why is this? Because this purity of ignorance and the purity of the fruit of the once-returner, the non-returner, and arhatship are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! The purity of ignorance is the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha; the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is the purity of ignorance. Why is this?
This purity of ignorance and the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha are non-dual; they are not divided into two, are not distinct, and are not severed. "Subhūti!..."
The purity of ignorance is the purity of all the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; the purity of all the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is the purity of ignorance.
Why is this? Because this purity of ignorance and the purity of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! The purity of ignorance is the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas; the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is the purity of ignorance.”

Why is this? Because this purity of ignorance and the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because desire is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure. Why is that?
Whether it be the purity of desire, the purity of form, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because craving is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of desire, or the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because desire is pure, the sense-sphere of the eye is pure; because the sense-sphere of the eye is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of desire, the purity of the sense base of the eye, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and inseparable.

Because greed is pure, the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of desire, or the purity of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because desire is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is that?

Whether it be the purity of craving, the purity of the sense-sphere of form, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because greed is pure, the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure; because the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of desire, the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because desire is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of desire, the purity of the eye-element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because desire is pure, the form realm, the eye-consciousness realm, and eye-contact, as well as all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, are pure; because the form realm up to all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of desire, the purity of the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because desire is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is that?

Whether it be the purity of desire, the purity of the ear-element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because greed is pure, the sound element, the ear-consciousness element, and ear-contact, as well as all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, are pure; because the sound element up to all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of desire, the purity of the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because desire is pure, the nose element is pure; because the nose element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of desire, the purity of the nose element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because greed is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because if desire is pure, if the realm of fragrance—and indeed all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition—are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because desire is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of desire, the purity of the tongue-element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because greed is pure, the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, and tongue-contact, as well as all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, are pure; because the taste-element up to all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because if desire is pure, if the taste element and even the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because desire is pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is that?

Whether it be the purity of craving, the purity of the body element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because craving is pure, the sphere of tangibles, the sphere of body-consciousness, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because if desire is pure, if the sphere of tangibles and even the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because desire is pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of desire, the purity of the mental faculty (manodhātu), or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because craving is pure, the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, and mind-contact, as well as all feelings produced with mind-contact as condition, are pure; because the dharma-element up to all feelings produced with mind-contact as condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because if desire is pure, and if the dharma-realm, up to and including the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition, are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because desire is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of desire, the purity of the earth element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because greed is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of desire, the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because desire is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of craving, the purity of ignorance, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because craving is pure, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of craving, or the purity of the formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because desire is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of desire, the purity of the perfection of generosity, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
Because greed is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure.
Because the perfections of ethical discipline up to wisdom are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of desire, the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because desire is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of desire, the purity of internal emptiness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because greed is pure, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure. Because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of desire, the purity of external emptiness up to the purity of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because desire is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is that?
Whether it be the purity of desire, the purity of suchness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because greed is pure, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-falsity, the immutability, the equality, the nature free from birth, the fixedness of dharma, the stability of dharma, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm are pure; because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of desire, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because desire is pure, the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure; because the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

If the purification of anger, the purification of the fruit of stream-entry, and the purification of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because hatred is pure, the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure; because the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because if the purification of anger is the same as the purification of the fruit of a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat, and the purification of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because hatred is pure, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is that?
If the purity of anger, the purity of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because hatred is pure, all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure; because all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because if hatred is pure, if the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because hatred is pure, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is pure; because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because if the purification of anger, the purification of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas, and the purification of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because ignorance is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is that?
If ignorance is pure, if form is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because delusion is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because if ignorance is pure, and if feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because delusion is pure, the eye-base is pure; because the eye-base is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If delusion is pure, if the sense-base of the eye is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
Because delusion is pure, the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because if ignorance is pure, and if the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because ignorance is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If ignorance is pure, if the sphere of form is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because ignorance is pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of ignorance, the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, and the purity of the knowledge of all-knowledge are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because ignorance is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of ignorance, the purity of the eye-element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because delusion is pure, the form realm, the eye-consciousness realm, and eye-contact, as well as all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, are pure; because the form realm up to all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because if ignorance is pure, and if everything from the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because ignorance is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If delusion is pure, if the ear-element is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because delusion is pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of ear-consciousness, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of sound up to all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because if ignorance is pure, and if the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because ignorance is pure, the nose-element is pure; because the nose-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If delusion is pure, if the nose element is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because delusion is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because if ignorance is pure, if the fragrance-element up to the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because ignorance is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If delusion is pure, if the tongue element is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because delusion is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because if ignorance is pure, and if the taste element, up to and including the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because delusion is pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is that?
If delusion is pure, if the body element is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not severed.

Because delusion is pure, the sphere of tangibles, the sphere of body-consciousness, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because if ignorance is pure, and if the sphere of contact, up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not separate.
“Subhūti! Because ignorance is pure, the mind-element (*manodhātu*) is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure. Why is that?
If delusion is pure, if the mind-element is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because delusion is pure, the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness element, and mental contact, as well as all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are pure; because the dharma-element up to all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because if ignorance is pure, and if everything from the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because delusion is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If ignorance is pure, if the earth element is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because delusion is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of ignorance, the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (sarvajñajñāna), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because ignorance is pure, non-ignorance is pure; because non-ignorance is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is that?
Whether it is the purity of delusion, the purity of ignorance, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because ignorance is pure, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of ignorance, or the purity of formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because delusion is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of ignorance, the purity of the perfection of generosity, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because delusion is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of delusion, the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because delusion is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If delusion is pure, if internal emptiness is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because delusion is pure, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure; because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because if ignorance is pure, and if the emptiness of the external up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because delusion is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of delusion, the purity of suchness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because delusion is pure, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-erroneous nature, the unchanging nature, the state of equality, the nature free from birth, the fixedness of dharma, the stability of dharma, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm are pure. Because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because if ignorance is pure, if the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because ignorance is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure; because the noble truth of suffering is pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure. Why is this?
If delusion is pure, if the noble truth of suffering is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
Because delusion is pure, the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because if ignorance is pure, if the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because ignorance is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If there is purity of ignorance, purity of the four dhyānas, and purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because delusion is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of ignorance, the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because delusion is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is that?
If there is purity of delusion, purity of the eight liberations, and purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because delusion is pure, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because if ignorance is pure, and if the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because delusion is pure, the four applications of mindfulness are pure; because the four applications of mindfulness are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is that?"

If ignorance is pure, if the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because delusion is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because if ignorance is pure, and if the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because delusion is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If delusion is pure, if the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and inseparable.
Because delusion is pure, the gates of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are pure; because the gates of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of delusion, the purity of the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and inseparable.
"Subhūti! Because delusion is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is that?
If ignorance is pure, if the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because delusion is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of ignorance, the purity of the five eyes, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because ignorance is pure, the six supernormal powers are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of ignorance, the purity of the six supernormal powers, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because ignorance is pure, the ten powers of the Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of the Buddha are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If delusion is pure, if the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because delusion is pure, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because if ignorance is pure, if the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because delusion is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If delusion is pure, if the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because ignorance is pure, the state of constant abiding in equanimity is pure; because the state of constant abiding in equanimity is pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure. Why is this?

Because whether it is the purity of ignorance, the purity of the state of constant abiding in equanimity, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because delusion is pure, all-knowledge is pure; because all-knowledge is pure, the knowledge of all-knowledge is pure. Why is that?
If ignorance is pure, if omniscience is pure, and if the knowledge of omniscience is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because delusion is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because if ignorance is pure, if the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because delusion is pure, all dhāraṇī-doors are pure; because all dhāraṇī-doors are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of ignorance, the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because delusion is pure, all gateways to samādhi are pure; because all gateways to samādhi are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure. Why is this?
If ignorance is pure, if all doors of samādhi are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because delusion is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If delusion is pure, if the fruit of stream-entry is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because delusion is pure, the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure; because the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of ignorance, the purity of the fruit of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because delusion is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If ignorance is pure, if the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because delusion is pure, all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure; because all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of ignorance, the purity of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because delusion is pure, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is pure; because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of ignorance, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
The Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle Two Hundred and Three; Fascicle Two Hundred and Four,
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang under imperial decree.
The First Division, Chapter Thirty-Four, Part Twenty-Three:
"Furthermore, Subhūti, because form is pure, feeling is pure; because feeling is pure, form is pure."
Why is this? Because the purity of form and the purity of feeling are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
Because feeling is pure, perception is pure; because perception is pure, feeling is pure.
Why is this? Because this purity of feeling and this purity of perception are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
Because perception is pure, volitional formations are pure; because volitional formations are pure, perception is pure.
Why is this? It is because the purity of perception and the purity of formations are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
Because formations are pure, consciousness is pure; because consciousness is pure, formations are pure.
Why is this? Because the purity of these formations and the purity of consciousness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
Because consciousness is pure, the sense base of the eye is pure; because the sense base of the eye is pure, consciousness is pure.
Why is this? This purity of consciousness and the purity of the eye-base are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.
Because the eye-base is pure, the ear-base is pure; because the ear-base is pure, the eye-base is pure.
Why is this? Because the purity of the sense-base of the eye and the purity of the sense-base of the ear are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Through the purity of the sense-base of the ear, there is the purity of the sense-base of the nose; through the purity of the sense-base of the nose, there is the purity of the sense-base of the ear.
Why is this? Because the purity of the sense-base of the ear and the purity of the sense-base of the nose are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Through the purity of the sense-base of the nose, there is the purity of the sense-base of the tongue; through the purity of the sense-base of the tongue, there is the purity of the sense-base of the nose.
Why is this? Because the purity of the sense base of the nose and the purity of the sense base of the tongue are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the sense base of the tongue is pure, the sense base of the body is pure; because the sense base of the body is pure, the sense base of the tongue is pure.
Why is this? Because the purity of the sense-base of the tongue and the purity of the sense-base of the body are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Through the purity of the sense-base of the body, there is the purity of the sense-base of the mind; through the purity of the sense-base of the mind, there is the purity of the sense-base of the body.
Why is this? Because the purity of the sphere of body and the purity of the sphere of mind are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
Because the sphere of mind is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the sphere of mind is pure.
Why is this? Because the purity of the sense base of mind and the purity of the sense base of form are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
Because the sense base of form is pure, the sense base of sound is pure; because the sense base of sound is pure, the sense base of form is pure.
Why is this? Because the purity of the sphere of form and the purity of the sphere of sound are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
Through the purity of the sphere of sound, there is the purity of the sphere of odor; through the purity of the sphere of odor, there is the purity of the sphere of sound.
Why is this? Because the purity of the sphere of sound and the purity of the sphere of odor are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
Because the sphere of odor is pure, the sphere of taste is pure; because the sphere of taste is pure, the sphere of odor is pure.
Why is this? Because the purity of the sphere of fragrance and the purity of the sphere of taste are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
Because the sphere of taste is pure, the sphere of tangibles is pure; because the sphere of tangibles is pure, the sphere of taste is pure.
Why is this? Because the purity of the sphere of taste and the purity of the sphere of tangibles are non-dual, not two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
Because the sphere of tangibles is pure, the sphere of phenomena is pure; because the sphere of phenomena is pure, the sphere of tangibles is pure.
Why is this? Because the purity of the sense-field of tangibles and the purity of the sense-field of mental objects are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
Because the sense-field of mental objects is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the sense-field of mental objects is pure.
Why is this? Because the purity of the sphere of mental objects (*dharmāyatana*) and the purity of the eye-element (*cakṣurdhātu*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
"Because the eye-element is pure, the form-element (*rūpadhātu*) is pure; because the form-element is pure, the eye-element is pure."
Why is this? Because the purity of the eye-element and the purity of the form-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
Through the purity of the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element is pure; through the purity of the eye-consciousness-element, the form-element is pure.
Why is this? Because the purity of the form realm and the purity of the eye-consciousness realm are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the eye-consciousness element is pure, eye-contact is pure; because eye-contact is pure, the eye-consciousness element is pure.
Why is this? Because this purity of the eye-consciousness element and this purity of eye-contact are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because eye-contact is pure, the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure; because the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, eye-contact is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of eye-contact and the purity of the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure.
Why is this? Because the purity of all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition and the purity of the ear-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Because the ear-element is pure, the sound-element is pure; because the sound-element is pure, the ear-element is pure.
Why is this? Because this purity of the ear-element and the purity of the sound-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.”
Because the sphere of sound is pure, the sphere of ear-consciousness is pure; because the sphere of ear-consciousness is pure, the sphere of sound is pure.
Why is this? Because this purity of the sphere of sound and the purity of the sphere of ear-consciousness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the ear-consciousness element is pure, auditory contact is pure; because auditory contact is pure, the ear-consciousness element is pure.
Why is this? Because this purity of the ear-consciousness element and the purity of auditory contact are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor separate.

Because ear-contact is pure, the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure; because the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure, ear-contact is pure.
Why is this? Because the purity of ear-contact and the purity of the various sensations arising with ear-contact as a condition are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure, the nose-element is pure; because the nose-element is pure, the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure.
Why is this? Because the purity of all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition and the purity of the nose element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Because the nose-element is pure, the odor-element is pure; because the odor-element is pure, the nose-element is pure.
Why is this? Because this purity of the nose-element and the purity of the odor-element are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.”
Because the realm of fragrance is pure, the realm of olfactory consciousness is pure; because the realm of olfactory consciousness is pure, the realm of fragrance is pure. Why is this?
Because this purity of the realm of fragrance and the purity of the realm of olfactory consciousness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the nose-consciousness element is pure, nose-contact is pure; because nose-contact is pure, the nose-consciousness element is pure.
Why is this? Because this purity of the nose-consciousness element and this purity of nose-contact are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.

Because nose-contact is pure, the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, nose-contact is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of nose-contact and the purity of the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.

Because the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure.
Why is this? Because the purity of all sensations produced with nose-contact as condition and the purity of the tongue-element are non-dual; they are not two, indivisible, distinct, or separate.
“Because the tongue-element is pure, the taste-element is pure; because the taste-element is pure, the tongue-element is pure.
Why is this? Because this purity of the tongue-element and the purity of the taste-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.”
Because the realm of taste is pure, the realm of tongue-consciousness is pure; because the realm of tongue-consciousness is pure, the realm of taste is pure.
Why is this? Because this purity of the realm of taste and the purity of the realm of tongue-consciousness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the tongue-consciousness element is pure, tongue-contact is pure; because tongue-contact is pure, the tongue-consciousness element is pure.
Why is this? Because this purity of the tongue-consciousness element and the purity of tongue-contact are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the purity of tongue-contact, the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as condition are pure; because the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as condition are pure, tongue-contact is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of tongue-contact and the purity of the various sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition are non-dual; they are not two, not divided, not distinct, and not separate.

Because the various sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, the various sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition and the purity of the body-element are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are without distinction, and they are not separate.
“Because the body element (*kāyadhātu*) is pure, the touch element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*) is pure; because the touch element is pure, the body element is pure. Why is this?
Because this purity of the body element and the purity of the touch element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.”
Because the realm of tangibles is pure, the realm of body-consciousness is pure; because the realm of body-consciousness is pure, the realm of tangibles is pure. Why is this?
Because the purity of the realm of tangibles and the purity of the realm of body-consciousness are non-dual, not two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
Because the body-consciousness element is pure, body-contact is pure; because body-contact is pure, the body-consciousness element is pure.
Why is this? Because this purity of the body-consciousness element and the purity of body-contact are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because body-contact is pure, the various feelings arising with body-contact as condition are pure; because the various feelings arising with body-contact as condition are pure, body-contact is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of body-contact and the purity of the various feelings arising with body-contact as a condition are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, not separate, and not discontinuous.

Because the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of all sensations produced with bodily contact as a condition and the purity of the mental element (manodhātu) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Because the mind-element (*manodhātu*) is pure, the dharma-element (*dharmadhātu*) is pure; because the dharma-element is pure, the mind-element is pure. Why is this?
Because this purity of the mind-element and the purity of the dharma-element are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.”
Because the dharma-realm is pure, the consciousness-realm is pure; because the consciousness-realm is pure, the dharma-realm is pure.
Why is this? Because this purity of the dharma-realm and the purity of the consciousness-realm are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
Because the sphere of mental consciousness is pure, mental contact is pure; because mental contact is pure, the sphere of mental consciousness is pure.
Why is this? Because this purity of the sphere of mental consciousness and this purity of mental contact are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because mental contact is pure, the various feelings arising with mental contact as a condition are pure; because the various feelings arising with mental contact as a condition are pure, mental contact is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of mental contact and the purity of all sensations produced with mental contact as a condition are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.

Because the feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition and the purity of the earth element are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“Because the earth element is pure, the water element is pure; because the water element is pure, the earth element is pure.
Why is this? Because this purity of the earth element and the purity of the water element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.”
Because the water element is pure, the fire element is pure; because the fire element is pure, the water element is pure.
Why is this? Because this purity of the water element and the purity of the fire element are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the fire element is pure, the wind element is pure; because the wind element is pure, the fire element is pure.
Why is this? Because this purity of the fire element and the purity of the wind element are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the wind element is pure, the space element is pure; because the space element is pure, the wind element is pure.
Why is this? Because this purity of the wind element and the purity of the space element are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the element of space is pure, the element of consciousness is pure; because the element of consciousness is pure, the element of space is pure. Why is this?
Because this purity of the element of space and the purity of the element of consciousness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the element of consciousness is pure, the element of space is pure; because the element of space is pure, the element of consciousness is pure. Why is this?
Because this purity of the element of consciousness and the purity of the element of space are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Because ignorance is pure, volitional formations are pure; because volitional formations are pure, ignorance is pure.
Why is this? Because this purity of ignorance and this purity of volitional formations are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.”
Because formations are pure, consciousness is pure; because consciousness is pure, formations are pure.
Why is this? Because these purities of formations and purities of consciousness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
Because consciousness is pure, name-and-form are pure; because name-and-form are pure, consciousness is pure.
Why is this? Because this purity of consciousness and the purity of name-and-form are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because name-and-form (*nāmarūpa*) is pure, the six sense bases (*ṣaḍāyatana*) are pure; because the six sense bases are pure, name-and-form is pure. Why is this?
Because this purity of name-and-form and the purity of the six sense bases are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the six sense bases are pure, contact is pure; because contact is pure, the six sense bases are pure.
Why is this? Because this purity of the six sense bases and the purity of contact are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
Because contact is pure, feeling is pure; because feeling is pure, contact is pure.
Why is this? Because this purity of contact and purity of feeling are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because feeling is pure, craving is pure; because craving is pure, feeling is pure.
Why is this? Because this purity of feeling and this purity of craving are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because craving is pure, grasping is pure; because grasping is pure, craving is pure.
Why is this? Because this purity of craving and the purity of grasping are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
Because of clinging there is becoming; because of becoming there is clinging. Why is this?
