Because this clinging and this becoming are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because of existence there is birth, and because of birth there is existence. Why is this?
Because this existence and this birth are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because birth is pure, old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are pure; because old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are pure, birth is pure. Why is this?
This purity of birth and the purity of old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are non-dual; they are not two, they are not distinct, and they are not separate.

Because of the purity of old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, there is the purity of the perfection of generosity (*dānapāramitā*); because of the purity of the perfection of generosity, there is the purity of old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair.

Why is this? Because the purity of old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair is non-dual with the purity of the perfection of generosity; they are not two, cannot be divided, are not distinct, and are not separate.
Because the perfection of generosity is pure, the perfection of ethical discipline is pure; because the perfection of ethical discipline is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure.
Why is this? Because the purity of this perfection of generosity and the purity of the perfection of ethical discipline are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
Because the perfection of ethical discipline is pure, the perfection of patience is pure; because the perfection of patience is pure, the perfection of ethical discipline is pure.
Why is this? Because the purity of this perfection of ethical discipline and the purity of the perfection of patience are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
Because the perfection of patience is pure, the perfection of diligence is pure; because the perfection of diligence is pure, the perfection of patience is pure.
Why is this? Because the purity of this perfection of patience and the purity of the perfection of diligence are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
Because the perfection of diligence is pure, the perfection of meditative concentration is pure; because the perfection of meditative concentration is pure, the perfection of diligence is pure.
Why is this? Because the purity of this perfection of diligence and the purity of the perfection of meditative concentration are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
Because the perfection of meditative concentration is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the perfection of wisdom is pure, the perfection of meditative concentration is pure.
Why is this? Because the purity of this perfection of meditative concentration and the purity of the perfection of wisdom are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure. Why is this?
This purity of the perfection of wisdom and the purity of internal emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
Because internal emptiness is pure, external emptiness is pure; because external emptiness is pure, internal emptiness is pure.
Why is this? Because the purity of internal emptiness and the purity of external emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
Because external emptiness is pure, internal-and-external emptiness is pure; because internal-and-external emptiness is pure, external emptiness is pure.
Why is this? Because the purity of external emptiness and the purity of internal-and-external emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
Because internal and external emptiness is pure, the emptiness of emptiness is pure; because the emptiness of emptiness is pure, internal and external emptiness is pure. Why is this?
Because this purity of internal and external emptiness and this purity of the emptiness of emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
Because the emptiness of emptiness is pure, the great emptiness is pure; because the great emptiness is pure, the emptiness of emptiness is pure. Why is this?
Because this purity of the emptiness of emptiness and the purity of the great emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the great emptiness (*mahāśūnyatā*) is pure, the ultimate emptiness (*paramārtha-śūnyatā*) is pure; because the ultimate emptiness is pure, the great emptiness is pure. Why is this?
Because this purity of the great emptiness and the purity of the ultimate emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because ultimate emptiness is pure, conditioned emptiness is pure; because conditioned emptiness is pure, ultimate emptiness is pure.
Why is this? Because this purity of ultimate emptiness and the purity of conditioned emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because the emptiness of the conditioned is pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure; because the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure, the emptiness of the conditioned is pure. Why is this?
Because the purity of the emptiness of the conditioned and the purity of the emptiness of the unconditioned are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the emptiness of the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta-śūnyatā*) is pure, the ultimate emptiness (*atyanta-śūnyatā*) is pure; because the ultimate emptiness is pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure. Why is this?
Because this purity of the emptiness of the unconditioned and the purity of the ultimate emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the emptiness of ultimate limit is pure, the emptiness of no-limit is pure; because the emptiness of no-limit is pure, the emptiness of ultimate limit is pure. Why is this?
Because this purity of the emptiness of ultimate limit and the purity of the emptiness of no-limit are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
Because the emptiness of the limitless is pure, the emptiness of dispersion is pure; because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, the emptiness of the limitless is pure. Why is this?
Because this purity of the emptiness of the limitless and the purity of the emptiness of dispersion are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, the emptiness of non-alteration is pure; because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, the emptiness of dispersion is pure. Why is this?
Because this purity of the emptiness of dispersion and this purity of the emptiness of non-alteration are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, the emptiness of intrinsic nature is pure; because the emptiness of intrinsic nature is pure, the emptiness of non-alteration is pure. Why is this?
This purity of the emptiness of non-alteration and the purity of the emptiness of intrinsic nature are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
Because the emptiness of intrinsic nature is pure, the emptiness of self-characteristics is pure; because the emptiness of self-characteristics is pure, the emptiness of intrinsic nature is pure.
Why is this? Because this purity of essential nature and the purity of emptiness of self-characteristics are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the emptiness of self-characteristics is pure, the emptiness of common characteristics is pure; because the emptiness of common characteristics is pure, the emptiness of self-characteristics is pure. Why is this?
Because this purity of the emptiness of self-characteristics and this purity of the emptiness of common characteristics are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
Because the emptiness of common characteristics is pure, all dharmas are pure; because all dharmas are pure, the emptiness of common characteristics is pure. Why is this?
The purity of the emptiness of common characteristics and the purity of the emptiness of all phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the purity of the emptiness of all phenomena exists, there is the purity of the emptiness of the unapprehendable; because the purity of the emptiness of the unapprehendable exists, there is the purity of the emptiness of all phenomena.
Why is this? Because the purity of the emptiness of all dharmas and the purity of the emptiness of the unapprehendable are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
Because the emptiness of non-apprehension is pure, the emptiness of non-existence is pure; because the emptiness of non-existence is pure, the emptiness of non-apprehension is pure. Why is this?
The purity of the emptiness of the unapprehendable and the purity of the emptiness of non-existence are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate,

because the purity of the emptiness of non-existence is the purity of the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the purity of the emptiness of intrinsic nature is the purity of the emptiness of non-existence.
Why is this? Because the purity of the emptiness of non-existence and the purity of the emptiness of intrinsic nature are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not severed.

Because the emptiness of intrinsic nature is pure, the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature is pure; because the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature is pure, the emptiness of intrinsic nature is pure. Why is this?
This is because the purity of the emptiness of intrinsic nature and the purity of the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
Because the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature is pure.
Why is this? Because the purity of the self-nature-emptiness of non-existence and the purity of suchness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Because suchness is pure, the dharma-realm is pure; because the dharma-realm is pure, suchness is pure.
Why is this? Because this purity of suchness and the purity of the dharma-realm are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.”
Because the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*) is pure, the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*) is pure; because the nature of phenomena is pure, the dharma-realm is pure.
Why is this? Because this purity of the dharma-realm and the purity of the nature of phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
Because the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*) is pure, the non-falsity is pure; because the non-falsity is pure, the nature of phenomena is pure. Why is this?
Because this purity of the nature of phenomena and the purity of non-falsity are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
Because the nature of non-falsity is pure, the nature of immutability is pure; because the nature of immutability is pure, the nature of non-falsity is pure. Why is this?
This purity of non-falsity and purity of immutability are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
Because of the purity of immutability, there is the purity of equality; because of the purity of equality, there is the purity of immutability.
Why is this? Because this purity of immutability and purity of equality are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the purity of equality is the purity of the nature of being free from birth, and because the purity of the nature of being free from birth is the purity of equality. Why is this?
Because this purity of equality and the purity of the nature of being free from birth are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
Because the nature of detachment from birth is pure, phenomena are pure; because phenomena are pure, the nature of detachment from birth is pure.
Why is this? Because this purity of the nature of detachment from birth and the purity of phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the purity of phenomena is the purity of the abiding of phenomena; because the purity of the abiding of phenomena is the purity of the nature of phenomena. Why is this?
Because this purity of the nature of phenomena and the purity of the abiding of phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the abiding of phenomena (*dharmasthiti*) is pure, the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) is pure; because the limit of reality is pure, the abiding of phenomena is pure. Why is this?
Because this purity of the abiding of phenomena and the purity of the limit of reality are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) is pure, the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*) is pure; because the realm of space is pure, the limit of reality is pure.
Why is this? Because this purity of the limit of reality and the purity of the realm of space are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
Because the realm of space is pure, the inconceivable realm is pure; because the inconceivable realm is pure, the realm of space is pure. Why is this?
The purity of the realm of space and the purity of the inconceivable realm are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
Because the inconceivable realm is pure, the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure; because the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure, the inconceivable realm is pure.
Why is this? Because the purity of this inconceivable realm and the purity of the noble truth of suffering are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Because the noble truth of suffering is pure, the noble truth of the origin of suffering is pure; because the noble truth of the origin of suffering is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure. Why is this?
Because this purity of the noble truth of suffering and the purity of the noble truth of the origin of suffering are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.”
Because the noble truth of origination is pure, the noble truth of cessation is pure; because the noble truth of cessation is pure, the noble truth of origination is pure. Why is this?
Because the purity of the noble truth of origination and the purity of the noble truth of cessation are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
Because the noble truth of cessation is pure, the noble truth of the path is pure; because the noble truth of the path is pure, the noble truth of cessation is pure. Why is this?
Because this purity of the noble truth of cessation and the purity of the noble truth of the path are non-dual, not divided into two, not distinct, and not discontinuous.
Because the noble truth of the path is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the noble truth of the path is pure. Why is this?
Because this purity of the noble truth of the path and the purity of the four dhyānas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Because the four dhyānas are pure, the four immeasurables are pure; because the four immeasurables are pure, the four dhyānas are pure.
Why is this? Because the purity of these four dhyānas and the purity of the four immeasurables are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.”
Because the four immeasurables are pure, the four formless absorptions are pure; because the four formless absorptions are pure, the four immeasurables are pure. Why is this?
The purity of these four immeasurables and the purity of the four formless absorptions are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
Because the four formless absorptions are pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the four formless absorptions are pure.
Why is this? Because the purity of these four formless absorptions and the purity of the eight liberations are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Because the eight liberations are pure, the eight bases of mastery are pure; because the eight bases of mastery are pure, the eight liberations are pure. Why is this?
Because this purity of the eight liberations and this purity of the eight bases of mastery are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.”
Because the eight bases of mastery are pure, the nine successive attainments are pure; because the nine successive attainments are pure, the eight bases of mastery are pure. Why is this?
The purity of these eight bases of mastery and the purity of the nine successive attainments are non-dual, not divided, distinct, and uninterrupted.
Because the nine successive attainments are pure, the ten totalities are pure; because the ten totalities are pure, the nine successive attainments are pure.
Why is this? Because the purity of these nine successive attainments and the purity of the ten totalities are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the ten spheres of totality (*daśa kṛtsnāyatana*) are pure, the four foundations of mindfulness (*catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni*) are pure; because the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, the ten spheres of totality are pure.
Why is this? Because this purity of the ten spheres of totality and the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

“Because the purification of the four foundations of mindfulness is the purification of the four right endeavors, and because the purification of the four right endeavors is the purification of the four foundations of mindfulness. Why is this?
Because this purification of the four foundations of mindfulness and the purification of the four right endeavors are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.”
Because the purity of the four right efforts is the purity of the four bases of power, and because the purity of the four bases of power is the purity of the four right efforts. Why is this?
Because this purity of the four right efforts and the purity of the four bases of power are non-dual, not divided into two, not distinct, and not discontinuous.
Because the four bases of psychic power are pure, the five faculties are pure; because the five faculties are pure, the four bases of psychic power are pure. Why is this?
Because these purities of the four bases of psychic power and the purities of the five faculties are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the five faculties are pure, the five powers are pure; because the five powers are pure, the five faculties are pure.
Why is this? Because this purity of the five faculties and this purity of the five powers are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.
Because the five powers are pure, the seven factors of enlightenment are pure; because the seven factors of enlightenment are pure, the five powers are pure.
Why is this? Because this purity of the five powers and this purity of the seven factors of enlightenment are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
Because the seven factors of enlightenment are pure, the eightfold noble path is pure; because the eightfold noble path is pure, the seven factors of enlightenment are pure. Why is this?
The purity of these seven factors of enlightenment and the purity of the eightfold noble path are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
Because the eightfold noble path is pure, the doors of liberation through emptiness are pure; because the doors of liberation through emptiness are pure, the eightfold noble path is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of these eight branches of the noble path and the purity of the gate of liberation of emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the gate of liberation of emptiness is pure, the gate of liberation of signlessness is pure; because the gate of liberation of signlessness is pure, the gate of liberation of emptiness is pure.
Why is this? Because the purity of the gate of liberation of emptiness and the purity of the gate of liberation of signlessness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the gate of liberation of signlessness is pure, the gate of liberation of wishlessness is pure; because the gate of liberation of wishlessness is pure, the gate of liberation of signlessness is pure.
Why is this? Because the purity of the signless gate of liberation and the purity of the wishless gate of liberation are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the liberation door of wishlessness is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the liberation door of wishlessness is pure.
Why is this? Because the purity of this wishless gate of liberation and the purity of the ten stages of the bodhisattva are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure.
Why is this? Because these—the purity of the ten stages of the bodhisattva and the purity of the five eyes—are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.”
“Because the five eyes are pure, the six supernormal powers are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, the five eyes are pure.
Why is this? Because this purity of the five eyes and this purity of the six supernormal powers are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.”
Because the six supernormal powers are pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, the six supernormal powers are pure.
Why is this? Because this purity of the six supernormal powers and the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Because the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, the four fearlessnesses are pure; because the four fearlessnesses are pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure. Why is this?
The purity of the ten powers of a Buddha and the purity of the four fearlessnesses are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
Because the four fearlessnesses are pure, the four analytical knowledges are pure; because the four analytical knowledges are pure, the four fearlessnesses are pure.
Why is this? Because the purity of these four fearlessnesses and the purity of the four analytical knowledges are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the four analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*) are pure, great loving-kindness (*mahāmaitrī*) is pure; because great loving-kindness is pure, the four analytical knowledges are pure. Why is this?
Because this purity of the four analytical knowledges and the purity of great loving-kindness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
Because great loving-kindness (*mahāmaitrī*) is pure, great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*) is pure; because great compassion is pure, great loving-kindness is pure.
Why is this? Because this purity of great loving-kindness and the purity of great compassion are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
Because great compassion is pure, great joy is pure; because great joy is pure, great compassion is pure.
Why is this? Because this purity of great compassion and this purity of great joy are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
Because great joy (*muditā*) is pure, great equanimity (*upekṣā*) is pure; because great equanimity is pure, great joy is pure. Why is this?
Because the purity of great joy and the purity of great equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
Because great equanimity is pure, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure; because the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, great equanimity is pure. Why is this?
This purity of great equanimity and the purity of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of these eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha and the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the state of constant equanimity is pure; because the state of constant equanimity is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure. Why is this?
The purity of this dharma of non-forgetfulness and the purity of the nature of constant equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
Because the nature of constant equanimity is pure, all-knowledge is pure; because all-knowledge is pure, the nature of constant equanimity is pure.
Why is this? Because the purity of this ever-abiding equanimity and the purity of all-knowledge are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Because all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) is pure, the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*) is pure; because the knowledge of the paths is pure, all-knowledge is pure. Why is this?
Because this purity of all-knowledge and the purity of the knowledge of the paths are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.”

Because the knowledge of the aspects of the path is pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure; because the knowledge of all aspects is pure, the knowledge of the aspects of the path is pure. Why is this?
The purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the purity of the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
Because the knowledge of all aspects is pure, all doors of dhāraṇī are pure; because all doors of dhāraṇī are pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure.
Why is this? Because the purity of all-aspect omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*) and the purity of all dharanī-doors are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
Because all dharani-doors are pure, all samadhi-doors are pure; because all samadhi-doors are pure, all dharani-doors are pure.
Why is this? Because the purity of all these dhāraṇī-gates and the purity of all samādhi-gates are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
Because all gateways to samādhi are pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, all gateways to samādhi are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of all these gateways of samādhi and the purity of the fruit of stream-entry are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“Because the fruit of the stream-enterer is pure, the fruit of the once-returner is pure; because the fruit of the once-returner is pure, the fruit of the stream-enterer is pure. Why is this?
Because this purity of the fruit of the stream-enterer and this purity of the fruit of the once-returner are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.”
Because the fruit of the once-returner is pure, the fruit of the non-returner is pure; because the fruit of the non-returner is pure, the fruit of the once-returner is pure. Why is this?
Because the purity of the fruit of the once-returner and the purity of the fruit of the non-returner are not two, are not divided into two, are not distinct, and are not discontinuous.
Because the fruit of non-returning is pure, the fruit of arhatship is pure; because the fruit of arhatship is pure, the fruit of non-returning is pure. Why is this?
The purity of the fruit of non-returning and the purity of the fruit of arhatship are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
Because the fruit of arhatship is pure, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure, the fruit of arhatship is pure.
Why is this? Because the purity of the fruit of arhatship and the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, the practice of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is pure; because the practice of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of this pratyekabuddha-enlightenment and the purity of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas is pure; because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the practice of all these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle Two Hundred and Four (and Two Hundred and Five).
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Dharma Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree.
The First Division, Chapter Thirty-Four, Part Twenty-Four:
"Furthermore, Subhūti, because the perfection of wisdom is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the perfection of wisdom, the purity of form, and the purity of the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because if the perfection of wisdom is pure, and if feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, the sense base of the eye is pure; because the sense base of the eye is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the perfection of wisdom, the purity of the sense-base of the eye, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.

Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the perfection of wisdom, the purity of the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the perfection of wisdom, the purity of the sphere of form, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the perfection of wisdom, the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.
"Subhūti! Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the perfection of wisdom, the purity of the eye-element, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, the form element, the eye-consciousness element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure; because the form element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the *prajñāpāramitā*, the purity of everything from the form realm (*rūpadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the perfection of wisdom, the purity of the ear-element, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of auditory consciousness, and ear-contact, as well as all sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition, are pure; because the sphere of sound up to all sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the perfection of wisdom, the purity of the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, the nose-element is pure; because the nose-element is pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the perfection of wisdom, the purity of the nose-element, and the purity of the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the perfection of wisdom, the purity of the realm of fragrance up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the perfection of wisdom, the purity of the tongue constituent, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the perfection of wisdom, the purity of the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the perfection of wisdom, the purity of the body element, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, the sphere of tangibles, the sphere of body-consciousness, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the perfection of wisdom, the purity of the sphere of tangibles up to the various feelings produced with body-tangibles as conditions, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the perfection of wisdom, the purity of the mental constituent (*manodhātu*), and the purity of the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvajñajñāna*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are pure; because the dharma-element up to all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the perfection of wisdom, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”
Why is this? Because the purity of the perfection of wisdom, the purity of the earth element, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the perfection of wisdom, the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure."
Why is this? Because the purity of the perfection of wisdom, the purity of non-duality, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because if the perfection of wisdom is pure, and if everything from conditioned phenomena up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair is pure, and if all-knowledge is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, the perfection of giving is pure; because the perfection of giving is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the perfection of wisdom, the purity of the perfection of generosity, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, and meditative concentration are pure; because the perfections of ethical discipline up to meditative concentration are pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the perfection of wisdom, the purity of the perfections from ethical discipline up to meditative concentration, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the perfection of wisdom, the purity of internal emptiness, and the purity of the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, infinite emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure; because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because if the perfection of wisdom is pure, and if the emptiness of the external up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-entities is pure, and if the knowledge of all aspects is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the perfection of wisdom, the purity of suchness, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-erroneous nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm are pure; because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the perfection of wisdom, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure; because the noble truth of suffering is pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the perfection of wisdom, the purity of the noble truth of suffering, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because if the perfection of wisdom is pure, and if the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path are pure, and if the knowledge of all aspects is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the perfection of wisdom, the purity of the four dhyānas, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.

Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because if the perfection of wisdom is pure, and if the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, and if the knowledge of all aspects is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the *prajñāpāramitā*, the purity of the eight liberations, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because if the perfection of wisdom is pure, and if the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, and if the knowledge of all aspects is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, the four applications of mindfulness are pure; because the four applications of mindfulness are pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the perfection of wisdom, the purity of the four applications of mindfulness, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.

Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the perfection of wisdom, the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the perfection of wisdom, the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.

Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are pure; because the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the perfection of wisdom, the purity of the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the perfection of wisdom, the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the perfection of wisdom, the purity of the five eyes, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, the six supernormal powers are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the perfection of wisdom is pure, if the six superknowledges are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, the ten powers of the Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of the Buddha are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the perfection of wisdom, the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, and the purity of the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the perfection of wisdom, the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, and the purity of the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the perfection of wisdom, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, the state of constant abiding in equanimity is pure; because the state of constant abiding in equanimity is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the perfection of wisdom, the purity of the nature of constant equanimity, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, all-knowledge is pure; because all-knowledge is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”
Why is this? Because the purity of the perfection of wisdom, the purity of all-knowledge, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because if the perfection of wisdom is pure, and if the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, all dharanī-doors are pure; because all dharanī-doors are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the perfection of wisdom, the purity of all gateways of dhāraṇī, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure; because all doors of samādhi are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the perfection of wisdom, the purity of all doors of samādhi, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the perfection of wisdom, the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the fruit of arhatship are pure; because the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the fruit of arhatship are pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure.

Why is this? Because if the perfection of wisdom is pure, and if the fruit of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are pure, and if all-knowledge is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the perfection of wisdom, the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the perfection of wisdom is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Because external emptiness is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of external emptiness, the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because external emptiness is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of external emptiness, the purity of non-arising, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Why is this? Because the purity of external emptiness, the purity of everything from formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.
“Subhūti! Because external emptiness is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because external emptiness, the purity of the perfection of generosity, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because external emptiness is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of external emptiness, the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because external emptiness is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of external emptiness, the purity of internal emptiness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because external emptiness is pure, there is purity of internal-and-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, emptiness of all phenomena, unapprehendable emptiness, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, and emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence. Because internal-and-external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of external emptiness, the purity of internal-and-external emptiness up to the purity of the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because external emptiness is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of external emptiness, the purity of suchness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because external emptiness is pure, the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm are pure; because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of external emptiness, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because external emptiness is pure, the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure; because the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If external emptiness is pure, if the noble truth of suffering is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the emptiness of the external is pure, the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because external emptiness is pure, the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure, and the knowledge of all modes is pure; they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because external emptiness is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

“Subhūti! Because external emptiness is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Because external emptiness is pure, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Because the purity of external emptiness, the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Whether it be the purity of external emptiness, the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because external emptiness is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eight branches of the noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eight branches of the noble path are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of external emptiness, the purity of the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.
“Subhūti! Because external emptiness is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of external emptiness, the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because external emptiness is pure, the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are pure; because the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of external emptiness, the purity of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Whether it be the purity of external emptiness, the purity of the six supernormal powers, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because external emptiness is pure, the ten powers of the Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of the Buddha are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is that?
If the emptiness of the external is pure, and if the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because external emptiness is pure, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of external emptiness, the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because external emptiness is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”
Why is this? Because external emptiness, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
Because external emptiness is pure, the state of constant equanimity is pure; because the state of constant equanimity is pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure. Why is this?

If external emptiness is pure, if the nature of constant dwelling in equanimity is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not severed.
“Subhūti! Because external emptiness is pure, all-knowledge is pure; because all-knowledge is pure, the knowledge of all-knowledge is pure. Why is that?
If the emptiness of the external is pure, if all-knowledge is pure, and if the knowledge of all-knowledge is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because external emptiness is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

“Subhūti! Because external emptiness is pure, all dhāraṇī-doors are pure; because all dhāraṇī-doors are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because external emptiness being pure, all dhāraṇī-doors being pure, and the knowledge of all modes of knowledge being pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
Because external emptiness is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure; because all doors of samādhi are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of external emptiness, the purity of all doors of samādhi, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because external emptiness is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is that?
If external emptiness is pure, if the fruit of stream-entry is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because external emptiness is pure, the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure; because the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because external emptiness is pure, the fruit of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship is pure, and the knowledge of all modes is pure; these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Why is this? Because the purity of external emptiness, the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

“Subhūti! Because external emptiness is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of external emptiness, the purity of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because external emptiness is pure, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of external emptiness, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because internal and external emptiness is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If internal and external emptiness is pure, if form is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because internal and external emptiness is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of internal and external emptiness, the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

If internal and external emptiness is pure, if the sense base of the eye is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because internal and external emptiness is pure, the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because if the emptiness of the internal and external is pure, if the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because internal and external emptiness is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the emptiness of the internal and external is pure, if the sphere of form is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because internal and external emptiness is pure, the bases of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena are pure; because the bases of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because if the emptiness of the internal and external is pure, and if the bases of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because internal and external emptiness is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If internal and external emptiness is pure, if the eye-element is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because internal and external emptiness is pure, the form element (*rūpadhātu*), the eye-consciousness element (*cakṣurvijñānadhātu*), and eye-contact (*cakṣu-saṃsparśa*), as well as all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, are pure; because the form element up to all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because if the emptiness of the internal and external is pure, if the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because internal and external emptiness is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the emptiness of the internal and external is pure, if the ear-element is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because internal and external emptiness is pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of auditory consciousness, auditory contact, and all feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of sound up to all feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because if internal and external emptiness is pure, if the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because internal and external emptiness is pure, the nose element is pure; because the nose element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the emptiness of the internal and external is pure, if the nose element is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because internal and external emptiness is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because if internal and external emptiness is pure, if the realm of fragrance up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because internal and external emptiness is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because if the emptiness of the internal and external is pure, if the tongue-element is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Why is this? Because if internal and external emptiness is pure, if the taste element and even the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

If the emptiness of the internal and external is pure, if the mental constituent (*manodhātu*) is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*) is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because internal and external emptiness is pure, the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness element, and mental contact, as well as all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are pure; because the dharma-element up to all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because if the emptiness of the internal and external is pure, and if the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

“Subhūti! Because internal and external emptiness is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Why is this? Because if the emptiness of the internal and external is pure, if the perfection of generosity is pure, and if the knowledge of all aspects is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of both internal and external phenomena is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of internal and external emptiness, the purity of internal emptiness, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

If the emptiness of conditioned phenomena is pure, and if the four dhyānas are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because conditioned phenomena are empty and pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the emptiness of the conditioned is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are pure, and the knowledge of all modes is pure; these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of conditioned phenomena is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

If conditioned phenomena are pure, if the eight liberations are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because conditioned phenomena are empty and pure, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of conditioned emptiness, the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten pervasive bases, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
