Because the purity of the emptiness of the limitlessness (*anavasthā-śūnyatā*), the purity of the four right efforts (*samyak-prahāṇa*) up to the eightfold noble path (*āryāṣṭāṅga-mārga*), and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of the limitless is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the emptiness of the limitlessness (anavara-śūnyatā), the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the emptiness of the limitless is pure, the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure; because the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the emptiness of the limitlessness (anavasthā-śūnyatā), the purity of the gateways to liberation of signlessness (animitta) and wishlessness (apraṇihita), and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of the limitless is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the emptiness of the limitlessness (*anavakāra-śūnyatā*), the purity of the ten stages (*daśabhūmi*) of a bodhisattva, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of the limitless is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

If the emptiness of the limitlessness is pure, and if the five eyes are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
Because the emptiness of the limitless is pure, the six supernormal powers are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Because whether it is the purity of the emptiness of the limitless, the purity of the six supernormal powers, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the emptiness of the limitless is pure, the ten powers of the Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of the Buddha are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

If the emptiness of the limitlessness is pure, and if the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the emptiness of the limitless is pure, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the emptiness of the limitlessness (anavasthā-śūnyatā) and the purity of the four fearlessnesses (vaiśāradya), up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (āveṇika-buddhadharma), and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of the limitless is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the emptiness of the limitlessness (*anavakāra-śūnyatā*), the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness (*asaṃpramoṣa-dharma*), and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
Because the emptiness of the limitless is pure, the state of equanimity is pure; because the state of equanimity is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

If the emptiness of the limitlessness is pure, if the nature of constant equanimity is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of the limitless is pure, all-knowledge is pure; because all-knowledge is pure, the knowledge of all-knowledge is pure. Why is this?

If the emptiness of the limitlessness of phenomena is pure, and if all-knowledge is pure, and if the knowledge of all-knowledge is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the emptiness of the limitless is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowing is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the emptiness of the limitlessness (anavasthā-śūnyatā), the purity of the knowledge of the paths (mārgākārajñatā) and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā), and the purity of the knowledge of all knowledge (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of the limitlessness of phenomena is pure, all dhāraṇī doors are pure; because all dhāraṇī doors are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the emptiness of the limitlessness (*anavara-śūnyatā*), the purity of all *dhāraṇī* gates, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
Because the emptiness of the limitless is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure; because all doors of samādhi are pure, the knowledge of all-knowledge is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the emptiness of the limitlessness of phenomena, the purity of all gateways to samādhi, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of the limitless is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is that?

If the emptiness of the limitlessness is pure, and if the fruit of stream-entry is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the emptiness of the limitless is pure, the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are pure; because the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the emptiness of the limitlessness (anavasthā-śūnyatā) and the purity of the fruits of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat, as well as the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of the limitless is pure, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the emptiness of the limitlessness (*anavasthā-śūnyatā*), the purity of the enlightenment of the solitary realizer (*pratyekabuddha-bodhi*), and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of the limitless is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the emptiness of the limitlessness (anavasthā-śūnyatā), the purity of all the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of the limitless is pure, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the emptiness of the limitlessness of phenomena, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is that?
If the emptiness of dispersion is pure, if form is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of the emptiness of dispersion, or the purity of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not severed.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, the eye-base is pure; because the eye-base is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

If the emptiness of dispersion is pure, if the sense base of the eye is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not separate.

Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the emptiness of dispersion, the purity of the bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

If the emptiness of dispersion is pure, if the sphere of form is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, the bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure; because the bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the emptiness of dispersion, the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the emptiness of dispersion, the purity of the eye-element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, the form element, the eye-consciousness element, and eye-contact, as well as all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition, are pure; because the form element up to all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the emptiness of dispersion, the purity of the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual; they are not two, not divided, not distinct, and not severed.
"Subhūti! Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the emptiness of dispersion is pure, if the ear-element is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of auditory consciousness, and ear-contact, as well as all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, are pure; because the sphere of sound up to all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the emptiness of dispersion, the purity of the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, the nose-element is pure; because the nose-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is that?
If the emptiness of dispersion is pure, if the sphere of the nose is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the emptiness of dispersion, the purity of the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

If the emptiness of dispersion is pure, if the tongue-element is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of emptiness of dispersion, or the purity of the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, the body element (*kāyadhātu*) is pure; because the body element is pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*) is pure. Why is this?

If the emptiness of dispersion is pure, if the body element is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, the sphere of tangibles, the sphere of body-consciousness, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the emptiness of dispersion and the purity of the sphere of tangibility, up to and including the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, the mind-element (manodhātu) is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the emptiness of dispersion, the purity of the mental faculty element (*manodhātu*), or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, the dharma-realm, the mental consciousness realm, mental contact, and the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are pure; because the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the emptiness of dispersion, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

If the emptiness of dispersion is pure, if the earth element is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure.
Because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of the emptiness of dispersion, or the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the emptiness of dispersion, the purity of the emptiness of non-existence, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and aging, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through aging, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the emptiness of dispersion and the purity of everything from conditioned formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, as well as the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the emptiness of dispersion, the purity of the perfection of generosity, or the purity of the knowledge of all aspects, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of the emptiness of dispersion, the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the emptiness of dispersion, the purity of internal emptiness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, there is purity of the emptiness of the external, the emptiness of the internal and external, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of the conditioned, the emptiness of the unconditioned, absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self-characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature. Because the emptiness of the external up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of the emptiness of dispersion, the purity of the emptiness of the external, up to the purity of the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of the emptiness of dispersion, the purity of suchness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-erroneous nature, the unchanging nature, the nature of equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm are pure; because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of the emptiness of dispersion, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure; because the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the emptiness of dispersion is pure, if the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the emptiness of dispersion, the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the emptiness of dispersion, the purity of the four dhyānas, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the emptiness of dispersion, the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the emptiness of dispersion, the purity of the eight liberations, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of the emptiness of dispersion, the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, or the ten pervasive bases, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, the four applications of mindfulness are pure; because the four applications of mindfulness are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the emptiness of dispersion, the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the emptiness of dispersion, the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of the emptiness of dispersion, the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not two distinct parts, without differentiation, and without interruption.

Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, the gates of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are pure; because the gates of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of emptiness of dispersion, the purity of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the emptiness of dispersion, the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the emptiness of dispersion, the purity of the five eyes, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, the six supernormal powers are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the emptiness of dispersion, the purity of the six supernormal powers, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, the ten powers of the Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of the Buddha are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the emptiness of dispersion, the purity of the Buddha’s ten powers, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the emptiness of dispersion, the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the emptiness of dispersion, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, the state of constant equanimity is pure; because the state of constant equanimity is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the emptiness of dispersion is pure, if the nature of constant equanimity is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, all-knowledge is pure; because all-knowledge is pure, the knowledge of all-knowledge is pure. Why is this?

If the emptiness of dispersion is pure, and if all-knowledge is pure, and if the knowledge of all-knowledge is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the emptiness of dispersion, the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, or the purity of the knowledge of all-knowledge, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, all dharanī-doors are pure; because all dharanī-doors are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the emptiness of dispersion, the purity of all dharani-doors, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure; because all doors of samādhi are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the emptiness of dispersion, the purity of all doors of samādhi, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the emptiness of dispersion, the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure; because the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the emptiness of dispersion, the purity of the fruit of once-returner, non-returner, or arhatship, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the emptiness of dispersion, the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the emptiness of dispersion, the purity of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual; they are not two, not divided, not distinct, and not severed.

“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of dispersion is pure, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the emptiness of dispersion, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual; they are not two, not divided, not distinct, and not severed.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is that?

If there is no alteration, there is the purity of emptiness; if there is the purity of form, there is the purity of the knowledge of all modes. These are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because if there is no differentiation in the purity of emptiness, and if there is purity in feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, and if there is purity in the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, the eye-base is pure; because the eye-base is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

If there is no alteration, it is the purity of emptiness; if there is the purity of the eye-base, it is the purity of the knowledge of all modes. These two are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because if there is no alteration, there is the purity of emptiness; if there is the purity of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind; and if there is the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

If there is no alteration, it is the purity of emptiness; if there is the purity of the sense-sphere of form, it is the purity of the knowledge of all modes. These are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because non-alteration emptiness is pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of non-alteration and emptiness, the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental objects, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not separate.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

If there is no alteration, it is the purity of emptiness; if there is the purity of the eye-element, it is the purity of the knowledge of all modes. These are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, the form element, the eye-consciousness element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure; because the form element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of non-alteration and emptiness, the purity of everything from the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If there is no alteration and emptiness is pure, and if the ear-element is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of auditory consciousness, and auditory contact, as well as all sensations produced with auditory contact as a condition, are pure; because the sphere of sound up to all sensations produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of non-alteration-emptiness and the purity of everything from the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), are non-dual; they are not two, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.

“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, the nose-element (*ghrāṇadhātu*) is pure; because the nose-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure. Why is this?
If there is no alteration, space is pure; if the nose element is pure, if the knowledge of all modes is pure—these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because non-alteration, emptiness, and purity; the purity of everything from the fragrance-element up to the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition; and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If there is no alteration, space is pure; if the tongue element is pure, if the knowledge of all modes is pure—these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because non-alteration and emptiness are pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of unchanging emptiness, the purity of the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, the body-element (*kāyadhātu*) is pure; because the body-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*) is pure. Why is this?
If there is no alteration, space is pure; if the body element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure; for these two are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, the sphere of tangibles, the sphere of body-consciousness, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, the elements from the sphere of tangibility up to the various feelings produced with body-tangibility as a condition are pure, and the knowledge of all modes is pure; these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, the mind-element (*manodhātu*) is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure. Why is that?

If there is no alteration, there is the purity of emptiness; if there is the purity of the mind-element, there is the purity of the knowledge of all modes. These are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, and mind-contact, as well as all feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition, are pure; because the dharma-element up to all feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of non-alteration and emptiness, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If there is no alteration, space is pure; if the earth element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure; for these two are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of non-alteration is the same as the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna); they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, the purity of non-arising is pure; because the purity of non-arising is pure, the purity of the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

If there is purity through the absence of transformation, if there is purity through the absence of clarity, and if there is purity through the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of non-alteration and emptiness, the purity of [the links of dependent origination] from formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 212. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter Thirty-Four, "Difficult to Believe and Understand," Section Three of Three. "Subhūti!
Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure, and the knowledge of all aspects is pure; these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of non-alteration and emptiness, the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

If there is no alteration, it is the purity of emptiness; if there is the purity of internal emptiness, it is the purity of the knowledge of all modes; for these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, there is purity of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence. Because the emptiness of external [phenomena] up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the emptiness of non-alteration, the purity of external emptiness up to the purity of the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

If there is no alteration, it is the purity of emptiness; if there is the purity of suchness, it is the purity of the knowledge of all modes. These are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), the dharma-nature (*dharmatā*), the non-falsity (*avitathatā*), the non-alteration (*ananyathābhāva*), equality (*samatā*), the state beyond birth (*anupapattitā*), the fixed nature of dharmas (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of dharmas (*dharmasthititā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*) are pure; because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of non-alteration and emptiness, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual; they are not two, they are not distinct, and they are not separate.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure; because the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of non-alteration and emptiness, the purity of the noble truth of suffering, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, the Noble Truths of origination, cessation, and the path are pure; because the Noble Truths of origination, cessation, and the path are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because if there is the purity of non-alteration and emptiness, the purity of the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of non-alteration and emptiness, the purity of the four dhyānas, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of non-alteration and emptiness, the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of non-alteration and emptiness, the purity of the eight liberations, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual; they are not two, not divided, not distinct, and not severed.

Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of non-alteration and emptiness, the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual; they are not two, they are not distinct, and they are not separate.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, the four applications of mindfulness are pure; because the four applications of mindfulness are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of non-alteration and emptiness, the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not separate.

Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of non-alteration and emptiness, the purity of the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of non-alteration, the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure; because the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the emptiness of non-alteration, the purity of the doors of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of non-alteration and emptiness, the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

If there is no alteration, it is the purity of emptiness; if there is the purity of the five eyes, it is the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna). These are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, the six supernormal powers are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

If there is no differentiation, then emptiness is pure; if the six supernormal powers are pure, then the knowledge of all modes is pure; for these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, the ten powers of the Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of the Buddha are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, and the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure; they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of non-alteration and emptiness, the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”
Why is this? Because non-alteration purity, non-forgetfulness purity, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, the state of constant abiding in equanimity is pure; because the state of constant abiding in equanimity is pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of non-alteration and emptiness, the purity of the state of constant equanimity, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, all-knowledge is pure; because all-knowledge is pure, the knowledge of all-knowledge is pure.”

Why is this? Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, the purity of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) is pure, and the purity of the knowledge of all-knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure.

Why is this? Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, and the purity of the knowledge of all-knowledge are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, all dhāraṇī-doors are pure; because all dhāraṇī-doors are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because if there is the purity of non-alteration and emptiness, and if there is the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors and the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure; because all doors of samādhi are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of non-alteration and emptiness, the purity of all gateways to samādhi, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because if there is the purity of unchanging emptiness, the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, the fruit of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship is pure; because the fruit of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship is pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of non-alteration and emptiness, the purity of the fruit of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of non-alteration and emptiness, the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the non-alteration of emptiness, the purity of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of non-alteration and emptiness, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because intrinsic nature is empty and pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If intrinsic nature is pure, if form is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because intrinsic nature is empty and pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of intrinsic nature, the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because intrinsic nature is empty and pure, the eye base is pure; because the eye base is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If intrinsic nature is pure, if the eye-base is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the emptiness of intrinsic nature is pure, the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of intrinsic nature, the purity of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because intrinsic nature is pure through emptiness, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the emptiness of intrinsic nature is pure, if the sphere of form is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because intrinsic nature is empty and pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because if the emptiness of intrinsic nature is pure, and if the bases of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because intrinsic nature is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of intrinsic emptiness, the purity of the eye-element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the emptiness of intrinsic nature is pure, the form element (*rūpadhātu*), the eye-consciousness element (*cakṣurvijñānadhātu*), and eye-contact (*cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa*), as well as all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, are pure. Because the form element up to all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because intrinsic nature is pure, and the purity of the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of intrinsic nature is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

If the emptiness of intrinsic nature is pure, if the ear-element is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the emptiness of intrinsic nature is pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of auditory consciousness, and ear-contact, as well as all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, are pure; because the sphere of sound up to all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of intrinsic nature-emptiness, the purity of the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because intrinsic nature is pure, the nose-element is pure; because the nose-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the emptiness of intrinsic nature is pure, if the nose element is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because intrinsic nature is empty and pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of intrinsic nature, the purity of the sphere of fragrance up to the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.
“Subhūti! Because intrinsic nature is pure through emptiness, the tongue element is pure; because the tongue element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

If the emptiness of intrinsic nature is pure, if the tongue-element is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because intrinsic nature is empty and pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because intrinsic nature is pure, the taste element—and indeed all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition—is pure, and the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure; for these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because intrinsic emptiness is pure, the body element (*kāyadhātu*) is pure; because the body element is pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure. Why is this?

If the emptiness of intrinsic nature is pure, and if the body-element is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because intrinsic nature is empty and pure, the sphere of tangibles, the sphere of body-consciousness, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because if intrinsic nature is pure and empty, and if the sphere of tangibles, up to and including the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the intrinsic nature of emptiness is pure, the mind-element (*manodhātu*) is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*) is pure. Why is this?
If the emptiness of intrinsic nature is pure, if the mind-element is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the emptiness of intrinsic nature is pure, the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness element, and mental contact, as well as all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are pure; because the dharma-element up to all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of intrinsic nature, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of intrinsic nature is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If intrinsic nature is pure, if the earth element is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the emptiness of intrinsic nature is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of intrinsic nature, the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because intrinsic nature is pure through emptiness, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of intrinsic nature, the purity of non-arising, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, undivided, distinctless, and uninterrupted.

Because the emptiness of intrinsic nature is pure, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of intrinsic nature, the purity of everything from formative activities up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes—these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because intrinsic nature is pure through emptiness, the perfection of giving is pure; because the perfection of giving is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because intrinsic nature is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure, and the knowledge of all aspects is pure; these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because intrinsic nature is empty and pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because intrinsic nature is pure, and because the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), as well as the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*), are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because intrinsic nature is pure through emptiness, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

If the emptiness of intrinsic nature is pure, if internal emptiness is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because intrinsic nature is pure, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature are pure; because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of intrinsic nature emptiness, the purity of external emptiness up to the purity of the emptiness of the non-existence of self-nature, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because intrinsic emptiness is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of intrinsic emptiness, the purity of suchness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not separate.

Because intrinsic nature is empty and pure, the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), the dharma-nature (*dharmatā*), the non-falsity (*avitathatā*), the unalterability (*ananyathātā*), equality (*samatā*), the state of being free from birth (*anirodhatā*), the fixedness of dharma (*dharmasthititā*), the stability of dharma (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*) are pure. Because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of intrinsic nature-emptiness, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because intrinsic nature is empty and pure, the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure; because the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

If the emptiness of intrinsic nature is pure, if the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the emptiness of intrinsic nature is pure, the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of intrinsic nature-emptiness, the purity of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the emptiness of intrinsic nature is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of intrinsic emptiness, the purity of the four dhyānas, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because intrinsic nature is empty and pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because intrinsic nature emptiness is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, and the knowledge of all modes is pure; these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because intrinsic nature is pure through emptiness, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

If the emptiness of intrinsic nature is pure, and if the eight liberations are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because intrinsic nature is empty and pure, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because intrinsic nature is pure, and the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten universal bases are pure, and the knowledge of all modes is pure; these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because intrinsic nature is pure by way of emptiness, the four applications of mindfulness are pure; because the four applications of mindfulness are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

If the emptiness of intrinsic nature is pure, if the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because intrinsic nature is pure and empty, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure.
