“Subhūti! Because suchness is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of suchness, the purity of the eight liberations, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because suchness is pure, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of suchness, the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten pervasive bases, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because suchness is pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure; because the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If suchness is pure, if the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because suchness is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of suchness, the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because suchness is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure."

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of suchness, the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because suchness is pure, the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are pure; because the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of suchness, the purity of the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because suchness is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of suchness, the purity of the ten stages of the bodhisattva, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because suchness is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of suchness, the purity of the five eyes, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
Because suchness is pure, the six supernormal powers are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of suchness, the purity of the six supernormal powers, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because suchness is pure, the ten powers of the Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of the Buddha are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of suchness, the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because suchness is pure, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of suchness, the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because suchness is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure."

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of suchness, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
Because suchness is pure, the state of constant equanimity is pure; because the state of constant equanimity is pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of suchness, the purity of the nature of constant equanimity, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, undivided, distinctless, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because suchness is pure, all-knowledge is pure; because all-knowledge is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of suchness, the purity of all-knowledge, or the purity of the knowledge of all-knowledge, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because suchness is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, the knowledge of all-knowing is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of suchness, the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path, the purity of all-aspect omniscience, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because suchness is pure, all dhāraṇī-doors are pure; because all dhāraṇī-doors are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure."

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of suchness, the purity of all dharani-doors, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
Because suchness is pure, all gateways to samādhi are pure; because all gateways to samādhi are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of suchness, the purity of all doors of samādhi, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of suchness, the purity of the fruit of once-returning, non-returning, or arhatship, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of suchness, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the dharma-realm is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the dharma-realm, the purity of form, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the dharma-realm is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the dharma-realm, the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the dharma-realm is pure, the eye-base is pure; because the eye-base is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of the dharma-realm, the purity of the eye-base, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the dharma-realm is pure, the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the dharma-realm, the purity of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the dharma-realm is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the dharma-realm, the purity of the sphere of form, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the dharma-realm is pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of the dharma-realm, the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena, or the purity of the knowledge of all-knowledge, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the dharma-realm is pure, the eye-faculty is pure; because the eye-faculty is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the dharma-realm, the purity of the eye-realm, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the dharma-realm is pure, the form realm, the eye-consciousness realm, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure; because the form realm up to all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the dharma-realm, the purity of the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the dharma-realm is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the dharma-realm, the purity of the ear-realm, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the dharma-realm is pure, the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure; because the sound-element up to all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the dharma-realm, or the purity of the sound-realm up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the dharma-realm is pure, the nose-realm is pure; because the nose-realm is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the dharma-realm, the purity of the nose-realm, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the dharma-realm is pure, the fragrance-realm, the nose-consciousness-realm, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance-realm up to all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the dharma-realm, or the purity of the fragrance-realm up to the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the dharma-realm is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the dharma-realm, the purity of the tongue-realm, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the dharma-realm is pure, the taste-realm, the tongue-consciousness-realm, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste-realm up to all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the dharma-realm, the purity of the taste-realm up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the dharma-realm is pure, the body-realm is pure; because the body-realm is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the dharma-realm, the purity of the body-realm, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the dharma-realm is pure, the touch-element, the body-consciousness-element, and body-contact, as well as all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, are pure; because the touch-element up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the dharma-realm, the purity of the realm of tangibles up to the various feelings produced with body-tangibles as conditions, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the dharma-realm is pure, the mind-realm is pure; because the mind-realm is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the dharma-element, the purity of the mind-element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the dharma-realm is pure, the consciousness-realm, mental contact, and all sensations produced with mental contact as a condition are pure; because the dharma-realm up to all sensations produced with mental contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the dharma-realm, or the purity of all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the dharma-realm is pure, the earth-element is pure; because the earth-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the dharma-realm, the purity of the earth-element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the dharma-realm is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the dharma-realm, the purity of the realms of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the dharma-realm is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the dharma-realm, the purity of the outflow-free realm, or the purity of the knowledge of all-knowledge, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the dharma-realm is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of the dharma-realm, the purity of the perfection of generosity, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the dharmadhātu is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom are pure, the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the dharma-realm, the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the dharma-realm is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the dharma-realm, the purity of internal emptiness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the *dharmadhātu* is pure, external emptiness (*bahirdhā-śūnyatā*), internal-and-external emptiness (*adhyātma-bahirdhā-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of emptiness (*śūnyatā-śūnyatā*), great emptiness (*mahā-śūnyatā*), ultimate emptiness (*paramārtha-śūnyatā*), conditioned emptiness (*saṃskṛta-śūnyatā*), unconditioned emptiness (*asaṃskṛta-śūnyatā*), absolute emptiness (*atyanta-śūnyatā*), boundless emptiness (*anavara-agra-śūnyatā*), dispersed emptiness (*anavakāra-śūnyatā*), non-alteration emptiness (*anavakāra-śūnyatā*), essential nature emptiness (*prakṛti-śūnyatā*), self-characteristic emptiness (*svalakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*), common characteristic emptiness (*sāmānya-lakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of all phenomena (*sarvadharma-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of the unapprehendable (*anupalambha-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of non-existence (*abhāva-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of intrinsic nature (*svabhāva-śūnyatā*), and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence (*abhāva-svabhāva-śūnyatā*) are pure. Because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the dharma-realm, the purity of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the dharma-realm is pure, the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the non-falsity of phenomena, the immutability of phenomena, the equality of phenomena, the state of being free from birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm are pure. Because the nature of phenomena up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the dharma-realm, the purity of the dharma-nature up to the inconceivable realm, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the nature of phenomena, the purity of form, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*) is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is pure, the eye-base (cakṣur-āyatana) is pure; because the eye-base is pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the nature of phenomena, the purity of the eye-base, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the nature of phenomena is pure, the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the purity of the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Whether it be the purity of the nature of phenomena, the purity of the sense-base of form, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental objects are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental objects are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental objects (*dharmāyatana*), or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is pure, the eye-faculty (cakṣurdhātu) is pure; because the eye-faculty is pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvākārajñatā) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the nature of phenomena, the purity of the eye-element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*) is pure, the form element (*rūpadhātu*), the eye-consciousness element (*cakṣurvijñānadhātu*), eye-contact (*cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa*), and all feelings (*vedanā*) produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure; because the form element up to all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the purity of the form realm (*rūpadhātu*) up to the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with eye-contact as a condition, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), they are non-dual, not two distinct parts, without differentiation, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is pure, the ear-element (śrotradhātu) is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure. Why is that?
Whether it be the purity of the nature of phenomena, the purity of the ear-element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of auditory consciousness, auditory contact, and all feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of sound up to all feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the nature of phenomena, the purity of the sphere of sound up to the various sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is pure, the nose-element (ghrāṇadhātu) is pure; because the nose-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the nature of phenomena, the purity of the nose element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*) is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the purity of the realm of fragrance up to the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

“Subhūti! Because the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is pure, the tongue-element (jihvā-dhātu) is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the nature of phenomena, the purity of the tongue element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*) is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the purity of the taste element (*rasadhātu*) up to the various sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is pure, the body element (kāyadhātu) is pure; because the body element is pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the nature of phenomena, the purity of the body-element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*) is pure, the sphere of tangibles (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*), the sphere of body-consciousness (*kāyavijñānadhātu*), body-contact (*kāyasparśa*), and all feelings (*vedanā*) produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the purity of the various feelings produced with the contact element as condition up to the body-contact as condition, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is pure, the mind-element (manodhātu) is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the nature of phenomena, the purity of the mind-element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*) is pure, the dharma-element (*dharmadhātu*), the mental consciousness-element (*manovijñānadhātu*), mental contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*), and all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are pure; because the dharma-element up to all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the purity of the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the nature of phenomena, the purity of the earth element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the nature of phenomena, the purity of non-arising, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*) is pure, volitional formations (*saṃskāra*), consciousness (*vijñāna*), name-and-form (*nāmarūpa*), the six sense bases (*ṣaḍāyatana*), contact (*sparśa*), feeling (*vedanā*), craving (*tṛṣṇā*), grasping (*upādāna*), becoming (*bhava*), birth (*jāti*), and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the purity of [the factors] from formations up to old age, death, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the nature of phenomena is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the nature of phenomena, the purity of the perfection of generosity, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*) is pure, the perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is pure, internal emptiness (adhyātma-śūnyatā) is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the nature of phenomena, the purity of internal emptiness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*) is pure, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature are pure. Because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the purity of external emptiness up to the purity of the emptiness of the essential nature of non-entities (*abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā*), or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is pure, suchness (tathatā) is pure; because suchness is pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the purity of suchness (*tathatā*), or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*) is pure, the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the non-falsity, the immutability, the equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*) are pure. Because the realm of phenomena up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure.

Why is this? "Subhūti! Because non-falsity is pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure; because the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the nature of non-falsity, the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the nature of non-falsity is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eight branches of the noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eight branches of the noble path are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the nature of non-falsity, the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the nature of non-falsity is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the nature of non-falsity, the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the nature of non-falsity is pure, the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure; because the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the nature of non-falsity, the purity of the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the nature of non-falsity is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the nature of non-falsity, the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are without distinction, and they are without interruption.
