Because the nature of detachment is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure. Why is this?

Because whether it be the purity of the nature of detachment, the purity of form, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the nature of arising is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the nature of arising, the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not separate.
"Subhūti! Because the nature of arising is pure, the eye-base is pure; because the eye-base is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the nature of arising, the purity of the eye-base, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the nature of being free from arising is pure, the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the nature of arising, the purity of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the nature of arising is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the nature of arising, the purity of the sense-sphere of form, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the nature of being free from birth is pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because if the purity of the nature of arising, the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena, and the purity of the knowledge of all-knowledge are non-dual, undivided, distinctless, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the nature of non-arising is pure, the eye-faculty is pure; because the eye-faculty is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the nature of arising, the purity of the eye-element, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, without division, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the nature of being free from birth is pure, the form realm (*rūpadhātu*), the eye-consciousness realm (*cakṣurvijñānadhātu*), eye-contact (*cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa*), and all feelings (*vedanā*) arising with eye-contact as condition are pure; because the form realm up to all feelings arising with eye-contact as condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the nature of arising, the purity of everything from the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the nature of being free from arising is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the nature of arising, the purity of the ear-element, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the nature of being free from birth is pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of auditory consciousness, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of sound up to all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the nature of arising, the purity of the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are without distinction, and they are without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the nature of arising is pure, the nose element is pure; because the nose element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the nature of arising, the purity of the nose element, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience are non-dual, without division, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the nature of being free from birth is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the nature of arising, the purity of the realm of fragrance up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
"Subhūti! Because the nature of arising is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the nature of arising, the purity of the tongue element, and the purity of the knowledge of all-knowledge are non-dual, undivided, distinctless, and uninterrupted.

Because the nature of being free from birth is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the nature of arising, the purity of the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the nature of arising is pure, the body-element (kāyadhātu) is pure; because the body-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the nature of arising, the purity of the body-element, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, without division, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the nature of being free from birth is pure, the sphere of tangibles, the sphere of body-consciousness, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the nature of arising, the purity of the elements from the realm of touch up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are without distinction, and they are not separate.
"Subhūti! Because the nature of arising is pure, the mind-element (*manodhātu*) is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure. Why is this?..."
If the purity of the nature of arising, the purity of the mind-element, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the nature of being free from birth is pure, the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, and mind-contact, as well as all feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition, are pure; because the dharma-element up to all feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the nature of arising, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the nature of non-arising is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the nature of arising, the purity of the earth element, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the nature of arising is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the nature of arising, the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the purity of the nature of non-arising is pure, the purity of non-manifestation is pure; because the purity of non-manifestation is pure, the purity of the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the nature of arising, the purity of non-arising, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the nature of arising is pure, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the nature of arising, the purity of [the factors] from formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.
“Subhūti! Because the nature of arising is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the nature of arising, the purity of the perfection of generosity, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the nature of being free from birth is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections of ethical discipline through to wisdom are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the nature of arising, the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the nature of being free from arising is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the nature of arising, the purity of internal emptiness, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the nature of being free from arising is pure, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, limitless emptiness, dispersal emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure; because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the nature of arising, the purity of external emptiness up to the purity of the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
"Subhūti! Because the nature of being free from birth is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the nature of arising, the purity of suchness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the nature of being free from arising is pure, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-falsity, the non-alteration, the equality, the dharma-constancy, the dharma-abiding, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm are pure; because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the nature of arising, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! Because the nature of arising is pure, the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure; because the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the nature of arising, the purity of the noble truth of suffering, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the nature of being free from arising is pure, the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the nature of arising, the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the purity of the nature of non-arising is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the nature of arising, the purity of the four dhyānas, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the nature of being free from birth is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the nature of arising, the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the purity of the nature of non-arising is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the nature of arising, the purity of the eight liberations, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the nature of being free from birth is pure, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the nature of arising, the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

"Subhūti! Because the nature of being free from birth is pure, the four applications of mindfulness are pure; because the four applications of mindfulness are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the nature of arising, the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous; therefore, they are one.

Because the nature of being free from birth is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the nature of arising, the purity of the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the nature of being free from birth is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the nature of arising, the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the nature of being free from birth is pure, the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure; because the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the nature of arising, the purity of the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the nature of being free from birth is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the nature of arising, the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the nature of being free from birth is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the nature of arising, the purity of the five eyes, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
Because the nature of being free from birth is pure, the six supernormal powers are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Because whether it be the purity of the nature of being free from birth, the purity of the six supernormal powers, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the nature of being free from birth is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the nature of arising, the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the nature of being free from birth is pure, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the nature of arising, the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

“Subhūti! Because the purity of the nature of non-arising is pure, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the purity of the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the nature of non-arising, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
Because the nature of detachment is pure, the state of constant equanimity is pure; because the state of constant equanimity is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the nature of non-arising, the purity of the state of constant equanimity, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous; therefore they are one.
“Subhūti! Because the nature of non-arising is pure, all-knowledge is pure; because all-knowledge is pure, the knowledge of all-knowledge is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the nature of arising, the purity of all-knowledge, and the purity of the knowledge of all-knowledge are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous; therefore, they are one.

Because the nature of being free from birth is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowing is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the nature of arising, the purity of the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), the purity of the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), and the purity of the knowledge of all-knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! Because the nature of being free from birth is pure, all dharanī-doors are pure; because all dharanī-doors are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the nature of arising, the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the nature of being free from birth is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure; because all doors of samādhi are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the nature of arising, the purity of all gateways to samādhi, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge are non-dual; they are not two, not divided, not distinct, and not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the nature of being free from birth is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the nature of arising, the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the nature of being free from birth is pure, the fruit of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat are pure; because the fruits of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the nature of arising, the purity of the fruit of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the nature of being free from arising is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the nature of arising, the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

“Subhūti! Because the nature of arising is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the nature of arising, the purity of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the nature of arising is pure, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is pure; because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the nature of arising, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the Dharma is intrinsically pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of dharmas, the purity of form, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the dharma-nature is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of dharmas, the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the dharma-realm is pure, the eye-base is pure; because the eye-base is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of dharmas, the purity of the eye-base, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the dhātus of the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure by way of the purity of the Dharma, the dhātus of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the dhātus of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of dharmas, the purity of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the dharma-element is pure, the form-base is pure; because the form-base is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purification of dharmas, the purification of the sense-base of form, or the purification of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the sphere of phenomena is pure by nature, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental objects are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental objects are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of dharmas, the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental objects, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the dharma-element is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of dharmas, the purity of the eye-element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the sphere of form (*rūpadhātu*) is pure, the sphere of eye-consciousness (*cakṣurvijñānadhātu*), eye-contact (*cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa*), and all feelings (*vedanā*) produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure. Because the sphere of form up to all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of dharmas, the purity of the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the dharma-element is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purification of dharmas, the purification of the ear-element, or the purification of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the dharma-realm is pure, the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, and ear-contact, as well as all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, are pure; because the sound-element up to all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of dharmas, the purity of the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the dharma-nature is pure, the nose-element is pure; because the nose-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the dharmas, the purity of the nose element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the dharma-realm is pure, the fragrance-element, the nose-consciousness-element, nose-contact, and all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance-element up to all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of phenomena, the purity of the sphere of fragrance up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the dharma-element is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of the dharmas, the purity of the tongue element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the realm of taste is pure by nature, the realm of tongue-consciousness, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the realm of taste up to all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of dharmas, the purity of the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the dharma-element is pure, the body-element is pure; because the body-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of dharmas, the purity of the body-element, or the purity of the knowledge of all-knowledge, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the sphere of tangibles is pure by way of the purity of the Dharma, the sphere of body-consciousness, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as condition are pure; because the sphere of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of dharmas, the purity of the sphere of contact (*spraṣṭavya-dhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the dharma-realm is pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the Dharma-realm, the purity of the mind-element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the dharma-element is pure, the consciousness-element, the mental faculty-contact, and all feelings produced with mental faculty-contact as condition are pure; because the dharma-element up to all feelings produced with mental faculty-contact as condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of phenomena, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the dharma-realm is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of dharmas, the purity of the earth element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the fundamental elements are pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of dharmas, the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the dharmas are pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of dharmas, the purity of non-arising, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because volitional formations are pure, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of dharmas, the purity of conditioned activities up to and including old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the nature of phenomena is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of phenomena, the purity of the perfection of generosity, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the purification of the Dharma is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of phenomena, the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the dharma-element is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of dharmas, the purity of internal emptiness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the dharmas of purification are pure, there is the purity of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence. Because the purity of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence exists, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of dharmas, the purity of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the dharmas are pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of phenomena, the purity of suchness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the dharmadhātu is pure by way of being established as pure, the dharmatā, the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the state beyond birth, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm are pure; because the dharmadhātu up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of dharmas, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the dharma-element is pure, the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure; because the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of dharmas, the purity of the noble truth of suffering, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not separate.

Because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure by virtue of the purity of the Dharma-realm, the knowledge of all modes is pure by virtue of the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of dharmas, the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the dharmas are pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of dharmas, the purity of the four dhyānas, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the dharmas are pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of dharmas, the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the dharmas are pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of dharmas, the purity of the eight liberations, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the dharmas of purification are pure, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of dharmas, the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten universal bases, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the dharmas are pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure; because the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of dharmas, the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the dharmas of purification are pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of dharmas, the purity of the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the dharmas are pure, the door of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the door of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of dharmas, the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the dharmas are intrinsically pure, the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure; because the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of dharmas, the purity of the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the Dharma-nature is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of dharmas, the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the dharmas are pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of dharmas, the purity of the five eyes, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the dharmas are pure, the six supernormal powers are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the dharmas, the purity of the six supernormal powers, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the dharma-element is pure, the ten powers of the Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of the Buddha are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of the dharmas, the purity of the Buddha’s ten powers, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the dharmas of purity are pure, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of dharmas, the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the dharmas are pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of dharmas, the purity of the dharma of non-forgetfulness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the purity of the dharmas is established, the purity of the state of constant equanimity is established; because the state of constant equanimity is pure, the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is established. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of dharmas, the purity of the nature of constant equanimity, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the dharmas are pure, all-knowledge is pure; because all-knowledge is pure, the knowledge of all-knowledge is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of dharmas, the purity of omniscience, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the purity of the factors of enlightenment is established by law, the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects is established; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, the knowledge of all-knowing is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of dharmas, the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, or the purity of the knowledge of all-knowingness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the nature of phenomena is pure, all dhāraṇī-doors are pure; because all dhāraṇī-doors are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of dharmas, the purity of all dharani-doors, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the dharmas are pure, all gateways to samādhi are pure; because all gateways to samādhi are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of dharmas, the purity of all doors of samādhi, or the purity of the knowledge of all-knowledge, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the dharmas are fundamentally pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of dharmas, the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the dharma-realm is pure, the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure; because the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of dharmas, the purity of the fruit of once-returning, non-returning, or arhatship, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the dharmas are pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of dharmas, the purity of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the dharma-nature is pure, all the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure; because all the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of dharmas, the purity of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the dharmas are pure, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because if the dharmas are pure, if the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
