Because the abiding of phenomena (*dharmasthiti*) is pure, form (*rūpa*) is pure; because form is pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure. Why is this?

Because whether it be the purity of the abiding of phenomena, the purity of form, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the abiding of phenomena is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the abiding of phenomena, the purity of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (sarvajñajñāna), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the abiding of phenomena is pure, the eye-base is pure; because the eye-base is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the abiding nature of phenomena, the purity of the eye-base, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the abiding of phenomena is pure, the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the abiding of phenomena, the purity of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the abiding of phenomena is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the abiding of phenomena, the purity of the sense-sphere of form, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the abiding of phenomena is pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental objects are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental objects are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the dharmas, the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental objects, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the abiding of phenomena (dharmasthititā) is pure, the eye-element (cakṣurdhātu) is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvākārajñatā) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the abiding of phenomena, the purity of the eye-element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the dharma-abiding is pure, the form element, the eye-consciousness element, and eye-contact, as well as all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, are pure; because the form element up to all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the abiding of phenomena, the purity of the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the abiding of phenomena is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of the abiding of phenomena, the purity of the ear-element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the abiding of the Dharma is pure, the sound element, the ear-consciousness element, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure; because the sound element up to all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the abiding of phenomena, the purity of the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the abiding of phenomena is pure, the nose element is pure; because the nose element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the abiding of phenomena, the purity of the nose element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the abiding of phenomena is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, and nose-contact, as well as all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, are pure; because the fragrance element up to all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the dharmas, the purity of the fragrance-element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the abiding of phenomena is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is that?

Whether it be the purity of the abiding of phenomena, the purity of the tongue element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the abiding of phenomena is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the dharmas abiding, or the purity of the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the abiding of phenomena is pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the abiding of phenomena, the purity of the body-element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the abiding of the Dharma is pure, the sphere of tangibles, the sphere of body-consciousness, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because if the abiding of phenomena is pure, if the contact element—and even the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition—is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

“Subhūti! Because the abiding nature of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*) is pure, the mind-element (*manodhātu*) is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the abiding of phenomena, the purity of the mental constituent (*manodhātu*), or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the dharma-element is pure, the consciousness-element, the mind-contact, and all feelings produced with mind-contact as condition are pure; because the dharma-element up to all feelings produced with mind-contact as condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the dharmas abiding, or the purity of the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the abiding of phenomena is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the abiding of phenomena, the purity of the earth element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the abiding of phenomena is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the abiding of phenomena, the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (sarvajñajñāna), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the abiding of phenomena is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the abiding of phenomena, the purity of non-arising, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the abiding of the Dharma is pure, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of the abiding of phenomena, or the purity of [the links from] formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the abiding of phenomena is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the abiding of phenomena, the purity of the perfection of generosity, and the purity of omniscient wisdom are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the abiding of phenomena is pure, the perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of the abiding of phenomena, the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the abiding of phenomena is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the abiding of phenomena, the purity of internal emptiness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the abiding of phenomena (*dharmasthiti*) is pure, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure; because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of the abiding of phenomena, the purity of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the abiding of phenomena is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the abiding nature of phenomena, the purity of suchness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the abiding of phenomena (*dharmasthiti*) is pure, the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the non-falsity of phenomena (*avitathatā*), the unalterability of phenomena (*ananyathābhāva*), equality (*samatā*), the state beyond birth (*anirodhatā*), the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmadharmatā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*) are pure. Because the realm of phenomena up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the dharmas abiding, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the abiding nature of phenomena (dharmasthititā) is pure, the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure; because the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvākārajñatā) is pure. Why is this?

If the stability of phenomena is pure, if the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the abiding of phenomena is pure, the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the abiding of phenomena, the purity of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the abiding of phenomena is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the abiding of phenomena, the purity of the four dhyānas, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the abiding of the Dharma is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of the abiding of phenomena, the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the abiding of phenomena is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the abiding of phenomena, the purity of the eight liberations, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the abiding of the Dharma is pure, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of the abiding of phenomena, the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, the ten totalities, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the abiding of phenomena is pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure; because the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the abiding of phenomena, the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the abiding of phenomena (*dharmasthiti*) is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eight branches of the noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eight branches of the noble path are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of the abiding of phenomena, the purity of the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

"Subhūti! Because the abiding nature of phenomena is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure."

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the abiding of phenomena, the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the abiding of phenomena is pure, the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure; because the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the abiding of phenomena, the purity of the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the abiding of phenomena is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the abiding of phenomena, the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the abiding of phenomena is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the abiding of phenomena, the purity of the five eyes, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the abiding of phenomena (*dharmasthiti*) is pure, the six supernormal powers (*ṣaḍabhijñā*) are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the abiding of phenomena, the purity of the six supernormal powers, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the abiding nature of phenomena is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the abiding of phenomena, the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the abiding of the Dharma is pure, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of the abiding of phenomena, the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the abiding of phenomena is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the abiding of phenomena, the purity of the dharma that is without forgetfulness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the abiding of phenomena (*dharmasthiti*) is pure, the state of constant equanimity (*upekṣā*) is pure; because the state of constant equanimity is pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the abiding nature of phenomena, the purity of the constant state of equanimity, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

“Subhūti! Because the abiding of phenomena (dharmasthititā) is pure, all-knowledge (sarvajñatā) is pure; because all-knowledge is pure, the knowledge of all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the abiding of phenomena, the purity of all-knowledge, or the purity of the knowledge of all-knowledge, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the abiding of phenomena is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, the knowledge of all-knowingness is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the abiding of phenomena, the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, or the purity of the knowledge of all-knowledge, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the abiding of phenomena is pure, all dhāraṇī-doors are pure; because all dhāraṇī-doors are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure."

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the abiding of phenomena, the purity of all dharani-doors, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the abiding of phenomena is pure, all gateways to samādhi are pure; because all gateways to samādhi are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the abiding of phenomena, the purity of all doors of samādhi, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the abiding of dharmas is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the abiding of phenomena, the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the persistence of the Dharma is pure, the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are pure; because the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the abiding of phenomena, the purity of the fruit of once-returning, non-returning, or arhatship, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the abiding of phenomena is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the abiding of phenomena, the purity of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

“Subhūti! Because the abiding of phenomena is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the abiding of phenomena, the purity of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the abiding of phenomena is pure, the unsurpassed perfect enlightenment of all Buddhas is pure; because the unsurpassed perfect enlightenment of all Buddhas is pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the abiding of phenomena, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) is pure, form (*rūpa*) is pure; because form is pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*) is pure. Why is this?
The purity of the reality-limit, the purity of form, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.

Because the limit of reality is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) is pure, the eye-base (cakṣurāyatana) is pure; because the eye-base is pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvākārajñatā) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the reality-limit, the purity of the eye-base, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the limit of reality is pure, the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the purity of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) is pure, the sphere of form (*rūpāyatana*) is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*) is pure. Why is that?

Whether it be the purity of the limit of reality, the purity of the sphere of form, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the reality-limit (*bhūtakoṭi*) is pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena (*dharmāyatana*) are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena (*dharmāyatana*), or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) is pure, the eye-element (cakṣurdhātu) is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvākārajñatā) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the limit of reality, the purity of the eye-element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) is pure, the form element (*rūpadhātu*), the eye-consciousness element (*cakṣurvijñānadhātu*), eye-contact (*cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa*), and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure. Because the form element up to all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the purity of everything from the form realm (*rūpadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the limit of reality is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the limit of reality, the purity of the ear-element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) is pure, the sound-element (*śabdadhātu*), the ear-consciousness-element (*śrotravijñānadhātu*), ear-contact (*śrotrasaṃsparśa*), and all feelings produced with ear-contact as condition are pure; because the sound-element up to all feelings produced with ear-contact as condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the purity of the sphere of sound (*śabdadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) are non-dual; they are not two, not divided, not distinct, and not separate.

"Subhūti! Because the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) is pure, the nose-element (*ghrāṇadhātu*) is pure; because the nose-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure. Why is this?..."

Whether it be the purity of the limit of reality, the purity of the nose element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the purity of the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

"Subhūti! Because the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) is pure, the tongue-element (jihvādhātu) is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the limit of reality, the purity of the tongue element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) is pure, the taste element (*rasadhātu*), the tongue-consciousness element (*jihvavijñānadhātu*), tongue-contact (*jihvāsamsparśa*), and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the purity of the taste element (*rasadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) is pure, the body-element (kāyadhātu) is pure; because the body-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure. Why is that?
Whether it be the purity of the limit of reality, the purity of the body-element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) is pure, the sphere of tangibles, the sphere of body-consciousness, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the purity of the sphere of tangibles (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*) up to the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with body-contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the limit of reality is pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the limit of reality, the purity of the mind-element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the reality-limit (*bhūtakoṭi*) is pure, the dharma-element (*dharmadhātu*), the mind-consciousness-element (*manovijñānadhātu*), mental contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*), and all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are pure; because the dharma-element up to all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), or the purity of the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the limit of reality, the purity of the earth element, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the limit of reality is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) is pure, non-arising (anutpāda) is pure; because non-arising is pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvākārajñatā) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the limit of reality, the purity of non-arising, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) is pure, formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), or the purity of [the links of dependent origination] from formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the limit of reality is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the purity of the perfection of generosity (*dānapāramitā*), and the purity of the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.

Because the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

“Subhūti! Because the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) is pure, internal emptiness (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*) is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the limit of reality, the purity of internal emptiness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) is pure, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena (*sarvadharmaśūnyatā*), the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure; because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the purity of outer emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature (*abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā*), or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the limit of reality is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the limit of reality, the purity of suchness, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) is pure, the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*) are pure. Because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the purity of the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*) up to the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*), or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure; because the noble truth of suffering is pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the limit of reality, the purity of the noble truth of suffering, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the limit of reality is pure, the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the reality limit, the purity of the four dhyānas, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the reality-limit (bhūtakoṭi) is pure, the four immeasurables (apramāṇa) and the four formless absorptions (ārūpyasamāpatti) are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the purity of the four immeasurables (*apramāṇa*) and the four formless attainments (*ārūpyasamāpatti*), or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) is pure, the eight liberations (aṣṭavimokṣa) are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the limit of reality, the purity of the eight liberations, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) is pure, the eight spheres of mastery (*abhibhvāyatana*), the nine successive attainments (*anupūrvavihārasamāpatti*), and the ten totalities (*kṛtsnāyatana*) are pure; because the eight spheres of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the purity of the eight bases of mastery (*abhibhvāyatana*), the nine successive meditative attainments (*anupūrvavihārasamāpatti*), and the ten totalities (*kṛtsnāyatana*), and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

“Subhūti! Because the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) is pure, the four applications of mindfulness (*smṛtyupasthāna*) are pure; because the four applications of mindfulness are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*) is pure. Why is that?

Whether it be the purity of the reality limit (*bhūtakoṭi*), the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness (*smṛtyupasthāna*), or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the reality-limit (*bhūtakoṭi*) is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eight branches of the noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eight branches of the noble path are pure, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) are non-dual, not two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the limit of reality is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness (*śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha*), or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the limit of reality is pure, the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are pure; because the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of the reality-limit (*bhūtakoṭi*), the purity of the gateways to liberation of signlessness (*animitta*) and wishlessness (*apraṇihita*), or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the limit of reality is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure."

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the purity of the ten stages (*daśabhūmi*) of a bodhisattva, or the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle Two Hundred and Twenty-one. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter on Difficult to Believe and Understand, Thirty-fourth, Section Four. "Furthermore, Subhūti!

Because the purification of the eight bases of mastery, the purification of [the links of dependent origination] from formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, and the purification of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle Two Hundred and Twenty-Six. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. First Division, Chapter Thirty-Four on Difficult-to-Believe Understanding, Part Four of Six. "Subhūti!

“Subhūti! Because the eight bases of mastery are pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the eight bases of mastery are pure, if inner emptiness is pure, and if the knowledge of all modes is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Why is this? Because the purification of the eight stages of mastery, the purification of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, and the purification of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Why is this? Because the purification of the eight bases of mastery, the purification of the four right efforts up to the eight branches of the noble path, and the purification of the knowledge of all modes are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

"Subhūti! Because the eight bases of mastery are pure, all-knowledge is pure; because all-knowledge is pure, the knowledge of all-knowledge is pure. Why is this?

"Furthermore, Subhūti!
