Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of the perfection of meditative concentration are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are without distinction, and they are not separate.
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the state of constant equanimity is pure; because the state of constant equanimity is pure, the perfection of meditative concentration is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the nature of constant equanimity (upekṣā), and the purity of the perfection of meditative concentration (dhyānapāramitā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the knowledge of all things is pure; because the knowledge of all things is pure, the perfection of meditative concentration is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all-knowledge, and the purity of the perfection of meditative concentration are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, the perfection of meditative concentration is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, and the purity of the perfection of meditative concentration, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all dharani-doors are pure; because all dharani-doors are pure, the perfection of meditative concentration is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors, and the purity of the perfection of meditative concentration are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure; because all doors of samādhi are pure, the perfection of meditative concentration is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all doors of samādhi, and the purity of the perfection of meditative concentration are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, the perfection of meditative concentration is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, and the purity of the perfection of meditative concentration are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure; because the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure, the perfection of meditative concentration is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship, and the purity of the perfection of meditative concentration (dhyānapāramitā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the enlightenment of the solitary realizers is pure; because the enlightenment of the solitary realizers is pure, the perfection of meditative concentration is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of the perfection of meditative concentration are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure, the perfection of meditative concentration is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of the perfection of meditative concentration (dhyānapāramitā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, the perfection of meditative concentration is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, and the purity of the perfection of meditative concentration are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the perfection of vigor is pure."
Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of form, and the purity of the perfection of diligence are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the perfection of diligence is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, and the purity of the perfection of diligence are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of the eye is pure; because the sphere of the eye is pure, the perfection of diligence is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the sense base of the eye, and the purity of the perfection of diligence are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the perfection of diligence is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the sense bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, and the purity of the perfection of diligence (vīryapāramitā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the perfection of diligence is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the sphere of form, and the purity of the perfection of diligence are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure, the perfection of vigor is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental objects (dharmāyatana), and the purity of the perfection of diligence (vīryapāramitā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the perfection of diligence is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the eye-element, and the purity of the perfection of diligence are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the form realm (rūpadhātu), the eye-consciousness element (cakṣurvijñānadhātu), eye-contact (cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa), and the various feelings (vedanā) produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure; because the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, the perfection of vigor (vīryapāramitā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowing, the purity of everything from the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, and the purity of the perfection of diligence, are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the perfection of diligence is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ear-element, and the purity of the perfection of diligence are non-dual; they are not two, not divided, not distinct, and not separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of ear-consciousness, auditory contact, and all sensations produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of sound up to all sensations produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure, the perfection of vigor (vīryapāramitā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the sphere of sound (*śabdadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, and the purity of the perfection of vigor (*vīryapāramitā*), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the nose element is pure; because the nose element is pure, the perfection of diligence is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the nose element, and the purity of the perfection of diligence are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are distinct from nothing, and there is no separation between them.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the perfection of vigor (vīryapāramitā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the realm of fragrance up to the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition, and the purity of the perfection of diligence (vīryapāramitā) are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the tongue element is pure; because the tongue element is pure, the perfection of diligence is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the tongue element (jihvādhātu), and the purity of the perfection of diligence (vīryapāramitā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the perfection of vigor (vīryapāramitā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and the purity of the perfection of diligence, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 245. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter on Difficult-to-Believe Understanding, Thirty-Four, Section Sixty-Five. "Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the body-element (kāyadhātu) is pure; because the body-element is pure, the perfection of vigor (vīryapāramitā) is pure. Why is this?

The purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the body element, and the purity of the perfection of diligence are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the perfection of vigor (vīryapāramitā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the sensations arising from the condition of the sphere of tangibles (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*) up to bodily contact, as well as the purity of the perfection of diligence (*vīryapāramitā*), are non-dual; they are not two, they are undivided, they are without distinction, and they are uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the intentionality of the knowledge of all modes is pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the perfection of diligence is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the mental faculty, and the purity of the perfection of diligence are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are pure; because the dharma-element up to all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are pure, the perfection of vigor (vīryapāramitā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of everything from the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, and the purity of the perfection of diligence (*vīryapāramitā*), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the perfection of diligence is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the earth element, and the purity of the perfection of diligence are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the perfection of diligence is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, as well as the purity of the perfection of diligence, are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the perfection of vigor is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna), the purity of the light of wisdom (prabhāsvara), and the purity of the perfection of diligence (vīryapāramitā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, volitional formations (saṃskāra), consciousness (vijñāna), name-and-form (nāmarūpa), the six sense bases (ṣaḍāyatana), contact (sparśa), sensation (vedanā), craving (tṛṣṇā), grasping (upādāna), becoming (bhava), birth (jāti), and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the perfection of vigor (vīryapāramitā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of everything from conditioned activities up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, and the purity of the perfection of diligence (*vīryapāramitā*) are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, the perfection of diligence is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the perfection of generosity (dānapāramitā), as well as the purity of the perfection of diligence (vīryapāramitā), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, the perfection of diligence is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the perfections—from pure ethical discipline up to the perfection of wisdom, and the purity of the perfection of diligence—are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the perfection of diligence is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of internal emptiness, and the purity of the perfection of diligence are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*) is pure, there is the purity of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, emptiness of self-characteristic, emptiness of common characteristic, emptiness of all phenomena, emptiness of non-apprehensibility, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, and emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence; because there is the purity of external emptiness up to the purity of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, there is the purity of the perfection of diligence (*vīryapāramitā*).

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of outer emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence (abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā), and the purity of the perfection of diligence (vīryapāramitā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the perfection of diligence is pure.”
Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of suchness, and the purity of the perfection of diligence are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), the non-falsity of phenomena (avitathatā), the unalterability of phenomena (ananyathātā), the sameness of phenomena (samatā), the state beyond birth (anabhibhavatā), the fixedness of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu) are pure; because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the perfection of vigor (vīryapāramitā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu) up to the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu), and the purity of the perfection of diligence (vīryapāramitā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure; because the noble truth of suffering is pure, the perfection of diligence is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the noble truth of suffering, and the purity of the perfection of diligence are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure, the perfection of diligence is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, and the purity of the perfection of diligence (vīryapāramitā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the perfection of vigor is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four dhyānas, and the purity of the perfection of diligence are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, the perfection of diligence is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna), the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, and the purity of the perfection of diligence (vīryapāramitā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the perfection of diligence is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eight liberations, and the purity of the perfection of diligence are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the eight bases of mastery (abhibhvāyatana), the nine successive attainments (anupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (kṛtsnāyatana) are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the perfection of vigor (vīryapāramitā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the eight bases of mastery (aṣṭavimokṣa), the nine successive attainments (navānupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (daśakṛtsnāyatana), as well as the purity of the perfection of diligence (vīryapāramitā), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four applications of mindfulness are pure; because the four applications of mindfulness are pure, the perfection of diligence is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, and the purity of the perfection of diligence are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are without distinction, and they are not separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eight branches of the noble path are pure; because the four right endeavors up to the eight branches of the noble path are pure, the perfection of vigor (vīryapāramitā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, and the purity of the perfection of diligence are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the door of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the door of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the perfection of diligence is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, and the purity of the perfection of diligence are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the gateways of liberation of signlessness (animitta) and wishlessness (apraṇihita) are pure; because the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure, the perfection of vigor (vīryapāramitā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, and the purity of the perfection of diligence are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the perfection of diligence is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, and the purity of the perfection of diligence are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are distinct from one another, and they are not separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the perfection of vigor is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience, the purity of the five eyes, and the purity of the perfection of diligence are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the six supernormal knowledges (ṣaḍabhijñā) are pure; because the six supernormal knowledges are pure, the perfection of vigor (vīryapāramitā) is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is [identical to] the purity of the six supernormal powers, and the purity of the perfection of diligence, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten powers of a buddha are pure; because the ten powers of a buddha are pure, the perfection of diligence is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, and the purity of the perfection of diligence are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are distinct from one another, and they are not severed.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the four fearlessnesses (vaiśāradya), the four analytical knowledges (pratisaṃvid), great loving-kindness (maitrī), great compassion (karuṇā), great sympathetic joy (muditā), great equanimity (upekṣā), and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (āveṇikabuddhadharma) are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, the perfection of vigor (vīryapāramitā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and the purity of the perfection of diligence are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the perfection of diligence is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of the perfection of diligence are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the state of constant dwelling in equanimity is pure; because the state of constant dwelling in equanimity is pure, the perfection of vigor is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the nature of constant equanimity, and the purity of the perfection of diligence are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the knowledge of all is pure; because the knowledge of all is pure, the perfection of vigor is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all-knowledge, and the purity of the perfection of diligence are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, the perfection of diligence is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, and the purity of the perfection of diligence, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all dharanī-doors are pure; because all dharanī-doors are pure, the perfection of vigor is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all dharani-doors, and the purity of the perfection of diligence are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, all doors of meditative concentration (*samādhi-mukha*) are pure; because all doors of meditative concentration are pure, the perfection of vigor (*vīrya-pāramitā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all gateways of samādhi, and the purity of the perfection of diligence are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, the perfection of vigor is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, and the purity of the perfection of diligence are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the fruit of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship is pure; because the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure, the perfection of vigor (vīryapāramitā) is pure.

Why is this?
