“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, internal emptiness is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of non-duality, or the purity of internal emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, internal emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from formative activities up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, as well as the purity of internal emptiness (adhyātmaśūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, internal emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the perfection of generosity, and the purity of internal emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, internal emptiness (adhyātma-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), as well as the purity of internal emptiness (adhyātmaśūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, outer emptiness is pure; because outer emptiness is pure, inner emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if external emptiness is pure, and if internal emptiness is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, there is the purity of internal and external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence. Because internal and external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure, internal emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from internal and external emptiness up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence (abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā), as well as the purity of internal emptiness, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, internal emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if suchness is pure, and if internal emptiness is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), non-falsity (avitathatā), non-alteration (ananyathābhāva), sameness (samatā), the state beyond birth (anabhisamskāratā), the fixedness of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu) are pure; because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, internal emptiness (adhyātmaśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, or the purity of internal emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure; because the noble truth of suffering is pure, internal emptiness is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the noble truth of suffering is pure, and if internal emptiness is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are pure, internal emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, and the purity of internal emptiness (adhyātmaśūnyatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, internal emptiness is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is [identical to] the purity of the four dhyānas, and the purity of internal emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, internal emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the four immeasurables (apramāṇa), the four formless attainments (ārūpyasamāpatti), and internal emptiness (adhyātma-śūnyatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, internal emptiness is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eight liberations, or the purity of internal emptiness, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the eight bases of mastery (abhibhvāyatana), the nine successive attainments (anupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (kṛtsnāyatana) are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, internal emptiness (adhyātmaśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, the ten universal bases, or the purity of internal emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure; because the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, internal emptiness is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, and if internal emptiness is pure, this is because they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eight branches of the noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eight branches of the noble path are pure, internal emptiness (adhyātmaśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, as well as the purity of internal emptiness (adhyātmaśūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, internal emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the door of liberation that is emptiness (śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha), and the purity of internal emptiness (adhyātma-śūnyatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the gates of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are pure; because the gates of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are pure, internal emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the gateways to liberation—signlessness (animitta) and wishlessness (apraṇihita)—as well as the purity of internal emptiness (adhyātmaśūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, internal emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, and the purity of internal emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, internal emptiness is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the five eyes, or the purity of internal emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, the six supernormal knowledges (*ṣaḍabhijñā*) are pure; because the six supernormal knowledges are pure, internal emptiness (*adhyātmaśūnyatā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the six supernormal knowledges, or the purity of internal emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, internal emptiness is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, or the purity of internal emptiness, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, internal emptiness (adhyātma-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, or the purity of internal emptiness (adhyātma-śūnyatā), they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, internal emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of internal emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the state of constant equanimity is pure; because the state of constant equanimity is pure, internal emptiness is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is [identical to] the purity of the nature of constant equanimity, and the purity of internal emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all-knowledge is pure; because all-knowledge is pure, internal emptiness is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all-knowledge, or the purity of internal emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, internal emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects, and the purity of internal emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all dhāraṇī-doors are pure; because all dhāraṇī-doors are pure, internal emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all dharani-doors, and the purity of internal emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure; because all doors of samādhi are pure, internal emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of all doors of samādhi, and the purity of internal emptiness (adhyātmaśūnyatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, internal emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, and the purity of internal emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship is pure; because the fruit of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship is pure, internal emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the fruit of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship, and the purity of internal emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, internal emptiness is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of internal emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure, internal emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of internal emptiness (adhyātma-śūnyatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, internal emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, and the purity of internal emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, external emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if form is pure, and if external emptiness is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, external emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna), the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, and the purity of external emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye base is pure; because the eye base is pure, external emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sense-base of the eye is pure, and if external emptiness is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, external emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, as well as the purity of external emptiness (bahirdhā-śūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, external emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sphere of form is pure, and if external emptiness is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena (śabda-, gandha-, rasa-, spraṣṭavya-, and dharmāyatana) are pure; because the bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure, external emptiness (bahirdhā-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena (dharmāyatana), as well as the purity of external emptiness (bahirdhāśūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, external emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the eye-element is pure, and if external emptiness is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the form element, the eye-consciousness element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure; because the form element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, external emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of everything from the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, and the purity of external emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, external emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the ear-element is pure, and if external emptiness is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of ear-consciousness, auditory contact, and the various feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure, external emptiness (bahirdhā-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience and the purity of the sphere of sound, up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, and the purity of external emptiness, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the nose element is pure; because the nose element is pure, external emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the nose element is pure, and if external emptiness is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, external emptiness (bahirdhā-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the realm of fragrance, up to and including the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of external emptiness, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, external emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the tongue element is pure, and if external emptiness is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, external emptiness (bahirdhā-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and the purity of external emptiness are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, external emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the body element, and the purity of external emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous; such is their nature.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, external emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the sensations arising with the body as the condition, from the element of tangibility up to [the element of sound], as well as the purity of external emptiness (bahirdhāśūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

“Subhūti! Because the intention for the purification of all-knowledge is pure, the mind-element (*manodhātu*) is pure; because the mind-element is pure, external emptiness (*bahirdhāśūnyatā*) is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the mental faculty, or the purity of external emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, and mind-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition, are pure. Because the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition are pure, external emptiness (bahirdhā-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purification of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purification of the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition, and the purification of external emptiness, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, external emptiness is pure. Why is this?
The purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the earth element, and the purity of external emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, external emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, as well as the purity of external emptiness, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, external emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the light of wisdom is pure, and if external emptiness is pure, this is because they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, volitional formations (saṃskāra), consciousness (vijñāna), name-and-form (nāmarūpa), the six sense bases (ṣaḍāyatana), contact (sparśa), feeling (vedanā), craving (tṛṣṇā), grasping (upādāna), becoming (bhava), birth (jāti), and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair (jarāmaraṇa-śoka-parideva-duḥkha-daurmanasyopāyāsa) are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, external emptiness (bahirdhā-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, as well as the purity of external emptiness (bahirdhāśūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, external emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the perfection of generosity (dānapāramitā), and the purity of external emptiness (bahirdhāśūnyatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, external emptiness (bahirdhā-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), as well as the purity of external emptiness (bahirdhāśūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, external emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if internal emptiness is pure, and if external emptiness is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, there is purity of internal and external emptiness (adhyātma-bahirdhā-śūnyatā), emptiness of emptiness (śūnyatā-śūnyatā), great emptiness (mahā-śūnyatā), emptiness of the ultimate (paramārtha-śūnyatā), emptiness of the conditioned (saṃskṛta-śūnyatā), emptiness of the unconditioned (asaṃskṛta-śūnyatā), absolute emptiness (atyanta-śūnyatā), emptiness of the limitless (anavara-agra-śūnyatā), emptiness of dispersion (anavakāra-śūnyatā), emptiness of non-alteration (anavakāra-śūnyatā), emptiness of essential nature (prakṛti-śūnyatā), emptiness of specific characteristics (svalakṣaṇa-śūnyatā), emptiness of common characteristics (sāmānya-lakṣaṇa-śūnyatā), emptiness of all phenomena (sarvadharma-śūnyatā), emptiness of the unapprehendable (anupalambha-śūnyatā), emptiness of non-existence (abhāva-śūnyatā), emptiness of intrinsic nature (svabhāva-śūnyatā), and emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence (abhāvasvabhāva-śūnyatā). Because internal and external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure, external emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of the emptiness of the internal and external up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence (*abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā*), or the purity of the emptiness of the external, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, external emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if suchness is pure, and if external emptiness is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the dharma-nature (dharmatā), the non-falsity (avitathatā), the non-alteration (ananyathābhāva), equality (samatā), the state beyond birth (anupapattitā), the fixed nature of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the stability of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu) are pure; because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, external emptiness (bahirdhāśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, and the purity of external emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure; because the noble truth of suffering is pure, external emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the noble truth of suffering is pure, and if external emptiness is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure, external emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, and the purity of external emptiness (bahirdhāśūnyatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, external emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the same as the purity of the four dhyānas and the purity of external emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four immeasurables (apramāṇa) and the four formless attainments (ārūpyasamāpatti) are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are pure, external emptiness (bahirdhāśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the four immeasurables (apramāṇa) and the four formless attainments (ārūpyasamāpatti), and the purity of external emptiness (bahirdhāśūnyatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, external emptiness is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is such, and the purity of the eight liberations is such, and the purity of external emptiness is such, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, the eight bases of mastery (*abhibhvāyatana*), the nine successive attainments (*anupūrvavihārasamāpatti*), and the ten totalities (*kṛtsnāyatana*) are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, external emptiness (*bahirdhāśūnyatā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the eight bases of mastery (aṣṭavimokṣa), the nine successive attainments (navānupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten pervasive bases (daśakṛtsnāyatana), as well as the purity of external emptiness (bahirdhāśūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four applications of mindfulness are pure; because the four applications of mindfulness are pure, external emptiness is pure. Why is this?
The purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, and the purity of external emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, external emptiness (bahirdhā-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, and the purity of external emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, external emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness (śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha), and the purity of external emptiness (bahirdhā-śūnyatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure; because the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure, external emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, and the purity of external emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the emptiness of the external is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, and the purity of external emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, external emptiness is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the five eyes, or the purity of external emptiness, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the six supernormal powers (ṣaḍabhijñā) are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, external emptiness (bahirdhā-śūnyatā) is pure. Why is this?

Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the six supernormal powers, or the purity of external emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, external emptiness is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, and if external emptiness is pure, this is because they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, external emptiness (bahirdhā-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and the purity of external emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, external emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of external emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the state of constant equanimity (upekṣā-svabhāva) is pure; because the state of constant equanimity is pure, external emptiness (bahirdhā-śūnyatā) is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the state of constant equanimity, and if the purity of external emptiness [is that same purity], they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all-knowledge is pure; because all-knowledge is pure, external emptiness is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all-knowledge, or the purity of external emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, external emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the knowledge of the paths (mārgākārajñatā) and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā), and the purity of external emptiness (bahirdhāśūnyatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all dhāraṇī-doors are pure; because all dhāraṇī-doors are pure, external emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of all dharanī-doors, and the purity of external emptiness (bahirdhā-śūnyatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure; because all doors of samādhi are pure, external emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all doors of samādhi, and the purity of external emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, external emptiness is pure. Why is that?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, and the purity of external emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the fruit of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship is pure; because the fruit of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship is pure, external emptiness (bahirdhā-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the fruit of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship, and the purity of external emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, external emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of external emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure, external emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of external emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the unexcelled, perfect enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unexcelled, perfect enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, external emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, and the purity of external emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 248. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter Thirty-four, "Difficult to Believe and Understand," Section Sixty-eight. "Furthermore, Subhūti!"
Because the knowledge of all modes of omniscience (*sarvajñājñāna*) is pure, form (*rūpa*) is pure; because form is pure, internal and external emptiness (*adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience, the purity of form, and the purity of internal and external emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, internal and external emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, as well as the purity of internal and external emptiness (adhyātma-bahirdhā-śūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sense-sphere of the eye is pure; because the sense-sphere of the eye is pure, internal and external emptiness is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the sense-base of the eye is pure, and if internal and external emptiness is pure, this is because they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, internal and external emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, as well as the purity of internal and external emptiness (adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, internal and external emptiness is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sphere of form is pure, and if internal and external emptiness is pure, this is because they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena are pure, internal and external emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena (dharmāyatana), as well as the purity of internal and external emptiness (adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, internal and external emptiness is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purification of the knowledge of all modes, the purification of the eye-element, or the purification of internal and external emptiness, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the form element (rūpadhātu), the eye-consciousness element (cakṣurvijñānadhātu), eye-contact (cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa), and the various feelings (vedanā) produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure; because the form element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, internal-external emptiness (adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the form realm (rūpadhātu) up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of internal and external emptiness (adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, internal and external emptiness is pure. Why is that?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ear-element, or the purity of internal and external emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of sounds, the sphere of ear-consciousness, ear-contact, and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of sounds up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure, internal and external emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience, the purity of the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, and the purity of internal and external emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the nose element is pure; because the nose element is pure, internal and external emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sphere of the nose is pure, and if internal and external emptiness is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, internal and external emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the realm of fragrance up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of internal and external emptiness (adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, internal and external emptiness is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purification of the knowledge of all modes, the purification of the tongue-element, or the purification of internal and external emptiness, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, internal-external emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and the purity of internal and external emptiness (adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā) are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, internal and external emptiness is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the body element, or the purity of internal and external emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, internal and external emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the sensations produced with the body as the basis for contact, up to the element of tangibles, and the purity of internal and external emptiness (adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the intention for the purity of the knowledge of all modes is pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, internal and external emptiness is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the mental faculty, or the purity of internal and external emptiness, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, mental contact, and the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition are pure; because the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition are pure, internal and external emptiness (adhyātma-bahirdhā-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of everything from the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, as well as the purity of internal and external emptiness, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, internal and external emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the earth element is pure, and if internal and external emptiness is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, internal and external emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, or the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, or the purity of internal and external emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, internal and external emptiness is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of non-duality, or the purity of internal and external emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*) is pure, formations (*saṃskāra*), consciousness (*vijñāna*), name-and-form (*nāmarūpa*), the six sense bases (*ṣaḍāyatana*), contact (*sparśa*), feeling (*vedanā*), craving (*tṛṣṇā*), grasping (*upādāna*), becoming (*bhava*), birth (*jāti*), and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair (*jarāmaraṇa-śoka-parideva-duḥkha-daurmanasyopāyāsa*) are pure; because formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, internal and external emptiness (*adhyātmabahirdhā-śūnyatā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of everything from conditioned activities up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, or the purity of internal and external emptiness, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, internal and external emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the perfection of giving (dānapāramitā), and the purity of internal and external emptiness (adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, internal and external emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the precepts up to the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), as well as the purity of internal and external emptiness (adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, internal-and-external emptiness is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if inner emptiness is pure, and if both inner and outer emptiness are pure, this is because they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, there is the purity of external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence. Because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is pure, internal-external emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence (abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā), as well as the purity of internal-external emptiness, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, internal and external emptiness is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of suchness, or the purity of internal and external emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the dharma-nature (dharmatā), the non-falsity (avitathatā), the non-alteration (ananyathābhāva), equality (samatā), the state beyond birth (anupapattitā), the fixed nature of dharmas (dharmasthititā), the stability of dharmas (dharmaniyāmatā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu) are pure; because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, internal and external emptiness (adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), up to the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu), as well as the purity of internal and external emptiness (adhyātma-bahirdhā-śūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure; because the noble truth of suffering is pure, internal and external emptiness is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the noble truth of suffering is pure, and if internal and external emptiness is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure, internal and external emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path, and the purity of internal and external emptiness (adhyātma-bahirdhā-śūnyatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, internal and external emptiness is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is so, and the purity of the four dhyānas, and the purity of internal and external emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are pure, internal and external emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, and the purity of internal and external emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, internal and external emptiness is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the eight liberations are pure, and if internal and external emptiness is pure, this is because they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the eight bases of mastery (abhibhvāyatana), the nine successive attainments (anupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (kṛtsnāyatana) are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, internal and external emptiness (adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the eight bases of mastery (abhibhvāyatana), the nine successive attainments (anupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten universal bases (kṛtsnāyatana), as well as the purity of internal and external emptiness (adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four applications of mindfulness are pure; because the four applications of mindfulness are pure, internal and external emptiness is pure. Why is this?
