Because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, the emptiness of emptiness (śūnyatā-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is identical to the purity of the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; and the purity of the emptiness of emptiness is non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the emptiness of emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of the emptiness of emptiness (śūnyatā-śūnyatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the state of constant equanimity is pure; because the state of constant equanimity is pure, the emptiness of emptiness is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is such, and the purity of the state of constant equanimity is such, and the purity of the emptiness of emptiness is such, it is because they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all-knowledge is pure; because all-knowledge is pure, the emptiness of emptiness is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all-knowledge, or the purity of emptiness of emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, the emptiness of emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, and the purity of emptiness of emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all dhāraṇī-doors are pure; because all dhāraṇī-doors are pure, the emptiness of emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all dharani-doors, and the purity of emptiness of emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure; because all doors of samādhi are pure, the emptiness of emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience, the purity of all doors of samādhi, and the purity of emptiness of emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, the emptiness of emptiness is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, and the purity of emptiness of emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous; therefore, they are one and the same.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the fruit of arhatship are pure; because the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the fruit of arhatship are pure, the emptiness of emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhat are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption. This is because they are the purity of the emptiness of emptiness (śūnyatā-śūnyatā).
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, the emptiness of emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of emptiness of emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure, the emptiness of emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of emptiness of emptiness (śūnyatā-śūnyatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, the emptiness of emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas, and the purity of emptiness of emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the great emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if form is pure, and if great emptiness is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, great emptiness (mahāśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, as well as the purity of great emptiness (mahāśūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sense-sphere of the eye is pure; because the sense-sphere of the eye is pure, great emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the eye base is pure, and if the great emptiness is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, great emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes and the purity of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, as well as the purity of great emptiness, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the great emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sphere of form is pure, and if the great emptiness is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure, great emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena (dharmāyatana), as well as the purity of the great emptiness (mahāśūnyatā), are non-dual; they are not two, not divided, not distinct, and not separate.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the great emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the eye-element is pure, and if the great emptiness is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the form realm, the eye-consciousness realm, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure; because the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, the great emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the form realm (rūpadhātu) up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of great emptiness (mahāśūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, great emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the ear element is pure, and if the great emptiness is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of ear-consciousness, ear-contact, and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure, the great emptiness (mahāśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the sphere of sound (*śabdadhātu*)—up to and including the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition—and the purity of the great emptiness (*mahāśūnyatā*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the nose element is pure; because the nose element is pure, great emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the nose element is pure, and if the great emptiness is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the great emptiness (mahāśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the realm of fragrance up to the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the great emptiness (mahāśūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 249. Translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter on Difficult-to-Believe Understanding, Number Thirty-Four, Section Sixty-Nine. "Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the tongue-element (jihvādhātu) is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the great emptiness (mahāśūnyatā) is pure. Why is this?

Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the tongue-element, or the purity of the great emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to the various sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the great emptiness (mahāśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the taste element (*rasadhātu*)—up to and including the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition—as well as the purity of the great emptiness (*mahāśūnyatā*), are non-dual; they are not two, not divided, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body-element is pure; because the body-element is pure, the great emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the body element is pure, and if the great emptiness is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the great emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the various feelings arising with the body as the basis and tangibles as conditions—up to the element of tangibles—are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted, just like the purity of the great emptiness (mahāśūnyatā).
“Subhūti! Because the intentionality of the knowledge of all modes is pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the great emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the mind-element is pure, and if the great emptiness is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are pure; because the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are pure, the great emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu) up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the great emptiness (mahāśūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, great emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the earth element, and the purity of great emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the great emptiness (mahāśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, as well as the purity of great emptiness, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, great emptiness is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the light of non-duality, or the purity of great emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, great emptiness (mahāśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of everything from formative activities up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, as well as the purity of great emptiness, are non-dual; they are not two, are not divided, are not distinct, and are not severed.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, the great emptiness is pure.”
Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the perfection of giving, and the purity of great emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, the great emptiness (mahāśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), and the purity of great emptiness (mahāśūnyatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, inner emptiness is pure; because inner emptiness is pure, great emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if inner emptiness is pure, and if great emptiness is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, there is the purity of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate (paramārtha-śūnyatā), the emptiness of the conditioned (saṃskṛta-śūnyatā), the emptiness of the unconditioned (asaṃskṛta-śūnyatā), absolute emptiness (atyanta-śūnyatā), the emptiness of the beginningless and endless (anavarāgra-śūnyatā), the emptiness of dispersion (anavakāra-śūnyatā), the emptiness of non-alteration (anavakāra-śūnyatā), the emptiness of intrinsic nature (prakṛti-śūnyatā), the emptiness of self-characteristics (svalakṣaṇa-śūnyatā), the emptiness of common characteristics (sāmānya-lakṣaṇa-śūnyatā), the emptiness of all phenomena (sarvadharma-śūnyatā), the emptiness of the unapprehendable (anupalambha-śūnyatā), the emptiness of non-existence (abhāva-śūnyatā), the emptiness of intrinsic nature (svabhāva-śūnyatā), and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence (abhāvasvabhāva-śūnyatā). Because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is pure, the great emptiness (mahā-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of outer emptiness up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence (abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā), as well as the purity of great emptiness (mahāśūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the great emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of suchness, and the purity of great emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the dharma-nature (dharmatā), the non-falsity (avitathatā), the unalterability (ananyathātā), the sameness (samatā), the state beyond birth (anupapattitva), the fixedness of dharma (dharmasthititā), the stability of dharma (dharmaniyāmatā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu) are pure. Because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the great emptiness (mahāśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) up to the inconceivable realm, and the purity of great emptiness (*mahāśūnyatā*) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure; because the noble truth of suffering is pure, great emptiness is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the noble truth of suffering is pure, and if great emptiness is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are pure, great emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, and the purity of great emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, great emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four dhyānas, and the purity of great emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, the great emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, and the purity of great emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the great emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eight liberations, and the purity of great emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the eight bases of mastery (abhibhvāyatana), the nine successive attainments (anupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (kṛtsnāyatana) are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, great emptiness (mahāśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience, the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases, as well as the purity of great emptiness, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure; because the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, the great emptiness is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, and the purity of the great emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, great emptiness (mahāśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, as well as the purity of great emptiness (mahāśūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, great emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness (śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha), and the purity of great emptiness (mahāśūnyatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure; because the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure, great emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purification of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purification of the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, and the purification of great emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, great emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, and the purity of great emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the great emptiness is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purification of the knowledge of all modes, the purification of the five eyes, or the purification of great emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*) is pure, the six supernormal powers (*ṣaḍabhijñā*) are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, great emptiness (*mahāśūnyatā*) is pure. Why is this?

Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the six supernormal powers, or the purity of great emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, great emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, and if great emptiness is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, the great emptiness (mahāśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, and the purity of great emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, great emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of great emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the state of constant equanimity is pure; because the state of constant equanimity is pure, great emptiness is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the purity of the state of constant equanimity is pure, and if the purity of great emptiness is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all-knowledge is pure; because all-knowledge is pure, great emptiness is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all-knowledge, or the purity of great emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, great emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, and the purity of great emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all dhāraṇī-doors are pure; because all dhāraṇī-doors are pure, great emptiness is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience, the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors, and the purity of great emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure; because all doors of samādhi are pure, great emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all doors of samādhi, and the purity of great emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, great emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, and the purity of great emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure; because the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure, great emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship, and the purity of great emptiness (mahāśūnyatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, the great emptiness is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of great emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure, great emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the sphere of sound (*śabdadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the emptiness of the conditioned (*saṃskṛtaśūnyatā*), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the nose element is pure; because the nose element is pure, conditioned emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the nose element is pure, and if the emptiness of the conditioned is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, conditioned emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the realm of fragrance up to the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the emptiness of the conditioned (saṃskṛtaśūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, conditioned emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the tongue element is pure, and if the emptiness of the conditioned is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, conditioned emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) and the purity of the taste element (*rasadhātu*), up to and including the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with tongue-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the emptiness of the conditioned (*saṃskṛtaśūnyatā*), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, conditioned emptiness is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the body-element is pure, and if the emptiness of the conditioned is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, conditioned emptiness (saṃskṛta-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the various feelings arising with the body as the condition, from the element of tangibility up to [the element of] mental contact, as well as the purity of conditioned emptiness, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the intentionality of the knowledge of all modes is pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, conditioned emptiness is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the mind-element is pure, and if the emptiness of the conditioned is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the dharma-element, the mental consciousness-element, and mind-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition, are pure; because the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition are pure, the emptiness of the conditioned (saṃskṛtaśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu) up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the emptiness of the conditioned (saṃskṛtaśūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 253. Translated by the Dharma Master Xuanzang under Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter Thirty-Four (70), "Difficult to Believe and Understand. "Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*) is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, conditioned emptiness (*saṃskṛta-śūnyatā*) is pure. Why is this?

Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the earth element, and the purity of conditioned emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, conditioned emptiness (saṃskṛta-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, as well as the purity of conditioned emptiness (saṃskṛta-śūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the emptiness of the conditioned is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the light of non-arising, or the purity of the emptiness of the conditioned, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, volitional formations (saṃskāra), consciousness (vijñāna), name-and-form (nāmarūpa), the six sense bases (ṣaḍāyatana), contact (sparśa), feeling (vedanā), craving (tṛṣṇā), grasping (upādāna), becoming (bhava), birth (jāti), and old age, death, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations up to old age, death, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are pure, conditioned emptiness (saṃskṛta-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience and the purity of everything from conditioned phenomena through old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of giving is pure; because the perfection of giving is pure, conditioned emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the perfection of generosity (dānapāramitā), and the purity of the emptiness of the conditioned (saṃskṛtaśūnyatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, conditioned emptiness (saṃskṛta-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowing and the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom, as well as the purity of the emptiness of the conditioned, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the emptiness of the conditioned is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if inner emptiness is pure, and if the emptiness of conditioned phenomena is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure; because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure, conditioned emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from outer emptiness up to the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature, as well as the purity of conditioned emptiness, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the emptiness of the conditioned is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if suchness is pure, and if the emptiness of the conditioned is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), non-falsity (avitathatā), non-alteration (ananyathābhāva), sameness (samatā), the state beyond birth (anabhibhavatā), the fixed nature of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu) are pure. Because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the emptiness of the conditioned (saṃskṛtaśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, and the purity of the emptiness of the conditioned are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure; because the noble truth of suffering is pure, conditioned emptiness is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the noble truth of suffering is pure, and if the emptiness of conditioned phenomena is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure, conditioned emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, and the purity of the emptiness of the conditioned are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, conditioned emptiness is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the same as the purity of the four dhyānas, and the purity of the emptiness of the conditioned, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not severed.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are pure, conditioned emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because if the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are pure, and if conditioned emptiness is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, conditioned emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the eight liberations are pure, and if the emptiness of the conditioned is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the eight bases of mastery (abhibhvāyatana), the nine successive attainments (anupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (kṛtsnāyatana) are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, conditioned emptiness (saṃskṛtaśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the eight bases of mastery (aṣṭavimokṣa), the nine successive attainments (navānupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (daśakṛtsnāyatana), as well as the purity of conditioned emptiness (saṃskṛta-śūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four applications of mindfulness are pure; because the four applications of mindfulness are pure, conditioned emptiness is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, and if conditioned emptiness is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, conditioned emptiness (saṃskṛta-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purification of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purification of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, and the purification of the emptiness of the conditioned are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, conditioned emptiness is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, and the purity of the emptiness of conditioned phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure; because the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure, the emptiness of the conditioned is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, and the purity of the emptiness of the conditioned are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, conditioned emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowing, the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, and the purity of conditioned emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, conditioned emptiness is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the five eyes, or the purity of conditioned emptiness, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the six supernormal powers are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, conditioned emptiness is pure. Why is this?

Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the six supernormal powers, or the purity of conditioned emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, conditioned emptiness is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, and if the emptiness of the conditioned is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, conditioned emptiness (saṃskṛta-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, as well as the purity of the emptiness of the conditioned, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of the emptiness of the conditioned are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the state of constant equanimity is pure; because the state of constant equanimity is pure, conditioned emptiness is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is such, and the purity of the state of constant equanimity is such, and the purity of the emptiness of the conditioned is such, it is because they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the knowledge of all things is pure; because the knowledge of all things is pure, conditioned emptiness is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the knowledge of all things is pure, and if the emptiness of the conditioned is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, conditioned emptiness (*saṃskṛtaśūnyatā*) is pure.

Why is this? Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path, the knowledge of all aspects, or the purity of conditioned emptiness, these are non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
Because there is no distinction and no interruption. "Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all dhāraṇī-doors are pure; because all dhāraṇī-doors are pure, conditioned emptiness is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors, and the purity of the emptiness of the conditioned are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, all doors of meditative concentration (*samādhi-mukha*) are pure; because all doors of meditative concentration are pure, conditioned emptiness (*saṃskṛta-śūnyatā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all doors of samādhi, and the purity of the emptiness of the conditioned are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, conditioned emptiness is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the fruit of stream-entry is pure, and if the emptiness of conditioned phenomena is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure; because the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure, conditioned emptiness (saṃskṛtaśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhat are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous; for they are equally pure through the emptiness of the conditioned (saṃskṛtaśūnyatā).
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, conditioned emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of the emptiness of conditioned phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure, the emptiness of the conditioned is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of the emptiness of the conditioned (saṃskṛtaśūnyatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the unexcelled, perfect enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unexcelled, perfect enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, the emptiness of the conditioned is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, and the purity of the emptiness of the conditioned are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if form is pure, and if the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, and the purity of the emptiness of the unconditioned (asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-base is pure; because the eye-base is pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sense base of the eye is pure, and if the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, and the purity of the emptiness of the unconditioned are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sense-base of form is pure, and if the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, and the purity of unconditioned emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor separate.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eye-element, or the purity of the emptiness of the unconditioned, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the form element, the eye-consciousness element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure; because the form element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned (asaṃskṛta-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the form realm (rūpadhātu) up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the emptiness of the unconditioned (asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā), are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because omniscient wisdom is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ear-element, or the purity of the emptiness of the unconditioned, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of ear-consciousness, ear-contact, and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as condition are pure; because the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as condition are pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned (asaṃskṛta-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, and the purity of the emptiness of the unconditioned, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the nose element is pure; because the nose element is pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the nose element, and the purity of the emptiness of the unconditioned are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned (asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the realm of fragrance up to the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition, and the purity of unconditioned emptiness, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the tongue element is pure, and if the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and the purity of the emptiness of the unconditioned (asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the body element is pure, and if the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) and the purity of the various feelings arising with the body as the basis and tangibles as the condition—up to the tangibles themselves—and the purity of the emptiness of the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā*), are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.

“Subhūti! Because the intention for the purity of the knowledge of all modes is pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the mental faculty is pure, and if the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the dharma-element, the mental consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are pure; because the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition, and the purity of unconditioned emptiness, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the earth element is pure, and if the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, unconditioned emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, or the purity of unconditioned emptiness (asaṃskṛta-śūnyatā), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of signlessness, or the purity of the emptiness of the unconditioned, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because formations through to old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned (asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of [the links from] formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, or the purity of the emptiness of the unconditioned—these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the perfection of giving, and the purity of the emptiness of the unconditioned are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned (asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), and the purity of the emptiness of the unconditioned (asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of internal emptiness, or the purity of the emptiness of the unconditioned, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure; because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned (asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, as well as the purity of unconditioned emptiness, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of suchness, or the purity of the emptiness of the unconditioned, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), the non-erroneous nature, the unchanging nature, the state of equality, the nature free from birth, the fixedness of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the stability of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu) are pure. Because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned (asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, or the purity of the emptiness of the unconditioned, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure; because the noble truth of suffering is pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the noble truth of suffering is pure, and if the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not severed.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned (asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path, and the purity of the emptiness of the unconditioned are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is such, and the purity of the four dhyānas is such, and the purity of unconditioned emptiness is such, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the four immeasurables (apramāṇa), the four formless attainments (ārūpyasamāpatti), and the emptiness of the unconditioned (asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eight liberations, or the purity of unconditioned emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the eight bases of mastery (aṣṭāv abhibhvāyatanāni), the nine successive attainments (navānupūrvavihārasamāpattayaḥ), and the ten totalities (daśa kṛtsnāyatanāni) are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned (asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the eight bases of mastery (aṣṭavimokṣa), the nine successive attainments (navānupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (daśakṛtsnāyatana), as well as the purity of the emptiness of the unconditioned (asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure; because the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, and if the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned (asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, and the purity of the emptiness of the unconditioned are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience, the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, and the purity of the emptiness of the unconditioned are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure; because the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, and the purity of the emptiness of the unconditioned are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, and the purity of unconditioned emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the five eyes, or the purity of the emptiness of the unconditioned, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the six supernormal powers (ṣaḍabhijñā) are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned (asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the six supernormal powers, or the purity of the emptiness of the unconditioned, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, or the purity of the emptiness of the unconditioned, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñājñāna*) is pure, the four fearlessnesses (*vaiśāradya*), the four analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*), great loving-kindness (*mahāmaitrī*), great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*), great sympathetic joy (*mahāmuditā*), great equanimity (*mahopekṣā*), and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇikabuddhadharma*) are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and the purity of the emptiness of the unconditioned are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of the emptiness of the unconditioned are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the wisdom of all-knowledge is pure, the state of constant abiding in equanimity is pure; because the state of constant abiding in equanimity is pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the state of constant equanimity, and the purity of the emptiness of the unconditioned are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the knowledge of all is pure; because the knowledge of all is pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all-knowledge, or the purity of the emptiness of the unconditioned, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path, the knowledge of all aspects, or the purity of the emptiness of the unconditioned, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all dharanī-doors are pure; because all dharanī-doors are pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all dharani-doors, and the purity of the emptiness of the unconditioned are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure; because all doors of samādhi are pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all doors of samādhi, and the purity of unconditioned emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, and the purity of the emptiness of the unconditioned are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure; because the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure.

Why is this?
