Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship, and the purity of the emptiness of the unconditioned (asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of the emptiness of the unconditioned are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of the emptiness of the unconditioned are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, the emptiness of the unconditioned is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, and the purity of the emptiness of the unconditioned are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, ultimate emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if form is pure, and if ultimate emptiness is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, ultimate emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, and the purity of ultimate emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye base is pure; because the eye base is pure, ultimate emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sense base of the eye is pure, and if ultimate emptiness is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, ultimate emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the sense bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, or the purity of ultimate emptiness, they are non-dual, not two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, ultimate emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the sphere of form, and the purity of ultimate emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure, ultimate emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena (dharmāyatana), as well as the purity of ultimate emptiness (atyantaśūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-faculty is pure; because the eye-faculty is pure, ultimate emptiness is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eye-element, or the purity of ultimate emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the form realm (rūpadhātu), the eye-consciousness realm (cakṣurvijñānadhātu), eye-contact (cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa), and the various feelings (vedanā) arising with eye-contact as condition are pure; because the form realm up to the various feelings arising with eye-contact as condition are pure, ultimate emptiness (atyanta-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the form realm (rūpadhātu) up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of ultimate emptiness (atyantaśūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, ultimate emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the ear-element is pure, and if ultimate emptiness is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of auditory consciousness, auditory contact, and all feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of sound up to all feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure, ultimate emptiness (atyanta-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, and the purity of ultimate emptiness (atyantaśūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the nose-element is pure; because the nose-element is pure, ultimate emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the nose element is pure, and if ultimate emptiness is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, and the contact of the nose, as well as the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, are pure; because the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, ultimate emptiness (atyantaśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the realm of fragrance up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are non-dual; they are not two, not divided, without distinction, and without interruption. Thus, because of this purity, there is no duality between them.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, ultimate emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the tongue element is pure, and if ultimate emptiness is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, ultimate emptiness (atyantaśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the taste element up to the various sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and the purity of ultimate emptiness are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are without distinction, and they are not separate.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, ultimate emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the body-element is pure, and if ultimate emptiness is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, ultimate emptiness (atyanta-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) and the purity of the various feelings arising with the body as the basis for contact, up to the element of tangibles, and the purity of ultimate emptiness (*atyantaśūnyatā*), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

“Subhūti! Because the intention for the purity of the knowledge of all modes is pure, the mind-element (*manodhātu*) is pure; because the mind-element is pure, ultimate emptiness (*atyanta-śūnyatā*) is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the mind-element is pure, and if ultimate emptiness is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness element, and mental contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are pure; because the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are pure, ultimate emptiness (atyanta-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu) up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of ultimate emptiness (atyantaśūnyatā), are non-dual, without division, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, ultimate emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the earth element is pure, and if ultimate emptiness is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, ultimate emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purification of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purification of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, or the purification of ultimate emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, ultimate emptiness is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of non-arising, or the purity of ultimate emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, ultimate emptiness (atyanta-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from formative forces up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, as well as the purity of ultimate emptiness (atyantaśūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, ultimate emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the perfection of giving, and the purity of ultimate emptiness are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are without distinction, and they are uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, ultimate emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), as well as the purity of ultimate emptiness (atyantaśūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, ultimate emptiness is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of internal emptiness, or the purity of ultimate emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, infinite emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure; because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure, absolute emptiness (atyantaśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence, as well as the purity of ultimate emptiness, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, ultimate emptiness is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of suchness, or the purity of ultimate emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), non-falsity (avitathatā), unalterability (ananyathābhāva), sameness (samatā), the state beyond birth (anabhibhavatā), the fixedness of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu) are pure. Because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, ultimate emptiness (atyanta-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, and the purity of ultimate emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure; because the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure, ultimate emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the noble truth of suffering, and the purity of ultimate emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure, ultimate emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path, and the purity of ultimate emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, ultimate emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four dhyānas, and the purity of ultimate emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, ultimate emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, and the purity of ultimate emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, ultimate emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the eight liberations, and the purity of ultimate emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the eight bases of mastery (aṣṭāv abhibhvāyatanāni), the nine successive attainments (navānupūrvavihārasamāpattayaḥ), and the ten totalities (daśa kṛtsnāyatanāni) are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, ultimate emptiness (atyantaśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because if the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten pervasive bases are pure, and if ultimate emptiness is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure; because the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, ultimate emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, and the purity of ultimate emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, ultimate emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, and the purity of ultimate emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the door of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the door of liberation that is emptiness is pure, ultimate emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness (śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha), and the purity of ultimate emptiness (atyanta-śūnyatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are pure; because the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are pure, ultimate emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, and the purity of ultimate emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, ultimate emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, and the purity of ultimate emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll 251. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter on Difficult-to-Believe Understanding, Thirty-Fourth, Section Seventy-One. "Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, ultimate emptiness (atyantaśūnyatā) is pure. Why is this?

Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the five eyes, or the purity of ultimate emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the six supernormal powers (ṣaḍabhijñā) are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, ultimate emptiness (atyantaśūnyatā) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the six supernormal powers, or the purity of ultimate emptiness, they are non-dual and not divided into two; they are without distinction and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, ultimate emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, and if ultimate emptiness is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, ultimate emptiness (atyanta-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and the purity of ultimate emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, ultimate emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of ultimate emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the state of abiding in equanimity is pure; because the state of abiding in equanimity is pure, ultimate emptiness is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the nature of constant equanimity, and the purity of ultimate emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the knowledge of all things is pure; because the knowledge of all things is pure, ultimate emptiness is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all-knowledge, or the purity of ultimate emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, ultimate emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, and the purity of ultimate emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all dharanī-doors are pure; because all dharanī-doors are pure, ultimate emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors, and the purity of ultimate emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure; because all doors of samādhi are pure, ultimate emptiness (atyantaśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience, the purity of all gateways to samādhi, and the purity of ultimate emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, ultimate emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, and the purity of ultimate emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the fruit of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship is pure; because the fruit of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship is pure, ultimate emptiness (atyanta-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship, and the purity of ultimate emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, ultimate emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of ultimate emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure, ultimate emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of ultimate emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, ultimate emptiness is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, and the purity of ultimate emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the emptiness of the limitless is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if form is pure, and if the emptiness of the limitless is pure, this is because they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the emptiness of the limitless is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, as well as the purity of the emptiness of the limitless (anantānta-śūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye base is pure; because the eye base is pure, the emptiness of the limitless is pure. Why is that?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sense base of the eye is pure, and if the emptiness of the limitless is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the emptiness of the limitless is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, and the purity of the emptiness of the limitless are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the emptiness of the limitless is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sphere of form is pure, and if the emptiness of the limitless is pure, it is because they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena are pure, the emptiness of the limitless is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena (dharmāyatana), as well as the purity of the emptiness of the limitless (anantānta-śūnyatā), are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the emptiness of the limitless is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eye-element, or the purity of the emptiness of the limitless, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the form realm, the eye-consciousness realm, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition are pure; because the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition are pure, the emptiness of the limitless is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of everything from the form realm (*rūpadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, or the purity of the emptiness of the limitless (*anavasthā-śūnyatā*), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the emptiness of the limitless is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the ear-element is pure, and if the emptiness of the limitless is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of auditory consciousness, auditory contact, and the various feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure, the emptiness of the limitless (anavakāraśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the sphere of sound, up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, and the purity of the emptiness of the limitless, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the nose element is pure; because the nose element is pure, the emptiness of the limitless is pure. Why is that?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the olfactory element, and the purity of the emptiness of the limitless are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the emptiness of the limitless (anavakāraśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the realm of fragrance up to the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition, and the purity of the emptiness of the limitless (anavakāraśūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the emptiness of the limitless is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the tongue element, or the purity of the emptiness of the limitless, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the emptiness of the limitless is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the various feelings produced with the gustatory element up to tongue-contact as conditions, as well as the purity of the emptiness of the limitless (anavakāraśūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, the emptiness of the limitless is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the body element is pure, and if the emptiness of the limitless is pure, this is because they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the emptiness of the limitless (anavakāraśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience, the purity of the sense-field of tangibles up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, and the purity of the emptiness of the limitless are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the intentionality of the knowledge of all modes is pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the emptiness of the limitless is pure. Why is that?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the mind-element is pure, and if the emptiness of the limitless is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, mental contact, and the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition are pure; because the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition are pure, the emptiness of the limitless (anavakāraśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) and the purity of everything from the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the emptiness of the limitless (*anavakāraśūnyatā*), are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the emptiness of the limitless is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the earth element is pure, and if the emptiness of the limitless is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the emptiness of the limitless is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, or the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, or the purity of the emptiness of the limitless, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the emptiness of limits is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the light of non-arising, or the purity of the emptiness of the limitless, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, formations (saṃskāra), consciousness (vijñāna), name-and-form (nāmarūpa), the six sense bases (ṣaḍāyatana), contact (sparśa), feeling (vedanā), craving (tṛṣṇā), grasping (upādāna), becoming (bhava), birth (jāti), and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the emptiness of the limitless (anavarāgra-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, as well as the purity of the emptiness of the limitless (anavakāraśūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, the emptiness of the limitless is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the perfection of generosity, and the purity of the emptiness of the limitless are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom are pure, the emptiness of the limitless (anavarāgra-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the precepts up to the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), or the purity of the emptiness of the limitless (anantakoṭiśūnyatā), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the emptiness of the limitless is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of internal emptiness, or the purity of the emptiness of the limitless, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, there is purity of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, emptiness of dispersion, unchanging emptiness, essential emptiness, emptiness of own-marks, common emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of own-nature, and the emptiness of the own-nature of non-existence. Because there is purity of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the own-nature of non-existence, there is purity of the emptiness of the limitless.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from external emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, as well as the purity of the emptiness of the limitless, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the emptiness of the limitless is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if suchness is pure, and if the emptiness of the limitless is pure, this is because they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm are pure. Because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the emptiness of the limitless (anavarāgra-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, or the purity of the emptiness of the limitless (anavasthā-śūnyatā), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure; because the noble truth of suffering is pure, the emptiness of the limitless is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the noble truth of suffering is pure, and if the emptiness of the limitless is pure, this is because they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure, the emptiness of the limitless (anavarāgra-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, and the purity of the emptiness of the limitless (anavasthā-śūnyatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the emptiness of the limitless is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the four dhyānas are pure, and if the emptiness of the limitless is pure, this is because they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four immeasurables (apramāṇa) and the four formless attainments (ārūpyasamāpatti) are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are pure, the emptiness of the limitless (anavakāraśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because if the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, and if the emptiness of the limitless is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the emptiness of the limitless is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the eight liberations are pure, and if the emptiness of the limitless is pure, it is because they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, the eight bases of mastery (*abhibhvāyatana*), the nine successive attainments (*anupūrvavihārasamāpatti*), and the ten totalities (*kṛtsnāyatana*) are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the emptiness of the limitless (*anavakāraśūnyatā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the eight bases of mastery (aṣṭavimokṣa), the nine successive attainments (navānupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten universal bases (daśakṛtsnāyatana), as well as the purity of the emptiness of the limitless (anavakāraśūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure; because the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, the emptiness of the limitless is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, and if the emptiness of the limitless is pure, this is because they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, the emptiness of the limitless (anavarāgra-śūnyatā) is pure.

Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and the purity of the emptiness of the limitless (*anavakāraśūnyatā*) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

"Furthermore, Subhūti!

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, and the purity of the emptiness of dispersion (avakāraśūnyatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the emptiness of dispersion is pure. Why is this?

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure, the emptiness of dispersion is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena (dharmāyatana), as well as the purity of the emptiness of dispersion (vidaraśūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the emptiness of dispersion is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the eye-element is pure, and if the emptiness of dispersion is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the form realm (rūpadhātu), the eye-consciousness realm (cakṣurvijñānadhātu), eye-contact (cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa), and the various feelings (vedanā) produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure; because the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, the emptiness of scattering (vidara-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the form realm (rūpadhātu) up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the emptiness of dispersion (vidaraśūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the emptiness of dispersion is pure. Why is this?

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, the emptiness of dispersion is pure. Why is this?

"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the emptiness of dispersion is pure. Why is this?"

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from conditioned activities up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, as well as the purity of the emptiness of dispersion (vidigata-śūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of external emptiness up to the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature (*abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā*), or the purity of the emptiness of dispersion (*atyantaśūnyatā*), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
