“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, the emptiness of scattering is pure. Why is that?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, and the purity of the emptiness of dispersion are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four fearlessnesses (vaiśāradya), the four analytical knowledges (pratisaṃvid), great loving-kindness (mahāmaitrī), great compassion (mahākaruṇā), great sympathetic joy (mahāmuditā), great equanimity (mahopekṣā), and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (āveṇika-buddhadharma) are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, the emptiness of dispersion (anavakāra-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, as well as the purity of the emptiness of scattering (avakāraśūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the emptiness of dispersion is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of the emptiness of dispersion are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the state of constant abiding in equanimity is pure; because the state of constant abiding in equanimity is pure, the emptiness of dispersion is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is such, and the purity of the state of constant equanimity is such, and the purity of the emptiness of dispersion is such, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the knowledge of all is pure; because the knowledge of all is pure, the emptiness of dispersion is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all-knowledge, or the purity of the emptiness of dispersion, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, the emptiness of dispersion is pure.

Why is this? Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path (mārgākārajñatā) and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā), or the purity of the emptiness of dispersion (vidaraśūnyatā), these are non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
Because there is no distinction and no interruption. "Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all dhāraṇī gateways are pure; because all dhāraṇī gateways are pure, the emptiness of dispersion is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all dharani-doors, and the purity of the emptiness of dispersion are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure; because all doors of samādhi are pure, the emptiness of dispersion is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all gateways of samādhi, and the purity of the emptiness of dispersion are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, the emptiness of scattering is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, and the purity of the emptiness of dispersion are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the fruit of arhatship are pure; because the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the fruit of arhatship are pure, the emptiness of scattering is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the fruit of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship, and the purity of the emptiness of scattering are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, the emptiness of dispersion is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of the emptiness of dispersion are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure, the emptiness of dispersion is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of the emptiness of scattering (vichitra-śūnyatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, the emptiness of scattering is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, and the purity of the emptiness of scattering are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll Two Hundred and Fifty-Two. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter Thirty-Four, "Difficult to Believe and Understand," Number Seventy-Two. "Furthermore, Subhūti!..."
Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, form (rūpa) is pure; because form is pure, the emptiness of non-alteration is pure. Why is this?

Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of form, or the purity of the emptiness of non-alteration, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the emptiness of non-alteration is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, as well as the purity of the emptiness of non-alteration, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sense base of the eye is pure; because the sense base of the eye is pure, the emptiness of non-alteration is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sense-base of the eye is pure, and if the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, this is because they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the emptiness of non-alteration is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed. This is because they are the purity of unchanging emptiness.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the emptiness of non-alteration is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sphere of form is pure, and if the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, it is because they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure, the emptiness of non-alteration is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience, the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, and the purity of unchanging emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the emptiness of non-alteration is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eye-element, or the purity of unchanging emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the form realm (rūpadhātu), the eye-consciousness realm (cakṣurvijñānadhātu), eye-contact (cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa), and the various feelings (vedanā) produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure; because the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, the emptiness of non-alteration (ananyathā-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of everything from the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, and the purity of unchanging emptiness, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the emptiness of non-alteration is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the ear-element is pure, and if the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, it is because they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of auditory consciousness, and auditory contact, as well as the various sensations produced with auditory contact as a condition, are pure; because the sphere of sound up to the various sensations produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure, the emptiness of non-alteration is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the sphere of sound (*śabdadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate, because they are the purity of unchanging emptiness (*avikāra-śūnyatā*).
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the nose element is pure; because the nose element is pure, the emptiness of non-alteration is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the nose element is pure, and if the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*) is pure, the fragrance element (*gandhadhātu*), the nose-consciousness element (*ghrāṇavijñānadhātu*), nose-contact (*ghrāṇasparśa*), and the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the emptiness of non-alteration (*ananyathā-śūnyatā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the realm of fragrance up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate. This is because they are both non-altering emptiness and pure.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the emptiness of non-alteration is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the tongue element is pure, and if the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, this is because they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the emptiness of non-alteration (ananyathā-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) and the purity of the various feelings arising with the gustatory element and up to tongue-contact as conditions are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted, being identical with the purity of unchanging emptiness (*avikāra-śūnyatā*).
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, the emptiness of non-alteration is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the body element is pure, and if the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, this is because they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the emptiness of non-alteration (ananyathā-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the various feelings produced with the body as the basis for contact, up to the sphere of tangibles, and the purity of the emptiness of non-alteration, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the intentionality of the knowledge of all modes is pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the emptiness of non-alteration is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the mental element is pure, and if the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, this is because they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are pure; because the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are pure, the emptiness of non-alteration is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition, and the purity of unchanging emptiness, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the emptiness of non-alteration is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the earth element is pure, and if the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, this is because they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the emptiness of non-alteration is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, or the purity of unchanging space, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the emptiness of non-alteration is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the purity of luminosity is pure, and if the purity of the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, because they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, volitional formations (saṃskāra), consciousness (vijñāna), name-and-form (nāmarūpa), the six sense bases (ṣaḍāyatana), contact (sparśa), feeling (vedanā), craving (tṛṣṇā), grasping (upādāna), becoming (bhava), birth (jāti), and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair (jarāmaraṇa-śoka-parideva-duḥkha-daurmanasyopāyāsa) are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the emptiness of non-alteration (avikāra-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate, due to the purity of the emptiness of non-alteration.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of giving is pure; because the perfection of giving is pure, the emptiness of non-alteration is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the perfection of giving, and the purity of the emptiness of non-alteration are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, the emptiness of non-alteration (ananyathā-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom, and the purity of the emptiness of non-alteration are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the emptiness of non-alteration is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if internal emptiness is pure, and if the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, this is because they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure; because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure, the emptiness of non-alteration is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, or the purity of the unchanging emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the emptiness of non-alteration is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of suchness, or the purity of the emptiness of non-alteration, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*) is pure, the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), non-falsity (*avitathatā*), non-alteration (*ananyathābhāva*), sameness (*samatā*), the state beyond birth (*anirodhatā*), the fixedness of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*) are pure; because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the emptiness of non-alteration (*ananyathā-śūnyatā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, or the purity of unchanging emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure; because the noble truth of suffering is pure, the emptiness of non-alteration is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the noble truth of suffering, and the purity of unchanging emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are pure, the emptiness of non-alteration (avikāra-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path, and the purity of unchanging emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the emptiness of non-alteration is pure.”
Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four dhyānas, and the purity of unchanging emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, the emptiness of non-alteration is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the four immeasurables (catur-apramāṇa), the four formless attainments (catasra ārūpya-samāpattayaḥ), and the purity of the emptiness of non-alteration (avikāra-śūnyatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the emptiness of non-alteration is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eight liberations, and the purity of unchanging emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the eight bases of mastery (abhibhvāyatana), the nine successive attainments (anupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (kṛtsnāyatana) are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the emptiness of non-alteration (ananyathā-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the eight bases of mastery (aṣṭau vimokṣāḥ), the nine successive attainments (navānupūrvavihārasamāpattayaḥ), and the ten pervasive bases (daśakṛtsnāyatanāni), as well as the purity of the emptiness of non-alteration (ananyathā-śūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure; because the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, the emptiness of non-alteration is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness (smṛtyupasthāna), and the purity of unchanging emptiness (avikāra-śūnyatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, the emptiness of non-alteration (ananyathā-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because if the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, and if the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the emptiness of non-alteration is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, and the purity of unchanging emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the gates of liberation—signlessness (animitta) and wishlessness (apraṇihita)—are pure; because the gates of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are pure, the emptiness of non-alteration (ananyathā-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, and the purity of the emptiness of non-alteration are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the emptiness of non-alteration is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, and the purity of unchanging emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the emptiness of non-alteration is pure. Why is that?

Whether it be the purification of the knowledge of all modes, the purification of the five eyes, or the purification of the emptiness of non-alteration, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the six supernormal powers are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, the emptiness of non-alteration is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the six supernormal powers, or the purity of unchanging emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, the emptiness of non-alteration is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, and the purity of unchanging emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, the emptiness of non-alteration is pure.

Why is this? Because if the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha are pure, and if the emptiness of non-alteration is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the emptiness of non-alteration is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the state of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of the emptiness of non-alteration are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the state of constant equanimity (upekṣā) is pure; because the state of constant equanimity is pure, the emptiness of non-alteration (ananyathā-śūnyatā) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the state of constant equanimity, or the purity of unchanging emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the knowledge of all things is pure; because the knowledge of all things is pure, the emptiness of non-alteration is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all-knowledge, or the purity of the emptiness of non-alteration, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, the emptiness of non-alteration is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, and the purity of the emptiness of non-alteration are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all dhāraṇī gateways are pure; because all dhāraṇī gateways are pure, the emptiness of non-alteration is pure."

Why is this? Because the purification of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purification of all dharani-doors, and the purification of the emptiness of non-alteration are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure; because all doors of samādhi are pure, the emptiness of non-alteration is pure.

Why is this? Because the purification of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purification of all doors of samādhi, and the purification of unchanging emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, the emptiness of non-alteration is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, and the purity of unchanging emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship is pure; because the fruit of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship is pure, the emptiness of non-alteration is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship, and the purity of unchanging emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, the emptiness of non-alteration is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of the emptiness of non-alteration are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure, the emptiness of non-alteration is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of unchanging emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the unexcelled, perfect enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unexcelled, perfect enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, the emptiness of non-alteration is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, and the purity of the unchanging emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the emptiness of intrinsic nature is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if form is pure, and if the purity of intrinsic emptiness are [identical], they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the emptiness of intrinsic nature is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, and the purity of intrinsic emptiness (prakṛtiśūnyatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sense base of the eye is pure; because the sense base of the eye is pure, intrinsic emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sense-sphere of the eye is pure, and if intrinsic emptiness is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, intrinsic emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, and the purity of intrinsic emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, intrinsic emptiness is pure. Why is that?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is such, and the purity of the sphere of form is such, and the purity of intrinsic emptiness is such, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena are pure, intrinsic emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena (dharmāyatana), as well as the purity of intrinsic emptiness (prakṛtiśūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, intrinsic nature emptiness is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eye-element, or the purity of intrinsic emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the form element, the eye-consciousness element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure; because the form element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, intrinsic emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the form realm (rūpadhātu) up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, and the purity of intrinsic emptiness (prakṛtiśūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, intrinsic emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the ear-element is pure, and if intrinsic emptiness is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of ear-consciousness, auditory contact, and all feelings produced with auditory contact as condition are pure; because the sphere of sound up to all feelings produced with auditory contact as condition are pure, intrinsic emptiness (prakṛti-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience, the purity of the realm of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, and the purity of intrinsic emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the nose element is pure; because the nose element is pure, intrinsic nature emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the nose element, and the purity of intrinsic emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, intrinsic emptiness (prakṛti-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the realm of fragrance (*gandhadhātu*) up to the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition are non-dual; they are not two, not divided, not distinct, and not separate, for they are the purity of intrinsic emptiness (*prakṛtiśūnyatā*).
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, intrinsic emptiness is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the tongue-element, or the purity of essential emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, intrinsic nature emptiness (prakṛtiśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of the taste element (*rasadhātu*) up to the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and the purity of intrinsic emptiness (*prakṛtiśūnyatā*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body element (*kāyadhātu*) is pure; because the body element is pure, intrinsic emptiness (*prakṛtiśūnyatā*) is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the body element, and the purity of essential emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, intrinsic emptiness (prakṛtiśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purification of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purification of the sphere of tangibles up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, and the purification of intrinsic emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the intention for the purity of the knowledge of all modes is pure, the mind-element (*manodhātu*) is pure; because the mind-element is pure, intrinsic emptiness (*prakṛtiśūnyatā*) is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the mind-element is pure, and if intrinsic emptiness is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, and mind-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition, are pure; because the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition are pure, intrinsic emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, and the purity of intrinsic emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, intrinsic emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the earth element, and the purity of intrinsic emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, intrinsic emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, or the purity of intrinsic emptiness (prakṛtiśūnyatā), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the emptiness of intrinsic nature is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the light of wisdom, or the purity of essential emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*) is pure, volitional formations (*saṃskāra*), consciousness (*vijñāna*), name-and-form (*nāmarūpa*), the six sense bases (*ṣaḍāyatana*), contact (*sparśa*), feeling (*vedanā*), craving (*tṛṣṇā*), grasping (*upādāna*), becoming (*bhava*), birth (*jāti*), and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair (*jarāmaraṇa-śoka-parideva-duḥkha-daurmanasyopāyāsa*) are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are pure, intrinsic emptiness (*prakṛtiśūnyatā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of everything from formative activities up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, and the purity of intrinsic emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, intrinsic emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the perfection of generosity, and the purity of intrinsic emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, intrinsic emptiness (prakṛtiśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom, and the purity of intrinsic emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, essential nature emptiness is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if internal emptiness is pure, and if essential nature emptiness is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature are pure. Because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature are pure, fundamental nature emptiness (prakṛtiśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence (abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā), as well as the purity of intrinsic emptiness (prakṛtiśūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the emptiness of intrinsic nature is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of suchness, or the purity of intrinsic emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the dharma-nature (dharmatā), the non-falsity (avitathatā), the non-alteration (ananyathābhāva), equality (samatā), the state beyond birth (anabhibhūtatā), the fixed nature of dharmas (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of dharmas (dharmasthititā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu) are pure. Because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, intrinsic emptiness (prakṛtiśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, and the purity of essential emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure; because the noble truth of suffering is pure, intrinsic emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the noble truth of suffering is pure, and if intrinsic emptiness is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are pure, intrinsic emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, and the purity of intrinsic emptiness (prakṛtiśūnyatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, intrinsic emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four dhyānas, and the purity of intrinsic emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, intrinsic nature emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, and the purity of intrinsic emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, intrinsic nature emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eight liberations, and the purity of intrinsic emptiness are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the eight bases of mastery (abhibhvāyatana), the nine successive attainments (anupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (kṛtsnāyatana) are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, intrinsic nature emptiness (prakṛtiśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases, as well as the purity of intrinsic emptiness, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four applications of mindfulness are pure; because the four applications of mindfulness are pure, intrinsic emptiness is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, and if intrinsic emptiness is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, intrinsic emptiness (prakṛtiśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, and the purity of intrinsic emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the door of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the door of liberation that is emptiness is pure, intrinsic nature emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness (śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha), and the purity of essential emptiness (prakṛti-śūnyatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure; because the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure, intrinsic nature emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, or the purity of essential emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, intrinsic emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, and the purity of intrinsic emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, intrinsic emptiness is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the five eyes, or the purity of intrinsic emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the six supernormal knowledges (ṣaḍabhijñā) are pure; because the six supernormal knowledges are pure, essential emptiness (prakṛtiśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the six supernormal knowledges, or the purity of essential emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, intrinsic emptiness is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, and if intrinsic emptiness is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, intrinsic nature emptiness (prakṛtiśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and the purity of intrinsic emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, essential emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of intrinsic emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the state of constant equanimity is pure; because the state of constant equanimity is pure, essential emptiness is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is such, and the purity of the state of constant equanimity is such, and the purity of the emptiness of intrinsic nature is such, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all-knowledge is pure; because all-knowledge is pure, the emptiness of intrinsic nature is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all-knowledge, or the purity of intrinsic emptiness, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, intrinsic nature emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects, and the purity of intrinsic emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all dhāraṇī-doors are pure; because all dhāraṇī-doors are pure, intrinsic nature emptiness is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience, the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors, and the purity of intrinsic emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure; because all doors of samādhi are pure, intrinsic nature emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all doors of samādhi, and the purity of intrinsic emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, intrinsic emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, and the purity of intrinsic emptiness are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the fruit of arhatship are pure; because the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the fruit of arhatship are pure, intrinsic nature emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship, and the purity of intrinsic emptiness (prakṛtiśūnyatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, intrinsic emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of intrinsic emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure, the emptiness of intrinsic nature is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of intrinsic emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, intrinsic emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi) of the Buddhas, and the purity of essential emptiness (prakṛti-śūnyatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, and the purity of emptiness of intrinsic characteristics are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sense base of the eye is pure; because the sense base of the eye is pure, emptiness of intrinsic characteristics is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the sense base of the eye, or the purity of emptiness of intrinsic characteristics, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the emptiness of self-characteristics is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, as well as the purity of emptiness of intrinsic characteristics, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, self-characteristic emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sphere of form is pure, and if the emptiness of self-characteristics is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena are pure; because the bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena are pure, the emptiness of intrinsic characteristics is pure.
