Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the emptiness of common characteristics (sāmānyalakṣaṇaśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the emptiness of common characteristics (sāmānyalakṣaṇaśūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, the emptiness of common characteristics is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the body element is pure, and if the emptiness of common characteristics is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the emptiness of common characteristics (sāmānyalakṣaṇaśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the various feelings arising with the body as the condition, from the element of tangibles up to [the element of] contact, and the purity of the emptiness of common characteristics (sāmānyalakṣaṇaśūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the intentionality of the knowledge of all modes is pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the emptiness of common characteristics is pure. Why is that?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the mind-element is pure, and if the emptiness of common characteristics is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, as well as mental contact and the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition, are pure; because the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition are pure, the emptiness of common characteristics (sāmānyalakṣaṇaśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu) up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the emptiness of common characteristics (sāmānyalakṣaṇaśūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the emptiness of common characteristics is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the earth element is pure, and if the emptiness of common characteristics is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the emptiness of common characteristics (sādhāraṇalakṣaṇaśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, as well as the purity of the emptiness of common characteristics, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the emptiness of common characteristics is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the light of non-arising, or the purity of the emptiness of common characteristics, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct from one another, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, volitional formations (saṃskāra), consciousness (vijñāna), name-and-form (nāmarūpa), the six sense bases (ṣaḍāyatana), contact (sparśa), feeling (vedanā), craving (tṛṣṇā), grasping (upādāna), becoming (bhava), birth (jāti), and old age, death, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, death, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are pure, mutual emptiness (itaretara-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of everything from conditioned activities up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, as well as the purity of mutual emptiness, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, the emptiness of common characteristics is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the perfection of generosity, and the purity of the emptiness of common characteristics are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, the emptiness of common characteristics (sāmānyalakṣaṇaśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom, and the purity of the emptiness of common characteristics are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the emptiness of common characteristics is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of internal emptiness, or the purity of the emptiness of common characteristics, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure; because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure, the emptiness of common characteristics is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, as well as the purity of the emptiness of common characteristics, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the emptiness of common characteristics is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if suchness is pure, and if the emptiness of common characteristics is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, the state of equality, the nature free from birth, the fixedness of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the stability of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm are pure. Because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the emptiness of common characteristics (sāmānyalakṣaṇaśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, and the purity of the emptiness of common characteristics are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure; because the noble truth of suffering is pure, the emptiness of common characteristics is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the noble truth of suffering is pure, and if the emptiness of common characteristics is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure, the emptiness of common characteristics is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, and the purity of the emptiness of common characteristics (sāmānyalakṣaṇaśūnyatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the emptiness of common characteristics is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four dhyānas, and the purity of the emptiness of common characteristics are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, the emptiness of common characteristics is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, and the purity of the emptiness of common characteristics are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the emptiness of common characteristics is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eight liberations, and the purity of the emptiness of common characteristics are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the eight bases of mastery (aṣṭau abhibhvāyatanāni), the nine successive attainments (navānupūrvavihārasamāpattayaḥ), and the ten totalities (daśa kṛtsnāyatanāni) are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the emptiness of common characteristics (sāmanyalakṣaṇaśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the eight bases of mastery (aṣṭāv abhibhvāyatanāni), the nine successive attainments (navānupūrvavihārasamāpattayaḥ), and the ten pervasive bases (daśa kṛtsnāyatanāni), as well as the purity of the emptiness of common characteristics (sāmānyalakṣaṇaśūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four applications of mindfulness are pure; because the four applications of mindfulness are pure, the emptiness of common characteristics is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, and if the emptiness of common characteristics is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, the emptiness of common characteristics is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, and the purity of the emptiness of common characteristics are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the emptiness of common characteristics is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, and the purity of the emptiness of common characteristics are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the gates of liberation—signlessness (animitta) and wishlessness (apraṇihita)—are pure; because the gates of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are pure, the emptiness of common characteristics (sāmānyalakṣaṇaśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, or the purity of the emptiness of common characteristics, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the emptiness of common characteristics is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, or the purity of the emptiness of common characteristics, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the emptiness of common characteristics is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purification of the knowledge of all modes, the purification of the five eyes, or the purification of the emptiness of common characteristics, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the six supernormal powers (ṣaḍabhijñā) are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, the emptiness of common characteristics (sādhāraṇalakṣaṇaśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the six supernormal powers, or the purity of the emptiness of common characteristics, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, the emptiness of common characteristics is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, and if the emptiness of common characteristics is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the four fearlessnesses (vaiśāradya), the four analytical knowledges (pratisaṃvid), great loving-kindness (maitrī), great compassion (karuṇā), great sympathetic joy (muditā), great equanimity (upekṣā), and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (āveṇikabuddhadharma) are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, the emptiness of common characteristics (sādhāraṇalakṣaṇa-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, as well as the purity of the emptiness of common characteristics, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the emptiness of specific characteristics is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of the emptiness of common characteristics are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the wisdom of all-knowledge is pure, the state of constant abiding in equanimity is pure; because the state of constant abiding in equanimity is pure, the emptiness of common characteristics is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the state of constant equanimity, and the purity of the emptiness of common characteristics are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the knowledge of all things is pure; because the knowledge of all things is pure, the emptiness of common characteristics is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all-knowledge, or the purity of the emptiness of common characteristics, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, the emptiness of common characteristics is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects, and the purity of the emptiness of common characteristics are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all dhāraṇī gateways are pure; because all dhāraṇī gateways are pure, the emptiness of common characteristics is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all dharani-doors, and the purity of the emptiness of common characteristics are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure; because all doors of samādhi are pure, the emptiness of common characteristics is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all doors of samādhi, and the purity of the emptiness of common characteristics are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, the emptiness of common characteristics is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the fruit of stream-entry is pure, and if the emptiness of common characteristics is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the fruit of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship is pure; because the fruit of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship is pure, the emptiness of common characteristics (sādhāraṇalakṣaṇaśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship, and the purity of the emptiness of common characteristics are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, the emptiness of common characteristics is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of the emptiness of common characteristics are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure, the emptiness of mutual characteristics is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of mutual emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, the emptiness of common characteristics is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, and the purity of the emptiness of common characteristics are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the emptiness of all phenomena is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if form is pure, and if the emptiness of all phenomena is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the emptiness of all phenomena (sarvadharma-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, and the purity of the emptiness of all phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sense-sphere of the eye is pure; because the sense-sphere of the eye is pure, the emptiness of all phenomena is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purification of the knowledge of all modes of knowing, the purification of the sense-base of the eye, or the purification of the emptiness of all phenomena, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the emptiness of all phenomena is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the sense bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, and the purity of the emptiness of all phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the emptiness of all phenomena is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sphere of form is pure, and if the emptiness of all phenomena is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure, the emptiness of all phenomena is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental objects (dharmāyatana), as well as the purity of the emptiness of all phenomena (sarvadharma-śūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the emptiness of all phenomena is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eye-element, or the purity of the emptiness of all phenomena, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the form element (rūpadhātu), the eye-consciousness element (cakṣurvijñānadhātu), eye-contact (cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa), and the various feelings (vedanā) produced with eye-contact as condition are pure. Because the form element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition are pure, the emptiness of all phenomena (sarvadharma-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) and the purity of everything from the form realm (*rūpadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the emptiness of all phenomena (*sarvadharma-śūnyatā*), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the emptiness of all phenomena is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purification of the knowledge of all modes, the purification of the ear-element, or the purification of the emptiness of all phenomena, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of auditory consciousness, auditory contact, and the various feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure, the emptiness of all phenomena (*sarvadharma-śūnyatā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowing and the purity of everything from the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the emptiness of all phenomena, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
