Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the nose-element (ghrāṇadhātu) is pure; because the nose-element is pure, the emptiness of all phenomena (sarvadharmaśūnyatā) is pure. Why is this?

Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the nose-element, or the purity of the emptiness of all phenomena, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the emptiness of all phenomena is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of the realm of fragrance (*gandhadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, and the purity of the emptiness of all phenomena (*sarvadharmaśūnyatā*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the emptiness of all phenomena is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purification of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purification of the tongue element, or the purification of the emptiness of all phenomena, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to the various sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the emptiness of all phenomena (sarvadharma-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of the taste element (*rasadhātu*) up to the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and the purity of the emptiness (*śūnyatā*) of all phenomena (*sarvadharma*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body-element is pure; because the body-element is pure, the emptiness of all phenomena is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the realm of the body is pure, and if the emptiness of all phenomena is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the emptiness of all phenomena (sarvadharma-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) and the purity of the various sensations arising with the body as the basis for contact, up to the realm of touch, and the purity of the emptiness of all phenomena (*sarvadharma-śūnyatā*), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the intention for the purity of the knowledge of all modes is pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the emptiness of all phenomena is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the mental constituent, or the purity of the emptiness of all phenomena, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the dharma-element, the mental consciousness-element, mental contact, and the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are pure; because the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are pure, the emptiness of all phenomena is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) and the purity of everything from the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the emptiness of all phenomena (*sarvadharma-śūnyatā*), are non-dual, without division, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the emptiness of all phenomena is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the earth element, or the purity of the emptiness of all phenomena, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the emptiness of all phenomena is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, or the purity of the emptiness of all phenomena, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the emptiness of all phenomena is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of non-duality, or the purity of the emptiness of all phenomena, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, formations (saṃskāra), consciousness (vijñāna), name-and-form (nāmarūpa), the six sense bases (ṣaḍāyatana), contact (sparśa), sensation (vedanā), craving (tṛṣṇā), grasping (upādāna), becoming (bhava), birth (jāti), and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair (jarāmaraṇa-śoka-parideva-duḥkha-daurmanasyopāyāsa) are pure; because formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, all phenomena (sarvadharma) are pure by way of emptiness (śūnyatā).

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of everything from formative activities up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate, for all phenomena are pure in their emptiness.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, the emptiness of all phenomena is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the perfection of giving, and the purity of the emptiness of all phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñājñāna*) is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, the emptiness of all phenomena (*sarvadharma-śūnyatā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom, and the purity of the emptiness of all phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the emptiness of all phenomena is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of internal emptiness, or the purity of the emptiness of all phenomena, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, emptiness of limits, emptiness of dispersion, emptiness of non-alteration, emptiness of intrinsic nature, emptiness of self-characteristic, emptiness of common characteristic, emptiness of non-apprehensibility, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, and emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure; because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure, the emptiness of all phenomena (*sarvadharmaśūnyatā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, and the purity of the emptiness of all phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the emptiness of all phenomena is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of suchness, and the purity of the emptiness of all phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), the non-falsity of phenomena (avitathatā), the unchanging nature of phenomena (ananyathābhāvatā), equality (samatā), the state beyond birth (anirodhatā), the fixedness of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu) are pure. Because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the emptiness of all phenomena (sarvadharma-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) up to the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*), and the purity of the emptiness of all phenomena (*sarvadharma-śūnyatā*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure; because the noble truth of suffering is pure, the emptiness of all phenomena is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the noble truth of suffering, and the purity of the emptiness of all phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure, the emptiness of all phenomena (sarvadharma-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, and the purity of the emptiness of all phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the emptiness of all phenomena is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four dhyānas, and the purity of the emptiness of all phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, the four immeasurables (*apramāṇa*) and the four formless attainments (*ārūpyasamāpatti*) are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are pure, the emptiness of all phenomena (*sarvadharmaśūnyatā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, and the purity of the emptiness of all phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the emptiness of all phenomena is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the eight liberations, and the purity of the emptiness of all phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñājñāna*) is pure, the eight bases of mastery (*abhibhvāyatana*), the nine successive attainments (*anupūrvavihārasamāpatti*), and the ten totalities (*kṛtsnāyatana*) are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the emptiness of all phenomena (*sarvadharmaśūnyatā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases, and the purity of the emptiness of all phenomena, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure; because the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, the emptiness of all phenomena is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowing, the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, and the purity of the emptiness of all phenomena are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, the emptiness of all phenomena is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, and the purity of the emptiness of all phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the door of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the door of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the emptiness of all phenomena is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, and the purity of the emptiness of all phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure; because the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure, the emptiness of all phenomena (sarvadharma-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowing, the purity of the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—and the purity of the emptiness of all phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the emptiness of all phenomena is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, and the purity of the emptiness of all phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the emptiness of all phenomena is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the five eyes, or the purity of the emptiness of all phenomena, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the wisdom of all-knowledge is pure, the six supernormal powers are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, the emptiness of all phenomena is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purification of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience, the purification of the six supernormal powers, or the purification of the emptiness of all phenomena, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, the emptiness of all phenomena is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, and the purity of the emptiness of all phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, the emptiness of all phenomena (sarvadharma-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and the purity of the emptiness of all phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the emptiness of all phenomena is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of the emptiness of all phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the state of constant abiding in equanimity is pure; because the state of constant abiding in equanimity is pure, the emptiness of all phenomena is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the state of constant equanimity, or the purity of the emptiness of all phenomena, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the knowledge of all things is pure; because the knowledge of all things is pure, the emptiness of all phenomena is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all-knowledge, and the purity of the emptiness of all phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, the emptiness of all phenomena is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects, and the purity of the emptiness of all phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all dhāraṇī-doors are pure; because all dhāraṇī-doors are pure, the emptiness of all phenomena is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all dharani-doors, and the purity of the emptiness of all phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure; because all doors of samādhi are pure, the emptiness of all phenomena is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all gateways of samādhi, and the purity of the emptiness of all phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, the emptiness of all phenomena is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, and the purity of the emptiness of all phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the fruits of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat are pure; because the fruits of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat are pure, the emptiness of all phenomena (sarvadharma-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship, and the purity of the emptiness of all phenomena (sarvadharma-śūnyatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, the emptiness of all phenomena is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of the emptiness of all phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure, the emptiness of all phenomena is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of the emptiness of all phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, the emptiness of all phenomena is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, and the purity of the emptiness of all phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the emptiness of non-apprehension is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if form is pure, and if the emptiness of non-apprehensibility is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility (anupalambha-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, as well as the purity of the emptiness of non-apprehensibility (anupalambhaśūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sense base of the eye is pure; because the sense base of the eye is pure, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sense base of the eye is pure, and if the emptiness of non-apprehensibility is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the sense bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, and the purity of the emptiness of non-apprehensibility (anupalambha-śūnyatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the emptiness of non-apprehension is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the sphere of form, and the purity of the emptiness of non-apprehensibility are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena (śabda-, gandha-, rasa-, spraṣṭavya-, and dharmāyatana) are pure; because the bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility (anupalambha-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental objects (dharmāyatana), as well as the purity of the emptiness of the unapprehendable (anupalambhaśūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-faculty is pure; because the eye-faculty is pure, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eye-element, or the purity of the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the form element, the eye-consciousness element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure; because the form element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of everything from the form realm (rūpadhātu) up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, and the purity of the emptiness of non-apprehensibility (anupalambha-śūnyatā) are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the ear-element is pure, and if the emptiness of non-apprehensibility is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of auditory consciousness, auditory contact, and the various feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility (anupalambha-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the sphere of sound (*śabdadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are without distinction, and they are not separate. Thus, the purity of the emptiness of the unapprehendable (*anupalambha-śūnyatā*) is [identical to them].
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the nose element is pure; because the nose element is pure, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the sphere of the nose, and the purity of the emptiness of non-apprehensibility are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility (anupalambha-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the realm of fragrance up to the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are without distinction, and they are not separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the tongue element, or the purity of the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to the various sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the emptiness of the unapprehendable (anupalambha-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and the purity of the emptiness of non-apprehensibility are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, the emptiness of non-apprehension is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the body-element is pure, and if the emptiness of non-apprehensibility is pure, this is because they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility (anupalambha-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the sense-sphere of tangibles up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, and the purity of the emptiness of non-apprehensibility are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the intentionality of the knowledge of all modes is pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the mind-element is pure, and if the emptiness of non-apprehensibility is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, mental contact, and the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition are pure; because the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition are pure, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility (anupalambha-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of everything from the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, and the purity of the emptiness of the unapprehendable, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the emptiness of non-apprehension is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the earth element, it is the purity of the emptiness of non-apprehensibility; for they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, as well as the purity of the emptiness of the unapprehendable (anupalambhaśūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of non-duality, or the purity of the emptiness of the unapprehendable, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, volitional formations (saṃskāra), consciousness (vijñāna), name-and-form (nāmarūpa), the six sense bases (ṣaḍāyatana), contact (sparśa), feeling (vedanā), craving (tṛṣṇā), clinging (upādāna), becoming (bhava), birth (jāti), and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair (jarāmaraṇa-śoka-parideva-duḥkha-daurmanasyopāyāsa) are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility (anupalambha-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of everything from formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed. This is because of the purity of the emptiness of the unapprehendable.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, the emptiness of non-apprehension is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the perfection of generosity (dānapāramitā), and the purity of the emptiness of the non-apprehendable (anupalambhaśūnyatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility (anupalambha-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom, and the purity of the emptiness of the unapprehendable are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the emptiness of the unapprehendable is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if internal emptiness is pure, and if the emptiness of the unapprehendable is pure, it is because they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the emptiness of the external, the emptiness of the internal and external, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate, the emptiness of the conditioned, the emptiness of the unconditioned, absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self-characteristic, the emptiness of common characteristic, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure. Because the emptiness of the external up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility (anupalambha-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of external emptiness up to the purity of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, or the purity of the emptiness of the unapprehendable, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the emptiness of non-apprehension is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of suchness, or the purity of the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the stability of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm are pure. Because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the emptiness of the unapprehendable (anupalambhaśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, and the purity of the emptiness of the unapprehendable are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure; because the noble truth of suffering is pure, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the noble truth of suffering, and the purity of the emptiness of non-apprehensibility are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure, the emptiness of non-apprehension is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path, and the purity of the emptiness of non-apprehensibility are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the four dhyānas, and the purity of the emptiness of the unapprehendable (anupalambhaśūnyatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are pure, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, and the purity of the emptiness of the unapprehendable are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the emptiness of non-apprehension is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the eight liberations, and the purity of the emptiness of non-apprehensibility are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the eight spheres of mastery (abhibhvāyatana), the nine successive attainments (anupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (kṛtsnāyatana) are pure; because the eight spheres of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility (anupalambhaśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases, as well as the purity of the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four applications of mindfulness are pure; because the four applications of mindfulness are pure, the emptiness of non-apprehension is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, and the purity of the emptiness of non-apprehensibility are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path are pure, the emptiness of non-apprehension is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, and the purity of the emptiness of the unapprehendable are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the door of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the door of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the emptiness of the unapprehendable is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, and the purity of the emptiness of the unapprehendable are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the gates of liberation of signlessness (animitta) and wishlessness (apraṇihita) are pure; because the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure, the emptiness of the unapprehendable (anupalambhaśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, and the purity of the emptiness of the unapprehendable are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, and the purity of the emptiness of non-apprehensibility are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the emptiness of non-apprehension is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the five eyes, or the purity of the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, the six supernormal powers (*ṣaḍabhijñā*) are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility (*anupalambhaśūnyatā*) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the six superknowledges, or the purity of the emptiness of non-apprehension, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten powers of a buddha are pure; because the ten powers of a buddha are pure, the emptiness of non-apprehension is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, and the purity of the emptiness of non-apprehensibility are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, the emptiness of the unapprehendable (anupalambha-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and the purity of the emptiness of the unapprehendable are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of the emptiness of the unapprehendable are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the state of constant equanimity (upekṣā) is pure; because the state of constant equanimity is pure, the emptiness of the unapprehendable (anupalambha-śūnyatā) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the state of constant equanimity, or the purity of the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the knowledge of all is pure; because the knowledge of all is pure, the emptiness of non-apprehension is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all-knowledge, and the purity of the emptiness of the unapprehendable are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, the emptiness of the unapprehendable is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects, and the purity of the emptiness of the unapprehendable, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all dhāraṇī-doors are pure; because all dhāraṇī-doors are pure, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all dharani-doors, and the purity of the emptiness of non-apprehensibility are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure; because all doors of samādhi are pure, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience, the purity of all doors of samādhi, and the purity of the emptiness of non-apprehensibility are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, the emptiness of non-apprehension is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, and the purity of the emptiness of non-apprehensibility are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the fruit of arhatship are pure; because the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the fruit of arhatship are pure, the emptiness of the unapprehendable is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship, and the purity of the emptiness of the unapprehendable (anupalambha-śūnyatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the enlightenment of a Pratyekabuddha, and the purity of the emptiness of non-apprehensibility are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure, the emptiness of non-apprehension is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience, the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of the emptiness of the unapprehendable are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the unexcelled, perfect enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unexcelled, perfect enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, the emptiness of non-apprehension is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, and the purity of the emptiness of non-apprehensibility are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the emptiness of non-existence is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if form is pure, and if the emptiness of non-existence is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not severed.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the emptiness of non-existence is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, and the purity of the emptiness of non-existence are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sense base of the eye is pure; because the sense base of the eye is pure, the emptiness of non-existence is pure. Why is that?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sense-base of the eye is pure, and if the emptiness of non-existence is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the emptiness of non-existence is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are not distinct, and they are not separate. This is because they are the purity of the emptiness of non-existence.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the emptiness of non-existence is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sphere of form is pure, and if the emptiness of non-existence is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure, the emptiness of non-existence is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena (dharmāyatana), as well as the purity of the emptiness of non-existence (abhāvaśūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the emptiness of non-existence is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eye-element, or the purity of the emptiness of non-existence, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the form realm (rūpadhātu), the eye-consciousness realm (cakṣurvijñānadhātu), eye-contact (cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa), and the various feelings (vedanā) produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure; because the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, the emptiness of non-existence (abhāvaśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of everything from the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, and the purity of the emptiness of non-existence, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the emptiness of non-existence is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ear-element, or the purity of the emptiness of non-existence, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of auditory consciousness, and ear-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, are pure; because the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure, the emptiness of non-existence (abhāva-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of the sphere of sound (*śabdadhātu*) up to the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with ear-contact as a condition, and the purity of the emptiness of non-existence (*abhāvaśūnyatā*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the nose element is pure; because the nose element is pure, the emptiness of non-existence is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the nose element is pure, and if the emptiness of non-existence is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*) is pure, the fragrance element (*gandhadhātu*), the nose-consciousness element (*ghrāṇavijñānadhātu*), nose-contact (*ghrāṇasparśa*), and the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the emptiness of non-existence (*abhāvaśūnyatā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the realm of fragrance up to the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition are non-dual; they are not two, they cannot be divided, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous. This is because they are the purity of the emptiness of non-existence (abhāva-śūnyatā).

Because the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, the tongue-element (*jihvādhātu*) is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the emptiness of non-existence (*abhāvaśūnyatā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the tongue-element, or the purity of the emptiness of non-existence, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the emptiness of non-existence (abhāva-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and the purity of the emptiness of non-existence, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, the emptiness of non-existence is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the body element is pure, and if the emptiness of non-existence is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the emptiness of non-existence (abhāva-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the various feelings arising with the body as the condition, from the element of tangibility up to [the feeling born of] body-contact, as well as the purity of the emptiness of non-existence, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the intentionality of the knowledge of all modes is pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the emptiness of non-existence is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the mind-element is pure, and if the emptiness of non-existence is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, mind-contact, and the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition are pure. Because the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition are pure, the emptiness of non-existence (abhāvaśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of everything from the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, and the purity of the emptiness of non-existence, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the emptiness of non-existence is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the earth element is pure, and if the emptiness of non-existence is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the emptiness of non-existence is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, or the purity of the emptiness of non-existence (*abhāvaśūnyatā*), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the emptiness of intrinsic nature is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the purity of luminosity is pure, and if the purity of the emptiness of intrinsic nature is pure, this is because they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, volitional formations (saṃskāra), consciousness (vijñāna), name-and-form (nāmarūpa), the six sense bases (ṣaḍāyatana), contact (sparśa), feeling (vedanā), craving (tṛṣṇā), grasping (upādāna), becoming (bhava), birth (jāti), and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the emptiness of non-existence (abhāva-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of everything from formative activities up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, and the purity of the emptiness of non-existence are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, the emptiness of non-existence is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the perfection of generosity, and the purity of the emptiness of non-existence are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, the emptiness of non-existence (abhāva-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom, and the purity of the emptiness of non-existence are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the emptiness of non-existence is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if internal emptiness is pure, and if the emptiness of non-existence is pure, this is because they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure. Because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure, the emptiness of non-existence is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature (abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā), as well as the purity of the emptiness of non-existence (abhāvaśūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the emptiness of non-existence is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of suchness, or the purity of the emptiness of non-existence, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the dharma-nature (dharmatā), the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, the state of equality, the nature free from birth, the fixedness of dharmas (dharmasthititā), the stability of dharmas (dharmaniyāmatā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu) are pure. Because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the emptiness of non-existence (abhāvaśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, or the purity of the emptiness of non-existence, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure; because the noble truth of suffering is pure, the emptiness of non-existence is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the noble truth of suffering is pure, and if the emptiness of non-existence is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are pure, the emptiness of non-existence is pure.

Why is this? Because if the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, and if the emptiness of non-existence is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the nose-element is pure; because the nose-element is pure, its emptiness of intrinsic nature is pure. Why is this?
