Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, and the purity of intrinsic emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the emptiness of intrinsic nature is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the five eyes, or the purity of intrinsic emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the six supernormal powers (ṣaḍabhijñā) are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, intrinsic emptiness (svabhāvaśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the six supernormal powers, or the purity of intrinsic emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, the emptiness of intrinsic nature is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, or the purity of intrinsic emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four fearlessnesses (vaiśāradya), the four analytical knowledges (pratisaṃvid), great loving-kindness (mahāmaitrī), great compassion (mahākaruṇā), great sympathetic joy (mahāmuditā), great equanimity (mahopekṣā), and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (āveṇika-buddhadharma) are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, intrinsic emptiness (svabhāva-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and the purity of intrinsic emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the emptiness of intrinsic nature is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the state of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of intrinsic emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the state of constant equanimity (upekṣā) is pure; because the state of constant equanimity is pure, intrinsic emptiness (svabhāvaśūnyatā) is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is so, and if the purity of the nature of constant equanimity is so, and if the purity of the emptiness of intrinsic nature is so, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not severed.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the knowledge of all things is pure; because the knowledge of all things is pure, self-nature emptiness is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purification of the knowledge of all modes, the purification of all-knowledge, or the purification of intrinsic emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, intrinsic emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects, and the purity of intrinsic emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all dharani-doors are pure; because all dharani-doors are pure, the emptiness of intrinsic nature is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all dharani-doors, and the purity of intrinsic emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure; because all doors of samādhi are pure, the emptiness of intrinsic nature is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all doors of samādhi, and the purity of intrinsic emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, intrinsic emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, and the purity of intrinsic emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not severed.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure; because the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure, the emptiness of intrinsic nature (svabhāva-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship, and the purity of intrinsic emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, the emptiness of intrinsic nature is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of intrinsic emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure, the emptiness of intrinsic nature is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of intrinsic emptiness (svabhāva-śūnyatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, the emptiness of intrinsic nature is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening of the Buddhas, and the purity of intrinsic emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of form, and the purity of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, and the purity of the emptiness of the absence of intrinsic nature (abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye base is pure; because the eye base is pure, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the sense base of the eye, or the purity of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience, the purity of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, and the purity of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sphere of form is pure, and if the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena (dharmāyatana), as well as the purity of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence (abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eye-element, or the purity of the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature—these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the form element, the eye-consciousness element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure; because the form element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, and the purity of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the ear element is pure, and if the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of auditory consciousness, ear-contact, and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence (abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, and the purity of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the nose-element (ghrāṇadhātu) is pure; because the nose-element is pure, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence (abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the nose-element, or the purity of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence (abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of the realm of fragrance up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, and the purity of the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature (*abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the tongue element, or the purity of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence (abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and the purity of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the body element is pure, and if the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the various feelings produced with the body as the basis and tangibles as the condition, up to the element of tangibles, and the purity of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

“Subhūti! Because the intention for the knowledge of all modes is pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the mind-element is pure, and if the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is pure, this is because they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are pure; because the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are pure, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence (abhāvasvabhāva-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) and the purity of everything from the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu) up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the emptiness of the nature of non-existence (abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the earth element is pure, and if the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence (abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, or the purity of the emptiness of intrinsic nature (*abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā*), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the light of non-arising, or the purity of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, volitional formations (saṃskāra), consciousness (vijñāna), name-and-form (nāmarūpa), the six sense bases (ṣaḍāyatana), contact (sparśa), feeling (vedanā), craving (tṛṣṇā), grasping (upādāna), becoming (bhava), birth (jāti), and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the emptiness of intrinsic nature (abhāvasvabhāva-śūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because if the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if everything from formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair is pure, and if the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of giving is pure; because the perfection of giving is pure, the emptiness of intrinsic nature in the absence of intrinsic nature is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the perfection of giving (dānapāramitā), and the purity of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence (abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, the emptiness of intrinsic nature (abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), and the purity of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence (abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of internal emptiness, or the purity of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature are pure; because external emptiness up to the emptiness of intrinsic nature are pure, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from external emptiness up to the emptiness of intrinsic nature, as well as the purity of the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of suchness, or the purity of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), non-falsity (avitathatā), unalterability (ananyathābhāva), sameness (samatā), the state beyond birth (anabhibhūtatā), the fixedness of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the stability of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu) are pure. Because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence (abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, and the purity of the emptiness of the nature of non-nature are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure; because the noble truth of suffering is pure, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the noble truth of suffering, and the purity of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence (abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, and the purity of the emptiness of the absence of intrinsic nature (abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four dhyānas, and the purity of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are non-dual, not divided into two, not distinct, and not discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the four immeasurables (apramāṇa) and the four formless attainments (ārūpyasamāpatti) are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are pure, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence (abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, and the purity of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eight liberations, and the purity of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the eight bases of mastery (abhibhvāyatana), the nine successive attainments (anupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (kṛtsnāyatana) are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence (abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) and the purity of the eight bases of mastery (*abhibhvāyatana*), the nine successive attainments (*anupūrvavihārasamāpatti*), and the ten universal bases (*kṛtsnāyatana*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate; they are the purity of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence (*abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā*).

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four applications of mindfulness are pure; because the four applications of mindfulness are pure, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, and the purity of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four right efforts (samyakprahāṇa), the four bases of power (ṛddhipāda), the five faculties (indriya), the five powers (bala), the seven factors of enlightenment (bodhyaṅga), and the eightfold noble path (āryāṣṭāṅgamārga) are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence (abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, and the purity of the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, and the purity of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are pure; because the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are pure, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-entities is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purification of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purification of the gateways of liberation—the signless and the wishless—or the purification of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten stages of a bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of a bodhisattva are pure, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, and the purity of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the five eyes, or the purity of the emptiness of intrinsic nature by way of non-existence, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the six supernormal powers (ṣaḍabhijñā) are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence (abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the six supernormal powers, or the purity of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, and the purity of the emptiness of intrinsic nature are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha are pure, the emptiness of intrinsic nature (abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and the purity of the emptiness of intrinsic nature are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is pure.”

Why is this? Because if the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, and if the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the state of constant equanimity (upekṣā) is pure; because the state of constant equanimity is pure, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence (abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā) is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, if the purity of the state of constant equanimity, and if the purity of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all-knowledge is pure; because all-knowledge is pure, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all-knowledge, and the purity of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the knowledge of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), and the purity of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence (*abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā*) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all dharani-doors are pure; because all dharani-doors are pure, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all dharani-doors, and the purity of the emptiness of the self-nature of non-existence are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure; because all doors of samādhi are pure, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all doors of samādhi, and the purity of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, and the purity of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure; because the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure, the emptiness of intrinsic nature (abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship, and the purity of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the awakening of the solitary buddhas is pure; because the awakening of the solitary buddhas is pure, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, and the purity of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, suchness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if form is pure, and if suchness is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, suchness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, and the purity of suchness (tathatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sense base of the eye is pure; because the sense base of the eye is pure, suchness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sense-sphere of the eye is pure, and if suchness is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sense bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the sense bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, suchness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowing and the purity of the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, as well as the purity of suchness, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, suchness is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the sense-base of form, and the purity of suchness, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure, suchness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, and the purity of suchness are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are distinct from nothing, and they are uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, suchness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the eye-element is pure, and if suchness is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the form realm (rūpadhātu), the eye-consciousness realm (cakṣurvijñānadhātu), eye-contact (cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa), and the various feelings (vedanā) produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure; because the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, suchness (tathatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the form realm (rūpadhātu) up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of suchness (tathatā), are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, suchness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the ear-element is pure, and if suchness is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of auditory consciousness, auditory contact, and the various feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure, suchness (tathatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the sphere of sound, up to and including the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, and the purity of suchness, are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the nose element is pure; because the nose element is pure, suchness is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the nose-element, and the purity of suchness, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, suchness (tathatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the realm of fragrance up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, and the purity of suchness, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, suchness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the tongue element is pure, and if suchness is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, suchness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the taste element up to the various sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and the purity of suchness (tathatā) are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body-element is pure; because the body-element is pure, suchness is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the body element, and the purity of suchness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, suchness (tathatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the various feelings produced with the body as the basis for contact, up to the element of tangibles, as well as the purity of suchness, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the intentionality of the knowledge of all modes is pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, suchness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the mind-element is pure, and if suchness is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the dharma-element, the mental consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are pure; because the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are pure, suchness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of everything from the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, as well as the purity of suchness, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, suchness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the earth element is pure, and if suchness is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not severed.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, suchness is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, or the purity of suchness (tathatā), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, suchness is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the outflows-free, or the purity of suchness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, formative forces (saṃskāra), consciousness (vijñāna), name-and-form (nāmarūpa), the six sense bases (ṣaḍāyatana), contact (sparśa), sensation (vedanā), craving (tṛṣṇā), grasping (upādāna), becoming (bhava), birth (jāti), and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair (jarāmaraṇa-śoka-parideva-duḥkha-daurmanasyopāyāsa) are pure; because formative forces through old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, suchness (tathatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of everything from formations through old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are non-dual; they are not two, not divided, not distinct, and not severed. This is because of the purity of suchness.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of giving is pure; because the perfection of giving is pure, suchness is pure.”
Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the perfection of generosity, and the purity of suchness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, suchness (tathatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), and the purity of suchness (tathatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, suchness is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of internal emptiness, or the purity of suchness, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure; because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure, suchness (tathatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of external emptiness up to the purity of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, and the purity of suchness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the dharma-realm is pure; because the dharma-realm is pure, suchness is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the dharma-realm, or the purity of suchness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of phenomena (dharmatā-sthiti), the stability of phenomena (dharma-sthiti), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu) are pure; because the nature of phenomena up to the inconceivable realm are pure, suchness (tathatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the nature of phenomena up to the inconceivable realm, or the purity of suchness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure; because the noble truth of suffering is pure, suchness is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the noble truth of suffering, and the purity of suchness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure, suchness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, and the purity of suchness (tathatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, suchness is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the four dhyānas, and the purity of suchness, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, suchness is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, or the purity of suchness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, suchness is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eight liberations, and the purity of suchness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the eight bases of mastery (abhibhvāyatana), the nine successive attainments (anupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (kṛtsnāyatana) are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, suchness (tathatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the eight bases of mastery (aṣṭāv abhibhvāyatanāni), the nine successive meditative attainments (navānupūrvavihārasamāpattayaḥ), and the ten pervasive bases (daśa kṛtsnāyatanāni), as well as the purity of suchness (tathatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four applications of mindfulness are pure; because the four applications of mindfulness are pure, suchness is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, and the purity of suchness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, suchness (tathatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, and the purity of suchness (tathatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, suchness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, and the purity of suchness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes of omniscience is pure, the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are pure; because the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are pure, suchness is pure.

Why is this? Because if the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure, and if suchness is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, suchness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, and the purity of suchness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, suchness is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the five eyes, or the purity of suchness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the six supernormal powers (ṣaḍabhijñā) are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, suchness (tathatā) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the six supernormal powers, or the purity of suchness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, suchness is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, or the purity of suchness, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, the four fearlessnesses (*vaiśāradya*), the four analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*), great loving-kindness (*mahāmaitrī*), great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*), great sympathetic joy (*mahāmuditā*), great equanimity (*mahopekṣā*), and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇikabuddhadharma*) are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, suchness (*tathatā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and the purity of suchness (tathatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, suchness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of suchness are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, the state of constant abiding in equanimity is pure; because the state of constant abiding in equanimity is pure, suchness is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the nature of constant equanimity, and if it is the purity of suchness, because they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all-knowledge is pure; because all-knowledge is pure, suchness is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all-knowledge, or the purity of suchness, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, suchness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects, and the purity of suchness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all dharanī-doors are pure; because all dharanī-doors are pure, suchness is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all dharani-doors, and the purity of suchness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure; because all doors of samādhi are pure, suchness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all doors of samādhi, and the purity of suchness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, suchness is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, and the purity of suchness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the fruit of arhatship are pure; because the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the fruit of arhatship are pure, suchness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the fruits of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat, and the purity of suchness (tathatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, suchness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of suchness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the practice of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas is pure; because the practice of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas is pure, suchness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of suchness (*tathatā*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, suchness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, and the purity of suchness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the dharma-realm is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if form is pure, and if the dharma-realm is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the dharma-realm is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, and the purity of the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye base is pure; because the eye base is pure, the dharma realm is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sense base of the eye is pure, and if the dharma-realm is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the dharma-realm is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, and the purity of the dharma-realm are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are distinct from nothing, and they are uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the dharma-realm is pure. Why is this?
If the omniscience of all-knowledge is pure, if the sphere of form is pure, and if the dharma-realm is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure; because the bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure, the dharma-realm is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, and the purity of the dharma-realm are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the dharma-realm is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eye-element, or the purity of the dharma-realm, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the form realm (rūpadhātu), the eye-consciousness realm (cakṣurvijñānadhātu), eye-contact (cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa), and the various feelings (vedanā) produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure; because the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the form realm (rūpadhātu) up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the dharma-element is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ear-element, or the purity of the dharma-element, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, the sphere of sound (*śabdadhātu*), the sphere of auditory consciousness (*śrotravijñānadhātu*), auditory contact (*śrotrasaṃsparśa*), and the various feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure, the dharma-sphere (*dharmadhātu*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) and the purity of everything from the sphere of sound (*śabdadhātu*) up to the various sensations (*vedanā*) produced with ear-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the sphere of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll 257. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter on Difficult to Believe and Understand, Number Thirty-Four, Section Seven. "Sudhana! [Listen.]”
Because the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, the nose-element (*ghrāṇadhātu*) is pure; because the nose-element is pure, the dharma-element (*dharmadhātu*) is pure. Why is this?

Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the nose-element, or the purity of the dharma-element, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the dharma-element is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the fragrance-element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the dharma-element, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the dharma-element is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the tongue element is pure, and if the dharma element is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the dharma-element is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and the purity of the dharma-element are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, the dharma-element is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the realm of the body is pure, and if the realm of phenomena is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the dharma-element is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the various feelings arising with the body as the condition, from the element of tangibility up to the element of mental objects, are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the intention for the purity of omniscience is pure, the mind-element (manodhātu) is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the dharma-element (dharmadhātu) is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the mind-element is pure, and if the dharma-element is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as the various feelings arising with mental contact as condition, are pure; because the dharma-element up to the various feelings arising with mental contact as condition are pure, the dharma-element is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), or the purity of everything from the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu) up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, or the purity of the dharma-realm itself—they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the dharma-realm is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the earth element is pure, and if the dharma-realm is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, or the purity of the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the dharma-realm is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of non-duality, or the purity of the dharma-realm, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, volitional formations (saṃskāra), consciousness (vijñāna), name-and-form (nāmarūpa), the six sense bases (ṣaḍāyatana), contact (sparśa), feeling (vedanā), craving (tṛṣṇā), clinging (upādāna), becoming (bhava), birth (jāti), and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowing and the purity of everything from conditioned formations through old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, as well as the purity of the dharma-realm, are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of giving is pure; because the perfection of giving is pure, the dharma-realm is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowing, the purity of the perfection of generosity, and the purity of the dharma-realm are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are distinct neither in nature nor in continuity.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom are pure, the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom, and the purity of the dharma-realm are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the dharma-realm is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if internal emptiness is pure, and if the dharma-realm is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure; because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure, the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from outer emptiness up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence (abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā), as well as the purity of the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the dharma-realm is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of suchness, or the purity of the dharma-realm, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), the non-falsity of phenomena, the immutability of phenomena, the equality of phenomena, the nature of phenomena free from arising, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm are pure; because the nature of phenomena up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the dharma-nature up to the inconceivable realm, or the purity of the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure; because the noble truth of suffering is pure, the dharma-realm is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the noble truth of suffering is pure, and if the dharma-realm is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure, the dharma-realm is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path, and the purity of the dharma-realm are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the dharmadhātu is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the four dhyānas, and the purity of the dharma-realm, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, the dharma-realm is pure.

Why is this? Because if the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, and if the dharma-realm is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the dharma-realm is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eight liberations, and the purity of the dharma-realm are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the dharma-realm is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten pervasive bases, and the purity of the dharma-realm, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four applications of mindfulness are pure; because the four applications of mindfulness are pure, the dharma-realm is pure. Why is this?

The purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, and the purity of the dharma-realm are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu) is pure.
