Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, and the purity of the dharma-realm are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the dharma-realm is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, and the purity of the dharma-realm are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are pure; because the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are pure, the dharma-realm is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—and the purity of the dharma-realm are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the dharma-realm is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, and the purity of the dharma-realm are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the dharma-realm is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purification of the knowledge of all modes, the purification of the five eyes, or the purification of the dharma-realm, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the six supernormal powers (ṣaḍabhijñā) are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the six supernormal powers, or the purity of the realm of phenomena, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, the dharma-realm is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, or the purity of the dharma-realm, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and the purity of the dharma-realm are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the dharma-realm is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the state of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of the dharma-realm are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the state of constant equanimity is pure; because the state of constant equanimity is pure, the dharma-realm is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is [identical to] the purity of the state of constant equanimity, and if it is [identical to] the purity of the dharma-realm, this is because they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all-knowledge is pure; because all-knowledge is pure, the dharma-realm is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all-knowledge, or the purity of the dharma-realm, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, the dharma-realm is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, and the purity of the dharma-realm are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all dhāraṇī-doors are pure; because all dhāraṇī-doors are pure, the dharma-realm is pure."

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors, or the purity of the dharma-realm, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, all gateways to meditative concentration are pure; because all gateways to meditative concentration are pure, the dharma-realm is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all gateways of samādhi, and the purity of the dharma-realm are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, the dharma-realm is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, and the purity of the dharma-realm are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure; because the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure, the dharma-realm is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the fruit of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship, and the purity of the dharma-realm are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure, the dharma-realm is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience, the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of the dharma-realm are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure, the dharma-realm is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, the dharma-realm is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, and the purity of the dharma-realm are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if form is pure, and if the nature of phenomena is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, and the purity of the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye base is pure; because the eye base is pure, the dharma-nature is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sense-base of the eye is pure, and if the dharma-nature is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the sense bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, and the purity of the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the dharma-nature is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the sense-sphere of form, and the purity of the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure, the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena, and the purity of the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the dharma-nature is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eye-element, or the purity of the dharma-nature, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the form realm (rūpadhātu), the eye-consciousness realm (cakṣurvijñānadhātu), eye-contact (cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa), and the various feelings (vedanā) arising with eye-contact as a condition are pure; because the form realm up to the various feelings arising with eye-contact as a condition are pure, the dharma-nature (dharmatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of everything from the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, and the purity of the dharma-nature are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are without distinction, and they are without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the dharma-nature is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the ear-element is pure, and if the dharma-nature is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of auditory consciousness, auditory contact, and the various sensations produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of sound up to the various sensations produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure, the dharma-nature (dharmatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of the sphere of sound (*śabdadhātu*) up to the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with ear-contact as a condition, and the purity of the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the nose-element is pure; because the nose-element is pure, the dharma-nature is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the nose element, and the purity of the dharma-nature are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the fragrance element (gandhadhātu), the nose-consciousness element (ghrāṇavijñānadhātu), nose-contact (ghrāṇasparśa), and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the dharma-nature (dharmatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the realm of fragrance up to the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the dharma-nature (dharmatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the dharma-nature is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the tongue element, or the purity of the dharma-nature, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the dharma-nature (dharmatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and the purity of the dharma-nature are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, the dharma-nature is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the body element, or the purity of the dharma-nature, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the dharma-nature (dharmatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of the sphere of tangibles (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*) up to the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with body-tangibles as a condition, and the purity of the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the intention for the knowledge of all modes is pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the mental faculty element is pure, and if the nature of phenomena is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, as well as mental contact and the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are pure; because the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are pure, the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of everything from the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the earth element is pure, and if the nature of phenomena is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, or the purity of the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the nature of phenomena is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the light of wisdom, or the purity of the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the dharma-nature is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of everything from conditioned activities up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, and the purity of the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the perfection of generosity (dānapāramitā), and the purity of the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), and the purity of the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the nature of phenomena is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if inner emptiness is pure, and if the nature of phenomena is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure; because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure, the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of outer emptiness up to the purity of the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence, and the purity of the dharma-nature are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the nature of phenomena is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of suchness, or the purity of the dharma-nature, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the non-falsity, the non-alteration, the sameness, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of dharmas (dharmatā), the stability of dharmas (dharmaniyāmatā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu) are pure; because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the nature of dharmas (dharmatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, or the purity of the dharma-nature, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure; because the noble truth of suffering is pure, the dharma-nature is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the noble truth of suffering is pure, and if the nature of phenomena is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are pure, the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, and the purity of the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the dharmatā is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four dhyānas, and the purity of the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, the nature of phenomena is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, and the purity of the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is such, and the purity of the eight liberations is such, and the purity of the nature of phenomena is such, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the eight bases of mastery (aṣṭāv abhibhvāyatanāni), the nine successive attainments (navānupūrvavihārasamāpattayaḥ), and the ten totalities (daśa kṛtsnāyatanāni) are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten universal bases, as well as the purity of the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure; because the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, and the purity of the nature of phenomena, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, and the purity of the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the nature of phenomena is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, and the purity of the dharmadhātu are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the gates of liberation of signlessness (animitta) and wishlessness (apraṇihita) are pure; because the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure, the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—or the purity of the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, and the purity of the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is pure. Why is this?"

Whether it be the purification of the knowledge of all modes, the purification of the five eyes, or the purification of the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, the six supernormal powers (*ṣaḍabhijñā*) are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the six supernormal powers, or the purity of the nature of phenomena, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten powers of the Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of the Buddha are pure, the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, or the purity of the nature of phenomena, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, or the purity of the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the nature of phenomena is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the state of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the state of constant equanimity is pure; because the state of constant equanimity is pure, the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the nature of constant equanimity, and if it is the purity of the dharma-nature, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all-knowledge is pure; because all-knowledge is pure, the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all-knowledge, or the purity of the nature of phenomena, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, and the purity of the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all dhāraṇī-doors are pure; because all dhāraṇī-doors are pure, the nature of phenomena is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all dharani-doors, and the purity of the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
Because the knowledge of all modes of omniscience is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure; because all doors of samādhi are pure, the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all gateways to meditative concentration, and the purity of the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, the dharma-nature is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, and the purity of the nature of phenomena, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the fruit of arhatship are pure; because the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the fruit of arhatship are pure, the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the fruit of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship, and the purity of the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure, the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the unexcelled, perfect enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unexcelled, perfect enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, and the purity of the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the nature of non-falsity is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if form is pure, and if the nature of non-falsity is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the nature of non-falsity (avitathatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, as well as the purity of the nature of non-falsity, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-base is pure; because the eye-base is pure, the nature of non-falsity is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sense-base of the eye is pure, and if the nature of non-falsity is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the nature of non-falsity is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, as well as the purity of the nature of non-falsity, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the nature of non-falsity is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sense base of form is pure, and if the nature of non-falsity is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure, the nature of non-falsity is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena (dharmāyatana), as well as the purity of non-falsity, are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the nature of non-falsity is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the eye-element is pure, and if the nature of non-falsity is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the form element (rūpadhātu), the eye-consciousness element (cakṣurvijñānadhātu), eye-contact (cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa), and all feelings (vedanā) arising with eye-contact as condition are pure. Because the form element up to all feelings arising with eye-contact as condition are pure, the nature of non-falsity (amṛṣādharmatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of non-falsity, are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the nature of non-falsity is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the ear element is pure, and if the nature of non-falsity is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the sphere of sounds, the sphere of auditory consciousness, auditory contact, and the various feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of sounds up to the various feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure, the nature of non-falsity is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the sphere of sound up to the feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are without distinction, and they are not separate. This is because of the purity of the nature of non-falsity.
“Subhūti! Because all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the nose-element (ghrāṇadhātu) is pure; because the nose-element is pure, the nature of non-falsity (amṛṣātā) is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the nose element is pure, and if the nature of non-falsity is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*) is pure, the fragrance element (*gandhadhātu*), the nose-consciousness element (*ghrāṇavijñānadhātu*), nose-contact (*ghrāṇasparśa*), and the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the nature of non-falsity (*amṛṣātva*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the realm of fragrance up to the various sensations produced with nose-contact as condition are non-dual; they are not two, not divided, not distinct, and not discontinuous, because of their non-falsity.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the nature of non-falsity is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the tongue element is pure, and if the nature of non-falsity is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the nature of non-falsity is pure.

Why is this? Because if the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the taste element, up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, are pure, and if the nature of non-falsity is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, the nature of non-falsity is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the body element is pure, and if the nature of non-falsity is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the nature of non-falsity is pure.

Why is this? Because if the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, and if the objects of touch (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*) up to the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, and if the nature of non-falsity (*amṛṣātmatā*) is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the intentionality of the knowledge of all modes is pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the nature of non-falsity is pure. Why is that?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the mind-element is pure, and if the nature of non-falsity is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, as well as mental contact and the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition are pure; because the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition are pure, the nature of non-falsity is pure.

Why is this? Because if the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if everything from the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition is pure, and if the nature of non-falsity is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll Two Hundred and Fifty-Eight. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter Thirty-Four, "Difficult to Believe and Understand," Section Seventy-Eight. "Subhūti!

Because the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, the earth element (*pṛthivīdhātu*) is pure; because the earth element is pure, the nature of non-falsity (*avitathatā*) is pure. Why is this?

Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the earth element, or the purity of the nature of non-falsity, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the nature of non-falsity is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, or the purity of the nature of non-falsity, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the nature of non-falsity is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the purity of non-duality is pure, and if the nature of non-falsity is pure, this is because they are non-dual, not two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, volitional formations (saṃskāra), consciousness (vijñāna), name-and-form (nāmarūpa), the six sense bases (ṣaḍāyatana), contact (sparśa), feeling (vedanā), craving (tṛṣṇā), grasping (upādāna), becoming (bhava), birth (jāti), and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure. Because volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the nature of non-falsity (avitathatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the factors ranging from formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, or the purity of the nature of non-falsity—these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, the nature of non-falsity is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the perfection of generosity, and the purity of the nature of non-falsity are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, the nature of non-falsity is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the precepts up to the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), as well as the purity of non-falsity, are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, inner emptiness is pure; because inner emptiness is pure, the nature of non-falsity is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if internal emptiness is pure, and if the nature of non-falsity is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, there is the purity of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersal emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence. Because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is pure, the nature of non-falsity is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence (abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā), or the purity of the non-false nature (avitathatā), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the nature of non-falsity is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if suchness is pure, and if the nature of non-falsity is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), unchangingness, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the stability of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu) are pure; because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the non-falsity (avitathatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*) up to the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*), or the purity of the nature of non-falsity (*avitathatā*), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure; because the noble truth of suffering is pure, the nature of non-falsity is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the noble truth of suffering, and the purity of non-falsity are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure, the nature of non-falsity is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path, and the purity of the nature of non-falsity are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the nature of non-falsity is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four dhyānas, and the purity of non-falsity are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the four immeasurables (apramāṇa) and the four formless attainments (ārūpyasamāpatti) are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are pure, the nature of non-falsity (avitathatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, and the purity of the nature of non-falsity are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the nature of non-falsity is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the eight liberations (aṣṭavimokṣa), and the purity of the nature of non-falsity are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the eight bases of mastery (abhibhvāyatana), the nine successive attainments (anupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (kṛtsnāyatana) are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the nature of non-falsity (avitathatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because if the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases are pure, and if the nature of non-falsity is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four applications of mindfulness are pure; because the four applications of mindfulness are pure, the nature of non-falsity is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, and the purity of non-falsity are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, the nature of non-falsity is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, and the purity of non-falsity are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the door of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the door of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the nature of non-falsity is pure.”

Why is this? Because if the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, and if the nature of non-falsity is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the gateways of liberation of signlessness (animitta) and wishlessness (apraṇihita) are pure; because the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure, the nature of non-falsity (avitathatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, or the purity of the nature of non-falsity, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the nature of non-falsity is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the ten stages of the bodhisattva, and the purity of non-falsity are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the nature of non-falsity is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purification of the knowledge of all modes, the purification of the five eyes, or the purification of the nature of non-falsity, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the six supernormal powers (ṣaḍabhijñā) are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, the nature of non-falsity (amṛṣādharmatā) is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is such, and the purity of the six supernormal powers is such, and the purity of the nature of non-falsity is such, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten powers of the Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of the Buddha are pure, the nature of non-falsity is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, and the purity of the nature of non-falsity are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, the nature of non-falsity is pure.

Why is this? Because if the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, and if the nature of non-falsity is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the nature of non-falsity is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, or the purity of the nature of non-falsity, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the state of constant equanimity is pure; because the state of constant equanimity is pure, the nature of non-falsity is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is [identical to] the purity of the nature of constant equanimity, and the purity of the nature of non-falsity, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the knowledge of all things is pure; because the knowledge of all things is pure, the nature of non-falsity is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all-knowledge, and the purity of the nature of non-falsity are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, the nature of non-falsity is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path, or the purity of the nature of non-falsity, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all dhāraṇī-doors are pure; because all dhāraṇī-doors are pure, the nature of non-falsity is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors, or the purity of the nature of non-falsity, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the knowledge of all modes of omniscience is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure; because all doors of samādhi are pure, the nature of non-falsity is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all doors of samādhi, and the purity of the nature of non-falsity are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, the nature of non-falsity is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, and the purity of non-falsity are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the fruit of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship is pure; because the fruit of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship is pure, the nature of non-falsity is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the fruits of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat, as well as the purity of the nature of non-falsity, are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure, the nature of non-falsity is pure.”

Why is this? Because if the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure, and if the nature of non-falsity is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure, the nature of non-falsity is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience, the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of non-falsity are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, the nature of non-falsity is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, and the purity of the nature of non-falsity are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the nature of non-alteration is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if form is pure, and if non-alteration is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the nature of non-alteration is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, as well as the purity of the nature of non-alteration, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-base is pure; because the eye-base is pure, the nature of non-alteration is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sense base of the eye is pure, and if the nature of non-alteration is pure, this is because they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the nature of non-alteration is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience, the purity of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, and the purity of non-alteration are non-dual; they are not two, not divided, not distinct, and not severed.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the nature of non-alteration is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sense-sphere of form is pure, and if the nature of non-alteration is pure, this is because they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure, the nature of non-alteration is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena (dharmāyatana), and the purity of non-alteration are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the nature of non-alteration is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the eye-element is pure, and if non-alteration is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the form realm (rūpadhātu), the eye-consciousness realm (cakṣurvijñānadhātu), eye-contact (cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa), and the various feelings (vedanā) produced with eye-contact as condition are pure; because the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition are pure, the nature of non-alteration (avikāritva) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of everything from the realm of form up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, and the purity of non-alterability are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because omniscience is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the nature of non-alteration is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the ear-element is pure, and if the nature of non-alteration is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of auditory consciousness, auditory contact, and the various feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure, the nature of non-alteration is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) and the purity of everything from the sphere of sound (*śabdadhātu*) up to the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with ear-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of non-alteration (*avikāratā*), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the nose element is pure; because the nose element is pure, the nature of non-alteration is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the nose element is pure, and if the nature of non-alteration is pure, this is because they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the fragrance element (gandhadhātu), the nose-consciousness element (ghrāṇavijñānadhātu), nose-contact (ghrāṇasparśa), and the various feelings (vedanā) produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the nature of non-alteration (avikāritva) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the realm of fragrance up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divisible, they are not distinct, and they are not separate, for they are pure in their unchanging nature.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the nature of non-alteration is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the tongue element is pure, and if the nature of non-alteration is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the nature of non-alteration is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of everything from the taste element (*rasadhātu*) up to the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and the purity of non-alteration are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body-element is pure; because the body-element is pure, the nature of non-alteration is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the realm of the body is pure, and if the nature of non-alteration is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the nature of non-alteration is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the various feelings produced with the body as the basis for contact, up to the element of tangibles, and the purity of the nature of non-alteration, are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the omniscient wisdom is pure, the mind-element (*manodhātu*) is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the nature of non-alteration is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the mental constituent is pure, and if the nature of non-alteration is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, as well as mental contact and the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition, are pure. Because the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition are pure, the nature of non-alteration is pure.

Why is this? Because if the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if everything from the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition is pure, and if the nature of non-alteration is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the nature of non-alteration is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the earth element is pure, and if the nature of non-alteration is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the nature of non-alteration is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, as well as the purity of non-alteration, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the nature of immutability is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the light of non-arising, or the purity of the nature of non-alteration, these are non-dual, undivided, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, volitional formations (saṃskāra), consciousness (vijñāna), name-and-form (nāmarūpa), the six sense bases (ṣaḍāyatana), contact (sparśa), feeling (vedanā), craving (tṛṣṇā), grasping (upādāna), becoming (bhava), birth (jāti), and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair (jarāmaraṇa-śoka-parideva-duḥkha-daurmanasyopāyāsa) are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the nature of non-alteration (avikāratā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of everything from conditioned phenomena up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not separate, for they are the purity of the nature of non-alteration.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, the nature of non-alteration is pure.”
Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the perfection of generosity, and the purity of non-alteration are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, the nature of non-alteration is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), and the purity of non-alteration are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the nature of non-alteration is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if internal emptiness is pure, and if the nature of non-alteration is pure, this is because they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure; because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure, the nature of non-alteration is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence (abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā), as well as the purity of the unchanging nature, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the nature of non-alteration is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if suchness is pure, and if the unchanging nature is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), non-falsity (avitathatā), sameness (samatā), the state beyond birth (ananyatathatā), the fixedness of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu) are pure. Because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the unchanging nature (avikāritva) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, or the purity of unchanging nature, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure; because the noble truth of suffering is pure, the nature of non-alteration is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the noble truth of suffering, and the purity of unchanging nature are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure, the nature of non-alteration is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, and the purity of unchanging nature are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the nature of non-alteration is pure."
Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four dhyānas, and the purity of non-alteration are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, the nature of non-alteration is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, and the purity of unchanging nature are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because omniscient wisdom is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the nature of non-alteration is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eight liberations, and the purity of unchanging nature are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the eight bases of mastery (abhibhvāyatana), the nine successive attainments (anupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (kṛtsnāyatana) are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the nature of non-alteration (avikāratā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the eight bases of mastery (aṣṭavimokṣa), the nine successive attainments (navānupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (daśakṛtsnāyatana) are non-dual; they are not two, not divided, not distinct, and not severed. Thus, the purity of the nature of non-alteration is [identical to] them.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four applications of mindfulness are pure; because the four applications of mindfulness are pure, the nature of non-alteration is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, and the purity of non-alteration are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
