Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, the nature of non-alteration is pure.

Why is this? Because if the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, and if the nature of non-alteration is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the nature of non-alteration is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience, the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, and the purity of non-alteration are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the gates of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are pure; because the gates of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are pure, the nature of non-alteration is pure.

Why is this? Because if the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure, and if the nature of non-alteration is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the nature of non-alteration is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the ten stages of the bodhisattva (daśabhūmi), and the purity of unchanging nature are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the nature of non-alteration is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the five eyes are pure, and if the nature of non-alteration is pure, it is because they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the six supernormal powers are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, the nature of non-alteration is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the six supernormal powers, or the purity of non-alteration, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, the nature of non-alteration is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, and the purity of unchanging nature are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, the nature of non-alteration is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and the purity of non-alteration are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the nature of immutability is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of unchanging nature are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the state of constant equanimity is pure; because the state of constant equanimity is pure, the nature of non-alteration is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the state of constant equanimity, and the purity of the state of non-alteration, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all-knowledge is pure; because all-knowledge is pure, the nature of non-alteration is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all-knowledge, and the purity of non-alteration are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, the nature of non-alteration is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, and the purity of non-alteration are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all dhāraṇī gateways are pure; because all dhāraṇī gateways are pure, the nature of non-alteration is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all dharani-doors, and the purity of non-alteration are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure; because all doors of samādhi are pure, the nature of non-alteration is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience, the purity of all gateways to meditative concentration, and the purity of unchanging nature are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, the nature of non-alteration is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, and the purity of non-alteration are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are pure; because the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are pure, the nature of immutability is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the fruit of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship, and the purity of unchanging nature are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, the nature of non-alteration is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of unchanging nature are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure, the nature of non-alteration is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of non-alteration are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the unexcelled, perfect enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unexcelled, perfect enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, the nature of non-alteration is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, and the purity of unchanging nature are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the nature of equality is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if form is pure, and if the nature of equality is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the nature of equality is pure.

Why is this? Because if the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, and if the nature of equality is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-base is pure; because the eye-base is pure, the nature of equality is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sense base of the eye is pure, and if the state of equality is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, equality is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna), the purity of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, and the purity of equality are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, equality is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sphere of form is pure, and if the nature of equality is pure, they are non-dual, not two, without distinction, and not separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure, the state of equality is pure.

Why is this? Because if the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena are pure, and if the nature of equality is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the nature of equality is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eye-element, or the purity of sameness, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, the form element (*rūpadhātu*), the eye-consciousness element (*cakṣurvijñānadhātu*), eye-contact (*cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa*), and the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure; because the form element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, the nature of equality (*samatā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of everything from the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, and the purity of equality are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the nature of equality is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the ear-element is pure, and if the state of equality is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of auditory consciousness, auditory contact, and the various feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure, the nature of equality (samatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purification of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purification of the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, and the purification of the state of equality are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the nose-element is pure; because the nose-element is pure, the state of equality is pure. Why is this?
If the omniscience of all-knowledge is pure, if the nose-element is pure, and if the state of equality is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the state of equality (samatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the realm of fragrance up to the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition, and the purity of equality are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the nature of equality is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the tongue-element is pure, and if the state of equality is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the nature of equality (samatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of everything from the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and the purity of the state of equality, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, the nature of equality is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the body element is pure, and if the nature of equality is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the nature of equality (samatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of the sphere of tangibles (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*) up to the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with body-contact as a condition, and the purity of equality (*samatā*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the intentionality of the knowledge of all modes is pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, equality is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the mind-element is pure, and if equality is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, as well as mental contact and the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition are pure; because the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition are pure, the state of equality (samatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu) up to the feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, as well as the purity of equality, are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, equality is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the earth element is pure, and if the nature of equality is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the nature of equality is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, or the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, or the purity of equality, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, equality is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the light of non-arising, or the purity of sameness, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the nature of equality (samatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from formative activities up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed. This is because of the purity of the nature of equality.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll Two Hundred and Fifty-nine. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter Thirty-four, "Difficult to Believe and Understand," Section Seventy-nine. "Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, equality is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the perfection of generosity, and the purity of equality are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, equality is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), as well as the purity of sameness, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the nature of equality is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if internal emptiness is pure, and if the nature of equality is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, there is the purity of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence. Because the purity of external emptiness up to the purity of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence exists, there is the purity of equality.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence, and the purity of sameness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the nature of equality is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of suchness, or the purity of sameness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, immutability, the state of being free from birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm are pure; because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the nature of equality is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu) up to the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu), or the purity of sameness (samatā), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure; because the noble truth of suffering is pure, equality is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the noble truth of suffering is pure, and if equality is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not severed.
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure, equality is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path, and the purity of equality are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, equality is pure. Why is that?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the same as the purity of the four dhyānas, and the purity of equality, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, the nature of equality is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, and the purity of equality are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the nature of equality is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eight liberations, and the purity of equality are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the eight bases of mastery (aṣṭāv abhibhvāyatanāni), the nine successive attainments (navānupūrvavihārasamāpattayaḥ), and the ten totalities (daśa kṛtsnāyatanāni) are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the nature of equality (samatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the eight bases of mastery (aṣṭau vimokṣāḥ), the nine successive meditative attainments (navānupūrvavihārasamāpattayaḥ), and the ten pervasive bases (daśakṛtsnāyatanāni) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption; they are identical with the purity of the nature of equality (samatā).
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four applications of mindfulness are pure; because the four applications of mindfulness are pure, equality is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, and if equality is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eight branches of the noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eight branches of the noble path are pure, equality is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path, and the purity of equality are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the door of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the door of liberation that is emptiness is pure, equality is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness (śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha), or the purity of equality (samatā), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure; because the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure, the nature of equality is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the gateways of liberation—signlessness (animitta) and wishlessness (apraṇihita)—and the purity of sameness (samatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the nature of equality is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of the ten stages (*daśabhūmi*) of a bodhisattva, and the purity of the nature of equality (*samatā*) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, equality is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the five eyes, or the purity of equality, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, the six supernormal powers (*ṣaḍabhijñā*) are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, the nature of equality (*samatā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the six supernormal powers, or the purity of the nature of equality, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, the nature of equality is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, and if the nature of equality is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, the nature of equality is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, or the purity of the nature of equality, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, equality is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of equality are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the state of constant abiding in equanimity is pure; because the state of constant abiding in equanimity is pure, the nature of equality is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the state of constant equanimity, and if the purity of the nature of equality is [the same], they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the knowledge of all things is pure; because the knowledge of all things is pure, the nature of equality is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all-knowledge, or the purity of sameness—these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, the nature of equality is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects, and the purity of equality are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all dhāraṇī gateways are pure; because all dhāraṇī gateways are pure, the nature of equality is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience, the purity of all dharani-doors, and the purity of the nature of equality are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure; because all doors of samādhi are pure, the nature of equality is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all gateways to samādhi, and the purity of equality are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, equality is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, and the purity of equality, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure; because the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure, the nature of equality is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship, and the purity of the nature of equality are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure, equality is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of equality are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure, the nature of equality is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of the nature of equality are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the unsurpassed perfect enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unsurpassed perfect enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, the nature of equality is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, and the purity of sameness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the nature of being free from arising is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if form is pure, and if the nature of detachment from arising is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the nature of arising is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, and the purity of the nature of detachment are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye base is pure; because the eye base is pure, the nature of being free from arising is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sense base of the eye is pure, and if the nature of detachment from birth is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the nature of arising is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, as well as the purity of the nature of detachment, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the nature of being free from arising is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the sphere of form, and the purity of the nature of detachment are non-dual, undivided, indistinguishable, and inseparable.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena are pure, the nature of being free from birth is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, and the purity of the nature of detachment from birth are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the nature of being free from birth is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the eye-element is pure, and if the nature of detachment from birth is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the form realm (rūpadhātu), the eye-consciousness element (cakṣurvijñānadhātu), eye-contact (cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa), and the various feelings (vedanā) produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure. Because the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, the nature of detachment (vivekatva) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the form realm (rūpadhātu) up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the nature of detachment, are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divisible, they are not distinct, and they are not separate.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the nature of detachment from birth is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the ear element is pure, and if the nature of detachment is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of ear-consciousness, ear-contact, and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure, the nature of detachment is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, and the purity of the nature of detachment, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the nose element is pure; because the nose element is pure, the nature of being free from arising is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the nose element, and the purity of the nature of detachment are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the fragrance element (gandhadhātu), the nose-consciousness element (ghrāṇavijñānadhātu), nose-contact (ghrāṇasparśa), and the various feelings (vedanā) produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the nature of detachment (vivekatva) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the realm of fragrance up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, and the purity of the nature of detachment from birth, are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the nature of detachment is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the tongue element is pure, and if the nature of detachment is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the nature of detachment is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the various feelings arising with the gustatory element as their condition, up to those arising with tongue-contact as their condition, and the purity of the nature of detachment are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, the nature of arising is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is such, and the purity of the body-element is such, and the purity of the nature of detachment from birth are such, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the nature of detachment is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) and the purity of the various feelings arising with the body as the basis and contact as the condition—from the element of touch (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*) onwards—are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted; they are the same as the purity of the nature of detachment (*vivekadharma*).

“Subhūti! Because the intention for the purity of the knowledge of all modes is pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the nature of being free from birth is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the mind-element is pure, and if the nature of detachment from birth is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness element, mind-contact, and the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition are pure; because the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition are pure, the nature of being free from birth is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, and the purity of the nature of detachment from birth, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the nature of being free from birth is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the earth element, and the purity of the nature of detachment from birth are non-dual, without division, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the nature of arising is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, or the purity of the nature of detachment from birth—these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the nature of detachment from birth is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the light of omniscience, or the purity of the nature of detachment, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, volitional formations (saṃskāra), consciousness (vijñāna), name-and-form (nāmarūpa), the six sense bases (ṣaḍāyatana), contact (sparśa), feeling (vedanā), craving (tṛṣṇā), grasping (upādāna), becoming (bhava), birth (jāti), and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair (jarāmaraṇa-śoka-parideva-duḥkha-daurmanasyopāyāsa) are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the nature of arising is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from formative activities up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous; so too is the purity of the nature of detachment. Thus they are non-dual, without division, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of giving is pure; because the perfection of giving is pure, the nature of being free from birth is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the perfection of generosity, and the purity of the nature of detachment are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, the nature of being free from birth is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), as well as the purity of the nature of detachment, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the nature of detachment from arising is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if internal emptiness is pure, and if the nature of detachment from arising is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure; because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure, the purity of the nature of detachment is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, as well as the purity of the nature free from arising, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the nature free from arising is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of suchness, and the purity of the nature free from arising are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), non-falsity, immutability, equality, the fixed nature of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the stability of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu) are pure. Because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the nature of being free from birth is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, and the purity of the nature of being free from birth, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because omniscient wisdom is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure; because the noble truth of suffering is pure, the nature of arising through detachment is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the noble truth of suffering is pure, and if the nature of detachment from arising is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure, the nature of detachment is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, and the purity of the nature of detachment are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the nature of being free from birth is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the four dhyānas, and the purity of the nature of detachment, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four immeasurables (apramāṇa) and the four formless attainments (ārūpyasamāpatti) are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are pure, the nature of detachment from birth is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the four immeasurables (apramāṇa) and the four formless attainments (ārūpyasamāpatti), and the purity of the nature of detachment are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the nature of detachment from birth is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eight liberations, and the purity of the nature of detachment are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the eight bases of mastery (abhibhvāyatana), the nine successive attainments (anupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (kṛtsnāyatana) are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the nature of detachment is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience, the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases, and the purity of the nature of detachment from birth, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four applications of mindfulness are pure; because the four applications of mindfulness are pure, the nature of detachment from birth is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, and the purity of the nature of detachment, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eight branches of the noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eight branches of the noble path are pure, the nature of detachment is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path, and the purity of the nature of detachment are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the door of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the door of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the nature of detachment from arising is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, and the purity of the nature of detachment are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are pure; because the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are pure, the nature of detachment from birth is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—or the purity of the nature of detachment from birth, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the nature of being free from birth is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, and the purity of the nature free from birth are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the nature of being free from birth is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the five eyes, or the purity of the nature of detachment from birth—these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the six supernormal knowledges (ṣaḍabhijñā) are pure; because the six supernormal knowledges are pure, the nature of being free from birth is pure. Why is this?

Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the six supernormal knowledges, or the purity of the nature of being free from birth, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, the nature of being free from birth is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, and the purity of the nature of being free from birth are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, the nature of detachment from birth is pure.

Why is this? Because if the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, and if the nature of being free from birth is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the nature of being free from birth is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the state of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of the nature of detachment from birth are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the wisdom of all-knowledge is pure, the state of constant abiding in equanimity is pure; because the state of constant abiding in equanimity is pure, the nature of being free from birth is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the state of constant equanimity, and the purity of the nature of being free from birth, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all-knowledge is pure; because all-knowledge is pure, the nature of being free from birth is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all-knowledge, or the purity of the nature of detachment from birth, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, the nature of being free from birth is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path, and the purity of the nature of detachment are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all dhāraṇī-doors are pure; because all dhāraṇī-doors are pure, the nature of being free from birth is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all dharani-doors, and the purity of the nature of detachment from birth are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure; because all doors of samādhi are pure, the nature of being free from birth is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all doors of samādhi, and the purity of the nature of being free from birth are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, the nature of being free from birth is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, and the purity of the nature of transcendence are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the fruit of once-returner, the fruit of non-returner, and the fruit of arhatship are pure; because the fruit of once-returner, the fruit of non-returner, and the fruit of arhatship are pure, the nature of detachment from birth is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the fruits of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat, as well as the purity of the nature of detachment, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, the nature of being free from birth is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of the nature of detachment are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure, the nature of being free from birth is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience, the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of the nature of detachment from birth are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, the nature of being free from birth is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, and the purity of the nature free from birth are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the dharma-realm is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if form is pure, and if the purity of phenomena is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the dharma-realm is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, as well as the purity of the dharma-realm, are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye base is pure; because the eye base is pure, the dharma-realm is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sense-sphere of the eye is pure, and if the dharma-realm is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the dharma-element is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the sense bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, as well as the purity of phenomena and the purity of concentration, are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the dharma-realm is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the sense-base of form, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of dharmas, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena are pure; because the bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena are pure, the dharma-element is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental objects, and the purity of the dharma-realm are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the dharma-realm is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eye-element, or the purity of the dharma-realm, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the form element (rūpadhātu), the eye-consciousness element (cakṣurvijñānadhātu), eye-contact (cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa), and the various feelings (vedanā) produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure; because the form element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, the dharma-element (dharmadhātu) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the form realm (rūpadhātu) up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the dharmas of concentration, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the dharma-realm is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ear-element, or the purity of the dharma-realm, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the sphere of sounds, the sphere of ear-consciousness, auditory contact, and the various sensations produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of sounds up to the various sensations produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure, the dharma-element is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the sphere of sound, up to and including the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the dharma-realm, are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are distinct from nothing, and they are uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the nose-element is pure; because the nose-element is pure, the dharma-realm is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the same as the purity of the nose element, and the purity of the dharma-realm, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the dharma-element is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the realm of fragrance up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, and the purity of the dharmas of concentration, are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the tongue element is pure; because the tongue element is pure, the dharma-element is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the tongue element is pure, and if the dharma-realm is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the dharma-element is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the taste element, up to and including the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and the purity of the dharmas of concentration, are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, the dharma-realm is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the body-element and the purity of the dharma-realm, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the dharma-element is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the various feelings produced with the body as the basis and tangibles as conditions—up to the tangibles themselves—and the purity of dharmas are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are not distinct, and they are not separate.
“Subhūti! Because the intention for the purity of the knowledge of all modes is pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the dharma-nature is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the mind-element is pure, and if the dharma-realm is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, as well as mental contact and the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are pure; because the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are pure, the dharma-nature (dharmatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of everything from the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the fixed nature of phenomena, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the dharma-realm is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the earth element is pure, and if the purity of phenomena is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the dharmas are pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, or the purity of the dharma-realm, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the dharma-nature is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the light of non-arising, or the purity of the fixed nature of phenomena, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, volitional formations (saṃskāra), consciousness (vijñāna), name-and-form (nāmarūpa), the six sense bases (ṣaḍāyatana), contact (sparśa), feeling (vedanā), craving (tṛṣṇā), grasping (upādāna), becoming (bhava), birth (jāti), and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair (jarāmaraṇa-śoka-parideva-duḥkha-daurmanasyopāyāsa) are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are pure, the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of [the factors] from formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, or the purity of the dharmas of fixed nature—these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of giving is pure; because the perfection of giving is pure, the dharma-realm is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the perfection of giving (dānapāramitā), and the purity of the dharmas are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are without distinction, and they are not severed.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom, as well as the purity of the dharma-realm, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 263. Translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter Thirty-Four, "Difficult to Believe and Understand," Section Eighty. "Subhūti!

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, internal emptiness (adhyātmaśūnyatā) is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the fixed nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is pure. Why is this?

Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of internal emptiness, or the purity of the fixed nature of phenomena, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, there is the purity of external emptiness (*bahirdhā-śūnyatā*), internal-and-external emptiness (*adhyātma-bahirdhā-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of emptiness (*śūnyatā-śūnyatā*), great emptiness (*mahā-śūnyatā*), ultimate emptiness (*paramārtha-śūnyatā*), conditioned emptiness (*saṃskṛta-śūnyatā*), unconditioned emptiness (*asaṃskṛta-śūnyatā*), absolute emptiness (*atyanta-śūnyatā*), boundless emptiness (*anavara-agra-śūnyatā*), dispersed emptiness (*anavakāra-śūnyatā*), non-alteration emptiness (*anavakāra-śūnyatā* [variant: *ananyathā-śūnyatā*]), essential nature emptiness (*prakṛti-śūnyatā*), self-characteristic emptiness (*svalakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*), common characteristic emptiness (*sāmānya-lakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of all phenomena (*sarvadharma-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of the unapprehendable (*anupalambha-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of non-existence (*abhāva-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of intrinsic nature (*svabhāva-śūnyatā*), and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence (*abhāva-svabhāva-śūnyatā*). Because there is the purity of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, there is the purity of the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmatā-viniyata*).

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from external emptiness up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence (abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā), as well as the purity of the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the dharma-realm is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of suchness, or the purity of the fixed nature of phenomena, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the stability of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm are pure; because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the fixed nature of phenomena (dharmavyavasthāna) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the dharma-realm, up to the inconceivable realm, as well as the purity of the fixed nature of phenomena, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure; because the noble truth of suffering is pure, the purity of the Dharma is established. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is such, and the purity of the noble truth of suffering is such, and the purity of the fixed nature of phenomena is such, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct from one another, and inseparable.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure, the fixed nature of phenomena is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path, and the purity of the fixed nature of phenomena (dharmatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the dharma-realm is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the four dhyānas, and the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the dharmas, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, the dharma-nature is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, and the purity of the dharmas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the dharma-nature is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the eight liberations, and if the purity of the dharma-nature is [the same], they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the eight bases of mastery (abhibhvāyatana), the nine successive attainments (anupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (kṛtsnāyatana) are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the dharma-nature (dharmatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of the eight bases of mastery (*abhibhvāyatana*), the nine successive meditative attainments (*anupūrvavihārasamāpatti*), and the ten pervasive bases (*kṛtsnāyatana*), as well as the purity of the dharmas and the purity of concentration, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure; because the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, the dharma-nature is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, and if the purity of the dharma-realm is [the same], they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.
