Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eight branches of the noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eight branches of the noble path are pure, the purity of the Dharma is established.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) and the purity of the four right efforts (*samyakprahāṇa*) up to the eightfold noble path (*āryāṣṭāṅgamārga*), as well as the purity of the dharma and the purity of concentration (*samādhi*), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the dharma-nature is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the gateway of liberation that is emptiness, and the purity of the dharma-nature are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the gateways of liberation of signlessness (animitta) and wishlessness (apraṇihita) are pure; because the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure, the dharma-nature (dharmatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—or the purity of the dharma-realm, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the dharma-realm is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, or the purity of the dharma-realm, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the dharma-nature is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purification of the knowledge of all modes, the purification of the five eyes, or the purification of the dharmas, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, the six supernormal powers (*ṣaḍabhijñā*) are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, the dharma-nature (*dharmatā*) is pure. Why is this?

Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the six supernormal powers, or the purity of the dharma-nature, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, the Dharma-realm is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, and if the dharma-realm is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, the dharma-element (dharmadhātu) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and the purity of the dharmas are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the dharma-nature is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of the dharmas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the state of constant equanimity is pure; because the state of constant equanimity is pure, the fixed nature of phenomena is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the nature of constant equanimity, and if the purity of the dharmas is the purity of the nature of constant equanimity, because they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the knowledge of all things is pure; because the knowledge of all things is pure, the dharma-nature is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all-knowledge, or the purity of the dharma-element, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, the purity of the dharma-nature is established.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, and the purity of the dharmas are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all dharanī-doors are pure; because all dharanī-doors are pure, the dharma-realm is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors, and the purity of the dharma-seal are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure; because all doors of samādhi are pure, the dharma-nature is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all doors of samādhi, and the purity of the dharmas are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are without distinction, and they are not separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, the dharma-realm is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, and if the purity of the dharma-realm is so, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure; because the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure, the purity of the dharma-realm is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship, and the purity of the dharmas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, the dharma-realm is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of the dharmas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure, the dharma-realm is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience, the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of dharmas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, the purity of the Dharma is established.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, and the purity of the dharmas are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the abiding of phenomena is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if form is pure, and if the abiding of phenomena is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the abiding of phenomena is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, or the purity of the abiding of phenomena (dharmasthiti), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye base is pure; because the eye base is pure, the stability of phenomena is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sense-base of the eye is pure, and if the stability of phenomena is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the abiding of phenomena is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, or the purity of the abiding of phenomena, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the stability of phenomena is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the sphere of form, and the purity of the abiding of phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena are pure, the abiding of phenomena is pure.

Why is this? Because if the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena are pure, and if the abiding of phenomena is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the abiding of phenomena is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eye-element, or the purity of the abiding of phenomena, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the form element (rūpadhātu), the eye-consciousness element (cakṣurvijñānadhātu), eye-contact (cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa), and the various feelings (vedanā) arising with eye-contact as condition are pure; because the form element up to the various feelings arising with eye-contact as condition are pure, the stability of phenomena (dharmasthititā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of everything from the form realm (*rūpadhātu*) up to the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with eye-contact as a condition, and the purity of the abiding of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the stability of phenomena is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ear-element, or the purity of the stability of phenomena, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of ear-consciousness, ear-contact, and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as condition are pure; because the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as condition are pure, the stability of phenomena (dharmasthititā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, and the purity of the abiding of phenomena (dharmasthititā), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the nose element is pure; because the nose element is pure, the stability of phenomena is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the nose element, or the purity of the abiding of phenomena, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the stability of phenomena (dharmasthiti) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the various sensations produced with the fragrance-element up to the nose-contact as condition, and the purity of the abiding of phenomena (dharmasthititā), are non-dual; they are not two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the stability of phenomena is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the tongue element, and the purity of the abiding of phenomena are non-dual, without division, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste-element up to all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the stability of phenomena (dharmasthiti) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the various sensations produced with the gustatory element up to tongue-contact as a condition, and the purity of the abiding of phenomena (dharmasthititā), are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, the stability of phenomena is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the body element, and the purity of the stability of phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the stability of phenomena (dharmasthiti) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) and the purity of the various feelings arising with the body as the basis and tangibles as conditions—up to the sphere of tangibles (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*)—and the purity of the abiding of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the intention for the purity of the knowledge of all modes is pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the stability of phenomena is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the mental faculty, and the purity of the abiding of phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are pure; because the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are pure, the stability of phenomena (dharmasthiti) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu) up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the stability of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the abiding of phenomena is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the earth element, and the purity of the abiding of phenomena are non-dual, undivided, distinctless, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the abiding of phenomena (dharmasthiti) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, as well as the purity of the abiding of phenomena (dharmasthititā), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the abiding of phenomena is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purification of the knowledge of all modes, the purification of non-arising, or the purification of the abiding of phenomena, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, volitional formations (saṃskāra), consciousness (vijñāna), name-and-form (nāmarūpa), the six sense bases (ṣaḍāyatana), contact (sparśa), feeling (vedanā), craving (tṛṣṇā), clinging (upādāna), becoming (bhava), birth (jāti), and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the abiding of phenomena (dharmasthititā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, as well as the purity of the abiding of phenomena (dharmasthiti), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, the abiding of the Dharma is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the perfection of generosity, and the purity of the abiding of phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, the abiding of the Dharma (dharmasthiti) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom, and the purity of the abiding of phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the abiding of phenomena is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if inner emptiness is pure, and if the abiding of phenomena is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, there is purity of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential emptiness, emptiness of self-characteristic, emptiness of common characteristic, emptiness of all phenomena, emptiness of non-apprehensibility, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, and emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence; because there is purity from external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, the stability of phenomena (*dharmasthiti*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of outer emptiness up to the purity of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, and the purity of the abiding of phenomena (dharmasthititā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the abiding of phenomena is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of suchness, or the purity of the stability of phenomena, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), non-falsity (avitathatā), non-alteration (ananyathābhāvatā), sameness (samatā), the state beyond birth (anirodhatā), the fixed nature of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu) are pure; because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the abiding of phenomena (dharmasthiti) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, or the purity of the stability of phenomena, they are non-dual, not two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure; because the noble truth of suffering is pure, the stability of phenomena (dharmasthititā) is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the noble truth of suffering, and the purity of the stability of phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure, the stability of phenomena is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, and the purity of the stability of phenomena (dharmasthititā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because omniscience is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the abiding of phenomena is pure. Why is that?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the four dhyānas, and the purity of the stability of phenomena, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are pure, the abiding of phenomena is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the four immeasurables (apramāṇa) and the four formless attainments (ārūpyasamāpatti), and the purity of the abiding of phenomena (dharmasthititā) are non-dual, not divided into two, not distinct, and not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the stability of phenomena is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eight liberations, and the purity of the abiding of phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the eight bases of mastery (abhibhvāyatana), the nine successive attainments (anupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (kṛtsnāyatana) are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the abiding of the Dharma (dharmasthititā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the eight bases of mastery (aṣṭavimokṣa), the nine successive attainments (navānupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (daśakṛtsnāyatana), as well as the purity of the abiding of phenomena (dharmasthititā), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure; because the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, the stability of phenomena is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, and the purity of the abiding of phenomena, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eight branches of the noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eight branches of the noble path are pure, the stability of the Dharma (dharmasthiti) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, and the purity of the stability of phenomena (dharmasthiti) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the abiding of phenomena is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, and the purity of the abiding of phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the gateways of liberation of signlessness (animitta) and wishlessness (apraṇihita) are pure; because the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure, the abiding of phenomena (dharmasthiti) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—or the purity of the abiding of phenomena, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the abiding of the Dharma is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, and the purity of the abiding of phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor severed.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the abiding of the Dharma is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the five eyes, or the purity of the abiding of phenomena, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the six supernormal powers (ṣaḍabhijñā) are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, the stability of phenomena (dharmasthiti) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the six supernormal powers, or the purity of the stability of phenomena, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, the stability of the Dharma is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, or the purity of the abiding of the Dharma, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, the abiding of the Dharma (dharmasthiti) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and the purity of the abiding of phenomena (dharmasthititā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the abiding of the Dharma is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of the abiding of phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the wisdom of all-knowledge is pure, the state of constant equanimity is pure; because the state of constant equanimity is pure, the abiding of phenomena is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the state of constant equanimity, and if it is the purity of the abiding nature of phenomena, this is because they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the knowledge of all things is pure; because the knowledge of all things is pure, the abiding of the Dharma is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all-knowledge, or the purity of the abiding of phenomena, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, the stability of the Dharma is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, and the purity of the abiding of phenomena are non-dual, not two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all dhāraṇī-doors are pure; because all dhāraṇī-doors are pure, the abiding of the Dharma is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all dharani-doors, and the purity of the abiding of phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, all doors of meditative concentration (*samādhi-mukha*) are pure; because all doors of meditative concentration are pure, the abiding of the Dharma (*dharmasthiti*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all doors of samādhi, and the purity of the abiding of phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, the abiding of the Dharma is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, and the purity of the abiding of phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure; because the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure, the abiding of the Dharma (dharmasthiti) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the fruit of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship, and the purity of the abiding of phenomena (dharmasthiti) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, the stability of phenomena is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of the abiding of phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure, the abiding of the Dharma is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of the abiding of phenomena are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, the abiding of the Dharma is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi) of the Buddhas, and the purity of the abiding of phenomena (dharmasthiti) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the limit of reality is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if form is pure, and if the limit of reality is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the limit of reality is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, and the purity of the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-base is pure; because the eye-base is pure, the limit of reality is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sense base of the eye is pure, and if the limit of reality is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, and the purity of the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the limit of reality is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the sphere of form, and the purity of the limit of reality are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena are pure, the reality limit is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena, and the purity of the limit of reality are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the limit of reality is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eye-element, or the purity of the limit of reality, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the form realm (rūpadhātu), the eye-consciousness realm (cakṣurvijñānadhātu), eye-contact (cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa), and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure; because the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, the reality-limit (bhūtakoṭi) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of everything from the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, and the purity of the limit of reality, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the limit of reality is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the ear-element is pure, and if the limit of reality is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of auditory consciousness, and ear-contact, as well as all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, are pure; because the sphere of sound up to all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure, the reality-limit (bhūtakoṭi) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, and the purity of the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the nose-element is pure; because the nose-element is pure, the limit of reality is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the nose element, and the purity of the limit of reality are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the realm of fragrance up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, and the purity of the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), are non-dual; they are not two, not divided, not distinct, and not severed.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the limit of reality is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purification of the knowledge of all modes, the purification of the tongue-element, or the purification of the limit of reality, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and the purity of the reality limit (bhūtakoṭi) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, the limit of reality is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the body-element is pure, and if the limit of reality is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the various feelings produced with the body as the basis and contact as the condition—up to the touch element—and the purity of the reality limit (bhūtakoṭi) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the intention for the purity of all-knowledge is pure, the mind-element (*manodhātu*) is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) is pure. Why is this?
The purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the mental constituent, and the purity of the limit of reality are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are pure; because the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are pure, the reality-limit (bhūtakoṭi) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of everything from the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the limit of reality, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the limit of reality is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the earth element, or the purity of the limit of reality, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the limit of reality is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience, the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, and the purity of the limit of reality are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the reality limit is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the light of non-arising, or the purity of the reality limit, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of everything from conditioned formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, and the purity of the limit of reality are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, the limit of reality is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the perfection of generosity, and the purity of the limit of reality are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom, and the purity of the limit of reality are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the reality-limit is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of internal emptiness, or the purity of the limit of reality, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure; because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is pure, the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of outer emptiness up to the purity of the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence, and the purity of the limit of reality, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the reality limit is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of suchness, or the purity of the reality-limit, they are non-dual, not divided into two, not distinct, and not severed.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*) are pure; because the realm of phenomena up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, or the purity of the limit of reality, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure; because the noble truth of suffering is pure, the reality-limit is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the noble truth of suffering is pure, and if the reality limit is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure, the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, and the purity of the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle Two Hundred and Sixty-one. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter Thirty-four, "Difficult to Believe and Understand," Section Eighty-one. "Subhūti!..."
Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) is pure. Why is this?

Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four dhyānas, or the purity of the limit of reality, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, the limit of reality is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the four immeasurables (apramāṇa) and the four formless attainments (ārūpyasamāpatti), and the purity of the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the limit of reality is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eight liberations, and the purity of the limit of reality are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the eight bases of mastery (abhibhvāyatana), the nine successive attainments (anupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (kṛtsnāyatana) are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases, and the purity of the limit of reality, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure; because the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, the limit of reality is pure. Why is that?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, and the purity of the limit of reality are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, and the purity of the limit of reality are non-dual; they are not two, not divided, not distinct, and not severed.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the reality limit is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, and the purity of the limit of reality are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor severed.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are pure; because the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are pure, the reality limit is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience, the purity of the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—and the purity of the limit of reality are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the limit of reality is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, and the purity of the limit of reality are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the limit of reality is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purification of the knowledge of all modes, the purification of the five eyes, or the purification of the limit of reality, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes of omniscience (*sarvajñājñāna*) is pure, the six supernormal powers (*ṣaḍabhijñā*) are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) is pure. Why is this?

Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience, the purity of the six supernormal powers, or the purity of the limit of reality, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, the reality limit is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, and if the limit of reality is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and the purity of the limit of reality are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the reality limit is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the state of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of the limit of reality are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
Because the wisdom of all-knowledge is pure, the state of constant equanimity is pure; because the state of constant equanimity is pure, the limit of reality is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the state of constant equanimity, and the purity of the limit of reality are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the knowledge of all things is pure; because the knowledge of all things is pure, the limit of reality is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all-knowledge, or the purity of the limit of reality, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, the reality limit (*bhūtakoṭi*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, and the purity of the limit of reality are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all dhāraṇī gateways are pure; because all dhāraṇī gateways are pure, the limit of reality is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all dharani-doors, and the purity of the limit of reality are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, all gateways to samādhi are pure; because all gateways to samādhi are pure, the limit of reality is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all gateways to samādhi, and the purity of the limit of reality are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, the limit of reality is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is such, and the purity of the fruit of stream-entry is such, and the purity of the limit of reality is such, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the fruit of arhatship are pure; because the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the fruit of arhatship are pure, the reality-limit (bhūtakoṭi) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship, and the purity of the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, the reality limit is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of the limit of reality are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure, the reality limit is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, the reality limit is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, and the purity of the limit of reality are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the realm of space is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if form is pure, and if the realm of space is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the realm of space is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, and the purity of the realm of space are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye base is pure; because the eye base is pure, the realm of space is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sense base of the eye is pure, and if the realm of space is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the realm of space is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, and the purity of the realm of space are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! Because omniscient wisdom is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the realm of space is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the sphere of form, and the purity of the realm of space are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure, the realm of space is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental objects (dharmāyatana), and the purity of the realm of space (ākāśadhātu) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the space-element is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the eye-element is pure, and if the space-element is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the form element, the eye-consciousness element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure; because the form element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, the space element is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowing and the purity of everything from the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, and the purity of the realm of space, are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the realm of space is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the ear element is pure, and if the space element is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of auditory consciousness, auditory contact, and the various feelings produced with auditory contact as condition are pure; because the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with auditory contact as condition are pure, the sphere of space (ākāśadhātu) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the sphere of sound (*śabdadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the sphere of space (*ākāśadhātu*), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the nose-element is pure; because the nose-element is pure, the space-element is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the nose-element, and the purity of the space-element, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the space element is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, and the purity of the space element, are non-dual; they are not two, not divided, not distinct, and not separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the space-element is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the tongue element, or the purity of the space element, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the space-element is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and the purity of the space element, are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, the space element is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the realm of the body is pure, and if the realm of space is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as condition are pure, the space-element is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the various feelings arising with the body as the condition for contact, up to the element of tangibility, as well as the purity of the realm of space, are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the intentionality of the knowledge of all modes is pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the space-element is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the mind-element is pure, and if the space-element is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are pure; because the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are pure, the space-element is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, and the purity of the realm of space are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the realm of space is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the earth element is pure, and if the space element is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the realm of empty space (ākāśadhātu) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, as well as the purity of the realm of empty space, are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the realm of space is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the light of wisdom, or the purity of the realm of space, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the realm of space is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of everything from formative activities through aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, and the purity of the realm of space are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, the realm of space is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the perfection of generosity, and the purity of the realm of space are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, the realm of space (ākāśadhātu) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom, and the purity of the realm of space are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the realm of space is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if internal emptiness is pure, and if the realm of space is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*) is pure, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure. Because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure, the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of outer emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature (abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā), and the purity of the realm of space are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
