“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure. Why is this?
The purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four dhyānas, and the purity of the noble truth of suffering are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and inseparable.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, and the purity of the noble truth of suffering are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eight liberations, or the purity of the noble truth of suffering, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the eight bases of mastery (abhibhvāyatana), the nine successive attainments (anupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (kṛtsnāyatana) are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the noble truth of suffering (duḥkha-āryasatya) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the eight bases of mastery (aṣṭavimokṣa), the nine successive attainments (navānupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (daśakṛtsnāyatana), as well as the purity of the noble truth of suffering (duḥkhasatyāryasatya), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four applications of mindfulness are pure; because the four applications of mindfulness are pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the same as the purity of the four applications of mindfulness and the purity of the noble truth of suffering, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path are pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path, as well as the purity of the noble truth of suffering, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.

"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, and the purity of the noble truth of suffering are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the gateways of liberation—signlessness (animitta) and wishlessness (apraṇihita)—are pure; because the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are pure, the noble truth of suffering (duḥkha-āryasatya) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, and the purity of the noble truth of suffering are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not severed.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, and the purity of the noble truth of suffering are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the five eyes, or the purity of the noble truth of suffering, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the six supernormal powers (ṣaḍabhijñā) are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, the noble truth of suffering (duḥkha-āryasatya) is pure. Why is this?

Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the six supernormal powers, or the purity of the noble truth of suffering, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, and if it is the purity of the noble truth of suffering, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and the purity of the noble truth of suffering are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of the noble truth of suffering are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the state of constant abiding in equanimity is pure; because the state of constant abiding in equanimity is pure, the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the state of constant equanimity, or the purity of the noble truth of suffering, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all-knowledge is pure; because all-knowledge is pure, the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure. Why is that?

The purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all-knowledge, and the purity of the noble truth of suffering are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.

Because the knowledge of all-knowledge is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects, and the purity of the noble truth of suffering are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all dharanī-doors are pure; because all dharanī-doors are pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of all gateways of dhāraṇī (*dhāraṇīmukha*), and the purity of the noble truth of suffering (*duḥkhasatyāryasatya*) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all gateways to meditative concentration are pure; because all gateways to meditative concentration are pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all doors of samādhi, and the purity of the noble truth of suffering are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because omniscience is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, and the purity of the noble truth of suffering are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure; because the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the fruit of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship, and the purity of the noble truth of suffering, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of the noble truth of suffering are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of the noble truth of suffering are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the unsurpassed perfect enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unsurpassed perfect enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, and the purity of the noble truth of suffering are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the noble truth of the origin [of suffering] is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if form is pure, and if the noble truth of the origin is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the noble truth of the origin of suffering is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowing, the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, and the purity of the noble truth of origination, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-base is pure; because the eye-base is pure, the noble truth of origination is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sense base of the eye is pure, and if the noble truth of origination is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the noble truth of origination is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, and the purity of the noble truth of origination are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the noble truth of origination is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the sense-base of form, and the purity of the noble truth of origination are non-dual, undivided, distinctless, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena are pure, the noble truth of the origin of suffering is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena (dharmāyatana), as well as the purity of the noble truth of origination (samudayasatya), are non-dual; they are not two, they are undivided, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the noble truth of the origin is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the eye-element is pure, and if the noble truth of origination is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the form element (rūpadhātu), the eye-consciousness element (cakṣurvijñānadhātu), eye-contact (cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa), and the various feelings (vedanā) produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure; because the form element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, the noble truth of origination (samudayasatya) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the form realm (rūpadhātu) down to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the noble truth of origination (samudayasatya), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the noble truth of origination is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ear-element, and the purity of the noble truth of origination are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of auditory consciousness, auditory contact, and all feelings produced with auditory contact as condition are pure; because the sphere of sound up to all feelings produced with auditory contact as condition are pure, the Noble Truth of Origination is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the sphere of sound, up to and including the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, and the purity of the noble truth of origination, are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the nose element is pure; because the nose element is pure, the noble truth of origination is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the nose element, and the purity of the noble truth of origination are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous; therefore they are one.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the fragrance element (gandhadhātu), the nose-consciousness element (ghrāṇavijñānadhātu), nose-contact (ghrāṇasparśa), and the various feelings (vedanā) produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the noble truth of origination (samudayasatyāryasatya) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the fragrance-element up to the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition, and the purity of the noble truth of origination, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the noble truth of origination is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the tongue element, and the purity of the noble truth of origination are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the Noble Truth of Origination is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the taste element, up to and including the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and the purity of the noble truth of origination, are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, the noble truth of origination is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the body element, and the purity of the noble truth of origination are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the Noble Truth of Origination is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) and the purity of the various feelings arising with the body as the basis and tangibles as the condition—up to the touch element—and the purity of the noble truth of origination (*samudayasatya*), are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are distinct, and they are not separate.
“Subhūti! Because the intention for the purity of all-knowledge is pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the noble truth of the origin [of suffering] is pure. Why is this?
The purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the mind-element, and the purity of the noble truth of origination are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the dharma-element, the mental consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are pure; because the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are pure, the noble truth of origination is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of everything from the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition, and the purity of the noble truth of origination, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the noble truth of the origin [of suffering] is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the earth element, and the purity of the noble truth of origination are non-dual, without division, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the noble truth of the origin [of suffering] is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, as well as the purity of the noble truth of origination, are non-dual, without division, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the path is pure; because the path is pure, the noble truth of the origin is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, if the purity of non-arising, and if the purity of the noble truth of the origin are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, volitional formations (saṃskāra), consciousness (vijñāna), name-and-form (nāmarūpa), the six sense bases (ṣaḍāyatana), contact (sparśa), feeling (vedanā), craving (tṛṣṇā), clinging (upādāna), becoming (bhava), birth (jāti), and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the noble truth of origination (samudayasatya) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, as well as the purity of the noble truth of origination, are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of giving is pure; because the perfection of giving is pure, the noble truth of the origin [of suffering] is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the perfection of generosity, and the purity of the noble truth of origination are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, the noble truth of the origin [of suffering] is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom, as well as the purity of the noble truth of origination, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the noble truth of the origin [of suffering] is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of internal emptiness, and the purity of the noble truth of origination are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*) is pure, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, emptiness of all phenomena, unobtainable emptiness, non-existence emptiness, intrinsic nature emptiness, and non-existence-intrinsic-nature emptiness are pure. Because external emptiness up to non-existence-intrinsic-nature emptiness are pure, the noble truth of origination is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from external emptiness up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence (abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā), as well as the purity of the noble truth of origination (samudayasatya), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the noble truth of the origin [of suffering] is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of suchness, and the purity of the noble truth of origination are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), the non-falsity of phenomena (avitathatā), the unalterability of phenomena (ananyathābhāvatā), equality (samatā), the state beyond birth (anupapattitva), the fixedness of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu) are pure; because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the noble truth of the origin of suffering (samudayasatyam) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the dharma-realm, up to the inconceivable realm, and the purity of the noble truth of origination, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure; because the noble truth of suffering is pure, the noble truth of the origin of suffering is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the noble truth of suffering, and the purity of the noble truth of the origin [of suffering], these two are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the noble truth of cessation and the noble truth of the path are pure; because the noble truth of cessation and the noble truth of the path are pure, the noble truth of origination is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the noble truth of cessation, the noble truth of the path, and the noble truth of origination, because they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the noble truth of the origin [of suffering] is pure. Why is that?
The purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four dhyānas, and the purity of the noble truth of origination are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are pure, the noble truth of the origin is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, and the purity of the noble truth of origination are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the noble truth of the origin of suffering is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eight liberations, and the purity of the noble truth of origination are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the eight bases of mastery (abhibhvāyatana), the nine successive attainments (anupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (kṛtsnāyatana) are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the noble truth of the origin (samudayasatya) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases, and the purity of the noble truth of origination, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure; because the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, the noble truth of the origin is pure. Why is this?

The purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, and the purity of the noble truth of origination are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and inseparable.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, the noble truth of the origin is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path, as well as the purity of the noble truth of origination, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the noble truth of the origin [of suffering] is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, and the purity of the noble truth of origination are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the gateways of liberation of signlessness (animitta) and wishlessness (apraṇihita) are pure; because the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure, the noble truth of origination (samudayasatya) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the gates of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—and the purity of the noble truth of origination are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the noble truth of origination is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, and the purity of the noble truth of the origin [of suffering] are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle Two Hundred and Sixty-Three. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter Thirty-Four, "Difficult to Believe and Understand," Section Eighty-Three. "Subhūti!

Because the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*) is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the noble truth of the origin of suffering (*samudayasatya*) is pure. Why is this?

Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the five eyes, or the purity of the noble truth of the origin of suffering, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not separate.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure, the noble truth of cessation is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of the noble truth of cessation are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, the noble truth of cessation is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, and the purity of the noble truth of cessation are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the Noble Truth of the Path is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if form is pure, and if the noble truth of the path is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the Noble Truth of the Path is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, and the purity of the noble truth of the path are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-base is pure; because the eye-base is pure, the noble truth of the path is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sense base of the eye is pure, and if the noble truth of the path is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the Noble Truth of the Path is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the sense bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, and the purity of the noble truths of the path are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the noble truth of the path is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the sense-base of form, and the purity of the noble truth of the path are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure, the Noble Truth of the Path is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena (dharmāyatana), and the purity of the noble truth of the path are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the Noble Truth of the Path is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the eye-element is pure, and if the noble truth of the path is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the form realm (rūpadhātu), the eye-consciousness realm (cakṣurvijñānadhātu), eye-contact (cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa), and the various feelings (vedanā) produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure; because the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, the Noble Truth of the Path (mārgasatya) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the form realm (rūpadhātu) up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, and the purity of the noble truth of the path, are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.
"Subhūti! Because omniscient wisdom is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the noble truth of the path is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ear-element, and the purity of the noble truth of the path are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of auditory consciousness, auditory contact, and all feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of sound up to all feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure, the Noble Truth of the Path is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the sphere of sound (*śabdadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, and the purity of the noble truth of the path, are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the nose-element is pure; because the nose-element is pure, the Noble Truth of the Path is pure. Why is this?
The purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the nose element, and the purity of the noble truth of the path are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the fragrance element (gandhadhātu), the nose-consciousness element (ghrāṇavijñānadhātu), nose-contact (ghrāṇasparśa), and the various feelings (vedanā) produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the Noble Truth of the Path (mārgasatya) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the various feelings produced with the nose-contact as condition—extending from the realm of fragrance up to the noble truth of the path—are non-dual; they are not two, they are not distinct, and there is no division between them.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the noble truth of the path is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the tongue element, and the purity of the noble truth of the path are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the Noble Truth of the Path is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the taste element (*rasadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and the purity of the noble truth of the path (*mārgasatya*), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because omniscient wisdom is pure, the body-element is pure; because the body-element is pure, the noble truth of the path is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the body element is pure, and if the noble truth of the path is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the Noble Truth of the Path is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the various feelings arising with the body as the basis and contact as the condition—up to the touch-object (spraṣṭavyadhātu)—and the purity of the Noble Truth of the Path are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are distinct from one another, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! Because the intentionality of the knowledge of all modes is pure, the mental faculty is pure; because the mental faculty is pure, the Noble Truth of the Path is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the mental constituent, and the purity of the noble truth of the path are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the dharma-element, the mental consciousness-element, mental contact, and the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition are pure; because the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition are pure, the Noble Truth of the Path is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of everything from the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, and the purity of the noble truth of the path, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the Noble Truth of the Path is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the earth element, and the purity of the noble truth of the path are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the Noble Truth of the Path is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, as well as the purity of the noble truth of the path, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the noble truth of the path is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the light of non-arising, or the purity of the noble truth of the path—these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the Noble Truth of the Path is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, as well as the purity of the noble truth of the path, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, the noble truth of the path is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the perfection of generosity (dānapāramitā), and the purity of the noble truth of the path are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, the noble truth of the path is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom, and the purity of the noble truth of the path are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the noble truth of the path is pure. Why is this?

The purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of internal emptiness, and the purity of the noble truth of the path are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersal emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure; because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure, the Noble Truth of the Path is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from outer emptiness up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence, as well as the purity of the noble truths of the path, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the noble truth of the path is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of suchness, and the purity of the noble truth of the path are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), non-falsity (avitathatā), unalterability (ananyathābhāvatā), equality (samatā), the state beyond birth (anabhibhavatā), the fixedness of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu) are pure; because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the Noble Truth of the Path is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, and the purity of the noble truth of the path are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure; because the noble truth of suffering is pure, the noble truth of the path is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the noble truth of suffering is pure, and if the noble truth of the path is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the noble truth of the origin and the noble truth of cessation are pure; because the noble truths of the origin and cessation are pure, the noble truth of the path is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, or the purity of the noble truths of origination and cessation, or the purity of the noble truth of the path, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the noble truths of the path are pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four dhyānas, and the purity of the noble truths are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, the noble truth of the path is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, and the purity of the noble truth of the path are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the noble truth of the path is pure. Why is this?
The purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eight liberations, and the purity of the noble truth of the path are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the eight bases of mastery (abhibhvāyatana), the nine successive attainments (anupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (kṛtsnāyatana) are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the noble truth of the path (mārgasatya) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the eight bases of mastery (aṣṭavimokṣa), the nine successive attainments (navānupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (daśakṛtsnāyatana), as well as the purity of the noble truth of the path (mārgasatya), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four applications of mindfulness are pure; because the four applications of mindfulness are pure, the noble truth of the path is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four applications of mindfulness, and the purity of the noble truths of the path are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eight branches of the noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eight branches of the noble path are pure, the noble truth of the path is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path, as well as the purity of the noble truth of the path, are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the gateway to liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the gateway to liberation that is emptiness is pure, the noble truth of the path is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of the gateway of liberation that is emptiness (*śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha*), and the purity of the noble truth of the path (*mārga-āryasatya*) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are pure; because the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are pure, the noble truth of the path is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, and the purity of the noble truth of the path are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the noble truth of the path is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, and the purity of the noble truth of the path are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle Two Hundred and Sixty-Four. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. First Division, Chapter Thirty-Four, Part Eighty-Four: "Difficult to Believe and Understand. "Subhūti!..."
Because the knowledge of all modes of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the noble truth of the path is pure. Why is this?

Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience, the purity of the five eyes, or the purity of the noble truth of the path, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the six supernormal powers (ṣaḍabhijñā) are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, the noble truth of the path (mārgasatya) is pure. Why is this?

Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the six supernormal powers, or the purity of the noble truth of the path, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, the noble truth of the path is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, and the purity of the noble truth of the path are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four fearlessnesses (vaiśāradya), the four analytical knowledges (pratisaṃvid), great loving-kindness (mahāmaitrī), great compassion (mahākaruṇā), great sympathetic joy (mahāmuditā), great equanimity (mahopekṣā), and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (āveṇikabuddhadharma) are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, the noble truth of the path (mārgasatya) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and the purity of the noble truth of the path are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the noble truth of the path is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of the noble truth of the path are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the state of constant equanimity is pure; because the state of constant equanimity is pure, the Noble Truth of the Path is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the state of constant equanimity, and the purity of the noble truth of the path are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the knowledge of all things is pure; because the knowledge of all things is pure, the noble truth of the path is pure. Why is this?
The purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all-knowledge, and the purity of the noble truth of the path are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not severed.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, the noble truth of the path is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, and the purity of the noble truth of the path are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all dhāraṇī-doors are pure; because all dhāraṇī-doors are pure, the noble truth of the path is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of all dharani-doors, and the purity of the noble truths of the path are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure; because all doors of samādhi are pure, the noble truth of the path is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all doors of samādhi, and the purity of the noble truth of the path are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, the noble truth of the path is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, and the purity of the noble truth of the path are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are pure; because the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are pure, the noble truth of the path is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship, and the purity of the noble truth of the path are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure, the noble truth of the path is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of the noble truth of the path are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure, the Noble Truth of the Path is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of the noble truth of the path are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, the noble truth of the path is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, and the purity of the noble truth of the path are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the four dhyānas are pure. Why is this?
The purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of form, and the purity of the four dhyānas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the four dhyānas are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, and the purity of the four dhyānas are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye base is pure; because the eye base is pure, the four dhyānas are pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sense base of the eye is pure, and if the four dhyānas are pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the four dhyānas are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, as well as the purity of the four dhyānas, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the four dhyānas are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the sphere of form, and the purity of the four dhyānas, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena are pure; because the bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena are pure, the four dhyānas are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental objects, as well as the purity of the four dhyānas, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the four dhyānas are pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the eye-element is pure, and if the four dhyānas are pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the form realm (rūpadhātu), the eye-consciousness realm (cakṣurvijñānadhātu), eye-contact (cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa), and the various feelings (vedanā) produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure; because the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, the four dhyānas are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowing and the purity of everything from the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the four dhyānas, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the four dhyānas are pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ear-element, or the purity of the four dhyānas, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the sound element, the ear-consciousness element, auditory contact, and the various feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure; because the sound element up to the various feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure, the four dhyānas are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, and the purity of the four dhyānas, are non-dual; they are not two, they are not distinct, and they are not separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the nose element is pure; because the nose element is pure, the four dhyānas are pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the same as the purity of the nose element and the purity of the four dhyānas, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, and nose-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, are pure; because the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the four dhyānas are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the realm of fragrance up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the four dhyānas, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the tongue element is pure; because the tongue element is pure, the four dhyānas are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is such, and the purity of the tongue element is such, and the purity of the four dhyānas is such, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the four dhyānas are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the taste element, up to and including the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and the purity of the four dhyānas, are non-dual; they are not two, they are not distinct, and there is no division between them.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, the four dhyānas are pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the body element, and the purity of the four dhyānas, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the four dhyānas are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the various feelings arising with the body as the condition, from the element of tangibility up to [the element of mental phenomena], and the purity of the four dhyānas, are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are without distinction, and they are not separate.
“Subhūti! Because the intentionality of the knowledge of all modes is pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the four dhyānas are pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the mind-element, and the purity of the four dhyānas are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are pure; because the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are pure, the four dhyānas are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu) up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the four meditative concentrations (dhyāna), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the four dhyānas are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the same as the purity of the earth element and the purity of the four dhyānas, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the four dhyānas are pure.

Why is this? Because the purification of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purification of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, as well as the purification of the four dhyānas, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the four dhyānas are pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the light of wisdom, or the purity of the four dhyānas, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, volitional formations (saṃskāra), consciousness (vijñāna), name-and-form (nāmarūpa), the six sense bases (ṣaḍāyatana), contact (sparśa), feeling (vedanā), craving (tṛṣṇā), grasping (upādāna), becoming (bhava), birth (jāti), and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the four dhyānas are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from conditioned activities up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, as well as the purity of the four dhyānas, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of giving is pure; because the perfection of giving is pure, the four dhyānas are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the perfection of generosity, and the purity of the four meditative concentrations are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, the four dhyānas are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience and the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom, as well as the purity of the four dhyānas, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the four dhyānas are pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if inner emptiness is pure, and if the four dhyānas are pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, there is purity of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersal emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, emptiness of all phenomena, unapprehendable emptiness, non-existence emptiness, self-nature emptiness, and non-existence-of-self-nature emptiness. Because of the purity of external emptiness up to the purity of non-existence-of-self-nature emptiness, there is purity of the four dhyānas.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from outer emptiness (bahirdhā-śūnyatā) up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence (abhāvasvabhāva-śūnyatā), as well as the purity of the four dhyānas, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the four dhyānas are pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of suchness, and the purity of the four dhyānas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, non-alteration, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of empty space, and the inconceivable realm are pure; because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the four meditative concentrations are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, and the purity of the four dhyānas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure; because the noble truth of suffering is pure, the four dhyānas are pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the noble truth of suffering, and the purity of the four dhyānas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are pure, the four dhyānas are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path, and the purity of the four dhyānas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four immeasurables are pure; because the four immeasurables are pure, the four dhyānas are pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four immeasurables, or the purity of the four dhyānas, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four formless absorptions are pure; because the four formless absorptions are pure, the four dhyānas are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the same as the purity of the four formless attainments, and the purity of the four dhyānas, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the four dhyānas are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the eight liberations, and the purity of the four dhyānas, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the eight bases of mastery (abhibhvāyatana), the nine successive attainments (anupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (kṛtsnāyatana) are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the four dhyānas are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the eight bases of mastery (aṣṭavimokṣa), the nine successive attainments (navānupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (daśakṛtsnāyatana), as well as the purity of the four dhyānas, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four applications of mindfulness are pure; because the four applications of mindfulness are pure, the four dhyānas are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, and the purity of the four dhyānas, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, the four dhyānas are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the four right efforts, up to and including the eight branches of the noble path, as well as the purity of the four dhyānas, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the four dhyānas are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, and the purity of the four meditative concentrations are non-dual; they are not two, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the gateways to liberation of signlessness (animitta) and wishlessness (apraṇihita) are pure; because the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure, the four dhyānas are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, and the purity of the four dhyānas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the four meditative concentrations are pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva (daśabhūmi), and the purity of the four dhyānas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
