“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the four dhyānas are pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the five eyes, or the purity of the four dhyānas, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the six supernormal powers (ṣaḍabhijñā) are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, the four meditative concentrations (catvāri dhyānāni) are pure. Why is this?

Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the six supernormal powers, or the purity of the four meditative concentrations, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, the four dhyānas are pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, or the purity of the four dhyānas, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four fearlessnesses (vaiśāradya), the four analytical knowledges (pratisaṃvid), great loving-kindness (mahāmaitrī), great compassion (mahākaruṇā), great sympathetic joy (mahāmuditā), great equanimity (mahopekṣā), and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (āveṇikabuddhadharma) are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, the four dhyānas are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, as well as the purity of the four dhyānas, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the four dhyānas are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of the four dhyānas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not severed.
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the state of constant equanimity is pure; because the state of constant equanimity is pure, the four dhyānas are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is pure, and the purity of the state of constant equanimity is pure, and the purity of the four dhyānas are pure, because they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all-knowledge is pure; because all-knowledge is pure, the four dhyānas are pure. Why is this?
The purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all-knowledge, and the purity of the four dhyānas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, the four dhyānas are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, and the purity of the four dhyānas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all dharani-doors are pure; because all dharani-doors are pure, the four dhyanas are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors, and the purity of the four dhyānas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure; because all doors of samādhi are pure, the four dhyānas are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of all doors of samādhi, and the purity of the four dhyānas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, the four dhyānas are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the same as the purity of the fruit of stream-entry and the purity of the four dhyānas, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure; because the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure, the four dhyānas are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship, and the purity of the four dhyānas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, the four dhyānas are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of the four dhyānas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure, the four dhyānas are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of the four dhyānas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, the four dhyānas are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, and the purity of the four dhyānas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the four immeasurables are pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if form is pure, and if the four immeasurables are pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the four immeasurables are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, and the purity of the four immeasurables (catur-apramāṇa) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-base is pure; because the eye-base is pure, the four immeasurables are pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the sense base of the eye is pure, and if the four immeasurables are pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the four immeasurables are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, as well as the purity of the four immeasurables (catur-apramāṇa), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the four immeasurables are pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the sphere of form is pure, and if the four immeasurables are pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure; because the bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure, the four immeasurables are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental objects (dharmāyatana), as well as the purity of the four immeasurables (apramāṇa), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the four immeasurables are pure. Why is this?"

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eye-element, or the purity of the four immeasurables, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the form realm (rūpadhātu), the eye-consciousness realm (cakṣurvijñānadhātu), eye-contact (cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa), and the various feelings (vedanā) produced with eye-contact as condition are pure; because the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition are pure, the four immeasurables (catvāry apramāṇāni) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of everything from the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the four immeasurables, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the four immeasurables are pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the ear-element is pure, and if the four immeasurables are pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, and ear-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, are pure; because the sound-element up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure, the four immeasurables (catvāry apramāṇāni) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the realm of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, and the purity of the four immeasurables, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the nose element is pure; because the nose element is pure, the four immeasurables are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is such, and the purity of the nose element is such, and the purity of the four immeasurables is such, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the four immeasurables are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñājñāna*), the purity of the realm of fragrance up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, and the purity of the four immeasurables (*catur-apramāṇa*) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the four immeasurables are pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the tongue element is pure, and if the four immeasurables are pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the four immeasurables (catvāry apramāṇāni) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and the purity of the four immeasurables are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, the four immeasurables are pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the body element is pure, and if the four immeasurables are pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the four immeasurables are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience and the purity of the various feelings arising from contact with the element of touch, up to those arising with body-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the four immeasurables, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the intention for the purity of the knowledge of all modes is pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the four immeasurables are pure. Why is that?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the mental faculty, and the purity of the four immeasurables are non-dual, undivided, indistinguishable, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, mental contact, and the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition are pure; because the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition are pure, the four immeasurables (catur-apramāṇa) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of everything from the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, and the purity of the four immeasurables (*catur-apramāṇa*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the four immeasurables are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the earth element, and the purity of the four immeasurables are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the four immeasurables are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, as well as the purity of the four immeasurables, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-self is pure; because non-self is pure, the four immeasurables are pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the light of wisdom, or the purity of the four immeasurables, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, volitional formations (saṃskāra), consciousness (vijñāna), name-and-form (nāmarūpa), the six sense bases (ṣaḍāyatana), contact (sparśa), feeling (vedanā), craving (tṛṣṇā), grasping (upādāna), becoming (bhava), birth (jāti), and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the four immeasurables (catur-apramāṇa) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, as well as the purity of the four immeasurables, are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, the four immeasurables are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the perfection of generosity (dānapāramitā), and the purity of the four immeasurables (catvāry apramāṇāni) are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, the four immeasurables are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the perfections from ethical discipline up to the perfection of wisdom, as well as the purity of the four immeasurables, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the four immeasurables are pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if inner emptiness is pure, and if the four immeasurables are pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*) is pure, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena (*sarvadharmaśūnyatā*), the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure; because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure, the four immeasurables (*catur-apramāṇa*) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of everything from external emptiness up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence, as well as the purity of the four immeasurables, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the four immeasurables are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is such, and the purity of suchness is such, and the purity of the four immeasurables is such, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), the non-falsity of phenomena (avitathatā), the unchanging nature of phenomena (ananyathābhāvatā), the equality of phenomena (samatā), the state beyond arising (anirodhatā), the fixedness of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu) are pure; because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the four immeasurables (caturapramāṇa) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, and the purity of the four immeasurables are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure; because the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure, the four immeasurables are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the noble truth of suffering, and the purity of the four immeasurables are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure, the four immeasurables are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, and the purity of the four immeasurables are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the four immeasurables are pure. Why is this?"

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the same as the purity of the four dhyānas and the purity of the four immeasurables, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four formless absorptions are pure; because the four formless absorptions are pure, the four immeasurables are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the four formless absorptions, and the purity of the four immeasurables, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the four immeasurables are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is [identical to] the purity of the eight liberations, or the purity of the four immeasurables, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the eight bases of mastery (abhibhvāyatana), the nine successive attainments (anupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (kṛtsnāyatana) are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the four immeasurables (apramāṇa) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, the ten universal bases, and the four immeasurables are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure; because the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, the four immeasurables are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, and the purity of the four immeasurables, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, the four immeasurables are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, as well as the purity of the four immeasurables, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the four immeasurables are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowing, the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, and the purity of the four immeasurables are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñājñāna*) is pure, the gateways of liberation of signlessness (*animitta*) and wishlessness (*apraṇihita*) are pure; because the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure, the four immeasurables (*catur-apramāṇa*) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, and the purity of the four immeasurables are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the four immeasurables are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, and the purity of the four immeasurables are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle Two Hundred and Sixty-five. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter on Difficult to Believe and Understand, Thirty-fourth, Section Eighty-five. “Subhūti!

Because the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, the five eyes (*pañca-cakṣus*) are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the four immeasurables (*catvāry apramāṇāni*) are pure. Why is this?

Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the five eyes, or the purity of the four immeasurables, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the six supernormal powers (ṣaḍabhijñā) are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, the four immeasurables (catvāry apramāṇāni) are pure. Why is this?

Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the six supernormal powers, or the purity of the four immeasurables, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, the four immeasurables are pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, or the purity of the four immeasurables, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, the four immeasurables are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and the purity of the four immeasurables are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the four immeasurables are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of the four immeasurables are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the state of constant equanimity (upekṣā) is pure; because the state of constant equanimity is pure, the four immeasurables (apramāṇa) are pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the state of constant equanimity, or the purity of the four immeasurables, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the knowledge of all things is pure; because the knowledge of all things is pure, the four immeasurables are pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all-knowledge, or the purity of the four immeasurables, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all-knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, the four immeasurables (*catur-apramāṇa*) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path (mārgākārajñatā) and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā), and the purity of the four immeasurables (catur-apramāṇa) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all dhāraṇī gateways are pure; because all dhāraṇī gateways are pure, the four immeasurables are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors, and the purity of the four immeasurables are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure; because all doors of samādhi are pure, the four immeasurables are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all doors of samādhi, and the purity of the four immeasurables are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, the four immeasurables are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, and the purity of the four immeasurables, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are pure; because the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are pure, the four immeasurables are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship, and the purity of the four immeasurables (catur-apramāṇa) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure, the four immeasurables are pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of the four immeasurables are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure, the four immeasurables are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of the four immeasurables (catvāry apramāṇāni) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, the four immeasurables are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, and the purity of the four immeasurables are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the four formless attainments are pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if form is pure, and if the four formless absorptions are pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the four formless absorptions are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, and the purity of the four formless absorptions (ārūpyasamāpatti) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sense base of the eye is pure; because the sense base of the eye is pure, the four formless absorptions are pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sense base of the eye is pure, and if the four formless absorptions are pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the four formless absorptions are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) and the purity of the bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, as well as the purity of the four formless absorptions (ārūpyasamāpatti), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the four formless absorptions are pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the sphere of form is pure, and if the four formless attainments are pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena are pure; because the bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena are pure, the four formless absorptions are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental objects (dharmāyatana), as well as the purity of the four formless absorptions (ārūpyasamāpatti), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the four formless absorptions are pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the eye-element is pure, and if the four formless absorptions are pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the form realm (rūpadhātu), the eye-consciousness realm (cakṣurvijñānadhātu), eye-contact (cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa), and the various feelings (vedanā) produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure; because the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, the four formless attainments (ārūpyasamāpatti) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the form realm (rūpadhātu) up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the four formless attainments (ārūpyasamāpatti), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the four formless absorptions are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the same as the purity of the ear-element and the purity of the four formless absorptions, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of auditory consciousness, auditory contact, and the various feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure, the four formless absorptions (ārūpyasamāpatti) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of everything from the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the four formless absorptions, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the nose-element is pure; because the nose-element is pure, the four formless absorptions are pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the nose element is pure, and if the four formless absorptions are pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the four formless absorptions (ārūpyasamāpatti) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) and the purity of everything from the realm of fragrance up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, and the purity of the four formless absorptions, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the tongue element is pure; because the tongue element is pure, the four formless absorptions are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is such, and the purity of the tongue element is such, and the purity of the four formless absorptions are such, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the four formless absorptions (ārūpyasamāpatti) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of the taste element (*rasadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and the purity of the four formless attainments (*ārūpyasamāpatti*) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, the four formless absorptions are pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the body element is pure, and if the four formless absorptions are pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the four formless absorptions (ārūpyasamāpatti) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the various feelings arising with the body as the condition, from the element of tangibility up to the four formless attainments, are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! Because the intentionality of the knowledge of all modes is pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the four formless absorptions are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the mental faculty element, and the purity of the four formless absorptions are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, mind-contact, and the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition are pure; because the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition are pure, the four formless absorptions (ārūpyasamāpatti) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, and the purity of the four formless absorptions, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the four formless absorptions are pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the earth element, and the purity of the four formless absorptions are non-dual, undivided, indistinguishable, and inseparable.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the four formless absorptions are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, as well as the purity of the four formless absorptions, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-duality is pure; because non-duality is pure, the four formless absorptions are pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the light of wisdom, or the purity of the four formless absorptions, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, volitional formations (saṃskāra), consciousness (vijñāna), name-and-form (nāmarūpa), the six sense bases (ṣaḍāyatana), contact (sparśa), feeling (vedanā), craving (tṛṣṇā), grasping (upādāna), becoming (bhava), birth (jāti), and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the four formless absorptions (ārūpyasamāpatti) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, as well as the purity of the four formless concentrations, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of giving is pure; because the perfection of giving is pure, the four formless absorptions are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the perfection of generosity (dānapāramitā), and the purity of the four formless absorptions (ārūpyasamāpatti) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, the four formless absorptions (ārūpyasamāpatti) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), as well as the purity of the four formless absorptions (ārūpyasamādhi), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the four formless absorptions are pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of internal emptiness, or the purity of the four formless attainments, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure; because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure, the four formless absorptions (ārūpyasamāpatti) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from outer emptiness (bahirdhā-śūnyatā) up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence (abhāvasvabhāva-śūnyatā), as well as the purity of the four formless attainments (ārūpyasamāpatti), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the four formless absorptions are pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of suchness, and the purity of the four formless absorptions are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu) are pure; because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the four formless absorptions (ārūpyasamāpatti) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, and the purity of the four formless absorptions are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure; because the noble truth of suffering is pure, the four formless absorptions are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the noble truth of suffering, and the purity of the four formless absorptions are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure, the four formless absorptions (ārūpyasamādhi) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path, and the purity of the four formless absorptions (ārūpyasamāpatti) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the four formless absorptions are pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the four dhyānas, as well as the purity of the four formless attainments (ārūpyasamāpatti), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four immeasurables are pure; because the four immeasurables are pure, the four formless attainments are pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four immeasurables, or the purity of the four formless absorptions, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the four formless attainments are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eight liberations, and the purity of the four formless attainments are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the eight bases of mastery (abhibhvāyatana), the nine successive attainments (anupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (kṛtsnāyatana) are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the four formless attainments (ārūpyasamāpatti) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, the ten pervasive bases, and the four formless attainments are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure; because the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, the four formless absorptions are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness (smṛtyupasthāna), and the purity of the four formless absorptions (ārūpyasamāpatti) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, the four formless absorptions are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, as well as the purity of the four formless attainments, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the four formless absorptions are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness (śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha), and the purity of the four formless absorptions (ārūpyasamāpatti) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure; because the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure, the four formless absorptions are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, and the purity of the four formless absorptions (ārūpyasamāpatti) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the four formless absorptions are pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva (daśabhūmi), and the purity of the four formless absorptions (ārūpyasamādhi) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the four formless absorptions are pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purification of the knowledge of all modes, the purification of the five eyes, or the purification of the four formless absorptions, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, the six supernormal powers (*ṣaḍabhijñā*) are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, the four formless attainments (*catasra ārūpyasamāpattayaḥ*) are pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the six supernormal powers, or the purity of the four formless absorptions, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, the four formless absorptions are pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, and the purity of the four formless absorptions are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, the four formless absorptions are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, as well as the purity of the four formless absorptions (ārūpyasamādhi), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the four formless absorptions are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of the four formless absorptions are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the state of constant equanimity is pure; because the state of constant equanimity is pure, the four formless absorptions are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is so, and the purity of the state of constant equanimity is so, and the purity of the four formless absorptions is so, it is because they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all-knowledge is pure; because all-knowledge is pure, the four formless absorptions are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all-knowledge, and the purity of the four formless absorptions are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, the four formless absorptions are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, and the purity of the four formless absorptions are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all dhāraṇī-doors are pure; because all dhāraṇī-doors are pure, the four formless absorptions are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all dharani-doors, and the purity of the four formless absorptions are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure; because all doors of samādhi are pure, the four formless attainments are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all doors of samādhi, and the purity of the four formless absorptions are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, the four formless absorptions are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, and the purity of the four formless absorptions are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the fruit of arhatship are pure; because the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the fruit of arhatship are pure, the four formless absorptions are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship, and the purity of the four formless attainments (ārūpyasamāpatti) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, the four formless absorptions are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of the four formless absorptions are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure, the four formless absorptions are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of the four formless absorptions (ārūpyasamāpatti) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the unexcelled, perfect enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unexcelled, perfect enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, the four formless absorptions are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, and the purity of the four formless absorptions are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the eight liberations are pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if form is pure, and if the eight liberations are pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the eight liberations are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, and the purity of the eight liberations (aṣṭavimokṣa) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye base is pure; because the eye base is pure, the eight liberations are pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sense base of the eye is pure, and if the eight liberations are pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the eight liberations are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, and the purity of the eight liberations (aṣṭavimokṣa) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the eight liberations are pure. Why is this?

The purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the sense-field of form, and the purity of the eight liberations are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure, the eight liberations are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, and the purity of the eight liberations are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the eight liberations are pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the eye-element is pure, and if the eight liberations are pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the form realm (rūpadhātu), the eye-consciousness realm (cakṣurvijñānadhātu), eye-contact (cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa), and the various feelings (vedanā) produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure; because the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, the eight liberations (aṣṭavimokṣa) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of everything from the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the eight liberations, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the eight liberations are pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the ear-element is pure, and if the eight liberations are pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of auditory consciousness, and ear-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, are pure; because the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure, the eight liberations (aṣṭavimokṣa) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, and the purity of the eight liberations, are non-dual; they are not two, they are not distinct, and there is no division between them.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the nose-element is pure; because the nose-element is pure, the eight liberations are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is identical to the purity of the nose element and the purity of the eight liberations, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the eight liberations (aṣṭavimokṣa) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of the realm of fragrance up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, and the purity of the eight liberations (*aṣṭavimokṣa*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the tongue element is pure; because the tongue element is pure, the eight liberations are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is [identical to] the purity of the tongue-element, and the purity of the eight liberations, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the eight liberations (aṣṭavimokṣa) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience, the purity of the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and the purity of the eight liberations are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, the eight liberations are pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the body-element is pure, and if the eight liberations are pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the eight liberations (aṣṭavimokṣa) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the various feelings arising with the body as the condition, from the element of tangibles up to [the feeling] produced with body-contact as the condition, and the purity of the eight liberations, are non-dual; they are not two, they are not distinct, and there is no division between them.
“Subhūti! Because the intentionality of the knowledge of all modes is pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the eight liberations are pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the mental faculty, and the purity of the eight liberations are non-dual, undivided, indistinguishable, and inseparable.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness element, mental contact, and the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition are pure; because the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition are pure, the eight liberations are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) and the purity of everything from the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition, and the purity of the eight liberations (*aṣṭavimokṣa*), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the eight liberations are pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the earth element is pure, and if the eight liberations are pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the eight liberations are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, as well as the purity of the eight liberations, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the eight liberations are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is such, and the purity of the light of wisdom is such, and the purity of the eight liberations is such, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct from one another, and inseparable.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, volitional formations (saṃskāra), consciousness (vijñāna), name-and-form (nāmarūpa), the six sense bases (ṣaḍāyatana), contact (sparśa), feeling (vedanā), craving (tṛṣṇā), grasping (upādāna), becoming (bhava), birth (jāti), and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair (jarāmaraṇa-śoka-parideva-duḥkha-daurmanasyopāyāsa) are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the eight liberations (aṣṭavimokṣa) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from conditioned formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, as well as the purity of the eight liberations (aṣṭavimokṣa), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of giving is pure; because the perfection of giving is pure, the eight liberations are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the perfection of generosity, and the purity of the eight liberations are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, the eight liberations (aṣṭavimokṣa) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom, as well as the purity of the eight liberations, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the eight liberations are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the same as the purity of internal emptiness and the purity of the eight liberations, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, there is the purity of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence. Because there is the purity of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, there is the purity of the eight liberations (aṣṭavimokṣa).

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of outer emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature (*abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā*), and the purity of the eight liberations (*aṣṭavimokṣa*) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the eight liberations are pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of suchness, and the purity of the eight liberations are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), non-falsity (avitathatā), non-alteration (ananyathābhāva), sameness (samatā), the state beyond birth (anabhibhūtatā), the fixedness of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu) are pure; because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the eight liberations (aṣṭavimokṣa) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, and the purity of the eight liberations are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure; because the noble truth of suffering is pure, the eight liberations are pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the noble truth of suffering is pure, and if the eight liberations are pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are pure, the eight liberations (aṣṭavimokṣa) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path, and the purity of the eight liberations are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the eight liberations are pure. Why is this?
The purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four dhyānas, and the purity of the eight liberations are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are pure, the eight liberations are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, and the purity of the eight liberations are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight bases of mastery are pure; because the eight bases of mastery are pure, the eight liberations are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is such, and the purity of the eight bases of mastery and the purity of the eight liberations are such, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the nine successive attainments (navānupūrvavihārasamāpatti) and the ten totalities (daśakṛtsnāyatana) are pure; because the nine successive attainments and the ten totalities are pure, the eight liberations (aṣṭavimokṣa) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the nine successive attainments and the ten totalities, and the purity of the eight liberations are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four applications of mindfulness are pure; because the four applications of mindfulness are pure, the eight liberations are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, and the purity of the eight liberations, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, the eight liberations are pure.
