Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path, and the purity of the ten spheres of totality are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the ten spheres of totality are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the same as the purity of the four dhyānas, and the purity of the ten totalities, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are pure, the ten spheres of totality are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the four immeasurables (apramāṇa) and the four formless attainments (ārūpyasamāpatti), and the purity of the ten totalities (kṛtsnāyatana) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the ten spheres of totality are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is such, and the purity of the eight liberations is such, and the purity of the ten totalities is such, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight bases of mastery and the nine successive attainments are pure; because the eight bases of mastery and the nine successive attainments are pure, the ten totalities are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the eight bases of mastery (aṣṭavimokṣa), the nine successive attainments (navānupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (daśakṛtsnāyatana) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure; because the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, the ten spheres of totality are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness and the purity of the ten totalities, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, the ten spheres of totality (daśakṛtsnāyatana) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) and the purity of the four right efforts (*samyakprahāṇa*) up to the eightfold noble path (*āryāṣṭāṅgamārga*), as well as the purity of the ten spheres of totality (*daśakṛtsnāyatana*), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the ten spheres of totality are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, and the purity of the ten spheres of totality are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñājñāna*) is pure, the gates of liberation of signlessness (*animitta*) and wishlessness (*apraṇihita*) are pure; because the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure, the ten spheres of totality (*daśakṛtsnāyatana*) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, and the purity of the ten universal bases (daśakṛtsnāyatana) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the ten spheres of totality are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, and the purity of the ten spheres of totality are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the ten spheres of totality are pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the five eyes, or the purity of the ten spheres of totality, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the six supernormal knowledges (ṣaḍabhijñā) are pure; because the six supernormal knowledges are pure, the ten spheres of totality (daśakṛtsnāyatana) are pure. Why is this?

Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the six supernormal knowledges, or the purity of the ten spheres of totality, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, the ten spheres of totality are pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, and if the ten spheres of totality are pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, the ten spheres of totality (daśakṛtsnāyatana) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and the purity of the ten spheres of totality are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the ten spheres of totality are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of the ten totalities are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the state of constant abiding in equanimity is pure; because the state of constant abiding in equanimity is pure, the ten spheres of totality are pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, if the purity of the state of constant equanimity, and if the purity of the ten totalities are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the knowledge of all things is pure; because the knowledge of all things is pure, the ten spheres of totality are pure. Why is this?

The purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all-knowledge, and the purity of the ten spheres of totality are non-dual; they are not divided into two, are not distinct, and are not discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, the ten spheres of totality are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path (mārgākārajñatā) and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā), and the purity of the ten spheres of totality (daśakṛtsnāyatana) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all dhāraṇī-doors are pure; because all dhāraṇī-doors are pure, the ten spheres of totality are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors, and the purity of the ten spheres of totality are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure; because all doors of samādhi are pure, the ten spheres of totality are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of all doors of samādhi, and the purity of the ten spheres of totality (daśakṛtsnāyatana) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, the ten spheres of totality are pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, and the purity of the ten universal bases are non-dual, undivided, indistinguishable, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the fruit of arhatship are pure; because the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the fruit of arhatship are pure, the ten spheres of totality are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience, the purity of the fruits of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat, and the purity of the ten spheres of totality are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, the ten spheres of totality are pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of the ten spheres of totality are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure, the ten spheres of totality are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of the ten spheres of totality (daśakṛtsnāyatana) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, the ten spheres of totality are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, and the purity of the ten spheres of totality are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if form is pure, and if the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not severed.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, and the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness are non-dual; they are not two, they are not distinct, and they are not separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sense base of the eye is pure; because the sense base of the eye is pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sense base of the eye is pure, and if the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the four foundations of mindfulness (smṛtyupasthāna) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, as well as the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, are non-dual; they are not two, they are not distinct, and they are not separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the same as the purity of the sense-sphere of form and the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure; because the bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena (dharmāyatana), as well as the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness (smṛtyupasthāna), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eye-element, or the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the form element (rūpadhātu), the eye-consciousness element (cakṣurvijñānadhātu), eye-contact (cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa), and the various feelings (vedanā) produced with eye-contact as condition are pure; because the form element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition are pure, the four foundations of mindfulness (catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the form realm (rūpadhātu) up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness (smṛtyupasthāna), are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and inseparable.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the ear-element, and the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, and ear-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, are pure; because the sound-element up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure, the four foundations of mindfulness (catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, and the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness (catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni), are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the nose element is pure; because the nose element is pure, the four applications of mindfulness are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the nose element, and the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness are non-dual, without division, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the four foundations of mindfulness (smṛtyupasthāna) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purification of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) and the purification of everything from the realm of fragrance (*gandhadhātu*) up to the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with nose-contact as a condition, as well as the purification of the four foundations of mindfulness (*smṛtyupasthāna*), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the tongue element, and the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the four foundations of mindfulness (smṛtyupasthāna) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the taste-element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body-element is pure; because the body-element is pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the body element is pure, and if the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the four foundations of mindfulness (catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the sensations produced with the body as the basis and contact as the condition—from the element of touch up to those sensations—are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the intentionality of the knowledge of all modes is pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the four applications of mindfulness are pure. Why is that?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the mental faculty, and the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness are non-dual, undivided, distinctless, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, as well as mental contact and the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition, are pure; because the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition are pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) and the purity of everything from the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness (*smṛtyupasthāna*), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the earth element, and the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the four foundations of mindfulness (catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, and the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness (catur-smṛtyupasthāna) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the four applications of mindfulness are pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of non-duality, or the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, volitional formations (saṃskāra), consciousness (vijñāna), name-and-form (nāmarūpa), the six sense bases (ṣaḍāyatana), contact (sparśa), feeling (vedanā), craving (tṛṣṇā), grasping (upādāna), becoming (bhava), birth (jāti), and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the four foundations of mindfulness (catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from conditioned activities up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, as well as the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, are non-dual; they are not two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of giving is pure; because the perfection of giving is pure, the four applications of mindfulness are pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the perfection of giving (dānapāramitā), and the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness (catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the perfection of ethical discipline up to the perfection of wisdom, as well as the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if internal emptiness is pure, and if the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, there is purity of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature; because of the purity of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, there is purity of the four foundations of mindfulness (smṛtyupasthāna).

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from external emptiness up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence (abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā), as well as the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness (smṛtyupasthāna), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the four applications of mindfulness are pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of suchness, and the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu) are pure; because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the four foundations of mindfulness (catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) up to the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*), and the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness (*smṛtyupasthāna*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure; because the noble truth of suffering is pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the noble truth of suffering, and the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path, and the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the same as the purity of the four dhyānas and the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, and the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure. Why is that?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eight liberations, and the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, the eight bases of mastery (*abhibhvāyatana*), the nine successive attainments (*anupūrvavihārasamāpatti*), and the ten totalities (*kṛtsnāyatana*) are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the four foundations of mindfulness (*smṛtyupasthāna*) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the eight bases of mastery (aṣṭavimokṣa), the nine successive attainments (navānupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (daśakṛtsnāyatana), as well as the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness (catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four right endeavors are pure; because the four right endeavors are pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is such, and the purity of the four right efforts is such, and the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness is such, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eight branches of the noble path are pure; because the four bases of psychic power up to the eight branches of the noble path are pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the four bases of psychic power up to the eightfold noble path, as well as the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, and the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the gateways to liberation of signlessness (animitta) and wishlessness (apraṇihita) are pure; because the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure, the foundations of mindfulness (smṛtyupasthāna) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, and the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the four applications of mindfulness are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, and the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the five eyes, or the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the six supernormal powers (ṣaḍabhijñā) are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, the four foundations of mindfulness (catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni) are pure. Why is this?

Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the six supernormal powers, or the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, or the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four fearlessnesses (vaiśāradya), the four analytical knowledges (pratisaṃvid), great loving-kindness (maitrī), great compassion (karuṇā), great sympathetic joy (muditā), great equanimity (upekṣā), and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (āveṇika-buddhadharma) are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, the four foundations of mindfulness (smṛtyupasthāna) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and inseparable.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the state of constant abiding in equanimity is pure; because the state of constant abiding in equanimity is pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is such, and if the purity of the state of constant equanimity is such, and if the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness is such, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the knowledge of all is pure; because the knowledge of all is pure, the four applications of mindfulness are pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all-knowledge, and the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, and the purity of the four applications of mindfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all dharanī-doors are pure; because all dharanī-doors are pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors, and the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure; because all doors of samādhi are pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all doors of samādhi, and the purity of the four applications of mindfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is [identical to] the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, and the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship is pure; because the fruit of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship is pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship, and the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness (catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, the four applications of mindfulness are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and inseparable.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure, the four applications of mindfulness are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, the four applications of mindfulness are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi) of the Buddhas, and the purity of the four applications of mindfulness (catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the four right efforts are pure. Why is this?"

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is such, and the purity of form is such, and the purity of the four right efforts are such, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are pure, the four right endeavors are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, and the purity of the four right efforts (samyakprahāṇa) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye base is pure; because the eye base is pure, the four right efforts are pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the sense base of the eye, and the purity of the four right efforts are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the four right endeavors are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, as well as the purity of the four right efforts (samyakprahāṇa), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sense-field of form is pure; because the sense-field of form is pure, the four right endeavors are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the sphere of form, and the purity of the four right efforts, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena are pure, the four right efforts are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena (dharmāyatana), and the purity of the four right efforts (samyakprahāṇa) are non-dual; they are not two, they are not distinct, and there is no separation between them.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle Two Hundred and Sixty-Eight. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter Thirty-Four, "Difficult to Believe and Understand," Section Eighty-Eight. "Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes of being (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, the eye-element (*cakṣurdhātu*) is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the four right efforts (*samyakprahāṇa*) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of being, the purity of the eye-element, and the purity of the four right efforts are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the form element (rūpadhātu), the eye-consciousness element (cakṣurvijñānadhātu), eye-contact (cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa), and the various feelings (vedanā) produced with eye-contact as condition are pure; because the form element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition are pure, the four right efforts (samyakprahāṇa) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the form realm (rūpadhātu) down to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the four right efforts (samyakprahāṇa), are non-dual; they are not two, they are not distinct, and there is no separation between them.
“Subhūti! Because omniscient wisdom is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the four right efforts are pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ear-element, and the purity of the four right endeavors are non-dual, undivided, distinctless, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of auditory consciousness, and auditory contact, as well as the various feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition, are pure; because the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure, the four right endeavors (samyakprahāṇa) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) and the purity of the realm of sound (*śabdadhātu*) up to the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with ear-contact as a condition, and the purity of the four right efforts (*samyakprahāṇa*), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the nose element is pure; because the nose element is pure, the four right efforts are pure. Why is that?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is such, and the purity of the nose element is such, and the purity of the four right endeavors is such, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the four right efforts (samyakprahāṇa) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the realm of fragrance up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, and the purity of the four right efforts, are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are without distinction, and they are without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the four right efforts are pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the tongue element, and the purity of the four right endeavors are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the four right efforts (samyakprahāṇa) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of everything from the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the four right efforts, are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are without distinction, and they are without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, the four right efforts are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the body element, and the purity of the four right endeavors, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the four right efforts (samyakprahāṇa) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) and the purity of the sensations produced with the body as the basis for contact, up to the sphere of tangibles (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*), and the purity of the four right efforts (*samyakprahāṇa*) are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are not distinct, and they are not separate.

“Subhūti! Because the intention for the purification of the knowledge of all modes is pure, the mind-element is purified; because the mind-element is purified, the four right efforts are purified. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the mind-element, and the purity of the four right endeavors are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, and mind-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition, are pure; because the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition are pure, the four right efforts are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of everything from the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the four right efforts, are non-dual, not two distinct parts, without differentiation, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the four right endeavors are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the earth element, and the purity of the four right efforts, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the four right endeavors are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, as well as the purity of the four right efforts (samyakprahāṇa), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the four right endeavors are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the purity of the light of wisdom is pure, and if the purity of the four right endeavors is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the four right efforts are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from formations up to old age, death, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, as well as the purity of the four right efforts (samyakprahāṇa), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, the four right endeavors are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the perfection of generosity, and the purity of the four right efforts are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, the four right endeavors are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the precepts up to the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), as well as the purity of the four right efforts (samyakprahāṇa), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the four right efforts are pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of internal emptiness, and the purity of the four right endeavors are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersal emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure; because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is pure, the four right endeavors (samyakprahāṇa) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of outer emptiness up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence (abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā), as well as the purity of the four right efforts (samyakprahāṇa), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the four right efforts are pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of suchness, and the purity of the four right efforts are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), non-falsity (*avitathatā*), non-alteration (*ananyathātva*), equality (*samatā*), the state beyond birth (*anabhibhavatā*), the fixedness of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*) are pure; because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the four right efforts (*samyakprahāṇa*) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, and the purity of the four right efforts are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure; because the noble truth of suffering is pure, the four right endeavors are pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the noble truth of suffering, and the purity of the four right endeavors are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are pure, the four right efforts are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, and the purity of the four right efforts are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the four right efforts are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is [identical to] the purity of the four dhyānas and the purity of the four right efforts, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, the four right efforts are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, and the purity of the four right efforts are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are without distinction, and they are not separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the four right endeavors are pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the eight liberations, and the purity of the four right efforts, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the eight bases of mastery (abhibhvāyatana), the nine successive attainments (anupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (kṛtsnāyatana) are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the four right efforts (samyakprahāṇa) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, the ten totalities, and the four right efforts are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not separate.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure; because the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, the four right endeavors are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is [identical to] the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, and the purity of the four right efforts, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the four bases of power (ṛddhipāda), the five faculties (indriya), the five powers (bala), the seven factors of enlightenment (bodhyaṅga), and the eightfold noble path (āryāṣṭāṅgamārga) are pure; because the four bases of power up to the eightfold noble path are pure, the four right efforts (samyakprahāṇa) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the four bases of power up to the eightfold noble path, as well as the purity of the four right efforts, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the four right efforts are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, and the purity of the four right efforts are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure; because the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure, the four right efforts are pure.

Why is this? Because the purification of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purification of the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, and the purification of the four right efforts are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten stages of a bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of a bodhisattva are pure, the four right endeavors are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the ten stages of the bodhisattva (daśabhūmi), and the purity of the four right efforts (catvāri samyakprahāṇāni) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the four right endeavors are pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the five eyes, or the purity of the four right efforts, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the six supernormal knowledges (ṣaḍabhijñā) are pure; because the six supernormal knowledges are pure, the four right efforts (catvāri samyakprahāṇāni) are pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the six supernormal knowledges, or the purity of the four right efforts, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, the four right endeavors are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, and the purity of the four right efforts are non-dual, without division, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, the four right efforts are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and the purity of the four right efforts are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the four right endeavors are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of the four right endeavors are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are without distinction, and they are not separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the state of constant abiding in equanimity is pure; because the state of constant abiding in equanimity is pure, the four right efforts are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is such, and the purity of the nature of constant equanimity is such, and the purity of the four right efforts is such, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the knowledge of all is pure; because the knowledge of all is pure, the four right efforts are pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, if the purity of all-knowledge, and if the purity of the four right efforts are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, the four right endeavors are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the knowledge of the paths (mārgākārajñatā) and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā), and the purity of the four right efforts (samyakprahāṇa) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all dhāraṇī gateways are pure; because all dhāraṇī gateways are pure, the four right efforts are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors, and the purity of the four right efforts are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not separate.
Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure; because all doors of samādhi are pure, the four right efforts are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all doors of samādhi, and the purity of the four right efforts are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are without distinction, and they are not separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, the four right endeavors are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, and the purity of the four right efforts, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure; because the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure, the four right efforts are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship, and the purity of the four right efforts (samyakprahāṇa) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, the four right efforts are pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of the four right efforts are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure, the four right endeavors are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience, the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of the four right efforts are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the unsurpassed perfect enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unsurpassed perfect enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, the four right efforts are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, and the purity of the four right efforts are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the four bases of psychic power are pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the same as the purity of form, and the purity of the four bases of power, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the four bases of power are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, as well as the purity of the four bases of psychic power, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-base is pure; because the eye-base is pure, the four bases of psychic power are pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the sphere of the eye is pure, and if the four bases of psychic power are pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the four bases of psychic power are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, as well as the purity of the four bases of psychic power (ṛddhipāda), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the four bases of psychic power are pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the sphere of form, and the purity of the four bases of psychic power, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure; because the bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure, the four bases of psychic power are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental objects (dharmāyatana), as well as the purity of the four bases of psychic power (ṛddhipāda), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the four bases of power are pure. Why is that?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eye-element, or the purity of the four bases of power, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the form element (rūpadhātu), the eye-consciousness element (cakṣurvijñānadhātu), eye-contact (cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa), and the various feelings (vedanā) produced with eye-contact as condition are pure; because the form element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition are pure, the four bases of psychic power (catvāra ṛddhipādāḥ) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the form realm (rūpadhātu) up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, and the purity of the four bases of psychic power (ṛddhipāda), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the four bases of power are pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the ear-element is pure, and if the four bases of psychic power are pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of auditory consciousness, auditory contact, and the various feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure, the four bases of spiritual power (ṛddhipāda) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, and the purity of the four bases of psychic power (ṛddhipāda), are non-dual; they are not two, they are not distinct, and they are not separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the nose element is pure; because the nose element is pure, the four bases of psychic power are pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the sphere of the nose, and the purity of the four bases of psychic power are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the four bases of psychic power (catvāra ṛddhipādāḥ) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the various sensations produced with the nose-contact as condition—ranging from the fragrance-element up to the sensations produced with nose-contact as condition—and the purity of the four bases of psychic power (ṛddhipāda) are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the four bases of psychic power are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is [identical to] the purity of the tongue-element, or the purity of the four bases of psychic power, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*) is pure, the taste element (*rasadhātu*), the tongue-consciousness element (*jihvāvijñānadhātu*), tongue-contact (*jihvāsaṃsparśa*), and the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the four bases of psychic power (*catvāra ṛddhipādāḥ*) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowing and the purity of everything from the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and the purity of the four bases of psychic power, are non-dual; they are not two, they are not distinct, and there is no division between them.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, the four bases of psychic power are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is [identical to] the purity of the body-element, or the purity of the four bases of psychic power, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the four bases of psychic power (ṛddhipāda) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the sensations arising from contact with the sphere of tangibles (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*) up to those arising from body-contact as a condition, and the purity of the four bases of psychic power (*ṛddhipāda*), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the intention for the purification of the knowledge of all modes is pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the four bases of psychic power are pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the mind-element is pure, and if the four bases of power are pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the dharma-element, the mental consciousness-element, and mind-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition, are pure; because the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition are pure, the four bases of psychic power (ṛddhipāda) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) and the purity of everything from the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, and the purity of the four bases of psychic power (*ṛddhipāda*), are non-dual; they are not two, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the four bases of psychic power are pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the earth element, and the purity of the four bases of psychic power are non-dual, undivided, indistinguishable, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the four bases of psychic power are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, as well as the purity of the four bases of psychic power (ṛddhipāda), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the four bases of psychic power are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is [identical to] the purity of the light of wisdom, and the purity of the four bases of psychic power, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, volitional formations (saṃskāra), consciousness (vijñāna), name-and-form (nāmarūpa), the six sense bases (ṣaḍāyatana), contact (sparśa), feeling (vedanā), craving (tṛṣṇā), clinging (upādāna), becoming (bhava), birth (jāti), and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the four bases of psychic power (catvāra ṛddhipādāḥ) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, as well as the purity of the four bases of power (ṛddhipāda), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, the four bases of psychic power are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the perfection of giving (dānapāramitā), and the purity of the four bases of psychic power (ṛddhipāda) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
