Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, the four bases of psychic power (ṛddhipāda) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), and the purity of the four bases of power (ṛddhipāda) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the four bases of power are pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of internal emptiness, and the purity of the four bases of psychic power are non-dual, undivided, indistinguishable, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*) is pure, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure; because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure, the four bases of psychic power (*ṛddhipāda*) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, as well as the purity of the four bases of psychic power, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the four bases of psychic power are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of suchness, and the purity of the four bases of psychic power are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm are pure. Because the realm of phenomena up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the four bases of psychic power (*ṛddhipāda*) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, and the purity of the four bases of psychic power are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure; because the noble truth of suffering is pure, the four bases of power are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the same as the purity of the noble truth of suffering, and the purity of the four bases of power, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are pure, the four bases of power (ṛddhipāda) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path, and the purity of the four bases of power (ṛddhipāda) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the four bases of psychic power are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the same as the purity of the four dhyānas and the purity of the four bases of psychic power, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, the four bases of spiritual power are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, and the purity of the four bases of psychic power are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the four bases of power are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the eight liberations, and the purity of the four bases of power, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the eight bases of mastery (abhibhvāyatana), the nine successive attainments (anupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (kṛtsnāyatana) are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the four bases of psychic power (ṛddhipāda) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the eight bases of mastery (abhibhvāyatana), the nine successive attainments (anupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (kṛtsnāyatana), as well as the purity of the four bases of psychic power (ṛddhipāda), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure; because the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, the four bases of psychic power are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the same as the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness and the purity of the four bases of psychic power, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four right endeavors, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path are pure, the four bases of psychic power are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the four right efforts (samyakprahāṇa), up to and including the eightfold noble path (āryāṣṭāṅgamārga), as well as the purity of the four bases of power (ṛddhipāda), are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the four bases of psychic power are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, and the purity of the four bases of psychic power are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure; because the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure, the four bases of psychic power (ṛddhipāda) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, and the purity of the four bases of psychic power are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the four bases of psychic power are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva (daśabhūmi), and the purity of the four bases of power (catvāra ṛddhipādāḥ) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the four bases of psychic power are pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the five eyes, or the purity of the four bases of power, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, the six supernormal powers (*ṣaḍabhijñā*) are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, the four bases of power (*catvāra ṛddhipādāḥ*) are pure. Why is this?

Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the six supernormal powers, or the purity of the four bases of power, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, the four bases of psychic power are pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, or the purity of the four bases of psychic power, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four fearlessnesses (vaiśāradya), the four analytical knowledges (pratisaṃvid), great loving-kindness (mahāmaitrī), great compassion (mahākaruṇā), great sympathetic joy (mahāmuditā), great equanimity (mahopekṣā), and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (āveṇikabuddhadharma) are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, the four bases of spiritual power (ṛddhipāda) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, as well as the purity of the four bases of power (ṛddhipāda), are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the four bases of power are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of the four bases of psychic power are non-dual; they are not two, they are not distinct, and they are not separate.
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the state of abiding in equanimity is pure; because the state of abiding in equanimity is pure, the four bases of psychic power are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the purity of the state of constant equanimity is pure, and if the purity of the four bases of power is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all-knowledge is pure; because all-knowledge is pure, the four bases of psychic power are pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all-knowledge, and the purity of the four bases of psychic power are non-dual, undivided, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, the four bases of psychic power are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path (mārgākārajñatā) and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā), and the purity of the four bases of power (ṛddhipāda) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all dhāraṇī-doors are pure; because all dhāraṇī-doors are pure, the four bases of psychic power are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all dharani-doors, and the purity of the four bases of psychic power are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure; because all doors of samādhi are pure, the four bases of psychic power are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all gateways to samādhi, and the purity of the four bases of psychic power are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, the four bases of psychic power are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, and the purity of the four bases of power are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of once-returner, the fruit of non-returner, and the fruit of arhatship are pure; because the fruit of once-returner, the fruit of non-returner, and the fruit of arhatship are pure, the four bases of psychic power are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship, and the purity of the four bases of psychic power are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, the four bases of power are pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of the four bases of power are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure, the four bases of psychic power are pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of the four bases of psychic power (ṛddhipāda) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the unsurpassed perfect enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unsurpassed perfect enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, the four bases of power are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, and the purity of the four bases of psychic power are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the five faculties are pure. Why is this?
The purity of the knowledge of all modes and the purity of form, as well as the purity of the five faculties, are non-dual, not divided into two, indistinct, and inseparable.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the five faculties are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, as well as the purity of the five faculties, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-base is pure; because the eye-base is pure, the five faculties are pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the sense-base of the eye is pure, and if the five faculties are pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the five faculties are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, as well as the purity of the five faculties, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the five faculties are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the sense-base of form, and the purity of the five faculties, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure, the five faculties are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena (dharmāyatana), as well as the purity of the five faculties, are non-dual; they are not two, without division, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the five faculties are pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purification of the knowledge of all modes, the purification of the eye-element, or the purification of the five faculties, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the form element (rūpadhātu), the eye-consciousness element (cakṣurvijñānadhātu), eye-contact (cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa), and the various feelings (vedanā) produced with eye-contact as condition are pure; because the form element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition are pure, the five faculties (pañcendriya) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the form realm (rūpadhātu) down to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the five faculties, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the five faculties are pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ear-element, or the purity of the five faculties, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of ear-consciousness, ear-contact, and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure, the five faculties are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the five faculties, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the nose-element is pure; because the nose-element is pure, the five faculties are pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sphere of the nose is pure, and if the five faculties are pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as condition are pure, the five faculties are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the realm of fragrance up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the five faculties, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the five faculties are pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the tongue element, or the purity of the five faculties, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct from one another, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the five faculties are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and the purity of the five faculties are non-dual; they are not two, they are without distinction, and they are not separate.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle Two Hundred and Sixty-nine. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter on Difficult to Believe and Understand, Thirty-four, Section Eighty-nine. "Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the body-element (kāyadhātu) is pure; because the body-element is pure, the five faculties (pañcendriya) are pure. Why is this?

Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the body-element, or the purity of the five faculties, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the five faculties are pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the elements of touch up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, or the purity of the five faculties, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the intentionality of the knowledge of all modes is pure, the mental faculty is pure; because the mental faculty is pure, the five faculties are pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the mind-element, or the purity of the five faculties, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, mental contact, and the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition are pure; because the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition are pure, the five faculties (pañcendriya) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of everything from the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the five faculties, are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the five faculties are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the earth element, and the purity of the five faculties, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the five faculties are pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, or the purity of the five faculties, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the five faculties are pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the light of wisdom, or the purity of the five faculties, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, volitional formations (saṃskāra), consciousness (vijñāna), name-and-form (nāmarūpa), the six sense bases (ṣaḍāyatana), contact (sparśa), feeling (vedanā), craving (tṛṣṇā), grasping (upādāna), becoming (bhava), birth (jāti), and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the five faculties (pañcendriya) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of everything from conditioned activities up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, as well as the purity of the five faculties, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of giving is pure; because the perfection of giving is pure, the five faculties are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the perfection of generosity, and the purity of the five faculties are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, the five faculties (pañcendriya) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the precepts up to the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), as well as the purity of the five faculties, are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the five faculties are pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of internal emptiness, or the purity of the five faculties, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*) is pure, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena (*sarvadharmaśūnyatā*), the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure; because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure, the five faculties (*pañcendriya*) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence (abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā), as well as the purity of the five faculties, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the five faculties are pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of suchness, and the purity of the five faculties are non-dual, without division, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), non-illusory nature, non-alteration, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the stability of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm are pure; because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the five faculties (pañcendriya) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, and the purity of the five faculties are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure; because the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure, the five faculties are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is such, and the purity of the noble truth of suffering is such, and the purity of the five faculties is such, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are pure, the five faculties are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path, and the purity of the five faculties are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the five faculties are pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the four dhyānas, and the purity of the five faculties, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, the five faculties are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience, the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, and the purity of the five faculties are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the five faculties are pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eight liberations, or the purity of the five faculties, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the eight bases of mastery (abhibhvāyatana), the nine successive attainments (anupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (kṛtsnāyatana) are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the five faculties (pañcendriya) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the eight bases of mastery (aṣṭāv abhibhvāyatanāni), the nine successive meditative attainments (navānupūrvavihārasamāpattayaḥ), and the ten pervasive bases (daśa kṛtsnāyatanāni), as well as the purity of the five faculties (pañcendriyāṇi), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure; because the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, the five faculties are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is [identical to] the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, or the purity of the five faculties, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and inseparable.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path are pure, the five faculties are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, as well as the purity of the five faculties, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the door of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the door of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the five faculties are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness (śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha), and the purity of the five faculties (pañcendriya) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the gates of liberation of signlessness (animitta) and wishlessness (apraṇihita) are pure; because the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure, the five faculties (pañcendriya) are pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purification of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purification of the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, or the purification of the five faculties, they are non-dual, without division, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the five faculties are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the ten stages of the bodhisattva (daśabhūmi), and the purity of the five faculties (pañcendriya) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the five faculties are pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purification of the knowledge of all modes, the purification of the five eyes, or the purification of the five faculties, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the six supernormal knowledges (ṣaḍabhijñā) are pure; because the six supernormal knowledges are pure, the five faculties (pañcendriya) are pure. Why is this?

Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the six supernormal knowledges, or the purity of the five faculties, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, the five faculties are pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, and if the five faculties are pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, the five faculties are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, as well as the purity of the five faculties, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the five faculties are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of the five faculties are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the state of equanimity (upekṣā) is pure; because the state of equanimity is pure, the five faculties (pañcendriya) are pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the state of constant equanimity, or the purity of the five faculties, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, all-knowledge (sarvajñatā) is pure; because all-knowledge is pure, the five faculties (pañcendriya) are pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all-knowledge, or the purity of the five faculties, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, the five faculties are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, and the purity of the five faculties are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all dharanī-doors are pure; because all dharanī-doors are pure, the five faculties are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors, and the purity of the five faculties are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
Because the knowledge of all modes of omniscience is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure; because all doors of samādhi are pure, the five faculties are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all doors of samādhi, and the purity of the five faculties are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, the five faculties are pure. Why is that?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is such, and the purity of the fruit of stream-entry is such, and the purity of the five faculties is such, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure; because the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure, the five faculties are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship, and the purity of the five faculties are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, the five faculties are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of the five faculties are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure, the five faculties are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of the five faculties (pañcendriya) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, the five faculties are pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, and the purity of the five faculties are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor separate.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the five powers are pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the same as the purity of form and the purity of the five powers, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the five powers are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, and the purity of the five powers (pañcabala) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sense base of the eye is pure; because the sense base of the eye is pure, the five powers are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is [identical to] the purity of the sense-sphere of the eye, or the purity of the five powers, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the five powers are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, as well as the purity of the five powers (pañcabala), are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the five powers are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the sense-field of form, and the purity of the five powers, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental objects are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental objects are pure, the five powers (pañcabala) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental objects (dharmāyatana), as well as the purity of the five powers (pañcabala), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the five powers are pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eye-element, or the purity of the five powers, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the form realm (rūpadhātu), the eye-consciousness realm (cakṣurvijñānadhātu), eye-contact (cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa), and the various sensations (vedanā) produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure; because the form realm up to the various sensations produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, the five powers (pañcabala) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the form realm (rūpadhātu) up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the five powers (pañcabala), are non-dual, without division, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the five powers are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the same as the purity of the ear-element, and the purity of the five powers, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*) is pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of auditory consciousness, auditory contact, and the various feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure, the five powers (*pañcabala*) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the five powers (pañcabala), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the nose-element is pure; because the nose-element is pure, the five powers are pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the nose element, and the purity of the five powers are non-dual, undivided, distinctless, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes of being (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the five powers (pañcabala) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowing, the purity of the realm of fragrance up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, and the purity of the five powers, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the five powers are pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the tongue-element, and the purity of the five powers, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the five powers (pañcabala) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the various feelings produced with the taste element as object and conditioned by tongue-contact, as well as the purity of the five powers (pañcabala), are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body-element is pure; because the body-element is pure, the five powers are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the body element, and the purity of the five powers, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the five powers (pañcabala) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) and the purity of the various feelings arising with the body as the basis for contact, up to the sphere of tangibles, as well as the purity of the five powers (pañcabala), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the intentionality of the knowledge of all modes is pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the five powers are pure. Why is that?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the mind-element is pure, and if the five powers are pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are pure; because the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are pure, the five powers (pañcabala) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu) up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the five powers (pañcabala), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the five powers are pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the earth element, and the purity of the five powers are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the five powers are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience and the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, as well as the purity of the five powers, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the five powers are pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of non-duality, or the purity of the five powers, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, volitional formations (saṃskāra), consciousness (vijñāna), name-and-form (nāmarūpa), the six sense bases (ṣaḍāyatana), contact (sparśa), feeling (vedanā), craving (tṛṣṇā), grasping (upādāna), becoming (bhava), birth (jāti), and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the five powers (pañcabala) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from formative activities up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, as well as the purity of the five powers (pañcabala), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, the five powers are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the perfection of giving (dānapāramitā), and the purity of the five powers (pañcabala) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, the five powers (pañcabala) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), as well as the purity of the five powers (pañcabala), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the five powers are pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of internal emptiness, and the purity of the five powers are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure; because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure, the five powers (pañcabala) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of outer emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence (abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā), as well as the purity of the five powers (pañcabala), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the five powers are pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of suchness, and the purity of the five powers are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), the non-falsity of phenomena (avitathatā), the unchanging nature of phenomena (ananyathābhāvatā), equality (samatā), the state beyond birth (anupapattitva), the fixedness of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the stability of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu) are pure. Because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the five powers (pañcabala) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, as well as the purity of the five powers, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure; because the noble truth of suffering is pure, the five powers are pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the noble truth of suffering, and the purity of the five powers are non-dual, undivided, indistinguishable, and inseparable.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure, the five powers (pañcabala) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path, and the purity of the five powers (pañcabala) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the five powers are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the four dhyānas, and the purity of the five powers, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, the five powers are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, and the five powers are non-dual; they are not two, not divided, not distinct, and not separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the five powers are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is such, and the purity of the eight liberations is such, and the purity of the five powers is such, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes of being is pure, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the five powers are pure.

Why is this? Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, and the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-base is pure; because the eye-base is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sense-base of the eye is pure, and if the door of liberation that is emptiness is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness (śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the sense bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, and the purity of the door of liberation that is emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sense-sphere of form is pure, and if the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena (śabda-gandha-rasa-spraṣṭavya-dharmāyatana) are pure; because the bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness (śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena, and the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye faculty is pure; because the eye faculty is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eye-element, or the purity of the gateway of liberation that is emptiness, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the form realm (rūpadhātu), the eye-consciousness realm (cakṣurvijñānadhātu), eye-contact (cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa), and the various feelings (vedanā) produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure. Because the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, the gate of liberation of emptiness (śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, and the purity of the door of liberation that is emptiness, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the ear element is pure, and if the door of liberation that is emptiness is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of auditory consciousness, auditory contact, and the various feelings arising with auditory contact as condition are pure; because the sphere of sound up to the various feelings arising with auditory contact as condition are pure, the gate of liberation of emptiness (śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of the sphere of sound (*śabdadhātu*) up to the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with ear-contact as a condition, and the purity of the gate of liberation of emptiness (*śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the nose element is pure; because the nose element is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the same as the purity of the nose element, and the purity of the door of liberation of emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the door of liberation that is emptiness (śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of the realm of fragrance up to the feelings produced with nose-contact as condition, and the purity of the door of liberation of emptiness (*śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha*) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the tongue element is pure, and if the door of liberation that is emptiness is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the gate of liberation of emptiness (śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) and the purity of the various feelings produced with the tongue-contact as condition—extending from the taste-element (*rasadhātu*) up to that point—are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate. They are one and the same.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the body-element is pure, and if the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, and bodily contact—as well as the various feelings produced with bodily contact as a condition—are pure. Because the element of tangibles up to the various feelings produced with bodily contact as a condition are pure, the gate of liberation of emptiness (śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) and the purity of the various feelings arising with the body as the basis and tangibles as conditions—up to the tangibles themselves—and the purity of the gate of liberation of emptiness (*śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.
“Subhūti! Because the intentionality of the knowledge of all modes is pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the gate of liberation of emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the mind-element is pure, and if the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, and mind-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition, are pure; because the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition are pure, the gate of liberation of emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of everything from the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, and the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness (*śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha*), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the earth element, and the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the liberation door of emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, as well as the purity of the gate of liberation of emptiness, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the light of non-arising, or the purity of the gate of liberation through emptiness, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, volitional formations (saṃskāra), consciousness (vijñāna), name-and-form (nāmarūpa), the six sense bases (ṣaḍāyatana), contact (sparśa), feeling (vedanā), craving (tṛṣṇā), grasping (upādāna), becoming (bhava), birth (jāti), and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness (śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of everything from formative activities up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not separate. Furthermore, the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness is likewise so. Why is this? Because they are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the perfection of generosity, and the purity of the gate of liberation through emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, the gateways to liberation of emptiness are pure.

Why is this? Because the purification of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purification of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom, as well as the purification of the gateways to liberation through emptiness, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
