Because the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*) is pure, internal emptiness (*adhyātmaśūnyatā*) is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness (*śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha*) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of internal emptiness, or the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersal emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure; because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure, the gate of liberation of emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, as well as the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the door of liberation that is emptiness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if suchness is pure, and if the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm are pure. Because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the gate of liberation of emptiness (śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, or the purity of the gateway of liberation that is emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure; because the noble truth of suffering is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the noble truth of suffering, and the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path, and the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the four dhyānas, and the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness (śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, the gate of liberation of emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because if the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, and the gate of liberation that is emptiness are pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the eight liberations (aṣṭavimokṣa), and the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness (śūnyatāvimokṣamukha) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, the eight bases of mastery (*abhibhvāyatana*), the nine successive attainments (*anupūrvavihārasamāpatti*), and the ten totalities (*kṛtsnāyatana*) are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the gate of liberation of emptiness (*śūnyatāvimokṣamukha*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the eight bases of mastery (aṣṭavimokṣa), the nine successive attainments (navānupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (daśakṛtsnāyatana), as well as the purity of the gate of liberation of emptiness (śūnyatāvimokṣamukha), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure; because the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, and the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, as well as the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the gate of liberation of signlessness is pure; because the gate of liberation of signlessness is pure, the gate of liberation of emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the signless door of liberation, and the purity of the emptiness door of liberation are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the door of liberation of wishlessness is pure; because the door of liberation of wishlessness is pure, the door of liberation of emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the door of liberation of wishlessness (apraṇihita-vimokṣamukha), and the purity of the door of liberation of emptiness (śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the ten stages of the bodhisattva, and the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the five eyes, or the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, the six supernormal powers (*ṣaḍabhijñā*) are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness (*śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha*) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the six supernormal powers, or the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, and the purity of the gate of liberation through emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, the gate of liberation of emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha (āveṇikabuddhadharma), or the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness (śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the state of constant equanimity is pure; because the state of constant equanimity is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the state of constant equanimity, or the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all-knowledge is pure; because all-knowledge is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all-knowledge, and the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path, or the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all dhāraṇī-doors are pure; because all dhāraṇī-doors are pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of all dharani-doors, and the purity of the doors of liberation through emptiness (*śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha*) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure; because all doors of samādhi are pure, the door of liberation that is emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all gateways of samādhi, and the purity of the gateway of emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, and the purity of the gate of liberation through emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are pure; because the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are pure, the gate of liberation of emptiness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the fruit of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship, and the purity of the gate of liberation through emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of the gateway of liberation that is emptiness (*śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha*) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, and the purity of the gateway of liberation that is emptiness, are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the door of liberation that is signlessness is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of form, and the purity of the gate of liberation through signlessness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the gate of liberation that is signless is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption; so too is the purity of the gate of liberation of signlessness (animitta-vimokṣamukha).
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye base is pure; because the eye base is pure, the gate of liberation that is signless is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sense base of the eye is pure, and if the gate of liberation of signlessness is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the gate of liberation of signlessness (animitta-vimokṣamukha) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, or the purity of the signless door of liberation, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the gate of liberation of signlessness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sphere of form is pure, and if the door of liberation of signlessness is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena are pure; because the bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena are pure, the gate of liberation that is signless is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena, as well as the purity of the gate of liberation that is signless, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the gate of liberation that is signless is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eye-element, or the purity of the signless door of liberation, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Why is this? Because if the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the taste element, up to and including the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, are pure, and if the door of liberation through wishlessness is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, the door of liberation of wishlessness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the body element is pure, and if the door of liberation of wishlessness is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*) is pure, the element of tangibles (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*), the element of body-consciousness (*kāyavijñānadhātu*), body-contact (*kāyasparśa*), and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the door of liberation of wishlessness (*apraṇihitavimokṣamukha*) is pure.

Why is this? Because if the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the objects of touch up to the feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, and if the door of liberation through wishlessness is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the intentionality of the knowledge of all modes is pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the door of liberation of wishlessness is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the mental constituent is pure, and if the door of liberation through wishlessness is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, mind-contact, and the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition are pure; because the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition are pure, the door of liberation of wishlessness is pure.

Why is this? Because if the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if everything from the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition is pure, and if the door of liberation through wishlessness is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 272. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Dharma Master Xuanzang under Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter on Difficult-to-Believe-and-Understand, Number Thirty-Four, Section Ninety-Two. "Subhūti!

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the door of liberation of wishlessness (apraṇihita-vimokṣamukha) is pure. Why is this?

Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the earth element, or the purity of the door of liberation of wishlessness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the door of liberation of wishlessness is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, or the purity of the door of liberation through wishlessness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the door of liberation of wishlessness is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purification of the knowledge of all modes, the purification of signlessness, or the purification of the door of liberation through wishlessness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the door of liberation of wishlessness (apraṇihita-vimokṣamukha) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, or the purity of everything from formative activities up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, or the purity of the door of liberation through wishlessness—these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, the door of liberation that is wishlessness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the perfection of generosity (dānapāramitā), and the purity of the door of liberation of wishlessness (apraṇihita-vimokṣamukha) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, the door of liberation that is wishlessness (apraṇihita-vimokṣamukha) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the precepts up to the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), as well as the purity of the door of liberation of wishlessness (apraṇihita-vimokṣamukha), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the door of liberation of wishlessness is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of internal emptiness, or the purity of the door of liberation through wishlessness—these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, external emptiness (*bahirdhā-śūnyatā*), internal-and-external emptiness (*adhyātma-bahirdhā-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of emptiness (*śūnyatā-śūnyatā*), great emptiness (*mahā-śūnyatā*), ultimate emptiness (*paramārtha-śūnyatā*), conditioned emptiness (*saṃskṛta-śūnyatā*), unconditioned emptiness (*asaṃskṛta-śūnyatā*), absolute emptiness (*atyanta-śūnyatā*), boundless emptiness (*anavara-agra-śūnyatā*), dispersion emptiness (*anavakāra-śūnyatā*), non-alteration emptiness (*anavakāra-śūnyatā* [sic; *ananyathā-śūnyatā]*) , essential nature emptiness (*prakṛti-śūnyatā*), self-characteristic emptiness (*svalakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*), common characteristic emptiness (*sāmānya-lakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of all phenomena (*sarvadharma-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of non-apprehensibility (*anupalambha-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of non-existence (*abhāva-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of intrinsic nature (*svabhāva-śūnyatā*), and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence (*abhāva-svabhāva-śūnyatā*) are pure. Because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure, the door of liberation of wishlessness (*apraṇihita-vimokṣamukha*) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature (abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā), or the purity of the door of liberation of wishlessness (apraṇihitavimokṣamukha), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the door of liberation that is wishlessness is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if suchness is pure, and if the door of liberation of wishlessness is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), non-falsity, non-alteration, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the stability of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu) are pure. Because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the gate of liberation of wishlessness (apraṇihita-vimokṣamukha) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purification of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purification of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, or the purification of the door of liberation through wishlessness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure; because the noble truth of suffering is pure, the door of liberation that is wishlessness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience, the purity of the noble truth of suffering, and the purity of the door of liberation through wishlessness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure, the door of liberation of wishlessness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna), the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, and the purity of the door of liberation through wishlessness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the door of liberation of wishlessness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four dhyānas, and the purity of the door of liberation through wishlessness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, the door of liberation of wishlessness is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, or the purity of the door of liberation that is wishlessness, they are non-dual, not two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the door of liberation that is wishlessness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the eight liberations (aṣṭavimokṣa), and the purity of the door of liberation through wishlessness (apraṇihitavimokṣamukha) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the eight bases of mastery (abhibhvāyatana), the nine successive attainments (anupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (kṛtsnāyatana) are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the door of liberation of wishlessness (apraṇihita-vimokṣamukha) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it is the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, or the ten universal bases, or the purity of the door of liberation through wishlessness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four applications of mindfulness are pure; because the four applications of mindfulness are pure, the door of liberation that is wishlessness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, and the purity of the door of liberation through wishlessness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, the door of liberation of wishlessness (apraṇihita-vimokṣamukha) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowing and the purity of the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path, as well as the purity of the door of liberation through wishlessness, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the gate of liberation of emptiness is pure; because the gate of liberation of emptiness is pure, the gate of liberation of wishlessness is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the gate of liberation of emptiness, or the purity of the gate of liberation of wishlessness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, the gate of liberation of signlessness is pure; because the gate of liberation of signlessness is pure, the gate of liberation of wishlessness is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of the gate of liberation of signlessness (*animitta-vimokṣamukha*), or the purity of the gate of liberation of wishlessness (*apraṇihita-vimokṣamukha*), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the door of liberation that is wishlessness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, and the purity of the door of liberation through wishlessness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the door of liberation that is wishlessness is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the five eyes, or the purity of the door of liberation through wishlessness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the six supernormal powers are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, the door of liberation of wishlessness is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the six supernormal powers, or the purity of the door of liberation through wishlessness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, the door of liberation of wishlessness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, and the purity of the door of liberation through wishlessness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*) is pure, the four fearlessnesses (*vaiśāradya*), the four analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*), great loving-kindness (*mahāmaitrī*), great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*), great sympathetic joy (*mahāmuditā*), great equanimity (*mahopekṣā*), and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇika-buddhadharma*) are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, the door of liberation of wishlessness (*apraṇihita-vimokṣamukha*) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, or the purity of the door of liberation through wishlessness—these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the door of liberation of wishlessness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of the door of liberation through wishlessness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the state of equanimity (upekṣā) is pure; because the state of equanimity is pure, the door of liberation of wishlessness (apraṇihita-vimokṣamukha) is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, if the purity of the state of constant equanimity, and if the purity of the door of liberation through wishlessness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the knowledge of all things is pure; because the knowledge of all things is pure, the door of liberation that is wishlessness is pure."

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all-knowledge, or the purity of the door of liberation through wishlessness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, the door of liberation of wishlessness is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path (mārgākārajñatā) and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā), or the purity of the door of liberation of wishlessness (apraṇihita-vimokṣamukha), they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all dhāraṇī-doors are pure; because all dhāraṇī-doors are pure, the door of liberation through wishlessness is pure.”

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors, or the purity of the door of liberation through wishlessness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure; because all doors of samādhi are pure, the door of liberation of wishlessness is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience, the purity of all doors of samādhi, or the purity of the door of liberation through wishlessness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, the door of liberation of wishlessness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, and the purity of the door of liberation through wishlessness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure; because the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure, the door of liberation of wishlessness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship, as well as the purity of the door of liberation through wishlessness, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, the door of liberation of wishlessness is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of the door of liberation through wishlessness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure, the door of liberation that is wishlessness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of the door of liberation through wishlessness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, the door of liberation of wishlessness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, and the purity of the door of liberation through wishlessness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, form (rūpa) is pure; because form is pure, the ten stages (daśabhūmi) of a bodhisattva are pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of form, or the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, and the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva (daśabhūmi) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sense base of the eye is pure; because the sense base of the eye is pure, the ten stages of a bodhisattva are pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sense base of the eye is pure, and if the ten stages of a bodhisattva are pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the sense bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, and the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva (daśabhūmi) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the ten stages of a bodhisattva are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the sphere of form, and the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena (śabda-gandha-rasa-spraṣṭavya-dharmāyatana) are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena are pure, the ten stages (daśabhūmi) of the bodhisattva are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena (dharmāyatana), and the purity of the ten stages (bhūmi) of a bodhisattva are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the ten stages of a bodhisattva are pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purification of the knowledge of all modes, the purification of the eye-element, or the purification of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the form realm (rūpadhātu), the eye-consciousness realm (cakṣurvijñānadhātu), eye-contact (cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa), and the various feelings (vedanā) produced with eye-contact as condition are pure; because the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition are pure, the ten stages (daśabhūmi) of a bodhisattva are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) and the purity of everything from the form realm (*rūpadhātu*) up to the various sensations (*vedanā*) produced with eye-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the ten stages (*daśabhūmi*) of a bodhisattva, are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the ten stages of a bodhisattva are pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the ear-element is pure, and if the ten stages of a bodhisattva are pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of auditory consciousness, auditory contact, and the various feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure, the ten stages (daśabhūmi) of the bodhisattva are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of the sphere of sound (*śabdadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, and the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva (*daśabhūmi*) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the nose element is pure; because the nose element is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is such, and the purity of the nose element is such, and the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva is such, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the ten stages (daśabhūmi) of the bodhisattva are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) and the purity of everything from the realm of fragrance (*gandhadhātu*) up to the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with nose-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the ten stages (*daśabhūmi*) of a bodhisattva, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the ten stages of a bodhisattva are pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the tongue element, or the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste-element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the ten stages (daśabhūmi) of the bodhisattva are pure.

Why is this? Because the purification of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purification of the taste element (*rasadhātu*) up to the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and the purification of the ten stages (*daśabhūmi*) of a bodhisattva are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the realm of the body is pure, and if the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the ten stages (daśabhūmi) of the bodhisattva are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the various feelings arising with the body as the basis and tangibles as the condition—up to the tangibles themselves—and the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva (daśabhūmi) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the intention for the purity of the knowledge of all modes is pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the ten stages of a bodhisattva are pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the mind-element is pure, and if the ten stages of a bodhisattva are pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the eight bases of mastery (abhibhvāyatana), the nine successive attainments (anupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (kṛtsnāyatana) are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the six supernormal powers (abhijñā) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the eight bases of mastery (aṣṭavimokṣa), the nine successive attainments (navānupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (daśakṛtsnāyatana), as well as the purity of the six supernormal powers (ṣaḍabhijñā), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four applications of mindfulness are pure; because the four applications of mindfulness are pure, the six supernormal powers are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is so, and the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, and the purity of the six supernormal powers are so, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, the six supernormal knowledges (ṣaḍabhijñā) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, as well as the purity of the six supernormal powers (ṣaḍabhijñā), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the six supernormal powers are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, and the purity of the six supernormal powers are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure; because the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure, the six supernormal powers are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, and the purity of the six supernormal powers are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the six supernormal powers are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, and the purity of the six supernormal powers are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the six supernormal powers are pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purification of the knowledge of all modes, the purification of the five eyes, or the purification of the six supernormal powers, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, the six supernormal knowledges are pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, or the purity of the six supernormal knowledges, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha are pure, the six supernormal powers are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, as well as the purity of the six supernormal powers, are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the six supernormal powers are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of the six supernormal powers are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the state of constant abiding in equanimity is pure; because the state of constant abiding in equanimity is pure, the six supernormal powers are pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the state of constant equanimity, or the purity of the six supernormal powers, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the knowledge of all is pure; because the knowledge of all is pure, the six supernormal powers are pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all-knowledge, or the purity of the six supernormal powers, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, the six supernormal powers are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, and the purity of the six supernormal powers are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all dharani-doors are pure; because all dharani-doors are pure, the six supernormal powers are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all dharani-doors, and the purity of the six supernormal powers are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure; because all doors of samādhi are pure, the six supernormal powers are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all doors of samādhi, and the purity of the six supernormal powers are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, the six supernormal powers are pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, and the purity of the six supernormal powers are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure; because the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure, the six supernormal powers (ṣaḍabhijñā) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship, and the purity of the six supernormal powers are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, the six supernormal powers are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of the six supernormal powers are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure, the six supernormal powers are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of the six supernormal powers are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, the six supernormal powers are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, and the purity of the six supernormal powers are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if form is pure, and if the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness, and the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sense base of the eye is pure; because the sense base of the eye is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sense base of the eye is pure, and if the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes of omniscience is pure, the sense bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the sense bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the ten powers of the Buddha are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, and the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure. Why is that?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the sense-sphere of form, and the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena are pure, the ten powers of the Buddha are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, and the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eye-element, or the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the form element (rūpadhātu), the eye-consciousness element (cakṣurvijñānadhātu), eye-contact (cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa), and the various feelings (vedanā) produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure; because the form element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, the ten powers (daśabala) of the Buddha are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the form realm (rūpadhātu) up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the ten powers (daśabala) of a Buddha, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because omniscient wisdom is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the same as the purity of the ear-element and the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of auditory consciousness, auditory contact, and the various feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure, the ten powers (daśabala) of the Buddha are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the realm of sound, up to and including the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, and the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, are non-dual; they are not two, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the nose-element is pure; because the nose-element is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the nose element, and the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the ten powers (daśabala) of the Buddha are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of everything from the realm of fragrance up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, and the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, are non-dual, without division, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the tongue element, and the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to the various sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the ten powers (daśabala) of the Buddha are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, are non-dual; they are not two, they are without distinction, and they are not separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the body element, and the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the various feelings arising with the body as the condition, from the element of tangibility up to the body-contact, as well as the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the intention for the purity of all-knowledge is pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the mental constituent, and the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha are non-dual, without division, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are pure; because the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are pure, the ten powers (daśabala) of the Buddha are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*) up to the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with mental contact as a condition, and the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha (*daśabala*) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the ten powers of the Buddha are pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the earth element, and the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the ten powers of the Buddha are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) and the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, as well as the purity of the ten powers (*daśabala*) of a Buddha, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the ten powers of the Buddha are pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the absence of obscuration is pure, and if the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the ten powers of the Buddha are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of everything from conditioned activities through old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, as well as the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the perfection of generosity, and the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, the ten powers (daśabala) of a Buddha are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom, and the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if inner emptiness is pure, and if the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, there is the purity of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence. Because there is the purity of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, the ten powers of the Buddha are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of outer emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence (*abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā*), and the purity of the ten powers (*daśabala*) of a Buddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
