Because the knowledge of all modes of being (*sarvajñājñāna*) is pure, suchness (*tathatā*) is pure; because suchness is pure, the ten powers (*daśabala*) of a Buddha are pure. Why is this?

Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes of being, the purity of suchness, or the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), non-falsity (avitathatā), non-alteration (ananyathābhāva), sameness (samatā), the state beyond birth (anabhibhūtatā), the fixedness of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu) are pure. Because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the ten powers of the Buddha (buddhabala) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, and the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure; because the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the noble truth of suffering, and the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure, the ten powers of the Buddha are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path, and the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because omniscience is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure. Why is this?

The purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four dhyānas, and the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, and the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the ten powers of the Buddha are pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eight liberations, or the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the ten powers of the Buddha are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the eight bases of mastery (aṣṭavimokṣa), the nine successive attainments (navānupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten pervasive bases (daśakṛtsnāyatana), as well as the purity of the ten powers (daśabala) of a Buddha, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four applications of mindfulness are pure; because the four applications of mindfulness are pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, and the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, the ten powers of the Buddha are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, as well as the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, and the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñājñāna*) is pure, the gateways to liberation of signlessness (*animitta*) and wishlessness (*apraṇihita*) are pure; because the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure, the ten powers (*daśabala*) of a Buddha are pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, or the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the ten powers of the Buddha are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, and the purity of the ten powers of a buddha are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the five eyes, or the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the six supernormal powers (ṣaḍabhijñā) are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, the ten powers of a Buddha (daśabala) are pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the six supernormal powers, or the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four fearlessnesses are pure; because the four fearlessnesses are pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four fearlessnesses, and the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the four analytical knowledges (pratisaṃvid), great loving-kindness (mahāmaitrī), great compassion (mahākaruṇā), great sympathetic joy (mahāmuditā), great equanimity (mahopekṣā), and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (āveṇikabuddhadharma) are pure; because the four analytical knowledges up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, the ten powers of a Buddha (daśabala) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the four analytical knowledges up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the knowledge of all is pure; because the knowledge of all is pure, the ten powers of the Buddha are pure. Why is this?

Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental objects (dharmāyatana), as well as the purity of the four fearlessnesses (vaiśāradya), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the four fearlessnesses are pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the eye-element is pure, and if the four fearlessnesses are pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the form element (rūpadhātu), the eye-consciousness element (cakṣurvijñānadhātu), eye-contact (cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa), and the various feelings (vedanā) produced with eye-contact as condition are pure; because the form element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition are pure, the four fearlessnesses (vaiśāradya) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the form realm (rūpadhātu) up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, and the purity of the four fearlessnesses (vaiśāradya), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the same as the purity of the ear-element and the purity of the four fearlessnesses, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of auditory consciousness, ear-contact, and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure, the four fearlessnesses (caturvaiśāradya) are pure.

Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowing (*sarvajñajñāna*) and the purity of everything from the realm of sound up to the various sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the four fearlessnesses (*vaiśāradya*), are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the nose-element is pure; because the nose-element is pure, the four fearlessnesses are pure. Why is that?

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, the four fearlessnesses are pure. Why is this?

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of the four fearlessnesses are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure, the four fearlessnesses are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of the four fearlessnesses (catur-vaiśāradya) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, the four fearlessnesses are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, and the purity of the four fearlessnesses are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the four analytical knowledges are pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if form is pure, and if the four analytical knowledges are pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the four analytical knowledges are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, and the purity of the four analytical knowledges are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sense-base of the eye is pure, and if the four analytical knowledges are pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the sphere of form, or the purity of the four analytical knowledges, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena are pure, the four analytical knowledges are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental objects (dharmāyatana), as well as the purity of the four analytical knowledges (pratisaṃvid), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the four analytical knowledges are pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the eye-element is pure, and if the four analytical knowledges are pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the form element (rūpadhātu), the eye-consciousness element (cakṣurvijñānadhātu), eye-contact (cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa), and the various feelings (vedanā) produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure; because the form element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, the four analytical knowledges (pratisaṃvid) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of everything from the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, and the purity of the four analytical knowledges, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the four analytical knowledges are pure. Why is this?

Why is this? Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the realm of fragrance up to the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the four analytical knowledges (pratisaṃvid), are non-dual, without division, without distinction, and without interruption.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and the purity of the four analytical knowledges are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, the four analytical knowledges are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the same as the purity of the body-element and the purity of the four analytical knowledges, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not severed.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the four analytical knowledges are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) and the purity of the sensations produced with the body as the condition, from the sphere of touch (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*) onwards, as well as the purity of the four analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the intentionality of the knowledge of all modes is pure, the mental sphere is pure; because the mental sphere is pure, the four analytical knowledges are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the mental faculty, and the purity of the four analytical knowledges are non-dual, without division, without distinction, and without interruption.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of everything from the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition, and the purity of the four analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the four analytical knowledges are pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the earth element, and the purity of the four analytical knowledges are non-dual, without division, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the four analytical knowledges are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, and the purity of the four analytical knowledges (pratisaṃvid) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-duality is pure; because non-duality is pure, the four analytical knowledges are pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the light of omniscience, or the purity of the four analytical knowledges, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the four analytical knowledges are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of everything from formations through old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are not distinct, and they are not severed. The purity of the four unhindered analytical knowledges is likewise so. Why is this? Because they are non-dual, not two, not distinct, and not severed.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, the four analytical knowledges are pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the perfection of generosity, and the purity of the four analytical insights are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, the four analytical knowledges (pratisaṃvid) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), as well as the purity of the four analytical knowledges (pratisaṃvid), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the four analytical knowledges are pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if internal emptiness is pure, and if the four analytical knowledges are pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, there is the purity of outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersal emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature. Because there is the purity of outer emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, there is the purity of the four analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*).

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from outer emptiness up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence, as well as the purity of the four analytical knowledges (pratisaṃvid), are non-dual, without division, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the four analytical knowledges are pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of suchness, and the purity of the four analytical knowledges are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the non-falsity (*avitathatā*), the non-alteration (*ananyathābhāva*), equality (*samatā*), the state beyond birth (*anirodhatā*), the fixedness of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*) are pure. Because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the four analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, and the purity of the four analytical knowledges are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the form realm (rūpadhātu), the eye-consciousness realm (cakṣurvijñānadhātu), eye-contact (cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa), and the various feelings (vedanā) produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure; because the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, great loving-kindness (mahāmaitrī) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the form realm (rūpadhātu) up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, and the purity of great loving-kindness (mahāmaitrī), are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ear element is pure; because the ear element is pure, great loving-kindness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the ear-element is pure, and if great compassion is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of ear-consciousness, ear-contact, and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure, great loving-kindness (mahāmaitrī) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience, the purity of the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, and the purity of great loving-kindness are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the nose-element is pure; because the nose-element is pure, great loving-kindness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sphere of the nose is pure, and if great loving-kindness is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, great loving-kindness (mahāmaitrī) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the sphere of fragrance (*gandhadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, and the purity of great loving-kindness (*mahāmaitrī*) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the tongue element is pure; because the tongue element is pure, great loving-kindness is pure. Why is that?
Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the tongue element, or the purity of great compassion, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, great loving-kindness (mahāmaitrī) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the various feelings produced with the taste element as object and conditioned by tongue-contact, up to the purity of great loving-kindness, are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, great loving-kindness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the body-element is pure, and if great compassion is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, great loving-kindness (mahāmaitrī) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) and the purity of the various feelings arising with the body-tangible as a condition—extending from the tangible element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*) up to those produced by the body-tangible as a condition—and the purity of great loving-kindness (*mahāmaitrī*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the intention for the purity of the knowledge of all modes is pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, great loving-kindness is pure. Why is this?
The purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the mind-element, and the purity of great compassion are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, as well as mental contact and the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition, are pure; because the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition are pure, great loving-kindness (mahāmaitrī) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purification of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purification of everything from the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, and the purification of great loving-kindness (*mahāmaitrī*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, great loving-kindness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the earth element is pure, and if great compassion is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, great loving-kindness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience and the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, as well as the purity of great compassion, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, great loving-kindness is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the light of omniscience, or the purity of great compassion, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, formative forces (saṃskāra), consciousness (vijñāna), name-and-form (nāmarūpa), the six sense bases (ṣaḍāyatana), contact (sparśa), feeling (vedanā), craving (tṛṣṇā), grasping (upādāna), becoming (bhava), birth (jāti), and old age, death, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair (jarāmaraṇa-śoka-parideva-duḥkha-daurmanasyopāyāsa) are pure; because formative forces through old age, death, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are pure, great loving-kindness (mahāmaitrī) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of everything from formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, as well as the purity of great loving-kindness, are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, great loving-kindness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the perfection of generosity, and the purity of great loving-kindness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, great loving-kindness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the precepts up to the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), as well as the purity of great loving-kindness (mahāmaitrī), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, great loving-kindness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if inner emptiness is pure, and if great compassion is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure. Because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure, great loving-kindness (mahāmaitrī) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from external emptiness (bahirdhā-śūnyatā) up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence (abhāvasvabhāva-śūnyatā), as well as the purity of great compassion (mahāmaitrī), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, great loving-kindness is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of suchness, and the purity of great compassion are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), the non-erroneous nature, the unchanging nature, the state of equality, the nature free from birth, the fixedness of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the stability of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm are pure; because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, great loving-kindness (mahāmaitrī) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, and the purity of great compassion are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure; because the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure, great loving-kindness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the noble truth of suffering is pure, and if great compassion is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are pure, great loving-kindness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path, and the purity of great compassion are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, great loving-kindness is pure. Why is this?
The purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four dhyānas, and the purity of great loving-kindness are non-dual; they are not two, they are not distinct, and they are not separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, great loving-kindness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the four immeasurables (apramāṇa) and the four formless attainments (ārūpyasamāpatti), and the purity of great compassion (mahāmaitrī) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, great loving-kindness is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eight liberations, and the purity of great loving-kindness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the eight bases of mastery (aṣṭāv abhibhvāyatanāni), the nine successive attainments (navānupūrvavihārasamāpattayaḥ), and the ten totalities (daśa kṛtsnāyatanāni) are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, great loving-kindness (mahāmaitrī) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, the ten universal bases, and the purity of great loving-kindness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure; because the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, great loving-kindness is pure. Why is that?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, and if great loving-kindness is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, great loving-kindness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, as well as the purity of great loving-kindness, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the door of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the door of liberation that is emptiness is pure, great loving-kindness is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness (śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha), and the purity of great loving-kindness (mahāmaitrī) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are pure; because the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are pure, great loving-kindness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, and the purity of great compassion are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten stages of a bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of a bodhisattva are pure, great loving-kindness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, and the purity of great compassion are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, great loving-kindness is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purification of the knowledge of all modes, the purification of the five eyes, or the purification of great compassion, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the six supernormal powers (ṣaḍabhijñā) are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, great loving-kindness (mahāmaitrī) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the six supernormal powers, or the purity of great loving-kindness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, great loving-kindness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, and if great compassion is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, the four fearlessnesses (*vaiśāradya*), the four analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*), great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*), great joy (*mahāmuditā*), great equanimity (*mahopekṣā*), and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇikabuddhadharma*) are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, great loving-kindness (*mahāmaitrī*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and the purity of great compassion are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor separate.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, great loving-kindness is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of great compassion are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the state of constant equanimity (upekṣā) is pure; because the state of constant equanimity is pure, great loving-kindness (mahāmaitrī) is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is such, and the purity of the state of constant equanimity is such, and the purity of great compassion is such, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the knowledge of all is pure; because the knowledge of all is pure, great loving-kindness is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all-knowledge, or the purity of great compassion, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, great loving-kindness is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects, or the purity of great compassion, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all dhāraṇī-doors are pure; because all dhāraṇī-doors are pure, great loving-kindness is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors, and the purity of great compassion are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
Because the knowledge of all modes of omniscience is pure, all gateways to meditative concentration are pure; because all gateways to meditative concentration are pure, great loving-kindness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all doors of samādhi, and the purity of great loving-kindness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, great loving-kindness is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, and the purity of great compassion are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure; because the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure, great compassion is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship, and the purity of great compassion are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, great loving-kindness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, and the purity of great compassion are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure, great loving-kindness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of great loving-kindness (mahāmaitrī) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, great loving-kindness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, and the purity of great compassion are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, great compassion is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if form is pure, and if great compassion is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, great compassion is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, and the purity of great compassion are non-dual; they are not two, not divided, not distinct, and not severed.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-base is pure; because the eye-base is pure, great compassion is pure. Why is that?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sense-sphere of the eye is pure, and if great compassion is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, great compassion is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the sense bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, and the purity of great compassion (mahākaruṇā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, great compassion is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the sphere of form, and the purity of great compassion are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena are pure, great compassion is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena (dharmāyatana), and the purity of great compassion (mahākaruṇā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, great compassion is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eye-element, or the purity of great compassion, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the form element (rūpadhātu), the eye-consciousness element (cakṣurvijñānadhātu), eye-contact (cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa), and the various feelings (vedanā) produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure; because the form element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, great compassion (mahākaruṇā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of everything from the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of great compassion, are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, great compassion is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ear-element, or the purity of great compassion, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of auditory consciousness, auditory contact, and the various feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure, great compassion (mahākaruṇā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, and the purity of great compassion, are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the nose-element is pure; because the nose-element is pure, great compassion is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the nose element, and the purity of great compassion are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, great compassion (mahākaruṇā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the realm of fragrance up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, and the purity of great compassion are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, great compassion is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the tongue element is pure, and if great compassion is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, great compassion (mahākaruṇā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and the purity of great compassion, are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, great compassion is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the realm of the body is pure, and if great compassion is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, great compassion (mahākaruṇā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the various feelings produced with the body and its contact as conditions—ranging from the element of tangibility up to the body—are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate. Thus they are pure.
“Subhūti! Because the intention for the purity of the knowledge of all modes is pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, great compassion is pure. Why is this?
The purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the mind-element, and the purity of great compassion are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the dharma-element, the mental consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are pure; because the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are pure, great compassion (mahākaruṇā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of everything from the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, and the purity of great compassion, are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, great compassion is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the earth element is pure, and if great compassion is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, great compassion is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, as well as the purity of great compassion, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, great compassion is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of non-duality, or the purity of great compassion, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, great compassion is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from conditioned formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are non-dual; they are not two, they are without distinction, and they are not separate. Likewise, the purity of great compassion (mahākaruṇā) is non-dual with them; it is not two, it is without distinction, and it is not separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, great compassion is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the perfection of generosity, and the purity of great compassion are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, great compassion (mahākaruṇā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom, and the purity of great compassion are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, great compassion is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if internal emptiness is pure, and if great compassion is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, not distinct, and not discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, there is the purity of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence. Because the purity of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence exists, great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, and the purity of great compassion are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, great compassion is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of suchness, and the purity of great compassion are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state of being free from birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of empty space, and the inconceivable realm are pure; because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, great compassion is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu) up to the inconceivable realm, and the purity of great compassion are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure; because the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure, Great Compassion is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the noble truth of suffering, and the purity of great compassion are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure, great compassion is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, and the purity of great compassion (mahākaruṇā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, great compassion is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the same as the purity of the four dhyānas, and the purity of great compassion, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, great compassion is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, and the purity of great compassion are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle Two Hundred and Seventy-Six. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. First Division, Chapter Thirty-Four on Difficult Faith and Understanding, Part Nine of Sixteen. "Subhūti!
Because the wisdom of all-knowledge is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, great compassion is pure. Why is this?
If the wisdom of all-knowledge is pure, if the eight liberations are pure, and if great compassion is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, great compassion is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience, the purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten pervasive bases, and the purity of great compassion, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure; because the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, great compassion is pure. Why is that?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, and the purity of great compassion, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, great compassion is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path, as well as the purity of great compassion, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, great compassion is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, and the purity of great compassion are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñājñāna*) is pure, the gateways to liberation of signlessness (*animitta*) and wishlessness (*apraṇihita*) are pure; because the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure, great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, and the purity of great compassion are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, great compassion is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the ten stages of the bodhisattva, and the purity of great compassion are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, great compassion is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purification of the knowledge of all modes, the purification of the five eyes, or the purification of great compassion, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, the six supernormal powers (*ṣaḍabhijñā*) are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the six supernormal powers, or the purity of great compassion, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, great compassion is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, or the purity of great compassion, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, great compassion is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna), the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and the purity of great compassion (mahākaruṇā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, great compassion is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of great compassion are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the state of constant abiding in equanimity is pure; because the state of constant abiding in equanimity is pure, great compassion is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is [identical to] the purity of the state of constant equanimity, and the purity of great compassion, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the knowledge of all things is pure; because the knowledge of all things is pure, great compassion is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all-knowledge, or the purity of great compassion, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor severed.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, great compassion is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, and the purity of great compassion are non-dual; they are not two, indivisible, distinct, or separate.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all dharani-doors are pure; because all dharani-doors are pure, great compassion is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all dharani-doors, and the purity of great compassion are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure; because all doors of samādhi are pure, great compassion is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all doors of samādhi, and the purity of great compassion are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, great compassion is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, and the purity of great compassion are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are pure; because the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are pure, great compassion is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship, and the purity of great compassion are non-dual; they are not two, they are undivided, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, great compassion is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of great compassion are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure, great compassion is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of great compassion are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, great compassion is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, and the purity of great compassion are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, great joy is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if form is pure, and if great joy is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not severed.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, great joy is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, and the purity of great joy are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye base is pure; because the eye base is pure, great joy is pure. Why is that?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sense-field of the eye is pure, and if great joy is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, great joy is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, as well as the purity of great joy, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, great joy is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sense-sphere of form is pure, and if great joy is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena are pure; because the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena are pure, great joy is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, and the purity of great joy are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divisible, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, great joy is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eye-element, or the purity of great joy, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the form realm (rūpadhātu), the eye-consciousness realm (cakṣurvijñānadhātu), eye-contact (cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa), and the various feelings (vedanā) produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure; because the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, great joy (mahāmuditā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, and the purity of great joy, are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, great joy is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the ear-element is pure, and if great joy is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of auditory consciousness, and auditory contact, as well as the various feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition, are pure; because the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure, great joy (mahāmuditā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the sphere of sound (*śabdadhātu*) up to the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with ear-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of great joy (*mahāmuditā*), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the nose element is pure; because the nose element is pure, great joy is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sphere of the nose is pure, and if great joy is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, great joy is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) and the purity of everything from the fragrance-element (*gandhadhātu*) up to the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition, and the purity of great joy (*mahāmuditā*), are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the tongue element is pure; because the tongue element is pure, great joy is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the tongue element is pure, and if great joy is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes of omniscience is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, great joy is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the taste element, up to and including the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and the purity of great joy, are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
