“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, great joy is pure. Why is that?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the body element is pure, and if great joy is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, great joy (mahāmuditā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the various feelings produced with the body as the basis for contact, up to the realm of touch, and the purity of great joy, are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! Because the intentionality of the knowledge of all modes is pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, great joy is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the mind-element is pure, and if great joy is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness element, mental contact, and the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition are pure; because the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition are pure, great joy (mahāmuditā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of everything from the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, and the purity of great joy, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, great joy is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the earth element, and the purity of great joy are non-dual, without division, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, great joy is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, as well as the purity of great joy, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-self is pure; because non-self is pure, great joy is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the same as the purity of the light of wisdom, and the purity of great joy, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are pure, great joy is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) and the purity of everything from conditioned formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, as well as the purity of great joy, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, great joy is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the perfection of generosity, and the purity of great joy are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom are pure, great joy (mahāmuditā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), and the purity of great joy are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, inner emptiness is pure; because inner emptiness is pure, great joy is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if internal emptiness is pure, and if great joy is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure; because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure, great joy (*mahāmuditā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of external emptiness up to the purity of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, and the purity of great joy are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, great joy is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of suchness, and the purity of great joy are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu) are pure; because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, great joy (mahāmuditā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, and the purity of great joy are non-dual; they are not two, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure; because the noble truth of suffering is pure, great joy is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the noble truth of suffering is pure, and if great joy is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are pure, great joy is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, and the purity of great joy are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, great joy is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the same as the purity of the four dhyānas, and the purity of great joy, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are pure, great joy is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, and the purity of great joy are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, great joy is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eight liberations, and the purity of great joy are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the eight bases of mastery (abhibhvāyatana), the nine successive attainments (anupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (kṛtsnāyatana) are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, great joy (mahāmuditā) is pure.

Why is this? Because if the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, and if great joy is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure; because the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, great sympathetic joy is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, and if great joy is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, great joy (mahāmuditā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, as well as the purity of great joy, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the door of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the door of liberation that is emptiness is pure, great joy is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, and the purity of great joy are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the gateways of liberation of signlessness (animitta) and wishlessness (apraṇihita) are pure; because the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure, great joy (mahāmuditā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, and the purity of great joy are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, great joy is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, and the purity of great joy are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, great joy is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purification of the knowledge of all modes, the purification of the five eyes, or the purification of great joy, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the six supernormal powers are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, great joy is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the six supernormal powers are pure, and if great joy is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten powers of a buddha are pure; because the ten powers of a buddha are pure, great joy is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, and the purity of great joy are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, great joy is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, as well as the purity of great joy, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, great joy is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of great joy are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not separate.
Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the state of equanimity (upekṣā) is pure; because the state of equanimity is pure, great joy (mahāmuditā) is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the same as the purity of the state of constant equanimity, and the purity of great joy, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the knowledge of all is pure; because the knowledge of all is pure, great joy is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all-knowledge, and the purity of great joy are non-dual, undivided, indistinguishable, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, great joy is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects, and the purity of great joy are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all dharanī-doors are pure; because all dharanī-doors are pure, great joy is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all dharani-doors, and the purity of great joy are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, all gateways to samādhi are pure; because all gateways to samādhi are pure, great joy is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all doors of samādhi, and the purity of great joy are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, great joy is pure. Why is that?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the same as the purity of the fruit of stream-entry and the purity of great joy, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and inseparable.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are pure; because the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are pure, great joy is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship, and the purity of great joy are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, great joy is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of great joy are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure, great joy is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of great joy are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, great joy is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, and the purity of great joy are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, great equanimity is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if form is pure, and if great equanimity is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, great equanimity is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna), the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, and the purity of great equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sense base of the eye is pure; because the sense base of the eye is pure, great equanimity is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sense base of the eye is pure, and if great equanimity is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, great equanimity is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, as well as the purity of great equanimity (mahopekṣā), are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, great equanimity is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sense-sphere of form is pure, and if great equanimity is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure, great equanimity is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental objects, as well as the purity of great equanimity (mahopekṣā), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, great equanimity is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the eye-element is pure, and if great equanimity is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the form element, the eye-consciousness element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure; because the form element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, great equanimity is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) and the purity of everything from the form realm (*rūpadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of great equanimity (*mahopekṣā*), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, great equanimity is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the ear-element is pure, and if great equanimity is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of ear-consciousness, ear-contact, and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure, great equanimity (mahopekṣā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, and the purity of great equanimity (mahopekṣā), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the nose element is pure; because the nose element is pure, great equanimity is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sphere of the nose is pure, and if great equanimity is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, and nose-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, are pure; because the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, great equanimity (mahopekṣā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the realm of fragrance up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, and the purity of great equanimity are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, great equanimity is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the tongue element is pure, and if great equanimity is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, great equanimity (mahopekṣā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and the purity of great equanimity, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, great equanimity is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the realm of the body is pure, and if great equanimity is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, great equanimity (mahopekṣā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the various feelings arising with the sphere of tangibles as condition up to the body-tangibles, and the purity of great equanimity, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

“Subhūti! Because the intention for the purity of all-knowledge wisdom is pure, the mind-element (*manodhātu*) is pure; because the mind-element is pure, great equanimity (*mahopekṣā*) is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the mental element is pure, and if great equanimity is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the dharma-element, the mental consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition, are pure; because the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition are pure, great equanimity is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu) up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, and the purity of great equanimity (mahopekṣā), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, great equanimity is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the earth element is pure, and if great equanimity is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, great equanimity is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, as well as the purity of great equanimity, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-conceptualization is pure; because non-conceptualization is pure, great equanimity is pure. Why is this?
Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of non-duality, or the purity of great equanimity, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, volitional formations (saṃskāra), consciousness (vijñāna), name-and-form (nāmarūpa), the six sense bases (ṣaḍāyatana), contact (sparśa), feeling (vedanā), craving (tṛṣṇā), grasping (upādāna), becoming (bhava), birth (jāti), and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, great equanimity (mahopekṣā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from formative factors up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, as well as the purity of great equanimity, are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, great relinquishment is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the perfection of giving (dānapāramitā), and the purity of great relinquishment (mahatyāga) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, great equanimity (mahopekṣā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), as well as the purity of great equanimity (mahopekṣā), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, great equanimity is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if internal emptiness is pure, and if great equanimity is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, not distinct, and not discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure; because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure, great equanimity (mahopekṣā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of being, the purity of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, and the purity of great equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, great equanimity is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of suchness, and the purity of great equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), non-falsity (avitathatā), unalterability (ananyathābhāva), equality (samatā), the state beyond birth (anupapattitā), the fixedness of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu) are pure; because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, great equanimity (mahopekṣā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, and the purity of great equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure; because the noble truth of suffering is pure, great equanimity is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the noble truth of suffering, and the purity of great equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are pure, great equanimity (*mahopekṣā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path, and the purity of great equanimity (mahopekṣā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, great equanimity is pure. Why is that?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the same as the purity of the four dhyānas and the purity of great equanimity, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, great equanimity is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, and the purity of great equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, great equanimity is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the eight liberations, and the purity of great equanimity, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the eight bases of mastery (abhibhvāyatana), the nine successive attainments (anupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (kṛtsnāyatana) are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, great equanimity (mahopekṣā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the eight bases of mastery (aṣṭāv abhibhvāyatanāni), the nine successive meditative attainments (navānupūrvavihārasamāpattayaḥ), and the ten pervasive bases (daśa kṛtsnāyatanāni)—as well as the purity of great equanimity (mahopekṣā)—are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four applications of mindfulness are pure; because the four applications of mindfulness are pure, great equanimity is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is [identical to] the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, or the purity of great equanimity, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and inseparable.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, great equanimity (mahopekṣā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) and the purity of the four right efforts (*samyakprahāṇa*) up to the eightfold noble path (*āryāṣṭāṅgamārga*), as well as the purity of great equanimity (*mahopekṣā*), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, great equanimity is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, and the purity of great equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure; because the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure, great equanimity is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, and the purity of great equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, great equanimity is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, and the purity of great equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, great equanimity is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purification of the knowledge of all modes, the purification of the five eyes, or the purification of great equanimity, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the six supernormal powers (ṣaḍabhijñā) are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, great equanimity (mahopekṣā) is pure. Why is this?

Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the six supernormal powers, or the purity of great equanimity, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, great equanimity is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, and if great equanimity is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, the four fearlessnesses (*vaiśāradya*), the four analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*), great loving-kindness (*mahāmaitrī*), great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*), great sympathetic joy (*mahāmuditā*), and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇika-buddhadharma*) are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, great equanimity (*mahopekṣā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, as well as the purity of great equanimity, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, great equanimity is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of great equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the state of constant equanimity is pure; because the state of constant equanimity is pure, great relinquishment is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the state of constant equanimity, and the purity of great equanimity, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the knowledge of all things is pure; because the knowledge of all things is pure, great equanimity is pure. Why is this?

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the unexcelled, perfect enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unexcelled, perfect enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, and the purity of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if form is pure, and if the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, or the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, and the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Why is this? Because if the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena are pure, and if the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the eye-element is pure, and if the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of everything from the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, and the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the ear-element is pure, and if the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of auditory consciousness, and ear-contact, as well as all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, are pure; because the sphere of sound up to all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness (asaṃpramoṣadharma) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the realm of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, and the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the realm of fragrance up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, and the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of the taste element (*rasadhātu*) up to the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness (*asaṃpramoṣadharma*) are non-dual, not divided into two, not distinct, and not discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the body-element is pure, and if the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, this is because they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the sensations produced with the body as the condition, from the element of touch up to [the element of] mental contact, and the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the intention for the purity of all-knowledge is pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the mind-element is pure, and if the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), or the purity of the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu) up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, or the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness—these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the earth element is pure, and if the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness (asaṃpramoṣadharma) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, or the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-forgetfulness is pure; because non-forgetfulness is pure, the quality of being without forgetfulness is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of non-obscuration, or the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, volitional formations (saṃskāra), consciousness (vijñāna), name-and-form (nāmarūpa), the six sense bases (ṣaḍāyatana), contact (sparśa), feeling (vedanā), craving (tṛṣṇā), grasping (upādāna), becoming (bhava), birth (jāti), and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness (asaṃpramoṣadharmatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, or the purity of everything from formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, or the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness—these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the perfection of generosity (dānapāramitā), and the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness (asaṃpramoṣadharma) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) and the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), as well as the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the qualities of non-forgetfulness are pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if inner emptiness is pure, and if the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, this is because they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure; because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of external emptiness up to the purity of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, or the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if suchness is pure, and if the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), the non-falsity of phenomena (avitathatā), the non-alteration of phenomena (ananyathābhāvatā), equality (samatā), the state beyond birth (anirodhatā), the fixedness of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the stability of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu) are pure. Because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness (asaṃpramoṣadharma) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the noble truth of suffering, and the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path, and the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four dhyānas, and the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the four immeasurables (apramāṇa) and the four formless attainments (ārūpyasamāpatti) are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness (asaṃpramoṣadharma) is pure.

Why is this? Because if the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, and if the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eight liberations, and the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the eight bases of mastery (aṣṭāv abhibhvāyatanāni), the nine successive attainments (navānupūrvavihārasamāpattayaḥ), and the ten totalities (daśa kṛtsnāyatanāni) are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness (asaṃpramoṣadharma) is pure.

Why is this? “Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four applications of mindfulness are pure; because the four applications of mindfulness are pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, and the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, and the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, or the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all-knowledge, or the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all doors of samādhi, or the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, and the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, or the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena (dharmāyatana), and the purity of the nature of constant equanimity (upekṣā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the state of constant equanimity is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the eye-element is pure, and if the nature of constant equanimity is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the form realm, the eye-consciousness realm, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure; because the form realm up to all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, the state of constant abiding in equanimity is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowing and the purity of everything from the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the nature of constant equanimity, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ear element is pure; because the ear element is pure, the nature of equanimity that abides constantly is pure. Why is this?
The purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ear-element, and the purity of the state of constant equanimity are non-dual; they are not divided, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of auditory consciousness, auditory contact, and the various feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure, the state of equanimity (upekṣā) that abides constantly is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of the sphere of sound (*śabdadhātu*) up to the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with ear-contact as a condition, and the purity of the nature of constant equanimity (*upekṣā*) are non-dual; they are not two, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! Because omniscient wisdom is pure, the nose element is pure; because the nose element is pure, the nature of constant abiding in equanimity is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the nose element, and the purity of the nature of constant equanimity are non-dual, undivided, distinctless, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, and nose-contact, as well as the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition, are pure; because the fragrance element up to the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the state of constant abiding in equanimity (upekṣā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the sphere of fragrance up to the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition, and the purity of the nature of constant equanimity are non-dual; they are not two, not divided, not distinct, and not separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the nature of constant abiding in equanimity is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the tongue element, and the purity of the state of constant abiding in equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the state of equanimity (upekṣā) in which one dwells constantly is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and the purity of the state of constant equanimity are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are without distinction, and they are not separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, the nature of equanimity that abides constantly is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the body element, and the purity of the nature of constant equanimity are non-dual, undivided, distinctless, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the state of equanimity (upekṣā) is pure.

Why is this? Because if the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the objects of touch up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, and if the state of constant equanimity is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

“Subhūti! Because the intentionality of the knowledge of all modes is pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the nature of equanimity that abides constantly is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the mental element is pure, and if the state of constant dwelling in equanimity is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness element, mental contact, and the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition are pure; because the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition are pure, the state of equanimity (upekṣā) that abides constantly is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) and the purity of everything from the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, and the purity of the state of constant equanimity (*upekṣā*), are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the nature of equanimity that abides constantly is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the earth element is pure, and if the nature of constant equanimity is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the nature of equanimity is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, and the purity of the nature of constant equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-conceptualization is pure; because non-conceptualization is pure, the nature of equanimity is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, if the purity of non-duality, and if the purity of the nature of constant equanimity are non-dual, undivided, distinctless, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, volitional formations (saṃskāra), consciousness (vijñāna), name-and-form (nāmarūpa), the six sense bases (ṣaḍāyatana), contact (sparśa), feeling (vedanā), craving (tṛṣṇā), grasping (upādāna), becoming (bhava), birth (jāti), and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the nature of equanimity (upekṣā-dhātu) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of everything from formations through old age, death, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, as well as the purity of the nature of constant equanimity, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, the nature of constant equanimity is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the perfection of generosity, and the purity of the state of constant equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, the state of equanimity (upekṣā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), and the purity of the state of constant equanimity (upekṣā) are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the state of constant equanimity is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if inner emptiness is pure, and if the nature of constant equanimity is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature are pure; because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature are pure, the state of equanimity (upekṣā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from external emptiness up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence (abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā), as well as the purity of the state of constant equanimity (upekṣā), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the nature of equanimity that abides constantly is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of suchness, and the purity of the nature of constant equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, non-falsity, immutability, equanimity, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm are pure; because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the state of constant abiding in equanimity is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, and the purity of the nature of constant equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure; because the noble truth of suffering is pure, the state of constant abiding in equanimity is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the noble truth of suffering, and the purity of the state of constant equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure, the nature of equanimity that abides constantly is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path, and the purity of the nature of constant equanimity, are non-dual; they are not two, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the state of equanimity that abides constantly is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four dhyānas, and the purity of the nature of constant equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, the state of constant equanimity is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, and the purity of the nature of constant equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the nature of constant equanimity is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eight liberations, and the purity of the nature of constant equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the state of equanimity that abides constantly is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the eight bases of mastery (aṣṭavimokṣa), the nine successive attainments (navānupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (daśakṛtsnāyatana), as well as the purity of the nature of constant equanimity (upekṣā), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four applications of mindfulness are pure; because the four applications of mindfulness are pure, the nature of constant equanimity is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, and the purity of the nature of constant equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, the state of equanimity (upekṣā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, and the purity of the nature of constant equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the state of constant equanimity is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, and the purity of the nature of constant equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the gates of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are pure; because the gates of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are pure, the state of constant equanimity is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—and the purity of the nature of constant equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the nature of equanimity that abides constantly is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, and the purity of the nature of constant equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the nature of constant equanimity is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the five eyes, or the purity of the nature of constant equanimity, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the wisdom of all-knowledge is pure, the six supernormal powers are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, the nature of equanimity is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the same as the purity of the six supernormal powers, and the purity of the nature of constant equanimity, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, the state of constant equanimity is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, and the purity of the nature of constant equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha are pure, the state of constant abiding in equanimity is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and the purity of the nature of constant equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the state of constant equanimity is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of the nature of constant equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the knowledge of all is pure; because the knowledge of all is pure, the nature of equanimity that abides constantly is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all-knowledge, and the purity of the nature of constant equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all aspects is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all modes are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all modes are pure, the state of constant equanimity is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects, and the purity of the state of constant equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all dharani-doors are pure; because all dharani-doors are pure, the nature of equanimity that abides constantly is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors, and the purity of the nature of constant equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all gateways to meditative concentration are pure; because all gateways to meditative concentration are pure, the state of equanimity that abides perpetually is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience, the purity of all gateways to samādhi, and the purity of the nature of constant equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, the state of constant equanimity is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, and the purity of the nature of constant equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are pure; because the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are pure, the nature of equanimity in constant abiding is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the fruit of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship, and the purity of the nature of constant equanimity, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure, the nature of equanimity that abides constantly is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of the nature of constant equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure, the nature of equanimity is pure.”
