Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience, the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of the nature of constant equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, the nature of constant equanimity is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, and the purity of the nature of constant equanimity are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of form, and if the purity of the knowledge of all modes is [the purity of form], they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, and the purity of all-knowledge (sarvajña) are non-dual; they are not two, not divided, not distinct, and not severed.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sense base of the eye is pure; because the sense base of the eye is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, if the purity of the sense-sphere of the eye, and if the purity of all-knowledge are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the sense bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, and the purity of all-knowledge are non-dual; they are not two, are not divided, are not distinct, and are not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the sphere of form, and if the purity of the knowledge of all modes is [the purity of the sphere of form], they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena (dharmāyatana), as well as the purity of omniscience (sarvajñatā), are non-dual; they are not two, they are without division, they are distinct, and they are uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the eye-element is pure, and if omniscience is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the form element, the eye-consciousness element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure; because the form element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience and the purity of everything from the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate. Thus, the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience and the purity of everything up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are non-dual, being without division, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the ear-element, and if the purity of the knowledge of all modes is [the purity of the ear-element], they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of sounds, the sphere of ear-consciousness, auditory contact, and all feelings produced with auditory contact as condition are pure; because the sphere of sounds up to all feelings produced with auditory contact as condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the realm of sound, up to and including the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, and the purity of all-knowledge (sarvajña), are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the nose element is pure; because the nose element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the nose element, and the purity of all-knowledge are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the realm of fragrance up to the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the tongue element, and if the purity of the knowledge of all modes is [the purity of the tongue element], they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) and the purity of the taste element (*rasadhātu*)—up to and including the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition—are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous. Thus, the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the knowledge of all things (*sarvajña*) are one and the same.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is [identical to] the purity of the body-element, and if the purity of the knowledge of all modes is [identical to] the purity of the knowledge of all modes, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the various feelings produced with the body as the basis for contact, up to the element of tangibles, are non-dual; they are not two, they are indivisible, they are without distinction, and they are not separate.
"Subhūti! Because the intentionality of the omniscience of all modes is pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the omniscience of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the mental faculty, and the purity of all-knowledge are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the dharma-element, the mental consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are pure; because the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu) up to the various sensations produced with mind-contact as a condition are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous. Thus, the purity of the knowledge of all modes [is identical to] the purity of everything from the dharma-realm up to the various sensations produced with mind-contact as a condition. Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes and the purity of everything from the dharma-realm up to the various sensations produced with mind-contact as a condition are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous. Therefore, the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of everything from the dharma-realm up to the various sensations produced with mind-contact as a condition, and the purity of everything from the dharma-realm up to the various sensations produced with mind-contact as a condition is the purity of the knowledge of all modes. Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes and the purity of everything from the dharma-realm up to the various sensations produced with mind-contact as a condition are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous. Thus, the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the dharma-realm, and the purity of the dharma-realm is the purity of the knowledge of all modes. Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes and the purity of the dharma-realm are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous. Thus, the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the eye-faculty, and the purity of the eye-faculty is the purity of the knowledge of all modes. Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes and the purity of the eye-faculty are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous. Thus, the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the ear-faculty, the nose-faculty, the tongue-faculty, the body-faculty, and the mental faculty (manas), and the purity of the mental faculty is the purity of the knowledge of all modes. Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes and the purity of the mental faculty are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous. Thus, the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of form, and the purity of form is the purity of the knowledge of all modes. Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes and the purity of form are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous. Thus, the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and phenomena (dharma), and the purity of phenomena is the purity of the knowledge of all modes. Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes and the purity of phenomena are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous. Thus, the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of eye-consciousness, and the purity of eye-consciousness is the purity of the knowledge of all modes. Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes and the purity of eye-consciousness are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous. Thus, the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, and mind-consciousness, and the purity of mind-consciousness is the purity of the knowledge of all modes. Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes and the purity of mind-consciousness are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous. Thus, the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of eye-contact, and the purity of eye-contact is the purity of the knowledge of all modes. Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes and the purity of eye-contact are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous. Thus, the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, and mind-contact, and the purity of mind-contact is the purity of the knowledge of all modes. Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes and the purity of mind-contact are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous. Thus, the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of sensation born of eye-contact, and the purity of sensation born of eye-contact is the purity of the knowledge of all modes. Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes and the purity of sensation born of eye-contact are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous. Thus, the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of sensation born of ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, and mind-contact, and the purity of sensation born of mind-contact is the purity of the knowledge of all modes. Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes and the purity of sensation born of mind-contact are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous. Therefore, the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of everything from the dharma-realm up to sensation born of mind-contact as a condition, and the purity of everything from the dharma-realm up to sensation born of mind-contact as a condition is the purity of the knowledge of all modes. Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes and the purity of everything from the dharma-realm up to sensation born of mind-contact as a condition are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous. Thus, the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the conditioned (saṃskṛta), and the purity of the conditioned is the purity of the knowledge of all modes. Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes and the purity of the conditioned are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous. Thus, the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the unconditioned (asaṃskṛta), and the purity of the unconditioned is the purity of the knowledge of all modes. Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes and the purity of the unconditioned are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous. Thus, the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the past, and the purity of the past is the purity of the knowledge of all modes. Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes and the purity of the past are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous. Thus, the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the future, and the purity of the future is the purity of the knowledge of all modes. Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes and the purity of the future are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous. Thus, the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the present, and the purity of the present is the purity of the knowledge of all modes. Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes and the purity of the present are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous. Thus, the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the internal, and the purity of the internal is the purity of the knowledge of all modes. Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes and the purity of the internal are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous. Thus, the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the external, and the purity of the external is the purity of the knowledge of all modes. Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes and the purity of the external are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous. Thus, the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the near, and the purity of the near is the purity of the knowledge of all modes. Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes and the purity of the near are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous. Thus, the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the far, and the purity of the far is the purity of the knowledge of all modes. Why
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the earth element, and the purity of all-knowledge are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, as well as the purity of all-knowledge (sarvajñatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of non-duality, or the purity of all-knowledge, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are pure; because formations through to old age, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from conditioned formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are non-dual; they are not two, not divided, distinct, or separate. Because they are thus, [the purity of the knowledge of all modes] is the purity of the knowledge of all things (sarvajña). Because they are thus, there is no duality, no division, no distinction, and no interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the perfection of generosity, and the purity of omniscience are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), and the purity of all-knowledge (sarvajña) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of internal emptiness, and the purity of all-knowledge are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure; because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence (abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā), as well as the purity of all-knowledge (sarvajñatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of suchness, and the purity of all-knowledge are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm are pure; because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, and the purity of all-knowledge are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure; because the Noble Truth of Suffering is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the noble truth of suffering, and if the purity of the knowledge of all modes is [the purity of the noble truth of suffering], they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not severed.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, and the purity of all-knowledge (sarvajña) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four dhyānas, and the purity of all-knowledge are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, and the purity of all-knowledge are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eight liberations, and the purity of all-knowledge are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the eight bases of mastery (abhibhvāyatana), the nine successive attainments (anupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (kṛtsnāyatana) are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the eight bases of mastery (aṣṭau vimokṣāḥ), the nine successive attainments (navānupūrvavihārasamāpattayaḥ), and the ten totalities (daśakṛtsnāyatanāni), as well as the purity of all-knowledge (sarvajñatā), are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four applications of mindfulness are pure; because the four applications of mindfulness are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, and the purity of all-knowledge are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eight branches of the noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eight branches of the noble path are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, as well as the purity of all-knowledge (sarvajñatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the door of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the door of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, and the purity of all-knowledge are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the gateways to liberation of signlessness (animitta) and wishlessness (apraṇihita) are pure; because the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, and the purity of all-knowledge (sarvajñatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, and the purity of all-knowledge are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purification of the knowledge of all modes, the purification of the five eyes, or the purification of all-knowledge, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the wisdom of all-knowledge is pure, the six supernormal powers are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, the wisdom of all-knowledge is pure.

Why is this? Whether it be the purity of the wisdom of all-knowledge, the purity of the six supernormal powers, or the purity of the wisdom of all-knowledge, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, and the purity of all-knowledge are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and the purity of all-knowledge (sarvajña) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of all-knowledge are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the omniscience of all-knowledge is pure, the state of constant abiding in equanimity is pure; because the state of constant abiding in equanimity is pure, the omniscience of all-knowledge is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is [identical to] the purity of the state of constant equanimity, and if the purity of all-knowledge is [identical to it], they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the knowledge of the paths is pure; because the knowledge of the paths is pure, the knowledge of all is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the knowledge of the paths, or the purity of the knowledge of all things, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure; because the knowledge of all aspects is pure, the knowledge of all is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the knowledge of all aspects, or the purity of all-knowledge, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle Two Hundred and Seventy-nine. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter Thirty-four, "Difficult to Believe and Understand," Section Ninety-nine. "Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, all dharani-doors are pure; because all dharani-doors are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all dharani-doors, and the purity of all-knowledge are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.
Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure; because all doors of samādhi are pure, the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all doors of samādhi, and the purity of all-knowledge are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, and the purity of all-knowledge are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are pure; because the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship, and the purity of all-knowledge are non-dual; they are not two, not divided, not distinct, and not severed.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the enlightenment of the solitary realizers is pure; because the enlightenment of the solitary realizers is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of all-knowledge are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of all-knowledge are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, the knowledge of all modes is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, and the purity of all-knowledge are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the knowledge of the paths is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of form, and the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the knowledge of the aspects of the path is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness, and the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye base is pure; because the eye base is pure, the knowledge of the paths is pure. Why is that?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the sphere of the eye is pure, and if the knowledge of the aspects of the path is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the knowledge of the paths is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, and the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path (mārgākārajñatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not severed.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the knowledge of the paths is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the same as the purity of the sense-sphere of form, and the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and inseparable.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure, the knowledge of the paths is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, and the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the knowledge of the paths is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eye-element, or the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the form realm (rūpadhātu), the eye-consciousness realm (cakṣurvijñānadhātu), eye-contact (cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa), and the various feelings (vedanā) produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure; because the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of the aspects of the path (mārgākārajñatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) and the purity of everything from the form realm (*rūpadhātu*) up to the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with eye-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the knowledge of the paths is pure. Why is this?
The purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ear-element, and the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not divided.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of auditory consciousness, auditory contact, and the various sensations produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of sound up to the various sensations produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of the aspects of the path (mārgākārajñatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of the realm of sound (*śabdadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the nose-element is pure; because the nose-element is pure, the knowledge of the paths is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the nose element, and the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of the aspects of the path (mārgākārajñatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of the realm of fragrance up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the tongue element is pure; because the tongue element is pure, the knowledge of the aspects of the path is pure. Why is this?

The purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the tongue element, and the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path are non-dual; they are not two, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of the aspects of the path is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body-element is pure; because the body-element is pure, the knowledge of the paths is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the body element, and the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path are non-dual, not two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, the element of tangibles (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*), the element of body-consciousness (*kāyavijñānadhātu*), body-contact (*kāyasparśa*), and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) and the purity of the various feelings arising with the body as the basis and contact as the condition—from the element of touch (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*) onwards—and the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.
“Subhūti! Because the intentionality of the knowledge of all modes is pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the knowledge of the aspects of the path is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the mental faculty, and the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and inseparable.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the dharma-element, the mental consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are pure; because the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of the aspects of the path is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path (mārgākārajñatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the knowledge of the paths is pure. Why is this?
The purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the earth element, and the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the knowledge of the aspects of the path is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, as well as the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path (mārgākārajñatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the knowledge of the aspects of the path is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the knowledge of paths, or the purity of the knowledge of non-arising, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the knowledge of the aspects of the path (mārgākārajñatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of everything from conditioned formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, or the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, the knowledge of the paths is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the perfection of generosity, and the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, the knowledge of the aspects of the path (mārgākārajñatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom, and the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the knowledge of the paths is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of internal emptiness, or the purity of the knowledge of the paths, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, there is purity of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence. Because there is purity from external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of external emptiness up to the purity of the emptiness of the nature of non-existence (*abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā*), and the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the knowledge of the paths is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of suchness, or the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), non-falsity (*avitathatā*), unalterability (*ananyathātva*), equality (*samatā*), the state beyond birth (*anirodhatā*), the fixedness of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*) are pure; because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, and the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure; because the noble truth of suffering is pure, the knowledge of the paths is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the noble truth of suffering, and the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure, the knowledge of the paths is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, and the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path, are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct from one another, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the knowledge of the paths is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four dhyānas, and the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, the knowledge of the paths is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, and the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path (mārgākārajñatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the knowledge of the paths is pure. Why is this?

The purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eight liberations, and the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the knowledge of the paths is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the eight bases of mastery (aṣṭavimokṣa), the nine successive attainments (navānupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (daśakṛtsnāyatana), as well as the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path (mārgākārajñatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four foundations of mindfulness are pure; because the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, the knowledge of the paths is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is such, and the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, and the purity of the knowledge of the paths are such, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, the knowledge of the paths (mārgākārajñatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, as well as the purity of the knowledge of the paths (mārgākārajñatā), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the door of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the door of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the knowledge of the aspects of the path is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, and the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the gateways of liberation of signlessness (animitta) and wishlessness (apraṇihita) are pure; because the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure, the knowledge of the aspects of the path (mārgākārajñatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, and the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the knowledge of the aspects of the path is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, and the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the knowledge of the paths is pure. Why is this?"

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the five eyes, or the purity of the knowledge of the paths, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the six supernormal knowledges (ṣaḍabhijñā) are pure; because the six supernormal knowledges are pure, the knowledge of the aspects of the path (mārgākārajñatā) is pure. Why is this?

Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the six supernormal knowledges, or the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, the knowledge of the aspects of the path is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the same as the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, and the purity of the knowledge of the paths, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four fearlessnesses (vaiśāradya), the four analytical knowledges (pratisaṃvid), great loving-kindness (mahāmaitrī), great compassion (mahākaruṇā), great sympathetic joy (mahāmuditā), great equanimity (mahopekṣā), and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (āveṇika-buddhadharma) are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, the knowledge of the path (mārgākārajñatā) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and the purity of the knowledge of the paths (mārgākārajñatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the knowledge of the paths is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the state of constant equanimity (upekṣā) is pure; because the state of constant equanimity is pure, the knowledge of the aspects of the path (mārgākārajñatā) is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the state of constant equanimity, and the purity of the knowledge of the paths are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the knowledge of all things is pure; because the knowledge of all things is pure, the knowledge of the paths is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all-knowledge, or the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure; because the knowledge of all aspects is pure, the knowledge of the paths is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the knowledge of all aspects, or the purity of the knowledge of the paths, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all dharani-doors are pure; because all dharani-doors are pure, the knowledge of the paths is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors, and the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure; because all doors of samādhi are pure, the knowledge of the paths is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all doors of samādhi, and the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, the knowledge of the paths is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, and the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are pure; because the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are pure, the knowledge of the paths is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship, and the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path (mārgākārajñatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the enlightenment of the solitary buddhas is pure; because the enlightenment of the solitary buddhas is pure, the knowledge of the paths is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure, the knowledge of the aspects of the path is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path (mārgākārajñatā) are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, the knowledge of the paths is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, and the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of form, and the purity of the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, and the purity of the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye base is pure; because the eye base is pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the sense-sphere of the eye, and the purity of the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, and the purity of the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the sphere of form, and the purity of the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental objects (dharmāyatana), and the purity of the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-faculty is pure; because the eye-faculty is pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eye-element, or the purity of the knowledge of all aspects, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the form element, the eye-consciousness element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure; because the form element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of everything from the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ear-element, or the purity of the knowledge of all aspects, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of sounds, the sphere of ear-consciousness, ear-contact, and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of sounds up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the nose element is pure; because the nose element is pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the nose element, and the purity of the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the various feelings produced with the fragrance-element and so forth as conditions for nose-contact, and the purity of the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā), are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the tongue element, and the purity of the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the taste element and even the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the body element, and the purity of the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the various feelings arising with the body as the condition—beginning from the element of tangibility up to the contact of the body—are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate. This is because they are without differentiation and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the intentionality of the knowledge of all modes is pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure. Why is this?

The purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the mind-element, and the purity of the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness element, mental contact, and the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition are pure; because the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition are pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, and the purity of the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure. Why is this?

The purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the earth element, and the purity of the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, or the purity of the knowledge of all aspects, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the knowledge of non-arising, or the purity of the knowledge of all aspects, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the perfection of generosity, and the purity of the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom, and the purity of the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of internal emptiness, and the purity of the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, there is the purity of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence. Because there is the purity of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of external emptiness up to the purity of the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature, and the purity of the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of suchness, and the purity of the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the non-erroneous nature (*avitathatā*), the unchanging nature (*ananyathātā*), equality (*samatā*), the state of being free from birth (*anirodhatā*), the fixedness of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*) are pure; because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, and the purity of the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure; because the noble truth of suffering is pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the noble truth of suffering, and the purity of the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual; they are not two, not divided, not distinct, and not severed.

"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eight liberations, and the purity of the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight spheres of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure; because the eight spheres of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, and the purity of the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, and the purity of the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure."
