If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, if the purity of the state of constant equanimity, and if the purity of the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous; therefore, they are one and the same.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the knowledge of all is pure; because the knowledge of all is pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all-knowledge, and the purity of the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the knowledge of the paths, or the purity of the knowledge of all aspects, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all dhāraṇī gateways are pure; because all dhāraṇī gateways are pure, the knowledge of all aspects is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, and the purity of the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, all gateways to meditative concentration are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the perfection of generosity, and the purity of all gateways to meditative concentration are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), and the purity of all gateways of meditative concentration (*samādhi*) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of internal emptiness, and the purity of all doors of samādhi are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure; because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure, all doors of samādhi are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of outer emptiness up to the purity of the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, and the purity of all doors of samādhi, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of suchness, and the purity of all gateways to meditative concentration are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the non-falsity of phenomena (*avitathatā*), the unchanging nature of phenomena (*ananyathābhāvatā*), the equality of phenomena (*samatā*), the state beyond birth (*anirodhatā*), the fixedness of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*) are pure. Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, and the purity of all doors of samādhi are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure; because the noble truth of suffering is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the noble truth of suffering (duḥkha-āryasatya), and the purity of all doors of meditative concentration (samādhi-mukha) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure, all doors of meditative concentration (samādhi-mukha) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path, and the purity of all gateways to meditative concentration (*samādhi*) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, all doors of samādhi are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the four dhyānas, and the purity of all doors of samādhi are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are pure, all doors of samādhi are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience, the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, and the purity of all doors of samādhi are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, all doors of samādhi are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the eight liberations, and the purity of all doors of samādhi are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the eight bases of mastery (abhibhvāyatana), the nine successive attainments (anupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (kṛtsnāyatana) are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, all doors of samādhi (samādhimukha) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the eight bases of mastery (aṣṭavimokṣa), the nine successive attainments (navānupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (daśakṛtsnāyatana)—as well as the purity of all doors of samādhi—are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four applications of mindfulness are pure; because the four applications of mindfulness are pure, all doors of samādhi are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, and the purity of all doors of samādhi are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, all gateways to meditative concentration (*samādhi-mukha*) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) and the purity of the four right efforts (*samyakprahāṇa*) up to the eightfold noble path (*āryāṣṭāṅgamārga*), as well as the purity of all gateways to meditative concentration (*samādhi-mukha*), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, all gates of samādhi are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, and the purity of all gates of samādhi are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, the gateways of liberation of signlessness (*animitta*) and wishlessness (*apraṇihita*) are pure; because the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure, all gateways of meditative concentration (*samādhi*) are pure.

Why is this? Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—or the purity of all gateways of samādhi, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, all doors of samādhi are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, and the purity of all gateways to samādhi are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, all doors of samādhi are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the five eyes, and the purity of all doors of samādhi are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, the six supernormal powers are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, all doors of samādhi are pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the six supernormal powers, or the purity of all doors of samādhi, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten powers of a buddha are pure; because the ten powers of a buddha are pure, all doors of samādhi are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, and the purity of all doors of samādhi are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four fearlessnesses (vaiśāradya), the four analytical knowledges (pratisaṃvid), great loving-kindness (mahāmaitrī), great compassion (mahākaruṇā), great sympathetic joy (mahāmuditā), great equanimity (mahopekṣā), and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (āveṇikabuddhadharma) are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, all doors of meditative concentration (samādhimukha) are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and the purity of all doors of samādhi are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the state of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of all doors of samādhi are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.

Because the knowledge of all modes of omniscience is pure, the state of constant abiding in equanimity is pure; because the state of constant abiding in equanimity is pure, all gateways to meditative concentration are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the nature of constant equanimity, and the purity of all doors of samādhi are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all-knowledge is pure; because all-knowledge is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all-knowledge, and the purity of all doors of samādhi are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, all gateways to meditative concentration are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path (mārgākārajñatā) and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā), and the purity of all doors of samādhi are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all dhāraṇī-doors are pure; because all dhāraṇī-doors are pure, all samādhi-doors are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors, and the purity of all samādhi-doors are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, and the purity of all doors of samādhi are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure; because the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are pure, all doors of samādhi are pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the fruit of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship, and the purity of all doors of samādhi are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of all doors of samādhi are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure, all doors of samādhi are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of all samādhi-gates are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the unexcelled, perfect enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unexcelled, perfect enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, and the purity of all doors of samādhi are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if form is pure, and if the fruit of stream-entry is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience, the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, and the purity of the fruit of stream-entry are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not separate.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye base is pure; because the eye base is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure. Why is that?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sense base of the eye is pure, and if the fruit of stream-entry is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, as well as the purity of the fruit of stream-entry (srotāpattiphala), are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the sphere of form, and the purity of the fruit of stream-entry are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, and the purity of the fruit of stream-entry are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eye-element, and the purity of the fruit of stream-entry are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the form element (rūpadhātu), the eye-consciousness element (cakṣurvijñānadhātu), eye-contact (cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa), and the various feelings (vedanā) arising with eye-contact as condition are pure; because the form element up to the various feelings arising with eye-contact as condition are pure, the fruit of stream-entry (srotāpattiphala) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the form realm (*rūpadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the fruit of stream-entry (*srotāpattiphala*), are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure. Why is that?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the ear-element is pure, and if the fruit of stream-entry is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of auditory consciousness, auditory contact, and the various feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with auditory contact as a condition are pure, the fruit of stream-entry (srotāpattiphala) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, and the purity of the fruit of stream-entry (srotāpattiphala), are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not severed.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle Two Hundred and Eighty-one. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: The Chapter on Difficult-to-Believe Understanding, Thirty-fourth, Section One of One Hundred and One. "Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*) is pure, the nose-element (*ghrāṇadhātu*) is pure; because the nose-element is pure, the fruit of stream-entry (*srotāpattiphala*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the nose-element, and the purity of the fruit of stream-entry are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the fruit of stream-entry (srotāpattiphala) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the realm of fragrance up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, and the purity of the fruit of stream-entry (srotāpattiphala) are non-dual; they are not two, they are not divided, they are not distinct, and they are not separate.
“Subhūti! Because omniscience is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the tongue element, and the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to the various sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the fruit of stream-entry (srotāpattiphala) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the taste element, up to and including the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and the purity of the fruit of stream-entry (srotāpattiphala), are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the body element, and the purity of the fruit of stream-entry are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the fruit of stream-entry (srotāpattiphala) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the various feelings arising with the body as the basis for contact, up to the contact element, and the purity of the fruit of stream-entry (srotāpattiphala) are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.
“Subhūti! Because the intentionality of the knowledge of all modes is pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure. Why is that?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the mind-element is pure, and if the fruit of stream-entry is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, and mind-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition, are pure; because the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition are pure, the fruit of stream-entry (srotāpattiphala) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of everything from the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition, and the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure. Why is this?
The purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the earth element, and the purity of the fruit of stream-entry are non-dual; they are not two, not divided, not distinct, and not separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, as well as the purity of the fruit of stream-entry (srotāpattiphala), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the outflows-free state, and the purity of the fruit of stream-entry are non-dual, undivided, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, volitional formations (saṃskāra), consciousness (vijñāna), name-and-form (nāmarūpa), the six sense bases (ṣaḍāyatana), contact (sparśa), feeling (vedanā), craving (tṛṣṇā), grasping (upādāna), becoming (bhava), birth (jāti), and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair (jarāmaraṇa-śoka-parideva-duḥkha-daurmanasyopāyāsa) are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the fruit of stream-entry (srotāpattiphala) is pure.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of generosity is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the perfection of generosity, and the purity of the fruit of stream-entry are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the precepts up to the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), as well as the purity of the fruit of stream-entry (srotāpattiphala), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if inner emptiness is pure, and if the fruit of stream-entry is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, there is the purity of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence. Because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is pure, the fruit of stream-entry (srotāpattiphala) is pure.

Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the four immeasurables (apramāṇa), the four formless absorptions (ārūpyasamāpatti), and the fruit of once-returning (sakṛdāgāmiphala) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

"Subhūti! Because all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the eight liberations (aṣṭavimokṣa) are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the fruit of once-returning (sakṛdāgāmiphala) is pure. Why is this?..."
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eight liberations, and the purity of the fruit of once-returning are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the eight bases of mastery (abhibhvāyatana), the nine successive attainments (anupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (kṛtsnāyatana) are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the fruit of once-returning (sakṛdāgāmiphala) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the eight bases of mastery (aṣṭau vimokṣāḥ), the nine successive attainments (navānupūrvavihārasamāpattayaḥ), and the ten totalities (daśakṛtsnāyatanāni), as well as the purity of the fruit of once-returning (sakṛdāgāmiphala), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four applications of mindfulness are pure; because the four applications of mindfulness are pure, the fruit of once-returning is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, and the purity of the fruit of once-returning are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, the fruit of once-returning (sakṛdāgāmiphala) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path, as well as the purity of the fruit of once-returning, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the door of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the door of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the fruit of once-returning is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purification of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purification of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, and the purification of the fruit of once-returning are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the gateways of liberation of signlessness (animitta) and wishlessness (apraṇihita) are pure; because the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure, the fruit of once-returning (sakṛdāgāmiphala) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—and the purity of the fruit of once-returning are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the fruit of once-returning is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, and the purity of the fruit of once-returning are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the fruit of once-returning is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the five eyes, or the purity of the fruit of once-returning, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the six supernormal powers (ṣaḍabhijñā) are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, the fruit of once-returning (sakṛdāgāmiphala) is pure. Why is this?

Because whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the six supernormal powers, or the purity of the fruit of once-returning, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, the fruit of once-returning is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, and the purity of the fruit of once-returning are non-dual, without division, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, the fruit of the once-returner (sakṛdāgāmiphala) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and the purity of the fruit of the once-returner (sakṛdāgāmiphala) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the fruit of once-returning is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of the fruit of once-returning are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the state of constant equanimity is pure; because the state of constant equanimity is pure, the fruit of once-returning is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the state of constant equanimity, and the purity of the fruit of the once-returner are non-dual, without duality, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the knowledge of all things is pure; because the knowledge of all things is pure, the fruit of once-returning is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all-knowledge, or the purity of the fruit of once-returning, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, the fruit of once-returning is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, and the purity of the fruit of once-returning are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all dhāraṇī-doors are pure; because all dhāraṇī-doors are pure, the fruit of once-returning is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience, the purity of all dharani-doors, and the purity of the fruit of the once-returner are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure; because all doors of samādhi are pure, the fruit of once-returning is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of all doors of samādhi, and the purity of the fruit of once-returning are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, the fruit of once-returning is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the same as the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, and the purity of the fruit of once-returning, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of non-returning and the fruit of arhatship are pure; because the fruit of non-returning and the fruit of arhatship are pure, the fruit of once-returning is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the fruit of non-returning (anāgāmiphala) and the fruit of arhatship (arhattvaphala), and the purity of the fruit of once-returning (sakṛdāgāmiphala) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, the fruit of once-returning is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of the fruit of once-returning are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure, the fruit of once-returning is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of the fruit of once-returning (*sakṛdāgāmiphala*) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the unexcelled, perfect enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unexcelled, perfect enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, the fruit of once-returning is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, and the purity of the fruit of the once-returner are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the fruit of non-returning is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if form is pure, and if the fruit of non-returning is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the fruit of non-returning is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, and the purity of the fruit of non-returning (anāgāmiphala) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-base is pure; because the eye-base is pure, the fruit of non-returning is pure. Why is that?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sense base of the eye is pure, and if the fruit of non-returning is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the bases of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the fruit of non-returning is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, and the purity of the fruit of non-returning (anāgāmiphala) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the fruit of non-returning is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sphere of form is pure, and if the fruit of non-returning is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena (dharmāyatana) are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena are pure, the fruit of non-returning (anāgāmiphala) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena (dharmāyatana), as well as the purity of the fruit of non-returning (anāgāmiphala), are non-dual; they are not two, not divided, not distinct, and not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-faculty is pure; because the eye-faculty is pure, the fruit of non-returning is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the eye-element is pure, and if the fruit of non-returning is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the form realm (rūpadhātu), the eye-consciousness realm (cakṣurvijñānadhātu), eye-contact (cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa), and the various feelings (vedanā) produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure; because the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, the fruit of non-returning (anāgāmiphala) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the form realm (rūpadhātu) up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the fruit of non-returning (anāgāmiphala), are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the fruit of non-returning is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the ear-element is pure, and if the fruit of non-returning is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of ear-consciousness, ear-contact, and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure; because the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure, the fruit of non-returning is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the sphere of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, and the purity of the fruit of non-returning (anāgāmiphala) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the nose element is pure; because the nose element is pure, the fruit of non-returning is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the nose element, and the purity of the fruit of non-returning are non-dual, indivisible, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as condition are pure, the fruit of non-returning (anāgāmiphala) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the realm of fragrance up to the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition, and the purity of the fruit of non-returning (anāgāmiphala), are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the fruit of non-returning is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the tongue element is pure, and if the fruit of non-returning is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the fruit of non-returning (anāgāmiphala) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and the purity of the fruit of non-returning are non-dual; they are not divided into two, they are not distinct, and they are not discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, the fruit of non-returning is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the sphere of the body is pure, and if the fruit of non-returning is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the fruit of non-returning is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) and the purity of the sensations produced with the body as the basis and tangibles as the condition—up to the purity of the fruit of non-returning (*anāgāmiphala*)—are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the intentionality of the knowledge of all modes is pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the fruit of non-returning is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the mind-element is pure, and if the fruit of non-returning is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are pure; because the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are pure, the fruit of non-returning (anāgāmiphala) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of everything from the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the fruit of non-returning, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the fruit of non-returning is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the earth element, and the purity of the fruit of non-returning are non-dual, without division, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the fruit of non-returning is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowing and the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, as well as the purity of the fruit of non-returning, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the fruit of non-returning is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the fruit of non-returning is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, volitional formations (saṃskāra), consciousness (vijñāna), name-and-form (nāmarūpa), the six sense bases (ṣaḍāyatana), contact (sparśa), feeling (vedanā), craving (tṛṣṇā), clinging (upādāna), becoming (bhava), birth (jāti), and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the fruit of non-returning (anāgāmiphala) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from conditioned formations up to old age, death, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, as well as the purity of the fruit of non-returning (anāgāmiphala), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of giving is pure; because the perfection of giving is pure, the fruit of non-returning is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the perfection of generosity, and the purity of the fruit of non-returning are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, the fruit of non-returning (anāgāmiphala) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom, as well as the purity of the fruit of non-returning, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the fruit of non-returning is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if internal emptiness is pure, and if the fruit of non-returning is pure, it is because they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure; because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is pure, the fruit of non-returning (anāgāmiphala) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from outer emptiness up to the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature (abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā), as well as the purity of the fruit of non-returning (anāgāmiphala), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the fruit of non-returning is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if suchness is pure, and if the fruit of non-returning is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), the non-falsity of phenomena (avitathatā), the unchanging nature of phenomena (ananyathābhāvatā), equality (samatā), the state beyond birth (anupapattitā), the fixed nature of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu) are pure. Because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the fruit of non-returning (anāgāmiphala) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, and the purity of the fruit of non-returning are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure; because the noble truth of suffering is pure, the fruit of non-returning is pure. Why is this?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, and if the noble truth of suffering is pure, and if the fruit of non-returning is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure, the fruit of non-returning is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, and the purity of the fruit of non-returning (anāgāmiphala) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle Two Hundred and Eighty-Two. Translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter Thirty-Four, "Difficult to Believe and Understand," Section One of Two. "Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the fruit of non-returning (anāgāmiphala) is pure. Why is this?

Because whether it is the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four dhyānas, or the purity of the fruit of non-returning, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are pure, the fruit of non-returning is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the four immeasurables (apramāṇa) and the four formless attainments (ārūpyasamāpatti), and the purity of the fruit of non-returning (anāgāmiphala) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the fruit of non-returning is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the eight liberations, and the purity of the fruit of non-returning, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) is pure, the eight bases of mastery (*abhibhvāyatana*), the nine successive attainments (*anupūrvavihārasamāpatti*), and the ten totalities (*kṛtsnāyatana*) are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the fruit of non-returning (*anāgāmiphala*) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the eight bases of mastery (aṣṭavimokṣa), the nine successive attainments (navānupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten pervasive bases (daśakṛtsnāyatana), as well as the purity of the fruit of non-returning (anāgāmiphala), are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four applications of mindfulness are pure; because the four applications of mindfulness are pure, the fruit of non-returning is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes is the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, and the purity of the fruit of non-returning, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes of being (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, the fruit of non-returning (anāgāmiphala) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge and the purity of the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path, as well as the purity of the fruit of non-returning, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the fruit of non-returning is pure."
