"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure; because the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure, the fruit of arhatship is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, and the purity of the fruit of arhatship are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are pure, the fruit of arhatship is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of the fruit of arhatship are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, the fruit of arhatship is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, and the purity of the fruit of arhatship are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and not separate.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, form is pure; because form is pure, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if form is pure, and if the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, and the purity of the enlightenment of a solitary buddha (pratyekabuddhabodhi) are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-base is pure; because the eye-base is pure, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure. Why is that?

If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the sense-sphere of the eye is pure, and if the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure; because the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, and the purity of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the sphere of form is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the sphere of form, and the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena (dharmāyatana), and the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eye-element is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eye-element, or the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the form realm (rūpadhātu), the eye-consciousness realm (cakṣurvijñānadhātu), eye-contact (cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa), and the various feelings (vedanā) produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure. Because the form realm up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, the awakening of a solitary realizer (pratyekabuddhabodhi) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of everything from the form realm (rūpadhātu) up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, as well as the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ear-element is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ear-element, and the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the sphere of sound, the sphere of auditory consciousness, and ear-contact, as well as the various sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition, are pure; because the sphere of sound up to the various sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure, the enlightenment of a Pratyekabuddha is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the realm of sound up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, and the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the nose element is pure; because the nose element is pure, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the nose element, and the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous; therefore, they are one and the same.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure; because the fragrance element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the realm of fragrance up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, and the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the tongue-element is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the tongue element, and the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure; because the taste element up to the various sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the taste element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the body element is pure; because the body element is pure, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure. Why is this?
If the knowledge of all modes is pure, if the realm of the body is pure, and if the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure; because the element of tangibles up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience, the purity of the sense-sphere of tangibles up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, and the purity of the enlightenment of a Pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the intentionality of the knowledge of all modes is pure, the mind-element is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure. Why is this?
The purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the mental faculty, and the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, mind-contact, and the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition are pure; because the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition are pure, the enlightenment of a solitary realizer (pratyekabuddhabodhi) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of omniscience, the purity of everything from the dharma-realm up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, and the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the earth element is pure; because the earth element is pure, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure. Why is this?

The purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the earth element, and the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are pure, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and the purity of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, as well as the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
"Subhūti! Because omniscience is pure, non-arising is pure; because non-arising is pure, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the knowledge of non-arising, or the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, they are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, formative forces (saṃskāra), consciousness (vijñāna), name-and-form (nāmarūpa), the six sense bases (ṣaḍāyatana), contact (sparśa), feeling (vedanā), craving (tṛṣṇā), grasping (upādāna), becoming (bhava), birth (jāti), and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure; because formative forces through old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of everything from formative activities up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, and the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the perfection of giving is pure; because the perfection of giving is pure, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the perfection of giving, and the purity of pratyekabuddha enlightenment are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom are pure, the enlightenment of a solitary buddha (pratyekabuddhabodhi) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the pure precepts up to the perfection of wisdom, and the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, internal emptiness is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure. Why is this?
The purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of internal emptiness, and the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure. Because external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure, the enlightenment of the solitary realizer (pratyekabuddhabodhi) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of outer emptiness up to the purity of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence (abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā), and the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, suchness is pure; because suchness is pure, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure. Why is this?
If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of suchness, and the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), non-illusory nature, unchanging nature, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the stability of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm are pure; because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are pure, the enlightenment of the solitary realizer (pratyekabuddhabodhi) is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, and the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truth of suffering is pure; because the noble truth of suffering is pure, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the noble truth of suffering, and the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are pure; because the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are pure, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, and the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four dhyānas are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four dhyānas, and the purity of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, and the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the eight liberations are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the eight liberations, and the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the eight bases of mastery (abhibhvāyatana), the nine successive attainments (anupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and the ten totalities (kṛtsnāyatana) are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna), the purity of the eight bases of mastery (aṣṭāv abhibhvāyatanāni), the nine successive attainments (navānupūrvavihārasamāpattayaḥ), and the ten pervasive bases (daśa kṛtsnāyatanāni), and the purity of the enlightenment of a solitary buddha (pratyekabuddhabodhi) are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the four applications of mindfulness are pure; because the four applications of mindfulness are pure, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the four foundations of mindfulness, and the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are pure; because the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are pure, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, and the purity of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and inseparable.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure; because the gate of liberation that is emptiness is pure, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, and the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge is pure, the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure; because the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, the purity of the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, and the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten stages of a bodhisattva are pure; because the ten stages of a bodhisattva are pure, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten stages of a bodhisattva, and the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the five eyes are pure; because the five eyes are pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the five eyes, or the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñājñāna*) is pure, the six supernormal powers (*ṣaḍabhijñā*) are pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha (*pratyekabodhi*) is pure. Why is this?

Whether it be the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the six supernormal powers, or the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, these are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the ten powers of a Buddha are pure; because the ten powers of a Buddha are pure, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the ten powers of a Buddha, and the purity of the enlightenment of a Pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna) is pure, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are pure, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is pure, the state of dwelling in equanimity (upekṣāvihāritā) is pure; because the state of dwelling in equanimity is pure, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure. Why is this?

If the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the state of constant equanimity, and the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all-knowledge is pure; because all-knowledge is pure, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure."

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all-knowledge, and the purity of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are pure, the enlightenment of the solitary buddhas is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects, and the purity of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, all dharanī-doors are pure; because all dharanī-doors are pure, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of all dhāraṇī-doors, and the purity of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, nor discontinuous.
Because the knowledge of all modes of omniscience is pure, all doors of samādhi are pure; because all doors of samādhi are pure, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of all doors of samādhi, and the purity of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.
“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruit of stream-entry is pure; because the fruit of stream-entry is pure, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the fruit of stream-entry, and the purity of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are pure; because the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are pure, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is pure.

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), the purity of the fruit of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship, and the purity of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure; because the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are pure, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the purity of pratyekabuddha enlightenment are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and without interruption.

“Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes is pure, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure; because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is pure, the enlightenment of the Pratyekabuddhas is pure.”

Why is this? Because the purity of the knowledge of all modes, the purity of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, and the purity of the enlightenment of the Pratyekabuddhas are non-dual, not divided into two, without distinction, and uninterrupted.

Because the present is pure, the past and future are pure; because the past and future are pure, the present is pure. Why is this?

and without interruption. — *The Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, Fascicle 284 (Fascicle 285).
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang under Imperial Decree. Chapter 35:
Praise of Purity, Part One. Section 35-1: Praise of Purity. At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
Such purity is most profound.
The Buddha said:
"Because it is thus ultimately pure. Śāriputra asked:
"By virtue of which dharma being ultimately pure is this purity said to be most profound?"
The Buddha said,
“Śāriputra! Because form is ultimately pure, this purity is said to be most profound;”
Because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are ultimately pure, this purity is said to be most profound.
"Śāriputra! Because the eye-base is ultimately pure, this purity is said to be most profound; [and so on for the other bases]."
Because the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are ultimately pure, this purity is said to be most profound.
"Śāriputra! Because the sphere of form is ultimately pure, this purity is said to be most profound; [and so on for the other spheres]."
Because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are ultimately pure, this purity is said to be most profound.
"Śāriputra, because the eye-sphere is ultimately pure, this purity is said to be most profound; [and so forth for the other sense-spheres]."
Because the form realm, the eye-consciousness element, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are ultimately pure, this purity is said to be most profound.
“Śāriputra! Because the ear-element is ultimately pure, this purity is said to be most profound;
because the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are ultimately pure, this purity is said to be most profound.”
“Śāriputra! Because the nose element (*ghrāṇadhātu*) is ultimately pure, this purity is said to be most profound;

because the odor element (*gandhadhātu*), the nose-consciousness element (*ghrāṇavijñānadhātu*), nose-contact (*ghrāṇasparśa*), and all sensations (*vedanā*) produced with nose-contact as a condition are ultimately pure, this purity is said to be most profound.”
“Śāriputra! Because the tongue element is ultimately pure, this purity is said to be most profound;

because the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are ultimately pure, this purity is said to be most profound.”
“Śāriputra! Because the body element (*kāyadhātu*) is ultimately pure, this purity is said to be most profound;

because the touch element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*), the body-consciousness element (*kāyavijñānadhātu*), body-contact (*kāyasparśa*), and all feelings (*vedanā*) arising with body-contact as a condition are ultimately pure, this purity is said to be most profound.”
“Śāriputra! Because the mind-element (*manodhātu*) is ultimately pure, this purity is said to be most profound;

because the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element (*manovijñānadhātu*), as well as mind-contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*) and the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition are ultimately pure, this purity is said to be most profound.”
“Śāriputra! Because the earth element is ultimately pure, this purity is said to be most profound;
because the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are ultimately pure, this purity is said to be most profound.”
“Śāriputra! Because ignorance is ultimately pure, this purity is said to be most profound;

Chapter 36: On Attachment and Non-attachment, Part One. At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:

“Bhagavān! If sons and daughters of good family who abide in the bodhisattva vehicle lack skillful means, they will conceive the notion that this *prajñāpāramitā* is the *prajñāpāramitā*. Because they employ the method of apprehending [objects] as real, they abandon and distance themselves from the profound *prajñāpāramitā*.”
The Buddha said:
“Excellent, Subhūti! Excellent!”
Excellent! So it is! So it is!
It is as you have said.
Those sons and daughters of good family who become attached to names and signs regarding this Prajñāpāramitā will, for that reason, abandon and distance themselves from it.
The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha again, saying:
“World-Honored One,
how do those sons of good family and daughters of good family become attached to names and signs regarding this prajñāpāramitā?”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Those sons and daughters of good family grasp at names and grasp at signs regarding this *prajñāpāramitā*. Having grasped at names and signs, they become attached to the *prajñāpāramitā* and are unable to realize the *prajñāpāramitā* of true reality (*bhūtārtha*). For this reason, such individuals abandon and distance themselves from the profound *prajñāpāramitā*.”
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If sons of good family or daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle lack skillful means, they will grasp at names and grasp at signs regarding this *prajñāpāramitā*. Having grasped at these names and signs, they rely upon this *prajñāpāramitā* to give rise to arrogance; thus, they are unable to realize the *prajñāpāramitā* of true reality (*bhūtārtha*). Consequently, such individuals abandon and distance themselves from the profound *prajñāpāramitā*."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If those sons of good family or daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle possess skillful means, and by employing the method of non-apprehension, do not grasp at names or signs regarding this Prajñāpāramitā, do not give rise to attachment, and do not produce arrogance, they will be able to realize the Prajñā of the true nature (*dharmatā*). You should know that such individuals are said not to abandon or distance themselves from the Prajñāpāramitā."
The Venerable Subhūti then addressed the Buddha, saying:
“How marvelous!
World-Honored One, you have skillfully revealed and analyzed for the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas the characteristics of attachment and non-attachment regarding this prajñāpāramitā.”
At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra asked the Venerable Subhūti:
"When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, what constitutes the characteristic of attachment and the characteristic of non-attachment?"
Subhūti replied, “Śāriputra,

when sons of good family or daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle practice the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, they regard form as empty and give rise to the perception of emptiness regarding it; they regard feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness as empty and give rise to the perception of emptiness regarding them.”

If one regards the eye-base as empty and gives rise to the perception and notion of emptiness; if one regards the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases as empty and gives rise to the perception and notion of emptiness;

if one regards the form-base as empty and gives rise to the perception and notion of emptiness; if one regards the sound, odor, taste, tangible, and mental-object bases as empty and gives rise to the perception and notion of emptiness;

if one regards the eye-element as empty and gives rise to the perception and notion of emptiness; and if one regards the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as their condition as empty and gives rise to the perception and notion of emptiness—[this is so].
If one regards the ear-element as empty and gives rise to the perception of emptiness;
if one regards the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as conditions as empty and gives rise to the perception of emptiness;

or if one regards the nose-element as empty and gives rise to the perception of emptiness, regarding the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as conditions as empty and giving rise to the perception of emptiness;

If one regards the tongue element as empty and gives rise to the perception of emptiness; if one regards the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as conditions as empty, and gives rise to the perception of emptiness;

if one regards the body element as empty and gives rise to the perception of emptiness; if one regards the touch element, the body-consciousness element, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as conditions as empty, and gives rise to the perception of emptiness;

if one regards the mind element as empty and gives rise to the perception of emptiness; if one regards the mental-object element, the mind-consciousness element, mind-contact, and all feelings produced with mind-contact as conditions as empty, and gives rise to the perception of emptiness;

If one regards the earth element as empty and gives rise to the perception and attachment of emptiness; if one regards the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements as empty and gives rise to the perception and attachment of emptiness;

if one regards ignorance as empty and gives rise to the perception and attachment of emptiness; if one regards volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair as empty and gives rise to the perception and attachment of emptiness;

if one regards the perfection of generosity as empty and gives rise to the perception and attachment of emptiness; and if one regards the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom as empty and gives rise to the perception and attachment of emptiness—[this is so].

If one regards internal emptiness as empty and gives rise to a conceptual attachment to the notion of emptiness; or if one regards external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, emptiness of self-characteristic, emptiness of common characteristic, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence as being empty, and gives rise to a conceptual attachment to the notion of emptiness;

If one regards *tathatā* as empty and gives rise to the perception of emptiness regarding it; if one regards the *dharmadhātu*, the *dharmatā*, the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm as empty, and gives rise to the perception of emptiness regarding them;

if one regards the Noble Truth of Suffering as empty and gives rise to the perception of emptiness regarding it; if one regards the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path as empty, and gives rise to the perception of emptiness regarding them;

if one regards the four dhyānas as empty and gives rise to the perception of emptiness regarding them; and if one regards the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions as empty and gives rise to the perception of emptiness regarding them;

If one regards the eight liberations as empty and gives rise to the perception of emptiness regarding them; if one regards the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities as empty and gives rise to the perception of emptiness regarding them;

if one regards the four foundations of mindfulness as empty and gives rise to the perception of emptiness regarding them; if one regards the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path as empty and gives rise to the perception of emptiness regarding them;

if one regards the gate of liberation of emptiness as empty and gives rise to the perception of emptiness regarding it; and if one regards the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness as empty and gives rise to the perception of emptiness regarding them;
If one conceives of the ten stages of a bodhisattva as empty and gives rise to the perception of emptiness;
if one conceives of the five eyes as empty and gives rise to the perception of emptiness; if one conceives of the six supernormal powers as empty and gives rise to the perception of emptiness;

if one conceives of the ten powers of a Buddha as empty and gives rise to the perception of emptiness; and if one conceives of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha as empty and gives rise to the perception of emptiness—[this is so].

If one regards the quality of non-forgetfulness as empty and gives rise to a perception of emptiness regarding it; if one regards the state of constant equanimity as empty and gives rise to a perception of emptiness regarding it;

if one regards all-knowledge as empty and gives rise to a perception of emptiness regarding it; if one regards the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects as empty and gives rise to a perception of emptiness regarding them;

if one regards all doors of dhāraṇī as empty and gives rise to a perception of emptiness regarding them; if one regards all doors of samādhi as empty and gives rise to a perception of emptiness regarding them;

If one regards the fruit of stream-entry as empty and gives rise to a perception of emptiness regarding it; if one regards the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship as empty and gives rise to a perception of emptiness regarding them;
if one regards the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha as empty and gives rise to a perception of emptiness regarding it;
or if one regards all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas as empty and gives rise to a perception of emptiness regarding them—
If one regards the unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment of the Buddhas as empty and gives rise to the perception of emptiness;
or if one regards past phenomena as empty and gives rise to the perception of emptiness, and regards future and present phenomena as empty and gives rise to the perception of emptiness.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when sons and daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle practice the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, they conceive of form as 'form' and give rise to perceptions and attachments regarding form; they conceive of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness as 'feeling,' 'perception,' 'mental formations,' and 'consciousness,' and give rise to perceptions and attachments regarding feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.

If they conceive of the eye-base as 'eye-base,' they give rise to perceptions and attachments regarding the eye-base; they conceive of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases as 'ear,' 'nose,' 'tongue,' 'body,' and 'mind-base,' and give rise to perceptions and attachments regarding the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases."

If one regards the sphere of form as the sphere of form and gives rise to the perception and attachment of the sphere of form; if one regards the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena as the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena, and gives rise to the perception and attachment of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena;

if one regards the eye-element as the eye-element and gives rise to the perception and attachment of the eye-element; and if one regards the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as conditions as the form-element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as conditions, and gives rise to the perception and attachment of the form-element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as conditions.

If, regarding the ear element, one perceives it as the ear element and gives rise to attachment to the ear element; and regarding the sound element, the ear-consciousness element, ear-contact, and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as condition, one perceives them as the sound element up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as condition and gives rise to attachment to the sound element up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as condition;

if, regarding the nose element, one perceives it as the nose element and gives rise to attachment to the nose element; and regarding the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as condition, one perceives them as the odor element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as condition and gives rise to attachment to the odor element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as condition.

If, regarding the tongue-element, one says "tongue-element" and gives rise to a perception and attachment to the tongue-element; and regarding the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, one says "taste-element" up to "feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition," and gives rise to a perception and attachment to the taste-element up to the feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition;

if, regarding the body-element, one says "body-element" and gives rise to a perception and attachment to the body-element; and regarding the touch-element, the body-consciousness-element, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, one says "touch-element" up to "feelings produced with body-contact as a condition," and gives rise to a perception and attachment to the touch-element up to the feelings produced with body-contact as a condition;

If one regards the mind-element as the mind-element and gives rise to the conceptual attachment of "mind-element," or regards the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, and mental contact—as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as their condition—as the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as their condition, and gives rise to the conceptual attachment of "dharma-element" up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as their condition;

or if one regards the earth-element as the earth-element and gives rise to the conceptual attachment of "earth-element," or regards the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness-elements as the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness-elements, and gives rise to the conceptual attachment of "water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness-elements."

If, regarding ignorance, one perceives it as ignorance and gives rise to the conceptual attachment of ignorance; regarding formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair, one perceives them as formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair, and gives rise to the conceptual attachment of formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair;

if, regarding the perfection of generosity, one perceives it as the perfection of generosity and gives rise to the conceptual attachment of the perfection of generosity; regarding the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, one perceives them as ethical discipline up to wisdom, and gives rise to the conceptual attachment of ethical discipline up to wisdom.

If, regarding inner emptiness, one says "it is inner emptiness" and gives rise to the conceptual attachment of thinking "inner emptiness"; or regarding outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—one says "it is outer emptiness" up to "it is the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence," and gives rise to the conceptual attachment of thinking "outer emptiness" up to "the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence."

If, regarding suchness, one says "suchness" and gives rise to the conceptual attachment of suchness; or regarding the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the non-erroneous nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the nature free from birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm—one says "the realm of phenomena" up to "the inconceivable realm" and gives rise to the conceptual attachment of the realm of phenomena up to the inconceivable realm;

or if, regarding the noble truth of suffering, one says "the noble truth of suffering" and gives rise to the conceptual attachment of the noble truth of suffering; or regarding the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, one says "the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path" and gives rise to the conceptual attachment of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path.

If one regards the four dhyānas as the four dhyānas and gives rise to the perception of attachment to the four dhyānas; if one regards the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments as the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments and gives rise to the perception of attachment to the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments;

if one regards the eight liberations as the eight liberations and gives rise to the perception of attachment to the eight liberations; and if one regards the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative concentrations, and the ten totalities as the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative concentrations, and the ten totalities and gives rise to the perception of attachment to the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative concentrations, and the ten totalities;

If, regarding the four foundations of mindfulness, one perceives them as the four foundations of mindfulness and gives rise to the conceptualization of the four foundations of mindfulness; if, regarding the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path, one perceives them as the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path and gives rise to the conceptualization of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path;

if, regarding the gate of liberation of emptiness, one perceives it as the gate of liberation of emptiness and gives rise to the conceptualization of the gate of liberation of emptiness; if, regarding the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, one perceives them as the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness and gives rise to the conceptualization of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness;
if, regarding the ten stages of a bodhisattva, one perceives them as the ten stages of a bodhisattva and gives rise to the conceptualization of the ten stages of a bodhisattva;

If one regards the five eyes as the five eyes and gives rise to the conceptual attachment of the five eyes; if one regards the six supernormal powers as the six supernormal powers and gives rise to the conceptual attachment of the six supernormal powers;

if one regards the ten powers of a Buddha as the ten powers of a Buddha and gives rise to the conceptual attachment of the ten powers of a Buddha; if one regards the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha as the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha and gives rise to the conceptual attachment of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;

if one regards the quality of non-forgetfulness as the quality of non-forgetfulness and gives rise to the conceptual attachment of the quality of non-forgetfulness; if one regards the state of constant abiding in equanimity as the state of constant abiding in equanimity and gives rise to the conceptual attachment of the state of constant abiding in equanimity.

If one regards all-knowledge as "all-knowledge" and gives rise to the conceptual attachment of regarding it as all-knowledge; if one regards the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects as "knowledge of the paths" and "knowledge of all aspects" respectively, and gives rise to the conceptual attachment of regarding them as such;

if one regards all dharani-doors as "all dharani-doors" and gives rise to the conceptual attachment of regarding them as such; and if one regards all samadhi-doors as "all samadhi-doors" and gives rise to the conceptual attachment of regarding them as such;

If one regards the fruit of stream-entry as the fruit of stream-entry and gives rise to the perception of the fruit of stream-entry; if one regards the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship as the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship, and gives rise to the perceptions of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship;
if one regards pratyekabuddha-enlightenment as pratyekabuddha-enlightenment and gives rise to the perception of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment;

or if one regards all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas as all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and gives rise to the perception of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas—[this is so].

If one regards the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas as "the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas," one gives rise to the conceptualization and attachment of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas;

if one regards past phenomena as "past phenomena," one gives rise to the conceptualization and attachment of past phenomena; and regarding future and present phenomena as "future and present phenomena," one gives rise to the conceptualization and attachment of future and present phenomena.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle Two Hundred and Eighty-Seven. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter Thirty-Six, Part Two, "The Characteristics of Clinging and Non-clinging. "Furthermore, Śāriputra!"

If sons of good family or daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle, by means of the method of apprehending something as real, give rise to conceptual attachments regarding the practice of the perfection of generosity from the first production of the thought of enlightenment, and likewise give rise to conceptual attachments regarding the practice of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom;

If one gives rise to conceptualizations and attachments regarding internal emptiness; or if one gives rise to conceptualizations and attachments regarding external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature;

or if one gives rise to conceptualizations and attachments regarding suchness; or if one gives rise to conceptualizations and attachments regarding the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, non-alteration, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm.

If one gives rise to conceptualizations of practice regarding the noble truth of suffering, or gives rise to conceptualizations of practice regarding the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path;
if one gives rise to conceptualizations of practice regarding the four dhyānas, or gives rise to conceptualizations of practice regarding the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments;

if one gives rise to conceptualizations of practice regarding the eight liberations, or gives rise to conceptualizations of practice regarding the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative concentrations, and the ten totalities;

If one gives rise to conceptualizations of activity regarding the four foundations of mindfulness; if one gives rise to conceptualizations of activity regarding the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path;
if one gives rise to conceptualizations of activity regarding the gate of liberation of emptiness, or the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness;
or if one gives rise to conceptualizations of activity regarding the ten stages of a bodhisattva.
If one gives rise to conceptualizations and attachments regarding the five eyes; if one gives rise to conceptualizations and attachments regarding the six supernormal powers;

if one gives rise to conceptualizations and attachments regarding the ten powers of a Buddha; if one gives rise to conceptualizations and attachments regarding the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;

if one gives rise to conceptualizations and attachments regarding the quality of non-forgetfulness; or if one gives rise to conceptualizations and attachments regarding the state of constant abiding in equanimity.

If one gives rise to conceptualizations and attachments regarding all-knowledge; if one gives rise to conceptualizations and attachments regarding the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects;
if one gives rise to conceptualizations and attachments regarding all dharani-doors;
or if one gives rise to conceptualizations and attachments regarding all samadhi-doors;
If one gives rise to conceptualizations regarding the fruit of stream-entry; if one gives rise to conceptualizations regarding the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, or arhatship;
if one gives rise to conceptualizations regarding the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha;
or if one gives rise to conceptualizations regarding the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
If one gives rise to conceptualizations and attachments regarding the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas— Śāriputra,

when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they lack skillful means and employ the approach of apprehending something as real, giving rise to such various conceptualizations and attachments, this is called "clinging to signs."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra! Regarding what you previously asked:
'How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), remain unattached to signs? "

"Śāriputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they possess skillful means such that they do not give rise to the notion of emptiness or the notion of non-emptiness regarding form; nor do they give rise to the notion of emptiness or the notion of non-emptiness regarding feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.

They do not give rise to the notion of emptiness or the notion of non-emptiness regarding the sense base of the eye; nor do they give rise to the notion of emptiness or the notion of non-emptiness regarding the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind."

One does not give rise to the notion of emptiness or non-emptiness regarding the sphere of form; one likewise does not give rise to the notion of emptiness or non-emptiness regarding the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena. One does not give rise to the notion of emptiness or non-emptiness regarding the eye-element;

nor does one give rise to the notion of emptiness or non-emptiness regarding the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, or the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition. One does not give rise to the notion of emptiness or non-emptiness regarding the ear-element;

nor does one give rise to the notion of emptiness or non-emptiness regarding the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, or the various feelings produced with ear-contact as condition. One does not give rise to the notion of emptiness or non-emptiness regarding the nose-element; nor does one give rise to the notion of emptiness or non-emptiness regarding the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, nose-contact, or the various feelings produced with nose-contact as condition.

One does not give rise to the notion of emptiness or non-emptiness regarding the tongue element; nor does one give rise to the notion of emptiness or non-emptiness regarding the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, or the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as condition.

One does not give rise to the notion of emptiness or non-emptiness regarding the body element; nor does one give rise to the notion of emptiness or non-emptiness regarding the tangible-object element, the body-consciousness element, body-contact, or the various feelings produced with body-contact as condition.

One does not give rise to the notion of emptiness or non-emptiness regarding the mind element; nor does one give rise to the notion of emptiness or non-emptiness regarding the mental-object element, the mind-consciousness element, mind-contact, or the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition.

One does not give rise to the notion of emptiness or non-emptiness regarding the earth element; nor does one give rise to the notion of emptiness or non-emptiness regarding the elements of water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness.

One does not give rise to the notion of emptiness or non-emptiness regarding ignorance; nor does one give rise to the notion of emptiness or non-emptiness regarding volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, or old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair.

One does not give rise to the notion of emptiness or non-emptiness regarding the perfection of generosity; nor does one give rise to the notion of emptiness or non-emptiness regarding the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom.

Within internal emptiness, one does not give rise to the notion of emptiness or the notion of non-emptiness; nor does one give rise to the notion of emptiness or the notion of non-emptiness regarding external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential emptiness, emptiness of self-characteristics, emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

One does not give rise to the notion of emptiness or non-emptiness regarding *tathatā* (suchness); nor does one give rise to the notion of emptiness or non-emptiness regarding the *dharmadhātu*, the *dharmatā*, the non-falsity, the unchanging nature, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, or the inconceivable realm.

One does not give rise to the notion of emptiness or non-emptiness regarding the Noble Truth of Suffering; nor does one give rise to the notion of emptiness or non-emptiness regarding the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path.

One does not give rise to the notion of emptiness or non-emptiness regarding the four dhyānas; nor does one give rise to the notion of emptiness or non-emptiness regarding the four immeasurables or the four formless absorptions.

Regarding the eight liberations, they do not give rise to the notion of emptiness nor the notion of non-emptiness; regarding the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten universal bases, they likewise do not give rise to the notion of emptiness nor the notion of non-emptiness.

Regarding the four foundations of mindfulness, they do not give rise to the notion of emptiness nor the notion of non-emptiness; regarding the four right endeavors, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path, they likewise do not give rise to the notion of emptiness nor the notion of non-emptiness.

Regarding the gate of liberation of emptiness, they do not give rise to the notion of emptiness nor the notion of non-emptiness; regarding the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, they likewise do not give rise to the notion of emptiness nor the notion of non-emptiness.
Regarding the ten stages of a bodhisattva, they do not give rise to the notion of emptiness or non-emptiness;

regarding the five eyes, they do not give rise to the notion of emptiness or non-emptiness; regarding the six supernormal powers, they likewise do not give rise to the notion of emptiness or non-emptiness;

regarding the ten powers of a Buddha, they do not give rise to the notion of emptiness or non-emptiness; and regarding the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, they likewise do not give rise to the notion of emptiness or non-emptiness.

Regarding the quality of non-forgetfulness, one does not give rise to the notion of emptiness or the notion of non-emptiness; regarding the state of constant equanimity, one likewise does not give rise to the notion of emptiness or the notion of non-emptiness.

Regarding all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), one does not give rise to the notion of emptiness or the notion of non-emptiness; regarding the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), one likewise does not give rise to the notion of emptiness or the notion of non-emptiness.

Regarding all doors of dhāraṇī, one does not give rise to the notion of emptiness or the notion of non-emptiness; regarding all doors of samādhi, one likewise does not give rise to the notion of emptiness or the notion of non-emptiness.

One does not give rise to the notion of emptiness or non-emptiness regarding the fruit of stream-entry; nor does one give rise to the notion of emptiness or non-emptiness regarding the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, or arhatship;
nor does one give rise to the notion of emptiness or non-emptiness regarding the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha;
nor does one give rise to the notion of emptiness or non-emptiness regarding any of the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
One does not give rise to notions of emptiness or non-emptiness regarding the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas;
one does not give rise to notions of emptiness or non-emptiness regarding past phenomena, nor does one give rise to notions of emptiness or non-emptiness regarding future or present phenomena.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,
when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, employing the method of non-apprehension, they do not form such thoughts as:
'I am able to give, that recipient is receiving, this is the object given, and this is the nature of the act of giving.'"
He does not form this thought:
"I am able to guard the precepts," nor "these are the precepts being guarded.
He does not form this thought:
"I am able to cultivate patience; this is the patience being cultivated.
They do not form such thoughts as:
"I am able to exert diligence; this is the diligence being exerted."
He does not form the thought:
"I am able to enter meditative absorption," nor does he form the thought: "This is the meditative absorption I have entered.
He does not form such thoughts.
He does not form such thoughts as: "I am able to cultivate wisdom; this is the wisdom being cultivated," nor:
"I am able to plant merit; this is the merit being planted and the fruit thereby obtained."
He does not form this thought:
"I am able to enter the bodhisattva’s state of rightness and departure from birth.
He does not form this thought:
"I can bring sentient beings to maturity," nor does he form this thought:
"I can adorn and purify a buddha-field."
They do not form this thought:
"I am able to realize the knowledge of all modes.
They do not form this thought:
"I am able to dwell in emptiness and realize the true nature of phenomena," nor does he form this thought:
"I am able to practice the various bodhisattva deeds."
He does not form this thought:
"I am able to fully realize all the merits of the Buddhas. "Śāriputra!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva possesses skillful means and practices the perfection of wisdom by way of non-apprehension, they will be free from all such conceptualizations, delusions, and attachments, because they have thoroughly mastered internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

Śāriputra! This is called the skillful means of a bodhisattva mahāsattva when practicing the perfection of wisdom; it takes non-apprehension as its skillful means and is characterized by non-attachment.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, asked the venerable Subhūti: "Venerable One,
when sons and daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle practice the perfection of wisdom, how do they become attached to signs?"
Subhūti replied, "Kauśika,

when sons and daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle practice the perfection of wisdom, they lack skillful means; taking 'attainment' as their means, they give rise to mental conceptions and become attached."

They give rise to conceptualizations regarding the perfection of generosity; they give rise to conceptualizations regarding the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; they give rise to conceptualizations regarding internal emptiness;

and they give rise to conceptualizations regarding external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

They give rise to conceptualizations regarding *tathatā* (suchness); they give rise to conceptualizations regarding the *dharmadhātu* (dharma-realm), *dharmatā* (dharma-nature), non-illusory nature, unchanging nature, equality, the state of being free from birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmasthiti*), the reality-limit (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm;
they give rise to conceptualizations regarding the noble truth of suffering; they give rise to conceptualizations regarding the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path;
they give rise to conceptualizations regarding the four dhyānas; and they give rise to conceptualizations regarding the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments.
They give rise to perceptions of the eight liberations; they give rise to perceptions of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities;

they give rise to perceptions of the four foundations of mindfulness; they give rise to perceptions of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path;
they give rise to perceptions of the liberation door of emptiness; and they give rise to perceptions of the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness.
They give rise to the conceptualization of the ten stages of a bodhisattva;
they give rise to the conceptualization of the five eyes; they give rise to the conceptualization of the six supernormal powers;

they give rise to the conceptualization of the ten powers of a buddha; and they give rise to the conceptualization of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha.
They give rise to the conceptualization of the quality of non-forgetfulness; they give rise to the conceptualization of the nature of constant equanimity;

they give rise to the conceptualization of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*); they give rise to the conceptualization of the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*);
they give rise to the conceptualization of all doors of dhāraṇī; and they give rise to the conceptualization of all doors of samādhi.
They give rise to the perception of being established in the fruit of stream-entry; they give rise to the perception of being established in the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship;
they give rise to the perception of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha;
and they give rise to the perception of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
They give rise to the conceptualization of the unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas;
they give rise to the conceptualization of all Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas;
and they give rise to the conceptualization of all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas.
They give rise to the conceptualization of planting various roots of goodness in the presence of the Buddha;
they give rise to the conceptualization of dedicating these planted roots of goodness, brought together as such, toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

Kauśika! This is called the attachment to signs that occurs when sons of good family or daughters of good family who have set out in the bodhisattva vehicle—lacking skillful means and employing the "attainment of something" as their means—practice the perfection of wisdom.

“Kauśika! Those sons and daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle, because they are attached to conceptual signs, are unable to practice the non-attached Prajñāpāramitā and dedicate it toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”
Why is this? Kauśika!
It is because the intrinsic nature of form cannot be dedicated; nor can the intrinsic nature of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness be dedicated.
The intrinsic nature of the eye-base cannot be dedicated, because the intrinsic nature of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases cannot be dedicated;
the intrinsic nature of the form-base cannot be dedicated, because the intrinsic nature of the sound, odor, taste, tangible, and mental-object bases cannot be dedicated;

the intrinsic nature of the eye-element cannot be dedicated, because the intrinsic nature of the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, and the eye-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, cannot be dedicated.

The intrinsic nature of the ear element cannot be dedicated; nor can the intrinsic nature of the sound element, the ear-consciousness element, ear-contact, or the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition be dedicated.

The intrinsic nature of the nose element cannot be dedicated; nor can the intrinsic nature of the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, or the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition be dedicated.

The intrinsic nature of the tongue element cannot be dedicated; nor can the intrinsic nature of the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, or the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition be dedicated.

The intrinsic nature of the body element cannot be dedicated; nor can the intrinsic nature of the tangible-object element, the body-consciousness element, body-contact, or the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition be dedicated.

The intrinsic nature of the mind element cannot be dedicated; nor can the intrinsic nature of the mental-object element, the mind-consciousness element, mind-contact, or the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition be dedicated.
The intrinsic nature of the earth element cannot be dedicated; nor can the intrinsic nature of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements be dedicated.

It is because the intrinsic nature of ignorance cannot be redirected, nor can the intrinsic nature of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, or old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair be redirected.
