If they do not practice whether the dharma of non-forgetfulness is permanent or impermanent, that is practicing the perfection of wisdom; if they do not practice whether the nature of constant equanimity is permanent or impermanent, that is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Not practicing the quality of non-forgetfulness as either pleasure or pain is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the state of constant equanimity as either pleasure or pain is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the quality of non-forgetfulness as either self or non-self is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the state of constant equanimity as either self or non-self is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing the quality of non-forgetfulness as either pure or impure is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the state of constant equanimity as either pure or impure is practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Why is this? Subhūti!

Since even the nature of the quality of non-forgetfulness does not exist, how much less could there be a quality of non-forgetfulness that is either permanent or impermanent, pleasant or painful, self or non-self, pure or impure!

Since the very nature of the state of constant abiding in equanimity does not exist, how much less could there be a state of constant abiding in equanimity that is either permanent or impermanent, pleasant or painful, self or non-self, pure or impure!

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle Two Hundred and Eighty-nine. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter Thirty-six, Part Four, "The Characteristics of Attachment and Non-attachment. "Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), that is practicing the perfection of wisdom; if they do not practice the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*) or the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), that is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If they do not practice all-knowledge as either permanent or impermanent, that is practicing the perfection of wisdom; if they do not practice the knowledge of the paths or the knowledge of all aspects as either permanent or impermanent, that is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If they do not practice all-knowledge as either pleasant or suffering, that is practicing the perfection of wisdom; if they do not practice the knowledge of the paths or the knowledge of all aspects as either pleasant or suffering, that is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with respect to omniscience (*sarvajñatā*) as being either self or non-self is practicing the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*); not practicing with respect to the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) or the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) as being either self or non-self is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with respect to omniscience as being either pure or impure is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing with respect to the knowledge of the aspects of the path or the knowledge of all aspects as being either pure or impure is practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Why is this? Subhūti,
since even the nature of omniscience does not exist, how much less could there be an omniscience that is either permanent or impermanent, pleasant or painful, self or non-self, pure or impure!

Since even the nature of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects does not exist, how much less could the knowledge of the aspects of the path or the knowledge of all aspects be permanent or impermanent, pleasant or suffering, self or non-self, pure or impure!

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice all the gateways of dhāraṇī, that is practicing the perfection of wisdom; if they do not practice all the gateways of samādhi, that is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If they do not practice whether all the gateways of dhāraṇī are permanent or impermanent, that is practicing the perfection of wisdom; if they do not practice whether all the gateways of samādhi are permanent or impermanent, that is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Not practicing that all dhāraṇī-doors are either pleasant or painful is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing that all samādhi-doors are either pleasant or painful is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing that all dhāraṇī-doors are either self or non-self is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing that all samādhi-doors are either self or non-self is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing that all dhāraṇī-doors are either pure or impure is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing that all samādhi-doors are either pure or impure is practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Why is this? Subhūti!

Since the very nature of all dhāraṇī-doors does not exist, how much less could there be any dhāraṇī-doors that are either permanent or impermanent, pleasant or painful, self or non-self, pure or impure!

Since even the intrinsic nature of all samādhi-gates does not exist, how could there be any samādhi-gates that are either permanent or impermanent, pleasant or painful, self or non-self, pure or impure?

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice for the fruit of a stream-enterer, that is practicing the perfection of wisdom; if they do not practice for the fruits of a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat, that is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If they do not practice for the fruit of a stream-enterer as being permanent or impermanent, that is practicing the perfection of wisdom; if they do not practice for the fruits of a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat as being permanent or impermanent, that is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Not practicing with regard to the fruit of stream-entry as being either pleasant or painful is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing with regard to the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, or arhatship as being either pleasant or painful is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the fruit of stream-entry as being either self or non-self is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing with regard to the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, or arhatship as being either self or non-self is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

Not practicing with regard to the fruit of stream-entry as being either pure or impure is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing with regard to the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, or arhatship as being either pure or impure is practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Why is this? Subhūti!

Since even the nature of the fruit of stream-entry does not exist, how could there be a fruit of stream-entry that is either permanent or impermanent, pleasant or painful, self or non-self, pure or impure?

Since even the natures of the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the fruit of arhatship do not exist, how much less could there be a fruit of once-returning, non-returning, or arhatship that is either permanent or impermanent, pleasant or painful, self or non-self, pure or impure!

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice the awakening of a pratyekabuddha, they are practicing the perfection of wisdom; if they do not practice the awakening of a pratyekabuddha as permanent or impermanent, they are practicing the perfection of wisdom; if they do not practice the awakening of a pratyekabuddha as pleasant or painful, they are practicing the perfection of wisdom; if they do not practice the awakening of a pratyekabuddha as self or non-self, they are practicing the perfection of wisdom; if they do not practice the awakening of a pratyekabuddha as pure or impure, they are practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!

Since even the nature of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment does not exist, how much less could there be a pratyekabuddha-enlightenment that is either permanent or impermanent, pleasant or painful, self or non-self, pure or impure!

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice any of the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom; if they do not practice any of the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva as either permanent or impermanent, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom; if they do not practice any of the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva as either pleasant or painful, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom; if they do not practice any of the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva as either self or non-self, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom; if they do not practice any of the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva as either pure or impure, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!

Since the very nature of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas’ practices does not exist, how much less could there be any bodhisattva-mahāsattvas’ practice that is either permanent or impermanent, pleasant or painful, self or non-self, pure or impure!

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice the unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment of the Buddhas, that is practicing the perfection of wisdom; if they do not practice the unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment of the Buddhas as either permanent or impermanent, that is practicing the perfection of wisdom; if they do not practice the unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment of the Buddhas as either pleasant or painful, that is practicing the perfection of wisdom; if they do not practice the unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment of the Buddhas as either self or non-self, that is practicing the perfection of wisdom; if they do not practice the unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment of the Buddhas as either pure or impure, that is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!

Since even the nature of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas does not exist, how much less could there be an unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas that is either permanent or impermanent, either blissful or suffering, either self or non-self, or either pure or impure!
"Furthermore, Subhūti,
when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice for the sake of the fulfillment or non-fulfillment of form, that is practicing the perfection of wisdom."
Why is this? Subhūti!
If form, whether complete or incomplete, is not called "form," then one does not practice in such a manner when practicing the perfection of wisdom.
If one does not practice for the sake of the fulfillment or non-fulfillment of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Why is that? Subhūti!

If feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness—whether complete or incomplete—are both not called feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness, and one does not practice in such a manner, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice the fulfillment or non-fulfillment of the sense base of the eye, that is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
Whether the eye-base is complete or incomplete, neither is called the "eye-base"; furthermore, to practice in such a manner is to practice the perfection of wisdom.
If one does not practice the perfection or non-perfection of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom. Why is that?

"Subhūti! Whether the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are complete or incomplete, they are in neither case called 'the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind. To practice in such a manner is to practice the perfection of wisdom."

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice for the sake of the fulfillment or non-fulfillment of the sense-base of form, that is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
Whether the sphere of form is complete or incomplete, it is in neither case called the "sphere of form"; furthermore, to practice in such a manner is to practice the perfection of wisdom.

If one does not practice with regard to the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena as being either complete or incomplete, this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom. Why is that?

Subhūti! Whether the bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are complete or incomplete, they are in neither case called the bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena; furthermore, to practice in such a manner is to practice the perfection of wisdom.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice for the sake of the fulfillment or non-fulfillment of the eye-element, that is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
Whether the eye-element is complete or incomplete, it is in neither case called the "eye-element"; to practice in such a manner is to practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

If one does not practice for the sake of the fulfillment or non-fulfillment of the form realm, the eye-consciousness realm, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.
Why is this? Subhūti!

Whether the form realm, up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, are fulfilled or unfulfilled, they are in neither case called the "form realm" nor the "various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition. Furthermore, to practice in such a manner is to practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice the fulfillment or non-fulfillment of the ear element, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
Whether the ear-element is complete or incomplete, neither is called the "ear-element"; furthermore, to practice in such a manner is to practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

If one does not practice for the sake of the perfection or non-perfection of the sphere of sound, the sphere of auditory consciousness, ear-contact, and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.
Why is this? Subhūti!

Whether the sound-element, up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, are fulfilled or unfulfilled, they are neither called the "sound-element" nor the "various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition. Furthermore, to practice in such a manner is to practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice for the sake of the fulfillment or non-fulfillment of the nose-element, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
Whether the nose-element is complete or incomplete, it is in neither case called the "nose-element"; furthermore, to practice in such a manner is to practice the perfection of wisdom.

If one does not practice for the sake of the fulfillment or non-fulfillment of the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Why is this so? Subhūti!

Whether the various feelings produced with the fragrance-element as condition, up to those produced with nose-contact as condition, are fulfilled or unfulfilled, they are in neither case called the "fragrance-element" nor "feelings produced with nose-contact as condition. Furthermore, to practice in such a manner is to practice the perfection of wisdom.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice for the sake of the fulfillment or non-fulfillment of the tongue element, that is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
Whether the tongue-element is complete or incomplete, it is not called the "tongue-element"; furthermore, to practice in such a manner is to practice the perfection of wisdom.

If one does not practice for the sake of the fulfillment or non-fulfillment of the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings arising with tongue-contact as a condition, this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.
Why is this? Subhūti!

Whether the various feelings produced with the taste-element up to tongue-contact as condition are complete or incomplete, they are both not called "the various feelings produced with the taste-element up to tongue-contact as condition. Furthermore, to practice in such a manner is to practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice for the fulfillment or non-fulfillment of the body element, that is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
Whether the body-element is complete or incomplete, neither is called the "body-element"; furthermore, to practice in such a manner is to practice the perfection of wisdom.

If one does not practice for the sake of the fulfillment or non-fulfillment of the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and the various feelings arising with body-contact as a condition, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Why is this? Subhūti!

Whether the various feelings produced with the contact element as a condition, up to those produced with body-contact as a condition, are fulfilled or unfulfilled, they are in neither case called "the various feelings produced with the contact element as a condition" nor "the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition. To practice in such a manner is to practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice the fulfillment or non-fulfillment of the mind-element, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
Whether the mind-element is complete or incomplete, it is neither called the "mind-element"; nor does one practice the perfection of wisdom in such a manner.

If one does not practice the perfection or non-perfection of the dharma-element, the consciousness-element, mental contact, and the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.
Why is this? Subhūti!

Whether the dharmadhātu, up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are fulfilled or unfulfilled, they are in neither case called the "dharmadhātu" nor "the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition. To practice in such a manner is to practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

"Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice for the sake of the fulfillment or non-fulfillment of the earth element, that is practicing the perfection of wisdom."
Why is this? Subhūti!
Whether the earth element is complete or incomplete, it is neither called the "earth element"; likewise, one who practices in such a manner is practicing the perfection of wisdom.
If one does not practice for the sake of the fulfillment or non-fulfillment of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom. Why is that?

"Subhūti! If the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness—whether complete or incomplete—are not called the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, and one does not practice in such a manner, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom."
“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice the fulfillment or non-fulfillment of ignorance, that is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
If both the fulfillment and non-fulfillment of ignorance are not called ignorance, then it is likewise not the case that such practice is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

If one does not practice the fulfillment or non-fulfillment of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair, this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.
Why is this? Subhūti!

If one practices until the fulfillment or non-fulfillment of old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair, these are neither called "practice" nor "old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair. Furthermore, practicing in such a manner is not practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

"Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice the fulfillment or non-fulfillment of the perfection of generosity, that is practicing the perfection of wisdom."
Why is this? Subhūti!
Whether the perfection of giving is fulfilled or unfulfilled, neither is designated as the perfection of giving; nor does one practice the perfection of wisdom in such a manner.
If one does not practice the perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, nor their non-perfection, this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.
Why is this? Subhūti!

Whether the perfection of ethical discipline up to the perfection of wisdom is fulfilled or unfulfilled, neither is designated as "the perfection of ethical discipline" up to "the perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, to practice in such a manner is not to practice the perfection of wisdom.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice the fulfillment or non-fulfillment of internal emptiness, that is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
Whether internal emptiness is fulfilled or unfulfilled, it is in neither case called "internal emptiness," nor does one practice the perfection of wisdom in such a manner.

If one does not practice the fulfillment or non-fulfillment of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.
Why is this? Subhūti!

Whether the emptiness of the external up to the emptiness of the nature of non-nature is fulfilled or unfulfilled, neither is called the "emptiness of the external" up to the "emptiness of the nature of non-nature. Furthermore, to practice in such a manner is not to practice the perfection of wisdom.
“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice the fulfillment or non-fulfillment of suchness, that is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
If both the perfection and the non-perfection of suchness were not called "suchness," nor would one practice in such a manner when practicing the perfection of wisdom.

If one does not practice the fulfillment or non-fulfillment of the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm, this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.
Why is this? Subhūti!

Whether the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm is fulfilled or unfulfilled, it is in neither case called the "dharma-realm" up to the "inconceivable realm. Furthermore, to practice in such a manner is to practice the perfection of wisdom.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice for the sake of the fulfillment or non-fulfillment of the noble truth of suffering, that is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this so? Subhūti!

If the noble truth of suffering were either complete or incomplete, it would not be called the noble truth of suffering; nor would one who acts in such a manner be practicing the perfection of wisdom.
If one does not practice for the sake of the fulfillment or non-fulfillment of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Why is that? Subhūti!

If the noble truths of suffering, origination, cessation, and the path—whether they are fulfilled or unfulfilled—are not both called the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path, nor does one practice in such a manner, then this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice for the sake of the fulfillment or non-fulfillment of the four dhyānas, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
Whether the four dhyānas are fulfilled or unfulfilled, neither is called "the four dhyānas"; furthermore, to practice in such a manner is not to practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
If one does not practice the fulfillment or non-fulfillment of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom. Why is that?

"Subhūti! If the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are neither fulfilled nor unfulfilled, they are not called 'the four immeasurables' or 'the four formless absorptions'; furthermore, to practice in such a manner is to practice the perfection of wisdom."

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice for the sake of the fulfillment or non-fulfillment of the eight liberations, that is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
If the eight liberations are both fulfilled and unfulfilled, they are neither called the "eight liberations," nor does one practice the perfection of wisdom in such a manner.

If one does not practice for the sake of the perfection or non-perfection of the eight spheres of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten universal bases, this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.
Why is this? Subhūti!

Whether the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities are perfected or unperfected, they are in neither case called the "eight bases of mastery," "nine successive attainments," or "ten totalities. Furthermore, to practice in such a manner is not to practice the perfection of wisdom.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice for the sake of the fulfillment or non-fulfillment of the four foundations of mindfulness, that is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!

Whether the four foundations of mindfulness are fulfilled or unfulfilled, they are both not called "the four foundations of mindfulness"; furthermore, to practice in such a manner is not to practice the perfection of wisdom.

If one does not practice the perfection of the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eight branches of the noble path—whether they are fulfilled or unfulfilled—that is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.
Why is this? Subhūti!

Whether the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are fulfilled or unfulfilled, they are neither called the four right efforts nor the eightfold noble path; furthermore, to practice in such a manner is not to practice the perfection of wisdom.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice for the sake of the fulfillment or non-fulfillment of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
Whether the gate of liberation of emptiness is fulfilled or unfulfilled, neither is called the gate of liberation of emptiness; nor does one practice the perfection of wisdom in such a manner.
If one does not practice the perfection or non-perfection of the gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom. Why is that?

"Subhūti! Whether the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are fulfilled or unfulfilled, neither is called the 'gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness,' nor does one practice the perfection of wisdom by practicing in such a manner."

"Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice for the fulfillment or non-fulfillment of the ten bodhisattva stages, that is practicing the perfection of wisdom."
Why is this? Subhūti!

Whether the ten stages of a bodhisattva are fulfilled or unfulfilled, they are in neither case called "the ten stages of a bodhisattva," nor does one practice the perfection of wisdom in such a manner.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice for the sake of the fulfillment or non-fulfillment of the five eyes, that is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
Whether the five eyes are perfected or unperfected, neither is designated as "the five eyes"; furthermore, to practice in such a manner is to practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
If one does not practice for the sake of the perfection or non-perfection of the six supernormal powers, that is practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Why is this? Subhūti!
If the six supernormal powers are both perfected and unperfected, they are neither called the "six supernormal powers," nor does one practice the perfection of wisdom in such a manner.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice for the sake of the fulfillment or non-fulfillment of the ten powers of a buddha, that is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!

Whether the ten powers of a Buddha are perfected or unperfected, they are both not called the "ten powers of a Buddha"; furthermore, to practice in such a manner is to practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

If one does not practice for the sake of the perfection or non-perfection of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.
Why is this? Subhūti!

Whether the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha are fulfilled or unfulfilled, they are neither called "the four fearlessnesses" nor "the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha. Furthermore, to practice in such a manner is to practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice for the sake of the fulfillment or non-fulfillment of the quality of non-forgetfulness, that is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!

If neither the perfection nor the non-perfection of the quality of non-forgetfulness is designated as the "quality of non-forgetfulness," then one does not practice in such a manner when practicing the perfection of wisdom.
If one does not practice the perfection or non-perfection of the state of constant abiding in equanimity, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Why is that? Subhūti!

If both the perfection and the non-perfection of the state of constant equanimity are not called the "state of constant equanimity," then practicing in such a manner is not practicing the *prajñāpāramitā*.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice for the sake of the fulfillment or non-fulfillment of all-knowledge, that is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
If both the perfection and the non-perfection of all-knowledge are not called "all-knowledge," then practicing in such a manner is not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
If one does not practice the perfection and non-perfection of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom. Why is that?

Subhūti! Whether the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are perfected or unperfected, they are neither called the "knowledge of the paths" nor the "knowledge of all aspects"; furthermore, to practice in such a manner is not to practice the perfection of wisdom.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice for the sake of the fulfillment or non-fulfillment of any of the dhāraṇī-doors, that is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!

If all the gateways of dhāraṇī—whether they are perfected or unperfected—are both not called "all the gateways of dhāraṇī," then practicing in such a manner is practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
If one does not practice for the sake of the fulfillment or non-fulfillment of all gateways to meditative concentration, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Why is that? Subhūti!
If all samādhi-gates, whether complete or incomplete, are both not called "all samādhi-gates," then practicing in such a manner is not practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice for the sake of the fulfillment or non-fulfillment of the fruit of a stream-enterer, that is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
Whether the fruit of a stream-enterer is perfected or unperfected, neither is called the fruit of a stream-enterer; nor does one who acts in such a manner practice the perfection of wisdom.
If one does not practice for the sake of the fulfillment or non-fulfillment of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, or arhatship, this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom. Why is that?

Subhūti! Whether the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, or arhatship are fulfilled or unfulfilled, they are in neither case called the fruit of once-returner, non-returner, or arhatship; nor does one who acts in such a manner practice the perfection of wisdom.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice for the fulfillment or non-fulfillment of pratyekabuddha enlightenment, that is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!

Whether the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is perfected or unperfected, neither is called the awakening of a pratyekabuddha; nor does one who acts in such a manner practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice the fulfillment or non-fulfillment of any bodhisattva mahāsattva practices, that is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!

Whether all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are fulfilled or unfulfilled, they are neither called "all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas," nor is it the case that practicing in such a manner constitutes practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice regarding the fulfillment or non-fulfillment of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas, that is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!

Whether the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is fulfilled or unfulfilled, neither is designated as "the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas. Furthermore, to practice in such a manner is not to practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
How extraordinary!
The Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha has well expounded for the sons and daughters of good family who belong to the Mahāyāna the various characteristics of attachment and non-attachment.
The Buddha said,
“So it is, Subhūti! So it is!”
"So it is! It is just as you have said.

All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas skillfully proclaim to sons and daughters of good family who are well-settled in the Mahāyāna the various characteristics of attachment and non-attachment, so that they may train in the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), become free from all defiled attachments, and swiftly attain the ultimate goal."

"Furthermore, Subhūti, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice by way of the signs of attachment or non-attachment regarding form, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom; if they do not practice by way of the signs of attachment or non-attachment regarding feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom."

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice with regard to the sense-field of the eye by way of signs of attachment or non-attachment, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom; if they do not practice with regard to the sense-fields of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind by way of signs of attachment or non-attachment, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice by way of the signs of attachment or non-attachment regarding the sphere of form, they are practicing the perfection of wisdom; if they do not practice by way of the signs of attachment or non-attachment regarding the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena, they are practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice by way of attachment or non-attachment to the eye-element, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom; if they do not practice by way of attachment or non-attachment to the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, or the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice by way of attachment or non-attachment to the sphere of the ear, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom; if they do not practice by way of attachment or non-attachment to the sphere of sounds, the sphere of ear-consciousness, ear-contact, or the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice by way of attachment or non-attachment to the nose element, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom; if they do not practice by way of attachment or non-attachment to the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, or the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice by way of attachment or non-attachment to the element of the tongue, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom; if they do not practice by way of attachment or non-attachment to the element of tastes, the element of tongue-consciousness, tongue-contact, or the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice with regard to the realm of the body by way of signs of attachment or non-attachment, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom. If they do not practice with regard to the realm of tangibles, the realm of body-consciousness, body-contact, or the various feelings produced conditioned by body-contact, by way of signs of attachment or non-attachment, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

"Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice by way of attachment or non-attachment to the mental faculty (*manodhātu*), this is practicing the perfection of wisdom. If they do not practice by way of attachment or non-attachment to the dharma-sphere (*dharmadhātu*), the mental-consciousness-sphere (*manovijñānadhātu*), mental contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*), or the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with mental contact as a condition, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom."

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice by way of attachment or non-attachment to the element of earth, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom; if they do not practice by way of attachment or non-attachment to the elements of water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice by way of the signs of attachment or non-attachment regarding ignorance, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom; if they do not practice by way of the signs of attachment or non-attachment regarding formative forces, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, existence, birth, or old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice the perfection of generosity while clinging to or not clinging to signs, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom; if they do not practice the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom while clinging to or not clinging to signs, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice by way of attachment or non-attachment to internal emptiness, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom. If they do not practice by way of attachment or non-attachment to external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential emptiness, the emptiness of self-characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice by way of the signs of attachment or non-attachment regarding *tathatā* (suchness), they are practicing the perfection of wisdom. If they do not practice by way of the signs of attachment or non-attachment regarding the *dharmadhātu* (dharma-realm), *dharmatā* (dharma-nature), *avitathatā* (non-falsity), *ananyathatā* (unchanging nature), *samatā* (equality), *anupapatti-dharmatā* (the nature of non-arising), *dharmasthititā* (stability of phenomena), *dharmaniyāmatā* (fixed course of phenomena), *bhūtakoṭi* (the limit of reality), *ākāśadhātu* (space-element), or *acintyadhātu* (inconceivable realm), they are practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice by way of attachment or non-attachment toward the noble truth of suffering, they are practicing the perfection of wisdom; if they do not practice by way of attachment or non-attachment toward the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, they are practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice the four dhyānas with attachment to or non-attachment to signs, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom; if they do not practice the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments with attachment to or non-attachment to signs, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice the eight liberations by clinging to or not clinging to their marks, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom; if they do not practice the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, or the ten totalities by clinging to or not clinging to their marks, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice by way of attachment or non-attachment to the four foundations of mindfulness, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom. If they do not practice by way of attachment or non-attachment to the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice the gate of liberation of emptiness by clinging to the signs of attachment or non-attachment, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom; if they do not practice the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness by clinging to the signs of attachment or non-attachment, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice the ten stages of a bodhisattva by clinging to the characteristics of attachment or non-attachment, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 293. Translated by the Dharma Master Xuanzang by Imperial Order. Part One: Chapter Thirty-Six, "Characteristics of Attachment and Non-attachment," Section Five. "Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice with regard to the five eyes by way of the signs of attachment or non-attachment, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom; if they do not practice with regard to the six supernormal powers by way of the signs of attachment or non-attachment, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice by way of attachment or non-attachment to the ten powers of a buddha, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom; if they do not practice by way of attachment or non-attachment to the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice the quality of non-forgetfulness by clinging to or not clinging to its marks, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom; if they do not practice the state of constant equanimity by clinging to or not clinging to its marks, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

"Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice by way of attachment to or non-attachment to the mark of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), this is practicing the perfection of wisdom; if they do not practice by way of attachment to or non-attachment to the marks of the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*) or the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), this is practicing the perfection of wisdom."

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice by way of the signs of attachment or non-attachment regarding any of the dhāraṇī-doors, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom; if they do not practice by way of the signs of attachment or non-attachment regarding any of the samādhi-doors, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice by way of attachment or non-attachment to the fruit of a stream-enterer, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom; if they do not practice by way of attachment or non-attachment to the fruits of a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice for the sake of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha by clinging to or not clinging to signs, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice any of the bodhisattva mahāsattva practices by way of clinging to or non-clinging to signs, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice by way of the signs of attachment or non-attachment regarding the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

"Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this way, they do not give rise to thoughts of attachment or non-attachment toward form; they do not give rise to thoughts of attachment or non-attachment toward feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness. This is practicing the perfection of wisdom."

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this manner, they do not give rise to thoughts of attachment or non-attachment toward the sense base of the eye; they do not give rise to thoughts of attachment or non-attachment toward the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind. This is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

"Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this way, they do not give rise to thoughts of attachment or non-attachment toward the sphere of form; they do not give rise to thoughts of attachment or non-attachment toward the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena. This is the practice of the perfection of wisdom."

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this manner, they give rise to neither attachment nor the notion of non-attachment toward the eye-element; they give rise to neither attachment nor the notion of non-attachment toward the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition. This is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

"Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this manner, they do not give rise to notions of attachment or non-attachment regarding the ear element; they do not give rise to notions of attachment or non-attachment regarding the sound element, the ear-consciousness element, ear-contact, or the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition. This is practicing the perfection of wisdom."

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this way, they do not give rise to thoughts of attachment or non-attachment toward the nose element; they do not give rise to thoughts of attachment or non-attachment toward the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, or the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition. This is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

"Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this way, they do not give rise to notions of attachment or non-attachment regarding the tongue element; they do not give rise to notions of attachment or non-attachment regarding the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, or the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition. This is practicing the perfection of wisdom."

"Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this way, they do not give rise to thoughts of attachment or non-attachment toward the body element; they do not give rise to thoughts of attachment or non-attachment toward the object-element of touch, the body-consciousness element, body-contact, or the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition. This is practicing the perfection of wisdom."

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this way, they do not give rise to thoughts of attachment or non-attachment toward the mind-element (*manodhātu*); nor do they give rise to thoughts of attachment or non-attachment toward the dharma-element (*dharmadhātu*), the mind-consciousness-element (*manovijñānadhātu*), mental contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*), or the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with mental contact as a condition. This is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this way, they do not give rise to thoughts of attachment or non-attachment toward the earth element; they do not give rise to thoughts of attachment or non-attachment toward the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements. This is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this way, they give rise to neither the thought of attachment nor the thought of non-attachment toward ignorance; they give rise to neither the thought of attachment nor the thought of non-attachment toward volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair. This is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.”

"Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this manner, they do not give rise to thoughts of attachment or non-attachment toward the perfection of generosity; they do not give rise to thoughts of attachment or non-attachment toward the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom. This is practicing the perfection of wisdom."

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this way, they do not give rise to thoughts of attachment or non-attachment toward internal emptiness; nor do they give rise to thoughts of attachment or non-attachment toward external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature. This is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this way, they do not give rise to thoughts of attachment or non-attachment toward suchness; they do not give rise to thoughts of attachment or non-attachment toward the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-falsity, the unchanging nature, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, or the inconceivable realm. This is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this way, they do not give rise to thoughts of attachment or non-attachment toward the noble truth of suffering; they do not give rise to thoughts of attachment or non-attachment toward the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path. This is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this way, they give rise to neither the thought of attachment nor the thought of non-attachment toward the four dhyānas; they give rise to neither the thought of attachment nor the thought of non-attachment toward the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments. This is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this manner, they give rise to neither the thought of attachment nor the thought of non-attachment toward the eight liberations; they give rise to neither the thought of attachment nor the thought of non-attachment toward the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities. This is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this way, they do not give rise to thoughts of attachment or non-attachment toward the four foundations of mindfulness; they do not give rise to thoughts of attachment or non-attachment toward the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, or the eightfold noble path—this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this way, they do not give rise to thoughts of attachment or non-attachment toward the gate of liberation of emptiness; they do not give rise to thoughts of attachment or non-attachment toward the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness. This is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this manner, they do not give rise to thoughts of attachment or non-attachment regarding the ten stages of a bodhisattva; this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this way, they give rise to neither the thought of attachment nor the thought of non-attachment toward the five eyes; they give rise to neither the thought of attachment nor the thought of non-attachment toward the six supernormal powers. This is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this manner, they do not give rise to thoughts of attachment or non-attachment toward the ten powers of a buddha; they do not give rise to thoughts of attachment or non-attachment toward the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha. This is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this manner, they do not give rise to thoughts of attachment or non-attachment toward the quality of non-forgetfulness, nor do they give rise to thoughts of attachment or non-attachment toward the state of constant equanimity; this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this manner, they give rise to neither the thought of attachment nor the thought of non-attachment toward omniscience; they give rise to neither the thought of attachment nor the thought of non-attachment toward the knowledge of the aspects of the path or the knowledge of all aspects. This is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this manner, they give rise to neither the thought of attachment nor the thought of non-attachment toward any of the doors of dhāraṇī, and they give rise to neither the thought of attachment nor the thought of non-attachment toward any of the doors of samādhi; this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

"Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this manner, they do not give rise to thoughts of attachment or non-attachment toward the fruit of stream-entry; they do not give rise to thoughts of attachment or non-attachment toward the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, or arhatship. This is practicing the perfection of wisdom."

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this manner, they give rise to neither the thought of attachment nor the thought of non-attachment toward the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha; this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this manner, they do not give rise to attachment toward any bodhisattva mahāsattva practice, nor do they form a notion of non-attachment; this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this manner, they give rise to neither the thought of attachment nor the thought of non-attachment toward the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas; this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.”
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“How extraordinary,
World-Honored One!
"Thus, regarding this profound dharmatā of the perfection of wisdom, whether it is taught or not taught, it neither increases nor decreases.
The Buddha said, "Subhūti!"
So it is! So it is! It is just as you have said.
Thus, regarding this profound dharmatā of the *prajñāpāramitā*, whether it is spoken or not spoken, there is neither increase nor decrease.

"Subhūti! Suppose that a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha were to remain for the full span of his life praising or reviling space; yet that space would neither increase nor decrease. In the same way, the profound dharmatā of the *prajñāpāramitā* is also like this: whether praised or reviled, it neither increases nor decreases."

“Subhūti! For example, when a phantom person is subjected to either disparagement or praise, they neither diminish nor increase, and feel neither sorrow nor joy. In this same way, the profound dharmatā of the perfection of wisdom is also like this: whether it is spoken or not spoken, it remains no different from its original state.”
The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

It is a most difficult task for bodhisattva-mahāsattvas to practice the perfection of wisdom; for this perfection of wisdom neither increases nor decreases whether it is practiced or not practiced, and it possesses no orientation or aversion. Yet, they diligently study and practice such a perfection of wisdom, never regressing until they reach unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”
Why is this? World-Honored One!
When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they practice it as if practicing emptiness, wherein there is absolutely nothing at all.
“World-Honored One!

Just as in empty space there is no form that can be designated, and no feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness that can be designated, so too is the prajñāpāramitā that is cultivated.”
“World-Honored One!
Just as in space there is no eye-base to be designated, and no ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-base to be designated, so too is the prajñāpāramitā that is cultivated.”
“World-Honored One!
Just as in space there is no locus of form to be designated, and no loci of sound, odor, taste, touch, or mental phenomena to be designated, so too is the prajñāpāramitā that is cultivated.”
“World-Honored One!

Just as in the midst of space, there is no eye-element to be designated, nor can a form-element, an eye-consciousness-element, or eye-contact, nor any feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, be designated; so too it is with the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.”
“World-Honored One!

Just as in space there is no ear-element to be designated, nor can a sound-element, an ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, or any feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition be designated, so too it is with the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.”
“World-Honored One!

Just as in space there is no nose-element to be designated, nor can a fragrance-element, a nose-consciousness-element, nose-contact, or the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition be designated, so too it is with the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.”
“World-Honored One!

Just as within space there is no tongue-element that can be designated, nor any taste-element, tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, or the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition that can be designated, so too is the perfection of wisdom that is cultivated.”
“World-Honored One!

Just as within the expanse of space, there is no body-element (kāyadhātu) that can be designated, nor can the touch-element (spraṣṭavyadhātu), the body-consciousness-element (kāyavijñānadhātu), body-contact (kāyasparśa), or any feelings (vedanā) arising with body-contact as a condition be designated; so too it is with the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).”

“Bhagavān, just as in space one cannot designate a mental element (*manodhātu*), nor can one designate a dharma-element (*dharmadhātu*), a mental-consciousness element (*manovijñānadhātu*), mental contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*), or the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with mental contact as condition— so too is the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) that is cultivated.”
“World-Honored One!

Just as within space there is no earth element that can be designated, and no water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness element that can be designated, so too is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.”
“World-Honored One!

Just as in space there is no ignorance that can be designated, nor can formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, or old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair be designated—so too it is with the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.”
“World-Honored One!

Just as in space there is no perfection of giving that can be designated, and no perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom that can be designated, so too it is with the perfection of wisdom that is practiced.”

“Bhagavān, just as within space there can be no designation of internal emptiness, nor external emptiness, nor internal-and-external emptiness, nor the emptiness of emptiness, nor great emptiness, nor the emptiness of the ultimate, nor the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, nor the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, nor absolute emptiness, nor the emptiness of the limitless, nor the emptiness of dispersion, nor the emptiness of non-alteration, nor the emptiness of intrinsic nature, nor the emptiness of self-characteristic, nor the emptiness of common characteristic, nor the emptiness of all phenomena, nor the emptiness of the unapprehendable, nor the emptiness of non-existence, nor the emptiness of intrinsic nature, nor the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature— so too is it with the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.”
“World-Honored One!

Just as in space there is no such thing as *tathatā* (suchness) that can be designated, nor can the *dharmadhātu* (dharma-realm), *dharmatā* (dharma-nature), *avitathatā* (non-falsity), *ananyathatā* (unchanging nature), *samatā* (equality), *anabhibhūtatā* (nature beyond arising), *dharmasthititā* (stability of dharma), *dharmaniyāmatā* (fixed course of dharma), *bhūtakoṭi* (limit of reality), *ākāśadhātu* (space-element), or *acintyadhātu* (inconceivable realm) be designated; so too is the *prajñāpāramitā* (perfection of wisdom) that is cultivated.”

“Bhagavān, just as in space there is no Noble Truth of Suffering that can be designated, and no Noble Truths of Origin, Cessation, or Path that can be designated, so too it is with the Prajñāpāramitā that is being cultivated.”
“World-Honored One!

Just as within space there can be no designation of the four dhyānas, nor any designation of the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments, so too it is with the prajñāpāramitā that is cultivated.”
“World-Honored One!

Just as in space there can be no designation of the eight liberations, nor the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities, so too it is with the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.”
“World-Honored One!

Just as in space there is nothing that can be designated as the four foundations of mindfulness, nor anything that can be designated as the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path—so too it is with the perfection of wisdom that is being cultivated.”
“World-Honored One!

Just as in space there is no gate of liberation of emptiness that can be established, nor any gate of liberation of signlessness or wishlessness that can be established, so too is the perfection of wisdom that is practiced.”
“World-Honored One!
Just as within empty space there are no bodhisattva stages that can be designated, so too it is with the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.”
“World-Honored One!

Just as within the expanse of space there can be no designation of the five eyes, nor can there be any designation of the six supernormal powers, so too it is with the prajñāpāramitā that is cultivated.”
“World-Honored One!

Just as within the expanse of space there is nothing that can be designated as the ten powers of a Buddha, nor anything that can be designated as the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha—so too it is with the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.”
“World-Honored One!

Just as in the midst of space there is no ‘dharma of non-forgetfulness’ that can be designated, and no ‘nature of constant equanimity’ that can be designated, so too it is with the prajñāpāramitā that is cultivated.”
“World-Honored One!

Just as in space there is no omniscience (*sarvajñatā*) that can be designated, and no knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*) or knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) that can be designated, so too it is with the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) that is cultivated.”
“World-Honored One!
Just as in the midst of space there are no gateways of dhāraṇī that can be established, and no gateways of samādhi that can be established, so too it is with the prajñāpāramitā that is cultivated.”
“World-Honored One!

Just as in empty space there is no fruit of stream-entry to be designated, and no fruits of once-returner, non-returner, or arhatship to be designated, so too it is with the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.”
“World-Honored One!
Just as there is no pratyekabuddha-enlightenment that can be designated within space, so too it is with the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.”
“World-Honored One!
Just as in the midst of space there is nothing that can be designated as the practice of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, so too it is with the prajñāpāramitā that one cultivates.”
“World-Honored One!
Just as in the midst of space there is no unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas that can be designated, so too is the perfection of wisdom that is cultivated.”
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
These bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who are able to don such great armor of merit—us sentient beings should all pay them homage."
“World-Honored One!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva dons the armor of merit and exerts diligent vigor for the sake of all sentient beings, it is as if they don the armor of merit and exert diligent vigor for the sake of empty space.”
“World-Honored One!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva dons the armor of merit and exerts diligent effort for the sake of maturing sentient beings for liberation, it is as if they don the armor of merit and exert diligent effort for the sake of maturing space for liberation.”
“World-Honored One!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva dons the great armor of merit and exerts diligent effort for the sake of all dharmas, it is as if they were donning the great armor of merit and exerting diligent effort for the sake of empty space.”
“World-Honored One!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva dons the armor of merit and exerts diligent vigor in order to uproot sentient beings and cause them to emerge from birth and death, it is as if one were donning the great armor of merit and exerting diligent vigor in order to lift up empty space and place it upon a high and sublime location.”
“World-Honored One!

A bodhisattva mahāsattva attains the perfection of great diligence in order that all sentient beings, who are like space, may swiftly be liberated from birth and death and proceed toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”
“World-Honored One!

Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas attain inconceivable and peerless spiritual power; for the sake of the ocean-like nature of all phenomena, which is like space, they don the great armor of merit and set out toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”
“World-Honored One!

Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are most supremely courageous and valiant; for the sake of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas—which is like space—they don the armor of merit and exert diligent vigor.”
“World-Honored One!

It is truly rare that Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas diligently practice asceticism for the sake of all sentient beings, who are like empty space, desiring to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”
Why is this? “World-Honored One!

Suppose the great trichiliocosm were filled with Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, as dense as a forest of bamboo, hemp, reeds, or sugarcanes; and if for one kalpa or more than one kalpa they were to constantly preach the True Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings, each delivering immeasurable and boundless sentient beings and causing them to enter parinirvāṇa in ultimate peace and happiness, yet the realm of sentient beings would neither increase nor decrease.”
Why is this? Because all sentient beings are non-existent, being by nature utterly remote [from intrinsic reality].
"World-Honored One!..."

Suppose that in each of the ten directions, as many worlds as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River were filled with Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, like a forest of bamboo, hemp, reeds, or sugarcanes; and suppose that for an eon or more than an eon, they constantly preached the sublime Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings, each delivering immeasurable and boundless sentient beings and causing them to enter nirvāṇa and ultimate peace and happiness, yet the realm of sentient beings neither increased nor decreased.
Why is this? Because all sentient beings are non-existent, being by nature utterly secluded.
"World-Honored One!..."

Suppose that all the worlds of the ten directions were filled with Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, as dense as forests of bamboo, hemp, reeds, or sugarcane; and suppose that for an eon or more than an eon, they constantly preached the sublime Dharma for the sake of sentient beings, each delivering immeasurable and boundless sentient beings and causing them to enter nirvāṇa and ultimate peace and happiness, yet the realm of sentient beings neither increased nor decreased.
Why is this? Because all sentient beings are non-existent by nature and are fundamentally detached.
"World-Honored One!..."
For this reason, I say:

it is truly rare that a bodhisattva mahāsattva, for the sake of maturing and liberating all sentient beings who are like space, diligently practices asceticism with the desire to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
At that time, there was a bhikṣu in the assembly who thought to himself: "I should pay homage to the profound *prajñāpāramitā*.

Although within this there is no arising or ceasing of any phenomena (*dharma*), the designation of the aggregate of ethical discipline (*śīlaskandha*), the aggregate of concentration (*samādhiskandha*), the aggregate of wisdom (*prajñāskandha*), the aggregate of liberation (*vimuktiskandha*), and the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation (*vimuktijñānadarśanaskandha*) can be found. Furthermore, the designations of the fruit of stream-entry (*srotāpattiphala*), the fruit of once-returning (*sakṛdāgāmiphala*), the fruit of non-returning (*anāgāmiphala*), and the fruit of arhatship (*arhattvaphala*) can be found; the designation of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment (*pratyekabodhi*) can be found; the designation of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment (*anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhi*) can be found; the designations of the Jewels of the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha can be found; and the designation of turning the sublime wheel of Dharma to deliver sentient beings can be found."
The Buddha, knowing his thought, addressed him, saying:
"Bhikṣu, it is so! It is thus!"
"So it is! This profound perfection of wisdom is subtle and difficult to fathom.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, addressed the Venerable Subhūti, saying:
“Venerable One!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to study the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), how should they study it? Subhūti replied:
“Kauśika! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to study the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they should study it as one would space.
At that time, Śakra, the Lord of Devas, again addressed the Buddha, saying:

“Bhagavān! If good sons and good daughters should receive, uphold, recite, contemplate according to principle, and explain to others this profound Prajñāpāramitā as it has been taught, how should I provide them with protection?”
“I only pray that the Blessed One will deign to show us compassion and grant us instruction!
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed Śakra, the Lord of the Devas, saying: “Kauśika!
"Do you see any dharma that can be guarded?
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, replied, "No!"
"Venerable One!
I do not see any dharma that is to be guarded. Subhūti said:
“Kauśika! If good sons and good daughters abide in this profound perfection of wisdom as it has been taught, they will thereby be protected.”
