If good sons or good daughters dwell, never departing from the profound perfection of wisdom as it has been described, you should know that no humans or non-humans who seek an opportunity to cause them harm will ever be able to succeed.
Kauśika! To wish to protect those bodhisattvas who dwell in the profound perfection of wisdom as it has been described is no different from wishing to protect empty space.
Kauśika! If one wishes to protect those bodhisattvas who practice the perfection of wisdom, all such toil will be in vain and provide no benefit whatsoever.
“Kauśika! What do you think?
Is it possible to guard or protect an illusion, a dream, an echo, a reflection, a mirage, a shadow, a transformation, or a city of Gandharvas?”
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, said: “No,
Venerable Sir!”
Subhūti said: "Kauśika!
It is likewise for those who wish to protect bodhisattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom; their efforts will be in vain and will bring no benefit at all."
“Kauśika! What do you think? Is there anyone who can protect all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, as well as the emanations produced by the Buddhas?”
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, said: "No,
Venerable Sir!"
Subhūti said: "Kauśika!
It is likewise for those who wish to protect bodhisattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom; their efforts will be in vain and will bring no benefit whatsoever."
“Kauśika, what do you think? Is there anyone who can guard and protect suchness (tathatā),

the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), or the inconceivable realm?”
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, said: "No,
Venerable Sir!"
Subhūti said, “Kauśika!
It is likewise for those who wish to protect bodhisattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom; their efforts will be in vain and will bring no benefit whatsoever.”
At that time, Śakra, the Lord of Devas, asked the Venerable Subhūti: "Venerable One,
how does a bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the perfection of wisdom, even while knowing all phenomena..."
Like a magical illusion, like a dream, like an echo, like a reflected image, like a mirage, like a shadow, like a transformation,
and like a city of Gandharvas— yet this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not grasp at these as being an illusion,
a dream, an echo, a reflected image, a mirage, or a shadow.
These are magical transformations and these are gandharva-cities; one does not grasp at them as being due to illusion,
dreams, echoes, reflections, mirages, shadows, magical transformations, or gandharva-cities,
nor does one grasp at them as belonging to illusion, dreams, echoes, reflections, or mirages.
...belonging to light and shadow, belonging to transformations, and belonging to the city of Gandharvas— would one also not grasp at that which relies on illusions,
relies on dreams, relies on echoes, relies on images, relies on mirages, relies on light and shadow, relies on transformations,
and relies on the city of Gandharvas?
Subhūti replied, “Kauśika!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not grasp at this as form, nor as feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.”
Nor does one grasp by means of form, nor by means of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness;
nor does one grasp as belonging to form, nor as belonging to feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness;
nor does one grasp as dependent upon form, nor as dependent upon feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.

When this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, although they know that all phenomena are like illusions and even like cities of gandharvas, they do not grasp at them as being illusions or even as being cities of gandharvas; nor do they grasp at them by means of illusions or even by means of cities of gandharvas; nor do they grasp at them as belonging to illusions or even as belonging to cities of gandharvas; nor do they grasp at them as depending upon illusions or even as depending upon cities of gandharvas.
“Kauśika! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not grasp at this eye-base, nor at these ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-bases;
nor do they grasp by means of the eye-base, or by means of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-bases.”
Nor does one grasp it as belonging to the sense-base of the eye, nor to the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind;
nor does one grasp it as depending on the sense-base of the eye, nor on the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind.

When this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, although they know that all phenomena are like illusions and even like cities of gandharvas, they do not grasp at them as being illusions or as being cities of gandharvas; nor do they grasp at them by means of illusions or by means of cities of gandharvas; nor do they grasp at them as belonging to illusions or as belonging to cities of gandharvas; nor do they grasp at them as depending upon illusions or as depending upon cities of gandharvas.

“Kauśika! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not grasp at these as the sense-bases of form, nor as the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena;
nor do they grasp by means of the sense-base of form, nor by means of the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena.”
Nor does one grasp at them as belonging to the sphere of forms, nor to the spheres of sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, or mental phenomena;
nor does one grasp at them as depending upon the sphere of forms, nor upon the spheres of sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, or mental phenomena.

The first of the seven: At that time, through the supernatural power of the Buddha,
all the gods of the Cāturmahārājakāyika, Trāyastriṃśa, Yāma, Tuṣita, Nirmāṇarati,
Paranirmitavaśavartin, Brahmakāyika, and Brahmapurohita heavens within this trichiliocosm [were present].
The Brahmakāyika devas, the Mahābrahmā devas, the Ābhāsvara devas, the Parīttābhā devas, the Apramāṇābhā devas, the Ābhāsvara-śuddha devas,
the Śubha devas, the Parīttaśubhā devas, the Apramāṇaśubhā devas, the Śubhakṛtsna devas, the Vṛhatphala devas,
the Parīttaśubha devas, the Apramāṇaśubha devas, the Vṛhatphala devas, and the Avṛha devas.
The gods of the Heaven of the Thirty-three, the Yāma Heaven, the Tuṣita Heaven, the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven, the Akaniṣṭha Heaven,
the Atapa Heaven, the Sudṛśa Heaven, the Sudarśana Heaven, and the Akaniṣṭha Heaven— each of these gods scattered exquisite celestial sandalwood powder from afar over the Buddha,
approached the Buddha’s presence, prostrated at his feet, and withdrew to stand to one side.

At that time, the Four Great Kings, Śakra Devānām Indra, Mahābrahmā the Lord of the Sahā World, the Ābhāsvara Heaven, the Śubhakṛtsna Heaven, the Bṛhatphala Heaven, and the gods of the Śuddhāvāsa Heavens, through the power of the Buddha’s mindfulness and spiritual might, each beheld in the ten directions a thousand Buddhas proclaiming the Prajñāpāramitā. The meaning, chapters, and names were all identical to those here: the leading bhikṣus requested to hear the Prajñāpāramitā were all named Subhūti, and the leading celestial hosts who posed questions regarding the Prajñāpāramitā were all named Śakra.
At that time, the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Subhūti, saying:

"When the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya attains unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, he too shall proclaim this very profound perfection of wisdom in this very place. Furthermore, all the future Buddhas of this Bhadrakalpa shall likewise proclaim this very profound perfection of wisdom in this very place."
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
When the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya attains unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, by what dharmas, characteristics, and marks will he proclaim this profound Prajñāpāramitā?"
The Buddha said, “Subhūti! When the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya attains unexcelled,

perfect, and complete enlightenment, he shall proclaim this profound perfection of wisdom by teaching that form is neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasure nor suffering, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor non-tranquil, neither detached nor non-detached, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.”

One should proclaim this profound *prajñāpāramitā* by teaching that feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasure nor suffering, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor untranquil, neither detached nor undetached, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.

“Subhūti! When the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya attains unexcelled, complete, and perfect enlightenment, he shall proclaim this profound Prajñāpāramitā by teaching that the sense-field of the eye is neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasure nor suffering, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor non-tranquil, neither detached nor non-detached, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.”

One should proclaim this profound *prajñāpāramitā* by way of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind as being neither impermanent nor permanent, neither pleasant nor painful, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor untranquil, neither secluded nor unsecluded, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.

“Subhūti! When the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya attains unexcelled, complete, and perfect enlightenment, he shall proclaim this profound Prajñāpāramitā by teaching that the sphere of form (rūpāyatana) is neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasure nor suffering, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor non-tranquil, neither detached nor non-detached, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.”

One should proclaim this profound *prajñāpāramitā* by teaching that the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are neither impermanent nor permanent, neither pleasant nor painful, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor untranquil, neither secluded nor unsecluded, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.

“Subhūti! When the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya attains unexcelled, complete, and perfect enlightenment, he shall proclaim this profound Prajñāpāramitā, declaring that the eye-faculty is neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasure nor suffering, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor non-tranquil, neither detached nor non-detached, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.”

One should proclaim this profound *prajñāpāramitā* by way of the form realm, the eye-consciousness realm, and eye-contact, as well as all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, as being neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasant nor painful, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor untranquil, neither detached nor undetached, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.

“Subhūti! When the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya attains unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, he shall proclaim this profound *prajñāpāramitā* by declaring that the sphere of the ear (*śrotradhātu*) is neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasure nor suffering, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor non-tranquil, neither detached nor non-detached, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.”

One should proclaim this profound *prajñāpāramitā* by teaching that the sphere of sound, the sphere of auditory consciousness, and the contact of the ear—as well as all feelings produced with that auditory contact as a condition—are neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasant nor painful, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor untranquil, neither detached nor undetached, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.

"Subhūti! When the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya attains unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, he shall proclaim this profound Prajñāpāramitā by teaching that the realm of the nose (ghrāṇadhātu) is neither impermanent nor permanent, neither pleasure nor suffering, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor non-tranquil, neither detached nor non-detached, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present."

One should proclaim this profound *prajñāpāramitā* by teaching that the realm of fragrance (*gandhadhātu*), the realm of nose-consciousness (*ghrāṇavijñānadhātu*), and the contact of the nose (*ghrāṇasparśa*), as well as all sensations (*vedanā*) produced with nose-contact as a condition, are neither impermanent nor permanent, neither pleasant nor painful, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor untranquil, neither detached nor undetached, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.

“Subhūti! When the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya attains unexcelled, complete, and perfect enlightenment, he shall proclaim this profound perfection of wisdom by means of the tongue-element as being neither impermanent nor non-impermanent, neither pleasant nor painful, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor non-tranquil, neither detached nor non-detached, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.”

One should proclaim this profound *prajñāpāramitā* by teaching that the realm of taste, the realm of tongue-consciousness, and tongue-contact, as well as all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, are neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasant nor painful, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor untranquil, neither detached nor undetached, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.

“Subhūti! When the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya attains unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, he shall proclaim this profound Prajñāpāramitā by teaching that the realm of the body is neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasure nor suffering, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor non-tranquil, neither detached nor non-detached, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.”

One should proclaim this profound *prajñāpāramitā* by teaching that the sphere of tangibles (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*), the sphere of body-consciousness (*kāyavijñānadhātu*), and the contact of the body (*kāyasparśa*), as well as all feelings (*vedanā*) produced with body-contact as their condition, are neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasant nor painful, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor untranquil, neither detached nor undetached, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.

“Subhūti! When the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya attains unexcelled, perfect, and complete awakening, he shall proclaim this profound perfection of wisdom by means of the mental realm as being neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasure nor suffering, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor non-tranquil, neither detached nor non-detached, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.”

One should proclaim this profound *prajñāpāramitā* by way of the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, as being neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasant nor painful, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor untranquil, neither secluded nor unsecluded, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.

“Subhūti! When the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya attains unexcelled, complete, and perfect enlightenment, he shall proclaim this profound *prajñāpāramitā* by teaching that the earth element is neither impermanent nor permanent, neither pleasant nor painful, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor non-tranquil, neither detached nor non-detached, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.”

One should proclaim this profound *prajñāpāramitā* by teaching that the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasure nor suffering, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor untranquil, neither detached nor non-detached, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.

“Subhūti! When the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya attains unexcelled, complete, and perfect enlightenment, he shall proclaim this profound Prajñāpāramitā by way of [teaching that] ignorance is neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasure nor suffering, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor non-tranquil, neither detached nor non-detached, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.”

One should proclaim this profound *prajñāpāramitā* by teaching that form, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasure nor pain, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor untranquil, neither detached nor undetached, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.

“Subhūti! When the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya attains unexcelled, complete, and perfect enlightenment, he shall proclaim this profound Prajñāpāramitā as follows: that the perfection of giving is neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasure nor suffering, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor non-tranquil, neither detached nor non-detached, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.”

One should proclaim this profound perfection of wisdom by teaching that the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are neither eternal nor impermanent, neither blissful nor suffering, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor untranquil, neither detached nor non-detached, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.

“Subhūti! When the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya attains unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, he shall proclaim this profound *prajñāpāramitā* by means of inner emptiness (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*) as being neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasure nor suffering, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor non-tranquil, neither detached nor non-detached, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.”

One should proclaim this profound *prajñāpāramitā* by way of outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, emptiness of dispersion, emptiness of non-alteration, essential emptiness, emptiness of self-characteristic, emptiness of common characteristic, emptiness of all phenomena, emptiness of the unapprehendable, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, and emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence; as being neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasure nor suffering, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor non-tranquil, neither detached nor non-detached, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.

“Subhūti! When the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya attains unexcelled, complete, and perfect enlightenment, he shall proclaim this profound perfection of wisdom by means of suchness—which is neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasure nor suffering, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor non-tranquil, neither detached nor non-detached, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.”

One should proclaim this profound *prajñāpāramitā* by means of the *dharmadhātu*, the *dharmatā*, the non-falsity, the immutability, the equality, the freedom from birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*)—as being neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasant nor painful, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor non-tranquil, neither detached nor non-detached, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.

“Subhūti! When the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya attains unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, he shall proclaim this profound *prajñāpāramitā* by teaching that the Noble Truth of Suffering is neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasure nor suffering, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor non-tranquil, neither detached nor non-detached, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.”

One should proclaim this profound *prajñāpāramitā* by way of the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path as being neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasure nor suffering, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor untranquil, neither detached nor undetached, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.

“Subhūti! When the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya attains unexcelled, complete, and perfect enlightenment, he shall proclaim this profound *prajñāpāramitā* by means of the four dhyānas as being neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasant nor painful, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor non-tranquil, neither detached nor non-detached, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.”

One should proclaim this profound *prajñāpāramitā* by means of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions as being neither impermanent nor permanent, neither pleasant nor painful, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor untranquil, neither detached nor undetached, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.

“Subhūti! When the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya attains unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, he shall proclaim this profound Prajñāpāramitā by means of the eight liberations as being neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasure nor suffering, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor non-tranquil, neither detached nor non-detached, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.”

One should proclaim this profound *prajñāpāramitā* by means of the eight spheres of mastery (*abhibhvāyatana*), the nine successive attainments (*anupūrvavihārasamāpatti*), and the ten totalities (*kṛtsnāyatana*), as being neither impermanent nor permanent, neither pleasant nor painful, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor untranquil, neither detached nor undetached, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.

“Subhūti! When the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya attains unexcelled, complete, and perfect enlightenment, he shall proclaim this profound *prajñāpāramitā* by means of the four foundations of mindfulness as being neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasure nor suffering, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor non-tranquil, neither detached nor non-detached, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.”

One should proclaim this profound *prajñāpāramitā* by means of the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path as being neither impermanent nor permanent, neither pleasant nor painful, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor untranquil, neither secluded nor unsecluded, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.

“Subhūti! When the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya attains unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, he shall proclaim this profound *prajñāpāramitā* by means of the gate of liberation that is emptiness (*śūnyatā*), teaching that it is neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasant nor painful, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor non-tranquil, neither detached nor non-detached, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.”

One should proclaim this profound *prajñāpāramitā* by means of the gateways of liberation that are signless (*animitta*) and wishless (*apraṇihita*), teaching that it is neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasant nor painful, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor untranquil, neither detached nor non-detached, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.

“Subhūti! When the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya attains unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, he shall proclaim this profound *prajñāpāramitā* by means of the ten stages of a bodhisattva as being neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasant nor painful, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor non-tranquil, neither secluded nor non-secluded, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.”

“Subhūti! When the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya attains unexcelled, complete, and perfect enlightenment, he shall proclaim this profound *prajñāpāramitā* by means of the five eyes, teaching that it is neither impermanent nor permanent, neither pleasant nor painful, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor non-tranquil, neither detached nor non-detached, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.”

One should proclaim this profound *prajñāpāramitā* by means of the six supernormal powers (*ṣaḍabhijñā*), teaching that it is neither impermanent nor permanent, neither pleasant nor painful, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor untranquil, neither detached nor undetached, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.

“Subhūti! When the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya attains unexcelled, complete, and perfect enlightenment, he shall proclaim this profound perfection of wisdom by means of the ten powers of a Buddha as being neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasure nor suffering, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor non-tranquil, neither detached nor non-detached, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.”

One should proclaim this profound *prajñāpāramitā* by means of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha—teaching that these are neither impermanent nor permanent, neither pleasant nor painful, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor non-tranquil, neither secluded nor non-secluded, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.

"Subhūti! When the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya attains unexcelled, complete, and perfect enlightenment, he shall proclaim this profound Prajñāpāramitā by means of the quality of non-forgetfulness, declaring it to be neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasure nor suffering, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor non-tranquil, neither detached nor non-detached, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present."

One should proclaim this profound *prajñāpāramitā* by means of the nature of equanimity that abides constantly: it is neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasant nor painful, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor untranquil, neither detached nor non-detached, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.

“Subhūti! When the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya attains unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, he shall proclaim this profound *prajñāpāramitā* by means of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) as being neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasure nor suffering, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor non-tranquil, neither detached nor non-detached, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.”

One should proclaim this profound *prajñāpāramitā* by means of the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), teaching that it is neither impermanent nor permanent, neither pleasant nor painful, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor non-peaceful, neither detached nor non-detached, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.

“Subhūti! When the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya attains unexcelled, complete, and perfect enlightenment, he shall proclaim this profound perfection of wisdom by means of all the doors of dhāraṇī, declaring that they are neither impermanent nor permanent, neither pleasant nor painful, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor non-tranquil, neither detached nor non-detached, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.”

One should proclaim this profound *prajñāpāramitā* by teaching that all gateways of samādhi are neither impermanent nor permanent, neither pleasant nor painful, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor untranquil, neither detached nor non-detached, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.

“Subhūti! When the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya attains unexcelled, perfect, and complete awakening, he shall proclaim this profound perfection of wisdom by teaching that the fruit of the stream-enterer is neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasure nor suffering, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor non-tranquil, neither secluded nor non-secluded, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.”

One should proclaim this profound *prajñāpāramitā* by teaching that the fruit of the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat is neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasure nor suffering, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor untranquil, neither detached nor non-detached, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.

“Subhūti! When the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya attains unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, he shall proclaim this profound perfection of wisdom by teaching that the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasure nor suffering, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor non-tranquil, neither secluded nor non-secluded, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.”

“Subhūti! When the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya attains *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, he shall proclaim this profound *prajñāpāramitā* by teaching that all practices of the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas are neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasant nor painful, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor non-tranquil, neither detached nor non-detached, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.”

“Subhūti! When the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya attains unexcelled, perfect, and complete awakening, he shall proclaim this profound perfection of wisdom by declaring that the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening of all Buddhas is neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasure nor suffering, neither self nor non-self, neither pure nor impure, neither tranquil nor non-tranquil, neither detached nor non-detached, neither bound nor liberated, neither existent nor empty, and neither past, nor future, nor present.”
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha,
saying: “World-Honored One,
when the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya attains unexcelled, complete, and perfect enlightenment, what dharma will he realize?”
"What further dharma did he speak?
The Buddha said,
"Suvikrāntavikrāmin!"

When the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya attains *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, he will realize the ultimate purity of form and teach the ultimate purity of form; he will realize the ultimate purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, and teach the ultimate purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness;

he will realize the ultimate purity of the sense-base of the eye and teach the ultimate purity of the sense-base of the eye; he will realize the ultimate purity of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, and teach the ultimate purity of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.

He realizes the ultimate purity of the sphere of form and teaches the ultimate purity of the sphere of form; he realizes the ultimate purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena and teaches the ultimate purity of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena.

He realizes the ultimate purity of the eye-element and teaches the ultimate purity of the eye-element; he realizes the ultimate purity of the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition, and he teaches the ultimate purity of the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition.

He realizes the dharma of the ultimate purity of the ear-element and teaches the dharma of the ultimate purity of the ear-element; he realizes the dharma of the ultimate purity of the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, and teaches the dharma of the ultimate purity of the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition;

he realizes the dharma of the ultimate purity of the nose-element and teaches the dharma of the ultimate purity of the nose-element; he realizes the dharma of the ultimate purity of the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, and teaches the dharma of the ultimate purity of the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition.

He realizes the dharma of the ultimate purity of the tongue-element and teaches the dharma of the ultimate purity of the tongue-element; he realizes the dharmas of the ultimate purity of the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, and he teaches the dharmas of the ultimate purity of the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition;

he realizes the dharma of the ultimate purity of the body-element and teaches the dharma of the ultimate purity of the body-element; he realizes the dharmas of the ultimate purity of the tangible-object-element, the body-consciousness-element, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, and he teaches the dharmas of the ultimate purity of the tangible-object-element, the body-consciousness-element, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition.

He has realized the ultimate purity of the mind-element (*manodhātu*) and teaches the ultimate purity of the mind-element; he has realized the ultimate purity of the dharma-element (*dharmadhātu*), the mind-consciousness-element (*manovijñānadhātu*), and all feelings born of mind-contact (*manaḥsparśa*) conditioned by mind-contact, and he teaches the ultimate purity of the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, and all feelings born of mind-contact conditioned by mind-contact.

He has realized the ultimate purity of the earth-element (*pṛthivīdhātu*) and teaches the ultimate purity of the earth-element; he has realized the ultimate purity of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness-elements (*ab-dhātu, tejo-dhātu, vāyu-dhātu, ākāśa-dhātu, vijñāna-dhātu*) and teaches the ultimate purity of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness-elements.

He realizes the dharma of the ultimate purity of ignorance and teaches the dharma of the ultimate purity of ignorance; he realizes the dharmas of the ultimate purity of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair, and he teaches the dharmas of the ultimate purity of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle Two Hundred and Ninety-Two. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter Thirty-Seven, Part Two, "Explaining the Characteristics of Prajñā. "Realizing the ultimate purity of the perfection of giving (*dāna-pāramitā*), he explains the ultimate purity of the perfection of giving; realizing the ultimate purity of the perfections of ethical discipline (*śīla*), patience (*kṣānti*), diligence (*vīrya*), meditative concentration (*dhyāna*), and wisdom (*prajñā*), he explains the ultimate purity of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom;

realizing the ultimate purity of internal emptiness (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*), he explains the ultimate purity of internal emptiness; realizing the ultimate purity of external emptiness (*bahirdhā-śūnyatā*)..."
Internal and external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena,
the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration,
the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self-characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, and the emptiness of the unapprehendable.

The emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are ultimately pure phenomena; they are taught as the emptiness of the external,

the emptiness of the internal and external, the emptiness of emptiness, the great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate, the emptiness of the conditioned, the emptiness of the unconditioned, the emptiness of the ultimate,
the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion, and the emptiness of non-alteration.

The ultimate purity of the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence;

the ultimate purity of realizing *tathatā* (suchness), the teaching of the ultimate purity of *tathatā*; the ultimate purity of realizing the *dharmadhātu*, the *dharmatā*, the non-erroneous nature, the unchanging nature, the nature of equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharma-niyama*), the stability of phenomena (*dharma-sthiti*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśa-dhātu*), and the inconceivable realm; and the teaching of the ultimate purity of the *dharmadhātu*, the *dharmatā*, the non-erroneous nature, the unchanging nature, the nature of equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm.

Having realized the ultimate purity of the noble truth of suffering, he teaches the ultimate purity of the noble truth of suffering; having realized the ultimate purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, he teaches the ultimate purity of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path;

having realized the ultimate purity of the four dhyānas, he teaches the ultimate purity of the four dhyānas; having realized the ultimate purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, he teaches the ultimate purity of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions;

having realized the ultimate purity of the eight liberations, he teaches the ultimate purity of the eight liberations; having realized the ultimate purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities, he teaches the ultimate purity of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities.

He realizes the ultimately pure dharmas of the four foundations of mindfulness and teaches the ultimately pure dharmas of the four foundations of mindfulness; he realizes the ultimately pure dharmas of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path, and he teaches the ultimately pure dharmas of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.

He realizes the ultimately pure dharma of the emptiness gate of liberation and teaches the ultimately pure dharma of the emptiness gate of liberation; he realizes the ultimately pure dharmas of the signless and wishless gates of liberation and teaches the ultimately pure dharmas of the signless and wishless gates of liberation;
he realizes the ultimately pure dharmas of the ten bodhisattva stages and teaches the ultimately pure dharmas of the ten bodhisattva stages.

He realizes the dharma of the ultimate purity of the five eyes and teaches the dharma of the ultimate purity of the five eyes; he realizes the dharma of the ultimate purity of the six supernormal powers and teaches the dharma of the ultimate purity of the six supernormal powers;

he realizes the dharma of the ultimate purity of the ten powers of a Buddha and teaches the dharma of the ultimate purity of the ten powers of a Buddha; he realizes the dharma of the ultimate purity of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and he teaches the dharma of the ultimate purity of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.

He realizes the quality of non-forgetfulness that is ultimately pure, and he teaches the quality of non-forgetfulness that is ultimately pure; he realizes the quality of constant abiding in equanimity that is ultimately pure, and he teaches the quality of constant abiding in equanimity that is ultimately pure;

he realizes the quality of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) that is ultimately pure, and he teaches the quality of all-knowledge that is ultimately pure; he realizes the qualities of the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) that are ultimately pure, and he teaches the qualities of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects that are ultimately pure;

he realizes all doors of dhāraṇī that are ultimately pure, and he teaches all doors of dhāraṇī that are ultimately pure; he realizes all doors of samādhi that are ultimately pure, and he teaches all doors of samādhi that are ultimately pure.

Realizing the ultimately pure dharma of the fruit of stream-entry, he teaches the ultimately pure dharma of the fruit of stream-entry; realizing the ultimately pure dharmas of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship, he teaches the ultimately pure dharmas of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship;
realizing the ultimately pure dharma of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, he teaches the ultimately pure dharma of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment;
realizing the ultimately pure dharmas of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, he teaches the ultimately pure dharmas of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.

"He has realized the ultimately pure dharmas of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas, and he teaches the ultimately pure dharmas of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"In this way, how is the perfection of wisdom pure?
The Buddha said,
"Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
Because form is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because form is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
How is it that because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”
“Subhūti! Because form is without arising and without cessation, and without defilement or purification, it is pure; because form is pure, the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) is pure.

Because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are without arising and without cessation, and without defilement or purification, they are pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, "Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
Because the sphere of the eye is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure."
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because the sphere of the eye is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
Why is it that because the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”
“Subhūti! Because the eye-base is without arising and without cessation, and without defilement and without purification, it is pure; because the eye-base is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.

Because the ear-base, nose-base, tongue-base, body-base, and mind-base are without arising and without cessation, and without defilement and without purification, they are pure; because the ear-base, nose-base, tongue-base, body-base, and mind-base are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!
Because the sphere of form is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the sphere of form (*rūpāyatana*) is pure, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure?
And how is it that because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena (*śabda-, gandha-, rasa-, spraṣṭavya-, dharmāyatana*) are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the sphere of form is without arising and without cessation, and without defilement and without purification, it is pure; because the sphere of form is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.

Because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are without arising and without cessation, and without defilement and without purification, they are pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the eye-element is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the eye-element is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
How is it that because the form-element, and so forth, up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the eye-element is without arising and without cessation, and without defilement or purification, it is pure; because the eye-element is pure, the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) is pure.

Because the form-element, up to and including all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, are without arising and without cessation, and without defilement or purification, they are pure; because the form-element, up to and including all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said: “Subhūti!

Because the ear-element is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the ear-element is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
And how is it that because the sound-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”
“Subhūti! Because the ear-element is without arising and without cessation, and without defilement or purification, it is pure; because the ear-element is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.

Because the sound-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, are without arising and without cessation, and without defilement or purification, they are pure; because the sound-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, "Subhūti!

Because the nose element (*ghrāṇadhātu*) is pure, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure; because the odor element (*gandhadhātu*), the nose-consciousness element (*ghrāṇavijñānadhātu*), nose-contact (*ghrāṇasparśa*), and all feelings (*vedanā*) produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure."
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the nose element is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
How is it that because the fragrance element, and so forth, up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the nose element (*ghrāṇadhātu*) is without arising and without cessation, and without defilement and without purification, it is pure; because the nose element is pure, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure.

Because the odor element (*gandhadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are without arising and without cessation, and without defilement and without purification, they are pure; because the odor element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

Because the tongue element is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the tongue-element is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
How is it that because the taste-element, and even all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the tongue-element is without arising and without cessation, and without defilement or purification, it is pure; because the tongue-element is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.

Because the taste-element, and even all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, are without arising and without cessation, and without defilement or purification, they are pure; because the taste-element, and even all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the body-element (*kāyadhātu*) is pure, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure; because the touch-element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*), the body-consciousness-element (*kāyavijñānadhātu*), as well as body-contact (*kāyasparśa*) and all feelings (*vedanā*) produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the body element (*kāyadhātu*) is pure, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure?
And how is it that because the contact element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*)—and even all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition—is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the body-element (kāyadhātu) is without arising and without cessation, and without defilement and without purification, it is pure; because the body-element is pure, the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) is pure.

Because the object-element of touch (spraṣṭavyadhātu) up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are without arising and without cessation, and without defilement and without purification, they are pure; because the object-element of touch up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the mind-element (*manodhātu*) is pure, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure; because the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element (*manovijñānadhātu*), as well as mind-contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*) and the various feelings (*vedanā*) arising with mind-contact as a condition are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the mind-element (*manodhātu*) is pure, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure?
And how is it that because the dharma-element (*dharmadhātu*), up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition, are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the mind-element (manodhātu) is without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purification, it is pure; because the mind-element is pure, the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) is pure.

Because the dharma-element (dharmadhātu), up to and including all feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition, are without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purification, they are pure; because the dharma-element, up to and including all feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition, are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
Because the earth element is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the earth element is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
And how is it that because the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the earth element is without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purification, it is pure; because the earth element is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.

Because the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purification, they are pure; because the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because ignorance is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because ignorance is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
How is it that because [the links from] volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”
“Subhūti! Because ignorance is without arising and without cessation, and is neither defiled nor pure, it is pure; because ignorance is pure, the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) is pure.

Because the formative forces up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are without arising and without cessation, and are neither defiled nor pure, they are pure; because the formative forces up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the perfection of generosity is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, and meditative concentration are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the perfection of generosity is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
And how is it that because the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, and meditative concentration are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the perfection of generosity is without arising and without cessation, and without defilement and without purification, it is pure; because the perfection of generosity is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.

Because the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, and meditative concentration are without arising and without cessation, and without defilement and without purification, they are pure; because the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, and meditative concentration are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because internal emptiness is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure. Because external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because internal emptiness is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
And how is it that because external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of non-existence and self-nature, is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because internal emptiness is without arising and without cessation, and without defilement and without purification, it is pure; because internal emptiness is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.

Because external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the essential nature of non-entities, is without arising and without cessation, and without defilement and without purification, it is pure; because external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the essential nature of non-entities, is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because true thusness (*tathatā*) is pure, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure. Because the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because true thusness (*tathatā*) is pure, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure?
How is it that because the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), up to the inconceivable realm, is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because true thusness (tathatā) is without arising or cessation, and without defilement or purification, it is pure; because true thusness is pure, the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) is pure.

Because the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), up to the inconceivable realm, is without arising or cessation, and without defilement or purification, it is pure; because the dharma-realm, up to the inconceivable realm, is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!
Because the noble truth of suffering is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the noble truth of suffering is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
And how is it that because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the noble truth of suffering is without arising and without cessation, and without defilement and without purification, it is pure; because the noble truth of suffering is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.

Because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are without arising and without cessation, and without defilement and without purification, they are pure; because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!
Because the four dhyānas are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the four dhyānas are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
How is it that because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the four dhyānas are without arising and without cessation, and without defilement and without purity, they are pure; because the four dhyānas are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.

Because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are without arising and without cessation, and without defilement and without purity, they are pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the eight liberations are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the eight liberations (aṣṭa-vimokṣa) are pure, the perfection of wisdom (prajñā-pāramitā) is pure?

How is it that because the eight bases of mastery (abhibhv-āyatana), the nine successive attainments (anupūrva-vihāra-samāpatti), and the ten totalities (kṛtsnāyatana) are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the eight liberations are without arising and without cessation, and are neither defiled nor purified, they are pure; because the eight liberations are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.

Because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are without arising and without cessation, and are neither defiled nor purified, they are pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

Because the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the four foundations of mindfulness are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?

How is it that because the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the four applications of mindfulness are without arising and without cessation, and without defilement and without purification, they are pure; because the four applications of mindfulness are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.

Because the four right efforts, up to and including the eight branches of the noble path, are without arising and without cessation, and without defilement and without purification, they are pure; because the four right efforts, up to and including the eight branches of the noble path, are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!
Because the gate of liberation of emptiness is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the gate of liberation of emptiness is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
How is it that because the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the gate of liberation of emptiness is without arising and without cessation, and without defilement and without purification, it is pure; because the gate of liberation of emptiness is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.

Because the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are without arising and without cessation, and without defilement and without purification, they are pure; because the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said,
“Subhūti! Because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the ten stages of a bodhisattva are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
