Because the six supernormal powers are ungraspable, they are without defilement; because the six supernormal powers are without defilement, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

Because the ten powers of a buddha are free from defilement, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha are free from defilement, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the ten powers of a Buddha are free from defilement, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
And how is it that because the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, are free from defilement, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”
“Subhūti! Because the ten powers of a Buddha cannot be grasped, they are without defilement; because the ten powers of a Buddha are without defilement, the perfection of wisdom is pure.

Because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha cannot be grasped, they are without defilement; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are without defilement, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the quality of non-forgetfulness is free from defilement, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the state of constant equanimity is free from defilement, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the quality of non-forgetfulness is free from defilement, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
How is it that because the state of constant dwelling in equanimity is free from defilement, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the quality of non-forgetfulness (*asaṃpramoṣadharma*) cannot be grasped, it is without defilement; because the quality of non-forgetfulness is without defilement, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure.

Because the state of constant abiding in equanimity (*upekṣā*) cannot be grasped, it is without defilement; because the state of constant abiding in equanimity is without defilement, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because all-knowledge (sarvajñatā) is without defilement, the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) is pure; because the knowledge of the paths (mārgākārajñatā) and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā) are without defilement, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because omniscience (*sarvajñatā*) is free from defilement, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure?
How is it that because the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are free from defilement, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”
“Subhūti! Because omniscience (*sarvajñatā*) is ungraspable, it is without defilement; because omniscience is without defilement, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure.

Because the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are ungraspable, they are without defilement; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are without defilement, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!
Because all dhāraṇī-doors are free from defilement, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because all samādhi-doors are free from defilement, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because all dharani-doors are free from defilement, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
Why is it that because all samadhi-doors are free from defilement, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”
“Subhūti! Because all dhāraṇī-doors are ungraspable, they are without defilement; because all dhāraṇī-doors are without defilement, the perfection of wisdom is pure.
Because all samādhi-doors are ungraspable, they are without defilement; because all samādhi-doors are without defilement, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the fruit of stream-entry is free from defilement, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are free from defilement, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the fruit of stream-entry is free from defilement, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
How is it that because the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are free from defilement, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”
“Subhūti! Because the fruit of stream-entry cannot be grasped, it is without defilement; because the fruit of stream-entry is without defilement, the perfection of wisdom is pure.

Because the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship cannot be grasped, they are without defilement; because the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are without defilement, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said,
“Subhūti, because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is free from defilement, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is free from defilement, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
“Because the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha cannot be grasped, it is without defilement; because the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is without defilement, the perfection of wisdom is pure.
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [It is so.]”
“Because all the practices of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas are free from defilement, the Prajñāpāramitā is pure.
“World-Honored One,
in what way are all the practices of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas free from defilement, such that the Prajñāpāramitā is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because all the practices of bodhisattva mahāsattvas cannot be grasped, they are free from defilement; because all the practices of bodhisattva mahāsattvas are free from defilement, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti! Because the unsurpassed,
perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is free from defilement, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is free from defilement, the perfection of wisdom is pure? “Subhūti!

Because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas cannot be grasped, it is without defilement; because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is without defilement, the perfection of wisdom is pure.
"Furthermore, Subhūti, because space is unstained, the perfection of wisdom is pure. [Subhūti said:
"World-Honored One!"
"How is it that because space is unstained, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
"Subhūti! Because space cannot be grasped, it is unstained; because space is unstained, the perfection of wisdom is pure."

"Furthermore, Subhūti, because form is merely a conventional designation, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure."
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because form is merely a conventional designation, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
How is it that because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Just as two things produce an echo depending upon space, so too are form through to consciousness merely conventional designations. Because form through to consciousness are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the eye-base is merely a conventional designation, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the sphere of the eye is merely a conventional designation, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
How is it that because the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Just as two things produce an echo in dependence upon space, so too it is with the sense bases from the eye base up to the mind base: they exist only as mere designations. Because the sense bases from the eye base up to the mind base are mere designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

Because the sphere of form is merely a conventional designation, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because the sphere of form is merely a conventional designation, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
Why is it that because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Just as two things produce an echo in dependence upon space, so too it is with the sense-sphere of form up to the sense-sphere of phenomena; they are merely conventional designations. Because the sense-spheres of form up to the sense-sphere of phenomena are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the eye-element is merely a conventional designation, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the eye-element is merely a conventional designation, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
How is it that because everything from the form-element up to the feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Just as two things produce an echo in dependence upon space, so too it is with the eye-faculty up to the feelings produced with eye-contact as condition; these are merely conventional designations. Because the eye-faculty up to the feelings produced with eye-contact as condition are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the ear-element is merely a conventional designation, the perfection of wisdom is pure. Because the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the ear-element is merely a conventional designation, the perfection of wisdom is pure?

And how is it that because the sound-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Just as two things produce an echo in dependence upon space, so too it is with the various feelings produced with the ear-element and so forth, up to ear-contact, as conditions; these are also merely conventional designations. Because the various feelings produced with the ear-element and so forth, up to ear-contact, as conditions are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the nose element is merely a conventional designation, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because the nose element (*ghrāṇadhātu*) is merely a conventional designation, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure?

Why is it that from the odor element (*gandhadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, because they are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Just as two things produce an echo in dependence upon space, so too it is with the nose element and even the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition; these exist only as provisional designations. Because the nose element and even the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are merely provisional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the tongue element is merely a conventional designation, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the tongue-element is merely a conventional designation, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
How is it that because the taste-element, and even all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Just as two things produce an echo in dependence upon space, so too it is with the various feelings produced with the tongue-element and up to tongue-contact as conditions; these are merely conventional designations. Because the various feelings produced with the tongue-element and up to tongue-contact as conditions are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the body element (*kāyadhātu*) is merely a conventional designation, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure. Because the tangible object element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*), the body-consciousness element (*kāyavijñānadhātu*), as well as body-contact (*kāyasparśa*) and all feelings (*vedanā*) produced with body-contact as a condition, are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the body element (*kāyadhātu*) is merely a conventional designation, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure?

How is it that from the contact element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*) up to the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with body-contact as a condition, because they are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Just as two things produce an echo in dependence upon space, so too are all feelings produced with the body-element and so forth, up to body-contact, as conditions; they are likewise merely conventional designations. Because all feelings produced with the body-element and so forth, up to body-contact, as conditions are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the mind-element (manodhātu) is merely a conventional designation, the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) is pure. Because the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, as well as mental contact (manaḥsaṃsparśa) and the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the mind-element (*manodhātu*) is merely a conventional designation, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure?

How is it that because the dharma-element (*dharmadhātu*), up to and including the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition, are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Just as two things produce an echo in dependence upon space, so too it is with the mental faculty and all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition; these are merely conventional designations. Because the mental faculty and all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

Because the earth element is merely a conventional designation, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
In what sense is the perfection of wisdom pure because the earth element is merely a conventional designation?
In what sense is the perfection of wisdom pure because the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are merely conventional designations?”

“Subhūti! Just as two things produce an echo depending upon space, so too it is with the earth element up to the consciousness element; they exist only as conventional designations. Because the earth element up to the consciousness element are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because ignorance is merely a conventional designation, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because ignorance is merely a conventional designation, the perfection of wisdom is pure?

And why is it that because [the links] from volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Just as two things produce an echo depending upon space, so too it is with ignorance through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair; they exist only as conventional designations. Because ignorance through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are mere conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the perfection of generosity is merely a conventional designation, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because the perfection of giving is merely a conventional designation, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
Why is it that because everything from the perfection of ethical discipline up to the perfection of wisdom is merely a conventional designation, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Just as two things produce an echo in dependence upon space, so too it is with the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom: they exist only as conventional designations. Because the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom exists only as conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because internal emptiness is merely a conventional designation, the perfection of wisdom is pure. Because external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because internal emptiness is merely a provisional designation, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
And how is it that from external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, because they are merely provisional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Just as two things produce an echo in dependence upon space, so too it is with inner emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature; these are merely conventional designations. Because inner emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature are mere conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because *tathatā* (suchness) is merely a conventional designation, the perfection of wisdom is pure. Because *dharmadhātu* (the realm of phenomena), *dharmatā* (the nature of phenomena), *avitathatā* (non-falsity), *ananyathatā* (unchanging nature), *samatā* (equality), *anupapattitā* (freedom from arising), *dharmasthititā* (stability of phenomena), *dharmaniyāmatā* (fixed course of phenomena), *bhūtakoṭi* (the limit of reality), *ākāśadhātu* (the realm of space), and *acintyadhātu* (the inconceivable realm) are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because *tathatā* (suchness) is merely a provisional designation, the *prajñāpāramitā* is pure?
How is it that because the *dharmadhātu* (dharma-realm), up to the *acintyadhātu* (inconceivable realm), are merely provisional designations, the *prajñāpāramitā* is pure?”

“Subhūti! Just as two things produce an echo based upon space, so too it is with the true nature (tathatā) up to the inconceivable realm; these exist only as provisional designations. Because the true nature up to the inconceivable realm are merely provisional designations, the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the noble truth of suffering is merely a conventional designation, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the noble truth of suffering is merely a conventional designation, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
And how is it that because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Just as two things produce an echo depending upon space, so too are the Noble Truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path; they exist only as provisional designations. Because the Noble Truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path are mere provisional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the four dhyānas are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the four dhyānas are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
How is it that because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Just as two things produce an echo depending upon space, so too it is with the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments; they exist only as provisional designations. Because the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments are merely provisional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the eight liberations are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the eight liberations are merely provisional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
How is it that because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities are merely provisional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Just as two things produce an echo in dependence upon space, so too it is with the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities; they exist only as provisional designations. Because the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities are merely provisional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the four foundations of mindfulness are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the four foundations of mindfulness are merely provisional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
And how is it that because the four right endeavors, up to and including the eightfold noble path, are merely provisional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Just as two things produce an echo in dependence upon space, so too it is with the four applications of mindfulness up to the eight branches of the noble path; they exist only as provisional designations. Because the four applications of mindfulness up to the eight branches of the noble path are merely provisional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

Because the gate of liberation of emptiness is merely a provisional designation, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are merely provisional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the gate of liberation of emptiness is merely a provisional designation, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
How is it that because the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are merely provisional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Just as two things produce an echo in dependence upon space, so too are the gateways of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—merely conventional designations. Because the gateways of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!
Because the ten stages of a bodhisattva are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the ten stages of a bodhisattva are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure? “Subhūti!

Just as two things produce an echo in dependence upon space, so too are the ten stages of a bodhisattva; they exist only as provisional designations. Because the ten stages of a bodhisattva are merely provisional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure.
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

Because the five eyes are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the six supernormal powers are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the five eyes are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
How is it that because the six supernormal powers are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Just as two things produce an echo in dependence upon space, so too are the five eyes and the six supernormal powers merely conventional designations. Because the five eyes and the six supernormal powers are mere conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the ten powers of a buddha are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the ten powers of a Buddha are merely provisional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
How is it that because the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, are merely provisional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Just as two things produce an echo depending upon space, so too it is with the Buddha’s ten powers up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; they exist only as provisional designations. Because the Buddha’s ten powers up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are merely provisional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the quality of non-forgetfulness is merely a conventional designation, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the state of constant abiding in equanimity is merely a conventional designation, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because the quality of non-forgetfulness is merely a conventional designation, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
Why is it that because the state of constant abiding in equanimity is merely a conventional designation, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Just as two things produce an echo based upon space, so too are the quality of non-forgetfulness (*asaṃpramoṣadharma*) and the nature of constant equanimity (*upekṣāsatatvakārin*); they exist only as provisional designations. Because the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity are merely provisional designations, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because omniscience (*sarvajñatā*) is merely a conventional designation, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure; because the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because omniscience (*sarvajñatā*) is merely a conventional designation, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure?

How is it that because the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Just as two things produce an echo in dependence upon space, so too it is with all-knowledge (*sarvajñā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*); they exist only as provisional designations. Because all-knowledge, the knowledge of the aspects of the path, and the knowledge of all aspects are merely provisional designations, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
Because all dhāraṇī-doors are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because all samādhi-doors are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because all dharani-doors are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
Why is it that because all samadhi-doors are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Just as two things produce an echo in dependence upon space, so too it is with all the doors of dhāraṇī and all the doors of samādhi: they exist only as provisional designations. Because all the doors of dhāraṇī and all the doors of samādhi are merely provisional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

Because the fruit of stream-entry is merely a conventional designation, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because the fruit of stream-entry is merely a conventional designation, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
Why is it that because the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Just as two things produce an echo depending upon space, so too it is with the fruits from that of a stream-enterer up to that of an arhat; they exist only as provisional designations. Because the fruits from a stream-enterer up to an arhat are merely provisional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti,
because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is merely a conventional designation, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the enlightenment of a solitary realizer (pratyekabuddha) is merely a conventional designation, the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) is pure? “Subhūti!

Just as two things produce an echo depending upon space, so too is the awakening of a pratyekabuddha: it exists only as a conventional designation. Because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is merely a conventional designation, the perfection of wisdom is pure.
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!
Because all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because all practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure? “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
[Because they are merely conventional designations.]”

Just as two things produce an echo based upon space, so too is all the practice of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas: it exists only as a provisional designation. Because all the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are merely provisional designations, the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) is pure.
The Buddha said, “Subhūti! Because the unsurpassed,
perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is merely a conventional designation, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is merely a provisional designation, the perfection of wisdom is pure? “Subhūti!

Just as two things produce an echo based upon space, so too is the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas: it exists only as a conventional designation. Because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is merely a conventional designation, the perfection of wisdom is pure.
"Furthermore, Subhūti, because space is merely a conventional designation, the perfection of wisdom is pure. [Subhūti said:

"How is it that because space is merely a conventional designation, the perfection of wisdom is pure?

"Subhūti! Just as echoes appear in dependence upon space through two factors and are merely conventional designations—because they are merely conventional designations, the perfection of wisdom is pure."
"Furthermore, Subhūti, because form is ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure."
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because form is ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
Why is it that because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Form is ineffable because it has no object that can be expressed; feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are ineffable because they have no object that can be expressed. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!
Because the sense-base of the eye is ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because the sphere of the eye is ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
Why is it that because the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the eye-base has no thing that can be described, it is ineffable; because the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases have no thing that can be described, they are ineffable. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the sphere of form is ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because the sphere of form is ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
Why is it that because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the sphere of form (rūpāyatana) has no thing that can be expressed, it is inexpressible; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena (dharmāyatana) have no thing that can be expressed, they are inexpressible. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the eye-element is ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because the eye-element is ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
Why is it that because the form-element, and so forth, up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the eye-element has no thing that can be expressed, it is inexpressible; because the form-element, and so on up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, have no thing that can be expressed, they are inexpressible. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the ear-element is ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because the ear-element is ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
Why is it that because the sound-element, and even the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the ear-element has no thing that can be expressed, it is inexpressible; because the sound-element, and so forth, up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, have no thing that can be expressed, they are inexpressible. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

Because the nose element (*ghrāṇadhātu*) is ineffable, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure; because the odor element (*gandhadhātu*), the nose-consciousness element (*ghrāṇavijñānadhātu*), as well as nose-contact (*ghrāṇasparśa*) and the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with nose-contact as a condition are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is the perfection of wisdom pure because the nose-element is ineffable?
Why is the perfection of wisdom pure because the fragrance-element, and even all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, are ineffable?”

“Subhūti! Because the nose element (*ghrāṇadhātu*) has nothing that can be expressed, it is inexpressible; because everything from the odor element (*gandhadhātu*) up to the feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition has nothing that can be expressed, they are inexpressible. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the tongue element is ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because the tongue-element is ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
Why is it that because the taste-element, and even all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the tongue element has no thing that can be expressed, it is inexpressible; because the taste element, and even the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, have no thing that can be expressed, they are inexpressible. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the body-element (kāyadhātu) is ineffable, the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) is pure; because the touch-element (spraṣṭavyadhātu), the body-consciousness-element (kāyavijñānadhātu), as well as body-contact (kāyasparśa) and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because the body-element (*kāyadhātu*) is ineffable, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure?
Why is it that because the contact-element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*)—and even all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition—are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the body element has no thing that can be expressed, it is inexpressible; because the tangible element and even the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition have no thing that can be expressed, they are inexpressible. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the mind-element (*manodhātu*) is ineffable, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure; because the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, and the mental contact, as well as all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because the mind-element (*manodhātu*) is ineffable, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure?

Why is it that because everything from the dharma-element (*dharmadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition (*manas-saṃsparśapratyayaja-vedanā*) is ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the mind-element has no thing that can be expressed, it is inexpressible; because the dharma-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition, have no thing that can be expressed, they are inexpressible. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!
Because the earth element is ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because the earth element is ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
Why is it that because the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the earth element has no thing that can be expressed, it is inexpressible; because the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements have no thing that can be expressed, they are inexpressible. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti, because ignorance is inexpressible,

the perfection of wisdom is pure; because volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are inexpressible, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because ignorance is ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
And why is it that because [the links from] volitional formations up to old age, death, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Ignorance is ineffable because there is no entity that can be described; the formative forces, and so on, up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, are ineffable because there is no entity that can be described. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

Because the perfection of generosity is ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because the perfection of giving is ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
And why is it that because the perfections from ethical discipline up to the perfection of wisdom are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the perfection of generosity has no object that can be expressed, it is inexpressible; because the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom have no object that can be expressed, they are inexpressible. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

Because inner emptiness is ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, emptiness of all phenomena, emptiness of the unapprehendable, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, and emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because inner emptiness is ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
And why is it that from outer emptiness up to the emptiness of the nature of non-nature, because they are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because internal emptiness has no thing that can be expressed, it is inexpressible; because external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, have no thing that can be expressed, they are inexpressible. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because true suchness (*tathatā*) is ineffable, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure. Because the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), non-erroneousness, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because true thusness (*tathatā*) is ineffable, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure?
Why is it that because the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), up to the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*), are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because true suchness has no object that can be expressed, it is inexpressible; because the dharma-realm, up to and including the inconceivable realm, have no object that can be expressed, they are inexpressible. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti,
because the noble truth of suffering is ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the Noble Truth of Suffering is ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
How is it that because the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the noble truth of suffering has no thing that can be expressed, it is inexpressible; because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path have no thing that can be expressed, they are inexpressible. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
Because the four dhyānas are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because the four dhyānas are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
Why is it that because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the four dhyānas have no thing that can be expressed, they are inexpressible; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions have no thing that can be expressed, they are inexpressible. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said: “Subhūti!

Because the eight liberations are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because the eight liberations are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
Why is it that because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! The eight liberations are ineffable because they have no thing that can be expressed; the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are ineffable because they have no thing that can be expressed. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the four applications of mindfulness are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because the four foundations of mindfulness are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
Why is it that because the four right endeavors, up to and including the eightfold noble path, are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the four foundations of mindfulness have no object that can be expressed, they are inexpressible; because the four right efforts up to the eight branches of the noble path have no object that can be expressed, they are inexpressible. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the gate of liberation of emptiness is ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because the gate of liberation of emptiness is ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
Why is it that because the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the gate of liberation of emptiness has no thing that can be expressed, it is inexpressible; because the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness have no thing that can be expressed, they are inexpressible. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said,
“Subhūti! Because the ten stages of a bodhisattva are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because the ten stages of a bodhisattva are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
"The ten stages of a bodhisattva are ineffable because there is nothing that can be expressed; it is by virtue of this that the *prajñāpāramitā* is pure.

Thus spoke the Buddha in the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, Scroll 294, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by imperial decree, in the first division, Chapter Thirty-Seven, Part Four, "Explaining the Characteristics of Prajñā": "Subhūti!..."
Because the five eyes are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the six supernormal powers are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure.

Why is it that because the five eyes are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
Why is it that because the six supernormal powers are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the five eyes have no thing that can be described, they are ineffable; because the six supernormal powers have no thing that can be described, they are ineffable. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the ten powers of a buddha are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because the ten powers of a Buddha are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
Why is it that because the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the ten powers of a Buddha have no basis for verbal expression, they are ineffable; because the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, have no basis for verbal expression, they are ineffable. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!
Because the quality of non-forgetfulness is ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the state of constant equanimity is ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because the quality of non-forgetfulness is ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
Why is it that because the state of constant abiding in equanimity is ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! The quality of non-forgetfulness is ineffable because there is no phenomenon to be expressed; the state of constant equanimity is ineffable because there is no phenomenon to be expressed. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because omniscience (sarvajñatā) is ineffable, the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) is pure; because the knowledge of the aspects of the path (mārgākārajñatā) and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā) are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) is ineffable, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure?
Why is it that because the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because omniscience has no phenomenon that can be expressed, it is ineffable; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects have no phenomenon that can be expressed, they are ineffable. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said:
“Subhūti, because all dhāraṇī-doors are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because all samādhi-doors are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because all dhāraṇī-doors are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
Why is it that because all samādhi-doors are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! All dhāraṇī-doors are ineffable because there is nothing that can be expressed; all samādhi-doors are ineffable because there is nothing that can be expressed. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!
Because the fruit of stream-entry is ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“Bhagavān, why is it that because the fruit of stream-entry is ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
Why is it that because the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are ineffable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the fruit of stream-entry has no phenomenon that can be expressed, it is inexpressible; because the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship have no phenomena that can be expressed, they are inexpressible. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said,
“Subhūti! Because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is inexpressible, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”

“Subhūti! Because all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas involve no phenomenon that can be expressed, they are inexpressible; it is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”

Why is it that because form (*rūpa*) is unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure?
Why is it that because feeling (*vedanā*), perception (*saṃjñā*), formations (*saṃskāra*), and consciousness (*vijñāna*) are unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Form is unattainable because there is no entity to be found; feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are unattainable because there is no entity to be found. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

Because the sense base of the eye is unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because the eye-base (*cakṣur-āyatana*) is unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure?
Why is it that because the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-bases (*śrotra-, ghrāṇa-, jihvā-, kāya-, mana-āyatana*) are unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the eye-base cannot be apprehended due to its non-apprehensibility, it is unapprehendable; because the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases cannot be apprehended due to their non-apprehensibility, they are unapprehendable. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

Because the sphere of form (*rūpāyatana*) is unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena (*śabdāyatana*, *gandhāyatana*, *rasāyatana*, *spraṣṭavyāyatana*, *dharmāyatana*) are unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because the sphere of form (*rūpāyatana*) cannot be apprehended, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure?

Why is it that because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena (*śabdāyatana*, *gandhāyatana*, *rasāyatana*, *spraṣṭavyāyatana*, *dharmāyatana*) cannot be apprehended, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the sphere of form cannot be apprehended as a real entity, it is unapprehendable; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena cannot be apprehended as real entities, they are unapprehendable. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the eye-element is unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because the eye-element is unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
Why is it that because the form-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, are unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the eye-element cannot be apprehended as a real entity, it is unapprehendable; because the form-element, and so on up to the feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, cannot be apprehended as real entities, they are unapprehendable. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the ear-element (*śrotra-dhātu*) cannot be apprehended, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure; because the sound-element (*śabda-dhātu*), the ear-consciousness-element (*śrotra-vijñāna-dhātu*), ear-contact (*śrotra-saṃsparśa*), and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition (*śrotra-saṃsparśa-pratyaya-jātā vedanā*) cannot be apprehended, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because the ear-element is unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
Why is it that because the sound-element, and even the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, are unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the ear-element cannot be apprehended as a real entity, it is unapprehendable; because the sound-element, and even the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, cannot be apprehended as real entities, they are unapprehendable. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said: “Subhūti!

Because the nose element (*ghrāṇadhātu*) cannot be apprehended, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure; because the odor element (*gandhadhātu*), the nose-consciousness element (*ghrāṇavijñānadhātu*), as well as nose-contact (*ghrāṇasparśa*) and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition (*sparśapratyayaja-vedanā*) cannot be apprehended, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because the nose element (*ghrāṇadhātu*) is unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure?

Why is it that because the odor element (*gandhadhātu*) and even all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition (*ghrāṇasamsparśapratyayaja-vedanā*) are unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the nose element cannot be apprehended as a real entity, it is unapprehendable; because the odor element, and so forth, up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, cannot be apprehended as real entities, they are unapprehendable. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the tongue element (*jihvā-dhātu*) cannot be apprehended, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure; because the taste element (*rasa-dhātu*), the tongue-consciousness element (*jihvā-vijñāna-dhātu*), tongue-contact (*jihvā-saṃsparśa*), and all feelings (*vedanā*) produced with tongue-contact as a condition cannot be apprehended, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because the tongue element (*jihvā-dhātu*) is unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure?

Why is it that because the taste element (*rasa-dhātu*) and even all feelings (*vedanā*) produced with tongue-contact (*jihvā-saṃsparśa*) as a condition are unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the tongue-element cannot be apprehended due to its non-apprehensibility, it is unapprehendable; because the taste-element, and so forth, up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition cannot be apprehended due to their non-apprehensibility, they are unapprehendable. By this, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the body-element (kāyadhātu) cannot be apprehended, the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) is pure; because the touch-element (spraṣṭavyadhātu), the body-consciousness-element (kāyavijñānadhātu), as well as body-contact (kāyasparśa) and all feelings (vedanā) produced with body-contact as a condition cannot be apprehended, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because the body-element (*kāyadhātu*) is unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure?
Why is it that because the touch-element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*) and even all feelings (*vedanā*) produced with body-touch as a condition are unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the body element (*kāyadhātu*) cannot be apprehended as an entity, it is unapprehendable; because the touch element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*) and even the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with body-contact as a condition cannot be apprehended as entities, they are unapprehendable. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the mind-element (manodhātu) is unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element (manovijñānadhātu), as well as mind-contact (manaḥsaṃsparśa) and the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition are unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because the mind-element (*manodhātu*) is unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure?

Why is it that because the dharma-element (*dharmadhātu*) and even all feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition (*manas-saṃsparśapratyaya-utpanna-vedanā*) are unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the mind-element (manodhātu) has no objective basis to be apprehended, it is unapprehendable; because the dharma-element (dharmadhātu), up to and including the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition, have no objective basis to be apprehended, they are unapprehendable. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

Because the earth element cannot be apprehended, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements cannot be apprehended, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because the earth element is unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
Why is it that because the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the earth element cannot be apprehended due to its lack of any objective basis for apprehension, it is unapprehendable; because the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements cannot be apprehended due to their lack of any objective basis for apprehension, they are unapprehendable. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because ignorance is unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because ignorance is unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
Why is it that because [the links from] formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Ignorance is unattainable because there is no objective basis for its attainment; the formative forces, and so on, up to old age, death, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, are unattainable because there is no objective basis for their attainment. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

Because the perfection of generosity cannot be apprehended, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom cannot be apprehended, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because the perfection of giving cannot be apprehended, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
Why is it that because from the perfection of ethical discipline up to the perfection of wisdom cannot be apprehended, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the perfection of giving has no object that can be apprehended, it cannot be apprehended; because the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom have no objects that can be apprehended, they cannot be apprehended. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because internal emptiness is unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom is pure. Because external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, limitless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because internal emptiness is unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
And why is it that because external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the essential nature of non-entities, is unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because internal emptiness has no objective entity that can be apprehended, it is unapprehendable; because external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of non-existence and intrinsic nature, have no objective entity that can be apprehended, they are unapprehendable. By this, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said:

“Subhūti, because true suchness (*tathatā*) cannot be apprehended, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure. Because the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), non-erroneousness, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*) cannot be apprehended, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because true thusness (*tathatā*) cannot be apprehended, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure?
Why is it that because the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), up to the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*), cannot be apprehended, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because true thusness (tathatā) has no object that can be apprehended, it is unapprehendable; because the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), up to the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu), have no objects that can be apprehended, they are unapprehendable. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the noble truth of suffering cannot be apprehended, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path cannot be apprehended, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the noble truth of suffering is unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
How is it that because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the noble truth of suffering has no objective entity that can be apprehended, it is unapprehendable; because the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path have no objective entities that can be apprehended, they are unapprehendable. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the four dhyānas are unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because the four dhyānas are unattainable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
Why is it that because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are unattainable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the four dhyānas have no objective basis that can be apprehended, they are unapprehendable; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions have no objective basis that can be apprehended, they are unapprehendable. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the eight liberations are unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because the eight liberations are unattainable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
Why is it that because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are unattainable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the eight liberations have no objective basis to be apprehended, they are unapprehendable; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases have no objective basis to be apprehended, they are unapprehendable. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the four foundations of mindfulness are unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because the four foundations of mindfulness are unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
Why is it that because the four right endeavors, up to and including the eightfold noble path, are unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the four applications of mindfulness have no objective basis for apprehension, they are unapprehendable; because the four right endeavors up to the eight branches of the noble path have no objective basis for apprehension, they are unapprehendable. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

Because the gate of liberation of emptiness is unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because the gate of liberation of emptiness cannot be apprehended, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
Why is it that because the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness cannot be apprehended, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the gate of liberation of emptiness has no object that can be apprehended, it is unapprehendable; because the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness have no object that can be apprehended, they are unapprehendable. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said,
“Subhūti! Because the ten stages of a bodhisattva cannot be apprehended, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because the ten stages of a bodhisattva are unobtainable, the perfection of wisdom is pure? “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
[Because they are unobtainable.]”
“Because the ten stages of a bodhisattva cannot be apprehended as any real entity, they are unapprehendable; it is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
Because the five eyes are unobtainable, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the six supernormal powers are unobtainable, the perfection of wisdom is pure.
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because the five eyes are unobtainable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
Why is it that because the six supernormal powers are unobtainable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the five eyes have no object that can be apprehended, they cannot be apprehended; because the six supernormal powers have no object that can be apprehended, they cannot be apprehended. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

Because the ten powers of a buddha cannot be apprehended, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha cannot be apprehended, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because the ten powers of a Buddha are unobtainable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
Why is it that because the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, are unobtainable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the ten powers of a Buddha cannot be apprehended as having any objective reality, they are unapprehendable; because the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, cannot be apprehended as having any objective reality, they are unapprehendable. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti,
because the quality of non-forgetfulness is unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the state of constant equanimity is unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because the quality of non-forgetfulness is unattainable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
Why is it that because the state of constant abiding in equanimity is unattainable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the quality of non-forgetfulness has no object that can be apprehended, it is unapprehendable; because the state of constant abiding in equanimity has no object that can be apprehended, it is unapprehendable. By this, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti,

because all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) is non-apprehendable, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure; because the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are non-apprehendable, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because omniscience (*sarvajñatā*) is unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure?
Why is it that because the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti!
