Because omniscience (sarvajñatā) is not an object that can be apprehended, it cannot be apprehended; because the knowledge of the paths (mārgākārajñatā) and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā) are not objects that can be apprehended, they cannot be apprehended. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!
Because all dhāraṇī-doors are unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because all samādhi-doors are unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because all dharani-doors are unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
Why is it that because all samadhi-doors are unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because all dhāraṇī-doors are non-apprehendable due to the non-existence of anything to be apprehended, they are unapprehendable; because all samādhi-doors are non-apprehendable due to the non-existence of anything to be apprehended, they are unapprehendable. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the fruit of stream-entry is unattainable, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are unattainable, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“Bhagavān, how is it that because the fruit of stream-entry is unattainable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
How is it that because the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are unattainable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the fruit of stream-entry is a non-entity that cannot be apprehended, it is unapprehendable; because the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are non-entities that cannot be apprehended, they are unapprehendable. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said: “Subhūti,
because solitary awakening (pratyekabodhi) is unattainable, the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because solitary awakening (pratyekabodhi) is unattainable, the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) is pure? “Subhūti!
"Because there is no objective entity to be attained, Pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is unattainable; it is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.
The Buddha said, "Suvikrāntavikrāmin!"
“Because all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom is pure.
“World-Honored One,
why is it that because all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”
“Subhūti! Because all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas cannot be apprehended as real entities, they are unapprehendable; it is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti, because the unsurpassed,
perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas cannot be apprehended, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas cannot be apprehended, the perfection of wisdom is pure? “Subhūti!
Because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is a non-entity that cannot be apprehended, it is by this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!..."
Because space is ungraspable, the perfection of wisdom is pure.
“World-Honored One,
why is it that because space is ungraspable, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”
“Subhūti! Because space has no objective entity that can be apprehended, it cannot be apprehended; by this, the perfection of wisdom is pure.
Furthermore, Subhūti!”

Because form is neither arising nor ceasing, and neither defiled nor pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are neither arising nor ceasing, and neither defiled nor pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because form is neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
How is it that because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because form is ultimately empty, it is neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are ultimately empty, they are neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the sense base of the eye is neither produced nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are neither produced nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the sense-base of the eye is neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
How is it that because the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the eye-base is ultimately empty, it is neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified; because the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-bases are ultimately empty, they are neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the sphere of form (rūpāyatana) is neither arising nor ceasing, and neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) is pure. Because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena (śabdāyatana, gandhāyatana, rasāyatana, spraṣṭavyāyatana, dharmāyatana) are neither arising nor ceasing, and neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the sphere of form (*rūpāyatana*) is neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure?

And how is it that because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental objects (*śabdāyatana*, *gandhāyatana*, *rasāyatana*, *spraṣṭavyāyatana*, *dharmāyatana*) are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the sphere of form (*rūpāyatana*) is ultimately empty, it is neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena (*dharmāyatana*) are ultimately empty, they are neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure.”
The Buddha said: “Subhūti!

Because the eye-element is neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom is pure. Because the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, and eye-contact, as well as all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the eye-element is neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom is pure?

How is it that because the form-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the eye-element is ultimately empty, it is neither produced nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified; because the form-element, and so on up to the feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, are ultimately empty, they are neither produced nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the ear-element is neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom is pure. Because the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the ear-element is neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?

And how is it that because the sound-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the ear-element is ultimately empty, it is neither produced nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified; because the sound-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, are ultimately empty, they are neither produced nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

Because the nose element (*ghrāṇadhātu*) is neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure. Because the odor element (*gandhadhātu*), the nose-consciousness element (*ghrāṇavijñānadhātu*), as well as nose-contact (*ghrāṇasparśa*) and the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with nose-contact as a condition are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the nose element (*ghrāṇadhātu*) is neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor purified, the *prajñāpāramitā* is pure?

And how is it that because the odor element (*gandhadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor purified, the *prajñāpāramitā* is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the nose element is ultimately empty, it is neither produced nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified; because the odor element and even the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are ultimately empty, they are neither produced nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the tongue element is neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure. Because the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the tongue-element is neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?

How is it that because the taste-element, and so forth, up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the tongue element is ultimately empty, it is neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified; because the taste element, up to and including the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, are ultimately empty, they are neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the body element (*kāyadhātu*) is neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure. Because the touch element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*), the body-consciousness element (*kāyavijñānadhātu*), as well as body-contact (*kāyasparśa*) and all feelings (*vedanā*) produced with body-contact as a condition, are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the body-element (*kāyadhātu*) is neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure?

And how is it that because the element of tangibility (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*)—up to and including the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with body-contact as a condition—is neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the body-element (*kāyadhātu*) is ultimately empty, it is neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure. Because the touch-element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*) and, up to, the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition are ultimately empty, they are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure; by this, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is purified.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the mind-element (*manodhātu*) is neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure. Because the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, and mental contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*), as well as all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the mind-element (*manodhātu*) is neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure, the *prajñāpāramitā* is pure?

How is it that because the dharma-element (*dharmadhātu*), up to and including the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition, are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure, the *prajñāpāramitā* is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the mind-element (*manodhātu*) is ultimately empty, it is neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified; because the dharma-element (*dharmadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition are ultimately empty, they are neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the earth element is neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure. Because the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the earth element is neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure, the *prajñāpāramitā* is pure?
How is it that because the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure, the *prajñāpāramitā* is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the earth element is ultimately empty, it is neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified; because the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are ultimately empty, they are neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because ignorance is neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom is pure. Because volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because ignorance is neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor purified, the *prajñāpāramitā* is pure?

And how is it that because [the links] from volitional formations through old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor purified, the *prajñāpāramitā* is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because ignorance is ultimately empty, it is neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified; because formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are ultimately empty, they are neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the perfection of generosity is neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom is pure. Because the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the perfection of giving is neither arising nor ceasing, and neither defiled nor pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Why is it that because the perfection of ethical discipline up to the perfection of wisdom are neither arising nor ceasing, and neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom is pure? “Subhūti!

Because the perfection of giving is ultimately empty, it is neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor pure; because the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom are ultimately empty, they are neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor pure; by virtue of this, the perfection of wisdom is pure.
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because internal emptiness is neither arising nor ceasing, and neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom is pure. Because external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, emptiness of dispersion, emptiness of non-alteration, essential emptiness, emptiness of self-characteristics, emptiness of common characteristics, emptiness of all phenomena, emptiness of the unapprehendable, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, and emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are neither arising nor ceasing, and neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because internal emptiness is neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure, the *prajñāpāramitā* is pure?

And how is it that from external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence (*abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā*), because they are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure, the *prajñāpāramitā* is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because internal emptiness is ultimate emptiness, it is neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor pure; because external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, is ultimate emptiness, they are neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor pure. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because true suchness (tathatā) is neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) is pure. Because the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm are neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because true thusness is neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
How is it that because the dharma-realm, up to and including the inconceivable realm, is neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because true suchness is ultimately empty, it is neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified; because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm is ultimately empty, it is neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the noble truth of suffering is neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom is pure. Because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!

How is it that because the Noble Truth of Suffering is neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor purified, the Perfection of Wisdom is pure; and how is it that because the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor purified, the Perfection of Wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the noble truth of suffering is ultimately empty, it is neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified; because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are ultimately empty, they are neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the four dhyānas are neither produced nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are neither produced nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the four dhyānas are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
How is it that because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the four dhyānas are ultimately empty, they are neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are ultimately empty, they are neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the eight liberations are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure. Because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!

How is it that because the eight liberations are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure; and how is it that because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the eight liberations are ultimately empty, they are neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor pure; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten pervasive bases are ultimately empty, they are neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor pure. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

Because the four foundations of mindfulness are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom is pure. Because the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the four foundations of mindfulness are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
And how is it that because the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path, are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the four foundations of mindfulness are ultimately empty, they are neither produced nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified; because the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are ultimately empty, they are neither produced nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the gate of liberation of emptiness is neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the gate of liberation of emptiness is neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”
“Why is it that because the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—are neither arising nor ceasing, and neither defiled nor pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure? “Subhūti!

Because the gate of liberation of emptiness is ultimately empty, it is neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor pure; because the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are ultimately empty, they are neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor pure; by this, the perfection of wisdom is purified.
The Buddha said: “Subhūti,
because the ten stages of a bodhisattva are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure, the *prajñāpāramitā* is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the ten stages of a bodhisattva are ultimately empty, they are neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified; it is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 295. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter on Explaining the Characteristics of Prajñā, Thirty-Seventh, Part Five.
The Buddha said: "Subhūti!..."

Because the five eyes are neither produced nor extinguished, neither defiled nor pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the six supernormal powers are neither produced nor extinguished, neither defiled nor pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the five eyes are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
How is it that because the six supernormal powers are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the five eyes are ultimately empty, they are neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor pure; because the six supernormal powers are ultimately empty, they are neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor pure. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the ten powers of a buddha are neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom is pure. Because the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha are neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the ten powers of a Buddha are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure, the *prajñāpāramitā* is pure?

How is it that because the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure, the *prajñāpāramitā* is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the ten powers of a Buddha are ultimately empty, they are neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor pure; because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are ultimately empty, they are neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor pure. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the quality of non-forgetfulness is neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the state of constant abiding in equanimity is neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the quality of non-forgetfulness is neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”
“Why is it that because the state of constant abiding in equanimity is neither arising nor ceasing, and neither defiled nor pure, the *prajñāpāramitā* is pure?

“Subhūti! Because the qualities of non-forgetfulness are ultimately empty, they are neither arising nor ceasing, and neither defiled nor pure; because the state of constant abiding in equanimity is ultimately empty, it is neither arising nor ceasing, and neither defiled nor pure. It is by virtue of this that the *prajñāpāramitā* is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

Because all-knowledge (sarvajñatā) is neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) is pure. Because the knowledge of the aspects of the path (mārgākārajñatā) and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā) are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
Why is it that because all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) is neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure?

Why is it that because the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) is ultimately empty, it is neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified; because the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are ultimately empty, they are neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because all dhāraṇī-doors are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure. Because all samādhi-doors are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because all dhāraṇī-doors are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”
“Because all doors of samādhi are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor purified, is the perfection of wisdom pure?
“Excellent, Subhūti!”

Because all dhāraṇī-doors are ultimately empty, they are neither produced nor extinguished, neither defiled nor pure; because all samādhi-doors are ultimately empty, they are neither produced nor extinguished, neither defiled nor pure; it is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the fruit of stream-entry is neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom is pure. Because the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!

How is it that because the fruit of stream-entry is neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom is pure; and how is it that because the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the fruit of stream-entry is ultimately empty, it is neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified; because the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are ultimately empty, they are neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified. It is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti,
because solitary awakening (pratyekabodhi) is neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure, the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”
“Subhūti! Because the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is ultimately empty, it is neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified; by this, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!
Because all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are neither produced nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because all practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure, the *prajñāpāramitā* is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are ultimately empty, they are neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor pure; it is by virtue of this that the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
The Buddha said:
“Subhūti! Because the unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment of all Buddhas is neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure?”

“Subhūti! Because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is ultimately empty, it is neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified; by this, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because space is neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom is pure.
[Subhūti said: "World-Honored One!"
"How is it that because space is neither produced nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified, the perfection of wisdom is pure?
"Subhūti, because space is ultimately empty, it is neither produced nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified; by virtue of this, the perfection of wisdom is pure."
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

If sons or daughters of good family uphold, recite, contemplate according to the principle, and explain to others this Prajñāpāramitā, these sons or daughters of good family will have no affliction of the six sense faculties and will possess complete limbs and members; their bodies shall not decay, nor shall they suffer premature death; and they will always be reverently surrounded, followed, and protected by immeasurable hundreds of thousands of devas.”
When these sons and daughters of good family recite and proclaim this Prajñāpāramitā on the eighth, fourteenth, and fifteenth days of both the waxing and waning moon,
at that time the Cāturmahārājika devas, the Trāyastriṃśa devas, the Yāma devas, and the Tuṣita devas...
The Heaven of the Thirty-three, the Heaven of Delighting in Emanations, the Heaven of Mastery over Others' Emanations, the Heaven of the Brahma-multitude, the Heaven of the Brahma-assistants,
the Heaven of the Great Brahma Assembly, the Heaven of the Great Brahma, the Heaven of Radiance, the Heaven of Limited Radiance, the Heaven of Immeasurable Radiance,
the Heaven of Utmost Purity of Radiance, the Heaven of Purity, the Heaven of Limited Purity, the Heaven of Immeasurable Purity, and the Heaven of Pervasive Purity.
The Śuddhāvāsa, Vṛhatphala, Parittaśubha, Apramāṇaśubha, Bṛhatphala, Avṛha, Atapa, Sudṛśa, Sudarśana, and Akaniṣṭha devas—
all these hosts of devas gathered together at the place where this Dharma-preacher was, to hear and receive the Prajñāpāramitā.
Much indeed!

These sons and daughters of good family, by reading, reciting, and proclaiming the profound *prajñāpāramitā* within immeasurable great assemblies, shall obtain immeasurable, innumerable, boundless, inconceivable, and unfathomable, supreme merits.
The Buddha said,
"So it is, Subhūti! It is just so."
"So it is! It is just as you have said.

If good sons and good daughters receive, uphold, read, recite, contemplate according to principle, and explain to others this *prajñāpāramitā*, these good sons and good daughters will have no afflictions of the six sense faculties and will be complete in their limbs and members; their bodies will not decay, nor will they meet with untimely death, and they will always be reverently surrounded, followed, and protected by immeasurable hundreds of thousands of devas."

When these sons and daughters of good family read, recite, and proclaim this Prajñāpāramitā on the eighth, fourteenth, and fifteenth days of both the dark and light fortnights, at that time the gods from the Heaven of the Four Great Kings up to the Akaniṣṭha Heaven will all assemble at the place where this Dharma-preacher is, in order to hear and receive the Prajñāpāramitā.

Because these sons and daughters of good family read, recite, and proclaim the profound *prajñāpāramitā* within immeasurable great assemblies, they shall obtain immeasurable, innumerable, boundless, inconceivable, and incomparable, preeminent merits.
"Why is this? Subhūti!
This perfection of wisdom is a great treasure-store; by means of this perfection of wisdom..."

Because it is a great treasury of jewels, it can liberate immeasurable and boundless sentient beings from the great suffering of poverty within the realms of hell-beings, animals, hungry ghosts, humans, and devas;
and it can bestow upon immeasurable and boundless sentient beings the status of great kṣatriya clans, great brāhmaṇa clans, great householder clans, and great lay clans.

They can bestow wealth, nobility, and happiness upon immeasurable and boundless sentient beings; they can bestow wealth, nobility, and happiness upon the gods of the Four Great Kings, the Heaven of the Thirty-three, the Yāma Heaven, the Tuṣita Heaven, the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, and the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven;
and they can bestow [happiness] upon immeasurable and boundless sentient beings in the Brahmakāyika Heaven.
The Heaven [of the Four Great Kings], the Heaven of the Thirty-three, the Yāma Heaven, the Tuṣita Heaven, the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven;
the Brahmakāyika Heaven, the Brahmapurohita Heaven, the Brahmapārṣadya Heaven, the Mahābrahmā Heaven; the Ābhāsvara Heaven, the Parīttābhā Heaven, the Apramāṇābhā Heaven, the Ābhāsvara Heaven;
the Śubhakṛtsna Heaven, the Parīttaśubha Heaven, the Apramāṇaśubha Heaven, the Śubhakṛtsna Heaven; the Bṛhatphala Heaven, the Parīttaśubha Heaven, the Apramāṇaśubha Heaven, the Bṛhatphala Heaven.
The Fruit Heaven (Bṛhatphala), the Heaven Without Affliction (Avṛha), the Heaven Without Heat (Atapa), the Heaven of Excellent Appearance (Sudṛśa), the Heaven of Good Vision (Sudarśana),
and the Heaven of Ultimate Form (Akaniṣṭha) possess wealth, honor, and happiness; they are able to bestow [these] upon immeasurable and boundless sentient beings in the Sphere of Infinite Space,
the Sphere of Infinite Consciousness, the Sphere of Nothingness, and the Sphere of Neither-Perception-nor-Non-perception.
Heavenly wealth, nobility, and happiness can bestow upon immeasurable and boundless sentient beings the wealth,
nobility, and peace of the fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, the fruit of arhatship, and the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha;
it can bestow upon immeasurable and boundless sentient beings the wealth, nobility, and peace of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

"Why is this? Because within this great jewel-treasury of the *prajñāpāramitā*, the ten paths of wholesome action, the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments are extensively explained and revealed; the four [truths] are extensively explained and revealed..."
The foundations of mindfulness, the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment,
the eight branches of the noble path, the three doors of liberation, the eight liberations, the eight spheres of mastery,
the nine successive attainments, the ten totalities, the four noble truths, and the Triple Gem of the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha— these are explained in detail.
He revealed the pāramitās of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, wisdom, skillful means, aspiration, power, and knowledge;
the ten stages of a bodhisattva; all the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas;
and internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, and great [emptiness].
Emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena,
absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of specific characteristics,
the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, and the emptiness of self-nature.
The emptiness of non-existence as intrinsic nature, suchness, the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, non-illusory nature,
non-alteration, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena,
the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm; [these are] extensively explained and revealed as the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
The supernormal powers, the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges,
great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, the quality of non-forgetfulness,
the nature of constant abiding in equanimity, all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, the knowledge of all aspects, and all [phenomena].
The gateways of dhāraṇīs and all the gateways of samādhi—
such immeasurable and great dharma-treasures as these are cultivated and mastered by countless sentient beings who belong to the great clans of kṣatriyas, brahmins, householders, and lay merchants.
Innumerable sentient beings, practicing therein, were reborn as gods of the Four Great Kings up to the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven;
innumerable sentient beings, practicing therein, were reborn as gods of the Brahmakāyika Heaven up to the Akaniṣṭha Heaven;
and innumerable sentient beings, practicing therein, were reborn as gods of the Ākāśānantyāyatana Heaven up to the Naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana Heaven.

In the Heaven of Neither Perception nor Non-Perception, countless sentient beings practice and train therein to attain the fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the fruit of arhatship; countless sentient beings practice and train therein to attain the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha;
and countless sentient beings practice and train therein to enter the bodhisattva’s state of rightness and departure from error.
Birth: Within this, countless sentient beings train and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. Subhūti!
For these reasons, this perfection of wisdom is called a great treasury of jewels.

“Subhūti! Within this great jewel-treasury of the perfection of wisdom, it is not taught that there is even the slightest dharma that arises or ceases, that is defiled or purified, or that is grasped or abandoned.”
Why is this? Because there is not the slightest dharma that can arise or cease, that can be defiled or purified, or that can be grasped or abandoned. "Subhūti!..."

In this great jewel-treasury of the Prajñāpāramitā, it is not taught that there exists any phenomenon that is wholesome or unwholesome, mundane or supramundane, with outflows or without outflows, faulty or faultless, defiled or pure, conditioned or unconditioned.
"Subhūti! For this reason, this Prajñāpāramitā is called the great Dharma-treasury of non-apprehension. Subhūti!"
Within this great jewel-treasury of the Prajñāpāramitā, it is not taught that there is even the slightest phenomenon capable of defilement.
Why is this? Because there is not the slightest phenomenon that can be defiled.
Subhūti! For these reasons, this Prajñāpāramitā is called the great dharma-treasury free from defilement. Subhūti!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they have no such perception, no such discrimination, no such attainment, and no such conceptual proliferation as:
"I am practicing the perfection of wisdom; I am cultivating the perfection of wisdom."

This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) as it truly is, and is also able to draw near to, pay homage to, and serve the Buddhas. From one buddha-field to another buddha-field, they make offerings to, revere, respect, and praise the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones; they travel through the buddha-fields to mature sentient beings and purify buddha-lands, cultivating the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva and swiftly realizing unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

“Subhūti! Thus, this prajñāpāramitā does not lean toward nor turn away from any phenomena; it does not attract nor repel them; it does not grasp nor relinquish them; it is neither arising nor ceasing; it is neither defiled nor pure; it is neither eternal nor annihilated; it is neither identical nor different; it neither comes nor goes; it neither enters nor exits; it neither increases nor decreases.”
Subhūti! Thus, this perfection of wisdom is neither past, nor future, nor present. Subhūti!

In this way, the perfection of wisdom does not transcend the desire realm nor abide in the desire realm; it does not transcend the form realm nor abide in the form realm; it does not transcend the formless realm nor abide in the formless realm.

“Subhūti! Thus, this perfection of wisdom neither gives nor relinquishes the perfection of generosity; it neither gives nor relinquishes the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, wisdom, skillful means, aspiration, power, and knowledge.”

“Subhūti! Thus, this perfection of wisdom neither gives nor relinquishes internal emptiness; it neither gives nor relinquishes external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.”

“Subhūti! Thus, this perfection of wisdom neither gives nor relinquishes suchness; it neither gives nor relinquishes the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), the non-erroneous nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm.”
"Subhūti! Thus, this perfection of wisdom neither bestows nor relinquishes the noble truth of suffering; it neither bestows nor relinquishes the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path."
“Subhūti! Thus, this prajñāpāramitā neither bestows nor relinquishes the four dhyānas; it neither bestows nor relinquishes the four immeasurables or the four formless absorptions.”

“Subhūti! In this way, the perfection of wisdom neither bestows nor relinquishes the eight liberations; it neither bestows nor relinquishes the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, or the ten universal bases.”

“Subhūti! Thus, this perfection of wisdom neither bestows nor relinquishes the four foundations of mindfulness; it neither bestows nor relinquishes the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path.”
“Subhūti! Thus, this perfection of wisdom neither gives nor abandons the gate of liberation of emptiness; it neither gives nor abandons the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.”
“Subhūti! Thus, this perfection of wisdom neither bestows nor relinquishes the ten stages of a bodhisattva. Subhūti!”
"In this way, Subhūti, this perfection of wisdom neither gives nor relinquishes the five eyes, and it neither gives nor relinquishes the six supernormal powers."

In this way, the perfection of wisdom neither gives nor relinquishes the ten powers of a Buddha; it neither gives nor relinquishes the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“Subhūti! Thus, this perfection of wisdom neither bestows nor relinquishes the quality of non-forgetfulness; it neither bestows nor relinquishes the nature of constant equanimity.”
“Subhūti! In this way, the perfection of wisdom neither bestows nor relinquishes all-knowledge; it neither bestows nor relinquishes the knowledge of the paths or the knowledge of all aspects.”
“Subhūti! In this way, the perfection of wisdom neither gives nor relinquishes any of the doors of dhāraṇī; it neither gives nor relinquishes any of the doors of samādhi.”

“Subhūti! In this way, the perfection of wisdom neither bestows nor relinquishes the fruit of stream-entry; it neither bestows nor relinquishes the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, or arhatship.”
“Subhūti! In this way, the perfection of wisdom neither gives nor relinquishes the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha. Subhūti!”
In this way, the perfection of wisdom neither bestows nor relinquishes anything regarding the practices of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas.
"Subhūti! In this way, the perfection of wisdom neither bestows nor relinquishes anything regarding the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas."

“Subhūti! Thus, this perfection of wisdom does not bestow the dharmas of śrāvakas nor does it abandon the dharmas of ordinary beings; it does not bestow the dharmas of pratyekabuddhas nor does it abandon the dharmas of śrāvakas; it does not bestow the dharmas of the Buddhas nor does it abandon the dharmas of pratyekabuddhas; it does not bestow unconditioned (asaṃskṛta) dharmas nor does it abandon conditioned (saṃskṛta) dharmas.”
Why is this so? Subhūti!

Whether a Buddha appears in the world or does not appear, these phenomena (dharmas) are eternally unchanging—the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), the fixedness of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), and the stability of phenomena (dharmanetrī). All Tathāgatas, having fully awakened to and directly realized them, proclaim, reveal, analyze, and clarify them for all sentient beings, causing them to likewise enter into realization and become free from all false imaginings, conceptual discriminations, and inversions.

At that time, immeasurable hundreds of thousands of devaputras dwelling in the sky leaped for joy; they scattered upon the Buddha all kinds of celestial flowers—*utpala*, *padma*, *kumuda*, and *pundarīka*—as well as exquisite fragrant blossoms and various powdered incenses, while exhorting one another with a single voice, saying:
"We now behold in Jambudvīpa the Buddha’s second turning of the sublime Wheel of Dharma."

"In this regard, immeasurable hundreds of thousands of devaputras, upon hearing the teaching of the *prajñāpāramitā*, simultaneously realized the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Venerable Subhūti, saying:
'Such a turning of the wheel of Dharma is neither the first turning nor the second turning.'"
Why is that? Subhūti! This perfection of wisdom appears in the world not for the sake of turning toward all phenomena, nor for the sake of returning from them.
"Why is this? Because they are empty of the self-nature of non-existence.
The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

By virtue of which dharma being empty of its own intrinsic nature (*svabhāva-śūnyatā*), does this *prajñāpāramitā* appear in the world so as neither to turn toward nor to turn back from any phenomena?”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the perfection of wisdom is empty of the intrinsic nature of the perfection of wisdom; because the perfections of meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity—from meditative concentration down to generosity—are empty of the intrinsic nature of those perfections.”

“Subhūti! Because inner emptiness is empty of the nature of inner emptiness, and because outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersal emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, emptiness of all phenomena, emptiness of the unapprehendable, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, and emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are empty of the nature of outer emptiness up to the nature of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.”

“Subhūti! Because suchness is empty of the nature of suchness; because the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-erroneous nature, the unchanging nature, the nature of equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm—indeed, because the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are empty of the nature of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm.”

“Subhūti! The noble truth of suffering is empty of the intrinsic nature of the noble truth of suffering; the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are empty of the intrinsic nature of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path.”

“Subhūti! This is because the four dhyānas are empty of the nature of the four dhyānas; and because the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are empty of the nature of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments.”

“Subhūti! Because the eight liberations are empty of the nature of the eight liberations; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are empty of the nature of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities.”

“Subhūti! Because the four applications of mindfulness are empty of the nature of the four applications of mindfulness; because the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path—from the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path—are empty of the nature of the four right efforts through to the eightfold noble path.”

“Subhūti! Because the gate of liberation of emptiness is empty of the intrinsic nature of the gate of liberation of emptiness; because the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are empty of the intrinsic nature of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.”
“Subhūti! This is because the ten stages of a bodhisattva are empty of the intrinsic nature of the ten stages of a bodhisattva. Subhūti!”

Because the ten powers of a Buddha are empty of the nature of the ten powers of a Buddha; and because the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha—from the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha—are empty of the nature of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“Subhūti! Because the quality of non-forgetfulness is empty of the nature of non-forgetfulness, and because the state of constant equanimity is empty of the nature of constant equanimity. Subhūti!”
Because all-knowledge is empty of the nature of all-knowledge, and because the knowledge of the paths, the knowledge of all aspects, and the nature of the knowledge of all aspects are empty.
"Subhūti! This is because all dhāraṇī-doors are empty of the intrinsic nature of all dhāraṇī-doors, and all samādhi-doors are empty of the intrinsic nature of all samādhi-doors."

"Subhūti! This is because the fruit of stream-entry is empty of the nature of the fruit of stream-entry; and because the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are empty of the nature of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship."
“Subhūti! Because solitary awakening is empty of the nature of solitary awakening. Subhūti!”
Because all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are empty of the intrinsic nature of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
"Subhūti! Because the unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas is empty of the intrinsic nature of the unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas."

“Subhūti! Because all such phenomena are empty of intrinsic nature (*svabhāva-śūnya*), this perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) appears in the world neither for the sake of turning toward nor for the sake of returning from any phenomenon.”
The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
The prajñāpāramitā of the bodhisattva mahāsattva is the great pāramitā, because it realizes that the intrinsic nature of all phenomena is empty.”

Although they have realized that the intrinsic nature of all phenomena is empty, the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas nevertheless, by means of this Prajñāpāramitā, realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, turn the wondrous wheel of Dharma, and deliver immeasurable multitudes.
Although he realizes enlightenment, there is nothing realized, for neither the dharma of realization nor the dharma of non-realization can be apprehended.
Although he turns the wheel of Dharma, there is nothing turned, for neither the turning of the Dharma nor its reversal can be apprehended.
Although one delivers sentient beings, there is nothing delivered, because neither seen nor unseen phenomena can be apprehended.
World-Honored One!
Within this Great Prajñāpāramitā, the turning of the wheel of Dharma is ultimately unapprehendable, because all phenomena are eternally unborn.
Why is this? Because within the dharmas of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, there can be no such thing as turning forward or turning back.
World-Honored One!
Regarding this Prajñāpāramitā, if one can thus proclaim, reveal, analyze, clarify, and make it easy to enter into, this is called the skillful and pure proclamation of the Prajñāpāramitā.

Within this, there is neither a speaker nor a recipient; since there is neither speaker nor recipient, those who could realize [the truth] are likewise unattainable. Because there is no one who realizes, there is also no one who can attain nirvāṇa. Within this well-expounded Dharma of the Prajñāpāramitā, there is also no field of merit, for the giver, the receiver, and the gift are all empty of intrinsic nature.

38. Chapter on the Perfections (Pāramitā-varga), Part One: The First Sub-section of the Chapter on the Perfections, Number Thirty-Eight. At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”
"In this way, this perfection of wisdom is the boundless perfection.
The Buddha said, "So it is!"
"Just as space is without limit, so too,
World-Honored One,
this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of equality."
The Buddha said: "It is so!
Because the nature of all dharmas is equal."
“World-Honored One!
This Prajñāpāramitā is the pāramitā of detachment.
The Buddha said:
"So it is! Because it is ultimately empty.
"World-Honored One!"
"In this way, this perfection of wisdom is a perfection that is difficult to overcome.
The Buddha said, "It is so!"
"Because the nature of all phenomena is unapprehendable.
"World-Honored One!
This Prajñāpāramitā is the trackless pāramitā."
The Buddha said: "It is so! Because it has no name and no substance."
“World-Honored One!
This Prajñāpāramitā is the Pāramitā of space.
The Buddha said:
"So it is! Because inhalation and exhalation are unapprehendable.
"World-Honored One!"
"In this way, this Prajñāpāramitā is an ineffable pāramitā. The Buddha said, "So it is!"
"Because within this, vitarka and vicāra are unattainable.
"World-Honored One!
Thus, this prajñāpāramitā is the nameless pāramitā."
The Buddha said: "It is so!
Because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness cannot be apprehended."
“World-Honored One!
This prajñāpāramitā is the pāramitā of non-practice.
The Buddha said:
"So it is! Because all dharmas have neither coming nor going.
"World-Honored One!"
"In this way, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection that cannot be taken away.
The Buddha said, "It is so!"
"Because all dharmas are ungraspable.
"World-Honored One!
This prajñāpāramitā is the pāramitā of exhaustion."
The Buddha said: "It is so!
Because all dharmas are ultimately exhausted."
“World-Honored One!
This perfection of prajñāpāramitā is the perfection of non-arising and non-ceasing.
The Buddha said:
"So it is! Because all dharmas are without arising or ceasing.
"World-Honored One!"
"In this way, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of non-action.
The Buddha said, "So it is!"
"Because no agent can be apprehended.
"World-Honored One!
This perfection of wisdom is the perfection of non-cognition."
The Buddha said: "It is so! Because those who know cannot be apprehended."
“World-Honored One!
This Prajñāpāramitā is the pāramitā that is without transition.
The Buddha said:
"So it is! Because death and birth cannot be apprehended.
"World-Honored One!"
"In this way, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection that is without loss or destruction.
The Buddha said: "So it is!"
"Because all phenomena are without destruction.
World-Honored One,
this Prajñāpāramitā is the dream-like Pāramitā."
The Buddha said: “It is so!
For all dharmas are like what is seen in a dream and are thus unattainable.”
“World-Honored One!
This Prajñāpāramitā is an echo-like pāramitā.
The Buddha said:
"So it is! Because neither the subject that hears nor the object that is spoken can be apprehended.
"World-Honored One!"
"In this way, this perfection of wisdom is a perfection that is like a reflection. The Buddha said, "So it is!"
"Because all phenomena are like reflections in a bright mirror and are thus unattainable.
"World-Honored One!
This Prajñāpāramitā is the Pāramitā of Illusion and Mirage."
The Buddha said: "It is so!
For all dharmas are like flowing transformations, and their characteristics cannot be apprehended."
“World-Honored One!
This Prajñāpāramitā is thus a pāramitā of illusory transformations.
The Buddha said:
"So it is! All phenomena are like that which is conjured by transformation.
"World-Honored One!"
"In this way, this perfection of wisdom is like the perfection of a city of gandharvas.
The Buddha said, "So it is!"
"Because all phenomena are like a city of Gandharvas.
"World-Honored One!
Thus, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of neither defilement nor purity."
The Buddha said: "So it is!
For the causes of both defilement and purification are unapprehendable."
“World-Honored One!
This Prajñāpāramitā is the pāramitā of non-apprehension.
The Buddha said:
"So it is! Because the basis of all phenomena cannot be apprehended.
"World-Honored One!"
"In this way, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection that is free from conceptual proliferation.
The Buddha said, "So it is!"
"Because it destroys all phenomena of conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*).
World-Honored One!
Thus, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of non-arrogant attachment."
The Buddha said:
"It is so! For it destroys all matters of prideful attachment."
“World-Honored One!
This Prajñāpāramitā is the pāramitā of immovability.
The Buddha said:
"So it is! Because they abide in the dharma-realm.
"World-Honored One!"
"In this way, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of detachment.
The Buddha said, "So it is!"
“Because one awakens to the fact that all phenomena are not false.
“World-Honored One!
This Prajñāpāramitā is the pāramitā of non-arising.”
The Buddha said: "It is so!
Because there is no discrimination regarding all phenomena."
“World-Honored One!
This Prajñāpāramitā is the most profoundly quiescent pāramitā.
The Buddha said:
"So it is! Because one cannot apprehend any characteristic of phenomena.
"World-Honored One!"
"In this way, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of non-attachment.
The Buddha said, "So it is!"
"Because all matters of sensual desire are unattainable.
"World-Honored One!
Thus, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of non-ill will."
The Buddha said: "It is so!
Because it destroys all matters of anger."
“World-Honored One!
This perfection of wisdom is the perfection of non-delusion.
The Buddha said:
"So it is! Because it extinguishes all ignorance and darkness.
"World-Honored One!"
"In this way, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection free from afflictions.
The Buddha said, "So it is!"
"Because it is free from conceptual discrimination. "World-Honored One!
Thus, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection that is free from sentient beings."
The Buddha said: “It is so!
For one penetrates that all sentient beings are non-existent.”
“World-Honored One!
This Prajñāpāramitā is the pāramitā that is without interruption or destruction.
The Buddha said:
"So it is! Because all phenomena are without origination.
"World-Honored One!"
"In this way, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection that is free from the two extremes.
The Buddha said, "So it is!"
"Because it is free from the two extremes.
"World-Honored One!
Thus, this prajñāpāramitā is the prajñāpāramitā that is without confusion or destruction."
The Buddha said: “It is so!
Because one knows that all phenomena are without confusion or destruction.”
“World-Honored One!
This prajñāpāramitā is the pāramitā of non-attachment.
The Buddha said:
"So it is! Because it transcends the stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.
"World-Honored One!"
"In this way, this perfection of wisdom is the non-conceptual perfection of wisdom.
The Buddha said, "So it is!"
"Because all conceptual discriminations are unattainable.
"World-Honored One!
This Prajñāpāramitā is a measureless pāramitā."
The Buddha said: "It is so!
Because the limits of all phenomena cannot be apprehended."
“World-Honored One!
This prajñāpāramitā is the space-like pāramitā.
The Buddha said:
"So it is! Because one penetrates all dharmas without obstruction.
"World-Honored One!"
"In this way, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of impermanence.
The Buddha said, "So it is!"
"Because it can eternally destroy and extinguish all phenomena.
"World-Honored One!
Thus, this Prajñāpāramitā is the Pāramitā of Suffering."
The Buddha said: "It is so!
For it is able to forever expel all dharmas."
“World-Honored One!
This prajñāpāramitā is the pāramitā of selflessness.
The Buddha said:
"So it is! Because there is no attachment to any phenomena.
"World-Honored One!"
"In this way, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of emptiness.
The Buddha said, "So it is!"
"Because one realizes that all phenomena are unattainable.
"World-Honored One!
This Prajñāpāramitā is the formless (animitta) pāramitā."
The Buddha said: “It is so!
Because one realizes that all dharmas have the characteristic of non-arising.”
“World-Honored One!
This perfection of wisdom is the perfection of internal emptiness.
The Buddha said:
"So it is! For one thoroughly understands that internal phenomena are unattainable.
"World-Honored One!"
"In this way, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of external emptiness.
The Buddha said, "So it is!"
“Because one thoroughly realizes that external phenomena are unapprehendable.
“World-Honored One!
This Prajñāpāramitā is the Pāramitā of Internal and External Emptiness.”
The Buddha said: "It is so!
Because internal and external phenomena are found to be ungraspable."
“World-Honored One!
This prajñāpāramitā is the pāramitā of emptiness of emptiness.
The Buddha said:
“So it is! Because the dharma of the emptiness of emptiness cannot be apprehended.
“World-Honored One!”
"In this way, the perfection of wisdom is the perfection of great emptiness.
The Buddha said, "So it is!"
“Because one realizes that the dharma of great emptiness is unapprehendable.
“World-Honored One!
This perfection of wisdom is the perfection of ultimate emptiness.”
The Buddha said: “It is so!
Because the dharmas of ultimate emptiness are ungraspable.”
“World-Honored One!
This perfection of prajñāpāramitā is the perfection of conditioned emptiness.
The Buddha said:
"So it is! Because all conditioned phenomena (*saṃskṛtadharma*) are unattainable.
"World-Honored One!"
"In this way, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of the emptiness of the unconditioned.
The Buddha said, "So it is!"
“Because all unconditioned phenomena (*asaṃskṛtadharma*) are unapprehendable.
“World-Honored One!
This Prajñāpāramitā is the pāramitā of ultimate emptiness (*atyantaśūnyatā*).”
The Buddha said: "It is so!
Because the dharma of ultimate emptiness cannot be apprehended."
“World-Honored One!
This Prajñāpāramitā is the Pāramitā of the Emptiness of Boundlessness.
The Buddha said:
"So it is! Because the dharma of the emptiness of the limitless is unapprehendable.
"World-Honored One!"
"In this way, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of the emptiness of dispersion.
The Buddha said, "So it is!"
“Because all phenomena of emptiness through dispersal (*vibhava-śūnyatā*) are unapprehendable.
“World-Honored One!
Thus, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of the emptiness of non-alteration (*ananyathā-śūnyatā*).”
The Buddha said: "It is so!
Because the unchanging and empty dharmas are unattainable."
“World-Honored One!
This Prajñāpāramitā is the pāramitā of the emptiness of intrinsic nature.
The Buddha said:
"So it is! Because conditioned and unconditioned phenomena are unapprehendable.
"World-Honored One!"
"Thus, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of emptiness of self-characteristics.
The Buddha said, "So it is!"
"Because all phenomena are realized to be devoid of their own characteristics.
"World-Honored One!
Thus, this Prajñāpāramitā is the pāramitā of the emptiness of common characteristics."
The Buddha said: "It is so!
For one has realized that all phenomena are devoid of common characteristics."
“World-Honored One!
This Prajñāpāramitā is the pāramitā of the emptiness of all dharmas.
The Buddha said:
"So it is! Because internal and external phenomena are found to be unobtainable.
"World-Honored One!"
"In this way, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of the emptiness of the unobtainable.
The Buddha said, "So it is!"
“Because the nature of all phenomena is unattainable.
“World-Honored One!
This perfection of wisdom is the perfection of the emptiness of non-existence.”
The Buddha said: "It is so!
Because the dharma of the emptiness of non-nature is unattainable."
“World-Honored One!
This Prajñāpāramitā is the pāramitā of the emptiness of intrinsic nature.
The Buddha said:
"So it is! Because the dharmas that are empty by their own nature cannot be apprehended.
"World-Honored One!"
"In this way, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
The Buddha said, "So it is!"
“Because the dharma of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence cannot be apprehended.
“World-Honored One!
This perfection of wisdom is the perfection of suchness.”
The Buddha said: "It is so!
For one knows that the nature of true thusness (tathatā) is ungraspable."
“World-Honored One!
This Prajñāpāramitā is the Dharmadhātu-pāramitā.
The Buddha said:
"So it is! Because all dharma-realms are unattainable.
"World-Honored One!"
"In this way, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of the dharma-nature.
The Buddha said, "So it is!"
"Because all dharmas are realized as being unattainable.
"World-Honored One!
This perfection of prajñāpāramitā is the perfection of non-falsity."
The Buddha said: "It is so!
Because the nature of non-falsity cannot be apprehended."
“World-Honored One!
This perfection of prajñāpāramitā is the perfection of non-alteration.
The Buddha said:
“So it is! Because an unchanging nature cannot be apprehended.
“World-Honored One!”
"In this way, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of equality. The Buddha said, "So it is!"
"Because equality is realized as being unapprehendable.
"World-Honored One!
This perfection of wisdom is the perfection that is free from the nature of arising."
The Buddha said: "It is so!
For one knows that the nature of arising apart from [conditions] is unattainable."
“World-Honored One!
This prajñāpāramitā is the dharma-dhātu-pāramitā.
The Buddha said:
"So it is! For one thoroughly understands that dharmas are ultimately unattainable.
"World-Honored One! [The interlocutor replied.]
"In this way, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of the abiding of phenomena (dharmasthititā). The Buddha said: "So it is!"
"Because one thoroughly realizes that the abiding of phenomena is unattainable.
"World-Honored One!
This Prajñāpāramitā is the Pāramitā of the Reality Limit (bhūtakoṭi)."
The Buddha said: "It is so!
For the nature of the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) is ultimately ungraspable."
“World-Honored One!
This prajñāpāramitā is the pāramitā of the realm of empty space.
The Buddha said:
"So it is! Because the realm of empty space cannot be apprehended.
"World-Honored One!"
"In this way, the perfection of wisdom is the perfection of the inconceivable realm.
The Buddha said, "So it is!"
“Because the inconceivable realm is unapprehendable.
“World-Honored One!
This perfection of wisdom is the perfection of the Four Noble Truths.”
The Buddha said: "It is so!
For the four noble truths cannot be apprehended."
“World-Honored One!
This perfection of wisdom is the perfection of the four foundations of mindfulness.
The Buddha said:
"So it is! Because body, sensation, mind, and phenomena are unapprehendable.
"World-Honored One!"
"In this way, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of the four right endeavors.
The Buddha said, "So it is!"
“Because wholesome and unwholesome dharmas cannot be apprehended.
“World-Honored One!
This perfection of wisdom is the perfection of the four bases of psychic power.”
The Buddha said: "It is so!
Because the nature of the four bases of psychic power is unattainable."
“World-Honored One!
This prajñāpāramitā is the pāramitā of the five faculties.
The Buddha said:
"So it is! Because the intrinsic nature of the five faculties cannot be apprehended.
"World-Honored One!"
"In this way, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of the five powers.
The Buddha said, "So it is!"
“Because the intrinsic nature of the five powers cannot be apprehended.
“World-Honored One!
This perfection of wisdom is the perfection of the seven factors of enlightenment.”
The Buddha said: "It is so!
Because the nature of the seven factors of enlightenment cannot be apprehended."
“World-Honored One!
This Prajñāpāramitā is the perfection of the eightfold noble path.
The Buddha said:
"So it is! Because the nature of the eight branches of the noble path cannot be apprehended.
"World-Honored One!"
"In this way, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of the gate of liberation that is emptiness.
The Buddha said, "So it is!"
“Because the characteristics of emptiness are unapprehendable due to its being detached from formative activity. “World-Honored One!
Thus, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of the gate of liberation that is signless.”
The Buddha said: “It is so!
Because the characteristics of tranquil conduct cannot be apprehended.”
“World-Honored One!
This Prajñāpāramitā is the pāramitā of the gate of liberation through wishlessness.
The Buddha said:
"So it is! Because the characteristic of wishlessness cannot be apprehended.
"World-Honored One!"
"In this way, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of the eight liberations.
The Buddha said, "So it is!"
“Because the nature of the eight liberations cannot be apprehended.
“World-Honored One!
This perfection of wisdom is the perfection of the eight bases of mastery.”
The Buddha said: “It is so!
For the nature of the eight bases of mastery cannot be apprehended.”
“World-Honored One!
This Prajñāpāramitā is the pāramitā of the nine successive concentrations.
The Buddha said:
"So it is! Because the nature of the nine successive stages of concentration is unattainable.
"World-Honored One!"
"In this way, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of the ten bases of totality.
The Buddha said: "So it is!"
“Because the nature of the ten spheres of totality cannot be apprehended.
“World-Honored One,
this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of giving.”
The Buddha said: "It is so!
Because giving and stinginess are unapprehendable."
“World-Honored One!
This perfection of wisdom is the perfection of ethical discipline.
The Buddha said:
"So it is! Because neither upholding the precepts nor violating the precepts can be apprehended.
"World-Honored One!"
"In this way, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of patience.
The Buddha said, "So it is!"
"Because patience and anger are both unapprehendable.
"World-Honored One!
Thus, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of diligence."
The Buddha said:
"It is so! For diligence and indolence are both unapprehendable."
“World-Honored One!
This perfection of wisdom is the perfection of meditative concentration.
The Buddha said:
"So it is! Because meditative concentration and distraction are both unapprehendable.
"World-Honored One!"
"This Prajñāpāramitā is indeed Prajñāpāramitā. The Buddha said, "So it is!"
“Because wholesome wisdom and unwholesome wisdom are both unapprehendable.
“World-Honored One!
This perfection of wisdom is the perfection of skillful means.”
The Buddha said: “It is so!
Because skillful means and the absence of skillful means are both unapprehendable.”
“World-Honored One!
This perfection of wisdom is the perfection of aspiration.
The Buddha said:
"So it is! Because wishing and non-wishing cannot be apprehended.
"World-Honored One!"
"In this way, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of power.
The Buddha said, "So it is!"
“Because the phenomena of power and lack of power cannot be apprehended.
“World-Honored One!
This Prajñāpāramitā is the Jñānapāramitā (Perfection of Wisdom).”
The Buddha said: “It is so!
Because neither wisdom nor the objects of non-wisdom can be apprehended.”
“World-Honored One!
This Prajñāpāramitā is the pāramitā of the ten stages of the bodhisattva.
The Buddha said:
"So it is! Because the ten stages and the ten obstacles are unapprehendable.
