“Śāriputra! Because the suchness of ignorance is difficult to fathom, the perfection of wisdom is difficult to fathom. Because the suchness of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and aging-and-death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair is difficult to fathom, the perfection of wisdom is difficult to fathom.”

“Śāriputra! Because the suchness (*tathatā*) of the perfection of generosity is difficult to fathom, the perfection of wisdom is difficult to fathom; because the suchness of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom is difficult to fathom, the perfection of wisdom is difficult to fathom.”

“Śāriputra! Because the *tathatā* (suchness) of internal emptiness is difficult to fathom, the *prajñāpāramitā* is difficult to fathom. Because the *tathatā* of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is difficult to fathom, the *prajñāpāramitā* is difficult to fathom.”

“Śāriputra! Because suchness (*tathatā*) is difficult to measure, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is difficult to measure. Because the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm are suchness that is difficult to measure, the perfection of wisdom is difficult to measure.”

“Śāriputra! Because the suchness of the noble truth of suffering is difficult to fathom, the perfection of wisdom is difficult to fathom; because the suchness of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path is difficult to fathom, the perfection of wisdom is difficult to fathom.”

“Śāriputra! Because the suchness of the four dhyānas is difficult to measure, the perfection of wisdom is difficult to measure; because the suchness of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions is difficult to measure, the perfection of wisdom is difficult to measure.”

“Śāriputra! Because the *tathatā* (suchness) of the eight liberations is difficult to fathom, the *prajñāpāramitā* is difficult to fathom; because the *tathatā* of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities is difficult to fathom, the *prajñāpāramitā* is difficult to fathom.”

“Śāriputra! Because the suchness (*tathatā*) of the four foundations of mindfulness is difficult to fathom, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is difficult to fathom; because the suchness of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path is difficult to fathom, the perfection of wisdom is difficult to fathom.”

“Śāriputra! Because the suchness of the gate of liberation of emptiness is difficult to fathom, the perfection of wisdom is difficult to fathom; because the suchness of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness is difficult to fathom, the perfection of wisdom is difficult to fathom.”
“Śāriputra, because the suchness of the ten stages of a bodhisattva is difficult to measure, the perfection of wisdom is difficult to measure.
Śāriputra, [it is for this reason that...]”

Because the suchness of the five eyes is difficult to measure, the perfection of wisdom is difficult to measure; because the suchness of the six supernormal powers is difficult to measure, the perfection of wisdom is difficult to measure.

“Śāriputra! Because the suchness of the Buddha’s ten powers is difficult to fathom, the perfection of wisdom is difficult to fathom. Because the suchness of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is difficult to fathom, the perfection of wisdom is difficult to fathom.”

“Śāriputra! Because the suchness of the quality of non-forgetfulness is difficult to fathom, the perfection of wisdom is difficult to fathom; because the suchness of the state of constant equanimity is difficult to fathom, the perfection of wisdom is difficult to fathom.”

“Śāriputra! Because the *tathatā* of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) is difficult to measure, the *prajñāpāramitā* is difficult to measure; because the *tathatā* of the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) is difficult to measure, the *prajñāpāramitā* is difficult to measure.”

“Śāriputra! Because the suchness (*tathatā*) of all dharanī-doors is difficult to fathom, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is difficult to fathom; because the suchness of all samādhi-doors is difficult to fathom, the perfection of wisdom is difficult to fathom.”

“Śāriputra! Because the reality-limit (tathatā) of the fruit of stream-entry is difficult to measure, the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) is difficult to measure. Because the reality-limit of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship is difficult to measure, the perfection of wisdom is difficult to measure.”
“Śāriputra, because the suchness of pratyekabuddha-awakening is difficult to fathom, the perfection of wisdom is difficult to fathom.
Śāriputra, [it is likewise].”
"Śāriputra, because the *tathatā* (suchness) of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is difficult to fathom, the *prajñāpāramitā* (perfection of wisdom) is difficult to fathom."
"Because the suchness of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is difficult to fathom, the perfection of wisdom is difficult to fathom.
At that time, Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"In this way, the perfection of wisdom is most immeasurable. The Buddha said, "So it is!"

Śāriputra! Because the suchness of form is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable; because the suchness of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.

“Śāriputra! Because the suchness of the eye-base is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable; because the suchness of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.”

“Śāriputra! Because the suchness of the sense base of form is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable; because the suchness of the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.”

“Śāriputra! Because the suchness of the eye-element is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable. Because the suchness of the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.”

“Śāriputra! Because the suchness of the ear-element is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable; because the suchness of the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.”

“Śāriputra! Because the suchness of the nose element is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable; because the suchness of the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.”

“Śāriputra! Because the suchness of the tongue element is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable; because the suchness of the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.”

“Śāriputra! Because the *tathatā* of the body-element (*kāyadhātu*) is immeasurable, the *prajñāpāramitā* is immeasurable; because the *tathatā* of the touch-element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*), the body-consciousness-element (*kāyavijñānadhātu*), as well as body-contact (*kāyasparśa*) and all feelings (*vedanā*) produced with body-contact as a condition, is immeasurable, the *prajñāpāramitā* is immeasurable.”

“Śāriputra! Because the suchness of the mind-element (manodhātu) is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) is immeasurable. Because the suchness of the dharma-element (dharmadhātu), the mind-consciousness-element (manovijñānadhātu), mental contact (manaḥsaṃsparśa), and all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.”

“Śāriputra! Because the suchness of the earth element is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable; because the suchness of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.”

“Śāriputra! Because the suchness of ignorance is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable. Because the suchness of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.”

“Śāriputra! Because the suchness of the perfection of giving is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable; because the suchness of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.”

“Śāriputra! Because the *tathatā* (suchness) of internal emptiness is immeasurable, the *prajñāpāramitā* is immeasurable. Because the *tathatā* of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, emptiness of self-characteristics, emptiness of common characteristics, emptiness of all phenomena, emptiness of the unapprehendable, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, and emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is immeasurable, the *prajñāpāramitā* is immeasurable.”

“Śāriputra! Because suchness is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable. Because the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), the non-erroneous nature, the unchanging nature, the nature of equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm are immeasurable in their suchness, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.”

“Śāriputra! Because the suchness of the noble truth of suffering is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable; because the suchness of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.”

“Śāriputra! Because the suchness of the four dhyānas is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable; because the suchness of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.”

“Śāriputra! Because the suchness of the eight liberations is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable; because the suchness of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.”

“Śāriputra! Because the suchness of the four foundations of mindfulness is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable; because the suchness of the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.”

“Śāriputra! Because the suchness of the gate of liberation of emptiness is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable; because the suchness of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.”
“Śāriputra! Because the suchness (*tathatā*) of the ten stages of the bodhisattva is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is immeasurable. Śāriputra!”

Because the suchness of the five eyes is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable; because the suchness of the six supernormal powers is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.

“Śāriputra! Because the *tathatā* of the Buddha’s ten powers is immeasurable, the *prajñāpāramitā* is immeasurable; because the *tathatā* of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is immeasurable, the *prajñāpāramitā* is immeasurable.”

“Śāriputra! Because the suchness of the quality of non-forgetfulness is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable; because the suchness of the state of constant equanimity is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.”

“Śāriputra! Because the suchness of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is immeasurable; because the suchness of the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.”

“Śāriputra! Because the suchness of all dharanī-doors is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable; because the suchness of all samādhi-doors is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.”

“Śāriputra! Because the reality-limit (tathatā) of the fruit of stream-entry is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable; because the reality-limit of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.”
“Śāriputra, because the suchness of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
Śāriputra, [the same applies to the others].”
Because the *tathatā* (suchness) of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is immeasurable, the *prajñāpāramitā* is immeasurable.
"Śāriputra! Because the *tathatā* of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening of all buddhas is immeasurable, the *prajñāpāramitā* is immeasurable."
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
how does a bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the perfection of wisdom?”
The Buddha said, “Śāriputra!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing that the profound nature of form is [the practice] is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing that the profound nature of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness is [the practice] is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, because the profound nature of form is not form; the profound nature of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is not feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the profound nature of the sense-base of the eye is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the profound nature of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, because the profound nature of the eye-base is not the eye-base; and because the profound nature of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases is not the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the profound nature of the sphere of form is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the profound nature of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, because the profound nature of the sense-base of form is not the sense-base of form; and because the profound natures of the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are not the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing that the profound nature of the eye-element is the practice of the perfection of wisdom; not practicing that the profound nature of the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, because the profound nature of the eye-element is not the eye-element; and because the profound nature of the form-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, is not those various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the profound nature of the ear-element is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the profound nature of the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, the profound nature of the ear-element is not the ear-element; likewise, the profound nature of the sound-element, and even the various sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition, is not the sound-element, nor is it the various sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the profound nature of the nose element is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the profound nature of the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, the profound nature of the nose-element is not the nose-element; the profound nature of the fragrance-element, and even the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, is not the fragrance-element, nor the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the profound nature of the tongue-element is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the profound nature of the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, the profound nature of the tongue-element (*jihvā-dhātu*) is not the tongue-element; the profound nature of the taste-element (*rasa-dhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition is not the taste-element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing that the profound nature of the body-element is the practice of the perfection of wisdom; not practicing that the profound nature of the contact-element, the body-consciousness-element, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, because the profound nature of the body-element (kāyadhātu) is not the body-element itself; and because the profound nature of the contact-element (spraṣṭavyadhātu), up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, is not the contact-element, up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the profound nature of the mind-element (manodhātu) is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the profound nature of the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element (manovijñānadhātu), mental contact (manaḥsaṃsparśa), and the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, the profound nature of the mind-element (manodhātu) is not the mind-element; and because the profound nature of the dharma-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition, is not the dharma-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the profound nature of the earth element is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the profound nature of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, because the profound nature of the earth element is not the earth element; and because the profound natures of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are not the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the profound nature of ignorance is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the profound nature of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, the profound nature of ignorance is not ignorance; likewise, the profound nature of the formations up to old age, death, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair is not the formations up to old age, death, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the profound nature of the perfection of generosity is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the profound nature of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Śāriputra,

it is because the profound nature of the perfection of generosity is not the perfection of generosity, and the profound nature of the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom is not those perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the profound nature of internal emptiness is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the profound nature of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential emptiness, emptiness of self-characteristic, emptiness of common characteristic, emptiness of all phenomena, emptiness of non-apprehensibility, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, and emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, because the profound nature of internal emptiness is not internal emptiness; and because the profound nature of external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, is not external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the profound nature of suchness is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the profound nature of the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-erroneous nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, or the inconceivable realm is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Śāriputra,

because the profound nature of true thusness (tathatā) is not true thusness, and the profound nature of the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), up to the inconceivable realm, is not the realm of phenomena, up to the inconceivable realm.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), not practicing the profound nature of the noble truth of suffering is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the profound nature of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, because the profound nature of the noble truth of suffering is not the noble truth of suffering; and because the profound nature of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path is not the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the profound nature of the four dhyānas is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the profound nature of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, because the profound nature of the four dhyānas is not the four dhyānas; and because the profound nature of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions is not the four immeasurables or the four formless absorptions.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the profound nature of the eight liberations is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the profound nature of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, the profound nature of the eight liberations is not the eight liberations; the profound nature of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities is not the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the profound nature of the four foundations of mindfulness is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the profound nature of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Śāriputra,

because the profound nature of the four foundations of mindfulness is not the four foundations of mindfulness, and the profound nature of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path is not the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path.

"Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the profound nature of the liberation door of emptiness is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the profound nature of the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness is practicing the perfection of wisdom."

Why is this? Śāriputra, the profound nature of the gate of liberation of emptiness is not the gate of liberation of emptiness; the profound nature of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness is not the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.
“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the profound nature of the ten bodhisattva stages is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Śāriputra,
the profound nature of the ten stages of a bodhisattva is, in fact, not the ten stages of a bodhisattva.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the profound nature of the five eyes is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the profound nature of the six supernormal powers is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Śāriputra,
it is because the profound nature of the five eyes is not the five eyes, and the profound nature of the six supernormal powers is not the six supernormal powers.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle Two Hundred and Ninety-eight. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter Thirty-nine on the Merit of Hearing What is Difficult to Hear, Part Three. "Śāriputra!

If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not practice the profound nature of the ten powers of a buddha, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom; if they do not practice the profound nature of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.

Why is this? Śāriputra, because the profound nature of the Buddha’s ten powers is not the Buddha’s ten powers; and because the profound nature of the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, is not the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the profound nature of the quality of non-forgetfulness is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the profound nature of the constant abiding in equanimity is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Śāriputra,

because the profound nature of the quality of non-forgetfulness is not itself the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the profound nature of the state of constant equanimity is not itself the state of constant equanimity.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the profound nature of all-knowledge is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the profound nature of the knowledge of the aspects of the path or the knowledge of all aspects is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, because the profound nature of all-knowledge (sarvajñatā) is not itself all-knowledge; the profound nature of the knowledge of the aspects of the path (mārgākārajñatā) and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā) is not itself the knowledge of the aspects of the path or the knowledge of all aspects.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the profound nature of all dhāraṇī-doors is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the profound nature of all samādhi-doors is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Śāriputra,
because the profound nature of all dhāraṇī-gates is not itself the dhāraṇī-gates, and the profound nature of all samādhi-gates is not itself the samādhi-gates.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the profound nature of the fruit of stream-entry is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the profound nature of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, or arhatship is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, because the profound nature of the fruit of stream-entry is not the fruit of stream-entry; likewise, the profound nature of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship is not the fruit of once-returning, non-returning, or arhatship.
“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the profound nature of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Śāriputra,
the profound nature of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is not, in fact, pratyekabuddha-enlightenment.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the profound nature of any bodhisattva mahāsattva practice is itself the practice of the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Śāriputra,
the profound nature of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is not, in fact, the practice of any bodhisattva-mahāsattva.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the profound nature of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Śāriputra,
the profound nature of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is, in fact, not the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the nature of form as being difficult to fathom is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the nature of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness as being difficult to fathom is practicing the perfection of wisdom."

Why is this? Śāriputra, because the nature of form is difficult to fathom, it is not form; because the nature of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is difficult to fathom, they are not feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the nature of the eye-faculty as being difficult to fathom is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the natures of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-faculties as being difficult to fathom is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, because the immeasurable nature of the eye-base is not the eye-base; and because the immeasurable nature of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases is not the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases.

“Śāriputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the nature of the sphere of form as being difficult to fathom is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the nature of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena as being difficult to fathom is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, because the immeasurable nature of the sense-base of form is not the sense-base of form; and because the immeasurable natures of the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are not the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the incalculable nature of the eye-element is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the incalculable nature of the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, because the nature of the eye-element (cakṣurdhātu) is difficult to measure, it is not the eye-element; and because the nature of the form-element (rūpadhātu), up to and including the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, is difficult to measure, they are not the form-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the incalculable nature of the ear element is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the incalculable nature of the sound element, the ear-consciousness element, ear-contact, and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, because the immeasurable nature of the ear-element is not the ear-element; and because the immeasurable nature of the sound-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, is not the sound-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the incalculable nature of the nose element is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the incalculable nature of the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, the immeasurability of the nature of the nose-element (ghrāṇadhātu) is not the nose-element; the immeasurability of the nature of the odor-element (gandhadhātu), and so forth, up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, is not the odor-element, and so forth, up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the incalculable nature of the tongue-element is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the incalculable nature of the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, because the incalculable nature of the tongue-element is not the tongue-element itself; and because the incalculable nature of the taste-element, up to and including the various sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition, is not those very taste-elements, up to and including the various sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the incalculable nature of the body element is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the incalculable nature of the contact element, the body-consciousness element, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, because the immeasurable nature of the body-element (kāyadhātu) is not the body-element; and because the immeasurable nature of the tangible-object-element (spraṣṭavyadhātu), up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, is not the tangible-object-element, up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the incalculable nature of the mind-element is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the incalculable nature of the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, mental contact, and the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, the nature of the mind-element (manodhātu) that is difficult to measure is not the mind-element; and because the nature of the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition that are difficult to measure is not the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), not practicing the immeasurability of the nature of the earth element is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the immeasurability of the nature of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, because the immeasurable nature of the earth element is not the earth element; and because the immeasurable natures of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are not the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), not practicing the incalculable nature of ignorance is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the incalculable nature of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, the immeasurable nature of ignorance is not itself ignorance; likewise, the immeasurable nature of volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair is not itself those volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the immeasurability of the nature of the perfection of generosity is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the immeasurability of the natures of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Śāriputra,

because the immeasurability of the perfection of generosity is not the perfection of generosity, and likewise, the immeasurability of the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom is not those perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the incalculable nature of internal emptiness is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the incalculable nature of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, emptiness of all phenomena, unapprehendable emptiness, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, and emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, because the unmeasurability of the emptiness of the internal is not itself the emptiness of the internal; and because the unmeasurability of the emptiness of the external, up to and including the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, is not itself the emptiness of the external, up to and including the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the incalculable nature of suchness is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the incalculable nature of the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-illusory nature, unchanging nature, equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, or the inconceivable realm is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, because the unmeasurability of the nature of suchness is not itself suchness; and because the unmeasurability of the dharma-realm, up to and including the inconceivable realm, is not itself the dharma-realm, up to and including the inconceivable realm.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the nature of the noble truth of suffering as being difficult to fathom is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the nature of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as being difficult to fathom is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, because the immeasurability of the noble truth of suffering is not itself the noble truth of suffering; and because the immeasurability of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path is not itself the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the incalculable nature of the four dhyānas is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the incalculable nature of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, because the immeasurability of the four dhyānas is not itself the four dhyānas; and because the immeasurability of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is not itself the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the immeasurability of the nature of the eight liberations is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the immeasurability of the nature of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, because the immeasurable nature of the eight liberations is not the eight liberations; and because the immeasurable nature of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities is not the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, or the ten totalities.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the incalculable nature of the four foundations of mindfulness is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the incalculable nature of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, the nature of the four foundations of mindfulness being unfathomable is not itself the four foundations of mindfulness; likewise, the nature of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path being unfathomable is not itself the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the immeasurable nature of the liberation door of emptiness is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the immeasurable nature of the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, the immeasurable nature of the gate of liberation of emptiness is not itself the gate of liberation of emptiness; likewise, the immeasurable nature of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness is not itself the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the nature of the ten bodhisattva stages that are difficult to fathom is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Śāriputra,
the nature of the ten stages of a bodhisattva is difficult to fathom because it is not, in fact, the ten stages of a bodhisattva.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the unmeasurability of the nature of the five eyes is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the unmeasurability of the nature of the six supernormal powers is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Śāriputra,
because the nature that is difficult to measure by the five eyes is not the five eyes, and the nature that is difficult to measure by the six supernormal powers is not the six supernormal powers.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the incalculable nature of the Buddha’s ten powers is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the incalculable nature of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, because the nature of the Buddha’s ten powers is unfathomable, it is not the Buddha’s ten powers; because the nature of the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, is unfathomable, they are not the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the nature of the dharma of non-forgetfulness as being difficult to fathom is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the nature of constant abiding in equanimity as being difficult to fathom is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Śāriputra,

because the immeasurable nature of the quality of non-forgetfulness is not itself the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the immeasurable nature of the state of constant equanimity is not itself the state of constant equanimity.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the incalculable nature of all-knowledge is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the incalculable nature of the knowledge of the aspects of the path or the knowledge of all aspects is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, because the incalculable nature of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) is not itself all-knowledge; the incalculable nature of the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) is not itself the knowledge of the paths or the knowledge of all aspects. Thus it is.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the nature of the immeasurability of all dhāraṇī-doors is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the nature of the immeasurability of all samādhi-doors is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Śāriputra,
because the immeasurable nature of all dhāraṇī-doors is not itself the dhāraṇī-doors, and the immeasurable nature of all samādhi-doors is not itself the samādhi-doors.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the incalculable nature of the fruit of stream-entry is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the incalculable nature of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, or arhatship is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, because the nature of the fruit of stream-entry is unfathomable, it is not the fruit of stream-entry; because the natures of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are unfathomable, they are not the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, or arhatship.

“Śāriputra! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the perfection of wisdom, does not practice by way of the incalculable nature of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, that is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Śāriputra,
because the nature of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha, which is difficult to measure, is not [itself] the awakening of a pratyekabuddha.
“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the immeasurable nature of all bodhisattva mahāsattva practices is to practice the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Śāriputra,
the nature of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas’ practices that is difficult to fathom is not, in fact, the practice of any bodhisattva-mahāsattva.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the nature of the unsurpassed, perfectly complete enlightenment of all buddhas as being difficult to fathom is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Śāriputra,
the nature of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas, which is immeasurable, is not itself the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the immeasurability of form is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the immeasurability of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness is practicing the perfection of wisdom."
Why is this? Śāriputra,

because the immeasurable nature of form is not form, and the immeasurable nature of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is not feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the immeasurable nature of the eye-base is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the immeasurable nature of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-base is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, because the immeasurable nature of the eye-base is not the eye-base; and because the immeasurable nature of the ear-base, nose-base, tongue-base, body-base, and mind-base is not the ear-base, nose-base, tongue-base, body-base, or mind-base.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the immeasurable nature of the sense-sphere of form is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the immeasurable nature of the sense-spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, because the immeasurable nature of the sense-base of form is not the sense-base of form; and because the immeasurable natures of the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are not the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the immeasurable nature of the eye-element is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the immeasurable nature of the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Śāriputra,

because the immeasurable nature of the eye-element is not the eye-element, and the immeasurable nature of the form-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, is not those various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the immeasurable nature of the ear-element is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the immeasurable nature of the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, the immeasurable nature of the ear-element is not the ear-element; likewise, the immeasurable nature of the sound-element, and even the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, is not the sound-element, nor is it the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the immeasurable nature of the nose element is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the immeasurable nature of the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, the immeasurable nature of the nose-element (*ghrāṇadhātu*) is not the nose-element; and because the immeasurable nature of the fragrance-element (*gandhadhātu*) up to the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition (*ghrāṇasamsparśapratyayaja-vedanā*) is not the fragrance-element up to the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the immeasurable nature of the tongue element is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the immeasurable nature of the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, the immeasurable nature of the tongue-element is not the tongue-element; likewise, the immeasurable nature of the taste-element, up to and including those sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition, is not the taste-element, up to and including those sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the immeasurability of the body-element is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the immeasurability of the touch-element, the body-consciousness-element, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, the immeasurable nature of the body-element (*kāyadhātu*) is not the body-element; likewise, the immeasurable nature of the touch-element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition is not the touch-element up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the immeasurable nature of the mind-element (*manodhātu*) is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the immeasurable nature of the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element (*manovijñānadhātu*), mental contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*), and the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, the immeasurability of the mind-element (manodhātu) is not the mind-element; the immeasurability of the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition is not the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the immeasurability of the earth element is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the immeasurability of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Śāriputra,

because the immeasurable nature of the earth element is not the earth element, and the immeasurable natures of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are not the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the immeasurable nature of ignorance is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the immeasurable nature of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Śāriputra, the immeasurable nature of ignorance is not ignorance;

likewise, the immeasurable nature of the formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair is not the formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair. Therefore, it is so.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the immeasurable nature of the perfection of generosity is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the immeasurable nature of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Śāriputra,

because the immeasurability of the perfection of giving is not the perfection of giving, and the immeasurability of the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom is not the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), not practicing the immeasurability of internal emptiness is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the immeasurability of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, emptiness of all phenomena, unapprehendable emptiness, emptiness of nature, emptiness of intrinsic nature, or emptiness of the nature of non-nature is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Śāriputra,

because the immeasurable nature of internal emptiness is not internal emptiness, and the immeasurable nature of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature is not external emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the immeasurability of *tathatā* (suchness) is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the immeasurability of the *dharmadhātu* (dharma-realm), *dharmatā* (dharma-nature), non-illusory nature, unchanging nature, equality, nature free from birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space, or the inconceivable realm is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Śāriputra,

because the immeasurable nature of true thusness (tathatā) is not true thusness, and because the immeasurable nature of the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), up to the inconceivable realm, is not the realm of phenomena, up to the inconceivable realm.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the immeasurability of the noble truth of suffering is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the immeasurability of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, because the immeasurable nature of the noble truth of suffering is not the noble truth of suffering; and because the immeasurable nature of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path is not the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the nature of the immeasurability of the four dhyānas is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the nature of the immeasurability of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, because the immeasurable nature of the four dhyānas is not the four dhyānas; and because the immeasurable nature of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is not the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the immeasurability of the eight liberations is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the immeasurability of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, or the ten universal bases is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, the immeasurable nature of the eight liberations is not the eight liberations; the immeasurable nature of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities is not the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), not practicing the immeasurable nature of the four foundations of mindfulness is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the immeasurable nature of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, the immeasurability of the four foundations of mindfulness is not the four foundations of mindfulness; the immeasurability of the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path, is not the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the immeasurability of the gate of liberation of emptiness is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the immeasurability of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Śāriputra,

because the immeasurability of the gate of liberation of emptiness is not the gate of liberation of emptiness, and the immeasurability of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness is not the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.
“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the immeasurable nature of the ten bodhisattva stages is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Śāriputra,
the immeasurable nature of the ten stages of a bodhisattva is not, in fact, the ten stages of a bodhisattva.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the immeasurable nature of the five eyes is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the immeasurable nature of the six supernormal powers is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Śāriputra,
because the immeasurable nature of the five eyes is not the five eyes, and the immeasurable nature of the six supernormal powers is not the six supernormal powers.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the immeasurable nature of the ten powers of a buddha is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the immeasurable nature of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Śāriputra,

because the immeasurable nature of the Buddha’s ten powers is not the Buddha’s ten powers, and the immeasurable nature of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is not the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the immeasurability of the quality of non-forgetfulness is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the immeasurability of the quality of constant equanimity is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Śāriputra,

because the immeasurability of the quality of non-forgetfulness is not itself the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the immeasurability of the quality of constant equanimity is not itself the quality of constant equanimity.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the immeasurability of all-knowledge is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the immeasurability of the knowledge of the aspects of the path or the knowledge of all aspects is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, because the immeasurability of all-knowledge is not itself all-knowledge; and because the immeasurability of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects is not itself the knowledge of the paths or the knowledge of all aspects.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the immeasurable nature of all dhāraṇī-doors is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the immeasurable nature of all samādhi-doors is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Śāriputra,
because the immeasurability of all dhāraṇī-gates is not itself all dhāraṇī-gates, and the immeasurability of all samādhi-gates is not itself all samādhi-gates.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, not practicing the immeasurability of the fruit of a stream-enterer is practicing the perfection of wisdom; not practicing the immeasurability of the fruits of a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, because the immeasurable nature of the fruit of stream-entry is not the fruit of stream-entry; and because the immeasurable nature of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship is not the fruit of once-returner, non-returner, or arhatship.

“Śāriputra! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the perfection of wisdom, does not practice the immeasurable nature of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, that is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Śāriputra,
because the immeasurable nature of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is not, in fact, pratyekabuddha-enlightenment.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice the ‘immeasurability-nature’ of all bodhisattva mahāsattva practices, that is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Śāriputra,
because the immeasurable nature of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas' practices is not, in fact, the practice of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not practice the immeasurable nature of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas, that is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Śāriputra, the immeasurable nature of the unsurpassed,
perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is not, in fact, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas.
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

Since this Prajñāpāramitā is so exceedingly profound, immeasurable, difficult to fathom, and difficult to believe and understand, it should not be spoken before those bodhisattvas who have newly begun their training in the Mahāyāna. Lest they, upon hearing this profound Prajñāpāramitā, become startled, terrified, and doubtful, and thus fail to believe and understand it.”

However, it should be taught only before those bodhisattvas who are in the stage of non-retrogression; for when they hear such profound *prajñāpāramitā*, their minds will not be startled, terrified, or afraid, nor will they harbor any doubt. Having heard it, they will believe and understand it, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, contemplate it according to the principle, and explain it to others.
Then, Śakra, the Lord of Devas, asked Śāriputra: "Venerable One,
what fault is there in teaching such profound *prajñāpāramitā* before a beginner bodhisattva who has newly set out in the Mahāyāna?"
Śāriputra said: “Kauśika!

If one were to preach such profound *prajñāpāramitā* before a newly initiated bodhisattva mahāsattva, they would hear it with alarm, terror, and doubt; they would be unable to believe or understand it, or might even give rise to slander. Because of this, they would create and increase karma that leads to rebirth in the evil destinies, sinking into the three miserable realms and remaining for a long time in saṃsāra, making it difficult for them to attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. Therefore, one should not preach the profound *prajñāpāramitā* before such a newly initiated bodhisattva.”
At that time, Śakra, the Lord of Devas, again asked the Venerable Śāriputra: "Virtuous One,

are there any bodhisattva mahāsattvas who have not yet received a prediction [of enlightenment], who, upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught, would not be startled, terrified, or afraid?"
Śāriputra said: “There is, Kauśika!”
This bodhisattva mahāsattva shall before long receive the prediction of great enlightenment. Kausika!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught, their mind is not startled, not terrified, and not afraid, you should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has already received the prediction of unsurpassed great enlightenment.
"Even if they have not yet received it, they will not pass more than one or two Buddhas before they will certainly receive the prediction of great enlightenment.
At that time, the Buddha said to Śāriputra: "So it is!"
"So it is! It is just as you have said, Śāriputra."

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva has long studied the Mahāyāna, long made great vows, long cultivated the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā), long made offerings to the Buddhas, and long served spiritual friends, then upon hearing this profound *prajñāpāramitā* being taught, their mind will not be startled, terrified, or afraid; having heard it, they will believe and understand it, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, contemplate it according to principle, and explain it to others, or practice accordingly as it has been taught to the best of their ability.
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 299 [and 300]. Translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang under Imperial Decree.
The First Division, Chapter Thirty-nine on the Merit of Hearing What is Difficult to Hear, Part Four.
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”
"I now wish to speak of a parable concerning the bodhisattva.
The Buddha said, "Śāriputra!"
"Speak as you wish. Śāriputra said:
"World-Honored One!"

Just as those sons and daughters of good family who abide in the Great Vehicle may, even in their dreams, practice the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, and sit at the site of enlightenment to realize unsurpassed awakening—one should know that these sons and daughters of good family are already close to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; how much more so for a bodhisattva mahāsattva who, seeking unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, practices the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity while awake, yet does not swiftly achieve unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment?
World-Honored One!

This bodhisattva mahāsattva will before long sit beneath the tree of enlightenment, realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, and turn the wondrous wheel of Dharma to deliver immeasurable multitudes.
“World-Honored One!

If good sons and good daughters hear this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, and practice according to the teaching, you should know that these good sons and good daughters have long studied the Mahāyāna, their roots of goodness are matured, they have made offerings to many Buddhas, served many virtuous friends, and planted the foundations of all virtues; thus are they able to accomplish such a feat.”

"Bhagavān! If good sons or good daughters hear this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, and having heard it, believe in and understand it, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, practice it, contemplate it according to the principle, and expound it for others—these good sons and good daughters have either already received the prediction of great enlightenment (*mahābodhi*), or they are close to receiving the prediction of great enlightenment."
World-Honored One!

Such sons and daughters of good family are like bodhisattva-mahāsattvas established in the stage of non-retrogression; they will swiftly attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. Because they have heard this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they are able to believe and understand it with deep conviction, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, contemplate it according to principle, practice in accordance with its teachings, and expound it for others.
“World-Honored One!

It is as if there were a person traveling through a vast wilderness who, after traversing a perilous road for one hundred *yojana*, or two, three, four, or five hundred, sees the preliminary signs of a city or royal capital—such as herdsmen, groves, and fields. Having seen these signs, he then thinks:
‘The city or royal capital is not far from here.’”
Having formed this thought, his body and mind became serene; he feared neither wild beasts, nor evil bandits, nor hunger and thirst.
World-Honored One!

It is the same for all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas: if they hear this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, uphold it, recite it, contemplate it according to principle, and give rise to deep faith and understanding, you should know that before long they shall receive a prediction of enlightenment, or have already received it, and will swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening. These bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have no fear of falling into the stages of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas.
Why is this? Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have already seen, heard, paid homage to, and made offerings to the unsurpassed precursor signs of the profound *prajñāpāramitā*.
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śāriputra, saying: "So it is! So it is!"
"It is as you have said.
Sustained by the Buddha's power, you should speak further.
At that time, Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
It is like a person who wishes to behold the great ocean; traveling toward it gradually over a long period of time, when they do not see mountains or forests, they think to themselves:
‘Now that I see these signs, the great ocean is not far away.’”
"Why is this? Because land near the seashore must gradually slope downward and be devoid of mountains and forests.
At that time, although that person had not yet seen the sea, seeing these proximate signs, he was filled with joy and leaped for gladness.

"Bhagavān! It is likewise for all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas: if they hear this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, receive and uphold it, recite and study it, contemplate it according to the principle, and give rise to deep faith and understanding, then even though these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have not yet received a face-to-face prophecy from a Buddha saying:

'In a future life, after such a number of kalpas—whether after a hundred kalpas, a thousand kalpas, a hundred thousand kalpas, or even after a hundred thousand koṭi-nayuta kalpas—you shall attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.'"
One should know for oneself that the prediction of enlightenment is not far off. Why is this?

Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have already seen, heard, paid homage to, made offerings to, upheld, recited, and reflected upon the profound *prajñāpāramitā*—the precursor signs of unsurpassed bodhi.
“World-Honored One!
It is like the flowering and fruiting trees during the springtime; when their withered leaves have fallen and their branches and twigs are lush and moist, all people who see them say:
‘New flowers, fruits, and leaves will soon emerge.’”
