"Why is this? Because these signs have first appeared upon these trees—new flowers, fruits, and leaves.
Having seen these signs, the men and women, the great and small, of Jambudvīpa were filled with joy and leaped for gladness, all saying:
“World-Honored One! Just as we shall before long behold this profusion of flowers and fruit, so it is with the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas:

if they hear this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, uphold it, recite it, contemplate it according to principle, and give rise to deep faith and understanding, one should know that their roots of goodness from past lives have matured, that they have made many offerings to the Buddhas, and have served many spiritual friends; they shall before long receive the prediction of great enlightenment.”
“World-Honored One!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva should form this thought:
‘I must certainly have possessed superior roots of goodness in the past, capable of drawing forth unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.’”

Now, one should see, hear, revere, and make offerings to the profound *prajñāpāramitā*; one should read, recite, receive, and uphold it; generate deep faith and understanding; contemplate it according to the principle; and practice it to the best of one's ability.
"World-Honored One!
In this assembly there are many sons of gods who have seen past Buddhas preach this Dharma; they all give rise to joy and together deliberate, saying:

'In the past, when Bodhisattvas heard the preaching of the Prajñāpāramitā, they immediately received their predictions [of enlightenment]. Now that these Bodhisattvas have heard this profound Prajñāpāramitā being preached, it is certain that before long they shall receive their prediction of Bodhi.'"

“World-Honored One! It is like a woman who has been pregnant for some time; her body becomes increasingly heavy and her movements become unstable. Her food, drink, and sleep all diminish; she takes no pleasure in much speech and grows weary of her usual activities. Because she suffers from pain, all her affairs suddenly come to a halt.”
World-Honored One, it is just as when a woman who has given birth previously sees these signs and immediately knows that she will give birth before long;

so too, World-Honored One, are the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. Because they have planted roots of goodness in the past, made extensive offerings to the Buddhas, long served virtuous friends, and their roots of goodness have now matured, they are able to hear this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, contemplate it according to the principle, develop deep faith and understanding, and practice it according to their capacity.
World-Honored One!
You should know that by virtue of these causes and conditions, this bodhisattva mahāsattva will before long receive the prediction of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
At that time, the Buddha praised Śāriputra, saying:
“Excellent! Excellent!”
You have skillfully spoken this parable of the bodhisattvas who hear such profound prajñāpāramitā; you should know that this is entirely due to the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas are most wonderful and marvelous; they are well able to entrust the Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and well able to sustain the Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.”
The Buddha said, “So it is, Subhūti!”
"So it is! Why is this? Subhūti!"

The bodhisattva-mahāsattvas seek to attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment for the sake of securing benefit and happiness for many sentient beings, and out of compassion to bring welfare to gods and humans.

When these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the bodhisattva path, they embrace and sustain immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of sentient beings for their benefit by means of the four articles of attraction.
What are the four? First, giving; second, kind speech.
Third is beneficial conduct;
fourth is cooperation.
Furthermore, they establish others so that they may diligently practice the ten paths of wholesome action.

“Subhūti! These bodhisattva mahāsattvas themselves practice the four dhyānas and also teach others to practice the four dhyānas; they themselves practice the four immeasurables and also teach others to practice the four immeasurables; they themselves practice the four formless attainments and also teach others to practice the four formless attainments; they themselves practice the six pāramitās and also teach others to practice the six pāramitās.”

Subhūti! These bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, by relying on the power of skillful means based upon the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), although they instruct sentient beings to realize the fruit of stream-entry (srotāpanna), they do not realize it themselves; although they instruct sentient beings to realize the fruits of once-returner (sakṛdāgāmin), non-returner (anāgāmin), and arhatship, they do not realize them themselves; and although they instruct sentient beings to realize the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, they do not realize it themselves.
“Subhūti! These bodhisattva mahāsattvas personally cultivate the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence,
meditative concentration, and wisdom, and they also exhort immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis [of others to do so].”
Those nayutas of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the pāramitās of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom;
they themselves abide on the stage of non-retrogression and also encourage others to abide on the stage of non-retrogression;
they themselves adorn and purify their buddha-fields and also encourage others to adorn and purify their buddha-fields; they themselves...

They bring sentient beings to maturity and also encourage others to bring sentient beings to maturity; they personally give rise to the supernormal powers of a bodhisattva and also encourage others to give rise to the supernormal powers of a bodhisattva;
they personally cultivate the gates of dhāraṇī and also encourage others to cultivate the gates of dhāraṇī;
they personally cultivate the gates of samādhi and also encourage others to cultivate the gates of samādhi; they themselves possess [the absence of]...
Possessing unimpeded eloquence, they also encourage others to possess unimpeded eloquence; possessing a sublime physical form, they also encourage others to possess a sublime physical form;
possessing all the primary and secondary marks, they also encourage others to possess all the primary and secondary marks;

possessing the conduct of perpetual youth, they also encourage others to possess the conduct of perpetual youth; and practicing the four foundations of mindfulness themselves, they also teach others to practice the four foundations of mindfulness.
Abiding [in this], he himself cultivates the four right efforts and also teaches others to cultivate the four right efforts;

he himself cultivates the four bases of psychic power and also teaches others to cultivate the four bases of psychic power; he himself cultivates the five faculties and also teaches others to cultivate the five faculties;
he himself cultivates the five powers and also teaches others to cultivate the five powers; he himself cultivates the seven factors of enlightenment and also teaches others to cultivate them.
Possessing the seven factors of enlightenment, they themselves practice the eightfold noble path and also teach others to practice the eightfold noble path;
they themselves abide in internal emptiness and also teach others to abide in internal emptiness;

they themselves abide in external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, and absolute emptiness...
They also instruct them to abide in emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature,
the emptiness of self-characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable,
the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, as well as from external emptiness up to the emptiness of non-existence.
Being empty of intrinsic nature, they themselves abide in true suchness (*tathatā*) and also teach others to abide in true suchness; they themselves abide in the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*),
the dharma-nature (*dharmatā*), non-illusory nature, unchanging nature, equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixed nature of dharmas (*dharmaniyāmatā*),
the stability of dharmas (*dharmasthititā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm, and they also teach others [to do so].
Abiding in the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, they themselves abide in the noble truth of suffering and also teach others to abide in the noble truth of suffering;
they themselves abide in the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path and also teach others to abide in the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path;
they themselves cultivate the four dhyānas and also teach others to cultivate the four dhyānas; they themselves cultivate the four...

They themselves cultivate the four immeasurables and also teach others to cultivate the four immeasurables; they themselves cultivate the four formless attainments and also teach others to cultivate the four formless attainments;
they themselves cultivate the eight liberations and also teach others to cultivate the eight liberations;

they themselves cultivate the eight bases of mastery and also teach others to cultivate the eight bases of mastery; they themselves cultivate the nine successive attainments and also teach others [to cultivate] them.
They cultivate the nine successive attainments; they themselves cultivate the ten totalities and also teach others to cultivate the ten totalities;
they themselves cultivate the three gates of liberation and also teach others to cultivate the three gates of liberation;

they themselves cultivate the ten stages of a bodhisattva and also teach others to cultivate the ten stages of a bodhisattva; they themselves cultivate the five eyes and also teach others to cultivate the five eyes.
They personally cultivate the six supernormal powers and also teach others to cultivate the six supernormal powers;

they personally cultivate all doors of dhāraṇī and also teach others to cultivate all doors of dhāraṇī; they personally cultivate all doors of samādhi and also teach others to cultivate all doors of samādhi;
they personally cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha and also teach others to cultivate them.
The Buddha possesses the ten powers; he himself cultivates the four analytical knowledges and also teaches others to cultivate the four analytical knowledges;

he himself cultivates great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity, and also teaches others to cultivate great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity;
he himself cultivates the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha and also teaches others to cultivate them.
Regarding the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha: they themselves cultivate all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) and also teach others to cultivate all-knowledge;

they themselves cultivate the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) and also teach others to cultivate the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects;

they themselves cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness (*asaṃpramoṣadharma*) and the state of constant equanimity (*upekṣā*) and also teach others to cultivate non-forgetfulness... [and so forth].
Having lost the Dharma and abiding in equanimity, they themselves sever all habitual tendencies of affliction and also teach others to sever all habitual tendencies of affliction;
they themselves realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, turn the sublime wheel of Dharma,
and deliver immeasurable multitudes, and they also teach others to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment and to turn the sublime wheel of Dharma.
...and deliver immeasurable multitudes.
The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“How extraordinary!”
World-Honored One! How rare!
Well-Gone One!

These bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, having accomplished such a great mass of merit, practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of benefiting all sentient beings and seek to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
“World-Honored One,
how does a bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the perfection of wisdom so as to swiftly attain its fulfillment?
The Buddha said:

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive form as increasing or decreasing; they do not perceive feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness as increasing or decreasing. This bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing the perfection of wisdom, will swiftly attain its fulfillment.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive an increase or decrease in the sense base of the eye; they do not perceive an increase or decrease in the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind. This bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing the perfection of wisdom, will swiftly attain its fulfillment.”

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, he does not perceive the sphere of form as increasing or decreasing, nor does he perceive the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena as increasing or decreasing, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring the practice of the perfection of wisdom to full completion.”

"Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the eye-element as increasing or decreasing, and do not perceive the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, or the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition as increasing or decreasing, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring the practice of the perfection of wisdom to full completion."

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the ear-element as increasing or decreasing, nor do they perceive the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, or the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition as increasing or decreasing, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring the practice of the perfection of wisdom to fulfillment.”

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do not perceive the increase or decrease of the nose element (ghrāṇadhātu), nor do they perceive the increase or decrease of the odor element (gandhadhātu), the nose-consciousness element (ghrāṇavijñānadhātu), nose-contact (ghrāṇasparśa), or the various feelings (vedanā) produced with nose-contact as a condition; this bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing the perfection of wisdom, will swiftly attain its fulfillment.”

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the tongue element as increasing or decreasing, nor do they perceive the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, or the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition as increasing or decreasing—this bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing the perfection of wisdom, will swiftly attain its fulfillment.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the body element as increasing or decreasing; they do not perceive the tangible object element, the body-consciousness element, body-contact, or the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition as increasing or decreasing. This bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing the perfection of wisdom, will swiftly attain its fulfillment.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the mind-element as increasing or decreasing; nor do they perceive the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, or mental contact, nor the various feelings produced with mental contact as their condition, as increasing or decreasing. This bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing the perfection of wisdom, will swiftly attain its fulfillment.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the earth element as increasing or decreasing; they do not perceive the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements as increasing or decreasing. This bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing the perfection of wisdom, will swiftly attain its fulfillment.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive ignorance as increasing or decreasing; they do not perceive volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, existence, birth, or old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair as increasing or decreasing. This bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing the perfection of wisdom, will swiftly attain its fulfillment.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the perfection of giving as increasing or decreasing; they do not perceive the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom as increasing or decreasing. Such a bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing the perfection of wisdom, will swiftly attain its fulfillment.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive an increase or decrease in internal emptiness; nor do they perceive an increase or decrease in external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, emptiness of all phenomena, emptiness of the unapprehendable, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, or emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence. When this is so, that bodhisattva mahāsattva’s cultivation of the perfection of wisdom will swiftly reach fulfillment.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the increase or decrease of suchness; they do not perceive the increase or decrease of the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, non-falsity, immutability, sameness, the nature of being free from birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, or the inconceivable realm. Such a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom will swiftly attain its full completion.”

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the noble truth of suffering as increasing or decreasing, and do not perceive the noble truths of origin, cessation, or the path as increasing or decreasing, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring the practice of the perfection of wisdom to full completion.”

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the four dhyānas as increasing or decreasing, nor do they perceive the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments as increasing or decreasing, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring the practice of the perfection of wisdom to full completion.”

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the eight liberations as increasing or decreasing, and do not perceive the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, or the ten totalities as increasing or decreasing, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring the practice of the perfection of wisdom to fulfillment.”

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the four applications of mindfulness as increasing or decreasing, and do not perceive the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, or the eightfold noble path as increasing or decreasing, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring the practice of the perfection of wisdom to full completion.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the increase or decrease of the gate of liberation of emptiness, nor do they perceive the increase or decrease of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness. Such a bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing the perfection of wisdom, will swiftly attain its full completion.”

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do not perceive the ten stages (bhūmi) of a bodhisattva as either increasing or decreasing, this bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring the practice of the perfection of wisdom to full completion.”

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the five eyes as increasing or decreasing, nor do they perceive the six supernormal powers as increasing or decreasing, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring the practice of the perfection of wisdom to full completion.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the ten powers of a buddha as increasing or decreasing; they do not perceive the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha as increasing or decreasing. Such a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom will swiftly attain its fulfillment.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the dharma of non-forgetfulness as increasing or decreasing, nor do they perceive the nature of constant equanimity as increasing or decreasing. It is by such means that this bodhisattva mahāsattva swiftly brings the practice of the perfection of wisdom to fulfillment.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive any increase or decrease in all-knowledge (sarvajñatā), nor do they perceive any increase or decrease in the knowledge of the aspects of the path (mārgākārajñatā) or the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā). Such a bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing the perfection of wisdom, will swiftly attain its fulfillment.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive any increase or decrease in any of the dhāraṇī-doors, nor do they perceive any increase or decrease in any of the samādhi-doors; such a bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring the perfection of wisdom to full completion.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the fruit of a stream-enterer as increasing or decreasing; they do not perceive the fruits of a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat as increasing or decreasing. Such a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom will swiftly attain its full completion.”

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the awakening of a pratyekabuddha as either increasing or decreasing, that bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring the practice of the perfection of wisdom to full completion.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not perceive any increase or decrease in the practice of any bodhisattva mahāsattva, that bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring the perfection of wisdom to full completion through their cultivation.”

"Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas as either increasing or decreasing, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring the practice of the perfection of wisdom to full completion."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive this dharma, nor do they perceive non-dharma; they do not perceive the outflowing, nor do they perceive the non-outflowing; they do not perceive the conditioned, nor do they perceive the unconditioned. This bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing the perfection of wisdom, will swiftly attain its fulfillment."

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the past, do not perceive the future, and do not perceive the present; if they do not perceive the wholesome, do not perceive the unwholesome, and do not perceive the indeterminate; if they do not perceive the desire realm, do not perceive the form realm, and do not perceive the formless realm—then this bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring the practice of the perfection of wisdom to full completion.”

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the perfection of giving, nor do they perceive the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring the practice of the perfection of wisdom to full completion.”

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do not perceive internal emptiness, nor do they perceive external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—then this bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring the practice of the perfection of wisdom to full completion.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not perceive true suchness, nor perceive the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, non-falsity, immutability, equality, the nature of transcendence from birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, or the inconceivable realm—then this bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring the practice of the perfection of wisdom to full completion.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the perfection of wisdom, does not perceive the noble truth of suffering, nor perceive the noble truths of origin, cessation, or the path, this bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring the practice of the perfection of wisdom to full completion.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not perceive the four foundations of mindfulness, nor perceive the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, or the eightfold noble path, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring the practice of the perfection of wisdom to full completion.”

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the four dhyānas, nor do they perceive the four immeasurables or the four formless absorptions, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring the practice of the perfection of wisdom to fulfillment.”

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the eight liberations, nor do they perceive the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring the practice of the perfection of wisdom to full completion.”

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the gate of liberation that is emptiness, nor do they perceive the gates of liberation that are signlessness and wishlessness, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring the practice of the perfection of wisdom to full completion.”

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the five eyes nor do they perceive the six supernormal powers, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring the practice of the perfection of wisdom to full completion.”

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive any dhāraṇī-doors and do not perceive any samādhi-doors, this bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring the practice of the perfection of wisdom to full completion.”

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the quality of non-forgetfulness, nor do they perceive the state of constant equanimity, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring the practice of the perfection of wisdom to full completion.”

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive the ten powers of a buddha, nor do they perceive the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha—then this bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring the practice of the perfection of wisdom to full completion.”

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do not perceive all-knowledge (sarvajñatā), nor do they perceive the knowledge of the paths (mārgajñatā) or the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā), then that bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring the practice of the perfection of wisdom to full completion.”
"Why is this so, Subhūti?

Because all dharmas are without the characteristic of intrinsic nature; because they are without activity; because they are unchangeable; because they are false, deceptive, unstable by nature, and lacking self-mastery; because they are without sensation; and because they are devoid of a self, a sentient being, a life-principle, a nourisher, and so forth, up to a knower or a seer."
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
That which the Tathāgata has spoken is inconceivable.”
The Buddha told Subhūti: “So it is! So it is!”
"What the Tathāgata has spoken is inconceivable.

Subhūti! Because form is inconceivable, what the Tathāgata has spoken is inconceivable; because feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are inconceivable, what the Tathāgata has spoken is inconceivable."

“Subhūti! Because the eye-base is inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable; because the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-bases are inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable.”

"Subhūti! Because the sphere of form is inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable."

“Subhūti! Because the eye-element is inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable. Because the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable.”

"Subhūti! Because the ear element is inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable; because the sound element, the ear-consciousness element, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable."

“Subhūti! Because the nose element (*ghrāṇadhātu*) is inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable; because the odor element (*gandhadhātu*), the nose-consciousness element (*ghrāṇavijñānadhātu*), nose-contact (*ghrāṇasparśa*), and all feelings (*vedanā*) produced with nose-contact as a condition are inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable.”

“Subhūti! Because the tongue element is inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable. Because the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable.”

“Subhūti! Because the body-element (kāyadhātu) is inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable; because the touch-element (spraṣṭavyadhātu), the body-consciousness-element (kāyavijñānadhātu), as well as body-contact (kāyasparśa) and all feelings (vedanā) produced with body-contact as a condition are inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable.”

"Subhūti! Because the mind-element (manodhātu) is inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable. Because the dharma-element (dharmadhātu), the mind-consciousness-element (manovijñānadhātu), mental contact (manaḥsaṃsparśa), and all feelings (vedanā) arising with mental contact as condition are inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable."

“Subhūti! Because the earth element is inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable; because the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable.”

“Subhūti! Because ignorance is inconceivable, that which is taught by the Tathāgata is inconceivable; because volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are inconceivable, that which is taught by the Tathāgata is inconceivable.”

“Subhūti! Because the perfection of generosity is inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable; because the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable.”

“Subhūti! Because internal emptiness is inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable. Because external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature are inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable.”

“Subhūti! Because true thusness (*tathatā*) is inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable. Because the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the non-erroneous nature, the unchanging nature, the state of equality, the nature free from arising, the fixedness of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm are inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable.”

“Subhūti! Because the noble truth of suffering is inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable; because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable.”

"Subhūti! Because the four dhyānas are inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable; because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable."

“Subhūti! Because the eight liberations are inconceivable, that which is taught by the Tathāgata is inconceivable; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are inconceivable, that which is taught by the Tathāgata is inconceivable.”

“Subhūti! Because the four foundations of mindfulness are inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable; because the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable.”

“Subhūti! Because the gate of liberation of emptiness is inconceivable, that which is taught by the Tathāgata is inconceivable; because the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are inconceivable, that which is taught by the Tathāgata is inconceivable.”
“Subhūti! Because the ten stages of a bodhisattva are inconceivable, that which is taught by the Tathāgata is inconceivable. Subhūti!”

Because the five eyes are inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable; because the six supernormal powers are inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable.

“Subhūti! Because the ten powers of a Buddha are inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable; because the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable.”

"Subhūti! Because the quality of non-forgetfulness is inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable; because the state of constant equanimity is inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable."

"Subhūti! Because all-knowledge (sarvajñatā) is inconceivable, that which is taught by the Tathāgata is inconceivable; because the knowledge of the paths (mārgākārajñatā) and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā) are inconceivable, that which is taught by the Tathāgata is inconceivable."

"Subhūti! Because all dhāraṇī-doors are inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable; because all samādhi-doors are inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable."

“Subhūti! Because the fruit of stream-entry is inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable; because the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable.”
“Subhūti! Because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable. Subhūti!”
Because the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable.
"Subhūti! Because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas is inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable."

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the perfection of wisdom, does not give rise to the thought of inconceivability regarding form, nor gives rise to the thought of inconceivability regarding feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring the practice of the perfection of wisdom to full completion.”

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not give rise to thoughts of inconceivability regarding the sense base of the eye, nor give rise to thoughts of inconceivability regarding the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring the practice of the perfection of wisdom to fulfillment.”

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not give rise to the notion of inconceivability regarding the sphere of form, nor do they give rise to the notion of inconceivability regarding the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring the practice of the perfection of wisdom to full completion.”

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, he does not give rise to the thought of inconceivability regarding the eye-element, nor does he give rise to the thought of inconceivability regarding the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, or the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly attain the fulfillment of the practice of the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not give rise to the thought of inconceivability regarding the element of the ear, nor do they give rise to the thought of inconceivability regarding the element of sounds, the element of ear-consciousness, ear-contact, or the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly attain the fulfillment of the practice of the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not give rise to the thought of inconceivability regarding the element of the nose, nor do they give rise to the thought of inconceivability regarding the element of odors, the element of nose-consciousness, nose-contact, or the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly attain the fulfillment of the practice of the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not give rise to the thought of inconceivability regarding the tongue element, nor do they give rise to the thought of inconceivability regarding the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, or the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva will quickly attain the fulfillment of the practice of the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not give rise to the thought of inconceivability regarding the body element (*kāyadhātu*), nor do they give rise to the thought of inconceivability regarding the touch element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*), the body-consciousness element (*kāyavijñānadhātu*), body-contact (*kāyasparśa*), or the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with body-contact as a condition, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly attain the fulfillment of the practice of the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not give rise to the thought of inconceivability regarding the mind-element (*manodhātu*), nor do they give rise to the thought of inconceivability regarding the dharma-element (*dharmadhātu*), the mind-consciousness-element (*manovijñānadhātu*), as well as mental contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*) and the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with mental contact as a condition, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring the practice of the perfection of wisdom to full completion.”

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not give rise to the thought of inconceivability regarding the earth element, nor do they give rise to the thought of inconceivability regarding the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring the practice of the perfection of wisdom to fulfillment.”

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not give rise to the thought of inconceivability regarding ignorance; and do not give rise to the thought of inconceivability regarding formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair—then this bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring the practice of the perfection of wisdom to full completion.”
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Volume Three Hundred and One.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree.
Chapter Thirty-Nine, Part Five: The Merit of Hearing What Is Difficult to Hear.

"Subhūti, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they do not give rise to the thought of inconceivability regarding the perfection of generosity, and do not give rise to the thought of inconceivability regarding the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring the practice of the perfection of wisdom to full completion."

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not give rise to thoughts of inconceivability regarding internal emptiness; nor do they give rise to thoughts of inconceivability regarding external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of essential nature, the emptiness of self-characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence. It is by means of this that a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom swiftly attains its fulfillment.”

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not give rise to the thought of inconceivability regarding suchness; and if they do not give rise to the thought of inconceivability regarding the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, non-falsity, immutability, equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, or the inconceivable realm—then this bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring the practice of the perfection of wisdom to full completion.”

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not give rise to the thought of inconceivability regarding the noble truth of suffering, nor do they give rise to the thought of inconceivability regarding the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring the practice of the perfection of wisdom to full completion.”

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not give rise to the thought of inconceivability regarding the four dhyānas, nor do they give rise to the thought of inconceivability regarding the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring the perfection of wisdom to full completion.”

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not give rise to the notion of inconceivability regarding the eight liberations, nor do they give rise to the notion of inconceivability regarding the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, or the ten totalities, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring the practice of the perfection of wisdom to full completion.”

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not give rise to the thought of inconceivability regarding the four foundations of mindfulness; and if they do not give rise to the thought of inconceivability regarding the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path—then this bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring the practice of the perfection of wisdom to full completion.”

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not give rise to the thought of inconceivability regarding the gate of liberation of emptiness, nor do they give rise to the thought of inconceivability regarding the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring the practice of the perfection of wisdom to full completion.”

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not give rise to the thought that the ten stages of a bodhisattva are inconceivable, this bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring the practice of the perfection of wisdom to full completion.”

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not give rise to the thought of inconceivability regarding the five eyes, nor do they give rise to the thought of inconceivability regarding the six supernormal powers, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring the practice of the perfection of wisdom to full completion.”

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not give rise to the thought of inconceivability regarding the ten powers of a buddha, nor do they give rise to the thought of inconceivability regarding the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring the practice of the perfection of wisdom to full completion.”

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not give rise to the thought of inconceivability regarding the quality of non-forgetfulness, nor do they give rise to the thought of inconceivability regarding the nature of constant equanimity, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring the practice of the perfection of wisdom to full completion.”

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not give rise to the thought of inconceivability regarding all-knowledge, nor do they give rise to the thought of inconceivability regarding the knowledge of the paths or the knowledge of all aspects, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring the practice of the perfection of wisdom to full completion.”

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not give rise to the thought of inconceivability regarding any of the doors of dhāraṇī, and do not give rise to the thought of inconceivability regarding any of the doors of samādhi, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly attain the fulfillment of the practice of the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not give rise to the thought of inconceivability regarding the fruit of stream-entry, nor give rise to the thought of inconceivability regarding the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, or arhatship, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring the practice of the perfection of wisdom to fulfillment.”

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not give rise to the thought of inconceivability regarding the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, this bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring the practice of the perfection of wisdom to full completion.”

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not give rise to the thought of inconceivability regarding any of the practices of bodhisattva mahāsattvas, that bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring the practice of the perfection of wisdom to full completion.”

“Subhūti! If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do not give rise to the thought of inconceivability regarding the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas, this bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring the practice of the perfection of wisdom to full completion.”
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
this principle of the profound perfection of wisdom— whom is it possible for them to believe and understand?”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva has long practiced the six pāramitās, has long planted roots of goodness, has made offerings to many buddhas, and has served many virtuous friends, such a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to believe and understand this profound prajñāpāramitā.”
The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!

To what extent should it be known that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has long practiced the six pāramitās, has long planted roots of goodness, has already made offerings to many buddhas, and has already served many virtuous friends?"
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not engage in conceptualization regarding form, nor do they engage in conceptualization regarding feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.”

One does not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the characteristics of form; one does not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the characteristics of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.

One does not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the nature of form; one does not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the nature of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.
Why is this? Because form, up to and including consciousness, is inconceivable. Subhūti!

Based on this, it should be known that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has long practiced the six pāramitās, long planted roots of virtue, long made offerings to many buddhas, and long served many spiritual friends.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not engage in discursive thought or conceptualization regarding the sense base of the eye; they do not engage in discursive thought or conceptualization regarding the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind.

They do not engage in discursive thought or conceptualization regarding the characteristics of the sense base of the eye; they do not engage in discursive thought or conceptualization regarding the characteristics of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind.”
One does not contemplate or differentiate the nature of the eye-base; one does not contemplate or differentiate the nature of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-bases. Why is this?
"Subhūti, because the sense base of the eye up to the sense base of the mind are inconceivable,

one should know that to this extent a bodhisattva mahāsattva has long practiced the six perfections, has long planted roots of virtue, has made offerings to many buddhas, and has served many spiritual friends."

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not engage in conceptualization regarding the sphere of form; they do not engage in conceptualization regarding the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena.

They do not engage in conceptualization regarding the characteristics of the sphere of form; they do not engage in conceptualization regarding the characteristics of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena.”

One does not engage in discursive thought or conceptualization regarding the nature of the sense-base of form; one does not engage in discursive thought or conceptualization regarding the nature of the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena. Why is this?
Because the sense base of form, up to and including the sense base of mental phenomena, is inconceivable. Subhūti!

To this extent it should be known that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has long practiced the six perfections, has long planted roots of virtue, has already made offerings to many Buddhas, and has already served many spiritual friends.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the eye-element; they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, or the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.

They do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the characteristics of the eye-element, nor do they engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the characteristics of the form-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.”

One does not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the nature of the eye-element, nor does one engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the nature of the form-element, up to and including the nature of the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition. Why is this?
Subhūti, because the eye-element, and so forth, up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, are inconceivable; by this much,

it should be known that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has long practiced the six pāramitās, has long planted roots of goodness, has made offerings to many Buddhas, and has served many spiritual friends.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the ear-element, the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, or the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition;

they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the characteristics of the ear-element, nor the characteristics of the sound-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition.”

One does not contemplate or differentiate the nature of the ear-element, nor does one contemplate or differentiate the nature of the sound-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition. Why is this?
Subhūti, because the ear-element and even all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are inconceivable,

you should know that up to this point, such a bodhisattva mahāsattva has long practiced the six pāramitās, has long planted roots of goodness, has made offerings to many buddhas, and has served many virtuous friends.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the nose element; they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, or the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition.

They do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the characteristics of the nose element, nor do they engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the characteristics of the odor element, up to and including the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition.”

One does not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the nature of the nose element, nor does one engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the nature of the fragrance element, up to and including the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition. Why is this?
"Subhūti, because the nose element, and so on up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, are inconceivable; by this much, Subhūti,

it should be known that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has long practiced the six pāramitās, has long planted roots of goodness, has made offerings to many Buddhas, and has served many spiritual friends."

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the tongue element; they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, or the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition.

They do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the characteristics of the tongue element; they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the characteristics of the taste element, up to and including the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition.”

One does not conceptualize or discriminate the nature of the tongue-element, nor does one conceptualize or discriminate the nature of the taste-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition. Why is this?
"Subhūti, because the tongue element and even the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are inconceivable,

you should know that a bodhisattva mahāsattva who reaches this point has long practiced the six pāramitās, has long planted roots of goodness, has made offerings to many Buddhas, and has served many virtuous friends."

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the body element; they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the tangible object element, the body-consciousness element, body-contact, or the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition.

They do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the characteristics of the body element, nor do they engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the characteristics of the tangible object element, up to and including the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition.”

One does not conceptualize or discriminate the nature of the body-element, nor does one conceptualize or discriminate the nature of the touch-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition. Why is this?
"Subhūti, because the body element, up to and including the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition,

are inconceivable, it should be known that a bodhisattva mahāsattva has, to this extent, long practiced the six pāramitās, long planted roots of virtue, made offerings to many buddhas, and served many spiritual friends."

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not engage in conceptualization regarding the mental faculty (manodhātu), nor do they engage in conceptualization regarding the phenomena-object faculty (dharmadhātu), the mental-consciousness faculty (manovijñānadhātu), mental contact (manaḥsaṃsparśa), or the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition;

they do not engage in conceptualization regarding the characteristics of the mental faculty, nor do they engage in conceptualization regarding the characteristics of the phenomena-object faculty up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition.”

One does not conceptualize or discriminate the nature of the mental faculty (*manodhātu*), nor does one conceptualize or discriminate the nature of the phenomena-object (*dharmadhātu*) up to the various feelings produced with mental contact as condition. Why is this?
Subhūti, because the mental faculty, up to and including the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition,

are inconceivable, you should know that a bodhisattva mahāsattva has, to this extent, long practiced the six pāramitās, long planted roots of goodness, long made offerings to many Buddhas, and long served many virtuous friends.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the earth element; they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements.

They do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the characteristics of the earth element; they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the characteristics of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements.”
One does not conceptually discriminate the nature of the earth element, nor does one conceptually discriminate the nature of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements. Why is this?
Because the earth element up to the consciousness element are inconceivable,

Subhūti! To this extent it should be known that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has long practiced the six pāramitās, has long planted roots of goodness, has already made offerings to many Buddhas, and has already served many spiritual friends.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding ignorance; they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, or aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.

They do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the characteristics of ignorance, nor do they engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the characteristics of volitional formations up to aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.”

One does not conceptualize or discriminate regarding the nature of ignorance; one does not conceptualize or discriminate regarding the nature of volitional formations, up to and including old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair. Why is this?
"Subhūti, because ignorance up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are inconceivable,

you should know that to this extent a bodhisattva mahāsattva has long practiced the six pāramitās, has long planted roots of goodness, has already made offerings to many Buddhas, and has already served many virtuous friends."

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not engage in discursive thought or conceptualization regarding the desire realm; they do not engage in discursive thought or conceptualization regarding the form realm or the formless realm.

They do not engage in discursive thought or conceptualization regarding the characteristics of the desire realm; they do not engage in discursive thought or conceptualization regarding the characteristics of the form realm or the formless realm.”

One does not engage in discursive thought or conceptualization regarding the nature of the desire realm, nor does one engage in discursive thought or conceptualization regarding the nature of the form and formless realms. Why is this?
Because the desire realm, the form realm, and the formless realm are inconceivable.

“Subhūti! To this extent it should be known that these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have long practiced the six pāramitās, have long planted roots of goodness, have already made offerings to many buddhas, and have already served many spiritual friends.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the perfection of generosity; they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom;

nor do they engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the characteristics of the perfection of generosity, nor the characteristics of the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom.”

One does not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the nature of the perfection of generosity, nor does one engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the nature of the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom.
Why is this? Because the perfection of generosity up to the perfection of wisdom are inconceivable, Subhūti.

Based on this, it should be known that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has long practiced the six pāramitās, long planted roots of virtue, long made offerings to many buddhas, and long served many spiritual friends.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding internal emptiness; they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

They do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the characteristic of internal emptiness, nor do they engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the characteristics of external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.”

One does not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding internal emptiness, nor does one engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the nature of non-existence.
Why is this? Because internal emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the nature of non-existence, is inconceivable.

"Subhūti! To this extent, it should be known that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has long practiced the six pāramitās, has long planted roots of goodness, has already made offerings to many buddhas, and has already served many spiritual friends."

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding suchness; they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-erroneous nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, or the inconceivable realm;
nor do they engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the characteristics of suchness, or the characteristics of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm.”

One does not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the nature of suchness, nor does one engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the nature of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm. Why is this?
Because suchness up to the inconceivable realm is itself inconceivable.

"Subhūti! To this extent, it should be known that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has long practiced the six pāramitās, has long planted roots of goodness, has already made offerings to many buddhas, and has already served many virtuous friends."

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the noble truth of suffering; they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the noble truths of origin, cessation, or the path.

They do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the characteristics of the noble truth of suffering; they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the characteristics of the noble truths of origin, cessation, or the path.”

One does not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the nature of the noble truth of suffering, nor does one engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the nature of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path. Why is this?
Because the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path are inconceivable.

"Subhūti! To this extent, it should be known that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has long practiced the six pāramitās, has long planted roots of goodness, has already made offerings to many buddhas, and has already served many virtuous friends."

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the four dhyānas; they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments;

they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the characteristics of the four dhyānas; and they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the characteristics of the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments.”

One does not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the nature of the four dhyānas, nor does one engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the nature of the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments. Why is this?
Because the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments are inconceivable.

"Subhūti! To this extent, it should be known that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has long practiced the six pāramitās, has long planted roots of goodness, has made offerings to many buddhas, and has served many spiritual friends."

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the eight liberations; they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities.

They do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the characteristics of the eight liberations; they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the characteristics of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities.”

One does not conceptualize or discriminate the nature of the eight liberations; one does not conceptualize or discriminate the nature of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities. Why is this?
Because the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative absorptions, and the ten totalities are inconceivable. Subhūti,

by this you should know that these bodhisattva mahāsattvas have long practiced the six pāramitās, have long planted roots of virtue, have made offerings to many buddhas, and have served many spiritual friends.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the four foundations of mindfulness; they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path;

nor do they engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the characteristics of the four foundations of mindfulness, nor do they engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the characteristics of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path.”

One does not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the nature of the four foundations of mindfulness, nor does one engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the nature of the four right efforts up to the eight branches of the noble path. Why is this?
Subhūti, because the four applications of mindfulness up to the eight branches of the noble path are inconceivable,

one should know that a bodhisattva mahāsattva has, to this extent, long practiced the six perfections, long planted roots of virtue, long made offerings to many buddhas, and long served many spiritual friends.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the liberation door of emptiness; they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness.

They do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the characteristics of the liberation door of emptiness; they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the characteristics of the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness.”

One does not conceptualize or discriminate the nature of the emptiness liberation door, nor does one conceptualize or discriminate the nature of the signlessness or wishlessness liberation doors. Why is this?
Because the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness are inconceivable. Subhūti!

To this extent, it should be known that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has long practiced the six pāramitās, has long planted roots of goodness, has already made offerings to many buddhas, and has already served many virtuous friends.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not engage in conceptualization regarding the ten stages of a bodhisattva; they do not engage in conceptualization regarding the characteristics of the ten stages of a bodhisattva; they do not engage in conceptualization regarding the nature of the ten stages of a bodhisattva.”
Why is this? Because the ten stages of a bodhisattva are inconceivable, Subhūti!

Based on this, one should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has long practiced the six pāramitās, has long planted roots of virtue, has already made offerings to many buddhas, and has already served many spiritual friends.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the five eyes, nor do they engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the six supernormal powers;

they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the characteristics of the five eyes, nor do they engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the characteristics of the six supernormal powers.”
