One does not engage in conceptualization regarding the nature of the five eyes, nor does one engage in conceptualization regarding the nature of the six supernormal powers. Why is this?
Because the five eyes and the six supernormal powers are inconceivable.

Subhūti! To this extent, it should be known that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has long practiced the six pāramitās, has long planted roots of goodness, has already made offerings to many buddhas, and has already served many spiritual friends.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the ten powers of a buddha; they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha.

They do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the characteristics of the ten powers of a buddha, nor do they engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the characteristics of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha.”

One does not engage in conceptualization regarding the nature of the ten powers of a Buddha, nor does one engage in conceptualization regarding the nature of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha. Why is this?
Because the ten powers of a Buddha, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, are inconceivable. Subhūti,

by this you should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has long practiced the six perfections, has long planted roots of goodness, has already made offerings to many Buddhas, and has already served many virtuous friends.

"Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the qualities of non-forgetfulness, nor do they engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the nature of constant equanimity;

they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the marks of the qualities of non-forgetfulness, nor do they engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the marks of the nature of constant equanimity."

One does not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the nature of the quality of non-forgetfulness, nor does one engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the nature of the constant abiding in equanimity. Why is this?
Because the quality of non-forgetfulness and the constant abiding in equanimity are inconceivable.

"Subhūti! To this extent, it should be known that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has long practiced the six pāramitās, has long planted roots of virtue, has made offerings to many buddhas, and has served many spiritual friends."

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not engage in conceptualization regarding all-knowledge; they do not engage in conceptualization regarding the knowledge of the paths or the knowledge of all aspects.

They do not engage in conceptualization regarding the characteristics of all-knowledge; they do not engage in conceptualization regarding the characteristics of the knowledge of the paths or the knowledge of all aspects.”

One does not engage in discursive thought regarding the nature of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), nor does one engage in discursive thought regarding the nature of the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*) or the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*). Why is this?
Because all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects are inconceivable.

"Subhūti! To this extent, it should be known that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has long practiced the six pāramitās, has long planted roots of virtue, has made offerings to many buddhas, and has served many spiritual friends."

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not engage in conceptualization regarding any of the doors of dhāraṇī, nor do they engage in conceptualization regarding any of the doors of samādhi;

they do not engage in conceptualization regarding the characteristics of any of the doors of dhāraṇī, nor do they engage in conceptualization regarding the characteristics of any of the doors of samādhi.”

One does not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the nature of all dharanī-gates, nor does one engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the nature of all samādhi-gates. Why is this?
Because all doors of dhāraṇī and all doors of samādhi are inconceivable. Subhūti!

To this extent, it should be known that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has long practiced the six pāramitās, has long planted roots of goodness, has already made offerings to many Buddhas, and has already served many virtuous friends.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, he does not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the fruit of a stream-enterer; he does not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the fruits of a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat.

He does not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the characteristics of the fruit of a stream-enterer; he does not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the characteristics of the fruits of a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat.”

One does not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the nature of the fruit of stream-entry, nor does one engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the nature of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, or arhatship. Why is this?
Because the fruits of stream-entry, once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are inconceivable. Subhūti!

To this extent, it should be known that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has long practiced the six pāramitās, has long planted roots of goodness, has already made offerings to many buddhas, and has already served many virtuous friends.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha; they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the marks of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha; they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the nature of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha.”
Why is this? Because the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is inconceivable, Subhūti!

Based on this, it should be known that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has long practiced the six pāramitās, has long planted roots of virtue, has already made offerings to many buddhas, and has already served many spiritual friends.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding any bodhisattva mahāsattva practice; they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the characteristics of any bodhisattva mahāsattva practice; they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the nature of any bodhisattva mahāsattva practice.”
Why is this? Because the practice of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is inconceivable. Subhūti!

Based on this, it should be known that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has long practiced the six pāramitās, has long planted roots of virtue, has already made offerings to many buddhas, and has already served many spiritual friends.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas; they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the characteristics of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas; and they do not engage in conceptualization or discrimination regarding the nature of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas.”
Why is this? Because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is inconceivable, Subhūti!

Based on this, it should be known that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has long practiced the six pāramitās, long planted roots of virtue, long made offerings to many buddhas, and long served many spiritual friends.
The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
this Prajñāpāramitā is exceedingly profound.”
The Buddha said, “So it is, Subhūti!”
Because form is profound, the perfection of wisdom is profound; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are profound, the perfection of wisdom is profound.

“Subhūti! Because the sense base of the eye is profound, the perfection of wisdom is profound; because the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are profound, the perfection of wisdom is profound.”

"Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

“Subhūti! Because the quality of non-forgetfulness is profound, the perfection of wisdom is profound; because the state of constant equanimity is profound, the perfection of wisdom is profound.”

"Subhūti! Because all-knowledge is profound, the perfection of wisdom is profound; because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are profound, the perfection of wisdom is profound."
“Subhūti! Because all dhāraṇī-doors are profound, the perfection of wisdom is profound; because all samādhi-doors are profound, the perfection of wisdom is profound.”

“Subhūti! Because the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is profound, the perfection of wisdom is profound. Subhūti!”

"Subhūti! Because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas is profound, the perfection of wisdom is profound."
"Therefore, the Prajñāpāramitā is called exceedingly profound.
The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"In this way, the perfection of wisdom is a great mass of jewels.
The Buddha said, "So it is!"
Because it can bestow upon sentient beings the jewels of merit. "Subhūti!

In this way, the great treasury of jewels that is the perfection of wisdom can bestow upon sentient beings the jewels of the ten paths of wholesome action, the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, and the five superknowledges."

“Subhūti! This great treasury of jewels that is the perfection of wisdom can bestow upon sentient beings the jewels of the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.”

“Subhūti! This great treasure-trove of the perfection of wisdom is able to bestow upon sentient beings the jewels of internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.”

“Subhūti! This great treasure-heap of the perfection of wisdom is able to bestow upon sentient beings the jewels of the noble truths: suchness, the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm.”

“Subhūti! This great treasury of jewels that is the perfection of wisdom can bestow upon sentient beings the jewels of the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities.”

“Subhūti! This great treasury of jewels that is the perfection of wisdom can bestow upon sentient beings the jewels of the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.”
"Subhūti! This great treasury of jewels that is the perfection of wisdom can bestow upon sentient beings the jewels of the gates of liberation: emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness."
“Subhūti! This great treasury of the perfection of wisdom is able to bestow upon sentient beings the jewels of the ten stages of a bodhisattva. Subhūti!”
In this way, the great treasury of jewels that is the perfection of wisdom can bestow upon sentient beings the jewels of the five eyes and the six superknowledges. "Subhūti!

In this way, the great treasury of jewels that is the perfection of wisdom can bestow upon sentient beings the jewels of the Buddha’s ten powers, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha."

“Subhūti! Thus, this great jewel-treasury of the perfection of wisdom can bestow upon sentient beings the jewel of the quality of non-forgetfulness and the jewel of the nature of constant equanimity.”

"Subhūti! This great jewel-treasury of the perfection of wisdom is able to bestow upon sentient beings the jewels of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*)."
"Subhūti! Thus, this great treasury of jewels that is the perfection of wisdom can bestow upon sentient beings all the gateways of dhāraṇī and all the gateways of samādhi."
“Subhūti! This great treasury of jewels that is the perfection of wisdom can bestow upon sentient beings the jewels of the fruits of stream-entry, once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship.”
"Subhūti! This great treasury of jewels that is the perfection of wisdom can bestow upon sentient beings the jewel of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment. Subhūti!"
"Thus, this great treasury of the Perfection of Wisdom is able to bestow upon all sentient beings and all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas the jewel of their practice. Subhūti! "

In this way, this great treasury of jewels that is the perfection of wisdom can bestow upon sentient beings the jewel of the wheel of Dharma of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas.
"Therefore, the Prajñāpāramitā is called a great treasury of jewels.

The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
This Prajñāpāramitā is a collection of purity.
The Buddha said:
"So it is, Subhūti!

“Subhūti! Because the sphere of the eye is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”

“Subhūti! Because the sphere of form is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”

“Subhūti! Because the eye-element is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”

"Subhūti! Because the body element is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the tangible object element, the body-consciousness element, as well as body-contact and the various feelings arisen with body-contact as a condition are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure."

“Subhūti! Because the mind-element (*manodhātu*) is pure, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is pure; because the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element (*manovijñānadhātu*), and the mental contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*), as well as all feelings (*vedanā*) arising with mental contact as condition, are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”
“Subhūti! Because the earth element is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”

“Subhūti! Because ignorance is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”

“Subhūti! Because the perfection of generosity is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, and meditative concentration are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”

“Subhūti! Because internal emptiness is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure. “Subhūti! “Subhūti! Because the noble truth of suffering is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”

“Subhūti! Because the ten stages of the bodhisattva are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure. Subhūti!”
Because the five eyes are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the six supernormal powers are pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure. "Subhūti!

“Subhūti! Because the quality of non-forgetfulness is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure; because the state of constant equanimity is pure, the perfection of wisdom is pure.”

"Therefore, the perfection of wisdom is called a 'mass of purity.
The Venerable Subhūti then addressed the Buddha again, saying:
"How extraordinary!"
World-Honored One! How rare! Sugata!
"Such is the Prajñāpāramitā; because it is extremely profound, there are many obstacles, yet now that it is being extensively taught, no obstacles shall arise.
The Buddha said, "Subhūti!"
"So it is! So it is! This profound *prajñāpāramitā* encounters many obstacles; yet, by the spiritual power of the Buddha, although it is now being extensively expounded, no obstacles shall arise."

Therefore, sons and daughters of good family who belong to the Mahāyāna, if they wish to transcribe this Prajñāpāramitā, they should transcribe it quickly; if they wish to read and recite it, they should read and recite it quickly; if they wish to receive and uphold it, they should receive and uphold it quickly; if they wish to practice it, they should practice it quickly; if they wish to contemplate it, they should contemplate it quickly; and if they wish to proclaim it, they should proclaim it quickly.
Why is this? Subhūti!

There are many obstacles to the profound *prajñāpāramitā*; do not allow such obstructive matters to arise so that those who write it down, recite it, uphold it, cultivate it, contemplate it, or explain it to others may fail to reach completion.

“Subhūti! If these sons and daughters of good family wish to complete the transcription of this profound *prajñāpāramitā* within one month, or two, or three, or four, or five, or six, or seven months, or even for as long as a year, they should transcribe it with diligent effort and focused mindfulness, so that it may be brought to completion within that time.”

Subhūti! If these sons of good family and daughters of good family wish to master this Prajñāpāramitā—whether for one month, or two, or three, or four, or five, or six, or seven, or even for a year—by upholding, reciting, practicing, contemplating, and explaining it to others, they should apply themselves with diligent vigor, maintaining mindfulness while upholding it and so forth until they explain it, so that they may achieve mastery within that time.
Why is this? Subhūti,
it is because the priceless jewel of the profound *prajñāpāramitā* encounters many obstacles.
At that time, Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"How extraordinary!
World-Honored One!"
"How rare! Well-gone One!

This profound *prajñāpāramitā* is like a priceless jewel beset by many obstacles; yet, for those who write it down, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, cultivate it, contemplate it, and explain it to others, Māra will seek to create hindrances, wishing to prevent them from writing it down, up to and including its exposition."
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
Although Māra, the Evil One,

may wish to create obstacles so that this profound *prajñāpāramitā* is not written down, received, upheld, recited, practiced, contemplated, or explained to others, he lacks the power to obstruct this bodhisattva mahāsattva’s activities such as writing down and receiving the *prajñāpāramitā*.
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!

By whose spiritual power is it that those evil Māras are unable to obstruct bodhisattva-mahāsattvas as they write down, receive and uphold, read and recite, practice and cultivate, contemplate, and extensively explain this profound Prajñāpāramitā?"
The Buddha said, “Śāriputra!

It is through the supernatural power of the Buddha that those evil Māras are unable to obstruct or hinder bodhisattva-mahāsattvas as they write down, receive and uphold, read and recite, practice, contemplate, and extensively expound the profound *prajñāpāramitā*.”
Furthermore, Śāriputra!

It is also through the spiritual power of all the Buddhas in the worlds of the ten directions that those evil Māras are unable to obstruct Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas in their writing, upholding, reciting, practicing, contemplating, and extensively explaining the profound Prajñāpāramitā.
Furthermore, Śāriputra!

Because all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, collectively protect and keep in mind those bodhisattvas who practice the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), they ensure that those evil Māras cannot obstruct any of the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, preventing them from copying, upholding, reciting, practicing, contemplating, or extensively explaining to others this profound perfection of wisdom.
Why is this? Śāriputra!

All the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, together protect and keep in mind the wholesome deeds performed by those bodhisattvas who practice the perfection of wisdom, so that those evil Māras are unable to create obstacles for them.

“Śāriputra! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to write down, receive and uphold, read, recite, cultivate, contemplate, and extensively explain this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, it is by the very nature of things (*dharmatā*) that they shall be protected and remembered by the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas currently teaching the Dharma in the immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless worlds of the ten directions. If they are protected and remembered by those Buddhas, it is by the very nature of things that evil Māras will be unable to obstruct them.”

Śāriputra! If good sons or good daughters are able to write down, receive and uphold, read, recite, practice, contemplate, and extensively explain this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they should form this thought:

"That I am now writing down, receiving and upholding, reading, reciting, practicing, contemplating, and extensively explaining this profound *prajñāpāramitā* for others is entirely due to the power of the protection and mindfulness of the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, currently teaching the Dharma throughout the ten directions—immeasurable, innumerable, and boundless."
At that time, Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

If sons and daughters of good family are able to copy, receive and uphold, read and recite, practice, contemplate, and extensively explain such profound *prajñāpāramitā*, all of these are due to the protective mindfulness of the supernatural power of the Tathāgatas, the Buddhas of the worlds of the ten directions, which causes all the supreme wholesome karmas performed by them to be unable to be obstructed by any evil Māras.”
The Buddha said:
“Śāriputra, it is so! It is thus!”
"So it is! It is just as you have said, Śāriputra."

If sons or daughters of good family are able to write down, receive and uphold, read, recite, practice, contemplate, and extensively explain this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, it should be known that they are all protected and sustained by the spiritual power of all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas.
At that time, Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

If sons or daughters of good family are able to write down, receive and uphold, read, recite, practice, contemplate, and extensively explain this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, then all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas currently preaching the Dharma throughout the immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless worlds of the ten directions will collectively recognize these sons and daughters of good family who are writing down, receiving and upholding, reading, reciting, practicing, contemplating, and extensively explaining the profound *prajñāpāramitā*; by virtue of this cause and condition, they will joyfully protect and keep them in mind.”

“Bhagavān! If good sons and good daughters are able to write down, receive and uphold, read and recite, practice, contemplate, and extensively explain this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, these good sons and good daughters will always be beheld by the Buddha-eye of all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas currently teaching the Dharma in the immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless worlds of the ten directions; by virtue of this cause and condition, they will be protected and sustained by their compassion.”
The Buddha said,
“Śāriputra, it is so! It is thus!”
"So it is! It is just as you have said, Śāriputra."

If sons or daughters of good family write down, receive and uphold, read and recite, practice, contemplate, and extensively explain this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, these sons and daughters of good family will always be observed, known, and mindfully protected by the Buddha-eye of all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas currently teaching the Dharma in immeasurable, innumerable, and boundless worlds throughout the ten directions. Consequently, no evil Māras shall be able to disturb or afflict them, and the wholesome deeds they cultivate will swiftly reach fulfillment.

Śāriputra! If those sons and daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle can write down, receive and uphold, read and recite, practice, contemplate, and extensively explain this profound Prajñāpāramitā, you should know that these sons and daughters of good family have already drawn near to unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and that no evil Māras or adversaries can obstruct them.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, if sons and daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle are able to write down this profound *prajñāpāramitā* with its various adornments, and uphold, read, and recite it, you should know that these sons and daughters of good family have generated deep faith and understanding toward this *prajñāpāramitā*."

Furthermore, if any sons or daughters of good family should offer flowers, incense, precious banners, pennants, canopies, robes, necklaces, music, and lamps to this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, and honor, revere, respect, and praise it, you should know that these sons and daughters of good family are constantly beheld, known, and protected by the Buddha-eye of the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas. By virtue of these causes and conditions, they will certainly obtain great wealth, great benefits, great fruits, and great maturation.

“Śāriputra! Because these sons and daughters of good family are able to write down, receive and uphold, read and recite, and offer worship, respect, honor, and praise to this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, by virtue of these roots of goodness they shall eventually attain the stage of non-retrogression. During that interval, they will never be separated from the Buddhas, will constantly hear the true Dharma, and will not fall into the evil destinies.”

“Śāriputra! By virtue of these roots of goodness, these sons and daughters of good family shall, until they reach unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, never be separated from the perfection of generosity, and shall never be separated from the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.”

“Śāriputra! By virtue of these roots of goodness, these sons and daughters of good family shall, until they reach unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, never be separated from internal emptiness; they shall never be separated from external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self-characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.”

“Śāriputra! By virtue of these roots of goodness, these sons and daughters of good family shall, until they reach unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, never be separated from suchness; they shall never be separated from the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, the nature of equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm.”

“Śāriputra! By virtue of these roots of goodness, these sons and daughters of good family shall, until they reach unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, never be separated from the noble truth of suffering, and shall never be separated from the noble truths of its origin, its cessation, and the path.”

“Śāriputra! By virtue of these roots of goodness, these sons and daughters of good family shall, until they attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, never be separated from the four dhyānas, nor ever be separated from the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions.”

“Śāriputra! By virtue of these roots of goodness, these sons and daughters of good family shall, until they reach unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, never be separated from the eight liberations, never be separated from the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities.”

“Śāriputra! By virtue of these roots of goodness, these sons and daughters of good family shall, until they reach unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, never be separated from the four foundations of mindfulness; they shall never be separated from the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path.”

“Śāriputra! By virtue of these roots of goodness, these sons and daughters of good family shall, until they reach unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, never be separated from the liberation door of emptiness, nor ever be separated from the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness.”

“Śāriputra! By virtue of these roots of goodness, these sons and daughters of good family shall, until they attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, never be separated from the cultivation of the five eyes, nor ever be separated from the cultivation of the six supernormal powers.”

"Śāriputra! By virtue of these roots of goodness, these sons and daughters of good family shall, until they attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, never be separated from the cultivation of the ten powers of a Buddha; they shall never be separated from the cultivation of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha."

“Śāriputra! By virtue of these roots of goodness, these sons and daughters of good family shall, until they reach unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, never be separated from the cultivation of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and never be separated from the cultivation of the nature of constant equanimity.”

“Śāriputra! By virtue of these roots of goodness, these sons and daughters of good family shall, until they attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, never be separated from the cultivation of all-knowledge (sarvajñatā), and shall never be separated from the cultivation of the knowledge of the paths (mārgākārajñatā) and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā).”

“Śāriputra! By virtue of these roots of goodness, these sons and daughters of good family shall, until they reach unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, never be separated from the cultivation of all dharanī-doors, and never be separated from the cultivation of all samādhi-doors.”

“Śāriputra! By virtue of these roots of goodness, these sons and daughters of good family shall never be separated from skillful means until they attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. They teach sentient beings to attain the fruit of stream-entry while they themselves do not realize it;
they teach sentient beings to attain the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship while they themselves do not realize them.”

“Śāriputra! By virtue of these roots of goodness, these sons and daughters of good family shall never be separated from skillful means until they reach unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening; they teach all sentient beings to attain the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, yet they themselves do not realize it.”

“Śāriputra! By virtue of these roots of goodness, these sons and daughters of good family shall, until they reach unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, never be separated from the playful mastery of the bodhisattvas’ supernormal powers; they shall travel from one buddha-field to another, making offerings, honoring, respecting, and praising the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, and the assemblies of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.”

“Śāriputra! By virtue of these roots of goodness, these sons and daughters of good family shall never be separated from the purification of Buddha-fields and the maturation of sentient beings, until they reach unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”

“Śāriputra! By virtue of these roots of goodness, these sons and daughters of good family shall, until they reach unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, never be separated from sovereign supernormal powers as they travel through the buddha-fields, exhorting the Buddhas to turn the sublime wheel of Dharma and deliver immeasurable multitudes.”

“Śāriputra! By virtue of these roots of goodness, these sons and daughters of good family shall never be separated from the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas until they reach unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening.”

“Śāriputra! For this reason, sons and daughters of good family who abide in the bodhisattva vehicle should diligently transcribe, uphold, read, recite, cultivate, contemplate, and extensively explain this Prajñāpāramitā for the sake of others.”
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
After the Parinirvāṇa of the Buddha, in which direction will this profound Prajñāpāramitā flourish and prosper?”
The Buddha said,
“Śāriputra! This profound Prajñāpāramitā, after my parinirvāṇa, shall gradually flourish in the southeastern direction.”

In that direction, there will be bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, kings, ministers, elders, and householders who have set out on the bodhisattva vehicle, and who will develop deep faith and understanding in this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, and who will copy it, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, practice it, contemplate it, and explain it extensively; furthermore, they will honor, revere, respect, and praise this *prajñāpāramitā* with various kinds of exquisite flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, garments, necklaces, precious banners, flags and canopies, music, and lamps.

By virtue of such supreme roots of goodness, they will never fall into the perilous evil realms, but will always be born among gods and humans, experiencing noble and sublime pleasures. Through this power, they increase the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā) so that they may be swiftly perfected; because of this, they are further able to make offerings to, revere, honor, and praise the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, and subsequently, according to their respective capacities, gradually practice the Dharma of the Three Vehicles to attain liberation.
“Śāriputra! This profound Prajñāpāramitā, after my parinirvāṇa, shall spread from the southeast to the south and gradually flourish there.”

In that direction, there will be bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, kings, ministers, elders, and householders who have set out upon the bodhisattva vehicle, who will develop deep faith and understanding in this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, and who will copy, uphold, read, recite, cultivate, contemplate, and extensively explain it; furthermore, they will honor, revere, respect, and praise this *prajñāpāramitā* with various kinds of exquisite flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, precious banners, flags and canopies, music, and lamps.

By virtue of such supreme roots of goodness, they will never fall into the perilous evil realms, but will always be born among gods and humans to experience noble and sublime happiness. Through this power, they increase the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā) so that they may be swiftly perfected; consequently, they are able to make offerings to, revere, honor, and praise the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, and subsequently, according to their respective capacities, practice the stages of the Three Vehicles in succession to attain liberation.
“Śāriputra! This profound Prajñāpāramitā, after my parinirvāṇa, shall gradually flourish and spread from the south to the southwest.”

In that direction, there will be bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, kings, ministers, elders, and householders who have set out upon the bodhisattva vehicle, who will develop deep faith and understanding in this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, and who will copy, uphold, read, recite, cultivate, contemplate, and extensively explain it; furthermore, they will honor, revere, respect, and praise this *prajñāpāramitā* with various kinds of exquisite flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, precious banners, flags, canopies, music, and lamps.

By virtue of such supreme and wholesome roots, they will never fall into the perilous and miserable realms, but will always be born among gods and humans to experience noble and sublime happiness. Through this power, they will augment the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā) so that they may be swiftly perfected; consequently, they will be able to make offerings to, revere, respect, and praise the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, and subsequently, according to their respective capacities, gradually practice the Dharma of the Three Vehicles to attain liberation.
“Śāriputra! This profound Prajñāpāramitā, after my parinirvāṇa, shall gradually flourish and spread from the southwest to the northwest.”

In that direction, there will be bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, kings, ministers, elders, and householders who have set out on the bodhisattva vehicle, who will develop deep faith and understanding in this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, and who will copy, uphold, read, recite, cultivate, contemplate, and extensively explain it; furthermore, they will honor, revere, respect, and praise this *prajñāpāramitā* with various kinds of exquisite flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, precious banners, flags, canopies, music, and lamps.

By virtue of such supreme and wholesome roots, they will never fall into the perilous and evil realms, but will always be born among gods and humans to experience noble and sublime happiness. Through this power, they will increase the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā) so that they may be swiftly perfected; consequently, they will be able to make offerings to, revere, respect, and praise the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, and subsequently, according to their respective capacities, gradually practice the Dharma of the Three Vehicles to attain liberation.
"Śāriputra! This profound Prajñāpāramitā, after my parinirvāṇa, shall gradually flourish as it spreads from the northwest to the north."

In that direction, there will be bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, kings, ministers, elders, and householders who have set out upon the bodhisattva vehicle, and who will develop deep faith and understanding in this profound *prajñāpāramitā*. They will write it down, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, cultivate and contemplate it, and explain it extensively; furthermore, they will honor, revere, respect, and praise this *prajñāpāramitā* with various kinds of exquisite flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, precious banners, flags, canopies, music, and lamps.

By virtue of such supreme roots of goodness, they will never fall into the perilous evil realms, but will always be born among gods and humans to experience noble and sublime pleasures. Through this power, they increase the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā) so that they may be swiftly perfected; consequently, they are able to make offerings to, revere, respect, and praise the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, and subsequently, according to their respective capacities, practice the stages of the three vehicles (triyāna) in succession to attain liberation.
“Śāriputra! This profound Prajñāpāramitā, after my parinirvāṇa, shall gradually flourish and spread from the north to the northeast.”

In that direction, there will be bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, kings, ministers, elders, and householders who have set out upon the bodhisattva vehicle, and who will be able to develop deep faith and understanding in this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, and to write it down, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, cultivate and contemplate it, and explain it extensively; furthermore, they will honor, revere, respect, and praise this *prajñāpāramitā* with various kinds of exquisite flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, precious banners, flags, canopies, music, and lamps.

By virtue of such supreme and wholesome roots, they will never fall into the perilous evil realms, but will always be born among gods and humans to experience noble and sublime bliss. Through this power, they increase the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā) so that they may be swiftly perfected; consequently, they are able to make offerings to, revere, honor, and praise the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, and subsequently, according to their respective capacities, practice the gradual cultivation of the three vehicles (triyāna) to attain liberation.
“Śāriputra! After my parinirvāṇa, in a future time, a future period, during the final five hundred years, this profound Prajñāpāramitā will perform great Buddha-work in the northeastern region.”

Why is this? Śāriputra, the Dharma revered by all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas is precisely this Prajñāpāramitā; likewise, this Prajñāpāramitā is collectively protected and mindful of by all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas.

Śāriputra! The unsurpassed true Dharma of the Dharma and Vinaya attained by the Buddhas has no characteristic of extinction or disappearance; that unsurpassed true Dharma of the Dharma and Vinaya attained by all Buddhas is precisely the Prajñāpāramitā.

Śāriputra! Those sons and daughters of good family in the northeastern direction who are able to have faith and understanding in this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, and who receive, uphold, read, recite, practice, contemplate, and extensively explain it—these sons and daughters of good family I shall constantly protect and keep in mind, so that they may be free from affliction and harm.
“Śāriputra! Those sons and daughters of good family in the northeastern direction who are able to write out this profound *prajñāpāramitā*,
and furthermore, [honor it] with various kinds of exquisite flower garlands, ointments, incense, and so forth— ”
...with robes, necklaces, precious banners, pennants, canopies, music, and lamps, making offerings,
showing reverence, honoring, and praising the profound *prajñāpāramitā*,
I declare that those sons and daughters of good family will, by virtue of these roots of goodness, ultimately never fall into any [unfortunate states].
Having escaped from the perilous evil realms, they will be born among gods and humans and constantly experience sublime bliss;

through this power, they will further increase the six perfections (*ṣaṭ-pāramitā*), and by means of this, they will be able to make offerings to, revere, respect, and praise the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones.
Thereafter, according to their respective capacities, they will gradually practice the Dharma of the Three Vehicles and attain parinirvāṇa.
Why is this? Śāriputra!

With my Buddha-eye, I observe, witness, know, praise, and extol the merit obtained by these sons and daughters of good family; likewise, all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas currently dwelling in peace and teaching the Dharma in the immeasurable, innumerable, and boundless worlds of the east, west, south, north, the four intermediate directions, and the zenith and nadir, also observe, witness, know, praise, and extol the merit obtained by these sons and daughters of good family with their Buddha-eyes.
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha,
saying: “World-Honored One,
will this profound *prajñāpāramitā* be widely disseminated in the northeast during the later period, the later division, and the final five hundred years after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa?”
The Buddha said,
“Śāriputra, it is so! It is thus!”
It is so! After my parinirvāṇa, in a future time, a future period, during the final five hundred years, this profound Prajñāpāramitā shall be widely disseminated in the northeastern direction.
Śāriputra! After my parinirvāṇa, in a future time, a future period, during the final five hundred years,
those sons and daughters of good family in the northeastern direction who shall hear this profound *prajñāpāramitā*—
Those who, having conceived deep faith and understanding in the Prajñāpāramitā, write it down, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, practice and contemplate it, and explain it extensively—
those sons and daughters of good family should be known as ones who have long since resolved their minds upon unexcelled,
perfect, and complete enlightenment, who have long practiced the conduct of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and who have made extensive offerings to many Buddhas.
Having associated with many virtuous friends, the roots of goodness they have planted have all reached maturity;
through the power of this merit, they are able to hear this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, develop deep faith and understanding, and further transcribe,
receive and uphold, read and recite, practice, contemplate, and extensively explain it to others.
Then, Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

After the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, in a future time, a future period, during the final five hundred years, how many sons and daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle will there be in the northeastern direction who, upon hearing such profound Prajñāpāramitā, will give rise to deep faith and understanding, and further be able to copy, receive and uphold, read and recite, practice, contemplate, and extensively explain it to others?”
The Buddha said, “Śāriputra!

After my parinirvāṇa, in the future time, the final period, during the last five hundred years, although there may be immeasurable sons and daughters of good family who abide in the bodhisattva vehicle in the northeastern direction, they will rarely hear the profound *prajñāpāramitā* and yet give rise to deep faith and understanding; their minds will not be startled, terrified, or frightened, nor will they feel anxiety or regret, and they will further be able to copy, uphold, read, recite, practice, contemplate, and extensively explain it to others.”

Śāriputra! When those sons and daughters of good family hear this Prajñāpāramitā, their minds are not startled, not terrified, and not afraid; nor do they feel any anxiety or regret. They give rise to profound faith and understanding, and they copy, receive and uphold, read and recite, practice, contemplate, and extensively expound it—this is truly most rare.
Why is this? Śāriputra,

these sons and daughters of good family have already approached, made offerings to, honored, revered, and praised immeasurable Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, as well as the assemblies of Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas, and have inquired about the meaning and intent associated with such profound Prajñāpāramitā.

“Śāriputra! These sons and daughters of good family will, before long, certainly fulfill the perfection of generosity; they will, before long, certainly fulfill the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.”

“Śāriputra! These sons and daughters of good family will, before long, certainly fulfill internal emptiness; they will, before long, certainly fulfill external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.”

“Śāriputra! These sons and daughters of good family will, before long, certainly fulfill true suchness (tathatā); they will, before long, certainly fulfill the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state of being free from birth, the fixedness of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm.”

“Śāriputra! These sons and daughters of good family will, before long, certainly fulfill the Noble Truth of Suffering; they will, before long, certainly fulfill the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path.”

“Śāriputra! These sons and daughters of good family will, before long, certainly fulfill the four dhyānas; they will, before long, certainly fulfill the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments.”

“Śāriputra! These sons and daughters of good family will, before long, certainly fulfill the eight liberations; they will, before long, certainly fulfill the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities.”

“Śāriputra! These sons and daughters of good family will, before long, certainly fulfill the four foundations of mindfulness; they will, before long, certainly fulfill the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.”

“Śāriputra! These sons and daughters of good family will, before long, certainly fulfill the gate of liberation of emptiness; they will, before long, certainly fulfill the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.”
“Śāriputra! These sons and daughters of good family will, before long, certainly fulfill the ten stages of a bodhisattva. Śāriputra!”
"These sons and daughters of good family will, before long, certainly fulfill the five eyes; they will, before long, certainly fulfill the six superknowledges. Śāriputra!"

These sons and daughters of good family will, before long, certainly fulfill the ten powers of a Buddha; they will, before long, certainly fulfill the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.

“Śāriputra! These sons and daughters of good family will, before long, certainly fulfill the quality of non-forgetfulness; they will, before long, certainly fulfill the state of constant abiding in equanimity.”

“Śāriputra! These sons and daughters of good family will, before long, certainly fulfill all-knowledge; before long, they will certainly fulfill the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects.”
“Śāriputra! These sons and daughters of good family will, before long, certainly fulfill all doors of dhāraṇī; they will, before long, certainly fulfill all doors of samādhi.”
“Śāriputra! These sons and daughters of good family will, before long, certainly fulfill all the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva. Śāriputra!”
These sons and daughters of good family will, before long, certainly fulfill unexcelled, perfect, and complete awakening.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

Because those sons and daughters of good family are protected and remembered by all Tathāgatas, are sustained by immeasurable spiritual friends, and are upheld by superior roots of goodness, they seek to attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment for the sake of benefiting many sentient beings.

Why is this? Śāriputra, I constantly teach the Dharma associated with the knowledge of all modes to those sons and daughters of good family; likewise, the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past also constantly taught the Dharma associated with the knowledge of all modes to those sons and daughters of good family.

By virtue of these causes and conditions, those sons and daughters of good family will, in future lives, be able to seek and advance toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and they will also be able to teach the Dharma to others as appropriate, leading them toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

“Śāriputra! Those sons and daughters of good family possess such stability of body and mind that even Māra, the Evil One, together with his retinue, cannot destroy their resolve to seek unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening; how much less could others who delight in evil deeds and revile the *prajñāpāramitā* ever discourage their minds or prevent them from seeking unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening!”

“Śāriputra! When such sons and daughters of good family of the Mahāyāna hear me teach this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, their minds attain the vast and sublime joy of the Dharma; they are also able to establish immeasurable sentient beings in the supreme wholesome dharmas, leading them toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”
"Śāriputra! These sons and daughters of good family have now made a great vow before me, saying:

'I shall establish immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of sentient beings, causing them to resolve upon unexcelled, perfect, and complete awakening, to cultivate the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and by demonstrating, exhorting, encouraging, and inspiring them, lead them toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete awakening, even unto receiving the prediction of non-retrogression.'"
“Śāriputra! I deeply rejoice in that vow. Why is this?

"Śāriputra! I observe that when these sons and daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle have made such great vows, their minds and words are in accord. Those sons and daughters of good family will certainly, in a future age, establish immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of sentient beings, causing them to resolve upon unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, to cultivate the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and by demonstrating, exhorting, encouraging, and gladdening them, lead them toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete bodhi, even unto receiving the prediction of non-retrogression."
“Śāriputra! These sons and daughters of good family have also, in the presence of immeasurable Buddhas of the past, made this great vow:

‘I shall establish immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of sentient beings, causing them to resolve upon unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, to cultivate the practices of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, and by demonstrating, exhorting, encouraging, and inspiring them, lead them toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete bodhi, even until they receive the prediction of non-retrogression.’”
“Śāriputra! The Buddhas of the past also gave their deep approval of that vow. Why is this?

Śāriputra! The Buddhas of the past also observed those sons and daughters of good family who have set out in the Bodhisattva vehicle and whose great vows correspond with their words and thoughts. Those sons and daughters of good family will, in future ages, certainly be able to establish immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of sentient beings, causing them to resolve upon unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, to cultivate the practices of the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, and by demonstrating, exhorting, encouraging, and inspiring them, lead them toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete bodhi, even unto receiving the prediction of non-retrogression.

“Śāriputra! These sons and daughters of good family possess vast faith and understanding; they are able to practice vast giving based upon sublime forms, sounds, odors, tastes, and tangibles. Having practiced this giving, they are further able to plant vast roots of goodness. By virtue of these roots of goodness, they are able to gather vast fruits of retribution. Gathering such vast fruits of retribution, they do so solely for the benefit and happiness of all sentient beings, and are thus able to relinquish all internal and external possessions to those beings.”

He dedicates these roots of merit thus, vowing to be born in the Buddha-fields of other directions where Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas currently reside and proclaim this unsurpassed Dharma of the profound *prajñāpāramitā*. Having heard this unsurpassed Dharma of the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, he is further able to establish immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of sentient beings within those Buddha-fields, causing them to resolve upon unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*), to cultivate the practices of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and—by means of demonstration, exhortation, encouragement, and inspiration—to cause them to attain non-retrogression from unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
At that time, Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“How extraordinary!
World-Honored One!”
How rare! Well-gone One!

The Buddha has realized and known all phenomena of the past, future, and present without exception; he has realized and known all phenomena, suchness, the dharma-realm, and the nature of phenomena, without exception; he has realized and known the teachings on all phenomena without exception; he has realized and known the distinctions in the mental activities of all sentient beings without exception; he has realized and known the Buddhas, bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, and buddha-fields of the past without exception; he has realized and known the Buddhas, bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, and buddha-fields of the future without exception; he has realized and known the Buddhas, bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, and buddha-fields of the present without exception; and he has realized and known all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas in the realms of the ten directions, as well as the dharmas they teach and the matters concerning their bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, and buddha-fields, without exception.
“World-Honored One!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with courageous diligence, constantly seeks the six pāramitās without ceasing, will there be times when they attain these six pāramitās and times when they do not?”
The Buddha said, “Śāriputra!
Those sons and daughters of good family who always seek these six pāramitās with courageous diligence and tireless joy shall, at all times, never fail to attain them.”
Why is this? Śāriputra!

Because those sons and daughters of good family constantly seek these six pāramitās with courageous diligence and tireless aspiration, and because all Buddhas and bodhisattvas always protect and keep them in mind.
Śāriputra said: “World-Honored One!
If those sons and daughters of good family do not obtain sūtras associated with the six pāramitās, how can it be said that they have attained these six pāramitās?”
The Buddha said: “Śāriputra!

Those sons and daughters of good family who always seek these six pāramitās with courageous faith, disregarding even their own bodies and lives—it is impossible that they should at any time fail to obtain this sutra corresponding [to them].”

Why is this? Śāriputra, those sons and daughters of good family, seeking unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, manifest themselves to encourage, exhort, inspire, and gladden all sentient beings, causing them to receive, uphold, read, recite, contemplate, and practice these sūtras associated with the six pāramitās. By virtue of these roots of goodness, wherever they are born, they will always encounter these sūtras associated with the six pāramitās; they will receive, uphold, read, and recite them, practicing with courageous diligence according to the teachings, maturing sentient beings and purifying buddha-fields, and swiftly realizing unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle Three Hundred and Two;
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle Three Hundred and Three.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree.
Chapter 40: On the Deeds of Māra, Part One, Section 40-1.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

The Buddha has already praised and described all the merits of those sons and daughters of good family who, having realized unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, practice the six perfections, bring sentient beings to maturity, and purify buddha-fields.
"Bhagavān, what are the obstructive deeds of Māra that occur when sons and daughters of good family cultivate various practices in order to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening?"
The Buddha said,
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva delights in expounding the essential points of the Dharma, yet eloquence does not arise immediately, you should know that this is a work of Māra for the bodhisattva.”
“World-Honored One!
For what reason does this bodhisattva mahāsattva delight in preaching the essentials of the Dharma, yet eloquence does not arise immediately? Is this a work of Māra?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [It is so.]”

When this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, it is difficult for them to bring that practice of the perfection of wisdom to fulfillment; likewise, it is difficult for them to bring the practices of the perfections of meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity to fulfillment.

For this reason, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva delights in expounding the essential teachings of the Dharma but eloquence does not immediately arise, you should know that this is a work of Māra for the bodhisattva.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva who delights in cultivating superior practices suddenly finds eloquence arising, you should know that this is a deed of Māra for the bodhisattva."
“World-Honored One!
For what reason does this bodhisattva mahāsattva, who delights in practicing sublime conduct, suddenly find eloquence arising? Is this the work of Māra? “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
[The Buddha replied: “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!”

When this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of generosity, and practices the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, because they lack skillful means, eloquence arises only at the very last moment.
For this reason, when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva delights in practicing sublime conduct and eloquence suddenly arises, one should know that this is a work of Māra for the bodhisattva.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
When copying this profound *prajñāpāramitā* sūtra, if one yawns or stretches frequently, you should know that this is a work of Māra for a bodhisattva."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
When one is copying this profound *prajñāpāramitā* sūtra, if they suddenly break into laughter or jesting, you should know that this is a work of Māra for a bodhisattva."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
When copying the profound sūtra of the *prajñāpāramitā*, if they treat one another with contempt, you should know that this is a work of Māra for bodhisattvas."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
When one is copying this profound *Prajñāpāramitā* sūtra, if the body and mind become disturbed and distracted, you should know that this is the work of Māra for a bodhisattva."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

When copying this profound *prajñāpāramitā* sūtra, if a different interpretation arises in the mind and the phrasing becomes inverted or disordered, you should know that this is a work of Māra for a bodhisattva."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
When one is copying this profound *prajñāpāramitā* sūtra and some sudden event arises that prevents its completion, you should know that this is a deed of Māra for a bodhisattva."
"Furthermore, Subhūti, while copying this profound *Prajñāpāramitā* sūtra, one might suddenly think:
'I find no flavor in this sūtra; what is the use of copying it? "
"Having thus abandoned it and departed, you should know that this is a work of Māra for a bodhisattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti, when one receives,

upholds, recites, contemplates, practices, explains, or listens to the profound *prajñāpāramitā* sūtra, if one yawns or stretches frequently, you should know that this is a work of Māra for a bodhisattva."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

When one is upholding, reciting, contemplating, practicing, explaining, or listening to this profound *prajñāpāramitā* sūtra, if one suddenly breaks into laughter or jesting, you should know that this is a work of Māra for a bodhisattva."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

When, while upholding, reciting, contemplating, practicing, explaining, or listening to this profound *Prajñāpāramitā* Sūtra, they treat one another with contempt, you should know that this is a work of Māra for bodhisattvas."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

When one upholds, recites, contemplates, cultivates, explains, or listens to this profound *prajñāpāramitā* sūtra, if the body and mind become disturbed and agitated, you should know that this is the work of Māra for a bodhisattva."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

When one receives, upholds, recites, contemplates, cultivates, explains, or listens to this profound *prajñāpāramitā* sūtra, if a divergent understanding arises in the mind and the words and phrases become inverted or confused, you should know that this is a work of Māra for a bodhisattva."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

When one is upholding, reciting, contemplating, practicing, explaining, or listening to this profound *Prajñāpāramitā* sūtra, if a sudden event arises that prevents its completion, you should know that this is a work of Māra for a bodhisattva."
"Furthermore, Subhūti, when one is upholding, reciting, contemplating, practicing, explaining, or listening to this profound *Prajñāpāramitā* sūtra, one might suddenly think:
'I find no flavor in this sūtra; what is the use of such diligent toil?'"
"Having thus abandoned it and departed, you should know that this is a demonic deed (mārakarman) of a bodhisattva.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
“For what reason do these sons and daughters of good family fail to find the flavor in this profound sūtra and instead abandon it?
The Buddha said,
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

These sons and daughters of good family have not practiced the perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity for long in past lives; therefore, they do not find the flavor of this profound perfection of wisdom and abandon it.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
If good sons or good daughters, upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught, should think:
'We shall not receive a prediction [of enlightenment] regarding this; what is the use of listening? "
"With a mind that is not pure, he rises from his seat and departs; you should know that this is a work of Māra for a bodhisattva.
Then, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"For what reason, within this profound *Prajñāpāramitā* sūtra, do you not grant them a prediction of enlightenment and instead cause them to depart?
The Buddha said,
"Suvikrāntavikrāmin!..."
"A Bodhisattva who has not yet entered the state of correct determination beyond rebirth (samyaktva-niyāma) should not be granted the prediction of great enlightenment. Furthermore, Subhūti,
if a son of good family or a daughter of good family, upon hearing this profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) being taught, should form this thought:"
"If our names are not mentioned here, what is the use of listening?
Thinking thus with an impure mind, they rise from their seats and depart; one should know that this is an act of Māra for a bodhisattva.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One,
for what reason and by what causal conditions is the name of that bodhisattva not recorded and proclaimed within this profound *prajñāpāramitā* sūtra?"
The Buddha said,
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
It is the nature of things that a bodhisattva who has not yet received the prediction of great enlightenment should not have their name proclaimed.”
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
If good sons or good daughters, when hearing this profound Sūtra on the Perfection of Wisdom being preached, give rise to such a thought as this:
'This does not mention the cities, towns, or villages where we were born; what is the use of listening to it? "
"With a mind that is not pure, he rises from his seat and departs; you should know that this is a work of Māra for a bodhisattva.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
For what reason, within this profound *Prajñāpāramitā* sūtra, is the city, town, or village of birth for that bodhisattva not recorded or explained?
The Buddha said,
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
If the name of that bodhisattva has not yet been prophesied, one should not speak of the distinctions regarding their place of birth.”
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, upon hearing the teaching of the *prajñāpāramitā*, leaves with a mind that is not pure, then according to the number of steps taken while harboring that impure mind of aversion and abandonment toward this sūtra, they shall lose that many eons of merit and incur that many eons of offenses obstructing enlightenment. Only after having undergone those offenses for that same duration may they again apply diligent effort to seek and attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, thereby restoring their original state."
Therefore, if a bodhisattva wishes to swiftly realize unsurpassed enlightenment, they should not weary of or abandon the profound perfection of wisdom.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

One should know that for sons and daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle, to abandon the profound sūtras of the *prajñāpāramitā* and seek to study other sūtras is an act of Māra.
Why is this? Subhūti!

Because these sons and daughters of good family abandon the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, which is the root of all-knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), and instead cling to other scriptures that are but branches and leaves; they will ultimately be unable to attain great enlightenment (*mahābodhi*).
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
what other sūtras are like branches and leaves, unable to bring forth the knowledge of all modes?”
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If one speaks of the dharmas associated with the two vehicles—namely, the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, the eightfold noble path, as well as all the sūtras concerning the gates of liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—if a son of good family or a daughter of good family practices and studies therein, they may attain the fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, the fruit of arhatship, or the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, but they will not attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. These are called ‘other sūtras,’ which are like branches and leaves; they cannot bring forth the knowledge of all modes.”
The profound *prajñāpāramitā* is certainly able to bring forth the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), possessing great power like the roots of a tree.
Those sons and daughters of good family who abandon the profound sūtras of the *prajñāpāramitā* to seek and study other sūtras will certainly be unable to attain the knowledge of all modes.
Why is this? Subhūti!
It is because this profound sūtra of the perfection of wisdom gives birth to all mundane and supramundane dharmas of merit for bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices and studies the perfection of wisdom, they are practicing and studying all mundane and supramundane dharmas.”
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

It is just as if a starving dog were to abandon its own master’s food and instead go seeking it from a servant. In a future age, there will be sons and daughters of good family belonging to the Bodhisattva Vehicle who likewise abandon the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, the very root of all Buddha-dharmas, to seek and study scriptures associated with the two vehicles; you should know that this is a work of Māra for a bodhisattva."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Suppose there were a person who, desiring to seek a fragrant elephant, having found this elephant, abandoned it to seek its tracks.
What do you think?"
"Does this person possess wisdom? Subhūti replied,
"This person lacks wisdom."
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

In a future age, there will be sons and daughters of good family belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle who abandon the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, the root of all buddha-dharmas, and instead seek to study sūtras associated with the two vehicles; this, too, should be known as a work of Māra for a bodhisattva.”
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
It is as if there were a person who, wishing to see the great ocean, having reached the shore, instead looked back at a cow's footprint and thought:
'How could the depth and volume of the water in the great ocean possibly equal this? "
“What do you think? Would this person be considered wise? Subhūti replied:
"This person lacks wisdom," the Buddha said.
"Suvikrāntavikrāmin!..."

In future ages, there will be sons and daughters of good family belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle who abandon the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, the root of all Buddha-dharmas, and instead seek to study sūtras associated with the two vehicles; know that this, likewise, is a work of Māra for a bodhisattva.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

It is as if a master craftsman or his apprentice, wishing to construct a great hall equal in scale to the supreme palace of Śakra, Lord of the Devas, were to go and measure the palaces of the sun and moon after having seen that [divine] hall."
"What do you think?
Would such a craftsman or his apprentice be able to construct a great palace equal in size to the magnificent palace of Śakra? Subhūti replied:
"No, World-Honored One! The Buddha said:
“Subhūti, what do you think? Does this person possess wisdom?”
Subhūti replied, “Such a person lacks wisdom; they belong to the class of the deluded.
The Buddha said:

“Subhūti! In a future age, there will be sons and daughters of good family belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle who, desiring to seek unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, will likewise abandon this profound perfection of wisdom and instead seek to study scriptures associated with the two vehicles.”
"What do you think?
Can these sons and daughters of good family attain unsurpassed Buddha-enlightenment? Subhūti replied, "No!"
“World-Honored One!
The Buddha said,
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!”
"What do you think?
Are these sons and daughters of good family wise? Subhūti replied:
"They belong to the class of the deluded," the Buddha said, "Suvīta!"
"So it is! So it is! You should know that this is a work of Māra for a bodhisattva."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

It is like a person who seeks to see a wheel-turning monarch (cakravartin), but having seen him, fails to recognize him and leaves for another place; there he sees an ordinary minor king and, observing his physical characteristics, thinks to himself:
'How does the physical appearance and majestic power of the wheel-turning monarch differ from this? "
"What do you think? Would this person be considered wise? Subhūti replied:
"This person lacks wisdom," the Buddha said. "Suvīra!..."

In future ages, there will be sons of good family and daughters of good family belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle who, desiring to seek unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, abandon this profound perfection of wisdom and instead seek to study sūtras associated with the two vehicles; it shall be just so.
"What do you think?
Will these sons and daughters of good family be able to realize great enlightenment? Subhūti replied:
"No, World-Honored One! The Buddha said:
“Subhūti, what do you think?
Are these sons of good family and daughters of good family wise?”
Subhūti replied, “They are of a foolish nature.
The Buddha said:
“Excellent, Subhūti! It is so, it is so!”
"You should know that this is a work of Māra for a bodhisattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti, it is like a hungry person who,
having obtained food of a hundred flavors, discards it to seek out and eat two-month-old grain porridge."
"What do you think?
Would this person be considered wise? Subhūti replied:
"This person lacks wisdom," the Buddha said, "Subhūti!"

In future ages, there will be sons and daughters of good family belonging to the Bodhisattva vehicle who abandon the profound sūtras of the Great Prajñāpāramitā and seek to study sūtras associated with the two vehicles; their desire to seek the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) therein shall be exactly like this.
"What do you think?
Are these sons and daughters of good family wise? Subhūti replied:
"They belong to the class of the deluded," the Buddha said.
"Suvikrāntavikrāmin!..."
"So it is! So it is! You should know that this is a work of Māra for a bodhisattva."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Suppose there were a poor man who, having obtained a priceless jewel, cast it aside and sought instead a *kācamaṇi*. What do you think?"
"Does this person possess wisdom? Subhūti replied,
"This person lacks wisdom."
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!
