Within this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, true suchness (*tathatā*) does not exist; the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm do not exist.

If, in this regard, true thusness is non-existent, and the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm are non-existent, then in this regard the Buddha is non-existent, and bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, and pratyekabuddhas are also non-existent.
Why is this? Because all dharmas are empty of intrinsic nature.
"Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
Within this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, the noble truth of suffering does not exist, nor do the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path exist.

Where the noble truth of suffering does not exist, and where the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path do not exist, there the Buddha does not exist, and bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, and pratyekabuddhas likewise do not exist.
Why is this? Because all phenomena are empty of intrinsic nature. "Subhūti!
Within this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, the four dhyānas do not exist; the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments do not exist.

If, in a certain place, the four dhyānas are non-existent, and the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are non-existent, then in that place the Buddha is non-existent, and bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, and pratyekabuddhas are likewise non-existent.
Why is this? Because all phenomena are empty of intrinsic nature. "Subhūti!

Within this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, the eight liberations (*aṣṭavimokṣa*) do not exist; the eight bases of mastery (*aṣṭābhibhvāyatana*), the nine successive attainments (*navānupūrvavihārasamāpatti*), and the ten totalities (*daśakṛtsnāyatana*) do not exist.

If, in this place, the eight liberations are non-existent, and the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are non-existent, then in this place the Buddha is non-existent, and bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, and pratyekabuddhas are likewise non-existent.
Why is this? Because all phenomena are empty of intrinsic nature.
"Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [It is thus.]”

Within this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, the four foundations of mindfulness do not exist; the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path do not exist.

If, in a certain place, the four foundations of mindfulness are non-existent, and the four right endeavors up to the eight branches of the noble path are non-existent, then in that place the Buddha is non-existent, and bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, and pratyekabuddhas are also non-existent.
Why is this? Because all phenomena are empty of intrinsic nature.
"Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [It is thus.]”
Within this profound perfection of wisdom, the gate of liberation of emptiness does not exist; the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness do not exist.

If, in this regard, the gate of liberation of emptiness is non-existent, and the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are non-existent, then in this regard the Buddha is non-existent, and bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, and pratyekabuddhas are likewise non-existent.
Why is this? Because all dharmas are empty of intrinsic nature.
"Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
Within this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, the ten stages (*bhūmi*) of a bodhisattva do not exist.
Where the ten stages of a bodhisattva do not exist, there the Buddha does not exist; likewise, the bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, and pratyekabuddhas do not exist.
Why is this? Because all phenomena are empty of intrinsic nature.
"Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
Within this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, the five eyes do not exist, and the six supernormal powers (*ṣaḍabhijñā*) do not exist.
Where the five eyes do not exist and the six supernormal powers do not exist, there the Buddha does not exist; likewise, the bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, and pratyekabuddhas do not exist.
Why is this? Because all phenomena are empty of intrinsic nature.
"Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

Within this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, the ten powers of a Buddha do not exist; the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha do not exist.

If, in this regard, the ten powers of a Buddha are non-existent, and the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are non-existent, then in that regard the Buddha is non-existent, and bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, and pratyekabuddhas are likewise non-existent.
Why is this? Because all phenomena are empty of intrinsic nature. "Subhūti!..."
Within this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, the quality of non-forgetfulness (*asaṃpramoṣadharma*) does not exist, and the state of constant equanimity (*upekṣā*) does not exist.
Where there is no quality of non-forgetfulness and no state of constant equanimity, therein the Buddha does not exist; likewise, the bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, and pratyekabuddhas do not exist.
Why is this? Because all phenomena are empty of intrinsic nature. "Subhūti!
Within this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, omniscience (*sarvajñatā*) does not exist; the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) do not exist.

If, in this place, all-knowledge is non-existent, and the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are non-existent, then in that place the Buddha is non-existent, and bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, and pratyekabuddhas are also non-existent.
Why is this? Because all phenomena are empty of intrinsic nature. "Sudhana!..."
Within this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, all *dhāraṇī* gates are non-existent, and all *samādhi* gates are non-existent.

If, in this state, all dharani-doors are non-existent and all samadhi-doors are non-existent, then in this state the Buddha is non-existent, and bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, and pratyekabuddhas are likewise non-existent.
Why is this? Because all phenomena are empty of intrinsic nature. "Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [All phenomena are empty of intrinsic nature.]"
Within this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, the fruit of stream-entry does not exist; the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship do not exist.

If, in this state, the fruit of stream-entry is non-existent, and the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are non-existent, then in this state the Buddha is non-existent, and bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, and all pratyekabuddhas are likewise non-existent.
Why is this? Because all phenomena are empty of intrinsic nature.
"Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [It is thus.]”
Within this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, the awakening of a pratyekabuddha does not exist.
Where the awakening of a pratyekabuddha does not exist, there the Buddha does not exist; likewise, the bodhisattva, the śrāvaka, and all pratyekabuddhas do not exist.
Why is this? Because all phenomena are empty of intrinsic nature. "Subhūti!..."
Within this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, the practice of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is non-existent.
Where the practice of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is non-existent, there the Buddha is non-existent, and bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, and pratyekabuddhas are likewise non-existent.
Why is this? Because all phenomena are empty of intrinsic nature.
"Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
Within this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas does not exist.
Where the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas does not exist, there the Buddha does not exist; nor do the bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, or pratyekabuddhas exist.
Why is this? Because all phenomena are empty of intrinsic nature. Furthermore, Subhūti!

When sons and daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle hear, write down, receive and uphold, read and recite, practice, contemplate, and explain to others such a profound *prajñāpāramitā* sūtra as this, many obstacles and hindering circumstances will arise, causing those with little merit to fail in their undertakings.

Just as there are various precious treasures in Jambudvīpa—namely, vaidūrya, conch shells, jade, coral, stone deposits, maṇi-jewels, pearls, sapphire, emerald, gold, silver, and other such gems—which are subject to many thieves, harms, and obstacles, so that persons of meager merit cannot obtain them despite seeking them.
The precious jewel of the profound *prajñāpāramitā* is likewise so: when those of little merit hear it and the like, many evil Māras create obstacles for them.
The Venerable Subhūti then addressed the Buddha, saying: “So it is,
World-Honored One!”

"So it is, Sugata! This profound perfection of wisdom is like the various precious gems of Jambudvīpa, such as vaidūrya and the like, which are beset by many obstacles and cannot be obtained by those of meager merit."

Because those sons and daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle possess little merit, they encounter many obstacles when hearing [the Dharma] and so forth; thus, although they have the desire [to practice], they are unable to achieve success.

Why is this so? Because there are those who are deluded and act under the influence of Māra; when sons and daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle hear, write down, receive, uphold, recite, practice, contemplate, and explain to others such a profound sūtra as this Prajñāpāramitā, they create obstacles for them.

“Bhagavān! Those foolish ones, whose awakening-wisdom is meager and inferior, do not themselves hear, write down, receive and uphold, recite, practice, contemplate, or explain the profound *prajñāpāramitā*. Furthermore, they delight in obstructing others from hearing, writing down, receiving and upholding, reciting, practicing, contemplating, and explaining the profound *prajñāpāramitā* for others.”
Blessed One!

Those deluded persons do not delight in the Great Dharma; they themselves take no pleasure in hearing, writing, receiving, upholding, reciting, practicing, contemplating, or explaining the profound sūtras of the *prajñāpāramitā*, and furthermore, they create obstacles for others when those others hear, write, receive, uphold, recite, practice, contemplate, or explain such profound sūtras of the *prajñāpāramitā*.
The Buddha said, “So it is, Subhūti!”

It is so! There are foolish people who are instigated by Māra; they have not planted roots of goodness, their merit and wisdom are meager and inferior, they have not yet made great vows before the Buddha, and they have not been sustained by virtuous friends. Consequently, they themselves are unable to hear, write, receive and uphold, read and recite, practice, contemplate, or explain these profound sūtras of the *Prajñāpāramitā*. When newly initiated sons and daughters of good family who study the Mahāyāna hear, write, receive and uphold, read and recite, practice, contemplate, or explain these profound sūtras of the *Prajñāpāramitā* for others, such persons create obstacles and hindrances.

"Subhūti! In future ages, there will be sons of good family and daughters of good family whose awakening wisdom is meager and whose roots of virtue are slight. Their minds will find no joy in the vast merits of the Tathāgatas; they themselves will be unable to hear, write down, receive and uphold, read and recite, practice, contemplate, or extensively explain the profound sūtras of the *prajñāpāramitā*. Furthermore, they will delight in obstructing others from hearing, writing down, receiving and upholding, reading and reciting, practicing, contemplating, or expounding for others the profound *prajñāpāramitā*."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

When sons and daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle hear, write down, receive and uphold, read and recite, practice, contemplate, and explain to others this profound *prajñāpāramitā* sūtra, many demonic obstacles will arise."
“Subhūti! If sons or daughters of good family hear, write down, receive and uphold, read and recite,
cultivate, contemplate, and explain to others this Perfection of Wisdom in this way,..."
During the time of these profound sūtras, there will be no demonic activities; furthermore, one will be able to fulfill the pāramitās of wisdom,
meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, and further be able to fulfill internal emptiness,
external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, and existence...
[They are] emptiness, the emptiness of the unconditioned, ultimate emptiness, boundless emptiness, emptiness of dispersion, emptiness of non-alteration,
emptiness of intrinsic nature, emptiness of self-characteristics, emptiness of common characteristics, emptiness of all dharmas, emptiness of the unapprehendable,
emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, and emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence; furthermore—
They are able to fulfill suchness, the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, non-falsity, immutability, equality,
the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space,
and the inconceivable realm; furthermore, they are able to fulfill the noble truth of suffering, its origin, and its cessation.
The Noble Truth of the Path can further bring to perfection the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments;
it can further bring to perfection the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative concentrations, and the ten totalities;
and it can further bring to perfection the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of miraculous power, and the five faculties.
the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path;
furthermore, they are able to fulfill the gate of liberation of emptiness, the signless, and the wishless gates of liberation; furthermore, they are able to fulfill the ten stages of a bodhisattva;
furthermore, they are able to fulfill the five eyes and the six supernormal powers; furthermore, they are able to fulfill the ten powers of a Buddha.
The four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity;
the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; furthermore, they are able to fulfill the quality of non-forgetfulness and the constant abiding in equanimity;
and furthermore, they are able to fulfill all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects.
Furthermore, they are able to fulfill all dharani-doors and all samadhi-doors;
furthermore, they are able to fulfill all bodhisattva-mahasattva practices; and furthermore, they are able to fulfill the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas.
“Subhūti! You should know that it is all due to the majestic power and sustaining grace of the Buddha that these sons and daughters of good family are enabled to hear,
write down, receive and uphold, read and recite, practice, and contemplate [this teaching].”
When this profound *prajñāpāramitā* sūtra is being expounded, may no works of Māra arise; furthermore, may the *prajñā*,
*dhyāna*, *vīrya*, *kṣānti*, *śīla*, and *dāna* pāramitās be brought to fulfillment,
and may inner emptiness (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*), outer emptiness (*bahirdhā-śūnyatā*), and inner-and-outer emptiness (*adhyātma-bahirdhā-śūnyatā*) be brought to fulfillment.
Emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, emptiness of the ultimate truth, emptiness of the conditioned, emptiness of the unconditioned,
absolute emptiness, emptiness of the limitless, emptiness of dispersion, emptiness of non-alteration, emptiness of intrinsic nature, emptiness of specific characteristics,
emptiness of common characteristics, emptiness of all phenomena, emptiness of non-apprehensibility, and emptiness of non-existence.
...emptiness of intrinsic nature, emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature; and furthermore, they cause the fulfillment of true thusness (*tathatā*),
the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), non-erroneousness, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth,

the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*).
Furthermore, they cause them to fulfill the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path;
furthermore, they cause them to fulfill the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments;

furthermore, they cause them to fulfill the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities; furthermore, they cause them to fulfill the four foundations of mindfulness.
The four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path;
furthermore, he causes them to fulfill the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness;
furthermore, he causes them to fulfill the ten stages of a bodhisattva; furthermore, he causes them to fulfill the five eyes.

The six supernormal powers; furthermore, they cause the perfection of the Buddha’s ten powers, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
furthermore, they cause the perfection of the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant dwelling in equanimity; furthermore, they cause the perfection of the one...
They cause the knowledge of all things, the knowledge of the aspects of the path, and the knowledge of all aspects to be perfected;
they further cause all doors of dhāraṇī and all doors of samādhi to be perfected; they further cause all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas to be perfected;
and they further cause the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas to be perfected.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas throughout the worlds of the ten directions who currently teach the Dharma for the sake of sentient beings also bestow their spiritual power and protection upon such sons and daughters of good family, so that when they hear, write down, receive and uphold, read and recite, practice, contemplate, and explain this profound Sūtra of the Perfection of Wisdom, no demonic obstacles shall arise."

Subhūti! All the bodhisattva mahāsattvas in the worlds of the ten directions who abide in the stage of non-retrogression likewise empower and assist these sons and daughters of good family through their spiritual power, so that when they hear, write down, receive and uphold, read and recite, practice, contemplate, and expound this profound *prajñāpāramitā* sūtra, no demonic obstacles shall arise.
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle Three Hundred and Four;
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle Three Hundred and Five.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang under Imperial Decree.
Chapter 41: The Mother of Buddhas, Part One, Section 41-1.
The Buddha said:
"Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [Listen well...]"

For example, suppose a woman gives birth to many sons—perhaps five, ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, or even a hundred or a thousand—and that mother falls ill. Each of her sons diligently seeks out medical treatment, thinking to themselves:
"How may our mother become free from illness, attain long life and peace and happiness, have no physical suffering, and have her mind freed from sorrow and anxiety?"

At that time, the sons each devised skillful means to seek out articles of comfort and protection for their mother’s body, so that she would not be afflicted by the touch of mosquitoes, gadflies, snakes, scorpions, cold, heat, hunger, or thirst. Furthermore, they venerated and made offerings to her with various kinds of exquisite and wonderful comforts, saying:
"Our mother is compassionate; she gave birth to us and raised us, teaching us all manner of worldly affairs. How could we fail to repay our mother's kindness?"
"Subhūti! In the same way, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha likewise constantly beholds and protects with mindfulness the profound Prajñāpāramitā by means of his Buddha-eye."
Why is this? Subhūti!
The profound perfection of wisdom can give birth to all our buddha-dharmas and can reveal the true reality of all phenomena in the world.

All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas currently teaching the Dharma in the worlds of the ten directions likewise constantly observe, protect, and keep in mind this profound Prajñāpāramitā with their Buddha-eye.
Why is this? Subhūti!
The profound perfection of wisdom can give birth to all the merits of the Buddhas and can reveal the true reality of all phenomena in the world.
For this reason, we Buddhas constantly observe and protect the profound *prajñāpāramitā* with our Buddha-eye; to repay that kindness, we should not abandon it for even a moment.
Why is this? "Subhūti!

All the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas' perfections of wisdom, meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity are all produced by means of this very profound perfection of wisdom."

All internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—all these are made manifest by means of this profound *prajñāpāramitā*.

All suchness, the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm—all these are manifested through this profound perfection of wisdom;
all the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path—all these are manifested through this profound perfection of wisdom;
all four meditative concentrations, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments—all these arise through this profound perfection of wisdom.
All eight liberations, eight bases of mastery, nine successive attainments, and ten totalities arise from this very profound perfection of wisdom;

all four foundations of mindfulness, four right efforts, four bases of power, five faculties, five powers, seven factors of enlightenment, and eight branches of the noble path arise from this very profound perfection of wisdom;
and all doors to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—arise from this very profound perfection of wisdom.
All the ten stages of the bodhisattvas arise from this very profound perfection of wisdom;
all the five eyes and six supernormal powers arise from this very profound perfection of wisdom;

and all the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all arise from this very profound perfection of wisdom.
All qualities of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant abiding in equanimity arise from this very profound perfection of wisdom;
all forms of omniscience—knowledge of all things, knowledge of the paths, and knowledge of all aspects—arise from this very profound perfection of wisdom;
and all gateways of dhāraṇī and all gateways of samādhi arise from this very profound perfection of wisdom.

All stream-enterers and the fruit of stream-entry, once-returners and the fruit of once-returning, non-returners and the fruit of non-returning, arhats and the fruit of arhatship—all arise from this very profound perfection of wisdom;
all pratyekabuddhas and the enlightenment of pratyekabuddhas—all arise from this very profound perfection of wisdom;
all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas—all arise from this very profound perfection of wisdom.
The unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas arises entirely from this profound Prajñāpāramitā.

“Subhūti! All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas—who have attained, are attaining, or will attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment—all do so because of this profound perfection of wisdom.”
For this reason, the profound *prajñāpāramitā* possesses great merit toward all Tathāgatas; therefore, the Buddhas constantly regard and protect the profound *prajñāpāramitā* with their Buddha-eye.

"Subhūti! If sons of good family or daughters of good family who abide in the bodhisattva vehicle are able to hear, write down, receive and uphold, read and recite, practice, contemplate, and extensively explain this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas will constantly regard and protect them with their Buddha-eyes, causing their bodies and minds to always attain peace and happiness, and ensuring that no obstacles arise to the wholesome deeds they cultivate."

"Subhūti! If any sons of good family or daughters of good family who abide in the bodhisattva vehicle can hear, write down, receive and uphold, read and recite, practice, contemplate, and explain to others this profound perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas in the worlds of the ten directions will together protect and mindfully attend to them, causing them to attain non-retrogression from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“As the Blessed One has said:
‘The profound perfection of wisdom gives birth to all Buddhas; the profound perfection of wisdom reveals the true reality of all phenomena in the world.’”
"Bhagavān! How is it that the profound *prajñāpāramitā* can give birth to all Buddhas?
How is it that the profound *prajñāpāramitā* can reveal the true reality (*dharmatā*) of all phenomena in the world?"
"How is it that all Buddhas are born from the profound *prajñāpāramitā*,
and how do all Buddhas explain the characteristics of the world? The Buddha said:

“Subhūti! This profound *prajñāpāramitā* can give birth to all the five eyes and six supernormal powers (*ṣaḍabhijñā*) of the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas; it gives birth to the ten powers (*daśabala*), the four fearlessnesses (*caturvaiśāradya*), the four analytical knowledges (*catasraḥ pratisaṃvidah*), great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity, as well as the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇika-buddhadharma*); it gives birth to the quality of non-forgetfulness, the state of constant dwelling in equanimity, and all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).”

Subhūti! Such immeasurable and boundless qualities of all Buddhas as these are born from the profound *prajñāpāramitā*; it is by virtue of attaining such qualities of all Buddhas that one is called a "Buddha."

The profound *prajñāpāramitā* can give rise to such meritorious qualities of all Buddhas; for this reason, it is said that she gives rise to all Buddhas, and it is also said that all Buddhas are born from the profound *prajñāpāramitā*.

"Subhūti! That which is able to demonstrate the true reality (*dharmatā*) of all phenomena in the world—the profound *prajñāpāramitā*—is that which demonstrates the true reality of the five aggregates (*pañcaskandha*) of the world; indeed, all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas also teach the true reality of the five aggregates of the world."
“World-Honored One!
How do the Buddhas teach and reveal the true nature of the five aggregates in this world through the profound *prajñāpāramitā*?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

The Prajñāpāramitā of all Buddhas does not teach that the five aggregates have arising or destruction, birth or cessation, defilement or purification, increase or decrease, entering or exiting; nor does it teach that the five aggregates have a past, a future, or a present, or that they are wholesome, unwholesome, or indeterminate, or that they are bound to the desire realm, the form realm, or the formless realm.

Why is this so? Subhūti! It is because among all empty phenomena there is neither arising nor perishing; among signless phenomena there is neither arising nor perishing; among wishless phenomena there is neither arising nor perishing; among non-conditioned phenomena there is neither arising nor perishing; among phenomena without birth or cessation there is neither arising nor perishing; and among phenomena without intrinsic nature there is neither arising nor perishing.

"Subhūti! The Prajñāpāramitā of all Buddhas thus reveals the true reality of the five aggregates. Since these characteristics of the five aggregates are themselves the world, the world likewise possesses no characteristics such as formation or destruction, arising or ceasing."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, relying upon the Prajñāpāramitā, are universally able to realize and know the distinctions among the immeasurable and innumerable mental activities of all classes of sentient beings."
However, within this profound principle of the *prajñāpāramitā*, there is no sentient being, nor can any designation of a sentient being be apprehended;
there is no form, nor can any designation of form be apprehended;
there is no feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, nor can any designation of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness be apprehended.
There is no eye-base, nor can the designation "eye-base" be apprehended;
there is no ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-base, nor can the designations "ear," "nose," "tongue," "body," or "mind-base" be apprehended;
there is no form-base, nor can the designation "form-base" be apprehended.

There is no sphere of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena (*dharmāyatana*), nor can any designation of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena be apprehended;
there is no eye-element (*cakṣurdhātu*), nor can any designation of the eye-element be apprehended;

there is no element of form, no element of eye-consciousness, and no eye-contact, nor any feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, nor can any designations for the element of form up to the feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition be apprehended.

There is no ear element, nor can the designation "ear element" be apprehended; there is no sound element, no ear-consciousness element, no ear-contact, and no feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, nor can the designations for the sound element up to the feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition be apprehended.

There is no nose element, nor can the designation "nose element" be apprehended; there is no odor element, no nose-consciousness element, no nose-contact, and no feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, nor can the designations for the odor element up to the feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition be apprehended.

There is no tongue element, nor can the designation "tongue element" be apprehended; there is no taste element, no tongue-consciousness element, no tongue-contact, and no feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, nor can the designations for the taste element up to the feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition be apprehended.

There is no body-element (*kāyadhātu*), nor can the designation of a body-element be apprehended; there is no tangible-object-element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*), no body-consciousness-element (*kāyavijñānadhātu*), no body-contact (*kāyasparśa*), and no feelings produced with body-contact as condition, nor can the designations for the tangible-object-element up to the feelings produced with body-contact as condition be apprehended.
There is no mind-element (*manodhātu*), nor can the designation of a mind-element be apprehended;

there is no mental-object-element (*dharmadhātu*), no mind-consciousness-element (*manovijñānadhātu*), no mind-contact (*manaḥsparśa*), and no feelings produced with mind-contact as condition, nor can the designations for the mental-object-element up to the feelings produced with mind-contact as condition be apprehended.
There is no earth element, nor can the designation "earth element" be apprehended;
there is no water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness element, nor can the designations "water," "fire," "wind," "space," or "consciousness element" be apprehended;
there is no ignorance, nor can the designation "ignorance" be apprehended.

There is no volitional formation, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, or aging, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair; nor is there any designation of volitional formations up to aging, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair that can be apprehended.
There is no perfection of generosity, nor is there any designation of the perfection of generosity that can be apprehended.

There is no perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom; nor is there any designation of the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom that can be apprehended.
There is no internal emptiness, nor can the designation "internal emptiness" be apprehended;

there is no external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, emptiness of all phenomena, emptiness of the unapprehendable, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, or emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature—nor can the designations for external emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature be apprehended;
there is no such thing as *tathatā* (thusness), nor can the designation "thusness" be apprehended.

There is no dharma-realm, no dharma-nature, no non-falsity, no immutability, no sameness, no nature free from arising, no dharma-constancy, no dharma-abiding, no limit of reality, no realm of space, and no inconceivable realm; nor is there any establishment or obtainment of a dharma-realm, up to and including the inconceivable realm.
There is no noble truth of suffering, nor is there any establishment or obtainment of the noble truth of suffering.
There is no noble truth of origination, cessation, or the path, nor is there any establishment or obtainment of the noble truths of origination, cessation, or the path.
There are no four dhyānas, nor can any designation of the four dhyānas be apprehended;
there are no four immeasurables or four formless attainments, nor can any designation of the four immeasurables or four formless attainments be apprehended;
there are no eight liberations, nor can any designation of the eight liberations be apprehended.
There are no eight bases of mastery, nine successive attainments, or ten totalities, nor can any designation of the eight bases of mastery, nine successive attainments, or ten totalities be found;
there are no four foundations of mindfulness, nor can any designation of the four foundations of mindfulness be found;

there are no four right efforts, four bases of power, five faculties, five powers, seven factors of enlightenment, or eight branches of the noble path, nor can any designation of the four right efforts up to the eight branches of the noble path be found.
There is no gate of liberation of emptiness, nor can the designation of the gate of liberation of emptiness be apprehended;
there are no gate of liberation of signlessness and no gate of liberation of wishlessness, nor can the designations of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness be apprehended;
there are no ten stages of a bodhisattva, nor can the designation of the ten stages of a bodhisattva be apprehended.
There are no five eyes, nor can any designation of five eyes be apprehended;
there are no six supernormal powers, nor can any designation of six supernormal powers be apprehended;
there are no ten powers of a Buddha, nor can any designation of ten powers of a Buddha be apprehended.

There are no four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; there is no obtainable designation for the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
There is no quality of non-forgetfulness, nor is there any obtainable designation for the quality of non-forgetfulness.
There is no state of constant abiding in equanimity, nor is there any obtainable designation for the state of constant abiding in equanimity.
There is no omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), nor can any designation of omniscience be apprehended;
there is no knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*) or knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), nor can any designation of knowledge of the paths or knowledge of all aspects be apprehended;
there are no all dhāraṇī-doors, nor can any designation of all dhāraṇī-doors be apprehended; there are no all samādhi-doors, nor can any designation of all samādhi-doors be apprehended.
There is no fruit of stream-entry, nor is there any designation of a fruit of stream-entry to be found;
there is no fruit of once-returning, non-returning, or arhatship, nor is there any designation of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, or arhatship to be found;
there is no enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, nor is there any designation of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha to be found.
There is no such thing as the practice of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, nor can any designation for the practice of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas be apprehended;

there is no such thing as the unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas, nor can any designation for the unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas be apprehended.
"Subhūti! The prajñāpāramitā of all Buddhas teaches and reveals the true reality of the world in this way. Subhūti!"
However, within this profound principle of the *prajñāpāramitā*, form is not manifested, nor are feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness manifested. Why is this?

Subhūti! Within this profound principle of the perfection of wisdom, even the profound perfection of wisdom itself does not exist and cannot be apprehended; how much less can form, feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness be apprehended or manifested!
"In this profound principle of the Prajñāpāramitā, the sense-base of the eye is not manifested, nor are the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind manifested."
Why is this? Subhūti!

Within the profound principle of this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, even the profound *prajñāpāramitā* itself does not exist and cannot be apprehended; how much less could the sense bases of the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind be found or demonstrated!
"In this profound principle of the *prajñāpāramitā*, the sphere of form is not manifested, nor are the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, or mental phenomena manifested."
Why is this? Subhūti!

Within the profound principle of this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, even the profound *prajñāpāramitā* itself does not exist and cannot be apprehended; how much less can the sense bases of form, sound, odor, taste, touch, or mental phenomena (*dharmāyatana*) be apprehended or demonstrated!

"In this profound principle of the Prajñāpāramitā, the eye-element is not manifested; the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are not manifested."
Why is this? Subhūti!

Within the profound principle of this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, even the profound *prajñāpāramitā* itself does not exist and cannot be apprehended; how much less could the eye-sphere, up to and including the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, be apprehended or demonstrated?

"In this profound principle of the perfection of wisdom, the ear-element is not manifested; the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and the various sensations arising conditioned by ear-contact are not manifested."
Why is this so? Subhūti!

Within the profound principle of this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, even the profound *prajñāpāramitā* itself does not exist and cannot be apprehended; how much less could the ear-element, or even the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, be apprehended or demonstrated!

"In this profound principle of the *prajñāpāramitā*, the nose-element is not manifested; the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, nose-contact, and the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition are not manifested."
Why is this? Subhūti!

Within the profound principle of this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, even the profound *prajñāpāramitā* itself does not exist and cannot be apprehended; how much less could the nose element, or even the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition, be found or demonstrated!

"In this profound principle of the Prajñāpāramitā, the tongue-element is not manifested; the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and the various sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition are not manifested."
Why is this? Subhūti!

Within the profound principle of this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, even the profound *prajñāpāramitā* itself does not exist and cannot be apprehended; how much less can the tongue-element, or even the various feelings arising with tongue-contact as a condition, be found or demonstrated!

"In this profound principle of the Prajñāpāramitā, there is no manifestation of the body-element (kāyadhātu), nor is there the manifestation of the touch-element (spraṣṭavyadhātu), the body-consciousness-element (kāyavijñānadhātu), body-contact (kāyasparśa), or the various feelings (vedanā) produced with body-contact as a condition."
Why is this? Subhūti!

Within the profound principle of this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, even the profound *prajñāpāramitā* itself does not exist and cannot be apprehended; how much less could the body-element (*kāyadhātu*), up to and including the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, be apprehended or demonstrated!

“In this profound principle of the *prajñāpāramitā*, the mind-element (*manodhātu*) is not manifested; the dharma-element (*dharmadhātu*), the mind-consciousness-element (*manovijñānadhātu*), as well as mind-contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*) and the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with mind-contact as a condition, are not manifested.”
Why is this? Subhūti!

Within the profound principle of this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, even the profound *prajñāpāramitā* itself does not exist and cannot be apprehended; how much less can the mind-element, or the various feelings arising with mind-contact as a condition, be apprehended or demonstrated!
"In this profound principle of the Prajñāpāramitā, the earth element is not manifested, nor are the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements manifested."
Why is this? Subhūti!

Within the profound principle of this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, even the profound *prajñāpāramitā* itself does not exist and cannot be apprehended; how much less could the elements of earth, water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness be found or manifested!

"In this profound principle of the *prajñāpāramitā*, ignorance is not manifested; nor are volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, or old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair manifested."
Why is this so? Subhūti!

Within the profound principle of this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, even the profound *prajñāpāramitā* itself does not exist and cannot be apprehended; how much less could ignorance, up to and including old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, be found or manifested?
"In this profound principle of the *prajñāpāramitā*, the *dānapāramitā* is not manifested; the *śīla*, *kṣānti*, *vīrya*, *dhyāna*, and *prajñāpāramitā* are not manifested."
Why is this? Subhūti!

Within the profound principle of this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, even the profound *prajñāpāramitā* itself does not exist and cannot be apprehended; how much less could the *dānapāramitā* up to the *prajñāpāramitā* be found or manifested?

"In this profound principle of the *prajñāpāramitā*, internal emptiness is not manifested; external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential emptiness, emptiness of self-characteristics, emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are not manifested."
Why is this so? Subhūti!

Within the profound principle of this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, even the profound *prajñāpāramitā* itself does not exist and cannot be apprehended; how much less could internal emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, be apprehended or manifested!

"In this profound principle of the *prajñāpāramitā*, there is no manifestation of *tathatā* (suchness), nor the manifestation of the *dharmadhātu* (dharma-realm), *dharmatā* (dharma-nature), *avitathatā* (non-falsity), *ananyathābhāvatā* (unchanging nature), *samatā* (equality), *anupapattidharmatā* (the nature of non-arising), *dharmasthititā* (stability of phenomena), *dharmaniyāmatā* (fixed order of phenomena), *bhūtakoṭi* (the limit of reality), the *ākāśadhātu* (space-element), or the *acintyadhātu* (inconceivable realm)."
Why is this? Subhūti!

Within the profound principle of this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, even the profound *prajñāpāramitā* itself does not exist and cannot be apprehended; how much less could there be anything to be apprehended or manifested, from *tathatā* up to the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*)!
"In this profound principle of the *prajñāpāramitā*, the noble truth of suffering is not manifested, nor are the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path manifested."
Why is this? Subhūti!

Within the profound principle of this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, even the profound *prajñāpāramitā* itself does not exist and cannot be apprehended; how much less could the Noble Truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path be apprehended or demonstrated!
"In this profound principle of the *prajñāpāramitā*, the four dhyānas are not manifested, nor are the four immeasurables or the four formless absorptions manifested."
Why is this? Subhūti!

Within the profound principle of this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, even the profound *prajñāpāramitā* itself does not exist and cannot be apprehended; how much less can the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments be apprehended or demonstrated!
"In this profound principle of the *prajñāpāramitā*, the eight liberations are not manifested; the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are not manifested."
Why is this so? Subhūti!

Within the profound principle of this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, even the profound *prajñāpāramitā* itself does not exist and cannot be apprehended; how much less could the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities be apprehended or manifested!

"In this profound principle of the *prajñāpāramitā*, the four applications of mindfulness are not manifested; the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path are not manifested."
Why is this? Subhūti!

Within the profound principle of this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, even the profound *prajñāpāramitā* itself does not exist and cannot be apprehended; how much less can the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path be apprehended or demonstrated!
"In this profound principle of the Prajñāpāramitā, the gate of liberation of emptiness is not manifested, nor are the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness manifested."
Why is this? Subhūti!

Within the profound principle of this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, even the profound *prajñāpāramitā* itself does not exist and cannot be apprehended; how much less could the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—be found or manifested!
“In this profound principle of the *prajñāpāramitā*, the ten stages (*bhūmi*) of a bodhisattva are not manifested.
Why is that? Subhūti!...”

Within such profound principle of the *prajñāpāramitā*, even the profound *prajñāpāramitā* itself does not exist and cannot be apprehended; how much less could the ten stages (*daśabhūmi*) of a bodhisattva be found or manifested!
"In this profound principle of the Prajñāpāramitā, the five eyes are not manifested, nor are the six supernormal powers manifested. Why is this? "

"Subhūti! Within this profound principle of the perfection of wisdom, even the profound perfection of wisdom itself does not exist and cannot be apprehended; how much less could the five eyes or the six supernormal powers be apprehended or manifested!"

"In this profound principle of the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), the ten powers of a Buddha are not manifested; the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are not manifested."
Why is this? Subhūti!

Within the profound principle of this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, even the profound *prajñāpāramitā* itself does not exist and cannot be apprehended; how much less could the ten powers of a Buddha, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, be found or manifested!
"In this profound principle of the perfection of wisdom, the quality of non-forgetfulness is not manifested, nor is the state of constant equanimity manifested."
Why is this? Subhūti!

Within the profound principle of this *prajñāpāramitā*, even the profound *prajñāpāramitā* itself does not exist and cannot be apprehended; how much less could the "qualities of non-forgetfulness" (*asaṃpramoṣadharma*) or the "nature of constant equanimity" (*upekṣā*) be found or manifested!
"In this profound principle of the perfection of wisdom, all-knowledge is not manifested; the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are not manifested."
Why is this? Subhūti!

Within the profound principle of this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, even the profound *prajñāpāramitā* itself does not exist and cannot be apprehended; how much less can omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*), or the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) be apprehended or manifested!
"In this profound principle of the Prajñāpāramitā, no gateways of dhāraṇī are manifested, nor are any gateways of samādhi manifested."
Why is this? Subhūti!

Within the profound principle of this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, even the profound *prajñāpāramitā* itself does not exist and cannot be apprehended; how much less can any *dhāraṇīmukhas* or *samādhimukhas* be found or manifested!
"In this profound principle of the *prajñāpāramitā*, the fruit of a stream-enterer is not manifested, nor are the fruits of a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat manifested."
Why is this? Subhūti!

Within the profound principle of this Prajñāpāramitā, even the profound Prajñāpāramitā itself does not exist and cannot be apprehended; how much less can the fruits of stream-entry, once-returning, non-returning, or arhatship be found or manifested!
"In this profound principle of the *prajñāpāramitā*, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is not manifested.
Why is that? Subhūti!..."

Within such profound principle of the *prajñāpāramitā*, even the profound *prajñāpāramitā* itself does not exist and cannot be apprehended; how much less could the awakening of a pratyekabuddha be found or manifested!
"In this profound principle of the Prajñāpāramitā, the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are not manifested. Why is this? "

Subhūti! Within this profound principle of the perfection of wisdom, even the profound perfection of wisdom itself does not exist and cannot be apprehended; how much less can any practice of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas be apprehended or manifested!
“In this profound principle of the perfection of wisdom, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is not manifested. Why is this?

"Subhūti! Within this profound principle of the perfection of wisdom, even the profound perfection of wisdom itself does not exist and cannot be apprehended; how much less could the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas exist or be demonstrated!"
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

Regarding the designations and conventional expressions for all sentient beings—whether they possess form or are formless, whether they possess perception, lack perception, or are neither percipient nor non-percipient; whether they belong to this world or to all other worlds throughout the ten directions—the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, by means of the profound perfection of wisdom, know them all as they truly are, whether their minds are contracted or distracted."
“World-Honored One!
How does the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, know those classes of sentient beings as they truly are—whether their minds are contracted or distracted?”

“Subhūti! By virtue of the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas know, as they truly are, the contracted minds and distracted minds of those various classes of sentient beings.”
“World-Honored One!

How does the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, by means of the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), know those various classes of sentient beings as having their minds either contracted or distracted, exactly as they are?”

“Subhūti! All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, in accordance with reality, know that within the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), even the nature of phenomena itself cannot be apprehended; how much less so a concentrated mind or a distracted mind!”

"Subhūti! In this way, by means of the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, knows those classes of sentient beings as they truly are—whether their minds are contracted or distracted."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, by means of their exhaustion, detachment, cessation, abandonment, tranquility, and seclusion, know as they truly are the concentrated minds and distracted minds of those various classes of sentient beings."
“World-Honored One!

How does the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, by means of exhaustion, detachment, cessation, abandonment, tranquility, and seclusion, know as they truly are the contracted minds and distracted minds of those various classes of sentient beings?”

“Subhūti! All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, in accordance with reality, know that within exhaustion, detachment from passion, cessation, abandonment, tranquility, and seclusion, even the nature of exhaustion and so forth cannot be apprehended; how much less could there be a concentrated mind or a distracted mind!”

"Subhūti! In this way, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, by relying on the profound perfection of wisdom, through the knowledge of exhaustion and so forth, knows as they truly are the contracted minds and distracted minds of those various classes of sentient beings."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, by relying on the profound Prajñāpāramitā, know those classes of sentient beings as they truly are: those with minds possessed of desire and those with minds free from desire; those with minds possessed of hatred and those with minds free from hatred; those with minds possessed of delusion and those with minds free from delusion."
“World-Honored One!

How does the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, know as they truly are those classes of sentient beings who possess minds of lust and those who are free from lust; who possess minds of hatred and those who are free from hatred; and who possess minds of delusion and those who are free from delusion?”

“Subhūti! All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas know, in accordance with reality, the true nature of the minds of those sentient beings characterized by greed, hatred, and delusion; they know that there is no mind of greed, hatred, and delusion, yet no mind that is apart from greed, hatred, and delusion.”

Why is this? Within the nature of reality as it truly is (*yathābhūtatā*), even the mind and mental factors (*citta-caittadharma*) cannot be apprehended; how much less could there be a mind with greed, hatred, and delusion, or a mind free from greed, hatred, and delusion!

"Subhūti! All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas know, in accordance with reality, the true nature of the minds of those sentient beings as being free from greed, hatred, and delusion—neither possessing a mind of greed, hatred, and delusion, nor being a mind free from greed, hatred, and delusion."

Why is this? Within the nature of reality as it truly is (*yathābhūtatā*), even the mind and mental factors (*citta-caittadharma*) cannot be apprehended; how much less could there be a mind possessed of greed, hatred, and delusion, or a mind free from greed, hatred, and delusion!

Subhūti! In this way, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, by relying on the profound Prajñāpāramitā, knows those classes of sentient beings as they truly are: those with minds possessed of desire and those with minds free from desire; those with minds possessed of hatred and those with minds free from hatred; those with minds possessed of delusion and those with minds free from delusion.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas know, as it truly is, that those classes of sentient beings possess minds with greed, hatred, and delusion; they do not possess minds with greed, hatred, and delusion; nor are their minds free from greed, hatred, and delusion."
Why is this? Because these two minds do not harmonize, Subhūti!

All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas know, in accordance with reality, that those classes of sentient beings possess minds free from greed, hatred, and delusion; they do not possess minds characterized by greed, hatred, and delusion, nor do they possess minds that are not free from greed, hatred, and delusion.
Why is this? Because these two minds do not harmonize. Subhūti!

In this way, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, relying on the profound perfection of wisdom, knows as they truly are the minds of those various sentient beings—whether their minds are possessed of greed or free from greed, possessed of hatred or free from hatred, and possessed of delusion or free from delusion.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, relying on the profound Prajñāpāramitā, know as they truly are the expansive minds of all those classes of sentient beings."
“World-Honored One!
How does the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, know, in accordance with reality, the expansive minds of those various classes of sentient beings? “Subhūti!

All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas know, in accordance with reality, that the expansive minds of those various classes of sentient beings are neither expansive nor narrow, neither increasing nor decreasing, neither departing nor arriving; because the nature of the mind is detached, it is neither expansive nor narrow, neither increasing nor decreasing, neither departing nor arriving.
Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of the mind is non-existent, who could be expansive and who could be narrow?
Who could increase and who could decrease?
Who goes? Who comes? Subhūti!
In this way, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, relying on the profound Prajñāpāramitā, knows as they truly are the expansive minds of all those classes of sentient beings.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, relying upon the profound Prajñāpāramitā, know as they truly are the great minds of all those classes of sentient beings."
“World-Honored One!
How does the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, know, according to reality, the great minds possessed by those various classes of sentient beings? “Subhūti!

All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas know, in accordance with reality, that the great mind of those various classes of sentient beings has no going and no coming, no arising and no ceasing, no abiding and no differentiation, and is neither large nor small.
Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of the mind is non-existent; it neither goes nor comes, neither arises nor ceases, neither abides nor changes, and is neither great nor small.

"Subhūti! In this way, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, relying upon the profound perfection of wisdom, knows as they truly are all those great minds belonging to those classes of sentient beings."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, relying upon the profound Prajñāpāramitā, know as they truly are all the immeasurable minds of those various classes of sentient beings."
“World-Honored One!
How does the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, know, in accordance with reality, all the immeasurable minds of those various classes of sentient beings?”

“Subhūti! All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas know, in accordance with reality, that all those classes of sentient beings possess immeasurable minds that neither abide nor do not abide, neither depart nor do not depart.”
Why is this? Because the nature of the mind of immeasurable beings is untainted and without support; how could it be said that there is dwelling or non-dwelling, or going or non-going? Subhūti!
In this way, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, relying upon the profound Prajñāpāramitā, knows as they truly are all the immeasurable minds of those various classes of sentient beings.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, by relying on the profound Prajñāpāramitā, know as they truly are all those classes of sentient beings who possess minds that are invisible and non-obstructive."
“World-Honored One!
How does the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, know, in accordance with reality, that those various classes of sentient beings possess minds that are invisible and non-obstructive?”

“Subhūti! All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas know, in accordance with reality, that all those classes of sentient beings possess minds that are invisible, non-obstructive, and entirely devoid of the characteristics of mind.”
Why is this? Because all minds are empty of their own characteristics. Subhūti!

In this way, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, by relying on the profound Prajñāpāramitā, knows as they truly are all those states of mind of sentient beings that are invisible and non-obstructive.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, relying upon the profound Prajñāpāramitā, know, as they truly are, all those classes of sentient beings' formless and invisible minds."
“World-Honored One!
How does the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, know, in accordance with reality, all those classes of sentient beings’ formless and invisible minds?”
“Subhūti! All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas know, as they truly are, all those formless and invisible minds of sentient beings; even the five eyes of the Buddhas cannot see them.”
Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of all minds is empty. Subhūti!
In this way, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, by relying on the profound Prajñāpāramitā, knows as they truly are all those formless and invisible minds of sentient beings.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, relying upon the profound Prajñāpāramitā, know, as they truly are, the arising and ceasing, the contraction and expansion, of the minds and mental factors of other sentient beings."
“World-Honored One!

How does the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, know, in accordance with reality, the arising and ceasing, the contraction and expansion, of the minds and mental factors of other sentient beings?”

“Subhūti! All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas know, in accordance with reality, that the arising and ceasing, the contraction and expansion, of the minds and mental factors of other sentient beings all arise in dependence upon form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness.”

“Subhūti! In this way, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, by relying on the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, knows as they truly are the arising and ceasing, the contraction and expansion, of the minds and mental factors of other sentient beings. That is to say, the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas know as they truly are the arising, ceasing, contraction, and expansion of the minds and mental factors of other sentient beings: how some, based on form (*rūpa*), or based on feeling (*vedanā*), perception (*saṃjñā*), formations (*saṃskāra*), or consciousness (*vijñāna*), cling to the self and the world as eternal, asserting:

‘This alone is the truth; all else is delusion’; or how others, based on form, or based on feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness, cling to the self and the world as impermanent, asserting: ‘This alone is the truth; all else is delusion.’”

Either based on form, or based on feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, one clings to the view that the self and the world are both eternal and non-eternal, asserting: "This alone is the truth and reality; all else is delusion and falsehood.

Or, based on form, or based on feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, one clings to the view that the self and the world are neither eternal nor non-eternal, asserting: "This alone is the truth and reality; all else is delusion and falsehood.

Or, based on form, or based on feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, one clings to the view that the self and the world are finite, asserting: "This alone is the truth and reality; all else is delusion and falsehood."

Either based on form, or based on feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, one clings to the self and the world as being infinite, asserting: "This alone is the truth and reality; all else is delusion.

Or, based on form, or based on feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, one clings to the self and the world as being both finite and infinite, asserting: "This alone is the truth and reality; all else is delusion.

Or, based on form, or based on feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, one clings to the self and the world as being neither finite nor infinite, asserting: "This alone is the truth and reality; all else is delusion."

Either relying on form, or relying on feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, they cling to the idea that the life-principle is identical to the body, asserting: "This alone is true and real; all else is delusion and falsehood.

Or, relying on form, or relying on feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, they cling to the idea that the life-principle is different from the body, asserting: "This alone is true and real; all else is delusion and falsehood.

Or, relying on form, or relying on feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, they cling to the idea that the Tathāgata exists after death, asserting: "This alone is true and real; all else is delusion and falsehood."

Either based on form, or based on feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, one clings to the view that the Tathāgata does not exist after death, asserting: "This alone is the truth; all else is delusion.

Or, based on form, or based on feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, one clings to the view that the Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death, asserting: "This alone is the truth; all else is delusion.

Or, based on form, or based on feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, one clings to the view that the Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death, asserting: "This alone is the truth; all else is delusion."

“Subhūti! In this way, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, by relying on the profound Prajñāpāramitā, knows as they truly are the arising and passing away, the contraction and expansion of the minds and mental factors of other sentient beings.”
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle Three Hundred and Five (and Three Hundred and Six),
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang under Imperial Decree.
The First Division, Chapter Forty-one, Part Two: The Mother of Buddhas.

"Furthermore, Subhūti, all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, by relying on the profound Prajñāpāramitā, know form as it truly is; they know feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness as they truly are."
“World-Honored One!
How does the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha know form as it truly is, and know feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness as they truly are?”

“Subhūti! All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas know form as it truly is—as suchness, as the dharma-realm, and as the nature of phenomena (dharmatā)—as non-false, unchanging, non-conceptual, signless, inactive, beyond proliferation (niṣprapañca), and unapprehendable. They know feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness as they truly are—as suchness, as the dharma-realm, and as the nature of phenomena—as non-false, unchanging, non-conceptual, signless, inactive, beyond proliferation, and unapprehendable.”

“Subhūti! In this way, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, by means of the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, knows, as they truly are, the arising and ceasing, the contraction and expansion of the minds and mental factors of other sentient beings; he knows them as they are in *tathatā* (suchness), as the *dharmadhātu* (dharma-realm), and as the *dharmatā* (dharma-nature)—unfalsified, unchanging, non-conceptual, signless, inactive, beyond discursive proliferation (*niṣprapañca*), and non-apprehendable.”
“Subhūti! The suchness of the mind and mental factors—the arising and ceasing, the bending and extending—of all sentient beings is the suchness of the five aggregates;
the suchness of the five aggregates is the suchness of the twelve bases; the suchness of the twelve bases is the suchness of the eighteen elements.”
The suchness of the elements: the suchness of the eighteen elements is the suchness of the six elements;
the suchness of the six elements is the suchness of the twelve links of dependent origination; the suchness of the twelve links of dependent origination is the suchness of all phenomena;
the suchness of all phenomena is the suchness of the six perfections; the suchness of the six perfections...

Namely: internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena,
the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration,
the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self-characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, and all...

The emptiness of phenomena (*dharma-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of non-apprehensibility (*anupalambha-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of non-existence (*abhāva-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of intrinsic nature (*svabhāva-śūnyatā*),

and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence (*abhāvasvabhāva-śūnyatā*) are suchness (*tathatā*). From internal emptiness (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*) up to the suchness of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence,

these are indeed suchness, the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the state of non-falsity (*avitathatā*), the state of non-alteration (*ananyathābhāvatā*), equality (*samatā*), and detachment (*viviktatā*).

The nature of birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*) are suchness;
from suchness up to the suchness of the inconceivable realm is the suchness of the Noble Truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path;
and the suchness of the Noble Truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path is the four applications of mindfulness (*catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni*).
Abiding in suchness: the suchness of the four foundations of mindfulness is the suchness of the four right endeavors;
the suchness of the four right endeavors is the suchness of the four bases of psychic power; the suchness of the four bases of psychic power is the suchness of the five faculties;
the suchness of the five faculties is the suchness of the five powers; the suchness of the five powers is the suchness of the seven factors of enlightenment.
The suchness of the seven factors of enlightenment is the suchness of the eightfold noble path;
the suchness of the eightfold noble path is the suchness of the four dhyānas; the suchness of the four dhyānas is the suchness of the four immeasurables;
the suchness of the four immeasurables is the suchness of the four formless attainments; the suchness of the four formless attainments is...
The suchness of the eight liberations is the suchness of the eight bases of mastery;
the suchness of the eight bases of mastery is the suchness of the nine successive attainments; the suchness of the nine successive attainments is the suchness of the ten totalities;
the suchness of the ten totalities is the suchness of the three doors of liberation. The three doors of liberation...
The suchness of the gates is the suchness of the ten stages of the bodhisattva; the suchness of the ten stages of the bodhisattva is the suchness of the five eyes;
the suchness of the five eyes is the suchness of the six supernormal powers;
the suchness of the six supernormal powers is the suchness of all dharani-gates; the suchness of all dharani-gates is all...
The suchness of the gateways of samādhi is the suchness of all gateways of samādhi; the suchness of all gateways of samādhi is the suchness of the ten powers of a Buddha;
the suchness of the ten powers of a Buddha is the suchness of the four fearlessnesses; the suchness of the four fearlessnesses is the suchness of the four analytical knowledges;
the suchness of the four analytical knowledges is the suchness of great loving-kindness and great...
The suchness of compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity is the suchness of great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity;
the suchness of great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity is the suchness of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;

the suchness of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is the suchness of the quality of non-forgetfulness; and the suchness of the quality of non-forgetfulness is the suchness of the state of constant abiding in equanimity.
Suchness is the suchness of the nature of constant equanimity; the suchness of the nature of constant equanimity is the suchness of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*);

the suchness of all-knowledge is the suchness of the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*); the suchness of the knowledge of the paths is the suchness of the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*);
the suchness of the knowledge of all aspects is the suchness of wholesome phenomena (*kuśaladharma*); and the suchness of wholesome phenomena is the suchness of unwholesome [phenomena].
The suchness of dharmas: the suchness of unwholesome dharmas is the suchness of indeterminate dharmas;
the suchness of indeterminate dharmas is the suchness of mundane dharmas; the suchness of mundane dharmas is the suchness of supramundane dharmas;
the suchness of supramundane dharmas is the suchness of outflowing dharmas; the suchness of outflowing dharmas is...
The suchness of untainted phenomena is the suchness of tainted phenomena;
the suchness of tainted phenomena is the suchness of untainted phenomena; the suchness of untainted phenomena is the suchness of defiled phenomena;
the suchness of defiled phenomena is the suchness of purified phenomena; the suchness of purified phenomena is...
The suchness of past phenomena is the suchness of future phenomena; the suchness of future phenomena is the suchness of present phenomena;
the suchness of present phenomena is the suchness of phenomena of the desire realm;
the suchness of phenomena of the desire realm is the suchness of phenomena of the form realm; the suchness of phenomena of the form realm is...
The suchness of the dharmas of the formless realm is the suchness of conditioned dharmas;
the suchness of conditioned dharmas is the suchness of unconditioned dharmas; the suchness of unconditioned dharmas is the suchness of the fruit of stream-entry;
the suchness of the fruit of stream-entry is the suchness of the fruit of once-returning; the suchness of the fruit of once-returning...
The suchness of the fruit of non-returning is the suchness of the fruit of arhatship;
the suchness of the fruit of arhatship is the suchness of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha;
the suchness of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is the suchness of the practice of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; [the suchness] of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas...
The suchness of practice is the suchness of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas;
the suchness of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is the suchness of all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas;
and the suchness of all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas is the suchness of all sentient beings.
