“Subhūti! Whether it be the suchness of all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas; the suchness of all sentient beings; or the suchness of all phenomena—they are non-dual and without distinction; they are a single suchness.”
Because such *tathatā* (thusness) is without differentiation, it is indestructible, inexhaustible, and cannot be conceptualized. Subhūti!

All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, by relying on the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, realize the ultimate *tathatā* of all phenomena and thereby attain unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment. For this reason, it is said that the profound *prajñāpāramitā* gives birth to all Buddhas; she is the mother of all Buddhas, capable of revealing to all Buddhas the true reality of the world.
"Subhūti! In this way, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, relying upon the profound Prajñāpāramitā, realizes as they truly are the suchness of all phenomena—unfalsified and unchanging."
“Because he has awakened to the characteristics of suchness as they truly are, he is called a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”
The suchness of all dharmas realized by the profound perfection of wisdom is non-erroneous and unchanging; it is exceedingly profound, difficult to see, and difficult to realize.

"Bhagavān! All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas manifest and distinguish the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas by means of the suchness of all phenomena, which is non-erroneous and unchanging."
“World-Honored One!
Who is able to believe and understand the profound suchness (*tathatā*) of all phenomena?

Only bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have reached the stage of non-retrogression, as well as arhats who have exhausted their outflows and possess right view, can give rise to faith and understanding upon hearing the Buddha speak of this profound suchness. For their sake, the Tathāgata reveals and distinguishes the characteristics of suchness according to what he has personally realized.”
The Buddha said,
“So it is, Subhūti! It is just so.”
So it is! It is just as you have said. Why is this?
"Subhūti! Because true suchness is inexhaustible, it is profound.
"World-Honored One!"
"Why is suchness inexhaustible?
"Subhūti, it is because all phenomena are inexhaustible that suchness is inexhaustible."

"Subhūti! All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas have realized unexcelled, perfect enlightenment by means of realizing suchness; they manifest and distinguish the characteristics of the suchness of all phenomena for the sake of all sentient beings. For this reason, they are called 'those who speak the truth.'"

At that time, all the devaputras of the desire realm and the form realm within the trichiliocosm each scattered various kinds of exquisite celestial flowers and incense from afar as an offering. They approached the Buddha’s presence, prostrated at his feet, and withdrew to stand to one side. With palms joined in reverence, they addressed the Buddha together, saying:
“World-Honored One!
“What are the characteristics of this profound *prajñāpāramitā* that has been taught?
At that time, the Buddha addressed the devaputras, saying:
“Devaputras, you should know this!”

The profound *prajñāpāramitā* has emptiness as its characteristic; the profound *prajñāpāramitā* has signlessness as its characteristic; the profound *prajñāpāramitā* has wishlessness as its characteristic;
the profound *prajñāpāramitā* has non-activity as its characteristic; the profound *prajñāpāramitā*...
The *pāramitā* has non-arising and non-ceasing as its characteristic; the profound *prajñāpāramitā* has non-defilement and non-purity as its characteristic;
the profound *prajñāpāramitā* has the absence of intrinsic nature as its characteristic;
the profound *prajñāpāramitā* has the absence of self-nature as its characteristic; the profound *prajñā*...
The pāramitās have the nature of being without intrinsic nature as their characteristic;
the profound prajñāpāramitā has the characteristic of being without any basis; the profound prajñāpāramitā has the characteristic of being neither annihilated nor eternal;
the profound prajñāpāramitā has the characteristic of being neither identical nor different.
The profound *prajñāpāramitā* has non-coming and non-going as its characteristic;
the profound *prajñāpāramitā* has space as its characteristic; the profound *prajñāpāramitā* possesses such immeasurable characteristics as these.
"O Son of Heaven, you should know!
Such characteristics as these are all spoken by the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas in reliance upon conventional truth, not in reliance upon ultimate truth."
"O Son of Heaven, you should know that these characteristics of the profound *prajñāpāramitā* cannot be destroyed by any in the world, whether gods, humans, or asuras."
Why is this? Because the world, including its devas, humans, and asuras, is also characterized by signs.
O Son of Heaven, you should know this!
Characteristics cannot destroy characteristics, nor can characteristics fully comprehend characteristics.
Characteristics cannot destroy the absence of characteristics, nor can characteristics fully comprehend the absence of characteristics.
The signless cannot destroy signs, nor can the signless fully comprehend signs.
The signless cannot destroy the signless, nor can the signless fully comprehend the signless.

Why is this? Whether it be with marks, without marks, or both with and without marks, all are non-existent; for neither the one who destroys nor the one who knows, nor that which is destroyed or known, nor the act of destroying or knowing can be apprehended.
“Son of Heaven, you should know!
These marks are not produced by form; they are not produced by sensation, perception, mental formations, or consciousness;
they are not produced by the sense-base of the eye; nor are they produced by the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind.”
It is not produced by the sphere of form, nor by the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena;
it is not produced by the eye-element, nor by the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, or the eye-contact, nor by the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition;
it is not produced by the ear-element, nor by the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, or the ear-contact, nor by the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition.
It is not produced by the nose element; it is not produced by the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, or the various feelings produced with nose-contact as their condition.

It is not produced by the tongue element; it is not produced by the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, or the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as their condition.

It is not produced by the body element; it is not produced by the tangible-object element, the body-consciousness element, body-contact, or the various feelings produced with body-contact as their condition.

It is not produced by the element of mind, nor by the element of phenomena, the element of mental consciousness, or by mental contact and the various feelings produced with mental contact as their condition;
it is not produced by the earth element, nor by the elements of water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness;

it is not produced by ignorance, nor by volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, or aging, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.
It is not produced by the perfection of generosity; it is not produced by the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom.

It is not produced by inner emptiness; nor is it produced by outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self-characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

It is not produced by suchness; it is not produced by the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-erroneous nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the nature free from birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, or the inconceivable realm.
It is not produced by the noble truth of suffering; it is not produced by the noble truths of origination, cessation, or the path.
It is not produced by the four dhyānas; it is not produced by the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments.
It is not produced by the eight liberations; it is not produced by the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, or the ten totalities;

it is not produced by the four foundations of mindfulness; it is not produced by the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path;
it is not produced by the gate of liberation of emptiness, nor by the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.
It is not produced by the ten stages of a bodhisattva;
it is not produced by the five eyes, nor by the six supernormal powers;

it is not produced by the ten powers of a Buddha, nor by the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
It is not produced by the quality of non-forgetfulness; it is not produced by the nature of constant equanimity;
it is not produced by all-knowledge; it is not produced by the knowledge of the aspects of the path or the knowledge of all aspects;
it is not produced by any of the doors of dhāraṇī; it is not produced by any of the doors of samādhi.
It is not produced by the fruit of stream-entry; it is not produced by the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, or arhatship;
it is not produced by the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha;
it is not produced by the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; nor is it produced by the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas.

"O Son of Heaven, you should know that these marks are not made by devas, nor are they made by non-devas; they are not made by humans, nor are they made by non-humans; they are neither with outflows nor without outflows; they are neither mundane nor supramundane; they are neither conditioned nor unconditioned; they are without attachment and cannot be described."
"O Son of Heaven, you should know!
The profound *prajñāpāramitā* is free from all marks; therefore, one should not ask what the mark of the profound *prajñāpāramitā* is."
The Buddha addressed the devaputras:
"What do you think? If someone were to ask, 'What are the characteristics of space?', would such a question be considered a correct question?"
The devaputras replied: "No, World-Honored One!"
"Why is this? Because space has no substance, no marks, and is unconditioned; it is not something to be questioned.
The Buddha told the devaputra:
“The profound *prajñāpāramitā* is likewise; it should not be the subject of such inquiry.

However, the nature of all phenomena (*dharmalakṣaṇa*) is the very nature of the realm of reality (*dharmadhātu*), whether a Buddha exists or not. Because the Buddha has realized this nature as it truly is, he is called the Tathāgata.”
Then, the sons of the gods again addressed the Buddha, saying:

"The various marks realized by the Tathāgata are exceedingly profound, difficult to see and difficult to realize; because the Tathāgata has directly awakened to such marks, unimpeded wisdom operates regarding all phenomena."

All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas abide in such a manner, analyzing and revealing the profound Prajñāpāramitā; for the sake of all sentient beings, they gather the characteristics of all phenomena and skillfully reveal them, enabling them to attain unimpeded wisdom regarding the Prajñāpāramitā.
“Rare, World-Honored One!

This profound *prajñāpāramitā* is the constant sphere of activity for all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas. Because all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas practice within this sphere, they realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and for the sake of all sentient beings, they analytically reveal the characteristics of all phenomena—namely, they analytically reveal the characteristic of form, and they analytically reveal the characteristics of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.”
He analytically reveals the characteristics of the sense base of the eye; he analytically reveals the characteristics of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.
He analytically reveals the characteristics of the sense base of forms; he analytically reveals the characteristics of the sense bases of sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, and mental phenomena.

He analytically reveals the characteristics of the eye element; he analytically reveals the characteristics of the form element, the eye-consciousness element, as well as eye-contact and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as their condition.

He analytically reveals the characteristics of the ear element; he analytically reveals the characteristics of the sound element, the ear-consciousness element, as well as ear-contact and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition.

He analytically reveals the characteristics of the nose element; he analytically reveals the characteristics of the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, as well as nose-contact and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition.

He analytically reveals the characteristics of the tongue element; he analytically reveals the characteristics of the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, as well as tongue-contact and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition.

He analytically reveals the characteristics of the body-element (*kāyadhātu*); he analytically reveals the characteristics of the touch-element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*), the body-consciousness-element (*kāyavijñānadhātu*), body-contact (*kāyasparśa*), and all sensations (*vedanā*) produced with body-contact as a condition;

he analytically reveals the characteristics of the mind-element (*manodhātu*); he analytically reveals the characteristics of the phenomena-element (*dharmadhātu*), the mind-consciousness-element (*manovijñānadhātu*), mind-contact (*manaḥsparśa*), and all sensations produced with mind-contact as a condition;

he analytically reveals the characteristics of the earth-element (*pṛthivīdhātu*); and he analytically reveals the characteristics of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness-elements (*ab-, tejo-, vāyu-, ākāśa-, and vijñānadhātu*).

He analytically reveals the characteristics of ignorance; he analytically reveals the characteristics of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair;

he analytically reveals the characteristics of the perfection of generosity; and he analytically reveals the characteristics of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.

He analytically reveals the characteristic of internal emptiness; he analytically reveals the characteristics of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

He analytically reveals the characteristic of suchness; he analytically reveals the characteristics of the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, non-alteration, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm.
He analytically reveals the characteristics of the noble truth of suffering; he analytically reveals the characteristics of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path;
he analytically reveals the characteristics of the four dhyānas; he analytically reveals the characteristics of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments;

he analytically reveals the characteristics of the eight liberations; and he analytically reveals the characteristics of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities.

He analytically reveals the characteristics of the four foundations of mindfulness; he analytically reveals the characteristics of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path;
he analytically reveals the characteristics of the gate of liberation of emptiness; he analytically reveals the characteristics of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness;
and he analytically reveals the characteristics of the ten stages of the bodhisattva.
He analytically reveals the characteristics of the five eyes; he analytically reveals the characteristics of the six supernormal powers;

he analytically reveals the characteristics of the ten powers of a Buddha; he analytically reveals the characteristics of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
he analytically reveals the characteristics of the quality of non-forgetfulness; and he analytically reveals the characteristics of the state of constant abiding in equanimity.

They analytically reveal the characteristics of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*); they analytically reveal the characteristics of the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).
They analytically reveal the characteristics of all dhāraṇī-doors; they analytically reveal the characteristics of all samādhi-doors.

They analytically reveal the characteristics of the fruit of stream-entry (*srotāpattiphala*); they analytically reveal the characteristics of the fruits of once-returning (*sakṛdāgāmiphala*), non-returning (*anāgāmiphala*), and arhatship (*arhattvaphala*).
He analytically reveals the characteristics of the enlightenment of the pratyekabuddhas;
he analytically reveals the characteristics of all the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas;
and he analytically reveals the characteristics of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the sons of the gods: “So it is! So it is!”
"It is as you have said.

Son of Heaven, you should know that the Tathāgata has awakened to the characteristics of all phenomena as being without characteristics (*animitta*) according to reality. That is to say, the characteristic of form (*rūpa*) is transformation and resistance; the Tathāgata has awakened to this as being without characteristics."
Apprehension is the characteristic of sensation (*vedanā*); the Tathāgata has awakened to it as being without characteristics (*animitta*) according to reality.
Grasping at signs is the characteristic of perception (*saṃjñā*); the Tathāgata has awakened to it as being without characteristics according to reality.
Volitional formation is the characteristic of mental formations (*saṃskāra*); the Tathāgata has awakened to it as being without characteristics according to reality.
Discrimination is the characteristic of consciousness; the Tathāgata has realized it, as it truly is, as being without characteristics.
The mass of suffering and affliction is the characteristic of the aggregates; the Tathāgata has realized it, as it truly is, as being without characteristics.
The gateways for growth are the characteristics of the sense bases; the Tathāgata has realized them, as they truly are, as being without characteristics.
The characteristic of this realm is manifold harm; the Tathāgata has awakened to it as being without characteristics, just as it truly is.
The characteristic of dependent origination is arising through conjunction; the Tathāgata has awakened to it as being without characteristics, just as it truly is.
The characteristic of the perfection of generosity is the ability to give with a generous heart; the Tathāgata has awakened to it as being without characteristics, just as it truly is.

Freedom from the affliction of heat is the characteristic of the perfection of ethical discipline (*śīla-pāramitā*); the Tathāgata has realized it as being without characteristics (*animitta*) just as it truly is.
Absence of anger and resentment is the characteristic of the perfection of patience (*kṣānti-pāramitā*); the Tathāgata has realized it as being without characteristics just as it truly is.
Invincibility is the characteristic of the perfection of diligence (*vīrya-pāramitā*); the Tathāgata has realized it as being without characteristics just as it truly is.

The characteristic of the perfection of meditative concentration (*dhyānapāramitā*) is the gathering and sustaining of the mind; the Tathāgata has realized it as it truly is to be signless (*animitta*).
The characteristic of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is the absence of obstruction; the Tathāgata has realized it as it truly is to be signless.
The characteristic of internal emptiness (*adhyātmaśūnyatā*) and so forth is non-existence; the Tathāgata has realized it as it truly is to be signless.
Non-perversion is the characteristic of suchness and so forth; the Tathāgata has realized it as being without characteristics according to reality.
Non-falsity is the characteristic of the Four Noble Truths; the Tathāgata has realized it as being without characteristics according to reality.
Absence of agitation and affliction is the characteristic of the four dhyānas; the Tathāgata has realized it as being without characteristics according to reality.
Boundlessness and non-obstruction are the characteristics of the four immeasurables; the Tathāgata has awakened to them as being without characteristics according to reality.
Absence of clamor and confusion are the characteristics of the four formless attainments; the Tathāgata has awakened to them as being without characteristics according to reality.
Absence of bondage is the characteristic of the eight liberations; the Tathāgata has awakened to them as being without characteristics according to reality.
The ability to subdue these eight bases of mastery (*abhibhvāyatana*) is their characteristic; the Tathāgata has awakened to them as they truly are, as being without characteristics (*animitta*).
Non-distraction is the characteristic of the nine successive attainments (*anupūrvavihārasamāpatti*); the Tathāgata has awakened to them as they truly are, as being without characteristics.
Boundlessness is the characteristic of the ten spheres of totality (*kṛtsnāyatana*); the Tathāgata has awakened to them as they truly are, as being without characteristics.
The characteristic of these thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, which are capable of leading to transcendence, the Tathāgata has awakened to as being signless according to reality;
the characteristic of this gate of liberation of emptiness, which is utterly remote, the Tathāgata has awakened to as being signless according to reality;
the characteristic of this gate of liberation of signlessness, which is most tranquil, the Tathāgata has awakened to as being signless according to reality.
The weariness with all sufferings is the characteristic of the door of liberation of wishlessness; the Tathāgata awakens to it as being without marks according to reality.
The progression toward great enlightenment is the characteristic of the ten stages of the bodhisattva; the Tathāgata awakens to it as being without marks according to reality.
The ability to observe and reflect is the characteristic of the five eyes; the Tathāgata awakens to it as being without marks according to reality.
The absence of obstruction is the characteristic of the six supernormal powers; the Tathāgata awakens to them as they truly are, as being signless.
Thorough determination is the characteristic of the Buddha’s ten powers; the Tathāgata awakens to them as they truly are, as being signless.
Thorough establishment is the characteristic of the four fearlessnesses; the Tathāgata awakens to them as they truly are, as being signless.
The absence of interruption is the characteristic of the four analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*); the Tathāgata awakens to it as being without marks (*animitta*) according to reality.
Bestowing benefit and happiness is the characteristic of great loving-kindness (*mahāmaitrī*); the Tathāgata awakens to it as being without marks according to reality.
Eradicating decline and suffering is the characteristic of great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*); the Tathāgata awakens to it as being without marks according to reality.
Celebrating auspicious events is the mark of great joy; the Tathāgata realizes it, as it truly is, to be signless.
Abandoning clamor and confusion is the mark of great equanimity; the Tathāgata realizes it, as it truly is, to be signless.
Being unassailable is the mark of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; the Tathāgata realizes it, as it truly is, to be signless.
Excellent mindfulness is the characteristic of the quality of non-forgetfulness; the Tathāgata awakens to it as being without characteristics according to reality.
Non-attachment is the characteristic of the nature of constant equanimity; the Tathāgata awakens to it as being without characteristics according to reality.
Manifestly perfect awakening is the characteristic of omniscience; the Tathāgata awakens to it as being without characteristics according to reality.
He thoroughly masters the characteristics of the knowledge of the paths; the Tathāgata awakens to them as they truly are, as being without characteristics.
He manifests the distinct awakening to the characteristics of the knowledge of all aspects; the Tathāgata awakens to them as they truly are, as being without characteristics.
He universally upholds the characteristics of all dharani-doors; the Tathāgata awakens to them as they truly are, as being without characteristics.
The characteristic of universally encompassing all gateways to samādhi, the Tathāgata has awakened to as being signless according to reality;
the characteristic of properly receiving the teaching, which is the fruit of the śrāvaka, the Tathāgata has awakened to as being signless according to reality;
the characteristic of self-awakening, which is the enlightenment of the pratyekabuddha, the Tathāgata has awakened to as being signless according to reality.
The progression toward the great fruit is the characteristic of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; the Tathāgata has awakened to it as it truly is, as being signless (animitta).
That which is without equal is the characteristic of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas; the Tathāgata has awakened to it as it truly is, as being signless.
"Son of Heaven, you should know!

All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas are able to realize, in accordance with reality, that all such characteristics of phenomena are signless. For this reason, I say that the Buddhas have attained unimpeded wisdom, which is without equal."
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Venerable Subhūti, saying:
"Subhūti, you should know this!

The profound *prajñāpāramitā* is the mother of all Buddhas; the profound *prajñāpāramitā* can reveal the true reality (*dharmatā*) of all phenomena in the world. Therefore, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha dwells in reliance upon this Dharma, and he honors, reveres, respects, praises, embraces, and protects the Dharma upon which he relies and abides—this Dharma is precisely the profound *prajñāpāramitā*."
Why is this? Subhūti!
The profound perfection of wisdom can give birth to all Buddhas, can serve as the locus of reliance for all Buddhas, and can reveal the true reality of all phenomena in the world.
"Subhūti! All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas are knowers of gratitude and are capable of repaying that gratitude. Subhūti!"
If someone should ask,
"Who is it that knows gratitude and is able to repay it?
one should answer correctly:
“The Buddha is one who knows gratitude and is able to repay it. Why is this so, Subhūti?
"In all the worlds, there is none who knows gratitude and repays kindness better than the Buddha.
"World-Honored One!
In what way does the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha know gratitude and repay kindness?"

“Subhūti! All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas mount this very vehicle and travel this very path to arrive at unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. Having attained enlightenment, they have at all times made offerings to, honored, revered, praised, embraced, and protected this vehicle and this path, never ceasing for even a moment. You should know that this vehicle and this path are none other than the profound perfection of wisdom.”
"Subhūti! This is called the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha’s knowing gratitude and repaying kindness.
Furthermore, Subhūti!"

All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, without exception, rely upon the profound Prajñāpāramitā to attain perfect awakening regarding all phenomena, whether with signs or signless; yet they do so without any real activity, because there is no agent who acts.

All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas have, without exception, relied upon the profound Prajñāpāramitā to realize perfect awakening regarding all phenomena—both those with signs and those without signs—without anything being established, because no substantial form can be apprehended.

"Subhūti! Because the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, relying upon this profound Prajñāpāramitā, are able to manifestly and perfectly awaken to phenomena that are both with and without marks—phenomena which are entirely without activity and without anything to be accomplished—and because they at all times provide offerings, respect, reverence, praise, and protective sustenance to it without interruption, they are therefore called those who truly know gratitude and repay kindness."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

There are no Tathāgatas, Arhats, or Samyaksaṃbuddhas who do not rely upon this profound Prajñāpāramitā to turn the wheel of wisdom regarding all phenomena as being uncreated, unaccomplished, and unarisen; furthermore, they are able to know the causes and conditions for this non-turning."
"Therefore, you should know that the profound perfection of wisdom can give birth to all Buddhas, and can also reveal the characteristics of the world as they truly are.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"

Since the nature of all phenomena is without birth, without arising, without cognition, and without vision, how can it be said that the profound *prajñāpāramitā* gives birth to all Buddhas, is the mother of these Buddhas, and can also reveal the characteristics of the world as they truly are?
The Buddha said, “So it is, Subhūti!”
So it is! It is as you have said.

The nature of all phenomena is without birth, without arising, without cognition, and without vision; yet, according to worldly convention, it is said that the profound *prajñāpāramitā* gives birth to all Buddhas, is the mother of those Buddhas, and can also reveal the characteristics of the world as they truly are.
“World-Honored One!
How is it that all dharmas are without birth, without arising, without cognition, and without vision? “Subhūti!
Because all phenomena are empty and non-existent, entirely lacking self-mastery, deceptive and unsubstantial, all phenomena are without birth, without arising, without cognition, and without vision.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
The nature of all phenomena has no basis of dependence and no point of attachment; for this reason, they are without birth, without arising, without cognition, and without vision."
“Subhūti! Although the profound *prajñāpāramitā* can give birth to all Buddhas and can reveal the characteristics of the world, it gives birth to nothing and reveals nothing.”

“Subhūti! Because the profound perfection of wisdom does not perceive form, it is called the manifestation of the characteristic of form; because it does not perceive feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, it is called the manifestation of the characteristics of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.”

“Subhūti! Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* does not perceive the sense-base of the eye, it is called the manifestation of the characteristic of the sense-base of the eye; because it does not perceive the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind, it is called the manifestation of the characteristics of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.”

"Subhūti! Because the profound perfection of wisdom does not perceive the sphere of form, it is called the manifestation of the characteristic of the sphere of form; because it does not perceive the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena, it is called the manifestation of the characteristics of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena."

“Subhūti! Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* does not perceive the eye-element (*cakṣurdhātu*), it is said to demonstrate the characteristic of the eye-element; because it does not perceive the form-element (*rūpadhātu*), the eye-consciousness-element (*cakṣurvijñānadhātu*), eye-contact (*cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa*), or the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with eye-contact as a condition, it is said to demonstrate the characteristics of the form-element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.”

"Subhūti! Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* does not perceive the ear-element (*śrotra-dhātu*), it is said to demonstrate the characteristic of the ear-element; because it does not perceive the sound-element (*śabda-dhātu*), the ear-consciousness-element (*śrotra-vijñāna-dhātu*), as well as ear-contact (*śrotra-saṃsparśa*) and the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with ear-contact as a condition, it is said to demonstrate the characteristics of the sound-element up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition."

“Subhūti! Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* does not perceive the nose-element (*ghrāṇadhātu*), it is said to demonstrate the characteristic of the nose-element; because it does not perceive the odor-element (*gandhadhātu*), the nose-consciousness-element (*ghrāṇavijñānadhātu*), nose-contact (*ghrāṇasparśa*), or the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, it is said to demonstrate the characteristics of the odor-element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition.”

“Subhūti! Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* does not perceive the tongue-element (*jihvādhātu*), it is said to demonstrate the characteristic of the tongue-element; because it does not perceive the taste-element (*rasadhātu*), the tongue-consciousness-element (*jihvāvijñānadhātu*), tongue-contact (*jihvāsamsparśa*), or the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with tongue-contact as a condition, it is said to demonstrate the characteristics of the taste-element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition.”

“Subhūti! Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* does not perceive the body-element (*kāyadhātu*), it is said to demonstrate the characteristic of the body-element; because it does not perceive the touch-element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*), the body-consciousness-element (*kāyavijñānadhātu*), body-contact (*kāyasparśa*), or the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with body-contact as a condition, it is said to demonstrate the characteristics of the touch-element up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition.”

“Subhūti! Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* does not perceive the mind-element (*manodhātu*), it is called the ‘demonstration of the characteristics of the mind-element. Because it does not perceive the dharma-element (*dharmadhātu*), the mind-consciousness-element (*manovijñānadhātu*), mental contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*), or the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, it is called the ‘demonstration of the characteristics of the dharma-element’ up to the ‘demonstration of the characteristics of the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition.’”

“Subhūti! Because the profound perfection of wisdom does not perceive the earth element, it is called the manifestation of the earth element; because it does not perceive the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements, it is called the manifestation of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements.”

“Subhūti! Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* does not perceive ignorance, it is called the manifestation of the characteristic of ignorance; because it does not perceive volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, or old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair, it is called the manifestation of the characteristics of volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.”

“Subhūti! Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* does not perceive the *dānapāramitā*, it is called the manifestation of the characteristics of the *dānapāramitā*; because it does not perceive the *śīla*, *kṣānti*, *vīrya*, *dhyāna*, or *prajñāpāramitā*, it is called the manifestation of the characteristics of the *śīlapāramitā* up to the *prajñāpāramitā*.

“Subhūti! Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* does not perceive internal emptiness (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*), it is said to demonstrate the characteristic of internal emptiness. Because it does not perceive external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, it is said to demonstrate the characteristics of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.”

“Subhūti! Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* does not perceive *tathatā*, it is called the manifestation of the characteristic of *tathatā*. Because it does not perceive the *dharmadhātu*, the *dharmatā*, the non-erroneous nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, or the inconceivable realm, it is called the manifestation of the characteristics of the *dharmadhātu* up to the inconceivable realm.”

“Subhūti! Because the profound perfection of wisdom does not perceive the noble truth of suffering, it is called the manifestation of the characteristic of the noble truth of suffering; because it does not perceive the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, it is called the manifestation of the characteristics of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path.”

“Subhūti! Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* does not perceive the four dhyānas, it is called the manifestation of the characteristics of the four dhyānas; because it does not perceive the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments, it is called the manifestation of the characteristics of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments.”

“Subhūti! Because the profound perfection of wisdom does not perceive the eight liberations, it is called the manifestation of the characteristics of the eight liberations; because it does not perceive the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities, it is called the manifestation of the characteristics of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities.”

“Subhūti! Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* does not perceive the four foundations of mindfulness, it is called the manifestation of the characteristics of the four foundations of mindfulness; because it does not perceive the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path, it is called the manifestation of the characteristics of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path.”

"Subhūti! Because the profound perfection of wisdom does not perceive the gate of liberation of emptiness, it is called the manifestation of the sign of the gate of liberation of emptiness; because it does not perceive the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, it is called the manifestation of the signs of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness."
“Subhūti! Because the profound perfection of wisdom does not perceive the ten stages of a bodhisattva, it is said to demonstrate the characteristics of the ten stages of a bodhisattva. Subhūti!”

The profound *prajñāpāramitā* does not perceive the five eyes, and for this reason it is said to demonstrate the characteristics of the five eyes; it does not perceive the six supernormal powers, and for this reason it is said to demonstrate the characteristics of the six supernormal powers.

“Subhūti! Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* does not perceive the ten powers of a Buddha, it is called the manifestation of the characteristics of the ten powers of a Buddha; because it does not perceive the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, it is called the manifestation of the characteristics of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.”

"Subhūti! Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* does not perceive the quality of non-forgetfulness (*asaṃpramoṣadharma*), it is called the manifestation of the characteristic of non-forgetfulness; because it does not perceive the state of constant equanimity (*upekṣā-vihāra*), it is called the manifestation of the characteristic of constant equanimity."

“Subhūti! Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* does not perceive all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), it is called the manifestation of the mark of all-knowledge; because it does not perceive the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*) or the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), it is called the manifestation of the marks of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects.”

“Subhūti! Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* does not perceive any *dhāraṇī* gates, it is called the manifestation of the characteristics of all *dhāraṇī* gates; because it does not perceive any *samādhi* gates, it is called the manifestation of the characteristics of all *samādhi* gates.”

“Subhūti! Because the profound perfection of wisdom does not perceive the fruit of stream-entry, it is called the manifestation of the characteristics of the fruit of stream-entry; because it does not perceive the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, or arhatship, it is called the manifestation of the characteristics of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship.”

“Subhūti! Because the profound perfection of wisdom does not perceive the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, it is called the manifestation of the characteristics of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha. Subhūti!”

The profound perfection of wisdom does not perceive any practice of a bodhisattva mahāsattva; therefore, it is called that which demonstrates the characteristics of all practices of bodhisattva mahāsattvas.

"Subhūti! Because the profound perfection of wisdom does not perceive the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, it is therefore said to demonstrate the characteristics of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas."
"Subhūti! By this principle, the profound perfection of wisdom can reveal the true reality of the world to all Buddhas; therefore, it is called the Mother of all Buddhas."
The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:

“World-Honored One, how is it that the profound *prajñāpāramitā* does not see form, yet is called the manifestation of the characteristics of form; and does not see feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, yet is called the manifestation of the characteristics of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness?”

"How is it that by not seeing the eye-base one is said to demonstrate the characteristic of the eye-base, and by not seeing the ear-base, nose-base, tongue-base, body-base, or mind-base one is said to demonstrate the characteristics of the ear-base, nose-base, tongue-base, body-base, or mind-base?"

"How is it that by not seeing the sphere of form (*rūpāyatana*), one is said to demonstrate the characteristic of the sphere of form; and by not seeing the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena (*dharmāyatana*), one is said to demonstrate the characteristics of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena?"

"How is it that by not seeing the eye-element one is said to demonstrate the characteristic of the eye-element; and by not seeing the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition, one is said to demonstrate the characteristics of the form-element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition?"

"How is it that by not seeing the ear-element (*śrotra-dhātu*), one is said to demonstrate the characteristic of the ear-element; and by not seeing the sound-element (*śabda-dhātu*), the ear-consciousness-element (*śrotra-vijñāna-dhātu*), as well as ear-contact (*śrotra-saṃsparśa*) and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, one is said to demonstrate the characteristics of the sound-element up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition?"

"How is it that by not seeing the nose-element (*ghrāṇadhātu*), one is said to demonstrate the characteristic of the nose-element; and by not seeing the odor-element (*gandhadhātu*), the nose-consciousness-element (*ghrāṇavijñānadhātu*), as well as nose-contact (*ghrāṇasamsparśa*) and all feelings (*vedanā*) produced with nose-contact as a condition, one is said to demonstrate the characteristics of the odor-element up to all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition?"

"How is it that by not seeing the tongue-element (jihvā-dhātu), one is said to demonstrate the characteristic of the tongue-element; and by not seeing the taste-element (rasa-dhātu), the tongue-consciousness-element (jihvā-vijñāna-dhātu), tongue-contact (jihvā-saṃsparśa), and all feelings (vedanā) produced with tongue-contact as a condition, one is said to demonstrate the characteristics of the taste-element up to all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition?"

"How is it that by not seeing the body-element (*kāyadhātu*), one is said to demonstrate the characteristic of the body-element; and by not seeing the touch-element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*), the body-consciousness-element (*kāyavijñānadhātu*), as well as body-contact (*kāyasparśa*) and the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with body-contact as a condition, one is said to demonstrate the characteristics of the touch-element up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition?"

"How is it that by not seeing the mind-element (*manodhātu*), one indicates the characteristic of the mind-element; and by not seeing the dharma-element (*dharmadhātu*), the mind-consciousness-element (*manovijñānadhātu*), mind-contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*), and the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with mind-contact as condition, one indicates the characteristics of the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as condition?"

"How is it that by not seeing the earth element one is said to demonstrate the characteristic of the earth element, and by not seeing the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements one is said to demonstrate the characteristics of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements?"

"How is it that by not seeing ignorance, one is said to demonstrate the characteristic of ignorance; and by not seeing volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair, one is said to demonstrate the characteristics of volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair?"

“How is it that by not seeing the perfection of generosity, one demonstrates the characteristic of the perfection of generosity; and by not seeing the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, one demonstrates the characteristics of the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom?”

"How is it that by not seeing internal emptiness one demonstrates the characteristic of internal emptiness; and by not seeing external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, one demonstrates the characteristics of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature?"

"How is it that by not seeing *tathatā* (suchness), one is said to demonstrate the characteristic of *tathatā*; and by not seeing the *dharmadhātu* (dharma-realm), the *dharmatā* (dharma-nature), the non-erroneous nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm, one is said to demonstrate the characteristics of the *dharmadhātu* up to the inconceivable realm?"

"How is it that by not seeing the noble truth of suffering, one demonstrates the characteristic of the noble truth of suffering; and by not seeing the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, one demonstrates the characteristics of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path?"

"How is it that by not seeing the four dhyānas, one demonstrates the characteristics of the four dhyānas; and by not seeing the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, one demonstrates the characteristics of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments?"

"How is it that by not seeing the eight liberations, one is said to demonstrate the characteristics of the eight liberations; and by not seeing the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities, one is said to demonstrate the characteristics of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities?"

"How is it that by not seeing the four foundations of mindfulness, one demonstrates the characteristics of the four foundations of mindfulness; and by not seeing the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path, one demonstrates the characteristics of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path?"

"How is it that by not seeing the gate of liberation of emptiness, one demonstrates the characteristics of the gate of liberation of emptiness; and by not seeing the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, one demonstrates the characteristics of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness?"
"How is it that by not seeing the ten stages of a bodhisattva, one demonstrates the characteristics of the ten stages of a bodhisattva?

How is it that by not seeing the five eyes, one demonstrates the characteristics of the five eyes, and by not seeing the six supernormal powers, one demonstrates the characteristics of the six supernormal powers?"

"How is it that by not seeing the ten powers of a Buddha, one demonstrates the characteristics of the ten powers of a Buddha; and by not seeing the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, one demonstrates the characteristics of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?"

"Why is it that by not seeing the quality of non-forgetfulness, one demonstrates the characteristic of non-forgetfulness; and by not seeing the state of constant equanimity, one demonstrates the characteristic of constant equanimity?"

"How is it that by not seeing all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), one demonstrates the characteristic of all-knowledge; and by not seeing the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), one demonstrates the characteristics of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects?"

"How is it that by not seeing any dharanī-gates, one is said to demonstrate the characteristics of all dharanī-gates; and by not seeing any samādhi-gates, one is said to demonstrate the characteristics of all samādhi-gates?"

"How is it that by not seeing the fruit of a stream-enterer, one is said to demonstrate the characteristics of the fruit of a stream-enterer; and by not seeing the fruits of a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat, one is said to demonstrate the characteristics of the fruits of a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat?"
"How is it that by not seeing the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, one demonstrates the characteristic of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha?
How is it that by not seeing all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, one demonstrates the characteristic of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas?"

"How is it that by not seeing the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas, one is said to demonstrate the characteristics of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas?
*The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, Fascicle 306; *The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, Fascicle 307.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang under Imperial Decree.
Part One: The Chapter on the Mother of Buddhas, Forty-one, Section Three.
The Buddha said:

"Subhūti! Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* does not give rise to consciousness by taking form as its object, it is called 'indicating the characteristic of form' because it does not perceive form.

Because it does not give rise to consciousness by taking feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness as its objects, it is called 'indicating the characteristics of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness' because it does not perceive feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness."
“Because consciousness does not arise by taking the eye-base as its object, this is called ‘showing the characteristic of the eye-base’ because of not seeing the eye-base;

because consciousness does not arise by taking the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-base as its object, this is called ‘showing the characteristic of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-base’ because of not seeing the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-base.”

"Because consciousness arises without taking the sense-sphere of form as its object, this is called 'showing the characteristic of the sense-sphere of form' by way of not seeing the sense-sphere of form;

because consciousness arises without taking the sense-spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, or mental phenomena as its objects, this is called 'showing the characteristics of the sense-spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena' by way of not seeing those sense-spheres."
“Because consciousness does not arise by taking the eye-element as its object, this is called ‘showing the characteristic of the eye-element’ through the non-seeing of the eye-element.

Because consciousness does not arise by taking the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, or the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition as their objects, this is called ‘showing the characteristics of the form-element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition’ through the non-seeing of the form-element up to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.”
“Because consciousness does not arise by taking the ear-element as its object, this is called ‘showing the characteristic of the ear-element’ because of not seeing the ear-element.

Because consciousness does not arise by taking the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, or the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition as its objects, this is called ‘showing the characteristics of the sound-element up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition’ because of not seeing the sound-element up to the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition.”
“Because consciousness arises without taking the nose-element as its object, this is called ‘showing the characteristic of the nose-element’ by way of not seeing the nose-element.

Because consciousness arises without taking the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, nose-contact, or the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition as their objects, this is called ‘showing the characteristics of the odor-element up to the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition’ by way of not seeing them.”

“Because consciousness does not arise by taking the tongue-element as its object, this is called ‘not seeing the tongue-element,’ and thus it is designated as the characteristic of the tongue-element.

Because consciousness does not arise by taking the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, or the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition as their objects, this is called ‘not seeing the taste-element’ up to ‘the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition,’ and thus it is designated as the characteristic of the taste-element up to the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition.”
“Because consciousness arises without taking the body-element as its object, this is called ‘not seeing the body-element,’ and thus it is designated as the characteristic of the body-element.

Because consciousness arises without taking the touch-element, the body-consciousness-element, body-contact, or the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition as their objects, this is called ‘not seeing the touch-element up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition,’ and thus it is designated as the characteristic of the touch-element up to the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition.”
"Because consciousness does not arise by taking the mind-element as its object, this is called 'indicating the characteristic of the mind-element' through the non-seeing of the mind-element.

Because consciousness does not arise by taking the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, mind-contact, or the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition as their objects, this is called 'indicating the characteristics of the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition' through the non-seeing of the dharma-element up to the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition."
“Because consciousness arises without taking the earth element as its object, this is called ‘showing the characteristic of the earth element’ by way of not seeing the earth element;

because consciousness arises without taking the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements as its objects, this is called ‘showing the characteristics of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements’ by way of not seeing the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements.”
"Because consciousness does not arise by taking ignorance as its condition, this is called 'not seeing ignorance,' and thus it is shown as the characteristic of ignorance;

because consciousness does not arise by taking volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, or old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair as their conditions, this is called 'not seeing volitional formations' up to 'not seeing old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair,' and thus it is shown as the characteristic of volitional formations up to old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair."

“Because consciousness does not arise by taking the perfection of generosity as its object, this is called ‘showing the characteristic of the perfection of generosity’ because the perfection of generosity is not seen;

because consciousness does not arise by taking the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom as its objects, this is called ‘showing the characteristics of ethical discipline through to wisdom’ because ethical discipline through to wisdom are not seen.”
“Because consciousness does not arise by taking internal emptiness as its object, this is called ‘showing the characteristic of internal emptiness’ because of not seeing internal emptiness.

Because consciousness does not arise by taking external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, emptiness of all phenomena, unapprehendable emptiness, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of own-nature, or emptiness of the own-nature of non-existence as its object, this is called ‘showing the characteristics of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the own-nature of non-existence’ because of not seeing external emptiness up to the emptiness of the own-nature of non-existence.”

"Because consciousness arises without taking True Suchness as its object, this is called 'indicating the characteristic of True Suchness' by virtue of not seeing True Suchness. Because consciousness arises without taking the Dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), non-illusory nature, unchanging nature, equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space, or the inconceivable realm as its objects, this is called 'indicating the characteristics of the Dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm' by virtue of not seeing the Dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm."

"Because consciousness does not arise by taking the Noble Truth of Suffering as its object, this is called 'not seeing' the Noble Truth of Suffering; it is for this reason that the characteristic of the Noble Truth of Suffering is demonstrated.

Because consciousness does not arise by taking the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path as their objects, this is called 'not seeing' the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path; it is for this reason that the characteristics of the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path are demonstrated."
"Because consciousness does not arise by taking the four dhyānas as its object, this is called 'showing the characteristics of the four dhyānas' because of not seeing the four dhyānas;

because consciousness does not arise by taking the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments as its object, this is called 'showing the characteristics of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments' because of not seeing the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments."

"Because consciousness does not arise by taking the eight liberations as its object, this is called 'showing the characteristics of the eight liberations' through the non-seeing of the eight liberations;

because consciousness does not arise by taking the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities as its objects, this is called 'showing the characteristics of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities' through the non-seeing of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities."

"Because consciousness does not arise by taking the four foundations of mindfulness as its object, this is called 'not seeing' the four foundations of mindfulness; it is for this reason that they are designated as the characteristics of the four foundations of mindfulness.

Because consciousness does not arise by taking the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path as its object, this is called 'not seeing' the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path; it is for this reason that they are designated as the characteristics of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path."

“Because consciousness arises without taking the liberation door of emptiness as its object, this is called ‘showing the characteristic of the liberation door of emptiness’ by way of not seeing the liberation door of emptiness;

because consciousness arises without taking the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness as their objects, this is called ‘showing the characteristics of the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness’ by way of not seeing the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness.”

"Because consciousness does not arise by taking the ten stages of a bodhisattva as its object, this is called 'not seeing' the ten stages of a bodhisattva; it is for this reason that they are said to manifest the characteristics of the ten stages of a bodhisattva."

"Because consciousness does not arise by taking the five eyes as its object, this is called 'not seeing the five eyes,' and thus it is termed the manifestation of the characteristics of the five eyes;

because consciousness does not arise by taking the six supernormal powers as its object, this is called 'not seeing the six supernormal powers,' and thus it is termed the manifestation of the characteristics of the six supernormal powers."
"Because consciousness does not arise by taking the ten powers of a Buddha as its object, this is called 'showing the characteristics of the ten powers of a Buddha' because of not seeing them.

Because consciousness does not arise by taking the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha as its objects, this is called 'showing the characteristics of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha' because of not seeing them."

“Because consciousness arises without taking the quality of non-forgetfulness as its object, this is called ‘showing the characteristic of non-forgetfulness’ because one does not perceive the quality of non-forgetfulness;

because consciousness arises without taking the state of constant equanimity as its object, this is called ‘showing the characteristic of constant equanimity’ because one does not perceive the state of constant equanimity.”
"Because consciousness does not arise by taking all-knowledge as its object, this is called 'indicating the characteristic of all-knowledge' because all-knowledge is not seen;

because consciousness does not arise by taking the knowledge of the aspects of the path or the knowledge of all aspects as its objects, this is called 'indicating the characteristic of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects' because the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are not seen."

"Because consciousness does not arise by taking all dharani-gates as its object, this is called 'not seeing all dharani-gates,' and is therefore termed the manifestation of the characteristics of all dharani-gates;

because consciousness does not arise by taking all samadhi-gates as its object, this is called 'not seeing all samadhi-gates,' and is therefore termed the manifestation of the characteristics of all samadhi-gates."

"Because consciousness does not arise by taking the fruit of stream-entry as its object, this is called 'indicating the characteristic of the fruit of stream-entry' because the fruit of stream-entry is not seen;

because consciousness does not arise by taking the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, or arhatship as its objects, this is called 'indicating the characteristics of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship' because those fruits are not seen."

"Because consciousness does not arise by taking solitary-buddha enlightenment as its object, this non-seeing of solitary-buddha enlightenment is called the manifestation of the characteristics of solitary-buddha enlightenment."

"Because consciousness does not arise by taking all bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices as its object, this is called 'not seeing all bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices,' and is thus termed the manifestation of the characteristics of all bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices."

"Because consciousness does not arise by taking the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas as its object, this is called 'not seeing' the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas; it is therefore termed the 'characteristic of demonstrating' the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas."
"Subhūti! By this meaning, the profound perfection of wisdom can reveal the true reality of the world to all Buddhas; therefore, it is called the Mother of all Buddhas."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

This profound *prajñāpāramitā* can reveal the emptiness of the world for all Buddhas; therefore, it is called the Mother of Buddhas, as it can demonstrate to all Buddhas the true reality of the world."
“World-Honored One!
How is it that the perfection of wisdom can manifest the emptiness of the world for all Buddhas? “Sudhana!
[The World-Honored One replied:]”

The profound *prajñāpāramitā* is able to reveal the emptiness of the world of form for all Buddhas; it reveals the emptiness of the worlds of sensation, perception, mental formations, and consciousness;
