they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s quiescent aspect of ignorance, and the world’s quiescent aspects of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair;

they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s quiescent aspect of the perfection of generosity, and the world’s quiescent aspects of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s sign of tranquility as internal emptiness; and the world’s sign of tranquility as external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, emptiness of the ultimate truth, emptiness of the conditioned, emptiness of the unconditioned, absolute emptiness, emptiness of the limitless, emptiness of dispersion, emptiness of non-alteration, emptiness of intrinsic nature, emptiness of specific characteristics, emptiness of common characteristics, emptiness of all phenomena, emptiness of the unapprehendable, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, and emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s quiescent aspect of true thusness (*tathatā*); the world’s quiescent aspect of the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), non-falsity (*avitathatā*), immutability (*ananyathābhāva*), equality (*samatā*), the nature of being free from birth (*niḥsaraṇatā*), the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*).

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s quiescent aspect of the noble truth of suffering (*duḥkha-āryasatya*), and the world’s quiescent aspects of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path (*samudaya-nirodha-mārga-āryasatya*).

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s quiescent aspect of the four dhyānas, and the world’s quiescent aspects of the four immeasurables (*apramāṇa*) and the four formless attainments (*ārūpyasamāpatti*).

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s aspect of tranquility within the eight liberations; the world’s aspect of tranquility within the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases;

they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s aspect of tranquility within the four foundations of mindfulness; the world’s aspect of tranquility within the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path;

they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s aspect of tranquility within the liberation door of emptiness, and the world’s aspect of tranquility within the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness.
It can demonstrate to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas the world’s sign of tranquility regarding the ten stages;
it can demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s sign of tranquility regarding the five eyes and the six supernormal powers;

it can demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s sign of tranquility regarding the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s sign of tranquility as the quality of non-forgetfulness; the world’s sign of tranquility as the constant abiding in equanimity;

they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s sign of tranquility as omniscience (*sarvajñatā*); the world’s sign of tranquility as the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*);
they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s sign of tranquility as all doors of dhāraṇī and all doors of samādhi.

It can demonstrate to all Buddhas the sign of worldly tranquility of the fruit of stream-entry; it can demonstrate the sign of worldly tranquility of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship;
it can demonstrate to all Buddhas the sign of worldly tranquility of the awakening of the solitary buddhas (pratyekabuddha);
and it can demonstrate to all Buddhas the sign of worldly tranquility of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
"It can demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s aspect of tranquility within the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas. Subhūti!
By such a meaning, the profound perfection of wisdom can demonstrate the true aspect of the world to all Buddhas; it is therefore called the Mother of all Buddhas."

“Furthermore, Subhūti, the profound perfection of wisdom can reveal to all Buddhas the mark of the ultimate emptiness of the world; it is called the mother of all Buddhas, for it can reveal to all Buddhas the true mark of the world.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that the perfection of wisdom can demonstrate to all Buddhas the ultimate mark of emptiness of the world? “Subhūti!

The profound *prajñāpāramitā* can demonstrate to all Buddhas the ultimate emptiness of the world of form (*rūpa*), and the ultimate emptiness of the worlds of feeling (*vedanā*), perception (*saṃjñā*), mental formations (*saṃskāra*), and consciousness (*vijñāna*);

it can demonstrate to all Buddhas the ultimate emptiness of the world of the eye-base (*cakṣur-āyatana*), and the ultimate emptiness of the worlds of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases (*śrotra-, ghrāṇa-, jihvā-, kāya-, mana-āyatana*);

it can demonstrate to all Buddhas the ultimate emptiness of the world of the form-object (*rūpa-āyatana*), and the ultimate emptiness of the worlds of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental objects (*śabda-, gandha-, rasa-, spraṣṭavya-, dharma-āyatana*).

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the world of the eye-element is ultimately empty in nature; that the world of the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and the various sensations produced with eye-contact as a condition are ultimately empty in nature.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the world of the ear-element is ultimately empty in nature; that the world of the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and the various sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition are ultimately empty in nature.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the world of the nose-element is ultimately empty in nature; that the world of the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, nose-contact, and the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition are ultimately empty in nature.

They are able to demonstrate that for all Buddhas, the world of the tongue-element is ultimately empty; the world of the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition are ultimately empty.

They are able to demonstrate that for all Buddhas, the world of the body-element is ultimately empty; the world of the tangible-object-element, the body-consciousness-element, body-contact, and all sensations produced with body-contact as a condition are ultimately empty.

They are able to demonstrate that for all Buddhas, the world of the mind-element is ultimately empty; the world of the mental-object-element, the mind-consciousness-element, mind-contact, and all sensations produced with mind-contact as a condition are ultimately empty.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the world of the earth element is ultimately empty in nature; they are able to demonstrate that the worlds of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are ultimately empty in nature;

they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the world of ignorance is ultimately empty in nature; they are able to demonstrate that the worlds of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, sensation, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are ultimately empty in nature;

and they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the world of the perfection of generosity is ultimately empty in nature, as are the worlds of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom—all of which are ultimately empty in nature.

He is able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the ultimate emptiness of the world through internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, ultimate emptiness, boundless emptiness, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self-characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—all of which constitute the ultimate emptiness of the world.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the ultimate emptiness of the world’s marks of true thusness (*tathatā*); the ultimate emptiness of the world’s marks of the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), non-falsity, immutability, equality, freedom from birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm;

they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the ultimate emptiness of the world’s marks of the Noble Truth of Suffering, and the ultimate emptiness of the world’s marks of the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path;

they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the ultimate emptiness of the world’s marks of the four meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*), the four immeasurables (*apramāṇa*), and the four formless attainments (*ārūpyasamāpatti*).

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the ultimate emptiness of the world regarding the eight liberations; they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the ultimate emptiness of the world regarding the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities;

they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the ultimate emptiness of the world regarding the four foundations of mindfulness; they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the ultimate emptiness of the world regarding the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path;
they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the ultimate emptiness of the world regarding the liberation door of emptiness, and the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness.
It can demonstrate that the ten stages (*daśabhūmi*) of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas are the ultimate emptiness of the world;
it can demonstrate that the five eyes (*pañcacakṣus*) of all Buddhas and the six supernormal powers (*ṣaḍabhijñā*) are the ultimate emptiness of the world;

it can demonstrate that the ten powers (*daśabala*) of all Buddhas, the four fearlessnesses (*catvāri vaiśāradyāni*), the four analytical knowledges (*catasraḥ pratisamvidah*), great loving-kindness (*mahāmaitrī*), great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*), great sympathetic joy (*mahāmuditā*), great equanimity (*mahopekṣā*), and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇikabuddhadharma*) are the ultimate emptiness of the world.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s ultimate emptiness in the quality of non-forgetfulness; they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s ultimate emptiness in the nature of equanimity;

they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s ultimate emptiness in omniscience (*sarvajñatā*); they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s ultimate emptiness in the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*);
they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s ultimate emptiness in all doors of dhāraṇī and all doors of samādhi.

It can demonstrate to all Buddhas that the fruit of stream-entry in the world is ultimately empty; it can demonstrate to all Buddhas that the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship in the world are ultimately empty;
it can demonstrate to all Buddhas that the enlightenment of the solitary buddhas in the world is ultimately empty;
and it can demonstrate to all Buddhas that the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas in the world are ultimately empty.
"It can demonstrate to all Buddhas the ultimate mark of emptiness of the world within the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas. Subhūti!
By such a principle, the profound *prajñāpāramitā* can demonstrate the true reality of the world to all Buddhas; therefore, it is named the Mother of all Buddhas."

"Furthermore, Subhūti! This profound prajñāpāramitā can reveal to all Buddhas the mark of the emptiness of the lack of intrinsic nature in the world; it is called the Mother of all Buddhas, for it can reveal to all Buddhas the true reality of the world."
“World-Honored One!
How is it that the perfection of wisdom can demonstrate to all Buddhas the mark of the emptiness of the lack of intrinsic nature in the world? “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

The profound *prajñāpāramitā* can reveal to all Buddhas the mark of the emptiness of the lack of intrinsic nature in the world of form (*rūpa-loka*), and the mark of the emptiness of the lack of intrinsic nature in the worlds of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness (*vedanā-saṃjñā-saṃskāra-vijñāna*);

it can reveal to all Buddhas the mark of the emptiness of the lack of intrinsic nature in the world of the sense-base of the eye (*cakṣur-āyatana*), and the marks of the emptiness of the lack of intrinsic nature in the worlds of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind;

it can reveal to all Buddhas the mark of the emptiness of the lack of intrinsic nature in the world of the sense-object of form (*rūpa-āyatana*), and the marks of the emptiness of the lack of intrinsic nature in the worlds of the sense-objects of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and phenomena (*śabda-gandha-rasa-spraṣṭavya-dharma*).

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the eye-element is the world’s mark of emptiness due to the absence of intrinsic nature; that the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are the world’s mark of emptiness due to the absence of intrinsic nature.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the ear-element is the world’s mark of emptiness due to the absence of intrinsic nature; that the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are the world’s mark of emptiness due to the absence of intrinsic nature.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the nose-element is the world’s mark of emptiness due to the absence of intrinsic nature; that the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are the world’s mark of emptiness due to the absence of intrinsic nature.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the tongue-element (*jihvā-dhātu*) is the world’s mark of emptiness due to the absence of intrinsic nature; that the taste-element (*rasa-dhātu*), the tongue-consciousness-element (*jihvā-vijñāna-dhātu*), tongue-contact (*jihvā-saṃsparśa*), and all sensations (*vedanā*) produced with tongue-contact as a condition are the world’s mark of emptiness due to the absence of intrinsic nature;

they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the body-element (*kāya-dhātu*) is the world’s mark of emptiness due to the absence of intrinsic nature; that the tangible-object-element (*spraṣṭavya-dhātu*), the body-consciousness-element (*kāya-vijñāna-dhātu*), body-contact (*kāya-saṃsparśa*), and all sensations produced with body-contact as a condition are the world’s mark of emptiness due to the absence of intrinsic nature;

and they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the mind-element (*mano-dhātu*) is the world’s mark of emptiness due to the absence of intrinsic nature; that the mental-object-element (*dharma-dhātu*), the mind-consciousness-element (*mano-vijñāna-dhātu*), mind-contact (*manaḥ-saṃsparśa*), and all sensations produced with mind-contact as a condition are the world’s mark of emptiness due to the absence of intrinsic nature.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world of the earth element as being empty of intrinsic nature, and the worlds of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements as being empty of intrinsic nature;

they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world of ignorance as being empty of intrinsic nature, and the worlds of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair as being empty of intrinsic nature;

they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world of the perfection of generosity as being empty of intrinsic nature, and the worlds of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom as being empty of intrinsic nature.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s mark of the emptiness of intrinsic nature: the emptiness of the internal, the emptiness of the external, the emptiness of the internal and external, the emptiness of emptiness, the great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of the conditioned, the emptiness of the unconditioned, the absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of essential nature, the emptiness of self-characteristic, the emptiness of common characteristic, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of the absence of nature, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the absence of nature—the world’s mark of the emptiness of intrinsic nature.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s mark of emptiness through the absence of intrinsic nature (*niḥsvabhāva*) in True Suchness (*tathatā*); they are able to demonstrate the world’s mark of emptiness through the absence of intrinsic nature in the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the non-erroneous nature, the unchanging nature, the nature of equality, the nature free from birth, the fixedness of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm;

they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s mark of emptiness through the absence of intrinsic nature in the Noble Truth of Suffering, and the world’s mark of emptiness through the absence of intrinsic nature in the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path;

they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s mark of emptiness through the absence of intrinsic nature in the four meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*), and the world’s mark of emptiness through the absence of intrinsic nature in the four immeasurables (*apramāṇa*) and the four formless attainments (*ārūpyasamāpatti*).

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s mark of emptiness regarding the lack of intrinsic nature in the eight liberations; they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s mark of emptiness regarding the lack of intrinsic nature in the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities;

they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s mark of emptiness regarding the lack of intrinsic nature in the four foundations of mindfulness; they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s mark of emptiness regarding the lack of intrinsic nature in the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path;

they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s mark of emptiness regarding the lack of intrinsic nature in the liberation door of emptiness, and the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness.
It can demonstrate to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas the world’s mark of emptiness regarding the lack of intrinsic nature in the ten stages;
it can demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s mark of emptiness regarding the lack of intrinsic nature in the five eyes,

the six supernormal powers, the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s mark of emptiness regarding the naturelessness of the quality of non-forgetfulness; they are able to demonstrate the world’s mark of emptiness regarding the naturelessness of the constant abiding in equanimity;

they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s mark of emptiness regarding the naturelessness of all-knowledge; they are able to demonstrate the world’s mark of emptiness regarding the naturelessness of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects;
they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s mark of emptiness regarding the naturelessness of all doors of dhāraṇī and all doors of samādhi.

It can demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s mark of the emptiness of intrinsic nature regarding the fruit of stream-entry; it can demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s mark of the emptiness of intrinsic nature regarding the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship;
it can demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s mark of the emptiness of intrinsic nature regarding the enlightenment of pratyekabuddhas;
and it can demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s mark of the emptiness of intrinsic nature regarding the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
It can demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s characteristic of emptiness due to the absence of intrinsic nature within the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas. "Subhūti!
By such a meaning, the profound perfection of wisdom can demonstrate the true reality of the world to all Buddhas, and is thus named the Mother of all Buddhas."
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Volume Three Hundred and Seven;
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Volume Three Hundred and Eight.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang under Imperial Decree.
Chapter Forty-one, Part Four: The Mother of Buddhas.

"Furthermore, Subhūti, this profound *prajñāpāramitā* can reveal to all Buddhas the mark of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the world; it is called the Mother of all Buddhas, for it can reveal to all Buddhas the true reality of the world."
“World-Honored One!
How is it that the perfection of wisdom can demonstrate to all Buddhas the mark of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the world?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

The profound *prajñāpāramitā* can reveal to all Buddhas the mark of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the world of form; it reveals the mark of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the worlds of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.

It can reveal to all Buddhas the mark of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the world of the eye-base; it reveals the mark of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the worlds of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases.

It can reveal to all Buddhas the mark of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the world of the form-object; it reveals the mark of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the worlds of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental objects.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the world’s own-nature is empty in the eye-element, and that the world’s own-nature is empty in the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and all sensations produced with eye-contact as a condition;

they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the world’s own-nature is empty in the ear-element, and that the world’s own-nature is empty in the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and all sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition;

they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the world’s own-nature is empty in the nose-element, and that the world’s own-nature is empty in the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, nose-contact, and all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the world of the tongue-element has the characteristic of being empty of intrinsic nature; that the world of the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition have the characteristic of being empty of intrinsic nature;

they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the world of the body-element has the characteristic of being empty of intrinsic nature; that the world of the touch-element, the body-consciousness-element, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition have the characteristic of being empty of intrinsic nature;

and they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the world of the mind-element has the characteristic of being empty of intrinsic nature; that the world of the mental-object-element, the mind-consciousness-element, mind-contact, and the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition have the characteristic of being empty of intrinsic nature.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s own-nature of emptiness regarding the element of earth, and the world’s own-nature of emptiness regarding the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness;

they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s own-nature of emptiness regarding ignorance, and the world’s own-nature of emptiness regarding volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair;

they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s own-nature of emptiness regarding the perfection of generosity, and the world’s own-nature of emptiness regarding the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s characteristic of self-nature emptiness: the emptiness of the internal, the emptiness of the external, the emptiness of both internal and external, the emptiness of emptiness, the great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of the conditioned, the emptiness of the unconditioned, the absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of essential nature, the emptiness of self-characteristic, the emptiness of common characteristic, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of self-nature, and the emptiness of the self-nature of non-existence—the world’s characteristic of self-nature emptiness.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s own-nature of emptiness as the characteristic of *tathatā* (suchness), the *dharmadhātu*, *dharmatā*, non-illusory nature, unchanging nature, equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharma-sthititā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharma-vyavasthāna*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of empty space, and the inconceivable realm;

they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s own-nature of emptiness as the characteristic of the Noble Truth of Suffering, and the world’s own-nature of emptiness as the characteristics of the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path;

they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s own-nature of emptiness as the characteristic of the four *dhyānas*, and the world’s own-nature of emptiness as the characteristic of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s own-nature mark of emptiness regarding the eight liberations; they are able to demonstrate the world’s own-nature mark of emptiness regarding the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities;

they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s own-nature mark of emptiness regarding the four foundations of mindfulness; they are able to demonstrate the world’s own-nature mark of emptiness regarding the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path;

they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s own-nature mark of emptiness regarding the liberation door of emptiness, and the world’s own-nature mark of emptiness regarding the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness.
It can demonstrate that the world’s own nature is empty in the ten stages of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas;
it can demonstrate that the world’s own nature is empty in the five eyes of the Buddhas and the six supernormal powers;

it can demonstrate that the world’s own nature is empty in the ten powers of the Buddhas, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s mark of intrinsic emptiness as the quality of non-forgetfulness; they demonstrate the world’s mark of intrinsic emptiness as the nature of constant abiding in equanimity;

they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s mark of intrinsic emptiness as omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), the world’s mark of intrinsic emptiness as the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*);
and they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s mark of intrinsic emptiness as all doors of dhāraṇī and all doors of samādhi.

It can demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s intrinsic emptiness of the fruit of stream-entry; it can demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s intrinsic emptiness of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship;
it can demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s intrinsic emptiness of the enlightenment of pratyekabuddhas;
and it can demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s intrinsic emptiness of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
"It can demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s characteristic of being empty of intrinsic nature within their unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. Subhūti!
By such a principle, the profound *prajñāpāramitā* can demonstrate to all Buddhas the true reality of the world; therefore, it is called the Mother of all Buddhas."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

This profound prajñāpāramitā can reveal to all Buddhas the mark of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the non-existence of the world; it is called the Mother of all Buddhas, for it can reveal to all Buddhas the true reality of the world."
“World-Honored One!
How is it that the perfection of wisdom can demonstrate to all Buddhas the mark of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the lack of intrinsic nature in the world? “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

The profound *prajñāpāramitā* can reveal to all Buddhas the mark of the emptiness of the lack of intrinsic nature and of intrinsic nature in the world of form; it reveals the mark of the emptiness of the lack of intrinsic nature and of intrinsic nature in the worlds of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.

It can reveal to all Buddhas the mark of the emptiness of the lack of intrinsic nature and of intrinsic nature in the world of the eye-base; it reveals the mark of the emptiness of the lack of intrinsic nature and of intrinsic nature in the worlds of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases.

It can reveal to all Buddhas the mark of the emptiness of the lack of intrinsic nature and of intrinsic nature in the world of the form-base; it reveals the mark of the emptiness of the lack of intrinsic nature and of intrinsic nature in the worlds of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental objects.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the eye-element is a world characterized by the emptiness of the lack of intrinsic nature and intrinsic existence; that the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, and eye-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, are worlds characterized by the emptiness of the lack of intrinsic nature and intrinsic existence.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the ear-element is a world characterized by the emptiness of the lack of intrinsic nature and intrinsic existence; that the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, and ear-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, are worlds characterized by the emptiness of the lack of intrinsic nature and intrinsic existence.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the nose-element is a world characterized by the emptiness of the lack of intrinsic nature and intrinsic existence; that the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, and nose-contact, as well as the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, are worlds characterized by the emptiness of the lack of intrinsic nature and intrinsic existence.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the tongue-element of the world has the characteristic of emptiness regarding its lack of intrinsic nature; they are able to demonstrate that the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and the various sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition have the characteristic of emptiness regarding their lack of intrinsic nature in the world;

they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the body-element of the world has the characteristic of emptiness regarding its lack of intrinsic nature; they are able to demonstrate that the tangible-object-element, the body-consciousness-element, body-contact, and the various sensations produced with body-contact as a condition have the characteristic of emptiness regarding their lack of intrinsic nature in the world;

they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the mind-element of the world has the characteristic of emptiness regarding its lack of intrinsic nature; and they are able to demonstrate that the mental-object-element, the mind-consciousness-element, mind-contact, and the various sensations produced with mind-contact as a condition have the characteristic of emptiness regarding their lack of intrinsic nature in the world.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world of the earth element as being without intrinsic nature and having the characteristic of emptiness; they are able to demonstrate the worlds of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements as being without intrinsic nature and having the characteristic of emptiness.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world of ignorance as being without intrinsic nature and having the characteristic of emptiness; they are able to demonstrate the worlds of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair as being without intrinsic nature and having the characteristic of emptiness.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world of the perfection of generosity as being without intrinsic nature and having the characteristic of emptiness; they are able to demonstrate the worlds of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom as being without intrinsic nature and having the characteristic of emptiness.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the characteristic of the emptiness of the internal world and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature; as well as the emptiness of the external, the emptiness of the internal and external, the emptiness of emptiness, the great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of the conditioned, the emptiness of the unconditioned, the absolute emptiness, the boundless emptiness, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of essential nature, the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature—the characteristic of the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature in the world.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s mark of the emptiness of the non-existence and intrinsic nature of true suchness; they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s mark of the emptiness of the non-existence and intrinsic nature of the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, the nature of equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm;

they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s mark of the emptiness of the non-existence and intrinsic nature of the noble truth of suffering, and the world’s mark of the emptiness of the non-existence and intrinsic nature of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path;

they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s mark of the emptiness of the non-existence and intrinsic nature of the four meditative concentrations, and the world’s mark of the emptiness of the non-existence and intrinsic nature of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s mark of the emptiness of the self-nature of non-substantiality regarding the eight liberations; they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s mark of the emptiness of the self-nature of non-substantiality regarding the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten pervasive bases;

they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s mark of the emptiness of the self-nature of non-substantiality regarding the four foundations of mindfulness; they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s mark of the emptiness of the self-nature of non-substantiality regarding the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path;

they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s mark of the emptiness of the self-nature of non-substantiality regarding the liberation door of emptiness; and they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s mark of the emptiness of the self-nature of non-substantiality regarding the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness.
It can demonstrate to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas the world’s mark of the emptiness of the non-existence and self-nature of the ten stages;

it can demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s mark of the emptiness of the non-existence and self-nature of the five eyes, and the world’s mark of the emptiness of the non-existence and self-nature of the six supernormal powers;

it can demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s mark of the emptiness of the non-existence and self-nature of the ten powers of a Buddha, as well as the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s mark of the emptiness of the nature of non-nature regarding the quality of non-forgetfulness; they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s mark of the emptiness of the nature of non-nature regarding the state of constant abiding in equanimity;

they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s mark of the emptiness of the nature of non-nature regarding omniscience (*sarvajñatā*); they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s mark of the emptiness of the nature of non-nature regarding the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*);
they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s mark of the emptiness of the nature of non-nature regarding all doors of dhāraṇī and all doors of samādhi.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the mark of the emptiness of the non-existence and intrinsic nature of the world regarding the fruit of stream-entry; they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the mark of the emptiness of the non-existence and intrinsic nature of the world regarding the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship;
they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the mark of the emptiness of the non-existence and intrinsic nature of the world regarding the awakening of the pratyekabuddhas;
and they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the mark of the emptiness of the non-existence and intrinsic nature of the world regarding the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
"It can demonstrate to all Buddhas the mark of the emptiness of the self-nature of the lack of nature in the world—the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas. Subhūti!
By such a principle, this profound perfection of wisdom can demonstrate the true reality of the world to all Buddhas; therefore, it is named the Mother of all Buddhas."

"Furthermore, Subhūti! This profound prajñāpāramitā can reveal to all Buddhas the purely empty characteristic of the world; it is named the Mother of all Buddhas, for it can reveal to all Buddhas the true characteristic of the world."
“World-Honored One!
How is it that the perfection of wisdom can demonstrate to all Buddhas the purely empty characteristic of the world?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

The profound *prajñāpāramitā* can demonstrate to all Buddhas that the world of form (*rūpa*) is purely empty in its nature; it demonstrates that the worlds of feeling (*vedanā*), perception (*saṃjñā*), mental formations (*saṃskāra*), and consciousness (*vijñāna*) are purely empty in their nature.

It can demonstrate to all Buddhas that the world of the eye-base (*cakṣur-āyatana*) is purely empty in its nature; it demonstrates that the worlds of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases (*śrotra-, ghrāṇa-, jihvā-, kāya-, mana-āyatana*) are purely empty in their nature.

It can demonstrate to all Buddhas that the world of the form-object (*rūpa-āyatana*) is purely empty in its nature; it demonstrates that the worlds of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental objects (*śabda-, gandha-, rasa-, spraṣṭavya-, dharma-āyatana*) are purely empty in their nature.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the eye-element is a world characterized by absolute emptiness; that the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and the various sensations produced with eye-contact as a condition are worlds characterized by absolute emptiness.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the ear-element is a world characterized by absolute emptiness; that the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and the various sensations produced with ear-contact as a condition are worlds characterized by absolute emptiness.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the nose-element is a world characterized by absolute emptiness; that the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, nose-contact, and the various sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition are worlds characterized by absolute emptiness.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the world of the tongue-element has the characteristic of being purely empty; that the world of the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition have the characteristic of being purely empty;

they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the world of the body-element has the characteristic of being purely empty; that the world of the tangible-object-element, the body-consciousness-element, body-contact, and all sensations produced with body-contact as a condition have the characteristic of being purely empty;

and they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the world of the mind-element has the characteristic of being purely empty; that the world of the mental-object-element, the mind-consciousness-element, mind-contact, and all sensations produced with mind-contact as a condition have the characteristic of being purely empty.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the world of the earth element is purely empty in nature, and that the worlds of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are purely empty in nature;

they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the world of ignorance is purely empty in nature, and that the worlds of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are purely empty in nature;

they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the world of the perfection of generosity is purely empty in nature, and that the worlds of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are purely empty in nature.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s exclusively empty characteristics of internal emptiness, as well as the world’s exclusively empty characteristics of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the purely empty aspect of the world as true thusness (*tathatā*), as well as the purely empty aspects of the world as the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), the dharma-nature (*dharmatā*), the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, the equality, the nature free from arising, the fixedness of dharma (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of dharma (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm;

they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the purely empty aspect of the world as the noble truth of suffering (*duḥkha-āryasatya*), and the purely empty aspects of the world as the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path;

they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the purely empty aspect of the world as the four meditative absorptions (*catur-dhyāna*), and the purely empty aspects of the world as the four immeasurables (*catur-apramāṇa*) and the four formless attainments (*catasra ārūpyasamāpattayaḥ*).

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s exclusively empty characteristic of the eight liberations; they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s exclusively empty characteristic of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities;

they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s exclusively empty characteristic of the four foundations of mindfulness; they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s exclusively empty characteristic of the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path;

they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world’s exclusively empty characteristic of the liberation door of emptiness, and the world’s exclusively empty characteristic of the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness.
They are able to demonstrate that the world of the ten stages of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas is purely empty;
they are able to demonstrate that the world of the five eyes of all Buddhas is purely empty, and that the world of the six supernormal powers is purely empty;

they are able to demonstrate that the world of the ten powers of all Buddhas is purely empty, and that the world of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is purely empty.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world as a purely empty characteristic of the quality of non-forgetfulness; they demonstrate the world as a purely empty characteristic of the constant abiding in equanimity;

they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world as a purely empty characteristic of omniscience (*sarvajñatā*); they demonstrate the world as a purely empty characteristic of the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*);
they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the world as a purely empty characteristic of all doors of dhāraṇī and all doors of samādhi.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the world of the fruit of stream-entry (*srotāpatti-phala*) is purely empty in nature; they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the worlds of the fruit of once-returning (*sakṛdāgāmin*), non-returning (*anāgāmin*), and arhatship (*arhat-phala*) are purely empty in nature;
they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the world of the solitary buddha’s awakening (*pratyekabuddha-bodhi*) is purely empty in nature;
and they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the world of the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is purely empty in nature.
"It can demonstrate to all Buddhas the world's characteristic of being purely empty within the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas. Subhūti!
By such a meaning, the profound perfection of wisdom can demonstrate the true characteristic of the world to all Buddhas; it is therefore named the Mother of all Buddhas."

"Furthermore, Subhūti! This profound prajñāpāramitā can demonstrate to all Buddhas that the world is purely characterized by signlessness and wishlessness; it is called the mother of all Buddhas, for it can demonstrate the true reality of the world to all Buddhas."
“World-Honored One!
How is it that the perfection of wisdom can demonstrate to all Buddhas that the world is purely characterized by signlessness and wishlessness?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

The profound *prajñāpāramitā* can demonstrate to all Buddhas that the world of form (*rūpa*) is purely characterized by signlessness (*animitta*) and wishlessness (*apraṇihita*); that the worlds of feeling (*vedanā*), perception (*saṃjñā*), mental formations (*saṃskāra*), and consciousness (*vijñāna*) are purely characterized by signlessness and wishlessness;

it can demonstrate to all Buddhas that the world of the eye-base (*cakṣur-āyatana*) is purely characterized by signlessness and wishlessness, and that the worlds of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases (*śrotra-, ghrāṇa-, jihvā-, kāya-, mana-āyatana*) are purely characterized by signlessness and wishlessness;

it can demonstrate to all Buddhas that the world of the form-object (*rūpa-āyatana*) is purely characterized by signlessness and wishlessness, and that the worlds of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental objects (*śabda-, gandha-, rasa-, spraṣṭavya-, dharma-āyatana*) are purely characterized by signlessness and wishlessness.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the world of the eye-element is purely signless and wishless; that the world of the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition is purely signless and wishless.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the world of the ear-element is purely signless and wishless; that the world of the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition is purely signless and wishless.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the world of the nose-element is purely signless and wishless; that the world of the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition is purely signless and wishless.

They are able to demonstrate that for all Buddhas, the world of the tongue-element is purely signless and wishless; the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, as well as tongue-contact and the various sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition, are worlds that are purely signless and wishless.

They are able to demonstrate that for all Buddhas, the world of the body-element is purely signless and wishless; the touch-element, the body-consciousness-element, as well as body-contact and the various sensations produced with body-contact as a condition, are worlds that are purely signless and wishless.

They are able to demonstrate that for all Buddhas, the world of the mind-element is purely signless and wishless; the mental-object-element, the mind-consciousness-element, as well as mind-contact and the various sensations produced with mind-contact as a condition, are worlds that are purely signless and wishless.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the world of the earth element is purely signless and wishless; the worlds of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are purely signless and wishless.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the world of ignorance is purely signless and wishless; the worlds of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are purely signless and wishless.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the world of the perfection of generosity is purely signless and wishless; the worlds of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are purely signless and wishless.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the world is purely characterized by signlessness and wishlessness through internal emptiness; and through external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature—wherein the world is purely characterized by signlessness and wishlessness.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the world of True Suchness is purely characterized by signlessness and wishlessness; that the world of the Dharma-realm, the Dharma-nature, non-falsity, immutability, equality, the nature of transcendence from birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of empty space, and the inconceivable realm is purely characterized by signlessness and wishlessness;

they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the Noble Truth of Suffering is purely characterized by signlessness and wishlessness, and that the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path are purely characterized by signlessness and wishlessness;

they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the four dhyānas are purely characterized by signlessness and wishlessness, and that the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are purely characterized by signlessness and wishlessness.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the eight liberations of the world are purely characterized by signlessness and wishlessness; they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten universal bases of the world are purely characterized by signlessness and wishlessness;

they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the four foundations of mindfulness of the world are purely characterized by signlessness and wishlessness; they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eight branches of the noble path of the world are purely characterized by signlessness and wishlessness;

they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the door of liberation of emptiness of the world is purely characterized by signlessness and wishlessness, and that the doors of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness of the world are purely characterized by signlessness and wishlessness.
They are able to demonstrate that the world of the ten stages of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas is purely signless and wishless;
they are able to demonstrate that the world of the five eyes of all Buddhas is purely signless and wishless, and that the world of the six supernormal powers is purely signless and wishless;

they are able to demonstrate that the world of the ten powers of all Buddhas is purely signless and wishless, as well as the world of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, which are purely signless and wishless.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the quality of non-forgetfulness as being purely signless and wishless in the world; they are able to demonstrate that the world of constant abiding in equanimity is purely signless and wishless;

they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas the knowledge of all things (*sarvajñatā*) as being purely signless and wishless in the world; they are able to demonstrate that the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are purely signless and wishless in the world;
they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas all doors of dhāraṇī as being purely signless and wishless in the world, and all doors of samādhi as being purely signless and wishless in the world.

They are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the world of the fruit of stream-entry is purely characterized by signlessness and wishlessness; they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the worlds of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are purely characterized by signlessness and wishlessness;
they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the world of pratyekabuddha enlightenment is purely characterized by signlessness and wishlessness;
and they are able to demonstrate to all Buddhas that the world of all bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices is purely characterized by signlessness and wishlessness.
"It can demonstrate to all Buddhas that the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is in this world characterized solely by signlessness and wishlessness. Subhūti!
By such a principle, the profound *prajñāpāramitā* can demonstrate the true reality of the world to all Buddhas; therefore, it is named the Mother of all Buddhas."

"Furthermore, Subhūti, the profound *prajñāpāramitā* is that which can demonstrate the characteristics of the world to all Buddhas; that is to say, it causes one not to give rise to the notion of this world or the notion of another world."
Why is this? Because, in reality, there is no dharma that can give rise to the conceptualization of "this world" or "another world.
Chapter 42: On the Inconceivable, etc., Part One, Section 42-1. At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
This profound prajñāpāramitā appears in the world for the sake of a great matter.
World-Honored One!”
The profound *prajñāpāramitā* appears in the world for the sake of inconceivable matters.
"World-Honored One!
The profound *prajñāpāramitā* appears in the world for the sake of immeasurable matters."
“World-Honored One!
This profound *prajñāpāramitā* appears in the world for the sake of immeasurable matters.
World-Honored One!”
"The profound Prajñāpāramitā appears in the world for the sake of that which is unequaled.
The Buddha said,
"Suvikrāntavikrāmin!..."
So it is! So it is! It is just as you have said.
The profound perfection of wisdom appears in the world for a great purpose;
the profound perfection of wisdom appears in the world for an inconceivable purpose.
The profound perfection of wisdom appears in the world for the sake of matters that are immeasurable.
The profound perfection of wisdom appears in the world for the sake of matters that are incalculable.
The profound *prajñāpāramitā* appears in the world for the sake of that which is unequaled.
"World-Honored One,
in what way does the profound *prajñāpāramitā* appear in the world for the sake of a great task?"

“Subhūti! All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas take as their great task the universal rescue and deliverance of all sentient beings, never abandoning them for even a moment; it is for this great task that the profound Prajñāpāramitā appears in the world.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that the profound perfection of wisdom appears in the world for the sake of inconceivable matters? “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

The buddha-nature, tathāgata-nature, the nature of self-arisen dharma, and the nature of the wisdom of all-knowledge belonging to all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas are all inconceivable matters; it is for the sake of these inconceivable matters that the profound Prajñāpāramitā appears in the world.
“World-Honored One!
How is it that the profound *prajñāpāramitā* appears in the world for the sake of an immeasurable matter? “Subhūti!

The Buddha-nature, Tathāgata-nature, natural dharma-nature, and the nature of the knowledge of all-knowledge belonging to all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas cannot be measured by any sentient beings; it is for this immeasurable purpose that the profound Prajñāpāramitā appears in the world.
“World-Honored One!
In what way does the profound perfection of wisdom appear in the world for the sake of immeasurable matters? “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

Regarding all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas—their Buddha-nature, Tathāgata-nature, the nature of self-arisen phenomena, and the nature of the wisdom of omniscience—there is no one who can truly know their measure; it is for the sake of these immeasurable matters that the profound Prajñāpāramitā appears in the world.
“World-Honored One!
How is it that the profound perfection of wisdom appears in the world for the sake of the task of the unequaled? “Subhūti!

The buddha-nature, tathāgata-nature, nature of self-arisen dharma, and nature of the knowledge of all-knowledge possessed by all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, has no equal; how much less could there be anyone who surpasses it!
"The profound perfection of wisdom appears in the world for the sake of this peerless task.
The Venerable Subhūti then addressed the Buddha again, saying,
"World-Honored One!"

Is it only the Buddha-nature, Tathāgata-nature, self-arisen dharma-nature, and the nature of all-knowledge of the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas that is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled, or are there other dharmas as well?
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

It is not only the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha; rather, all the Buddha-nature, the Tathāgata-nature, the nature of self-arisen dharma, and the nature of the knowledge of all modes are inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled.”

“Subhūti! Form is also inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled; feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are also inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled.”

"Subhūti! The eye base is also inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled; the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind bases are also inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled."

“Subhūti! The sphere of form is also inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled; the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are also inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled.”

“Subhūti! The eye constituent is also inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled; the form constituent, the eye-consciousness constituent, and eye-contact, as well as all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, are also inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled.”

“Subhūti! The ear element is also inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled; the sound element, the ear-consciousness element, as well as ear-contact and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, are also inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled.”

“Subhūti! The nose element (*ghrāṇadhātu*) is also inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled; the odor element (*gandhadhātu*), the nose-consciousness element (*ghrāṇavijñānadhātu*), as well as nose-contact (*ghrāṇasparśa*) and the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with nose-contact as a condition, are also inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled.”

“Subhūti! The tongue element is also inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled; the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are also inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled.”

“Subhūti! The body element (*kāyadhātu*) is also inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled; the object-element of touch (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*), the body-consciousness element (*kāyavijñānadhātu*), as well as body-contact (*kāyasparśa*) and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, are also inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled.”

“Subhūti! The mind-element (manodhātu) is also inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled; the dharma-element (dharmadhātu), the mind-consciousness-element (manovijñānadhātu), as well as mind-contact (manaḥsaṃsparśa) and the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition, are also inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled.”

“Subhūti! The earth element is also inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled; the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are also inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled.”

“Subhūti! Ignorance is also inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled; likewise, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are also inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled.”

“Subhūti! The perfection of generosity is also inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled; the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are likewise inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled.”

“Subhūti! “Subhūti! “Subhūti! The noble truth of suffering is also inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled; the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are also inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled.”

“Subhūti! The four dhyānas are also inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled; the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are also inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled.”

"Subhūti! The eight liberations are also inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled; the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities are also inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled."

“Subhūti! The four applications of mindfulness are also inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled; the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are also inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled.”

“Subhūti! The gate of liberation of emptiness is also inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled; the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are also inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled.”
“Subhūti! The ten stages of a bodhisattva are likewise inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled. Subhūti!”
The five eyes are likewise inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled; the six supernormal powers are likewise inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled.

"Subhūti! The ten powers of a Buddha are also inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled; likewise, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are also inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled."

“Subhūti! The quality of non-forgetfulness is also inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled; the state of constant abiding in equanimity is also inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled.”

“Subhūti! All-knowledge (sarvajñatā) is also inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled; the knowledge of the paths (mārgākārajñatā) and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā) are also inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled.”
“Subhūti! All dhāraṇī-doors are likewise inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled; all samādhi-doors are likewise inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled.”

“Subhūti! The fruit of stream-entry is also inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled; the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are also inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled.”
"Subhūti! The enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is also inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled. Subhūti!"
"The practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are likewise inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled. Subhūti!"
"The unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is likewise inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled. Subhūti!..."

“Subhūti! “Subhūti! The eye-element is ineffable, inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and equal to the unequaled; likewise, the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are also ineffable, inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and equal to the unequaled.”

“Subhūti! The ear element cannot be designated as being inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, or equal to the unequaled; likewise, the sound element, the ear-consciousness element, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition cannot be designated as being inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, or equal to the unequaled.”

“Subhūti! The nose element cannot be designated as inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, or equal to the unequaled; the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, and the contact of the nose, as well as all feelings produced with that nose-contact as a condition, likewise cannot be designated as inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, or equal to the unequaled.”

“Subhūti! The tongue element cannot be designated as being inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, or equal to the unequaled; the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition likewise cannot be designated as being inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, or equal to the unequaled.”

"Subhūti! The body element cannot be designated as being inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, or equal to the unequaled; likewise, the tangible object element, the body-consciousness element, body-contact, and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition cannot be designated as being inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, or equal to the unequaled."

"Subhūti! The mind-element cannot be designated as being inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, or unequaled; likewise, the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, and the sensation produced with mind-contact as its condition cannot be designated as being inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, or unequaled."

“Subhūti! The element of earth cannot be designated as inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, or unequaled; likewise, the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness cannot be designated as inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, or unequaled.”

“Subhūti! Ignorance cannot be designated as inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, or equal to the unequaled; likewise, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair cannot be designated as inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, or equal to the unequaled.”

"Subhūti! “Subhūti! Inner emptiness cannot be designated as inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, or unequaled; likewise, outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence also cannot be designated as inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, or unequaled.”

“Subhūti! Suchness cannot be designated as inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, or unequaled; nor can the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, non-falsity, non-alteration, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, or the inconceivable realm be designated as inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, or unequaled.”

"Subhūti! The noble truth of suffering cannot be designated; it is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and of an unequaled nature. The noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path likewise cannot be designated; they are inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and of an unequaled nature."

“Subhūti! The four dhyānas cannot be designated as being inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, or unequaled; likewise, the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments also cannot be designated as being inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, or unequaled.”

“Subhūti! The eight liberations cannot be designated; they are inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and equal to the unequaled. The eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities likewise cannot be designated; they are inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and equal to the unequaled.”

“Subhūti! The four applications of mindfulness are unassignable, inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled; likewise, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are also unassignable, inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled.”

“Subhūti! The gate of liberation that is emptiness cannot be designated; it is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and of an unequaled nature. The gates of liberation that are signlessness and wishlessness likewise cannot be designated; they are inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and of an unequaled nature.”
"Subhūti! The ten stages of a bodhisattva cannot be designated; they are inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and equal to the unequaled."

"Subhūti! The five eyes cannot be designated as being inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, or unequaled; likewise, the six supernormal powers also cannot be designated as being inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, or unequaled."

“Subhūti! The ten powers of a Buddha cannot be designated; they are inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and of an unequaled nature. Likewise, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha also cannot be designated; they are inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and of an unequaled nature.”

"Subhūti! The quality of non-forgetfulness cannot be designated as inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, or unequaled; likewise, the state of constant abiding in equanimity cannot be designated as inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, or unequaled."

“Subhūti! All-knowledge (sarvajñatā) cannot be designated; it is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled. The knowledge of the paths (mārgākārajñatā) and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā) likewise cannot be designated; they are inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled.”

“Subhūti! All dhāraṇī-doors are ineffable, inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and of an unequaled nature; all samādhi-doors as well are ineffable, inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and of an unequaled nature.”

“Subhūti! The fruit of stream-entry cannot be designated as inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, or unequaled; likewise, the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship also cannot be designated as inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, or unequaled.”
“Subhūti! The awakening of a pratyekabuddha cannot be designated as inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, or unequaled.”
