“Subhūti! All the practices of bodhisattva mahāsattvas are unassignable, inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and of a nature that is unequaled.”
“Subhūti! The unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas cannot be designated; it is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled.”
The Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 308 (and 309). Translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree.
The second part of the forty-second chapter, "Inconceivable," etc.:
The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying,
"World-Honored One!"
For what reason is form (rūpa) unestablishable as being inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and equal to the unequaled?

Why are feeling (vedanā), perception (saṃjñā), formations (saṃskāra), and consciousness (vijñāna) likewise unestablishable as being inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and equal to the unequaled?
“World-Honored One!
For what reason is the sense base of the eye inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and of an unequaled nature, such that it cannot be designated?”
Are the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind also impossible to designate as being inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and equal to the unequaled?
“World-Honored One!
For what reason and by what causes and conditions is the sphere of form (rūpāyatana) impossible to designate as inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled?”
Are the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena also impossible to designate as being inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and equal to the unequaled?
“World-Honored One!
For what reason is the nature of the eye-element—inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled—not subject to conceptual designation?”

Are the form realm, the eye-consciousness element, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition also inconceivable, incomparable, immeasurable, incalculable, and of a nature equal to the unequaled?
“World-Honored One!
For what reason is the ear-element (śrotradhātu) inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and of an unequaled nature, such that it cannot be designated?”

Are the sphere of sound, the sphere of auditory consciousness, ear-contact, and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition also inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and of an unequaled nature that cannot be designated?
“World-Honored One!
For what reason and by what conditions is the nature of the nose-element (ghrāṇadhātu) inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and peerless, such that it cannot be designated?”

Are the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, and the nose-contact, as well as all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, also inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and of an unequaled nature that cannot be established?
“World-Honored One!
For what reason is the nature of the tongue-element (jihvā-dhātu) inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and peerless, such that it cannot be designated?”

Are the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition also to be designated as inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and equal to the unequaled?
“World-Honored One!
For what reason is the body-element (kāyadhātu) inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and of an unequaled nature, such that it cannot be conceptually designated?”

Are the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition also impossible to designate as inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and equal to the unequaled?
“World-Honored One!
For what reason is the mind-element (manodhātu) impossible to designate, inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and of an unequaled nature?”

Are the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, likewise incapable of being designated, inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and of an unequaled nature?
“World-Honored One!
For what reason is the nature of the earth element inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and peerless, such that it cannot be designated?”
Are the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness also incapable of being designated as inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and equal to the unequaled?
“World-Honored One!
For what reason is ignorance inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, beyond number, and of a nature equal to the unequaled? It cannot be designated.”

Are volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair also inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and of a nature equal to the unequaled, such that they cannot be designated?
“World-Honored One!
For what causes and conditions is the perfection of giving (dānapāramitā) inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and of an unequaled nature, such that it cannot be designated?”
Are the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom also incapable of being designated as inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled?
“World-Honored One!

For what reason and by what causes and conditions is the emptiness of the internal (adhyātma-śūnyatā) inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and of a nature that is unequaled, such that it cannot be designated?”

Are external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence also ineffable, inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and equal to the unequaled?
“World-Honored One!
For what reason is suchness (tathatā) incapable of being designated as inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and equal to the unequaled?”

Are the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, non-illusory nature, unchanging nature, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm also incapable of being designated as inconceivable, incomparable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled?
“World-Honored One!
For what reason is the Noble Truth of Suffering inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and of a nature that is unequaled? Why is it impossible to designate?”

Are the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path likewise incapable of being designated as inconceivable, incomparable, immeasurable, incalculable, and equal to the unequaled?
“World-Honored One!
For what reason are the four dhyānas inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and of a nature that is peerless? Why are they not subject to designation?”
Are the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions also to be designated as inconceivable, incomparable, immeasurable, incalculable, and equal to the unequaled?
“World-Honored One!
For what reason are the eight liberations inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and of an unequaled nature, such that they cannot be designated?”

Are the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten universal bases also to be designated as inconceivable, incomparable, immeasurable, incalculable, and equal to the unequaled?
“World-Honored One!
For what reason are the four foundations of mindfulness inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and of an unequaled nature that cannot be designated?”

Are the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path also to be designated as inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled?
“World-Honored One!
For what reason is the gate of liberation of emptiness inconceivable, incomparable, immeasurable, incalculable, and of an unequaled nature?”
Are the doors of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—likewise incapable of being designated as inconceivable, incomparable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled?
“World-Honored One!
For what reason are the ten stages of a bodhisattva inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and of a nature that is unequaled and beyond comparison?”
“World-Honored One!
For what reason are the five eyes inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and of an unequaled nature, such that they cannot be designated?”
"Are the six supernormal powers also inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and of a nature equal to the unequaled, such that they cannot be designated?
"World-Honored One! [The Bodhisattva asked.]
For what reason are the ten powers of a Buddha inconceivable, immeasurable, unfathomable, incalculable, and of an unequaled nature?

Are the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha also incapable of being designated as inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled?
“World-Honored One!

For what reason and by what causes and conditions is the quality of non-forgetfulness (asaṃpramoṣadharma) inconceivable, incomparable, immeasurable, incalculable, and of a nature equal to the unequaled (asamasama), such that it cannot be designated?”
"Is the nature of constant abiding in equanimity also inconceivable, incomparable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled?
"World-Honored One! [The interlocutor asked.]
For what reason is omniscience (sarvajñatā) ineffable, inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and of an unequaled nature?

Are the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects likewise incapable of being designated, inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and of a nature equal to the unequaled?
“World-Honored One!
For what reason are all the gateways of dhāraṇī inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and of an unequaled nature, such that they cannot be designated?”
Are all gateways to samādhi likewise incapable of being designated as inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and equal to the unequaled?
“World-Honored One!
For what reason is the fruit of stream-entry inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and of a nature that is unequaled and beyond comparison?”
Are the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship also incapable of being designated as inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and equal to the unequaled?
“World-Honored One!

For what reason and by what causes and conditions is the awakening of a pratyekabuddha inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and of a nature that is unequaled? Why is it impossible to designate?”
“World-Honored One!
For what cause and condition is the practice of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas unestablishable, inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and of a nature that is peerless?”
“World-Honored One!
For what reason are the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and of an unequaled nature, such that they cannot be designated?”
The Buddha said, "Subhūti!

Because form cannot be designated as having the nature of being conceivable, measurable, numerable, equal, or unequal, so too feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness cannot be designated as having the nature of being conceivable, measurable, numerable, equal, or unequal."

“Subhūti! The sense base of the eye cannot be designated as being conceivable, measurable, numerable, or characterized by equality or inequality; likewise, the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind cannot be designated as being conceivable, measurable, numerable, or characterized by equality or inequality.”

“Subhūti! Because the sphere of form cannot be designated as being conceivable, measurable, numerable, or characterized by equality or inequality, so too the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena cannot be designated as being conceivable, measurable, numerable, or characterized by equality or inequality.”

“Subhūti! Because the eye-element cannot be designated as being conceivable, measurable, quantifiable, or characterized by equality or inequality, the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition likewise cannot be designated as being conceivable, measurable, quantifiable, or characterized by equality or inequality.”

"Subhūti! Because the ear-element cannot be designated as having the nature of being conceivable, measurable, numerable, equal, or unequal, the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition likewise cannot be designated as having the nature of being conceivable, measurable, numerable, equal, or unequal."

"Subhūti! Because the nose element (ghrāṇadhātu) cannot be designated as being conceivable, measurable, quantifiable, or characterized by equality or inequality, the odor element (gandhadhātu), the nose-consciousness element (ghrāṇavijñānadhātu), nose-contact (ghrāṇasparśa), and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition (ghrāṇasparśapratyayaja-vedanā) likewise cannot be designated as being conceivable, measurable, quantifiable, or characterized by equality or inequality."

“Subhūti! Because the tongue element cannot be designated as having the nature of being conceivable, measurable, numerable, equal, or unequal, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition likewise cannot be designated as having the nature of being conceivable, measurable, numerable, equal, or unequal.”

“Subhūti! Because the body element cannot be designated as having the nature of being conceivable, measurable, quantifiable, equal, or unequal, the touch element, the body-consciousness element, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition also cannot be designated as having the nature of being conceivable, measurable, quantifiable, equal, or unequal.”

"Subhūti! Because the mind-element (manodhātu) cannot be designated in terms of conceptualization, measurement, calculation, or the nature of equality and inequality, the dharma-element (dharmadhātu), the mind-consciousness-element (manovijñānadhātu), as well as mind-contact (manaḥsaṃsparśa) and the various feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition, likewise cannot be designated in terms of conceptualization, measurement, calculation, or the nature of equality and inequality."

“Subhūti! Because the earth element cannot be designated as being conceivable, measurable, quantifiable, or characterized by equality or inequality, the same applies to the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements; they likewise cannot be designated as being conceivable, measurable, quantifiable, or characterized by equality or inequality.”

“Subhūti! Ignorance cannot be designated as having the nature of being conceivable, measurable, numerable, equal, or unequal; likewise, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair cannot be designated as having the nature of being conceivable, measurable, numerable, equal, or unequal.”

“Subhūti! Because the perfection of generosity cannot be designated as being conceivable, measurable, numerable, equal, or unequal, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom likewise cannot be designated as being conceivable, measurable, numerable, equal, or unequal.”

“Subhūti! Because inner emptiness cannot be designated as having the nature of being conceivable, measurable, quantifiable, equal, or unequal, so too outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence cannot be designated as having the nature of being conceivable, measurable, quantifiable, equal, or unequal.”

“Subhūti! Because true thusness cannot be designated as being conceivable, measurable, numerable, equal, or unequal, so too the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, non-alteration, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm cannot be designated as being conceivable, measurable, numerable, equal, or unequal.”

“Subhūti! The noble truth of suffering cannot be designated as having the nature of being conceivable, measurable, quantifiable, equal, or unequal; likewise, the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path cannot be designated as having the nature of being conceivable, measurable, quantifiable, equal, or unequal.”

“Subhūti! The four dhyānas cannot be designated in terms of conceptualization, measurement, calculation, or the nature of equality and inequality; likewise, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions also cannot be designated in terms of conceptualization, measurement, calculation, or the nature of equality and inequality.”

“Subhūti! The eight liberations cannot be designated as being conceivable, measurable, numerable, or characterized by equality or inequality; likewise, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities also cannot be designated as being conceivable, measurable, numerable, or characterized by equality or inequality.”

“Subhūti! The four foundations of mindfulness cannot be designated as being conceivable, measurable, quantifiable, or characterized by equality or inequality; likewise, the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path also cannot be designated as being conceivable, measurable, quantifiable, or characterized by equality or inequality.”

“Subhūti! Because the gate of liberation of emptiness cannot be designated as having the nature of being conceivable, measurable, numerable, equal, or unequal; and because the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness likewise cannot be designated as having the nature of being conceivable, measurable, numerable, equal, or unequal.”
“Subhūti! The ten stages of a bodhisattva cannot be designated, for they are beyond thought, measurement, calculation, and the nature of equality or inequality. Subhūti!”

The five eyes cannot be designated, conceived, measured, quantified, or characterized by equality or inequality; likewise, the six supernormal powers cannot be designated, conceived, measured, quantified, or characterized by equality or inequality.

“Subhūti! Because the ten powers of a Buddha cannot be designated as being conceivable, measurable, numerable, or characterized by equality or inequality, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha likewise cannot be designated as being conceivable, measurable, numerable, or characterized by equality or inequality.”

"Subhūti! The quality of non-forgetfulness cannot be designated as being conceivable, measurable, numerable, or characterized by equality or inequality; likewise, the state of constant equanimity cannot be designated as being conceivable, measurable, numerable, or characterized by equality or inequality."

"Subhūti! Because all-knowledge (sarvajñatā) cannot be designated as being conceivable, measurable, numerable, or characterized by equality or inequality, so too the knowledge of the paths (mārgākārajñatā) and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā) cannot be designated as being conceivable, measurable, numerable, or characterized by equality or inequality."

“Subhūti! Because all dhāraṇī-doors cannot be designated in terms of conceptualization, measurement, calculation, or the nature of equality and inequality; and because all samādhi-doors likewise cannot be designated in terms of conceptualization, measurement, calculation, or the nature of equality and inequality.”

“Subhūti! The fruit of stream-entry cannot be designated in terms of conceptualization, measurement, calculation, or the nature of equality and inequality; likewise, the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship also cannot be designated in terms of conceptualization, measurement, calculation, or the nature of equality and inequality.”
“Subhūti! The awakening of a pratyekabuddha cannot be designated because it is beyond thought, measurement, calculation, or the nature of equality and inequality. Subhūti!”
“Subhūti! Because all the practices of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas cannot be designated, they are inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and beyond the nature of equality or inequality.”
“Because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas cannot be designated, nor can it be conceived, measured, quantified, or characterized by equality or inequality.
The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”
For what reason is form (rūpa) impossible to designate as being conceivable, measurable, quantifiable, or characterized by equality or inequality?

Why is it that feeling (vedanā), perception (saṃjñā), mental formations (saṃskāra), and consciousness (vijñāna) are likewise impossible to designate as being conceivable, measurable, quantifiable, or characterized by equality or inequality?
“World-Honored One!
For what reason and by what conditions is the eye-base (cakṣur-āyatana) impossible to designate as being conceivable, measurable, quantifiable, or characterized by equality or inequality?”
Are the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind also impossible to designate, to conceive, to weigh, to quantify, or to characterize as equal or unequal?
“World-Honored One!
For what cause and condition is the sphere of form (rūpāyatana) impossible to designate as being conceivable, measurable, quantifiable, or characterized by equality or inequality?”
Are the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena likewise impossible to designate, to conceive, to weigh, to quantify, or to characterize as equal or unequal?
“World-Honored One!
For what reason and by what causes and conditions is the eye-element (cakṣurdhātu) impossible to designate, to conceive, to weigh, to quantify, or to characterize as equal or unequal?”

Are the form realm, the eye-consciousness realm, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition likewise impossible to designate, conceive, weigh, calculate, or determine in terms of equality or inequality?
“World-Honored One!
For what reason is the ear-element (śrotradhātu) impossible to designate as being conceivable, measurable, quantifiable, or characterized by equality or inequality?”

Are the sphere of sound, the sphere of ear-consciousness, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition also impossible to designate, conceive, weigh, quantify, or characterize in terms of equality or inequality?
“World-Honored One!

For what reason and by what causes and conditions is the nose-element (ghrāṇadhātu) impossible to designate as being conceivable, measurable, quantifiable, or characterized by equality or inequality?”

Are the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition also impossible to designate, to conceive, to weigh, to quantify, or to characterize in terms of equality or inequality?
“World-Honored One!
For what reason and by what conditions is the tongue-element (jihvā-dhātu) impossible to designate, to conceive, to weigh, to quantify, or to characterize as being equal or unequal?”

Are the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, and tongue-contact, as well as all feelings produced with tongue-contact as their condition, likewise impossible to designate, conceive, weigh, measure, or characterize in terms of equality or inequality?
“World-Honored One!
For what reason is the body-element (kāyadhātu) impossible to designate, to conceive, to weigh, to quantify, or to characterize as equal or unequal?”

Is it not also impossible to designate, conceive, weigh, measure, or calculate the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, body-contact, and the various feelings arising with body-contact as a condition, in terms of their equality or inequality?
“World-Honored One!
For what reason and by what causes and conditions is the mind-element (manodhātu) impossible to designate as being conceivable, measurable, numerable, or characterized by equality or inequality?”

Are the dharma-dhātu, the mental consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, likewise impossible to designate, to conceive, to weigh, to quantify, or to characterize in terms of equality or inequality?
“World-Honored One!
For what reason and by what conditions is the earth element impossible to designate, to conceive, to weigh, to quantify, or to characterize as being equal or unequal?”
Are the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness also impossible to designate, to conceive, to weigh, to calculate, or to characterize in terms of equality or inequality?
“World-Honored One!
For what reason and by what conditions is ignorance impossible to designate, to conceive, to weigh, to measure, or to characterize as either equal or unequal?”

Are volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, becoming, birth, and aging-and-death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair likewise impossible to designate, to conceive, to weigh, to quantify, or to characterize in terms of equality or inequality?
“Bhagavān, for what reason is the perfection of generosity (dānapāramitā) impossible to designate, to conceive, to weigh, to quantify, or to characterize as either equal or unequal?”

Are the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom also incapable of being designated as objects of thought, measurement, calculation, or as being equal or unequal?
“World-Honored One!

For what reason and by what conditions is internal emptiness (adhyātma-śūnyatā) incapable of being designated as something conceivable, measurable, quantifiable, or characterized by equality or inequality?”

Are external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence also incapable of being designated, conceived, measured, quantified, or characterized by equality or inequality?
“World-Honored One!
For what reason and by what conditions is suchness (tathatā) incapable of being designated as something conceivable, measurable, quantifiable, or characterized by equality or inequality?”

Can the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, the state of equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of dharma, the stability of dharma, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm also be designated as objects of thought, measurement, calculation, or as states of equality and inequality?
“World-Honored One!
For what cause and condition is the Noble Truth of Suffering impossible to designate as being conceivable, measurable, quantifiable, or characterized by equality or inequality?”
"Are the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path likewise incapable of being designated as objects of thought, measurement, calculation, or as being equal or unequal?
"World-Honored One! [he asked.]
For what reason are the four dhyānas incapable of being designated as being conceivable, measurable, quantifiable, or characterized by equality or inequality?
Why are the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments likewise incapable of being designated as being conceivable, measurable, quantifiable, or characterized by equality or inequality?
“World-Honored One!
For what reason are the eight liberations impossible to designate as being conceivable, measurable, quantifiable, or characterized by equality or inequality?”
Are the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities likewise impossible to designate, to conceive, to weigh, to quantify, or to characterize as equal or unequal?
“World-Honored One,

for what reason and by what causes and conditions are the four foundations of mindfulness impossible to designate as being conceivable, measurable, quantifiable, or characterized by equality or inequality?”

Are the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path also impossible to designate, to conceive, to weigh, to quantify, or to characterize as equal or unequal?
“World-Honored One!

For what reason and by what causes and conditions can the gate of liberation of emptiness not be designated as being conceivable, measurable, quantifiable, or characterized by equality or inequality?”
"Are the gateways of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—also beyond being designated as objects of thought, measurement, calculation, or the nature of equality and inequality?
"World-Honored One! [he asked.]
"For what reason, Blessed One, are the ten stages of a bodhisattva impossible to designate as being conceivable, measurable, quantifiable, or characterized by equality or inequality?
"World-Honored One! [The Bodhisattva asked.]
For what reason are the five eyes incapable of being designated as being conceivable, measurable, quantifiable, or characterized by equality or inequality?
And why are the six supernormal powers likewise incapable of being designated as being conceivable, measurable, quantifiable, or characterized by equality or inequality?
“World-Honored One!
For what cause and condition are the ten powers of the Buddha impossible to designate, to conceive, to weigh, to quantify, or to characterize as equal or unequal?”

Are the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha likewise incapable of being designated, conceived, measured, quantified, or characterized by equality or inequality?
“World-Honored One!

For what reason and by what causes and conditions is the quality of non-forgetfulness (asaṃpramoṣadharma) impossible to designate as being conceivable, measurable, quantifiable, or characterized by equality or inequality?”

"Is the nature of constant dwelling in equanimity also incapable of being designated as something that can be conceived, measured, quantified, or characterized by equality or inequality? World-Honored One,
for what reason is omniscience incapable of being designated as something that can be conceived, measured, quantified, or characterized by equality or inequality?"
“Can the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects also not be designated as being conceivable, measurable, numerable, or characterized by equality or inequality?
“World-Honored One! [The Venerable Subhūti asked.]
For what reason are all the gateways of dhāraṇī inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and beyond the nature of being either equal or unequal?
"Are all gateways to samādhi likewise incapable of being designated as objects of thought, measurement, calculation, or as having the nature of equality or inequality?
"World-Honored One! [he asked.]
For what reason are the fruit of stream-entry (srotāpatti-phala) not to be designated as conceivable, measurable, quantifiable, or characterized by equality or inequality?

And why are the fruits of once-returning (sakṛdāgāmin), non-returning (anāgāmin), and arhatship likewise not to be designated as conceivable, measurable, quantifiable, or characterized by equality or inequality?
“World-Honored One!
For what reason and by what conditions is the enlightenment of a Pratyekabuddha impossible to designate as being conceivable, measurable, quantifiable, or characterized by equality or inequality?”
“World-Honored One!
For what reason are all the practices of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas impossible to designate, to conceive, to weigh, to measure, or to calculate as being either equal or unequal?”
“World-Honored One!

For what reason and by what causes and conditions is the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas incapable of being designated, conceived, measured, quantified, or characterized as being equal or unequal?”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because the intrinsic nature of form is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without intrinsic nature, form cannot be designated as being conceivable, measurable, calculable, or as having the nature of equality or inequality.”

Because the intrinsic nature of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is likewise inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without intrinsic nature, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness cannot be designated as being conceivable, measurable, calculable, or characterized by equality or inequality.

“Subhūti! Because the intrinsic nature of the eye-base is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without intrinsic nature, the eye-base cannot be designated as having the qualities of being conceivable, measurable, calculable, equal, or unequal.

Because the intrinsic natures of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases are likewise inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without intrinsic nature, the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases also cannot be designated as having the qualities of being conceivable, measurable, calculable, equal, or unequal.”

"Subhūti! Because the intrinsic nature of the sphere of form is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and devoid of intrinsic nature, one cannot designate the sphere of form as being conceivable, measurable, calculable, equal, or unequal.

Because the intrinsic natures of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are likewise inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and devoid of intrinsic nature, one cannot designate the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena as being conceivable, measurable, calculable, equal, or unequal."

“Subhūti! Because the intrinsic nature of the eye-element (*cakṣurdhātu*) is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and devoid of intrinsic nature, the eye-element cannot be designated as having the qualities of being conceivable, measurable, calculable, equal, or unequal.

Because the intrinsic nature of the form-element (*rūpadhātu*), the eye-consciousness-element (*cakṣurvijñānadhātu*), and eye-contact (*cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa*), as well as all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, is likewise inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and devoid of intrinsic nature, the form-element up to all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition cannot be designated as having the qualities of being conceivable, measurable, calculable, equal, or unequal.”

“Subhūti! Because the intrinsic nature of the ear-element (*śrotra-dhātu*) is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without intrinsic nature, one cannot designate the ear-element as being conceivable, measurable, calculable, or as having the qualities of equality or inequality.

Because the intrinsic nature of the sound-element (*śabda-dhātu*), the ear-consciousness-element (*śrotra-vijñāna-dhātu*), ear-contact (*śrotra-saṃsparśa*), and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition is likewise inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without intrinsic nature, one cannot designate anything from the sound-element up to the feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition as being conceivable, measurable, calculable, or as having the qualities of equality or inequality.”

“Subhūti! Because the intrinsic nature of the nose-element (*ghrāṇadhātu*) is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and devoid of self-nature, one cannot designate the nose-element as having a nature that is conceivable, measurable, calculable, equal, or unequal.

Because the intrinsic nature of the odor-element (*gandhadhātu*), the nose-consciousness-element (*ghrāṇavijñānadhātu*), and the sensation produced with nose-contact as its condition (*ghrāṇasparśapratyayaja-vedanā*) is likewise inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and devoid of self-nature, one cannot designate anything from the odor-element up to the sensation produced with nose-contact as having a nature that is conceivable, measurable, calculable, equal, or unequal.”

“Subhūti! Because the intrinsic nature of the tongue element (*jihvā-dhātu*) is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without intrinsic nature, one cannot designate the tongue element as being conceivable, measurable, calculable, or as having the qualities of equality or inequality.

Because the intrinsic nature of the taste element (*rasa-dhātu*), the tongue-consciousness element (*jihvā-vijñāna-dhātu*), tongue-contact (*jihvā-saṃsparśa*), and all feelings (*vedanā*) produced with tongue-contact as a condition is likewise inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without intrinsic nature, one cannot designate anything from the taste element up to the feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition as being conceivable, measurable, calculable, or as having the qualities of equality or inequality.”

"Subhūti! Because the intrinsic nature of the body-element (*kāyadhātu*) is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and devoid of intrinsic nature, the body-element cannot be designated as having the qualities of being conceivable, measurable, calculable, equal, or unequal.

Because the intrinsic nature of the touch-object-element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*), the body-consciousness-element (*kāyavijñānadhātu*), body-contact (*kāyasparśa*), and all feelings (*vedanā*) produced with body-contact as a condition is likewise inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and devoid of intrinsic nature, everything from the touch-object-element up to the feelings produced with body-contact as a condition cannot be designated as having the qualities of being conceivable, measurable, calculable, equal, or unequal."

“Subhūti! Because the intrinsic nature of the mind-element (*manodhātu*) is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without intrinsic nature, the mind-element cannot be designated as having the qualities of being conceivable, measurable, calculable, equal, or unequal.

Because the intrinsic nature of the dharma-element (*dharmadhātu*), the mind-consciousness-element (*manovijñānadhātu*), mental contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*), and all feelings produced with mental contact as condition is likewise inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without intrinsic nature, the dharma-element up to all feelings produced with mental contact as condition cannot be designated as having the qualities of being conceivable, measurable, calculable, equal, or unequal.”

“Subhūti! Because the intrinsic nature of the earth element is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without self-nature, the earth element cannot be designated as having the qualities of being conceivable, measurable, calculable, equal, or unequal.

Because the intrinsic natures of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are likewise inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without self-nature, the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements also cannot be designated as having the qualities of being conceivable, measurable, calculable, equal, or unequal.”

“Subhūti! Because the intrinsic nature of ignorance is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and devoid of intrinsic nature, ignorance cannot be designated as having the nature of being conceivable, measurable, calculable, equal, or unequal.

Because the intrinsic nature of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair is likewise inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and devoid of intrinsic nature, these factors from volitional formations through old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair also cannot be designated as having the nature of being conceivable, measurable, calculable, equal, or unequal.”

“Subhūti! Because the intrinsic nature of the perfection of giving is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and devoid of self-nature, the perfection of giving cannot be designated as having the qualities of being conceivable, measurable, calculable, equal, or unequal.

Because the intrinsic natures of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are likewise inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and devoid of self-nature, these perfections—from ethical discipline up to wisdom—cannot be designated as having the qualities of being conceivable, measurable, calculable, equal, or unequal.”

“Subhūti! Because the intrinsic nature of internal emptiness is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without self-nature, internal emptiness cannot be designated as having the qualities of being conceivable, measurable, calculable, equal, or unequal.”

Because external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are themselves inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and equal to the unequaled due to their lack of intrinsic nature, so too—ranging from external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—cannot be established as objects of thought, measurement, calculation, or the states of equality and inequality.

“Subhūti! Because the intrinsic nature of *tathatā* (suchness) is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without intrinsic nature, it is impossible to designate *tathatā* as being conceivable, measurable, calculable, equal, or unequal.

Because the intrinsic natures of the *dharmadhātu*, *dharmatā*, non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*), the reality limit (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*) are likewise inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without intrinsic nature, it is impossible to designate anything from the *dharmadhātu* up to the inconceivable realm as being conceivable, measurable, calculable, equal, or unequal.”

“Subhūti! Because the intrinsic nature of the noble truth of suffering is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without self-nature, the noble truth of suffering cannot be designated as being conceivable, measurable, calculable, or as having the nature of equality or inequality.

Because the intrinsic natures of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are likewise inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without self-nature, the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path also cannot be designated as being conceivable, measurable, calculable, or as having the nature of equality or inequality.”

“Subhūti! Because the intrinsic nature of the four dhyānas is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without self-nature, the four dhyānas cannot be designated as being conceivable, measurable, calculable, or equal or unequal.

Because the intrinsic nature of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is likewise inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without self-nature, the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments also cannot be designated as being conceivable, measurable, calculable, or equal or unequal.”

“Subhūti! Because the intrinsic nature of the eight liberations is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without self-nature, the eight liberations cannot be designated as having the qualities of being conceivable, measurable, calculable, equal, or unequal.

Because the intrinsic nature of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities is likewise inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without self-nature, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities also cannot be designated as having the qualities of being conceivable, measurable, calculable, equal, or unequal.”

“Subhūti! Because the intrinsic nature of the four foundations of mindfulness is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without self-nature, one cannot designate the four foundations of mindfulness as being conceivable, measurable, calculable, or as having the nature of equality or inequality.

Because the intrinsic nature of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path is likewise inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without self-nature, one cannot designate the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path as being conceivable, measurable, calculable, or as having the nature of equality or inequality.”

“Subhūti! Because the intrinsic nature of the gate of liberation of emptiness is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without self-nature, the gate of liberation of emptiness cannot be designated as having the qualities of being conceivable, measurable, calculable, equal, or unequal.

Because the intrinsic nature of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness is likewise inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without self-nature, the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness also cannot be designated as having the qualities of being conceivable, measurable, calculable, equal, or unequal.”

“Subhūti! Because the intrinsic nature of the ten stages of a bodhisattva is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without self-nature, the ten stages of a bodhisattva likewise cannot be designated as being conceivable, measurable, calculable, or characterized by equality or inequality.”

“Subhūti! Because the intrinsic nature of the five eyes is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without self-nature, the five eyes cannot be designated as having the qualities of being conceivable, measurable, calculable, equal, or unequal.

Because the intrinsic nature of the six supernormal powers is likewise inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without self-nature, the six supernormal powers also cannot be designated as having the qualities of being conceivable, measurable, calculable, equal, or unequal.”

“Subhūti! Because the intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*) of the Buddha’s ten powers (*daśabala*) is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and devoid of intrinsic nature, the Buddha’s ten powers cannot be designated as being conceivable, measurable, calculable, or characterized by equality or inequality.

Because the intrinsic nature of the four fearlessnesses (*vaiśāradya*), the four analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*), great loving-kindness (*maitrī*), great compassion (*karuṇā*), great sympathetic joy (*muditā*), great equanimity (*upekṣā*), and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇika-buddhadharma*) is likewise inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and devoid of intrinsic nature, these qualities—from the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities—cannot be designated as being conceivable, measurable, calculable, or characterized by equality or inequality.”

“Subhūti! Because the nature of the quality of non-forgetfulness is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without intrinsic nature, the quality of non-forgetfulness cannot be designated as having the nature of being conceivable, measurable, calculable, equal, or unequal.

Because the nature of the state of constant equanimity is also inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without intrinsic nature, the state of constant equanimity likewise cannot be designated as having the nature of being conceivable, measurable, calculable, equal, or unequal.”

"Subhūti! Because the intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*) of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without intrinsic nature, all-knowledge cannot be designated as having the qualities of being conceivable, measurable, calculable, equal, or unequal.

Because the intrinsic nature of the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) is likewise inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without intrinsic nature, the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects also cannot be designated as having the qualities of being conceivable, measurable, calculable, equal, or unequal."

“Subhūti! Because the intrinsic nature of all dhāraṇī-doors is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and devoid of self-nature, one cannot designate any conceivability, measurement, calculation, or the state of equality or inequality regarding all dhāraṇī-doors.

Because the intrinsic nature of all samādhi-doors is likewise inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and devoid of self-nature, one cannot designate any conceivability, measurement, calculation, or the state of equality or inequality regarding all samādhi-doors.”

“Subhūti! Because the intrinsic nature of the fruit of stream-entry is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without intrinsic nature, the fruit of stream-entry cannot be designated as being conceivable, measurable, calculable, or characterized by equality or inequality.

Because the intrinsic natures of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are likewise inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without intrinsic nature, the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship also cannot be designated as being conceivable, measurable, calculable, or characterized by equality or inequality.”

“Subhūti! Because the nature of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without intrinsic nature, pratyekabuddha-enlightenment cannot be designated as being conceivable, measurable, calculable, or characterized by equality or inequality.”

“Subhūti! Because the intrinsic nature of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas’ practices is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without self-nature, it is impossible to designate any nature of conceivability, measurability, calculability, equality, or inequality regarding all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas’ practices.”

"Subhūti! Because the self-nature of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and devoid of intrinsic nature, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas cannot be designated as being conceivable, measurable, calculable, or characterized by equality or inequality."
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 393. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter Forty-two on the Inconceivable, etc., Part Three. "Subhūti!
What do you think?
Within form—which is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without intrinsic nature—is form to be apprehended?

Within feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness—which are inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and devoid of intrinsic nature—can feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness be apprehended?
"Subhūti, what do you think? Within the eye-base—
which is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without intrinsic nature— is the eye-base to be apprehended?"

Within the inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and selfless nature of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind—can these sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind be apprehended?
“Subhūti, what do you think? Within the form-base—
which is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without intrinsic nature— can a form-base be apprehended?”

Within the inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and selfless spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena—can these spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena be apprehended?
“Subhūti, what do you think? Within the eye-element—
which is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without intrinsic nature— can a ‘eye-element’ be apprehended?”

Within the inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and selfless nature of the form realm, the eye-consciousness element, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition—can the form realm, up to and including all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, be apprehended?
“Subhūti, what do you think? Within the auditory element—
which is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without intrinsic nature— is the auditory element to be apprehended?”

Within the inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and selfless nature of the sound element, the ear-consciousness element, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition—can the sound element, up to and including all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, be apprehended?
"Subhūti, what do you think? Within the nose-element—
which is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without intrinsic nature— is a nose-element to be apprehended?"

Within the inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and selfless nature of the fragrance element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition—can these, from the fragrance element up to the sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition, be apprehended?
“Subhūti, what do you think? Within the tongue-element—
which is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without intrinsic nature— is the tongue-element to be apprehended?”

Within the inconceivable, the immeasurable, the incalculable, the unequaled, and the absence of intrinsic nature of the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition—can the taste element, up to and including all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, be apprehended?
"Subhūti, what do you think? Within the body-element—
which is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without intrinsic nature— is the body-element to be apprehended?"

Within the inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and selfless nature of the tangible-object element, the body-consciousness element, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition—can these, from the tangible-object element up to the feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, be apprehended?
"Subhūti, what do you think? Within the mental realm—
which is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without intrinsic nature— is a mental realm to be apprehended?"

Within the inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and selfless nature of the dharma-realm, the consciousness-element, mental contact, and all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition—can the dharma-realm up to all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition be apprehended?
"Subhūti, what do you think? Within the earth element—
which is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without intrinsic nature— is the earth element to be apprehended?"

Within the inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and selfless elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, can these elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness be apprehended?
“Subhūti, what do you think? Within ignorance—
which is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without intrinsic nature— is ignorance to be apprehended?”

In the practice of formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair—which are inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and devoid of intrinsic nature—is it possible to apprehend anything from the practice up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair?
“Subhūti, what do you think? Within the perfection of giving—
which is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without intrinsic nature— can that perfection of giving be apprehended?”

Within the inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and selfless nature of the perfections of pure ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, can the perfections from pure ethical discipline through wisdom be apprehended?
“Subhūti, what do you think? Within inner emptiness—
which is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without intrinsic nature— is inner emptiness to be apprehended?”

Within the inconceivable, the immeasurable, the incalculable, the unequaled, and the absence of intrinsic nature—can one find external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence? Can these be found within that which lacks intrinsic nature?
“Subhūti, what do you think? Within suchness—
which is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without intrinsic nature— is suchness to be apprehended?”

Within the dharmadhātu, the dharma-nature, the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, the nature of equality, the nature free from birth, the fixedness of dharma, the stability of dharma, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm—which are themselves inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, peerless, and devoid of intrinsic nature—can these things, from the dharmadhātu up to the inconceivable realm, be apprehended?
“Subhūti, what do you think? Within the noble truth of suffering—
which is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without intrinsic nature— can the noble truth of suffering be apprehended?”

Within the noble truths of suffering, origination, cessation, and the path—which are inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and devoid of intrinsic nature—can the noble truths of suffering, origination, cessation, and the path be apprehended?
“Subhūti, what do you think? Within the four dhyānas—
which are inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without intrinsic nature— can those four dhyānas be apprehended?”

Within the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments—which are inconceivable, incomparable, immeasurable, unequaled, and without intrinsic nature—can the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments be apprehended?
“Subhūti, what do you think? Within the eight liberations—
which are inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and devoid of intrinsic nature— can those eight liberations be apprehended?”

Within the inconceivable, the immeasurable, the incalculable, the unequaled, and the absence of intrinsic nature of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities—can these eight bases of mastery, nine successive meditative attainments, and ten totalities be apprehended?
“Subhūti, what do you think? Within the four applications of mindfulness—
which are inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without intrinsic nature— can the four applications of mindfulness be apprehended?”

Within the inconceivable, the immeasurable, the incalculable, the unequaled, and the absence of intrinsic nature of the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path—can the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path be apprehended?
“Subhūti, what do you think? Can a liberation door of emptiness—
which is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and devoid of intrinsic nature— be apprehended within that very emptiness?”

Within the inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and selfless gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, can these gateways to liberation of signlessness and wishlessness be apprehended?
“Subhūti, what do you think? Within the ten stages of a bodhisattva—
which are inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without intrinsic nature— can those ten stages of a bodhisattva be apprehended?”
“Subhūti, what do you think? Within the five eyes—
which are inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without intrinsic nature— can the five eyes be apprehended?”
Within the six supernormal powers—which are inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and devoid of intrinsic nature—can the six supernormal powers be apprehended?
“Subhūti, what do you think? Within the Buddha’s ten powers—
which are inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without intrinsic nature— can those ten powers be apprehended?”

Within the inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and selfless nature of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha—can these four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha be apprehended?
“Subhūti, what do you think? Within the state of non-forgetfulness—
which is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without intrinsic nature— is any dharma of non-forgetfulness to be apprehended?”
Within the inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and selfless nature of the constant abiding in equanimity, can that constant abiding in equanimity be apprehended?
"Subhūti, what do you think? Within all-knowledge—
which is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without intrinsic nature— is all-knowledge to be apprehended?"

Can the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects—which are inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and equal to the unequaled—be apprehended within the absence of intrinsic nature? Can the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects be found therein?
“Subhūti, what do you think? Within all the gateways of dhāraṇī—
which are inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and devoid of intrinsic nature— can any gateway of dhāraṇī be apprehended?”
Within all samādhi-gates—which are inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and devoid of intrinsic nature—can any samādhi-gate be apprehended?
“Subhūti, what do you think? Within the fruit of stream-entry—
which is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without intrinsic nature— can the fruit of stream-entry be apprehended?”
Within that which is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without intrinsic nature, can the fruits of the once-returner, the non-returner, or the arhat be attained?
“Subhūti, what do you think? Within the inconceivable,
the immeasurable, the incalculable, the unequaled, and the lack of intrinsic nature of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, can a pratyekabuddha-enlightenment be apprehended?”
“Subhūti, what do you think?
Within all bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices— which are inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and devoid of intrinsic nature— can any bodhisattva-mahāsattva practice be apprehended?”
"Subhūti, what do you think? Within the unsurpassed, perfect,

and complete awakening of the Buddhas— which is inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, unequaled, and without intrinsic nature— is that unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening of the Buddhas to be apprehended?"
Subhūti replied, “No, World-Honored One!”
The Buddha said,
“So it is, Subhūti! It is just so.”
It is so! For this reason, all dharmas are inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled.

"Subhūti! Because all phenomena are inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled, so too are all the Buddha-dharmas, Tathāgata-dharmas, self-arisen dharmas, and the dharmas of the knowledge of all modes possessed by all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas—inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled."

"Subhūti! All the Buddha-dharmas, Tathāgata-dharmas, self-arisen dharmas, and the dharmas of the knowledge of all modes of all-knowledge belonging to all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas are inconceivable, because conceptualization has ceased;
they are immeasurable, because measurement has ceased."
It is immeasurable because all measure has ceased;
it is unequaled because all equality has ceased. Subhūti!
For this reason, all phenomena are likewise inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled. "Subhūti!

All the Buddha-dharmas, Tathāgata-dharmas, self-arisen dharmas, and the dharmas of the knowledge of all-knowledge belonging to all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas are inconceivable, because they transcend the conceivable;
they are immeasurable, because they transcend measurement;
they are innumerable, because they transcend number.
"Unequaled, because it transcends all that is equal. Subhūti!
For this reason, all phenomena are likewise inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled."

“Subhūti! That which is inconceivable is merely a designation for the inconceivable; that which is immeasurable is merely a designation for the immeasurable; that which is incalculable is merely a designation for the incalculable; that which is unequaled is merely a designation for the unequaled.”

"Subhūti! For this reason, all the Buddha-dharmas, Tathāgata-dharmas, self-arisen dharmas, and the dharmas of the knowledge of all modes possessed by all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas are inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled."

"Subhūti! That which is inconceivable is so because space is inconceivable; that which is immeasurable is so because space is immeasurable; that which is incalculable is so because space is incalculable; and that which is unequaled is so because space is unequaled."

"Subhūti! For this reason, all the Buddha-dharmas, Tathāgata-dharmas, self-arisen dharmas, and the dharmas of the knowledge of all modes possessed by all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas are inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled."

“Subhūti! All the Buddha-dharmas, Tathāgata-dharmas, self-arisen dharmas, and the dharmas of the knowledge of all modes possessed by all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas cannot be conceived, measured, calculated, or compared by Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, or any in the world—whether devas, humans, or asuras.”

"Subhūti! For this reason, all the Buddha-dharmas, Tathāgata-dharmas, self-arisen dharmas, and the dharmas of the knowledge of all-knowledge of all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas are inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled."

When the Buddha had spoken these inconceivable, immeasurable, incalculable, and unequaled dharmas, five hundred bhikṣus among the assembly attained liberation of mind through the destruction of the outflows.
Furthermore, there were two thousand bhikṣuṇīs who, through the non-clinging of all outflows, attained liberation of mind.
Additionally, there were sixty thousand upāsakas who, regarding all phenomena, became free from dust and removed from defilement, and the pure Dharma-eye arose within them.
Furthermore, thirty-seven thousand upāsikās also attained the stainless, dust-free Dharma-eye regarding all phenomena.

Additionally, twenty thousand bodhisattva-mahāsattvas attained the patience of the non-arising of phenomena (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*) and received the prediction that they would become buddhas within this Bhadrakalpa.
Chapter Forty-Three: On Accomplishing Deeds, Part One. At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”
The profound perfection of wisdom has appeared in the world for the sake of a great task;
the profound perfection of wisdom has appeared in the world for the sake of an inconceivable task;
the profound perfection of wisdom has appeared in the world for the sake of an immeasurable task.
The profound perfection of wisdom appears in the world for the sake of immeasurable matters;
the profound perfection of wisdom appears in the world for the sake of matters that are unequaled.
The Buddha said, “So it is, Subhūti!”
So it is! It is as you have said.

This profound *prajñāpāramitā* appears in the world for a great purpose; it appears in the world for an inconceivable purpose; it appears in the world for an immeasurable purpose; it appears in the world for an incalculable purpose; it appears in the world for a purpose that is unequaled.
Why is this? "Subhūti!
It is because the profound perfection of wisdom can bring to fulfillment the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom."

“Subhūti! This profound perfection of wisdom is able to accomplish inner emptiness, outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersal emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.”

"Subhūti! This profound *prajñāpāramitā* is able to accomplish suchness (*tathatā*), the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), non-falsity, non-alteration, equality, the state of being free from birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm."

“Subhūti! It is because the profound perfection of wisdom can bring about the noble truth of suffering, the noble truth of the origin [of suffering], the noble truth of the cessation [of suffering], and the noble truth of the path.”
"Subhūti! This profound perfection of wisdom is able to accomplish the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments."
"Subhūti! It is because the profound perfection of wisdom can accomplish the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities."

“Subhūti! This profound *prajñāpāramitā* is able to accomplish the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.”
"Subhūti! It is because the profound perfection of wisdom can accomplish the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness."
“Subhūti! The profound perfection of wisdom is able to accomplish the ten stages of a bodhisattva. Subhūti!”
The profound *prajñāpāramitā* is able to accomplish the five eyes and the six supernormal powers. "Subhūti!

The profound *prajñāpāramitā* is able to accomplish the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha."
“Subhūti! Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* can accomplish the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity. Subhūti!”
The profound perfection of wisdom is able to accomplish all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*). "Subhūti!..."
The profound perfection of wisdom is able to accomplish all dharani-doors and all samadhi-doors. "Subhūti!..."
The profound perfection of wisdom is able to accomplish the fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the fruit of arhatship.
“Subhūti! The profound perfection of wisdom is able to accomplish the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha. Subhūti!”
The profound *prajñāpāramitā* is able to accomplish all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. "Subhūti!
The profound *prajñāpāramitā* is able to accomplish the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas."

“Subhūti! It is like a Kṣatriya great king who has been consecrated by coronation, possessing majestic power and sovereignty to subdue all; having entrusted all affairs of state to his ministers, he sits with folded hands in non-action, dwelling in peace, security, and happiness.”

“Subhūti! The Tathāgata is likewise; as the Great Dharma King, he entrusts the Śrāvaka-dharma, the Pratyekabuddha-dharma, the Bodhisattva-dharma, and the Buddha-dharma entirely to this profound Prajñāpāramitā, for it is by means of this Prajñāpāramitā that all activities are accomplished.”

"Therefore, Subhūti, this profound perfection of wisdom appears in the world for a great purpose; it appears in the world for an inconceivable purpose; it appears in the world for an immeasurable purpose; it appears in the world for an incalculable purpose; it appears in the world for a purpose that is unequaled."
Why is that? "Subhūti!

Because it does not grasp at form, the profound perfection of wisdom appears in the world and is able to accomplish its tasks; because it does not grasp at feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, the profound perfection of wisdom appears in the world and is able to accomplish its tasks."

“Subhūti! Because it does not grasp at or adhere to the sense base of the eye, the profound *prajñāpāramitā* appears in the world and accomplishes its tasks; because it does not grasp at or adhere to the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind, it appears in the world and accomplishes its tasks.”

“Subhūti! The profound perfection of wisdom appears in the world and accomplishes its tasks because it does not grasp at or cling to the sphere of form; it appears in the world and accomplishes its tasks because it does not grasp at or cling to the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena.”

“Subhūti! Because it does not grasp or adhere to the eye-element, the profound *prajñāpāramitā* appears in the world and accomplishes its tasks; because it does not grasp or adhere to the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, or the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, it appears in the world and accomplishes its tasks.”

“Subhūti! Because it does not grasp or cling to the ear-element, the profound perfection of wisdom appears in the world and accomplishes its tasks; because it does not grasp or cling to the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, or the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, it appears in the world and accomplishes its tasks.”

“Subhūti! Because it does not grasp at or adhere to the nose element (*ghrāṇadhātu*), the profound *prajñāpāramitā* appears in the world and accomplishes its purposeful work.
