"Therefore, Subhūti, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should likewise neither grasp nor cling to form, nor should they grasp or cling to feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness."
A bodhisattva mahāsattva should likewise not grasp at or cling to the sense base of the eye, nor should they grasp at or cling to the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind;

a bodhisattva mahāsattva should likewise not grasp at or cling to the sense base of forms, nor should they grasp at or cling to the sense bases of sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, or mental phenomena;

a bodhisattva mahāsattva should likewise not grasp at or cling to the eye element, nor should they grasp at or cling to the form element, the eye-consciousness element, eye-contact, or the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva should likewise not grasp at or adhere to the ear-element, nor should they grasp at or adhere to the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, or the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition;

a bodhisattva mahāsattva should likewise not grasp at or adhere to the nose-element, nor should they grasp at or adhere to the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, nose-contact, or the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition;

a bodhisattva mahāsattva should likewise not grasp at or adhere to the tongue-element, nor should they grasp at or adhere to the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, or the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva should likewise not grasp at or adhere to the body element (*kāyadhātu*), nor should they grasp at or adhere to the contact element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*), the body-consciousness element (*kāyavijñānadhātu*), body-contact (*kāyasparśa*), or the various feelings (*vedanā*) produced with body-contact as their condition;

a bodhisattva mahāsattva should likewise not grasp at or adhere to the mind element (*manodhātu*), nor should they grasp at or adhere to the mental-object element (*dharmadhātu*), the mind-consciousness element (*manovijñānadhātu*), mind-contact (*manaḥsparśa*), or the various feelings produced with mind-contact as their condition;

a bodhisattva mahāsattva should likewise not grasp at or adhere to the earth element (*pṛthivīdhātu*), nor should they grasp at or adhere to the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements (*ab-, tejo-, vāyu-, ākāśa-, vijñānadhātu*).

A bodhisattva mahāsattva should likewise not grasp at or become attached to ignorance; they should not grasp at or become attached to volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, or old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva should likewise not grasp at or become attached to the perfection of generosity; they should not grasp at or become attached to the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva should likewise not grasp at or adhere to internal emptiness; nor should they grasp at or adhere to external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva should likewise not grasp at or adhere to *tathatā* (suchness); they should not grasp at or adhere to the *dharmadhātu* (dharma-realm), *dharmatā* (dharma-nature), non-falsity, immutability, equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, or the inconceivable realm.
A bodhisattva mahāsattva should likewise not grasp at or adhere to the noble truth of suffering; they should not grasp at or adhere to the noble truths of origination, cessation, or the path.
A bodhisattva mahāsattva should likewise not grasp at or adhere to the four dhyānas, nor should they grasp at or adhere to the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva should likewise not take up or become attached to the eight liberations; they should not take up or become attached to the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities;

a bodhisattva mahāsattva should likewise not take up or become attached to the four foundations of mindfulness; they should not take up or become attached to the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path;

a bodhisattva mahāsattva should likewise not take up or become attached to the gate of liberation of emptiness, nor should they take up or become attached to the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.
A bodhisattva mahāsattva should likewise not grasp at or adhere to the ten stages of a bodhisattva;
a bodhisattva mahāsattva should likewise not grasp at or adhere to the five eyes, nor should they grasp at or adhere to the six supernormal powers;

a bodhisattva mahāsattva should likewise not grasp at or adhere to the ten powers of a buddha, nor should they grasp at or adhere to the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha.
A bodhisattva mahāsattva should also not grasp at or adhere to the quality of non-forgetfulness, nor should they grasp at or adhere to the nature of constant equanimity;
a bodhisattva mahāsattva should also not grasp at or adhere to all-knowledge, nor should they grasp at or adhere to the knowledge of the aspects of the path or the knowledge of all aspects;
a bodhisattva mahāsattva should also not grasp at or adhere to any of the doors of dhāraṇī, nor should they grasp at or adhere to any of the doors of samādhi.
A bodhisattva mahāsattva should likewise not take up or cling to the fruit of a stream-enterer; they should not take up or cling to the fruits of a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat;
a bodhisattva mahāsattva should likewise not take up or cling to the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha;
and a bodhisattva mahāsattva should likewise not take up or cling to any of the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
A bodhisattva mahāsattva should also not grasp at or cling to the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas;

nor should a bodhisattva mahāsattva grasp at or cling to the buddha-nature, tathāgata-nature, self-arisen dharma-nature, or the nature of all-knowledge possessed by all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas.
At that time, the devaputras of the desire and form realms addressed the Buddha, saying:

“World-Honored One! This Prajñāpāramitā is most profound; it is difficult to see and difficult to realize. It is beyond the reach of discursive thought and transcends the sphere of conceptualization. It is tranquil, subtle, precise, and deep-seated; only those who are wise and of keen intelligence can fully comprehend it.”

"Bhagavān! If there are sentient beings who are able to have deep faith and understanding in this Prajñāpāramitā, one should know that they have already made offerings to immeasurable Buddhas of the past, have generated various roots of goodness by making great vows in the presence of those Buddhas, and have been taken into the care of immeasurable spiritual friends; only then can they believe and understand the profound Prajñāpāramitā."

“Bhagavān! Suppose all sentient beings in the trichiliocosm were to become followers by faith, followers by dharma, those at the eighth stage, stream-enterers, once-returners, non-returners, arhats, and pratyekabuddhas; the wisdom and abandonment they have achieved would not equal that of a person who, for a single day, endures with joy, contemplates, weighs, and examines this profound *prajñāpāramitā*.
The patience achieved by this person regarding this profound *prajñāpāramitā* surpasses that wisdom and abandonment [of others] by immeasurable and boundless degrees. Why is this?

"Bhagavān! All the wisdom and abandonment of those who follow by faith are but a small fraction of the forbearance possessed by a bodhisattva mahāsattva who has already attained the forbearance of the non-arising of dharmas."

"Bhagavān! All the knowledge and abandonment possessed by those who practice in accordance with the Dharma, the eighth-rank practitioners, stream-enterers, once-returners, non-returners, arhats, and pratyekabuddhas, are but a small fraction of the forbearance of a bodhisattva mahāsattva who has already attained the forbearance of the non-arising of phenomena."
At that time, the Buddha addressed the sons of the gods, saying: "So it is! So it is!"
It is as you have said.

All the knowledge and abandonment possessed by those who follow by faith, those who follow by dharma, the eighth-rank practitioners, stream-enterers, once-returners, non-returners, arhats, and pratyekabuddhas, are but a small portion of the forbearance of a bodhisattva mahāsattva who has already attained the forbearance of the non-arising of dharmas (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).
“Devaputra, you should know this!

If sons or daughters of good family briefly hear this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, and having heard it, write it down, read it, recite it, uphold it, contemplate it, and cultivate it, these sons and daughters of good family will swiftly transcend birth and death and realize *nirvāṇa*. They surpass other sons and daughters of good family who joyfully seek the states of *śrāvaka* or *pratyekabuddha*, yet remain far removed from the *prajñāpāramitā* while studying other sūtras for an eon or even more than an eon.”
Why is this? O sons of the gods!

Within this profound *prajñāpāramitā* sūtra, all subtle and supreme dharmas are extensively explained. Those who follow by faith (*śraddhānusārin*), those who follow by dharma (*dharmānusārin*), the eighth-rank practitioners (*aṣṭamaka*), stream-enterers (*srotāpanna*), once-returners (*sakṛdāgāmin*), non-returners (*anāgāmin*), arhats, pratyekabuddhas, and bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should all diligently train in this. All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas have relied upon this training; they have realized, will realize, and are currently realizing unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*).
Then, all the sons of the gods raised their voices together and said:
“World-Honored One!
This Prajñāpāramitā is the Great Pāramitā.”
“World-Honored One!
This prajñāpāramitā is an inconceivable pāramitā.
World-Honored One!”
"In this way, this perfection of wisdom is an immeasurable perfection.
'World-Honored One!
In this way, this perfection of wisdom is a perfection that is beyond measure.'"
“World-Honored One!
This perfection of wisdom is the unequaled perfection.
World-Honored One!”

All those who follow by faith, those who follow by Dharma, the eighth-rank practitioners, stream-enterers, once-returners, non-returners, arhats, and pratyekabuddhas—all of them, by diligently training in this profound perfection of wisdom, swiftly transcend birth and death and realize nirvana.
All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, by diligently training in this profound perfection of wisdom, will swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

"Bhagavān! Although all śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and bodhisattvas diligently train by relying upon this profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) and each attains their ultimate goal, yet this perfection of wisdom neither increases nor decreases."

At that time, having spoken these words, the assembly of devaputras from the desire and form realms prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, circumambulated him three times to the right, took their leave of the Buddha, and returned to their palaces; not far from the assembly, they suddenly vanished.
Chapter 44: A Collection of Similes, Part One, Section 44-1. At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!..."

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, upon hearing this profound *prajñāpāramitā* being taught, develops deep faith and understanding, and is further able to copy, recite, receive and uphold, contemplate, and cultivate it—where did such a bodhisattva mahāsattva pass away before coming to be born here?
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, upon hearing this profound *prajñāpāramitā* being taught, gives rise to deep faith and understanding—neither cowering nor weak, neither shrinking back nor fearing, neither doubting nor being confused, but with joy and delight—binding their mindfulness to contemplate all the meanings and principles of the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, never abandoning it for even a moment whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down; and constantly following the Dharma teacher to respectfully inquire about it, like a newborn calf that does not leave its mother.”

"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva, seeking the profound meaning and intent of the *prajñāpāramitā*, shall never be separated from the Dharma teacher of *prajñā* until they have obtained the profound *prajñāpāramitā* sūtras in their hands, having mastered them through receiving, upholding, reciting, contemplating, practicing, and achieving complete fluency; throughout this time, they shall constantly follow the Dharma teacher without ever abandoning them for even a moment."
“Subhūti, you should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has passed away from the human realm and been reborn among humans. Why is this?

Subhūti! These sons and daughters of good family belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle who, in previous lives, delighted in hearing the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, and having heard it, took it up, memorized it, recited it, contemplated it, and practiced it with diligence; and who further were able to transcribe it, adorning it with various jewels, and moreover made offerings of various exquisite flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, precious banners, pennants, canopies, music, and lamps, honoring, revering, respecting, and praising it.

By virtue of these roots of goodness, they pass away from the human realm and are reborn among humans; there, hearing this *prajñāpāramitā*, they develop profound faith and understanding, and are further able to write it down, recite it, receive and uphold it, contemplate it, and cultivate it.
The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:

“World-Honored One, are there any bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, having accomplished such extraordinary merits as these, have made offerings to and served the Buddhas of other directions, and having passed away from those places, are born here in this world; and upon hearing this profound *prajñāpāramitā* being taught, give rise to deep faith and understanding, and are further able to write it down, recite it, receive and uphold it, contemplate it, and practice it without weariness?”
The Buddha said, “So it is, Subhūti!”

It is so! There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have accomplished such sublime merits that, having made offerings to and served the Buddhas of other directions, they pass away from those places and are reborn here. Upon hearing this profound *prajñāpāramitā* being taught, they give rise to deep faith and understanding; furthermore, they are able to write it down, recite it, receive and uphold it, contemplate it, and cultivate it without weariness or indolence.

Why is this? It is because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have previously heard this profound *prajñāpāramitā* being taught from the presence of immeasurable Buddhas in other directions, and having developed deep faith and understanding, they were further able to write it down, read and recite it, receive and uphold it, contemplate it, and practice it without weariness. By the power of such roots of goodness, they pass away from those places and are born here in this world.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

There are also bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, passing away from the class of beings in Tuṣita Heaven, are reborn among human beings; you should know that they too have accomplished such sublime and excellent qualities."

Why is this? Because in previous lives, these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas had already inquired about the profound meaning and intent of the *prajñāpāramitā* from the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya in Tuṣita Heaven. By the power of such roots of goodness, they have passed away from that place and been reborn here; upon hearing this profound *prajñāpāramitā* being taught, they develop deep faith and understanding, and are further able to copy, recite, uphold, contemplate, and cultivate it without weariness.

"Furthermore, Subhūti, there are individuals belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle who, although they heard the *prajñāpāramitā* in previous lives, did not inquire about its profound meaning and intent. Consequently, when they hear this profound *prajñāpāramitā* taught in their present human existence, their minds become confused and bewildered, they fall into hesitation, they become timid, or they develop erroneous interpretations."

"Furthermore, Subhūti, there are individuals belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle who, although they heard the perfection of meditative concentration in previous lives, did not inquire about its profound meaning. Now, having been born among humans and hearing this profound perfection of wisdom being taught, their minds become confused and bewildered, hesitant, timid, or they develop erroneous interpretations."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

There are individuals belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle who, although they heard of the perfection of diligence in previous lives, did not inquire about its profound meaning and intent. Now, having been born among humans and hearing this teaching of the profound perfection of wisdom, their minds become confused and bewildered, they fall into hesitation and cowardice, or they develop divergent interpretations."

"Furthermore, Subhūti, there may be individuals belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle who, although they heard the perfection of patience (kṣāntipāramitā) in previous lives, did not inquire into its profound meaning and intent. "Furthermore, Subhūti!

"Furthermore, Subhūti!

"Furthermore, Subhūti!

"Furthermore, Subhūti!

There may be an individual belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle who, although having heard of great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity in previous lives, did not inquire into their profound meaning and intent. "Furthermore, Subhūti!

"Furthermore, Subhūti, there are individuals belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle who, although they heard the teaching of the quality of non-forgetfulness in previous lives, did not inquire about its profound meaning and intent. "Furthermore, Subhūti!

There may be a person belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle who, although having heard of 'all-knowledge' in previous lives, did not inquire about its profound meaning and intent. Now, having been born among humans and hearing this profound *prajñāpāramitā* being taught, their mind becomes confused and bewildered, hesitant, timid, or they may develop a mistaken understanding."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

There are individuals belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle who, although they heard of the knowledge of the aspects of the path in previous lives, did not inquire about its profound meaning and intent. Consequently, when they hear this profound *prajñāpāramitā* preached in their present human existence, their minds become bewildered and distressed, they fall into hesitation and timidity, or they develop erroneous interpretations."

"Furthermore, Subhūti, there are individuals belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle who, although they heard of all-aspect omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*) in previous lives, did not inquire into its profound meaning and intent. Consequently, when they hear this profound *prajñāpāramitā* being taught in their present human birth, their minds become confused and bewildered, they fall into hesitation, they become timid and weak, or they develop divergent interpretations."

"Furthermore, Subhūti, there may be individuals belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle who, although they heard all the gateways of dhāraṇī in previous lives, did not inquire about their profound meaning and intent. Consequently, when they hear this profound perfection of wisdom being taught in their present human life, their minds become confused and bewildered, they fall into hesitation and timidity, or they develop erroneous interpretations."

"Furthermore, Subhūti, there are individuals belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle who, although they heard all the gateways of samādhi in previous lives, did not inquire about their profound meaning and intent. Consequently, when they hear this profound *prajñāpāramitā* being taught in their present human life, their minds become confused and bewildered, they fall into hesitation and timidity, or they develop erroneous interpretations."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

There may be a person belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle who, although having heard all the practices of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas in previous lives, did not inquire about their profound meaning and intent. Consequently, when hearing this profound *prajñāpāramitā* preached in this present human life, their mind becomes confused and bewildered, hesitant, timid, or they may even develop a mistaken understanding."

"Furthermore, Subhūti, there are individuals belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle who, although they heard of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas in previous lives, did not inquire about its profound meaning and intent. Now, having been born among humans and hearing this profound *prajñāpāramitā* being taught, their minds become confused and bewildered, they fall into hesitation, they become timid, or they develop erroneous interpretations."

"Furthermore, Subhūti, there are individuals belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle who, although they heard the *prajñāpāramitā* in previous lives and even inquired about its profound meaning, were unable to practice in accordance with it for one day, two days, three, four, or five days. Now, having been born among humans and hearing this profound *prajñāpāramitā* being taught, their minds remain firm and indestructible for one day up to five days; yet, if they are separated from what they have heard, they immediately fall away and lose it."
Why is this? Subhūti!

Because these individuals belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle, although they heard the *prajñāpāramitā* in previous lives and inquired about its profound meaning, did not practice in accordance with what was taught; therefore, in this present life, if they encounter virtuous friends who earnestly exhort them, they will delight in hearing and receiving the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, but if they do not encounter virtuous friends who earnestly exhort them, they will have no desire to hear or receive this sūtra.

Regarding the perfection of wisdom, at times they delight in hearing it and at other times do not; at times they are steadfast and at other times they fall away. Their minds are light and fickle, fluctuating between progress and retreat without constancy, like cotton wool drifting in the wind.

“Subhūti, you should know that such a person has not long set out upon the Mahāyāna sūtras; they have not yet closely attended to true spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra); they have never made offerings to the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones; and they have never upheld, recited, copied, contemplated, or explained the profound Prajñāpāramitā.”
“Subhūti, you should know that such a person has never trained in the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, nor have they ever trained in the *dhyāna*, *vīrya*, *kṣānti*, *śīla*, and *dāna* *pāramitās*;

they have never trained in internal emptiness, nor have they ever trained in external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.”

They have never practiced the study of *tathatā* (suchness); they have never practiced the study of the *dharmadhātu* (dharma-realm), *dharmatā* (dharma-nature), *avitathatā* (non-falsity), *ananyathatā* (unchanging nature), *samatā* (equality), *anabhisamskāratā* (freedom from arising), *dharmatā-sthiti* (the stability of dharmas), *dharmāvasthāna* (the abiding of dharmas), *bhūtakoṭi* (the limit of reality), *ākāśadhātu* (space-element), or the *acintyadhātu* (inconceivable realm).
They have never practiced the study of the noble truth of suffering; they have never practiced the study of the noble truths of the origin, cessation, and the path.

They have never practiced the study of the four *dhyānas* (meditative concentrations); they have never practiced the study of the four *apramāṇas* (immeasurables) or the four *ārūpya-samāpattis* (formless attainments).
They have never trained in the eight liberations; they have never trained in the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive absorptions, or the ten totalities;

they have never trained in the four foundations of mindfulness; they have never trained in the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path;
they have never trained in the gate of liberation that is emptiness, nor have they trained in the gates of liberation that are signlessness and wishlessness.
They have never trained in the ten stages of a bodhisattva;
they have never trained in the five eyes, nor have they ever trained in the six supernormal powers;

they have never trained in the ten powers of a buddha, nor have they ever trained in the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha.
They have never trained in the quality of non-forgetfulness; they have never trained in the state of constant equanimity;
they have never trained in all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*); they have never trained in the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) or the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*);
they have never trained in all doors of dhāraṇī, nor have they ever trained in all doors of samādhi.
They have never trained in the dharmas of the fruit of stream-entry; they have never trained in the dharmas of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, or arhatship;
they have never trained in the dharmas of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment;
and they have never trained in all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
They have never trained in the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas.

"Subhūti, you should know that such a person, newly set out upon the Great Vehicle, possesses only a small degree of faith, respect, and affection for the Mahāyāna teachings; they have not yet been able to write down, receive, uphold, read, recite, contemplate, practice, or explain to others this profound *prajñāpāramitā*."

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll Three Hundred Eleven. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter Forty-Four, "Various Similes," Section Two. "Furthermore, Subhūti!"

If sons or daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle do not write down, receive, uphold, read, recite, contemplate, and practice this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, nor explain it for others; if they do not embrace other sentient beings through this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, nor embrace other sentient beings through the *dhyāna*, *vīrya*, *kṣānti*, *śīla*, and *dāna* *pāramitās*;

If one does not embrace other sentient beings through internal emptiness; or if one does not embrace other sentient beings through external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence;

If one does not encompass other sentient beings through suchness; if one does not encompass other sentient beings through the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), or the inconceivable realm;
if one does not encompass other sentient beings through the noble truth of suffering; if one does not encompass other sentient beings through the noble truths of origin, cessation, or the path;

if one does not encompass other sentient beings through the four dhyānas; or if one does not encompass other sentient beings through the four immeasurables or the four formless absorptions; [then one does not practice the perfection of wisdom].

If one does not gather other sentient beings through the eight liberations; if one does not gather other sentient beings through the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, or the ten totalities;

if one does not gather other sentient beings through the four foundations of mindfulness; if one does not gather other sentient beings through the four right endeavors, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eight branches of the noble path;

if one does not gather other sentient beings through the gate of liberation of emptiness; or if one does not gather other sentient beings through the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness;
If one does not gather other sentient beings by means of the ten stages of a bodhisattva;
if one does not gather other sentient beings by means of the five eyes; if one does not gather other sentient beings by means of the six supernormal powers;

if one does not gather other sentient beings by means of the ten powers of a Buddha; or if one does not gather other sentient beings by means of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
If they do not gather other sentient beings through the quality of non-forgetfulness; if they do not gather other sentient beings through the state of constant equanimity;

if they do not gather other sentient beings through all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*); if they do not gather other sentient beings through the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) or the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*);
if they do not gather other sentient beings through all the doors of dhāraṇī, or if they do not gather other sentient beings through all the doors of samādhi;

If one does not gather other sentient beings through the dharma of the fruit of stream-entry; if one does not gather other sentient beings through the dharmas of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, or arhatship;
if one does not gather other sentient beings through the dharma of pratyekabuddha enlightenment;
if one does not gather other sentient beings through all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas;
"If they do not embrace other sentient beings through the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas. Subhūti!

If sons of good family or daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle do not practice in accordance with the profound perfection of wisdom, or do not practice in accordance with the perfections of meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity;..."

If one does not practice in accordance with inner emptiness; if one does not practice in accordance with outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature;

if one does not practice in accordance with suchness; if one does not practice in accordance with the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, non-alteration, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm;
If one does not practice in accordance with the noble truth of suffering; if one does not practice in accordance with the noble truths of its origin, its cessation, and the path;
if one does not practice in accordance with the four dhyānas; if one does not practice in accordance with the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments;

if one does not practice in accordance with the eight liberations; or if one does not practice in accordance with the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative concentrations, and the ten totalities.

If one does not practice in accordance with the four foundations of mindfulness; if one does not practice in accordance with the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path;
if one does not practice in accordance with the gate of liberation of emptiness; if one does not practice in accordance with the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness;
or if one does not practice in accordance with the ten stages of a bodhisattva.
If one does not practice in accordance with the five eyes; if one does not practice in accordance with the six supernormal powers;

if one does not practice in accordance with the ten powers of a Buddha; if one does not practice in accordance with the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
if one does not practice in accordance with the quality of non-forgetfulness; or if one does not practice in accordance with the nature of constant abiding in equanimity;

If one does not practice in accordance with all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*); if one does not practice in accordance with the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) or the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*);
if one does not practice in accordance with all doors of dhāraṇī, or if one does not practice in accordance with all doors of samādhi;

if one does not practice in accordance with the dharma of the fruit of stream-entry (*srotāpattiphala*), or if one does not practice in accordance with the dharmas of the fruits of once-returning (*sakṛdāgāmin*), non-returning (*anāgāmin*), or arhatship (*arhattva*).
If one does not practice in accordance with the dharmas of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha;
if one does not practice in accordance with all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas;
or if one does not practice in accordance with unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening.

“Subhūti, you should know that for these sons and daughters of good family who abide in the vehicle of the bodhisattvas, by reason of this, they will fall into either of two states or two grounds— namely, the ground of the śrāvakas or the ground of the pratyekabuddhas.”

Why is this? Because these sons and daughters of good family are unable to write down, receive and uphold, read and recite, contemplate, and cultivate the profound *prajñāpāramitā*; nor can they, by means of the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, gather other sentient beings [into it], nor can they practice in accordance with the profound *prajñāpāramitā*. Due to these causes and conditions, these sons and daughters of good family will fall into either of two states or two stages, namely, the stage of a *śrāvaka* or the stage of a *pratyekabuddha*.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

It is like a ship sailing upon the great ocean that has been wrecked; if the people on board do not take hold of wood, do not take hold of vessels, do not take hold of floats, do not take hold of planks, and do not take hold of a corpse to cling to for support, it is certain they will drown and not reach the other shore."

"Subhūti! Suppose there are people crossing the great ocean whose ship has been wrecked; yet, if those among them are able to take hold of wood, utensils, flotation bags, planks, or even a corpse to rely upon, you should know that such persons will ultimately not perish, but will reach the safe shore of the great ocean, arriving without injury or harm and enjoying all manner of sublime bliss."

"In this way, Subhūti, although sons and daughters of good family who have set out in the bodhisattva vehicle may achieve a small measure of faith, respect, and joyful devotion toward the Great Vehicle, if they do not rely upon the profound *prajñāpāramitā* by copying it, upholding it, reading it, reciting it, contemplating it, and practicing it; or if they do not rely upon the *dhyāna*, *vīrya*, *kṣānti*, *śīla*, and *dāna* *pāramitās* by copying them, upholding them, reading them, reciting them, contemplating them, and practicing them;..."

If one does not write down, uphold, recite, contemplate, or cultivate inner emptiness as a point of reliance; or if one does not write down, uphold, recite, contemplate, or cultivate outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature as points of reliance;

If one does not write down, uphold, read, recite, contemplate, or cultivate True Suchness (tathatā) as a basis; if one does not write down, uphold, read, recite, contemplate, or cultivate the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), or the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu) as a basis;

if one does not write down, uphold, read, recite, contemplate, or cultivate the Noble Truth of Suffering as a basis; or if one does not write down, uphold, read, recite, contemplate, or cultivate the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path as a basis.

If they do not write down, uphold, read, recite, contemplate, or cultivate the four dhyānas as their support; if they do not write down, uphold, read, recite, contemplate, or cultivate the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments as their support;

if they do not write down, uphold, read, recite, contemplate, or cultivate the eight liberations as their support; or if they do not write down, uphold, read, recite, contemplate, or cultivate the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative concentrations, and the ten totalities as their support;

If they do not copy, uphold, recite, contemplate, or cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness as their support; if they do not copy, uphold, recite, contemplate, or cultivate the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path as their support;

if they do not copy, uphold, recite, contemplate, or cultivate the liberation door of emptiness as their support; if they do not copy, uphold, recite, contemplate, or cultivate the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness as their support;
or if they do not copy, uphold, recite, contemplate, or cultivate the ten stages of the bodhisattva as their support;

If one does not copy, uphold, read, recite, contemplate, or cultivate the five eyes as a basis for reliance; if one does not copy, uphold, read, recite, contemplate, or cultivate the six supernormal powers as a basis for reliance;

if one does not copy, uphold, read, recite, contemplate, or cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha as a basis for reliance; or if one does not copy, uphold, read, recite, contemplate, or cultivate the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha as a basis for reliance;

If one does not rely upon the quality of non-forgetfulness by copying, upholding, reciting, contemplating, and cultivating it; if one does not rely upon the state of constant equanimity by copying, upholding, reciting, contemplating, and cultivating it;

if one does not rely upon omniscience (*sarvajñatā*) by copying, upholding, reciting, contemplating, and cultivating it; or if one does not rely upon the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) by copying, upholding, reciting, contemplating, and cultivating them;

If they do not write down, uphold, recite, contemplate, and cultivate all *dhāraṇī* gates as their support; if they do not write down, uphold, recite, contemplate, and cultivate all *samādhi* gates as their support;
if they do not write down, uphold, recite, contemplate, and cultivate all the practices of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas as their support;
or if they do not write down, uphold, recite, contemplate, and cultivate the unexcelled, perfect enlightenment of all Buddhas as their support.

Subhūti, you should know that such sons and daughters of good family who abide in the bodhisattva vehicle may decline midway and fail to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, falling back instead into the level of a śrāvaka or a pratyekabuddha.

“Subhūti! Those sons of good family and daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle and have achieved perfect faith, reverence, and affection for the Mahāyāna—if they can write down, receive, uphold, read, recite, contemplate, and practice the profound *prajñāpāramitā* as their reliance; or if they can write down, receive, uphold, read, recite, contemplate, and practice the *dhyāna*, *vīrya*, *kṣānti*, *śīla*, and *dāna* *pāramitās* as their reliance;”

If one is able to write down, uphold, read, recite, contemplate, and cultivate inner emptiness as a refuge; or if one is able to write down, uphold, read, recite, contemplate, and cultivate outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence as a refuge;

If one can write down, receive and uphold, read and recite, contemplate, and cultivate *tathatā* (suchness) as a support; or if one can write down, receive and uphold, read and recite, contemplate, and cultivate the *dharmadhātu* (dharma-realm), the *dharmatā* (dharma-nature), the non-falsity, the non-alteration, the equality, the freedom from birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm as supports;

or if one can write down, receive and uphold, read and recite, contemplate, and cultivate the Noble Truth of Suffering as a support; or if one can write down, receive and uphold, read and recite, contemplate, and cultivate the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path as supports.

If one can write down, receive and uphold, read and recite, contemplate, and practice the four dhyānas as a support; if one can write down, receive and uphold, read and recite, contemplate, and practice the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions as a support;

if one can write down, receive and uphold, read and recite, contemplate, and practice the eight liberations as a support; if one can write down, receive and uphold, read and recite, contemplate, and practice the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive absorptions, and the ten totalities as a support;

If one can write down, uphold, recite, contemplate, and cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness as a basis for reliance; if one can write down, uphold, recite, contemplate, and cultivate the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path as a basis for reliance;

if one can write down, uphold, recite, contemplate, and cultivate the liberation door of emptiness as a basis for reliance; if one can write down, uphold, recite, contemplate, and cultivate the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness as a basis for reliance;
and if one can write down, uphold, recite, contemplate, and cultivate the ten stages of the bodhisattva as a basis for reliance—then [one shall attain this samādhi].

If one can write down, uphold, recite, contemplate, and cultivate the five eyes as a support; if one can write down, uphold, recite, contemplate, and cultivate the six supernormal powers as a support;

if one can write down, uphold, recite, contemplate, and cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha as a support; and if one can write down, uphold, recite, contemplate, and cultivate the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha as a support;

If one can write down, receive and uphold, read and recite, contemplate, and practice the quality of non-forgetfulness as a support; if one can write down, receive and uphold, read and recite, contemplate, and practice the state of constant equanimity as a support;

if one can write down, receive and uphold, read and recite, contemplate, and practice all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) as a support; if one can write down, receive and uphold, read and recite, contemplate, and practice the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) as a support;

If one can write down, receive and uphold, read and recite, contemplate, and practice all dharani-doors as a basis for reliance; if one can write down, receive and uphold, read and recite, contemplate, and practice all samadhi-doors as a basis for reliance;
if one can write down, receive and uphold, read and recite, contemplate, and practice all bodhisattva-mahasattva practices as a basis for reliance;
if one can write down, receive and uphold, read and recite, contemplate, and practice the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas as a basis for reliance.

Subhūti, you should know that such sons of good family or daughters of good family who abide in the vehicle of the bodhisattvas will never, midway, fall back into the level of a śrāvaka or a pratyekabuddha; they will certainly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening.

“Subhūti! It is as if a person wishing to cross a perilous and desolate wilderness could not reach a land of peace and happiness if they did not gather provisions and equipment; instead, they would encounter suffering and lose their lives along the way.”
"In this way, Subhūti!

If sons of good family or daughters of good family who have set out in the Bodhisattva vehicle possess faith, patience, a pure mind, a profound mind, aspiration, resolute understanding, equanimity, and diligence toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, yet do not embrace the profound perfection of wisdom, nor embrace the perfections of concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity; [they will not attain it]."

If one does not embrace inner emptiness; if one does not embrace outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature;

if one does not embrace suchness; if one does not embrace the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, non-alteration, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm;
If one does not embrace the noble truth of suffering, nor embrace the noble truths of its origin, its cessation, and the path;
if one does not embrace the four dhyānas, nor embrace the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments;
if one does not embrace the eight liberations, nor embrace the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities;

If one does not embrace the four foundations of mindfulness; if one does not embrace the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path;
if one does not embrace the gate of liberation of emptiness, or the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness;
or if one does not embrace the ten stages of a bodhisattva;
If one does not embrace the five eyes; if one does not embrace the six supernormal powers;

if one does not embrace the ten powers of a Buddha; if one does not embrace the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
if one does not embrace the quality of non-forgetfulness; if one does not embrace the state of constant abiding in equanimity;
If one does not embrace all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), nor the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), nor the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*);
if one does not embrace all doors of dhāraṇī, nor all doors of samādhi;
if one does not embrace all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas;
Subhūti, you should know that if they do not embrace the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas,

these sons and daughters of good family who abide in the vehicle of the bodhisattvas will perish midway; they will fail to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment and will instead fall back into the level of a śrāvaka or a pratyekabuddha.

“Subhūti! Just as a person who wishes to cross a perilous and desolate wilderness will surely reach a land of peace and happiness if they can gather the necessary provisions and equipment, and will never perish midway from suffering.
"In this way, Subhūti!

Those sons of good family and daughters of good family who abide in the vehicle of the bodhisattvas, if they possess faith, patience, a pure mind, a profound mind, aspiration, resolute conviction, equanimity, and diligence regarding unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and further are able to embrace the profound perfection of wisdom, and further are able to embrace the perfections of concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity;

Furthermore, they are able to embrace internal emptiness; they are also able to embrace external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

Furthermore, they are able to embrace suchness; they are also able to embrace the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, non-alteration, equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm.
Furthermore, it can encompass the noble truth of suffering, and it can also encompass the noble truths of the origin, cessation, and the path;
furthermore, it can encompass the four dhyānas, and it can also encompass the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments;
furthermore, it can encompass the eight liberations, and it can also encompass the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative concentrations, and the ten totalities.

Furthermore, they are able to embrace the four foundations of mindfulness; they are able to embrace the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path;
they are able to embrace the gateway of liberation of emptiness, as well as the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness;
and they are able to embrace the ten stages of the bodhisattva.
Furthermore, they are able to encompass the five eyes; furthermore, they are able to encompass the six supernormal powers;

furthermore, they are able to encompass the ten powers of a Buddha, as well as the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
furthermore, they are able to encompass the quality of non-forgetfulness, and furthermore, they are able to encompass the state of constant abiding in equanimity.
Furthermore, they are able to encompass all-knowledge; furthermore, they are able to encompass the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects;
furthermore, they are able to encompass all dharani-doors and all samadhi-doors;
furthermore, they are able to encompass all the practices of bodhisattva-mahasattvas.
Furthermore, they are able to embrace the unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment of all Buddhas.

Subhūti, you should know that such sons and daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle shall never suffer decline or regression along the way; they will transcend the stages of the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas, bring sentient beings to maturity, purify Buddha-fields, and realize unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.
“Subhūti! It is as if a man or a woman were to take an unbaked clay jar and go to a river, a pond, a well, a spring, or a canal to fetch water; you should know that this jar will soon rot and break.”
Why is this? Because this jar is not yet fired; it is incapable of holding water and will ultimately return to the earth.
"In this same way, Subhūti!"

There may be sons or daughters of good family belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle who, although they possess faith, patience, a pure mind, a profound mind, aspiration, resolute conviction, equanimity, and diligence toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, do not embrace the skillful means of the profound perfection of wisdom, nor do they embrace the perfections of meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity; [they will fall away].

If one does not embrace internal emptiness; if one does not embrace external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence;

if one does not embrace suchness; if one does not embrace the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, non-alteration, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm.
If they do not embrace the noble truth of suffering, nor embrace the noble truths of its origin, its cessation, and the path;
if they do not embrace the four dhyānas, nor embrace the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments;
if they do not embrace the eight liberations, nor embrace the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative concentrations, and the ten totalities.

If one does not embrace the four foundations of mindfulness; if one does not embrace the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path;
if one does not embrace the gate of liberation of emptiness, or the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness;
or if one does not embrace the ten stages of a bodhisattva;
If they do not embrace the five eyes; if they do not embrace the six supernormal powers;

if they do not embrace the ten powers of a Buddha; if they do not embrace the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
if they do not embrace the quality of non-forgetfulness; if they do not embrace the state of constant abiding in equanimity;
If one does not embrace all-knowledge; if one does not embrace the knowledge of the aspects of the path or the knowledge of all aspects;
if one does not embrace all dharani-doors or all samadhi-doors;
or if one does not embrace all the practices of Bodhisattvas Mahasattvas;
Subhūti, you should know that if they do not embrace the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas,

those sons of good family or daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle will perish midway; they will fail to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment and will instead fall back into the level of a Śrāvaka or a Pratyekabuddha.

"Subhūti! For example, suppose a man or a woman were to take a well-fired jar and go to a river, a pond, a well, a spring, or a canal to fetch water; you should know that this jar would never break or perish."
Why is this? Because this jar is well-fired, capable of holding water, and extremely durable.
"In the same way, Subhūti!"

There are sons and daughters of good family belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle who possess faith, patience, a pure mind, a profound mind, aspiration, resolute conviction, equanimity, and diligence regarding unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; and who are further able to embrace the skillful means of the profound perfection of wisdom, as well as the perfections of meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity.

Furthermore, they are able to embrace internal emptiness; they are also able to embrace external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

Furthermore, they are able to embrace suchness; they are also able to embrace the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, non-alteration, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm.
Furthermore, it can encompass the noble truth of suffering; furthermore, it can encompass the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path;
furthermore, it can encompass the four dhyānas; furthermore, it can encompass the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments;
furthermore, it can encompass the eight liberations; furthermore, it can encompass the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative concentrations, and the ten totalities.

Furthermore, they are able to embrace the four foundations of mindfulness; they are able to embrace the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path;
they are able to embrace the gate of liberation of emptiness, as well as the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness;
and they are able to embrace the ten stages of a bodhisattva.
Furthermore, they are able to encompass the five eyes; furthermore, they are able to encompass the six supernormal powers;

furthermore, they are able to encompass the ten powers of a Buddha, as well as the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
furthermore, they are able to encompass the quality of non-forgetfulness, and furthermore, they are able to encompass the state of constant abiding in equanimity.

Furthermore, they are able to encompass all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*); furthermore, they are able to encompass the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*);
furthermore, they are able to encompass all dharani-doors (*dhāraṇīmukha*) and all samādhi-doors (*samādhimukha*);
furthermore, they are able to encompass all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas (*bodhisattvamahāsattvacaryā*).
Furthermore, they are able to embrace the unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment of all Buddhas.

Subhūti, you should know that these sons and daughters of good family who abide in the bodhisattva vehicle shall never suffer decline or regression midway; they will transcend the stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, bring sentient beings to maturity, purify buddha-fields, and realize unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.

“Subhūti! It is as if there were a merchant who lacked skillful means; while his ship was still at the shore and not yet fully equipped or repaired, he placed his goods upon it and pushed it into the water, setting out in haste.

"Subhūti, you should know that if this ship were to break apart and sink midway, the people, the ship, and the goods would each be scattered to different places; thus, those merchants, lacking skillful means and wisdom, would lose their lives and their great wealth."

"In this way, Subhūti, there may be sons of good family or daughters of good family belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle who possess faith, patience, a pure mind, a profound mind, aspiration, resolute conviction, equanimity, and diligence regarding unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; yet, if they do not embrace the skillful means of the profound perfection of wisdom, and if they do not embrace the perfections of meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity;..."

If one does not embrace inner emptiness; if one does not embrace outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature;

if one does not embrace suchness; if one does not embrace the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, non-alteration, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm.
If they do not embrace the noble truth of suffering, nor embrace the noble truths of its origin, its cessation, and the path;
if they do not embrace the four dhyānas, nor embrace the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments;
if they do not embrace the eight liberations, nor embrace the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative concentrations, and the ten totalities;

If one does not embrace the four foundations of mindfulness; if one does not embrace the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path;
if one does not embrace the gate of liberation of emptiness; if one does not embrace the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness;
or if one does not embrace the ten stages of a bodhisattva;
If one does not embrace the five eyes; if one does not embrace the six supernormal powers;

if one does not embrace the ten powers of a Buddha; if one does not embrace the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
if one does not embrace the quality of non-forgetfulness; or if one does not embrace the state of constant abiding in equanimity;
If one does not embrace all-knowledge; if one does not embrace the knowledge of the aspects of the path or the knowledge of all aspects;
if one does not embrace all dharani-doors or all samadhi-doors;
or if one does not embrace all the practices of bodhisattva-mahasattvas;

Subhūti, you should know that if they do not embrace the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas, these sons and daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle will suffer a mid-course collapse and lose both their lives and great wealth. To lose one's life means to fall into the level of a Śrāvaka or a Pratyekabuddha; to lose one's wealth means to lose the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

“Subhūti! It is, for example, like a merchant who possesses skillful wisdom: having first prepared a ship at the seashore and then drawn it into the water to ensure there are no leaks, he subsequently loads his goods upon it and departs.”
"Subhūti, you should know that this boat will certainly not be destroyed or sink; the people and goods will reach their destination in safety and peace. Thus it is, Subhūti!"

There are sons and daughters of good family belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle who possess faith, patience, a pure mind, a profound mind, aspiration, resolute conviction, equanimity, and diligence regarding unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; and who are further able to embrace the skillful means of the profound perfection of wisdom, as well as the perfections of meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity.

Furthermore, they are able to embrace internal emptiness; they are also able to embrace external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

Furthermore, they are able to embrace suchness; they are also able to embrace the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, non-alteration, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm.
Furthermore, it can encompass the noble truth of suffering; furthermore, it can encompass the noble truths of the origin, cessation, and the path;
furthermore, it can encompass the four dhyānas; furthermore, it can encompass the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments;
furthermore, it can encompass the eight liberations; furthermore, it can encompass the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative concentrations, and the ten totalities.

Furthermore, they are able to embrace the four foundations of mindfulness; they are able to embrace the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path;
they are able to embrace the gate of liberation of emptiness, as well as the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness;
and they are able to embrace the ten stages of the bodhisattva.
Furthermore, they are able to encompass the five eyes; furthermore, they are able to encompass the six supernormal powers;

furthermore, they are able to encompass the ten powers of a Buddha, as well as the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
furthermore, they are able to encompass the quality of non-forgetfulness, and furthermore, they are able to encompass the state of constant abiding in equanimity.

Furthermore, they are able to encompass all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*); furthermore, they are able to encompass the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*);
furthermore, they are able to encompass all dharani-doors; furthermore, they are able to encompass all samadhi-doors;
furthermore, they are able to encompass all the practices of Bodhisattvas Mahasattvas.
Furthermore, they are able to embrace the unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment of all Buddhas.

Subhūti, you should know that such sons and daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle will never suffer decline or regression midway; they will transcend the stages of the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas, bring sentient beings to maturity, purify Buddha-fields, and realize unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.

“Subhūti! It is as if there were a person one hundred and twenty years old, aged, decrepit, and worn out, further afflicted by various ailments—namely, wind disorders, bile disorders, phlegm disorders, or a combination of these three.
"Subhūti! What do you think?
Is this old, sick man able to rise from his bed by himself?"
Subhūti replied, “No, World-Honored One!”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!
Even if someone were to support this person and help them stand up, they would still lack the strength to walk even one krośa, two krośas, or three krośas.”
Why is that? Because old age and sickness are extreme.
"It is thus, Subhūti!"

There may be sons or daughters of good family belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle who possess faith, patience, a pure mind, a profound mind, aspiration, resolute conviction, equanimity, and diligence toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; yet, if they do not embrace the skillful means of the profound perfection of wisdom, and do not embrace the perfections of concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity;

If one does not embrace inner emptiness; if one does not embrace outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature;

if one does not embrace suchness; if one does not embrace the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, non-alteration, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm;
If one does not embrace the noble truth of suffering, nor embrace the noble truths of its origin, its cessation, and the path;
if one does not embrace the four dhyānas, nor embrace the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments;
if one does not embrace the eight liberations, nor embrace the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative concentrations, and the ten totalities;

If one does not embrace the four foundations of mindfulness; if one does not embrace the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path;
if one does not embrace the gate of liberation of emptiness; if one does not embrace the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness;
or if one does not embrace the ten stages of a bodhisattva;
If one does not embrace the five eyes; if one does not embrace the six supernormal powers;

if one does not embrace the ten powers of a Buddha; if one does not embrace the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
if one does not embrace the quality of non-forgetfulness; if one does not embrace the state of constant abiding in equanimity;
If one does not embrace all-knowledge; if one does not embrace the knowledge of the aspects of the path or the knowledge of all aspects;
if one does not embrace all doors of dhāraṇī or all doors of samādhi;
or if one does not embrace the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas;
Subhūti, you should know that if they do not embrace the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas,

these sons and daughters of good family who abide in the vehicle of the bodhisattvas will perish midway; they will fail to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment and will instead fall back into the level of a śrāvaka or a pratyekabuddha.

Why is this? Because they do not embrace the profound *prajñāpāramitā* up to the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas, and because they lack skillful means (*upāyakauśalya*).

“Subhūti! It is as if there were a person, one hundred and twenty years old, decrepit and worn out by age, further afflicted by various illnesses—namely, wind-disorders, bile-disorders, phlegm-disorders, or combinations of these three. This aged and sick person wishes to rise from his bed and go elsewhere, yet is unable to do so himself. Then two strong men each support one of his armpits, gently assisting him to stand up, and say to him:
‘Do not be distressed; go wherever you wish. We two shall never abandon you; we will surely reach your destination safely and without harm.’”

"Thus it is, Subhūti! There are sons of good family and daughters of good family belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle who possess faith in unexcelled, perfect enlightenment; who possess patience, a pure mind, a profound mind, aspiration, resolute conviction, equanimity, and diligence; and who are further able to embrace the skillful means of the profound perfection of wisdom, as well as the perfections of meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity."

Furthermore, they are able to encompass internal emptiness; they are also able to encompass external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

Furthermore, they are able to encompass suchness; they are also able to encompass the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, non-alteration, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm.
Furthermore, it can encompass the Noble Truth of Suffering, and it can also encompass the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path;
furthermore, it can encompass the four dhyānas, and it can also encompass the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments;
furthermore, it can encompass the eight liberations, and it can also encompass the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative concentrations, and the ten totalities.

Furthermore, they are able to embrace the four foundations of mindfulness; they are able to embrace the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path;
they are able to embrace the liberation door of emptiness, as well as the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness;
and they are able to embrace the ten stages of the bodhisattva.
Furthermore, they are able to encompass the five eyes; furthermore, they are able to encompass the six supernormal powers;

furthermore, they are able to encompass the ten powers of a Buddha, as well as the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
furthermore, they are able to encompass the quality of non-forgetfulness, and furthermore, they are able to encompass the state of constant abiding in equanimity.
