When the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are not in conjunction, then the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are not mutually connected; when the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are not mutually connected, then the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are without arising; when the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are without arising, then the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are without cessation; and when the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are without cessation, then the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are not in conjunction.

"Subhūti! The non-conjunction of the sphere of form is the non-attachment of the sphere of form; the non-attachment of the sphere of form is the non-arising of the sphere of form; the non-arising of the sphere of form is the non-ceasing of the sphere of form; and the non-ceasing of the sphere of form is the non-conjunction of the sphere of form."

The non-conjunction of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena means that the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are not mutually connected; the lack of mutual connection among the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena means that the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are without arising; the absence of arising in the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena means that the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are without cessation; and the absence of cessation in the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena means that the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are not conjoined.

"Subhūti! The non-conjunction of the eye-element is the non-attachment of the eye-element; the non-attachment of the eye-element is the non-arising of the eye-element; the non-arising of the eye-element is the non-ceasing of the eye-element; and the non-ceasing of the eye-element is the non-conjunction of the eye-element."

The non-conjunction of the form element (*rūpadhātu*), the eye-consciousness element (*cakṣurvijñānadhātu*), eye-contact (*cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa*), and all feelings (*vedanā*) produced with eye-contact as condition, is the non-connection of the form element up to all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition; the non-connection of the form element up to all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition is the non-arising of the form element up to all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition; the non-arising of the form element up to all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition is the non-ceasing of the form element up to all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition; and the non-ceasing of the form element up to all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition is the non-conjunction of the form element up to all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition.

"Subhūti! The non-conjunction of the ear-element is itself the non-attachment of the ear-element; the non-attachment of the ear-element is itself the non-arising of the ear-element; the non-arising of the ear-element is itself the non-ceasing of the ear-element; and the non-ceasing of the ear-element is itself the non-conjunction of the ear-element."

The sound element, the ear-consciousness element, and ear-contact, as well as all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, do not come together; that they do not come together means that the sound element, up to and including all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, are not interconnected. That they are not interconnected means that the sound element, up to and including all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, are non-arising. That they are non-arising means that the sound element, up to and including all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, are non-ceasing. That they are non-ceasing means that the sound element, up to and including all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, do not come together.

"Subhūti! The non-conjunction of the nose-element is the non-attachment of the nose-element; the non-attachment of the nose-element is the non-arising of the nose-element; the non-arising of the nose-element is the non-ceasing of the nose-element; and the non-ceasing of the nose-element is the non-conjunction of the nose-element."

The non-association of the fragrance element (*gandhadhātu*), the nose-consciousness element (*ghrāṇavijñānadhātu*), and nose-contact (*ghrāṇasparśa*), as well as all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition, means that the fragrance element up to all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition are not interconnected. That the fragrance element up to all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition are not interconnected means that the fragrance element up to all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition are unarisen. That the fragrance element up to all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition are unarisen means that the fragrance element up to all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition are unceasing. That the fragrance element up to all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition are unceasing means that the fragrance element up to all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition are non-associated.

“Subhūti! The non-conjunction of the tongue element is the non-attachment of the tongue element; the non-attachment of the tongue element is the non-arising of the tongue element; the non-arising of the tongue element is the non-ceasing of the tongue element; and the non-ceasing of the tongue element is the non-conjunction of the tongue element.”

The taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, and tongue-contact, as well as all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, do not come together; that they do not come together means that the taste element up to the feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are not interconnected. That they are not interconnected means that the taste element up to the feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are without arising. That they are without arising means that the taste element up to the feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are without cessation. That they are without cessation means that the taste element up to the feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition do not come together.

"Subhūti! The non-conjunction of the body-element (*kāyadhātu*) is the non-attachment of the body-element; the non-attachment of the body-element is the non-arising of the body-element; the non-arising of the body-element is the non-ceasing of the body-element; and the non-ceasing of the body-element is the non-conjunction of the body-element."

The non-conjunction of the element of tangibles, the element of body-consciousness, and body-contact, as well as all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, is the non-association of the element of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition; the non-association of the element of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition is the non-arising of the element of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition; the non-arising of the element of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition is the non-ceasing of the element of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition; and the non-ceasing of the element of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition is the non-conjunction of the element of tangibles up to all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition.

“Subhūti! The non-conjunction of the mind-element is the non-attachment of the mind-element; the non-attachment of the mind-element is the non-arising of the mind-element; the non-arising of the mind-element is the non-ceasing of the mind-element; and the non-ceasing of the mind-element is the non-conjunction of the mind-element.”

The dharma-element, the mental-consciousness-element, and mind-contact, as well as all feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition, do not come together; that they do not come together means that the dharma-element up to all feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition are not interconnected. That the dharma-element up to all feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition are not interconnected means that the dharma-element up to all feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition are unarisen. That the dharma-element up to all feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition are unarisen means that the dharma-element up to all feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition are unceasing. That the dharma-element up to all feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition are unceasing means that the dharma-element up to all feelings produced with mind-contact as a condition do not come together.

"Subhūti! The non-conjunction of the earth element is the non-attachment of the earth element; the non-attachment of the earth element is the non-arising of the earth element; the non-arising of the earth element is the non-ceasing of the earth element; and the non-ceasing of the earth element is the non-conjunction of the earth element."

When the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are not in harmony, they are not interconnected; when the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are not interconnected, there is no arising of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness; when there is no arising of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, there is no cessation of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness; and when there is no cessation of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, they are not in harmony.

“Subhūti! The non-conjunction of ignorance is the non-attachment of ignorance; the non-attachment of ignorance is the non-arising of ignorance; the non-arising of ignorance is the non-ceasing of ignorance; and the non-ceasing of ignorance is the non-conjunction of ignorance.”

Volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, becoming, birth, and aging-and-death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are not conjoined; volitional formations through aging-and-death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are not connected. Because volitional formations through aging-and-death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are not connected, there is no arising of volitional formations through aging-and-death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair. Because there is no arising of volitional formations through aging-and-death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair, there is no cessation of volitional formations through aging-and-death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair. Because there is no cessation of volitional formations through aging-and-death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair, there is no conjunction of volitional formations through aging-and-death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.

“Subhūti! The non-union of the perfection of giving is the non-attachment of the perfection of giving; the non-attachment of the perfection of giving is the non-arising of the perfection of giving; the non-arising of the perfection of giving is the non-ceasing of the perfection of giving; and the non-ceasing of the perfection of giving is the non-union of the perfection of giving.”

The non-conjunction of the perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom is the lack of mutual connection among the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom; the lack of mutual connection among the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom is the non-arising of the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom; the non-arising of the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom is the non-cessation of the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom; and the non-cessation of the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom is the non-conjunction of the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom.

“Subhūti! The non-conjunction of internal emptiness is the non-attachment of internal emptiness; the non-attachment of internal emptiness is the non-arising of internal emptiness; the non-arising of internal emptiness is the non-ceasing of internal emptiness; and the non-ceasing of internal emptiness is the non-conjunction of internal emptiness.
This applies likewise to external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, and conditioned emptiness.”

...the emptiness of the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of the ultimate (*atyanta-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of the limitless (*anavarāgra-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of dispersion (*anavakāra-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of non-alteration (*anavakāra-śūnyatā*),

the emptiness of intrinsic nature (*prakṛti-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of specific characteristics (*svalakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of common characteristics (*sāmānya-lakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of all phenomena (*sarvadharma-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of the unapprehendable (*anupalambha-śūnyatā*),

the emptiness of non-existence (*abhāva-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of intrinsic nature (*svabhāva-śūnyatā*), and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence (*abhāvasvabhāva-śūnyatā*)— these do not combine.
The emptiness of the external, up to and including the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, are not mutually connected;

that the emptiness of the external, up to and including the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, are not mutually connected is precisely the non-arising of the emptiness of the external, up to and including the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature;

that the emptiness of the external, up to and including the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, are non-arising is precisely the non-existence of the emptiness of the external, up to and including the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.
Cessation—outer emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature—is itself without cessation;
that is, outer emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature does not combine with it. "Subhūti!

The non-combination of true thusness is the non-attachment of true thusness; the non-attachment of true thusness is the non-arising of true thusness; the non-arising of true thusness is the non-ceasing of true thusness; and the non-ceasing of true thusness is the non-combination of true thusness.

The dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the non-falsity, the non-alteration, the sameness, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*)—the non-conjunction of these is the non-connection of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm; the non-connection of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm is the non-arising of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm; the non-arising of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm is the non-extinction of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm; and the non-extinction of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm is the non-conjunction of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm.

“Subhūti! The non-union of the noble truth of suffering is the non-attachment of the noble truth of suffering; the non-attachment of the noble truth of suffering is the non-arising of the noble truth of suffering; the non-arising of the noble truth of suffering is the non-ceasing of the noble truth of suffering; and the non-ceasing of the noble truth of suffering is the non-union of the noble truth of suffering.

The non-union of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path is the non-attachment of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path; the non-attachment of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path is the non-arising of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path; the non-arising of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path is the non-ceasing of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path; and the non-ceasing of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path is the non-union of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path.”

“Subhūti! The non-conjunction of the four dhyānas is the non-connection of the four dhyānas; the non-connection of the four dhyānas is the non-arising of the four dhyānas; the non-arising of the four dhyānas is the non-ceasing of the four dhyānas; and the non-ceasing of the four dhyānas is the non-conjunction of the four dhyānas.

The non-conjunction of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is the non-connection of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments; the non-connection of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is the non-arising of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments; the non-arising of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is the non-ceasing of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments; and the non-ceasing of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is the non-conjunction of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments.”

“Subhūti! The non-conjunction of the eight liberations is the non-attachment of the eight liberations; the non-attachment of the eight liberations is the non-arising of the eight liberations; the non-arising of the eight liberations is the non-ceasing of the eight liberations; and the non-ceasing of the eight liberations is the non-conjunction of the eight liberations.”

The non-conjunction of the eight bases of mastery (*aṣṭāv abhibhvāyatanāni*), the nine successive attainments (*navānupūrvavihārasamāpattayaḥ*), and the ten totalities (*daśa kṛtsnāyatanāni*) is the non-connection of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities; the non-connection of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities is the non-arising of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities; the non-arising of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities is the non-extinction of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities; and the non-extinction of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities is the non-conjunction of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities.

“Subhūti! The non-conjunction of the four foundations of mindfulness is the non-attachment of the four foundations of mindfulness; the non-attachment of the four foundations of mindfulness is the non-arising of the four foundations of mindfulness; the non-arising of the four foundations of mindfulness is the non-ceasing of the four foundations of mindfulness; and the non-ceasing of the four foundations of mindfulness is the non-conjunction of the four foundations of mindfulness.”

The non-conjunction of the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path is the non-association of the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path; the non-association of the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path is the non-arising of the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path; the non-arising of the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path is the non-extinction of the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path; and the non-extinction of the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path is the non-conjunction of the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path.

"Subhūti! The non-conjunction of the gate of liberation that is emptiness is the non-attachment of the gate of liberation that is emptiness; the non-attachment of the gate of liberation that is emptiness is the non-arising of the gate of liberation that is emptiness; the non-arising of the gate of liberation that is emptiness is the non-ceasing of the gate of liberation that is emptiness; and the non-ceasing of the gate of liberation that is emptiness is the non-conjunction of the gate of liberation that is emptiness."

The non-conjunction of the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness is the non-association of the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness; the non-association of the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness is the non-arising of the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness; the non-arising of the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness is the non-extinction of the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness; and the non-extinction of the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness is the non-conjunction of the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.

"Subhūti! That the ten stages of a bodhisattva are not in combination means that the ten stages of a bodhisattva are not interconnected; that the ten stages of a bodhisattva are not interconnected means that the ten stages of a bodhisattva are non-arising; that the ten stages of a bodhisattva are non-arising means that the ten stages of a bodhisattva are non-ceasing; and that the ten stages of a bodhisattva are non-ceasing means that the ten stages of a bodhisattva are not in combination."

“Subhūti! The non-conjunction of the five eyes is the non-attachment of the five eyes; the non-attachment of the five eyes is the non-arising of the five eyes; the non-arising of the five eyes is the non-extinction of the five eyes; the non-extinction of the five eyes is the non-conjunction of the five eyes. The non-conjunction of the six supernormal powers is the non-attachment of the six supernormal powers;

the non-attachment of the six supernormal powers is the non-arising of the six supernormal powers; the non-arising of the six supernormal powers is the non-extinction of the six supernormal powers; the non-extinction of the six supernormal powers is the non-conjunction of the six supernormal powers.”

“Subhūti! The non-combination of the ten powers of a Buddha is the non-attachment of the ten powers of a Buddha; the non-attachment of the ten powers of a Buddha is the non-arising of the ten powers of a Buddha; the non-arising of the ten powers of a Buddha is the non-ceasing of the ten powers of a Buddha; and the non-ceasing of the ten powers of a Buddha is the non-combination of the ten powers of a Buddha.”

The non-conjunction of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is precisely the non-connection of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; the non-connection of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is precisely the non-arising of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; the non-arising of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is precisely the non-extinction of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; and the non-extinction of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is precisely the non-conjunction of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.

“Subhūti! The non-conjunction of the quality of non-forgetfulness (asaṃpramoṣadharma) is the non-association of the quality of non-forgetfulness; the non-association of the quality of non-forgetfulness is the non-arising of the quality of non-forgetfulness; the non-arising of the quality of non-forgetfulness is the non-ceasing of the quality of non-forgetfulness;

and the non-ceasing of the quality of non-forgetfulness is the non-conjunction of the quality of non-forgetfulness. The non-conjunction of the state of constant equanimity (upekṣā-vihāritā) is the non-association of the state of constant equanimity; the non-association of the state of constant equanimity is the non-arising of the state of constant equanimity; the non-arising of the state of constant equanimity is the non-ceasing of the state of constant equanimity; and the non-ceasing of the state of constant equanimity is the non-conjunction of the state of constant equanimity.”

“Subhūti! The non-conjunction of all-knowledge (sarvajñatā) is the non-attachment of all-knowledge; the non-attachment of all-knowledge is the non-arising of all-knowledge; the non-arising of all-knowledge is the non-ceasing of all-knowledge; and the non-ceasing of all-knowledge is the non-conjunction of all-knowledge.

The non-conjunction of the knowledge of the paths (mārgākārajñatā) and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā) is the non-attachment of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects; the non-attachment of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects is the non-arising of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects; the non-arising of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects is the non-ceasing of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects; and the non-ceasing of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects is the non-conjunction of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects.”

“Subhūti! The non-combination of all dhāraṇī-gates is the non-attachment of all dhāraṇī-gates; the non-attachment of all dhāraṇī-gates is the non-arising of all dhāraṇī-gates; the non-arising of all dhāraṇī-gates is the non-ceasing of all dhāraṇī-gates; and the non-ceasing of all dhāraṇī-gates is the non-combination of all dhāraṇī-gates.”

The non-conjunction of all samādhi-gates is the non-connection of all samādhi-gates; the non-connection of all samādhi-gates is the non-arising of all samādhi-gates; the non-arising of all samādhi-gates is the non-ceasing of all samādhi-gates; and the non-ceasing of all samādhi-gates is the non-conjunction of all samādhi-gates.

“Subhūti! The non-conjunction of the fruit of stream-entry is the non-attachment of the fruit of stream-entry; the non-attachment of the fruit of stream-entry is the non-arising of the fruit of stream-entry; the non-arising of the fruit of stream-entry is the non-ceasing of the fruit of stream-entry; and the non-ceasing of the fruit of stream-entry is the non-conjunction of the fruit of stream-entry.”

The non-conjunction of the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the fruit of arhatship is the non-association of the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the fruit of arhatship; the non-association of the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the fruit of arhatship is the non-arising of the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the fruit of arhatship; the non-arising of the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the fruit of arhatship is the non-ceasing of the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the fruit of arhatship; and the non-ceasing of the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the fruit of arhatship is the non-conjunction of the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the fruit of arhatship.

“Subhūti! The non-conjunction of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is the non-attachment of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment; the non-attachment of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is the non-arising of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment; the non-arising of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is the non-cessation of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment; and the non-cessation of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is the non-conjunction of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment.”

“Subhūti! The non-conjunction of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is the mutual non-attachment of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; the mutual non-attachment of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is the non-arising of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; the non-arising of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is the non-extinction of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; and the non-extinction of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is the non-conjunction of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.”

“Subhūti! The unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is non-composite; that which is non-composite is that which is unrelated to the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas. That which is unrelated to the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is that which is unarisen in the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas. That which is unarisen in the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is that which is unceasing in the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas. That which is unceasing in the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is that which is non-composite in the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas.”

“Subhūti! Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who wish to teach all phenomena to sentient beings—knowing that they all possess such characteristics of non-concordance—set out toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”
The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One,
how does a bodhisattva mahāsattva set out for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment in order to become the ultimate path for the world?"
The Buddha said,
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
A bodhisattva mahāsattva who has set out for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening desires to teach such a Dharma to sentient beings as follows:”

The ultimate limit of form is itself not form; the ultimate limits of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are themselves not feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.

The ultimate limit of the eye-base is itself not the eye-base; the ultimate limits of the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are themselves not the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind.

The ultimate limit of the form-base is itself not the form-base; the ultimate limits of the bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental objects are themselves not the bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, or mental objects.

The ultimate limit of the eye-element is not the eye-element; the ultimate limit of the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition is not the form-element, nor even the feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.

The ultimate limit of the ear-element is not the ear-element; the ultimate limit of the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition is not the sound-element, nor even the feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition.

The ultimate limit of the nose-element is not the nose-element; the ultimate limit of the odor-element, the nose-consciousness-element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition is not the odor-element, nor even the feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition.

The ultimate limit of the tongue-element is itself not the tongue-element; the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition are ultimately themselves not the taste-element, nor even all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition.

The ultimate limit of the body-element is itself not the body-element; the tangible-object-element, the body-consciousness-element, body-contact, and all sensations produced with body-contact as a condition are ultimately themselves not the tangible-object-element, nor even all sensations produced with body-contact as a condition.

The ultimate limit of the mind-element is itself not the mind-element; the mental-object-element, the mind-consciousness-element, mind-contact, and all sensations produced with mind-contact as a condition are ultimately themselves not the mental-object-element, nor even all sensations produced with mind-contact as a condition.

The ultimate limit of the earth element is itself not the earth element; the ultimate limits of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are themselves not the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements.

The ultimate limit of ignorance is itself not ignorance; the ultimate limits of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are themselves not volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.

The ultimate limit of the perfection of generosity is itself not the perfection of generosity; the ultimate limits of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are themselves not the perfections of ethical discipline through to wisdom.

The ultimate limit of internal emptiness is itself not internal emptiness; the ultimate limits of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are themselves not [the respective categories from] external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.

Ultimate suchness is not ultimate suchness; ultimate dharma-realm, dharma-nature, non-illusory nature, unchanging nature, equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm are ultimately not the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm;

ultimate noble truth of suffering is not the ultimate noble truth of suffering, and ultimate noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are not the ultimate noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path;
ultimate four dhyānas are not the ultimate four dhyānas, and ultimate four immeasurables and four formless attainments are not the ultimate four immeasurables and four formless attainments.

The ultimate limit of the eight liberations is itself not the eight liberations; the ultimate limit of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities is itself not the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities.

The ultimate limit of the four foundations of mindfulness is itself not the four foundations of mindfulness; the ultimate limit of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path is itself not the four right efforts up to and including the eightfold noble path.

The ultimate limit of the emptiness liberation door is itself not the emptiness liberation door; the ultimate limit of the signless and wishless liberation doors is itself not the signless and wishless liberation doors.
The ultimate perfection of the ten stages of a bodhisattva is not the ten stages of a bodhisattva;
the ultimate perfection of the five eyes is not the five eyes, and the ultimate perfection of the six supernormal powers is not the six supernormal powers;

the ultimate perfection of the ten powers of a Buddha is not the ten powers of a Buddha; and the ultimate perfection of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is not the four fearlessnesses up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.

The ultimate state of the quality of non-forgetfulness is itself not the quality of non-forgetfulness; the ultimate state of the nature of constant equanimity is itself not the nature of constant equanimity.

The ultimate state of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) is itself not all-knowledge; the ultimate state of the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) is itself not the knowledge of the aspects of the path or the knowledge of all aspects.
The ultimate state of all doors of dhāraṇī is itself not all doors of dhāraṇī; the ultimate state of all doors of samādhi is itself not all doors of samādhi.

The ultimate limit of the fruit of stream-entry is not the fruit of stream-entry; the ultimate limit of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship is not the fruit of once-returner, non-returner, or arhatship;
the ultimate limit of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is not pratyekabuddha-enlightenment;
and the ultimate limit of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is not all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
The ultimate nature of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is itself not the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas.
"Furthermore, Subhūti! Just as this is the ultimate characteristic of these dharmas, so too is the characteristic of all dharmas."
The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
if the marks of all phenomena are ultimately identical to the mark of reality itself, how should a bodhisattva mahāsattva manifest perfect awakening regarding all phenomena?”
Why is this? "World-Honored One!
Within the Ultimate of Form (Akaniṣṭha), there is no such discrimination as to say, 'This is form';"

"Nor is there, within the ultimate nature of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, such a discrimination as to say, 'This is feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.
World-Honored One!"
In the ultimate sense, there is no such conceptual differentiation within the eye-base as "this is the eye-base";
nor is there such conceptual differentiation within the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-bases as "this is the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-base."
“World-Honored One!
Within the ultimate limit of the sphere of form, there is no such discrimination as ‘this is the sphere of form.

Likewise, within the ultimate limits of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena, there is no such discrimination as ‘this is the sphere of sound, odor, taste, touch, or mental phenomena.’”
“World-Honored One!
Within the ultimate nature of the eye-element, there is no such discrimination as ‘this is the eye-element.

Nor is there such discrimination within the ultimate nature of the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, or the various feelings produced with eye-contact as their condition, such that one would say ‘this is the form-element,’ up to ‘these are the various feelings produced with eye-contact as their condition.’”
“World-Honored One!
Within the ultimate nature of the ear-element, there is no such discrimination as ‘this is the ear-element.

Nor is there such discrimination within the ultimate nature of the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, or the various feelings produced with ear-contact as their condition, such that one might say ‘this is the sound-element,’ and so forth, up to ‘these are the various feelings produced with ear-contact as their condition.’”
“World-Honored One!
Within the ultimate limit of the nose-element (*ghrāṇadhātu*), there is no such discrimination as ‘this is the nose-element’;

nor is there such discrimination within the ultimate limits of the odor-element (*gandhadhātu*), the nose-consciousness-element (*ghrāṇavijñānadhātu*), nose-contact (*ghrāṇasparśa*), or the various sensations produced with nose-contact as condition, such that one would say ‘this is the odor-element,’ up to ‘these are the various sensations produced with nose-contact as condition.’”
“World-Honored One!
Within the ultimate nature of the tongue-element, there is no such discrimination as ‘this is the tongue-element.

Nor is there, within the ultimate nature of the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, or the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition, any such discrimination as ‘this is the taste-element,’ up to and including ‘these are the various feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition.’”
“World-Honored One!
Within the ultimate nature of the body-element (kāyadhātu), there is no such discrimination as ‘this is the body-element.

“World-Honored One!

“World-Honored One!
Within the ultimate nature of the earth element, there is no such discrimination as ‘this is the earth element.

“World-Honored One!
Within the ultimate limit of ignorance, there is no such discrimination as ‘this is ignorance.

“Bhagavān! Within the ultimate state of internal emptiness (adhyātma-śūnyatā), there is no such conceptual differentiation as ‘this is internal emptiness.

“World-Honored One!

“World-Honored One!
Within the ultimate state of the four foundations of mindfulness, there is no such discrimination as ‘this is the four foundations of mindfulness.

World-Honored One!”

“World-Honored One!

“World-Honored One!
Within the ultimate state of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), there is no such discrimination as ‘this is all-knowledge.

“World-Honored One!
Within the ultimate state of all dharanī-gates, there is no such discrimination as ‘this is all the dharanī-gates’;
nor is there, within the ultimate state of all samādhi-gates, such discrimination as ‘this is all the samādhi-gates.’”

Within the ultimate realization of the fruit of stream-entry, there is no such discrimination as ‘this is the fruit of stream-entry’;

Within the ultimate state of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas, there is no such discrimination as to say, ‘This is the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas.’”

This is the difficult task of the bodhisattva mahāsattva: namely, although he contemplates all phenomena as having the characteristic of total quiescence, his mind does not sink into despondency, and he forms this thought:

"Having realized full and equal awakening regarding these phenomena, I shall attain unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and for the sake of all sentient beings, I shall proclaim and reveal such subtle and wondrous dharmas of quiescence."
“Subhūti! This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, desiring to establish the ultimate path for the world, sets out for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”
The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One,
how does a bodhisattva mahāsattva set out for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment in order to act as an island for the world?"
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin! For example,
in a vast ocean or within large and small rivers, any high and prominent land that can be inhabited, surrounded by water on all sides, is called an island.”
Thus it is, Subhūti! Form is severed at its prior and posterior limits; feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are severed at their prior and posterior limits.
The eye-base is severed at its prior and posterior limits; the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases are severed at their prior and posterior limits.
The sphere of visible forms is severed at its prior and posterior limits; the spheres of sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, and mental phenomena are severed at their prior and posterior limits.

The eye-element is severed at its prior and posterior limits; the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, and eye-contact, as well as all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, are severed at their prior and posterior limits.

The ear-element is severed at its prior and posterior limits; the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, and ear-contact, as well as all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, are severed at their prior and posterior limits.

The past and future limits of the nose element are severed; the past and future limits of the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition are severed.

The past and future limits of the tongue element are severed; the past and future limits of the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition are severed.

The past and future limits of the body element are severed; the past and future limits of the tangible-object element, the body-consciousness element, body-contact, and all sensations produced with body-contact as a condition are severed.

The past and future limits of the mind-element are cut off; the past and future limits of the phenomenon-element, the mind-consciousness-element, and mental contact, as well as all feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are cut off.
The past and future limits of the earth-element are cut off; the past and future limits of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness-elements are cut off.

The past and future limits of ignorance are cut off; the past and future limits of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are cut off.

The perfection of generosity is severed at its prior and posterior limits; the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are severed at their prior and posterior limits.

Internal emptiness is severed at its prior and posterior limits; external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are all severed at their prior and posterior limits.

Suchness is cut off at its prior and posterior limits; the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, the state of equality, the nature free from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of empty space, and the inconceivable realm are all cut off at their prior and posterior limits.
The noble truth of suffering is cut off at its prior and posterior limits; the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are all cut off at their prior and posterior limits.
The four dhyānas are cut off at their prior and posterior limits; the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are all cut off at their prior and posterior limits.

The eight liberations are severed at their prior and posterior limits; the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten universal bases are severed at their prior and posterior limits.

The four foundations of mindfulness are severed at their prior and posterior limits; the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eight branches of the noble path are severed at their prior and posterior limits.
The door of liberation of emptiness is severed at its prior and posterior limits; the doors of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are severed at their prior and posterior limits.
The ten stages of a bodhisattva are severed from the limits of the past and future;
the five eyes are severed from the limits of the past and future; the six supernormal powers are severed from the limits of the past and future;

the ten powers of a Buddha are severed from the limits of the past and future; and the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are severed from the limits of the past and future.
The quality of non-forgetfulness is severed at its prior and posterior limits; the state of constant abiding in equanimity is severed at its prior and posterior limits;
all-knowledge is severed at its prior and posterior limits; the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are severed at their prior and posterior limits;
all doors of dhāraṇī are severed at their prior and posterior limits; and all doors of samādhi are severed at their prior and posterior limits.
The fruit of stream-entry is severed from the limits of the past and future; the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are severed from the limits of the past and future;
the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is severed from the limits of the past and future;
and all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are severed from the limits of the past and future.
"The unexcelled, perfect enlightenment of all Buddhas is severed at both its prior and subsequent limits. Subhūti!
Because the prior and subsequent limits are thus severed, all phenomena are severed."

Subhūti! All these phenomena are severed at their prior and posterior limits; they are quiescence, they are sublime, and they are suchness. This refers to emptiness, non-apprehension, the path, the severance of craving, its exhaustion without remainder, freedom from defilement, and the eternal cessation that is nirvāṇa.

"Subhūti! A bodhisattva mahāsattva who seeks to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment desires to proclaim and reveal such a subtle and profound dharma of cessation for the sake of sentient beings."
