The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva set out for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment in order to act as a light for the world?
The Buddha said:

“Subhūti! It is for the sake of shattering the heavy darkness that envelops sentient beings—those covered by the eggshell of ignorance throughout the long night—that bodhisattva mahāsattvas set out for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; it is for the sake of healing the cataracts of ignorance in sentient beings so that they may see clearly, and for the sake of providing illumination for all sentient beings who dwell in folly and obscurity.”
“Subhūti! It is for this reason that bodhisattva mahāsattvas set out for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening in order to act as a light for the world.
The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva set out for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening in order to act as a lamp and torch for the world?
The Buddha said:

“Subhūti! A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to proclaim to sentient beings the true meaning and intent of the sūtras associated with the six pāramitās and the four means of attraction (*saṃgrahavastu*), and who wishes to instruct them through skillful means, exhorting them to practice and train for the sake of setting out toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment—”
“Subhūti! It is for this reason that a bodhisattva mahāsattva sets out for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening in order to act as a lamp and torch for the world.
The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva set out for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment in order to act as a guide for the world?
The Buddha said:

“Subhūti! A bodhisattva mahāsattva, wishing to cause sentient beings who have entered upon wrong paths to abandon the four improper courses of conduct, sets out for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment in order to teach them the single path so they may return to the right way; in order that those who are defiled may attain purification; in order that those who are sorrowful and distressed may attain joy; in order that those who are afflicted by grief and suffering may attain happiness; in order that sentient beings who act unreasonably may realize the Dharma that accords with reason; and in order that sentient beings caught in the cycle of saṃsāra may attain parinirvāṇa.”
"Subhūti! It is for the sake of acting as a guide for the world that bodhisattva mahāsattvas set out for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva set out for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment in order to act as a general for the world?
The Buddha said:

“Subhūti! A bodhisattva mahāsattva who seeks unexcelled, perfect enlightenment desires to proclaim and reveal to sentient beings that form is without arising or cessation, without defilement or purification; that feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are without arising or cessation, without defilement or purification;
and that the sense base of the eye is without arising or cessation, without defilement or purification, as are the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.”

Desiring to proclaim and reveal for the sake of sentient beings that the sphere of form (*rūpāyatana*) is without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity; that the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena (*dharmāyatana*) are without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity;

desiring to proclaim and reveal for the sake of sentient beings that the eye-element (*cakṣurdhātu*) is without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity; that the element of form, the eye-consciousness element, and eye-contact, as well as all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, are without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity;

desiring to proclaim and reveal for the sake of sentient beings that the ear-element is without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity; that the element of sound, the ear-consciousness element, and ear-contact, as well as all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, are without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity;

Desiring to proclaim and reveal for sentient beings that the nose element is without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity; that the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, and nose-contact, as well as all sensations produced with nose-contact as a condition, are without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity;

desiring to proclaim and reveal for sentient beings that the tongue element is without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity; that the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, and tongue-contact, as well as all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition, are without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity;

desiring to proclaim and reveal for sentient beings that the body element is without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity; that the tangible-object element, the body-consciousness element, and body-contact, as well as all sensations produced with body-contact as a condition, are without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity;

Desiring to proclaim and reveal for sentient beings that the element of mind (*manodhātu*) is without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity; desiring to proclaim and reveal for sentient beings that the element of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the element of mental consciousness (*manovijñānadhātu*), and mental contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*), as well as the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity;

desiring to proclaim and reveal for sentient beings that the earth element (*pṛthivīdhātu*) is without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity, and that the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements (*ab-, tejo-, vāyu-, ākāśa-, vijñānadhātu*) are without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity;

desiring to proclaim and reveal for sentient beings that ignorance (*avidyā*) is without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity, and that volitional formations (*saṃskāra*), consciousness (*vijñāna*), name-and-form (*nāmarūpa*), the six sense bases (*ṣaḍāyatana*), contact (*sparśa*), feeling (*vedanā*), craving (*tṛṣṇā*), grasping (*upādāna*), becoming (*bhava*), birth (*jāti*), and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair (*jarāmaraṇa-śoka-parideva-duḥkha-daurmanasyopāyāsa*) are without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity.
Wishing to proclaim and reveal to sentient beings the perfection of generosity as being without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity;
wishing to proclaim and reveal to sentient beings the perfection of ethical discipline as being without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity;
wishing to proclaim and reveal to sentient beings the perfection of patience as being without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity.
Desiring to proclaim and reveal to sentient beings the perfection of diligence as being without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity;
desiring to proclaim and reveal to sentient beings the perfection of meditative concentration as being without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity;
desiring to proclaim and reveal to sentient beings the perfection of wisdom as being without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity.
Desiring to proclaim and reveal to sentient beings the perfection of skillful means (*upāyakauśalyapāramitā*), which is without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity;
desiring to proclaim and reveal to sentient beings the perfection of aspiration (*praṇidhānapāramitā*), which is without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity;
desiring to proclaim and reveal to sentient beings the perfection of power (*balapāramitā*), which is without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity;
Desiring to proclaim and reveal to sentient beings the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) as being without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity;

desiring to proclaim and reveal to sentient beings that internal emptiness (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*) is without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity—and likewise external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, emptiness of all phenomena (*sarvadharma-śūnyatā*), emptiness of the unapprehendable, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, and emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature—all are without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity.

He desires to proclaim and reveal to sentient beings that suchness is without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity; that the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, the non-erroneous nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm are without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity;
and he desires to proclaim and reveal to sentient beings that the noble truth of suffering is without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity;
and that the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity.
He desires to proclaim and reveal to sentient beings that the four dhyānas are without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity;
that the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity;

and he desires to proclaim and reveal to sentient beings that the eight liberations are without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity, as are the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative concentrations, and the ten totalities.

He wishes to proclaim and reveal to sentient beings that the four foundations of mindfulness are without arising or cessation, without defilement or purification; that the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are without arising or cessation, without defilement or purification;

that he wishes to proclaim and reveal to sentient beings that the gate of liberation of emptiness is without arising or cessation, without defilement or purification, and that the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are without arising or cessation, without defilement or purification;
and that he wishes to proclaim and reveal to sentient beings that the ten stages of a bodhisattva are without arising or cessation, without defilement or purification.

He wishes to proclaim and reveal for the sake of sentient beings that the five eyes are without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity; that the six supernormal powers are without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity;

he wishes to proclaim and reveal for the sake of sentient beings that the ten powers of a Buddha are without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity; that the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity;

he wishes to proclaim and reveal for the sake of sentient beings that the quality of non-forgetfulness is without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity; and that the nature of constant abiding in equanimity is without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity.

Wishing to proclaim and reveal to sentient beings that all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) is without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity; wishing to proclaim and reveal to sentient beings that the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity;

wishing to proclaim and reveal to sentient beings that all doors of dhāraṇī (*dhāraṇīmukha*) are without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity; and wishing to proclaim and reveal to sentient beings that all doors of samādhi (*samādhimukha*) are without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity;

wishing to proclaim and reveal to sentient beings that the fruit of stream-entry (*srotāpattiphala*) is without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity, and that the fruits of once-returning (*sakṛdāgāmiphala*), non-returning (*anāgāmiphala*), and arhatship (*arhattvaphala*) are without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity.
They desire to proclaim and reveal to sentient beings the awakening of the pratyekabuddhas as being without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity;
they desire to proclaim and reveal to sentient beings all the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas as being without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity;
and they desire to proclaim and reveal to sentient beings the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening of all buddhas as being without arising or cessation, without defilement or purity.
“Subhūti! It is for this reason that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas set out for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening in order to act as generals for the world.
The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva set out for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment in order to serve as a destination for the world?
The Buddha said:

“Subhūti! A bodhisattva mahāsattva who seeks unexcelled, perfect enlightenment and wishes to proclaim and reveal to sentient beings that form has space as its destination, and that feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness likewise have space as their destination;
who wishes to proclaim and reveal to sentient beings that the eye-base has space as its destination, and that the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases likewise have space as their destination—”

Desiring to proclaim and reveal to sentient beings that the sphere of visible forms (*rūpāyatana*) has space as its destination, and that the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena (*dharmāyatana*) likewise have space as their destination;

desiring to proclaim and reveal to sentient beings that the eye-element (*cakṣurdhātu*) has space as its destination, and that the element of visible forms, the eye-consciousness element, eye-contact, and all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition likewise have space as their destination;

desiring to proclaim and reveal to sentient beings that the ear-element has space as its destination, and that the element of sounds, the ear-consciousness element, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition likewise have space as their destination.

Wishing to proclaim and reveal to sentient beings that the nose element has space as its destination, and that the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition likewise have space as their destination;

wishing to proclaim and reveal to sentient beings that the tongue element has space as its destination, and that the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition likewise have space as their destination;

wishing to proclaim and reveal to sentient beings that the body element has space as its destination, and that the tangible-object element, the body-consciousness element, body-contact, and all feelings produced with body-contact as a condition likewise have space as their destination.

Desiring to proclaim and reveal for the sake of sentient beings that the element of space has emptiness as its destination, he likewise proclaims and reveals that the element of phenomena, the element of mental consciousness, and the contact of the mind, as well as all feelings produced with the mind-contact as condition, have emptiness as their destination;

desiring to proclaim and reveal for the sake of sentient beings that the earth element has emptiness as its destination, he likewise proclaims and reveals that the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness have emptiness as their destination;

desiring to proclaim and reveal for the sake of sentient beings that ignorance has emptiness as its destination, he likewise proclaims and reveals that volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair also have emptiness as their destination.
Desiring to proclaim and reveal the perfection of generosity to sentient beings, one takes space as the destination;
desiring to proclaim and reveal the perfection of ethical discipline to sentient beings, one takes space as the destination;
desiring to proclaim and reveal the perfection of patience to sentient beings, one takes space as the destination.
Desiring to proclaim and reveal the perfection of diligence to sentient beings, taking space as the destination;
desiring to proclaim and reveal the perfection of meditative concentration to sentient beings, taking space as the destination;
desiring to proclaim and reveal the perfection of wisdom to sentient beings, taking space as the destination.
Wishing to proclaim and reveal to sentient beings the perfection of skillful means (*upāyakauśalyapāramitā*), they take space as their destination;
wishing to proclaim and reveal to sentient beings the perfection of aspiration (*praṇidhānapāramitā*), they take space as their destination;
wishing to proclaim and reveal to sentient beings the perfection of power (*balapāramitā*), they take space as their destination.
Desiring to proclaim and reveal the perfection of wisdom (*jñānapāramitā*) for the sake of sentient beings, one takes space as the destination;

desiring to proclaim and reveal internal emptiness (*adhyātmaśūnyatā*) for the sake of sentient beings, one takes space as the destination; and likewise, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, emptiness of self-characteristic, emptiness of common characteristic, emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature—all these likewise take space as their destination.

If one wishes to proclaim and reveal to sentient beings that suchness has space as its destination, then the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm likewise have space as their destination;

if one wishes to proclaim and reveal to sentient beings that the noble truth of suffering has space as its destination, then the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path likewise have space as their destination;

if one wishes to proclaim and reveal to sentient beings that the four dhyānas have space as their destination, then the four immeasurables (*apramāṇa*) and the four formless attainments (*ārūpyasamāpatti*) likewise have space as their destination.

Desiring to proclaim and reveal the eight liberations for the sake of sentient beings, he takes space as their destination; the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases likewise take space as their destination.

Desiring to proclaim and reveal the four foundations of mindfulness for the sake of sentient beings, he takes space as their destination; the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eight branches of the noble path likewise take space as their destination.

Desiring to proclaim and reveal the gate of liberation of emptiness for the sake of sentient beings, he takes space as its destination; the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness likewise take space as their destination.
He wishes to proclaim and reveal to sentient beings the ten stages of the bodhisattva, taking space as their destination;
he wishes to proclaim and reveal to sentient beings the five eyes, taking space as their destination, and likewise the six supernormal powers, taking space as their destination;

he wishes to proclaim and reveal to sentient beings the ten powers of a buddha, taking space as their destination, as well as the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, all taking space as their destination.

Desiring to proclaim and reveal for the sake of sentient beings the quality of non-forgetfulness (*asaṃpramoṣadharma*), they take space as their destination; the state of constant equanimity (*upekṣā*) likewise takes space as its destination.

Desiring to proclaim and reveal for the sake of sentient beings all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), they take space as their destination; the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) likewise take space as their destination.

Desiring to proclaim and reveal for the sake of sentient beings all doors of dhāraṇī (*dhāraṇīmukha*), they take space as their destination; all doors of meditative concentration (*samādhimukha*) likewise take space as their destination.

If one wishes to proclaim and reveal to sentient beings the fruit of stream-entry (*srotāpatti-phala*) as having space as its destination, and likewise the fruits of once-returning (*sakṛdāgāmin*), non-returning (*anāgāmin*), and arhatship (*arhat-phala*) as having space as their destination;
if one wishes to proclaim and reveal to sentient beings the enlightenment of a solitary buddha (*pratyekabuddha-bodhi*) as having space as its destination;
and if one wishes to proclaim and reveal to sentient beings all the practices of bodhisattva mahāsattvas as having space as their destination;
One desires to proclaim and reveal to sentient beings that the unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment of all Buddhas has space as its destination.
For the sake of sentient beings, one proclaims and reveals that form is neither a destination nor a non-destination.
Why is this? Because the nature of form is empty, and within emptiness there is neither going nor not-going.
Feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are likewise neither going nor not-going.
Why is this? Because the nature of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is empty; within emptiness, there is neither going nor not going.
"For the sake of all sentient beings, I proclaim and reveal that the sense-base of the eye is neither going nor not going."
Why is this? Because the nature of the sense-base of the eye is empty, and within emptiness there is neither going nor not-going.
The sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are likewise neither going nor not-going.
Why is this? Because the nature of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind is empty; within emptiness there is neither going nor not-going.
"For the sake of all sentient beings, I proclaim and reveal that the sense base of form is neither going nor not-going."
Why is this? Because the nature of the sphere of form is empty; within emptiness, there is neither going nor not-going.
The spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena are likewise neither going nor not-going.
Why is this? Because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena are empty of intrinsic nature; within emptiness, there is neither going nor not-going.
Therefore, for the sake of all sentient beings, one proclaims and reveals that the eye-sphere is neither going nor not-going.
Why is this? Because the nature of the eye-element is empty, and within emptiness there is neither going nor not-going.
The form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, as well as eye-contact and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, are likewise neither going nor not-going.
Why is this? Because the nature of form and all sensations produced with eye-contact as a condition up to the sphere of form are empty; within emptiness, there is neither going nor not-going.
"For the sake of sentient beings, one proclaims and reveals that the ear-sphere is neither going nor not-going."
Why is this? Because the nature of the ear-element (*śrotra-dhātu*) is empty, and within emptiness there is neither going nor not-going.

The sound-element (*śabda-dhātu*), the ear-consciousness-element (*śrotra-vijñāna-dhātu*), as well as ear-contact (*śrotra-saṃsparśa*) and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, are likewise neither going nor not-going.

Why is this? Because the nature of the sound-element, up to and including the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, is empty; within emptiness, there is neither going nor not-going.
"For the sake of all sentient beings, I proclaim and reveal that the nose-element is neither going nor not-going."
Why is this? Because the nature of the nose-element (*ghrāṇadhātu*) is empty; within emptiness there is neither going nor not-going.

The odor-element (*gandhadhātu*), the nose-consciousness-element (*ghrāṇavijñānadhātu*), as well as nose-contact (*ghrāṇasparśa*) and all feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, are likewise neither going nor not-going.
Why is this? Because the nature of all feelings produced with conditions ranging from the fragrance-element up to nose-contact is empty; within emptiness, there is neither going nor not-going.
"For the sake of all sentient beings, I proclaim and reveal that the tongue-element is neither going nor not-going."
Why is this? Because the nature of the tongue-element (*jihvā-dhātu*) is empty, and within emptiness there is neither going nor not-going.

The taste-element (*rasa-dhātu*), the tongue-consciousness-element (*jihvā-vijñāna-dhātu*), as well as tongue-contact (*jihvā-saṃsparśa*) and all sensations (*vedanā*) produced with tongue-contact as a condition, are likewise neither going nor not-going.
Why is this? Because the nature of all feelings produced with conditions ranging from the taste element up to tongue-contact is empty; within emptiness, there is neither going nor not-going.
"For the sake of all sentient beings, I proclaim and reveal that the body element is neither going nor not-going."
Why is this? Because the nature of the body-element (*kāyadhātu*) is empty; within emptiness, there is neither going nor not-going.

The touch-element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*), the body-consciousness-element (*kāyavijñānadhātu*), as well as body-contact (*kāyasparśa*) and all feelings (*vedanā*) produced with body-contact as a condition, are likewise neither going nor not-going.

Why is this? Because the various sensations produced with the sphere of tangibles, up to and including body-contact, as conditions are empty of intrinsic nature; within emptiness, there is neither going nor not-going.
"For the sake of all sentient beings, I proclaim and reveal that the sphere of mental objects is neither going nor not-going."
Why is this? Because the nature of the mind-element (*manodhātu*) is empty, and within emptiness there is neither going nor not-going.

The dharma-element (*dharmadhātu*), the mind-consciousness-element (*manovijñānadhātu*), as well as mental contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*) and the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, are likewise neither going nor not-going.
Why is this? Because the nature of the dharma-realm, and even all sensations produced with mental contact as a condition, is empty; within emptiness there is neither going nor not-going.
Therefore, for the sake of all sentient beings, one proclaims and reveals that the earth element is neither going nor not-going.
Why is this? Because the nature of the earth element is empty, and within emptiness there is neither going nor not-going.
Likewise, the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are neither going nor not-going.
Why is this? Because the natures of the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are empty; within emptiness, there is neither going nor not-going.
For the sake of all sentient beings, one proclaims and reveals that ignorance is neither going nor not-going.
Why is this? Because the nature of ignorance is empty; within emptiness, there is neither going nor not-going.

Formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are likewise neither going nor not-going.

Why is this? Because the nature of everything from volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair is empty; within emptiness, there is neither going nor not-going.
Therefore, for the sake of all sentient beings, one proclaims and reveals that the perfection of generosity is neither going nor not-going.
Why is this? Because the nature of the perfection of generosity (*dānapāramitā*) is empty; within emptiness, there is neither going nor not-going.
"For the sake of all sentient beings, one proclaims and reveals that the perfection of ethical discipline (*śīlapāramitā*) is neither going nor not-going."
Why is this? Because the nature of the perfection of ethical discipline (*śīlapāramitā*) is empty; within emptiness, there is neither going nor not-going.
"For the sake of all sentient beings, I proclaim and reveal that the perfection of patience (*kṣāntipāramitā*) is neither going nor not-going."
Why is this? Because the perfection of patience (*kṣānti-pāramitā*) is empty of intrinsic nature, and within emptiness there is neither going nor not-going.
[The Bodhisattva] proclaims and reveals to all sentient beings that the perfection of diligence (*vīrya-pāramitā*) is neither going nor not-going.
Why is this? Because the nature of the perfection of diligence is empty, and within emptiness there is neither going nor not-going.
"For the sake of all sentient beings, I proclaim and reveal that the perfection of meditative concentration is neither going nor not-going."
Why is this? Because the perfection of meditative concentration (*dhyānapāramitā*) is empty by nature, and within emptiness there is neither proceeding nor non-proceeding.
"For the sake of all sentient beings, one proclaims and reveals that the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is neither proceeding nor non-proceeding."
Why is this? Because the nature of the *prajñāpāramitā* is empty; within emptiness, there is neither going nor not-going.
"For the sake of all sentient beings, one proclaims and reveals the *upāyakauśalyapāramitā* as being neither going nor not-going."
Why is this? Because the perfection of skillful means is empty of intrinsic nature, and within emptiness there is neither going nor not-going.
"For the sake of all sentient beings, one proclaims and reveals that the perfection of aspiration is neither going nor not-going."
Why is this? Because the nature of the perfection of aspiration (*praṇidhāna-pāramitā*) is empty; within emptiness, there is neither going nor not-going.
"For the sake of all sentient beings, one proclaims and reveals that the perfection of power (*bala-pāramitā*) is neither going nor not-going."
Why is this? Because the nature of the perfection of power (*bala-pāramitā*) is empty, and within emptiness there is neither going nor not-going.
"For the sake of all sentient beings, one proclaims and reveals that the perfection of wisdom (*jñāna-pāramitā*) is neither going nor not-going."
Why is this? Because the nature of the perfection of wisdom is empty; within emptiness, there is neither going nor not-going.
"For the sake of all sentient beings, one proclaims and reveals that internal emptiness is neither going nor not-going."
Why is this? Because internal emptiness is empty of its own nature; within emptiness there is neither going nor not-going.

External emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature are likewise neither going nor not-going.
Why is this? Because from external emptiness up to the emptiness of the nature of non-existence, within emptiness there is neither going nor not-going.
"For the sake of all sentient beings, one proclaims and reveals that suchness is neither going nor not-going."
Why is this? Because the nature of true thusness is empty, and within emptiness there is neither going nor not-going.

The dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-falsehood nature, the unchanging nature, the nature of equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm are likewise neither going nor not-going.
Why is this? Because the nature of the dharma-realm, up to and including the inconceivable realm, is empty; within emptiness, there is neither going nor not-going.
"For the sake of all sentient beings, one proclaims and reveals the Noble Truth of Suffering as neither going nor not-going."
Why is this? Because the noble truth of suffering is empty of intrinsic nature, and within emptiness there is neither going nor not-going.
The noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are likewise neither going nor not-going.
Why is this? Because the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are empty of intrinsic nature, and within emptiness there is neither going nor not-going.
"For the sake of all sentient beings, one proclaims and reveals that the four dhyānas are neither going nor not-going."
Why is this? Because the nature of the four dhyānas is empty, and within emptiness there is neither going nor not-going.
The four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are likewise neither going nor not-going.
Why is this? Because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are by nature empty; within emptiness, there is neither going nor not-going.
"For the sake of all sentient beings, one proclaims and reveals the eight liberations as being neither going nor not-going."
Why is this? Because the nature of the eight liberations is empty, and within emptiness there is neither going nor not-going.
The eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten pervasive bases are likewise neither going nor not-going.
Why is this? Because the nature of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities is emptiness; within emptiness, there is neither proceeding nor not proceeding.
"For the sake of all sentient beings, I proclaim and reveal that the four foundations of mindfulness neither proceed nor do not proceed."
Why is this? Because the nature of the four foundations of mindfulness is empty, and within emptiness there is neither going nor not-going.
The four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are likewise neither going nor not-going.
Why is this? Because the nature of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path is empty; within emptiness there is neither proceeding nor not proceeding.
For the sake of all sentient beings, one proclaims and reveals the gate of liberation that is emptiness as being neither proceeding nor not proceeding.
Why is this? Because the nature of the gate of liberation through emptiness is empty, and within emptiness there is neither going nor not-going.
The gates of liberation through signlessness and wishlessness are likewise neither going nor not-going.
Why is this? Because the nature of the doors of liberation—signlessness and wishlessness—is empty; within emptiness, there is neither going nor not-going.
Thus, for the sake of all sentient beings, he proclaims and reveals that the ten stages of a bodhisattva are neither going nor not-going.
Why is this? Because the nature of the ten stages of a bodhisattva is empty, and within emptiness there is neither proceeding nor not proceeding.
"For the sake of all sentient beings, I proclaim and reveal that the five eyes are neither proceeding nor not proceeding."
Why is this? Because the nature of the five eyes is empty; within emptiness there is neither going nor not-going.
The six supernormal powers likewise are neither going nor not-going.
Why is this? Because the nature of the six supernormal powers (*ṣaḍabhijñā*) is empty, and within emptiness there is neither going nor not-going.
"For the sake of all sentient beings, I proclaim and reveal that the ten powers of a Buddha (*daśabala*) are neither going nor not-going."
Why is this? Because the nature of the Buddha’s ten powers is empty; within emptiness, there is neither going nor not-going.

The four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are likewise neither going nor not-going.
Why is this? Because the nature of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is empty; within emptiness, there is neither going nor not-going.
"For the sake of all sentient beings, he proclaims and reveals that the quality of non-forgetfulness is neither going nor not-going."
Why is this? Because the nature of the quality of non-forgetfulness is empty; within emptiness, there is neither going nor not-going.
The state of constant abiding in equanimity is likewise neither going nor not-going.
Why is this? Because the nature of the constant abiding in equanimity is empty; within emptiness, there is neither proceeding nor non-proceeding.
"For the sake of all sentient beings, I proclaim and reveal that omniscience is neither proceeding nor non-proceeding."
Why is this? Because the nature of all-knowledge is empty, and within emptiness there is neither going nor not-going.
The knowledge of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are likewise neither going nor not-going.
Why is this? Because the nature of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects is empty; within emptiness, there is neither proceeding nor not proceeding.
"For the sake of all sentient beings, one proclaims and reveals that all doors of dhāraṇī are neither proceeding nor not proceeding."
Why is this? Because the nature of all dhāraṇī-doors is empty; within emptiness there is neither going nor not-going.
All samādhi-doors likewise are neither going nor not-going.
Why is this? Because all gateways of samādhi are empty by nature, and within emptiness there is neither going nor not-going.
"For the sake of all sentient beings, I proclaim and reveal that the fruit of stream-entry is neither going nor not-going."
Why is this? Because the nature of the fruit of stream-entry is empty; within emptiness, there is neither going nor not-going.
The fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhat likewise are neither going nor not-going.
Why is this? Because the nature of the fruit of once-returner, non-returner, and arhat is empty; in emptiness there is neither proceeding nor not proceeding.
"For the sake of all sentient beings, one proclaims and reveals that pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is neither proceeding nor not proceeding."
Why is this? Because the nature of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is empty, and within emptiness there is neither going nor not-going.
"For the sake of all sentient beings, one proclaims and reveals that all bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices are neither going nor not-going."
Why is this? Because the nature of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas’ practices is empty; within emptiness, there is neither going nor not-going.
For the sake of all sentient beings, one proclaims and reveals that the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas is neither going nor not-going.
Why is this? Because the unexcelled, perfect enlightenment of all Buddhas is empty of intrinsic nature; within emptiness, there is neither proceeding nor not proceeding. "Subhūti!..."
This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva sets out for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment in order to provide a destination for the world.

*The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, Fascicle 315, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter Forty-five, "On the True and Good Friend," Section Four. "Why is this so?"
"Subhūti! All dharmas have emptiness as their destination, and they cannot transcend that destination. Why is this?"
Because in space, neither going nor coming can be apprehended.
"Subhūti! All phenomena have the signless as their destination; they cannot transcend that destination."
Why is this? Because within the signless, neither going nor not-going can be apprehended. "Subhūti!
All phenomena have wishlessness as their destination, and one cannot transcend that destination.
Why is this? Because within wishlessness, neither a destination nor a non-destination can be apprehended.

Because in that which is without arising and without activity, neither going nor not-going can be apprehended.

Why is this? Because within that which is neither arising nor ceasing, neither going nor coming can be apprehended. "Subhūti!..."

Why is this? Because within that which is neither increasing nor decreasing, neither coming nor going can be apprehended. "Subhūti!..."

Why? Because within non-entering and non-exiting, neither a goal nor a non-goal can be apprehended.

Because within non-accumulation and non-dispersion, neither a path nor a destination can be apprehended. "Subhūti!

Why is this? Because within that which is neither joined nor separated, neither going nor not-going cannot be apprehended. "Subhūti!..."

Why is this? Since the self ultimately does not exist at all, how could there be any obtainable "destination" or "non-destination"?

"Subhūti! All dharmas take the four bases of psychic power as their destination, and they cannot transcend that destination. Why is this?
Since even the four bases of psychic power (*ṛddhipāda*) are ultimately unobtainable, how much more so the going and non-going!
"Subhūti, all phenomena have the five faculties (*pañcendriya*) as their destination; they cannot transcend that destination."
Why is this? Because even the five faculties are ultimately unobtainable, let alone going or not going! "Subhūti!..."
All dharmas take the five powers as their destination, and one cannot transcend that destination.
Why is this? Since even the five powers are ultimately unobtainable, how much more so can there be a destination or a non-destination!
“Subhūti! All dharmas have the seven factors of enlightenment as their destination, and they cannot transcend that destination. Why is this?
"Even the seven factors of enlightenment are ultimately unattainable, let alone a going or a non-going!
Subhūti, all dharmas take the eightfold noble path as their destination, and they cannot transcend that destination."
Why is this? Because even the eight branches of the noble path are ultimately unattainable, let alone going or not going. "Subhūti!..."
All dharmas take the Noble Truth of Suffering as their destination, and one cannot transcend that destination.
Why is this? Since even the Noble Truth of Suffering is ultimately unattainable, how much more so the concepts of "destination" and "non-destination"!
“Subhūti! All dharmas have the noble truth of origination as their destination, and they cannot transcend that destination. Why is this?
Even the noble truth of cessation is ultimately unattainable, let alone going or not going!
"Subhūti, all phenomena take the noble truth of cessation as their destination, and they cannot transcend that destination."
Why is this? Because even the Noble Truth of Cessation is ultimately unobtainable, how much less so are there any going or non-going! "Subhūti!..."
All phenomena have the Noble Truth of the Path as their destination, and one cannot transcend that destination. Why is this?
Because even the Noble Truth of the Path is ultimately unattainable; how much more so, then, can there be a destination or a non-destination!
"Subhūti! All dharmas have the four dhyānas as their destination, and they cannot transcend that destination. Why is this?
"Even the four dhyānas are ultimately unattainable, let alone the states of going or not going!
Subhūti, all dharmas take the four immeasurables as their destination; they cannot transcend that destination."
Why is this? Because even the four immeasurables are ultimately unattainable, let alone going or not going! "Subhūti!
All dharmas take the four formless concentrations as their destination, and one cannot transcend that destination.
Why is this? Since even the four formless concentrations are ultimately unattainable, how much more so can there be a destination or a non-destination!
“Subhūti! All dharmas have the eight liberations as their destination, and they cannot transcend that destination. Why is this?
Since even the eight liberations are ultimately unobtainable, how much more so are there any going or non-going!
"Subhūti, all dharmas take the eight bases of mastery as their destination; they cannot transcend that destination."
Why is this? Even the eight bases of mastery (*aṣṭāv abhibhvāyatanāni*) are ultimately unapprehendable, let alone going or not going! "Subhūti!..."
All dharmas take the nine successive attainments as their destination, and they cannot transcend that destination.
Why is this? Since even the nine successive attainments are ultimately unattainable, how much more so the existence of a destination or a non-destination!
“Subhūti! All dharmas have the ten spheres of totality as their destination, and they cannot transcend that destination. Why is this?
Since even the ten spheres of totality (*daśa kṛtsnāyatana*) are ultimately unattainable, how much more so the states of going and not-going!
"Subhūti, all phenomena have the gate of liberation that is emptiness as their destination; they cannot transcend that destination."
Why is this? Since even the gate of liberation of emptiness is ultimately unattainable, how much more so are there any states of going or not going! "Subhūti!..."
All dharmas take the gateways of signlessness and wishlessness as their destination; one cannot transcend that destination.
Why is this? Since even the gateways of signlessness and wishlessness are ultimately unobtainable, how much more so the existence of a destination or a non-destination!
“Subhūti! All dharmas have the five eyes as their destination, and they cannot transcend that destination. Why is this?
Since even the five eyes are ultimately unattainable, how much more so are there any destinations or non-destinations!
"Subhūti, all dharmas take the six supernormal powers as their destination; they cannot transcend that destination."
Why is this? Even the six supernormal powers are ultimately unattainable, let alone coming or going! "Subhūti!..."
All dharmas take the gateways of samādhi as their destination, and they cannot transcend that destination.
Why is this? Since even the gateways of samādhi are ultimately unattainable, how much more so the existence of a destination or a non-destination!
"Subhūti! All dharmas have the gateways of dhāraṇī as their destination, and they cannot transcend that destination. Why is this?
Since even the gates of dhāraṇī are ultimately unattainable, how much more so the going and non-going!
"Subhūti, all phenomena take the ten powers of a Buddha as their destination; they cannot transcend that destination."
Why is this? Because even the ten powers of a Buddha are ultimately unattainable, let alone going or not going. "Subhūti!..."
All dharmas take the four fearlessnesses as their destination, and they cannot transcend that destination.
Why is this? Since even the four fearlessnesses are ultimately unattainable, how much more so the existence of a destination or a non-destination!
“Subhūti! All dharmas have the four analytical knowledges as their destination, and they cannot transcend that destination. Why is this?
Since even the four analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*) are ultimately unattainable, how much more so the going and not-going!
"Subhūti, all phenomena have great compassion as their destination; they cannot transcend that destination."
Why is this? Even great compassion is ultimately unattainable, let alone going or not going! "Subhūti!..."
All dharmas take great compassion, great joy, and great equanimity as their destination, and they cannot transcend that destination. Why is this?
Because even great compassion, great joy, and great equanimity are ultimately unattainable; how much more so, then, can there be a destination or a non-destination!
“Subhūti! All dharmas have the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha as their destination, and they cannot transcend that destination. Why is this?
Since even the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are ultimately unattainable, how much more so the states of going and not going!
"Subhūti, all dharmas take the fruit of stream-entry as their destination, and they cannot transcend that destination."
Why is this? Because even the fruit of stream-entry is ultimately unattainable, let alone going or not going. "Subhūti!..."
All dharmas have the fruit of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship as their destination; one cannot transcend that destination. Why is this?
Since even the fruits of Once-returner, Non-returner, and Arhat are ultimately unattainable, how much more so the going and non-going!
"Subhūti, all dharmas take the stream-enterer as their destination; they cannot transcend that destination."
Why is this? Even a stream-enterer is ultimately non-apprehensible, let alone going or not going! "Subhūti!..."
All dharmas have the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat as their destination; one cannot transcend that destination. Why is this?
Since even the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arhat are ultimately unfindable, how much more so the destination or non-destination!
"Subhūti, all dharmas take pratyekabuddha enlightenment as their destination; they cannot transcend that destination."
Why is this? Even the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is ultimately unattainable, let alone going or not going. "Subhūti!..."
All dharmas have the pratyekabuddha as their destination, and one cannot transcend that destination.
Why is this? Since even a pratyekabuddha is ultimately unattainable, how much more so can there be a destination or a non-destination!
“Subhūti! All dharmas have all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas as their destination, and they cannot transcend that destination. Why is this?
Since even all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are ultimately unobtainable, how much more so the going and the not-going!
"Subhūti! All dharmas take all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas as their destination; they cannot transcend that destination."
Why is this? Because even all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are ultimately non-apprehensible, let alone their going or not going!
"Suvikrāntavikrāmin!..."
All phenomena have the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas as their destination, and they cannot transcend that destination. Why is this?
Because even the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is ultimately unattainable; how much more so, then, can there be a destination or a non-destination!
“Subhūti! All dharmas have all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas as their destination; they cannot transcend that destination.”
Why is this? Because even all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas are ultimately unobtainable; how much more so, then, going or not going! "Subhūti!..."
All dharmas take all-knowledge as their destination, and one cannot transcend that destination.
Why is this? Since even all-knowledge is ultimately unattainable, how much more so can there be a destination or a non-destination!
“Subhūti! All dharmas take the knowledge of the paths as their destination, and they cannot transcend that destination. Why is this?
The knowledge of the aspects of the path is ultimately unattainable, let alone any coming or going!
"Subhūti, all phenomena have the knowledge of all aspects as their destination; they cannot transcend that destination."
Why is this? Because even omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*) is ultimately unobtainable, let alone coming or going!
"It is thus, Subhūti!"
"Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas set out for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment in order to serve as a destination for the world.
Chapter 46: On the Knowledge of the Destinations, Part One. At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
“Who, then, will be able to give rise to faith and understanding in such a profound perfection of wisdom?
The Buddha said, “Suvīra!...”

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva has long been intent upon unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, having resolved their mind to seek it with diligent practice; if they have already made offerings to hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of buddhas, having formed great vows in the presence of those buddhas; if their roots of goodness are fully matured and they are sustained by immeasurable virtuous friends—only then will they be able to give rise to faith and understanding in this profound prajñāpāramitā.
The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to give rise to faith and understanding toward such profound prajñāpāramitā, what is its nature?”
What are its characteristics? What are its signs?
What is its appearance?
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

This bodhisattva mahāsattva has a nature that subdues greed, hatred, and delusion; he has a characteristic that is remote from the signs of greed, hatred, and delusion; he has a form that is remote from the manifestations of greed, hatred, and delusion; he has an appearance that is remote from the features of greed, hatred, and delusion.”
Furthermore, Subhūti!

This bodhisattva mahāsattva takes as his nature the state of having subdued greed yet being without greed, hatred yet being without hatred, and delusion yet being without delusion; he takes as his characteristic the distancing from the marks of greed yet being without greed, hatred yet being without hatred, and delusion yet being without delusion; he takes as his manifestation the distancing from the signs of greed yet being without greed, hatred yet being without hatred, and delusion yet being without delusion; he takes as his appearance the distancing from the features of greed yet being without greed, hatred yet being without hatred, and delusion yet being without delusion.

"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is endowed with such a nature, characteristics, marks, and features, they will be able to give rise to faith and understanding in this profound perfection of wisdom."
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
if a bodhisattva mahāsattva has faith and understanding in such a profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), where will they be headed?”
The Buddha said,
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva shall proceed toward the knowledge of all modes.”
The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva proceeds toward the knowledge of all modes, they can serve as a place of refuge for all sentient beings.”
The Buddha said, “So it is, Subhūti!”
So it is! It is just as you have said.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to believe in and understand this profound perfection of wisdom, they will be able to advance toward the knowledge of all modes.
"If one is able to incline toward the knowledge of all modes, then that person can serve as a refuge for all sentient beings.
Subhūti spoke again:
"World-Honored One!"
This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to perform what is difficult to do, namely, donning such firm armor as this:

"I shall deliver all sentient beings and cause them all to realize ultimate nirvāṇa. Although they perform such deeds for sentient beings, they do not perceive the conceptual designation of "sentient beings" at all.
The Buddha said,
“So it is, Subhūti! It is so!”
"So it is! It is as you have said.
This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to perform what is difficult, namely, donning such firm armor as this:"

"I shall deliver all sentient beings, causing them all to realize ultimate nirvāṇa; yet, although I perform such deeds for sentient beings, I do not perceive the conceptual designation of 'sentient beings' at all."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
The armor donned by this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not belong to form. Why is that? "
Because form is ultimately non-existent—being neither the bodhisattva nor the armor—it is said that this armor does not belong to form.
This armor donned by the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not belong to feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.

Why is this? Because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are ultimately non-existent, being neither the bodhisattva nor the armor; therefore, it is said that this armor does not belong to feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.
“Subhūti! The armor donned by this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not belong to the sense-base of the eye. Why is that?
Because the sense-base of the eye is ultimately non-existent—being neither the bodhisattva nor the armor—it is said that this armor does not belong to the sense-base of the eye.
This armor donned by the bodhisattva mahāsattva likewise does not belong to the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind.

Why is this? Because the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are ultimately non-existent, being neither the bodhisattva nor the armor; therefore, it is said that this armor does not belong to the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind.
“Subhūti! The armor donned by this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not belong to the sphere of form. Why is that?
Because the sense-base of form is ultimately non-existent, being neither the bodhisattva nor the armor, it is said that this armor does not belong to the sense-base of form.
This armor donned by the bodhisattva-mahāsattva does not belong to the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena.

Why is this? Because the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena are ultimately non-existent, being neither the bodhisattva nor the armor; therefore, it is said that this armor does not belong to the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, touch, or mental phenomena.
“Subhūti! The armor donned by this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not belong to the eye-sphere. Why is that?
Because the eye-element is ultimately non-existent, being neither the bodhisattva nor the armor, it is said that this armor does not belong to the eye-element.
This armor donned by the bodhisattva-mahāsattva does not belong to the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-element.

Why is this? Because the realms of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are ultimately non-existent, being neither the bodhisattva nor the armor; therefore, it is said that this armor does not belong to the realms of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind.
“Subhūti! The armor donned by this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not belong to the realm of form. Why is that?
Because the realm of form (*rūpadhātu*) is ultimately non-existent, being neither the bodhisattva nor the armor, it is said that this armor does not belong to the realm of form.
This armor donned by the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not belong to the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena (*dharmadhātu*).

Why is this? Because the realms of sound, fragrance, taste, touch, and mental phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) are ultimately non-existent; since they are neither the bodhisattva nor the armor, it is said that this armor does not belong to the realms of sound, fragrance, taste, touch, or mental phenomena.
“Subhūti! This armor donned by the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not belong to the eye-consciousness element. Why is that?
Because the eye-consciousness element is ultimately non-existent, being neither the bodhisattva nor the armor, it is said that this armor does not belong to the eye-consciousness element.
This armor donned by the bodhisattva-mahāsattva likewise does not belong to the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-consciousness elements.

Why is this? Because the realms of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mental consciousness are ultimately non-existent, being neither the bodhisattva nor the armor; therefore, it is said that this armor does not belong to the realms of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mental consciousness.
“Subhūti! The armor donned by this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not belong to eye-contact. Why is that?
Because eye-contact is ultimately non-existent, being neither the bodhisattva nor the armor, it is said that this armor does not belong to eye-contact.
This armor donned by the bodhisattva-mahāsattva does not belong to ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact.

Why is this? Because ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, and mind-contact are ultimately non-existent, being neither the bodhisattva nor the armor; therefore, it is said that this armor does not belong to ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, or mind-contact.
“Subhūti! This armor donned by the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not belong to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition. Why is that?

Because the various sensations produced with eye-contact as a condition are ultimately non-existent—neither being a bodhisattva nor a suit of armor—it is said that this armor does not belong to the various sensations produced with eye-contact as a condition.
The armor donned by this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not belong to the various feelings produced with the contact of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind as a condition. Why is that?

The various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions are ultimately non-existent; because they are neither the bodhisattva nor the armor, it is said that this armor does not belong to the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions.
“Subhūti! This armor donned by the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not belong to the earth element. Why is that?
Because the earth element is ultimately non-existent—being neither the bodhisattva nor the armor—it is said that this armor does not belong to the earth element.
This armor donned by the bodhisattva-mahāsattva does not belong to the elements of water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness.

Why is this? Because the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are ultimately non-existent, being neither the bodhisattva nor the armor; therefore, it is said that this armor does not belong to the elements of water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness.
"Subhūti! This armor donned by the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not belong to ignorance. Why is that?
Because ignorance is ultimately non-existent—neither being the bodhisattva nor the armor—it is said that this armor does not belong to ignorance.

This armor donned by the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not belong to volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, sensation, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, or old age and death.

Why is this? Because from volitional formations up to old age and death, there is ultimately nothing that exists; since they are neither the bodhisattva nor the armor, it is said that this armor does not belong to volitional formations up to old age and death.
“Subhūti! This armor donned by the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not belong to a self. Why is that?
Since I am ultimately non-existent—being neither a bodhisattva nor armor—it is said that this armor does not belong to me.

This armor donned by the bodhisattva-mahāsattva does not belong to a sentient being (*sattva*), a life-principle (*jīva*), a creature (*jantu*), a nourisher (*poṣa*), a person (*puruṣa*), an individual (*pudgala*), a mind-born (*manuja*), a youth (*māṇava*), an agent (*kāraka*), an experiencer (*vedaka*), a knower (*jñātṛ*), or a seer (*draṣṭṛ*).

Why is this? Because sentient beings, up to and including the "seer," are ultimately non-existent; since they are neither the bodhisattva nor the armor, it is said that this armor does not belong to sentient beings, up to and including the seer.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle Three Hundred Sixteen. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter Forty-Six, "Proceeding to Knowledge," Section Two. "Subhūti!
The armor donned by this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not belong to the perfection of generosity. Why is that?
Because the perfection of generosity is ultimately non-existent, being neither the bodhisattva nor the armor; therefore, it is said that his armor does not belong to the perfection of generosity.
The armor donned by this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not belong to the perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom.

Why is this? Because from pure ethical discipline up to the perfection of wisdom, there is ultimately nothing that exists; since they are neither the bodhisattva nor the armor, it is said that this armor does not belong to pure ethical discipline up to the perfection of wisdom.
“Subhūti! This armor donned by the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not belong to internal emptiness. Why is that?
Because inner emptiness is ultimately non-existent—being neither the bodhisattva nor the armor—it is said that this armor does not belong to inner emptiness.

This armor donned by the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not belong to outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate, the emptiness of the conditioned, the emptiness of the unconditioned, absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self-characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

Why is this? Because from external emptiness up to the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature, there is ultimately nothing whatsoever; since they are neither the bodhisattva nor the armor, it is said that those armors do not belong to external emptiness up to the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature.
“Subhūti! This armor donned by the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not belong to suchness. Why is that?
Because suchness is ultimately non-existent—being neither the bodhisattva nor the armor—it is said that this armor does not belong to suchness.

This armor donned by the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not belong to the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the non-falsity of phenomena, the unchanging nature of phenomena, the equality of phenomena, the nature free from birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of empty space, or the inconceivable realm.

Why is this? Because from the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, there is ultimately nothing whatsoever; since they are neither the bodhisattva nor the armor, it is said that those armors do not belong to the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm.
"Subhūti! The armor donned by this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not belong to the four applications of mindfulness. Why is that?
Because the four foundations of mindfulness are ultimately non-existent—being neither the bodhisattva nor the armor—it is said that this armor does not belong to the four foundations of mindfulness.

This armor donned by the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not belong to the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path.

Why is this? Because the four right efforts up to the eight branches of the noble path ultimately do not exist, and because they are neither the bodhisattva nor the armor; therefore, it is said that this armor does not belong to the four right efforts up to the eight branches of the noble path.
“Subhūti! This armor donned by the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not belong to the noble truth of suffering. Why is that?
Because the noble truth of suffering is ultimately non-existent, being neither the bodhisattva nor the armor, it is said that this armor does not belong to the noble truth of suffering.
This armor donned by the bodhisattva mahāsattva likewise does not belong to the noble truths of origin, cessation, or the path.

Why is this? Because the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path ultimately do not exist; since they are neither the bodhisattva nor the armor, it is said that this armor does not belong to the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path.
“Subhūti! The armor donned by this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not belong to the four dhyānas. Why is that?
"The four dhyānas are ultimately non-existent; because they are neither the bodhisattva nor the armor, it is said that this armor does not belong to the four dhyānas. Subhūti!"
The armor donned by this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not belong to the four immeasurables.
Why is this? Because the four immeasurables are ultimately non-existent, being neither the bodhisattva nor the armor; therefore, it is said that his armor does not belong to the four immeasurables.
“Subhūti! The armor donned by this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not belong to the four formless absorptions. Why is that?

The four formless absorptions are ultimately non-existent; because they are neither the bodhisattva nor the armor, it is said that this armor does not belong to the four formless absorptions. "Subhūti!..."
The armor donned by this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not belong to the eight liberations.
Why is that? Because the eight liberations ultimately do not exist, being neither the bodhisattva nor the armor; therefore, it is said that the armor does not belong to the eight liberations.
“Subhūti! The armor donned by this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not belong to the eight bases of mastery. Why is that?
The eight bases of mastery are ultimately non-existent; because they are neither the bodhisattva nor the armor, it is said that this armor does not belong to the eight bases of mastery. "Subhūti!..."
The armor donned by this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not belong to the nine successive attainments.

Why is that? Because the nine successive attainments ultimately do not exist; since they are neither the bodhisattva nor the armor, it is said that the armor does not belong to the nine successive attainments.
“Subhūti! The armor donned by this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not belong to the ten spheres of totality. Why is that?

The ten spheres of totality (daśakṛtsnāyatana) are ultimately non-existent; because they are neither the bodhisattva nor the armor, it is said that this armor does not belong to the ten spheres of totality. "Subhūti!..."
The armor donned by this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not belong to the liberation door of emptiness.

Why is that? Because the liberation door of emptiness is ultimately non-existent, being neither the bodhisattva nor the armor; therefore, it is said that the armor does not belong to the liberation door of emptiness.
The armor donned by this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not belong to the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.

Why is that? Because the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are ultimately non-existent, being neither the bodhisattva nor the armor; therefore, it is said that his armor does not belong to the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.
“Subhūti! The armor donned by this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not belong to the five eyes. Why is that?
The five eyes are ultimately non-existent; because they are neither the bodhisattva nor the armor, it is said that this armor does not belong to the five eyes.
"Subhūti! This armor donned by the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not belong to the six supernormal powers."

Why is this? Because the six supernormal powers (ṣaḍabhijñā) are ultimately non-existent, being neither the bodhisattva nor the armor; therefore, it is said that this armor does not belong to the six supernormal powers.
“Subhūti! The armor donned by this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not belong to the gateways of samādhi. Why is that?

Because the gateways of samādhi ultimately do not exist, and because they are neither the bodhisattva nor the armor, it is said that this armor does not belong to the gateways of samādhi. "Subhūti!..."
The armor donned by this bodhisattva-mahāsattva does not belong to the gateways of dhāraṇī. Why is that?
Because the gateways of dhāraṇī are ultimately non-existent, being neither the bodhisattva nor the armor; therefore, it is said that the armor does not belong to the gateways of dhāraṇī.
“Subhūti! This armor donned by the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not belong to the ten powers of a Buddha. Why is that?
Because the ten powers of a Buddha are ultimately non-existent—being neither the bodhisattva nor the armor—it is said that this armor does not belong to the ten powers of a Buddha.

This armor donned by the bodhisattva-mahāsattva does not belong to the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.

Why is this? Because the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are ultimately non-existent, being neither the bodhisattva nor the armor; therefore, it is said that this armor does not belong to the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“Subhūti! The armor donned by this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not belong to the fruit of stream-entry. Why is that?
Because the fruit of stream-entry is ultimately non-existent—being neither the bodhisattva nor the armor—it is said that this armor does not belong to the fruit of stream-entry.
This armor donned by the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not belong to the fruit of once-returning, non-returning, or arhatship.

Why is this? Because the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhat are ultimately non-existent; since they are neither the bodhisattva nor the armor, it is said that this armor does not belong to the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, or arhat.
"Subhūti! The armor donned by this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not belong to the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha. Why is that?
"Because Pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is ultimately non-existent—being neither a bodhisattva nor armor—it is said that this armor does not belong to Pratyekabuddha-enlightenment. Subhūti!"
The armor donned by this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not belong to omniscience (*sarvajñatā*). Why is that?
Because omniscience is ultimately non-existent, being neither the bodhisattva nor the armor; therefore, it is said that the armor does not belong to omniscience.
The armor donned by this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not belong to the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) or the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*). Why is that?

Because the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are ultimately non-existent, being neither the bodhisattva nor the armor; therefore, it is said that this armor does not belong to the knowledge of the aspects of the path or the knowledge of all aspects.
“Subhūti! The armor donned by this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not belong to any phenomena. Why is that?
Because all phenomena are ultimately non-existent, being neither the bodhisattva nor the armor, it is said that this armor does not belong to any phenomenon. "Subhūti!

When these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the profound perfection of wisdom, they are able to don such firm armor as this: "I shall deliver all sentient beings and cause them all to realize ultimate nirvāṇa."
The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can don such firm armor as this—vowing, ‘I shall deliver all sentient beings and cause them all to realize parinirvāṇa’—they will not fall into the two levels of the śrāvaka or the pratyekabuddha.”

"Bhagavān! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can don such firm armor, saying, 'I shall deliver all sentient beings and cause them all to realize parinirvāṇa,' there is no possibility or occasion for that bodhisattva mahāsattva to fall into the two levels—namely, the level of the śrāvaka and the level of the pratyekabuddha."
Why is this so? World-Honored One!
It is because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do not establish limits regarding sentient beings when they don such firm armor.
The Buddha said,
“Sudhana! Based on what meaning do you speak these words?”
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can don such firm armor and practice the profound perfection of wisdom, will they not fall into the two levels of the śrāvaka or the pratyekabuddha?
Subhūti replied, “World-Honored One!

It is because this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not don the armor for the sake of liberating only a small portion of sentient beings, nor does he don the armor for the sake of seeking only a small portion of wisdom.”
Why is this? World-Honored One!

This bodhisattva mahāsattva dons the armor for the sake of universally rescuing and delivering all sentient beings so that they may attain parinirvāṇa; this bodhisattva mahāsattva dons the armor solely for the purpose of seeking to attain the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna). By virtue of these causes and conditions, he does not fall into the levels of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas.
