The Buddha said,
"Excellent, Subhūti! It is so!"
"So it is! It is as you have said.

This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not don the armor for the sake of liberating only a limited number of sentient beings, nor does he don the armor for the sake of seeking only a limited wisdom. Rather, this bodhisattva mahāsattva dons the armor for the purpose of rescuing and delivering all sentient beings so that they may attain parinirvāṇa; this bodhisattva mahāsattva dons the armor solely for the purpose of attaining the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna). By virtue of these causes and conditions, this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not fall into the levels of the śrāvaka or the pratyekabuddha."
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
This Prajñāpāramitā is most profound; there is no one who can practice it, no dharma to be practiced, no place for practice, and nothing by which it can be cultivated.”
Why is this so? World-Honored One,

within this profound meaning of the *prajñāpāramitā*, there is not even the slightest portion of a real dharma that can be designated as the "one who practices," the "dharma being practiced," the "place of practice," or that "by which one practices."
"Bhagavān! If one cultivates space, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā). Bhagavān!"
"Blessed One, if one cultivates all dharmas, that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.
Blessed One,
if one cultivates unreal dharmas, that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom."
Bhagavān! If one cultivates non-existence, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā). Bhagavān!
"Bhagavān, if one cultivates non-appropriation, that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom. Bhagavān,
if one cultivates thorough relinquishment, that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom."
The Buddha said,
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
What is it that one cultivates and eliminates when cultivating the perfection of wisdom?”
Subhūti replied, “World-Honored One,

to cultivate the elimination of form is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom; to cultivate the elimination of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.”
“World-Honored One!

To cultivate the elimination of the sense base of the eye is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom; to cultivate the elimination of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.”
“World-Honored One!

To cultivate the removal of the sphere of form is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom; to cultivate the removal of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.”
“World-Honored One!

To cultivate the removal of the eye-element is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom; to cultivate the removal of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-elements is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.”

“Bhagavān, to cultivate the removal of the sphere of form is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom; to cultivate the removal of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.”
“World-Honored One!

To cultivate the elimination of the eye-consciousness element is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom; to cultivate the elimination of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.”
“World-Honored One!

To cultivate the elimination of eye-contact is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom; to cultivate the elimination of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.”

“Bhagavān, to cultivate the removal of all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom; to cultivate the removal of all feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact as condition is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.”
“World-Honored One!

To cultivate the elimination of the earth element is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom; to cultivate the elimination of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.”
“World-Honored One!

To cultivate the elimination of ignorance is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom; to cultivate the elimination of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age and death is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.”

“Bhagavān, to cultivate the removal of a self is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom; to cultivate the removal of a sentient being, a life-principle, a creature, a nourisher, a spirit, a person, a soul, a youth, an agent, an experiencer, a knower, or a seer is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.”
“World-Honored One!

To cultivate the removal of the perfection of giving is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom; to cultivate the removal of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.”

“Bhagavān, the cultivation of the thorough removal of internal emptiness is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*). The cultivation of the thorough removal of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.”
“World-Honored One!

To cultivate the removal of suchness is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom; to cultivate the removal of the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-erroneousness, immutability, equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.”

“Bhagavān, the cultivation of the relinquishment of the four foundations of mindfulness is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom; the cultivation of the relinquishment of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.”
“World-Honored One!

To cultivate the removal of the noble truth of suffering is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom; to cultivate the removal of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.”

“Bhagavān, the cultivation of the thorough removal of the four dhyānas is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom. Bhagavān, [the cultivation of the thorough removal of the four formless attainments is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.]”
To cultivate the elimination of the four immeasurables is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.
"World-Honored One!
To cultivate the elimination of the four formless attainments is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom."
“World-Honored One!
To cultivate the removal of the eight liberations is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.
World-Honored One!”
To cultivate the removal of the eight bases of mastery is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.
“World-Honored One!
To cultivate the removal of the nine successive attainments is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.”
“World-Honored One!
To cultivate the thorough removal of the ten totalities (daśakṛtsnāyatana) is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
World-Honored One!”

To cultivate the removal of the door of liberation of emptiness is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom; to cultivate the removal of the doors of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.
“World-Honored One!
To cultivate the elimination of the five eyes is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.
World-Honored One!”
To cultivate the removal of the six supernormal powers is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.
"World-Honored One!
To cultivate the removal of the gateways of samādhi is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom."
“World-Honored One!
To cultivate the thorough removal of the gateways of dhāraṇī is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.
World-Honored One!”

To cultivate the elimination of the ten powers of a Buddha is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom; to cultivate the elimination of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.

“Bhagavān, the cultivation of the removal of the fruit of stream-entry is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom; the cultivation of the removal of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.”
“World-Honored One!
To cultivate the thorough removal of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.
World-Honored One!”

To cultivate the elimination of all-knowledge is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom; to cultivate the elimination of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.
The Buddha said,
“So it is, Subhūti! It is even so!”
"So it is! It is just as you have said, Subhūti."

To cultivate the removal of form is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom; to cultivate the removal of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.

“Subhūti! To cultivate the removal of the sphere of the eye is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom; to cultivate the removal of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! To cultivate the removal of the sphere of forms is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom; to cultivate the removal of the spheres of sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, and mental phenomena is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! To cultivate the elimination of the eye-element is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom; to cultivate the elimination of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! To cultivate the removal of the realm of form is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom; to cultivate the removal of the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! To cultivate the relinquishment of the eye-consciousness element is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom; to cultivate the relinquishment of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! To cultivate the elimination of eye-contact is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom; to cultivate the elimination of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! To cultivate the removal of all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom; to cultivate the removal of all feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! To cultivate the removal of the earth element is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom; to cultivate the removal of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! To cultivate the removal of ignorance is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom; to cultivate the removal of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age and death is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! To cultivate the removal of the notion of a self is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom; to cultivate the removal of the notions of a sentient being, a life-principle, a soul, a nourisher, a spirit, a person, a human, a youth, an agent, an experiencer, a knower, and a viewer is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! To cultivate the relinquishment of the perfection of generosity is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom; to cultivate the relinquishment of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! To cultivate the removal of internal emptiness is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom; to cultivate the removal of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! To cultivate the removal of suchness is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom; to cultivate the removal of the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-illusoriness, immutability, equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! To cultivate the elimination of the four applications of mindfulness is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom; to cultivate the elimination of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! To cultivate the removal of the noble truth of suffering is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom; to cultivate the removal of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.”
“Subhūti! To cultivate the removal of the four dhyānas is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom. Subhūti!”
To cultivate the removal of the four immeasurables is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.
Subhūti, to cultivate the removal of the four formless attainments is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.
“Subhūti! To cultivate the removal of the eight liberations is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom. Subhūti!”
To cultivate the elimination of the eight bases of mastery is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.
"Subhūti, to cultivate the elimination of the nine successive attainments is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom."
“Subhūti! To cultivate the removal of the ten totalities (daśakṛtsnāyatana) is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā). Subhūti!”

To cultivate the relinquishment of the gate of liberation of emptiness is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom; to cultivate the relinquishment of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.
“Subhūti! To cultivate the elimination of the five eyes is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom. Subhūti!”
To cultivate the elimination of the six supernormal powers is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.
"Subhūti! To cultivate the elimination of the gateways of samādhi is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom."
“Subhūti! Cultivating the removal of the gateways of dhāraṇī is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom. Subhūti!”

To cultivate the removal of the ten powers of a Buddha is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom; to cultivate the removal of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.

"Subhūti! To cultivate the removal of the fruit of stream-entry is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom; to cultivate the removal of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom."
“Subhūti! To cultivate the removal of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom. Subhūti!”

To cultivate the elimination of all-knowledge is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom; to cultivate the elimination of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects is to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Venerable Subhūti, saying: “Subhūti!

One should recognize a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva by means of the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā). If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not give rise to attachment toward the profound perfection of wisdom, you should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.”

“Subhūti! One should recognize a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva by means of the profound perfection of meditative concentration (dhyānapāramitā). If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not give rise to attachment toward the profound perfection of meditative concentration, you should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.”

“Subhūti! One should recognize a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva by means of the profound perfection of diligence. If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not give rise to attachment toward the profound perfection of diligence, you should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.”

“Subhūti! One should recognize a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva by means of the profound perfection of patience (kṣāntipāramitā). If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not give rise to attachment toward the profound perfection of patience, you should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.”

“Subhūti! One should recognize a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva by means of the profound perfection of ethical discipline (śīla-pāramitā). If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not give rise to attachment toward the profound perfection of ethical discipline, you should know that he is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.”

“Subhūti! One should recognize a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva by means of the profound perfection of generosity (dānapāramitā). If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not give rise to attachment toward the profound perfection of generosity, you should know that he is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.”

“Subhūti! One should verify that an irreversible bodhisattva mahāsattva relies upon inner emptiness (adhyātma-śūnyatā). If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not give rise to attachment toward inner emptiness, you should know that this is an irreversible bodhisattva mahāsattva.”

One should verify a non-retrogressive Bodhisattva Mahāsattva by means of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature. If a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva does not give rise to attachment toward these, from external emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, it should be known that this is a non-retrogressive Bodhisattva Mahāsattva.

"Subhūti! One should recognize a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva by means of *tathatā*. If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not give rise to attachment toward *tathatā*, you should know that he is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva."

One should verify that a bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-retrogressive by means of the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, the state of non-falsity, the state of non-alteration, equality, the state of being free from birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm. If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not give rise to attachment toward the dharma-realm and so forth, up to the inconceivable realm, one should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.

“Subhūti! One should verify that an irreversible bodhisattva mahāsattva relies upon the four foundations of mindfulness; if a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not give rise to attachment toward the four foundations of mindfulness, one should know him to be an irreversible bodhisattva mahāsattva.”

One should verify that a bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-retrogressive by means of the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path. If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not give rise to attachment toward the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path, one should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.

“Subhūti! One should verify an irreversible bodhisattva mahāsattva by means of the noble truth of suffering. If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not give rise to attachment toward the noble truth of suffering, you should know that he is an irreversible bodhisattva mahāsattva.”

One should verify that an irreversible bodhisattva mahāsattva relies upon the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path; if a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not give rise to attachment toward the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path, one should know that this is an irreversible bodhisattva mahāsattva.

"Subhūti! One should verify a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva by means of the four dhyānas. If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not give rise to attachment toward the four dhyānas, you should know that he is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva."

"Subhūti! One should recognize a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva by means of the four immeasurables. If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not give rise to attachment toward the four immeasurables, you should know that he is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva."

“Subhūti! One should verify that an irreversible bodhisattva mahāsattva relies upon the four formless absorptions; if a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not give rise to attachment toward the four formless absorptions, you should know that this is an irreversible bodhisattva mahāsattva.”

“Subhūti! One should verify that a bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-retrogressive by means of the eight liberations. If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not give rise to attachment toward the eight liberations, you should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.”

“Subhūti! One should verify that a bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-retrogressive by means of the eight bases of mastery (aṣṭāv abhibhvāyatanāni). If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not give rise to attachment toward the eight bases of mastery, you should know that he is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.”

“Subhūti! One should verify that a bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-retrogressive by means of the nine successive attainments (*navānupūrvavihārasamāpatti*). If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not give rise to attachment toward the nine successive attainments, one should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.”

“Subhūti! One should verify that an irreversible bodhisattva mahāsattva relies upon the ten spheres of totality (daśa kṛtsnāyatanāni). If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not give rise to attachment toward the ten spheres of totality, you should know that this is an irreversible bodhisattva mahāsattva.”

“Subhūti! One should verify a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva by means of the gate of liberation that is emptiness. If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not give rise to attachment toward the gate of liberation that is emptiness, you should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.”

One should verify that an irreversible Bodhisattva Mahāsattva relies upon the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness; if a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva does not give rise to attachment toward the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, one should know that this is an irreversible Bodhisattva Mahāsattva.

“Subhūti! One should verify that a bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-retrogressive by means of the five eyes. If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not give rise to attachment toward the five eyes, you should know that he is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.”

“Subhūti! One should recognize a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva by means of the six supernormal powers (*ṣaḍabhijñā*). If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not give rise to attachment toward these six supernormal powers, you should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.”

“Subhūti! One should verify that a bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-retrogressive by means of the gateways of samādhi. If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not give rise to attachment toward the gateways of samādhi, you should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.”

“Subhūti! One should recognize a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva by means of the dhāraṇī-doors. If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not give rise to attachment toward the dhāraṇī-doors, you should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.”

“Subhūti! One should verify that a bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-retrogressive by means of the ten powers of a Buddha. If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not give rise to attachment toward the ten powers of a Buddha, you should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.”

One should recognize a non-regressive bodhisattva mahāsattva by means of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha. If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not give rise to attachment toward these—from the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha—one should know that this is a non-regressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.

“Subhūti! One should recognize a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva by means of the verification of omniscience (*sarvajñatā*). If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not give rise to attachment toward omniscience, you should know that he is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.”

One should verify that a bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-retrogressive by relying on the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects; if a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not give rise to attachment toward the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, one should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
"Subhūti! Those non-retrogressive bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice profound prajñāpāramitā do not regard the words or instructions of others as the essential truth."
“Subhūti! When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who are non-retrogressive practice profound prajñāpāramitā, they do not act merely by relying on the faith of others.”

“Subhūti! Those non-retrogressive bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice profound prajñāpāramitā are not led astray by a mind of greed, nor led astray by a mind of hatred, nor led astray by a mind of delusion, nor led astray by a mind of pride, nor led astray by various other defiled minds.”

“Subhūti! All those non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattvas who practice the profound perfection of wisdom do not depart from the perfection of generosity, do not depart from the perfection of ethical discipline, do not depart from the perfection of patience, do not depart from the perfection of diligence, do not depart from the perfection of meditative concentration, and do not depart from the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! When bodhisattva mahāsattvas who are non-retrogressive hear this teaching of the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), their minds are not startled, not terrified, not frightened, do not sink, and do not become despondent; nor do they abandon it. They joyfully delight in hearing this profound perfection of wisdom, receiving and upholding it, reading and reciting it, mastering it thoroughly, reflecting upon it with focused mindfulness, and practicing according to the teaching without ever becoming weary.”

"Subhūti, you should know that such non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattvas have, in previous lives, already heard the meaning and purport of this profound perfection of wisdom, and have upheld, recited, and reflected upon it according to the principle."
Why is this? Subhūti!

Because when these non-retrogressive bodhisattva-mahāsattvas hear this teaching of the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), their minds are not startled, not terrified, not afraid, do not sink, and do not become despondent; nor do they turn back or abandon it. Rather, regarding this profound perfection of wisdom, they joyfully delight in hearing it, receiving and upholding it, reading and reciting it, mastering it thoroughly, reflecting upon it with focused mindfulness, and practicing according to the teaching without weariness.
The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying: “World-Honored One, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva,

upon hearing this teaching of the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, their mind is not startled, not terrified, not afraid, does not sink, does not become despondent, and neither retreats nor abandons it— how should such a bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the profound *prajñāpāramitā*?”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

This bodhisattva mahāsattva, whose mental continuity accords with, tends toward, and enters into all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna), should practice the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) in this manner.”
“World-Honored One!

How does this bodhisattva mahāsattva continuously accord with, incline toward, and enter into the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), practicing the profound perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*)?”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva continuously accords with, inclines toward, and enters into emptiness, practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva continuously accords with, inclines toward, and enters into the knowledge of all aspects, practicing the profound perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva continuously accords with, inclines toward, and enters into the signless, practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva who continuously accords with, inclines toward, and enters into all-knowledge, practicing the profound perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva continuously accords with, inclines toward, and enters into wishlessness, practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva who continuously accords with, inclines toward, and enters into the knowledge of all modes, practicing the profound perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva continuously accords with, inclines toward, and enters into space, practicing the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, this is what it means for a bodhisattva mahāsattva to continuously accord with, incline toward, and enter into the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*), practicing the profound *prajñāpāramitā*.

"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva continuously accords with, inclines toward, and enters into non-existence while practicing the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva who continuously accords with, inclines toward, and enters into the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*) while practicing the profound *prajñāpāramitā*."

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva continuously accords with, inclines toward, and enters into that which is without arising and without cessation, practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva who continuously accords with, inclines toward, and enters into the knowledge of all modes, practicing the profound perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva continuously accords with, inclines toward, and enters into that which is neither stained nor pure, practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva who continuously accords with, inclines toward, and enters into the knowledge of all modes, practicing the profound perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva continuously accords with, inclines toward, and enters into suchness while practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva continuously accords with, inclines toward, and enters into the knowledge of all modes while practicing the profound perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva continuously accords with, inclines toward, and enters the dharmadhātu while practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva who continuously accords with, inclines toward, and enters all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna) while practicing the profound perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, in a continuous stream, conforms to, inclines toward, and enters into the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), practicing the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva who, in a continuous stream, conforms to, inclines toward, and enters into the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), practicing the profound perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva continuously accords with, inclines toward, and enters into the nature of non-falsity, practicing the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, this is what it means for a bodhisattva mahāsattva to continuously accord with, incline toward, and enter into the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*), practicing the profound *prajñāpāramitā*.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva continuously accords with, inclines toward, and enters into the state of non-alteration while practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, this is what it means for a bodhisattva mahāsattva to continuously accord with, incline toward, and enter into all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna) while practicing the profound perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva continuously accords with, inclines toward, and enters into the state of equality while practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva continuously accords with, inclines toward, and enters into the knowledge of all modes while practicing the profound perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, in a continuous succession, conforms to, inclines toward, and enters into the state of certainty (*niyāma*), and practices the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva who, in a continuous succession, conforms to, inclines toward, and enters into the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*), and practices the profound *prajñāpāramitā*.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, in a continuous succession, conforms to, inclines toward, and enters into the concentration of dharmas, practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva who, in a continuous succession, conforms to, inclines toward, and enters into the knowledge of all modes, practicing the profound perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva continuously accords with, inclines toward, and enters into the abiding of phenomena (dharmasthiti), practicing the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), this is what it means for a bodhisattva mahāsattva to continuously accord with, incline toward, and enter into the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna), practicing the profound perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva continuously accords with, inclines toward, and approaches the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) while practicing the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva who continuously accords with, inclines toward, and approaches all-knowledge (sarvajñājñāna) while practicing the profound perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva continuously accords with, inclines toward, and enters the realm of space while practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva who continuously accords with, inclines toward, and enters the knowledge of all modes while practicing the profound perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva continuously accords with, inclines toward, and enters the inconceivable realm while practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva who continuously accords with, inclines toward, and enters the knowledge of all modes while practicing the profound perfection of wisdom.”

"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva continuously accords with, inclines toward, and enters into non-activity, practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva who continuously accords with, inclines toward, and enters into the knowledge of all modes, practicing the profound perfection of wisdom."

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva continuously accords with, inclines toward, and enters into illusion, practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, this is what it means for a bodhisattva mahāsattva to continuously accord with, incline toward, and enter into the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), practicing the profound perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while dreaming, continues in accordance with, inclines toward, and enters into the practice of profound prajñāpāramitā, this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva continuing in accordance with, inclining toward, and entering into omniscience (sarvajñājñāna) while practicing profound prajñāpāramitā.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva continuously accords with, inclines toward, and enters into resonance while practicing the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva continuously accords with, inclines toward, and enters into the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*) while practicing the profound *prajñāpāramitā*.

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva continuously accords with, inclines toward, and enters into the semblance [of omniscience], practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva who continuously accords with, inclines toward, and enters into all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna), practicing the profound perfection of wisdom.”

"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva continuously accords with, inclines toward, and enters into the reflection, practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva who continuously accords with, inclines toward, and enters into the knowledge of all modes, practicing the profound perfection of wisdom."

"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva continuously accords with, inclines toward, and enters into the mirage while practicing the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva continuously accords with, inclines toward, and enters into all-knowledge (*sarvajñājñāna*) while practicing the profound *prajñāpāramitā*."

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva continuously accords with, inclines toward, and enters into transformative activities while practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva continuously accords with, inclines toward, and enters into the knowledge of all modes while practicing the profound perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva continues in accordance with, proceeds toward, and enters the City of Fragrance, practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva continuing in accordance with, proceeding toward, and entering all-knowledge (sarvajñājñāna), practicing the profound perfection of wisdom.”

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll Three Hundred Seventeen. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Chapter Forty-Six, Part Three: "Proceeding toward Knowledge. At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
As the Buddha has taught, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva continuously accords with, inclines toward, and enters into emptiness, signlessness, wishlessness, space,
non-existence, non-arising and non-ceasing, non-defilement and non-purity,
suchness, the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, the non-erroneous nature, and immutability...
Otherness, equality, the state of being free from birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena,
the limit of reality, the realm of space, the inconceivable realm, non-activity, illusion, a dream, an echo, a reflection,
a shadow, a mirage, a magical creation, and a city of Gandharvas— [these are] the practice of profound prajñāpāramitā.

O Bhagavān, this is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva who practices the profound *prajñāpāramitā* continuously accords with, progresses toward, and enters into the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*). This is the *pāramitā*.
“Does this bodhisattva mahāsattva practice with respect to form?
Does he practice with respect to feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness?
“World-Honored One! [he asked.]
"Does this bodhisattva mahāsattva practice with respect to the sense-base of the eye?
Does he practice with respect to the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind? [He replied:
"World-Honored One!"
“Does this bodhisattva mahāsattva practice with respect to the sphere of form?
Does he practice with respect to the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena?
“World-Honored One!”
"Does this bodhisattva mahāsattva practice within the eye-element?
Does he practice within the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-element?
"World-Honored One! [he asked.]
“Does this bodhisattva mahāsattva practice within the realm of form?
Does he practice within the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, or mental phenomena?
“World-Honored One! [the interlocutor asked.]
"Does this bodhisattva mahāsattva practice within the sphere of eye-consciousness?
Does he practice within the spheres of ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-consciousness?
"World-Honored One!"
“Does this bodhisattva mahāsattva practice eye-contact?
Does he practice ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact?
“World-Honored One! [the bodhisattva asked.]
Does this bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition?
Does he practice the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as condition?
“World-Honored One!
Does this bodhisattva mahāsattva practice within the earth element?
Does he practice within the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements?”
“World-Honored One!
Does this bodhisattva-mahāsattva practice ignorance?
Or does he practice volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, or old age and death?”
“World-Honored One!
Does this bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the perfection of giving?
Does he practice the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom?”
“Bhagavān! Does this bodhisattva mahāsattva practice inner emptiness?

Or does he practice outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature?”
“World-Honored One!
Does this bodhisattva mahāsattva practice true thusness?

Or does he practice the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, non-alteration, equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of empty space, or the inconceivable realm?”
“World-Honored One!
Does this bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the four foundations of mindfulness?
Does he practice the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path?”
“World-Honored One!
Does this bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the noble truth of suffering?
Does he practice the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path?”
“World-Honored One!
Does this bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the four dhyānas? “World-Honored One! [The questioner continued.]
"Does this bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the four immeasurables?
"World-Honored One,
does this bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the four formless absorptions?"
“World-Honored One!
Does this bodhisattva-mahāsattva practice the eight liberations?
“World-Honored One! [The interlocutor asked.]
“Does this bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the eight bases of mastery?
World-Honored One!
Does this bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the nine successive attainments?”
“World-Honored One!
Does this bodhisattva-mahāsattva practice the ten spheres of totality?
“World-Honored One! [The Buddha replied: “No.”
“Does this bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the gate of liberation of emptiness?
Does he practice the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness? [He replied:
“World-Honored One!”
"Does this bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the five eyes?
"World-Honored One!
Does this bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the six supernormal powers?"
“World-Honored One!
Does this bodhisattva-mahāsattva practice the gates of samādhi? “World-Honored One! [The interlocutor asked.]
“Does this bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the gateways of dhāraṇī?
World-Honored One,
does this bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the ten powers of a Buddha?”

Is it for the sake of practicing the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?
“World-Honored One!
Does this bodhisattva mahāsattva practice all-knowledge?
Does he practice the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects?”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not course in form, nor does he course in feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.”
“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not course in the sense-base of the eye; he does not course in the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind. Subhūti!”
This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not course in the sphere of form, nor does he course in the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena. “Subhūti!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not course in the eye-element, nor does he course in the elements of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind.”
“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not course in the realm of form; he does not course in the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangible objects, or mental phenomena. Subhūti!”
This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not engage with the eye-consciousness element, nor does he engage with the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-consciousness elements.
"Suvikrāntavikrāmin!..."
This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not engage in eye-contact, nor does he engage in ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact. “Subhūti!

This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not engage in the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition, nor does he engage in the various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact as condition.”
“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not course in the earth element; he does not course in the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements. Subhūti!”

This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not engage in ignorance, nor does he engage in volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, or old age and death.

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not practice the perfection of giving; he does not practice the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom.”

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not practice inner emptiness; he does not practice outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, emptiness of all phenomena, unobtainable emptiness, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, or emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.”

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not course in suchness; he does not course in the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, or the inconceivable realm.”

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not practice the four foundations of mindfulness; he does not practice the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path.”
“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not practice the noble truth of suffering, nor does he practice the noble truths of origin, cessation, or the path. Subhūti!”
This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not practice the four dhyānas. "Subhūti!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not practice the four immeasurables."
“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not practice the four formless absorptions. Subhūti!”
This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not practice the eight liberations.
Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not practice the eight bases of mastery.
“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not practice the nine successive attainments. Subhūti!”
This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not practice the ten spheres of totality. Subhūti!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not practice the liberation door of emptiness, nor does he practice the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness.
“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not engage with the five eyes. Subhūti!”
This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not practice the six supernormal powers. Subhūti!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not practice the gateways of samādhi.
"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not practice the gateways of dhāraṇī. Subhūti!"

This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not practice the ten powers of a buddha, nor does he practice the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha.

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not practice all-knowledge (sarvajñatā), nor does he practice the knowledge of the aspects of the path (mārgākārajñatā) or the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā). Why is that?

"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva’s conformity with, orientation toward, and entry into the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) cannot be produced, cannot be destroyed; it comes from nowhere and goes nowhere, nor does it abide anywhere. It has no direction or region; it is incalculable and immeasurable; it neither departs nor arrives."
“Subhūti! Since this omniscience (sarvajñajñāna) is without measure or number, and neither coming nor going can be apprehended therein, there is likewise no one who can realize it. Subhūti!”
In this way, the knowledge of all modes cannot be realized through form; it cannot be realized through feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness. "Subhūti!
In this way, the knowledge of all modes cannot be realized through the sense base of the eye; it cannot be realized through the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind."
"Subhūti! This omniscience cannot be realized through the sphere of form; it cannot be realized through the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena."
“Subhūti! This omniscience cannot be realized by means of the eye-element; it cannot be realized by means of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-element.”
“Subhūti! This omniscience cannot be realized through the eye-consciousness element; it cannot be realized through the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-consciousness elements.”
“Subhūti! This omniscience cannot be realized through eye-contact; it cannot be realized through ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact.”

“Subhūti! This omniscience cannot be realized through any feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition; nor can it be realized through any feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact as a condition.”
“Subhūti! This omniscience cannot be realized through the earth element; it cannot be realized through the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements.”

“Subhūti! This omniscience cannot be realized through ignorance; it cannot be realized through volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, existence, birth, or old age and death.”

“Subhūti! This omniscience cannot be realized through the perfection of generosity; it cannot be realized through the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom.”

“Subhūti! This knowledge of all modes cannot be realized through internal emptiness; nor can it be realized through external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.”

“Subhūti! This omniscience cannot be realized through suchness; it cannot be realized through the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), non-falsity, non-alteration, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), or the inconceivable realm.”

“Subhūti! This omniscience cannot be realized by means of the four foundations of mindfulness; it cannot be realized by means of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path.”
“Subhūti! This omniscience cannot be realized through the noble truth of suffering, nor can it be realized through the noble truths of origin, cessation, or the path.”
“Subhūti! This omniscience cannot be realized by means of the four dhyānas. Subhūti!”
In this way, the knowledge of all modes cannot be realized through the four immeasurables.
Subhūti, in this way,
the knowledge of all modes cannot be realized through the four formless absorptions.
“Subhūti! This omniscience cannot be realized through the eight liberations. Subhūti!”
In this way, the knowledge of all modes cannot be realized through the eight bases of mastery. "Subhūti!

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll 318. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter Forty-seven, Part Two: On Suchness (Tathatā). At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the devaputras of the desire and form realms, saying:
"It is so! It is thus!"
"So it is! It is just as you have said.
O sons of the gods!"
Form is itself the knowledge of all modes; the knowledge of all modes is itself form.
Feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are themselves the knowledge of all modes; the knowledge of all modes is itself feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.
“O sons of the gods!
The eye-base is itself the knowledge of all modes; the knowledge of all modes is itself the eye-base.
The ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases are themselves the knowledge of all modes; the knowledge of all modes is itself the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases.”
“O sons of the gods!
The sphere of form is itself the knowledge of all modes; the knowledge of all modes is itself the sphere of form.

The spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are themselves the knowledge of all modes; the knowledge of all modes is itself the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena.”
“O sons of the gods!
The eye-element is itself the knowledge of all modes; the knowledge of all modes is itself the eye-element.
The ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements are themselves the knowledge of all modes; the knowledge of all modes is itself the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements.”
“O sons of the gods!
The realm of form is itself the knowledge of all modes; the knowledge of all modes is itself the realm of form.

The realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are themselves the knowledge of all modes; the knowledge of all modes is itself the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena.”
“O sons of the gods!
The eye-consciousness element is itself the knowledge of all modes; the knowledge of all modes is itself the eye-consciousness element.

The ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements are themselves the knowledge of all modes; the knowledge of all modes is itself the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements.”
“O sons of the gods!
Eye-contact is itself the knowledge of all modes; the knowledge of all modes is itself eye-contact.
Ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact are themselves the knowledge of all modes; the knowledge of all modes is itself ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact.”
“O sons of the gods!

The various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition are themselves the knowledge of all modes; the knowledge of all modes is itself the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition.

The various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions are themselves the knowledge of all modes; the knowledge of all modes is itself the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions.”
“O sons of the gods!
The earth element is itself the knowledge of all modes; the knowledge of all modes is itself the earth element.
The water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are themselves the knowledge of all modes; the knowledge of all modes is itself the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements.”
“O sons of the gods!
Ignorance is itself the knowledge of all modes; the knowledge of all modes is itself ignorance.

Formative forces, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, sensation, craving, grasping, existence, birth, and old age and death are themselves the knowledge of all modes; the knowledge of all modes is itself [the factors] from formative forces through old age and death.”
“O sons of the gods!
The perfection of generosity is itself the knowledge of all modes; the knowledge of all modes is itself the perfection of generosity.

The perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are themselves the knowledge of all modes; the knowledge of all modes is itself the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom.”
“O sons of the gods!
Internal emptiness is itself the knowledge of all modes; the knowledge of all modes is itself internal emptiness.

External emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature are themselves the knowledge of all modes; the knowledge of all modes is itself external emptiness, and so on, up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.”
“O sons of the gods!
Suchness (*tathatā*) is itself the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), and the knowledge of all modes is itself suchness.

The realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), non-falsity (*avitathatā*), immutability (*ananyathātva*), equality (*samatā*), the state beyond birth (*aniṣyandika*), the fixedness of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*) are themselves the knowledge of all modes; and the knowledge of all modes is itself the realm of phenomena, up to the inconceivable realm.”
“O sons of the gods!
The four foundations of mindfulness are themselves the knowledge of all modes; the knowledge of all modes is itself the four foundations of mindfulness.

The four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are themselves the knowledge of all modes; the knowledge of all modes is itself the four right efforts up to and including the eightfold noble path.”
“O sons of the gods!
The noble truth of suffering is itself the knowledge of all modes; the knowledge of all modes is itself the noble truth of suffering.
The noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are themselves the knowledge of all modes; the knowledge of all modes is itself the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path.”
“O sons of the gods!

O sons of the gods!”
The four immeasurables are themselves the knowledge of all modes; the knowledge of all modes is itself the four immeasurables.
"O sons of the gods!

The gate of liberation of emptiness is itself the knowledge of all modes; the knowledge of all modes is itself the gate of liberation of emptiness.

The six supernormal powers are themselves the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), and the knowledge of all modes is itself the six supernormal powers.
"O sons of the gods!

O sons of the gods!”

“O sons of the gods!
The fruit of stream-entry is itself the knowledge of all modes; the knowledge of all modes is itself the fruit of stream-entry.
The fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are themselves the knowledge of all modes; the knowledge of all modes is itself the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship.”
“O sons of the gods!
The awakening of a pratyekabuddha is itself the knowledge of all modes; the knowledge of all modes is itself the awakening of a pratyekabuddha.
O sons of the gods!”
All-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) is itself the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), and the knowledge of all modes is itself all-knowledge;

the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are themselves the knowledge of all modes, and the knowledge of all modes is itself the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects.
“O sons of the gods!

"Why is this so? O sons of the gods!

The eye-element is my self and what belongs to my self; the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-elements are my self and what belongs to my self.
The form-element is my self and what belongs to my self; the sound, odor, taste, tangible, and mental-object elements are my self and what belongs to my self.
The eye-consciousness-element is my self and what belongs to my self; the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness-elements are my self and what belongs to my self.
Eye-contact is my self and what belongs to my self; ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact are my self and what belongs to my self.

The various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition are my self and what belongs to my self; the various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions are my self and what belongs to my self.
The earth element is my self and what belongs to my self; the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are my self and what belongs to my self.
Ignorance is "I" and "mine"; volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age and death are "I" and "mine";

Inner emptiness is my self and what belongs to my self; outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature are my self and what belongs to my self;

This bodhisattva cannot realize internal emptiness, nor can they realize external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature;

this bodhisattva cannot realize suchness, nor can they realize the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, non-alteration, equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm.

This bodhisattva is unable to cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, nor can they cultivate the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path;
this bodhisattva is unable to realize the noble truth of suffering, nor can they realize the noble truths of its origin, its cessation, or the path;
this bodhisattva is unable to cultivate the four dhyānas, nor can they cultivate the four immeasurables or the four formless absorptions.
This bodhisattva is unable to cultivate the eight liberations, nor can they cultivate the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities;
this bodhisattva is unable to cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness, nor can they cultivate the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness;
this bodhisattva is unable to cultivate the five eyes, nor can they cultivate the six supernormal powers.
This bodhisattva is unable to cultivate the gates of samādhi, nor can they cultivate the gates of dhāraṇī;

this bodhisattva is unable to cultivate the ten powers of a buddha, nor can they cultivate the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha;
this bodhisattva is unable to cultivate all-knowledge, nor can they cultivate the knowledge of the aspects of the path or the knowledge of all aspects.
“O sons of the gods!

If a bodhisattva practices for the sake of grasping the ten powers of a Buddha, or practices for the sake of abandoning the ten powers of a Buddha; if they practice for the sake of grasping the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, or practices for the sake of abandoning the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha—such a bodhisattva cannot cultivate the perfection of wisdom, nor can they cultivate the perfections of meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity.”

This bodhisattva cannot realize internal emptiness, nor can they realize external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, emptiness of self-characteristic, emptiness of common characteristic, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature;

this bodhisattva is unable to realize the noble truth of suffering, nor can they realize the noble truths of its origin, its cessation, or the path;
this bodhisattva is unable to cultivate the four dhyānas, nor can they cultivate the four immeasurables or the four formless absorptions.

this bodhisattva cannot cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness, nor can they cultivate the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness;

this bodhisattva is unable to cultivate the ten powers of a buddha, nor can they cultivate the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha;
this bodhisattva is unable to cultivate all-knowledge, nor can they cultivate the knowledge of the paths or the knowledge of all aspects.
“O sons of the gods!

If a bodhisattva practices for the sake of grasping the fruit of stream-entry, or practices for the sake of abandoning the fruit of stream-entry; if he practices for the sake of grasping the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, or arhatship, or practices for the sake of abandoning the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, or arhatship—then this bodhisattva is unable to cultivate the perfection of wisdom, nor can he cultivate the perfections of meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, or generosity.”

this bodhisattva is unable to realize the noble truth of suffering, nor can they realize the noble truths of its origin, its cessation, or the path;

this bodhisattva is unable to cultivate the ten powers of a buddha, nor can they cultivate the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha;
this bodhisattva is unable to cultivate all-knowledge, nor can they cultivate the knowledge of the aspects of the path or the knowledge of all aspects.
“O sons of the gods!

If a bodhisattva practices for the sake of grasping the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, or practices for the sake of abandoning the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, that bodhisattva cannot cultivate the perfection of wisdom, nor can they cultivate the perfections of meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity.”

This bodhisattva cannot realize internal emptiness, nor can they realize external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature;

this bodhisattva is unable to cultivate the ten powers of a buddha, nor can they cultivate the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha;
this bodhisattva is unable to cultivate all-knowledge, nor can they cultivate the knowledge of the aspects of the path or the knowledge of all aspects.
“O sons of the gods!

If a bodhisattva practices for the sake of grasping all-knowledge, or practices for the sake of abandoning all-knowledge; if they practice for the sake of grasping the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, or practice for the sake of abandoning the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects—such a bodhisattva is unable to cultivate the perfection of wisdom, nor can they cultivate the perfections of meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity.”

This bodhisattva cannot realize internal emptiness, nor can they realize external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature;

this bodhisattva cannot realize suchness, nor can they realize the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, non-alteration, equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, or the inconceivable realm.

such a bodhisattva is unable to realize the noble truth of suffering, nor can they realize the noble truths of its origin, its cessation, or the path;
such a bodhisattva is unable to cultivate the four dhyānas, nor can they cultivate the four immeasurables or the four formless absorptions.
This bodhisattva is unable to cultivate the eight liberations, nor can they cultivate the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive concentrations, or the ten totalities;
this bodhisattva is unable to cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness, nor can they cultivate the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness;

this bodhisattva is unable to cultivate the ten powers of a buddha, nor can they cultivate the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha;
