At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
This profound and wondrous Dharma accords with all dharmas."
To what all phenomena does this profound and sublime Dharma accord?
“World-Honored One!
This profound and sublime Dharma accords with the *prajñāpāramitā*, and it also accords with the *dhyāna*, *vīrya*, *kṣānti*, *śīla*, and *dāna* *pāramitās*.”
“World-Honored One!

This profound and wondrous Dharma accords with internal emptiness, and likewise accords with external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.”
“World-Honored One!

This profound and wondrous Dharma accords with suchness; it also accords with the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of empty space, and the inconceivable realm.”
“World-Honored One!

This profound and subtle Dharma accords with the four foundations of mindfulness, and it also accords with the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.”
“World-Honored One!
This profound and wondrous Dharma accords with the Noble Truth of Suffering, and it also accords with the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path.
World-Honored One!”
"This profound and subtle Dharma accords with the four dhyānas, and it also accords with the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments.
'World-Honored One!
This profound and subtle Dharma accords with the eight liberations, and it also accords with the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities.'"
“World-Honored One!
This profound and wondrous Dharma accords with the liberation door of emptiness, and also accords with the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness.
World-Honored One!”
"This profound and wondrous Dharma accords with the five eyes and also accords with the six supernormal powers.
World-Honored One!
This profound and wondrous Dharma accords with the gates of samādhi and also accords with the gates of dhāraṇī."
“World-Honored One!

This profound and wondrous Dharma accords with the ten powers of a Buddha, and it also accords with the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.”
“World-Honored One!
This profound and wondrous Dharma accords with all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), and it also accords with the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).
World-Honored One!”
"This profound and subtle Dharma is entirely without obstruction.
In what, World-Honored One, is this profound and subtle Dharma unobstructed? "World-Honored One! [The interlocutor asks.]
"This profound and subtle Dharma is unimpeded with respect to form; it is unimpeded with respect to feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.
World-Honored One!
This profound and subtle Dharma is unimpeded with respect to the sense base of the eye; it is unimpeded with respect to the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind."
“World-Honored One!
This profound and wondrous Dharma is unimpeded in the sphere of form; it is unimpeded in the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena.
World-Honored One!”
"This profound and subtle Dharma is unimpeded within the eye-element; it is unimpeded within the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-elements.
World-Honored One!
This profound and subtle Dharma is unimpeded within the form-element; it is unimpeded within the sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental-object elements."
“World-Honored One!
This profound and wondrous Dharma is unimpeded within the visual consciousness element; it is unimpeded within the auditory, olfactory, gustatory, tactile, and mental consciousness elements.”
“World-Honored One!
This profound and wondrous Dharma is unimpeded in eye-contact; it is unimpeded in ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact.
World-Honored One!”

This profound and subtle Dharma is unimpeded regarding all feelings produced with eye-contact as their condition; it is unimpeded regarding all feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as their conditions.
“World-Honored One!
This profound and wondrous Dharma is unimpeded within the earth element; it is unimpeded within the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements.
World-Honored One!”

This profound and sublime Dharma is unimpeded regarding ignorance; it is unimpeded regarding volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, becoming, birth, and old age and death.

“Bhagavān! This profound and wondrous Dharma is unimpeded in the perfection of generosity; it is unimpeded in the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.”
“World-Honored One!

This profound and wondrous Dharma is unimpeded within internal emptiness; it is unimpeded in external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self-characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.”
“World-Honored One!

This profound and wondrous Dharma is unimpeded in true thusness; it is unimpeded in the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-falsity, the non-alteration, the equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixedness of dharma, the stability of dharma, the limit of reality, the realm of empty space, and the inconceivable realm.”
“World-Honored One!

This profound and wondrous Dharma is unimpeded regarding the four foundations of mindfulness; it is unimpeded regarding the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.”
“World-Honored One!
This profound and wondrous Dharma is unimpeded regarding the Noble Truth of Suffering, and it is unimpeded regarding the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path.
World-Honored One!”
"This profound and wondrous Dharma is unimpeded within the four dhyānas; it is unimpeded within the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments.
World-Honored One!
This profound and wondrous Dharma is unimpeded within the eight liberations; it is unimpeded within the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities."
“World-Honored One!
This profound and wondrous Dharma is unimpeded in the gate of liberation of emptiness; it is unimpeded in the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.
World-Honored One!”
"This profound and wondrous Dharma is unimpeded regarding the five eyes; it is unimpeded regarding the six supernormal powers.
World-Honored One!
This profound and wondrous Dharma is unimpeded regarding the gates of samādhi; it is unimpeded regarding the gates of dhāraṇī."
“World-Honored One!

This profound and wondrous Dharma is unimpeded regarding the ten powers of a Buddha; it is unimpeded regarding the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.”
“World-Honored One!
This profound and wondrous Dharma is unimpeded regarding the fruit of stream-entry; it is unimpeded regarding the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship.
World-Honored One!”
"This profound and subtle Dharma is unimpeded regarding the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha.
World-Honored One!
This profound and subtle Dharma is unimpeded regarding all-knowledge, and it is unimpeded regarding the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects."
“World-Honored One!
This profound and wondrous Dharma takes non-obstruction as its characteristic. Why is this so?

World-Honored One! Because of the equality of space; because of the equality of true suchness (*tathatā*); because of the equality of the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*); because of the equality of the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*); because of the equality of non-falsity; because of the equality of immutability; because of the equality of the equality of equality; because of the equality of the nature free from arising; because of the equality of the fixed nature of phenomena; because of the equality of the abiding nature of phenomena; because of the equality of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*); because of the equality of the realm of space; because of the equality of the inconceivable realm; because of the equality of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; because of the equality of non-creation and non-action; and because of the equality of non-defilement and non-purity.
“World-Honored One!
This profound and wondrous Dharma is without arising and without cessation. Why is this?
“World-Honored One!
Because form is without arising and without cessation; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are without arising and without cessation.
World-Honored One!”
Because the sense-base of the eye is without arising and without cessation; because the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are without arising and without cessation.
"World-Honored One!
Because the sense-base of form is without arising and without cessation; because the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are without arising and without cessation."
“World-Honored One!
Because the eye-element is without arising and without cessation; because the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements are without arising and without cessation.
World-Honored One!”
Because the realm of form is without arising and without cessation; because the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are without arising and without cessation.
"World-Honored One!
Because the realm of eye-consciousness is without arising and without cessation; because the realms of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness are without arising and without cessation."
“World-Honored One!
Because eye-contact is without arising and without cessation; because ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact are without arising and without cessation.
World-Honored One!”

Because all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are neither arising nor ceasing; and because all feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions are neither arising nor ceasing.
“World-Honored One!
Because the earth element is without arising and without cessation, and because the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are without arising and without cessation.
World-Honored One!”

Because ignorance is without arising and without cessation, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, becoming, birth, and old age and death are without arising and without cessation.
“World-Honored One!

Because the perfection of giving is without arising and without cessation, and because the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are without arising and without cessation.”
“World-Honored One!

Because internal emptiness is without arising and without cessation, and because external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersal emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, all-dharma emptiness, unobtainable emptiness, non-existence emptiness, self-nature emptiness, and non-existence-of-self-nature emptiness are without arising and without cessation.
“World-Honored One!

Because true thusness (tathatā) is without arising and without cessation, so too are the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of empty space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu) without arising and without cessation.”
“World-Honored One!

Because the four foundations of mindfulness are without arising and without cessation, and because the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are without arising and without cessation.”
“World-Honored One!
Because the noble truth of suffering is without arising and without cessation, and because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are without arising and without cessation.
World-Honored One!”
Because the four dhyānas are without arising and without cessation; because the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are without arising and without cessation.
"World-Honored One!

Because the eight liberations are without arising and without cessation; because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are without arising and without cessation."
“World-Honored One!
Because the gate of liberation of emptiness is without arising and without cessation; because the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are without arising and without cessation.
World-Honored One!”
Because the five eyes are without arising and without cessation; because the six supernormal powers are without arising and without cessation.
"World-Honored One!
Because the gateways of samādhi are without arising and without cessation; because the gateways of dhāraṇī are without arising and without cessation."
“World-Honored One!

Because the ten powers of a Buddha are without arising and without cessation; because the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are without arising and without cessation.”
“World-Honored One!
Because the fruit of stream-entry is without arising and without cessation; because the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are without arising and without cessation.
World-Honored One!”
Because Pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is without arising and without cessation.
"World-Honored One!
Because omniscience is without arising and without cessation; because the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are without arising and without cessation."
“World-Honored One!
This profound and wondrous Dharma is entirely without trace. Why is this?
“World-Honored One!
Because the footprint of form cannot be apprehended, and because the footprints of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness cannot be apprehended.
World-Honored One!”
Because the footprint of the eye-base cannot be apprehended, and because the footprints of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases cannot be apprehended.
"World-Honored One!"
Because a trace of the sphere of form cannot be found, and because traces of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena cannot be found.
"World-Honored One!..."
Because the footprint of the eye-element cannot be apprehended, and because the footprints of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements cannot be apprehended.
"World-Honored One!..."
Because the footprint of the form realm cannot be apprehended, and because the footprints of the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena cannot be apprehended.
"World-Honored One!..."

Because the footprint of the visual consciousness element cannot be found, and because the footprints of the auditory, olfactory, gustatory, tactile, and mental consciousness elements cannot be found.
"World-Honored One!..."
Because the footprint of eye-contact cannot be apprehended, and because the footprints of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact cannot be apprehended.
"World-Honored One!..."

Because the trace of any feeling produced with eye-contact as a condition cannot be found; and because the traces of any feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as conditions cannot be found.
“World-Honored One!
Because the footprint of the earth element cannot be apprehended, and because the footprints of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements cannot be apprehended.”
“World-Honored One!

Because the footprint of ignorance cannot be apprehended, the footprints of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age and death cannot be apprehended.”

“Blessed One, because the footprint of the perfection of generosity cannot be apprehended, and because the footprints of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom cannot be apprehended.”
“World-Honored One!

Because the footprint of internal emptiness cannot be apprehended, and because the footprints of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersal emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence cannot be apprehended.
“World-Honored One!

Because no trace of suchness can be found; because no trace can be found of the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of empty space, or the inconceivable realm.”
“World-Honored One!

Because the footprint of the four foundations of mindfulness cannot be apprehended; because the footprints of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path cannot be apprehended.”
“World-Honored One!
Because the footprint of the noble truth of suffering cannot be apprehended, and because the footprints of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path cannot be apprehended.
World-Honored One!”
Because the tracks of the four dhyānas cannot be apprehended; because the tracks of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments cannot be apprehended.
"World-Honored One!
Because the tracks of the eight liberations cannot be apprehended; because the tracks of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive concentrations, and the ten totalities cannot be apprehended."
“World-Honored One!
Because the footprint of the liberation door of emptiness cannot be apprehended, and because the footprints of the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness cannot be apprehended.”
“World-Honored One!
Because the tracks of the five eyes cannot be apprehended, and because the tracks of the six supernormal powers cannot be apprehended.
World-Honored One!”
Because the footprint of the gateways to samādhi cannot be apprehended, and because the footprint of the gateways to dhāraṇī cannot be apprehended.
"World-Honored One!

Because the footprint of the Buddha’s ten powers cannot be apprehended; because the footprint of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha cannot be apprehended."
“World-Honored One!
Because the footprint of the fruit of stream-entry cannot be apprehended, and because the footprints of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship cannot be apprehended.”
“World-Honored One!
Because the footprint of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment cannot be apprehended.
World-Honored One!”
"Because the footprint of all-knowledge is unattainable, and because the footprint of the knowledge of the paths and the footprint of all-aspect knowledge are unattainable.
At that time, the devaputras of the desire and form realms again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
The Elder Subhūti is born after the Tathāgata; he is a true disciple of the Buddha. Why is this?
It is because all the teachings expounded by the Elder Subhūti are entirely in accord with emptiness.
At that time, Subhūti addressed the devaputras of the desire and form realms, saying:
"O devaputras, you say that I, Subhūti, am born after the Tathāgata and am a true disciple of the Buddha. In what way, however, is Subhūti born after the Tathāgata?"
This is because he is born in accordance with the *tathatā* (suchness) of the Tathāgata. Why is this so?

The *tathatā* of the Tathāgata neither comes nor goes; the *tathatā* of the Venerable Subhūti is likewise, neither coming nor going. For this reason, it is said that the Venerable Subhūti is born in accordance with the Tathāgata.

"Furthermore, the Tathāgata’s suchness is the suchness of all phenomena, and the suchness of all phenomena is the Tathāgata’s suchness. This suchness has no nature of suchness, nor does it have a nature of non-suchness; the suchness of the Venerable Subhūti is likewise. For this reason, it is said that the Venerable Subhūti is born after the likeness of the Tathāgata."

"Furthermore, the Tathāgata has the characteristic of being eternally abiding in suchness; the Elder Subhūti’s suchness is likewise characterized by eternal abiding. For this reason, it is said that the Elder Subhūti is born after the likeness of the Tathāgata."

"Furthermore, the Tathāgata’s suchness is without change and without differentiation; it pervades and functions throughout all phenomena. The suchness of the Venerable Subhūti is likewise without change and without differentiation, pervading and functioning throughout all phenomena. For this reason, it is said that the Venerable Subhūti is born in accordance with the Tathāgata."

"Furthermore, the Tathāgata’s true suchness (tathatā) is without obstruction, and the true suchness of all phenomena is likewise without obstruction. Whether it be the true suchness of the Tathāgata or the true suchness of all phenomena, they are one and the same true suchness—non-dual, undifferentiated, uncreated, and unconditioned. Such true suchness is eternally the characteristic of true suchness; there is no time when it is not the characteristic of true suchness. Because it is eternally the characteristic of true suchness and there is no time when it is not the characteristic of true suchness, it is non-dual and undifferentiated. The true suchness of the Venerable Subhūti is also thus; for this reason, it is said that the Venerable Subhūti is born after the manner of the Tathāgata."

"Furthermore, the Tathāgata’s suchness is, in all respects, without recollection and without conceptual differentiation; the Elder Subhūti’s suchness is likewise, in all respects, without recollection and without conceptual differentiation. For this reason, it is said that the Elder Subhūti is born after the manner of the Tathāgata."

"Furthermore, the Tathāgata’s suchness is without distinction, without difference, and is ungraspable; the Elder Subhūti’s suchness is likewise without distinction, without difference, and is ungraspable. For this reason, it is said that the Elder Subhūti is born in accordance with the Tathāgata."

"Furthermore, the Tathāgata’s suchness is not separate from the suchness of all phenomena, and the suchness of all phenomena is not separate from the Tathāgata’s suchness. Such suchness is eternally the characteristic of suchness; there is no time when it is not the characteristic of suchness. The suchness of the Elder Subhūti is also like this. For this reason, it is said that the Elder Subhūti is born after the manner of the Tathāgata."
"Although it is said that he is born in accordance [with the Tathāgata], there is nothing with which he is born in accordance, because Subhūti’s suchness is not different from the Buddha’s.

Furthermore, the suchness of the Tathāgata is neither past, nor future, nor present; the suchness of all phenomena is likewise neither past, nor future, nor present; and the suchness of the Elder Subhūti is also thus. For this reason, it is said that the Elder Subhūti is born in accordance with the Tathāgata."
"Furthermore, because the *tathatā* (suchness) of the past is equal, the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal; because the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal, the *tathatā* of the past is equal."
Because the *tathatā* of the future is equal, the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal; because the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal, the *tathatā* of the future is equal.
Because the *tathatā* of the present is equal, the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal; because the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal, the *tathatā* of the present is equal.
If the suchness of the past, future, and present is equal, and if the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal, they are one and the same in their equality of suchness—non-dual and without distinction.
"Furthermore, because the suchness of form is equal, the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal; because the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal, the suchness of form is equal.

Because the suchness of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is equal, the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal; because the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal, the suchness of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is equal."

In this way, whether it be the equality of the suchness of form, the equality of the suchness of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, or the equality of the suchness of the Tathāgata—they are all the same single suchness, equal, non-dual, and without distinction.

"Furthermore, because the *tathatā* (suchness) of the eye-base is equal, the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal; because the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal, the *tathatā* of the eye-base is equal.

Because the *tathatā* of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-bases is equal, the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal; because the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal, the *tathatā* of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-bases is equal."

In this way, whether it be the equality of the suchness of the eye-base, or the equality of the suchness of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases, or the equality of the suchness of the Tathāgata—they are all one single suchness, equal, non-dual, and without distinction.

"Furthermore, because the suchness of the sense-base of form is equal, the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal; because the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal, the suchness of the sense-base of form is equal.

Because the suchness of the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is equal, the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal; because the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal, the suchness of the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is equal."

In this way, the suchness of the sphere of form is equal, the suchness of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena is equal, and the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal; they are all one and the same suchness, equal, non-dual, and without distinction.

"Furthermore, because the *tathatā* (suchness) of the eye-element is equal, the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal; because the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal, the *tathatā* of the eye-element is equal.

Because the *tathatā* of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements is equal, the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal; because the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal, the *tathatā* of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements is equal."

In this way, whether it be the equality of the suchness of the eye-element, or the equality of the suchness of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-elements, or the equality of the suchness of the Tathāgata—they are all one single suchness, equal, non-dual, and without distinction.
"Furthermore, because the suchness of the realm of form is equal, the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal; because the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal, the suchness of the realm of form is equal.

Because the suchness of the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and phenomena is equal, the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal; because the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal, the suchness of the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and phenomena is equal."

In this way, the suchness of the realm of form is equal, the suchness of the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is equal, and the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal; they are all the same single suchness, equal, non-dual, and without distinction.

"Furthermore, because the *tathatā* (suchness) of the visual consciousness element is equal, the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal; because the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal, the *tathatā* of the visual consciousness element is equal.

Because the *tathatā* of the auditory, olfactory, gustatory, tactile, and mental consciousness elements is equal, the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal; because the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal, the *tathatā* of the auditory, olfactory, gustatory, tactile, and mental consciousness elements is equal."

In this way, whether it be the suchness of the eye-consciousness element, the suchness of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements, or the suchness of the Tathāgata, they are all the same single suchness—equal, non-dual, and without distinction.
"Furthermore, because the suchness of eye-contact is equal, the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal; because the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal, the suchness of eye-contact is equal.

Because the suchness of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact is equal, the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal; because the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal, the suchness of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact is equal."

In this way, whether it be the equality of the suchness of eye-contact, or the equality of the suchness of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact, or the equality of the suchness of the Tathāgata—they are all one and the same suchness, equal, non-dual, and without distinction.

"Furthermore, because the suchness of all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition is equal, the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal; because the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal, the suchness of all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition is equal.

Because the suchness of all feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions is equal, the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal; because the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal, the suchness of all feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions is equal."

In this way, the suchness of all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition is equal; the suchness of all feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions is equal; and the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal—these are one and the same suchness, equal, non-dual, and without distinction.

"Furthermore, because the *tathatā* (suchness) of the earth element is equal, the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal; because the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal, the *tathatā* of the earth element is equal.

Because the *tathatā* of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements is equal, the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal; because the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal, the *tathatā* of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements is equal."

In this way, whether it be the equality of the suchness of the earth element, or the equality of the suchness of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements, or the equality of the suchness of the Tathāgata—they are all the same single suchness, equal, non-dual, and without distinction.
"Furthermore, because the *tathatā* (suchness) of ignorance is equal, the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal; because the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal, the *tathatā* of ignorance is equal.

Because the *tathatā* of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age and death is equal, the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal; because the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal, the *tathatā* of volitional formations through to old age and death is equal."

In this way, if the suchness of ignorance is equal, and if the suchness of volitional formations up to old age and death is equal, and if the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal, they are all the same single suchness, equal, non-dual, and without distinction.

"Furthermore, because the *tathatā* (suchness) of the perfection of generosity (*dāna-pāramitā*) is equal, the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal; because the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal, the *tathatā* of the perfection of generosity is equal.

Because the *tathatā* of the perfections of ethical discipline (*śīla*), patience (*kṣānti*), diligence (*vīrya*), meditative concentration (*dhyāna*), and wisdom (*prajñā*) is equal, the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal; because the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal, the *tathatā* of ethical discipline up to the perfection of wisdom is equal."

In this way, the equality of the suchness of the perfection of generosity, the equality of the suchness of the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom, and the equality of the suchness of the Tathāgata, are all one and the same suchness—equal, non-dual, and without distinction.

"Furthermore, because the *tathatā* (suchness) of internal emptiness is equal, the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal; because the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal, the *tathatā* of internal emptiness is equal.

Because the *tathatā* of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, limitless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, emptiness of all phenomena, unapprehendable emptiness, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, and emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is equal, the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal; because the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal, the *tathatā* of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is equal."

In this way, whether it be the equality of the suchness of internal emptiness, or the equality of the suchness of external emptiness up to the emptiness of the nature of non-nature, or the equality of the suchness of the Tathāgata—they are all the same suchness, equal, non-dual, and without distinction.

"Furthermore, because the *tathatā* (suchness) of true suchness is equal, the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal; because the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal, the *tathatā* of true suchness is equal.

Because the *dharmadhātu*, *dharmatā*, non-falsity, immutability, equality, freedom from birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharma-niyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharma-sthititā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm are equal in their *tathatā*, the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal; because the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal, the *tathatā* of the *dharmadhātu* up to the inconceivable realm is equal."

In this way, the suchness of suchness is equal; the suchness of the dharma-realm, up to the inconceivable realm, is equal; and the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal—all are the same single suchness, equal, non-dual, and without distinction.

"Furthermore, because the suchness of the four foundations of mindfulness is equal, the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal; because the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal, the suchness of the four foundations of mindfulness is equal.

Because the suchness of the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path is equal, the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal; because the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal, the suchness of the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path is equal."

In this way, whether it be the equality of the suchness of the four applications of mindfulness, or the equality of the suchness of the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path, or the equality of the suchness of the Tathāgata—they are all the same single suchness, equal, non-dual, and without distinction.

"Furthermore, because the suchness of the noble truth of suffering is equal, the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal; because the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal, the suchness of the noble truth of suffering is equal.

Because the suchness of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path is equal, the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal; because the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal, the suchness of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path is equal."

In this way, the suchness that is the equality of the noble truth of suffering, the suchness that is the equality of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path, and the suchness that is the equality of the Tathāgata, are all the same single suchness—equal, non-dual, and without distinction.
"Furthermore, because the suchness of the four dhyānas is equal, the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal; because the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal, the suchness of the four dhyānas is equal.

Because the suchness of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is equal, the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal; because the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal, the suchness of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is equal."

In this way, the suchness of the four dhyānas is equal, the suchness of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is equal, and the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal; they are all one and the same suchness, equal, non-dual, and without distinction.

"Furthermore, because the suchness of the eight liberations is equal, the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal; because the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal, the suchness of the eight liberations is equal.

Because the suchness of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities is equal, the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal; because the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal, the suchness of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities is equal."

Thus, whether it be the equality of the suchness of the eight liberations, the equality of the suchness of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases, or the equality of the suchness of the Tathāgata—they are all one and the same suchness, equal, non-dual, and without distinction.

"Furthermore, because the *tathatā* (suchness) of the liberation door of emptiness is equal, the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal; because the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal, the *tathatā* of the liberation door of emptiness is equal.

Because the *tathatā* of the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness is equal, the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal; because the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal, the *tathatā* of the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness is equal."

In this way, the suchness of the equality of the emptiness gate of liberation, the suchness of the equality of the signless and wishless gates of liberation, and the suchness of the Tathāgata are one and the same suchness of equality—non-dual and without distinction.
"Furthermore, because the suchness of the five eyes is equal, the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal; because the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal, the suchness of the five eyes is equal.

Because the suchness of the six supernormal powers is equal, the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal; because the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal, the suchness of the six supernormal powers is equal."

In this way, whether it be the equality of the true nature (*tathatā*) of the five eyes, the equality of the true nature of the six supernormal powers (*ṣaḍabhijñā*), or the equality of the true nature of the Tathāgata—they are all one and the same equality of true nature, non-dual and without distinction.

"Furthermore, because the *tathatā* (suchness) of the gates of *samādhi* is equal, the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal; because the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal, the *tathatā* of the gates of *samādhi* is equal.
Because the *tathatā* of the gates of *dhāraṇī* is equal, the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal; because the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal, the *tathatā* of the gates of *dhāraṇī* is equal."

In this way, whether it be the equality of the suchness of the gateways of samādhi, the equality of the suchness of the gateways of dhāraṇī, or the equality of the suchness of the Tathāgata, they are all the same single suchness—equal, non-dual, and without distinction.

"Furthermore, because the *tathatā* (suchness) of the ten powers of a Buddha is equal, the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal; because the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal, the *tathatā* of the ten powers of a Buddha is equal.

Because the *tathatā* of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is equal, the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal; because the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal, the *tathatā* of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is equal."

In this way, whether it be the equality of the Tathatā of the Buddha’s ten powers, the equality of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, or the equality of the Tathāgata’s Tathatā—they are all one single Tathatā, equal, non-dual, and without distinction.

"Furthermore, because the *tathatā* (suchness) of the fruit of stream-entry is equal, the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal; because the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal, the *tathatā* of the fruit of stream-entry is equal.

Because the *tathatā* of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship is equal, the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal; because the *tathatā* of the Tathāgata is equal, the *tathatā* of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship is equal."

In this way, the suchness of the fruit of stream-entry is equal; the suchness of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship is equal; and the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal—this single suchness is equal, non-dual, and without distinction.

"Furthermore, because the suchness of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is equal, the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal; because the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal, the suchness of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is equal."
Thus, the suchness that is equal in the awakening of a pratyekabuddha and the suchness that is equal in a Tathāgata are one and the same suchness, equal, non-dual, and without distinction.
"Furthermore, because the suchness of all-knowledge is equal, the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal; because the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal, the suchness of all-knowledge is equal.

Because the suchness of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects is equal, the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal; because the suchness of the Tathāgata is equal, the suchness of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects is equal."

In this way, the equality of the suchness of all-knowledge, the equality of the suchness of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects, and the equality of the suchness of the Tathāgata, are one and the same suchness-equality, non-dual and without distinction.
“O sons of the gods!
Because Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have directly realized the equality of the suchness (tathatā) of all these phenomena, they are called Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas.”
"The Elder Subhūti has profound faith and understanding in this suchness; for this reason, it is said that the Elder Subhūti is born after the Tathāgata.

When these characteristics of suchness were thus being explained, this trichiliocosm shook in six ways: it surged in the east and subsided in the west; it surged in the west and subsided in the east; it surged in the south and subsided in the north; it surged in the north and subsided in the south;

it surged in the center and subsided at the edges; and it surged at the edges and subsided in the center. *The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, Fascicle 321, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Order. Part One, Chapter Forty-seven on Suchness, Section Five. The Actual Exposition of the Characteristics of Suchness.

At that time, the devaputras of the desire and form realms again took powdered celestial tagara, tamāla, and sandalwood incense, as well as celestial utpala, padma, kumuda, and puṇḍarīka flowers, along with flowers of exquisite fragrance and flowers of exquisite sound—such as the mahā-susvara flower—and scattered them over the Bhagavān and Subhūti, addressing the Buddha, saying:
"How marvelous! How extraordinary!"
World-Honored One!
This is unprecedented!
The Elder Subhūti is born after the Tathāgata by virtue of suchness.
At that time, Subhūti addressed the devaputras of the desire and form realms, saying:
"Devaputras, you should know this!

The Elder Subhūti does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by way of form, nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth by way of the suchness of form; he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from form, nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the suchness of form."

One does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by virtue of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness; one does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by virtue of the suchness of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness; one follows the Tathāgata’s birth without being separate from feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness; and one follows the Tathāgata’s birth without being separate from the suchness of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.
“Son of Heaven, you should know this!

The Elder Subhūti does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by way of the sense-base of the eye, nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth by way of the suchness of the sense-base of the eye; he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the sense-base of the eye, nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the suchness of the sense-base of the eye.

He does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by way of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind; he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by way of the suchness of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind; he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind, nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the suchness of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind.”

“Son of Heaven, you should know this! The Elder Subhūti does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by way of the sphere of form (*rūpāyatana*); he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by way of the suchness (*tathatā*) of the sphere of form; he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the sphere of form; he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the suchness of the sphere of form.

He does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by way of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena (*dharmāyatana*); he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by way of the suchness of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena; he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena; he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the suchness of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena.”
“Son of Heaven, you should know this!

The Elder Subhūti does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by way of the eye-element, nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth by way of the suchness of the eye-element; he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the eye-element, nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the suchness of the eye-element.

He does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by way of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-element, nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth by way of the suchness of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-element; he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-element, nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the suchness of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-element.”
“Son of Heaven, you should know this!

The Elder Subhūti does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by way of the realm of form (*rūpadhātu*), nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth by way of the suchness (*tathatā*) of the realm of form; he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the realm of form, nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the suchness of the realm of form.

He does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by way of the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or phenomena (*dharmadhātu*); he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by way of the suchness of the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or phenomena; he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or phenomena, nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the suchness of the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or phenomena.”
“Son of Heaven, you should know this!

The Elder Subhūti does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by virtue of the visual consciousness element, nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth by virtue of the suchness of the visual consciousness element; he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the visual consciousness element, nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the suchness of the visual consciousness element.

He does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by virtue of the auditory, olfactory, gustatory, tactile, or mental consciousness elements, nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth by virtue of the suchness of the auditory, olfactory, gustatory, tactile, or mental consciousness elements; he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the auditory, olfactory, gustatory, tactile, or mental consciousness elements, nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the suchness of the auditory, olfactory, gustatory, tactile, or mental consciousness elements.”
“Son of Heaven, you should know this!

The Elder Subhūti does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by way of eye-contact, nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth by way of the suchness of eye-contact; he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from eye-contact, nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the suchness of eye-contact.

He does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by way of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact, nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth by way of the suchness of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact; he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact, nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the suchness of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact.”
“Son of Heaven, you should know this!

The Elder Subhūti does not follow the Tathāgata by virtue of the feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition; he does not follow the Tathāgata by virtue of the suchness of the feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition. He does not follow the Tathāgata apart from the feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition; nor does he follow the Tathāgata apart from the suchness of the feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.”

One follows the Tathāgata’s birth not because of the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions; one follows the Tathāgata’s birth not because of the suchness of the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions; one follows the Tathāgata’s birth not by being separate from the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions; and one follows the Tathāgata’s birth not by being separate from the suchness of the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions.
“Son of Heaven, you should know this!

The Elder Subhūti does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by way of the earth element, nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth by way of the suchness of the earth element; he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the earth element, nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the suchness of the earth element.

He does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by way of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements, nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth by way of the suchness of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements; he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements, nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the suchness of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements.”
“Son of Heaven, you should know this!

The Elder Subhūti does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by virtue of ignorance (*avidyā*), nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth by virtue of the suchness (*tathatā*) of ignorance; he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from ignorance, nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the suchness of ignorance.

He does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by virtue of volitional formations (*saṃskāra*), consciousness (*vijñāna*), name-and-form (*nāmarūpa*), the six sense bases (*ṣaḍāyatana*), contact (*sparśa*), feeling (*vedanā*), craving (*tṛṣṇā*), grasping (*upādāna*), becoming (*bhava*), birth (*jāti*), or old age and death (*jarāmaraṇa*); nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth by virtue of the suchness of volitional formations through to old age and death; nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from volitional formations through to old age and death, nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the suchness of volitional formations through to old age and death.”
“Son of Heaven, you should know this!

The Elder Subhūti does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth because of a self, nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth because of the *tathatā* (suchness) of a self; he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by being separate from a self, nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth by being separate from the *tathatā* of a self.

He does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth because of a sentient being, a life-principle, a soul, a nourisher, a spirit, a person, an individual, a mind-born, a youth, an agent, an experiencer, a knower, or a seer; he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth because of the *tathatā* of a sentient being up to a seer; he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by being separate from a sentient being up to a seer, nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth by being separate from the *tathatā* of a sentient being up to a seer.”
“Son of Heaven, you should know this!

The Elder Subhūti does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by virtue of the perfection of giving (*dānapāramitā*); he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by virtue of the suchness (*tathatā*) of the perfection of giving; he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the perfection of giving; nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the suchness of the perfection of giving.

One does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by virtue of the perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom; nor does one follow the Tathāgata’s birth by virtue of the suchness of the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom; nor is it by being separate from the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom that one follows the Tathāgata’s birth; nor is it by being separate from the suchness of the perfections from ethical discipline through wisdom that one follows the Tathāgata’s birth.
“Son of Heaven, you should know this!

The Elder Subhūti does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by virtue of internal emptiness, nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth by virtue of the true suchness (*tathatā*) of internal emptiness; he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from internal emptiness, nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the true suchness of internal emptiness.

One follows the birth of the Tathāgata not by way of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, emptiness of all dharmas, unapprehendable emptiness, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, or emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence; nor does one follow the birth of the Tathāgata by way of the suchness of external emptiness up to the suchness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence; nor does one follow the birth of the Tathāgata by not being apart from external emptiness up to the intrinsic nature of non-existence; nor does one follow the birth of the Tathāgata by not being apart from the suchness of external emptiness up to the suchness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
“Son of Heaven, you should know this!

The Elder Subhūti does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by means of *tathatā* (suchness); he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by means of *tathatā* being *tathatā*; he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from *tathatā*; nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from *tathatā* being *tathatā*.

One follows the Tathāgata’s birth not by means of the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), or the inconceivable realm; nor does one follow the Tathāgata’s birth by means of the suchness (tathatā) of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm; nor does one follow the Tathāgata’s birth by being separate from the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm; nor does one follow the Tathāgata’s birth by being separate from the suchness of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm.
“Son of Heaven, you should know this!

The Elder Subhūti does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by virtue of the four foundations of mindfulness, nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth by virtue of the suchness of the four foundations of mindfulness; yet he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the four foundations of mindfulness, nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the suchness of the four foundations of mindfulness.

He does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by virtue of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path; nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth by virtue of the suchness of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path; yet he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the suchness of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path.”
"O Son of Heaven, you should know this!

The Elder Subhūti does not follow after the Tathāgata by virtue of the noble truth of suffering, nor does he follow after the Tathāgata by virtue of the suchness of the noble truth of suffering; he does not follow after the Tathāgata by being separate from the noble truth of suffering, nor does he follow after the Tathāgata by being separate from the suchness of the noble truth of suffering.

He does not follow after the Tathāgata by virtue of the noble truths of origin, cessation, or the path; he does not follow after the Tathāgata by virtue of the suchness of the noble truths of origin, cessation, or the path; he does not follow after the Tathāgata by being separate from the noble truths of origin, cessation, or the path, nor does he follow after the Tathāgata by being separate from the suchness of the noble truths of origin, cessation, or the path."

“Son of Heaven, you should know this! The Elder Subhūti does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by virtue of the four dhyānas; he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by virtue of the suchness of the four dhyānas; he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the four dhyānas; nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the suchness of the four dhyānas.

He does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by virtue of the four immeasurables or the four formless concentrations; he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by virtue of the suchness of the four immeasurables or the four formless concentrations; he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the four immeasurables or the four formless concentrations; nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the suchness of the four immeasurables or the four formless concentrations.”
"O Son of Heaven, you should know this!

The Elder Subhūti does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by virtue of the eight liberations, nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth by virtue of the suchness of the eight liberations; yet he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the eight liberations, nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the suchness of the eight liberations.

He does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by virtue of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities; nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth by virtue of the suchness of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities; yet he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities, nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the suchness of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities."
“Son of Heaven, you should know this!

The Elder Subhūti does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by virtue of the liberation door of emptiness, nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth by virtue of the suchness of the liberation door of emptiness; yet he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the liberation door of emptiness, nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the suchness of the liberation door of emptiness.

He does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by virtue of the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness, nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth by virtue of the suchness of the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness; yet he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness, nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the suchness of the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness.”
“Son of Heaven, you should know this!

The Elder Subhūti does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by virtue of the five eyes, nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth by virtue of the suchness of the five eyes; he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the five eyes, nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the suchness of the five eyes.

He does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by virtue of the six supernormal powers, nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth by virtue of the suchness of the six supernormal powers; he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the six supernormal powers, nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the suchness of the six supernormal powers.”
“Son of Heaven, you should know this!

The Elder Subhūti does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by way of the gateways of samādhi, nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth by way of the suchness of the gateways of samādhi; he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the gateways of samādhi, nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the suchness of the gateways of samādhi.

He does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by way of the gateways of dhāraṇī, nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth by way of the suchness of the gateways of dhāraṇī; he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the gateways of dhāraṇī, nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the suchness of the gateways of dhāraṇī.”
“Son of the gods, you should know this:

the Elder Subhūti does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by virtue of the Buddha’s ten powers; he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by virtue of the suchness of the Buddha’s ten powers; he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the Buddha’s ten powers; nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the suchness of the Buddha’s ten powers.

One does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by virtue of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; nor does one follow the Tathāgata’s birth by virtue of the suchness of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; nor does one follow the Tathāgata’s birth by being separate from the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; nor does one follow the Tathāgata’s birth by being separate from the suchness of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.

“Son of Heaven, you should know this! The Elder Subhūti does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by virtue of the fruit of stream-entry; he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by virtue of the suchness of the fruit of stream-entry; he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the fruit of stream-entry; nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the suchness of the fruit of stream-entry.

He does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by virtue of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, or arhatship; he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by virtue of the suchness of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, or arhatship; he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, or arhatship; nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the suchness of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, or arhatship.”
“Son of Heaven, you should know this!

The Elder Subhūti follows the Tathāgata’s birth not by virtue of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, nor by virtue of the suchness of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment; he follows the Tathāgata’s birth because he is not separate from pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, nor is he separate from the suchness of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment.”
“Son of Heaven, you should know this!

The Elder Subhūti does not follow after the Tathāgata by virtue of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), nor does he follow after the Tathāgata by virtue of the suchness (*tathatā*) of all-knowledge; he does not follow after the Tathāgata apart from all-knowledge, nor does he follow after the Tathāgata apart from the suchness of all-knowledge.

He does not follow after the Tathāgata by virtue of the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*) or the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), nor does he follow after the Tathāgata by virtue of the suchness of the knowledge of the paths or the knowledge of all aspects; he does not follow after the Tathāgata apart from the knowledge of the paths or the knowledge of all aspects, nor does he follow after the Tathāgata apart from the suchness of the knowledge of the paths or the knowledge of all aspects.”
“Son of Heaven, you should know this!

The Elder Subhūti does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by virtue of conditioned phenomena (*saṃskṛta*); he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by virtue of the suchness (*tathatā*) of conditioned phenomena; he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from conditioned phenomena; nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the suchness of conditioned phenomena.”
“Son of Heaven, you should know this!

The Elder Subhūti does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by virtue of the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*); he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth by virtue of the suchness (*tathatā*) of the unconditioned; he does not follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the unconditioned; nor does he follow the Tathāgata’s birth apart from the suchness of the unconditioned.”
"Why is this so? O sons of the gods!

All these dharmas are entirely non-existent; those who undergo dependent origination, that which is dependently originated, the means by which there is dependent origination, and the locus of dependent origination—all of these are unapprehendable."
At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

The suchness of all dharmas, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-falsity, the non-alteration, the equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of dharma, the stability of dharma, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm are all most profound.”
“World-Honored One!
Herein, form cannot be apprehended, nor can the suchness of form be apprehended. Why is this?
In this, even form cannot be apprehended, much less can the suchness of form be apprehended!
In this, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness cannot be apprehended, nor can the suchness of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness be apprehended.

Why is this? Because herein even feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness cannot be apprehended; how much less could the suchness of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness be apprehended!
“World-Honored One!
Within this, the eye-base is unattainable, and the suchness of the eye-base is also unattainable. Why is this?
Within this, even the sense-base of the eye cannot be apprehended, let alone the suchness of the sense-base of the eye!
Within this, the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind cannot be apprehended, nor can the suchness of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind be apprehended.

Why is this? Because herein even the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind cannot be apprehended; how much less could the suchness of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind be apprehended!
“World-Honored One!
Within this, the sphere of form (rūpāyatana) cannot be apprehended, nor can the suchness (tathatā) of the sphere of form be apprehended. Why is this?
In this context, even the sense-base of form cannot be apprehended, much less can the suchness of the sense-base of form be apprehended!

In this context, the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena cannot be apprehended, nor can the suchness of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena be apprehended.

Why is this? Because within this, even the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena cannot be apprehended; how much less could the suchness of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena be apprehended!
“World-Honored One!
Within this, the eye-element cannot be apprehended, and the suchness of the eye-element also cannot be apprehended. Why is this?
In this context, even the eye-element cannot be apprehended, much less can the suchness of the eye-element be apprehended!
In this context, the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements cannot be apprehended, and the suchness of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements likewise cannot be apprehended.

Why is this? Because within this, even the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind elements (*dhātu*) cannot be apprehended; how much less could the suchness (*tathatā*) of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind elements be apprehended!
“World-Honored One!
Herein, the realm of form cannot be apprehended, nor can the suchness of the realm of form be apprehended. Why is this?
Within this, even the realm of form (*rūpadhātu*) cannot be apprehended, much less can the suchness (*tathatā*) of the realm of form be apprehended!

Within this, the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental objects (*dharmadhātu*) cannot be apprehended, nor can the suchness of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental objects be apprehended.

Why is this? Because within this, even the elements of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena cannot be apprehended; how much less could the suchness of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena be apprehended!
“World-Honored One!
Within this, the eye-consciousness element cannot be apprehended, nor can the suchness of the eye-consciousness element be apprehended. Why is this?
In this context, even the eye-consciousness element cannot be apprehended, much less can the suchness of the eye-consciousness element be apprehended!

In this context, the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements cannot be apprehended, nor can the suchness of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements be apprehended.

Why is this? Because herein even the auditory, olfactory, gustatory, tactile, and mental consciousness elements cannot be apprehended; how much less could the suchness of the auditory, olfactory, gustatory, tactile, and mental consciousness elements be apprehended!
“World-Honored One!
Within this, eye-contact cannot be apprehended, nor can the suchness of eye-contact be apprehended. Why is this?
In this regard, even eye-contact cannot be apprehended, much less can the suchness of eye-contact be apprehended!
In this regard, ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact cannot be apprehended, and the suchness of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact likewise cannot be apprehended.

Why is this? Because herein even the contact of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind cannot be apprehended; how much less can the suchness of the contact of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind be apprehended!
“World-Honored One!

Within this, the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition cannot be apprehended, and the suchness of those various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition also cannot be apprehended.”

Why is this? Within this, even the various sensations produced with eye-contact as a condition cannot be apprehended; how much less could the suchness of those various sensations produced with eye-contact as a condition be apprehended!

In this regard, the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions cannot be apprehended; nor can the suchness of the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions be apprehended.

Why is this?
