“Subhūti! Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not regress from suchness, he is called ‘non-regressive. Because he does not regress from the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu), he is called ‘non-regressive.’”
Why is this? Subhūti!

The intrinsic nature of true suchness (tathatā) does not exist; the intrinsic nature of the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), up to and including the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu), likewise does not exist. Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not abide therein, they are said to be "regressing."

"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is called 'non-retrogressive' because he does not regress from the four foundations of mindfulness; he is called 'non-retrogressive' because he does not regress from the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path."
Why is this? Subhūti!

The intrinsic nature of the four foundations of mindfulness does not exist, nor does the intrinsic nature of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path exist; because a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not abide within these, they are said to be "regressing."

"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is called 'non-retrogressive' because they retrogress from the noble truth of suffering; they are called 'non-retrogressive' because they retrogress from the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path."
Why is this? Subhūti!

The intrinsic nature of the noble truth of suffering does not exist; the intrinsic natures of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path likewise do not exist. Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not abide within these, they are said to be "regressing."

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is called ‘non-retrogressive’ because he retrogresses from the four dhyānas; he is called ‘non-retrogressive’ because he retrogresses from the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments.”
Why is this? Subhūti!

The intrinsic nature of the four dhyānas does not exist, and the intrinsic nature of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments likewise does not exist; because a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not abide within them, it is called "regression."

“Subhūti! Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva turns back from the eight liberations, he is called ‘non-retrogressive’; because he turns back from the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities, he is called ‘non-retrogressive.’”
Why is this? Subhūti!

The intrinsic nature of the eight liberations is non-existent; the intrinsic nature of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive absorptions, and the ten totalities is likewise non-existent. Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not abide within these, they are said to be "regressing."

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is called ‘non-retrogressive’ because they retrogress from the gate of liberation of emptiness; they are called ‘non-retrogressive’ because they retrogress from the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.”
Why is this? Subhūti!

The intrinsic nature of the gate of liberation of emptiness is non-existent; the intrinsic nature of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness is likewise non-existent. Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not abide therein, they are said to be "regressing."

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is called ‘non-retrogressive’ because he does not regress from the five eyes; he is called ‘non-retrogressive’ because he does not regress from the six supernormal powers.”
Why is this? Subhūti!

The intrinsic nature of the five eyes does not exist, and the intrinsic nature of the six supernormal powers likewise does not exist; because a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not dwell within them, they are said to "recede."

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is called ‘non-retrogressive’ because they retrogress from the gateways of samādhi; they are called ‘non-retrogressive’ because they retrogress from the gateways of dhāraṇī.”
Why is this? Subhūti!

The intrinsic nature of the gateways to samādhi does not exist, and the intrinsic nature of the gateways to dhāraṇī likewise does not exist; because a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not abide therein, they are said to be "regressing."

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is called ‘non-retrogressive’ because he does not retrogress from the ten powers of a buddha; he is called ‘non-retrogressive’ because he does not retrogress from the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha.”
Why is this? Subhūti!

The intrinsic nature of the Buddha’s ten powers is non-existent; the intrinsic nature of the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, is likewise non-existent. Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not abide within these, they are said to be "regressing."

“Subhūti! Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva falls back from the fruit of a stream-enterer, he is called ‘non-retrogressive’; because he falls back from the fruits of a once-returner, a non-returner, and an arhat, he is called ‘non-retrogressive.’”
Why is this? Subhūti!

The intrinsic nature of the fruit of stream-entry does not exist; the intrinsic nature of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhat likewise does not exist. Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not dwell within these, they are said to be "regressing."
“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is called ‘non-retrogressive’ because he does not retrogress from the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha. Why is that?
"Subhūti! The nature of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is non-existent; because a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not abide therein, he is said to be 'receding. Subhūti!"

This bodhisattva mahāsattva is called "non-retrogressive" because they do not regress from all-knowledge; they are called "non-retrogressive" because they do not regress from the knowledge of the aspects of the path or the knowledge of all aspects.
Why is this? Subhūti!

The intrinsic nature of all-knowledge (sarvajñatā) is non-existent; the intrinsic nature of the knowledge of the paths (mārgākārajñatā) and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā) is likewise non-existent. Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not abide within these, they are said to be "regressing."

"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is called 'non-retrogressive' because they do not retrogress from the stage of ordinary beings; they are called 'non-retrogressive' because they do not retrogress from the stage of śrāvakas, the stage of pratyekabuddhas, the stage of bodhisattvas, or the stage of tathāgatas."
Why is this? Subhūti!

The intrinsic nature of the stage of ordinary beings does not exist; the intrinsic nature of the stages of śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and tathāgatas also does not exist. Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not abide within these, they are said to be "receding."
“Subhūti! It is because this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not regress from unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment that he is called ‘non-regressive. Why is this?
"Subhūti! The intrinsic nature of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi is non-existent; because a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not abide therein, he is said to be 'receding'."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

A bodhisattva mahāsattva in the stage of non-retrogression never takes pleasure in observing the physical forms, speech, or doctrines of externalist śramaṇas, brahmins, and the like. It is absolutely impossible that those śramaṇas and brahmins could truly know or truly see the dharmas to be known, or that they could establish a gateway to the Dharma of right view."
"Subhūti! If one is endowed with such practices, characteristics, and signs, you should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti!"

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva in the stage of non-retrogression develops deep faith and understanding in the well-expounded Dharma and Vinaya of the Buddha, they will never harbor doubt or uncertainty; they will not grasp at precepts and prohibitions nor fall into wrong views; they will not cling to worldly auspicious rites as being pure; they will never prostrate to other celestial deities such as those served by the various worldlings and non-Buddhists; nor will they ever offer various kinds of flower garlands, powdered and scented incense, clothing, necklaces, precious banners, flags, canopies, music, or lamps to celestial deities or non-Buddhist practitioners.
"Subhūti! If one accomplishes such practices, characteristics, and signs, you should know that this is an irreversible bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti!"

If a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva at the stage of non-retrogression is not born in the hells, among animals, in the realm of hungry ghosts, or among the asuras; nor is he born into lowly castes, such as the Caṇḍālas or Pukkasas; nor does he ever receive the body of a *śaṇḍha*, a *paṇḍaka*, one without sexual organs, one with dual sexual organs, or a woman; nor does he receive a body that is blind, deaf, mute, crippled, lame, epileptic, or deformed; nor does he ever take birth in an unfavorable state (*akṣaṇa*).
"Subhūti! If one accomplishes such practices, characteristics, and signs, you should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti!"

If a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva in the stage of non-retrogression constantly delights in practicing the ten paths of wholesome action: he himself abstains from taking life and also encourages others to abstain from taking life; he always correctly extols the dharma of abstaining from taking life and joyfully praises those who abstain from taking life;

he himself abstains from taking what is not given and also encourages others to abstain from taking what is not given; he always correctly extols the dharma of abstaining from taking what is not given and joyfully praises those who abstain from taking what is not given;

he himself abstains from sexual misconduct and also encourages others to abstain from sexual misconduct; he always correctly extols the dharma of abstaining from sexual misconduct and joyfully praises those who abstain from sexual misconduct.

They themselves abstain from false speech and also encourage others to abstain from false speech; they constantly and correctly praise the practice of abstaining from false speech and joyfully extol those who abstain from it.

They themselves abstain from harsh speech and also encourage others to abstain from harsh speech; they constantly and correctly praise the practice of abstaining from harsh speech and joyfully extol those who abstain from it.

They themselves abstain from divisive speech and also encourage others to abstain from divisive speech; they constantly and correctly praise the practice of abstaining from divisive speech and joyfully extol those who abstain from it.

He himself abstains from frivolous speech and also encourages others to abstain from frivolous speech; he constantly and correctly extols the practice of abstaining from frivolous speech and joyfully praises those who abstain from it.

He himself abstains from covetousness and also encourages others to abstain from covetousness; he constantly and correctly extols the practice of abstaining from covetousness and joyfully praises those who abstain from it.

He himself abstains from ill will and also encourages others to abstain from ill will; he constantly and correctly extols the practice of abstaining from ill will and joyfully praises those who abstain from it.

They themselves abandon wrong views and also encourage others to abandon them; they constantly and correctly praise the Dharma of abandoning wrong views, and they joyfully extol those who have abandoned wrong views.
This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not manifest even the ten paths of unwholesome action within a dream, let alone while awake!
Subhūti, if they are endowed with such practices, tokens, and signs, you should know that they are a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.

"Furthermore, Subhūti! A bodhisattva mahāsattva in the stage of non-retrogression constantly cultivates the perfection of generosity for the universal benefit of all sentient beings; constantly cultivates the perfection of ethical discipline for the universal benefit of all sentient beings; constantly cultivates the perfection of patience for the universal benefit of all sentient beings; constantly cultivates the perfection of diligence for the universal benefit of all sentient beings; constantly cultivates the perfection of meditative concentration for the universal benefit of all sentient beings; and constantly cultivates the perfection of wisdom for the universal benefit of all sentient beings."
"Subhūti! If one is endowed with such practices, characteristics, and signs, you should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti!"

If a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva at the stage of non-retrogression takes up, contemplates, recites, and masters to perfection the pure teachings—namely, the sūtras, geyas, vyākaraṇas, gāthās, udānas, nidānas, avadānas, jātakas, vaipulyas, adbhutadharmas, avadānas, and upadeśas—and constantly delights in bestowing such dharmas upon all sentient beings, always forming this thought:
"How may I cause all classes of sentient beings who seek the true Dharma to have their aspirations fully satisfied?"

"Furthermore, taking these roots of goodness from such Dharma-giving, he dedicates them together with all sentient beings toward the unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas. Subhūti!"
If one accomplishes such practices, characteristics, and signs, you should know that this is an irreversible bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti!
"A Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who has reached the stage of non-retrogression will never give rise to doubt or hesitation regarding the profound Dharma-gates spoken by the Buddha.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"For what reason, Subhūti, does a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva never give rise to doubt or hesitation regarding the profound Dharma-gates spoken by the Buddha?
The Buddha said: "Subhūti!"

This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive any dharma that could give rise to doubt or hesitation; that is to say, they do not perceive form, nor do they perceive feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness, such that doubt or hesitation could arise regarding them.
They do not perceive the sense-base of the eye, nor do they perceive the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind, such that doubt or hesitation could arise regarding them.
They do not perceive the sense-base of forms, nor do they perceive the sense-bases of sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, or mental phenomena, such that doubt or hesitation could arise regarding them.
One does not perceive the eye-element, nor does one perceive the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-element, such that doubt or hesitation could arise regarding them;
one does not perceive the form-element, nor does one perceive the sound, odor, taste, tangible, or mental-object-element, such that doubt or hesitation could arise regarding them;
one does not perceive the eye-consciousness-element, nor does one perceive the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-consciousness-element, such that doubt or hesitation could arise regarding them.
One does not perceive the existence of eye-contact, nor does one perceive the existence of ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact, such that doubt or hesitation could arise therein;

one does not perceive the existence of the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition, nor does one perceive the existence of the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as condition, such that doubt or hesitation could arise therein;

one does not perceive the existence of the earth element, nor does one perceive the existence of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements, such that doubt or hesitation could arise therein.

One does not perceive ignorance, nor does one perceive volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, or old age and death, such that doubt or hesitation could arise regarding them;

one does not perceive the perfection of generosity, nor does one perceive the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom, such that doubt or hesitation could arise regarding them.

One does not perceive an internal emptiness, nor does one perceive external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, such that one might give rise to doubt or hesitation regarding them.

They do not perceive the existence of *tathatā* (suchness), nor do they perceive the existence of the *dharmadhātu* (dharma-realm), the *dharmatā* (dharma-nature), the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, or the inconceivable realm, such that they might give rise to doubt or hesitation regarding them;

they do not perceive the existence of the four foundations of mindfulness, nor do they perceive the existence of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path, such that they might give rise to doubt or hesitation regarding them;

they do not perceive the existence of the noble truth of suffering, nor do they perceive the existence of the noble truths of origin, cessation, or the path, such that they might give rise to doubt or hesitation regarding them.
One does not perceive the four dhyānas, nor does one perceive the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, such that doubt or hesitation could arise regarding them;

one does not perceive the eight liberations, nor does one perceive the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities, such that doubt or hesitation could arise regarding them;
one does not perceive the five eyes, nor does one perceive the six supernormal powers, such that doubt or hesitation could arise regarding them.
One does not perceive any gateways of samādhi, nor does one perceive any gateways of dhāraṇī, such that one could give rise to doubt or hesitation regarding them;

one does not perceive the ten powers of a Buddha, nor does one perceive the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, such that one could give rise to doubt or hesitation regarding them;
one does not perceive the fruit of stream-entry, nor does one perceive the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, or arhatship, such that one could give rise to doubt or hesitation regarding them.
One does not perceive the existence of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment such that one might give rise to doubt or hesitation regarding it;

one does not perceive the existence of omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), nor does one perceive the existence of the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) or the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), such that one might give rise to doubt or hesitation regarding them;

one does not perceive the existence of the stage of ordinary beings (*pṛthagjanabhūmi*), nor does one perceive the existence of the stage of śrāvakas, the stage of pratyekabuddhas, the stage of bodhisattvas, or the stage of Tathāgatas, such that one might give rise to doubt or hesitation regarding them.
One does not perceive an *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* in which one could give rise to doubt or hesitation.
Subhūti! If they are endowed with such practices, characteristics, and signs, you should know that they are non-retrogressive bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle Three Hundred and Twenty-five. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter Forty-nine on Non-retrogression, Section Two. "Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva in the stage of non-retrogression accomplishes supple, lovely, and delightful actions of body, speech, and mind, their mind will be free from obstruction toward all sentient beings.
"Subhūti! If one is endowed with such practices, characteristics, and signs, you should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti!"

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva in the stage of non-retrogression constantly accomplishes physical, verbal, and mental actions that are associated with the arising of loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity.
"Subhūti! If one is endowed with such practices, characteristics, and signs, you should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti!"

If a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva is at the stage of non-retrogression, they will certainly not dwell together with the five hindrances, namely: the hindrance of sensual desire, ill-will, sloth and torpor, restlessness and remorse, and doubt.
"Subhūti! If one is endowed with such practices, characteristics, and signs, you should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti!"

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva in the stage of non-retrogression has already subdued all latent propensities (*anuśaya*), then all fetters (*saṃyojana*), bonds (*bandhana*), secondary afflictions (*upakleśa*), and entanglements (*paryavasthāna*) will never arise again and cannot be found in their manifestation.
"Subhūti! If one is endowed with such practices, characteristics, and signs, you should know that this is an irreversible bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti!"

If a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva in the stage of non-retrogression enters and exits, goes and returns, his mind is never deluded or mistaken; he constantly dwells in right mindfulness and clear comprehension. Whether advancing or halting, standing, walking, sitting, or lying down, as well as lifting or lowering his feet, it is likewise so. Wherever he travels, he necessarily observes the ground; he walks with composure, maintaining focused attention and gazing straight ahead. In his movements and speech, he is always free from abruptness or violence.
"Subhūti! If one is endowed with such practices, characteristics, and signs, you should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti!"

If a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva is at the stage of non-retrogression, all the bedding and clothing they use will always be fragrant and pure, free from any foul odors or impurities; furthermore, they will be devoid of grime, grease, lice, or other insects; their mind will delight in purity and refinement, and their body will be free from disease.
"Subhūti! If one is endowed with such practices, traits, and characteristics, you should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti!"

If a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva at the stage of non-retrogression possesses purity of body and mind, they are not subject to being constantly devoured by the eighty thousand families of parasites within the body, as is the case with ordinary persons.

Why is this so? Because these bodhisattvas possess roots of goodness that are superior and transcend the world; their physical forms, both internally and externally, are pure, and thus no insects or creatures can invade or consume their bodies.

As their roots of goodness gradually increase, so too do their bodies and minds become increasingly pure. By virtue of this cause and condition, the bodies and minds of these bodhisattvas become as firm and solid as a diamond, such that they cannot be harmed or disturbed by adverse conditions.
“Subhūti! If one is endowed with such practices, characteristics, and signs, you should know that this is an irreversible bodhisattva mahāsattva.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
How does this bodhisattva-mahāsattva attain purity of body and mind?
The Buddha said:

"Subhūti! To the extent that the roots of virtue of this bodhisattva mahāsattva gradually increase, to that same extent the deceit and crookedness of body and mind are eliminated by the power of those roots of virtue; thus, they never arise again until the end of the future, and by this means, he attains purity of body and mind."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

To the extent that the roots of virtue of this bodhisattva mahāsattva gradually increase, to that same extent their physical, verbal, and mental actions are polished by the power of those roots of virtue; thus they become free from all turbidity, defilement, and crookedness. By means of this, they attain purity of body and mind, and because body and mind are pure, they transcend the levels of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, abiding firmly and immovably in the bodhisattva stage."
"Subhūti! If one is endowed with such practices, characteristics, and signs, you should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti!"

If a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva at the stage of non-retrogression does not value gain and offerings, does not seek fame and reputation, and feels no greedy attachment toward food, drink, clothing, bedding, dwellings, or material wealth, then although he may practice the twelve dhūta virtues, he relies on none of them at all.
"Subhūti! If one is endowed with such practices, characteristics, and signs, you should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti!"
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva at the stage of non-retrogression constantly cultivates the perfection of generosity, the mind of stinginess and greed will never arise;
if they constantly cultivate the perfection of ethical discipline, the mind of violating precepts will never arise;
if they constantly cultivate the perfection of patience, the mind of anger and resentment will never arise.
They constantly cultivate the perfection of diligence, so that a mind of indolence never arises;
they constantly cultivate the perfection of meditative concentration, so that a mind of distraction never arises;
they constantly cultivate the perfection of wisdom, so that a mind of delusion never arises.
By this means, such states of mind as envy, guile, deceit, arrogance, negligence, concealment, and resentment will also never arise again. Subhūti!
If one is endowed with such practices, attributes, and characteristics, you should know that this is a non-retrogressive Bodhisattva Mahāsattva.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva at the stage of non-retrogression possesses firm awakening-wisdom and is able to penetrate deeply, hearing the true Dharma with reverence and faith, then whatever mundane or supramundane dharmas they hear, they are all able to skillfully bring them into accord with the profound principle of the Prajñāpāramitā. Furthermore, whatever worldly activities they perform, they also bring them into accord with the *dharmatā* by means of the Prajñāpāramitā, seeing not a single thing that departs from the *dharmatā*. Even if there were something that did not correspond to the *dharmatā*, they would still be able to skillfully bring it into accord with the profound principle of the Prajñāpāramitā, because of this, they do not see anything that departs from the *dharmatā*."
"Subhūti! If one is endowed with such practices, characteristics, and signs, you should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti!"

If a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who has reached the stage of non-retrogression were to encounter an evil Māra manifesting eight great hells, and within each of those great hells, further manifesting many hundreds, many thousands, many hundreds of thousands, many koṭis, many hundreds of koṭis, many thousands of koṭis, many hundreds of thousands of koṭis, or many hundreds of thousands of koṭi-nayutas of Bodhisattvas, all being scorched by intersecting fierce flames and each undergoing bitter, painful, and agonizing suffering; having performed such a transformation, [the Māra] would speak to those non-retrogressive Bodhisattvas, saying:

"These bodhisattvas have all received from the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, the prediction of non-retrogression; therefore, they are born in such great hells and constantly undergo these various kinds of intense suffering. You bodhisattvas, having likewise received from the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, the prediction of non-retrogression, shall also fall into this great hell and undergo various intense sufferings."

The Buddha has granted you the prediction that you shall undergo extreme suffering within the great hells; he has not granted you the prediction of non-retrogression toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. Therefore, you should quickly abandon the mind of great enlightenment, so that you may escape the sufferings of the great hells and be reborn among the gods or among humans to enjoy various forms of wealth and happiness.
“Subhūti! At that time, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva who is non-retrogressive sees or hears this matter, their mind remains unmoved and they feel neither alarm nor doubt; they simply think:

‘It is absolutely impossible for a bodhisattva mahāsattva who has received the prediction of non-retrogression to fall into the hells, the animal realm, the realm of hungry ghosts, or among the asuras.’”

Why is this? Because a Bodhisattva in the stage of non-retrogression is definitively free from unwholesome karma, nor does he possess wholesome karma that would bring about bitter fruits; because the Tathāgata never utters false speech; and because all that is spoken by the Buddhas is for the benefit and happiness of all sentient beings, flowing forth from a heart of great compassion. Therefore, whatever is seen or heard [to the contrary] must certainly be the work and the teaching of an evil Māra.
"Subhūti! If one is endowed with such practices, characteristics, and signs, you should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti!"
If a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who is in the stage of non-retrogression should encounter an evil Māra appearing in the guise of a śramaṇa, who comes to him and proclaims these words:

"That which you have previously heard—that you should practice the perfection of giving until it is ultimately perfected, and that you should practice the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom until they are ultimately perfected, and that you shall realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment—all such things you have heard are false teachings; you should quickly abandon them."

Furthermore, that which you previously heard—that one should, regarding all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, and their disciples of the past, future, and present, from their initial generation of the mind of awakening until the duration of the Dharma, rejoice in all their merits and roots of goodness, collect them all together, and dedicate them toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete awakening for the sake of all sentient beings—this which you have heard is also a false teaching and should be swiftly abandoned.

If you abandon the false teachings you have heard, I shall instruct you in the true Buddha-dharma, enabling you to practice and study so that you may swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
"What you have previously heard is not the true word of the Buddha; it is a false compilation by authors of verses. What I have spoken is the true word of the Buddha.
Thus spoke Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, upon hearing such words, experiences mental agitation, alarm, or doubt, it should be known that they have not yet received from the Buddhas the prediction of non-retrogression; they have not yet reached certainty regarding unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, upon hearing such words, remains unmoved and neither startled nor doubtful, but dwells in accordance with the nature of phenomena that are unconditioned, signless, and unborn.

“Subhūti! In all that this bodhisattva mahāsattva does, he does not rely on the words of others; he practices the perfection of generosity without following the instructions of others, and he practices the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom without following the instructions of others.

He dwells in internal emptiness without following the instructions of others, and he dwells in external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential emptiness, the emptiness of self-characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, without following the instructions of others.”

They abide in suchness without relying on the instruction of others; they abide in the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm without relying on the instruction of others.

They cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness without relying on the instruction of others; they cultivate the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path without relying on the instruction of others.

They abide in the noble truth of suffering without relying on the instruction of others; they abide in the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path without relying on the instruction of others.
They cultivate the four dhyānas without following the instructions of others; they cultivate the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments without following the instructions of others;

they cultivate the eight liberations without following the instructions of others, and they cultivate the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities without following the instructions of others;

they cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness without following the instructions of others, and they cultivate the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness without following the instructions of others.

They cultivate the Ground of Utmost Joy without following the instructions of others; they cultivate the Ground of Purity, the Ground of Radiance, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Extreme Difficulty to Conquer, the Ground of Manifestation, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, and the Ground of the Dharma Cloud without following the instructions of others.
They cultivate the five eyes without following the instructions of others, and they cultivate the six supernormal powers without following the instructions of others.
They cultivate the gateways of samādhi without following the instructions of others, and they cultivate the gateways of dhāraṇī without following the instructions of others.

They cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha without following the instructions of others; they cultivate the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha without following the instructions of others;
they cultivate the contemplation of the twelve links of dependent origination in both forward and reverse order without following the instructions of others;
and they realize suffering, abandon its origin, realize its cessation, and cultivate the path without following the instructions of others.

They do not give rise to the wisdom that realizes the fruit of stream-entry through the instruction of another; they do not give rise to the wisdom that realizes the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, or arhatship through the instruction of another;
they do not give rise to the wisdom that realizes pratyekabuddha-enlightenment through the instruction of another;
and they do not give rise to the wisdom that enters the bodhisattva’s stage of correct nature and departure from birth through the instruction of another.
They do not purify buddha-fields following the instructions of others; they do not bring sentient beings to maturity following the instructions of others;
they do not give rise to the superknowledges of a bodhisattva following the instructions of others;

they do not cultivate all-knowledge following the instructions of others, nor do they cultivate the knowledge of the aspects of the path or the knowledge of all aspects following the instructions of others.
Without relying on the instructions of others, one cuts off the continuity of all afflictions along with their habitual tendencies;
without relying on the instructions of others, one cultivates the quality of non-forgetfulness; without relying on the instructions of others, one cultivates the state of constant equanimity;
and without relying on the instructions of others, one personally attains a perfect lifespan.
They do not turn the wheel of Dharma following the instructions of others;
they do not protect the true Dharma following the instructions of others;
and they do not proceed toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment following the instructions of others.

“Subhūti! Just as an arhat whose outflows are exhausted does not rely on the words of others regarding whatever he undertakes, but directly realizes the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) without confusion or doubt, such that no māra can shake him.

Thus, all śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, followers of external paths, and evil māras are unable to destroy or subdue the mind of such a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva, nor can they cause them to become discouraged or retreat from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva has certainly already dwelled in the stage of non-retrogression; all his undertakings are conceived by himself, and he does not initiate actions merely out of faith in others. He would not even practice based on the teachings of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha without first having conviction in them, let alone act upon the words of śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, outsiders, or evil Māras.”
It is impossible that these bodhisattvas would ever act solely out of faith in the practices of others.
Why is this? Subhūti!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive any dharma that can be trusted or practiced.
Why is this? "Subhūti!..."
This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive form, nor does he perceive feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness as something that can be practiced with faith;
nor does he perceive the suchness of form, nor does he perceive the suchness of feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness as something that can be practiced with faith.

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the sense base of the eye as something to be practiced with faith; nor does he perceive the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind as something to be practiced with faith.

Furthermore, he does not perceive the suchness of the sense base of the eye as something to be practiced with faith; nor does he perceive the suchness of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind as something to be practiced with faith.”

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the sphere of form as something to be practiced with faith; nor does he perceive the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena as such.

Furthermore, he does not perceive the *tathatā* (suchness) of the sphere of form as something to be practiced with faith; nor does he perceive the *tathatā* of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena as such.”

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the eye-element as something to be practiced with faith; nor does he perceive it as something to be practiced with faith. He likewise does not perceive the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-element as something to be practiced with faith;

nor does he perceive the suchness (*tathatā*) of the eye-element as something to be practiced with faith, nor the suchness of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-element as something to be practiced with faith.”
“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the realm of form, nor does he perceive the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, or phenomena as something to be practiced with faith;
nor does he perceive the suchness of the realm of form, nor does he perceive the suchness of the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, or phenomena as something to be practiced with faith.”

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the eye-consciousness element as something that can be practiced with faith; nor does he perceive the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-consciousness elements as things that can be practiced with faith.

Furthermore, he does not perceive the suchness of the eye-consciousness element as something that can be practiced with faith; nor does he perceive the suchness of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-consciousness elements as things that can be practiced with faith.”
“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive eye-contact, nor does he perceive ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact as something to be practiced with faith;
nor does he perceive the suchness of eye-contact, nor does he perceive the suchness of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact as something to be practiced with faith.”

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive any feeling produced with eye-contact as a condition as something that can be practiced; nor does he perceive any feeling produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as a condition as something that can be practiced.

Furthermore, he does not perceive the suchness of any feeling produced with eye-contact as a condition as something that can be practiced; nor does he perceive the suchness of any feeling produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as a condition as something that can be practiced.”
“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the earth element, nor does he perceive the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements as something to be practiced with faith;
nor does he perceive the suchness of the earth element, nor does he perceive the suchness of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements as something to be practiced with faith.”

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive ignorance, nor does he perceive formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, or old age and death as something that can be practiced with conviction.

Furthermore, he does not perceive the suchness of ignorance, nor does he perceive the suchness of formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, or old age and death as something that can be practiced with conviction.”

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the perfection of generosity, nor does he perceive the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom as something to be practiced with faith.

Furthermore, he does not perceive the suchness of the perfection of generosity, nor does he perceive the suchness of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom as something to be practiced with faith.”

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive internal emptiness, nor does he perceive external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersal emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence as something to be trusted and practiced.”

Furthermore, one does not perceive the *tathatā* (suchness) of internal emptiness, nor does one perceive the *tathatā* of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of essential nature, the emptiness of self-characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence as something to be trusted or practiced.

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive true thusness (*tathatā*), nor does he perceive the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the non-falsity, the unchanging nature, equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), or the inconceivable realm as something to be trusted and practiced.

Furthermore, he does not perceive true thusness as true thusness, nor does he perceive the realm of phenomena, the nature of phenomena, the non-falsity, the unchanging nature, equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, or the inconceivable realm as true thusness that can be trusted and practiced.”

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the four foundations of mindfulness; he does not perceive the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, or the eightfold noble path as something to be practiced with faith.

Furthermore, he does not perceive the suchness of the four foundations of mindfulness, nor does he perceive the suchness of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, or the eightfold noble path as something to be practiced with faith.”
“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the noble truth of suffering, nor does he perceive the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as something to be practiced with faith.

Furthermore, he does not perceive the suchness of the noble truth of suffering, nor does he perceive the suchness of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as something to be practiced with faith.”
“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the four dhyānas, nor does he perceive the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments as something to be practiced with conviction;
nor does he perceive the suchness of the four dhyānas, nor does he perceive the suchness of the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments as something to be practiced with conviction.”

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the eight liberations as something that can be practiced with conviction; nor does he perceive the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities as something that can be practiced with conviction.

Furthermore, he does not perceive the suchness of the eight liberations as something that can be practiced with conviction; nor does he perceive the suchness of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities as something that can be practiced with conviction.”

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the gate of liberation of emptiness, nor does he perceive the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness as something to be practiced with conviction;

nor does he perceive the suchness of the gate of liberation of emptiness, nor does he perceive the suchness of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness as something to be practiced with conviction.”
“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the five eyes, nor does he perceive any trustworthy practitioner of the six supernormal powers;
nor does he perceive the suchness of the five eyes, nor does he perceive any trustworthy practitioner of the suchness of the six supernormal powers.”
"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the gates of samādhi, nor does he perceive any practitioner who can be relied upon regarding the gates of dhāraṇī;
nor does he perceive the suchness of the gates of samādhi, nor does he perceive any practitioner who can be relied upon regarding the suchness of the gates of dhāraṇī."

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the ten powers of a buddha as something to be practiced with faith; nor does he perceive the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha as something to be practiced with faith.

Furthermore, he does not perceive the suchness of the ten powers of a buddha as something to be practiced with faith; nor does he perceive the suchness of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha as something to be practiced with faith.”

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the fruit of a stream-enterer, nor does he perceive the fruits of a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat as something to be practiced with conviction;

nor does he perceive the suchness of the fruit of a stream-enterer, nor does he perceive the suchness of the fruits of a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat as something to be practiced with conviction.”

"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive a practitioner who can be trusted regarding the awakening of a pratyekabuddha, nor does he perceive a practitioner who can be trusted regarding the suchness of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha."

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive omniscience, nor does he perceive the knowledge of the aspects of the path or the knowledge of all aspects as something to be practiced with faith;

nor does he perceive the suchness of omniscience, nor does he perceive the suchness of the knowledge of the aspects of the path or the knowledge of all aspects as something to be practiced with faith.”

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive a stage of ordinary beings, nor does he perceive a stage of śrāvakas, a stage of pratyekabuddhas, a stage of bodhisattvas, or a stage of tathāgatas as something to be practiced with faith.

Furthermore, he does not perceive the suchness of the stage of ordinary beings, nor does he perceive the suchness of the stages of śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, or tathāgatas as something to be practiced with faith.”

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive any unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas as something that can be practiced with conviction, nor does he perceive the *tathatā* (suchness) of the unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas as something that can be practiced with conviction.”
“Subhūti! If one is endowed with such practices, characteristics, and signs, you should know that this is an irreversible bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti!”
If a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who is in the stage of non-retrogression should encounter an evil Māra appearing in the guise of a bhikṣu, who comes to him and speaks these words:

"The practices you are engaged in are the dharmas of saṃsāra; by these you will not attain the knowledge of all modes. You should now cultivate the path that exhausts suffering, quickly bring an end to all sufferings, and realize parinirvāṇa."

At that time, Māra the Evil One immediately expounded to the Bodhisattva the counterfeit dharmas of the path that lead to birth and death, namely: the perception of bones, or the perception of bluish discoloration, or the perception of festering pus, or the perception of bloating, or the perception of being devoured by worms, or the perception of a bloody corpse; or loving-kindness, or compassion, or sympathetic joy, or equanimity; or the first dhyāna, or even up to the fourth dhyāna; or the sphere of infinite space, or even up to the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. He addressed the Bodhisattva, saying: "This is the true path and the true practice.

By employing this path and this practice, you shall attain the fruit of a Stream-enterer, or the fruit of a Once-returner, or the fruit of a Non-returner, or the fruit of Arhatship, or the enlightenment of a Pratyekabuddha."
By means of this path and through this practice, you shall swiftly exhaust all birth, aging, sickness, and death; why endure the suffering of birth and death for so long?
You should even feel weary of and abandon this present suffering body, let alone seek to receive a future suffering body!
"You should examine yourself and abandon what you previously believed. "Subhūti!
When that bodhisattva mahāsattva hears those words, his mind remains unmoved and he is neither startled nor doubtful; he simply thinks this:"

"This bhikṣu has benefited me no small amount, for he has been able to explain to me a counterfeit dharma of the path, by which I have come to recognize that this path cannot realize the fruit of a stream-enterer, nor the fruit of a once-returner, nor the fruit of a non-returner, nor the fruit of an arhat, nor even the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha—how much less could it realize the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas!"
Having formed this thought, that bodhisattva mahāsattva experiences profound joy and further reflects:

"This bhikṣu has been of great benefit to me; he has skillfully taught me the dharmas of obstruction. Now that I have understood these dharmas of obstruction, I shall train with mastery in the paths of the three vehicles."
"Subhūti! At that time, the Evil Māra, knowing that this bodhisattva’s mind was deeply filled with joy, spoke these words again:
'O son of good family!'"
"Do you wish to see how the bodhisattva mahāsattvas have for a long time diligently engaged in what appears to be fruitless practice?

That is to say, these assemblies of bodhisattva mahāsattvas, throughout great kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, have made offerings, shown reverence, honored, and praised Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, with immeasurable kinds of superior and exquisite clothing, food and drink, bedding, medicinal requisites, wealth and resources, flowers, incense, and other such items; furthermore, in the presence of Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, they have practiced the perfection of generosity, and practiced the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom."

Furthermore, at the abodes of Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, they trained in and dwelt in internal emptiness; they trained in and dwelt in external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.

Furthermore, at the abodes of Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, they trained in and dwelt within suchness; they trained in and dwelt within the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-erroneous nature, the unchanging nature, the state of equality, the nature free from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm.

Furthermore, at the abodes of Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, they cultivated the four foundations of mindfulness; they cultivated the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.

Furthermore, at the abodes of Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, they trained in and dwelt within the noble truth of suffering; they trained in and dwelt within the noble truths of the origin, cessation, and the path.
Furthermore, at the abodes of Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, they cultivated the four dhyānas; they cultivated the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments;
they also, at the abodes of Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, cultivated the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities;
they also, at the abodes of Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, cultivated the liberation door of emptiness, and the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness.

Furthermore, in the presence of Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, they cultivated the Stage of Extreme Joy, the Stage of Purity, the Stage of Radiance, the Stage of Blazing Wisdom, the Stage of Difficult Victory, the Stage of Presence, the Stage of Far-Going, the Immovable Stage, the Stage of Excellent Intelligence, and the Stage of the Dharma Cloud;
furthermore, in the presence of Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, they cultivated the five eyes and the six supernormal powers;
furthermore, in the presence of Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, they cultivated the gates of samādhi and the gates of dhāraṇī.

Furthermore, at the abodes of Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, they cultivated the ten powers of a Buddha; they cultivated the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity, as well as the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
Furthermore, at the abodes of Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, they cultivated the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant dwelling in equanimity.
Furthermore, at the abodes of Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, they cultivated the contemplation of the twelve links of dependent origination in both forward and reverse order.
Furthermore, at the abodes of Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, they purified Buddha-fields and brought sentient beings to maturity;
at the abodes of Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, they cultivated the sublime supernatural powers of bodhisattvas;
and at the abodes of Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, they cultivated a perfect lifespan, learning how to turn the wheel of Dharma and upholding the True Dharma.

Furthermore, at the abodes of Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, they cultivated all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).

"These multitudes of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas also drew near to and served Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, and in the presence of those Buddhas, they inquired about the path of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, saying:
'How does a bodhisattva-mahāsattva abide in the Great Vehicle (*mahāyāna*)?'"
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the perfection of generosity, and practice the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom?

How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva train in and abide in internal emptiness, and train in and abide in external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature?

How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva train in and abide in suchness; how do they train in and abide in the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, the nature of equality, the nature free from birth, the fixedness of dharma, the stability of dharma, the limit of reality, the realm of empty space, and the inconceivable realm?

How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, and cultivate the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path?
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva train in and abide in the noble truth of suffering, and train in and abide in the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path?
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivate the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments?
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivate the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities?
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness, and the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness?

How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivate the stage of Extreme Joy, and cultivate the stage of Purity, the Radiant Stage, the Blazing Wisdom Stage, the Extremely Difficult to Conquer Stage, the Manifest Stage, the Far-Reaching Stage, the Immovable Stage, the Stage of Excellent Intelligence, and the Cloud of Dharma Stage?
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivate the five eyes and cultivate the six supernormal powers?
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivate the gates of samādhi and cultivate the gates of dhāraṇī?

How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivate the ten powers of a buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha?
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and cultivate the nature of constant abiding in equanimity?
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivate the contemplation of the twelve links of dependent origination in both forward and reverse order?
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva purify a buddha-field and bring sentient beings to maturity?
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivate the various sublime supernormal powers of a bodhisattva?
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivate a perfect lifespan?
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva learn to turn the great wheel of Dharma?
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva protect and uphold the true Dharma so that it may endure for a long time?
"How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivate all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*)?

'The Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, have explained these matters in successive order according to your inquiries. These assemblies of bodhisattva mahāsattvas, dwelling and training according to the Buddha’s instructions, have not attained the knowledge of all-knowledge even after blazing with diligence for immeasurable eons; how much less can you, who are now merely practicing and learning, realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment! "

"Subhūti! Although this bodhisattva mahāsattva hears these words, his mind remains unchanged; he is neither startled nor terrified, and he is without doubt or confusion. Instead, he becomes even more joyful and thinks to himself:

'This bhikṣu has greatly benefited me by skillfully explaining to me the dharmas that obstruct the path. Now that I know these obstructing dharmas, it is certain that I cannot realize the fruit of a stream-enterer, or the fruit of a once-returner, or the fruit of a non-returner, or the fruit of an arhat, or even solitary-buddha enlightenment; how much less could I possibly realize the knowledge of all modes! "

"Subhūti! At that time, when that evil Māra knows that the bodhisattva’s mind is not discouraged, undaunted, and free from doubt, he immediately manifests the forms of immeasurable bhikṣus at that very spot and says to the bodhisattva:

'All these bhikṣus sought unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment in the past; yet after practicing various difficult and painful austerities for immeasurable eons, they were unable to attain it. Now they have all regressed and abide in the fruit of arhatship, with all taints exhausted and having reached the end of suffering. How can you possibly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?'"
"Subhūti! Having seen and heard this, that bodhisattva mahāsattva immediately reflects:

'This must certainly be a wicked Māra who has manifested in the form of such a bhikṣu to disturb my mind. By teaching a counterfeit dharma that resembles the path but is actually an obstacle, he intends to ensure that the assembly of bodhisattva mahāsattvas never reaches the stage of perfection in the practice of the prajñāpāramitā, nor attains unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, but instead falls back into the level of a śrāvaka or a pratyekabuddha.'"
At that time, the Bodhisattva again had this thought:

"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of generosity, and practices the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom until they reach the stage of fulfillment, it is impossible that they would not attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in and dwells in internal emptiness, and trains in and dwells in external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, emptiness of self-characteristic, emptiness of common characteristic, emptiness of all phenomena, emptiness of the unapprehendable, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, and emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, until reaching the stage of perfection, it is impossible that they would not attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; such a thing could never occur.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in and dwells in suchness (*tathatā*), and trains in and dwells in the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), non-falsity (*avitathatā*), non-alteration (*ananyathābhāvatā*), equality (*samatā*), the nature of being free from birth (*aniyata-jāti*), the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*) until reaching the stage of perfection, it is impossible that they would not attain unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*).

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the four foundations of mindfulness (*smṛtyupasthāna*), cultivates the four right efforts (*samyakprahāṇa*), the four bases of power (*ṛddhipāda*), the five faculties (*indriya*), the five powers (*bala*), the seven factors of enlightenment (*bodhyaṅga*), and the eightfold noble path (*āryāṣṭāṅgamārga*) until reaching the stage of perfection, it is impossible that they would not attain unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in and dwells within the noble truth of suffering, and trains in and dwells within the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path until reaching the stage of perfection, it is impossible that they would not attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment;

if a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions until reaching the stage of perfection, it is impossible that they would not attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment;

if a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive absorptions, and the ten totalities until reaching the stage of perfection, it is impossible that they would not attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the gate of liberation of emptiness, and cultivates the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness until they reach the stage of perfection, it is impossible that they would not attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment;

if a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the Stage of Extreme Joy, the Stage of Purity, the Radiant Stage, the Stage of Blazing Wisdom, the Stage Difficult to Conquer, the Manifest Stage, the Far-Reaching Stage, the Immovable Stage, the Stage of Excellent Intelligence, and the Cloud of Dharma Stage until they reach the stage of perfection, it is impossible that they would not attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment;

if a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the five eyes and cultivates the six supernormal powers until they reach the stage of perfection, it is impossible that they would not attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the gateways of samādhi and the gateways of dhāraṇī until they reach the stage of perfection, yet does not attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment—such a thing is impossible;

if a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the ten powers of a buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha until they reach the stage of perfection, yet does not attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment—such a thing is impossible;

if a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant abiding in equanimity until they reach the stage of perfection, yet does not attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment—such a thing is impossible.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the contemplation of the twelve links of dependent origination in both forward and reverse order until reaching the stage of perfection, yet does not attain unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment—such a thing is impossible;

if a bodhisattva mahāsattva purifies buddha-fields and matures sentient beings until reaching the stage of perfection, yet does not attain unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment—such a thing is impossible;

if a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the various sublime supernormal powers of a bodhisattva until reaching the stage of perfection, yet does not attain unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment—such a thing is impossible.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the perfection of lifespan until reaching the stage of fulfillment, it is impossible that they would not attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment;

if a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in turning the wheel of Dharma and upholding the true Dharma until reaching the stage of fulfillment, it is impossible that they would not attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment;

if a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) until reaching the stage of fulfillment, it is impossible that they would not attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
"Subhūti! If one accomplishes such practices, characteristics, and signs, you should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti!"
If a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who has reached the stage of non-retrogression constantly practices the perfection of wisdom, they always maintain this thought:

"If a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva diligently trains according to the instructions of all Buddhas, they shall never be separated from the sublime conduct comprised by the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; they shall never be separated from the mental engagements associated with the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; they shall never be separated from the mental engagement associated with the knowledge of all aspects; and they shall always, through skillful means, exhort all sentient beings to diligently train in the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom."

This bodhisattva mahāsattva is certain not to regress from the perfection of generosity; they are certain not to regress from the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.

They are certain not to regress from internal emptiness; they are certain not to regress from external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

They are definitively non-retrogressive regarding suchness; they are definitively non-retrogressive regarding the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, non-illusory nature, unchanging nature, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm;

they are definitively non-retrogressive regarding the four foundations of mindfulness; they are definitively non-retrogressive regarding the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path;
they are definitively non-retrogressive regarding the noble truth of suffering; and they are definitively non-retrogressive regarding the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path.
They are certain not to regress from the four dhyānas; they are certain not to regress from the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments;
they are certain not to regress from the eight liberations; they are certain not to regress from the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities;
they are certain not to regress from the liberation door of emptiness; they are certain not to regress from the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness.

They are certain not to regress from the Stage of Extreme Joy; they are certain not to regress from the Stage of Purity, the Stage of Radiance, the Stage of Blazing Wisdom, the Stage of Difficult Victory, the Stage of Presence, the Stage of Far-Going, the Immovable Stage, the Stage of Good Intelligence, or the Stage of Dharma Clouds;
they are certain not to regress from the five eyes; they are certain not to regress from the six supernormal powers;
they are certain not to regress from the gateways of samādhi; and they are certain not to regress from the gateways of dhāraṇī.

They are certain not to regress from the ten powers of a Buddha; they are certain not to regress from the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
they are certain not to regress from the quality of non-forgetfulness; they are certain not to regress from the nature of constant abiding in equanimity;
they are certain not to regress from all-knowledge; and they are certain not to regress from the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects.
"He is certain not to fall back from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Subhūti! If one is endowed with such practices, tokens, and signs, you should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva in the stage of non-retrogression constantly practices the perfection of wisdom, they always maintain this thought:

'If a bodhisattva mahāsattva recognizes demonic activities and does not follow them; recognizes evil associates and does not follow their words; and recognizes sense objects and does not revolve according to them.'"

This bodhisattva mahāsattva is certain not to regress from the perfection of generosity; they are certain not to regress from the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom;
