they are certain not to regress from inner emptiness; and they are certain not to regress from outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

They are definitively non-retrogressive regarding suchness; they are definitively non-retrogressive regarding the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm;

they are definitively non-retrogressive regarding the four foundations of mindfulness; they are definitively non-retrogressive regarding the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path;
they are definitively non-retrogressive regarding the noble truth of suffering; and they are definitively non-retrogressive regarding the noble truths of the origin, cessation, and the path.
They are certain not to regress from the four dhyānas; they are certain not to regress from the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments;
they are certain not to regress from the eight liberations; they are certain not to regress from the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities;
they are certain not to regress from the liberation door of emptiness; and they are certain not to regress from the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness.

They are certain not to regress from the Stage of Extreme Joy; they are certain not to regress from the Stage of Purity, the Stage of Radiance, the Stage of Blazing Wisdom, the Stage of Difficult Victory, the Stage of Presence, the Stage of Far-Going, the Stage of Immovability, the Stage of Excellent Intelligence, or the Stage of the Cloud of Dharma.
They are certain not to regress from the five eyes; they are certain not to regress from the six supernormal powers;
they are certain not to regress from the gates of samādhi; and they are certain not to regress from the gates of dhāraṇī.

They are certain not to regress from the ten powers of a Buddha; they are certain not to regress from the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
they are certain not to regress from the quality of non-forgetfulness; they are certain not to regress from the nature of constant abiding in equanimity;
they are certain not to regress from all-knowledge; and they are certain not to regress from the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects.
They are certain not to fall back from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Subhūti! If they are endowed with such practices, characteristics, and signs, you should know that they are irreversible bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva who has reached the stage of non-retrogression hears the essential teachings spoken by the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, they will rejoice with deep resolve, respectfully accept them with faith, and skillfully understand their meaning and intent. Their minds will be as firm as a vajra, unshakable and incapable of being led astray or deprived. They will constantly and diligently practice the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, and they will also exhort sentient beings to diligently practice the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom."
“Subhūti! If one is endowed with such practices, characteristics, and signs, you should know that this is an irreversible bodhisattva mahāsattva.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
Regarding those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who abide in the stage of non-retrogression, by what kind of retrogression are they called ‘non-retrogressive’?
The Buddha said:

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is called ‘non-retrogressive’ because they have turned back from the perception of form; they are called ‘non-retrogressive’ because they have turned back from the perceptions of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness.”

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is called ‘non-retrogressive’ because they have turned back from the conceptualization of the sense-base of the eye; they are called ‘non-retrogressive’ because they have turned back from the conceptualizations of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.”

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is called ‘non-retrogressive’ because they have turned back from the perception of the sphere of form; they are called ‘non-retrogressive’ because they have turned back from the perceptions of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena.”

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is called ‘non-retrogressive’ because they have turned back from the perception of the eye-element; they are called ‘non-retrogressive’ because they have turned back from the perceptions of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements.”

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is called ‘non-retrogressive’ because they have turned back from the perception of the form realm; they are called ‘non-retrogressive’ because they have turned back from the perceptions of the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena.”

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is called ‘non-regressive’ because they have turned back from the notion of the eye-consciousness element; they are called ‘non-regressive’ because they have turned back from the notions of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements.”

"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is called 'non-retrogressive' because they have turned back from the perception of eye-contact; they are called 'non-retrogressive' because they have turned back from the perceptions of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact."

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is called ‘non-retrogressive’ because they have turned back from all perceptions and feelings arising with eye-contact as a condition; they are called ‘non-retrogressive’ because they have turned back from all perceptions and feelings arising with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions.”

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is called ‘non-retrogressive’ because they have turned back from the perception of the earth element; they are called ‘non-retrogressive’ because they have turned back from the perceptions of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements.”

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is called ‘non-retrogressive’ because they have turned back from the notion of ignorance; they are called ‘non-retrogressive’ because they have turned back from the notions of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age and death.”

"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is called 'non-retrogressive' because they have turned back from the perception of desire; they are called 'non-retrogressive' because they have turned back from the perception of hatred, the perception of delusion, and the perceptions of all evil views."

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Volume Three Hundred and Twenty-Six. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter Forty-Nine on Non-Retrogression, Section Three. "Subhūti!

This bodhisattva mahāsattva is called "non-retrogressive" because they do not conceive thoughts of retrogression regarding the perfection of generosity; they are called "non-retrogressive" because they do not conceive thoughts of retrogression regarding the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.

"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is called 'non-retrogressive' because they have turned back from the conceptualization of internal emptiness; they are called non-retrogressive because they have turned back from the conceptualizations of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature."

“Subhūti! Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva has turned back from the notion of *tathatā*, he is called ‘irreversible. Because he has turned back from the notions of the *dharmadhātu*, the *dharmatā*, the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm, he is called ‘irreversible.’”

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is called ‘non-retrogressive’ because they have turned back from the conceptualization of the four foundations of mindfulness; they are called ‘non-retrogressive’ because they have turned back from the conceptualization of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path.”

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is called ‘non-retrogressive’ because they have turned back from the conception of the noble truth of suffering; they are called ‘non-retrogressive’ because they have turned back from the conceptions of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path.”

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is called ‘non-retrogressive’ because they have turned back from the conceptualization of the four dhyānas; they are called ‘non-retrogressive’ because they have turned back from the conceptualization of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments.”

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is called ‘non-retrogressive’ because he turns away from the notion of the eight liberations; he is called ‘non-retrogressive’ because he turns away from the notion of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases.”

"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is called 'non-retrogressive' because he has turned back from the conceptualization of the gate of liberation of emptiness; he is called 'non-retrogressive' because he has turned back from the conceptualizations of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness."

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is called ‘non-retrogressive’ because they have turned back from the conceptualization of the Stage of Extreme Joy; they are called ‘non-retrogressive’ because they have turned back from the conceptualizations of the Stage of Purity, the Stage of Radiance, the Stage of Blazing Wisdom, the Stage of Supreme Difficulty to Conquer, the Stage of Presence, the Stage of Far-Going, the Immovable Stage, the Stage of Excellent Intelligence, and the Stage of the Dharma Cloud.”

"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is called 'non-retrogressive' because they have turned back from the notion of the five eyes; they are called 'non-retrogressive' because they have turned back from the notion of the six supernormal powers."

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is called ‘non-retrogressive’ because they have turned back from the conceptualization of the gateways to samādhi; they are called ‘non-retrogressive’ because they have turned back from the conceptualization of the gateways to dhāraṇī.”

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is called ‘non-retrogressive’ because they have turned back from the conceptualization of the ten powers of a buddha; they are called ‘non-retrogressive’ because they have turned back from the conceptualization of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha.”

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is called ‘non-retrogressive’ because he has turned back from the notion of the quality of non-forgetfulness; he is called ‘non-retrogressive’ because he has turned back from the notion of the state of constant equanimity.”

"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is called 'non-retrogressive' because he turns back from the notion of the fruit of a stream-enterer; he is called 'non-retrogressive' because he turns back from the notions of the fruit of a once-returner, a non-returner, and an arhat."
“Subhūti! Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva has turned back from the notion of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, he is called ‘non-retrogressive. Subhūti!”

This bodhisattva mahāsattva is called "non-retrogressive" because they have turned back from the notion of omniscience; they are called "non-retrogressive" because they have turned back from the notions of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects.

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is called ‘non-retrogressive’ because he has turned back from the notion of an ordinary person; he is called ‘non-retrogressive’ because he has turned back from the notions of a śrāvaka, a pratyekabuddha, a bodhisattva, and a tathāgata.”

"Why is this so? Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates all phenomena as empty of their own characteristics (*svalakṣaṇa-śūnya*). Having entered the bodhisattva’s state of certainty (*samyaktva-niyāma*), they do not perceive even the slightest phenomenon that can be apprehended; because it cannot be apprehended, there is no volitional construction (*abhisamskāra*); because there is no volitional construction, there is ultimate non-arising (*atyantānutpāda*); because there is ultimate non-arising, it is called the 'patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena' (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*); and by attaining such patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena, one is called an irreversible bodhisattva mahāsattva."
“Subhūti! If one is endowed with such practices, characteristics, and signs, know that this is an irreversible bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti!”
If a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who has reached the stage of non-retrogression should encounter an evil Māra who, for the purpose of causing distress and ruin, says to him:

"Unsurpassed Bodhi is equal to space; its self-nature and self-characteristics are ultimately empty and utterly non-existent. The self-nature and self-characteristics of all dharmas are likewise equal to space; within the ultimate emptiness of self-nature and self-characteristics, there is not a single dharma that can be called the 'realizer,' nor a single dharma that can be called the 'realized. Neither the locus of realization, the time of realization, nor that by which one realizes can be apprehended."

Since the nature and characteristics of all phenomena are entirely empty and equal to space, why do you undergo such toil and hardship in vain to seek the realization of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?

"All those bodhisattvas you previously heard of who were to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment—these are all the words of Māra and not the true words of the Buddha. You should abandon your vow for great enlightenment; do not, throughout the long night, pointlessly undergo hardships and toil for yourselves while seeking to benefit and bring happiness to all sentient beings, for though you practice various difficult and painful austerities desiring enlightenment, you will ultimately never attain it."
"Subhūti! When that bodhisattva mahāsattva hears those words, he is able to examine them carefully, thinking:

'This is the work of Māra, intended to cause me to regress and destroy the mind of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment that I have generated; I must not now believe or accept what he says.'"

Although all phenomena are equal to space, their intrinsic nature and specific characteristics being ultimately empty, sentient beings wander through the long night of birth and death, unknowing, unseeing, uncomprehending, and unaware; they fall into perversion and negligence, undergoing intense suffering. I shall don the great armor of merit—whose nature and characteristics are as empty as the great void—and swiftly proceed toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, so that I may teach the Dharma to all sentient beings according to their needs, causing them to be liberated from the great suffering of birth and death, and to attain the fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, the fruit of arhatship, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, or even unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

"Subhūti! From the moment they first resolve their mind [on awakening], these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas hear this Dharma; their minds are firm, unshakable, and irreversible. Relying upon this firm, unshakable, and irreversible mind, they constantly and correctly practice the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom."

By virtue of these six kinds of partial accomplishments, having already entered the bodhisattva's state of correctness and departure from birth (*samyaktva-niyāma*), they further correctly practice the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; through this, they enter the stage of non-retrogression (*avaivartika*).
Therefore, although Māra may employ various deceptive expedients, he cannot cause the bodhisattva’s great resolve for enlightenment to regress.
"Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [It is thus.]”
"If one accomplishes such practices, characteristics, and signs, you should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"Is this bodhisattva mahāsattva called 'non-retrogressive' because he is non-retrogressive, or is he called 'non-retrogressive' because he is retrogressive?
The Buddha said, "Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [He is called so] because he is non-retrogressive."
"This Bodhisattva Mahāsattva is called 'non-retrogressive' because he does not retrogress, yet he is also called 'non-retrogressive' because he does retrogress.
"World-Honored One!"
How is it that this bodhisattva-mahāsattva is called "non-retrogressive" by virtue of being non-retrogressive?
And how is it that he is also called "non-retrogressive" by virtue of being retrogressive?

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva has transcended the stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas and shall no longer fall back into those two stages; for this reason, he is called ‘non-retrogressive’ because he does not retrogress.

Furthermore, this bodhisattva mahāsattva remains far removed from the stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas and definitively abandons those two stages; for this reason, he is called ‘non-retrogressive’ by virtue of his retrogression [from them].”
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva at the stage of non-retrogression wishes to enter the first dhyāna, he is able to enter it at will; if he wishes to enter the second, third, or fourth dhyānas, he is likewise able to enter them at will.

If he wishes to enter the immeasurable state of loving-kindness (*maitrī*), he is able to enter it at will; if he wishes to enter the immeasurable states of compassion (*karuṇā*), sympathetic joy (*muditā*), or equanimity (*upekṣā*), he is likewise able to enter them at will."

If he wishes to enter the meditative absorption of the sphere of infinite space, he can enter it at will; if he wishes to enter the meditative absorptions of the sphere of infinite consciousness, the sphere of nothingness, or the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, he can likewise enter them at will.

If he wishes to give rise to the four foundations of mindfulness, he can give rise to them at will; if he wishes to give rise to the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path, he can likewise give rise to them at will.

If he wishes to give rise to the first liberation, he can give rise to it at will; if he wishes to give rise to the second liberation up to the eighth liberation, he can likewise give rise to them at will.

If he wishes to give rise to the first sphere of mastery (*abhibhvāyatana*), he can do so at will; if he wishes to give rise to the second sphere of mastery up to the eighth, he can likewise do so at will.

If he wishes to enter the first dhyāna concentration, he can do so at will; if he wishes to enter the second dhyāna concentration up to the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling (*saṃjñāvedayitanirodhasamāpatti*), he can likewise do so at will.
If he wishes to give rise to the first universal base (*kṛtsnāyatana*), he can do so at will; if he wishes to give rise to the second universal base up to the tenth, he can likewise do so at will.
If they wish to give rise to the liberation door of emptiness, they can do so at will; if they wish to give rise to the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness, they can also do so at will;
and if they wish to manifest the five supernormal powers, they can manifest them at will.

"Subhūti! Although this bodhisattva mahāsattva enters the first dhyāna, he does not experience the fruit of the first dhyāna; although he enters the second, third, and fourth dhyānas, he does not experience the fruits of the second, third, and fourth dhyānas;

although he enters the immeasurable state of loving-kindness (*maitrī*), he does not experience the fruit of the immeasurable state of loving-kindness; and although he enters the immeasurable states of compassion (*karuṇā*), sympathetic joy (*muditā*), and equanimity (*upekṣā*), he does not experience the fruits of the immeasurable states of compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity."

Although they enter the meditative absorption of the sphere of infinite space, they do not experience the fruit of the sphere of infinite space; although they enter the meditative absorptions of the sphere of infinite consciousness, the sphere of nothingness, and the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, they do not experience the fruits of the sphere of infinite consciousness, the sphere of nothingness, or the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.

Although they give rise to the four foundations of mindfulness, they do not experience the fruit of the four foundations of mindfulness; although they give rise to the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path, they do not experience the fruits of the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path.

Although they give rise to the first liberation, they do not experience the fruit of the first liberation; although they give rise to the second liberation up to the eighth liberation, they do not experience the fruits of the second liberation up to the eighth liberation.

Although they give rise to the first sphere of mastery (*abhibhvāyatana*), they do not experience the fruit of the first sphere of mastery; although they give rise to the second sphere of mastery up to the eighth sphere of mastery, they do not experience the fruit of the second sphere of mastery up to the eighth sphere of mastery.

Although they enter the first dhyāna concentration, they do not experience the fruit of the first dhyāna concentration; although they enter the second dhyāna concentration up to the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling (*saṃjñāvedayitanirodhasamāpatti*), they do not experience the fruit of the second dhyāna concentration up to the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling.

Although they give rise to the first universal base (*kṛtsnāyatana*), they do not experience the fruit of the first universal base; although they give rise to the second universal base up to the tenth universal base, they do not experience the fruit of the second universal base up to the tenth universal base.

Although they give rise to the liberation door of emptiness, they do not experience the fruit of the liberation door of emptiness; although they give rise to the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness, they do not experience the fruits of the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness;
and although they manifest the five supernormal powers, they do not experience the fruits of the five supernormal powers.

“Subhūti! By virtue of these causes and conditions, this bodhisattva mahāsattva is not reborn through the power of the dhyānas, the immeasurables, the attainments, or other meritorious qualities; nor does he realize the fruit of a stream-enterer, or the fruit of a once-returner, or the fruit of a non-returner, or the fruit of an arhat, or the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha.”

“Subhūti! Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas desire to bring benefit and happiness to all sentient beings, they assume whatever bodies are appropriate to be assumed according to their wishes; indeed, they are able to assume them exactly as they have vowed.”
“Subhūti! If one is endowed with such practices, characteristics, and signs, you should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti!”

If a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva in the stage of non-retrogression accomplishes the mental orientation toward unsurpassed enlightenment, they are never separated from the great bodhicitta; they do not prize form, nor do they prize feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness;
they do not prize the sense-base of the eye, nor do they prize the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind;
they do not prize the sense-base of forms, nor do they prize the sense-bases of sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, or mental phenomena.
They do not prize the eye-element; they do not prize the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-element.
They do not prize the form-element; they do not prize the sound-, odor-, taste-, tangible-, or mental-object-element.
They do not prize the eye-consciousness-element; they do not prize the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-consciousness-element.
One does not prize eye-contact; one does not prize ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact.
One does not prize the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition; one does not prize the various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact as condition.
One does not prize the earth element; one does not prize the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements.
They do not value the nature of conditions or dependent origination;
they do not value the primary marks or the secondary characteristics;

they do not value phenomena with form or without form; they do not value phenomena that are visible or invisible; they do not value phenomena that are resistant or non-resistant; they do not value phenomena that are outflowing or non-outflowing; they do not value phenomena that are conditioned or unconditioned; they do not value mundane or supramundane phenomena.
They do not value themselves; they do not value sentient beings, living souls, creatures, nourishers, persons, individuals, mind-born ones, sons of the Manu, agents, experiencers, knowers, or seers;
they do not value their retinues or their followers;
they do not value the perfection of generosity, nor do they value the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom.
They do not value the ten paths of wholesome action;
they do not value the four dhyānas, nor do they value the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments;
they do not value the five supernormal powers.

They do not hold the four foundations of mindfulness in high esteem; they do not hold the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path in high esteem.
They do not hold the eight liberations in high esteem; they do not hold the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities in high esteem.
They do not hold the gate of liberation of emptiness in high esteem; they do not hold the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness in high esteem.
They do not hold the noble truth of suffering in high esteem, nor do they hold the noble truths of its origin, its cessation, and the path in high esteem;

they do not hold internal emptiness in high esteem, nor do they hold external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

They do not prize *tathatā* (suchness), nor do they prize the *dharmadhātu* (dharma-realm), the *dharmatā* (dharma-nature), the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmasthiti*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of empty space, or the inconceivable realm;

they do not prize the stage of extreme joy (*pramuditā-bhūmi*), nor do they prize the stage of freedom from stain (*vimalā-bhūmi*), the stage of radiant light (*prabhākārī-bhūmi*), the stage of flaming wisdom (*arciṣmatī-bhūmi*), the stage of extreme difficulty to conquer (*sudurjayā-bhūmi*), the stage of presence (*abhimukhī-bhūmi*), the stage of far-reaching progress (*dūraṅgamā-bhūmi*), the immovable stage (*acalā-bhūmi*), the stage of excellent wisdom (*sādhumatī-bhūmi*), or the stage of the cloud of dharma (*dharmameghā-bhūmi*);
they do not prize the five eyes, nor do they prize the six supernormal powers (*ṣaḍ-abhijñā*).

They do not value the ten powers of a Buddha; they do not value the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
they do not value the quality of non-forgetfulness, nor do they value the state of constant dwelling in equanimity; they do not value śrāvakas, nor pratyekabuddhas, nor bodhisattvas, nor tathāgatas.
They do not prize the fruit of stream-entry; they do not prize the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, or arhatship;
they do not prize pratyekabuddha-enlightenment;
they do not prize all-knowledge, nor the knowledge of the aspects of the path, nor the knowledge of all aspects.
They do not value *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*;
they do not value the adornment and purification of Buddha-fields, nor do they value the maturation of sentient beings;
they do not value frequently beholding the Buddhas.
They do not value the planting of various roots of goodness.
Why is this? "Subhūti!..."

This bodhisattva mahāsattva realizes that all dharmas are equal to space; their intrinsic nature and intrinsic characteristics are ultimately empty and utterly non-existent. He does not perceive any dharma that can be regarded as precious, nor can he find the producer, the produced, the time of production, the place of production, or the cause by which it is produced—all of these are unobtainable.
Why is this so? Subhūti!
Because all these dharmas are equal to space; their nature and characteristics are all empty, having the meaning of non-arising.

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes the mental attention of unsurpassed enlightenment and is never separated from the great mind of enlightenment. Whether moving about or entering and exiting, whether lifting or lowering the feet, his mind is never distracted during the four postures of standing, walking, sitting, and lying down. In all his movements and activities, he abides in right mindfulness.”
“Subhūti! If one is endowed with such practices, characteristics, and signs, know that this is an irreversible bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti!”

If a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva at the stage of non-retrogression, desiring to benefit all sentient beings, manifests living as a householder; through skillful means (*upāya-kauśalya*), although he appears to accept the five objects of sensual pleasure, he does not give rise to attachment toward them. All this is for the sake of providing for sentient beings: that is to say, to those who need food he gives food; to those who need drink he gives drink; to those who need clothing he gives clothing; to those who need bedding he gives bedding; to those who need medicine he gives medicine; to those who need a dwelling he gives a dwelling; to those who need wealth and resources he gives wealth and resources. He gives whatever is requested by sentient beings, causing their wishes and intentions to be entirely fulfilled.

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva personally practices the perfection of giving and also encourages others to practice the perfection of giving; he constantly delights in praising the dharma of practicing the perfection of giving and joyfully extols those who practice the perfection of giving.

He personally practices the perfection of ethical discipline and also encourages others to practice the perfection of ethical discipline; he constantly delights in praising the dharma of practicing the perfection of ethical discipline and joyfully extols those who practice the perfection of ethical discipline.”

They personally practice the perfection of patience and also encourage others to practice the perfection of patience; they constantly delight in praising the dharma of practicing the perfection of patience and joyfully extol those who practice the perfection of patience.

They personally practice the perfection of diligence and also encourage others to practice the perfection of diligence; they constantly delight in praising the dharma of practicing the perfection of diligence and joyfully extol those who practice the perfection of diligence.

They personally practice the perfection of meditative concentration and also encourage others to practice the perfection of meditative concentration; they constantly delight in praising the dharma of practicing the perfection of meditative concentration and joyfully extol those who practice the perfection of meditative concentration.

They practice the perfection of wisdom themselves and also encourage others to practice the perfection of wisdom; they constantly delight in praising the dharma of practicing the perfection of wisdom, and they joyfully extol those who practice the perfection of wisdom.

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva, while dwelling in the life of a householder, uses the power of supernormal knowledges or the power of great vows to gather precious wealth sufficient to fill Jambudvīpa, which he then offers as sustenance to the Triple Gem of Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha, and bestows upon all destitute sentient beings;

or, by the power of supernormal knowledges or the power of great vows, he gathers precious wealth sufficient to fill the four great continents, which he then offers as sustenance to the Triple Gem of Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha, and bestows upon all destitute sentient beings.”

By the power of supernormal knowledges or the power of great vows, they gather precious wealth filling a small thousand-world system, which they offer to the Triple Gem of Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha, and bestow upon all destitute sentient beings;

by the power of supernormal knowledges or the power of great vows, they gather precious wealth filling a medium thousand-world system, which they offer to the Triple Gem of Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha, and bestow upon all destitute sentient beings;

by the power of supernormal knowledges or the power of great vows, they gather precious wealth filling a trichiliocosm, which they offer to the Triple Gem of Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha, and bestow upon all destitute sentient beings.

“Subhūti! Although these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas appear to dwell in the household life, they constantly cultivate pure conduct and never enjoy the objects of exquisite sensual desire. Although they appear to acquire various kinds of precious wealth, they do not give rise to stained attachment toward them.
Furthermore, when acquiring the requisites for sensual pleasures and precious wealth, they never oppress sentient beings, causing them to experience sorrow or suffering.”
“Subhūti! If one is endowed with such practices, characteristics, and signs, you should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti!”
If a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who is in the stage of non-retrogression has a Vajradhara Yakṣa lord constantly following at his left and right to secretly provide protection, he will always think:

"This Bodhisattva Mahāsattva shall before long realize unsurpassed bodhi; may I constantly follow him and secretly protect him until unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening. Furthermore, the assembly of five Vajradhara Yakṣas shall also follow and protect him without ever abandoning him for a moment, so that humans, non-humans, and others cannot cause him harm. Nor can any among the devas, Māras, Brahmās, or other worldly beings use any means to destroy the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening mind he has resolved upon."

"By virtue of these causes and conditions, these bodhisattvas remain serene in body and mind, forever free from disturbance, until they attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. Subhūti!"
If one accomplishes such practices, characteristics, and signs, you should know that this is an irreversible Bodhisattva Mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva in the stage of non-retrogression possesses the five mundane faculties without ever lacking or diminishing them— namely, the faculty of the eye, the faculty of the ear, the faculty of the nose, the faculty of the tongue, and the faculty of the body—

and likewise possesses the five supramundane faculties without lacking or diminishing them— namely, the faculty of faith, the faculty of diligence, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, and the faculty of wisdom.

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva’s physical limbs are perfected and adorned with the marks and signs, and his mental qualities increase in every thought-moment until he reaches unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”
“Subhūti! If one is endowed with such practices, characteristics, and signs, you should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti!”
"If a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who has reached the stage of non-retrogression is always a superior person and never an inferior one," at that time,
the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying,
"World-Honored One!"
"Why is it said that this bodhisattva mahāsattva is always an upper-rank person and never a lower-rank person?
The Buddha said, "Suvīra!..."

For this bodhisattva mahāsattva, all afflictions no longer manifest; from moment to moment their merits increase until they reach unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment. At all times their mind remains undistracted; therefore, I say that this bodhisattva mahāsattva is always a superior person, not an inferior one.
“Subhūti! If one is endowed with such practices, characteristics, and signs, you should know that this is an irreversible bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti!”
If a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva in the stage of non-retrogression accomplishes the mental application for unsurpassed enlightenment and never departs from the great bodhicitta,
then for the sake of a pure livelihood, he does not practice incantations, medicine, divination,
or other forms of wrong livelihood; nor does he, for the sake of fame or profit, cast spells upon spirits and ghosts to cause them to possess men or women.
He does not inquire about their fortune or misfortune; nor does he perform incantations or prohibitions for men, women, the elderly, the young, animals, or spirits to manifest rare wonders.
He does not practice physiognomy to predict the length of one's lifespan, wealth and status, or various matters concerning sons, daughters, good and evil.
Nor does he make prophetic declarations regarding cold or heat, abundance or scarcity, auspiciousness or misfortune, or favorable and unfavorable circumstances that would cause confusion.

Regarding sentient beings, he does not practice incantations or the compounding of decoctions, nor does he employ heterodox methods to treat illnesses or cultivate intimacy with persons of high status;
he does not even allow his mind to be stained by observing men and women laughing or conversing, much less engage in any other such matters!
Why is this? Subhūti!

This bodhisattva mahāsattva knows that the self-characteristics of all phenomena are empty; within the emptiness of self-characteristics, they do not perceive any marks. Because they do not perceive marks, they remain far removed from various wrong livelihoods, incantations, medical arts, and divination, seeking only unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment to ultimately bring benefit and happiness to all classes of sentient beings.
"Subhūti! If one is endowed with such practices, characteristics, and signs, you should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti!"
If a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who is in the stage of non-retrogression attains skillfulness in the various worldly literatures and arts, he does not become attached to them.
Why is this so? Subhūti!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva realizes that all phenomena are ultimately empty; within ultimate emptiness, all worldly literature and arts are unfindable.
Furthermore, Subhūti, all worldly literature and arts are comprised within frivolous speech and wrong livelihood; therefore, the bodhisattva knows them but does not practice them. Subhūti!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva, although well-versed in the secular and heterodox treatises, does not delight in or cling to them.
Why is this? Subhūti!
This bodhisattva-mahāsattva realizes that the nature and characteristics of all phenomena are entirely empty; within this emptiness, no books or treatises can be apprehended.

Furthermore, the principles and matters taught in the secular and non-Buddhist books and treatises often involve increase or decrease [of the truth] and do not accord with the bodhisattva path. They are all categorized as frivolous proliferation and impure speech; therefore, the bodhisattva knows them but does not delight in them.
“Subhūti! If one is endowed with such practices, characteristics, and signs, you should know that this is an irreversible bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti!”

Furthermore, there are other practices, characteristics, and signs of the irreversible bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; I shall analyze and explain them for you. You should listen attentively and reflect upon them thoroughly.
Subhūti replied, “Indeed! I pray that you will speak.”
"We now intend to listen with focused attention.
The Buddha said,
"Suvikrāntavikrāmin!"

When a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva in the stage of non-retrogression practices the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they penetrate the fact that all phenomena are utterly non-existent. They never depart from the mind of great enlightenment (*mahābodhicitta*), nor do they delight in examining or discoursing upon the aggregate of form (*rūpaskandha*), nor do they delight in examining or discoursing upon the aggregates of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness;

they do not delight in examining or discoursing upon the sense base of the eye (*cakṣurāyatana*), nor do they delight in examining or discoursing upon the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind;

they do not delight in examining or discoursing upon the sense base of visible forms (*rūpāyatana*), nor do they delight in examining or discoursing upon the sense bases of sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, or mental objects (*dharmāyatana*).
They do not delight in examining or discoursing upon the eye-element; they do not delight in examining or discoursing upon the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-element.
They do not delight in examining or discoursing upon the form-element; they do not delight in examining or discoursing upon the sound-, odor-, taste-, tangible-, or mental-object-element.

They do not delight in examining or discoursing upon the eye-consciousness-element; they do not delight in examining or discoursing upon the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-consciousness-element.
They do not delight in examining or discussing eye-contact; they do not delight in examining or discussing ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact.

They do not delight in examining or discussing the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition; they do not delight in examining or discussing the various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact as condition.
They do not delight in examining or discussing the earth element; they do not delight in examining or discussing the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements.

One does not delight in examining discourses on ignorance, nor does one delight in examining discourses on volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, or aging-and-death.
Why is this? Subhūti!

It is because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have already well reflected upon and thoroughly realized the principle of ultimate emptiness regarding the aggregates, bases, elements, conditions, and dependent origination.
“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not delight in observing or discussing matters of statecraft. Why is that?

"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells well in the emptiness of phenomena (dharma-śūnyatā), because they do not perceive even the slightest phenomenon as having the characteristics of being superior or inferior, noble or base. Subhūti!"
This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not delight in observing or discussing matters concerning thieves.
Why is this? Subhūti!

This bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in the emptiness of self-characteristics (*svalakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*), because they do not perceive even the slightest phenomenon as having the characteristics of gain or loss, or of giving or taking away. "Subhūti!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not delight in observing or discussing matters of military affairs."
Why is this? Subhūti!

Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas abide in the emptiness of intrinsic nature (prakṛti-śūnyatā) and do not perceive any signs of increase or decrease, or of gathering or dispersal, among all phenomena.
“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not delight in observing or discussing matters of contention. Why is that?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells securely in suchness, because he does not perceive even the slightest dharma as having the characteristics of strength or weakness, or of attachment and aversion.
Suvikrāntavikrāmin!”
This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not delight in observing or discoursing upon men and women.
Why is that? Subhūti!

This bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in the emptiness of all phenomena; because they do not perceive even the slightest phenomenon as having the characteristics of being beautiful or ugly, or of being objects of love or hatred.
"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not delight in observing or discoursing upon villages."
Why is this? Subhūti!

Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas abide in the true nature of phenomena (dharmatā), and do not perceive even the slightest phenomenon as having the characteristics of increase or decrease, or of gathering or dispersing.
"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not delight in observing or discoursing upon cities. Why is that?

"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in the realm of empty space, because they do not perceive any phenomena as having the characteristics of victory or defeat, or being good or bad. Subhūti!"
This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not delight in observing or discoursing upon realms.
Why is this? Subhūti!

This bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells securely in the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), because he does not perceive any phenomena as having the characteristics of belonging or not belonging to this or that.
"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not delight in examining or discoursing upon various signs."
Why is this? Subhūti!
Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas abide in the signless and do not perceive any signs of increase, decrease, or differentiation among all phenomena.

"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not delight in examining or discoursing upon the notions of a self, a sentient being, a life-force, a living being, a nourisher, a spirit, a person, a soul, a youth, an agent, an experiencer, a knower, or a viewer."
Why is this? Subhūti!
Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas abide in ultimate emptiness and do not perceive any distinguishing marks of existence or non-existence regarding anything from the self up to the knower.

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not delight in examining or discussing such worldly matters as these; rather, he delights only in examining and discussing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).”
Why is this? Subhūti!
Because the profound perfection of wisdom is free from all marks and is able to realize unsurpassed, great bodhi.

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is never separated from the mental engagement associated with the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvajñajñāna*). He practices the perfection of generosity (*dānapāramitā*) while remaining free from stinginess and greed; he practices the perfection of ethical discipline (*śīlapāramitā*) while remaining free from immoral conduct; he practices the perfection of patience (*kṣāntipāramitā*) while remaining free from anger and contention; he practices the perfection of diligence (*vīryapāramitā*) while remaining free from laziness; he practices the perfection of meditative concentration (*dhyānapāramitā*) while remaining free from distraction; and he practices the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) while remaining free from delusion.”

“Subhūti! Although this bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in the emptiness of all phenomena, he delights in the true Dharma and does not delight in what is not the Dharma; although he dwells in the emptiness of the unapprehendable, he constantly praises the indestructible nature of reality (dharmatā) and benefits sentient beings; although he dwells in suchness (tathatā) and the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), he loves virtuous friends and does not delight in evil friends.”
Regarding "virtuous friends," this refers to the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, and the assembly of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.

Furthermore, those belonging to the vehicles of the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas who are able to skillfully teach and establish sentient beings, leading them toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, are also called virtuous friends.

“Subhūti! For the sake of hearing the Dharma, these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas always delight in seeing the Buddhas. If they hear that a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha is currently expounding the sublime Dharma in another world-system, they immediately take rebirth in that realm through the power of their vows, where they reverently make offerings and listen to the sublime Dharma.”

“Subhūti! Whether by day or by night, this bodhisattva mahāsattva is never apart from the mental attention of mindfulness of the Buddha, and is never apart from the mental attention of listening to the Dharma.”

By virtue of these causes and conditions, wherever there are Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas currently preaching the sublime Dharma in various lands, he will travel there to take birth by means of the power of his vows, or travel there to listen to the Dharma by means of supernormal powers.

By reason of these causes and conditions, these bodhisattvas, in every place where they are born, are never separated from the Buddha and constantly hear the true Dharma without interruption or cessation. "Subhūti!..."

Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly seeks the benefit and happiness of all sentient beings, although he is able to manifest the profound meditative absorptions of the dhyānas and the formless realms, he skillfully employs expedient means to give rise to a mind belonging to the desire realm, teaching sentient beings the ten paths of wholesome action; furthermore, by the power of his vows, he manifests birth in the desire realm within buddha-fields.
“Subhūti! If one is endowed with such practices, characteristics, and signs, you should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti!”

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva in the stage of non-retrogression constantly practices the perfection of generosity, and constantly practices the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly dwells in internal emptiness; he constantly dwells in external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of self-nature, and the emptiness of the self-nature of non-existence.”

"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly abides in true thusness; he constantly abides in the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, non-alteration, equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm."

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly cultivates the four foundations of mindfulness; he constantly cultivates the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path.”
“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly abides in the noble truth of suffering, and constantly abides in the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path. Subhūti!”
This bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly cultivates the four dhyānas, and constantly cultivates the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments. "Subhūti!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly cultivates the eight liberations, and constantly cultivates the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities."

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly cultivates the gate of liberation that is emptiness, and constantly cultivates the gates of liberation that are signlessness and wishlessness. Subhūti!”
This bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly cultivates the five eyes and constantly cultivates the six supernormal powers. "Subhūti!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly cultivates the gateways of samādhi and constantly cultivates the gateways of dhāraṇī."

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly cultivates the ten powers of a buddha; he constantly cultivates the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha.”

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly cultivates all-knowledge (sarvajñā), constantly cultivates the knowledge of the aspects of the path (mārgākārajñatā), and constantly cultivates the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā). Subhūti!”
This bodhisattva mahāsattva always remains free from doubt regarding their own stage, never entertaining such thoughts as:
"I am non-retrogressive" or "I am not non-retrogressive."
Why is this? Subhūti!

This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive even the slightest dharma that could be said to regress from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, nor does he perceive even the slightest dharma that could be said not to regress from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva has no confusion or doubt regarding the dharmas of his own stage. Why is this?
"Subhūti! This is because that bodhisattva mahāsattva has already thoroughly understood and fully realized the dharmas of his own stage. Subhūti!"
Just as a stream-enterer abiding in the fruit of stream-entry has no confusion or doubt regarding the dharmas of their own fruit;
so too, a once-returner, a non-returner, an arhat, and a pratyekabuddha, each abiding in their respective fruits, have likewise no confusion or doubt regarding the dharmas of their own fruits.

In the same way, this bodhisattva mahāsattva also directly knows and directly sees, without confusion or doubt, all the dharmas subsumed within the stage of non-retrogression in which he himself abides.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva who is non-retrogressive dwells in this stage, they purify buddha-fields, mature sentient beings, and cultivate all manner of meritorious qualities. Should any demonic activities arise, they are immediately able to recognize them; they do not succumb to the power of such demonic activities, but are well able to suppress and destroy various demonic deeds so that they do not obstruct the meritorious qualities they are cultivating.”

"Subhūti! For example, when one has committed an act of immediate retribution (*ānantarya-karman*), that mind of immediacy constantly follows them, such that even until the end of life it cannot be abandoned."
Why is this? Subhūti!

Because the powerful influence of the entanglements that give rise to the immediate karmic offenses (ānantarya-karma) constantly persists; it cannot be subdued even until the end of one’s life, and no other state of mind can obstruct it.

Subhūti! It is just the same for a bodhisattva mahāsattva in this stage of non-retrogression: abiding securely in their own ground, their mind is unmoving and free from conceptual discrimination, such that neither the gods, humans, nor asuras of the world can cause them to waver.

Why is this? Because the mind of this bodhisattva mahāsattva is firm and steadfast; he has transcended all worlds—including gods, humans, māras, brahmās, and asuras—and has entered the bodhisattva’s state of rightness and departure from birth (*samyaktva-niyāma*), abiding on the stage of non-retrogression. Having attained the bodhisattva’s sublime supernormal powers, he brings sentient beings to maturity and purifies buddha-fields. Traveling from one buddha-field to another, he makes offerings, pays homage, respects, and praises the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, and listens to the True Dharma. In the presence of these Buddhas, he plants roots of goodness and inquires about the meaning of the dharmas studied by bodhisattvas.

“Subhūti! When these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dwell securely in their own stage, they are able to recognize as soon as demonic activities arise; they never follow after such demonic activities, but through the power of skillful means, they gather all demonic activities and place them within the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), thereby eliminating them through expedient means. Thus, regarding the dharmas of their own stage, they have neither confusion nor doubt.”
Why is this? Subhūti!

This bodhisattva mahāsattva knows that all dharmas enter the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi); he penetrates the limit of reality as being neither one nor many, and within the limit of reality, he makes no conceptual distinctions.
Because they are without confusion or doubt regarding the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), they likewise have no hesitation regarding the dharmas of their own stage. "Subhūti!
Even if these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas were to take rebirth again, they would never again regress from the limit of reality toward the level of a śrāvaka or a pratyekabuddha."
Why is this? Subhūti!

This bodhisattva mahāsattva knows that the self-characteristics of all phenomena are empty; within this emptiness, they do not perceive any phenomenon that arises or ceases, or that is defiled or purified.
“Subhūti! Even when this bodhisattva mahāsattva undergoes a change of existence, he does not doubt whether he will attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening or not.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva penetrates that all phenomena are empty of their own characteristics, and this itself is unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells securely in his own stage and does not rely on external conditions; no one can destroy him regarding the dharmas of his own stage. Why is this?
"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva has accomplished unshakable and non-retrogressive wisdom, such that no adverse conditions can cause them to waver. Subhūti!"
If one accomplishes such practices, characteristics, and signs, you should know that this is an irreversible bodhisattva mahāsattva.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
If a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who has reached the stage of non-retrogression should encounter an evil Māra appearing in the form of a Buddha and coming to him, saying:
"You should now seek the fruit of Arhatship, exhaust all outflows, and realize Parinirvāṇa."

"You have not yet been worthy of receiving the prediction of great enlightenment (*mahābodhi*), nor have you yet realized the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*). You do not yet possess the practices, marks, and signs of the stage of non-retrogression; therefore, the Tathāgata should not grant you the prediction of unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment. Only when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva is fully endowed with the practices, marks, and signs of the stage of non-retrogression can they receive from the Buddha the prediction of unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment."

"Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva at this stage of non-retrogression hears those words, his mind remains unaltered; he is not startled, not terrified, does not retreat, and does not sink into despondency."
"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva should personally realize and know:
'In the presence of the Tathāgatas of the past, I have certainly already received the prediction of great enlightenment.'"

Why is this? Because a bodhisattva who has accomplished such supreme dharmas will certainly receive the prediction of enlightenment from all Buddhas; since I have already accomplished such supreme dharmas, why would the Buddhas not grant me their prediction?
"Therefore, I must have already received the prediction of great enlightenment from the various Buddhas in the past. "Subhūti!

Suppose an evil Māra, or a messenger of Māra, were to appear in the form of a Buddha and come to give a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva a prediction regarding the stage of a Śrāvaka, or a prediction regarding the stage of a Pratyekabuddha, saying to that Bodhisattva:"
"Alas, O man! Of what use is unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?

You have long endured great suffering within the cycle of birth and death; you should instead swiftly realize nirvana without remainder for yourself, forever departing from birth and death for ultimate peace and bliss!"
"Subhūti! Having heard those words, that bodhisattva mahāsattva forms this thought:

'This is surely an evil Māra, or a messenger of Māra, who has falsely manifested the form of a Buddha to disturb my mind and grant me a prediction of the stage of a śrāvaka or a pratyekabuddha, intending to cause me to retreat from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.'"

Why is this? It is because it is certainly not the case that the Buddhas teach bodhisattvas to incline toward the levels of śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, thereby abandoning unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
“Subhūti! Suppose an evil Māra or a messenger of Māra were to falsely manifest in the form of a Buddha and say to the bodhisattva mahāsattva:

‘The Mahāyāna sūtras that you have received and uphold were not spoken by the Buddha, nor were they spoken by the disciples of the Tathāgata; these were spoken by various evil Māras or non-Buddhist outsiders in order to deceive and delude you. You should not now receive, uphold, read, or recite them.’”
"Subhūti! When that bodhisattva mahāsattva hears those words, he thinks to himself:

'This must be Māra, or a follower of Māra, who wishes to cause me to become weary of and abandon unsurpassed enlightenment; therefore, he says that these profound Mahāyāna sūtras were not spoken by the Buddha, nor were they spoken by the disciples of the Tathāgata.'"
Why is this? Because it is absolutely impossible to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment apart from this sutra. “Subhūti!

It should be known that this bodhisattva mahāsattva already dwells on the stage of non-retrogression; long ago, the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past have already bestowed upon him the prediction of great enlightenment.
Why is this? Subhūti!

This bodhisattva mahāsattva is fully endowed with the practices, signs, and marks of the stage of non-retrogression. If a bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes such practices, signs, and marks, it should be known that they have already received the prediction of great enlightenment and have certainly already established themselves in the stage of non-retrogression.
“Subhūti! If one is endowed with such practices, characteristics, and signs, you should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti!”
When a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva at the stage of non-retrogression practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they uphold the true Dharma without sparing their own body or life, constantly reflecting:
"I would rather abandon wealth, treasures, kinsmen, and even my own life than ever forsake the true Dharma of the Buddhas."

Why is this so? Wealth, treasures, relatives, and even one’s own life are always easily obtained throughout every birth; however, the true Dharma of the Buddhas is encountered but once in hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of kalpas, and having encountered it, one obtains great benefit and happiness for a long night.
"Subhūti! When these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas protect the true Dharma, they form this thought:

'I do not protect the true Dharma of one Buddha, two Buddhas, or even hundreds of thousands of Buddhas; rather, I universally uphold and maintain the true Dharma of all Buddhas of the ten directions and the three periods of time so that it shall not be diminished.'"
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
what is called the true Dharma of all Buddhas?”
"How does this bodhisattva mahāsattva protect and uphold [the Dharma] without begrudging body or life?
The Buddha said, "Suvikrāntavikrāmin! "
All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas have taught the emptiness of phenomena (dharma-śūnyatā) for the sake of all bodhisattvas; this is what is called the true Dharma of the Buddhas.

There are those of a deluded nature who slander and revile it, saying: "This is not the Dharma, not the Vinaya, nor the holy teaching spoken by the Teacher of Gods and Humans; practicing this Dharma will not lead to awakening, nor will one realize the peace and bliss of nirvāṇa."
“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva upholds this Dharma without begrudging body or life, constantly thinking: ‘All dharmas spoken by the Tathāgata are empty;

these are the place of refuge for all sentient beings. By practicing and training in them, a bodhisattva swiftly realizes unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, thereby uprooting the birth, aging, sickness, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, and distress of all sentient beings, and enabling them to attain ultimate peace and bliss in nirvāṇa. For this reason, one should uphold [this Dharma] without begrudging body or life.’”
Furthermore, he reflects:

"I too am included among the number of future Buddhas; the Buddha has already bestowed upon me the prediction of great enlightenment (*mahābodhi*). For this reason, the true Dharma of all Buddhas is my own Dharma, and I should protect and uphold it without sparing even my body or life. When I attain Buddhahood in a future age, I too shall preach that all these phenomena are empty."
"Subhūti! Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva perceives these benefits, he protects and upholds the true Dharma spoken by the Tathāgata, not begrudging his own body or life. Subhūti!"
If one accomplishes such practices, characteristics, and signs, you should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva at the stage of non-retrogression hears the sublime Dharma spoken by the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, they will be without confusion or doubt; having heard it, they will receive and uphold it, never forgetting it until they reach unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
"Why is this? It is because these bodhisattvas have already well realized and attained the dhāraṇīs.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

By having attained what kind of dhāraṇī has this bodhisattva-mahāsattva come to hear all the sūtras spoken by the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, such that he never forgets them and remains free from confusion and doubt?”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have already attained the *akṣaragarbha* dhāraṇī, the *sāgaramudrā* dhāraṇī, the *padmakulagarbha* dhāraṇī, and others, they hear the sūtras spoken by the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, and do not forget them, nor do they have any confusion or doubt.”
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha,
saying: “World-Honored One,

does this bodhisattva mahāsattva merely hear the true Dharma spoken by the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha without confusion or doubt, and having heard it, receive and uphold it so as not to forget it, until reaching unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?”

When hearing the sublime Dharma spoken by śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and others, will you likewise be without confusion or doubt regarding it? Having heard it, will you receive and uphold it so that you never forget it, until you attain great enlightenment?
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

This bodhisattva mahāsattva universally hears all the sounds, words, and meanings of every class of sentient beings; he is able to understand them all completely, without confusion or doubt, and will never forget them until the end of the future.”
Why is this? Because they have already attained the *akṣaragarbha-dhāraṇī* and other such spells, which sustain what has been taught so that it may not be forgotten. "Subhūti!..."
"If one accomplishes such practices, characteristics, and signs, it should be known that this is an irreversible Bodhisattva Mahāsattva.
*The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, Fascicle 327 (Fascicle 328).
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang under Imperial Decree.
Chapter 50: Skillful Means, Part One, Section Fifty-1. At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva at the stage of non-retrogression has accomplished a vast and supreme accumulation of merit.
World-Honored One!”
"This is a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva in the stage of non-retrogression who has accomplished an immeasurable accumulation of supreme merit.
'World-Honored One!
This Bodhisattva Mahāsattva in the stage of non-retrogression has accomplished a boundless accumulation of supreme merit.'"
“World-Honored One!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva at the stage of non-retrogression has accomplished an immeasurable and inconceivable accumulation of supreme merits.
The Buddha said:
“Excellent, Subhūti! It is so, it is so!”
As you have said,
these Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas at the stage of non-retrogression have accomplished a vast, immeasurable, boundless, incalculable, and inconceivable accumulation of supreme merit.
Why is that? Subhūti!

This bodhisattva mahāsattva has already attained a vast, immeasurable, boundless, incalculable, and inconceivable wisdom that is not shared with śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas. Abiding in this wisdom, this bodhisattva mahāsattva brings forth the four supreme analytical knowledges (pratisaṃvid).

By virtue of these four supreme analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*), no one among the world’s gods, humans, or asuras is able to pose a challenge that could exhaust this bodhisattva’s wisdom and eloquence.
The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

One could speak for as many eons as there are grains of sand in the Ganges of the various practices, characteristics, and signs of bodhisattva mahāsattvas in the stage of non-retrogression; by means of these spoken practices, characteristics, and signs, one reveals that bodhisattva mahāsattvas in the stage of non-retrogression have accomplished various kinds of sublime merits.”

I only pray that the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, will further explain for the sake of bodhisattvas the profound state, so that all bodhisattvas may dwell therein, being able to cultivate the perfection of generosity until it is swiftly fulfilled, and being able to cultivate the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom until they are swiftly fulfilled.

They are able to abide in internal emptiness and cause it to be swiftly perfected; they are able to abide in external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, causing them to be swiftly perfected;

they are able to abide in suchness and cause it to be swiftly perfected; they are able to abide in the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, non-alteration, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm, causing them to be swiftly perfected.

They are able to cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness so that they are swiftly perfected; they are able to cultivate the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path so that they are swiftly perfected;

they are able to abide in the noble truth of suffering so that it is swiftly perfected, and they are able to abide in the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path so that they are swiftly perfected;

“Subhūti! The suchness of the eye-element is neither identical to the eye-element nor separate from the eye-element; therefore, it is profound.

The suchness of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements is neither identical to the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements nor separate from the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements; therefore, it is profound.”
“Subhūti! The suchness of the form realm is neither identical to the form realm nor separate from the form realm; therefore, it is profound.

The suchness of the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and phenomena is neither identical to those realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and phenomena, nor separate from them; therefore, it is profound.”
“Subhūti! The suchness of the visual consciousness element is neither identical to the visual consciousness element nor separate from the visual consciousness element; therefore, it is profound.

The suchness of the auditory, olfactory, gustatory, tactile, and mental consciousness elements is neither identical to the auditory, olfactory, gustatory, tactile, and mental consciousness elements nor separate from the auditory, olfactory, gustatory, tactile, and mental consciousness elements; therefore, they are profound.”
"Subhūti! The suchness of eye-contact is neither identical to eye-contact nor separate from eye-contact; therefore, it is profound.

The suchness of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact is neither identical to ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact nor separate from ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact; therefore, it is profound."

“Subhūti! The suchness of all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition is neither identical to those feelings produced with eye-contact as condition nor separate from those feelings produced with eye-contact as condition; therefore, it is profound.

The suchness of all feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions is neither identical to those feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions nor separate from those feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions; therefore, it is profound.”
“Subhūti! The suchness of the earth element is neither identical to the earth element nor separate from the earth element; therefore, it is profound.

The suchness of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements is neither identical to the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements nor separate from the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements; therefore, it is profound.”
“Subhūti! The suchness of ignorance is neither identical to ignorance nor separate from ignorance; therefore, it is profound.
