The suchness of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair is neither identical to volitional formations through to old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair, nor separate from volitional formations through to old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair; therefore, it is profound.”
“Subhūti! The suchness of the perfection of generosity is neither identical to the perfection of generosity nor separate from the perfection of generosity; therefore, it is profound.

The suchness of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom is neither identical to the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, nor separate from the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; therefore, they are profound.”
“Subhūti! The suchness of internal emptiness is neither identical to internal emptiness nor separate from internal emptiness; therefore, it is profound.

The suchness of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, emptiness of self-characteristic, emptiness of common characteristic, emptiness of all phenomena, unapprehendable emptiness, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, and emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is neither identical to external emptiness up to and including emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, nor is it separate from external emptiness up to and including emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence; therefore, it is profound.”
“Subhūti! Suchness is not identical to suchness, nor is it separate from suchness; therefore, it is profound.

The realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), the non-erroneous nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the nature free from arising, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm—suchness is not identical to these, from the realm of phenomena up to the inconceivable realm, nor is it separate from them; therefore, they are profound.”
“Subhūti! The suchness of the four foundations of mindfulness is neither identical to the four foundations of mindfulness nor separate from them; therefore, it is profound.

The suchness of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path is neither identical to the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path nor separate from them; therefore, it is profound.”
“Subhūti! The suchness of the noble truth of suffering is neither identical to the noble truth of suffering nor separate from the noble truth of suffering; therefore, it is profound.

The suchness of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path is neither identical to the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path nor separate from the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path; therefore, they are profound.”
“Subhūti! The suchness of the four dhyānas is neither identical to the four dhyānas nor separate from the four dhyānas; therefore, it is profound.

The suchness of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is neither identical to the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments nor separate from the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments; therefore, it is profound.”
“Subhūti! The suchness of the eight liberations is neither identical to the eight liberations nor separate from the eight liberations; therefore, it is profound.

The suchness of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities is neither identical to the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities, nor separate from the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities; therefore, it is profound.”

“Subhūti! The suchness of the gate of liberation of emptiness is neither identical to the gate of liberation of emptiness nor separate from the gate of liberation of emptiness; therefore, it is profound.

The suchness of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness is neither identical to the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness nor separate from the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness; therefore, it is profound.”
“Subhūti! The suchness of the Ground of Extreme Joy is neither identical to the Ground of Extreme Joy nor separate from the Ground of Extreme Joy; therefore, it is profound.

The suchness of the Ground of Purity, the Ground of Radiance, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Utmost Difficulty to Conquer, the Ground of Manifestation, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, and the Ground of the Dharma Cloud is neither identical to the Ground of Purity up to the Ground of the Dharma Cloud, nor is it separate from the Ground of Purity up to the Ground of the Dharma Cloud; therefore, it is profound.”
"Subhūti! The suchness of the five eyes is neither identical to the five eyes nor separate from the five eyes; therefore, it is profound.
The suchness of the six supernormal powers is neither identical to the six supernormal powers nor separate from the six supernormal powers; therefore, it is profound."
“Subhūti! The suchness of the gateways of samādhi is not identical to the gateways of samādhi, nor is it separate from the gateways of samādhi; therefore, it is profound.
The suchness of the gateways of dhāraṇī is not identical to the gateways of dhāraṇī, nor is it separate from the gateways of dhāraṇī; therefore, it is profound.”
“Subhūti! The suchness of the ten powers of a Buddha is neither identical to the ten powers of a Buddha nor separate from the ten powers of a Buddha; therefore, it is profound.

The suchness of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is neither identical to those qualities from the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, nor is it separate from them; therefore, it is profound.”
“Subhūti! The suchness of the quality of non-forgetfulness is neither identical to the quality of non-forgetfulness nor separate from the quality of non-forgetfulness; therefore, it is profound.
The suchness of the nature of constant equanimity is neither identical to the nature of constant equanimity nor separate from the nature of constant equanimity; therefore, it is profound.”
"Subhūti! The suchness of the fruit of stream-entry is neither identical to the fruit of stream-entry nor separate from the fruit of stream-entry; therefore, it is profound.
The suchness of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship is neither identical to those fruits nor separate from those fruits; therefore, they are profound."
“Subhūti! The suchness of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is neither identical to pratyekabuddha-enlightenment nor separate from pratyekabuddha-enlightenment;
therefore, it is profound. Subhūti!”
The suchness of all-knowledge is neither identical to all-knowledge nor separate from all-knowledge; therefore, it is profound.

The suchness of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects is neither identical to the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects, nor is it separate from the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects; therefore, it is profound.

“Subhūti! The suchness of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas’ practices is neither identical to all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas’ practices nor distinct from all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas’ practices; therefore, it is profound.”

“Subhūti! The suchness of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is neither identical to the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas, nor is it separate from the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas; therefore, it is profound.”
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:

“World-Honored One, how marvelous and subtle is this skillful means! For the sake of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, you eliminate all forms and reveal nirvāṇa; you eliminate feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, and reveal nirvāṇa.”

“The World-Honored One possesses most marvelous and subtle skillful means; for the sake of Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, he sets aside the sense-base of the eye to reveal nirvāṇa, and sets aside the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind to reveal nirvāṇa.”

“The World-Honored One possesses most marvelous and subtle skillful means; for the sake of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, he sets aside the sphere of form to reveal nirvāṇa, and sets aside the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena to reveal nirvāṇa.”

“The World-Honored One possesses most marvelous and subtle skillful means; for the sake of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, he negates the eye-element to reveal nirvāṇa, and negates the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements to reveal nirvāṇa.”

“The World-Honored One possesses most marvelous and subtle skillful means; for the sake of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, he sets aside the realm of form to reveal nirvāṇa, and sets aside the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena to reveal nirvāṇa.”

“The World-Honored One possesses most marvelous and subtle skillful means; for the sake of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, he sets aside the eye-consciousness element to reveal nirvāṇa, and sets aside the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements to reveal nirvāṇa.”

“The World-Honored One possesses most marvelous and subtle skillful means; for the sake of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, he sets aside eye-contact to reveal nirvāṇa, and sets aside ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact to reveal nirvāṇa.”

“The World-Honored One possesses most marvelous and subtle skillful means; for the sake of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, he sets aside all sensations produced with eye-contact as a condition and reveals Nirvāṇa, and he sets aside all sensations produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions and reveals Nirvāṇa.”

“The World-Honored One possesses most marvelous and subtle skillful means; for the sake of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, he sets aside the earth element to reveal nirvāṇa, and sets aside the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness to reveal nirvāṇa.”

“The World-Honored One possesses most marvelous and subtle skillful means; for the sake of Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, he dispels ignorance and reveals Nirvāṇa, and he dispels volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, thereby revealing Nirvāṇa.”

“The Blessed One possesses most marvelous and subtle skillful means; for the sake of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, he sets aside the perfection of giving and reveals nirvāṇa, and he sets aside the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, and reveals nirvāṇa.”

“World-Honored One, how truly marvelous and subtle is your skillful means! For the sake of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, you set aside internal emptiness to reveal *nirvāṇa*; you set aside external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersal emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, thereby revealing *nirvāṇa*.”

“World-Honored One, how marvelous and subtle is Your skillful means! For the sake of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, You negate *tathatā* (suchness) to reveal *nirvāṇa*; You negate the *dharmadhātu*, *dharmatā*, *avitathatā*, *ananyathābhāvatā*, *samatā*, *anabhibhūtatā*, *dharmasthititā*, *dharmaniyāmatā*, *bhūtakoṭi*, *ākāśadhātu*, and *acintyadhātu* to reveal *nirvāṇa*.

“World-Honored One, how truly marvelous and subtle is your skillful means! For the sake of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dwelling on the stage of non-retrogression, you set aside the four foundations of mindfulness and reveal nirvāṇa; you set aside the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path, and reveal nirvāṇa.”

“The World-Honored One possesses most marvelous and subtle skillful means; for the sake of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, he sets aside the Noble Truth of Suffering to reveal nirvāṇa, and sets aside the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path to reveal nirvāṇa.”

“The World-Honored One possesses most marvelous and subtle skillful means; for the sake of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, he sets aside the four dhyānas to reveal nirvāṇa, and sets aside the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments to reveal nirvāṇa.”

“The World-Honored One possesses most marvelous and subtle skillful means; for the sake of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas of the stage of non-retrogression, he sets aside the eight liberations to reveal Nirvāṇa, and sets aside the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities to reveal Nirvāṇa.”

“World-Honored One, how truly marvelous and subtle is your skillful means! For the sake of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, you set aside the liberation door of emptiness to reveal nirvāṇa, and you set aside the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness to reveal nirvāṇa.”

“World-Honored One, how wondrous and subtle is Your skillful means! For the sake of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, You have set aside the Stage of Extreme Joy and revealed nirvāṇa; You have set aside the Stage of Purity, the Radiant Stage, the Blazing Wisdom Stage, the Extremely Difficult to Conquer Stage, the Manifesting Stage, the Far-Reaching Stage, the Immovable Stage, the Stage of Excellent Intelligence, and the Dharma Cloud Stage, and revealed nirvāṇa.”

“The World-Honored One possesses most marvelous and subtle skillful means; for the sake of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas of the stage of non-retrogression, he sets aside the five eyes to reveal nirvāṇa, and sets aside the six supernormal powers to reveal nirvāṇa.”

“The World-Honored One possesses most wonderful and subtle skillful means; for the sake of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, he reveals nirvāṇa by setting aside the gateways of samādhi, and reveals nirvāṇa by setting aside the gateways of dhāraṇī.”

“World-Honored One, how extraordinary and subtle is your skillful means! For the sake of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the stage of non-retrogression, you set aside the ten powers of a buddha to reveal nirvāṇa; you set aside the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha to reveal nirvāṇa.”

“The World-Honored One possesses most marvelous and subtle skillful means; for the sake of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, he sets aside the quality of non-forgetfulness to reveal nirvāṇa, and sets aside the state of constant equanimity to reveal nirvāṇa.”

“The World-Honored One possesses most marvelous and subtle skillful means, for he sets aside the fruit of stream-entry for bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the stage of non-retrogression and reveals nirvāṇa; he sets aside the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship and reveals nirvāṇa.”

"How extraordinary and subtle is the Blessed One’s skillful means! For the sake of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, he sets aside the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha and reveals nirvāṇa."

“World-Honored One, how truly marvelous and subtle is Your skillful means! For the sake of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, You set aside all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) to manifest nirvāṇa, and set aside the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) to manifest nirvāṇa.”

“The World-Honored One possesses most marvelous and subtle skillful means; for the sake of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, he sets aside all bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices and reveals nirvāṇa.”

“World-Honored One, how marvelous and subtle is your skillful means! For the sake of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, you set aside the unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment of all Buddhas and manifest nirvāṇa.”

“The World-Honored One possesses most marvelous and subtle skillful means; for the sake of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas of the stage of non-retrogression, he eliminates all phenomena—whether worldly or supramundane, common or uncommon, with outflows or without outflows, conditioned or unconditioned—and reveals Nirvāṇa to them.”
The Buddha said, “So it is, Subhūti!”
"So it is! It is just as you have said.

By means of most wondrous and subtle skillful means, the Buddha, for the sake of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, sets aside all forms to reveal nirvāṇa; he sets aside feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness to reveal nirvāṇa."

"The Buddha, by means of most marvelous and subtle skillful means, for the sake of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, negates the sense base of the eye to reveal nirvāṇa, and negates the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind to reveal nirvāṇa."

“The Buddha, through most extraordinary and subtle skillful means, for the sake of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, sets aside the sphere of form to reveal nirvāṇa, and sets aside the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena to reveal nirvāṇa.”

“By means of most marvelous and subtle skillful means, the Buddha, for the sake of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the stage of non-retrogression, negates the eye-element to reveal nirvāṇa, and negates the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements to reveal nirvāṇa.”

"The Buddha, by means of most marvelous and subtle skillful means, for the sake of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, sets aside the realm of form to reveal nirvāṇa, and sets aside the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena to reveal nirvāṇa."

"The Buddha, through most extraordinary and subtle skillful means, for the sake of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, has set aside the eye-consciousness element to reveal nirvāṇa, and set aside the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements to reveal nirvāṇa."

“The Buddha, through most marvelous and subtle skillful means, for the sake of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, sets aside eye-contact to reveal nirvāṇa, and sets aside ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact to reveal nirvāṇa.”

“By means of most marvelous and subtle skillful methods, the Buddha, for the sake of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, reveals nirvāṇa by setting aside all sensations produced with eye-contact as condition; he reveals nirvāṇa by setting aside all sensations produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions.”

“By means of most marvelous and subtle skillful means, the Buddha, for the sake of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, sets aside the earth element to reveal nirvāṇa, and sets aside the elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness to reveal nirvāṇa.”

“By means of most wonderful and subtle skillful means, the Buddha, for the sake of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, dispels ignorance and reveals nirvāṇa; he dispels volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, and reveals nirvāṇa.”

“By means of most wonderful and subtle skillful means, the Buddha, for the sake of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, sets aside the perfection of giving and reveals nirvāṇa; he sets aside the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, and reveals nirvāṇa.”

“The Buddha, through most marvelous and subtle skillful means, for the sake of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, sets aside internal emptiness to reveal nirvāṇa; he sets aside external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature to reveal nirvāṇa.”

“By means of most wonderful and subtle skillful means, the Buddha, for the sake of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, sets aside *tathatā* (suchness) to reveal *nirvāṇa*; he sets aside the *dharmadhātu*, the *dharmatā*, the non-erroneous nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm to reveal *nirvāṇa*.

“By means of most wonderful and subtle skillful means, the Buddha, for the sake of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, sets aside the four foundations of mindfulness to reveal nirvāṇa; he sets aside the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path to reveal nirvāṇa.”

“By means of most extraordinary and subtle skillful means, the Buddha, for the sake of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, sets aside the Noble Truth of Suffering to reveal nirvāṇa, and sets aside the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path to reveal nirvāṇa.”

“By means of most marvelous and subtle skillful means, the Buddha, for the sake of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, sets aside the four dhyānas to reveal nirvāṇa, and sets aside the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions to reveal nirvāṇa.”

“The Buddha, through most marvelous and subtle skillful means, for the sake of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, sets aside the eight liberations to reveal nirvāṇa; he sets aside the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities to reveal nirvāṇa.”

"The Buddha, through most marvelous and subtle skillful means, for the sake of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, sets aside the liberation door of emptiness to manifest nirvāṇa, and sets aside the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness to manifest nirvāṇa."

“By means of most marvelous and subtle skillful means, the Buddha, for the sake of Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, has set aside the manifestation of *nirvāṇa* for the Stage of Extreme Joy; he has likewise set aside the manifestation of *nirvāṇa* for the Stage of Purity, the Stage of Radiance, the Stage of Blazing Wisdom, the Stage of Difficult Victory, the Stage of Presence, the Stage of Far-Going, the Immovable Stage, the Stage of Good Intelligence, and the Stage of the Dharma Cloud.”

“The Buddha, through most marvelous and subtle skillful means, for the sake of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, sets aside the five eyes to reveal nirvāṇa, and sets aside the six supernormal powers to reveal nirvāṇa.”

“The Buddha, through most marvelous and subtle skillful means, for the sake of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, reveals nirvāṇa by setting aside the gates of samādhi, and reveals nirvāṇa by setting aside the gates of dhāraṇī.”

“By means of most marvelous and subtle skillful means, the Buddha, for the sake of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, sets aside the ten powers of a buddha to reveal nirvāṇa; he sets aside the four fearlessnesses, the four kinds of unimpeded understanding, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha to reveal nirvāṇa.”

“The Buddha, by means of most marvelous and subtle skillful means, for the sake of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, sets aside the quality of non-forgetfulness to reveal nirvāṇa, and sets aside the state of constant dwelling in equanimity to reveal nirvāṇa.”

“The Buddha, by means of most marvelous and subtle skillful means, for the sake of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, sets aside the fruit of stream-entry and reveals nirvāṇa; he sets aside the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship, and reveals nirvāṇa.”

"The Buddha, by means of most marvelous and subtle skillful means, for the sake of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, sets aside the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha and reveals nirvāṇa."

“The Buddha, through most marvelous and subtle skillful means, for the sake of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, sets aside all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) to manifest nirvāṇa, and sets aside the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) to manifest nirvāṇa.”

"The Buddha, through most extraordinary and subtle skillful means, for the sake of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, sets aside all bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices and reveals nirvāṇa."

"The Buddha, through most extraordinary and subtle skillful means, has for the sake of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression set aside the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas to manifest nirvāṇa."

"By means of most extraordinary and subtle skillful means, the Buddha, for the sake of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas on the stage of non-retrogression, has set aside all phenomena—whether worldly or supramundane, common or uncommon, with outflows or without outflows, conditioned or unconditioned—and revealed nirvāṇa."

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle Three Hundred Twenty-Eight. Translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter Fifty on Skillful Means, Section Two. "Furthermore, Subhūti!..."

All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should, regarding such profound points, rely on the principles corresponding to the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, and with careful reflection, weighing, and observation, they should think:
"I should now abide as taught in the profound *prajñāpāramitā*; I should now train as taught in the profound *prajñāpāramitā*."
"Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able, regarding such profound points, to reflect with precision, weigh, and examine them according to the principles corresponding to the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, and to abide as taught in the profound *prajñāpāramitā* and train as taught in the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, then by virtue of such diligent cultivation and training, that bodhisattva mahāsattva—by generating even a single thought-moment based on the profound *prajñāpāramitā*—is still able to gather countless, immeasurable, and boundless merits, transcend the flow of birth and death for immeasurable eons, and swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; how much more so if they can constantly cultivate the *prajñāpāramitā* without interruption and always abide in the mental engagement (*manasikāra*) associated with unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment!

"Subhūti! It is like a man addicted to desire who, having become mutually infatuated with a beautiful woman, makes an appointment with her; yet because of some obstacle, that woman is unable to keep the appointment, and the man's lustful mind continues to flow and intensify."
"Subhūti! What do you think?
In what respect does that person’s thought of desire operate?"
“World-Honored One!
This person’s thoughts turn toward women, thinking:
‘When will she come so that we may meet here and enjoy ourselves in pleasure and sport?’”
"Subhūti! What do you think? How many thoughts of desire arise in that person during a day and night?"
“World-Honored One!
This person has very many thoughts of desire day and night.
The Buddha said:

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, gives rise to even a single thought-moment and trains according to what is taught in the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, the number of kalpas of saṃsāric wandering they will transcend is equal to the number of lustful thoughts produced by a person addicted to desire over the course of a single day and night.”

"Subhūti! To the extent that this bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates and trains in accordance with the principles taught in the Prajñāpāramitā, to that same extent they are able to liberate themselves from the faults that obstruct unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment. Therefore, by relying on the profound Prajñāpāramitā and training with diligent effort, the bodhisattva swiftly realizes unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment."

"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in accordance with what is taught in this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, the merit obtained in a single day and night—if that merit were to have a physical form—could not be contained even within as many trichiliocosm buddha-worlds as there are grains of sand in the Ganges."

Even if one were to fill the Buddha-worlds of the three-thousandfold great thousandfold world-system as numerous as the sands of the Ganges with all other meritorious qualities, they would not equal even a hundredth part of this merit; they would not equal a thousandth part, nor a hundred-thousandth part, nor a ten-billionth part, nor a trillionth part, nor a hundred-trillionth part, nor a ten-quintillionth part, nor a hundred-quintillionth part, nor a thousand-quintillionth part, nor a hundred-thousand-quintillionth part. Thus, to speak extensively, they do not equal it by way of number, calculation, reckoning, analogy, or even by way of the *upaniṣad* (proportion).
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, being far removed from the perfection of wisdom, were to practice giving as an offering to the Triple Gem—the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha—for as many great eons as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River."
"Subhūti! What do you think?
By reason of this cause and condition, would that bodhisattva mahāsattva acquire much merit?"
Subhūti replied, “Very much so,
World-Honored One!”
"Very much so!
Sugata! That merit would be incalculable, immeasurable, and boundless."
The Buddha said,
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the profound perfection of wisdom, practices as taught for a single day and night, the merit they obtain is far greater than that.”
Why is this? Subhūti!

This profound perfection of wisdom is the vehicle of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; because all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas mount this vehicle, they swiftly arrive at unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva were to remain far removed from the perfection of wisdom, even if they were to respectfully serve, honor, and make offerings to stream-enterers, once-returners, non-returners, arhats, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas for as many great eons as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River."
"Subhūti! What do you think?
Would that bodhisattva mahāsattva, by reason of this cause and condition, acquire much merit?"
Subhūti replied, "Very many,
World-Honored One!"
"Very much so,
Sugata! That merit would be incalculable, immeasurable, and boundless."
The Buddha said,
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on the profound perfection of wisdom, studies as taught for even a single day and night, the merit they obtain is far greater than that.”
Why is this? Subhūti!

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the profound perfection of wisdom, they transcend the stages of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, swiftly enter the bodhisattva’s state of rightness and departure from birth, and are further able to cultivate the various bodhisattva practices, quickly realizing unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva were to remain far removed from the perfection of wisdom, even if they were to diligently practice generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom for as many great eons as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River."
"Subhūti! What do you think?
Would this bodhisattva mahāsattva, by reason of this cause and condition, acquire much merit?"
Subhūti replied, “Very much so,
World-Honored One!”
"Very much so,
Sugata! That merit would be incalculable, immeasurable, and boundless."
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in accordance with what is taught in this profound perfection of wisdom and, for a single day and night, diligently practices generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, the merit he obtains will be far greater than that.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
This profound perfection of wisdom is the mother of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas.

Why is this? It is because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* gives birth to the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas rely upon the *prajñāpāramitā*, whereby they are able to swiftly fulfill all Buddha-dharmas.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva were to be separated from the perfection of wisdom, even if they were to practice the gift of Dharma to all sentient beings for as many great eons as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River."
"Subhūti! What do you think?
By reason of this, would that bodhisattva mahāsattva acquire much merit?"
Subhūti replied, “It would be very much,
World-Honored One!”
"Very much so!
Sugata! That merit would be incalculable, immeasurable, and boundless."
The Buddha said,
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in accordance with what is taught in the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, and for even a single day and night bestows the gift of Dharma upon all sentient beings, the merit obtained will be far greater than that.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is far removed from the perfection of wisdom, then they are far removed from the knowledge of all modes.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not depart from the perfection of wisdom, then they do not depart from the knowledge of all aspects. Therefore, Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, they should always remain inseparable from the profound perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva were to remain far removed from the perfection of wisdom, even if they were to practice the perfection of generosity, and practice the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom for as many great eons as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River.
"Subhūti! What do you think?
By reason of this, would that bodhisattva mahāsattva acquire much merit?"
Subhūti replied, “It is very much so,
World-Honored One!”
"Very much so,
Sugata! That merit would be incalculable, immeasurable, and boundless."
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in accordance with what is taught in the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, and practices the *dānapāramitā*, the *śīlapāramitā*, the *kṣāntipāramitā*, the *vīryapāramitā*, the *dhyānapāramitā*, and the *prajñāpāramitā* for even a single day and night, the merit obtained will be far greater than that.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not depart from the perfection of wisdom, it is impossible for them to regress from the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of a Buddha.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, being far removed from the perfection of wisdom, were to regress from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, such a thing is possible.
Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, they should at all times never be separated from the profound perfection of wisdom.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, being far removed from the perfection of wisdom, were to dwell for as many great eons as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River in internal emptiness, and dwell in external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence."
"Subhūti! What do you think?
Would that bodhisattva mahāsattva, by reason of this cause and condition, acquire much merit?"
Subhūti replied, “Very much so,
World-Honored One!”
"Very much so,
Sugata! That merit would be incalculable, immeasurable, and boundless."
The Buddha said,
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in accordance with what is taught in the profound perfection of wisdom, and for a single day and night abides in internal emptiness and abides in external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, the merit he obtains is far greater than that.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not remain far removed from the perfection of wisdom, it is impossible that they should regress from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, being far removed from the perfection of wisdom, should fall back from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, such a thing is possible.
Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, they should at all times never be separated from the profound perfection of wisdom.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva were to remain far removed from the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), even for as many great eons as there are grains of sand in the Ganges, dwelling in suchness (tathatā), dwelling in the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), non-illusory nature, non-alteration, equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm."
"Subhūti! What do you think?
Would this bodhisattva mahāsattva, by reason of this cause and condition, acquire much merit?"
Subhūti replied, “It is very much so,
World-Honored One!”
"Very much so!
Sugata! That merit would be incalculable, immeasurable, and boundless."
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in accordance with what is taught in this profound perfection of wisdom, and for a single day and night abides in suchness, abides in the dharma-realm, and so forth up to the inconceivable realm, the merit they obtain will be far greater than that.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not remain far removed from the perfection of wisdom, it is impossible that they should regress from unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, being far removed from the perfection of wisdom, should regress from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, such a thing is possible.
Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, they should at all times never be separated from the profound perfection of wisdom.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, being far removed from the perfection of wisdom, were to practice the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path for as many great eons as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River;
"Subhūti! What do you think?
Would that bodhisattva mahāsattva, by reason of this cause and condition, acquire much merit?"
Subhūti replied, “It is very much so,
World-Honored One!”
"Very much so,
Sugata! That merit would be incalculable, immeasurable, and boundless."
The Buddha said,
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in accordance with what is taught in the profound perfection of wisdom and practices the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, and so forth up to the eight branches of the noble path for even a single day and night, the merit obtained will be far greater than that.”
Why is this? Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not remain far removed from the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), it is impossible that they should ever regress from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi).
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, being far removed from the perfection of wisdom, should regress from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, such a thing is possible.
Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, they should always remain inseparable from the profound perfection of wisdom.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, being far removed from the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), were to dwell for as many great eons as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River in the noble truth of suffering, and dwell in the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path.
"Subhūti! What do you think?
By virtue of this cause and condition, would that bodhisattva mahāsattva acquire much merit?"
Subhūti replied, “Very much so,
World-Honored One!”
"Very much so,
Sugata! That merit would be incalculable, immeasurable, and boundless."
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in accordance with what is taught in this profound perfection of wisdom, and for a single day and night abides in the noble truth of suffering, and abides in the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, the merit he obtains will be far greater than that.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not remain far removed from the perfection of wisdom, it is impossible that they would ever regress from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, having become distant from the perfection of wisdom, should regress from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, such a thing is possible.
Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, they should at all times remain inseparable from the profound perfection of wisdom.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, being far removed from the perfection of wisdom, were to practice the four dhyānas and practice the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions for as many great eons as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River."
"Subhūti! What do you think?
Would that bodhisattva mahāsattva, by reason of this cause and condition, acquire much merit?"
Subhūti replied, “Very much so,
World-Honored One!”
"Very much so!
Sugata! That merit would be incalculable, immeasurable, and boundless."
The Buddha said,
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in accordance with what is taught in the profound perfection of wisdom and practices the four dhyānas and the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments for even a single day and night, the merit obtained will be far greater than that.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not remain far removed from the perfection of wisdom, it is impossible that they should regress from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, being far removed from the perfection of wisdom, should regress from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, such a thing is possible.
Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, they should always remain inseparable from the profound perfection of wisdom.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, being far removed from the perfection of wisdom, were to practice the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities for as many great eons as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River."
"Subhūti, what do you think?
By reason of this, would that bodhisattva mahāsattva acquire much merit?"
Subhūti replied, “It is very much so,
World-Honored One!”
"Very much so!
Sugata! That merit would be incalculable, immeasurable, and boundless."
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in accordance with what is taught in the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) and practices the eight liberations (aṣṭa-vimokṣa), the eight bases of mastery (aṣṭābhibhv-āyatana), the nine successive attainments (navānupūrva-samāpatti), and the ten totalities (daśakṛtsnāyatana) for even a single day and night, the merit he obtains is far greater than that.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not remain far removed from the perfection of wisdom, it is impossible that they should regress from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, being far removed from the perfection of wisdom, should regress from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, such a thing is possible.
Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, they should always remain inseparable from the profound perfection of wisdom.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, being far removed from the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), were to practice the gate of liberation of emptiness (śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha) and practice the gates of liberation of signlessness (animitta) and wishlessness (apraṇihita) for as many great eons as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River."
"Subhūti! What do you think?
By reason of this cause and condition, would that bodhisattva mahāsattva acquire much merit?"
Subhūti replied, “Very much so,
World-Honored One!”
"Very much so,
Sugata! That merit would be incalculable, immeasurable, and boundless."
The Buddha said,
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in accordance with what is taught in the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, and practices the liberation door of emptiness (*śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha*) as well as the liberation doors of signlessness (*animitta*) and wishlessness (*apraṇihita*) for even a single day and night, the merit obtained will be far greater than that.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not remain far removed from the perfection of wisdom, it is impossible that they should ever regress from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening.
It is possible that a bodhisattva mahāsattva who is far removed from the perfection of wisdom may regress from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, they should always remain inseparable from the profound perfection of wisdom.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, being far removed from the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), were to practice for as many great eons as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River on the Stage of Extreme Joy (pramuditā-bhūmi), and practice on the Stage of Purity (vimalā-bhūmi), the Stage of Radiance (prabhākārī-bhūmi), the Stage of Blazing Wisdom (arciṣmatī-bhūmi), the Stage Difficult to Conquer (sudurjayā-bhūmi), the Stage of Presence (abhimukhī-bhūmi), the Stage of Far-Going (dūraṅgamā-bhūmi), the Immovable Stage (acalā-bhūmi), the Stage of Good Intelligence (sādhumatī-bhūmi), and the Stage of the Cloud of Dharma (dharmameghā-bhūmi)."
"Subhūti! What do you think?
Would that bodhisattva mahāsattva, by reason of this cause and condition, acquire much merit?"
Subhūti replied, “Very much so,
World-Honored One!”
"Very much so,
Sugata! That merit would be incalculable, immeasurable, and boundless."
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva abides according to what is taught in the profound *prajñāpāramitā* and practices the Stage of Extreme Joy (*pramuditā-bhūmi*) for a single day and night, and likewise practices the Stage of Purity (*vimalā-bhūmi*), the Radiant Stage (*prabhākārī-bhūmi*), the Stage of Blazing Wisdom (*arciṣmatī-bhūmi*), the Stage Difficult to Conquer (*sudurjayā-bhūmi*), the Manifest Stage (*abhimukhī-bhūmi*), the Far-Reaching Stage (*dūraṅgamā-bhūmi*), the Immovable Stage (*acalā-bhūmi*), the Stage of Excellent Intelligence (*sādhumatī-bhūmi*), and the Cloud of Dharma Stage (*dharmameghā-bhūmi*), the merit he obtains will be far greater than that.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not remain far removed from the perfection of wisdom, it is impossible that they should regress from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, being far removed from the perfection of wisdom, should regress from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, such a thing is possible.
Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, they should always remain inseparable from the profound perfection of wisdom.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva were to distance themselves from the perfection of wisdom, even if they were to practice the five eyes and practice the six supernormal powers for as many great eons as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River."
"Subhūti! What do you think?
By reason of this, would that bodhisattva mahāsattva acquire much merit?"
Subhūti replied, “Very much so,
World-Honored One!”
"Very much so,
Sugata! That merit would be incalculable, immeasurable, and boundless."
The Buddha said,
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in accordance with what is taught in the profound perfection of wisdom, and practices the five eyes and the six supernormal powers for even a single day and night, the merit they obtain will be far greater than that.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not remain far removed from the perfection of wisdom, it is impossible that they should ever regress from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, being far removed from the perfection of wisdom, should regress from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, such a thing is possible.
Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, they should always remain inseparable from the profound perfection of wisdom.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva were to remain far removed from the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) and, even for as many great eons as there are grains of sand in the Ganges, were to practice all the gateways of samādhi and practice all the gateways of dhāraṇī."
"Subhūti! What do you think?
By reason of this, would that bodhisattva mahāsattva acquire much merit?"
Subhūti replied, “Very much so,
World-Honored One!”
"Very much so,
Sugata! That merit would be incalculable, immeasurable, and boundless."
The Buddha said,
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in accordance with what is taught in the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), and practices all doors of samādhi and all doors of dhāraṇī for even a single day and night, the merit he obtains will be far greater than that.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not remain far removed from the perfection of wisdom, it is impossible that they should regress from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, being far removed from the perfection of wisdom, were to regress from unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, such a thing is possible.
Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, they should always remain inseparable from the profound perfection of wisdom.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva were to remain far removed from the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), even if they were to practice the ten powers of a buddha, the four fearlessnesses (vaiśāradya), the four analytical knowledges (pratisaṃvid), great loving-kindness (maitrī), great compassion (karuṇā), great sympathetic joy (muditā), great equanimity (upekṣā), and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha for as many great eons as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River."
"Subhūti! What do you think?
Would this bodhisattva mahāsattva, by reason of this cause and condition, acquire much merit?"
Subhūti replied, “It is very much so,
World-Honored One!”
"Very much so,
Sugata! That merit would be incalculable, immeasurable, and boundless."
The Buddha said,
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in accordance with what is taught in this profound prajñāpāramitā and practices the ten powers of a buddha, the four fearlessnesses, and even the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha for a single day and night, the merit he obtains will be far greater than that.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not remain far removed from the perfection of wisdom, it is impossible that they should regress from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, being far removed from the perfection of wisdom, should regress from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, such a thing is possible.
Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, they should always remain inseparable from the profound perfection of wisdom.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva were to remain far removed from the perfection of wisdom, even if they were to practice the quality of non-forgetfulness and practice the state of constant equanimity for as many great eons as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River."
"Subhūti, what do you think?
Would that bodhisattva mahāsattva, by reason of this cause and condition, acquire much merit?"
Subhūti replied, “It is very much so,
World-Honored One!”
"Very much so,
Sugata! That merit would be incalculable, immeasurable, and boundless."
The Buddha said,
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva abides in accordance with what is taught in this profound prajñāpāramitā and practices the dharma of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity for even a single day and night, the merit he obtains will be far greater than that.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not remain far removed from the perfection of wisdom, it is impossible that they should regress from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, being far removed from the perfection of wisdom, should regress from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, such a thing is possible.
Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, they should always remain inseparable from the profound perfection of wisdom.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva were to remain far removed from the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), even if they were to practice all-knowledge (sarvajñatā) and practice the knowledge of the aspects of the path (mārgākārajñatā) and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā) for as many great eons as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River."
"Subhūti! What do you think?
By reason of this, would that bodhisattva mahāsattva acquire much merit?"
Subhūti replied, “It is very much so,
World-Honored One!”
"Very much so,
Sugata! That merit would be incalculable, immeasurable, and boundless."
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in accordance with what is taught in this profound perfection of wisdom and practices all-knowledge (sarvajñatā), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (mārgākārajñatā), and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā) for even a single day and night, the merit they obtain will be far greater than that.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not remain far removed from the perfection of wisdom, it is impossible that they should regress from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, being far removed from the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), should regress from unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, such a thing is possible.
Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, they should always remain inseparable from the profound perfection of wisdom.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, being far removed from the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), were to spend as many great eons as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River practicing various kinds of material giving and the giving of Dharma, dwelling in secluded places, and with focused mindfulness reflecting upon their previous practices, universally dedicating them all toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment; [yet, because they lack the perfection of wisdom, this would not be called a true dedication]."
"Subhūti! What do you think?
Would this bodhisattva mahāsattva, by reason of this cause and condition, acquire much merit?"
Subhūti replied, “It is very much so,
World-Honored One!”
"Very much so,
Sugata! That merit would be incalculable, immeasurable, and boundless."
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in accordance with what is taught in the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, and for the duration of a single day and night practices various kinds of material giving and the giving of Dharma, dwelling in a secluded place and focusing his mindfulness to contemplate what he has previously practiced, dedicating it all universally toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, the merit he obtains will be far greater than that.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
You should know that the dedication arising from reliance upon the profound perfection of wisdom is the most supreme dedication.
One should know that a dedication arising apart from the perfection of wisdom is not called the supreme dedication.

Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, they should never be separated from the profound perfection of wisdom, and should dedicate all their practiced deeds universally toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, being far removed from the perfection of wisdom, were for as many great eons as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River to universally take as their object all the roots of virtue and merit of all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, and their disciples—past, future, and present—and having combined them, rejoice in them with sympathetic joy, and universally dedicate them all toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
"Subhūti, what do you think?
By this cause and condition, would that bodhisattva mahāsattva acquire much merit?"
Subhūti replied, “Very much so,
World-Honored One!”
"Very much so,
Sugata! That merit would be incalculable, immeasurable, and boundless."
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in accordance with what is taught in the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, and for the duration of a single day and night universally takes as their object all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, along with their disciples, of the past, future, and present, and rejoices in the roots of virtue of those merits by combining them together, and universally dedicates them toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, the merit obtained will be far greater than that.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
All roots of virtue consisting of merit from rejoicing and dedication have the profound perfection of wisdom as their foremost guide.

Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, they should always remain inseparable from the profound perfection of wisdom, rejoicing in all roots of goodness with a spirit of integration, and universally dedicating them toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!

As the Buddha has taught, all that is produced through conceptual discrimination is not truly existent. By what causes and conditions do these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas obtain incalculable, immeasurable, and boundless merit?"

"Bhagavān! That which is produced through conceptual discrimination cannot give rise to true right view; it cannot lead to the entry into the state of correctness and separation from birth (*samyaktva-niyāma*); nor can one thereby attain the fruit of a stream-enterer, or the fruit of a once-returner, or the fruit of a non-returner, or the fruit of an arhat, or the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, nor can one attain the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas."
The Buddha said,
“So it is, Subhūti! It is just so!”
It is so! It is as you have said.

Conceptualization and mental construction cannot give rise to true right view; they cannot lead one to enter the state of correctness and separation from birth (samyaktva-niyāma); nor can they result in the attainment of the fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, or the fruit of arhatship; nor can they result in the attainment of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha, or the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening of all Buddhas.
Subhūti! When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the profound perfection of wisdom, they know that all conceptual constructions are empty, non-existent, false, and unreal.
Why is this so? Subhūti!

Because all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have well studied internal emptiness, well studied external emptiness, well studied internal-and-external emptiness, well studied the emptiness of emptiness, well studied great emptiness, well studied the emptiness of the ultimate truth, well studied the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, well studied the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, well studied absolute emptiness, well studied boundless emptiness, well studied the emptiness of dispersion, well studied the emptiness of non-alteration, well studied the emptiness of intrinsic nature, well studied the emptiness of specific characteristics, well studied the emptiness of common characteristics, well studied the emptiness of all phenomena, well studied the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, well studied the emptiness of non-existence, well studied the emptiness of self-nature, and well studied the emptiness of the self-nature of non-existence.
"Subhūti! Once this bodhisattva mahāsattva is established in emptiness, however they observe, they discern that all conditioned things are empty, non-existent, false, and unreal—just so!"
It is so! One does not thereby remain far removed from the profound perfection of wisdom, Subhūti.
To the extent that this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not depart from the profound perfection of wisdom, in that same measure—
just so! just so!— they shall obtain incalculable, immeasurable, and boundless merit.
The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
What is the distinction between 'incalculable,' 'immeasurable,' and 'boundless'?"
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

That which is called ‘incalculable’ is such that its number cannot be apprehended; it cannot be counted within the realm of the conditioned, nor can it be counted within the realm of the unconditioned.”
As for "immeasurable," its measure cannot be apprehended; it is immeasurable within past phenomena, immeasurable within future phenomena, and immeasurable within present phenomena.
"Regarding 'boundless,' it means that no limit can be found, for its boundaries cannot be measured.
The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying,
"World-Honored One!"
Is there any cause or condition by which form (*rūpa*) is also incalculable, immeasurable, and boundless?
Are feeling (*vedanā*), perception (*saṃjñā*), formations (*saṃskāra*), and consciousness (*vijñāna*) also incalculable, immeasurable, and boundless?
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

By reason of certain causes and conditions, form (rūpa) is also incalculable, immeasurable, and boundless; feeling (vedanā), perception (saṃjñā), formations (saṃskāra), and consciousness (vijñāna) are likewise incalculable, immeasurable, and boundless.”
“World-Honored One!

For what reason and by what causes is form also incalculable, immeasurable, and boundless; and why are feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness also incalculable, immeasurable, and boundless?”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because form is empty, it is also incalculable, immeasurable, and boundless; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are empty, they too are incalculable, immeasurable, and boundless.”
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha,
saying: "World-Honored One, is it only form that is empty, and feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness that are empty, or are all phenomena likewise empty?"
The Buddha said,
“Subhūti, did I not previously say that all phenomena are empty?”
Subhūti replied, “Although the Buddha has already taught that all phenomena are empty, sentient beings do not know, see, or realize this; therefore, I have now asked this question again.”
“World-Honored One!
The Tathāgata has always said that form is empty, and that feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are also empty;
the Tathāgata has always said that the eye-base is empty, and that the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases are also empty.”
The Tathāgata has always taught that the sphere of form is empty, and that the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are likewise empty;
the Tathāgata has always taught that the eye-element is empty, and that the elements of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are likewise empty;
the Tathāgata has always taught that the form-element is empty, and that the elements of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are likewise empty.
The Tathāgata has always taught that the eye-consciousness element is empty, and that the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements are likewise empty;
the Tathāgata has always taught that eye-contact is empty, and that ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact are likewise empty;

the Tathāgata has always taught that all sensations produced with eye-contact as a condition are empty, and that all sensations produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions are likewise empty.
The Tathāgata has constantly taught that the earth element is empty, and that the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are also empty;
the Tathāgata has constantly taught that the nature of causes and conditions is empty, and that the nature of the immediate condition, the object-condition, and the dominant condition are also empty;

the Tathāgata has constantly taught that ignorance is empty, and that volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age and death are also empty.

The Tathāgata has constantly taught that the self is empty, and that sentient beings, life-principles, living beings, nourishers, persons, individuals, mind-born ones, young scholars, agents, experiencers, knowers, and seers are also empty;

the Tathāgata has constantly taught that the perfection of generosity is empty, and that the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are also empty.

The Tathāgata has always taught that internal emptiness is empty, and likewise external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are also empty.

The Tathāgata has always taught that True Suchness (tathatā) is empty, and likewise the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), non-falsity, non-alteration, equality, the nature of transcendence from birth, the fixedness of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the reality limit (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm are also empty.

The Tathāgata has always taught that the four foundations of mindfulness are empty; he has also taught that the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are likewise empty.
The Tathāgata has always taught that the noble truth of suffering is empty, and that the noble truths of the origin, cessation, and the path are likewise empty.
The Tathāgata has always taught that the four dhyānas are empty, and that the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are likewise empty.

The Tathāgata has constantly taught that the eight liberations (*aṣṭavimokṣa*) are empty; he has also constantly taught that the eight bases of mastery (*abhibhvāyatana*), the nine successive attainments (*navānupūrvavihārasamāpatti*), and the ten spheres of totality (*daśakṛtsnāyatana*) are likewise empty.

The Tathāgata has constantly taught that the gate of liberation of emptiness (*śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha*) is empty, and that the gates of liberation of signlessness (*animitta*) and wishlessness (*apraṇihita*) are also empty.

The Tathāgata has constantly taught that the Ground of Extreme Joy (*pramuditā-bhūmi*) is empty, and that the Ground of Purity (*vimalā*), the Ground of Radiance (*prabhākārī*), the Ground of Blazing Wisdom (*arciṣmatī*), the Ground Difficult to Conquer (*sudurjayā*), the Ground of Manifestation (*abhimukhī*), the Ground of Far-Going (*dūraṃgamā*), the Ground of Immovability (*acalā*), the Ground of Good Intelligence (*sādhumatī*), and the Ground of the Dharma Cloud (*dharmameghā*) are also empty.
The Tathāgata has always taught that the five eyes are empty, and the six supernormal powers are also empty;
the Tathāgata has always taught that the gates of samādhi are empty, and the gates of dhāraṇī are also empty;

the Tathāgata has always taught that the ten powers of a Buddha are empty, and likewise the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are also empty.
The Tathāgata constantly teaches that the quality of non-forgetfulness is empty, and that the state of constant abiding in equanimity is also empty;
the Tathāgata constantly teaches that all-knowledge is empty, and that the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are also empty;
the Tathāgata constantly teaches that the fruit of stream-entry is empty, and that the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are also empty.
The Tathāgata constantly teaches that the awakening of the pratyekabuddhas is empty;
the Tathāgata constantly teaches that all the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are empty;
and the Tathāgata constantly teaches that the unexcelled, perfect, and complete awakening of all Buddhas is empty.
The Tathāgata has constantly taught that the stage of the ordinary person is empty, and that the stages of the śrāvaka, pratyekabuddha, bodhisattva, and tathāgata are also empty.

The Tathāgata has constantly taught that material phenomena and immaterial phenomena are empty; likewise, visible phenomena and invisible phenomena, resistant phenomena and non-resistant phenomena, tainted phenomena and untainted phenomena, and conditioned phenomena and unconditioned phenomena are also empty.

The Tathāgata has constantly taught that past, future, and present phenomena are empty; likewise, wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate phenomena; phenomena bound to the desire realm, the form realm, and the formless realm; the phenomena of those in training, those beyond training, and those who are neither; and phenomena to be abandoned by vision, those to be abandoned by cultivation, and those not to be abandoned are also empty.
The Buddha said,
“So it is, Subhūti! It is so!”
"So it is! I have always taught that all these phenomena are empty.
The Venerable Subhūti then addressed the Buddha again, saying:
“World-Honored One!
The emptiness of all dharmas is itself inexhaustible; it is also incalculable, immeasurable, and boundless.
World-Honored One!”

Within the emptiness of all phenomena, exhaustion cannot be apprehended, number cannot be apprehended, measure cannot be apprehended, and limit cannot be apprehended. For this reason, there is no distinction between the meanings of the terms "exhaustless," "innumerable," "immeasurable," and "boundless."
The Buddha said:
“Excellent, Subhūti! It is so!”
So it is! It is as you have said.
The inexhaustible, the incalculable, the immeasurable, and the boundless—these expressions are not distinct in meaning, for they all collectively reveal and clarify the emptiness of all phenomena.

"Subhūti! All dharmas are empty and are all ineffable; yet through skillful means, the Tathāgata speaks of them as inexhaustible, or as innumerable, or as immeasurable, or as boundless, or as empty, or as signless, or as wishless, or as unconditioned, or as unarisen, or as unceasing, or as free from defilement, or as quiescence, or as nirvāṇa, or as suchness, or as the dharma-realm, or as the nature of phenomena, or as the limit of reality. Such meanings as these are all the Tathāgata’s skillful explications."
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
The Tathāgata possesses most marvelous skillful means; although the true nature of all phenomena cannot be expressed in words, he manifests it through skillful means for the sake of sentient beings.”
“World-Honored One!
As I understand the meaning of what the Buddha has taught, the nature of all phenomena is ultimately ineffable.
The Buddha said:
“Excellent, Subhūti! It is so, it is so!”
The nature of all phenomena is entirely ineffable. Why is this?
Because the nature of all phenomena is ultimately empty, and there is nothing that can be proclaimed to be ultimately empty.
The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
does the ineffable meaning increase or decrease?”
The Buddha said,
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
The ineffable meaning neither increases nor decreases.”
The Venerable Subhūti spoke again:
“World-Honored One!

If the ineffable meaning neither increases nor decreases, then the perfection of generosity should also neither increase nor decrease; likewise, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom should also neither increase nor decrease.”
“World-Honored One!

If the ineffable meaning neither increases nor decreases, then the four foundations of mindfulness should also neither increase nor decrease; likewise, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path should also neither increase nor decrease.”
“World-Honored One!

If the ineffable meaning neither increases nor decreases, then the four dhyānas should also neither increase nor decrease, and the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments should likewise neither increase nor decrease.”
“World-Honored One!

If the meaning that cannot be expressed neither increases nor decreases, then the eight liberations should also neither increase nor decrease; likewise, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities should also neither increase nor decrease.”
“World-Honored One!

If the ineffable meaning neither increases nor decreases, then the gate of liberation of emptiness (*śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha*) should likewise neither increase nor decrease; the gates of liberation of signlessness (*animitta-vimokṣamukha*) and wishlessness (*apraṇihita-vimokṣamukha*) should likewise neither increase nor decrease.”
“World-Honored One!
