'By what skillful means shall I rescue these classes of sentient beings, causing them to abandon their inclination toward the vehicles of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, and instead incline them solely toward the unsurpassed Great Vehicle?'"
Having reflected thus, he made this aspiration:

"I shall apply myself with diligence, disregarding body and life, to practice the six perfections (*ṣaṭ-pāramitā*), to bring sentient beings to maturity, and to purify Buddha-fields, so that I may swiftly fulfill [these requirements] and rapidly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*). In my Buddha-field, all classes of sentient beings shall seek only unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; they shall not delight in the fruits of the Śrāvaka or Pratyekabuddha vehicles, to the point that even the names of the two vehicles do not exist, and they hear only the various merits of the Mahāyāna."
"Subhūti! By means of these six perfections, this bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring them to fulfillment and draw near to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who fully cultivate the six perfections and see sentient beings giving rise to overweening pride (*adhimāna*). These beings have not yet truly abstained from taking life, yet they claim, 'I have truly abstained from taking life'; they have not yet truly abstained from taking what is not given or engaging in sexual misconduct, yet they claim, 'I have truly abstained from taking what is not given and engaging in sexual misconduct';

they have not yet truly abstained from false speech, yet they claim, 'I have truly abstained from false speech'; and they have not yet truly abstained from harsh speech, divisive speech, or frivolous speech, yet they claim, 'I have truly abstained from harsh speech, divisive speech, and frivolous speech.'

Not having truly abandoned sensual desire, one claims, "I have truly abandoned sensual desire"; not having truly abandoned ill will and abandoned wrong views, one claims, "I have truly abandoned ill will and abandoned wrong views";

not having attained the first dhyāna, one claims to have attained the first dhyāna; not having attained the second, third, or fourth dhyānas, one claims to have attained the second, third, or fourth dhyānas;

not having attained the sphere of infinite space, one claims to have attained the sphere of infinite space; and not having attained the spheres of infinite consciousness, nothingness, or neither-perception-nor-non-perception, one claims to have attained the spheres of infinite consciousness, nothingness, or neither-perception-nor-non-perception.

Not having attained the immeasurable of loving-kindness (*maitrī*), they claim to have attained the immeasurable of loving-kindness; not having attained the immeasurables of compassion (*karuṇā*), sympathetic joy (*muditā*), and equanimity (*upekṣā*), they claim to have attained the immeasurables of compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity.

Not having attained the supernormal power of the realization of the knowledge of the bases of psychic power (*ṛddhividhi-jñāna-sākṣātkriyā-abhijñā*), they claim to have attained the supernormal power of the realization of the knowledge of the bases of psychic power; not having attained the supernormal powers of the divine eye, the divine ear, the knowledge of others' minds, and the recollection of past lives (*pūrvanivāsānusmṛti-jñāna-sākṣātkriyā-abhijñā*), they claim to have attained the supernormal powers of the divine eye, the divine ear, the knowledge of others' minds, and the recollection of past lives.

Not having attained the contemplation of impurity (*aśubha-bhāvanā*), they claim to have attained the contemplation of impurity; not having attained the contemplations of loving-kindness, compassion, mindfulness of breathing (*ānāpānasmṛti*), dependent origination (*pratītyasamutpāda*), and the analysis of the elements (*dhātuprabheda*), they claim to have attained the contemplations of loving-kindness, compassion, mindfulness of breathing, dependent origination, and the analysis of the elements.

Not having attained the stage of śamatha-vipaśyanā, they claim to have attained the stage of śamatha-vipaśyanā; not having attained the stage of gotrabhū, the eighth stage, the stage of vision, the stage of refinement, the stage of freedom from desire, or the stage of completion, they claim to have attained the stage of gotrabhū, the eighth stage, the stage of vision, the stage of refinement, the stage of freedom from desire, or the stage of completion;
not having attained the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, they claim to have attained the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha;

not having attained the perfection of generosity, they claim to have attained the perfection of generosity; and not having attained the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom, they claim to have attained the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom.

Not having realized internal emptiness, one claims to have realized internal emptiness; not having realized external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, one claims to have realized external emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

Not having realized suchness, they claim to have realized suchness; not having realized the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the non-erroneous nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the state free from birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm, they claim to have realized the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm;

not having realized the noble truth of suffering, they claim to have realized the noble truth of suffering; not having realized the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, they claim to have realized the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path;

not having attained the four foundations of mindfulness, they claim to have attained the four foundations of mindfulness; not having attained the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path, they claim to have attained the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path.
They claim to have attained the four dhyānas when they have not attained them; they claim to have attained the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments when they have not attained them;

they claim to have attained the eight liberations when they have not attained them; they claim to have attained the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative concentrations, and the ten totalities when they have not attained them;

they claim to have attained the gate of liberation of emptiness when they have not attained it; and they claim to have attained the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness when they have not attained them.

Not having attained the Ground of Utmost Joy, they claim to have attained the Ground of Utmost Joy; not having attained the Ground of Freedom from Defilement, the Ground of Radiant Light, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Supreme Difficulty to Conquer, the Ground of Presence, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, or the Ground of Dharma Clouds, they claim to have attained the Ground of Freedom from Defilement up to the Ground of Dharma Clouds;
not having attained the five eyes, they claim to have attained the five eyes; not having attained the six supernormal powers, they claim to have attained the six supernormal powers;
not having attained the gateways of samādhi, they claim to have attained the gateways of samādhi; and not having attained the gateways of dhāraṇī, they claim to have attained the gateways of dhāraṇī.

Not having attained the ten powers of a Buddha, they claim to have attained the ten powers of a Buddha; not having attained the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, they claim to have attained the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;

not having attained the quality of non-forgetfulness, they claim to have attained the quality of non-forgetfulness; not having attained the state of constant abiding in equanimity, they claim to have attained the state of constant abiding in equanimity;

not having attained all-knowledge, they claim to have attained all-knowledge; and not having attained the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects, they claim to have attained the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects.
That which has not yet purified the Buddha-fields is called purifying the Buddha-fields; that which has not yet matured sentient beings is called maturing sentient beings;
that which has not yet mastered worldly crafts and arts is called mastering worldly crafts and arts;
that which has not yet practiced the conduct of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva is called practicing the conduct of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva.
Having not yet attained unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, they claim to have attained unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
"Subhūti! Having seen this, that bodhisattva mahāsattva reflects as follows:"
"How shall I rescue these classes of sentient beings and cause them to be free from the fetter of overweening pride?
Having reflected thus, he made this vow:

"I shall apply myself with diligence, regardless of body or life, to practice the six perfections, to bring sentient beings to maturity, and to purify the Buddha-fields, so that I may swiftly fulfill [the requirements] and quickly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. In my Buddha-field, there shall be no such as those possessed of overweening pride; all sentient beings shall be free from overweening pride."
"Subhūti! By means of these six perfections, this bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring them to fulfillment and draw near to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
"Furthermore, Subhūti,

there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who fully cultivate the six perfections and see sentient beings clinging to various phenomena— namely, clinging to form, clinging to feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness;
clinging to the eye base, and clinging to the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind bases."
They are attached to the sphere of form; they are attached to the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena.
They are attached to the eye-element; they are attached to the elements of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.
They are attached to the form-element; they are attached to the elements of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena.
They cling to the eye-consciousness element; they cling to the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements.
They cling to eye-contact; they cling to ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact.
They cling to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition; they cling to the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions.
They cling to the earth element, and they cling to the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements;
they cling to the nature of causes and conditions, and they cling to the nature of the equal-and-immediate condition, the object-condition, and the dominant condition;
they cling to ignorance, and they cling to volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, existence, birth, and old age and death.
They cling to a self; they cling to a sentient being, a life-force, a living being, a nourisher, a spirit, a person, a soul, a human, a youth, an agent, an experiencer, a knower, and a seer;
they cling to the perfection of generosity; and they cling to the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.

They cling to internal emptiness; they cling to external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

They cling to suchness; they cling to the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, non-alteration, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm.
They cling to the noble truth of suffering; they cling to the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path.

They cling to the four foundations of mindfulness; they cling to the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path;
they cling to the four dhyānas; they cling to the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments;
they cling to the eight liberations, the eight spheres of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten spheres of totality.
They cling to the gate of liberation of emptiness; they cling to the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness;

they cling to the Ground of Extreme Joy, the Ground of Purity, the Ground of Radiant Light, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Difficult Victory, the Ground of Manifestation, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, and the Ground of Dharma Clouds;
they cling to the five eyes; they cling to the six supernormal powers.
They are attached to the gateways of samādhi; they are attached to the gateways of dhāraṇī;

they are attached to the ten powers of a Buddha; they are attached to the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
they are attached to the quality of non-forgetfulness; and they are attached to the nature of constant dwelling in equanimity.
They cling to all-knowledge; they cling to the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects;
they cling to the fruit of stream-entry; they cling to the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship;
they cling to the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha.
They cling to the practice of a bodhisattva mahāsattva;
they cling to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. "Subhūti!
Having seen this, the bodhisattva mahāsattva reflects:
"How shall I rescue these classes of sentient beings and cause them to be free from attachment?"
Having reflected thus, he made this aspiration:

"I shall practice with diligence, disregarding even body and life, cultivating the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā) to ripen sentient beings and purify Buddha-fields, so that I may swiftly fulfill all requirements and quickly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; and within my Buddha-field, may the various classes of sentient beings be free from such diverse attachments."
"Subhūti! By means of these six perfections, this bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring them to fulfillment and draw near to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
"Furthermore, Subhūti,

there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who fully cultivate the six perfections and perceive that the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas have a limited radiance, a limited lifespan, and a finite number of disciples."
"Subhūti! Having seen this, the bodhisattva mahāsattva reflects thus:
'How may I attain immeasurable radiance, immeasurable lifespan, and a retinue of disciples whose number is without limit?'"
Having reflected thus, he made this vow:

"I shall apply myself with diligence, disregarding body and life, to practice the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā), to bring sentient beings to maturity, and to purify Buddha-fields, so that I may swiftly fulfill [these requirements] and quickly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. At that time, my own body’s radiance shall be immeasurable, my lifespan immeasurable, and the number of my disciples limitless."
"Subhūti! By means of these six perfections, this bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring them to fulfillment and draw near to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
"Furthermore, Subhūti,
there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who fully cultivate the six perfections and perceive a buddha-field inhabited by a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha as being circular and finite in extent."
"Subhūti! Having seen this, that bodhisattva mahāsattva reflects:
'How may I obtain a Buddha-field for my dwelling that is perfectly round and immeasurable?'"
Having reflected thus, he made this vow:

"I shall apply myself with diligence, disregarding body and life, to practice the six perfections, maturing sentient beings and purifying Buddha-fields, so that I may swiftly fulfill [the requirements] and quickly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. May the great trichiliocosms in each of the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, merge into a single land; therein I shall dwell, teaching the Dharma and transforming immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings."
"Subhūti! By means of these six perfections, this bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly bring them to fulfillment and draw near to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
"Furthermore, Subhūti,

there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who fully cultivate the six perfections and perceive that the cycle of birth and death for sentient beings is long and far-reaching, and that the realm of sentient beings is infinite in number."
"Subhūti! Having seen this, the bodhisattva mahāsattva reflects thus:

'The limits of birth and death are like space, and the realm of sentient beings is likewise. Although there are no truly existent sentient beings who transmigrate through birth and death or attain nirvāṇa, sentient beings falsely cling to them as being real, wandering in saṃsāra and undergoing boundless suffering. By what skillful means should I rescue and deliver them?'"
Having reflected thus, he made this vow:

"I shall diligently apply myself, regardless of body or life, to practice the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā), maturing sentient beings and purifying Buddha-fields, so that I may swiftly fulfill [the requirements] and rapidly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. For the sake of all sentient beings, I shall preach the unsurpassed Dharma, causing them all to be liberated from the great suffering of birth and death, and also leading them to realize and know that both birth and death and liberation are entirely non-existent and ultimately empty."
"Subhūti! By means of these six perfections, this bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly attain fulfillment and draw near to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening."

Chapter 52: The Gaṅgā Devī. Part One: The Gaṅgā Devī Chapter, Number Fifty-Two. At that time, there was a goddess in the assembly named Gaṅgā Devī. She rose from her seat, bared her left shoulder, knelt with her right knee on the ground, joined her palms toward the Buddha, and addressed him, saying:
“World-Honored One!

I shall practice the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; I shall bring sentient beings to maturity and purify a buddha-field, so that the qualities of the field I seek shall be entirely complete, just as the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha has described them for the great assembly in this profound Sūtra of the Perfection of Wisdom.

When the goddess Gaṅgā had spoken these words, she immediately took various golden flowers, silver flowers, and flowers grown on land and in water, as well as various ornaments, and holding a pair of golden celestial robes, she scattered them over the Buddha with reverent sincerity.

By the spiritual power of the Buddha, [the assembly] leaped upward into the void and circled to the right; above the crown of the Buddha’s head, it transformed into a jeweled terrace with four pillars and four corners, exquisitely adorned and most delightful.
Thereupon, the goddess took this jeweled terrace and dedicated it for the common possession of all sentient beings, dedicating it toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

At that time, the Tathāgata, knowing that the goddess’s aspirations were profound and vast, smiled. It is the natural law of all Buddhas that when they smile, various rays of light issue from their mouths; now the Buddha did likewise, emitting various lights—blue, yellow, red, white, crimson, azure, purple, and green—from his face, which illuminated the immeasurable, boundless, and innumerable worlds of the ten directions. These lights then returned to this land, manifesting great spiritual transformations, circumambulating the Buddha three times, and entering the crown of the Buddha’s head.
At that time, having witnessed this event, Ānanda rose from his seat, knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms toward the Buddha, and said:
"World-Honored One!"
"For what cause and for what reason do you manifest this smile?
The smiles of all Buddhas are never without cause or condition.
The Buddha told Ānanda:

"In the future, this goddess shall attain Buddhahood; the eon shall be named Star Simile (Tārakopama), and the Buddha shall be named Golden Flower (Suvarṇapuṣpa) Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed Worthy, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, Buddha, Bhagavān."

Ānanda, you should know that this goddess has received her female body for the very last time; after she casts off this body, she will receive a male body and shall never again become a woman until the end of the future.

Having passed away from here, she will be reborn in the eastern world-system of the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Akṣobhya, a most delightful Buddha-field. There, in the presence of that Buddha, she will diligently cultivate the holy life; in that realm, this woman shall also be known as Suvarṇapuṣpā, as she practices the various deeds of a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva.

Ānanda! This Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Golden Flower, having passed away from that place, will be reborn in other directions, traveling from one Buddha-field to another Buddha-field, never being separated from a Buddha in every place of his birth.

Just as a wheel-turning monarch, from one palace terrace to another, enjoys pleasures and delights until the end of his life without ever setting foot upon the ground, so too it is with the Bodhisattva Golden Flower: from one buddha-field to another, until he attains unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, he shall never be separated from a Buddha throughout his successive births, hearing and receiving the true Dharma and practicing the bodhisattva path.
At that time, Ānanda had this thought to himself:

"When the Bodhisattva Golden Flower attains Buddhahood, he too shall proclaim the profound Prajñāpāramitā, and the number of the assembly of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas in his gathering shall be equal to that of the present Buddha’s assembly of Bodhisattvas."
The Buddha, knowing his thought, addressed Ānanda, saying: "So it is! So it is!"

Just as you have conceived, when the Bodhisattva Golden Flower (Suvarṇapuṣpa) attains Buddhahood, he too shall proclaim this profound Prajñāpāramitā for the sake of an assembly; the number of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas in that assembly shall be equal to the number in the present assembly of the Buddha’s Bodhisattvas.

Ānanda, you should know that when this Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Suvarṇapuṣpa attains Buddhahood, the number of his disciples who leave the household life in that Buddha-world will be so vast as to be beyond calculation. “Subhūti! By virtue of these causes and conditions, this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not fall into the levels of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, but swiftly realizes unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”

“Subhūti! “Subhūti! It is like a strong man well-versed in the art of archery who, wishing to display his skill, shoots an arrow upward into the air. However, since sentient beings practice what is not the True Dharma, I shall repeatedly induce for their sake the liberations of tranquility, emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, so as to deliver them; yet though I repeatedly induce them, I shall not personally realize [nirvāṇa] therein.'"

"Subhūti! Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva has accomplished the power of skillful means, although he frequently manifests the three gates of liberation, he does not realize the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) in the interim. Until he has attained the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), he must first attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment before he finally realizes it."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas constantly delight in observing the profound depths; that is to say, they delight in observing internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence. They also delight in observing that the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, the eightfold noble path, as well as the doors of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are all empty of their own characteristics.
“Subhūti! Having made this observation, the bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to this thought:

‘Beings, through the power of evil friends, for a long night give rise to the conception of a self, the conception of a being, the conception of a life-sustainer, the conception of a living being, the conception of a nourisher, the conception of a person, the conception of an individual, the conception of a mind-born, the conception of a youth, the conception of an agent, the conception of an experiencer, the conception of a knower, and the conception of a viewer. Because they act with these conceptions, they apprehend objects; thus they cycle through birth and death, undergoing various sufferings.’”

In order to sever such conceptual attachments among sentient beings, one should aspire to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment and preach the profound and sublime Dharma for all sentient beings, so that they may sever their conceptual attachments and be liberated from the suffering of saṃsāra.
“Subhūti! At that time, although this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the gate of liberation of emptiness, he does not rely upon it to realize the limit of reality;
although he practices the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, he likewise does not rely upon them to realize the limit of reality.”

Because they do not realize the limit of reality, they do not fall into the fruit of stream-entry, once-returning, non-returning, or arhatship, nor do they fall into the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha.

“Subhūti! By means of such mindfulness, this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom and accomplishes roots of goodness without realizing the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*). Although they do not immediately realize the limit of reality, they do not fall away from the four dhyānas, nor do they fall away from the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments;

nor do they fall away from the four foundations of mindfulness, nor do they fall away from the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path.”
Furthermore, they do not fall away from the eight liberations; nor do they fall away from the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, or the ten universal bases.
They do not fall away from the liberation door of emptiness, nor do they fall away from the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness.

They do not fall away from internal emptiness, nor do they fall away from external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

Nor do they fall away from true suchness; nor do they fall away from the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, or the inconceivable realm.
Nor do they fall away from the noble truth of suffering, nor do they fall away from the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path.
Nor do they fall away from the perfection of generosity, nor do they fall away from the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
Furthermore, they do not fall away from the five eyes, nor do they fall away from the six supernormal powers;
they do not fall away from any of the doors of dhāraṇī, nor do they fall away from any of the doors of samādhi;

they do not fall away from the ten powers of a Buddha, nor do they fall away from the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; nor do they fall away from great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, or great equanimity.
They do not fall away from nor lose the quality of non-forgetfulness; they do not fall away from nor lose the nature of constant equanimity;
they do not fall away from nor lose all-knowledge, nor do they fall away from nor lose the knowledge of the aspects of the path or the knowledge of all aspects.

“Subhūti! At that time, this bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes all factors conducive to enlightenment (bodhipakṣadharma), and until he realizes unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, his various merits never decline.”

Subhūti! Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom and is sustained by skillful means, their pure qualities (*śukladharma*) increase moment by moment, and their faculties become so sharp and keen that they surpass all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.
"Furthermore, Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly reflects thus:

'Throughout the long night, the minds of all sentient beings have been perpetually inverted by the four inversions—namely, the inversion of perception, the inversion of mind, and the inversion of view regarding permanence; the inversion of perception, the inversion of mind, and the inversion of view regarding pleasure; the inversion of perception, the inversion of mind, and the inversion of view regarding self; and the inversion of perception, the inversion of mind, and the inversion of view regarding purity.'"

"For the sake of such sentient beings as these, I should proceed toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and upon realizing unsurpassed, great enlightenment, preach the unerring Dharma for all sentient beings. That is to say, I shall teach that saṃsāra is impermanent, without bliss, without self, and without purity; whereas only nirvāṇa is tranquil and sublime, fully endowed with the various true merits of permanence, bliss, self, and purity."

"Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes this mindfulness and practices the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), being sustained by skillful means (upāyakauśalya), they will never enter the supreme concentration of a Tathāgata until they have perfected the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha."

“Subhūti! Although at that time this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—and enters and emerges from them with mastery, he does not yet realize the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi). This is because until his unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, his cultivation of merit through practice has not yet reached full perfection; thus, he does not realize the limit of reality or other such merits. Only when he attains unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment will he be able to realize them.”
Subhūti! At that time, although this bodhisattva mahāsattva has not yet perfected the cultivation of other virtues, he has already perfected the cultivation of the door of the wishless samādhi.
"Furthermore, Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly reflects thus:

'Throughout the long night, sentient beings have practiced with the apprehension of something to be attained—namely, they cling to the notion of a self, or they cling to the notions of a sentient being, a life-principle, a living being, a nourisher, a spirit, a person, a soul, a mind-born, a youth, an agent, an experiencer, a knower, or a seer;'"
Some cling to the existence of form; some cling to the existence of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness;
some cling to the existence of the eye-base; some cling to the existence of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-base;
some cling to the existence of the form-base; or they cling to the existence of the sound, odor, taste, tangible, or mental-object base.
Some cling to the existence of the eye-element; some cling to the existence of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-element.
Some cling to the existence of the form-element; some cling to the existence of the sound, odor, taste, tangible, or mental-object-element.
Some cling to the existence of the eye-consciousness-element; some cling to the existence of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-consciousness-element.
Some cling to the existence of eye-contact; some cling to the existence of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact.
Some cling to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition; some cling to the various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact as condition.
Some cling to the existence of the earth element; some cling to the existence of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements.

Some cling to the existence of ignorance; some cling to the existence of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age and death;
some cling to the existence of the ten paths of wholesome action;
and some cling to the existence of the four dhyānas, or the four immeasurables, or the four formless attainments.
Or, there may be those who cling to the existence of the four means of attraction (*saṃgrahavastu*).

For the sake of such sentient beings, I should proceed toward unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment and cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, so that when I realize unsurpassed, great enlightenment, I may cause all sentient beings to forever sever such clinging to objective apprehension.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes this mindfulness and practices the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), being sustained by skillful means (upāyakauśalya), they do not realize the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) as long as the Buddha’s ten powers (daśabala), four fearlessnesses (vaiśāradya), four analytical knowledges (pratisaṃvid), great loving-kindness (maitrī), great compassion (karuṇā), great sympathetic joy (muditā), great equanimity (upekṣā), and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (āveṇikabuddhadharma) are not yet fully perfected.”

Subhūti! At that time, although this bodhisattva mahāsattva is not without practicing the concentration gates of signlessness and wishlessness, he has perfected his cultivation solely of the concentration gate of emptiness.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they see that sentient beings, through the power of evil friends, have for a long night been attached to immeasurable kinds of signs—namely, attachment to the sign of woman, the sign of man, the sign of form, the sign of sound, the sign of odor, the sign of taste, the sign of touch, and the sign of mental objects—and constantly think:

'For the sake of such sentient beings, I should proceed toward unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment, cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and when I realize unsurpassed, great enlightenment, cause all sentient beings to forever be free from such attachment to signs.'"

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes this mindfulness and practices the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), being sustained by skillful means (upāyakauśalya), they do not realize the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) as long as the Buddha’s ten powers (daśabala), four fearlessnesses (vaiśāradya), four analytical knowledges (pratisaṃvid), great loving-kindness (maitrī), great compassion (karuṇā), great sympathetic joy (muditā), great equanimity (upekṣā), and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (āveṇikabuddhadharma) have not yet been perfected.”

"Subhūti! At that time, although this bodhisattva mahāsattva is not without practicing the gateways of the samādhis of emptiness and wishlessness, he has already brought the practice of the gateway of the samādhi of signlessness to full completion."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva has already well practiced and studied the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence,
meditative concentration, and wisdom, and has already well established themselves in inner emptiness, outer [emptiness], and..."
Emptiness, internal and external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena,
the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration,
the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, and the emptiness of non-apprehensibility.
Emptiness, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence; having well established themselves in suchness,
the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-falsity, the immutability, the equality,
the state beyond arising, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, and the realm of space.
In this inconceivable realm, they have already well established themselves in the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path;

they have already well trained in the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path; and they have already well trained in emptiness and signlessness.
The door of liberation of wishlessness, as well as the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges,
great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha,
and all other immeasurable and boundless Buddha-dharmas, have been thoroughly cultivated and mastered.

"Subhūti! It is impossible for a bodhisattva mahāsattva who has accomplished such merit and wisdom to conceive a notion of pleasure regarding saṃsāra, or to describe it as pleasant, or to dwell with attachment within the triple world."

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva has already well trained in the factors of enlightenment and in the dharmas of all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, as well as the assembly of bodhisattva mahāsattvas, one should question him thus:

‘If a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, how should he train in the factors of enlightenment so that he does not realize emptiness, signlessness, wishlessness, non-arising, non-cessation, non-activity, the unconditioned, the absence of intrinsic nature, and the reality limit?’”

Because they do not realize [these fruits], how is it that they do not fall into the fruit of a stream-enterer, once-returner, non-returner, arhat, or pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, yet diligently practice the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) while always remaining without attachment?
“Subhūti! When this Bodhisattva Mahāsattva is asked such a question, if he should answer thus:

‘Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas who wish to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment should only contemplate emptiness, signlessness, wishlessness, non-arising, non-cessation, non-action, the unconditioned, the absence of intrinsic nature, and the limit of reality, as well as all other factors conducive to enlightenment; they should not practice or study [anything else].’”

"Subhūti, you should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has not yet received from the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, the prophecy of non-retrogression regarding unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
Why is this? Subhūti!

This bodhisattva mahāsattva has not yet been able to demonstrate, predict, or clarify the characteristics of the dharmas practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva who abides in the stage of non-retrogression.
“Subhūti! When this bodhisattva mahāsattva receives such a question, if he should answer thus:

‘Bodhisattvas mahāsattvas who wish to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening should correctly contemplate emptiness, signlessness, wishlessness, non-arising, non-cessation, non-activity, the unconditioned, the absence of intrinsic nature, and the reality-limit, as well as all other factors conducive to awakening; furthermore, they should skillfully train in the means as previously described, yet not realize [these states].’”

"Subhūti, you should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has already received from the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, the prediction of non-retrogression regarding unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
Why is this? Subhūti!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva has already been able to reveal, predict, and clarify the characteristics of the dharmas practiced by bodhisattva mahāsattvas who abide in the stage of non-retrogression.

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is unable to explain, predict, or clarify the characteristics of the dharmas practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva who dwells in the stage of non-retrogression, you should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has not yet well cultivated the factors of enlightenment consisting of the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; that he has not yet entered the Stage of Thinness (tanubhūmi); and that he has not yet explained, predicted, clarified, or established himself in the stage of non-retrogression in the manner of other bodhisattva mahāsattvas who dwell in the stage of non-retrogression.”

"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to reveal, predict, and clarify the characteristics of the dharmas practiced by a bodhisattva mahāsattva who dwells in the stage of non-retrogression, you should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has already well cultivated the factors conducive to enlightenment—namely, the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom—and has entered the Stage of Thinness (tanubhūmi). He has already revealed, predicted, clarified, and established himself in the stage of non-retrogression, just like all other bodhisattva mahāsattvas who dwell in the stage of non-retrogression."
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
is there any bodhisattva mahāsattva who has not yet attained the stage of non-retrogression yet is able to provide such a response in accordance with reality?”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!
There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, although they have not yet attained the stage of non-retrogression, are nevertheless able to provide such a response in accordance with reality.”

"Subhūti! Although this bodhisattva mahāsattva has not yet attained the stage of non-retrogression, he is able to cultivate the factors conducive to enlightenment—namely, the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom—and his awakened intelligence has already reached maturity and sharpness. Whether he hears it or not, he is able to answer according to reality, just like a bodhisattva mahāsattva who resides in the stage of non-retrogression."
The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

There are many bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, yet few are able to answer correctly, because they abide in stages that have not been well-cultivated, unlike those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas at the stage of non-retrogression whose stages have already been well-cultivated.”
The Buddha said, “So it is, Subhūti!”
So it is! It is as you have said. Why is this?

"Subhūti! Few are the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who receive such a prophecy of the subtle wisdom of the stage of non-retrogression; and those who do receive such a prophecy are all able to provide a response to this in accordance with reality."

"Subhūti! If one can provide such a response in accordance with reality, you should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva’s roots of goodness are clear and sharp, and cannot be destroyed by the gods, humans, asuras, or others in the world."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, even in a dream, does not take pleasure in or praise the levels of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, nor does he raise his mind to take pleasure in or praise the phenomena of the three realms; and though he constantly contemplates all phenomena as being like a dream, like an illusion, like an echo, like an image, like a reflection, like a mirage, like a magical creation, and like a city of gandharvas, he does not realize the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi)."
"Subhūti, you should know that these are the signs of a bodhisattva mahāsattva who is non-retrogressive. Furthermore, Subhūti!"
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva sees in a dream a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, surrounded by immeasurable multitudes,
immeasurable hundreds of multitudes, immeasurable thousands of multitudes, immeasurable hundreds of thousands of multitudes,
immeasurable koṭis of multitudes, immeasurable hundreds of koṭis of multitudes, immeasurable thousands of koṭis of multitudes, immeasurable...
There were hundreds of thousands of koṭis, immeasurable nayutas, immeasurable hundreds of nayutas,
immeasurable thousands of nayutas, and immeasurable hundreds of thousands of nayutas of beings—
namely, bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, devas, nāgas, and so forth.

Yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and others surrounded him with reverence as he preached the Dharma; having heard the Dharma, they well understood its meaning and intent;
having understood the meaning and intent, they practiced with diligence, conducting themselves in accordance with the Dharma.
Furthermore, Subhūti, you should know that practicing with harmony and respect, as well as practicing in accordance with the Dharma,
are the signs of a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, in a dream, sees a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha—endowed with the thirty-two marks of a great man and fully adorned with the eighty secondary characteristics, with a halo one fathom wide radiating light all around, leaping into the air together with a community of bhikṣus, manifesting great supernormal powers and preaching the essentials of the True Dharma, and creating emanations that travel to other infinite buddha-fields to perform the work of a Buddha."
"Subhūti, you should know that these are the signs of a bodhisattva mahāsattva who is non-retrogressive. Furthermore, Subhūti!"

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva sees in a dream mad bandits destroying villages and cities; or sees a fire breaking out and burning down a settlement; or sees tigers, wolves, lions, fierce beasts, venomous snakes, and vicious scorpions intending to harm his body; or sees an enemy wishing to cut off his head; or sees his father, mother, brothers, sisters, wife, children, or close friends on the verge of death; or sees himself afflicted by cold, heat, hunger, thirst, and other such painful conditions.
Upon seeing such terrifying things as these, they are neither startled nor afraid, nor do they feel distress; having awakened from the dream, they are immediately able to reflect:

"The three realms are false and provisional, all like what was seen in a dream. When I realize unsurpassed great bodhi, I shall proclaim to all sentient beings that everything within the three realms is illusory, just like the scenes in a dream."
“Suvīra, you should know that this is the mark of a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva. Furthermore, Suvīra!”
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, even in a dream, sees sentient beings in the realms of hell, animals, or hungry ghosts, they should form this thought:

"I shall diligently cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva and swiftly proceed toward unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment. I vow that when I attain unsurpassed, great bodhi, there shall be no sentient beings in the realms of hell, animals, or hungry ghosts within my buddha-field, nor even the names of any evil destinies."
Upon awakening from the dream, he also thinks this. Subhūti,
you should know that when this bodhisattva mahāsattva attains buddhahood, there will certainly be no evil realms within that buddha-field.
Why is this? Subhūti!
Whether in a dream or when awake, all phenomena are non-dual and cannot be divided into two.
"Subhūti, you should know that these are the signs of a bodhisattva mahāsattva who is non-retrogressive. Furthermore, Subhūti!"
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while dreaming, sees fire burning sentient beings in the hells and other realms, or sees cities, towns, and villages being consumed by flames, they then make this vow:

"If I have already received the prediction of non-retrogression and shall attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, may these great fires be instantly extinguished and transformed into coolness."

"Subhūti! When this bodhisattva mahāsattva has made such a vow, if the fire seen in his dream is immediately extinguished, you should know that he is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva. If, after making such a vow, the fire is not extinguished, you should know that he has not yet attained the stage of non-retrogression."
"Subhūti, you should know that these are the signs of a bodhisattva mahāsattva who is non-retrogressive. Furthermore, Subhūti!"
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while awake, suddenly sees a great fire breaking out that burns cities and towns, or perhaps burns villages, they should then form this thought:

"Whether I am in a dream or in the waking state, I have previously seen the practices, marks, and signs of my own stage of non-retrogression; I do not yet know their reality or unreality. If what I have seen truly exists, may this great fire be instantly extinguished and transformed into coolness."

"Subhūti! If, when this bodhisattva mahāsattva makes such a vow and utters these words of truth, the great fire is immediately and suddenly extinguished, you should know that he is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva. If, however, the fire is not extinguished when he makes such a vow and utters these words of truth, you should know that he has not yet attained the stage of non-retrogression."
"Subhūti, you should know that these are the signs of a bodhisattva mahāsattva who is non-retrogressive. Furthermore, Subhūti!"
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while awake, sees fire burning various cities or villages, he should form this thought:

"Whether I am in a dream or in the waking state, I have previously seen the practices, marks, and signs of my own stage of non-retrogression. If what I have seen is certainly real and I will surely attain unsurpassed great enlightenment, may this great fire be instantly extinguished and transformed into coolness."

"Subhūti! After this bodhisattva mahāsattva has made this vow and uttered these words of truth, at that time the great fire does not immediately go out; rather, it burns one house and skips another, then burns yet another house; or it burns one alleyway and skips another, then burns yet another alleyway. In this manner, as it spreads from one to another, the fire finally goes out."

"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva should know for himself that he has definitely attained the stage of non-retrogression. However, as for those who are being burned, it is because those sentient beings have created and accumulated karma that destroys the True Dharma; by virtue of this karma, they first fell into the evil destinies and underwent the full retribution of suffering for immeasurable kalpas. Now, having been born in the human realm, they undergo the remaining traces of that karma. Or, by virtue of this karma, they are destined to fall into the evil destinies and undergo the full retribution of suffering for immeasurable kalpas, yet now, while in the human realm, they first manifest these minor traces of their past."
"Subhūti, you should know that these are the signs of a bodhisattva mahāsattva who is non-retrogressive. Furthermore, Subhūti!"
Based on the various causes and conditions previously explained, one knows this to be a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva.

Furthermore, there are other accomplishments of practices, marks, and signs by which one knows this to be a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva; I shall now speak of them for you, so you should listen attentively!
Subhūti replied, “Indeed! I pray that you will speak.”
The Buddha told Subhūti:
"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva sees a man or a woman who has been possessed by a non-human spirit, he should then form this thought:

'If the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas know that my intention has become pure and have bestowed upon me the prediction of non-retrogression from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.'"

If I have long since generated pure mental attention, seeking to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, having distanced myself from the inclinations of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, and do not seek to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment through the mental attention of śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas.
If I shall in the future certainly attain unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and bring benefit, peace, and happiness to all classes of sentient beings until the end of the future;

and if there currently exist in the worlds of the ten directions immeasurable Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas who proclaim the subtle and wondrous Dharma to benefit and gladden sentient beings—those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, who see nothing that is not seen, know nothing that is not known, understand nothing that is not understood, and realize nothing that is not realized, and who presently know, see, and awaken to the differences in the inclinations of all sentient beings—I pray that you will graciously examine my thoughts and these words of truth.

If I am truly able to cultivate the bodhisattva practices and shall certainly attain unexcelled, perfect enlightenment to rescue sentient beings from the suffering of birth and death, may this man or this woman not be troubled or harassed by non-human spirits; at my word, they shall immediately depart.

"Subhūti! When this bodhisattva mahāsattva speaks these words, if that non-human being does not depart, you should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has not yet received from the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, the prophecy of non-retrogression regarding unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment."

"Subhūti! When this bodhisattva mahāsattva speaks these words, if that non-human being immediately departs, you should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has already received from the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, the prophecy of non-retrogression regarding unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes such practices, characteristics, and signs, you should know that this is a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva."

"Furthermore, Subhūti, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have not yet well practiced the perfection of generosity; who have not yet well practiced the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom;

who have not yet well established themselves in internal emptiness, nor well established themselves in external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate, the emptiness of the conditioned, the emptiness of the unconditioned, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential emptiness, the emptiness of self-characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature."

They have not yet well established themselves in suchness; they have not yet well established themselves in the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, or the inconceivable realm.
They have not yet well established themselves in the noble truth of suffering, nor have they well established themselves in the noble truths of the origin, cessation, and the path.

They have not yet well trained in the four foundations of mindfulness, nor have they well trained in the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path.
They have not yet skillfully cultivated the four dhyānas; they have not yet skillfully cultivated the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments;
they have not yet skillfully cultivated the eight liberations, nor the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities;
they have not yet skillfully cultivated the gate of liberation of emptiness, nor the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.
They have not yet skillfully trained in the gateways of dhāraṇī, nor have they skillfully trained in the gateways of samādhi;

they have not entered the bodhisattva’s state of right determination (*samyaktva-niyāma*), nor have they fully cultivated all Buddha-dharmas. They are far removed from the bodhisattva’s skillful means (*upāya-kauśalya*), have not escaped the afflictions and disturbances of evil Māras, and are unable to discern demonic activities. Without measuring the thickness of their own roots of goodness, they learn from other bodhisattvas to utter words of solemn truth, only to be deceived and deluded by evil Māras.
“Subhūti! When this bodhisattva mahāsattva sees a man or a woman who has been possessed by a non-human spirit, he immediately makes a sincere and truthful declaration:

‘If I have already received from the Buddhas of the past the prediction of non-retrogression regarding unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, let this man or this woman not be troubled or harassed by the non-human spirit; following my word, it shall quickly depart.’”

"Subhūti! After this bodhisattva mahāsattva has spoken these words, at that time, the evil Māra, for the sake of causing confusion and disturbance, will immediately drive away and coerce the non-human beings to depart."
Why is that? Subhūti!
The power of Māra is superior to that of those non-humans; therefore, having received Māra’s command, the non-humans immediately depart.
"Subhūti! Having seen this, that bodhisattva mahāsattva leaps for joy and thinks:
'That non-human being has now departed because of my own power.'"
"Why is this? It is not because the non-human beings released this man or woman simply by following my uttered vow, for there was no other cause. "Subhūti!"

This bodhisattva-mahāsattva is unable to recognize the deeds of Māra; instead, he falsely gives rise to joy, thinking it to be his own power, and relying on this, he treats other bodhisattvas with contempt, saying:

"I have already received from the Buddhas of the past the prediction of non-retrogression regarding unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment; the vows I have made shall not be in vain. You, however, have not yet received predictions from the Buddhas, so you should not emulate me by making solemn declarations of truth; even if you were to set such a goal, it would surely be empty and without fruit."

"Subhūti! Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas treat other bodhisattvas with contempt and derision, falsely relying on their meager abilities and giving rise to many forms of overweening pride regarding their merits, they distance themselves from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment and are unable to realize the knowledge of all modes."

"Subhūti! Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas lack the power of skillful means, because they have allowed various forms of overweening pride to grow, and because they despise and disparage other bodhisattvas, they fall to the level of a śrāvaka or a pratyekabuddha despite their diligent exertion."
"Subhūti! Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva possesses little merit, all the virtuous deeds he performs and his utterances of truthful words give rise to demonic activities. Subhūti!"

This bodhisattva-mahāsattva is unable to draw near to, make offerings to, revere, respect, and praise spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra); they are unable to inquire about the characteristics of the non-retrogressive conduct of bodhisattvas; and they are unable to consult with or receive instruction from them. Consequently, their activities are bound by Māra, and these bonds become even more firm and solid.
Why is this so? Subhūti!

Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have not long practiced the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, and because they lack skillful means, they are disturbed and distracted by Māra, the Evil One.
"Therefore, Subhūti, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should skillfully recognize the various deeds of Māra.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“Bhagavān, how is it that a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not practice for long in the pāramitās of generosity, ethical discipline,
patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, nor does he dwell for long in internal emptiness?”
External emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness,
conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersal emptiness, non-alteration emptiness,
essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, emptiness of all phenomena, and the unapprehendable...
Having attained emptiness, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence,
they will before long abide securely in suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth,
the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, and the realm of space.
...the inconceivable realm; before long they will dwell securely in the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path;

before long they will practice the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path; before long they will practice the four dhyānas.

They will not long practice the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments; they will not long practice the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative concentrations, or the ten universal bases;
they will not long practice the gateways of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; nor will they long practice the gateways of dhāraṇī or the gateways of samādhi. Not yet...
Having entered the bodhisattva’s state of certainty beyond regression, yet not having fully cultivated all Buddha-dharmas and being far removed from the bodhisattva’s skillful means,
one is disturbed and confused by various evil māras?
The Buddha said,
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! Māra,
the Evil One, transforms himself into various forms and approaches this bodhisattva mahāsattva, attempting to deceive him by saying:”
"Alas! Son of good family,
do you not know this for yourself?"

The Buddhas of the past have already bestowed upon you the prediction of great enlightenment (*mahābodhi-vyākaraṇa*). You shall certainly attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*) and never again fall back from it. Your name is such-and-such; your father’s name is such-and-such; your mother’s name is such-and-such; your brother’s name is such-and-such; your sister’s name is such-and-such; your friends and kinsmen, even your ancestors up to the seventh generation, each have names such-and-such. You were born in such-and-such a direction, in such-and-such a country, in such-and-such a city, in such-and-such a town, in such-and-such a village. You were born under such-and-such a year, such-and-such a month, such-and-such a day, at such-and-such a time, under such-and-such a lunar mansion (*nakṣatra*), and as a member of such-and-such a royal lineage.
"Subhūti! When an evil Māra perceives that this bodhisattva’s mental conduct is gentle and their faculties are dull, he will falsely prophesy:
'In your previous lives as well, your mental conduct was gentle and your faculties were dull.'"
When an evil Māra perceives that this bodhisattva’s mental conduct is firm and resolute, and his faculties are sharp and keen, he will falsely prophesy:
"In your previous lives as well, your mental conduct was firm and resolute, and your faculties were sharp and keen."
"In this way, if an evil Māra sees this bodhisattva dwelling in an araṇya, or among tombs, or in the open air, or at the foot of a tree;
or if he always begs for food, or accepts food only once, or eats while seated once, or eats from a single bowl;
or if he wears robes made of discarded rags, or possesses only the three robes—"
Some always sit and do not lie down; some prefer old bedding and requisites; some have few desires; some are content;
some delight in seclusion; some possess right mindfulness; some delight in tranquil concentration;
some possess sublime wisdom; some do not value material gain; some do not prize reputation; and some prefer frugality and do not even oil their feet.
Or they may reduce their sleep, or avoid restlessness, or prefer few words, or delight in gentle speech.
When the evil Māra observes these various practices of the bodhisattva, he falsely predicts:
"In previous lives, you have already dwelt in forest hermitages or among burial mounds, and so forth, up to speaking few words and using gentle speech."

Why is this so? Because you have now accomplished these various dhūta virtues as witnessed by the world, you must certainly have possessed such various and sublime virtues in previous lives as well; you should congratulate yourself and not disparage yourself.

"Subhūti! When this bodhisattva mahāsattva hears this evil Māra describe his superior merits in past lives as well as those yet to come, and describes the specific names of his current kinsmen, his place of birth, and the circumstances of his birth, while also praising various dhūta virtues; having heard this, he becomes joyful and conceives arrogance, looking down upon, despising, and reviling other bodhisattvas."
“Subhūti! At that time, Māra, knowing that this bodhisattva’s mind was dull and obscured, spoke to him again, saying:

‘Since you possess such marks and signs of merit, the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past have certainly already bestowed upon you the prediction of great enlightenment; you shall surely realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment and shall never again fall back.’”

"Subhūti! At that time, for the sake of causing disturbance, Māra the Evil One may falsely manifest himself in the form of a renunciant, or falsely manifest himself in the form of a householder, or falsely manifest himself in the form of a father or mother, or falsely manifest himself in the form of a brother, or falsely manifest himself in the form of a sister, or falsely manifest himself in the form of a friend or companion, or falsely manifest himself in the form of a brahmin, or falsely manifest himself in the form of a teacher, or falsely manifest himself in various forms such as those of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, humans, non-humans, and so forth; having approached this bodhisattva mahāsattva, he speaks these words:"

"The Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past have long ago bestowed upon you the prediction of great enlightenment; you shall certainly attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, never again to regress."
Why is this? You possess all the marks and characteristics of the merit of Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas in the stage of non-retrogression; you should respect yourself and not give rise to doubt.

"Subhūti! Those practices, tokens, and signs of a bodhisattva mahāsattva who has truly attained non-retrogression, as I have described them, do not exist at all for a bodhisattva mahāsattva who harbors overweening pride."
"Subhūti, you should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva is possessed by Māra and is bewitched by Māra. Why is this?"

This bodhisattva-mahāsattva has not yet truly attained any of the practices, marks, or signs of a non-retrogressive bodhisattva-mahāsattva; yet, merely hearing a wicked Māra describe their merits, name, place of birth, and time of birth—descriptions that are only partially similar to reality—they give rise to arrogance and treat other bodhisattvas with contempt, mockery, and abuse.
Therefore, Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, they should skillfully recognize such demonic activities.
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 332. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter Fifty-three on Skillful Training, Section Three. "Furthermore, Subhūti!
There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who are possessed by Māra and bewitched by Māra; they merely hear the names [of these dharmas] and give rise to false attachments. Why is this so?
"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva has not yet practiced the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom;
nor has he yet established himself in inner emptiness, outer [emptiness],..."
Emptiness, internal and external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth,
the emptiness of the conditioned, the emptiness of the unconditioned, absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration,
the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, and the emptiness of non-apprehensibility.
Emptiness, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—
prior to these, one has not yet established oneself in suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-falsity,
the immutability, the equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, or the realm of space.
In this inconceivable realm, one has not yet become established in the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path;

one has not yet practiced the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path; and one has not yet practiced the four dhyānas.

The immeasurables and the four formless absorptions; having previously not yet trained in the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive absorptions, or the ten totalities; having previously not yet trained in the gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness;
and having previously not yet trained in the ten stages of a bodhisattva or the five eyes.
Regarding the six supernormal powers, they have not previously studied the gates of dhāraṇī or the gates of samādhi;

they have not previously studied the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; they have not previously studied the absence of...

Through the loss of the dharmas and the state of constant equanimity, and because they have not previously trained in all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*);
because they have not previously trained in all the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva;
and because they have not previously trained in the unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas—for these reasons, Māra gains an opportunity.

"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is unable to discern the characteristics of the māra of the aggregates, is unable to discern the characteristics of the māra of death, is unable to discern the characteristics of the māra of the devas, and is unable to discern the characteristics of the māra of afflictions; by these causes and conditions, it allows the māras an opportunity."
“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not cognize form; he does not cognize feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness;
he does not cognize the eye-base, nor does he cognize the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-base.”
They do not understand the sphere of form; they do not understand the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena.
They do not understand the eye-element; they do not understand the elements of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind.
They do not understand the element of form; they do not understand the elements of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena.
They do not understand the eye-consciousness element; they do not understand the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-consciousness elements.
They do not understand eye-contact; they do not understand ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact.
They do not understand the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition; they do not understand the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as condition.
They do not understand the earth element, nor do they understand the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements;

they do not understand ignorance, nor do they understand volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, or old age and death;
they do not understand the perfection of generosity, nor do they understand the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom.

They do not understand internal emptiness; they do not understand external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.

They do not understand suchness; they do not understand the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, non-alteration, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm.

They do not fully understand the four foundations of mindfulness; they do not fully understand the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path;
they do not fully understand the noble truth of suffering, nor do they fully understand the noble truths of the origin, cessation, and the path;
they do not fully understand the four dhyānas, nor do they fully understand the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments.
They do not understand the eight liberations; they do not understand the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, or the ten pervasive bases;
