they do not understand the gate of liberation that is emptiness, nor do they understand the gates of liberation that are signlessness and wishlessness;
they do not understand the ten stages.
They do not fully comprehend the five eyes; they do not fully comprehend the six supernormal powers;
they do not fully comprehend the gates of samādhi; they do not fully comprehend the gates of dhāraṇī;

they do not fully comprehend the ten powers of a Buddha; they do not fully comprehend the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
They do not comprehend the fruit of stream-entry; they do not comprehend the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, or arhatship;
they do not comprehend pratyekabuddha-enlightenment;
they do not comprehend all-knowledge, nor the knowledge of the aspects of the path, nor the knowledge of all aspects.
Furthermore, they do not understand the true nature of the names of sentient beings and all phenomena.
By this cause and condition, Māra gains an opportunity and, through skillful means, manifests various forms and says to this bodhisattva mahāsattva:

"The practices and vows you have cultivated are already fulfilled; you shall realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. When you attain buddhahood, you shall obtain such supreme merits and a noble name."
"Subhūti! It is because that evil Māra knows that this bodhisattva has long harbored the thought and aspiration:
'When I attain buddhahood, I shall obtain such meritorious qualities and a name.'"
"According to their thoughts and aspirations, he shall prophesy for them. Subhūti!
At that time, because this bodhisattva is far removed from the perfection of wisdom and lacks skillful means, upon hearing the Māra’s prophecy, he will think to himself:"

"How marvelous! This person has prophesied for me that I shall attain Buddhahood and have described my future merit and name; this accords with the aspirations I have cherished throughout the long night. By this, I know that the Buddhas of the past must have already bestowed upon me the prophecy of Great Bodhi. I am certain that I shall attain Unsurpassed Perfect Enlightenment and never again regress; when I become a Buddha, I will surely obtain such meritorious and noble names."

"Subhūti! When such an evil Māra, or a member of Māra’s retinue, or a śramaṇa possessed by Māra, prophesies the name by which this bodhisattva mahāsattva shall become a Buddha in the future, his pride increases all the more:
'In the future I shall certainly become a Buddha and obtain such meritorious names; no other bodhisattvas are my equal.'"

"Subhūti! Regarding the practices, marks, and signs of non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattvas as I have described them, this bodhisattva mahāsattva has not yet accomplished any of them; yet, merely hearing the false reputation of attaining buddhahood spoken by Māra, he becomes arrogant and treats other bodhisattva mahāsattvas with contempt, mockery, and derision."

"Subhūti! Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to arrogance and treats other bodhisattva mahāsattvas with contempt, derision, and disdain, he distances himself from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."

Subhūti! Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva is far removed from the perfection of wisdom, lacks skillful means, abandons virtuous friends, and is constantly influenced by evil associates, he will fall to the level of a śrāvaka or a pratyekabuddha.

“Subhūti! Such a bodhisattva mahāsattva may regain right mindfulness regarding this body, sincerely repent their transgressions, and abandon their former prideful mind. By repeatedly drawing near to, making offerings to, honoring, respecting, and praising true and supreme spiritual friends, although they may continue to wander through saṃsāra for a long time, they will eventually rely once more upon the profound *prajñāpāramitā* to train and study progressively, and shall realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”

"Subhūti! If this bodhisattva mahāsattva, while possessing such a body, fails to attain right mindfulness, is unable to repent of his transgressions, does not relinquish his prideful mind, and does not wish to draw near to, make offerings to, revere, respect, or praise true and excellent spiritual friends, he will certainly wander through saṃsāra for a long time; even if he later exerts himself to cultivate various wholesome deeds, he will fall to the level of a śrāvaka or a pratyekabuddha."

“Subhūti! For example, suppose a bhikṣu seeking the state of a śrāvaka were to commit even one of the four grave offenses; he would then no longer be a śramaṇa nor a son of the Śākya, and he would certainly be unable to attain the fruit of stream-entry, once-returning, non-returning, or arhatship in this present life.”

"Subhūti! It is the same with a bodhisattva who falsely clings to an empty name: upon merely hearing a demonic prophecy of attaining the empty title of Buddhahood, they give rise to arrogance and treat other bodhisattva-mahāsattvas with contempt, mockery, and derision. You should know that this transgression is infinitely many times greater than the four grave offenses committed by that bhikṣu."
"Subhūti! Setting aside the four pārājika offenses committed by that bhikṣu, the transgression of this bodhisattva exceeds even the five ānantarya crimes by immeasurable multiples. Why is this so?"

"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva has not, in truth, accomplished any sublime merit; yet, upon hearing a wicked Māra proclaim the name he will attain as a Buddha, he becomes arrogant and looks down upon other bodhisattvas. Therefore, this transgression exceeds even the five deeds of immediate retribution."

Therefore, Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, they should skillfully recognize such subtle demonic activities as the recording and proclaiming of empty names and titles.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who dwell hidden in mountain forests, empty marshes, and vast wildernesses, sitting alone in meditation and practicing the conduct of seclusion."
At that time, an evil Māra came to where he was and, with respectful praise for the merit of seclusion, spoke these words:
"Excellent, Great Being!

One who is able to cultivate such a practice of seclusion is praised by all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas; Śakra, Lord of Devas, and other celestial beings and ṛṣis all protect, make offerings to, and revere them. You should dwell constantly in this place and not go elsewhere.
"Subhūti! I do not praise bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who dwell in forest hermitages, wildernesses, or mountain groves, sitting in meditation and contemplating while practicing the conduct of seclusion."
At that time, Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One,

what other practices of seclusion should bodhisattva-mahāsattvas cultivate, such that the Buddha does not praise dwelling in *āraṇyakas*, wildernesses, or mountain forests, being separated from all bedding and seats, and the merit of secluded meditation and reflection?"
“I only pray that you will explain the supreme practice of detachment for all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas!
The Buddha said,
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

Whether Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas dwell in mountain forests, empty marshes, vast wildernesses, or forest hermitages (āraṇya), or whether they dwell in cities, villages, royal capitals, or noisy, crowded places, as long as they can remain far removed from afflictions and evil karma, far removed from the mental orientations of Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas, and diligently cultivate the Prajñāpāramitā along with other sublime virtues, this is called the Bodhisattva’s true practice of seclusion.
"Subhūti! This practice of seclusion is praised by all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas; this practice of seclusion is authorized by all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas."

“Subhūti! These practices of seclusion should be constantly studied by bodhisattva mahāsattvas. Whether by day or by night, they should correctly contemplate and diligently practice this dharma of seclusion; this is called a bodhisattva’s cultivation of the practice of seclusion.”

"Subhūti! This practice of seclusion is unmixed with the mental orientations of śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas; it is unmixed with any afflictions or evil karma; it is free from all clamor and distraction, being ultimately pure. It causes all bodhisattvas to swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, benefiting and bringing happiness to sentient beings, continuing without end until the limits of the future."

“Subhūti! That which Māra praises—dwelling in seclusion in mountain forests, empty marshes, wildernesses, and *araṇya* hermitages, staying far from bedding and sitting alone in meditation—is not the supreme practice of seclusion for bodhisattvas.”
Why is this so? Subhūti!

That practice of seclusion is still subject to distraction; that is to say, it may be mixed with evil karma and afflictions, or mixed with the mental orientations of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas. Consequently, one cannot apply oneself diligently to believe in, accept, and train in the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, nor can one bring the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñatā*) to fulfillment.

“Subhūti! There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, although they diligently practice the dharmas of seclusion praised by Māra, give rise to a conceited and impure mind, treating other bodhisattva-mahāsattvas with contempt, derision, and disdain.”
This refers to those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, although residing in cities, villages, or royal capitals, maintain a pure mind,
untainted by various afflictions and evil karma, and unadulterated by the mental orientations of śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas,
as they diligently cultivate generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, and meditative concentration.
The Prajñāpāramitā consists in diligently and securely abiding in internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness,
the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness,
the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature.
The emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable,
the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence;
they diligently abide in suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, immutability, equality, and detachment.
The nature of arising, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space,
and the inconceivable realm; he diligently abides in the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path, and diligently cultivates the four foundations of mindfulness,
the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, and the seven factors of enlightenment.
Having perfected the mundane virtues such as the factors of enlightenment, the factors of the Eightfold Noble Path, the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables,
the four formless attainments, and the five supernormal powers, he diligently cultivated the gates of liberation—
emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness— and diligently cultivated the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
He diligently cultivates the gateways of dhāraṇī and the gateways of samādhi;

he diligently cultivates the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; and he diligently cultivates the quality of non-forgetfulness.
Abiding constantly in equanimity, they diligently cultivate all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*);

they purify buddha-fields and bring sentient beings to maturity; though dwelling amidst the clamor and bustle of the world, their minds remain tranquil, as they constantly and diligently practice the supreme conduct of seclusion.
"Subhūti! Toward such a truly pure assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, he conceives arrogance in his heart, treating them with contempt and mockery, slandering and despising them."

Because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva is far removed from the perfection of wisdom and lacks skillful means, even if he dwells in a wilderness extending a hundred yojanas that is utterly devoid of predatory beasts, snakes, scorpions, or bandits, there will only be gods, ghosts, and rākṣasas roaming and dwelling therein.

Dwelling in such a forest hermitage (āraṇyaka), although they may spend one year, or ten years, or a hundred years, or a thousand years, or a hundred thousand years, or ten million years, or a billion years, or ten billion years, or a hundred billion years, or even longer, practicing the conduct of seclusion, they do not understand the true conduct of seclusion of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas.

This refers to those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, though dwelling amidst the clamor and bustle of the world, maintain a mind of profound tranquility; they remain far removed from various afflictions and unwholesome karmas, set out toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and distance themselves from the mental orientations of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.

Although this bodhisattva-mahāsattva dwells in the wilderness for a long time, they harbor mental orientations associated with śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; they take pleasure in and become attached to the dharmas of the levels of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, rely upon those dharmas to practice the conduct of seclusion, and further develop a deep attachment to that very conduct.
"Subhūti! Although they thus practice the conduct of seclusion, they do not accord with the minds of the Tathāgatas. Subhūti!"

The true practice of seclusion that I praise for the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do not accomplish at all; nor do they perceive even a semblance of such a practice within that truly supreme seclusion.

Why is this? Because they do not give rise to love and joy for such genuine practice of seclusion; rather, they take pleasure only in practicing the empty seclusion of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.
“Subhūti! When this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the supreme conduct of detachment that is not real, a Māra comes through the air, joyfully praising him and saying:
‘O Great Being!’”
Excellent! Excellent!

You are able to practice the conduct of true seclusion; this conduct of seclusion is praised by all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas. By diligently cultivating this conduct, you will swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva clings to such dharmas of seclusion practiced by śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas as being supreme, and thus treats with contempt and derision those bhikṣus who abide in the vehicle of the bodhisattvas—even if they dwell in the midst of bustle—their minds are tranquil and they have accomplished the dharmas of discipline, saying:
‘They cannot practice the path of seclusion; though their bodies dwell in bustle, their minds are not tranquil.’”

"Subhūti! Such a bodhisattva mahāsattva disparages and treats with contempt those bodhisattva mahāsattvas who dwell in genuine seclusion and are praised by all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, saying: 'They dwell in bustle and their minds are not tranquil; they are unable to practice genuine seclusion.

Yet, they honor and praise those bodhisattva mahāsattvas who dwell in genuine clamor and are not praised by the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, saying: 'They do not dwell in clamor and their minds are tranquil; they are able to correctly practice genuine seclusion.'"
Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva fails to approach, serve, and honor those who should be approached, served, and honored as one would a Great Teacher; instead, he treats them with contempt.
Furthermore, he does not distance himself from those who should be avoided and not attended upon, such as evil friends, yet he serves, honors, and respects them as if they were a Great Teacher.
“Subhūti! Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva is far removed from the perfection of wisdom and lacks skillful means, he falsely gives rise to attachment. Why is that?
He thinks to himself:
"The practice I cultivate is true seclusion; therefore, non-human beings praise, protect, and mindfully attend to me.
Those who dwell in cities and towns have their bodies and minds agitated and disturbed—who would protect, mindfully attend to, revere, or praise them?"

"Subhūti! Because of these causes and conditions, this bodhisattva mahāsattva becomes frequently arrogant in mind, treating other bodhisattva mahāsattvas with contempt, mockery, and derision; thus, their afflictions and evil karma increase day and night."

Subhūti, you should know that such a bodhisattva mahāsattva is a caṇḍāla among bodhisattvas, a defiler of the assembly of bodhisattva mahāsattvas. Although he bears the semblance of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, he is a great thief among gods, humans, and asuras; though his body is clothed in the dharma-robes of a śramaṇa, his mind constantly harbors the intent of a thief.
Those who have set out upon the bodhisattva vehicle should not associate with, make offerings to, honor, respect, or praise such evil persons. Why is this?
"Subhūti, you should know that such a person harbors overweening pride; though appearing outwardly like a bodhisattva, they are inwardly full of afflictions. Therefore, Subhūti!"

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva truly does not abandon the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), does not abandon unsurpassed perfect enlightenment, and with a profound mind seeks to realize the knowledge of all modes and seeks to realize unsurpassed perfect enlightenment for the sake of universally benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings, they should not associate with, make offerings to, revere, respect, or praise such evil persons.

“Subhūti! All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should always diligently cultivate their own task: they should feel weary of and detached from birth and death, and not cling to the triple world; toward those wicked, outcaste-like people, they should constantly give rise to the minds of loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity. They should think thus:

‘I must not give rise to the faults that those evil persons give rise to; even if, through a lapse of mindfulness, such thoughts should momentarily arise, I shall immediately recognize them and swiftly cause them to be extinguished.’”

"Subhūti! Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who wish to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment should thoroughly recognize such demonic activities; they should apply themselves with diligent vigor to distance themselves from and eliminate those faults arising in those bodhisattvas."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a superior intention, desires to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, they should always draw near to, make offerings to, revere, respect, and praise true and excellent spiritual friends."
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha,
saying: “World-Honored One,
what are called the true, excellent, and virtuous spiritual friends of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas?”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas are the true, supreme, and virtuous friends of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. All Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are also the true, supreme, and virtuous friends of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. Furthermore, all Śrāvakas and other virtuous persons who are able to proclaim, reveal, analyze, and clarify for the assembly of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas the teachings associated with the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom so that they may be easily understood—these too should be known as the true, supreme, and virtuous friends of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.”

“Subhūti, you should know that the perfection of generosity is a true, excellent, and virtuous friend to a bodhisattva mahāsattva; the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are likewise true, excellent, and virtuous friends to a bodhisattva mahāsattva.”

“Subhūti, you should know that the four foundations of mindfulness are the true, supreme, and virtuous friends of a bodhisattva mahāsattva; the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are likewise the true, supreme, and virtuous friends of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.”

“Subhūti, you should know that the four dhyānas are the true, supreme, and virtuous friends of a bodhisattva mahāsattva; the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are likewise the true, supreme, and virtuous friends of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.”

“Subhūti, you should know that the eight liberations are the true, excellent, and virtuous friends of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities are likewise the true, excellent, and virtuous friends of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.”

“Subhūti, you should know that the gate of liberation of emptiness is the true, supreme, and virtuous friend of a bodhisattva mahāsattva; the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are likewise the true, supreme, and virtuous friends of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.”

“Subhūti, you should know that the Ground of Extreme Joy is a true, supreme, and virtuous friend to a bodhisattva mahāsattva; the Ground of Purity, the Ground of Radiant Light, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Utmost Difficulty to Conquer, the Ground of Manifestation, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, and the Ground of the Dharma Cloud are likewise true, supreme, and virtuous friends to a bodhisattva mahāsattva.”

“Subhūti, you should know that the five eyes are the true, supreme, and virtuous friends of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; the six supernormal powers are also the true, supreme, and virtuous friends of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.”

“Subhūti, you should know that the gateways of samādhi are the true, supreme, and virtuous friends of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; the gateways of dhāraṇī are likewise the true, supreme, and virtuous friends of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.”

“Subhūti, you should know that the ten powers of a Buddha are the true, supreme, and virtuous friends of a bodhisattva mahāsattva; likewise, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are also the true, supreme, and virtuous friends of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.”

"Subhūti, you should know that the quality of non-forgetfulness is a truly excellent and virtuous spiritual friend for a bodhisattva mahāsattva; likewise, the state of constant abiding in equanimity is also a truly excellent and virtuous spiritual friend for a bodhisattva mahāsattva."
“Subhūti, you should know that the permanent severance of all habitual tendencies of affliction is the true, supreme, and virtuous spiritual friend of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Subhūti, you should know!”

All-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) is the true, supreme, and virtuous friend of a bodhisattva mahāsattva; the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are also the true, supreme, and virtuous friends of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.

"Subhūti, you should know that all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are the true, supreme, and virtuous friends of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is also the true, supreme, and virtuous friend of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas."

“Suvikrāntavikrāmin, you should know that the noble truth of suffering is the true, supreme, and virtuous friend of a bodhisattva mahāsattva; the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are likewise the true, supreme, and virtuous friends of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.”

“Subhūti, you should know that the nature of conditions of all phenomena is the true, supreme, and virtuous friend of a bodhisattva mahāsattva; the members of dependent origination are also the true, supreme, and virtuous friends of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.”

“Subhūti, you should know that internal emptiness is a true, supreme, and virtuous friend to a bodhisattva mahāsattva. External emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature are likewise true, supreme, and virtuous friends to a bodhisattva mahāsattva.”

“Subhūti, you should know that suchness is the true, supreme, and virtuous friend of a bodhisattva mahāsattva. The dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-erroneous nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the nature free from birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm are also the true, supreme, and virtuous friends of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.”
“Subhūti, you should know this!

The perfection of giving (*dāna-pāramitā*) serves as the teacher and guide for the bodhisattva mahāsattvas; it is their illumination, their torch, their lamp, their light, their liberation, their awakening, their knowledge, their wisdom, their savior, their protector, their dwelling, their home, their island, their continent, their refuge, their destination, their father, and their mother.

Likewise, the perfections of ethical discipline (*śīla*), patience (*kṣānti*), diligence (*vīrya*), meditative concentration (*dhyāna*), and wisdom (*prajñā*) also serve as the teacher and guide for the bodhisattva mahāsattvas; they are their illumination, their torch, their lamp, their light, their liberation, their awakening, their knowledge, their wisdom, their savior, their protector, their dwelling, their home, their island, their continent, their refuge, their destination, their father, and their mother.”

“Subhūti, you should know that the four foundations of mindfulness serve as teachers and guides for the bodhisattva mahāsattvas; they are illumination, torches, lamps, and lights; they are understanding, awakening, knowledge, and wisdom; they are rescuers and protectors; they are dwellings and houses; they are islands and peninsulas; they are refuges and destinations; and they are fathers and mothers.

The four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path likewise serve as teachers and guides for the bodhisattva mahāsattvas; they are illumination, torches, lamps, and lights; they are understanding, awakening, knowledge, and wisdom; they are rescuers and protectors; they are dwellings and houses; they are islands and peninsulas; they are refuges and destinations; and they are fathers and mothers.”

“Subhūti, you should know this: the four dhyānas serve as teachers and guides for the bodhisattva mahāsattvas; they are illumination, torches, lamps, and lights; they are liberation, awakening, knowledge, and wisdom; they are rescuers and protectors; they are a chamber and a dwelling; they are an island and a promontory; they are a refuge and a destination; they are fathers and mothers.

Likewise, the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments also serve as teachers and guides for the bodhisattva mahāsattvas; they are illumination, torches, lamps, and lights; they are liberation, awakening, knowledge, and wisdom; they are rescuers and protectors; they are a chamber and a dwelling; they are an island and a promontory; they are a refuge and a destination; they are fathers and mothers.”

“Subhūti, you should know this: the eight liberations serve as teachers and guides for the bodhisattva mahāsattvas; they are illumination, torches, lamps, and lights; they are understanding, awakening, knowledge, and wisdom; they are rescuers and protectors; they are chambers and dwellings; they are islands and peninsulas; they are refuges and destinations; they are fathers and mothers.

The eight bases of mastery, the nine successive absorptions, and the ten totalities likewise serve as teachers and guides for the bodhisattva mahāsattvas; they are illumination, torches, lamps, and lights; they are understanding, awakening, knowledge, and wisdom; they are rescuers and protectors; they are chambers and dwellings; they are islands and peninsulas; they are refuges and destinations; they are fathers and mothers.”
“Subhūti, you should know this!

The gate of liberation of emptiness acts as the teacher and guide for the bodhisattva mahāsattvas; it is their light and torch, their lamp and illumination, their understanding and awakening, their wisdom and insight, their rescue and protection, their chamber and dwelling, their island and continent, their refuge and destination, and their father and mother.

The gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness likewise act as the teacher and guide for the bodhisattva mahāsattvas; they are their light and torch, their lamp and illumination, their understanding and awakening, their wisdom and insight, their rescue and protection, their chamber and dwelling, their island and continent, their refuge and destination, and their father and mother.”

“Subhūti, you should know that the Ground of Extreme Joy serves as the teacher and guide for all bodhisattva mahāsattvas; it is the illumination, the torch, the lamp, and the light; it is the liberation, the awakening, the knowledge, and the wisdom; it is the savior, the protector, the dwelling, and the home; it is the island, the peninsula, the refuge, and the destination; it is the father and the mother.”

The Ground of Freedom from Defilement, the Ground of Radiant Light, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Supreme Difficulty to Conquer, the Ground of Manifestation, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, and the Ground of the Dharma Cloud likewise serve as teachers and guides for the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; they act as illumination, as torches, as lamps, as lights, as liberation, as awakening, as knowledge, as wisdom, as rescue, as protection, as a chamber, as a dwelling, as an island, as a promontory, as a refuge, as a destination, and as fathers and mothers.

“Subhūti, you should know this! The five eyes serve as teachers and guides for the bodhisattva mahāsattvas; they are illumination, torches, lamps, and lights; they are understanding and awakening; they are knowledge and wisdom; they are rescuers and protectors; they are a chamber and a dwelling; they are an island and a shore;

they are a refuge and a destination; they are fathers and mothers. The six supernormal powers likewise serve as teachers and guides for the bodhisattva mahāsattvas; they are illumination, torches, lamps, and lights; they are understanding and awakening; they are knowledge and wisdom; they are rescuers and protectors; they are a chamber and a dwelling; they are an island and a shore; they are a refuge and a destination; they are fathers and mothers.”

“Subhūti, you should know this! The gateways of samādhi serve as teachers and guides for the bodhisattva mahāsattvas; they are the illumination, the torch, the lamp, and the light; they are the liberation, the awakening, the knowledge, and the wisdom; they are the rescue, the protection, the dwelling, and the home; they are the island, the peninsula, the refuge, and the destination; they are the father and the mother.

Likewise, the gateways of dhāraṇī also serve as teachers and guides for the bodhisattva mahāsattvas; they are the illumination, the torch, the lamp, and the light; they are the liberation, the awakening, the knowledge, and the wisdom; they are the rescue, the protection, the dwelling, and the home; they are the island, the peninsula, the refuge, and the destination; they are the father and the mother.”

"Subhūti, you should know that the ten powers of the Buddha serve as teachers and guides for the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; they are illumination and torches, lamps and lights, explanations and awakenings, knowledge and wisdom, rescuers and protectors, dwellings and houses, islands and peninsulas, refuges and destinations, and fathers and mothers."

The four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha likewise serve as teachers and guides for the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; they are the light, the torch, the lamp, and the illumination; they are the liberation, the awakening, the wisdom, and the insight; they are the rescue, the protection, the dwelling, and the home; they are the island, the peninsula, the refuge, and the destination; they are the father and the mother.
“Subhūti, you should know this:

the quality of non-forgetfulness (*asaṃpramoṣadharma*) serves as the teacher and guide for the bodhisattva mahāsattvas; it is their illumination, their torch, their lamp, their light, their liberation, their awakening, their knowledge, their wisdom, their rescue, their protection, their dwelling, their home, their island, their continent, their refuge, their destination, and their father and mother.

Likewise, the state of constant abiding in equanimity (*upekṣā*) also serves as the teacher and guide for the bodhisattva mahāsattvas; it is their illumination, their torch, their lamp, their light, their liberation, their awakening, their knowledge, their wisdom, their rescue, their protection, their dwelling, their home, their island, their continent, their refuge, their destination, and their father and mother.”

“Subhūti, you should know that the permanent severance of all habitual tendencies of affliction acts as the teacher and guide for the assembly of bodhisattva mahāsattvas; it serves as illumination, as a torch, as a lamp, as a light, as liberation, as awakening, as knowledge, as wisdom, as salvation, as protection, as a chamber, as a dwelling, as an island, as a shore, as a refuge, as a destination, and as father and mother.”
“Subhūti, you should know this:

All-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) acts as the teacher and guide for the bodhisattva mahāsattvas; it is their illumination, their torch, their lamp, their light, their understanding, their awakening, their wisdom, their insight, their rescue, their protection, their dwelling, their home, their island, their continent, their refuge, their destination, and their father and mother.

Path-knowledge (*mārgākārajñatā*) and all-aspect-knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*) likewise act as the teacher and guide for the bodhisattva mahāsattvas; they are their illumination, their torch, their lamp, their light, their understanding, their awakening, their wisdom, their insight, their rescue, their protection, their dwelling, their home, their island, their continent, their refuge, their destination, and their father and mother.”

“Subhūti, you should know this: all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas serve as teachers and guides for the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; they are illumination, torches, lamps, and lights; they are understanding, awakening, knowledge, and wisdom; they are rescuers and protectors; they are chambers and dwellings; they are islands and continents; they are refuges and destinations; and they are fathers and mothers.

Furthermore, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas also serves as teachers and guides for the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; it is illumination, torches, lamps, and lights; it is understanding, awakening, knowledge, and wisdom; it is rescue and protection; it is a chamber and a dwelling; it is an island and a continent; it is a refuge and a destination; and it is a father and a mother.”
“Subhūti, you should know this!

The Noble Truth of Suffering serves as the teacher and guide for the bodhisattva mahāsattvas; it is their light and torch, their lamp and illumination, their understanding and awakening, their knowledge and wisdom, their rescue and protection, their dwelling and home, their island and continent, their refuge and destination, and their father and mother.

The Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path likewise serve as the teacher and guide for the bodhisattva mahāsattvas; they are their light and torch, their lamp and illumination, their understanding and awakening, their knowledge and wisdom, their rescue and protection, their dwelling and home, their island and continent, their refuge and destination, and their father and mother.”

“Subhūti, you should know that the conditional nature of all phenomena (*dharmas*) serves as the teacher and guide for the bodhisattva mahāsattvas; it serves as the light, the torch, the lamp, the illumination, the understanding, the awakening, the wisdom, the insight, the rescue, the protection, the dwelling, the home, the island, the shore, the refuge, the destination, the father, and the mother.

Furthermore, the members of dependent origination (*pratītyasamutpāda*) also serve as the teacher and guide for the bodhisattva mahāsattvas; they serve as the light, the torch, the lamp, the illumination, the understanding, the awakening, the wisdom, the insight, the rescue, the protection, the dwelling, the home, the island, the shore, the refuge, the destination, the father, and the mother.”

“Subhūti, you should know that inner emptiness acts as the teacher and guide for the bodhisattva mahāsattvas; it is their illumination and torch, their lamp and light, their liberation and awakening, their knowledge and wisdom; it is their rescue and protection, their dwelling and home, their island and continent, their refuge and destination, and their father and mother.”

Outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence also serve as teachers and guides for the bodhisattva mahāsattvas; they serve as illumination and torches, as lamps and lights, as liberation and awakening, as knowledge and wisdom, as rescue and protection, as a chamber and a dwelling, as an island and a peninsula, as a refuge and a destination, and as fathers and mothers.

“Subhūti, you should know that True Suchness acts as the teacher and guide for all bodhisattva mahāsattvas; it is the illumination and the torch, the lamp and the light, the understanding and the awakening, the knowledge and the wisdom, the savior and the protector, the chamber and the dwelling, the island and the promontory, the refuge and the destination, and the father and the mother.”

The dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, non-illusory nature, non-alterability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm likewise serve as teachers and guides for the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; they serve as illumination and torches, as lamps and lights, as understanding and awakening, as knowledge and wisdom, as rescuers and protectors, as dwellings and houses, as islands and continents, as refuges and destinations, and as fathers and mothers.
"Why is this so, Subhūti? All Tathāgatas, Arhats,

and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past have all taken the perfection of generosity, and so on up to the inconceivable realm, as their teacher and guide, as their light and torch, as their lamp and illumination, as their liberation and awakening, as their knowledge and wisdom, as their savior and protector, as their dwelling and home, as their island and continent, as their refuge and destination, and as their father and mother."

All future Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas shall take this perfection of generosity, and so forth up to the inconceivable realm, as their teacher and guide, as their light and torch, as their lamp and illumination, as their liberation and awakening, as their knowledge and wisdom, as their savior and protector, as their chamber and abode, as their island and continent, as their refuge and destination, and as their father and mother.

All the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas currently dwelling in the infinite, incalculable, and boundless worlds of the ten directions—who sustain and bring peace to all sentient beings and proclaim and reveal the subtle and wondrous Dharma—all take the perfection of generosity (dānapāramitā), and so forth up to the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu), as their teacher and guide, as their light and torch, as their lamp and illumination, as their liberation and awakening, as their wisdom and insight, as their rescue and protection, as their chamber and abode, as their island and promontory, as their refuge and destination, and as their father and mother.
Why is this? Subhūti!
It is because all Buddhas of the past, future, and present are born from the perfection of generosity, and so on, up to the inconceivable realm.

"Therefore, Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, with a resolute intention, desires to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, to bring sentient beings to maturity, and to purify a buddha-field, they should train in the perfection of generosity; they should train in the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom;

they should train in the four foundations of mindfulness; and they should train in the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path."
One should train in the four dhyānas; one should train in the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments;
one should train in the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities;
one should train in the gate of liberation of emptiness, and one should train in the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.

One should study the Ground of Utmost Joy; one should study the Ground of Purity, the Ground of Radiance, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Difficult Victory, the Ground of Presence, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Good Intelligence, and the Ground of the Dharma Cloud;
one should study the five eyes; one should study the six supernormal powers;
one should study the gates of samādhi; and one should study the gates of dhāraṇī.

One should study the ten powers of a Buddha; one should study the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity, as well as the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
one should study the quality of non-forgetfulness, and one should study the nature of constant abiding in equanimity;
one should study the permanent severance of all habitual tendencies of affliction.
One should study all-knowledge; one should study the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects;
one should study all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas;
and one should study the unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas.
One should train in the noble truth of suffering; one should train in the noble truths of the origin, cessation, and the path;
one should train in the dependent nature of all phenomena; one should train in the members of dependent origination;

one should train in internal emptiness; and one should train in external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

One should study suchness; one should study the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of empty space, and the inconceivable realm.
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
Having trained in the perfection of giving, and so forth, up to the inconceivable realm, this bodhisattva mahāsattva should further gather all sentient beings through the four means of attraction.”
What are the four? First, giving; second, kind speech.
Third is beneficial conduct;
fourth is cooperation. Subhūti!
Observing this meaning, I have made this statement:

"The perfection of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom—extensively explained up to the inconceivable realm—act as teachers and guides for the assembly of bodhisattva mahāsattvas; they act as illumination, as torches, as lamps, as lights, as liberation, as awakening, as knowledge, as insight, as rescue, as protection, as a dwelling, as a home, as an island, as a continent, as a refuge, as a destination, and as fathers and mothers."

"Therefore, Subhūti! A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to practice without following the instructions of others, who wishes to abide without following the instructions of others, who wishes to sever the doubts of all sentient beings, who wishes to fulfill the aspirations of all sentient beings, who wishes to purify buddha-fields, and who wishes to mature sentient beings, should train in the perfection of wisdom."
Why is this? Subhūti!

Within this profound *prajñāpāramitā* sūtra, all the characteristics of the dharmas that the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should cultivate and study are extensively explained; therefore, all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should diligently practice and study within it.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
what are the characteristics of this Prajñāpāramitā, by which you exhort the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas to diligently practice and study it?”
The Buddha said: “Subhūti!
This perfection of wisdom has space as its characteristic; this perfection of wisdom has non-attachment as its characteristic; this perfection of wisdom has the signless as its characteristic.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
Within these profound characteristics of the *prajñāpāramitā*, all phenomena and all characteristics are unattainable because they are non-existent.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
Is there a causal basis by which one might say that the sublime characteristics possessed by the Prajñāpāramitā are also the characteristics possessed by all dharmas?”
The Buddha said,
“So it is, Subhūti! It is just so.”

"So it is! Just as you have said, because there are causes and conditions, one may speak of the sublime characteristics of the *prajñāpāramitā*; all phenomena likewise possess such sublime characteristics."
Why is this so? Subhūti!
It is because this perfection of wisdom has the emptiness of intrinsic nature as its characteristic, and all phenomena likewise have the emptiness of intrinsic nature as their characteristic.
Thus, the perfection of wisdom has detachment as its characteristic, and all phenomena likewise have detachment as their characteristic.
Subhūti! For this reason, it may be said:
"Whatever sublime characteristics the profound *prajñāpāramitā* possesses, all phenomena likewise possess such sublime characteristics;
for all phenomena are empty of intrinsic nature and devoid of manifold marks."
The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha again, saying:
“World-Honored One!

If all dharmas are empty of intrinsic nature and devoid of all marks, then all dharmas are empty of all dharmas, and all dharmas are detached from all dharmas; how can one conceptually establish the defilement or purification of sentient beings?”
“World-Honored One!
It is not that dharmas which are empty of intrinsic nature have defilement or purification, nor is it that dharmas which are detached have defilement or purification.
World-Honored One!”

“Neither by means of dharmas that are not empty of intrinsic nature can one realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, nor can one realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment by means of dharmas that are not detached.
World-Honored One!”
In the emptiness of intrinsic nature, no dharma can be apprehended; nor, in that which is detached, can any dharma be apprehended.
"World-Honored One!

It is not within the emptiness of intrinsic nature that a bodhisattva mahāsattva realizes unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; nor is it within that which is detached that a bodhisattva mahāsattva realizes unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
“World-Honored One!
How may I understand the profound meaning and intent of what the Buddha has spoken?
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Venerable Subhūti, saying:
“Subhūti, what do you think? For a long night have sentient beings harbored the notions of ‘I’ and ‘mine,’ grasping at ‘I’ and ‘mine’?”
Subhūti replied, "So it is, World-Honored One!"
"So it is! Sugata! For a long night, sentient beings have possessed the notions of 'I' and 'mine,' and have been attached to 'I' and 'mine.'"
The Buddha said,
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin, what do you think?”
"Is that mind which clings to 'self' and 'what belongs to self' empty and utterly devoid of them? Subhūti replied, "It is so!"
"So it is, World-Honored One!
So it is, Sugata!"
"The self and what belongs to the self grasped by that mind are all empty and utterly remote.
The Buddha said,
"Suvikrāntavikrāmin!"
"What do you think?
Is it not the case that sentient beings wander through birth and death due to the grasping at 'I' and 'mine'? Subhūti replied:
"So it is! World-Honored One! So it is!"
“Sugata! It is because sentient beings grasp at a self and what belongs to a self that they wander through birth and death.
The Buddha said:
“Subhūti! Thus, because sentient beings transmigrate through birth and death due to affliction, it is known by this that affliction is obtainable. Subhūti!”

If sentient beings were without mental attachment to "self" and "what belongs to self," there would be no defilement; and if there were no defilement, there would consequently be no wandering in saṃsāra.

Since the process of wandering through birth and death is perceptibly evident, one should know from this that there are defiled phenomena; and since there are defiled phenomena, there are also purified phenomena. Therefore, Subhūti!
"One should know that although sentient beings are empty of intrinsic nature and devoid of all marks, defilement and purification can still be found.

*The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, Fascicle 333, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree, Part One, Chapter Fifty-three on "Skillful Training," Section Four. At that time, the Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"

“World-Honored One, if Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice in this manner, they do not practice with respect to form, nor do they practice with respect to feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.”
If Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice in this manner, they do not course in the sense-base of the eye, nor do they course in the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind.
“World-Honored One!
If bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice in this manner, they do not course in the sphere of form, nor do they course in the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena.”
“World-Honored One!
If bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice in this manner, they do not practice with respect to the eye-element, nor do they practice with respect to the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-elements.”
“World-Honored One!
If bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice in this manner, they do not course in the realm of form, nor do they course in the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, or mental phenomena.”
“World-Honored One!

If bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice in this manner, they do not practice within the eye-consciousness element, nor do they practice within the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-consciousness elements.”
“World-Honored One!
If bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice in this way, they do not practice eye-contact, nor do they practice ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact.”
“World-Honored One!

If bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice in this manner, they do not practice with regard to the various sensations produced with eye-contact as a condition, nor do they practice with regard to the various sensations produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact as conditions.”
“World-Honored One!
If bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice in this manner, they do not course in the earth element, nor do they course in the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements.”
“World-Honored One!

If Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice in this manner, they do not practice ignorance, nor do they practice volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, or old age and death.”

“Bhagavān! If bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice in this manner, they do not practice the perfection of generosity, nor do they practice the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom.”
“World-Honored One!

If bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice in this manner, they do not practice inner emptiness, nor do they practice outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.”
“World-Honored One!

If Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice in this manner, they do not practice within suchness, nor do they practice within the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of empty space, or the inconceivable realm.”
“World-Honored One!

If bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice in this manner, they do not practice the four foundations of mindfulness, nor do they practice the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path.”
“World-Honored One!
If bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice in this manner, they do not practice the noble truth of suffering, nor do they practice the noble truths of origination, cessation, or the path.”
“World-Honored One!
If bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice in this manner, they do not practice the four dhyānas, nor do they practice the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments.”
“World-Honored One!

If bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice in this manner, they do not practice the eight liberations, nor do they practice the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities.”
“World-Honored One!
If bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice in this manner, they do not practice the liberation door of emptiness, nor do they practice the liberation doors of signlessness or wishlessness.”
“World-Honored One!
If bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice in this manner, they do not practice the five eyes, nor do they practice the six supernormal powers.
World-Honored One!”
"If Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice in this manner, they do not practice the gateways of dhāraṇī, nor do they practice the gateways of samādhi.
World-Honored One!"

If Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice in this manner, they do not practice the ten powers of a Buddha, nor do they practice the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“World-Honored One!
If bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice in this manner, they do not practice the quality of non-forgetfulness, nor do they practice the state of constant equanimity.”
“World-Honored One!
If bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice in this manner, they do not practice for the fruit of a stream-enterer, nor do they practice for the fruits of a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat.”
“World-Honored One!
If bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice in this manner, they do not practice for the sake of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment.
World-Honored One!”

If bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice in this manner, they do not practice all-knowledge (sarvajñatā), nor do they practice the knowledge of the aspects of the path (mārgākārajñatā) or the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā).
"Why is this? World-Honored One!
Because such dharmas as the one who practices, that which is practiced, the time of practice, the place of practice, and that by means of which one practices, are all unapprehendable."
“World-Honored One!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can practice in this way, they will not be overcome by any in the world—gods, humans, asuras, and so forth—but will be able to overcome all in the world—gods, humans, asuras, and so forth.”
“World-Honored One!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can practice in this way, they cannot be overcome by any śrāvaka or pratyekabuddha, and they are able to overcome all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.”
Why is this? World-Honored One!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva has already attained abiding in the state that cannot be overcome, namely, the bodhisattva’s stage of the certainty of liberation (niyāma).
“World-Honored One!
This bodhisattva-mahāsattva constantly abides in the mental attention of the knowledge of all modes and is invincible.
World-Honored One!”
"When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices in this manner, they draw near to the knowledge of all modes and will swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect,
and complete enlightenment. The Buddha said, "Subhūti!"
So it is! So it is! It is just as you have said.
"Furthermore, Subhūti! What do you think?

Suppose all the sentient beings in this Jambudvīpa were to obtain human bodies, and having obtained human bodies, were all to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. If some sons or daughters of good family, for as long as their lives lasted, were to provide offerings, honor, respect, and praise to these Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas with the most excellent worldly offerings, and furthermore, were to take these roots of goodness from such offerings and, sharing them equally with all sentient beings, dedicate them toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
"By this cause and condition, would these sons and daughters of good family acquire much merit? Subhūti replied, "Very much!"
"World-Honored One!
It is very much so! Sugata!"
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

If good sons and good daughters proclaim this profound *prajñāpāramitā* within the great assembly, establishing, defining, analyzing, and elucidating it so that it is easily understood, and remain with a mental orientation (*manasikāra*) associated with this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, the merit obtained by these good sons and good daughters through such causes and conditions will be far greater than that, immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable.”
"Furthermore, Subhūti, what do you think?

Suppose all the sentient beings in this Jambudvīpa and Pūrvavideha were to obtain human bodies, and having obtained human bodies, were all to realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment. If some sons or daughters of good family, for as long as their lives lasted, were to provide offerings, honor, respect, and praise to these Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas with the most excellent worldly offerings, and furthermore, were to take these roots of goodness from such offerings and, sharing them equally with all sentient beings, dedicate them toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
"By this cause and condition, would these sons and daughters of good family obtain much merit? Subhūti replied, "Very much!"
"World-Honored One!
It is very much so! Sugata!"
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

If good sons and good daughters proclaim this profound *prajñāpāramitā* within a great assembly, establishing, defining, analyzing, and elucidating it so that it may be easily understood, and if they abide in a mental engagement (*manasikāra*) associated with this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, then the merit obtained by these good sons and good daughters through such causes and conditions will be far greater than that, immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable.”
"Furthermore, Subhūti, what do you think?

Suppose all the sentient beings in this Jambudvīpa, Pūrvavideha, and Aparagoyānī were to obtain human bodies, and having obtained human bodies, were all to realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment. If some sons or daughters of good family, for as long as their lives lasted, were to provide offerings, honor, respect, and praise to these Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas with the most excellent worldly requisites, and furthermore, were to take these roots of goodness from such offerings and, sharing them equally with all sentient beings, dedicate them toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
“By this cause and condition, would these sons and daughters of good family acquire much merit? Subhūti replied, “Very much!”
“World-Honored One!
It is very much so! Sugata!”

The Buddha said, “Subhūti! If good sons and good daughters proclaim this profound *prajñāpāramitā* within a great assembly, establishing, defining, analyzing, and elucidating it so that it is easily understood, and if they abide in a mental orientation (*manasikāra*) associated with this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, then by these causes and conditions, the merit obtained by these good sons and good daughters shall be far greater than that [of the former], immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable.”
"Furthermore, Subhūti, what do you think?

Suppose all sentient beings within these four great continents were to obtain human bodies, and having obtained human bodies, were all to realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment. If a son of good family or a daughter of good family were to serve, honor, respect, and praise these Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas with all manner of supreme and exquisite worldly offerings for as long as their lives lasted, and furthermore, were to take these roots of goodness from such offerings and, sharing them equally with all sentient beings, dedicate them toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
“By this cause and condition, would these sons and daughters of good family acquire much merit? Subhūti replied, “Very much!”
"World-Honored One!
It is very much so! Sugata!"

The Buddha said, “Subhūti! If good sons and good daughters, among a great assembly, proclaim this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, establishing, defining, analyzing, and elucidating it so that it may be easily understood, and furthermore abide in the mental attention (*manasikāra*) associated with this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, then the merit obtained by these good sons and good daughters through these causes and conditions will be far greater than that, immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable.”
"Furthermore, Subhūti! What do you think?

Suppose all the sentient beings in this small chiliocosm were to obtain human bodies, and having obtained human bodies, were all to realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment. If some sons or daughters of good family, for as long as their lives lasted, were to provide offerings, honor, respect, and praise to these Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas with the most excellent and sublime worldly offerings, and furthermore, were to take these roots of goodness from such offerings and, sharing them equally with all sentient beings, dedicate them toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
"By this cause and condition, would these sons and daughters of good family obtain much merit? Subhūti replied, "Very much!"
“World-Honored One!
It is very much so! Sugata!”

The Buddha said, “Subhūti! If good sons and good daughters, among the great assembly, proclaim this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, establishing, defining, analyzing, and elucidating it so that it is easily understood, and furthermore abide in the mental engagement (*manasikāra*) associated with this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, then by these causes and conditions, the merit obtained by these good sons and good daughters shall be far greater than that, immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable.”
"Furthermore, Subhūti, what do you think?

Suppose all the sentient beings in this middle thousandfold world system were to obtain human bodies, and having obtained human bodies, were all to realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment. If a son of good family or a daughter of good family were, for as long as their life lasted, to provide these Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas with all manner of supreme and wonderful worldly offerings, honoring, revering, respecting, and praising them; and if they were then to take these roots of goodness from such offerings and, sharing them equally with all sentient beings, dedicate them toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
"By this cause and condition, would these sons and daughters of good family acquire much merit? Subhūti replied, "Very much!"
"World-Honored One!
It is very much so! Sugata!"
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

If good sons and good daughters proclaim this profound *prajñāpāramitā* within a great assembly, establishing, defining, analyzing, and elucidating it so that it is easily understood, and furthermore abide in a mental orientation (*manasikāra*) associated with this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, then the merit obtained by these good sons and good daughters through such causes and conditions will be far greater than that, immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable.”
"Furthermore, Subhūti! What do you think?

Suppose all the sentient beings in a trichiliocosm were to obtain human bodies, and having obtained human bodies, were all to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening. If some sons or daughters of good family, for as long as their lives lasted, were to provide offerings, honor, respect, and praise to these Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas with all the most excellent and sublime worldly offerings, and furthermore, were to take these roots of goodness from such offerings and, sharing them equally with all sentient beings, dedicate them toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening."
"By this cause and condition, would these sons and daughters of good family acquire much merit? Subhūti replied, "Very much!"
“World-Honored One!
It is very much so! Sugata!”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

If good sons or good daughters proclaim this profound *prajñāpāramitā* within a great assembly, establishing, defining, analyzing, and elucidating it so that it may be easily understood, and if they abide in mental attention (*manasikāra*) associated with this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, the merit obtained by these good sons and good daughters through such causes and conditions will be far greater than that, immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable.”
"Furthermore, Subhūti, what do you think?

Suppose all the sentient beings in this Jambudvīpa were to simultaneously obtain human bodies, and some sons or daughters of good family were to skillfully instruct and guide them all so that they abide in the ten paths of wholesome action; furthermore, taking these roots of goodness from such instruction and sharing them equally with all sentient beings, they dedicate them toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
"Would these sons and daughters of good family, by reason of this cause and condition,
acquire much merit? Subhūti replied, "Very much!"
“World-Honored One!
It is very much so! Sugata!”

The Buddha said, “Subhūti! If good sons and good daughters, among a great assembly, proclaim this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, establishing, defining, analyzing, and elucidating it so that it is easily understood, and correctly abide in mental attention associated with the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñatājñāna*), then the merit obtained by these good sons and good daughters through these causes and conditions will be far greater than that, immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable.”
"Furthermore, Subhūti! What do you think?

Suppose all the sentient beings in this Jambudvīpa and Pūrvavideha were to simultaneously obtain human bodies, and some sons or daughters of good family were to skillfully instruct and guide them so that they all abide in the ten paths of wholesome action; furthermore, taking these roots of goodness from such instruction and sharing them equally with all sentient beings, they dedicate them toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
“By this cause and condition, would these sons and daughters of good family obtain much merit? Subhūti replied, “Very much!”
“World-Honored One!
It is very much so! Sugata!”

The Buddha said, “Subhūti! If good sons or good daughters, amidst a great assembly, proclaim this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, establishing, defining, analyzing, and elucidating it so that it is easily understood, and correctly abide in the mental attention associated with the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñatā*), then the merit obtained by these good sons or good daughters through such causes and conditions will be far greater than that— immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable.”
"Furthermore, Subhūti, what do you think?

Suppose all the sentient beings in this Jambudvīpa, Pūrvavideha, and Aparagodānīya were to simultaneously obtain human bodies, and some sons or daughters of good family were to skillfully instruct and guide them all so that they abide in the ten paths of wholesome action; furthermore, taking these roots of goodness from such instruction, they would share them equally with all sentient beings and dedicate them toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
“By this cause and condition, would these sons and daughters of good family acquire much merit? Subhūti replied, “Very much!”
"World-Honored One!
