“Subhūti, you should know that by the superior power of this diligent exertion, these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas reach the further shore of the field of merit for all sentient beings.”
Why is this? Subhūti!

Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva exerts such superior power in his diligent application toward the Dharma that no sentient being can equal him, with the sole exception of the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha.
Why is this so? Subhūti!

Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, give rise to the mind of great loving-kindness (*maitrī*) upon seeing that sentient beings lack benefit and happiness; they give rise to the mind of great compassion (*karuṇā*) upon seeing that sentient beings undergo decline and suffering; they give rise to the mind of great sympathetic joy (*muditā*) upon seeing that sentient beings obtain benefit and happiness; and they give rise to the mind of great equanimity (*upekṣā*) upon seeing that sentient beings lack intrinsic nature and characteristics.

"Subhūti! Although these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas impartially give rise to great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity toward sentient beings, they remain unattached to anything whatsoever."

“Subhūti! When these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the profound perfection of wisdom, they attain great illumination; that is to say, they attain the illumination of the perfection of giving, and they also attain the illumination of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.”

"Subhūti! Although this bodhisattva mahāsattva has not yet realized the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvajñajñāna*), because he has attained non-retrogression from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, he reaches the further shore of the field of merit for sentient beings and is worthy of receiving all requisites for life, such as clothing, food and drink, bedding and seats, medicine, and other articles of sustenance."

"Subhūti! Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva abides in the mental engagement associated with the perfection of wisdom, they are able to ultimately repay the kindness of their benefactors and also draw near to the knowledge of all modes."

Therefore, Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes not to receive in vain the faithful offerings of kings, ministers, elders, householders, and sentient beings; if they wish to show sentient beings the path of true goodness; if they wish to act as a pure light for sentient beings; if they wish to liberate sentient beings from the prison of the three realms; and if they wish to bestow upon sentient beings the pure Dharma-eye, they should always abide in the mental engagement associated with the profound perfection of wisdom.

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva abides in the mental engagement associated with the perfection of wisdom, everything they speak is the teaching of the perfection of wisdom—that is, they teach the dharmas associated with the perfection of wisdom. Having taught the dharmas associated with the perfection of wisdom, they are further able to correctly contemplate those dharmas associated with the perfection of wisdom.”
“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly dwells in mental attention associated with the perfection of wisdom; there is no room for any other mental attentions to arise in the interim.”
"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva exerts himself day and night, dwelling securely in the mental engagement associated with the perfection of wisdom, never for a moment abandoning it."

"Subhūti! It is as if there were a person who had never before possessed a maṇi jewel, but later encountered and obtained one; he rejoiced deeply within himself, treasuring it without weariness. Suddenly, having lost it, he was overcome with great anguish and constant lamentation, saying: 'Alas!'"
"When shall I recover the lost maṇi-jewel?
That person never for a moment ceases to apply their attention to that maṇi-jewel.
Subhūti, you should know this!

So it is with the bodhisattva mahāsattvas: they should always be diligent in abiding in the mental engagement associated with the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*). If they are separated from this mental engagement associated with the perfection of wisdom, they will lose the mental engagement associated with the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*).
Chapter 54: Abandoning Conceptualization, Part One. At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”
All acts of mental attention are by nature detached; all acts of mental attention are by nature empty. All phenomena are likewise: they are all by nature detached and all by nature empty.

Within that which is devoid of intrinsic nature and empty of intrinsic nature, neither the bodhisattva mahāsattva, nor the perfection of wisdom, nor omniscience, nor any mental engagements can be apprehended.

How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva not depart from the mental engagement associated with the perfection of wisdom, nor likewise depart from the mental engagement associated with the knowledge of all modes?
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva knows that all phenomena and all mental engagements are by nature detached and by nature empty—such detachment and emptiness being neither made by śrāvakas, nor made by pratyekabuddhas, nor made by bodhisattva mahāsattvas, nor made by buddhas, nor made by anyone else; yet, all phenomena abide as phenomena, are fixed as phenomena, and their dharma-nature, dharma-realm, non-falsity, non-alteration, suchness, and reality-limit remain eternally established by the very nature of things.”

This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not depart from the mental engagement associated with the perfection of wisdom, nor does he depart from the mental engagement associated with the knowledge of all modes.
Why is this? Subhūti!

Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*), and all mental engagements (*manasikāra*) are all by nature detached and by nature empty; thus, this detachment and emptiness neither increase nor decrease, and because one can correctly penetrate them as being non-detached, it is called "non-detachment."
Then, the Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

If the profound *prajñāpāramitā* is also by nature detached and by nature fundamentally empty, how does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, having cultivated and realized the equality of the *prajñāpāramitā*, attain unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment?”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

When bodhisattva mahāsattvas cultivate and realize the equality of the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), there is neither increase nor decrease in the qualities of a buddha (buddhadharma). Nor is there increase or decrease in the abiding nature of all phenomena (sarvadharma), their fixed nature, their essential nature, the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), their non-falsity, their immutability, suchness (tathatā), or the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi).”
Why is this? Subhūti!
Because the profound perfection of wisdom is neither one, nor two, nor three, nor four, nor many.

"Subhūti! If, upon hearing this teaching of the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s mind is not startled, not terrified, not afraid, does not sink, does not become despondent, and is without hesitation, you should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has already attained the ultimate in practicing the profound *prajñāpāramitā* and dwells securely on the stage of the bodhisattva’s non-retrogression."

Why is that? Subhūti!

The Buddha said,

"So it is! It is just as you have said, Subhūti."
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not apprehend any phenomena, they do not form such thoughts as:

"I shall realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment; I will use these dharmas to realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment; by means of these dharmas, at such a time and in such a place, I shall realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
Why is this so? Subhūti! When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the profound perfection of wisdom, they have no such conceptual discriminations at all.
Why is this? Subhūti,
it is because the profound perfection of wisdom is without conceptual differentiation.

Kauśika! Suppose all sentient beings within this Jambudvīpa were to fully accomplish the ten paths of wholesome action, as well as immeasurable virtues such as the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, and the five superknowledges.

There may be sons of good family or daughters of good family who, regarding this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā, constantly delight in hearing it, receiving and upholding it, reading and reciting it, mastering it thoroughly, reflecting upon it according to the principle, practicing in accordance with the teaching, and correctly explaining it to others.

The merit obtained by these sons and daughters of good family surpasses the merit accomplished by all sentient beings in Jambudvīpa as previously described, being a hundred times superior, a thousand times superior, a hundred-thousand times superior, ten million times superior, a hundred-ten-million times superior, a thousand-ten-million times superior, a hundred-thousand-ten-million times superior, ten billion times superior, a hundred-billion times superior, a trillion times superior, ten trillion times superior, and even a hundred-trillion times superior; it is superior by calculation, by number, by reckoning, by analogy, and even by the *upaniṣad* (the infinitesimal) multiple.
At that time, a certain bhikṣu in the assembly said to Śakra, the Lord of Devas: "Kauśika!

Śakra, Lord of the Devas, said:

If you study in this manner, you will swiftly sit upon the sublime seat of awakening (bodhimaṇḍa) and quickly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi), turning the sublime wheel of Dharma to deliver immeasurable multitudes."
“Bhikṣus, you should know!

Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom and constantly trains in that which all bodhisattva mahāsattvas should train in, the Suyāma Heaven King, leading the assembly of the Suyāma devas, comes to his presence to make offerings, pay homage, show respect, and offer praise, saying: ‘Excellent!’”
"O Great Being!

You should diligently apply yourself with vigor to study those dharmas that all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas ought to learn; do not study the practices that śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas ought to learn. If you study in this manner, you will swiftly sit upon the sublime seat of awakening (bodhimanda) and quickly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi), turning the sublime wheel of Dharma to deliver immeasurable multitudes."

“Bhikṣus, you should know that when this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, because he constantly trains in what the assembly of bodhisattva mahāsattvas should train in, the divine king Śāntuṣita, leading the host of Tuṣita devas, comes to his presence to make offerings, pay homage, show respect, and offer praise, saying: ‘Excellent!’”
"O Great Being!

You should diligently apply yourself with vigor to learn the dharmas that all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas ought to study; do not study the practices that śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas ought to study. If you study in this manner, you will swiftly sit upon the sublime seat of enlightenment (bodhimanda), quickly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, and turn the sublime wheel of Dharma to deliver immeasurable multitudes."

“Bhikṣus, you should know that when this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, because he constantly trains in what the assembly of bodhisattva mahāsattvas ought to train in, the Deva King of Wondrous Transformations (Nirmāṇarati) arrives at his location with the host of the Heaven of Delighting in Emanations, making offerings, paying homage, honoring,
and praising him, saying: ‘Excellent!’”
"O Great Being!

You should diligently apply yourself with vigor to study the dharmas that all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas ought to learn; do not study the practices that śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas ought to learn. If you study in this way, you will swiftly and securely sit upon the sublime seat of awakening, quickly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and turn the sublime wheel of Dharma to deliver immeasurable multitudes."
“Bhikṣus, you should know!

Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom and constantly trains in that which all bodhisattva mahāsattvas ought to train in, the King of the Gods of Mastery over Others’ Emanations (Vaśavartin), leading the host of the Heaven of Mastery over Others’ Emanations, comes to his presence to make offerings, pay homage, show respect, and offer praise, saying: ‘Excellent!’”
"O Mahāsattva!

You should diligently apply yourself with vigor to study the dharmas that all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas ought to learn; do not study the practices that śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas ought to learn. If you train in this way, you will swiftly sit upon the sublime seat of awakening, quickly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and turn the sublime wheel of Dharma to deliver immeasurable multitudes."
“Bhikṣus, you should know!

Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom and constantly trains in that which all bodhisattva mahāsattvas ought to train in, Mahābrahmā, the Lord of the Sahā World, leading the hosts of the Brahmakāyika, Brahmapurohita, and Brahmakāyika devas, comes to his presence to make offerings, pay homage, show respect, and offer praise, saying these words: ‘Excellent!’”
"O Great Being!

You should diligently apply yourself with vigor to study the dharmas that all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas ought to study; do not study the practices that śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas ought to study. If you study in this manner, you will swiftly sit upon the sublime seat of awakening (bodhimanda), quickly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and turn the sublime wheel of Dharma to deliver immeasurable multitudes."
“Bhikṣus, you should know!

Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound *prajñāpāramitā* and constantly trains in that which all bodhisattva mahāsattvas ought to train in, the gods of the Ābhāsvara Heaven—the Ābhāsvara, Parīttābha, Apramāṇābha, and Ābhāsvara hosts—come to his presence to make offerings, pay respect, honor, and praise him, saying: ‘Excellent!’”
"O Mahāsattva!

You should diligently apply yourself with vigor to study the dharmas that all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas ought to study; do not study the practices that śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas ought to study. If you study in this manner, you will swiftly sit upon the sublime seat of awakening (bodhimanda) and quickly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi), turning the sublime wheel of Dharma to deliver immeasurable multitudes."

“Bhikṣus, you should know that when this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, because he constantly trains in what the assembly of bodhisattva mahāsattvas ought to train in, the gods of the Śubhakṛtsna Heaven, the Apramāṇaśubha Heaven, the Parīttaśubha Heaven, and the Śubhakṛtsna Heaven will come to his presence to make offerings, pay homage, show respect, and offer praise, saying: ‘Excellent!’”
"O Mahāsattva!

You should diligently apply yourself with vigor to study the dharmas that all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas ought to learn; do not study the practices that śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas ought to learn. If you study in this manner, you will swiftly sit upon the sublime seat of awakening (bodhimaṇḍa), quickly realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete awakening (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi), and turn the sublime wheel of Dharma to deliver immeasurable multitudes."
“Bhikṣus, you should know!

Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom and constantly trains in that which the assembly of bodhisattva mahāsattvas ought to train in, the gods of the Vast Fruit Heaven—the Bṛhatphala, Parīttābha, Apramāṇābha, and Abṛha deities—come to his presence to make offerings, pay homage, show respect, and offer praise, saying: ‘Excellent!’”
"O Great Being!

You should diligently apply yourself with vigor to study the dharmas that all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas ought to study; do not study the practices that śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas ought to study. If you study in this manner, you will quickly sit upon the sublime seat of awakening (bodhimanda) and swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi), turning the sublime wheel of Dharma to deliver immeasurable multitudes."

“Bhikṣus, you should know that when this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, because he constantly trains in what the assembly of bodhisattva mahāsattvas ought to train in, the gods of Akaniṣṭha, Avṛha, Atapa, Sudṛśa, and Sudarśana come to his presence to make offerings, pay homage, show respect, and offer praise, saying: ‘Excellent!’”
"O Mahāsattva!

You should diligently apply yourself with vigor to study the dharmas that all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas ought to learn; do not study the practices that śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas ought to learn. If you study in this manner, you will swiftly sit upon the sublime seat of awakening (bodhimaṇḍa) and quickly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi), turning the sublime wheel of Dharma to deliver immeasurable multitudes."
“Bhikṣus, you should know!

Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) as it has been taught, all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, as well as the assembly of bodhisattva mahāsattvas, together with the devas, nāgas, asuras, and others, constantly follow, protect, and keep him in mind.”
By virtue of these causes and conditions, this bodhisattva mahāsattva cannot be harmed by any worldly perils, dangers, calamities, or physical and mental anxieties and sufferings.
"Bhikṣus, you should know!"

Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound *prajñāpāramitā* as it has been taught, and because all Buddhas, bodhisattvas, devas, nāgas, asuras, and others constantly protect and keep them in mind, they are not afflicted by any diseases arising from the discordance of the great elements (*mahābhūta*) found in the world. These include: diseases of the eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, and various ailments of the limbs and joints; pain in the body, heart, head, teeth, ribs, waist, back, and abdomen; and pain in the various limbs and joints. All such four hundred and four types of diseases shall forever cease to exist within their bodies, with the sole exception that heavy karma may be transformed into a light experience.
“Bhikṣus, you should know!

Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) as it has been taught, they obtain such present-life merits, and their merits in future lives will be immeasurable and boundless.”
At that time, the Venerable Ānanda had this thought to himself:
"Is it by his own eloquence that Śakra, Lord of the Devas, extols such profound and sublime merits of the perfection of wisdom?"
"Is this due to the majestic spiritual power of the Tathāgata?
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, immediately knew what Ānanda was thinking and said to him:
"The supreme merits of the profound Prajñāpāramitā that I have praised and described are entirely due to the majestic spiritual power of the Tathāgata."
At that time, the Buddha said to Ānanda: "So it is! So it is!"

Today, when Śakra, Lord of the Devas, praises the rare and marvelous merits of the profound Prajñāpāramitā, you should know that this is entirely due to the Tathāgata’s spiritual power and not his own eloquence.
Why is this? Because the rare and profound merits of the *prajñāpāramitā* cannot be known by humans, devas, or others.
"Ānanda, you should know this!"
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva studies, contemplates, and practices this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, all the evil Māras of this trichiliocosm will give rise to doubt and think to themselves:

"Will this bodhisattva mahāsattva realize the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) and thereby regress to attain the fruit of a stream-enterer, a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat, or the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha; or will he proceed toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?"

"Furthermore, Ānanda! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not depart from such profound prajñāpāramitā, at that time all evil Māras will give rise to great sorrow and suffering, their bodies and minds trembling as if pierced by poisoned arrows."
Furthermore, Ānanda!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, an evil Māra may come to that place and manifest various terrifying things—namely, swords and blades, fierce beasts, venomous snakes, and blazing fires erupting from all four directions—with the intent to cause the bodhisattva’s body and mind to be filled with dread, to lose the unsurpassed mind of great *bodhi*, to cause their mind to become discouraged regarding their practice, or even to give rise to a single thought of distraction, thereby obstructing their attainment of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
At that time, the Venerable Ānanda addressed the Buddha,
saying: “World-Honored One,
when all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the profound perfection of wisdom, are they all disturbed and distracted by Māra, or are there some who are disturbed and some who are not?”
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"It is not the case that all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practicing the profound *prajñāpāramitā* are disturbed and distracted by Māra; rather, there are those who are disturbed and those who are not."
The Venerable Ānanda again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
which bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, when practicing the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), are disturbed and distracted by Māra?”
“What kind of bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, will not be disturbed by Māra?
The Buddha told Ānanda:

“If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, having heard this profound *prajñāpāramitā* in previous lives, does not believe or understand it in his heart and instead gives rise to slander, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, will be disturbed by Māra.”

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, having heard this profound *prajñāpāramitā* in previous lives, has deep faith and understanding and does not give rise to slander, then when that bodhisattva mahāsattva practices this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they will not be disturbed or confused by Māra.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, having heard this profound perfection of wisdom in a previous life, conceives doubt in their mind, thinking:
'Does this profound perfection of wisdom truly exist?'"
"Is it that this profound *prajñāpāramitā* does not truly exist?
When such a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they will then be disturbed and distracted by Māra, the Evil One.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, having heard this profound *prajñāpāramitā* in previous lives, does not give rise to doubt or confusion, but possesses resolute faith that the profound *prajñāpāramitā* exists, then when this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they will not be disturbed or distracted by Māra.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva distances himself from virtuous friends and is influenced by evil associates, he will not hear this profound *prajñāpāramitā*. Because he does not hear it, he cannot comprehend it; because he does not comprehend it, he cannot practice it; and because he does not practice it, he cannot realize this profound *prajñāpāramitā* as it truly is. When such a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, he will then be disturbed and distracted by Māra, the Evil One."

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva associates with virtuous friends and is not influenced by evil friends, they will hear this profound *prajñāpāramitā*. Because they hear it, they are able to comprehend it; because they comprehend it, they are able to cultivate it; and because they cultivate it, they realize the profound *prajñāpāramitā* as it truly is. When such a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they will not be disturbed or distracted by Māra, the Evil One.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva remains far removed from the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) and instead embraces and praises what is not the truly sublime Dharma, then when that bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they will be disturbed and distracted by Māra, the Evil One."

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva draws near to the perfection of wisdom and does not embrace or praise that which is not the true, sublime Dharma, then when this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they will not be disturbed or confused by Māra.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva distances himself from the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) and slanders and reviles the sublime Dharma, at that time Māra the Evil One thinks:

'Now this bodhisattva is my companion; because he slanders and reviles the sublime Dharma, there will be immeasurable sons of good family and daughters of good family dwelling in the Bodhisattva Vehicle who will likewise give rise to slander against the sublime Dharma. By this cause and condition, my wish shall be fulfilled.'"

"Even if these sons and daughters of good family belonging to the Bodhisattva vehicle exert themselves with diligence in cultivating various wholesome dharmas, they may fall into the stage of a Śrāvaka or a Pratyekabuddha, and cause others to fall as well."
Ānanda, you should know that when these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the profound perfection of wisdom, they will be disturbed and distracted by Māra, the Evil One.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva draws near to the perfection of wisdom, places faith in and praises the sublime and true Dharma, and likewise causes immeasurable sons and daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva Vehicle to place faith in and praise the sublime and true Dharma, then the evil Māra will become terrified, distressed, and afflicted. Consequently, even if these sons and daughters of good family in the Bodhisattva Vehicle do not diligently cultivate wholesome dharmas, they will nonetheless certainly prevent themselves and others from falling back into the stages of the Śrāvaka or Pratyekabuddha, and will surely realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Ānanda, you should know that when these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the profound perfection of wisdom, they are not disturbed or distracted by Māra.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, upon hearing the teaching of the profound *prajñāpāramitā* sūtra, speaks these words:

'This *prajñāpāramitā* is extremely profound, difficult to see and difficult to realize; what is the use of proclaiming it, hearing it, receiving and upholding it, reading and reciting it, contemplating it, diligently practicing it, writing it down, or disseminating it? "
"I cannot even fathom its source or its depths, much less those of others with shallow wisdom!

At that time, immeasurable sons and daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle heard what was said and were struck with fear; they all retreated from their resolve for unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Ānanda, you should know that when these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they will be disturbed and distracted by Māra, the Evil One.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, upon hearing the teaching of this profound *prajñāpāramitā* sūtra, speaks as follows:

"This *prajñāpāramitā* is exceedingly profound, difficult to see and difficult to realize; it is impossible that one could realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening without its being proclaimed, heard, received, upheld, recited, contemplated, diligently practiced, written down, and disseminated."

At that time, immeasurable sons and daughters of good family who abide in the vehicle of the bodhisattvas, hearing what was said, rejoiced and leaped for joy; they all constantly delighted in hearing, receiving, upholding, reading, reciting, thoroughly mastering, reflecting upon according to the principle, diligently practicing, explaining to others, and transcribing and disseminating this *prajñāpāramitā*, thereby swiftly proceeding toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Ānanda, you should know that when these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the profound perfection of wisdom, they are not disturbed or distracted by Māra.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on his own meritorious roots of virtue, disparages other bodhisattva mahāsattvas, saying:
'I am able to practice the pāramitās of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, whereas you are not.'"

I am able to abide in internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, emptiness of self-characteristics, emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence; you, however, are not able to do so.

I am able to abide in suchness, the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm; you, however, are not able to do so.
"I am able to dwell securely in the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path, whereas you are not.
I am able to cultivate the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments, whereas you are not."
I am able to cultivate the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities, whereas you are not.

I am able to cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path, whereas you are not.
"I am able to cultivate the gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—but you are not.
I am able to cultivate the ten stages of a bodhisattva, but you are not."
"I am able to purify Buddha-fields and bring sentient beings to maturity, whereas you are not.
I am able to contemplate the twelve links of dependent origination in both forward and reverse order, whereas you are not."
I am able to cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers, whereas you cannot.

I am able to cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, whereas you cannot.
"I am able to cultivate śamatha and vipaśyanā, whereas you are not.
I am able to cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity, whereas you are not."
"I am able to cultivate the gateways of dhāraṇī and the gateways of samādhi, whereas you are not.
I am able to cultivate all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), whereas you are not."
I am able to observe the specific and general characteristics of all phenomena, whereas you are not.
I am able to cultivate all the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, whereas you are not.
"I am able to cultivate the unexcelled, perfect enlightenment of all Buddhas, whereas you are not.
At that time, the evil Māra, filled with joy and exultation, said:
"This bodhisattva is my companion; there will be no end to his wandering in birth and death."
"Ānanda, you should know that when these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the profound perfection of wisdom, they will be disturbed and distracted by Māra, the Evil One."

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not rely on their own meritorious roots of goodness, does not disparage other bodhisattva mahāsattvas, and although they constantly exert themselves in cultivating all wholesome dharmas, does not cling to the characteristics of those wholesome dharmas.
Ānanda, you should know that when these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the profound perfection of wisdom, they are not disturbed or distracted by Māra.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!

If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva, relying on his own name and lineage known to the multitude, looks down upon other bodhisattvas who cultivate goodness; constantly praising his own virtues and disparaging others; and though he actually lacks the practices, marks, and signs of a non-retrogressive bodhisattva-mahāsattva, claims they truly exist; and gives rise to various afflictions to praise himself and disparage others, saying:
'You all lack the name and lineage of a bodhisattva; I alone possess the name and lineage of a bodhisattva.'"
Because they, out of overweening pride, despise and revile the assembly of other bodhisattva-mahāsattvas,
at that time the evil Māra, having seen this, thinks to himself:
"Now this bodhisattva makes my realm and palaces not empty, but increases the realms of hell-beings, animals, and hungry ghosts."

At that time, Māra, the Evil One, aided him with his supernatural power, causing his majesty and eloquence to increase further; consequently, many people believed and accepted his words, and because of this, they were exhorted and incited to share in those same evil views.

Having seen that, they follow their wrong teachings; having followed those teachings, their afflictions blaze forth. Because their minds are inverted, all the physical, verbal, and mental actions they initiate are capable of bringing about undesirable, ruinous, and painful results.

By these causes and conditions, the three evil realms increase, causing the palaces and lands of Māra to become filled; consequently, the evil Māras rejoice and leap for joy, their every undertaking proceeding according to their will with complete mastery.
Ānanda, you should know that when these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the profound perfection of wisdom, they will be disturbed and distracted by Māra, the Evil One.

If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva does not rely on their own false name and lineage to despise other bodhisattvas who cultivate goodness; if they possess no overweening pride regarding their merits; if they never praise themselves nor disparage others; and if they are able to skillfully recognize the activities of Māra.
Ānanda, you should know that when these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the profound perfection of wisdom, they are not disturbed or distracted by Māra.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva engages in mutual disparagement, abuse, quarreling, and slander with those who seek the vehicle of the śrāvakas or the pratyekabuddhas."
At that time, having seen this event, Māra the Evil One thought to himself:
"This son of good family is distancing himself from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and is drawing near to the realms of hell, animals, and hungry ghosts."

Why is this? Mutual disparagement, humiliation, strife, and slander are not the path to bodhi; rather, they are the paths to the various evil destinies of the hells, the animal realm, and the realm of hungry ghosts.
Having formed this thought, he rejoices and leaps for joy.
Ānanda, you should know that when such a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they are then disturbed and distracted by Māra, the Evil One.

If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva does not revile, insult, quarrel with, or slander those who seek the vehicles of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, but instead uses skillful means to guide and transform them so that they may enter the Mahāyāna, or causes them to diligently cultivate the wholesome dharmas of their own respective vehicles.
Ānanda, you should know that when these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the profound perfection of wisdom, they are not disturbed or distracted by Māra.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva should engage in mutual insults, strife, and slander with other sons and daughters of good family who seek unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
At that time, having seen this event, Māra the Evil One thought to himself:
"These two bodhisattvas are both far removed from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and both are close to the realms of hell, animals, and hungry ghosts."

Why is this? Mutual disparagement, humiliation, strife, and slander are not the path to bodhi; rather, they are the paths to the various evil destinies of the hells, the animal realm, and the realm of hungry ghosts.
Having formed this thought, he leaps for joy with exultation.
Ānanda, you should know that when such a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they are then disturbed and distracted by Māra, the Evil One.

If Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas do not disparage, insult, contend with, or slander those sons and daughters of good family who seek unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, but instead instruct and exhort one another to diligently cultivate wholesome dharmas, they will cause them to swiftly realize the knowledge of all modes.
Ānanda, you should know that when these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the profound perfection of wisdom, they are not disturbed or distracted by Māra.
“Ānanda, you should know this!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva who has not yet received the prediction of non-retrogression for unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment gives rise to a harmful mind toward other bodhisattvas who have received that prediction—engaging in strife, quarreling, insulting, disparaging, or slandering them—that bodhisattva mahāsattva, in accordance with the number of such thoughts of non-benefit he has produced, shall retrogress for that many eons from the sublime practices he had previously cultivated; for that length of time he shall remain far removed from virtuous friends, and he shall once again undergo that many cycles of birth and death.”
"If one does not abandon the great bodhicitta, one must again diligently cultivate sublime practices for as many eons as were lost, and only then can the regressed merit be restored.
At that time, the Venerable Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
Will this Bodhisattva Mahāsattva necessarily continue to transmigrate for such a duration due to the suffering of birth and death resulting from the evil thoughts he has generated,
or will he also attain liberation in the interim?

Regarding the superior practices from which this bodhisattva-mahāsattva has regressed: must they necessarily exert diligent effort for that many kalpas before they can be restored, or is there a way to recover them in the interim?
The Buddha told Ānanda:
“For bodhisattvas, pratyekabuddhas, and śrāvakas, I have taught the existence of dharmas for the restoration of virtue and the expiation of offenses.
Ānanda, you should know this!”

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, who has not yet received the prediction of non-retrogression regarding unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, gives rise to a mind of malice toward those bodhisattvas who have received such a prediction—engaging in conflict, disparagement, contempt, and slander—and furthermore, lacking shame and remorse, harbors resentment without relinquishing it, and is unable to confess and repent according to the Dharma, I say that for such a person there is no possibility of emerging from the offense or restoring their virtue during that interval; they must instead wander through birth and death for as many eons as were involved, remaining far removed from virtuous friends and bound by manifold sufferings.
If one does not abandon the great bodhicitta, one must diligently cultivate sublime practices for that many eons before the lost merit can be restored.

If a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who has not yet received the prediction of non-retrogression from unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment should harbor a harmful mind toward other Bodhisattvas who have received such a prediction—engaging in strife, disparagement, contempt, or slander—and subsequently feels shame and remorse, with no lingering resentment in their heart, quickly confesses and reforms according to the Dharma, thinking thus:
"I have now obtained this human body so difficult to find; how could I again give rise to such faults and evils as to lose this great and wholesome benefit?"
"I ought to benefit all sentient beings; how could I, instead, cause them harm?
I ought to revere all sentient beings as a servant serves his master; how could I, instead, give rise to arrogance, disparage, or treat them with contempt?"
"I ought to endure all the beatings and verbal abuse of sentient beings; how could I, in turn, retaliate against them with violent physical or verbal acts?
I ought to reconcile all sentient beings so that they may respect and love one another; why then would I give rise to harsh and evil speech to provoke conflict with them?"
I should endure being trodden upon by all sentient beings for a long time, like a road or a bridge; how could I, on the contrary, treat them with contempt?

I seek unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment in order to liberate sentient beings from the great suffering of birth and death and to enable them to attain ultimate peace and happiness in nirvana; how could I possibly wish to inflict further suffering upon them?

From this day forth until the end of the future, I shall be like one who is dull-witted, mute, deaf, and blind; I shall not engage in any discrimination toward sentient beings. Even if my head, feet, or limbs were to be severed, I would never give rise to malice toward those beings, lest I produce evil thoughts that would destroy the unsurpassed mind of perfect enlightenment and obstruct the attainment of all-knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*).

"Ānanda, you should know that for these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, I say there is also the principle of emerging from transgressions and restoring their virtue during the interim; it is not necessary for them to undergo the cycle of birth and death for such a vast number of kalpas, and evil Māras will be unable to disturb them."
“Ānanda, you should know this!

Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should not engage in conversation with those who seek the vehicle of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas; even if they do engage in conversation, they should not dwell together with them; and even if they dwell together, they should not debate or resolve doctrinal points with them.”
Why is this? If one were to engage in debate and deliberation with such persons, they might give rise to thoughts of anger and resentment, or cause harsh and abusive speech to emerge.

Nevertheless, Bodhisattvas should not give rise to thoughts of anger or resentment toward sentient beings, nor should they utter harsh or abusive speech; even if their heads, feet, or limbs were to be severed, they should still not give rise to anger or malicious words.
Why is this? One should reflect thus:

"I seek unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment in order to uproot the manifold sufferings of birth and death for sentient beings and enable them to attain ultimate benefit and peace; how could I, in turn, give rise to harmful actions toward them?"
"Ānanda, you should know this!

If bodhisattvas give rise to a mind of malice toward sentient beings and utter harsh and evil words, they thereby obstruct the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) of a bodhisattva and also destroy boundless, supreme dharmas of practice."
Therefore, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who wish to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening should not harbor anger toward sentient beings, nor should they utter harsh or abusive speech.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 337. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter Fifty-five, Part Two, "Skillful Means and Training. At that time, Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"Bodhisattvas, how should bodhisattvas dwell together?
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"When bodhisattvas dwell together, they should regard one another as they would the Great Teacher."
Why is this? When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas look at one another, they should form this thought: "That person is our true spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra);
he is my companion, traveling with me on the same ship. Between us, there is no difference whatsoever regarding the precepts we observe, the time of training, or the dharmas to be learned."
Just as they should train in the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, so too should I train;

just as they should train in internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, so too should I train.

Just as they should study suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-falsity, the immutability, the equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm, so too should I study;
just as they should study the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path, so too should I study;
just as they should study the four meditative concentrations, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments, so too should I study.
Just as they should train in the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities, so too should I train;

just as they should train in the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path, so too should I train;
just as they should train in the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—so too should I train.
Just as they should train in the ten stages of a bodhisattva, so too should I train;
just as they should train in the five eyes and the six supernormal powers, so too should I train;

just as they should train in the ten powers of a buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, so too should I train.
Just as they should train in the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity, so too should I train;
just as they should train in the gateways of dhāraṇī and the gateways of samādhi, so too should I train;
just as they should train in purifying buddha-fields and maturing sentient beings, so too should I train.

"Just as they should train in all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), so too should I train. Furthermore, he thinks:
"Those bodhisattvas who teach us the path to great enlightenment are my true companions and also my teachers."

If that bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in distracted mental attention and remains far removed from mental attention associated with the knowledge of all modes, then I do not follow their training therein.

If that bodhisattva mahāsattva is free from distracted mental engagement and does not depart from mental engagement associated with the knowledge of all modes, then I shall always train in accordance with him therein.
"Ānanda, you should know this!

If the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas can train in this way, they will swiftly bring the provisions for enlightenment to full completion. When the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas trains in this manner, it is called 'training in equality.'"
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha,
saying: "World-Honored One,
what is the equality of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, such that because bodhisattva-mahāsattvas train therein, it is called 'training in equality'?"
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Internal emptiness is the sameness of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are the sameness of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. Because bodhisattva-mahāsattvas train in these, it is called ‘training in sameness. Through this training in sameness, they swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

That form is empty of the intrinsic nature of form is the sameness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva; that feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are empty of the intrinsic nature of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is the sameness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva. Because all bodhisattva mahāsattvas train in this, it is called 'training in sameness. Through training in sameness, they swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
"Furthermore, Subhūti! The eye-base is empty of the intrinsic nature of the eye-base;

this is the sameness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva. The ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases are empty of the intrinsic nature of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases; this is the sameness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva. Because bodhisattva mahāsattvas train in these, it is called 'training in sameness. Through training in sameness, they swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The fact that the sphere of form is empty of the intrinsic nature of the sphere of form is the sameness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva; the fact that the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are empty of the intrinsic nature of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is the sameness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva. Because all bodhisattva mahāsattvas train in this, it is called 'training in sameness. Through this training in sameness, they swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
"Furthermore, Subhūti! The eye-sphere is empty of the intrinsic nature of the eye-sphere;

this is the sameness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva. The ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-spheres are empty of the intrinsic nature of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-spheres; this is the sameness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva. Because bodhisattva mahāsattvas train in these, it is called 'training in sameness. Through training in sameness, they swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The fact that the form realm is empty of the intrinsic nature of the form realm is the sameness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva; the fact that the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and phenomena are empty of the intrinsic nature of the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and phenomena is the sameness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva. Because all bodhisattva mahāsattvas train in this, it is called 'training in sameness. Through this training in sameness, they swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."

"Furthermore, Subhūti! The eye-consciousness element is empty of the intrinsic nature of the eye-consciousness element; this is the sameness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva. The ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements are empty of the intrinsic nature of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements; this is the sameness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva. Because all bodhisattva mahāsattvas train in this, it is called 'training in sameness. Through training in sameness, they swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."

"Furthermore, Subhūti! Eye-contact is empty of the intrinsic nature of eye-contact; this is the sameness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva. Ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact are empty of the intrinsic nature of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact; this is the sameness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva. Because bodhisattva mahāsattvas train in these, it is called 'training in sameness. Through training in sameness, they swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The feelings produced with eye-contact as condition—the self-nature of these feelings produced with eye-contact as condition being empty—is the sameness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva. The feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as condition—the self-nature of these feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as condition being empty—is the sameness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva. Because bodhisattva mahāsattvas train in this, it is called 'training in sameness. Through training in sameness, they swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."

"Furthermore, Subhūti! The earth element is empty of the intrinsic nature of the earth element; this is the sameness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva. The water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are empty of the intrinsic nature of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements; this is the sameness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva. Because bodhisattva mahāsattvas train in these, it is called 'training in sameness. Through training in sameness, they swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."

"Furthermore, Subhūti! Ignorance is empty of the intrinsic nature of ignorance; this is the sameness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva. Formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age and death are empty of the intrinsic nature of formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age and death; this is the sameness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva. Because bodhisattva mahāsattvas train in these, it is called 'training in sameness. Through training in sameness, they swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

That the perfection of generosity is empty of the intrinsic nature of the perfection of generosity is the equality of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; that the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are empty of the intrinsic nature of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom is the equality of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. Because bodhisattva-mahāsattvas train within these, it is called 'equal training,' and through this equal training, they swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
"Furthermore, Subhūti! The emptiness of inner emptiness—the fact that inner emptiness is empty of its own intrinsic nature—is the sameness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate, the emptiness of the conditioned, and the emptiness of the unconditioned..."
emptiness, ultimate emptiness, boundless emptiness, emptiness of dispersion, emptiness of non-alteration, emptiness of essential nature,
emptiness of self-characteristic, emptiness of common characteristic, emptiness of all phenomena, emptiness of the unapprehendable,
emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, external emptiness, and internal-external emptiness.
Emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, emptiness of the ultimate truth, emptiness of the conditioned, emptiness of the unconditioned,
absolute emptiness, emptiness of the limitless, emptiness of dispersion, emptiness of non-alteration, emptiness of intrinsic nature, emptiness of specific characteristics,
emptiness of common characteristics, emptiness of all phenomena, emptiness of non-apprehensibility, and emptiness of non-existence.
Emptiness of intrinsic nature and emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—this emptiness of intrinsic nature is the state of equality of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas.
Because bodhisattva mahāsattvas train in this, it is called "training in equality.
Through this training in equality, they swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
"Furthermore, Subhūti! The suchness of suchness is empty of its own intrinsic nature;

this is the state of equality of the bodhisattva mahāsattva. The dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-erroneous nature, the unchanging nature, the state of equality, the state of being free from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm—these, being empty of their own intrinsic nature, are the state of equality of the bodhisattva mahāsattva. Because all bodhisattva mahāsattvas train in these, it is called 'training in equality. Through this training in equality, they swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."

"Furthermore, Subhūti! The noble truth of suffering is empty of the intrinsic nature of the noble truth of suffering; this is the sameness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva. The noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are empty of the intrinsic nature of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path; this is the sameness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva. Because bodhisattva mahāsattvas train in these, it is called 'training in sameness. Through training in sameness, they swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
"Furthermore, Subhūti! The four dhyānas are empty of the intrinsic nature of the four dhyānas;

this is the sameness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva. The four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are empty of the intrinsic nature of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments; this is the sameness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva. Because bodhisattva mahāsattvas train in these, it is called 'training in sameness. Through training in sameness, they swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The eight liberations (aṣṭa-vimokṣa) are the equality of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas because the intrinsic nature of the eight liberations is empty; the eight bases of mastery (aṣṭābhibhv-āyatana), the nine successive attainments (navānupūrva-samāpatti), and the ten totalities (daśa-kṛtsnāyatana) are the equality of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas because the intrinsic nature of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities is empty. Because bodhisattva-mahāsattvas train in these, it is called 'training in equality. Through this training in equality, they swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the four applications of mindfulness is the sameness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva; the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eight branches of the noble path is the sameness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva. Because bodhisattva mahāsattvas train in these, it is called 'training in sameness. Through this training in sameness, they swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The emptiness of the gate of liberation of emptiness—the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the gate of liberation of emptiness—is the sameness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva. The signlessness and wishlessness of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness—the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness—is the sameness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva. Because all bodhisattva mahāsattvas train in this, it is called 'training in sameness. Through training in sameness, they swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The intrinsic emptiness of the Ground of Extreme Joy is the sameness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva. The intrinsic emptiness of the Ground of Purity, the Ground of Radiance, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Utmost Difficulty to Conquer, the Ground of Manifestation, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, and the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma—this intrinsic emptiness of the Ground of Purity, the Ground of Radiance, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Utmost Difficulty to Conquer, the Ground of Manifestation, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, and the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma is the sameness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva. Because bodhisattva mahāsattvas train in this, it is called 'training in sameness. Through training in sameness, they swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
"Furthermore, Subhūti! The five eyes are empty of the intrinsic nature of the five eyes;

this is the sameness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva. The six supernormal powers are empty of the intrinsic nature of the six supernormal powers; this is the sameness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva. Because bodhisattva mahāsattvas train in these, it is called 'training in sameness. Through training in sameness, they swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."

"Furthermore, Subhūti! The ten powers of a Buddha are empty of the intrinsic nature of the ten powers of a Buddha; this is the sameness of a bodhisattva mahāsattva. The four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are empty of the intrinsic nature of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; this is the sameness of a bodhisattva mahāsattva. Because bodhisattva mahāsattvas train in these, it is called 'training in sameness. Through training in sameness, they swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."

"Furthermore, Subhūti! The quality of non-forgetfulness is empty of the intrinsic nature of the quality of non-forgetfulness; this is the sameness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva. The state of constant abiding in equanimity is empty of the intrinsic nature of the state of constant abiding in equanimity; this is the sameness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva. Because bodhisattva mahāsattvas train in these, it is called 'training in sameness. Through this training in sameness, they swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The emptiness of the intrinsic nature of all-knowledge (sarvajñatā) is the state of equality of the bodhisattva mahāsattva; the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the knowledge of the paths (mārgajñatā) and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā) is the state of equality of the bodhisattva mahāsattva. Because bodhisattvas mahāsattvas train in these, it is called 'training in equality,' and through this training in equality, they swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The fact that all dhāraṇī-doors are empty of the intrinsic nature of all dhāraṇī-doors is the sameness of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; the fact that all samādhi-doors are empty of the intrinsic nature of all samādhi-doors is the sameness of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. Because bodhisattva-mahāsattvas train in these, it is called 'training in sameness. Through this training in sameness, they swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the fruit of stream-entry is the sameness of a bodhisattva mahāsattva; the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship is the sameness of a bodhisattva mahāsattva. Because bodhisattva mahāsattvas train in these, it is called 'training in sameness. Through this training in sameness, they swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The awakening of a pratyekabuddha—the self-nature of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha—is empty; this is the sameness of the bodhisattva mahāsattva. Because bodhisattva mahāsattvas train in this, it is called 'training in sameness. Through training in sameness, they swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The fact that the practice of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is empty of an intrinsic nature—that is the equality of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. Because bodhisattva-mahāsattvas train in this, it is called 'equal training' (*samatā-śikṣā*); through this equal training, they swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas—the very self-nature of which is empty—is the state of equality for bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. Because bodhisattva-mahāsattvas train in this, it is called 'training in equality. Through this training in equality, they swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
if a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the exhaustion of form, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?”
If one trains for the sake of the exhaustion of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the detachment from form, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If one trains for the sake of the detachment from feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the cessation of form, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If one trains for the sake of the cessation of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the non-arising of form, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If one trains for the sake of the non-arising of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness, is this training in the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna)?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the non-extinction of form, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If one trains for the sake of the non-extinction of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the primordial tranquility of form, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If one trains for the sake of the primordial stillness of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the intrinsic nirvāṇa of form, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
“Is training for the sake of the self-nature nirvāṇa of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness training in the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna)?
“World-Honored One!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the exhaustion of the eye-base (cakṣur-āyatana), is this training in the knowledge of all modes?”
If one trains for the sake of the exhaustion of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, is this training in the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna)?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the detachment from the sense base of the eye, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If one trains for the sake of the detachment from the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the cessation of the sense base of the eye, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If one trains for the sake of the cessation of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the non-arising of the sense base of the eye, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If one trains for the sake of the non-arising of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, is this training in the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*)?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the non-extinction of the sense base of the eye, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
Is the training for the sake of the non-extinction of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind the training for the knowledge of all modes?
Is the training of a bodhisattva mahāsattva for the sake of the primordial stillness of the sense base of the eye the training for the knowledge of all modes?
If one trains for the sake of the primordial stillness of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the self-nature nirvāṇa of the sense base of the eye, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
“Is training for the sake of the self-nature nirvāṇa of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind training for the sake of the knowledge of all modes?
“World-Honored One! [The Venerable Subhūti replied.]
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the exhaustion of the sense-base of form, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
