If they train for the sake of the exhaustion of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of detachment from the four foundations of mindfulness, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If they train for the sake of detachment from the four right efforts, up to and including the eight branches of the noble path, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the cessation of the four foundations of mindfulness, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If they train for the sake of the cessation of the four right efforts, up to and including the eight branches of the noble path, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the non-arising of the four foundations of mindfulness, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If they train for the sake of the non-arising of the four right endeavors, up to and including the eight branches of the noble path, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the non-extinction of the four foundations of mindfulness, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If they train for the sake of the non-extinction of the four right endeavors, up to and including the eight branches of the noble path, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains because the four foundations of mindfulness are primordially quiescent, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If they train because the four right endeavors, up to and including the eight branches of the noble path, are primordially quiescent, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the self-nature nirvāṇa of the four foundations of mindfulness, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If they train for the sake of the self-nature nirvāṇa of the four right endeavors, up to the eight branches of the noble path, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
“World-Honored One!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the exhaustion of the liberation door of emptiness, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If they train for the sake of the exhaustion of the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?”
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of detachment from the gate of liberation of emptiness, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If they train for the sake of detachment from the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the cessation of the liberation door of emptiness, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If they train for the sake of the cessation of the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the non-arising of the liberation door of emptiness, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If they train for the sake of the non-arising of the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the non-extinction of the liberation door of emptiness, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If they train for the sake of the non-extinction of the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains because the gate of liberation of emptiness is primordially quiescent, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If they train because the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are primordially quiescent, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the self-nature nirvāṇa of the emptiness gate of liberation, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If they train for the sake of the self-nature nirvāṇa of the signlessness and wishlessness gates of liberation, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
“World-Honored One!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of exhausting the Stage of Extreme Joy, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?

If one trains for the sake of exhausting the Stage of Freedom from Defilement, the Radiant Stage, the Blazing Wisdom Stage, the Extremely Difficult to Conquer Stage, the Manifest Stage, the Far-Reaching Stage, the Immovable Stage, the Stage of Excellent Intelligence, and the Cloud of Dharma Stage, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?”
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of detachment from the Stage of Extreme Joy, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If they train for the sake of detachment from the Stage of Stainless up to the Stage of Dharma Cloud, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the cessation of the Stage of Extreme Joy, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If they train for the sake of the cessation of the Stage of Freedom from Defilement, up to the Stage of the Cloud of Dharma, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the non-arising of the Stage of Extreme Joy, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If they train for the sake of the non-arising of the Stage of Freedom from Defilement, up to the Stage of the Cloud of Dharma, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the non-extinction of the Stage of Extreme Joy, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If they train for the sake of the non-extinction of the Stage of Freedom from Defilement, up to the Stage of the Cloud of Dharma, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the primordial stillness of the Stage of Extreme Joy, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If they train for the sake of the primordial stillness of the Stages from the Stainless up to the Cloud of Dharma, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the intrinsic nirvāṇa of the Stage of Extreme Joy, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If they train for the sake of the intrinsic nirvāṇa of the Stage Free from Defilement up to the Stage of the Cloud of Dharma, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
“World-Honored One,
if a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the exhaustion of the five eyes, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If he trains for the sake of the exhaustion of the six supernormal powers, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?”
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the detachment of the five eyes, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If they train for the sake of the detachment of the six supernormal powers, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the cessation of the five eyes, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If he trains for the sake of the cessation of the six supernormal powers, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the non-arising of the five eyes, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If they train for the sake of the non-arising of the six supernormal powers, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the non-extinction of the five eyes, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If they train for the sake of the non-extinction of the six supernormal powers, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains because the five eyes are fundamentally quiescent, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If they train because the six supernormal powers are fundamentally quiescent, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the intrinsic nirvāṇa of the five eyes, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If they train for the sake of the intrinsic nirvāṇa of the six supernormal powers, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
“World-Honored One!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the exhaustion of the Buddha’s ten powers, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?

If they train for the sake of the exhaustion of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?”
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of being detached from the ten powers of a buddha, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If they train for the sake of being detached from the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the cessation of the Buddha’s ten powers, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If they train for the sake of the cessation of the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the non-arising of the ten powers of a buddha, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If they train for the sake of the non-arising of the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the non-extinction of the ten powers of a buddha, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If they train for the sake of the non-extinction of the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains because the ten powers of a buddha are originally quiescent, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If one trains because the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, are originally quiescent, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the self-nature nirvāṇa of the Buddha’s ten powers, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If they train for the sake of the self-nature nirvāṇa of the four fearlessnesses, up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
“World-Honored One!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the exhaustion of the quality of non-forgetfulness, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If one trains for the sake of the exhaustion of the nature of constant equanimity, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?”
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of being free from the state of non-forgetfulness, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If one trains for the sake of being free from the state of constant equanimity, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the cessation of the quality of non-forgetfulness, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If they train for the sake of the cessation of the state of constant equanimity, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the non-arising of the quality of non-forgetfulness, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If they train for the sake of the non-arising of the state of constant equanimity, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the non-forgetfulness and non-extinction of the dharmas, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If one trains for the sake of the non-extinction of the state of constant equanimity, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the dharma of non-forgetfulness being primordially quiescent, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If they train for the sake of the nature of constant equanimity being primordially quiescent, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the self-nature nirvāṇa of the quality of non-forgetfulness, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If they train for the sake of the self-nature nirvāṇa of the state of constant equanimity, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
“World-Honored One!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the exhaustion of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), is this training in the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*)?

If they train for the sake of the exhaustion of the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), is this training in the knowledge of all modes?”
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of detachment from all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), is this training in the knowledge of all-knowledge?

If they train for the sake of detachment from the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), is this training in the knowledge of all-knowledge?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the cessation of all-knowledge, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If they train for the sake of the cessation of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the non-arising of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), is this training in the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*)?
If they train for the sake of the non-arising of the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the non-extinction of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), is this training in the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*)?
If they train for the sake of the non-extinction of the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains because all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) is primordially quiescent, is this training in the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*)?
If one trains because the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are primordially quiescent, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the self-nature nirvāṇa of all-knowledge, is this training in the knowledge of all aspects?
If they train for the sake of the self-nature nirvāṇa of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects, is this training in the knowledge of all aspects?
“Bhagavān! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of exhausting all dhāraṇī-doors, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If he trains for the sake of exhausting all samādhi-doors, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?”
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the detachment of all dhāraṇī-doors, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If they train for the sake of the detachment of all samādhi-doors, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the cessation of all dhāraṇī-doors, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If they train for the sake of the cessation of all samādhi-doors, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the non-arising of all dhāraṇī-doors, is this training in the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna)?
If one trains for the sake of the non-arising of all samādhi-doors, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the non-extinction of all dhāraṇī-doors, is this training in the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna)?
If they train for the sake of the non-extinction of all samādhi-doors, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains because all dhāraṇī-doors are fundamentally quiescent, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If one trains because all samādhi-doors are fundamentally quiescent, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the intrinsic nirvāṇa of all dhāraṇī-doors, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If one trains for the sake of the intrinsic nirvāṇa of all samādhi-doors, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
“World-Honored One!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the exhaustion of the fruit of stream-entry, does this training constitute training in the knowledge of all modes?
If one trains for the sake of the exhaustion of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, or arhatship, does this training constitute training in the knowledge of all modes?”
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of detachment from the fruit of a stream-enterer, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If they train for the sake of detachment from the fruits of a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the cessation of the fruit of a stream-enterer, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If they train for the sake of the cessation of the fruits of a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the non-arising of the fruit of a stream-enterer, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If they train for the sake of the non-arising of the fruits of a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the non-extinction of the fruit of stream-entry, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If they train for the sake of the non-extinction of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, or arhatship, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the fruit of stream-entry because it is originally quiescent, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If one trains for the sake of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, or arhatship because they are originally quiescent, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the intrinsic nirvāṇa of the fruit of a stream-enterer, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If they train for the sake of the intrinsic nirvāṇa of the fruits of a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
“Bhagavān, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the exhaustion of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the detachment from pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?”
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the cessation of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, is that training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the non-arising of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, is that training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha because it is non-extinguished, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha because it is originally quiescent, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
“If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the self-nature nirvāṇa of pratyekabuddha awakening, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
“World-Honored One! [The Bodhisattva asked.]
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of exhausting all the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, is this training in the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna)?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of detaching from all the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the cessation of all bodhisattva mahāsattva practices, is this training in the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna)?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the non-arising of all bodhisattva mahāsattva practices, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the non-extinction of all bodhisattva mahāsattva practices, is this training in the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna)?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the primordial quiescence of all bodhisattva mahāsattva practices, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the intrinsic nirvāṇa of the practice of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
“World-Honored One!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas until its exhaustion, is this training in the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna)?”
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas by way of detachment, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas by way of cessation, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the non-arising of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the non-cessation of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas is fundamentally quiescent, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the self-nature nirvāṇa of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
“World-Honored One!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the exhaustion of sentient beings, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the separation from sentient beings, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?”
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of extinguishing sentient beings, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the non-arising of sentient beings, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the non-extinction of sentient beings, is this training in the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna)?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the primordial quiescence of sentient beings, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
“If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the self-nature nirvāṇa of sentient beings, is this training in the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna)?
“World-Honored One!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the exhaustion of a bodhisattva, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?”
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the bodhisattva’s detachment, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the bodhisattva’s cessation, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the non-arising of a bodhisattva, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the non-ceasing of a bodhisattva, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the primordial stillness of a bodhisattva, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the self-nature nirvāṇa of a bodhisattva, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
“World-Honored One!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the Tathāgata’s exhaustion [of defilements], is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the Tathāgata’s detachment, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?”
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the Tathāgata’s cessation, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the Tathāgata’s non-arising, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the Tathāgata being non-extinguished, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the Tathāgata being originally quiescent, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the self-nature nirvāṇa of the Tathāgata, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
The Buddha said, "Subhūti!..."
As you have said: "If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the exhaustion of form, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If one trains for the sake of the exhaustion of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?"
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of detachment from form, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If they train for the sake of detachment from feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the cessation of form, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If he trains for the sake of the cessation of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the non-arising of form, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If they train for the sake of the non-arising of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the non-extinction of form, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If he trains for the sake of the non-extinction of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains because form is originally quiescent, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If one trains because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are originally quiescent, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the intrinsic nature of form being nirvāṇa, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If he trains for the sake of the intrinsic nature of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness being nirvāṇa, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
"Subhūti, what do you think? Is the suchness of form exhausted, ceased, or severed?"
Subhūti replied, “No, World-Honored One!”
"No, Sugata! the Buddha said.
“Subhūti, what do you think? Is the suchness of feeling,
perception, mental formations, and consciousness exhausted, ceased, or abandoned?”
Subhūti replied, “No, World-Honored One!”
"No, Sugata," he replied. The Buddha said:
"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in suchness in this way, they are training in the knowledge of all modes.
Subhūti, you should know this!"

Suchness is inexhaustible, unceasing, uninterrupted, and cannot be realized as an object; if a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in suchness in this way, they are training in the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin! As you have said:
‘If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the exhaustion of the eye-base, is this training in the knowledge of all aspects?’”
If one trains for the sake of the exhaustion of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the detachment from the sense base of the eye, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If one trains for the sake of the seclusion of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the cessation of the sense base of the eye, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
Is training for the sake of the cessation of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind training for the sake of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna)?

If they train for the sake of detachment from external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the cessation of internal emptiness, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If they train for the sake of the cessation of external emptiness, up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-entities, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the non-extinction of internal emptiness, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If they train for the sake of the non-extinction of external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-entities, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains because inner emptiness is primordially quiescent, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If they train because outer emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the essential nature of non-entities, is primordially quiescent, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?

Subhūti replied, “No, World-Honored One!”

Suchness is inexhaustible, unceasing, uninterrupted, and cannot be realized as an attainment; if a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in suchness in this way, they are training in the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).

If one trains for the sake of the total exhaustion of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path, is this training in the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*)?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the detachment from the noble truth of suffering, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If one trains for the sake of detachment from the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the cessation of the noble truth of suffering, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If one trains for the sake of the cessation of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the non-arising of the noble truth of suffering, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If one trains for the sake of the non-arising of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the primordial tranquility of the noble truth of suffering, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If one trains for the sake of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path because they are primordially quiescent, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the self-nature nirvāṇa of the noble truth of suffering, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?

is this training in the knowledge of all aspects? "Subhūti, what do you think?"

The Buddha said, “Subhūti, what do you think?”
“Are the suchness of the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path exhausted,

"Is it a training in the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) when one trains for the sake of the self-nature nirvāṇa of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions?

Is the suchness of the four dhyānas exhausted, ceased, or abandoned? Subhūti replied:

"If one trains for the sake of the self-nature nirvāṇa of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten universal bases, is this training in the knowledge of all aspects?

up to and including the eight branches of the noble path, exhausted, extinguished, or severed?”
Subhūti replied, “No, World-Honored One!”

Suchness is inexhaustible, unceasing, uninterrupted, and cannot be realized as an attainment.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases, they are training in the knowledge of all modes.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they are training in the four foundations of mindfulness; they are training in the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path."

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, and so forth, up to the eight branches of the noble path, this is training in the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*). Furthermore, Subhūti!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they are training in the gate of liberation of emptiness; they are training in the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in the gates of liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, they are training in the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they are training in the Ground of Extreme Joy; they are training in the Ground of Purity, the Ground of Radiant Light, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Difficult Victory, the Ground of Presence, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, and the Ground of the Dharma Cloud."

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in the Stage of Extreme Joy, the Stage of Purity, and so forth, up to the Stage of the Dharma Cloud, this is training in the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna). Furthermore, Subhūti!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they are training in the five eyes; they are training in the six supernormal powers.
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in the five eyes and the six supernormal powers, they are training in the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they are training in the ten powers of a Buddha; they are training in the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha."

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva studies the ten powers of a buddha, the four fearlessnesses, and even the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, they are studying the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they are training in the quality of non-forgetfulness; they are training in the nature of constant equanimity."
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in the quality of non-forgetfulness and abides constantly in equanimity, this is training in the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvajñajñāna*).
"Furthermore, Subhūti!"
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, they are training in all-knowledge; they are training in the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects.
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in all-knowledge, the knowledge of the aspects of the path, and the knowledge of all aspects, they are training in the knowledge of all modes of knowledge.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they are training in all the doors of dhāraṇī; they are training in all the doors of samādhi."
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in all dharanī-doors and all samādhi-doors, this is training in the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*).
"Furthermore, Subhūti!..."
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they are training in all the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in all the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, they are training in the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they are training in the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas.
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas, they are training in the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna)."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they reach the perfection of the fulfillment of all training.
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, none of the māras of the devas or any heterodox teachers can destroy them."
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they swiftly reach the stage of non-retrogression.
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they practice that which was to be practiced by all their ancestral fathers, the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas.
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they unfailingly follow and turn toward the Dharma that protects.
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they are able to practice the deeds appropriate for one who has departed from darkness.
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they are training in the dharmas that adorn and purify their own buddha-field.
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they are training in the dharmas that bring all sentient beings to maturity.
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they are able to purify buddha-fields as they truly are.
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they are able to bring sentient beings to maturity as they truly are.
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they are able to give rise to great loving-kindness and great compassion, feeling pity for all beings.
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they are training in the subtle Dharma wheel of the three turnings and twelve aspects.
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they are training to deliver all sentient beings and establish them in the realm of nirvana without remainder.
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they are training in the sublime conduct that ensures the lineage of the Buddhas is never interrupted.
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they are training to open the gate of the deathless for the sake of sentient beings.
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they are training to establish immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings in the three vehicles of the Dharma.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they are training to manifest the ultimate, quiescent, and truly unconditioned realm for all sentient beings; this is the true cultivation and study of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna). Those of inferior capacity among sentient beings are unable to train in this manner.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, they are truly able to rescue all sentient beings from birth, old age, sickness, and death, and cause them to diligently train in the points of training that ought to be studied.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, they will certainly never again fall into the realms of hell, the animal kingdom, or the world of hungry ghosts."
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they will certainly not be born in border regions, among the Daradas, or among the Mlecchas.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they will certainly not be born into the families of caṇḍālas, of pukkasas, or into any other various families that are impoverished, lowly, or lacking in moral discipline.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they will never be deaf, blind, mute, or paralyzed; nor will their faculties or limbs be incomplete, nor will they suffer from a hunched back, epilepsy, or any other various foul and loathsome diseases or sores.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, in every birth they will always obtain a complete retinue; their physical appearance will be dignified and handsome, their speech will be majestic and authoritative, and all people will love and respect them.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, in every place of birth, they abstain from taking life, abstain from taking what is not given, abstain from sexual misconduct, abstain from false speech, abstain from harsh speech, abstain from divisive speech, and abstain from frivolous speech; they also abstain from covetousness, ill will, and wrong views.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, in every place of birth they do not sustain their life by means of false teachings; they never accept false and deceptive doctrines, nor do they associate with sentient beings who break the precepts, hold evil views, or slander the Dharma.
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, they never take birth in the long-lived heavens of the gods who are attached to pleasure and possess little wisdom. Why is this?

Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva has accomplished the power of skillful means (*upāya-kauśalya*). By virtue of this power of skillful means, although they are able to repeatedly enter the meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*), the immeasurables (*apramāṇa*), and the formless attainments (*ārūpya-samāpatti*), they do not take birth according to the influence of those states. Being sustained by the profound *prajñāpāramitā* and having accomplished such skillful means, although they constantly attain mastery over entering and emerging from all these concentrations, they do not take birth in the long-lived heavens under the influence of those concentrations, nor do they neglect the practice of the bodhisattva mahāsattva path.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, they attain purification in all the immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless buddha-dharmas, such as the ten powers of a buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha; they are certain not to fall into the levels of any śrāvaka or pratyekabuddha."
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
If all phenomena are by nature pure, how does a bodhisattva mahāsattva further attain purity within all phenomena?”
The Buddha told Subhūti: "So it is! So it is!"
It is as you have said.

All phenomena are by nature pure from the very beginning; thus, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva diligently practices and studies the profound *prajñāpāramitā* within this natural purity of all phenomena, they penetrate it as it truly is, without sinking or stagnation, because they remain far removed from all defilements and attachments. For this reason, it is said that the bodhisattva further attains purity.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

Although the intrinsic nature of all phenomena is pure, ordinary beings do not know, see, or realize this. Therefore, a bodhisattva mahāsattva, desiring to cause them to know, see, and realize it, practices the perfection of generosity, and practices the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom."

They dwell in internal emptiness; they dwell in external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

They dwell in suchness; they dwell in the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, non-alteration, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm.
They dwell in the noble truth of suffering; they dwell in the noble truths of the origin, cessation, and the path.
They practice the four dhyānas; they practice the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments;
they practice the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities;

they practice the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
They practice the liberation door of emptiness; they practice the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness;

they practice the Ground of Extreme Joy, the Ground of Purity, the Ground of Radiant Light, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Difficult to Conquer, the Ground of Presence, the Ground of Far-reaching Practice, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, and the Ground of the Dharma Cloud;
they practice the five eyes and they practice the six supernormal powers.

They cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha; they cultivate the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity, as well as the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
they cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness, and they cultivate the nature of constant abiding in equanimity;
they cultivate all doors of dhāraṇī, and they cultivate all doors of samādhi.
They cultivate all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*). "Subhūti!

When these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas train in this way in the natural purity of all phenomena, they attain purification in the Buddha’s ten powers, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and so forth—all the immeasurable, innumerable, and boundless Buddha-dharmas—and they do not fall into the levels of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas."

Regarding the diverse mental activities of all sentient beings, he is able to penetrate them all to the ultimate further shore through skillful means, causing all sentient beings to realize that the intrinsic nature of all phenomena is pure.
“Subhūti, you should know this!

For example, on the great earth, precious things such as gold and silver appear in few places, while sand, stones, and rubble appear in many places. It is the same for all sentient beings: a small portion are able to study the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, while the majority study the dharmas of the stages of the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas.”
“Subhūti, you should know this!

For example, among those in the human realm, only a small portion are able to cultivate the karma of a universal monarch (*cakravartin*), while the vast majority practice the karma of minor kings; so it is with all sentient beings—only a small portion are able to cultivate the path to the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), while the vast majority practice the paths of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.”

“Subhūti, you should know that among the multitude of bodhisattvas who seek to attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, few attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; many fall into the stages of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.”

“Subhūti, you should know that those sons of good family and daughters of good family who abide in the bodhisattva vehicle, if they do not distance themselves from the profound perfection of wisdom and skillful means, will certainly enter the stage of non-retrogression.”
If one is devoid of skillful means regarding the profound perfection of wisdom, they will certainly regress from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Therefore, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who wish to attain the stage of non-retrogression for bodhisattvas and wish to enter the ranks of those bodhisattvas who do not retrogress should diligently practice and study the skillful means of the profound *prajñāpāramitā*.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva thus trains in the skillful means of this profound perfection of wisdom, they will never give rise to a mind associated with stinginess, greed, breaking the precepts, anger, laziness, distraction, or corrupt wisdom;
nor will they ever give rise to a mind associated with sensual desire, malice, delusion, or arrogance."
They never give rise to a mind associated with any other faults;

they never give rise to a mind associated with grasping at the signs of form (*rūpa*), nor do they give rise to a mind associated with grasping at the signs of feeling (*vedanā*), perception (*saṃjñā*), formations (*saṃskāra*), or consciousness (*vijñāna*);

they never give rise to a mind associated with grasping at the signs of the sense base of the eye (*cakṣur-āyatana*), nor do they give rise to a mind associated with grasping at the signs of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind (*manas-āyatana*).

They never give rise to a mind associated with grasping at the signs of the sense-base of form, nor do they give rise to a mind associated with grasping at the signs of the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena;

they never give rise to a mind associated with grasping at the signs of the eye-element, nor do they give rise to a mind associated with grasping at the signs of the elements of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind;

they never give rise to a mind associated with grasping at the signs of the form-element, nor do they give rise to a mind associated with grasping at the signs of the elements of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena.

He never gives rise to a mind associated with grasping at the characteristics of the eye-consciousness element, nor does he give rise to a mind associated with grasping at the characteristics of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-consciousness elements;

he never gives rise to a mind associated with grasping at the characteristics of eye-contact, nor does he give rise to a mind associated with grasping at the characteristics of ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact;

he never gives rise to a mind associated with grasping at the characteristics of the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition, nor does he give rise to a mind associated with grasping at the characteristics of the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as condition.

They never give rise to a mind associated with grasping at the characteristics of the earth element, nor do they give rise to a mind associated with grasping at the characteristics of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements;

they never give rise to a mind associated with grasping at the characteristic of ignorance, nor do they give rise to a mind associated with grasping at the characteristics of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, or aging-and-death;

they never give rise to a mind associated with grasping at the characteristic of the perfection of generosity, nor do they give rise to a mind associated with grasping at the characteristics of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom.

They never give rise to a mind associated with the apprehension of the characteristic of internal emptiness; nor do they give rise to a mind associated with the apprehension of the characteristics of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

They never give rise to a mind associated with grasping at the characteristics of *tathatā* (suchness), nor do they give rise to a mind associated with grasping at the characteristics of the *dharmadhātu*, *dharmatā*, non-illusory nature, unchanging nature, equality, freedom from arising, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space, or the inconceivable realm;

they never give rise to a mind associated with grasping at the characteristics of the Noble Truth of Suffering, nor do they give rise to a mind associated with grasping at the characteristics of the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, or the Path;

they never give rise to a mind associated with grasping at the characteristics of the four dhyānas, nor do they give rise to a mind associated with grasping at the characteristics of the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments.

They never give rise to a mind associated with grasping at the signs of the eight liberations, nor do they give rise to a mind associated with grasping at the signs of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities;

they never give rise to a mind associated with grasping at the signs of the four foundations of mindfulness, nor do they give rise to a mind associated with grasping at the signs of the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path;

they never give rise to a mind associated with grasping at the sign of the liberation door of emptiness, nor do they give rise to a mind associated with grasping at the signs of the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness.

He never gives rise to a mind associated with grasping at the signs of the Stage of Utmost Joy (*pramuditā-bhūmi*); nor does he give rise to a mind associated with grasping at the signs of the Stage of Purity (*vimalā-bhūmi*), the Stage of Radiance (*prabhākārī-bhūmi*), the Stage of Blazing Wisdom (*arciṣmatī-bhūmi*), the Stage of Difficult Victory (*sudurjayā-bhūmi*), the Stage of Presence (*abhimukhī-bhūmi*), the Stage of Far-Going (*dūraṃgamā-bhūmi*), the Immovable Stage (*acalā-bhūmi*), the Stage of Good Intelligence (*sādhumatī-bhūmi*), or the Stage of the Cloud of Dharma (*dharmameghā-bhūmi*).

He never gives rise to a mind associated with grasping at the signs of the five eyes (*pañca-cakṣus*); nor does he give rise to a mind associated with grasping at the signs of the six supernormal powers (*ṣaḍ-abhijñā*).

He never gives rise to a mind associated with grasping at the signs of the ten powers of a Buddha (*daśa-tathāgata-bala*); nor does he give rise to a mind associated with grasping at the signs of the four fearlessnesses (*catvāri vaiśāradyāni*), the four analytical knowledges (*catasraḥ pratisaṃvidah*), great loving-kindness (*mahāmaitrī*), great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*), great sympathetic joy (*mahāmuditā*), great equanimity (*mahopekṣā*), or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇika-buddhadharma*).

They never give rise to a mind associated with grasping at the signs of the qualities of non-forgetfulness, nor do they give rise to a mind associated with grasping at the signs of the state of constant equanimity;

they never give rise to a mind associated with grasping at the signs of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), nor do they give rise to a mind associated with grasping at the signs of the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*) or the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*);

they never give rise to a mind associated with grasping at the signs of any door of dhāraṇī (*dhāraṇīmukha*), nor do they give rise to a mind associated with grasping at the signs of any door of samādhi (*samādhimukha*).

They never give rise to a mind associated with grasping at the signs of the fruit of stream-entry; nor do they give rise to a mind associated with grasping at the signs of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, or arhatship;
they never give rise to a mind associated with grasping at the signs of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment;
and they never give rise to a mind associated with grasping at the signs of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
They never give rise to a mind associated with the conceptual signs of grasping at the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas.
"Why is this? Subhūti!..."

This bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing the profound perfection of wisdom through skillful means, does not perceive any dharma that can be apprehended; because there is nothing to be apprehended, he does not give rise to a mind associated with the grasping of the marks of dharmas such as form.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva thus trains in the skillful means of this profound perfection of wisdom, they are able to encompass all perfections, gather all perfections, and lead all perfections."
Why is this? Subhūti!
It is because within the profound perfection of wisdom all perfections are contained.

"Subhūti! Just as the view of a self-existent body (satkāyadṛṣṭi) universally encompasses all sixty-two views, so too is it with the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), which contains and sustains all perfections."

Subhūti! Just as when those who have passed away their life-faculty ceases and all the other faculties accordingly cease, so it is with the profound perfection of wisdom: all the perfections that are studied follow along with it; if there were no perfection of wisdom, there would be no perfections at all.
Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to reach the ultimate further shore of all pāramitās, they should diligently practice and study the profound prajñāpāramitā.
"Subhūti, you should know that if a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices and studies this profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they shall be the most preeminent among all sentient beings."
Why is this? Subhūti!
It is because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have already been able to train in and study the unsurpassed state.
"Furthermore, Subhūti, what do you think?
Are the sentient beings in this trichiliocosm many?"
Subhūti replied, “Very many,
World-Honored One!”
"Very many, Sugata!
The sentient beings within Jambudvīpa alone are already beyond counting; how much more so the sentient beings throughout the trichiliocosm!"
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

Suppose all the sentient beings in a trichiliocosm were to simultaneously attain human bodies, and having attained human bodies, were to simultaneously realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”

Suppose there are sons or daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle and, for as long as their lives last, are able to provide offerings, honor, respect, and praise to these Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas with excellent garments, food and drink, bedding, medicinal requisites, and other necessities.
“By this cause and condition, would these sons and daughters of good family acquire much merit? Subhūti replied, “Very much!”
"O Bhagavān,
it is very much so! O Sugata!"
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

If sons of good family or daughters of good family who abide in the bodhisattva vehicle are able to hear, receive and uphold, read and recite, copy, contemplate, and practice this profound perfection of wisdom, the mass of merit they obtain will be far greater than the former, immeasurable and incalculable.”
Why is this? Subhūti!

The profound perfection of wisdom possesses great benefit and purpose, for it can swiftly lead the bodhisattva mahāsattvas to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, surpassing all the roots of goodness previously acquired.
Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to stand at the head of all sentient beings, they should train in this profound perfection of wisdom.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to universally benefit all sentient beings—acting as a protector for those without protection, a refuge for those without refuge, a resort for those without a resort, eyes for those without eyes, and light for those without light; showing the path to those who have lost their way, and leading those who have not yet attained nirvāṇa to attain it—they should study this profound *prajñāpāramitā*.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; wishes to practice the sphere of activity traversed by all buddhas; wishes to sport in the places where all buddhas sport; wishes to let out the great lion’s roar of all buddhas; wishes to beat the unsurpassed Dharma drum of all buddhas; wishes to strike the unsurpassed Dharma bell of all buddhas; wishes to blow the unsurpassed Dharma conch of all buddhas; wishes to ascend the unsurpassed Dharma throne of all buddhas; wishes to expound the unsurpassed meaning of the Dharma of all buddhas; wishes to sever the net of doubts of all sentient beings; wishes to enter the nectar-like Dharma realm of all buddhas; and wishes to receive the subtle and wondrous joy of all buddhas—such a one should study this profound perfection of wisdom.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices and studies this profound perfection of wisdom in this manner, there is no merit or root of goodness that they cannot attain."
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice and study this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, can they also attain the merits and roots of goodness of Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas?”
The Buddha said:
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
The merits and roots of goodness of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas are also all attainable by these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; however, they neither dwell upon nor cling to them.”

Having observed correctly with superior wisdom and vision, they transcend that stage and enter the bodhisattva’s state of rightness and departure from birth; therefore, there is no root of merit or virtuous quality that these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas cannot attain.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, they draw near to the knowledge of all modes and will swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, they become a true field of merit for all the world, including its gods, humans, and asuras."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they transcend the field of merit of all worldly śramaṇas, brahmins, śrāvakas, and pratyekabuddhas, and are swiftly able to realize the knowledge of all modes."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, wherever they are born, they do not abandon the perfection of wisdom, do not depart from the perfection of wisdom, and constantly practice the perfection of wisdom."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices and studies this profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), you should know that they have attained non-retrogression regarding all-knowledge (sarvajñatā), have distanced themselves from the levels of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, and are in close proximity to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they form this thought:

'This is the perfection of wisdom; this is the time of cultivation; this is the place of cultivation. I am able to cultivate this profound perfection of wisdom. By means of this profound perfection of wisdom, I shall abandon those dharmas that ought to be abandoned, and I will certainly realize the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna).'"
If one forms such a thought, one is not practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), nor can one comprehend the profound perfection of wisdom.
They do not form such thoughts as:

"This is the perfection of wisdom; this is the time of cultivation; this is the place of cultivation; this is the cultivator; these are the dharmas of the afflictive obscurations that must be abandoned by means of the perfection of wisdom; and this is the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment to be realized by means of the perfection of wisdom."
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they form this thought:

"This is not the perfection of wisdom; this is not the time for cultivation; this is not the place for cultivation; this is not the cultivator. It is not by means of the perfection of wisdom that there can be anything abandoned or anything attained."
Why is this? Because all phenomena abide in suchness, the dharma-realm, and the limit of reality, being without distinction.
To practice in this manner is to practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
