Because the ten powers of a Buddha are ultimately detached, and because the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are also ultimately detached, a bodhisattva mahāsattva can attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”

“Subhūti! Because the quality of non-forgetfulness is ultimately detached, and because the state of constant abiding in equanimity is also ultimately detached, a bodhisattva mahāsattva can attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”

“Subhūti! Because omniscience is ultimately detached, and because the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are also ultimately detached, a bodhisattva mahāsattva can attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”
“Subhūti! Because all dharanī-doors are ultimately detached, and all samādhi-doors are also ultimately detached, a bodhisattva mahāsattva can attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”
“Subhūti! Because all practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are ultimately detached, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas can attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”
“Subhūti! Because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is ultimately detached, a bodhisattva mahāsattva can attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”
“Subhūti! Because omniscience is ultimately detached, a bodhisattva mahāsattva can attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Furthermore, Subhūti!”
If the perfection of wisdom were not ultimately detached, it would not be the perfection of wisdom;

if the perfections of meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity were not ultimately detached, they would not be the perfections of meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity.
“Subhūti! If internal emptiness were not ultimately detached, it would not be internal emptiness;

if external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, emptiness of all phenomena, unapprehendable emptiness, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, and emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence were not ultimately detached, they would not be external emptiness, up to and including emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.”
“Subhūti! If true suchness were not ultimately detached, it would not be true suchness;

if the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), the state of non-falsity, the state of non-alteration, equality, the state of being free from birth, the fixedness of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the reality limit (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm were not ultimately detached, they would not be the realm of phenomena up to the inconceivable realm.”
“Subhūti! If the noble truth of suffering were not ultimately detached, it would not be the noble truth of suffering;
if the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path were not ultimately detached, they would not be the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path.”
“Subhūti! If the four dhyānas were not ultimately detached, they would not be the four dhyānas;
if the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments were not ultimately detached, they would not be the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments.”
“Subhūti! If the eight liberations were not ultimately detached, they would not be the eight liberations;

if the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities were not ultimately detached, they would not be the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities.”
“Subhūti! If the four foundations of mindfulness were not ultimately detached, they would not be the four foundations of mindfulness;

if the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path were not ultimately detached, they would not be the four right efforts up to and including the eightfold noble path.”
“Subhūti! If the gate of liberation of emptiness were not ultimately detached, it would not be the gate of liberation of emptiness;
if the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness were not ultimately detached, they would not be the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.”
“Subhūti! If the Ground of Extreme Joy were not ultimately detached, it would not be the Ground of Extreme Joy;

if the Ground of Freedom from Defilement, the Ground of Radiant Light, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Utmost Difficulty to Conquer, the Ground of Manifestation, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, and the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma were not ultimately detached, they would not be the Ground of Freedom from Defilement up to the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma.”
"Subhūti! If the five eyes were not ultimately detached, they would not be the five eyes;
if the six superknowledges were not ultimately detached, they would not be the six superknowledges."
"Subhūti! If the ten powers of a Buddha were not ultimately detached, they would not be the ten powers of a Buddha;

if the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha were not ultimately detached, they would not be the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha."
“Subhūti! If the quality of non-forgetfulness were not ultimately detached, it would not be the quality of non-forgetfulness;
if the state of constant abiding in equanimity were not ultimately detached, it would not be the state of constant abiding in equanimity.”
“Subhūti! If omniscience were not ultimately detached, it would not be omniscience;
if the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects were not ultimately detached, they would not be the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects.”
“Subhūti! If all dharanī-doors were not ultimately detached, they would not be all dharanī-doors;
if all samādhi-doors were not ultimately detached, they would not be all samādhi-doors.”
“Subhūti! If all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas were not ultimately detached, they would not be the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. Subhūti!”
If the unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment of the Buddhas were not ultimately secluded, it would not be the unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment of the Buddhas.
Subhūti! If the knowledge of all modes were not ultimately secluded, it would not be the knowledge of all modes.
“Subhūti! Because the perfection of wisdom is ultimately detached, it is called the ‘perfection of wisdom’;

because the perfections of meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity are ultimately detached, they are called the ‘perfections of meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity.’”
“Subhūti! Because inner emptiness is ultimately detached, it is called ‘inner emptiness.

Because outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, all-dharma emptiness, unapprehendable emptiness, non-existence emptiness, self-nature emptiness, and the non-existence-of-self-nature emptiness are ultimately detached, they are called ‘outer emptiness’ up to ‘the non-existence-of-self-nature emptiness.’”
“Subhūti! Because *tathatā* (suchness) is ultimately detached, it is called ‘suchness.

Because the *dharmadhātu* (dharma-realm), *dharmatā* (dharma-nature), non-erroneous nature, unchanging nature, equality, detachment from birth, the fixedness of dharma, the stability of dharma, the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm are ultimately detached, they are called the ‘dharma-realm’ up to the ‘inconceivable realm.’”
“Subhūti! Because the noble truth of suffering is ultimately detached, it is called the noble truth of suffering;
because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are ultimately detached, they are called the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path.”
“Subhūti! Because the four dhyānas are ultimately detached, they are called ‘the four dhyānas’;
because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are ultimately detached, they are called ‘the four immeasurables’ and ‘the four formless absorptions.’”
“Subhūti! Because the eight liberations are ultimately detached, they are called the ‘eight liberations’;

because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities are ultimately detached, they are called the ‘eight bases of mastery,’ the ‘nine successive meditative attainments,’ and the ‘ten totalities.’”
“Subhūti! Because the four foundations of mindfulness are ultimately detached, they are called the ‘four foundations of mindfulness’;

because the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are ultimately detached, they are called the ‘four right efforts’ up to the ‘eightfold noble path.’”
"Subhūti! Because the gate of liberation of emptiness is ultimately detached, it is called the 'gate of liberation of emptiness';
because the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are ultimately detached, they are called the 'gates of liberation of signlessness' and 'wishlessness.'"
“Subhūti! Because the Ground of Utmost Joy is ultimately detached, it is called the Ground of Utmost Joy;

because the Ground of Purity, the Ground of Radiance, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Supreme Difficulty to Conquer, the Ground of Presence, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, and the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma are ultimately detached, they are called the Ground of Purity up to the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma.”
“Subhūti! Because the five eyes are ultimately detached, they are called the ‘five eyes’;
because the six supernormal powers are ultimately detached, they are called the ‘six supernormal powers.’”
“Subhūti! Because the ten powers of a Buddha are ultimately detached, they are called the ‘ten powers of a Buddha’;

because the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are ultimately detached, they are called the ‘four fearlessnesses’ up to the ‘eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.’”
“Subhūti! Because the quality of non-forgetfulness is ultimately detached, it is called the ‘quality of non-forgetfulness’;
because the state of constant abiding in equanimity is ultimately detached, it is called the ‘state of constant abiding in equanimity.’”
“Subhūti! Because omniscience (sarvajñatā) is ultimately detached, it is called omniscience;

because the knowledge of the paths (mārgākārajñatā) and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā) are ultimately detached, they are called the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects.”
"Subhūti! Because all dhāraṇī-doors are ultimately detached, they are called 'all dhāraṇī-doors';
because all samādhi-doors are ultimately detached, they are called 'all samādhi-doors.'"
“Subhūti! Because all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are ultimately detached, they are called ‘all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. Subhūti!”
Because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is ultimately detached, it is called the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas.
"Subhūti! Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) is ultimately detached, it is called the knowledge of all modes."

"Therefore, Subhūti, it is not that a bodhisattva mahāsattva can realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment without relying on the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā). Although one does not realize a dharma apart from dharmas, one realizes unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment without not relying upon the profound perfection of wisdom."
Therefore, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who wish to attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment should diligently practice and study the profound perfection of wisdom.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
The dharma and its meaning practiced by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are exceedingly profound.”
The Buddha said,
“So it is, Subhūti! So it is!”
"So it is! It is as you have said.
The dharma and its meaning practiced by the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are exceedingly profound."

Subhūti, you should know that bodhisattva mahāsattvas perform what is difficult to do: although they practice such profound meanings of the Dharma, they are able to refrain from realizing the stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.
At that time, Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
According to my understanding of the meaning of what the Buddha has taught, the deeds performed by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are not difficult."

Why is this so? Because the dharmas and meanings realized by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are entirely unapprehendable; the prajñāpāramitā that realizes them is also unapprehendable; and the realization itself, the one who realizes, the place of realization, and the time of realization are likewise unapprehendable.
"Bhagavān! Since all dharmas are observed by Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas to be unobtainable, what dharma-meaning could there be to be realized?
What Prajñāpāramitā could there be to serve as the means of realization?"
Furthermore, what can be established as the dharma to be realized, the one who realizes it, the place of realization, or the time of realization?
This being so, how could one maintain that by means of these one realizes unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?
Even unsurpassed enlightenment cannot be realized, let alone the dharmas of the stages of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas!

World-Honored One, this is called the bodhisattva’s practice of non-apprehension; if a bodhisattva mahāsattva can practice such a practice of non-apprehension, they will attain freedom from all darkness and obscurations regarding all dharmas.
“World-Honored One!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, upon hearing such words, does not sink in spirit, is not startled, is not terrified, and feels no anxiety or regret, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”

"Bhagavān! When this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices in this manner, he does not perceive any manifold signs; he does not perceive that 'I am practicing,' nor does he perceive 'not practicing. He does not perceive that the *prajñāpāramitā* is what he is practicing, nor does he perceive that unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*) is what he is realizing. Furthermore, he does not perceive the place of realization, the time, or any such factors."
“Bhagavān! When this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, he does not form such thoughts as:
‘I am far from the levels of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; I am near unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.’”
"World-Honored One!
It is like space, which does not form the thought:
'I am far from or near to these dharmas.'"
Why is this? Because space is without movement and without differentiation, being devoid of conceptual discrimination.
It is likewise for the bodhisattva mahāsattvas who practice the profound *prajñāpāramitā*; they do not form such thoughts:
"I am far from the levels of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; I am near unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment. Why is this?
Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* is free from conceptual discrimination.
“World-Honored One!
It is as if an illusory person does not form such thoughts:
‘The phenomena that resemble illusions are far from me; the illusionary implements and the illusionist are near to me; and the gathering of followers is both near and far.’”
Why is this? Because the illusory person created has no discrimination.
It is the same for Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas who practice the profound Prajñāpāramitā; they do not form such thoughts as:
"I am far from the levels of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; I am near unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment. Why is this?
Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* is without conceptual discrimination.
“World-Honored One!
For example, a reflected image does not form this thought:
‘Because I appear based on that [object], it is near to me; because I do not appear based on those non-causal dharmas, they are distant from me.’”
Why is this? Because the manifested images are devoid of conceptual discrimination.
It is likewise for the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the profound *prajñāpāramitā*; they do not form such thoughts:
"I am far from the stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; I am near unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment. Why is this?
Because the profound perfection of wisdom is free from conceptual discrimination.
“World-Honored One!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the profound perfection of wisdom have neither attachment nor aversion. Why is this? Because—”
Because the intrinsic nature of both the profound *prajñāpāramitā* and all phenomena cannot be apprehended, [they are free from love and hatred].
"World-Honored One!
Just as the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas have neither love nor hatred, so too are the Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas who practice the profound *prajñāpāramitā* likewise without love or hatred."
Why is this? Because all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas have severed both love and hatred.
"World-Honored One! [he said.]

Just as all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas have forever severed all conceptual constructions and discriminations, so too do the Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas who practice the profound Prajñāpāramitā likewise subdue and sever all conceptual constructions and discriminations.
Why is this? Because all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas are without discrimination regarding all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!... [text continues]”
Just as all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas do not form this thought:
"I am far from the stages of Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas; I am near to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
"So too it is for the bodhisattva mahāsattvas who practice the profound perfection of wisdom; they do not form such thoughts as:
'I am far from the levels of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, and I am near to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.'"
Why is this? Because all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas are free from discrimination.
"World-Honored One!..."
Just as those who are emanated by the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas do not form such thoughts as:
"I am far from the stages of Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas; I am near to unexcelled, perfect enlightenment."
Why is this? Because that which is emanated is without discrimination.
It is likewise for bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the profound perfection of wisdom; they do not form such a thought:
"I am far from the stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; I am near unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment. Why is this?
Because the profound perfection of wisdom is free from conceptual discrimination.
“World-Honored One!
Just as when the Tathāgatas and others wish to perform some task, they manifest an emanation and command that emanation to carry out that business, yet the emanated being does not form this thought:
‘I am able to accomplish such a deed.’”
Why is this? Because those who are emanated are without conceptual discrimination.

It is the same with the profound *prajñāpāramitā*: although one diligently cultivates it for a specific purpose, and once cultivated it can accomplish the task at hand, there is nonetheless no conceptual discrimination regarding that which is accomplished.
Why is this? Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* is without conceptual discrimination.
“World-Honored One!...”

For example, suppose a craftsman or his apprentice, for some purpose, constructs various mechanical devices—whether female or male figures, or elephants, horses, and so forth. Although these mechanical devices perform their respective functions, they possess no conceptual discrimination whatsoever regarding those activities.
Why is this so? Because mechanical devices are devoid of discrimination.

It is just the same with the profound *prajñāpāramitā*: it is established for the sake of a specific purpose, and once established, although it can accomplish various tasks, it remains entirely without discrimination regarding what it does.
"Why is this? Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* is without conceptual differentiation regarding all phenomena.
At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra addressed the Venerable Subhūti, saying:

“Subhūti! Is it only the perfection of wisdom that is without conceptual differentiation, or are the perfections of meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity also without conceptual differentiation?”
Subhūti replied, "Śāriputra!

It is not only the perfection of wisdom that is without conceptual differentiation; the perfections of meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity are likewise without conceptual differentiation."
Then, Śāriputra again asked Subhūti: “Subhūti,
is it that form is also without conceptual differentiation, and feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are likewise without conceptual differentiation?”
“Subhūti! Is it that the eye-base is also without conceptual differentiation, and the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases are likewise without conceptual differentiation?
“Subhūti! [he asked.]

"Is it that the sphere of form is also without conceptual differentiation, and the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are likewise without conceptual differentiation? Subhūti,
is it that the eye constituent is also without conceptual differentiation, and the constituents of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are likewise without conceptual differentiation?"
“Subhūti! Is it that the realm of form is also without conceptual differentiation, and that the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and phenomena are likewise without conceptual differentiation?
“Subhūti! [he asked.]

"Is it that the visual consciousness element is also without conceptual differentiation, and likewise the auditory, olfactory, gustatory, tactile, and mental consciousness elements are also without conceptual differentiation? "Subhūti!"
"Is it that eye-contact is also without conceptual differentiation, and that ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact are likewise without conceptual differentiation? Subhūti,

is it that the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are also without conceptual differentiation, and that the various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions are likewise without conceptual differentiation?"
“Subhūti! Is it that the earth element is also without conceptual discrimination, and that the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are likewise without conceptual discrimination?
“Subhūti! [he asked.]

If there is no discrimination regarding ignorance, are there likewise no discriminations regarding volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, becoming, birth, and old age and death?

“Subhūti! Is it that internal emptiness is also without conceptual differentiation? And are external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence also without conceptual differentiation?”

“Subhūti! Is it that suchness is also without conceptual differentiation, and that the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*) are likewise without conceptual differentiation?”
“Subhūti! Is it that the noble truth of suffering is also without conceptual differentiation, and the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are likewise without conceptual differentiation?
“Subhūti! [he asked.]
"Are the four dhyānas also without conceptual differentiation? Are the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments also without conceptual differentiation?

Subhūti, are the eight liberations also without conceptual differentiation? Are the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities also without conceptual differentiation?"

“Subhūti! Are the four foundations of mindfulness also without conceptual differentiation? Are the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path also without conceptual differentiation?”

“Subhūti! Is it that the gate of liberation of emptiness is also without conceptual differentiation, and the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are likewise without conceptual differentiation?
“Subhūti! [The Blessed One asked.]

Is the Ground of Utmost Joy also without conceptual differentiation? Are the Ground of Freedom from Defilement, the Ground of Radiant Light, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Supreme Difficulty to Conquer, the Ground of Manifestation, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, and the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma likewise without conceptual differentiation?
“Subhūti! Are the five eyes also without conceptual differentiation, and are the six supernormal powers also without conceptual differentiation?
“Subhūti! [he asked.]

Are the ten powers of a Buddha also without discrimination? Are the four fearlessnesses, the four unhindered analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha also without discrimination?
“Subhūti! Is the quality of non-forgetfulness also without conceptual differentiation, and is the state of constant abiding in equanimity likewise without conceptual differentiation?
“Subhūti! [he asked.]

"Are all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) also without conceptual differentiation, and are the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) also without conceptual differentiation? Subhūti,
are all doors of dhāraṇī (*dhāraṇīmukha*) also without conceptual differentiation, and are all doors of samādhi (*samādhimukha*) also without conceptual differentiation?"

“Subhūti! Is it that the fruit of stream-entry is also without conceptual differentiation, and that the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, arhatship, and the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha are likewise without conceptual differentiation?”

“Subhūti! Is the practice of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas also without conceptual differentiation, and is the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas likewise without conceptual differentiation?”
“Subhūti! Is it that the conditioned realm is also without conceptual differentiation, and the unconditioned realm is also without conceptual differentiation? Subhūti replied:
“Śāriputra, form is also without conceptual differentiation; feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are also without conceptual differentiation. Śāriputra!”
The eye-base is also without conceptual differentiation; the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases are likewise without conceptual differentiation.
"Śāriputra! The form-base is also without conceptual differentiation; the sound, odor, taste, tangible, and mental-object bases are likewise without conceptual differentiation."
“Śāriputra, the eye-element is also without discrimination; the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-elements are likewise without discrimination. Śāriputra,..."
The realm of form is also without conceptual differentiation; the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are likewise without conceptual differentiation. "Śāriputra!
The realm of eye-consciousness is also without conceptual differentiation; the realms of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness are likewise without conceptual differentiation."
“Śāriputra, visual contact is also without discrimination; auditory, olfactory, gustatory, tactile, and mental contact are likewise without discrimination. Śāriputra!”

The various sensations produced with eye-contact as a condition are also without conceptual discrimination; the various sensations produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions are likewise without conceptual discrimination.
“Śāriputra! The earth element is also without discrimination; the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are likewise without discrimination. Śāriputra!”

Ignorance is also without conceptual differentiation; likewise, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age and death are also without conceptual differentiation.

“Śāriputra! Internal emptiness is also without conceptual differentiation; external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self-characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature are likewise without conceptual differentiation.”

“Śāriputra! Suchness is also without conceptual differentiation; the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, the state of equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of empty space, and the inconceivable realm are likewise without conceptual differentiation.”
“Śāriputra, the noble truth of suffering is also without conceptual differentiation; the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are likewise without conceptual differentiation. Śāriputra!”
The four dhyānas are also without conceptual discrimination; the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are also without conceptual discrimination. "Śāriputra!
The eight liberations are also without conceptual discrimination; the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are also without conceptual discrimination."

“Śāriputra! The four foundations of mindfulness are also without conceptual differentiation; the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are likewise without conceptual differentiation.”

“Śāriputra, the gate of liberation of emptiness is also without conceptual differentiation; the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are likewise without conceptual differentiation. Śāriputra!”

The Stage of Utmost Joy is also without conceptual differentiation; the Stage of Purity, the Stage of Radiance, the Stage of Blazing Wisdom, the Stage of Supreme Difficulty to Conquer, the Stage of Presence, the Stage of Far-Going, the Immovable Stage, the Stage of Excellent Intelligence, and the Stage of the Dharma Cloud are likewise without conceptual differentiation.
“Śāriputra! The five eyes are also without conceptual discrimination, and the six supernormal powers are likewise without conceptual discrimination. Śāriputra!”

The ten powers of a Buddha are also without conceptual differentiation; the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are likewise without conceptual differentiation.
“Śāriputra! The quality of non-forgetfulness is also without conceptual discrimination, and the state of constant abiding in equanimity is likewise without conceptual discrimination. Śāriputra!”
All-knowledge is also without conceptual differentiation; the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are likewise without conceptual differentiation. "Śāriputra!
All doors of dhāraṇī are also without conceptual differentiation, and all doors of samādhi are likewise without conceptual differentiation."

“Śāriputra! The fruit of stream-entry is also without conceptual differentiation; likewise, the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, arhatship, and the awakening of a pratyekabuddha are also without conceptual differentiation.”

“Śāriputra! All the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are likewise without conceptual differentiation, and the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas is also without conceptual differentiation.”
“Śāriputra! The conditioned realm is also without conceptual differentiation, and the unconditioned realm is also without conceptual differentiation. Śāriputra said:
“Subhūti! If all phenomena are entirely without conceptual differentiation, how can there be the distinctions between the five destinies of hell-beings, animals, hungry ghosts, humans, and devas?”
"How then can there be distinctions in the stages of practicing for the sake of stream-entry, once-returning, non-returning, arhatship, pratyekabuddhahood,
bodhisattvahood, and buddhahood? Subhūti replied, "Śāriputra!"

Sentient beings, due to the causes and conditions of their inverted afflictions, perform various actions of body, speech, and mind; from these, they experience the ripening fruit of karma rooted in desire, and based upon this, the distinctions of the five destinies—hell-beings, animals, hungry ghosts, humans, and gods—are established.
As for the question of how there can be distinctions among the various stages, such as the cultivation of the stream-enterer and so forth:
Śāriputra, because of non-conceptualization, there is the cultivation of the stream-enterer and the fruit of the stream-enterer;
because of non-conceptualization, there is the cultivation of the once-returner and the fruit of the once-returner.
Because they are non-conceptual, there is the cultivation of the stage of non-returner and the fruit of non-returning;
because they are non-conceptual, there is the cultivation of arhatship and the fruit of arhatship;
because they are non-conceptual, there is the cultivation of pratyekabuddhahood and the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha.
Because of non-conceptualization, there is the cultivation of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and the path of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva;
because of non-conceptualization, there is the cultivation of the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, and the unsurpassed perfect enlightenment of a Buddha.
“Śāriputra! The Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past were established through non-conceptualization, because they had severed conceptualization;
the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the future will likewise be established through non-conceptualization, because they will have severed conceptualization.”

Furthermore, all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas currently teaching the Dharma in all the Buddha-worlds of the ten directions are likewise without conceptual discrimination; because discrimination has been severed, they can be provisionally designated as existing.

Śāriputra! By this cause and condition, one should know that all phenomena are entirely without discrimination, for they take non-discriminative suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, and the limit of reality as their definitive standard.

“Śāriputra! A bodhisattva mahāsattva should practice this profound perfection of wisdom characterized by non-conceptuality. If they practice this profound perfection of wisdom characterized by non-conceptuality, they will be able to realize the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening sought through that state of non-conceptuality.”
Chapter 57: Praise by Sthira and Others, Part One. At that time, Śāriputra asked Subhūti:
“When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, does he practice a firm and substantial dharma?”
"Is it that they practice a dharma that lacks solidity?
Subhūti replied, "When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they practice a dharma that lacks solidity; they do not practice a dharma that possesses solidity."
Why is this? "Śāriputra,
because the perfection of wisdom lacks any solid core, the perfections of meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity likewise lack any solid core."

“Śāriputra! Because internal emptiness lacks solidity and substance, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence likewise lack solidity and substance.”

“Śāriputra! Because true suchness (*tathatā*) lacks any solid core, the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the non-erroneous nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm likewise lack any solid core.”
“Śāriputra! Because the noble truth of suffering lacks solidity, the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path likewise lack solidity. Śāriputra!”
Because the four dhyānas lack solidity, the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions likewise lack solidity. "Śāriputra!
Because the eight liberations lack solidity, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive absorptions, and the ten totalities likewise lack solidity."

“Śāriputra, because the four applications of mindfulness lack solidity, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path likewise lack solidity.”
“Śāriputra! Because the gate of liberation of emptiness lacks solidity and substance, the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness likewise lack solidity and substance. Śāriputra!”

Because the Ground of Utmost Joy lacks solidity, the Ground of Purity, the Ground of Radiance, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Supreme Difficulty to Conquer, the Ground of Manifestation, the Ground of Far-Reaching Progress, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, and the Ground of the Dharma-Cloud likewise lack solidity.
“Śāriputra! Because the five eyes lack solidity, and because the six supernormal powers also lack solidity. Śāriputra!”

Because the ten powers of a Buddha lack any solid reality, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha likewise lack any solid reality.
“Śāriputra! Because the quality of non-forgetfulness lacks substantial reality, the state of constant abiding in equanimity also lacks substantial reality. Śāriputra!”
Because omniscience (*sarvajñatā*) lacks any solid core, the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) also lack any solid core. "Śāriputra!
Because all doors of dhāraṇī lack any solid core, all doors of samādhi also lack any solid core."
“Śāriputra! Because all practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas lack solidity, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas likewise lacks solidity.”
“Śāriputra! This is because the knowledge of all modes lacks any solid core. Why is that?

Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not even perceive the absence of solidity as something obtainable within the perfection of wisdom, much less perceive the presence of solidity as something obtainable!

Even regarding the perfections of meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, one does not perceive even the slightest lack of solidity as being obtainable, let alone perceive any solidity as being obtainable!

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not even perceive any lack of solidity within internal emptiness as something obtainable, much less perceive any solidity as obtainable!”

Even regarding external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—one does not even perceive the absence of solidity as something to be apprehended, much less perceive the presence of solidity as something to be apprehended!

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive even the lack of solidity in suchness as something obtainable, much less perceive any solidity as obtainable!

Even within the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm, one does not perceive even the slightest lack of substantiality that could be apprehended, much less perceive any substantiality that could be apprehended!

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive even the noble truth of suffering as having any substantiality that can be apprehended, let alone perceiving it as having any substantiality that can be apprehended!

"Śāriputra, regarding the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path, one does not even perceive anything substantial that can be apprehended, much less perceive anything substantial that exists! "Śāriputra!"

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive even the four dhyānas as having any substantiality that can be apprehended, much less perceive anything as having substantiality that can be apprehended!

"Even regarding the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, one does not perceive even the slightest lack of solidity as something obtainable, much less perceive any solidity as obtainable! Śāriputra!"

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive even the eight liberations as having any substantiality that can be apprehended, much less perceive anything as having substantiality that can be apprehended!

Even regarding the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten universal bases, one does not perceive even the slightest lack of solidity that can be apprehended, much less perceive any solidity that can be apprehended!

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, he does not even perceive the four foundations of mindfulness as having any substantiality that can be apprehended, much less perceive them as having any substantiality that can be apprehended!

Even regarding the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path, one does not perceive even the slightest lack of solidity as being obtainable, let alone perceive any solidity as being obtainable!

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive even the absence of solidity within the gate of liberation of emptiness as something obtainable, let alone perceive the presence of solidity as obtainable!”

"Even within the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, one does not perceive even the slightest lack of solidity that can be apprehended, much less perceive any solidity that can be apprehended! Śāriputra!"

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive even the "Extremely Joyful Ground" as having any substantiality that can be apprehended, much less perceive anything as having substantiality that can be apprehended!

Even on the Ground of Freedom from Defilement, the Ground of Radiant Light, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Ultimate Difficulty to Conquer, the Ground of Manifestation, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, and the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma, one does not yet perceive even the slightest lack of solidity that could be apprehended, let alone perceive any solidity that could be apprehended!

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not even perceive any lack of solidity as something obtainable within the five eyes, let alone perceive any solidity as obtainable!”

Even regarding the six supernormal powers (*ṣaḍabhijñā*), one does not perceive even the slightest lack of substantiality that could be apprehended, much less perceive any substantiality that could be apprehended! "Śāriputra,

when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they do not perceive even the slightest lack of substantiality in the ten powers (*daśabala*) of a Buddha that could be apprehended, much less perceive any substantiality that could be apprehended!"

Regarding the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, one does not even perceive them as having any substantial reality that can be apprehended, much less perceive them as having any substantial reality that can be found!

“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive even the quality of non-forgetfulness as having any substantiality that can be apprehended, much less do they perceive anything with substantiality that can be apprehended!”
Even regarding the state of constant equanimity (*upekṣā*), one does not perceive any lack of solidity as being obtainable, much less perceive any solidity as being obtainable! "Śāriputra,

when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), they do not even perceive any lack of solidity as being obtainable in relation to omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), much less perceive any solidity as being obtainable!"

"Śāriputra, regarding the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, one does not even perceive anything substantial that can be apprehended, much less perceive anything substantial that exists! "Śāriputra!"

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not even perceive any lack of solidity as being obtainable among all the dhāraṇī-doors, let alone perceive any solidity as being obtainable!
"Even regarding all doors of samādhi, one does not perceive anything substantial that can be apprehended, much less perceive anything substantial that can be apprehended! Śāriputra!"

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive even the lack of substantiality in any bodhisattva mahāsattva practice as something obtainable, let alone perceive any substantiality as obtainable!

"Even regarding the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of a Buddha, one does not perceive anything substantial that can be apprehended, much less perceive anything substantial that can be apprehended! Śāriputra!"

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not perceive even the lack of solidity as something obtainable in the knowledge of all modes; how much less could they perceive any solidity as obtainable!
At that time, there were immeasurable devaputras from the desire and form realms who all thought to themselves:

"If a son of good family or a daughter of good family can resolve upon unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and practice according to the meaning as taught in the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, yet without realizing the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) or the equality of the dharma-nature, and without falling into the stages of the śrāvaka or pratyekabuddha—then such a bodhisattva mahāsattva, by virtue of these causes and conditions, performs a most rare and difficult task, and should be paid homage."
The Venerable Subhūti, knowing what was in the minds of the devaputras, addressed them, saying:

"That a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not realize the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) as the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), and thus does not fall into the level of a śrāvaka or a pratyekabuddha, is not particularly marvelous and is not to be considered difficult."

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, knowing that all phenomena and all sentient beings are unapprehendable, yet gives rise to the mind of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment and dons the armor of merit in order to deliver immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless hundreds of thousands of sentient beings, enabling them to attain ultimate nirvana without remainder—this bodhisattva mahāsattva is truly most rare, for they are able to perform what is difficult to do.
“Son of Heaven, you should know!

Although these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas know that sentient beings are entirely non-existent, they nevertheless resolve their minds upon unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment and don the armor of merit, desiring to discipline all classes of sentient beings, as if they were desiring to discipline empty space.”
Why is this so? O sons of the gods!
Because space is detached, you should know that all sentient beings are likewise detached.
Because space is empty, one should know that all sentient beings are also empty;
because space is not solid or substantial, one should know that all sentient beings are also not solid or substantial;
because space is non-existent, one should know that all sentient beings are also non-existent.
For this reason, O sons of the gods!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva is most rare and is able to perform what is difficult to do.
"Sons of the gods, you should know this!"

The bodhisattva-mahāsattvas don the armor of great compassion, desiring to subdue all sentient beings; yet, since no such sentient beings exist at all, it is as if they were donning armor to battle with space.
“O Son of Heaven, you should know!

The bodhisattva-mahāsattvas don the armor of great compassion (mahākaruṇā-saṃnāha) out of a desire to bring benefit and happiness to all sentient beings; yet, both those sentient beings and the armor of great compassion are ultimately unapprehendable.”
Why is this so? O sons of the gods!
Because sentient beings are detached, you should know that this armor of great compassion is likewise detached.
Because sentient beings are empty, this armor of great compassion should be known as empty;
because sentient beings are not solid or substantial, this armor of great compassion should be known as not solid or substantial;
because sentient beings do not exist, this armor of great compassion should be known as non-existent.
“Son of Heaven, you should know that even the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas’ activities for taming, benefiting, and bringing happiness to sentient beings are unapprehendable. Why is this so?
Because sentient beings are detached, one should know that these matters of taming, benefiting, and bringing happiness are also detached;
because sentient beings are empty, one should know that these matters of taming, benefiting, and bringing happiness are also empty;
because sentient beings are not solid, one should know that these matters of taming, benefiting, and bringing happiness are also not solid.
Because sentient beings do not exist, you should know that these matters of taming, benefiting, and bringing happiness also do not exist.
"O Son of Heaven, you should know!
Even the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do not exist."
Why is this so? O sons of the gods!
Because sentient beings are detached, you should know that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are likewise detached.
Because sentient beings are empty, one should know that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are also empty;
because sentient beings are not solid, one should know that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are also not solid;
because sentient beings do not exist, one should know that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas also do not exist.
“O sons of the gods!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, upon hearing such matters as these, does not sink in spirit, and is neither startled, nor terrified, nor filled with regret, you should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).”

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 345. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter Fifty-seven, Part Five, "Praise of Firmness and Other Qualities. At that time, the Buddha addressed the Venerable Subhūti, saying: "Subhūti!"
"For what reason do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas not become despondent in their minds regarding the profound perfection of wisdom?
The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying,
"World-Honored One!"
Because all phenomena are non-existent, the minds of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas do not sink into despondency regarding this profound perfection of wisdom.
"World-Honored One! [they say.]
Because all phenomena are utterly remote, the minds of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do not sink into despondency regarding this profound perfection of wisdom.
"World-Honored One!..."
Because all phenomena are utterly quiescent, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas do not become despondent in their minds regarding the profound perfection of wisdom.
"World-Honored One!..."
Because all phenomena are non-existent, the minds of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas do not sink into despondency regarding the profound perfection of wisdom.
"World-Honored One!..."
Because all phenomena are without arising or ceasing, the minds of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas do not sink into despondency regarding this profound perfection of wisdom.
"World-Honored One!..."
Through these and various other such causes and conditions, the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do not become disheartened in their minds regarding the profound *prajñāpāramitā*. Why is this?

"Bhagavān! Regarding all dharmas, if for bodhisattva-mahāsattvas the one who might sink, that which is sunk, the time of sinking, the place where one sinks, and the agent by whom one sinks through this sinking are all unobtainable—because all dharmas are unobtainable."
“World-Honored One!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, upon hearing this teaching, does not sink in spirit, is not startled, not terrified, and feels no anxiety or regret, it should be known that this bodhisattva mahāsattva is practicing the profound *prajñāpāramitā*.”

Why is this? It is because this bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates that all phenomena are unapprehendable and cannot be designated; [he sees] that which causes one to sink, that which is sunk, the time of sinking, the place where one sinks, and the one who sinks by means of this sinking.
For this reason, when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas hear such matters, their minds do not sink; they are not startled, not terrified, and neither grieve nor regret.

“Bhagavān! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can practice the profound *prajñāpāramitā* in this way, they will be constantly honored and venerated by Śakra, the Lord of Devas, Mahābrahmā, and the lords of all worlds.”
The Buddha told Subhūti:

"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can practice the profound perfection of wisdom in this way, they will not only be constantly revered by Śakra, the Lord of Devas, Mahābrahmā, and the lords of the worlds; that bodhisattva mahāsattva will also be constantly revered by the devas of the Ābhāsvara Heaven, the Śubhakṛtsna Heaven, the Bṛhatphala Heaven, the Śuddhāvāsa Heavens, and other hosts of devas beyond these."

“Subhūti! A bodhisattva mahāsattva who can practice the profound perfection of wisdom in this way is also constantly protected and sustained in mind by all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas throughout the infinite, innumerable, and boundless worlds of the ten directions.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom in this manner, they will swiftly bring the perfection of wisdom to fulfillment, and they will also swiftly bring the perfections of meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity to fulfillment.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom in this way, they will swiftly bring internal emptiness to full completion; they will also swiftly bring external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence to full completion.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom in this manner, they will swiftly bring true thusness (tathatā) to full completion; they will also swiftly bring to full completion the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond arising, the fixed nature of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom in this manner, they will swiftly bring the noble truth of suffering to full completion, and they will also swiftly bring the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path to full completion.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom in this manner, they will swiftly bring the four dhyānas to full completion, and will also swiftly bring the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions to full completion.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom in this way, they will swiftly bring the eight liberations to full completion, and will also swiftly bring the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities to full completion.”

"Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom in this manner, they will swiftly bring the four applications of mindfulness to full completion, and will likewise swiftly bring the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path to full completion."

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom in this way, they cause the gate of liberation of emptiness to be swiftly perfected, and they also cause the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness to be swiftly perfected.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom in this manner, they will swiftly bring the Ground of Extreme Joy to full completion, and they will also swiftly bring the Ground of Freedom from Defilement, the Ground of Radiant Light, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Utmost Difficulty to Conquer, the Ground of Manifestation, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, and the Ground of the Dharma Cloud to full completion.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom in this manner, they will swiftly bring the five eyes to full completion, and they will also swiftly bring the six superknowledges to full completion.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom in this manner, they will swiftly bring to full completion the ten powers of a buddha, as well as the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom in this way, they cause the quality of non-forgetfulness to be swiftly perfected, and they also cause the state of constant abiding in equanimity to be swiftly perfected.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom in this manner, they will swiftly bring the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñatā) to full completion, and they will also swiftly bring the knowledge of the paths (mārgākārajñatā) and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā) to full completion.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom in this way, they will swiftly bring all the gateways of dhāraṇī to full completion, and they will also swiftly bring all the gateways of samādhi to full completion.”
“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva can practice the profound perfection of wisdom in this way, they cause the practice of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas to be swiftly brought to fulfillment.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom in this manner, they will swiftly bring to full completion the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas.”
“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom in this manner, they will swiftly bring the knowledge of all modes to complete fulfillment.”
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can practice the profound *prajñāpāramitā* in this manner, they will always be protected and remembered by all Buddhas, and will swiftly fulfill all merits. This bodhisattva mahāsattva should know that they are practicing where the Buddhas should practice, and will swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."

"Subhūti, you should know that the mind of this bodhisattva mahāsattva is firm and steadfast. Even if all sentient beings in worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in the ten directions were to become Māras, and each of those Māras were further to manifest as an equal number of Māras—all these evil Māras possessing immeasurable and boundless supernatural powers—even such Māras could not obstruct this bodhisattva mahāsattva, nor prevent him from practicing the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, nor prevent him from realizing the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment he seeks."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes two dharmas, all evil Māras will be unable to obstruct or destroy them, nor will they be able to prevent them from practicing the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, nor prevent them from realizing the sought-after unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
What are these two?
First, contemplating that all phenomena are ultimately empty.
Second, not abandoning any sentient beings.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes two dharmas, all evil Māras will be unable to obstruct or destroy them, nor can they prevent them from practicing the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, nor cause them to fail to realize the sought-after unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
What are these two? First, being able to accomplish everything exactly as spoken;
second, being constantly protected and remembered by all Buddhas.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can practice the profound perfection of wisdom in this manner, the sons of the gods will constantly come to pay homage, draw near to make offerings, inquire, and exhort him, saying:
'O son of good family!'"
If you wish to swiftly realize the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment that you seek, you should diligently abide in emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness. Why is this?
O son of good family!

If one diligently abides in emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, one should act as a protector for those without a protector, as a refuge for those without a refuge, as a savior for those without a savior, as a destination for those without a destination, as an island for those without an island, as a dwelling for those without a dwelling, as light for those in darkness, and as eyes for those who are blind.
Why is this? Son of good family!

To dwell in this way in emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness is itself to abide securely in the profound *prajñāpāramitā*. If one can abide securely in the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, then one will be able to swiftly realize the sought-after unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*).
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can abide in this manner within the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), then the Buddhas currently residing in the immeasurable, innumerable, and boundless worlds of the ten directions will, amidst their great assemblies, spontaneously rejoice and proclaim the name, clan, and various merits of that bodhisattva mahāsattva—namely, the preeminent merit of abiding in the profound perfection of wisdom."
“Subhūti, you should know this:

just as I now proclaim the profound *prajñāpāramitā* for the sake of the assembly, I spontaneously rejoice before this great multitude and extol the names, clans, and various merits of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas Ratnaketu and Śikhin, as well as those Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas who currently dwell in the presence of Akṣobhya Buddha, purifying their brahma-conduct and abiding in the profound *prajñāpāramitā*—namely, the sublime merits of dwelling securely in the profound *prajñāpāramitā*.

At present, in all the immeasurable, innumerable, and boundless worlds of the eastern direction, all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas proclaim the profound Prajñāpāramitā to the assemblies; there too, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the pure conduct of brahmacarya, never departing from the Prajñāpāramitā.

Those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas each, before their respective assemblies, spontaneously and joyfully proclaim and praise the names, lineages, and various merits of those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas—namely, their preeminent merit of never being separated from the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
The same applies to the south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, and the zenith and nadir.

"Subhūti, you should know that there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, from the first production of the thought of enlightenment, practice the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), gradually perfecting the path to great awakening until they realize the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvajñājñāna*). When the Buddhas currently residing in the immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless worlds of the ten directions preach the true Dharma, they will spontaneously and joyfully proclaim and praise the names, clans, and various merits of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas before the great assemblies—namely, their preeminent merit of practicing the profound perfection of wisdom."
Why is this so? Subhūti!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to perform what is difficult to do: they do not sever the lineage of the Buddhas, and they bring benefit, peace, and happiness to all sentient beings.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!

Which bodhisattva mahāsattvas are those whom the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas—by means of preaching the True Dharma—spontaneously rejoice in, extol, and praise by name, lineage, and all their merits before the great assembly, yet who remain in the stage of regression?"
“Are they non-retrogressive?
The Buddha told Subhūti:

“There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dwelling in the stage of non-retrogression who practice the profound perfection of wisdom; they receive from the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas the proclamation of their names, clans, and various merits through the teaching of the True Dharma before great assemblies, whereupon they naturally rejoice and are praised.”

Furthermore, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, although they have not yet received their prediction, practice the perfection of wisdom and likewise receive from the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha—by virtue of his preaching the True Dharma—the spontaneous joy of having their names, clans, and various merits proclaimed and praised before the great assembly.
The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"Of what bodhisattva is this that has been spoken?
The Buddha said:

“Subhūti! There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who train by following the conduct of Akṣobhya Buddha when he was a bodhisattva; having already attained abiding in the stage of non-retrogression, these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are naturally praised, extolled, and commended by name, clan, and all their merits before the great assembly by the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, as they preach the True Dharma.”

Furthermore, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who train by following the conduct of Bodhisattva Ratnaketu, Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Śikhin, and others. Although these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have not yet received their prediction, as they practice the *prajñāpāramitā*, they are likewise favored by the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, who—while preaching the True Dharma before the great assembly—spontaneously rejoice and extol their names, clans, and various merits.
"Furthermore, Subhūti,

there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who practice the profound perfection of wisdom and develop deep faith and understanding in the non-arising nature of all phenomena, yet have not yet realized the patience regarding the non-arising of dharmas (anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti);
they develop deep faith and understanding in the profound perfection of wisdom, yet have not yet realized the patience regarding the non-arising of dharmas."
They have developed deep faith and understanding in the ultimate emptiness of all phenomena, yet they have not yet realized the patience regarding the non-arising of dharmas;
they have developed deep faith and understanding in the quiescence of all phenomena, yet they have not yet realized the patience regarding the non-arising of dharmas;
they have developed deep faith and understanding in the detachment of all phenomena, yet they have not yet realized the patience regarding the non-arising of dharmas.
They have developed deep faith and understanding that all phenomena are devoid of intrinsic existence, yet they have not yet realized the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena;
they have developed deep faith and understanding that all phenomena lack self-mastery, yet they have not yet realized the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena;
they have developed deep faith and understanding that all phenomena are not solid or substantial, yet they have not yet realized the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena.

“Subhūti! Such bodhisattva-mahāsattvas as these, having been inspired by the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas through the preaching of the true Dharma, have their names, clans, and various merits spontaneously proclaimed, extolled, and praised before the great assembly.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is praised by the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas before the great assembly—spontaneously rejoicing and extolling their name, clan, and various merits due to their having been taught the true Dharma—then that bodhisattva mahāsattva has transcended the stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas and is certain to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”

"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the profound perfection of wisdom is, by the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, spontaneously praised and extolled for their name, clan, and various merits before a great assembly due to their teaching of the true Dharma, that bodhisattva mahāsattva will certainly abide in the stage of non-retrogression; having abided in this stage, they will surely realize the knowledge of all modes."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, upon hearing this teaching of the profound perfection of wisdom, has no doubt or confusion in their mind, but instead thinks:
'As the Buddha has taught, the principle of this profound perfection of wisdom is necessarily such that it is without inversion.'"

Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva has conceived deep pure faith in the perfection of wisdom, they shall gradually hear the perfection of wisdom extensively from the presence of the Buddha Acala and various bodhisattva mahāsattvas, and will conceive profound faith and understanding in its meaning and intent.
Having gained faith and understanding, one shall abide on the stage of non-retrogression; having abided on this stage, one will certainly realize the knowledge of all-knowledge. "Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva merely hears such profound *prajñāpāramitā* and does not give rise to slander, they will still acquire a great abundance of superior roots of goodness; how much more so if they can believe and understand it, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, contemplate it with mindfulness according to the principle of *tathatā*, and dwell in *tathatā* while diligently practicing and studying!
"These bodhisattvas shall quickly abide in the stage of non-retrogression and swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"

Since the true nature of all phenomena is entirely unapprehendable, how can a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwell in suchness, apply themselves with diligent cultivation, swiftly abide on the stage of non-retrogression, and rapidly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

Just as a transformation being conjured by a Buddha abides in suchness, practices the various deeds of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, will swiftly abide in the stage of non-retrogression, quickly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and proclaim the true Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings.”

In the same way, all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas likewise abide in suchness while practicing the various conducts of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; they shall swiftly abide in the stage of non-retrogression and quickly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:

“That which is emanated by the Tathāgata is entirely non-existent, and phenomena apart from suchness are likewise unattainable. Who, then, abiding in suchness, would cultivate the bodhisattva practice, swiftly dwell in the stage of non-retrogression, rapidly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and proclaim the true Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings?”

"Bhagavān, since even suchness cannot be apprehended, how much less could there be one who, abiding in suchness, practices the bodhisattva path, swiftly dwells in the stage of non-retrogression, quickly realizes unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and proclaims the true Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings?"
"If this were truly existent, it would be impossible," the Buddha said.
"Suvikrāntavikrāmin!"
So it is! So it is! It is just as you have said.

That which is emanated by the Tathāgata is entirely non-existent; since phenomena apart from suchness cannot be found, who could abide in suchness to cultivate the bodhisattva practice, swiftly dwell in the stage of non-retrogression, quickly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and proclaim the true Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings?

"Subhūti! Since even suchness cannot be apprehended, how much less can there be one who, abiding in suchness, practices the bodhisattva path, swiftly dwells in the stage of non-retrogression, rapidly realizes unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and proclaims the true Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings?"
If this were truly existent, it would be impossible. Why is that? Subhūti!

Whether a Tathāgata appears in the world or does not appear in the world, the nature of all phenomena remains as it is: they do not depart from suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, immutability, equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the reality-limit, the realm of empty space, and the inconceivable realm.

"Subhūti! There is certainly no one who, while dwelling in suchness, practices the bodhisattva path, who will swiftly abide on the stage of non-retrogression, quickly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and preach the true Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings."
Why is this? Subhūti!
