The suchness of all phenomena is without arising and without cessation, nor can even the slightest portion of abiding or alteration be found.

Subhūti! If there is no dharma that arises or ceases, and not even the slightest portion of abiding or alteration can be found, who could therein abide to practice the various deeds of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, swiftly dwell in the stage of non-retrogression, quickly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and proclaim the true Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings?
"If this were truly existent, it would be impossible.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"

This Prajñāpāramitā is thus subtle, profound, and extremely difficult to believe and understand. Although Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practicing the profound Prajñāpāramitā know that all phenomena are ungraspable, to seek unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is an exceedingly difficult matter.
Why is this? World-Honored One!

It is because there is certainly no one who, dwelling in *tathatā* (suchness), practices the various bodhisattva-mahāsattva deeds, and thereby swiftly dwells in the stage of non-retrogression, quickly realizes unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and performs the task of preaching the true Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings.

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they contemplate that all phenomena are utterly non-existent; yet their minds do not sink into this profound nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), nor do they feel fear, alarm, doubt, or obstruction. Such matters as these are truly rare and marvelous.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti said to Śakra, the Lord of the Devas: “Kauśika,
it is as you have said.”

When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they contemplate that all phenomena are utterly non-existent; yet their minds do not sink into the profound nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), nor do they fear, tremble, doubt, or become obstructed. Such matters as these are truly rare and marvelous.
Kauśika! When bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the profound perfection of wisdom, they contemplate all phenomena as being without exception empty.
That is to say, they contemplate all material phenomena as empty, and formless phenomena as likewise empty.
One contemplates that all phenomena with visibility are empty, and phenomena without visibility are also empty;
one contemplates that all phenomena with resistance are empty, and phenomena without resistance are also empty;
one contemplates that all phenomena with outflows are empty, and phenomena without outflows are also empty.
One contemplates that all conditioned phenomena are empty, and unconditioned phenomena are also empty;
one contemplates that all mundane phenomena are empty, and supramundane phenomena are also empty;
one contemplates that all quiescent phenomena are empty, and non-quiescent phenomena are also empty.
One contemplates that all phenomena of detachment are empty, and phenomena of non-detachment are also empty;
one contemplates that all past phenomena are empty, and future and present phenomena are also empty;
one contemplates that all wholesome phenomena are empty, and unwholesome and indeterminate phenomena are also empty.
One contemplates that all phenomena of the desire realm are empty, and that phenomena of the form and formless realms are also empty;
one contemplates that all phenomena of those in training are empty, and that phenomena of those beyond training and those who are neither in training nor beyond training are also empty;
one contemplates that all phenomena to be abandoned by vision are empty, and that phenomena to be abandoned by cultivation and those not to be abandoned are also empty.
One contemplates that all existent phenomena (*bhāva*) are empty; non-existent phenomena (*abhāva*), as well as that which is neither existent nor non-existent, are also empty. Kausika!

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they contemplate the emptiness of all such phenomena. Since within the emptiness of all phenomena there is nothing at all, who could sink, who could drown, who could fear, who could be startled, who could doubt, or who could be obstructed?

Therefore, Kauśika, it is not at all surprising that when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the profound perfection of wisdom, their minds do not sink into the profound nature of phenomena (dharmatā), nor do they feel fear, alarm, doubt, or obstruction.
Then Śakra, Lord of the Devas, addressed Subhūti, saying:
"Venerable One, all that you have spoken relies upon emptiness; therefore, your words are always free from obstruction."
"It is like shooting an arrow upward into the void; whether it is near or far, there is no obstruction. What the Venerable One has said is likewise so.
Chapter 58: Entrustment, Part One, Section 58-1. At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"

"Is it the case that what I have thus spoken, thus praised, and thus declared accords with the Dharma and the Vinaya as taught by the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, and that my declaration regarding the Dharma in accordance with the Dharma is free from error?"
The Buddha said: “Kauśika!

That you speak thus, praise thus, and declare thus is truly in accordance with the Dharma-discourse and Vinaya-discourse of the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha; it is an unerring declaration regarding the Dharma in accordance with the Dharma.”
Then, Śakra, the Lord of Devas, again addressed the Buddha, saying: “It is rare,
World-Honored One!”
Venerable Subhūti, everything that you say is without exception based upon emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness.

Venerable Subhūti, everything that you say is without exception based upon the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
Venerable Subhūti, everything that you say is without exception based upon the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.
Venerable Subhūti, everything that you say is without exception based upon the eight liberations, the eight spheres of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten spheres of totality.
Venerable Subhūti, everything you have said is entirely based upon the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.

"Venerable Subhūti, everything you have said is entirely based upon internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self-characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature."

Venerable Subhūti, everything that you say is entirely based upon suchness, the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm.
Venerable Subhūti, whatever you have spoken, there is nothing that does not rely upon the Noble Truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path.
Venerable Subhūti, whatever you have spoken, there is nothing that does not rely upon the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.
Venerable Subhūti, everything you have said is without exception based upon all the gateways of dhāraṇī and all the gateways of samādhi.

Venerable Subhūti, everything you have said is without exception based upon the Buddha’s ten powers, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha.
Venerable Subhūti, everything that you say is without exception based upon the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity.

Venerable Subhūti, everything that you say is without exception based upon all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).
Venerable Subhūti, everything that you say is invariably based upon the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
Venerable Subhūti, everything that you say is invariably based upon the unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas.
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra, the Lord of the Devas, saying: “Kauśika!
Because the venerable Subhūti abides in emptiness, even the perfection of giving cannot be apprehended; how much less so one who practices the perfection of giving!”

Since even the perfections of pure ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom cannot be apprehended through contemplation, how much less could there be anyone who practices these perfections of pure ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom!
“Because the Venerable Subhūti abides in emptiness, he perceives that even the four foundations of mindfulness cannot be apprehended, let alone one who practices them!

He perceives that even the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path cannot be apprehended, let alone one who practices the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path!”
“Because the Venerable Subhūti abides in emptiness, he does not perceive even the four dhyānas as obtainable, let alone one who cultivates the four dhyānas!
He does not perceive even the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments as obtainable, let alone one who cultivates the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments!”
“Because the Venerable Subhūti abides in emptiness, he does not perceive even the eight liberations as existing, let alone anyone who cultivates the eight liberations!

He does not perceive even the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, or the ten totalities as existing, let alone anyone who cultivates the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, or the ten totalities!”
“Venerable Subhūti, because he abides in emptiness, even internal emptiness (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*) cannot be apprehended; how much less so is there anyone who realizes internal emptiness!

Even external emptiness (*bahirdhā-śūnyatā*), internal-and-external emptiness (*adhyātma-bahirdhā-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of emptiness (*śūnyatā-śūnyatā*), great emptiness (*mahā-śūnyatā*), ultimate emptiness (*paramārtha-śūnyatā*), conditioned emptiness (*saṃskṛta-śūnyatā*), unconditioned emptiness (*asaṃskṛta-śūnyatā*), absolute emptiness (*atyanta-śūnyatā*), emptiness of the limitless (*anavarāgra-śūnyatā*), emptiness of dispersion (*anavakāra-śūnyatā*), emptiness of non-alteration (*anavakāra-śūnyatā*), emptiness of essential nature (*prakṛti-śūnyatā*), emptiness of self-characteristic (*svalakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*), emptiness of common characteristic (*sāmānya-lakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*), emptiness of all phenomena (*sarvadharma-śūnyatā*), emptiness of non-apprehensibility (*anupalambha-śūnyatā*), emptiness of non-existence (*abhāva-śūnyatā*), emptiness of intrinsic nature (*svabhāva-śūnyatā*), and emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence (*abhāva-svabhāva-śūnyatā*) cannot be apprehended; how much less so is there anyone who realizes external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence!”
“Venerable Subhūti, because he dwells in emptiness, even true thusness (*tathatā*) cannot be apprehended, let alone one who realizes true thusness!

Even the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm cannot be apprehended, let alone one who realizes the realm of phenomena up to the inconceivable realm!”
“Because the Venerable Subhūti abides in emptiness, even the Noble Truth of Suffering cannot be apprehended, let alone one who realizes the Noble Truth of Suffering!
Even the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path cannot be apprehended, let alone those who realize the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path!”
“Venerable Subhūti, because he dwells in emptiness, he does not perceive even the gate of liberation that is emptiness, let alone one who practices the gate of liberation that is emptiness!
He does not perceive even the gates of liberation that are signlessness and wishlessness, let alone those who practice the gates of liberation that are signlessness and wishlessness!”
"Venerable Subhūti, because he dwells in emptiness, even the five eyes cannot be apprehended by him, let alone anyone who cultivates the five eyes!
Even the six supernormal powers cannot be apprehended by him, let alone anyone who cultivates the six supernormal powers!"
“Because the Venerable Subhūti abides in emptiness, he does not perceive even all the gateways to dhāraṇī as existent, let alone anyone who cultivates all the gateways to dhāraṇī!”
Since even all the gateways to samādhi cannot be apprehended when one contemplates them, how much less can there be anyone who cultivates all the gateways to samādhi!

"Because the Venerable Subhūti abides in emptiness, even the ten powers of a Buddha cannot be apprehended when he contemplates them, how much less can there be anyone who cultivates the ten powers of a Buddha!"

When one contemplates that even the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha cannot be apprehended, how much less could there be anyone who cultivates the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha!
“Because the Venerable Subhūti abides in emptiness, he perceives that even the quality of non-forgetfulness cannot be apprehended, let alone one who cultivates the quality of non-forgetfulness!
He perceives that even the nature of constant equanimity cannot be apprehended, let alone one who cultivates the nature of constant equanimity!”
"Because the Venerable Subhūti abides in emptiness, even omniscience (*sarvajñatā*) cannot be apprehended, let alone one who cultivates omniscience!

Even the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) cannot be apprehended, let alone one who cultivates the knowledge of the paths or the knowledge of all aspects!"

“Because the Venerable Subhūti abides in emptiness, he does not perceive even the practice of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas as being obtainable, let alone one who practices the path of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas!”

"Because the Venerable Subhūti abides in emptiness, he perceives that even the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is unattainable, let alone anyone who realizes the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas!"
“Venerable Subhūti, because he dwells in emptiness, he perceives that even the Tathāgatas cannot be apprehended, much less one who turns the wheel of Dharma!
Venerable Subhūti, because he dwells in emptiness, he perceives that even dharmas without arising or cessation cannot be apprehended, much less one who realizes the absence of arising or cessation!”

"Venerable Subhūti, because he dwells in emptiness, even the thirty-two marks and eighty minor characteristics cannot be apprehended; how much less so can there be one who possesses a body endowed with these marks and characteristics!"
"Why is this, Kauśika?

Because the Venerable Subhūti dwells in all phenomena in a dwelling of detachment, a dwelling of tranquility, a dwelling of non-apprehension, a dwelling in emptiness, a dwelling in signlessness, and a dwelling in wishlessness."
Kauśika! The venerable Subhūti dwells in such immeasurable and supreme abodes regarding all phenomena. Kauśika!

Compared to the dwelling of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas in the supreme practice and dwelling of the *prajñāpāramitā*, the dwelling of Subhūti does not equal even a hundredth part, nor a thousandth part, nor a hundred-thousandth part, nor a *koṭi*-th part, nor a hundred-*koṭi*-th part, nor a thousand-*koṭi*-th part, nor a hundred-thousand-*koṭi*-th part, nor a *nayuta*-th part, nor a hundred-*nayuta*-th part, nor a thousand-*nayuta*-th part, nor a hundred-thousand-*nayuta*-th part, nor a hundred-thousand-*koṭi-nayuta*-th part; it does not even admit of a numerical fraction, a calculable fraction, a reckoned fraction, a metaphorical fraction, or even a fraction of the infinitesimal (*upaniṣad*).
Why is this? Kausika!

Excluding the dwelling of the Tathāgata, this most excellent dwelling in the practice of the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) wherein these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dwell is the foremost, the most excellent, the longest, the most venerable, the most sublime, the most exquisite, the highest, and the unsurpassed among all the dwellings of śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and others.
For this reason, Kauśika,
if a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to abide above all sentient beings, they should abide in the supreme practice-abiding of the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
Why is this? Kausika!

Because all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas abide in the supreme practice and dwelling of the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they transcend the stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, enter the bodhisattva’s state of right determination free from outflows (samyaktva-niyāma), swiftly fulfill all Buddha-dharmas, sever the continuity of all afflictions along with their habitual tendencies (vāsanā), and quickly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi), receiving the name of Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, and achieving the fulfillment of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajña-jñāna).

At that time, there were immeasurable and innumerable deities of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven in the assembly; filled with joy and leaping for gladness, they each took exquisite celestial *mañjūṣaka* flowers and scattered them over the Tathāgata and the community of bhikṣus.
At that time, six thousand bhikṣus within the assembly rose from their seats, bared their left shoulders, knelt with their right knees on the ground, and joined their palms toward the Buddha.

By the Buddha’s supernatural power, exquisite *sūkṣmasvara* flowers spontaneously filled the palms of each of them. These bhikṣus were filled with joy and leaped for gladness at such an unprecedented occurrence; they each took these flowers and scattered them as an offering over the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha.
Having paid homage to the Buddha, they all made this aspiration:

"By the power of these supreme roots of goodness, may we always dwell securely in the most excellent practice and abiding of the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, which cannot be dwelt upon by śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas; may we swiftly proceed toward unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment and transcend the stages of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas."

At that time, the World-Honored One, knowing that the mental conduct of the bhikṣus was pure and clear, smiled, according to the constant custom of the Buddhas. At the moment of his smile, various colored rays of light issued from his mouth—namely, blue, yellow, red, white, crimson, and pale violet—and illuminated this trichiliocosm, the world-system of the Buddha, in its entirety. These rays then circled the Buddha’s body three times and re-entered through the crown of his head.
The Venerable Ānanda rose from his seat, prostrated to the Buddha with palms joined, and said:
"World-Honored One,
for what cause and for what reason do you manifest this smile?"
"The Buddhas do not manifest a smile without cause or condition; I only pray that the Tathāgata will, out of compassion, explain it for us.
The Buddha told Ānanda:

"These six thousand bhikṣus who have made this supreme vow shall, in a future age known as the Star-like Kalpa (Tārakopama), attain unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment. They shall all share the same name: Saṃkusumita (Flower-Spreading) Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed Worthy, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, Buddha, Bhagavān."
Those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, along with their bhikṣu disciples, have identical lifespans in their buddha-fields, each living for exactly one thousand years.

From the time these Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas were first born, renounced the world, and attained enlightenment, wherever they may be—whether by day or by night—there constantly rains down subtle, five-colored flowers of exquisite sound.
For this reason, I smile. Ānanda,
you should know that if a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to abide in the most excellent abiding, they should train in the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
Ānanda, you should know this!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to dwell securely in the dwelling of the Tathāgata, they should train in the perfection of wisdom.
Ānanda, you should know this!

If good sons or good daughters diligently practice and study this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, these good sons and good daughters have, in previous lives, either passed away from the human realm and been reborn here, or passed away from the Tuṣita heaven and come to be born among humans. In those previous lives, whether among humans or in the heavens, they had extensively heard this profound *prajñāpāramitā*; it is because of this that they are now able to diligently practice and study this profound *prajñāpāramitā* in their present life.
Ānanda, you should know this:
if one is seen by the Tathāgata as diligently training in the profound *prajñāpāramitā* without looking back, that person is certainly a great bodhisattva.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!

If sons or daughters of good family are able to take delight in hearing, receiving, upholding, reading, reciting, thoroughly mastering, and reflecting upon this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, and further explain, reveal, instruct, and guide it for other sons or daughters of good family belonging to the Bodhisattva vehicle, you should know that such persons are great bodhisattvas. It is because they have, in the past, personally heard this profound *prajñāpāramitā* being taught by the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas; having heard it, they took delight in it, received, upheld, read, recited, thoroughly mastered, reflected upon it according to the principle, and extensively explained it to others. Therefore, they are now able to accomplish these matters in this present life."

“Ānanda, you should know that those sons and daughters of good family have planted many roots of merit in the presence of immeasurable Buddhas in the past; therefore, they are able to accomplish this matter in their present life.”
Those sons and daughters of good family should form this thought:

"I have not previously heard such profound *prajñāpāramitā* from Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas; I must have certainly heard such profound *prajñāpāramitā* from the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha."
"I have not previously planted roots of virtue under the Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas; rather, I have certainly planted roots of virtue under the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas.

By reason of these causes and conditions, I am now able to hear this profound Prajñāpāramitā, and with love and joy, I accept, uphold, read, recite, master, contemplate according to the principle, and extensively explain it to others, without ever becoming weary."
"Ānanda, you should know this:

if sons or daughters of good family are able to love, delight in hearing, receive, uphold, read, recite, master thoroughly, and reflect upon this profound *prajñāpāramitā* according to the principle, and practice in accordance with its meaning, its dharma, and its profound intent, then these sons and daughters of good family are, in effect, seeing us—Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas—before their very eyes."
“Ānanda, you should know this:

if sons or daughters of good family, upon hearing this profound *prajñāpāramitā* being taught, receive it with deep faith, do not disparage or slander it, and cannot be deterred from it, these sons or daughters of good family have already made offerings to immeasurable Buddhas, have planted many roots of merit in the presence of those Buddhas, and have also been sustained by immeasurable virtuous friends.”
“Ānanda, you should know this!

If sons or daughters of good family are able to plant roots of goodness within the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha—the supreme field of merit—then although they will certainly attain either the fruit of a śrāvaka, the fruit of a pratyekabuddha, or the fruit of a Tathāgata, they must nonetheless possess unimpeded mastery over this profound *prajñāpāramitā* and practice the *dānapāramitā*, as well as practice the *śīla*, *kṣānti*, *vīrya*, *dhyāna*, and *prajñāpāramitās*, in order to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”

They abide in internal emptiness; they abide in external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

They abide in suchness; they abide in the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm.
They dwell securely in the noble truth of suffering, and they dwell securely in the noble truths of its origin, its cessation, and the path.

They practice the four foundations of mindfulness; they practice the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
They practice the four dhyānas; they practice the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments.
They practice the eight liberations; they practice the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities.
He practices the gate of liberation of emptiness; he practices the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.
He practices the five eyes; he practices the six supernormal powers.

He practices the ten powers of a Buddha; he practices the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
They practice the dharma of non-forgetfulness; they practice the constant abiding in equanimity.
They practice all doors of dhāraṇī; they practice all doors of samādhi.

They cultivate all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), they cultivate the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and they cultivate the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), bringing them to full completion.
"Ānanda, you should know this:

if a bodhisattva mahāsattva can skillfully and unimpededly understand this profound perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), they cultivate the perfection of generosity (*dānapāramitā*), and they cultivate the perfections of ethical discipline (*śīla*), patience (*kṣānti*), diligence (*vīrya*), meditative concentration (*dhyāna*), and wisdom (*prajñā*)."

They abide in internal emptiness; they abide in external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.

They dwell securely in suchness; they dwell securely in the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm.
They dwell securely in the noble truth of suffering, and they dwell securely in the noble truths of its origin, its cessation, and the path.

They practice the four foundations of mindfulness; they practice the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
They practice the four dhyānas; they practice the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments.
They practice the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities.
They practice the gate of liberation of emptiness; they practice the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.
They practice the five eyes; they practice the six supernormal powers.

They practice the ten powers of a Buddha; they practice the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
They practice the dharma of non-forgetfulness; they practice the state of constant abiding in equanimity.
They practice all doors of dhāraṇī; they practice all doors of samādhi.
By practicing all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), they bring them to full completion.
It is impossible that such a bodhisattva mahāsattva, having failed to attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, would instead abide on the level of a śrāvaka or a pratyekabuddha.

Therefore, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening should attain unimpeded mastery of this profound perfection of wisdom and practice the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, up to and including the practice of all-knowledge (*sarvajñā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), so that they may bring them to fulfillment.
"Therefore, Ānanda, I entrust this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā to you; you should correctly receive, uphold, read, recite, and master it, so that it is not lost or forgotten!"
“Ānanda, you should know this!

Apart from this profound sūtra of the *Prajñāpāramitā*, if one were to forget any other teachings I have spoken that one has received and upheld, the transgression would still be small; however, if one does not properly receive and uphold this profound *Prajñāpāramitā* sūtra, even to the extent of forgetting a single verse, the transgression is exceedingly great.”
"Ānanda, you should know this!
If one can properly receive and uphold even a single verse from this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā without forgetting it, the merit obtained will be immeasurable."

"If there should be anyone who does not properly uphold this, even if it is only a single verse that they forget, the grave sin they incur shall be equal in measure to the aforementioned merit. Therefore, Ānanda!"

I entrust this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā to you with earnest care; you should correctly receive, uphold, read, recite, master, contemplate according to the principle, and extensively explain and reveal it to others, so that those who uphold it may ultimately understand its words, meanings, and underlying intent.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle Three Hundred and Forty-Six. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. First Division, Chapter Fifty-Eight, Part Two: Entrustment. "Ānanda, you should know this!

If sons or daughters of good family should receive, uphold, read, recite, master thoroughly, reflect upon according to the principle, extensively explain to others, analyze, and elucidate this profound sūtra of the *Prajñāpāramitā*, making it easy to understand, they will thereby be upholding the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment realized by all Buddhas of the past, future, and present.
“Ānanda, you should know this:

if sons or daughters of good family receive, uphold, read, recite, master, reflect upon according to the principle, extensively explain to others, analyze, and elucidate this profound sūtra of the *Prajñāpāramitā*, making it easy for others to understand, they thereby embrace the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment realized by all Buddhas of the past, future, and present.”
"Ānanda, you should know this!
If sons or daughters of good family, in my presence, should offer various kinds of exquisite flower garlands,
powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, precious banners, flags, and canopies;
Those who provide musical performances and lamps, making offerings with reverence, respect, honor, and praise without ceasing,
should receive, uphold, read, recite, master thoroughly, reflect upon according to principle, extensively explain to others, analyze, and elucidate this profound sutra of the *Prajñāpāramitā*.
This is easy to understand; furthermore, one should transcribe it adorned with various jewels, and constantly offer worship,

reverence, respect, and praise— without ever becoming weary— with all kinds of exquisite flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, precious banners, flags, canopies, music, and lamps.
"Ānanda, you should know this!

If sons or daughters of good family offer worship, honor, respect, and praise to the profound Prajñāpāramitā, they thereby offer worship, honor, respect, and praise to me; they also offer worship, honor, respect, and praise to all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas currently teaching the Dharma throughout the worlds of the ten directions, as well as to all Buddhas of the past and the future."

“Ānanda, you should know that if sons and daughters of good family hear this profound sūtra of the *prajñāpāramitā* and, with deep resolve, believe, accept, revere, and delight in it, they are thereby believing, accepting, revering, and delighting in all the Buddhas of the past, future, and present.”
"Ānanda! If you love me and do not forsake me, you should likewise love and not forsake this profound sūtra of the *prajñāpāramitā*, ensuring that not even a single phrase is forgotten."

“Ānanda! Although the causes and conditions for my entrusting this profound sūtra of the *prajñāpāramitā* are immeasurable, to speak of them in brief: just as I am your teacher, you should know that the profound *prajñāpāramitā* is likewise your teacher. Since you revere and honor me, you should likewise revere and honor the profound *prajñāpāramitā*.”

Therefore, Ānanda! By means of immeasurable skillful expedients, I entrust to you this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā; you should receive and uphold it, ensuring that it is not lost or forgotten.
Ānanda! I now entrust this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā to you, in the presence of this immeasurable assembly of devas, humans, asuras, and others.
“Ānanda! I now tell you this in truth:

those who possess pure faith and wish not to abandon the Buddha, wish not to abandon the Dharma, and wish not to abandon the Saṅgha; and who likewise wish not to abandon the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment realized by all Buddhas of the past, future, and present—such persons must certainly not abandon this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā.”
Ānanda! This is the method of instruction and admonition for all of us Buddhas regarding our disciples.

If sons or daughters of good family should take delight in hearing, upholding, reciting, and reflecting upon this profound *Prajñāpāramitā* sūtra according to the truth, and should extensively explain it to others through immeasurable gateways—analyzing, elucidating, establishing, and instituting it so that it is easily understood—then these sons or daughters of good family will swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and will be able to draw near to the full perfection of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*).
Why is this? Because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment attained by all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas arises in dependence upon such profound prajñāpāramitā.
“Ānanda, you should know that the Tathāgatas, Arhats,
and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past also gave birth to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment by relying upon this very profound perfection of wisdom.”
Future Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas will likewise give birth to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment by relying upon this very profound perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas currently teaching the Dharma in all worlds throughout the ten directions—east, west, south, north, the four intermediate points, above, and below—have likewise given birth to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment from this very profound Prajñāpāramitā.

Therefore, Ānanda! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, they should diligently apply themselves with vigor to the study and practice of the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
Why is this? Because this Prajñāpāramitā is the mother of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, for she gives birth to all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
“Ānanda, you should know that if bodhisattva-mahāsattvas diligently train in the six perfections, they shall all swiftly realize the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment they seek.”

Therefore, Ānanda! I entrust these profound sūtras on the six pāramitās to you once more before this great assembly; you should receive and uphold them correctly, ensuring they are not forgotten or lost.
Why is this? These six kinds of profound sūtras on the pāramitās are the inexhaustible Dharma-treasury of all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, for all the Buddha-dharmas arise from them.
“Ānanda, you should know this:

all the teachings currently being expounded by all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas throughout all the worlds of the east, west, south, north, the four intermediate directions, and the zenith and nadir, all flow forth from this inexhaustible Dharma-treasury of the six pāramitās.”
All the teachings previously expounded by the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past have issued forth from this inexhaustible Dharma-treasury of the six pāramitās.
Whatever dharmas future Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas shall teach, all will flow forth from this inexhaustible Dharma-treasury of the six pāramitās.
“Ānanda, you should know that the Tathāgatas, Arhats,
and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past also diligently trained in this inexhaustible Dharma-treasury of the six pāramitās, and thereby realized unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”
Future Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas shall likewise, by diligently training in this inexhaustible treasury of the six pāramitās, realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

All the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas currently teaching the Dharma in all the worlds of the east, west, south, north, the four intermediate directions, and above and below, have likewise diligently studied this inexhaustible treasury of the six pāramitās and have now realized unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

"Ānanda, you should know that the disciples of all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past diligently studied and trained in this inexhaustible Dharma-treasury of the six pāramitās, thereby attaining parinirvāṇa within the realm of the wondrous nirvana without remainder."

In the future, all the assemblies of disciples of the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas shall diligently train in this inexhaustible Dharma-treasury of the six pāramitās and shall attain parinirvāṇa in the realm of the wondrous nirvana without remainder.

All the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas currently residing in all worlds throughout the ten directions—east, west, south, north, the four intermediate points, above, and below—as well as their assemblies of disciples, all diligently train in this inexhaustible Dharma-treasury of the six pāramitās and have now entered parinirvāṇa in the realm of the wondrous nirvāṇa without remainder.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!

Suppose you were to teach the Dharma of the Śrāvakas to individuals belonging to the Śrāvaka Vehicle, and by means of that Dharma, every sentient being in the trichiliocosm were to attain the fruit of Arhatship; even so, you would still not have performed the duty of a disciple for me."

If you can explain even a single verse of the profound *prajñāpāramitā* to a person belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle, that shall be called doing my work as a disciple; I shall feel great sympathetic joy for this, which is superior to your teaching all sentient beings in a trichiliocosm so that they all attain the fruit of arhatship.

"Furthermore, Ānanda! Suppose all sentient beings in the trichiliocosm, through the power of another's instruction, were simultaneously to obtain human bodies and at once realize the fruit of arhatship. What do you think: regarding the merit consisting of the nature of giving, the nature of morality, and the nature of cultivation belonging to all those arhats—what is your opinion?"
"Would that meritorious action be great?
Ānanda replied, "It would be very great!"
"World-Honored One!
It is very much so! Sugata!"
The Buddha told Ānanda:

"If a śrāvaka disciple were able to proclaim for a single day and night the Dharma associated with the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) to a bodhisattva mahāsattva, the mass of merit obtained would be far greater than that."

Ānanda, you should know this! Setting aside one day and night, let us consider just one day; setting aside one day, let us consider just half a day; setting aside half a day, let us consider just one watch; setting aside one watch, let us consider just the time it takes to eat a meal; setting aside the time for a meal, let us consider just a brief moment; setting aside a brief moment, let us consider just an instant; and setting aside an instant, let us consider just a fleeting breath. If a śrāvaka were to proclaim to a bodhisattva the Dharma associated with the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) for even that duration, the mass of merit he would obtain would be far greater than the former.
Why is this? Because the mass of merit obtained by this śrāvaka surpasses all the roots of goodness of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!

If a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva were to proclaim various Śrāvaka-yāna teachings for the sake of individuals belonging to the Śrāvaka vehicle, and if, by means of these teachings, all sentient beings within the trichiliocosm were to realize the fruit of Arhatship and become endowed with all manner of sublime qualities—what do you think?
"By this cause and condition, would the mass of merit obtained by this bodhisattva mahāsattva be great?
Subhūti replied, "It would be very great!"
"O Bhagavan,
it is very much so! O Sugata!"
"The mass of merit acquired by this bodhisattva mahāsattva is immeasurable and boundless.
The Buddha told Ānanda:

"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva were to teach the Dharma associated with the perfection of wisdom for even a single day and night to a person belonging to the vehicle of the śrāvakas, or a person belonging to the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas, or a person belonging to the unsurpassed vehicle, the mass of merit acquired would be far greater than the former."

“Ānanda, you should know this! Setting aside one day and night, let us consider just one day; setting aside one day, let us consider just half a day; setting aside half a day, let us consider just one watch (muhūrta); setting aside one watch, let us consider just the time it takes to eat a meal; setting aside the time of a meal, let us consider just a brief moment (kṣaṇa); setting aside a brief moment, let us consider just an instant (lava); setting aside an instant, let us consider just the duration of a single breath. If a bodhisattva mahāsattva were to teach the Dharma associated with the perfection of wisdom for even that length of time to individuals belonging to the three vehicles, the mass of merit they would obtain would be immeasurably and infinitely greater than the former.”

Why is this? Because the gift of Dharma associated with the profound *prajñāpāramitā* surpasses all gifts of Dharma associated with the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas, as well as all the roots of goodness belonging to those two vehicles.

Why is this? Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas seek unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment for themselves, and they also manifest, instruct, exhort, inspire, and gladden sentient beings with dharmas corresponding to the Great Vehicle, causing them to attain non-retrogression from unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
“Ānanda, you should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva personally practices the perfection of generosity and also teaches others to practice the perfection of generosity;

he personally practices the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, and also teaches others to practice the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.”
By reason of these causes and conditions, their roots of goodness increase; it is impossible that such a person would ever regress from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
This bodhisattva mahāsattva personally cultivates the four foundations of mindfulness and also teaches others to cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness;

they personally cultivate the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path, and also teach others to cultivate the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path.
By this cause and condition, their roots of virtue will increase; it is impossible that such a bodhisattva mahāsattva would ever regress from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
This bodhisattva mahāsattva abides personally in internal emptiness (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*) and also teaches others to abide in internal emptiness;

they abide personally in external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, and they also teach others to abide in external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
By these causes and conditions, their roots of goodness increase; it is impossible that such a bodhisattva mahāsattva would ever regress from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
This bodhisattva mahāsattva abides in *tathatā* (suchness) themselves and also teaches others to abide in *tathatā*;

they abide in the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of empty space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*), and they also teach others to abide in the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm.
By this cause and condition, their roots of goodness increase; it is impossible that such a bodhisattva mahāsattva would ever regress from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
This bodhisattva mahāsattva abides personally in the noble truth of suffering and also teaches others to abide in the noble truth of suffering;
they abide personally in the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, and also teach others to abide in the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path.
By these causes and conditions, their roots of goodness increase; it is impossible that such a person would ever regress from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
This bodhisattva mahāsattva personally cultivates the four dhyānas and also teaches others to cultivate the four dhyānas;
they personally cultivate the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, and also teach others to cultivate the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments.
By reason of these causes and conditions, their roots of goodness increase; it is impossible that such a bodhisattva mahāsattva would ever regress from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
This bodhisattva mahāsattva personally cultivates the eight liberations and also teaches others to cultivate the eight liberations;

they personally cultivate the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities, and also teach others to cultivate the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities.
By these causes and conditions, their roots of goodness increase; it is impossible that such a person would ever regress from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
This bodhisattva mahāsattva personally cultivates the gate of liberation of emptiness and also teaches others to cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness;
they personally cultivate the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, and also teach others to cultivate the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.
By these causes and conditions, their roots of goodness increase; it is impossible that such a person would ever regress from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
This bodhisattva mahāsattva personally cultivates the five eyes and also teaches others to cultivate the five eyes;
they personally cultivate the six supernormal powers and also teaches others to cultivate the six supernormal powers.
By these causes and conditions, their roots of goodness increase; it is impossible that such a person would ever regress from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening.
This bodhisattva mahāsattva personally cultivates the ten powers of a buddha and also teaches others to cultivate the ten powers of a buddha;

they personally cultivate the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, and also teach others to cultivate these from the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha.
By these causes and conditions, their roots of goodness increase; it is impossible that such a person would ever regress from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
This bodhisattva mahāsattva personally cultivates the quality of non-forgetfulness and also teaches others to cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness;
they personally cultivate the state of constant equanimity and also teaches others to cultivate the state of constant equanimity.
By these causes and conditions, their roots of goodness increase; it is impossible that such a person would ever regress from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
This bodhisattva mahāsattva personally cultivates all doors of dhāraṇī and also teaches others to cultivate all doors of dhāraṇī;
they personally cultivate all doors of samādhi and also teach others to cultivate all doors of samādhi.
By reason of these causes and conditions, their roots of goodness increase; it is impossible that such a person would ever regress from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
This bodhisattva mahāsattva personally cultivates all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) and also teaches others to cultivate all-knowledge;

they personally cultivate the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), and also teach others to cultivate the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects.
By reason of these causes and conditions, their roots of goodness increase; it is impossible that such a person would ever regress from unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.
This bodhisattva mahāsattva personally cultivates all the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva and also teaches others to cultivate all the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
By reason of these causes and conditions, their roots of goodness increase; it is impossible that they would ever regress from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
This bodhisattva mahāsattva personally cultivates unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and also teaches others to cultivate unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
By these causes and conditions, their roots of goodness increase; it is impossible that such a person would ever regress from unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.

This bodhisattva mahāsattva personally cultivates the patience toward the non-arising of phenomena (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*) and also teaches others to cultivate the patience toward the non-arising of phenomena.
By this cause and condition, their roots of virtue will increase; it is impossible that such a person would ever regress from unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.
This bodhisattva mahāsattva purifies his own buddha-field and also teaches others to purify their buddha-fields;
he brings sentient beings to maturity himself and also teaches others to bring sentient beings to maturity.
By this cause and condition, their roots of goodness increase; it is impossible that they would ever regress from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
These bodhisattva-mahāsattvas themselves train to turn the unexcelled wheel of Dharma, and they also teach others to train in turning the unexcelled wheel of Dharma.
By these causes and conditions, their roots of goodness increase; it is impossible that such a person would ever regress from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

This Bodhisattva Mahāsattva adorns his own body with immeasurable, subtle, and wondrous marks and signs, and likewise teaches others to adorn their bodies with immeasurable, subtle, and wondrous marks and signs. By these causes and conditions, their roots of goodness increase; it is impossible that such a person would ever regress from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

“This bodhisattva mahāsattva personally contemplates the twelve links of dependent origination in both direct and reverse order, and also teaches others to contemplate the twelve links of dependent origination in both direct and reverse order.
By virtue of these causes and conditions, their roots of goodness increase; it is impossible that they would ever regress from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.”

“This bodhisattva mahāsattva personally contemplates that all phenomena are without a self, without a sentient being, without a life-principle, without a soul, without a nourisher, without a person, without an individual, without a mind-born, without a youth, without an agent, without an experiencer, without a knower, and without a seer; furthermore, they teach others to contemplate that all phenomena are without a self, up to and including being without a seer.”
By these causes and conditions, their roots of goodness increase; it is impossible that such a bodhisattva mahāsattva would ever regress from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

This bodhisattva mahāsattva personally contemplates all phenomena as being like an illusion, like a dream, like a reflection, like an echo, like a shadow, like a mirage, like a magical transformation, and like a city of Gandharvas—all of which appear to exist yet lack any real intrinsic nature. Furthermore, they teach others to contemplate all phenomena as being like an illusion and so forth, up to being like a city of Gandharvas—all of which appear to exist yet lack any real intrinsic nature.
"By this cause and condition, their roots of virtue will increase; it is impossible that they would ever regress from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

At that time, the World-Honored One, surrounded by the fourfold assembly, praised and spoke upon the *Prajñāpāramitā*, having entrusted it to Ānanda and caused him to receive and uphold it. Furthermore, before the great assembly of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans, he manifested supernatural powers, causing the entire multitude to behold the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Akṣobhya, surrounded before and behind by śrāvakas and bodhisattvas, as he proclaimed the sublime Dharma to the ocean-like assembly, and to behold the magnificent array of signs and marks of that land.

That community of śrāvakas were all arhats; their outflows were exhausted and they were free from further afflictions. They had attained true mastery, with minds well-liberated and wisdom well-liberated. Like well-trained thoroughbred horses or great dragons, they had done what was to be done and accomplished what was to be accomplished. Having laid down the heavy burden and attained their own benefit, they had exhausted the fetters of existence and were liberated through right knowledge, reaching the ultimate goal of supreme sovereignty over the mind.
All those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas were renowned and well-known to all; they had attained dhāraṇīs and unimpeded eloquence, and had accomplished immeasurable, sublime merits.

The Buddha withdrew his supernormal power, whereupon the great assembly suddenly no longer saw the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Acala, nor the śrāvakas, bodhisattvas, and the ocean-like assembly, nor the various marks and adornments of that buddha-field.
That Akṣobhya Buddha, his bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, the adornments of his land, and his assemblies are all not within the range of the visual faculty here. Why is this so?
The Buddha withdrew his supernormal power because there were no conditions for seeing that distant realm.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Venerable Ānanda:
"Do you still see the land and the assembly of the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Acalā?"
Ānanda replied, “I no longer see it,
for that matter is not within the range of these eyes.
The Buddha told Ānanda:

"Just as the assemblies and other phenomena of that Buddha-land are not within the range of the eyes here in this land, so it is with all dharmas: none are within the range of the eye-faculty. A dharma does not act upon a dharma; a dharma does not see a dharma; a dharma does not know a dharma."
“Ānanda, you should know that all phenomena have no agent, no seer, no knower; they are without movement and without action. Why is this?
Because all phenomena are devoid of functional activity, being free from the nature of grasper and grasped;
because all phenomena are inconceivable, being free from the nature of the conceivable and the object of conception.
Because all phenomena are like illusory things and the like, existing only as mere semblances through the conjunction of various conditions;
and because all phenomena lack an agent or recipient, appearing falsely as if they exist while lacking any solid reality.

Ānanda, you should know that if a bodhisattva mahāsattva knows thus, sees thus, and practices thus, they are practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), and yet they do not cling to the characteristics of these phenomena.
Ānanda, you should know that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, they are training in the perfection of wisdom.
Ānanda, you should know!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to swiftly bring all the pāramitās to full completion, they should train in the prajñāpāramitā. Why is this?

One who trains in this manner is the most supreme, the most excellent, the longest, the most venerable, the most wondrous, the most subtle, the highest, and the unsurpassed among all trainings; they bring benefit and happiness to the entire world, acting as a refuge for those without refuge, and are permitted and praised by the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones.

“Ānanda, you should know that when Buddhas and Bodhisattvas abide in this training, they can take up the trichiliocosm with their right hand, either casting it to another direction or placing it back in its original location, while the sentient beings therein remain unaware and unperceiving.”
Why is this? Because the merit and majestic power of the profound *prajñāpāramitā* are inconceivable.
"Ānanda, you should know this!"

The Buddhas of the past, future, and present, as well as the assembly of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, having studied this Prajñāpāramitā, have all attained unimpeded knowledge and vision regarding the dharmas of the past, future, present, and the unconditioned.
Therefore, Ānanda, I declare that among all trainings,
training in this profound perfection of wisdom is the foremost, the most excellent, the longest, the most venerable, the most sublime, the most exquisite, the highest, and the unsurpassed.
“Ānanda, you should know this:
those who wish to grasp the measure or the limit of the profound perfection of wisdom are like foolish people who wish to grasp the measure and the limit of space.”
Why is this? Because the merit of the profound *prajñāpāramitā* is immeasurable and limitless.
"Ānanda, you should know this!"
I do not say that the profound *prajñāpāramitā* has a measure or a limit such as those of name-bodies (*nāmakāya*) and so forth. Why is this?

All name-bodies, phrase-bodies (*padakāya*), and syllable-bodies (*vyañjanakāya*) are dharmas that possess measure; the profound *prajñāpāramitā* is not a dharma that possesses measure. Neither can all name-bodies, phrase-bodies, and syllable-bodies measure the *prajñāpāramitā*, nor is the *prajñāpāramitā* that which is measured by them.
At that time, the Venerable Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One,
for what reason and by what causal conditions is the profound *prajñāpāramitā* described as immeasurable?"

The Buddha told Ānanda: “Because the nature of the profound *prajñāpāramitā* is inexhaustible, it is called immeasurable; because the nature of the profound *prajñāpāramitā* is detached, it is called immeasurable; because the nature of the profound *prajñāpāramitā* is tranquil, it is called immeasurable; because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* is like the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), it is called immeasurable; because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* is like space, it is called immeasurable.”

Ānanda, you should know that all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past trained in the Prajñāpāramitā, realized unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and proclaimed and revealed it for the sake of all sentient beings; yet this Prajñāpāramitā is inexhaustible.

All future Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas will study this Prajñāpāramitā, realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and proclaim and reveal it for the sake of all sentient beings; yet this Prajñāpāramitā is inexhaustible.

At present, all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas in the infinite, innumerable, and boundless worlds of the ten directions study this Prajñāpāramitā, realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and proclaim and reveal it for the sake of all sentient beings; yet this Prajñāpāramitā is inexhaustible.
Why is this? Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* is, like space, inexhaustible; therefore, those who wish to exhaust the profound *prajñāpāramitā* would be wishing to exhaust the limits of space.
“Ānanda, you should know that because the perfection of wisdom is inexhaustible, it was not exhausted in the past, is not exhausted in the present,

and will not be exhausted in the future; likewise, because the perfections of meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity are also inexhaustible, they were not exhausted in the past, are not exhausted in the present, and will not be exhausted in the future.”
“Ānanda, you should know this:
because internal emptiness (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*) is inexhaustible, it was not exhausted in the past, is not exhausted now, and will not be exhausted in the future.

Because external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature are also inexhaustible, they were not exhausted in the past, are not exhausted now, and will not be exhausted in the future.”
"Ānanda, you should know this:
because True Suchness (*tathatā*) is inexhaustible, it was not exhausted in the past, is not exhausted in the present, and will not be exhausted in the future;

because the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the non-falsity of phenomena, the unchanging nature of phenomena, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm are likewise inexhaustible, they were not exhausted in the past, are not exhausted in the present, and will not be exhausted in the future."
"Ānanda, you should know this:
because the Noble Truth of Suffering is inexhaustible, it was not exhausted in the past, is not exhausted in the present, and will not be exhausted in the future;

and because the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path are likewise inexhaustible, they were not exhausted in the past, are not exhausted in the present, and will not be exhausted in the future."
“Ānanda, you should know that because the four dhyānas are inexhaustible, they were not exhausted in the past, are not exhausted now, and will not be exhausted in the future; likewise,
because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are also inexhaustible, they were not exhausted in the past, are not exhausted now, and will not be exhausted in the future.”
“Ānanda, you should know that because the eight liberations are inexhaustible, they were not exhausted in the past, are not exhausted now,

and will not be exhausted in the future; likewise, because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities are also inexhaustible, they were not exhausted in the past, are not exhausted now, and will not be exhausted in the future.”
“Ānanda, you should know this:
because the four foundations of mindfulness are inexhaustible, they were not exhausted in the past, are not exhausted now, and will not be exhausted in the future;

likewise, because the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are also inexhaustible, they were not exhausted in the past, are not exhausted now, and will not be exhausted in the future.”
"Ānanda, you should know this:
because the gate of liberation of emptiness is inexhaustible, it was not exhausted in the past, is not exhausted in the present, and will not be exhausted in the future;

because the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are likewise inexhaustible, they were not exhausted in the past, are not exhausted in the present, and will not be exhausted in the future."
"Ānanda, you should know that because the five eyes are inexhaustible, they were not exhausted in the past, are not exhausted now, and will not be exhausted in the future; likewise,
because the six supernormal powers are also inexhaustible, they were not exhausted in the past, are not exhausted now, and will not be exhausted in the future."
“Ānanda, you should know that because the ten powers of a Buddha are inexhaustible, they were not exhausted in the past, are not exhausted now,

and will not be exhausted in the future; likewise, because the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are also inexhaustible, they were not exhausted in the past, are not exhausted now, and will not be exhausted in the future.”
“Ānanda, you should know that because the quality of non-forgetfulness is inexhaustible, it was not exhausted in the past, is not exhausted now, and will not be exhausted in the future; likewise,
because the nature of constant dwelling in equanimity is also inexhaustible, it was not exhausted in the past, is not exhausted now, and will not be exhausted in the future.”
"Ānanda, you should know this:
because all dharanī-doors are inexhaustible, they were inexhaustible in the past, are inexhaustible now, and will be inexhaustible in the future;
likewise, because all samādhi-doors are inexhaustible, they were inexhaustible in the past, are inexhaustible now, and will be inexhaustible in the future."
“Ānanda, you should know that because omniscience (*sarvajñatā*) is inexhaustible, it was not exhausted in the past, is not exhausted now, and will not be exhausted in the future;

because the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are also inexhaustible, they were not exhausted in the past, are not exhausted now, and will not be exhausted in the future.”
“Ānanda, you should know that because the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are inexhaustible, they were not exhausted in the past, are not exhausted now,

and will not be exhausted in the future; likewise, because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas is also inexhaustible, it was not exhausted in the past, is not exhausted now, and will not be exhausted in the future.”
"Why is this so? Because these dharmas are without arising, without cessation, and without abiding or change; how, then, could they be established as having an end?
At that time, the World-Honored One extended his broad and long tongue until it completely covered his face, then withdrew the mark of his tongue and addressed Ānanda, saying:
“What do you think? Is there any falsehood in the speech uttered from such a tongue?
Ānanda replied to the Buddha:
"No, World-Honored One! No!"
“Excellent, Sugata!
The Buddha said to Ānanda:

“From this day forward, you should extensively expound such profound *prajñāpāramitā* for the fourfold assembly, analyzing and revealing it, establishing and defining it, so that it may be easily understood.”

“Ānanda, you should know that within this profound *prajñāpāramitā* sūtra, all factors conducive to enlightenment (*bodhipakṣadharma*) and the characteristics of all phenomena (*dharmalakṣaṇa*) are extensively explained. Therefore, all individuals seeking the vehicle of the śrāvakas, all individuals seeking the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas, and all individuals seeking the unsurpassed vehicle should constantly and diligently train in these dharma-gates taught in this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, never harboring weariness or abandonment. If they can do so, they will swiftly become established in the stage sought by each.”
"Furthermore, Ānanda!

This profound *prajñāpāramitā* is that which enables entry into all marks (*lakṣaṇa*), all syllables (*akṣara*), and all *dhāraṇī* gates. All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should practice and study these gates of all *dhāraṇīs*."
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva upholds such a gateway of dhāraṇīs, they will swiftly be able to realize all forms of eloquence and the various types of unimpeded analytical knowledge. Therefore, Ānanda!
I declare that this profound perfection of wisdom is the inexhaustible Dharma-treasury of all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past, future, and present.
“Ānanda! I now tell you clearly:

if there is anyone who receives, upholds, reads, recites, masters, and reflects upon this profound Prajñāpāramitā in accordance with reality, they are thereby receiving and upholding the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas of the past, future, and present.”

“Ānanda! I declare that this profound *prajñāpāramitā* is the firm foot for those who travel upon the path to enlightenment, and it is the great *dhāraṇī* of all unsurpassed Buddha-dharmas. If you are able to receive and uphold such a profound *prajñāpāramitā-dhāraṇī*, you will thereby retain all the Buddha-dharmas.”
Chapter 59: The Inexhaustible (Akṣaya-parivarta), Part One. At that time, the Venerable Subhūti had this thought to himself:
"The unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is most profound; likewise, this perfection of wisdom is also most profound!"
"I shall question the Buddha.
Having formed this thought, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
“Is this profound perfection of wisdom inexhaustible?
The Buddha said, “It is so;
this profound perfection of wisdom is truly inexhaustible, for it is like space, which cannot be exhausted.”
The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
how should a bodhisattva mahāsattva bring forth the perfection of wisdom?”
The Buddha told Subhūti:
"You should know that because form is inexhaustible, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should bring forth the perfection of wisdom;
because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are inexhaustible, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should bring forth the perfection of wisdom."
“Subhūti, you should know this!
Because the sense base of the eye is inexhaustible, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should draw forth the perfection of wisdom;
because the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are inexhaustible, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should draw forth the perfection of wisdom.”
"Subhūti, you should know this!
Because the sphere of form is inexhaustible, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should bring forth the perfection of wisdom;
because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are inexhaustible, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should bring forth the perfection of wisdom."
“Subhūti, you should know that because the eye-element is inexhaustible, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should bring forth the perfection of wisdom;

because the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are inexhaustible, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should bring forth the perfection of wisdom.”
"Subhūti, you should know that because the ear-element is inexhaustible, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should bring forth the perfection of wisdom;

because the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, ear-contact, and all feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition are inexhaustible, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should bring forth the perfection of wisdom."
“Subhūti, you should know that because the nose element is inexhaustible, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should bring forth the perfection of wisdom;

because the odor element, the nose-consciousness element, nose-contact, and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition are inexhaustible, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should bring forth the perfection of wisdom.”
“Subhūti, you should know that because the tongue-element is inexhaustible, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should bring forth the perfection of wisdom;

because the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and all feelings produced with tongue-contact as a condition are inexhaustible, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should bring forth the perfection of wisdom.”
“Subhūti, you should know this!
Because the body element (*kāyadhātu*) is inexhaustible, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should bring forth the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*);

because the tangible object element (*spraṣṭavyadhātu*), the body-consciousness element (*kāyavijñānadhātu*), as well as body-contact (*kāyasparśa*) and all feelings (*vedanā*) produced with body-contact as a condition are inexhaustible, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should bring forth the perfection of wisdom.”
“Subhūti, you should know that because the mind-element (*manodhātu*) is inexhaustible, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should bring forth the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*);

because the dharma-element (*dharmadhātu*), the mental-consciousness-element (*manovijñānadhātu*), as well as mental contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*) and the various feelings (*vedanā*) arising with mental contact as a condition are inexhaustible, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should bring forth the perfection of wisdom.”
“Subhūti, you should know that because the earth element is inexhaustible, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should practice the perfection of wisdom;
because the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are inexhaustible, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should practice the perfection of wisdom.”
“Subhūti, you should know this:
because ignorance is inexhaustible, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should bring forth the perfection of wisdom;

because volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are inexhaustible, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should bring forth the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti, you should know that because the perfection of generosity is inexhaustible, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should draw forth the perfection of wisdom; and because the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are inexhaustible, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should draw forth the perfection of wisdom.”
“Subhūti, you should know this!
Because internal emptiness is inexhaustible, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should bring forth the perfection of wisdom;
