If one does not increase the roots of goodness that have been planted, how can one fulfill the perfections?
If one does not fulfill the perfections, how can one attain the knowledge of all modes of knowledge?
“World-Honored One!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not contemplate the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, how do they increase the roots of goodness they have planted?
If they do not increase the roots of goodness they have planted, how do they fulfill the pāramitās?”
"If the perfections are not brought to fulfillment, how can one attain the knowledge of all modes?
"World-Honored One!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not contemplate all the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, how can the roots of goodness they have planted increase?"
If one does not increase the roots of virtue that have been planted, how can one fulfill the perfections?
If one does not fulfill the perfections, how can one attain the knowledge of all modes?
“World-Honored One!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not contemplate the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, how can the roots of goodness they have planted increase?”
If one does not increase the roots of virtue that have been planted, how can one fulfill the perfections?
If one does not fulfill the perfections, how can one attain the knowledge of all modes?
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not conceptualize form, nor does he conceptualize feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness— at that time, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to increase the roots of goodness he has planted.”
Because the roots of goodness they have planted increase, they are able to bring the *pāramitās* to perfection.
Because the *pāramitās* are brought to perfection, they are able to realize the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*).

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not contemplate the sense base of the eye, nor does he contemplate the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind, at that time the bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to increase the roots of goodness he has planted.”
Because the roots of goodness they have planted increase, they are able to bring the *pāramitās* to perfection.
Because the *pāramitās* are brought to perfection, they are able to realize the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*).

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not conceptualize the sphere of form, nor does he conceptualize the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena, at that time the bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to increase the roots of goodness he has planted.”
Because the roots of goodness they have planted increase, they are able to bring the pāramitās to fulfillment.
Because the pāramitās are brought to fulfillment, they are able to realize the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not contemplate the eye-element, nor does he contemplate the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-element, at that time the bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to increase the roots of goodness he has planted.”
Because the roots of goodness they have planted increase, they are able to bring the perfections (pāramitās) to fulfillment.
Because the perfections are brought to fulfillment, they are able to realize the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not conceptualize the realm of form, nor does he conceptualize the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena, at that time the bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to increase the roots of goodness he has planted.”
Because the roots of goodness they have planted increase, they are able to bring the pāramitās to fulfillment.
Because the pāramitās are brought to fulfillment, they are able to realize the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna).

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not conceptualize the sphere of eye-consciousness, nor does he conceptualize the spheres of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-consciousness, at that time the bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to increase the roots of goodness he has planted.”
Because the roots of virtue they have planted increase, they are able to bring the perfections (pāramitās) to fulfillment.
Because the perfections are brought to fulfillment, they are able to realize the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna).

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not contemplate eye-contact, nor does he contemplate ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact, at that time the bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to increase the roots of goodness he has planted.”
Because the roots of goodness they have planted increase, they are able to bring the perfections (pāramitās) to completion.
Because the perfections are brought to completion, they are able to realize the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not direct the mind toward the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition, nor does he direct the mind toward the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as condition—at that time, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to increase the roots of goodness he has planted.”
Because the roots of goodness they have planted increase, they are able to bring the pāramitās to fulfillment.
Because the pāramitās are brought to fulfillment, they are able to realize the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not contemplate the earth element, nor does he contemplate the elements of water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness—at that time, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to increase the roots of goodness he has planted.”
Because the roots of goodness they have planted increase, they are able to bring the pāramitās to fulfillment.
Because the pāramitās are brought to fulfillment, they are able to realize the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not conceptualize ignorance, nor does he conceptualize volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, or old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair—at that time, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to increase the roots of virtue he has planted.”
Because the roots of goodness they have planted increase, they are able to bring the pāramitās to fulfillment.
Because the pāramitās are brought to fulfillment, they are able to realize the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).

"Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not conceptualize the perfection of generosity, nor does he conceptualize the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom—at that time, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to increase the roots of virtue he has planted."
Because the roots of goodness they have planted increase, they are able to bring the pāramitās to fulfillment.
Because the pāramitās are brought to fulfillment, they are able to realize the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not contemplate inner emptiness, nor does he contemplate outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature—at that time, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to increase the roots of virtue he has planted.”
Because the roots of goodness they have planted increase, they are able to bring the pāramitās to fulfillment.
Because the pāramitās are brought to fulfillment, they are able to realize the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna).

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not contemplate suchness, nor does he contemplate the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, the non-erroneous nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, or the inconceivable realm—at that time, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to increase the roots of goodness he has planted.”
Because the roots of goodness they have planted increase, they are able to bring the pāramitās to fulfillment.
Because the pāramitās are brought to fulfillment, they are able to realize the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not contemplate the noble truth of suffering, nor does he contemplate the noble truths of origin, cessation, or the path, at that time the bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to increase the roots of goodness he has planted.”
Because the roots of goodness they have planted increase, they are able to bring the pāramitās to fulfillment.
Because the pāramitās are brought to fulfillment, they are able to realize the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not contemplate the four dhyānas, nor does he contemplate the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments, at that time the bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to increase the roots of goodness he has planted.”
Because the roots of goodness they have planted increase, they are able to bring the perfections (pāramitās) to completion.
Because the perfections are brought to completion, they are able to realize the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not contemplate the eight liberations, nor contemplate the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities, at that time the bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to increase the roots of goodness they have planted.”
Because the roots of goodness they have planted increase, they are able to bring the pāramitās to perfection.
Because the pāramitās are brought to perfection, they are able to realize the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not contemplate the four foundations of mindfulness, nor contemplate the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, or the eightfold noble path—at that time, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to increase the roots of goodness they have planted.”
Because the roots of goodness they have planted increase, they are able to bring the pāramitās to fulfillment.
Because the pāramitās are brought to fulfillment, they are able to realize the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not contemplate the gate of liberation of emptiness, nor contemplate the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, at that time the bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to increase the roots of goodness they have planted.”
Because the roots of virtue they have planted increase, they are able to bring the perfections (pāramitās) to completion.
Because the perfections are brought to completion, they are able to realize the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not contemplate the five eyes, nor does he contemplate the six supernormal powers, at that time the bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to increase the roots of goodness he has planted.”
Because the roots of goodness they have planted increase, they are able to bring the pāramitās to full completion.
Because the pāramitās are brought to full completion, they are able to realize the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not contemplate the ten powers of a buddha, nor contemplate the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, at that time the bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to increase the roots of goodness they have planted.”
Because the roots of goodness they have planted increase, they are able to bring the pāramitās to fulfillment.
Because the pāramitās are brought to fulfillment, they are able to realize the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not contemplate the quality of non-forgetfulness, nor does he contemplate the state of constant equanimity, at that time the bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to increase the roots of goodness he has planted.”
Because the roots of virtue they have planted increase, they are able to bring the perfections (pāramitās) to fulfillment.
Because the perfections are brought to fulfillment, they are able to realize the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not contemplate all-knowledge, nor contemplate the knowledge of the aspects of the path, nor the knowledge of all aspects, at that time the bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to increase the roots of goodness they have planted.”
Because the roots of goodness they have planted increase, they are able to bring the pāramitās to fulfillment.
Because the pāramitās are brought to fulfillment, they are able to realize the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not contemplate any of the doors of dhāraṇī, nor does he contemplate any of the doors of samādhi, at that time the bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to increase the roots of goodness he has planted.”
Because the roots of goodness they have planted increase, they are able to bring the pāramitās to fulfillment.
Because the pāramitās are brought to fulfillment, they are able to realize the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not contemplate the fruit of a stream-enterer, nor contemplate the fruits of a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat, at that time the bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to increase the roots of goodness they have planted.”
Because the roots of virtue they have planted increase, they are able to bring the pāramitās to fulfillment.
Because the pāramitās are brought to fulfillment, they are able to realize the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñājñāna).

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not contemplate the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, at that time the bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to increase the roots of goodness they have planted.”
Because the roots of goodness they have planted increase, they are able to bring the perfections (pāramitās) to fulfillment.
Because the perfections are brought to fulfillment, they are able to realize the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not conceptualize any of the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, at that time the bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to increase the roots of goodness they have planted.”
Because the roots of virtue they have planted increase, they are able to bring the perfections (pāramitās) to fulfillment.
Because the perfections are brought to fulfillment, they are able to realize the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not conceptualize the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, at that time the bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to increase the roots of goodness they have planted.”
Because the roots of goodness they have planted increase, they are able to bring the pāramitās to fulfillment.
Because the pāramitās are brought to fulfillment, they are able to realize the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
"Why is that? Subhūti!

It is because only when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas do not conceptualize form, nor conceptualize feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, are they able to fully cultivate the practices of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."

“Subhūti! Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas must not contemplate the sense base of the eye, nor contemplate the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind; only then can they fully cultivate the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”

“Subhūti! Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas must not conceptualize the sphere of form, nor conceptualize the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena; only then can they fully cultivate the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”

“Subhūti! Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas must not conceptualize the eye-element, nor must they conceptualize the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-elements; only then can they fully cultivate the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”

“Subhūti! Only when bodhisattva mahāsattvas do not conceptualize the realm of form, nor conceptualize the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena, are they able to fully cultivate the practices of bodhisattva mahāsattvas and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”

“Subhūti! Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas must not conceptualize the eye-consciousness element, nor should they conceptualize the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-consciousness elements; only then can they fully cultivate the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”

“Subhūti! Only when bodhisattva mahāsattvas do not contemplate eye-contact, nor do they contemplate ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact, are they able to fully cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”

“Subhūti! Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas must not contemplate the various sensations produced with eye-contact as a condition, nor must they contemplate the various sensations produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact as conditions; only then can they fully cultivate the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”

“Subhūti! Only when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do not contemplate the earth element, nor contemplate the elements of water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness, are they able to fully cultivate the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”

“Subhūti! Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas must not conceptualize ignorance, nor must they conceptualize volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, or old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair; only then can they fully cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”

“Subhūti! It is by not conceptualizing the perfection of generosity, and likewise by not conceptualizing the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, that bodhisattva mahāsattvas are able to fully cultivate the practices of bodhisattva mahāsattvas and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”

“Subhūti! It is by not conceptualizing internal emptiness, nor conceptualizing external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, that bodhisattva mahāsattvas are able to fully cultivate the practices of bodhisattva mahāsattvas and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”

“Subhūti! It is only when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do not contemplate suchness, nor contemplate the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-falsity, the immutability, the equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of empty space, and the inconceivable realm, that they are able to fully cultivate the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”

“Subhūti! It is by not contemplating the noble truth of suffering, nor contemplating the noble truths of origin, cessation, or the path, that bodhisattva mahāsattvas are able to fully cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”

“Subhūti! Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas must not contemplate the four dhyānas, nor contemplate the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments, before they can fully cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva and realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”

“Subhūti! It is by not contemplating the eight liberations, nor contemplating the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities, that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are able to fully cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva and realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”

“Subhūti! It is by not conceptualizing the four foundations of mindfulness, nor conceptualizing the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, or the eightfold noble path, that bodhisattva mahāsattvas are able to fully cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening.”

“Subhūti! It is by not contemplating the gate of liberation of emptiness, nor contemplating the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, that bodhisattva mahāsattvas are able to fully cultivate all the practices of bodhisattva mahāsattvas and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”

“Subhūti! It is by not conceptualizing the five eyes and also not conceptualizing the six supernormal powers that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are able to fully cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”

“Subhūti! It is by not conceptualizing the ten powers of a Buddha, nor conceptualizing the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are able to fully cultivate the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”

“Subhūti! It is by not conceptualizing the quality of non-forgetfulness (*asaṃpramoṣadharma*), nor by conceptualizing the state of constant equanimity (*upekṣā*), that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are able to fully cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva and realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”

“Subhūti! It is by not conceptualizing all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), nor conceptualizing the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), nor conceptualizing the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), that bodhisattva mahāsattvas are able to fully cultivate the practices of bodhisattva mahāsattvas and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”

“Subhūti! It is by not conceptualizing any of the dhāraṇī-doors, nor by conceptualizing any of the samādhi-doors, that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are able to fully cultivate the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”

“Subhūti! Only when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do not conceptualize the fruit of a stream-enterer, nor do they conceptualize the fruits of a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat, can they fully cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”

“Subhūti! It is only when bodhisattva mahāsattvas do not contemplate the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha that they are able to fully cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”

“Subhūti! Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas must not conceptualize any bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices; only then can they fully cultivate all bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”

“Subhūti! It is by not conceptualizing the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas that bodhisattva mahāsattvas are able to fully cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”
The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha,
saying: “World-Honored One,

for what reason must bodhisattva-mahāsattvas not contemplate form, nor contemplate feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, in order to be able to fully cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva and realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment?”
“World-Honored One!

For what reason must bodhisattva-mahāsattvas not contemplate the sense base of the eye, nor contemplate the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind, yet still be able to fully cultivate the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?”
“World-Honored One!

For what reason must bodhisattva-mahāsattvas not contemplate the sphere of form, nor contemplate the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena, in order to be able to fully cultivate the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?”
“World-Honored One!

For what reason must bodhisattva-mahāsattvas not contemplate the eye-element, nor contemplate the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-element, yet still be able to fully cultivate the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?”
“World-Honored One!

For what reason must bodhisattva-mahāsattvas not conceptualize the realm of form, nor conceptualize the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena, in order to be able to fully cultivate the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment?”
“World-Honored One!

For what reason must bodhisattva-mahāsattvas not contemplate the eye-consciousness element, nor contemplate the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-consciousness elements, yet still be able to fully cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?”
“World-Honored One!

For what reason must bodhisattva-mahāsattvas not contemplate eye-contact, nor contemplate ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact, yet still be able to fully cultivate the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?”

“Bhagavān, for what reason must bodhisattva-mahāsattvas not contemplate the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition, nor contemplate the various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact as condition, yet still be able to fully cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?”
“World-Honored One!

For what reason must bodhisattva-mahāsattvas not contemplate the earth element, nor contemplate the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements, yet still be able to fully cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?”
“World-Honored One!

For what reason must bodhisattva-mahāsattvas not contemplate ignorance, nor contemplate volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, or old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, yet still be able to fully cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva and realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment?”

“Bhagavān, for what reason can bodhisattva-mahāsattvas fulfill the practices of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment without conceptualizing the perfection of generosity, nor conceptualizing the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom?”

“Blessed One, for what reason must bodhisattva mahāsattvas not contemplate inner emptiness, nor contemplate outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, yet still be able to fully cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?”
“World-Honored One!

For what reason must Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas not contemplate *tathatā* (suchness), nor contemplate the *dharmadhātu* (dharma-realm), the *dharmatā* (dharma-nature), the non-falsity, the unchanging nature, equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixedness of dharma, the stability of dharma, the limit of reality, the realm of empty space, and the inconceivable realm, yet still be able to fully cultivate the practices of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?”
“World-Honored One!

For what reason can bodhisattva-mahāsattvas fulfill the practices of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment without contemplating the noble truth of suffering, nor contemplating the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path?”
“World-Honored One!

For what reason can bodhisattva-mahāsattvas fulfill the practices of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment without conceptualizing the four dhyānas, nor conceptualizing the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments?”
“World-Honored One!

For what reason must bodhisattva-mahāsattvas not contemplate the eight liberations, nor contemplate the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities, yet still be able to fully cultivate the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?”
“World-Honored One!

For what reason can bodhisattva-mahāsattvas fulfill the practices of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva and realize unexcelled, perfect enlightenment only by not contemplating the four foundations of mindfulness, nor contemplating the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, or the eightfold noble path?”
“World-Honored One!

For what reason can bodhisattva-mahāsattvas fulfill the practices of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, without even contemplating the gate of liberation of emptiness, nor contemplating the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness?”
“World-Honored One!
