The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva diligently practices and studies the profound perfection of wisdom, because they have no attachment to any phenomena, they should not dwell upon form, nor should they dwell upon feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.”
One should not dwell on the sense-base of the eye, nor should one dwell on the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind;
one should not dwell on the sense-base of forms, nor should one dwell on the sense-bases of sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, or mental phenomena;
one should not dwell on the eye-element, nor should one dwell on the elements of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind.
One should not dwell in the realm of forms, nor should one dwell in the realms of sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, or mental phenomena;
one should not dwell in the realm of eye-consciousness, nor should one dwell in the realms of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-consciousness;
one should not dwell in eye-contact, nor should one dwell in ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact.

One should not dwell on the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, nor should one dwell on the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as conditions;
one should not dwell on the earth element, nor should one dwell on the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements;

one should not dwell on ignorance, nor should one dwell on volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, or old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.
One should not dwell on the perfection of generosity, nor should one dwell on the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom;

one should not dwell on internal emptiness, nor should one dwell on external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

One should not dwell in *tathatā* (suchness), nor should one dwell in the *dharmadhātu* (dharma-realm), the *dharmatā* (dharma-nature), the non-false nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space, or the inconceivable realm;
one should not dwell in the noble truth of suffering, nor should one dwell in the noble truths of origination, cessation, or the path;
one should not dwell in the four meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*), nor should one dwell in the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments.
One should not dwell in the eight liberations, nor should one dwell in the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities;

one should not dwell in the four foundations of mindfulness, nor should one dwell in the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, or the eightfold noble path;
one should not dwell in the gate of liberation of emptiness, nor should one dwell in the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.
One should not dwell upon the five eyes, nor should one dwell upon the six supernormal powers;

one should not dwell upon the ten powers of a Buddha, nor should one dwell upon the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
one should not dwell upon the quality of non-forgetfulness, nor should one dwell upon the nature of constant equanimity.
One should not dwell in all-knowledge, nor should one dwell in the knowledge of the aspects of the path or the knowledge of all aspects;
one should not dwell in any dhāraṇī-doors, nor should one dwell in any samādhi-doors;
one should not dwell in the fruit of stream-entry, nor should one dwell in the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, or arhatship.
One should not dwell upon the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha;
one should not dwell upon any of the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva;
one should not dwell upon the unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas.
Why is this? Subhūti!
It is because this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive any dharma within which he could give rise to attachment or abide.
"Subhūti! In this way, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom by means of non-attachment and non-abiding."
"Furthermore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva forms this thought:
'If one can practice the profound perfection of wisdom in this way— without attachment and without dwelling anywhere— this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.'"
If one can thus practice the profound *prajñāpāramitā* without attachment and without dwelling anywhere, this is the practice of *prajñāpāramitā*.
"I should practice the profound perfection of wisdom in this way; I should cultivate the profound perfection of wisdom in this way. "Subhūti!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva grasps signs and clings to them through such recollections, they distance themselves from the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
If they distance themselves from the perfection of wisdom, they likewise distance themselves from the perfections of meditative concentration,
diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity, as well as from internal emptiness and external emptiness.

...emptiness of the internal and external (*adhyātma-bahirdhā-śūnyatā*), emptiness of emptiness (*śūnyatā-śūnyatā*), great emptiness (*mahā-śūnyatā*), emptiness of the ultimate (*paramārtha-śūnyatā*), emptiness of the conditioned (*saṃskṛta-śūnyatā*),

emptiness of the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta-śūnyatā*), absolute emptiness (*atyanta-śūnyatā*), emptiness of the beginningless and endless (*anavarāgra-śūnyatā*), emptiness of dispersion (*anavakāra-śūnyatā*), emptiness of non-alteration (*anavakāra-śūnyatā*),

emptiness of intrinsic nature (*prakṛti-śūnyatā*), emptiness of self-characteristics (*svalakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*), emptiness of common characteristics (*sāmānya-lakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*), emptiness of all phenomena (*sarvadharma-śūnyatā*), and emptiness of the unapprehendable (*anupalambha-śūnyatā*).
...emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, and emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence;
it is also far removed from suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state of being free from birth,
the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of empty space, and the inconceivable.
The sphere of deliberation is likewise remote from the noble truths of suffering,
its origin, its cessation, and the path; it is likewise remote from the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments,
the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, the ten totalities, and the four foundations of mindfulness.
...the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path;
it is also remote from the gate of liberation of emptiness, the signless, and the wishless;
it is also remote from the five eyes and the six supernormal powers; it is also remote from the ten powers of a Buddha and the four [assurances].
The fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
likewise, they are far removed from the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant dwelling in equanimity;
they are also far removed from all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects; they are also far removed.
All doors of dhāraṇī and all doors of samādhi are likewise far removed from all practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas,
and they are likewise far removed from the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas.
Why is this? Subhūti!
The profound perfection of wisdom has no attachment toward any phenomena; the profound perfection of wisdom does not possess the nature of attachment.
Why is that? Subhūti!
The profound perfection of wisdom has no intrinsic nature whatsoever by which it could have any attachment toward phenomena.
Therefore, Subhūti, when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they have no attachment to any phenomena nor to the profound perfection of wisdom itself.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, gives rise to such a thought as:
'This is the perfection of wisdom; I am practicing the perfection of wisdom,' this is to course in the true reality of all phenomena."
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a thought, they retreat from the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
If they retreat from the perfection of wisdom, then they retreat from meditative concentration (dhyāna), diligence (vīrya), patience (kṣānti),”
The perfections of pure ethical discipline and generosity also regress from internal emptiness,
external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena,
the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature.
The emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable,
the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence;
likewise, they also regress from true suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, immutability, equality, and the state free from birth.

...the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the persistence of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*);
they also regress from the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path; they also regress from the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments;
and they also regress from the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, and the nine successive [attainments].

Furthermore, they regress from the four concentrations and the ten totalities; they also regress from the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path;
they also regress from the gate of liberation of emptiness, the signless, and the wishless gates of liberation; and they also regress from the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.

Furthermore, they regress from the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;

they also regress from the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant abiding in equanimity; and they also regress from all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the [knowledge of] all aspects.
They will fall away from the wisdom of all characteristics, and they will also fall away from all dharani-doors and all samadhi-doors;
they will also fall away from all the practices of Bodhisattvas Mahasattvas, and they will also fall away from the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas.
Why is this? Subhūti!
This profound perfection of wisdom is the root of all pure dharmas; if one regresses from the perfection of wisdom, then one has lost all pure dharmas.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle Three Hundred and Fifty-three. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: The Chapter on the Many Questions on Non-duality, Number Sixty-one, Section Four. "Furthermore, Subhūti!..."
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva forms this thought:

"The profound perfection of wisdom is able to universally encompass the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; it also universally encompasses..."
Emptiness of the internal, emptiness of the external, emptiness of both internal and external, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, emptiness of the ultimate truth,
emptiness of the conditioned, emptiness of the unconditioned, absolute emptiness, emptiness of the limitless, emptiness of dispersion, emptiness of non-alteration,
emptiness of essential nature, emptiness of self-characteristics, emptiness of common characteristics, and emptiness of all phenomena.
...the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence;
these also universally encompass suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-falsity,
the non-alteration, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, and the limit of reality.
The realm of empty space and the inconceivable realm also universally encompass the Noble Truth of Suffering, as well as the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path;
they also universally encompass the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments;
and they also universally encompass the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten...

The spheres of totality also universally encompass the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path;
they also universally encompass the gateways to liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; and they also universally encompass the five eyes.

The six supernormal powers also universally encompass the Buddha’s ten powers, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
they also universally encompass the quality of never forgetting and the state of constant abiding in equanimity; they also universally encompass the one...

The knowledge of all things, the knowledge of the aspects of the path, and the knowledge of all aspects likewise universally encompass all dharani-doors and all samadhi-doors; they also universally encompass all the practices of bodhisattva-mahasattvas,
and they also universally encompass the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas.
"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva forms such a thought, they will fall away from the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
If they fall away from the perfection of wisdom, they will be unable to fully embrace generosity and pure ethical discipline."
...the perfections of patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom likewise cannot encompass internal emptiness,
external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena,
the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, and the emptiness of dispersion.
Furthermore, they cannot apprehend the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self-characteristic,
the emptiness of common characteristic, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature,
or the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence; nor can they apprehend suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, or the non-erroneous nature.

...neither can it encompass the noble truth of suffering, nor its origin, cessation, or the path; nor can it encompass the four dhyānas, the four [immeasurables], the four formless attainments, the five supernormal powers, the six superknowledges, the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path; nor can it encompass the emptiness of the internal, the emptiness of the external, the emptiness of both internal and external, the emptiness of emptiness, the great emptiness, the ultimate emptiness, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, the absolute emptiness, the emptiness of that which has neither beginning nor end, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of essential nature, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of self-characteristic, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of existence, the emptiness of non-attainment, the emptiness of nature, the emptiness of characteristics, the emptiness of non-characteristics, the emptiness of unarisen phenomena, the emptiness of unceasing phenomena, the emptiness of the unchanging, the emptiness of equality, the emptiness of the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharma-sthititā*), the reality-limit (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space, or the inconceivable realm;
nor can it encompass the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path, nor can it encompass the four dhyānas, the four [immeasurables]..."
The [four] immeasurables and the four formless attainments likewise cannot encompass the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery,
the nine successive meditative concentrations, or the ten totalities; nor can they encompass the four foundations of mindfulness,
the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path.
Furthermore, it cannot encompass the gate of liberation of emptiness, nor the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness;
it cannot encompass the five eyes or the six supernormal powers;
nor can it encompass the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, or great sympathetic joy.
...the great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; nor can they encompass the quality of non-forgetfulness or the state of constant abiding in equanimity;

nor can they encompass all-knowledge (*sarvajñā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), or the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*); nor can they encompass any of the doors of dhāraṇī or any of the samādhis.
The stage-gate likewise cannot encompass all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas,
nor can it encompass the unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas.
Why is this? Subhūti!
It is not apart from the perfection of wisdom that one can fully embrace the sublime and wholesome dharmas, nor realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva forms this thought:
'By abiding in the perfection of wisdom, one will certainly receive the prediction of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.'"
"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva should form such a thought, they will fall away from the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
If they fall away from the perfection of wisdom, they shall not receive the prediction of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
Why is this? Subhūti!
It is not apart from the perfection of wisdom that one can receive the prediction of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva forms this thought:
'Abiding in the perfection of wisdom, one then universally extends and deploys generosity, ethical discipline, [patience, diligence, concentration, and wisdom]...'"
The perfections of patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom likewise abide pervasively in internal emptiness,
external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness,
conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, and the emptiness of dispersion.
The emptiness of change, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics,
the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of self-nature,
and the emptiness of the self-nature of non-existence; these also universally abide in suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, and immutability.
They are also universally established in otherness, equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixed order of phenomena (*dharmatā*),

the stability of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*); they are also universally induced in the noble truths of suffering,
origin, cessation, and the path, as well as in the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.
Concentration also universally induces the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities;

it also universally induces the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eight branches of the noble path; it also universally induces emptiness.
The gates of liberation—the signless and the wishless—likewise fully induce the five eyes and the six supernormal powers;
they also fully induce the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
and they also fully induce the quality of non-forgetfulness and constant abiding.
The nature of relinquishment also universally induces all doors of dhāraṇī and all doors of samādhi;
it also universally induces all-knowledge, the knowledge of the aspects of the path, and the knowledge of all aspects;
and it also universally induces great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity.
"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva forms such a thought, they then fall away from the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
If they fall away from the perfection of wisdom, they will be unable to initiate generosity (dāna) and pure ethical discipline (śīla)."
...the perfections of patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom;
nor can they abide in internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness,
conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, or the emptiness of dispersion.
...the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self-characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics,
the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature,
and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence; nor can they abide in suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, or the non-falsity of reality.

...the unchanging nature, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*);
nor can they abide in the noble truth of suffering, its origin, its cessation, or the path; nor can they bring forth the four dhyānas or the four [immeasurables]...
The [four] immeasurables and the four formless attainments likewise cannot induce the eight liberations,
the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities; nor can they induce the four foundations of mindfulness,
the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the noble eightfold path.
Furthermore, it cannot bring forth the gate of liberation of emptiness, nor the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness;
it cannot bring forth the five eyes or the six supernormal powers;
nor can it bring forth the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha. Furthermore—
They cannot bring forth the quality of non-forgetfulness or the state of constant equanimity;
nor can they bring forth any of the doors of dhāraṇī or any of the doors of samādhi;
nor can they bring forth omniscience, the knowledge of the paths, or the knowledge of all aspects; nor can they bring forth great loving-kindness or great...
Compassion, great sympathetic joy,
and great equanimity.
Why is this so, Subhūti?
It is not apart from the perfection of wisdom that one can bring forth and abide in wholesome dharmas. "Furthermore, Subhūti,
if a bodhisattva mahāsattva should form such a thought:
"The Buddha, knowing that all phenomena have the characteristic of being without grasping, personally realized unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Having attained enlightenment, he proclaimed and revealed the true nature of all phenomena for the sake of all sentient beings."
“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva should form such a thought, they will thereby fall away from the profound perfection of wisdom. Why is that?
"Subhūti! The Tathāgata has no knowledge, no realization, no speech, and no demonstration regarding phenomena. Why is this so?"
The true nature of all phenomena is unknowable and cannot be designated; how, then, could there be one who perceives and teaches all phenomena?
If it were said that there truly exists one who perceives and teaches all phenomena, such a thing is impossible.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the perfection of wisdom so as to remain far removed from such various faults?”
The Buddha said,
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom forms such a thought:”

"All phenomena are non-existent and cannot be grasped; if phenomena are non-existent and cannot be grasped, then there is no one who can realize them through perfect awakening, nor is there anyone who can proclaim or reveal them."
"If one practices in this manner, one is practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) and remains free from all faults.
If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva becomes attached to non-existent and ungraspable phenomena, then they depart from the perfection of wisdom."
Why is this? Subhūti!

The profound *prajñāpāramitā* has no attachment to and no grasping of any phenomena (*dharma*). If one were to have attachment to or grasp at any phenomena, then one would be far removed from the *prajñāpāramitā*.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
is the perfection of wisdom distant from the perfection of wisdom, or is it not distant?”

Are the perfections of meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity distant from, or not distant from, the perfections of meditative concentration through to generosity?
“World-Honored One!
Is internal emptiness distant from internal emptiness, or is it not distant?

Are external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, emptiness of dispersion, emptiness of non-alteration, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence distant from external emptiness, up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, or are they not distant?”
“Bhagavān, is *tathatā* distant from *tathatā*, or is it not distant? Are the *dharmadhātu*,

*dharmatā*, *avitathatā*, *ananyathatā*, *samatā*, *anupapattitā*, *dharmasthititā*, *dharmaniyāmatā*, *bhūtakoṭi*, *ākāśadhātu*, and *acintyadhātu* distant from the *dharmadhātu* up to the *acintyadhātu*, or are they not distant?”
“World-Honored One!
Is the noble truth of suffering distant from the noble truth of suffering, or is it not distant?
Are the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path distant from the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path, or are they not distant?”
“World-Honored One!
Are the four dhyānas, in relation to the four dhyānas, distant or not distant?
Are the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, in relation to the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, distant or not distant?”
“World-Honored One!
Are the eight liberations distant from the eight liberations, or are they not distant?

Are the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities distant from the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities, or are they not distant?”
“World-Honored One!
Are the four foundations of mindfulness distant from the four foundations of mindfulness, or are they not distant?

Are the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path distant from the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path, or are they not distant?”
“World-Honored One!
Is the gate of liberation of emptiness distant from the gate of liberation of emptiness, or is it not distant?
Are the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness distant from the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, or are they not distant?”
“World-Honored One!
Are the five eyes distant from the five eyes, or are they not distant?
Are the six supernormal powers distant from the six supernormal powers, or are they not distant?”
“World-Honored One!
Are the ten powers of a Buddha distinct from the ten powers of a Buddha?

Are the four fearlessnesses, the four unhindered understandings, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha distinct from the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha? Are they separate, or are they not separate?”
“World-Honored One!
Is the quality of non-forgetfulness distant from the quality of non-forgetfulness, or is it not distant?
Is the state of constant equanimity distant from the state of constant equanimity, or is it not distant?”
“World-Honored One!
Are all dharani-doors distant from all dharani-doors, or are they not distant?
Are all samadhi-doors distant from all samadhi-doors, or are they not distant?”
“Bhagavān, is all-knowledge (sarvajñatā) remote from all-knowledge, or is it not remote?
Is the knowledge of the paths (mārgajñatā) and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā) remote from the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects, or are they not remote?”

“Bhagavān! If the perfection of wisdom is either distant from or not distant from the perfection of wisdom, how can a bodhisattva mahāsattva, free from attachment, bring forth the perfection of wisdom?”

“Bhagavān! If the perfection of meditative concentration, the perfection of diligence, the perfection of patience, the perfection of ethical discipline, and the perfection of generosity are either separate from or not separate from the perfections of meditative concentration through to generosity, how can a bodhisattva mahāsattva, without attachment, bring forth the perfections of meditative concentration through to generosity?”
“World-Honored One!
If internal emptiness is [identical to] internal emptiness—whether it be distant from it or not distant from it—how can a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwell without attachment in internal emptiness?”
“World-Honored One!

If external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—whether these, from external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, are distant or not distant, how can a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwell without attachment in external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence?”
“World-Honored One!
If true thusness is either distant from or not distant from true thusness, how can a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwell without attachment in true thusness?”
“World-Honored One!

If the dharma-realm, the nature of dharmas, non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state of being free from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of empty space, and the inconceivable realm—regarding these from the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm—are they distant or not distant? How can a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwell without attachment in the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm?”
“World-Honored One!
If the noble truth of suffering is either distant from or not distant from the noble truth of suffering, how can a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwell without attachment in the noble truth of suffering?”
“World-Honored One!

If the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path—whether they are distant from or not distant from the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path—how can a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwell without attachment within these noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path?”
“World-Honored One!
If the four dhyānas, in relation to the four dhyānas, are either detached or not detached, how is it that a bodhisattva mahāsattva can bring forth the four dhyānas without attachment?”
“World-Honored One!

If the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are either distant from or not distant from the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, how can a bodhisattva mahāsattva, being without attachment, bring forth the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions?”
“World-Honored One!
If the eight liberations are either distant from or not distant from the eight liberations, how can a bodhisattva mahāsattva, being without attachment, bring forth the eight liberations?”
“World-Honored One!

If the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are, within the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities, either distanced or not distanced, how is it that a bodhisattva mahāsattva can, without attachment, bring forth the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities?”
“World-Honored One!

If the four foundations of mindfulness are either distant from or not distant from the four foundations of mindfulness, how can a bodhisattva mahāsattva, free from attachment, bring forth the four foundations of mindfulness?”
“World-Honored One!

If the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eight branches of the noble path are—whether separated from or not separated from—the four right efforts up to the eight branches of the noble path, how can a bodhisattva mahāsattva, without attachment, bring forth the four right efforts up to the eight branches of the noble path?”
“World-Honored One!

If the gate of liberation of emptiness is either distant from or not distant from the gate of liberation of emptiness, how is it that a bodhisattva mahāsattva can, without attachment, bring forth the gate of liberation of emptiness?”
“World-Honored One!

If the gate of liberation of signlessness and the gate of liberation of wishlessness are, with respect to the gate of liberation of signlessness and the gate of liberation of wishlessness, either distant or not distant, how is it that a bodhisattva mahāsattva can, without attachment, bring forth the gate of liberation of signlessness and the gate of liberation of wishlessness?”
“World-Honored One!
If the five eyes are, with respect to the five eyes, either distant or not distant, how can a bodhisattva mahāsattva, free from attachment, bring forth the five eyes?”
“World-Honored One!
If the six supernormal powers are either distant from or not distant from the six supernormal powers, how can a bodhisattva mahāsattva, free from attachment, bring forth the six supernormal powers?”
“World-Honored One!
If the ten powers of a Buddha are either distant from or not distant from the ten powers of a Buddha, how can a bodhisattva mahāsattva, free from attachment, bring forth the ten powers of a Buddha?”
“World-Honored One!

If the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are—whether they are distant from or not distant from—the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, how can a bodhisattva mahāsattva, being without attachment, bring forth the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?”
“World-Honored One!

If there is no dharma of non-forgetfulness within the dharma of non-forgetfulness—whether it be characterized by detachment or non-detachment—how can a bodhisattva mahāsattva, being without attachment, bring forth the dharma of non-forgetfulness?”
“World-Honored One!

If the state of constant abiding in equanimity is either distant from or not distant from the state of constant abiding in equanimity, how can a bodhisattva mahāsattva, free from attachment, bring forth this state of constant abiding in equanimity?”
“World-Honored One!

If all dharani-doors are, with respect to all dharani-doors, either separated from them or not separated from them, how is it that a bodhisattva mahasattva can, without attachment, bring forth all dharani-doors?”
“World-Honored One!
If all samādhi-gates are, with respect to all samādhi-gates, either separated or not separated, how is it that a bodhisattva mahāsattva can, without attachment, bring forth all samādhi-gates?”
“World-Honored One!
If omniscience is either distant from or not distant from omniscience, how can a bodhisattva mahāsattva, being without attachment, bring forth omniscience?”

“Blessed One! If the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are, with respect to the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, either separated or not separated, how can a bodhisattva mahāsattva, without attachment, bring forth the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects?”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

The perfection of wisdom is neither distant from nor not distant from the perfection of wisdom; therefore, a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to bring forth the perfection of wisdom without attachment.”

“Subhūti! The perfections of meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity are neither distant from nor not distant from the perfections of meditative concentration through to generosity; therefore, bodhisattva mahāsattvas are able to bring forth the perfections of meditative concentration through to generosity without attachment.”
"Subhūti! Inner emptiness is neither distant from inner emptiness nor not distant from it; therefore, a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to dwell without attachment in inner emptiness."

“Subhūti! External emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self-characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—these, from external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, are neither separated nor not separated [from one another]. Therefore, a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to dwell without attachment in external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.”
“Subhūti! True suchness is neither separate from true suchness nor not separate from it; therefore, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are able to dwell in true suchness without attachment.”

“Subhūti! The dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm—these, from the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, are neither distant nor not distant from the dharma-realm and so forth, up to the inconceivable realm. Therefore, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to dwell without attachment in the dharma-realm and so forth, up to the inconceivable realm.”

“Subhūti! The noble truth of suffering is neither distant from nor not distant from the noble truth of suffering; therefore, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to dwell without attachment in the noble truth of suffering.”

“Subhūti! The noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are neither distant from nor not distant from the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path; therefore, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are able to abide without attachment in the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path.”
“Subhūti! The four dhyānas are neither distant from nor not distant from the four dhyānas; therefore, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are able to bring forth the four dhyānas without attachment.”

"Subhūti! The four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are neither distant from nor not distant from the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions; therefore, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are able to bring forth the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions without attachment."

“Subhūti! The eight liberations are neither distant from nor not distant from the eight liberations; therefore, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are able to bring forth the eight liberations without attachment.”

“Subhūti! The eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities—within these eight bases of mastery, nine successive attainments, and ten totalities, there is neither separation nor non-separation. Therefore, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are able to bring forth the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities without attachment.”

“Subhūti! The four foundations of mindfulness are neither distant from nor not distant from the four foundations of mindfulness; therefore, a bodhisattva mahāsattva can bring forth the four foundations of mindfulness without attachment.”

“Subhūti! The four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eight branches of the noble path are neither distant from nor not distant from the four right efforts up to the eight branches of the noble path. Therefore, a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to bring forth the four right efforts up to the eight branches of the noble path without attachment.”

“Subhūti! The liberation door of emptiness is neither distant from nor not distant from the liberation door of emptiness; therefore, the bodhisattva mahāsattva can bring forth the liberation door of emptiness without attachment.”

“Subhūti! The gate of liberation of signlessness and the gate of liberation of wishlessness are neither distant from nor not distant from the gate of liberation of signlessness and the gate of liberation of wishlessness; therefore, bodhisattva mahāsattvas are able to bring forth the gate of liberation of signlessness and the gate of liberation of wishlessness without attachment.”
“Subhūti! The five eyes are neither distant from nor not distant from the five eyes; therefore, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to bring forth the five eyes without attachment.”

"Subhūti! The six supernormal powers are neither separate from nor not separate from the six supernormal powers; therefore, a bodhisattva mahāsattva can bring forth the six supernormal powers without attachment."

“Subhūti! The ten powers of a Buddha, in relation to the ten powers of a Buddha, are neither separated nor not separated; therefore, a bodhisattva mahāsattva can bring forth the ten powers of a Buddha without attachment.”

“Subhūti! The four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha—these, from the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, are neither separated nor not separated [from suchness]. Therefore, a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to bring forth the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha without attachment.”

“Subhūti! The quality of non-forgetfulness is neither distant from nor not distant from the quality of non-forgetfulness; therefore, a bodhisattva mahāsattva can bring forth the quality of non-forgetfulness without attachment.”

“Subhūti! The state of constant abiding in equanimity is neither distant from nor not distant from the state of constant abiding in equanimity; therefore, a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to bring forth the state of constant abiding in equanimity without attachment.”
“Subhūti! All dhāraṇī-doors are neither distant from nor not distant from all dhāraṇī-doors; therefore, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are able to bring forth all dhāraṇī-doors without attachment.”
“Subhūti! All samādhi-gates are neither distant from nor not distant from all samādhi-gates; therefore, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are able to bring forth all samādhi-gates without attachment.”
“Subhūti! All-knowledge is neither distant from all-knowledge nor not distant from it; therefore, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to bring forth all-knowledge without attachment.”

"Subhūti! Path-knowledge and all-aspect knowledge are neither distant from path-knowledge and all-aspect knowledge, nor are they not distant. Therefore, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are able to bring forth path-knowledge and all-aspect knowledge without attachment."
"Why is that? Subhūti!
It is not by means of intrinsic nature itself, nor apart from intrinsic nature, that one can abide in or bring forth intrinsic nature."

"Furthermore, Subhūti, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not cling to form, thinking, 'This is form,' or 'This form belongs to that. Nor do they cling to feeling,

perception, mental formations, or consciousness, thinking, 'This is feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness,' or 'This feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness belongs to that.'"

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not cling to the sense base of the eye, thinking, ‘This is the sense base of the eye,’ or ‘This sense base of the eye belongs to that.

Nor do they cling to the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind, thinking, ‘These are the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind,’ or ‘These sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind belong to that.’”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not cling to the sphere of form, thinking, ‘This is the sphere of form,’ or ‘This sphere of form belongs to that.

Nor do they cling to the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena, thinking, ‘These are the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena,’ or ‘These spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena belong to that.’”
“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not cling to the eye-element, thinking, ‘This is the eye-element,’ or ‘This eye-element belongs to that.

Nor do they cling to the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-element, thinking, ‘This is the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-element,’ or ‘This ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-element belongs to that.’”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not cling to the realm of form, thinking, ‘This is the realm of form,’ or ‘The realm of form belongs to that.

Nor do they cling to the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena, thinking, ‘This is the realm of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena,’ or ‘These realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena belong to that.’”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not cling to the eye-consciousness element, thinking, ‘This is the eye-consciousness element,’ or ‘This eye-consciousness element belongs to that.

Nor do they cling to the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-consciousness elements, thinking, ‘This is the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-consciousness element,’ or ‘This ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-consciousness element belongs to that.’”
“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not cling to eye-contact, thinking, ‘This is eye-contact,’ or ‘This eye-contact belongs to that.
Nor do they cling to ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact, thinking, ‘This is ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact,’ or ‘This ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact belongs to that.’”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not cling to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, thinking, ‘This is the feeling produced with eye-contact as a condition; this feeling produced with eye-contact as a condition belongs to that.

Nor do they cling to the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as conditions, thinking, ‘This is the feeling produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as a condition; this feeling produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as a condition belongs to that.’”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not cling to the earth element, thinking, ‘This is the earth element,’ or ‘This earth element belongs to that.

Nor do they cling to the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements, thinking, ‘This is the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness element,’ or ‘This water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness element belongs to that.’”
“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not cling to ignorance, thinking, ‘This is ignorance,’ or ‘This ignorance belongs to that.

Nor do they cling to volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, or old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair, thinking, ‘These are volitional formations’ up to ‘these are old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair,’ or ‘These volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair belong to that.’”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not cling to the perfection of giving, thinking, ‘This is the perfection of giving,’ or ‘This perfection of giving belongs to that.

Nor do they cling to the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom, thinking, ‘This is ethical discipline up to wisdom,’ or ‘This ethical discipline up to wisdom belongs to that.’”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not cling to internal emptiness, thinking, ‘This is internal emptiness,’ or ‘This internal emptiness belongs to that.

Nor do they cling to external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersal emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, thinking, ‘This is external emptiness’ up to ‘this is the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature,’ or ‘this external emptiness up to this emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature belongs to that.’”
“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not cling to suchness, thinking, ‘This is suchness,’ or ‘This suchness belongs to that.

Nor do they cling to the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), or the inconceivable realm, thinking, ‘This is the realm of phenomena... up to the inconceivable realm,’ or ‘This realm of phenomena... up to the inconceivable realm belongs to that.’”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not cling to the noble truth of suffering, thinking, ‘This is the noble truth of suffering,’ or ‘This noble truth of suffering belongs to that.

Nor do they cling to the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, thinking, ‘This is the noble truth of origin, cessation, and the path,’ or ‘These noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path belong to that.’”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not cling to the four dhyānas, thinking, ‘These are the four dhyānas,’ or ‘These four dhyānas belong to that.

Nor do they cling to the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments, thinking, ‘These are the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments,’ or ‘These four immeasurables and four formless attainments belong to that.’”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not cling to the eight liberations, thinking, ‘These are the eight liberations,’ or ‘These eight liberations belong to that.

Nor do they cling to the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities, thinking, ‘These are the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities,’ or ‘These eight bases of mastery, nine successive attainments, or ten totalities belong to that.’”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not cling to the four applications of mindfulness, thinking, ‘These are the four applications of mindfulness,’ or ‘These four applications of mindfulness belong to that.

Nor do they cling to the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path, thinking, ‘These are the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path,’ or ‘These four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path belong to that.’”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not cling to the gate of liberation that is emptiness, thinking, ‘This is the gate of liberation that is emptiness,’ or ‘This gate of liberation that is emptiness belongs to that.

Nor do they cling to the gates of liberation that are signlessness and wishlessness, thinking, ‘These are the gates of liberation that are signlessness and wishlessness,’ or ‘These gates of liberation that are signlessness and wishlessness belong to that.’”
“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not cling to the five eyes, thinking, ‘These are the five eyes,’ or ‘These five eyes belong to that.
Nor do they cling to the six supernormal powers, thinking, ‘These are the six supernormal powers,’ or ‘These six supernormal powers belong to that.’”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not cling to the ten powers of a buddha, thinking, ‘These are the ten powers of a buddha,’ or ‘These ten powers of a buddha belong to that [person].

Nor do they cling to the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, thinking, ‘These are the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha,’ or ‘These four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha belong to that [person].”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not cling to the quality of non-forgetfulness, thinking, ‘This is the quality of non-forgetfulness,’ or ‘This quality of non-forgetfulness belongs to that person.
Nor do they cling to the state of constant equanimity, thinking, ‘This is the state of constant equanimity,’ or ‘This state of constant equanimity belongs to that person.’”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not cling to all-knowledge (sarvajñatā), thinking, ‘This is all-knowledge,’ or ‘This all-knowledge belongs to that person.

Nor do they cling to the knowledge of the paths (mārgajñatā) or the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā), thinking, ‘This is the knowledge of the paths,’ or ‘This is the knowledge of all aspects,’ or ‘This knowledge of the paths and this knowledge of all aspects belong to that person.’”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not cling to any of the dharanī-doors, thinking, ‘This is all the dharanī-doors,’ or ‘These all the dharanī-doors belong to that.
Nor do they cling to any of the samādhi-doors, thinking, ‘This is all the samādhi-doors,’ or ‘These all the samādhi-doors belong to that.’”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not cling to the fruit of stream-entry, thinking, ‘This is the fruit of stream-entry,’ or ‘This fruit of stream-entry belongs to that person.

Nor do they cling to the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, or arhatship, thinking, ‘This is the fruit of once-returner, non-returner, or arhatship,’ or ‘This fruit of once-returner, non-returner, or arhatship belongs to that person.’”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not cling to the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, thinking, ‘This is the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha,’ or ‘This enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha belongs to that person.’”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not cling to any bodhisattva mahāsattva practice, thinking: ‘This is all the bodhisattva mahāsattva practices,’ or ‘These all the bodhisattva mahāsattva practices belong to that.’”

"Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not cling to the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, thinking, 'This is the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas,' or 'This unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas belongs to that person.'"

“Subhūti! Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva has no attachment toward any such phenomena, he is able to bring forth the perfection of wisdom, and is also able to bring forth the perfections of meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity.”

“Subhūti! Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva has no attachment to any of these dharmas, he is able to abide in internal emptiness, and is also able to abide in external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.”

“Subhūti! Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva has no attachment to any of these dharmas, he is able to abide in suchness, and is also able to abide in the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the dharma-nature (dharmatā), the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, the nature of equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixedness of dharmas (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of dharmas (dharmanetrī), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of empty space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm.”

“Subhūti! Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva has no attachment to any of these phenomena, he is able to dwell securely in the noble truth of suffering, and is also able to dwell securely in the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path.”

“Subhūti! Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva has no attachment to any of these dharmas, he is able to bring forth the four dhyānas, and is also able to bring forth the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions.”

“Subhūti! Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva has no attachment to any of these phenomena, they are able to bring forth the eight liberations, as well as the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities.”

“Subhūti! Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva has no attachment to any of these phenomena, he is able to bring forth the four applications of mindfulness, and is also able to bring forth the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.”

“Subhūti! Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva has no attachment to any of these phenomena, he is able to bring forth the gate of liberation of emptiness, and is also able to bring forth the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.”
“Subhūti! Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva has no attachment to any such phenomena, he is able to bring forth the five eyes and also bring forth the six supernormal powers.”

“Subhūti! Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva has no attachment to any of these dharmas, he is able to bring forth the ten powers of a Buddha, and is also able to bring forth the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.”

"Subhūti! Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva has no attachment to any such phenomena, they are able to bring forth the quality of non-forgetfulness (*asaṃpramoṣadharma*) and are also able to bring forth the state of constant equanimity (*upekṣā-vihāritā*)."
“Subhūti! Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva has no attachment to any of these phenomena, he is able to bring forth all dhāraṇī-doors and also able to bring forth all samādhi-doors.”

“Subhūti! Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva has no attachment to any of these phenomena, he is able to bring forth all-knowledge (sarvajñā), and is also able to bring forth the knowledge of the aspects of the path (mārgākārajñatā) and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā).”
"Why is this so, Subhūti?

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, should have any attachment toward phenomena— thinking 'this is a phenomenon' or 'this phenomenon belongs to that'— then they will be unable to bring forth and abide in supreme qualities at will."

"Furthermore, Subhūti, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not contemplate form as permanent or impermanent, as pleasant or painful, as self or non-self, as pure or impure, as tranquil or untranquil, or as remote or non-remote; nor do they contemplate feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness as permanent or impermanent, as pleasant or painful, as self or non-self, as pure or impure, as tranquil or untranquil, or as remote or non-remote."

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not contemplate the sense base of the eye as either permanent or impermanent, pleasant or painful, self or non-self, pure or impure, tranquil or non-tranquil, or detached or non-detached; nor do they contemplate the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind as either permanent or impermanent, pleasant or painful, self or non-self, pure or impure, tranquil or non-tranquil, or detached or non-detached.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not contemplate the sphere of form as permanent or impermanent, as pleasant or painful, as self or non-self, as pure or impure, as tranquil or non-tranquil, or as detached or non-detached. Furthermore, they do not contemplate the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena as permanent or impermanent, as pleasant or painful, as self or non-self, as pure or impure, as tranquil or non-tranquil, or as detached or non-detached.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not contemplate the eye constituent as either permanent or impermanent, as either pleasant or painful, as either self or non-self, as either pure or impure, as either tranquil or non-tranquil, or as either detached or non-detached. Furthermore, they do not contemplate the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind constituents as either permanent or impermanent, as either pleasant or painful, as either self or non-self, as either pure or impure, as either tranquil or non-tranquil, or as either detached or non-detached.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not contemplate the realm of form as either permanent or impermanent, as either pleasant or painful, as either self or non-self, as either pure or impure, as either tranquil or non-tranquil, or as either secluded or non-secluded. Furthermore, they do not contemplate the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena as either permanent or impermanent, as either pleasant or painful, as either self or non-self, as either pure or impure, as either tranquil or non-tranquil, or as either secluded or non-secluded.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not contemplate the eye-consciousness element as permanent or impermanent, as pleasant or painful, as self or non-self, as pure or impure, as tranquil or untranquil, or as detached or undetached; nor do they contemplate the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-consciousness elements as permanent or impermanent, as pleasant or painful, as self or non-self, as pure or impure, as tranquil or untranquil, or as detached or undetached.”

"Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not contemplate eye-contact as either permanent or impermanent, pleasant or painful, self or non-self, pure or impure, tranquil or untranquil, or detached or non-detached. Furthermore, they do not contemplate ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact as either permanent or impermanent, pleasant or painful, self or non-self, pure or impure, tranquil or untranquil, or detached or non-detached."

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not contemplate the feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition as being either permanent or impermanent, pleasant or painful, self or non-self, pure or impure, tranquil or non-tranquil, or detached or non-detached. Furthermore, they do not contemplate the feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact as conditions as being either permanent or impermanent, pleasant or painful, self or non-self, pure or impure, tranquil or non-tranquil, or detached or non-detached.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not contemplate the earth element as permanent or impermanent, as pleasant or painful, as self or non-self, as pure or impure, as tranquil or non-tranquil, or as secluded or non-secluded; nor do they contemplate the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements as permanent or impermanent, as pleasant or painful, as self or non-self, as pure or impure, as tranquil or non-tranquil, or as secluded or non-secluded.”

"Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not observe ignorance as either permanent or impermanent, as either pleasant or painful, as either self or non-self, as either pure or impure, as either tranquil or non-tranquil, or as either detached or non-detached. Furthermore, they do not observe volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, or old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair as either permanent or impermanent, as either pleasant or painful, as either self or non-self, as either pure or impure, as either tranquil or non-tranquil, or as either detached or non-detached."

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle Three Hundred and Fifty-Four. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: The Chapter on the Many Questions on Non-Duality, Number Sixty-One, Section Five. "Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do not contemplate the perfection of generosity (dānapāramitā) as either permanent or impermanent, as either pleasant or painful, as either self or non-self, as either pure or impure, as either tranquil or non-tranquil, or as either secluded or non-secluded; nor do they contemplate the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom as either permanent or impermanent, as either pleasant or painful, as either self or non-self, as either pure or impure, as either tranquil or non-tranquil, or as either secluded or non-secluded.
"Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not contemplate inner emptiness as either permanent or impermanent,
as either pleasant or painful, as either self or non-self, or as either pure or impure."
Whether pure or impure, tranquil or not tranquil, detached or not detached, they do not likewise contemplate external emptiness,
internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness,

Whether they are tranquil or not tranquil, whether they are secluded or not secluded. "Subhūti!..."

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not contemplate whether suchness is permanent or impermanent, pleasant or painful, self or non-self, pure or impure, tranquil or non-tranquil, or detached or non-detached; nor do they contemplate whether the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-erroneous nature, the unchanging nature, the nature of equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, or the inconceivable realm are permanent or impermanent, pleasant or painful, self or non-self, pure or impure, tranquil or non-tranquil, or detached or non-detached.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not contemplate the noble truth of suffering as permanent or impermanent, as pleasant or painful, as self or non-self, as pure or impure, as tranquil or non-tranquil, or as detached or non-detached; nor do they contemplate the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as permanent or impermanent, as pleasant or painful, as self or non-self, as pure or impure, as tranquil or non-tranquil, or as detached or non-detached.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not contemplate the four dhyānas as permanent or impermanent, as pleasant or painful, as self or non-self, as pure or impure, as tranquil or non-tranquil, or as secluded or non-secluded; nor do they contemplate the four immeasurables or the four formless absorptions as permanent or impermanent, as pleasant or painful, as self or non-self, as pure or impure, as tranquil or non-tranquil, or as secluded or non-secluded.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not contemplate the eight liberations as either permanent or impermanent, as either pleasant or painful, as either self or non-self, as either pure or impure, as either tranquil or non-tranquil, or as either secluded or non-secluded; nor do they contemplate the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities as either permanent or impermanent, as either pleasant or painful, as either self or non-self, as either pure or impure, as either tranquil or non-tranquil, or as either secluded or non-secluded.”

"Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not contemplate the four foundations of mindfulness as either permanent or impermanent, pleasant or painful, self or non-self, pure or impure, tranquil or untranquil, or secluded or unsecluded. Furthermore, they do not contemplate the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path as either permanent or impermanent, pleasant or painful, self or non-self, pure or impure, tranquil or untranquil, or secluded or unsecluded."

"Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they do not contemplate the gate of liberation of emptiness as either permanent or impermanent, as either pleasant or painful, as either self or non-self, as either pure or impure, as either tranquil or non-tranquil, or as either secluded or non-secluded; nor do they contemplate the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness as either permanent or impermanent, as either pleasant or painful, as either self or non-self, as either pure or impure, as either tranquil or non-tranquil, or as either secluded or non-secluded."

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not contemplate the five eyes as permanent or impermanent, as pleasant or painful, as self or non-self, as pure or impure, as tranquil or non-tranquil, or as detached or non-detached; nor do they contemplate the six supernormal powers as permanent or impermanent, as pleasant or painful, as self or non-self, as pure or impure, as tranquil or non-tranquil, or as detached or non-detached.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not contemplate the ten powers of a buddha as either permanent or impermanent, as either pleasant or painful, as either self or non-self, as either pure or impure, as either tranquil or non-tranquil, or as either detached or non-detached. Furthermore, they do not contemplate the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha as either permanent or impermanent, as either pleasant or painful, as either self or non-self, as either pure or impure, as either tranquil or non-tranquil, or as either detached or non-detached.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not contemplate the quality of non-forgetfulness as either permanent or impermanent, as either pleasant or painful, as either self or non-self, as either pure or impure, as either tranquil or non-tranquil, or as either remote or non-remote; nor do they contemplate the nature of constant equanimity as either permanent or impermanent, as either pleasant or painful, as either self or non-self, as either pure or impure, as either tranquil or non-tranquil, or as either remote or non-remote.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not contemplate all-knowledge as either permanent or impermanent, as either pleasant or painful, as either self or non-self, as either pure or impure, as either tranquil or non-tranquil, or as either secluded or non-secluded; nor do they contemplate the knowledge of the aspects of the path or the knowledge of all aspects as either permanent or impermanent, as either pleasant or painful, as either self or non-self, as either pure or impure, as either tranquil or non-tranquil, or as either secluded or non-secluded.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not contemplate any of the dhāraṇī-doors as permanent or impermanent, as pleasant or painful, as self or non-self, as pure or impure, as tranquil or untranquil, or as detached or non-detached; nor do they contemplate any of the samādhi-doors as permanent or impermanent, as pleasant or painful, as self or non-self, as pure or impure, as tranquil or untranquil, or as detached or non-detached.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not regard the awakening of a pratyekabuddha as either permanent or impermanent, as either pleasant or painful, as either self or non-self, as either pure or impure, as either tranquil or non-tranquil, or as either secluded or non-secluded.”

“Subhūti!
