“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not contemplate the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas as either permanent or impermanent, as either pleasant or painful, as either self or non-self, as either pure or impure, as either tranquil or non-tranquil, or as either secluded or non-secluded.”

“Subhūti! Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not observe any of these phenomena, he is able to bring forth the perfection of wisdom, and is also able to bring forth the perfections of meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity.”

“Subhūti! Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not observe any of these phenomena, he is able to abide in internal emptiness, and is also able to abide in external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersal emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.”

“Subhūti! Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not observe any of these dharmas, he is able to abide in suchness, and is also able to abide in the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm.”

“Subhūti! Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not observe any of these phenomena, he is able to abide in the noble truth of suffering, and is also able to abide in the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path.”

“Subhūti! Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not observe any of these phenomena, he is able to bring forth the four dhyānas, and is also able to bring forth the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments.”

"Subhūti! Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not observe any of these phenomena, he is able to bring forth the eight liberations, as well as the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities."

“Subhūti! Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not observe any of these phenomena, he is able to bring forth the four foundations of mindfulness, and is also able to bring forth the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.”

“Subhūti! Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not observe any of these phenomena, he is able to bring forth the gate of liberation of emptiness, and is also able to bring forth the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.”
"Subhūti! Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not observe any of these phenomena, they are able to bring forth the five eyes and also bring forth the six supernormal powers."

“Subhūti! Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not observe any of these phenomena, he is able to bring forth the ten powers of a buddha, and is also able to bring forth the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha.”

“Subhūti! Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not conceptualize any of these phenomena, he is able to bring forth the quality of non-forgetfulness and is also able to bring forth the state of constant equanimity.”
“Subhūti! Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not observe any of these phenomena, he is able to bring forth all doors of dhāraṇī and also able to bring forth all doors of samādhi.”

“Subhūti! Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not observe any of these dharmas, they are able to bring forth all-knowledge (sarvajñā), and are also able to bring forth the knowledge of the aspects of the path (mārgākārajñatā) and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā).”
"Why is this? Subhūti!

If, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they observe among phenomena anything as permanent or impermanent, as pleasant or painful, as self or non-self, as pure or impure, as tranquil or non-tranquil, or as secluded or non-secluded, then they will be unable to give rise to and abide in the distinguished qualities as they wish."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they are practicing the perfection of meditative concentration, and they are also practicing the perfections of diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity."

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they are practicing inner emptiness, and they are also practicing outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they are practicing suchness; they are also practicing the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they are then practicing the noble truth of suffering, as well as the noble truths of its origin, its cessation, and the path.”
"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they are then practicing the four dhyānas, as well as the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments."

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they are practicing the eight liberations, as well as the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they are practicing the four foundations of mindfulness, as well as the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they are practicing the liberation door of emptiness, as well as the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness.”
“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they are practicing the five eyes and also practicing the six supernormal powers.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they are practicing the ten powers of a buddha, as well as the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha.”
“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they are practicing the dharma of non-forgetfulness, and they are also practicing the state of constant equanimity.”
“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they are practicing all the doors of dhāraṇī, and they are also practicing all the doors of samādhi.”

"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they are practicing all-knowledge (sarvajñā), as well as the knowledge of the aspects of the path (mārgākārajñatā) and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā)."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Wherever the profound perfection of wisdom proceeds, all the other perfections and all the remaining factors conducive to enlightenment follow after it."
Wherever this profound perfection of wisdom goes, all the other perfections and all the remaining factors conducive to enlightenment follow it there.

"Subhūti! Just as a wheel-turning sage king has four divisions of heroic forces that follow wherever that wheel-turning king travels, and reach whatever place that wheel-turning king arrives at—so too do these four heroic forces follow him."

The profound perfection of wisdom is likewise: wherever it proceeds and whithersoever it goes, all the other perfections and all the remaining factors conducive to enlightenment follow after it, until they ultimately reach the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
It is like a skilled charioteer who, driving a chariot drawn by four horses, avoids dangerous paths and travels upon the right road, reaching his destination according to his original intention.”

The profound *prajñāpāramitā* is likewise: it skillfully guides all the *pāramitās* and all other factors conducive to enlightenment (*bodhipakṣadharma*), causing them to avoid the perilous paths of saṃsāra and nirvāṇa, to travel upon the right path of self-benefit and benefit for others, and to reach the omniscience that was originally sought.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
what constitutes the path for a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
"What, then, is not the path?
The Buddha said,
"Suvikrāntavikrāmin!..."

The paths of ordinary beings are not the path of bodhisattva mahāsattvas; the paths of śrāvakas are not the path of bodhisattva mahāsattvas; the paths of pratyekabuddhas are not the path of bodhisattva mahāsattvas.

The path of benefiting oneself and others is the path of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas; the path of the knowledge of all modes is the path of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas; the path that dwells neither in saṃsāra nor in nirvāṇa is the path of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas.
"Subhūti! This is what constitutes the path and the non-path for bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
The Venerable Subhūti then addressed the Buddha again, saying:
“World-Honored One!

The appearance of the profound *prajñāpāramitā* in the world is able to perform a great task; that is to say, it reveals the characteristics of the path and the non-path for all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, enabling them to know what is the path and what is not the path, so that they may swiftly realize the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*).”
The Buddha said:
"Excellent, Subhūti! It is so!"
"So it is! It is just as you have said.

The appearance of the profound *prajñāpāramitā* in the world is capable of performing a great task; that is to say, it reveals the characteristics of the path and the non-path for all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, enabling them to know what is the path and what is not the path, so that they may swiftly realize the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*)."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The appearance of the profound *prajñāpāramitā* in the world is able to perform a great task; that is to say, it delivers immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings, causing them all to obtain benefit and happiness."
"Subhūti! Although the profound perfection of wisdom performs boundless deeds for the benefit and happiness of others, it remains without attachment to these deeds."
“Subhūti! Although profound prajñāpāramitā can manifest the functions of form, it does not grasp or cling to these functions;
although it can manifest the functions of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, it does not grasp or cling to these functions.”
“Subhūti! Although the profound *prajñāpāramitā* can manifest the functions of the sense base of the eye, it has no attachment to these functions;
although it can manifest the functions of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, it has no attachment to these functions.”
“Subhūti! Although the profound perfection of wisdom can manifest the activities associated with the sense base of form, it has no attachment to these activities;
although it can manifest the activities associated with the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, it has no attachment to these activities.”
“Subhūti! Although the profound *prajñāpāramitā* can manifest the functions of the eye-element, it has no attachment to these functions;
although it can manifest the functions of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements, it has no attachment to these functions.”
“Subhūti! Although profound prajñāpāramitā can manifest the activities performed within the realm of form, it has no attachment to these activities;
although it can manifest the activities performed within the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena, it has no attachment to these activities.”
“Subhūti! Although the profound perfection of wisdom can manifest the functions of the visual consciousness element, it has no attachment to these functions;
although it can manifest the functions of the auditory, olfactory, gustatory, tactile, and mental consciousness elements, it has no attachment to these functions.”
"Subhūti! Although profound prajñāpāramitā can manifest the activities produced by eye-contact, it has no attachment to these activities;
although it can manifest the activities produced by ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact, it has no attachment to these activities."
“Subhūti! Although profound prajñāpāramitā can manifest the functions performed by the feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, it has no attachment to these functions;
although it can manifest the functions performed by the feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions, it has no attachment to these functions.”
"Subhūti! Although the profound *prajñāpāramitā* can demonstrate the functions performed by the earth element, it has no attachment to these functions;
although it can demonstrate the functions performed by the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements, it has no attachment to these functions."
“Subhūti! Although profound prajñāpāramitā can manifest the activities performed by ignorance, it has no attachment to these activities;

“Subhūti! Although the profound *prajñāpāramitā* can manifest the deeds performed by the *dānapāramitā*, it has no attachment to those deeds;

“Subhūti! Although the profound *prajñāpāramitā* can manifest the activities of internal emptiness (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*), it does not grasp at or become attached to those activities;

although it can manifest the activities of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, emptiness of all phenomena, unapprehendable emptiness, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, and emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, it does not grasp at or become attached to those activities.”
“Subhūti! Although the profound perfection of wisdom can manifest the activities performed by suchness, it has no attachment to these activities;

although it can manifest the activities performed by the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, immutability, equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm, it has no attachment to these activities.”
“Subhūti! Although the profound perfection of wisdom can manifest the functions of the noble truth of suffering, it has no attachment to these functions;
although it can manifest the functions of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, it has no attachment to these functions.”
“Subhūti! Although the profound perfection of wisdom can manifest the activities performed by the four dhyānas, it has no attachment to these activities;
although it can manifest the activities performed by the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, it has no attachment to these activities.”
“Subhūti! Although the profound *prajñāpāramitā* can manifest the activities of the eight liberations (*aṣṭavimokṣa*), it has no attachment to these activities;

although it can manifest the activities of the eight bases of mastery (*abhibhvāyatana*), the nine successive attainments (*anupūrvavihārasamāpatti*), and the ten totalities (*kṛtsnāyatana*), it has no attachment to these activities.”
“Subhūti! Although profound prajñāpāramitā can manifest the functions of the four foundations of mindfulness, it has no attachment to these functions;

although it can manifest the functions of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path, it has no attachment to these functions.”
“Subhūti! Although the profound perfection of wisdom can manifest the activities of the liberation door of emptiness, it has no attachment to these activities;

“Subhūti! Although the profound *prajñāpāramitā* can manifest the functions of the five eyes, it has no attachment to these functions;

“Subhūti! Although the profound perfection of wisdom can manifest the activities performed by the ten powers of a Buddha, it has no attachment to these activities;

"Subhūti! Although the profound *prajñāpāramitā* can manifest the activities of the quality of non-forgetfulness (*asaṃpramoṣadharma*), it has no attachment to these activities;
although it can manifest the activities of the state of constant equanimity (*upekṣā*), it has no attachment to these activities."
“Subhūti! Although the profound perfection of wisdom can manifest the activities performed by all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), it has no attachment to these activities;
although it can manifest the activities performed by the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), it has no attachment to these activities.”
“Subhūti! Although the profound *prajñāpāramitā* can manifest all the functions of the *dhāraṇī* gates, it has no attachment to these functions;
although it can manifest all the functions of the *samādhi* gates, it has no attachment to these functions.”
“Subhūti! Although profound prajñāpāramitā can manifest the activities performed for the fruit of stream-entry, it has no attachment to these activities;
although it can manifest the activities performed for the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship, it has no attachment to these activities.”
“Subhūti! Although the profound perfection of wisdom can manifest the activities of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, it does not grasp at or adhere to these activities.”
“Subhūti! Although the profound *prajñāpāramitā* can manifest all the deeds and activities performed by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, it remains without attachment to these things.”

“Subhūti! Although the profound perfection of wisdom can manifest the deeds performed by the Buddhas for the sake of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, it has no attachment to these deeds.”
“Subhūti! The profound perfection of wisdom guides bodhisattva mahāsattvas toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, ensuring that they never regress in the interim.”

Although the profound *prajñāpāramitā* causes bodhisattva-mahāsattvas to distance themselves from the levels of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas and to draw near to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, it neither gives rise to nor extinguishes any phenomena, for it takes the abiding nature of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*) as its definitive standard.”

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they should cultivate the perfection of meditative concentration for the sake of all sentient beings, taking omniscience as their objective support.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they should practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of all sentient beings, taking omniscience as their objective support.

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva takes these roots of goodness and, sharing them equally with all sentient beings, dedicates them toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment. At the time of dedication, he remains far removed from the threefold mind, namely: ‘Who is it that dedicates?’”
With what does one dedicate?
To what place does one dedicate? Subhūti!

When this bodhisattva mahāsattva takes these roots of virtue and dedicates them in this way toward the sought-after unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, they will swiftly bring the six perfections (*ṣaṭ-pāramitā*) to fulfillment; they will also swiftly bring the bodhisattva’s loving-kindness, compassion, joy, and equanimity to fulfillment. By means of this, they will quickly attain the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), and until they sit upon the sublime seat of awakening (*bodhimaṇḍa*), they will never be separated from these six perfections.
“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not depart from the six perfections, then they do not distance themselves from the knowledge of all modes. Therefore, Subhūti!”

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to swiftly realize the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment they seek, they should diligently apply themselves with vigor to train in the six perfections!
"You should diligently apply yourself to the practice of the six perfections!

Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly and diligently trains in and practices these six perfections, all their roots of virtue will quickly reach fulfillment, and they will swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
Therefore, Subhūti, all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should always remain in conjunction with the six perfections and never be separated from them.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
how is it that a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to be constantly and inseparably associated with the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā)?”
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates form as neither associated nor dissociated with reality, and contemplates feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness as neither associated nor dissociated with reality, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to remain constantly and inseparably associated with the six perfections.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates the sphere of the eye as neither associated nor dissociated, and contemplates the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind as neither associated nor dissociated, this bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to remain constantly and inseparably associated with the six perfections.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates the sphere of form as neither associated nor dissociated, and contemplates the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena as neither associated nor dissociated, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to remain constantly and inseparably associated with the six perfections.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates the eye-element as neither associated nor dissociated, and contemplates the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements as neither associated nor dissociated, such a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to remain constantly and inseparably associated with the six perfections.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates the realm of form as neither associated nor dissociated with [the mind], and contemplates the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena as neither associated nor dissociated, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to be constantly and inseparably associated with the six perfections.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates the eye-consciousness element as neither associated nor dissociated, and contemplates the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements as neither associated nor dissociated, this bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to be constantly and inseparably associated with the six perfections.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates eye-contact as neither associated nor dissociated, and contemplates ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as neither associated nor dissociated, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to remain constantly and inseparably associated with the six perfections.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates, in accordance with reality, that the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are neither associated nor dissociated, and contemplates, in accordance with reality, that the various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions are neither associated nor dissociated, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to remain constantly and inseparably associated with the six perfections.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates the earth element as neither associated nor dissociated with [ultimate reality], and likewise contemplates the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements as neither associated nor dissociated, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to remain constantly and inseparably associated with the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā).”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates ignorance as neither associated nor dissociated with reality, and likewise contemplates volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair as neither associated nor dissociated with reality, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to remain constantly and inseparably associated with the six perfections.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates the perfection of giving as neither associated nor dissociated with [emptiness], and likewise contemplates the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom as neither associated nor dissociated, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to remain constantly and inseparably associated with these six perfections.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates inner emptiness as it truly is—neither associated nor dissociated—and contemplates outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature as they truly are—neither associated nor dissociated—then this bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to remain constantly and inseparably associated with the six perfections.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates true suchness (*tathatā*) as neither associated nor dissociated, and contemplates the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*) as neither associated nor dissociated, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to remain constantly and inseparably associated with the six perfections (*ṣaṭpāramitā*).”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates the noble truth of suffering as neither associated nor dissociated, and contemplates the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as neither associated nor dissociated, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to be constantly and inseparably associated with the six perfections.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates the four dhyānas as neither associated nor dissociated with [the ultimate nature], and contemplates the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions as neither associated nor dissociated, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to remain constantly and inseparably associated with the six pāramitās.”

"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates the eight liberations as neither associated nor dissociated with [the ultimate nature], and contemplates the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities as neither associated nor dissociated, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to remain constantly and inseparably associated with the six perfections."

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates the four foundations of mindfulness as neither associated nor dissociated, and contemplates the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path as neither associated nor dissociated, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to remain constantly and inseparably associated with the six perfections.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates the gate of liberation of emptiness as neither associated nor dissociated, and contemplates the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness as neither associated nor dissociated, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to remain constantly and inseparably associated with the six perfections.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates the five eyes as neither associated nor dissociated with reality, and contemplates the six supernormal powers as neither associated nor dissociated with reality, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to remain constantly and inseparably associated with the six perfections.”

"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates the ten powers of a Buddha as neither associated nor dissociated, and contemplates the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha as neither associated nor dissociated, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to remain constantly and inseparably associated with the six perfections."

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates the quality of non-forgetfulness as neither associated nor dissociated [with emptiness], and contemplates the nature of constant equanimity as neither associated nor dissociated, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to remain constantly and inseparably associated with the six perfections.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) as neither associated nor dissociated, and contemplates the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) as neither associated nor dissociated, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to remain constantly and inseparably associated with the six perfections (*ṣaṭpāramitā*).”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates all dhāraṇī-doors as neither associated nor dissociated, and contemplates all samādhi-doors as neither associated nor dissociated, this bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to be constantly and inseparably associated with the six perfections.”

"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates the fruit of stream-entry as neither associated nor dissociated, and contemplates the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship as neither associated nor dissociated, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to remain constantly and inseparably associated with the six perfections."

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates pratyekabuddha-enlightenment as it truly is—neither associated nor dissociated—then that bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to remain constantly and inseparably associated with the six perfections.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates all the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva as being neither associated nor dissociated with reality, that bodhisattva mahāsattva will be able to remain constantly and inseparably associated with the six perfections.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas as being neither associated nor dissociated, that bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to remain constantly and inseparably associated with the six perfections.”
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly reflects thus:
'I should not dwell in form, nor should I dwell in feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.'"

Why is this? Because form is neither that which abides nor that in which it abides; likewise, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are also neither that which abides nor that in which they abide.
"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to remain constantly and inseparably associated with the six perfections. Subhūti!"
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly forms this thought:
"I should not dwell in the sense-base of the eye, nor should I dwell in the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind."

Why is this? Because the sense-base of the eye is neither that which dwells nor that in which it dwells; and because the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are likewise neither that which dwells nor that in which they dwell.
"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to remain constantly associated with the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā), never being separated from them. Subhūti!"
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly reflects thus:
"I should not dwell in the sphere of form, nor should I dwell in the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena."

Why is this? Because the sphere of form is neither that which abides nor that in which it abides; and because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are likewise neither that which abides nor that in which they abide.
"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to remain constantly associated with, and never separated from, the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā).
[From] the Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 355, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree, Part One, Chapter Sixty-one, Part Six: 'The Questions on Non-duality. Subhūti!"
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly reflects:
"I should not abide in the eye-element, nor should I abide in the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-elements."

Why is this? Because the eye-element is neither that which abides nor that in which it abides; and the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements are likewise neither that which abides nor that in which they abide.
"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to remain constantly associated with the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā), never being separated from them. Subhūti!"
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly forms this thought:
"I should not dwell in the realm of form, nor should I dwell in the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena."

Why is this? Because the realm of form is neither that which abides nor that in which one abides; and because the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena are likewise neither that which abides nor that in which one abides.
"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to remain constantly associated with the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā), never being separated from them. Subhūti!"
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly forms this thought:
"I should not dwell in the eye-consciousness element, nor should I dwell in the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-consciousness elements."

Why is this? Because the visual consciousness element is neither that which abides nor that in which it abides; and because the auditory, olfactory, gustatory, tactile, and mental consciousness elements are likewise neither that which abides nor that in which they abide.
"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to remain constantly associated with the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā), never being separated from them. Subhūti!"
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly reflects thus:
"I should not dwell in eye-contact, nor should I dwell in ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact."

Why is this? Because eye-contact is neither that which abides nor that in which it abides; and because ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact are likewise neither that which abides nor that in which they abide.
"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to remain constantly associated with the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā), never being separated from them. Subhūti!"
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly reflects thus:
"I should not dwell upon any sensations produced with eye-contact as a condition, nor should I dwell upon any sensations produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as conditions."

Why is this? Because the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are neither that which abides nor that in which they abide; likewise, the various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions are also neither that which abides nor that in which they abide.
"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to remain constantly associated with and never separated from the six perfections. Subhūti!"
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly reflects thus:
"I should not abide in the earth element, nor should I abide in the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements."

Why is this? Because the earth element is neither that which abides nor that in which it abides; and likewise, the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are neither that which abides nor that in which they abide.
"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to remain constantly in conjunction with the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā), never being separated from them. Subhūti!"
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly reflects thus:

"I should not abide in ignorance, nor should I abide in volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, or old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair."

Why is this? Because ignorance is neither that which abides nor that in which it abides; and likewise, from volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, none are either that which abides nor that in which they abide.
"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to remain constantly in association with the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā), never being separated from them. Subhūti!"
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly reflects thus:
"I should not abide in the perfection of generosity, nor should I abide in the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom."

Why is this? Because the perfection of generosity is neither that which abides nor that in which one abides; and likewise, from the perfection of ethical discipline up to the perfection of wisdom, none are either that which abides or that in which one abides.
"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to remain constantly associated with the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā), never being separated from them. Subhūti!"
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly reflects thus:

"I should not abide in internal emptiness, nor should I abide in external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature."

Why is this? Because internal emptiness is neither that which abides nor that in which it abides; and because external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, is likewise neither that which abides nor that in which it abides.
"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to remain constantly associated with the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā), never being separated from them. Subhūti!"
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly forms this thought:

"I should not abide in suchness, nor should I abide in the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-falsity, the unchanging nature, the equality, the nature free from birth, the fixedness of dharma, the stability of dharma, the limit of reality, the realm of empty space, or the inconceivable realm."

Why is this? Because true thusness (tathatā) is neither that which abides nor that in which it abides; likewise, the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), up to the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu), is also neither that which abides nor that in which it abides.
"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to remain constantly associated with the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā), never being separated from them. Subhūti!"
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly reflects thus:
"I should not dwell in the noble truth of suffering, nor should I dwell in the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path."

Why is this? Because the Noble Truth of Suffering is neither that which abides nor that in which it abides; likewise, the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path are also neither that which abides nor that in which they abide.
"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to remain constantly associated with the six perfections, never being separated from them. Subhūti!"
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly reflects thus:
"I should not abide in the four dhyānas, nor should I abide in the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments."

Why is this? Because the four dhyānas are neither that which abides nor that in which one abides; likewise, the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are also neither that which abides nor that in which one abides.
"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to remain constantly in association with the six perfections, never being separated from them. Subhūti!"
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly reflects:
"I should not abide in the eight liberations, nor should I abide in the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive absorptions, or the ten universal bases."

Why is this? It is because the eight liberations are neither that which abides nor that in which one abides; likewise, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten pervasive bases are also neither that which abides nor that in which one abides.
"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to remain constantly in association with the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā), never being separated from them. Subhūti!"
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly reflects thus:

"I should not abide in the four foundations of mindfulness, nor should I abide in the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path."

Why is this? Because the four foundations of mindfulness are neither that which abides nor that in which one abides; and because the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path, are likewise neither that which abides nor that in which one abides.
"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to remain constantly associated with the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā), never being separated from them. Subhūti!"
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly reflects thus:
"I should not dwell in the gate of liberation of emptiness, nor should I dwell in the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness."

Why is this? It is because the gate of liberation of emptiness is neither that which abides nor that in which one abides, and the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are likewise neither that which abides nor that in which one abides.
"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to remain constantly in association with the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā), never being separated from them. Subhūti!"
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly reflects thus:
"I should not abide in the five eyes, nor should I abide in the six supernormal powers. Why is this?"
"Because the five eyes are neither that which abides nor that in which they abide, and the six supernormal powers are likewise neither that which abides nor that in which they abide. Subhūti!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to remain constantly associated with the six perfections, never being separated from them."
“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly reflects thus:

‘I should not abide in the ten powers of a buddha, nor should I abide in the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha.’”

Why is this? Because the ten powers of a Buddha are neither that which abides nor that in which they abide; likewise, the four fearlessnesses and even the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are neither that which abides nor that in which they abide.
"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to remain constantly in association with the six perfections, never being separated from them. Subhūti!"
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly reflects thus:
"I should not dwell in the quality of non-forgetfulness, nor should I dwell in the nature of constant equanimity."

Why is this? Because the quality of non-forgetfulness is neither that which abides nor that in which one abides, and the nature of constant equanimity is likewise neither that which abides nor that in which one abides.
Thus it is, Subhūti!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to remain constantly in association with the six perfections, never being separated from them.
"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva always forms this thought:
"I should not dwell in all-knowledge (sarvajñatā), nor should I dwell in the knowledge of the aspects of the path (mārgākārajñatā) or the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā). Why is this?

Because all-knowledge is neither that which dwells nor that in which one dwells; likewise, the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are neither that which dwells nor that in which one dwells."
"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to remain constantly in association with the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā), never being separated from them. Subhūti!"
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly reflects thus:
"I should not abide in any of the dhāraṇī-doors, nor should I abide in any of the samādhi-doors."
Why is this? Because all dharani-doors are neither that which abides nor that in which one abides, and all samadhi-doors are likewise neither that which abides nor that in which one abides.
“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to remain constantly associated with the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā), never being separated from them. Subhūti!”
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly reflects thus:
"I should not abide in the fruit of a stream-enterer, nor should I abide in the fruits of a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat."

Why is this? Because the fruit of stream-entry is neither that which abides nor that in which one abides; likewise, the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are also neither that which abides nor that in which one abides.
"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to remain constantly associated with the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā), never being separated from them. Subhūti!"
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly reflects thus:
"I should not abide in the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha. Why is that?"
"Because the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is neither that which abides nor that in which one abides. Subhūti!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to remain constantly associated with, and never separated from, the six perfections.
“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly reflects thus:
‘I should not abide in any of the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.’”
Why is this? Because the practice of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is neither that which abides nor that in which one abides.
Thus it was said, "Subhūti!"
This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to remain constantly and inseparably associated with the six perfections.
"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva always maintains this thought:"
"I should not abide in the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas.
Why is this? Because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is neither that which abides nor that in which one abides."
"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to remain constantly and inseparably associated with the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā). Subhūti!"

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can practice the six perfections through such skillful means of non-abiding, that bodhisattva mahāsattva will swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

“Subhūti! It is as if there were a person who, wishing to eat a mango or a *panasa* fruit, first takes its seed and plants it in fertile, excellent soil; he irrigates it at the proper times, guards and tends to it, and as it gradually grows with sprouts, stems, branches, and leaves, when the seasons harmonize, flowers and fruits appear, and once the fruit has ripened, he takes it and eats it.”
Thus it is, Subhūti!

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening must first train in the six perfections, and furthermore, must gather in sentient beings through giving, or through kind words, or through beneficial conduct, or through cooperation.

Having thus gathered them in, he instructs them to abide in the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; once they have so abided, they are liberated from all birth, aging, sickness, and death, and realize the eternal and ultimate bliss of permanence.
"In this way, a bodhisattva shall attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, turn the sublime wheel of Dharma, and deliver immeasurable multitudes. Therefore, Subhūti!"

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to realize and understand all phenomena through their own insight without depending on others, wishes to bring all sentient beings to maturity, wishes to skillfully adorn and purify buddha-fields, wishes to swiftly sit upon the sublime seat of awakening, wishes to subdue all demonic armies, wishes to quickly realize the knowledge of all modes, and wishes to turn the wheel of Dharma to liberate the classes of sentient beings from birth, old age, sickness, and death, they should train in the six perfections and gather in all sentient beings through the skillful means of the four means of attraction.
"When a bodhisattva thus diligently practices and trains, they should constantly and diligently train in the perfection of wisdom.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
“Does the Buddha say that a bodhisattva mahāsattva should constantly and diligently study the perfection of wisdom?
The Buddha said,
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!”
"So it is! So it is! I say that a bodhisattva mahāsattva should constantly and diligently train in the perfection of wisdom."
"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to attain great mastery over all phenomena, they should study the perfection of wisdom. Why is that?"
"Subhūti! This profound perfection of wisdom enables bodhisattvas to attain mastery over all phenomena.
Furthermore, Subhūti!"

The profound *prajñāpāramitā* is the gateway through which all wholesome dharmas grow and develop, just as the great ocean is the gateway through which all precious gems grow and develop, as well as all waters.
Thus it is, Subhūti!
This profound perfection of wisdom is the gateway through which all wholesome dharmas grow and develop. Therefore, Subhūti!

Those persons seeking the vehicle of the śrāvakas, those persons seeking the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas, and those persons seeking the vehicle of the bodhisattvas, should all constantly and diligently study this profound perfection of wisdom.

“Subhūti! When bodhisattva mahāsattvas diligently train in this perfection of wisdom, they should diligently train in the perfection of generosity; they should diligently train in the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.

They should diligently abide in internal emptiness; they should diligently abide in external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.”

One should diligently abide in suchness; one should diligently abide in the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm.
One should diligently abide in the noble truth of suffering; one should diligently abide in the noble truths of the origin, cessation, and the path.
One should diligently train in the four meditative concentrations; one should diligently train in the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions.
One should diligently train in the eight liberations; one should diligently train in the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities;

one should diligently train in the four foundations of mindfulness; one should diligently train in the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path;
one should diligently train in the gate of liberation of emptiness, and one should diligently train in the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.
One should diligently train in the five eyes; one should diligently train in the six supernormal powers;

one should diligently train in the ten powers of a Buddha; one should diligently train in the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
one should diligently train in the quality of non-forgetfulness; and one should diligently train in the nature of constant abiding in equanimity.
One should diligently train in all dharani-doors; one should diligently train in all samadhi-doors; one should diligently train in all-knowledge;
and one should diligently train in the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects.
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
Just as a skilled archer, clad in firm armor and wielding excellent bows and arrows, has no fear of enemies;
so too is it with the bodhisattva mahāsattva, who embraces the perfection of wisdom and embraces the perfections of meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity.”

They embrace internal emptiness; they embrace external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.

They embrace suchness; they embrace the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, non-alteration, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm.
They embrace the noble truth of suffering; they embrace the noble truths of the origin, cessation, and the path.
They embrace the four dhyānas; they embrace the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments;
they embrace the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten universal bases;

they embrace the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
They embrace the gate of liberation of emptiness, and they embrace the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness;
they embrace the five eyes, and they embrace the six supernormal powers;

they embrace the ten powers of a Buddha, and they embrace the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
They embrace the quality of non-forgetfulness and embrace the state of constant equanimity;
they embrace all doors of dhāraṇī and embrace all doors of samādhi;
they embrace all-knowledge, and they embrace the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects.

When embracing such meritorious qualities, one employs the perfection of wisdom as the skillful means; by virtue of this cause and condition, all the armies of Māra, non-Buddhists, and the arguments of others cannot subdue them.
Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, they should diligently practice and study the profound perfection of wisdom.
“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this manner, they are protected and sustained by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present.”
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha,
saying: “World-Honored One,
how is it that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this manner, they are protected and remembered by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present?”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this manner, because they are able to practice the perfection of generosity, and are able to practice the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, they are protected and remembered by all Buddhas of the past, future, and present.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this manner, they are able to practice inner emptiness, outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of essential nature, the emptiness of self-characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature; therefore, they are protected and remembered by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present.”

"Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this manner, they are able to practice true suchness (tathatā), and because they are able to practice the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), non-falsity, non-alteration, equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm, they are protected and remembered by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present."

"Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this manner, because they are able to practice the noble truth of suffering and the noble truths of its origin, its cessation, and the path, they are protected and remembered by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present."

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this manner, because they are able to practice the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions, they are protected and remembered by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this manner, because they are able to practice the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities, they are protected and sustained by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this manner, because they are able to practice the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path, they are protected and remembered by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this manner, because they are able to practice the gate of liberation of emptiness and the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, they are protected and remembered by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this manner, because they are able to practice the five eyes and the six supernormal powers, they are protected and sustained by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this manner, because they are able to practice the ten powers of a buddha, and are able to practice the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, they are protected and remembered by all buddhas of the past, future, and present.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this manner, because they are able to practice the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity, they are protected and remembered by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this manner, because they are able to practice all the doors of dhāraṇī and all the doors of samādhi, they are protected and remembered by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present.”

"Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this manner, because they are able to practice all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), they are protected and remembered by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present."
The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha,
saying: “World-Honored One,
how does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of giving, come to be protected and remembered by all the Buddhas of the past, future, and present?”

How is it that when one practices the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, one is then protected and remembered by all the Buddhas of the past, future, and present?
“World-Honored One!
How does this bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing inner emptiness, come to be protected and remembered by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present?”

When one practices outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, how is it that one is then protected and sustained by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present?
“World-Honored One!
How is it that when this bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices true thusness (tathatā), he is protected and remembered by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present?”

How is it that when one practices the dharma-realm, the nature of dharmas, non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm, one is then protected and remembered by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present?
“World-Honored One!
How does this bodhisattva-mahāsattva, when practicing the Noble Truth of Suffering, come to be protected and remembered by all Buddhas of the past, future, and present?”
"How is it that when one practices the noble truths of the origin, cessation, and the path, one is then protected by the mindfulness of all Buddhas of the past, future, and present?
'World-Honored One!
How is it that when this bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices the four dhyānas, he is then protected by the mindfulness of all Buddhas of the past, future, and present?'"
"How is it that when one practices the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, one is immediately protected and remembered by all Buddhas of the past, future, and present?
"World-Honored One! [he asked.]
How does this bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the eight liberations, come to be protected and remembered by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present?
How does he, when practicing the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities, come to be protected and remembered by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present?
“World-Honored One!
How does this bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the four foundations of mindfulness, come to be protected and remembered by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present?”

How is it that when one practices the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path, one is immediately protected and remembered by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present?
“World-Honored One!
How does this bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the gate of liberation that is emptiness, come to be protected and remembered by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present?”
"How is it that when one practices the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, one is immediately protected and remembered by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present?
"World-Honored One! [he asked.]
How is it that when this bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices the five eyes, he is protected and remembered by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present?
How is it that when he practices the six supernormal powers, he is protected and remembered by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present?
“World-Honored One!
How does this bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the ten powers of a Buddha, come to be protected and remembered by all Buddhas of the past, future, and present?”

How is it that when one practices the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, one is then protected and remembered by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present?
“World-Honored One!
How is it that when this bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices the dharma of non-forgetfulness, he is protected and remembered by all Buddhas of the past, future, and present?”
"How is it that when one practices the state of constant dwelling in equanimity, one is protected and sustained by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present?
'World-Honored One!
How is it that when this bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices all the gates of dhāraṇī, he is protected and sustained by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present?'"
"How is it that when practicing all the gateways of samādhi, one is protected and remembered by the Buddhas of the past,

future, and present? World-Honored One, how does this bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing for the sake of all-knowledge, become protected and remembered by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present?"
“How is it that when one practices the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, one is then protected and remembered by the Buddhas of the past, future,
and present? The Buddha said,
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

When this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of generosity, because they perceive the perfection of generosity as unapprehendable, they are protected and remembered by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present;

when they practice the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, because they perceive everything from ethical discipline up to the perfection of wisdom as unapprehendable, they are protected and remembered by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present.

“Subhūti! When this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices inner emptiness (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*), because he observes that inner emptiness is unapprehendable, he is protected and remembered by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present.

When he practices outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, because he observes that everything from outer emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature is unapprehendable, he is protected and remembered by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present.”

“Subhūti! When these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice within suchness (*tathatā*), because they perceive that suchness is unapprehendable, they are protected and remembered by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present.

When they practice within the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), non-falsity (*avitathatā*), non-alteration (*ananyathātā*), equality (*samatā*), the state beyond birth (*anirodhatā*), the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*), because they perceive that from the realm of phenomena up to the inconceivable realm they are unapprehendable, they are protected and remembered by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present.”

“Subhūti! When this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the noble truth of suffering, because he contemplates that the noble truth of suffering is unapprehendable, he is protected and remembered by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present;

when he practices the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path, because he contemplates that the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are unapprehendable, he is protected and remembered by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present.”

“Subhūti! When these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the four dhyānas, because they perceive that the four dhyānas are unapprehendable, they are protected and remembered by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present;

when they practice the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, because they perceive that the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are unapprehendable, they are protected and remembered by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present.”

“Subhūti! When these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the eight liberations, because they perceive that the eight liberations are unapprehendable, they are protected and remembered by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present.

When they practice the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities, because they perceive that the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are unapprehendable, they are protected and remembered by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present.”

“Subhūti! When these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the four foundations of mindfulness, because they perceive that the four foundations of mindfulness are unapprehendable, they are protected and remembered by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present.

When they practice the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path, because they perceive that the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are unapprehendable, they are protected and remembered by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present.”

“Subhūti! When this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the gate of liberation of emptiness, because he contemplates that the gate of liberation of emptiness is unapprehendable, he is protected and remembered by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present;

when he practices the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, because he contemplates that the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are unapprehendable, he is protected and remembered by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present.”

“Subhūti! When these bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the five eyes, because they contemplate that the five eyes are unapprehendable, they are protected and remembered by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present;

when they practice the six supernormal powers, because they contemplate that the six supernormal powers are unapprehendable, they are protected and remembered by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present.”

“Subhūti! When these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the ten powers of a buddha, because they perceive that the ten powers of a buddha are unapprehendable, they are protected and remembered by the buddhas of the past, future, and present;

when they practice the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, because they perceive that everything from the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha is unapprehendable, they are protected and remembered by the buddhas of the past, future, and present.”

"Subhūti! When this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the dharma of non-forgetfulness, because he contemplates that the dharma of non-forgetfulness is unapprehendable, he is protected and remembered by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present;

when he practices the nature of constant equanimity, because he contemplates that the nature of constant equanimity is unapprehendable, he is protected and remembered by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present."

"Subhūti! When this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices all the gateways of dhāraṇī, because he perceives that all gateways of dhāraṇī are unapprehendable, he is protected and remembered by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present;
when he practices all the gateways of samādhi, because he perceives that all gateways of samādhi are unapprehendable, he is protected and remembered by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present."

“Subhūti! When this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), because he contemplates that all-knowledge is unapprehendable, he is protected and remembered by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present;

when he practices the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), because he contemplates that the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are unapprehendable, he is protected and remembered by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present.”
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the past, future, and present Buddhas cannot apprehend form, they protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva;
because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness cannot be apprehended, they protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva."
“Subhūti! Because the past, future, and present Buddhas, Tathāgatas, cannot be apprehended in the sense base of the eye, they protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva;
because the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind sense bases cannot be apprehended, they protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva.”
"Subhūti! Because the past, future, and present Buddhas cannot apprehend the sphere of form (*rūpāyatana*), they protect and keep this bodhisattva mahāsattva in mind;
because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental objects (*dharmāyatana*) cannot be apprehended, they protect and keep this bodhisattva mahāsattva in mind."
“Subhūti! Because the past, future, and present Buddhas cannot apprehend the eye-element, they protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva;
because the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements cannot be apprehended, they protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva.”
“Subhūti! Because the past, future, and present Buddhas cannot be apprehended as being like the realm of form (*rūpadhātu*), they protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva;
because the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) cannot be apprehended, they protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva.”
“Subhūti! Because the past, future, and present Buddhas cannot be apprehended as the eye-consciousness element, they protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva;
