because the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements cannot be apprehended, they protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva.”
“Subhūti! Because the eye-contact of all Buddhas of the past, future, and present is unapprehendable, these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are protected by mindfulness;
because the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact is unapprehendable, these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are protected by mindfulness.”

“Subhūti! Because the feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition cannot be apprehended in the Buddhas of the past, future, and present, these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are protected and sustained by their mindful care;
because the feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions cannot be apprehended, these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are protected and sustained by their mindful care.”
"Subhūti! Because the past, future, and present Buddhas cannot be apprehended as the earth element, they protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva;
because they cannot be apprehended as the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements, they protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva."
“Subhūti! Because past, future, and present Buddhas cannot apprehend ignorance, they protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva;

because they cannot apprehend volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, or old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair, they protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva.”
“Subhūti! Because the past, future, and present Buddhas cannot apprehend the perfection of giving, they protect and keep this bodhisattva mahāsattva in mind;
because the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom cannot be apprehended, they protect and keep this bodhisattva mahāsattva in mind.”
“Subhūti! Because the Buddhas of the past, future, and present cannot be apprehended in the manner of internal emptiness, they protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva;

because external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, emptiness of dispersion, unchanging emptiness, essential emptiness, the emptiness of self-characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehension, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature cannot be apprehended, they protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva.”
"Subhūti! Because the Buddhas of the past, future, and present cannot be apprehended as being like suchness (*tathatā*), they protect and keep this bodhisattva mahāsattva in mind;

because the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm cannot be apprehended, they protect and keep this bodhisattva mahāsattva in mind."
“Subhūti! Because the noble truth of suffering cannot be apprehended in the Buddhas of the past, future, and present, these Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas are protected by their mindful care;
because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path cannot be apprehended, these Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas are protected by their mindful care.”

“Subhūti! Because the past, future, and present Buddhas cannot be apprehended in the same way that the four dhyānas cannot be apprehended, they protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva;
because the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments cannot be apprehended in the same way, they protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva.”
"Subhūti! Because the Buddhas of the past, future, and present cannot be apprehended as the eight liberations, they protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva;
because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities cannot be apprehended, they protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva."

"Subhūti! Because the Buddhas of the past, future, and present cannot be apprehended in the same way that the four applications of mindfulness cannot be apprehended, they protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva;

because the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path cannot be apprehended, they protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva."
“Subhūti! Because the past, future, and present Buddhas cannot be apprehended as being like the liberation door of emptiness, they protect and keep this bodhisattva mahāsattva in mind;
because the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness cannot be apprehended, they protect and keep this bodhisattva mahāsattva in mind.”
“Subhūti! Because the Buddhas of the past, future, and present cannot be apprehended as the five eyes, they protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva;
because the six supernormal powers cannot be apprehended, they protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva.”
“Subhūti! Because the ten powers of a Buddha cannot be apprehended in the Buddhas of the past, future, and present, these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are protected and remembered by them;

because the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha cannot be apprehended, these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are protected and remembered by them.”
“Subhūti! Because the past, future, and present Buddhas cannot be apprehended as having any dharma that is subject to forgetfulness, they protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva;
because the state of constant equanimity (*upekṣā*) cannot be apprehended, they protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva.”
“Subhūti! Because the Buddhas of the past, future, and present cannot be apprehended as having all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), they protect and keep these bodhisattva mahāsattvas in mind;

because the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) cannot be apprehended, they protect and keep these bodhisattva mahāsattvas in mind.”
“Subhūti! Because all the gateways of dhāraṇī of the Buddhas of the past, future, and present are non-apprehendable, these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are protected and sustained by mindfulness;
because all the gateways of samādhi are non-apprehendable, these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are protected and sustained by mindfulness.”

“Subhūti! Because the fruits of stream-entry, once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship cannot be apprehended in the Buddhas of the past, future, and present, these Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are protected by their mindful care;
because they cannot be apprehended, these Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are protected by their mindful care.”
"Subhūti! Because the Buddhas of the past, future, and present—just as the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha—are unapprehendable, they protect and mindfully sustain this bodhisattva mahāsattva."

"Subhūti! Because the past, future, and present Buddhas, as well as all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, cannot be apprehended in their practice, they protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva-mahāsattva."

“Subhūti! Because the Buddhas of the past, future, and present, as well as the unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment of those Buddhas, cannot be apprehended, they protect and mindfully attend this bodhisattva mahāsattva.”
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

The Buddhas of the past, future, and present do not protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva on account of form; they do not protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva on account of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness."

"Subhūti! The Buddhas of the past, future, and present do not protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva by way of the sense base of the eye; nor do they protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva by way of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind."

“Subhūti! The Buddhas of the past, future, and present do not protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva by way of the sense-base of form; they do not protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva by way of the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena.”

"Subhūti! The Buddhas of the past, future, and present do not protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva by way of the eye-element; nor do they protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva by way of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-element."

"Subhūti! The Buddhas of the past, future, and present do not protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva by means of the realm of form; nor do they protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva by means of the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena."

“Subhūti! The Buddhas of the past, future, and present do not protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva by means of the eye-consciousness element; nor do they protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva by means of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-consciousness elements.”

“Subhūti! The Buddhas of the past, future, and present do not protect and mindfully attend this bodhisattva mahāsattva by means of eye-contact; they do not protect and mindfully attend this bodhisattva mahāsattva by means of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact.”

“Subhūti! The Buddhas of the past, future, and present do not protect and mindfully attend to these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas because of the feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition; they do not protect and mindfully attend to these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas because of the feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact as conditions.”

“Subhūti! The Buddhas of the past, future, and present do not protect and mindfully attend this bodhisattva mahāsattva by virtue of the earth element; they do not protect and mindfully attend this bodhisattva mahāsattva by virtue of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements.”

“Subhūti! The Buddhas of the past, future, and present do not protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva because of ignorance; nor do they protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva because of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, becoming, birth, or old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.”

"Subhūti! The Buddhas of the past, future, and present do not protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva by means of the perfection of giving; nor do they protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva by means of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom."

“Subhūti! The Buddhas of the past, future, and present do not protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva by means of internal emptiness; nor do they protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva by means of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.”

“Subhūti! The Buddhas of the past, future, and present do not protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva by virtue of *tathatā* (suchness); nor do they protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva by virtue of the *dharmadhātu*, *dharmatā*, *avitathatā*, *ananyathatā*, *samatā*, *anupapadatā*, *dharmasthititā*, *dharmaniyāmatā*, *bhūtakoṭi*, *ākāśadhātu*, or *acintyadhātu*.

“Subhūti! The Buddhas of the past, future, and present do not protect and mindfully attend to these bodhisattva mahāsattvas by virtue of the noble truth of suffering; nor do they protect and mindfully attend to these bodhisattva mahāsattvas by virtue of the noble truths of the origin, cessation, or the path.”

“Subhūti! The Buddhas of the past, future, and present do not protect and mindfully attend this bodhisattva mahāsattva by means of the four dhyānas, nor do they protect and mindfully attend this bodhisattva mahāsattva by means of the four immeasurables or the four formless absorptions.”

“Subhūti! The Buddhas of the past, future, and present do not protect and mindfully attend this bodhisattva mahāsattva on account of the eight liberations; they do not protect and mindfully attend this bodhisattva mahāsattva on account of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, or the ten totalities.”

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle Three Hundred and Fifty-Six. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: The Chapter on the Many Questions Regarding Non-Duality, Number Sixty-One, Section Seven. "Subhūti!

The Buddhas of the past, future, and present do not protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva by means of the four foundations of mindfulness; nor do they protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva by means of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path.

“Subhūti! The Buddhas of the past, future, and present do not protect and keep this bodhisattva mahāsattva in mind by means of the liberation door of emptiness; nor do they protect and keep this bodhisattva mahāsattva in mind by means of the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness.”

“Subhūti! The Buddhas of the past, future, and present do not protect and mindfully attend to these bodhisattva mahāsattvas by means of the five eyes, nor do they protect and mindfully attend to these bodhisattva mahāsattvas by means of the six supernormal powers.”

"Subhūti! The Buddhas of the past, future, and present do not protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva by virtue of the ten powers of a Buddha; nor do they protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva by virtue of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha."

“Subhūti! The Buddhas of the past, future, and present do not protect and mindfully attend this bodhisattva mahāsattva by virtue of the quality of non-forgetfulness, nor do they protect and mindfully attend this bodhisattva mahāsattva by virtue of the state of constant abiding in equanimity.”

“Subhūti! The Buddhas of the past, future, and present do not protect and mindfully attend this bodhisattva mahāsattva by virtue of their all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*); they do not protect and mindfully attend this bodhisattva mahāsattva by virtue of their knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) or their knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).”

“Subhūti! The Buddhas of the past, future, and present do not protect and keep in mind this bodhisattva mahāsattva by means of all the dhāraṇī-doors, nor do they protect and keep in mind this bodhisattva mahāsattva by means of all the samādhi-doors.”

“Subhūti! The Buddhas of the past, future, and present do not protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva on account of the fruit of stream-entry; nor do they protect and mindfully attend to this bodhisattva mahāsattva on account of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, or arhatship.”
“Subhūti! The Buddhas of the past, future, and present do not protect and mindfully attend this bodhisattva mahāsattva for the sake of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment. Subhūti!”
“Subhūti! The Buddhas of the past, future, and present do not protect and keep this bodhisattva mahāsattva in mind because of all the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.”
"The Buddhas of the past, future, and present do not, by virtue of their unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, protect and mind this bodhisattva mahāsattva.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha,
saying, "World-Honored One!"
"Although the bodhisattva mahāsattvas train in many places, they have nothing in which to train.
The Buddha said,
"Suvikrāntavikrāmin!..."
So it is! So it is! It is just as you have said.
Although the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas train in many places, they have nothing in which to train.
Why is this? Subhūti!
"Indeed, there is no dharma whatsoever that can cause a bodhisattva mahāsattva to train therein.
The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"

The Tathāgata has taught the six perfections (*ṣaṭ-pāramitā*) in both concise and extensive forms for the sake of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva wishes to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, they should—whether in brief or in detail—hear, receive, uphold, read, and recite these teachings on the six perfections until they have mastered them. Having mastered them, they should reflect upon them according to the principle; having reflected, they should examine them with precise scrutiny. At the time of such precise examination, the mind and mental factors no longer turn toward the characteristics of objects of perception.
The Buddha said,
“So it is, Subhūti! It is thus!”
"So it is! It is just as you have said.
Furthermore, Subhūti!"

When the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas diligently study the teachings associated with the six perfections as taught by the Tathāgatas—whether in brief or in detail—they should understand, in accordance with reality, the characteristics of both brevity and detail regarding all phenomena.
The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One,
how does a bodhisattva mahāsattva correctly understand, in accordance with reality, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena?"
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands the suchness-characteristic (*tathatā-lakṣaṇa*) of form as it truly is, and understands the suchness-characteristic of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness as they truly are, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva understands the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena as they truly are.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the mark of the suchness of the sense base of the eye, and understands, as it truly is, the marks of the suchness of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and detailed marks of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the characteristic of the suchness of the sense-base of form, and understands, as they truly are, the characteristics of the suchness of the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the mark of the suchness of the eye-element, and understands, as they truly are, the marks of the suchness of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and detailed marks of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the mark of the suchness of the form realm (*rūpadhātu-tathatā-lakṣaṇa*), and understands, as it truly is, the marks of the suchness of the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena (*śabda-gandha-rasa-spraṣṭavya-dharmadhātu-tathatā-lakṣaṇa*), then that bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and detailed marks of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the characteristic of the suchness of the visual consciousness element, and understands, as it truly is, the characteristic of the suchness of the auditory, olfactory, gustatory, tactile, and mental consciousness elements, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the mark of the suchness of eye-contact, and understands, as it truly is, the marks of the suchness of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and detailed marks of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the characteristics of the suchness of all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition, and understands, as they truly are, the characteristics of the suchness of all feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the suchness-characteristic of the earth element, and understands, as they truly are, the suchness-characteristics of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the mark of the suchness of ignorance; and if they understand, as they truly are, the marks of the suchness of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair—then this bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the abbreviated and detailed marks of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the characteristic of the suchness of the perfection of giving; and understands, as they truly are, the characteristics of the suchness of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom—then that bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva correctly understands the characteristic of the suchness (*tathatā*) of internal emptiness, and correctly understands the characteristic of the suchness of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—then this bodhisattva mahāsattva correctly understands the concise and extensive characteristics of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands as they truly are the suchness of suchness, and understands as they truly are the suchness of the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-erroneous nature, the unchanging nature, the nature of equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm—this bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the characteristic of suchness of the noble truth of suffering, and understands, as it truly is, the characteristic of suchness of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path—this bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the mark of the suchness of the four dhyānas, and understands, as they truly are, the mark of the suchness of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, this bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and detailed marks of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the mark of the suchness of the eight liberations; if they understand, as they truly are, the mark of the suchness of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities—then this bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and detailed marks of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the mark of suchness of the four foundations of mindfulness; and if they understand, as they truly are, the marks of suchness of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path—then this bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and detailed marks of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the mark of suchness of the gate of liberation of emptiness, and understands, as they truly are, the marks of suchness of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and extensive marks of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the mark of the suchness of the five eyes, and understands, as they truly are, the mark of the suchness of the six supernormal powers, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and detailed marks of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the mark of the suchness of the ten powers of a buddha; if they understand, as they truly are, the mark of the suchness of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha—then this bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and detailed marks of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the mark of the *tathatā* (suchness) of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and understands, as they truly are, the mark of the *tathatā* of the state of constant equanimity, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and detailed marks of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva truly understands the suchness-characteristic of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), and truly understands the suchness-characteristic of the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), then that bodhisattva mahāsattva truly understands the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the mark of suchness of all dhāraṇī-doors, and understands, as they truly are, the mark of suchness of all samādhi-doors, that bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and extensive marks of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the suchness-characteristic of the fruit of stream-entry, and understands, as it truly is, the suchness-characteristic of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the mark of the suchness of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, that bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the concise and detailed marks of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the marks of the suchness of all bodhisattva mahāsattva practices, that bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and extensive marks of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the mark of the suchness of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas, that bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the concise and extensive marks of all phenomena.”
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:

"World-Honored One, what is the characteristic of the suchness of form? What are the characteristics of the suchness of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein? And how do they understand the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena as they truly are?"
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
The suchness of form is without arising and without cessation, nor can it be designated as having duration or change; this is called the characteristic of the suchness of form.”

The suchness of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is without arising and without cessation, nor can it be designated as having duration or change; this is called the characteristic of the suchness of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!”

What is the mark of the suchness of the eye-base? What are the marks of the suchness of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-bases? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, and how do they understand the concise and detailed marks of all phenomena as they truly are?

“Subhūti! The suchness of the eye-base is without arising and without cessation, nor can it be designated as having duration or alteration; this is called the characteristic of the suchness of the eye-base.

The suchness of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-bases is without arising and without cessation, nor can it be designated as having duration or alteration; this is called the characteristic of the suchness of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-bases.”
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!”

What is the characteristic of the suchness (*tathatā*) of the sphere of form (*rūpāyatana*), and what are the characteristics of the suchness of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena (*dharmāyatana*)? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, and how do they understand, in their true nature, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena?

“Subhūti! The suchness of the sense-base of form is without arising and without cessation, nor can it be designated as having duration or change; this is called the characteristic of the suchness of the sense-base of form.

The suchness of the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is without arising and without cessation, nor can it be designated as having duration or change; this is called the characteristic of the suchness of the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena.”
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and extensive characteristics of all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!”

What is the characteristic of the suchness of the eye-element? What is the characteristic of the suchness of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-elements? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, and how do they understand the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena as they truly are?

“Subhūti! The suchness of the eye-element is without arising and without cessation, nor can it be designated as having duration or change; this is called the characteristic of the suchness of the eye-element.

The suchness of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements is without arising and without cessation, nor can it be designated as having duration or change; this is called the characteristic of the suchness of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements.”
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!”

What is the characteristic of the suchness (*tathatā*) of the form realm (*rūpadhātu*), and what are the characteristics of the suchness of the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena (*dharmadhātu*)? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, and how do they understand the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena as they truly are?

“Subhūti! The suchness of the form realm (rūpadhātu-tathatā) is without arising and without cessation, nor can it be designated as having duration or change; this is called the characteristic of the suchness of the form realm.

The suchness of the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and phenomena (śabda-gandha-rasa-spraṣṭavya-dharmadhātu-tathatā) is without arising and without cessation, nor can it be designated as having duration or change; this is called the characteristic of the suchness of the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and phenomena.”
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!”

What is the characteristic of the suchness of the eye-consciousness element? What are the characteristics of the suchness of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, and how do they understand, in their true reality, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena?

“Subhūti! The suchness of the visual consciousness element is without arising and without cessation, nor can it be designated as having duration or change; this is called the characteristic of the suchness of the visual consciousness element.

The suchness of the auditory, olfactory, gustatory, tactile, and mental consciousness elements is without arising and without cessation, nor can it be designated as having duration or change; this is called the characteristic of the suchness of the auditory, olfactory, gustatory, tactile, and mental consciousness elements.”
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!”

What is the mark of the suchness of eye-contact? What are the marks of the suchness of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, and how do they understand, according to reality, the concise and detailed marks of all phenomena?

“Subhūti! The suchness of eye-contact is without arising and without cessation, and it cannot be established as having any duration or alteration; this is called the characteristic of the suchness of eye-contact.

The suchness of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact is without arising and without cessation, and it cannot be established as having any duration or alteration; this is called the characteristic of the suchness of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact.”
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and extensive characteristics of all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!”

What is the characteristic of the suchness of all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition? What is the characteristic of the suchness of all feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, understanding the abbreviated and detailed characteristics of all phenomena as they truly are?

“Subhūti! The suchness of all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition is without arising and without cessation, nor can it be designated as having duration or change; this is called the characteristic of the suchness of all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.

The suchness of all feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions is without arising and without cessation, nor can it be designated as having duration or change; this is called the characteristic of the suchness of all feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions.”
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and extensive characteristics of all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!”

What is the characteristic of the suchness of the earth element? What are the characteristics of the suchness of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, and how do they understand the concise and extensive characteristics of all phenomena as they truly are?

“Subhūti! The suchness of the earth element is without arising and without cessation, nor can it be designated as having duration or change; this is called the characteristic of the suchness of the earth element.

The suchness of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements is without arising and without cessation, nor can it be designated as having duration or change; this is called the characteristic of the suchness of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements.”
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!”

What is the mark of the suchness (*tathatā*) of ignorance? What are the marks of the suchness of volitional formations (*saṃskāra*), consciousness (*vijñāna*), name-and-form (*nāmarūpa*), the six sense bases (*ṣaḍāyatana*), contact (*sparśa*), feeling (*vedanā*), craving (*tṛṣṇā*), grasping (*upādāna*), becoming (*bhava*), birth (*jāti*), and old age, death, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, and how do they understand the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena as they truly are?
“Subhūti! The suchness of ignorance is without arising and without cessation, nor can it be designated as having duration or change; this is called the characteristic of the suchness of ignorance.

The suchness of volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair is without arising and without cessation, nor can it be designated as having duration or change; this is called the characteristic of the suchness of volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair.”
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!”

What is the characteristic of the suchness of the perfection of generosity? What are the characteristics of the suchness of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom? How do bodhisattva mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, and how do they understand the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena as they truly are?

“Subhūti! The suchness of the perfection of generosity is without arising and without cessation, and it cannot be established as having any alteration; this is called the characteristic of the suchness of the perfection of generosity.

The suchness of the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom is without arising and without cessation, and it cannot be established as having any alteration; this is called the characteristic of the suchness of the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom.”
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and extensive characteristics of all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!”

What is the characteristic of the suchness of internal emptiness? What are the characteristics of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersal emptiness, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of self-nature, and the emptiness of the self-nature of non-existence? How do the bodhisattva mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, and how do they understand the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena as they truly are?

“Subhūti! The suchness of internal emptiness is without arising and without cessation, nor can it be designated as having duration or change; this is called the characteristic of the suchness of internal emptiness.

From external emptiness up to the suchness of the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature, they are without arising and without cessation, nor can they be designated as having duration or change; this is called the characteristic of the suchness of external emptiness up to the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature.”
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and extensive characteristics of all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!”

What is the characteristic of suchness? What are the characteristics of the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), non-illusory nature, unchanging nature, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm? How do bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, and how do they understand the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena as they truly are?
“Subhūti! Suchness is suchness;
it is without arising and without cessation, and there is no abiding or alteration that can be designated. This is called the characteristic of the suchness of suchness.

From the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu) up to the inconceivable realm, their suchness is without arising and without cessation, and there is no abiding or alteration that can be designated. This is called the characteristic of the suchness of the realm of phenomena up to the inconceivable realm.”
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!”

What is the characteristic of the suchness of the noble truth of suffering? What are the characteristics of the suchness of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, and how do they understand the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena as they truly are?

“Subhūti! The suchness of the noble truth of suffering is without arising and without cessation, nor can it be designated as having duration or change; this is called the characteristic of the suchness of the noble truth of suffering.

The suchness of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path is without arising and without cessation, nor can it be designated as having duration or change; this is called the characteristic of the suchness of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path.”
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!”

What is the characteristic of the suchness (*tathatā*) of the four dhyānas? What is the characteristic of the suchness of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, and how do they understand the concise and extensive characteristics of all phenomena as they truly are?

“Subhūti! The suchness of the four dhyānas is without arising and without cessation, nor can it be designated as having duration or alteration; this is called the characteristic of the suchness of the four dhyānas.

The suchness of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions is without arising and without cessation, nor can it be designated as having duration or alteration; this is called the characteristic of the suchness of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions.”
"Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.
"World-Honored One!"

What is the mark of the suchness (*tathatā*) of the eight liberations? What is the mark of the suchness of the eight bases of mastery (*abhibhvāyatana*), the nine successive attainments (*anupūrvavihārasamāpatti*), and the ten totalities (*kṛtsnāyatana*)? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, and how do they understand the concise and detailed marks of all phenomena as they truly are?

“Subhūti! The suchness of the eight liberations is without arising and without cessation, nor can it be established as having any change of state; this is called the characteristic of the suchness of the eight liberations.

The suchness of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten universal bases is without arising and without cessation, nor can it be established as having any change of state; this is called the characteristic of the suchness of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten universal bases.”
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and extensive characteristics of all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!”

What is the characteristic of the suchness (*tathatā*) of the four foundations of mindfulness? What is the characteristic of the suchness of the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path? How do the bodhisattva mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, and how do they understand the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena as they truly are?

“Subhūti! The suchness of the four foundations of mindfulness is without arising and without cessation, and it cannot be designated as having any alteration of abiding; this is called the characteristic of the suchness of the four foundations of mindfulness.

The suchness of the four right endeavors up to the eight branches of the noble path is without arising and without cessation, and it cannot be designated as having any alteration of abiding; this is called the characteristic of the suchness of the four right endeavors up to the eight branches of the noble path.”
"Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.
"World-Honored One!"

What is the characteristic of suchness of the emptiness gate of liberation? What is the characteristic of suchness of the signless and wishless gates of liberation? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, and how do they understand the concise and extensive characteristics of all phenomena as they truly are?

“Subhūti! The suchness of the gate of liberation of emptiness is without arising and without cessation, nor can it be designated as having any change of state; this is called the characteristic of the suchness of the gate of liberation of emptiness.

The suchness of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness is without arising and without cessation, nor can it be designated as having any change of state; this is called the characteristic of the suchness of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.”
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!”

What is the mark of the suchness of the five eyes, and what is the mark of the suchness of the six supernormal powers? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, and how do they understand, in their true reality, the concise and detailed marks of all phenomena?

“Subhūti! The suchness of the five eyes is without arising and without cessation, and it cannot be designated as having any abiding or alteration; this is called the characteristic of the suchness of the five eyes.

The suchness of the six supernormal powers is without arising and without cessation, and it cannot be designated as having any abiding or alteration; this is called the characteristic of the suchness of the six supernormal powers.”
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and extensive characteristics of all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!”

What is the mark of the suchness of the ten powers of a Buddha? What is the mark of the suchness of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha? How do the bodhisattva mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, understanding as they truly are the concise and detailed marks of all phenomena?

“Subhūti! The suchness of the ten powers of a Buddha is without arising and without cessation, nor can it be established as having duration or change; this is called the characteristic of the suchness of the ten powers of a Buddha.

The suchness of the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, is without arising and without cessation, nor can it be established as having duration or change; this is called the characteristic of the suchness of the four fearlessnesses, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.”
"Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.
"World-Honored One!"

What is the characteristic of the suchness of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and what is the characteristic of the suchness of the nature of constant equanimity? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, and how do they understand the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena as they truly are?

“Subhūti! The suchness of the quality of non-forgetfulness is without arising and without cessation, nor can it be designated as having duration or change; this is called the characteristic of the suchness of the quality of non-forgetfulness.

The suchness of the state of constant equanimity is without arising and without cessation, nor can it be designated as having duration or change; this is called the characteristic of the suchness of the state of constant equanimity.”
"All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.
"World-Honored One!"

What is the mark of the suchness of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), what is the mark of the suchness of the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), such that the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand them as they truly are and train therein? How do they understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed marks of all phenomena (*dharmas*)?

“Subhūti! The suchness of all-knowledge (sarvajñatā) is without arising and without cessation, nor can it be established as having any alteration; this is called the characteristic of the suchness of all-knowledge.

The suchness of the knowledge of the paths (mārgākārajñatā) and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā) is without arising and without cessation, nor can it be established as having any alteration; this is called the characteristic of the suchness of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects.”
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!”

What is the mark of the suchness of all dharani-doors, and what is the mark of the suchness of all samadhi-doors? How do bodhisattva-mahasattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, and how do they understand the concise and extensive marks of all phenomena as they truly are?

“Subhūti! The suchness of all dhāraṇī-doors is without arising and without cessation, nor can it be established as having duration or change; this is called the characteristic of the suchness of all dhāraṇī-doors.

The suchness of all samādhi-doors is without arising and without cessation, nor can it be established as having duration or change; this is called the characteristic of the suchness of all samādhi-doors.”
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!”

What is the mark of suchness of the fruit of stream-entry? What is the mark of suchness of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, understanding the concise and extensive marks of all phenomena as they truly are?

“Subhūti! The suchness of the fruit of stream-entry is without arising and without cessation, and it cannot be designated as having duration or change; this is called the characteristic of the suchness of the fruit of stream-entry.

The suchness of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhat is without arising and without cessation, and it cannot be designated as having duration or change; this is called the characteristic of the suchness of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhat.”
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and extensive characteristics of all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!”

What is the mark of the suchness of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha, which the bodhisattva mahāsattvas understand as it truly is and train in; and how do they understand, as it truly is, the concise and detailed marks of all phenomena?

“Subhūti! The suchness of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is without arising and without cessation, nor can it be designated as having duration or change; this is called the characteristic of the suchness of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment.”
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and extensive characteristics of all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!”

What is the mark of the suchness of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, which all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand as it truly is and train in; and how do they understand, as it truly is, the concise and detailed marks of all phenomena?

“Subhūti! The suchness of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas’ practices is without arising and without cessation, nor can any abiding or alteration be predicated of it; this is called the characteristic of the suchness of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas’ practices.”
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!”

What is the characteristic of the suchness of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas, which the bodhisattva mahāsattvas understand as it truly is and train in; and how do they understand, as it truly is, the concise and extensive characteristics of all phenomena?

“Subhūti! The suchness of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is without arising and without cessation, nor can it be designated as having any alteration of abiding; this is called the characteristic of the suchness of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas.”
All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!"

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the reality-limit (bhūtakoṭi) of form, and understands, as it truly is, the reality-limit of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the mark of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) regarding the sense-field of the eye, and understands, as it truly is, the marks of the limit of reality regarding the sense-fields of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and detailed marks of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the mark of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) regarding the sphere of form; if he understands, as it truly is, the marks of the limit of reality regarding the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena—then that bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and detailed marks of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the mark of the reality-limit (*bhūtakoṭi*) of the eye-element, and understands, as it truly is, the marks of the reality-limit of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and detailed marks of all phenomena.”

"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the mark of the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) of the form realm, and understands, as it truly is, the marks of the limit of reality of the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and detailed marks of all phenomena."

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the mark of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) of the eye-consciousness element, and understands, as it truly is, the mark of the limit of reality of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and detailed marks of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the reality-limit (bhūtakoṭi) characteristic of eye-contact, and understands, as it truly is, the reality-limit characteristic of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the mark of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) of all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition, and understands, as they truly are, the mark of the limit of reality of all feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and detailed marks of all phenomena.”

"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the reality-limit (bhūtakoṭi) characteristic of the earth element, and understands, as it truly is, the reality-limit characteristic of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena."

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the reality-limit (bhūtakoṭi) characteristic of ignorance; and if they understand, as it truly is, the reality-limit characteristic of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair—then this bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the mark of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) of the perfection of generosity; and understands, as they truly are, the marks of the limit of reality of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom—then that bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and detailed marks of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva correctly understands the reality-limit (*bhūtakoṭi*) of internal emptiness, and correctly understands the reality-limit of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—then this bodhisattva mahāsattva correctly understands the abbreviated and extensive characteristics of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the characteristic of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) within suchness (*tathatā*); and if they understand, as it truly is, the characteristics of the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), non-falsity (*avitathatā*), non-alteration (*ananyathā*), equality (*samatā*), the state beyond birth (*anirodhatā*), the fixedness of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*)—then this bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the reality-limit (bhūtakoṭi) of the noble truth of suffering, and understands, as it truly is, the reality-limit of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the mark of the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) of the four dhyānas, and understands, as they truly are, the mark of the limit of reality of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and detailed marks of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the mark of the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) of the eight liberations; and if they understand, as they truly are, the mark of the limit of reality of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten pervasive bases—then this bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and detailed marks of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the mark of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) of the four foundations of mindfulness; and if they understand, as they truly are, the mark of the limit of reality of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path—then that bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and detailed marks of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the reality-limit (bhūtakoṭi) of the gate of liberation of emptiness, and understands, as it truly is, the reality-limit of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, in accordance with reality, the mark of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) of the five eyes, and understands, in accordance with reality, the mark of the limit of reality of the six supernormal powers (*abhijñā*), this bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, in accordance with reality, the concise and detailed marks of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the mark of the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) of the ten powers of a buddha; if they understand, as they truly are, the mark of the limit of reality of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha—then this bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and detailed marks of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the mark of the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and understands, as they truly are, the mark of the limit of reality of the state of constant equanimity, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and detailed marks of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), and understands, as they truly are, the limit of reality of the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), then this bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the reality-limit (bhūtakoṭi) characteristic of all dhāraṇī-doors, and understands, as it truly is, the reality-limit characteristic of all samādhi-doors, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the concise and extensive characteristics of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the reality-limit (bhūtakoṭi) of the fruit of stream-entry, and understands, as it truly is, the reality-limit of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship—this bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the characteristic of the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, this bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the mark of the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) of all bodhisattva mahāsattva practices, that bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and extensive marks of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the mark of the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas, that bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and detailed marks of all phenomena.”
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!

What is the mark of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) of form? What are the marks of the limit of reality of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein? And how do they understand, according to reality, the concise and extensive marks of all phenomena?"
The Buddha said: “Subhūti!

The limit of formlessness is called the characteristic of the reality-limit of form; the limits of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are called the characteristics of the reality-limit of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness. Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand these as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.”
“World-Honored One!

What is the mark of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) regarding the sphere of the eye? What is the mark of the limit of reality regarding the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein; and how do they understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed marks of all phenomena?”

“Subhūti! The limit of the eye-base (*cakṣur-āyatana*) is called the mark of the reality-limit (*bhūtakoṭi*) of the eye-base; the limits of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases are called the marks of the reality-limit of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases. Bodhisattvas mahāsattvas should understand these as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed marks of all phenomena.”
“World-Honored One!

What is the mark of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) regarding the sphere of form? What are the marks of the limit of reality regarding the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, and how do they understand the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena as they truly are?”

“Subhūti! The limit of the sphere of formlessness is called the characteristic of the reality-limit of the sphere of form; the limits of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are called the characteristics of the reality-limits of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena. Bodhisattvas mahāsattvas should understand these as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.”
“World-Honored One!

What is the mark of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) of the eye-element? What is the mark of the limit of reality of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-elements? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein; and how do they understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed marks of all phenomena?”

“Subhūti! The limitlessness of the eye-element is called the mark of the reality-limit (bhūtakoṭi) of the eye-element; the limitlessness of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements is called the mark of the reality-limit of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements. All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand these as they truly are and train therein, understanding the concise and detailed marks of all phenomena as they truly are.”
“World-Honored One!

What is the mark of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) of the form realm? What is the mark of the limit of reality of the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, and how do they understand, in their true nature, the concise and detailed characteristics of all dharmas?”

“Subhūti! The limit of the formless realm (*ārūpyadhātu*) is called the mark of the reality-limit (*bhūtakoṭi*) of the form realm; the limits of the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) are called the marks of the reality-limit of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and phenomena. Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand these as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.”
“World-Honored One!

What is the mark of the reality-limit (*bhūtakoṭi*) of the eye-consciousness element? What is the mark of the reality-limit of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, and how do they understand the concise and detailed marks of all phenomena as they truly are?”

“Subhūti! The limitlessness of the eye-consciousness element is called the characteristic of the reality-limit (bhūtakoṭi) of the eye-consciousness element. The limitlessness of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements is called the characteristic of the reality-limit of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements. Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand these as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.”
“World-Honored One!

What is the characteristic of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) regarding eye-contact? What are the characteristics of the limit of reality regarding ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, and how do they understand the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena as they truly are?”

“Subhūti! The absence of a limit to eye-contact is called the mark of the reality-limit of eye-contact; the absence of limits to ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact is called the mark of the reality-limit of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact. All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand these as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed marks of all phenomena.”
“World-Honored One!

What is the mark of the reality-limit (*bhūtakoṭi*) of all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition? What is the mark of the reality-limit of all feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, and how do they understand the concise and detailed marks of all phenomena as they truly are?”

“Subhūti! The limit of all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition is called the characteristic of the reality-limit (bhūtakoṭi) of all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition. The limit of all feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions is called the characteristic of the reality-limit of all feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions. Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand these as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.”
“World-Honored One!

What is the mark of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) of the earth element? What is the mark of the limit of reality of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein? And how do they understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed marks of all dharmas?”

“Subhūti! The absence of a limit to the earth element is called the reality-limit (bhūtakoṭi) characteristic of the earth element; the absence of limits to the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements is called the reality-limit characteristic of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements. Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand these as they truly are and train therein; they should understand the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena as they truly are.”
“World-Honored One!

What is the reality-limit (bhūtakoṭi) characteristic of ignorance? What are the reality-limit characteristics of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, and how do they understand the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena as they truly are?”

“Subhūti!
