The absence of a limit to ignorance is called the characteristic of the reality-limit of ignorance; the absence of a limit to volitional formations, up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, is called the characteristic of the reality-limit of volitional formations, up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair. Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand these as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.”

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll Three Hundred and Fifty-seven. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: The Chapter on the Many Questions on Non-duality, Number Sixty-one, Section Eight. "World-Honored One!

What is the mark of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) of the perfection of generosity? What are the marks of the limits of reality of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom? How do the bodhisattva mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein; and how do they understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena?

“Subhūti! The limitlessness of the perfection of generosity is called the mark of the reality-limit (bhūtakoṭi) of the perfection of generosity; the limitlessness of the perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom is called the mark of the reality-limit of those perfections from ethical discipline up to wisdom. Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand these as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed marks of all phenomena.”
“World-Honored One!

What is the mark of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) in inner emptiness? What are the marks of outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, emptiness of dispersion, emptiness of non-alteration, emptiness of intrinsic nature, emptiness of self-characteristic, emptiness of common characteristic, emptiness of all phenomena, emptiness of the unapprehendable, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, and emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, and how do they understand the concise and extensive characteristics of all phenomena as they truly are?”

“Subhūti! The absence of a limit to internal emptiness is called the characteristic of the reality-limit (bhūtakoṭi) of internal emptiness; the absence of a limit to external emptiness, up to and including the absence of a limit to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence, is called the characteristic of the reality-limit of external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence. Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand these as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.”
“World-Honored One!

What is the characteristic of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) as suchness (*tathatā*); what are the characteristics of the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), non-falsity, non-alteration, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the limit of reality, the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these according to reality and train therein; and how do they understand, according to reality, the concise and extensive characteristics of all phenomena?”

“Subhūti! The absence of a limit to suchness is called the characteristic of the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) of suchness; the absence of a limit to the dharma-realm, up to the inconceivable realm, is called the characteristic of the limit of reality of the dharma-realm, up to the inconceivable realm. Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand these as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.”
“World-Honored One!

What is the characteristic of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) of the noble truth of suffering? What are the characteristics of the limits of reality of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein; and how do they understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena?”

“Subhūti! The limit of the noble truth of suffering is called the mark of the reality-limit (bhūtakoṭi) of the noble truth of suffering; the limits of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are called the marks of the reality-limit of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path. Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand these as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.”
“World-Honored One!

What is the mark of the reality-limit (*bhūtakoṭi*) of the four dhyānas? What is the mark of the reality-limit of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, and how do they understand the concise and detailed marks of all phenomena as they truly are?”

“Subhūti! The absence of a limit to the four dhyānas is called the characteristic of the reality-limit of the four dhyānas; the absence of a limit to the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions is called the characteristic of the reality-limit of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions. Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand these as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.”
“World-Honored One!

What is the mark of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) of the eight liberations? What is the mark of the limit of reality of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, and how do they understand the concise and detailed marks of all phenomena as they truly are?”

“Subhūti! The non-existence of a limit to the eight liberations is called the characteristic of the reality-limit (bhūtakoṭi) of the eight liberations; the non-existence of a limit to the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities is called the characteristic of the reality-limit of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities. Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand these as they truly are and train therein, understanding the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena as they truly are.”
“World-Honored One!

What is the mark of the reality-limit (*bhūtakoṭi*) of the four foundations of mindfulness? What is the mark of the reality-limit of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, having understood these as they truly are, train therein, and how do they understand the concise and detailed marks of all dharmas as they truly are?”

"Subhūti! The non-limit of the four foundations of mindfulness is called the characteristic of the reality-limit (bhūtakoṭi) of the four foundations of mindfulness; the non-limit of the four right efforts up to the eight branches of the noble path is called the characteristic of the reality-limit of the four right efforts up to the eight branches of the noble path. Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand these as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena."
“World-Honored One!

What is the characteristic of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) regarding the gate of liberation of emptiness? What is the characteristic of the limit of reality regarding the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, and how do they understand the concise and extensive characteristics of all phenomena as they truly are?”

“Subhūti! The limit of the gate of liberation of emptiness is called the characteristic of the reality-limit (bhūtakoṭi) of the gate of liberation of emptiness; the limit of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness is called the characteristic of the reality-limit of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness. All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand these as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.”
“World-Honored One!

What is the mark of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) of the five eyes, and what is the mark of the limit of reality of the six supernormal powers? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, and how do they understand, as they truly are, the abbreviated and extensive marks of all phenomena?”

“Subhūti! The absence of a limit to the five eyes is called the mark of the reality-limit of the five eyes; the absence of a limit to the six supernormal powers is called the mark of the reality-limit of the six supernormal powers. All bodhisattva mahāsattvas should understand these as they truly are and train therein, understanding the abbreviated and detailed marks of all phenomena as they truly are.”
“World-Honored One!

What is the mark of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) of the ten powers of a Buddha? What is the mark of the limit of reality of the four fearlessnesses, the four unhindered understandings, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas truly comprehend these and train therein, and how do they truly comprehend the concise and detailed marks of all phenomena?”

“Subhūti! The limit of the non-existence of the ten powers of a Buddha is called the mark of the reality-limit (bhūtakoṭi) of the ten powers of a Buddha; the limit of the non-existence of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is called the mark of the reality-limit of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha. Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand these as they truly are and train therein, understanding as they truly are the concise and detailed marks of all phenomena.”
“World-Honored One!

What is the mark of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) regarding the quality of non-forgetfulness, and what is the mark of the limit of reality regarding the nature of constant abiding in equanimity? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, and how do they understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed marks of all phenomena?”

“Subhūti! The limit of the absence of non-forgetfulness is called the mark of the reality-limit of the absence of non-forgetfulness; the limit of the nature of constant abiding in equanimity is called the mark of the reality-limit of the nature of constant abiding in equanimity. All bodhisattva mahāsattvas should understand these as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed marks of all phenomena.”
“World-Honored One!

What is the mark of the reality-limit (*bhūtakoṭi*) of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), and what is the mark of the reality-limit of the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*)? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, and how do they understand the concise and detailed marks of all phenomena as they truly are?”

“Subhūti! The absence of a limit to all-knowledge is called the characteristic of the reality-limit of all-knowledge; the absence of a limit to the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects is called the characteristic of the reality-limit of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects. Bodhisattvas mahāsattvas should understand these as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.”
“World-Honored One!

What is the mark of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) of all dharanī-doors? What is the mark of the limit of reality of all samādhi-doors? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein? And how do they understand, as they truly are, the concise and extensive marks of all dharmas?”

“Subhūti! The absence of any limit to all dhāraṇī-doors is called the mark of the reality-limit (bhūtakoṭi) of all dhāraṇī-doors; the absence of any limit to all samādhi-doors is called the mark of the reality-limit of all samādhi-doors. Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand these as they truly are and train therein, understanding the concise and detailed marks of all phenomena as they truly are.”
“World-Honored One!

What is the mark of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) of the fruit of stream-entry? What is the mark of the limit of reality of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, and how do they understand the abbreviated and detailed marks of all phenomena as they truly are?”

“Subhūti! The non-limit of the fruit of stream-entry is called the characteristic of the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) of the fruit of stream-entry; the non-limit of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhat is called the characteristic of the limit of reality of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhat. All bodhisattva mahāsattvas should understand these as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and extensive characteristics of all phenomena.”
“World-Honored One!

What is the mark of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) of the enlightenment of a solitary realizer (*pratyekabuddha*), which the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand as it truly is and train within? And how do they understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed marks of all phenomena?”

“Subhūti! The limit of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is called the characteristic of the reality-limit (bhūtakoṭi) of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha. Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand this as it truly is and train therein; they should understand, as it truly is, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.”
“World-Honored One!

What is the mark of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) in the practice of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, such that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand it as it truly is and train therein? How do they understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed marks of all dharmas?”

“Subhūti! The non-existence of any limit to the conduct of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is called the characteristic of the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) of the conduct of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand this as it truly is and train therein; they should understand, as it truly is, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.”
“World-Honored One!

What is the mark of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas, which the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand as it truly is and train in; and how do they understand, as it truly is, the concise and detailed marks of all phenomena?”

"Subhūti! The limit of the non-existence of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is called the characteristic of the reality-limit (bhūtakoṭi) of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas. All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand this as it truly is and train therein; they should understand, as it truly is, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the characteristics of the dharma-realm of form, and understands, as they truly are, the characteristics of the dharma-realms of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all dharmas."

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the characteristic of the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu) of the sense-field of the eye, and understands, as it truly is, the characteristics of the dharma-realm of the sense-fields of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the dharma-realm characteristic of the sense-sphere of form; and understands, as they truly are, the dharma-realm characteristics of the sense-spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena—this bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all dharmas.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the characteristic of the eye-element and the dharma-element; and if they understand, as it truly is, the characteristics of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-element and the dharma-element—this bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the characteristic of the dharma-realm of the form realm; and understands, as it truly is, the characteristic of the dharma-realm of sound, odor, taste, touch, and the dharma-realm—this bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the concise and detailed characteristics of all dharmas.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the characteristics of the eye-consciousness element and the dharma-element; and if they understand, as they truly are, the characteristics of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements and the dharma-element—then this bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the characteristic of the dharma-sphere of eye-contact, and understands, as it truly is, the characteristics of the dharma-spheres of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the characteristic of the dharma-realm of all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition, and understands, as it truly is, the characteristic of the dharma-realm of all feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all dharmas.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the dharmadhātu-characteristics of the earth element, and understands, as they truly are, the dharmadhātu-characteristics of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the dharma-realm characteristic of ignorance; and understands, as they truly are, the dharma-realm characteristics of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair—then this bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all dharmas.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the characteristic of the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu) of the perfection of generosity (dānapāramitā), and understands, as it truly is, the characteristics of the dharma-realm of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the characteristic of the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*) of internal emptiness; and if they understand, as it truly is, the characteristics of the dharma-realm of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—then this bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the concise and extensive characteristics of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the characteristic of the *tathatā* (suchness) and the *dharmadhātu* (dharma-realm); if they understand, as it truly is, the characteristics of the *dharmadhātu*, the *dharmatā* (nature of phenomena), non-erroneousness, immutability, equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm—then this bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the characteristic of the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu) of the noble truth of suffering, and understands, as they truly are, the characteristics of the dharma-realm of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path—then that bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the characteristics of the dharma-realm of the four dhyānas, and understands, as they truly are, the characteristics of the dharma-realm of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all dharmas.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the characteristics of the dharma-realm of the eight liberations, and understands, as they truly are, the characteristics of the dharma-realm of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and extensive characteristics of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the characteristics of the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu) of the four foundations of mindfulness; and if they understand, as they truly are, the characteristics of the dharma-realm of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path—then this bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and extensive characteristics of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the characteristic of the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu) of the gate of liberation of emptiness, and understands, as it truly is, the characteristic of the dharma-realm of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the characteristics of the dharma-realm of the five eyes, and understands, as they truly are, the characteristics of the dharma-realm of the six supernormal powers, this bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the dharmadhātu-characteristic of the ten powers of a buddha; if he understands, as it truly is, the dharmadhātu-characteristic of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha—then this bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and extensive characteristics of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the dharmadhātu-characteristic of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and understands, as they truly are, the dharmadhātu-characteristic of the state of constant equanimity, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the characteristic of the dharma-realm of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), and understands, as it truly is, the characteristics of the dharma-realm of the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), then that bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the concise and extensive characteristics of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the dharma-realm characteristic of all dhāraṇī-doors, and understands, as it truly is, the dharma-realm characteristic of all samādhi-doors, this bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and extensive characteristics of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the characteristic of the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu) of the fruit of stream-entry; if they understand, as it truly is, the characteristic of the dharma-realm of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship—then that bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the characteristic of the dharma-realm of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha, that bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the concise and extensive characteristics of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the characteristics of the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu) of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas’ practices, that bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, the concise and extensive characteristics of all phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the characteristic of the dharma-realm of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas, that bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as it truly is, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.”
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

What is the characteristic of the dharma-realm of form? What are the characteristics of the dharma-realms of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness? How do bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, and how do they understand the concise and detailed characteristics of all dharmas as they truly are?”
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

The realm of form and the realm of space are called the dharma-realm of form. This dharma-realm of form is neither severed nor differentiated, and cannot be conceptually established; this is called the characteristic of the dharma-realm of form.”

The elements of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are the space-element; this is called the dharma-element of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness. This dharma-element of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness is neither severed nor differentiated such that it could be established as a designation; this is called the characteristic of the dharma-element of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness.
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and extensive characteristics of all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!”

What is the characteristic of the sphere of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) in relation to the eye-sphere? What are the characteristics of the spheres of phenomena in relation to the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-spheres? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, understanding the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena as they truly are?

“Subhūti! The sphere of the eye and the sphere of space are called the dharma-sphere of the eye-sphere; this dharma-sphere of the eye-sphere is without interruption and without distinction, and thus can be designated—this is called the characteristic of the dharma-sphere of the eye-sphere.

The spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, together with the sphere of space, are called the dharma-spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-spheres; these dharma-spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-spheres are likewise without interruption and without distinction, and thus can be designated—this is called the characteristic of the dharma-spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-spheres.”
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!”

What is the characteristic of the *dharmadhātu* regarding the sense-field of form (*rūpāyatana*), and what are the characteristics of the *dharmadhātu* regarding the sense-fields of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental objects (*dharmāyatana*)? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, and how do they understand the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena as they truly are?

“Subhūti! The sphere of form and the element of space are called the dharma-sphere of the sphere of form; this dharma-sphere of the sphere of form is without interruption and without distinction, and cannot be conceptually established—it is called the characteristic of the dharma-sphere of the sphere of form.

The spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental objects, together with the element of space, are called the dharma-spheres of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental objects; these dharma-spheres of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental objects are likewise without interruption and without distinction, and cannot be conceptually established—they are called the characteristics of the dharma-spheres of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental objects.”
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!”

What are the characteristics of the eye-element and the dharma-element? What are the characteristics of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements and the dharma-element? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, understanding the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena as they truly are?

“Subhūti! The eye-element and the space-element are called the dharma-element of the eye-element; this dharma-element of the eye-element is without interruption and without distinction, and can be so designated—this is called the characteristic of the dharma-element of the eye-element.

The ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements and the space-element are called the dharma-elements of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements; these dharma-elements of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements are likewise without interruption and without distinction, and can be so designated—this is called the characteristic of the dharma-elements of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements.”
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and extensive characteristics of all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!”

What is the characteristic of the form-element and the dharma-element? What are the characteristics of the sound, odor, taste, touch, and dharma-elements? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein; and how do they understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena?

“Subhūti! The realm of form and the realm of space are called the dharma-realm of the realm of form; this dharma-realm of the realm of form is neither interrupted nor differentiated, and thus can be designated—this is called the characteristic of the dharma-realm of the realm of form.

The realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and phenomena, together with the realm of space, are called the dharma-realm of the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and phenomena; this dharma-realm of the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and phenomena is likewise neither interrupted nor differentiated, and thus can be designated—this is called the characteristic of the dharma-realm of the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and phenomena.”
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!”

What is the characteristic of the eye-consciousness element and the dharma element? What are the characteristics of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements and the dharma element? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein; and how do they understand, as they truly are, the concise and extensive characteristics of all phenomena?

“Subhūti! The element of eye-consciousness and the element of space are called the dharma-element of the eye-consciousness element; this dharma-element of the eye-consciousness element is without interruption and without distinction, yet it can be designated—this is called the characteristic of the dharma-element of the eye-consciousness element.

The elements of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness, together with the element of space, are called the dharma-elements of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements; these dharma-elements of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements are likewise without interruption and without distinction, yet they can be designated—this is called the characteristic of the dharma-elements of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements.”
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and extensive characteristics of all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!”

What are the characteristics of the dharma-sphere of eye-contact, and what are the characteristics of the dharma-spheres of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, and how do they understand, in their true reality, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena?

“Subhūti! The sphere of eye-contact and the sphere of space are called the sphere of phenomena associated with eye-contact; this sphere of phenomena associated with eye-contact is without interruption and without distinction, and can be so designated—this is called the characteristic of the sphere of phenomena associated with eye-contact.

The spheres of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact and the sphere of space are called the spheres of phenomena associated with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact; these spheres of phenomena associated with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact are likewise without interruption and without distinction, and can be so designated—this is called the characteristic of the spheres of phenomena associated with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact.”
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!”

What is the characteristic of the dharma-element of all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition? What is the characteristic of the dharma-element of all feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, understanding the abbreviated and extensive characteristics of all dharmas as they truly are?

“Subhūti! The element of space that is the sphere of all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition is called the dharma-element of all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition. This dharma-element of all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition is neither interrupted nor differentiated, yet it can be designated; this is called the characteristic of the dharma-element of all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.”

The element of space within all feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions is called the dharma-element of all feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions. This dharma-element of all feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions is also neither interrupted nor distinct such that it could be conceptually designated; this is called the characteristic of the dharma-element of all feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions.
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and extensive characteristics of all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!”

What is the characteristic of the earth element as the dharma-element? What are the characteristics of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements as the dharma-element? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, understanding the concise and extensive characteristics of all phenomena as they truly are?

“Subhūti! The realm of the earth-element and the realm of space are called the dharma-realm of the earth-element; this dharma-realm of the earth-element is without interruption or distinction and cannot be conceptually established—this is called the characteristic of the dharma-realm of the earth-element.

The realms of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, together with the realm of space, are called the dharma-realms of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness; these dharma-realms of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are likewise without interruption or distinction and cannot be conceptually established—this is called the characteristic of the dharma-realms of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness.”
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!”

What is the dharma-realm characteristic of ignorance? What are the dharma-realm characteristics of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, understanding the concise and detailed characteristics of all dharmas as they truly are?

“Subhūti! The realm of ignorance and the realm of space are called the dharma-realm of ignorance; this dharma-realm of ignorance is neither severed nor differentiated, and cannot be conceptually established—this is called the characteristic of the dharma-realm of ignorance.

The realms from volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, as well as the realm of space, are called the dharma-realm from volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair; this dharma-realm from volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair is likewise neither severed nor differentiated, and cannot be conceptually established—this is called the characteristic of the dharma-realm from volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair.”
"All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.
"World-Honored One!"

What is the characteristic of the dharma-realm of the perfection of generosity? What are the characteristics of the dharma-realms of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom? How do bodhisattva mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train within them, and how do they understand the concise and extensive characteristics of all phenomena as they truly are?

“Subhūti! The realm of the perfection of generosity and the realm of space are called the dharma-realm of the perfection of generosity; this dharma-realm of the perfection of generosity is without interruption and without distinction, and thus can be designated—this is called the characteristic of the dharma-realm of the perfection of generosity.

The realms of morality up to the perfection of wisdom and the realm of space are called the dharma-realms of morality up to the perfection of wisdom; these dharma-realms of morality up to the perfection of wisdom are likewise without interruption and without distinction, and thus can be designated—this is called the characteristic of the dharma-realms of morality up to the perfection of wisdom.”
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and extensive characteristics of all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!”

What is the characteristic of the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*) of internal emptiness? What is the characteristic of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena (*sarvadharma-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein; and how do they understand, according to reality, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena?

“Subhūti! The internal space-element and the space-element of emptiness are called the dharma-realm of internal emptiness. This dharma-realm of internal emptiness is without interruption and without distinction such that it can be designated; this is called the characteristic of the dharma-realm of internal emptiness.

From external emptiness up to the space-element of the emptiness of non-existence and self-nature, these are called the dharma-realms of external emptiness up to the emptiness of non-existence and self-nature. These dharma-realms of external emptiness up to the emptiness of non-existence and self-nature are likewise without interruption and without distinction such that they can be designated; this is called the characteristic of the dharma-realms of external emptiness up to the emptiness of non-existence and self-nature.”
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!”

What is the characteristic of the true suchness-dharmadhātu? What is the characteristic of the dharmadhātu, the dharma-nature (dharmatā), the non-erroneous nature, the unchanging nature, the equality, the nature free from birth, the fixedness of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these according to reality and train therein, and how do they understand the concise and extensive characteristics of all phenomena according to reality?

“Subhūti! The realm of suchness and the realm of space are called the dharma-realm of suchness; this dharma-realm of suchness is without interruption and without distinction, and cannot be conceptually established—this is called the characteristic of the dharma-realm of suchness.

From the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, these realms of space are called the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm-dharma-realm; this dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm-dharma-realm is likewise without interruption and without distinction, and cannot be conceptually established—this is called the characteristic of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm-dharma-realm.”
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!”

What is the characteristic of the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu) of the noble truth of suffering? What are the characteristics of the dharma-realm of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, and how do they understand the concise and extensive characteristics of all phenomena as they truly are?

“Subhūti! The realm of the noble truth of suffering and the realm of space are called the dharma-realm of the noble truth of suffering. This dharma-realm of the noble truth of suffering is without interruption and without distinction, such that it can be designated; this is called the characteristic of the dharma-realm of the noble truth of suffering.

The realms of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, as well as the realm of space, are called the dharma-realms of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path. These dharma-realms of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are likewise without interruption and without distinction, such that they can be designated; this is called the characteristic of the dharma-realms of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path.”
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!”

What are the characteristics of the dharma-realm of the four meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*), what are the characteristics of the dharma-realm of the four immeasurables (*apramāṇa*) and the four formless attainments (*ārūpyasamāpatti*), such that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand them as they truly are and train therein? How do they understand, as they truly are, the concise and extensive characteristics of all phenomena?

“Subhūti! The realm of the four dhyānas and the realm of space are called the dharma-realm of the four dhyānas; this dharma-realm of the four dhyānas is without interruption and without distinction, and can thus be designated—this is called the characteristic of the dharma-realm of the four dhyānas.

The realm of the four immeasurables, the realm of the four formless attainments, and the realm of space are called the dharma-realm of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments; this dharma-realm of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is likewise without interruption and without distinction, and can thus be designated—this is called the characteristic of the dharma-realm of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments.”
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!”

What is the dharma-realm characteristic of the eight liberations? What are the dharma-realm characteristics of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, understanding the concise and detailed characteristics of all dharmas as they truly are?

“Subhūti! The element of the eight liberations and the element of space are called the dharma-element of the eight liberations. This dharma-element of the eight liberations is without interruption and without distinction, such that it can be designated; this is called the characteristic of the dharma-element of the eight liberations.

The element of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities and the element of space are called the dharma-element of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities. This dharma-element of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities is likewise without interruption and without distinction, such that it can be designated; this is called the characteristic of the dharma-element of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities.”
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and extensive characteristics of all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!”

What is the characteristic of the dharma-realm of the four foundations of mindfulness? What is the characteristic of the dharma-realm of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path? How do bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, understanding the concise and detailed characteristics of all dharmas as they truly are?

“Subhūti! The realm of the four foundations of mindfulness and the realm of space are called the dharma-realm of the four foundations of mindfulness; this dharma-realm of the four foundations of mindfulness is without interruption and without distinction, and cannot be conceptually established—it is called the characteristic of the dharma-realm of the four foundations of mindfulness.

The realm of the four right endeavors up to the realm of the eight branches of the noble path and the realm of space are called the dharma-realm of the four right endeavors up to the eight branches of the noble path; this dharma-realm of the four right endeavors up to the eight branches of the noble path is likewise without interruption and without distinction, and cannot be conceptually established—it is called the characteristic of the dharma-realm of the four right endeavors up to the eight branches of the noble path.”
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and extensive characteristics of all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!”

What is the characteristic of the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu) of the gate of liberation of emptiness? What is the characteristic of the dharma-realm of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, and how do they understand the concise and extensive characteristics of all phenomena as they truly are?

“Subhūti! The realm of the gate of liberation of emptiness (*śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha-dhātu*) is the space-realm; this is called the dharma-realm of the gate of liberation of emptiness. This dharma-realm of the gate of liberation of emptiness is without interruption and without distinction, and cannot be conceptually established; this is called the characteristic of the dharma-realm of the gate of liberation of emptiness.

The realm of the gates of liberation of signlessness (*animitta*) and wishlessness (*apraṇihita*) is the space-realm; this is called the dharma-realm of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness. This dharma-realm of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness is likewise without interruption and without distinction, and cannot be conceptually established; this is called the characteristic of the dharma-realm of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.”
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!”

What is the characteristic of the dharma-realm of the five eyes, and what is the characteristic of the dharma-realm of the six supernormal powers? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, and how do they understand the concise and extensive characteristics of all dharmas as they truly are?

“Subhūti! The realm of the five eyes and the realm of space are called the dharma-realm of the five eyes; this dharma-realm of the five eyes is without interruption or distinction and cannot be conceptually established—this is called the characteristic of the dharma-realm of the five eyes.

The realm of the six supernormal powers and the realm of space are called the dharma-realm of the six supernormal powers; this dharma-realm of the six supernormal powers is likewise without interruption or distinction and cannot be conceptually established—this is called the characteristic of the dharma-realm of the six supernormal powers.”
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!”

What is the characteristic of the dharma-realm of the ten powers of a Buddha? What are the characteristics of the dharma-realm of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train within them, and how do they understand the concise and extensive characteristics of all phenomena as they truly are?

“Subhūti! The realm of the Buddha’s ten powers and the realm of space are called the dharma-realm of the Buddha’s ten powers; this dharma-realm of the Buddha’s ten powers is without interruption and without distinction, and can be thus designated—this is called the characteristic of the dharma-realm of the Buddha’s ten powers.

The realm of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha and the realm of space are called the dharma-realm of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; this dharma-realm of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is likewise without interruption and without distinction, and can be thus designated—this is called the characteristic of the dharma-realm of the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.”
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!”

What is the characteristic of the dharma-realm of the quality of non-forgetfulness? What is the characteristic of the dharma-realm of the constant abiding in equanimity? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, understanding the concise and detailed characteristics of all dharmas as they truly are?

“Subhūti! The dharma-realm of non-forgetfulness and the realm of space are called the dharma-realm of non-forgetfulness; this dharma-realm of non-forgetfulness is without interruption and without distinction, and can be so designated—this is called the characteristic of the dharma-realm of non-forgetfulness.

The dharma-realm of constant abiding in equanimity and the realm of space are called the dharma-realm of constant abiding in equanimity; this dharma-realm of constant abiding in equanimity is likewise without interruption and without distinction, and can be so designated—this is called the characteristic of the dharma-realm of constant abiding in equanimity.”
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!”

What is the characteristic of the dharma-realm of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), and what are the characteristics of the dharma-realm of the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*)? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, and how do they understand the abbreviated and extensive characteristics of all phenomena as they truly are?

“Subhūti! The realm of all-knowledge and the realm of space are called the dharma-realm of all-knowledge; this dharma-realm of all-knowledge is without interruption and without distinction, and can be thus designated—this is called the characteristic of the dharma-realm of all-knowledge.

The realm of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the realm of all-aspect knowledge, and the realm of space, are called the dharma-realm of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the dharma-realm of all-aspect knowledge; this dharma-realm of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and all-aspect knowledge is likewise without interruption and without distinction, and can be thus designated—this is called the characteristic of the dharma-realm of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and all-aspect knowledge.”
"All Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.
"World-Honored One!"

What is the characteristic of the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu) of all dhāraṇī-gates, and what is the characteristic of the dharma-realm of all samādhi-gates? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein; and how do they understand, as they truly are, the concise and extensive characteristics of all phenomena?

“Subhūti! The realm of all dhāraṇī-gates is the realm of space; this is called the dharma-realm of all dhāraṇī-gates. This dharma-realm of all dhāraṇī-gates is without interruption and without distinction, and thus can be designated; this is called the characteristic of the dharma-realm of all dhāraṇī-gates.

The realm of all samādhi-gates is the realm of space; this is called the dharma-realm of all samādhi-gates. This dharma-realm of all samādhi-gates is likewise without interruption and without distinction, and thus can be designated; this is called the characteristic of the dharma-realm of all samādhi-gates.”
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and extensive characteristics of all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!”

What is the characteristic of the dharma-realm of the fruit of stream-entry? What are the characteristics of the dharma-realm of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship? How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand these as they truly are and train therein, and how do they understand the concise and extensive characteristics of all dharmas as they truly are?

“Subhūti! The realm of the fruit of stream-entry and the realm of empty space are called the dharma-realm of the fruit of stream-entry. This dharma-realm of the fruit of stream-entry cannot be established as having any cessation or distinction; this is called the characteristic of the dharma-realm of the fruit of stream-entry.

The realm of the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the realm of arhatship and the realm of empty space are called the dharma-realm of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship. This dharma-realm of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship likewise cannot be established as having any cessation or distinction; this is called the characteristic of the dharma-realm of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship.”
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and extensive characteristics of all phenomena.
“World-Honored One!”

What is the characteristic of the dharma-realm of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha, which the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand as it truly is and train in; and how do they understand, as it truly is, the concise and extensive characteristics of all phenomena?

"Subhūti! The realm of the pratyekabuddha’s awakening and the realm of empty space are called the dharma-realm of the pratyekabuddha’s awakening. This dharma-realm of the pratyekabuddha’s awakening cannot be established as having any interruption or differentiation; this is called the characteristic of the dharma-realm of the pratyekabuddha’s awakening.
All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand it as it truly is and train therein, understanding as it truly is the concise and extensive characteristics of all dharmas."
“World-Honored One!

How do all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the characteristics of the dharma-realm? How do all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand them as they truly are and train therein? And how do they understand, as they truly are, the concise and extensive characteristics of all dharmas?”

“Subhūti! The sphere of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas’ practices is the sphere of empty space; this is called the dharma-sphere of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas’ practices. This dharma-sphere of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas’ practices is without interruption and without distinction, and cannot be conceptually established; this is called the characteristic of the dharma-sphere of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas’ practices.”
"All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.
"World-Honored One!"

What is the characteristic of the dharma-realm of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas, which the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand as it truly is and train in; and how do they understand, as it truly is, the concise and extensive characteristics of all phenomena?

“Subhūti! The realm of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is the realm of space; this is called the dharma-realm of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas. This dharma-realm of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is neither interrupted nor differentiated, yet it can be designated as such; this is called the characteristic of the dharma-realm of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas.”
"All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should understand things as they truly are and train therein; they should understand, as they truly are, the concise and detailed characteristics of all phenomena.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll Three Hundred and Fifty-eight. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: The Chapter on Many Questions and Non-duality, Sixty-one, Section Nine. At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One!"
“Furthermore, Subhūti, how should a bodhisattva mahāsattva understand the concise and extensive characteristics of all phenomena?
The Buddha said: “Subhūti!”

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva understands, as they truly are, that all phenomena are neither conjoined nor dispersed, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva should thus know the concise and extensive characteristics of all phenomena.
The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
Which are all those dharmas that are neither conjoined nor dispersed?”
The Buddha said: "Subhūti!
Form is neither conjoined nor dispersed; feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are likewise neither conjoined nor dispersed."
The sense base of the eye is neither conjoined nor dispersed; the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are likewise neither conjoined nor dispersed.
The sense base of forms is neither conjoined nor dispersed; the sense bases of sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, and mental phenomena are likewise neither conjoined nor dispersed.
The eye element is neither conjoined nor dispersed; the elements of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are likewise neither conjoined nor dispersed.
The realm of form is neither conjoined nor dispersed; the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are likewise neither conjoined nor dispersed.
The realm of eye-consciousness is neither conjoined nor dispersed; the realms of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness are likewise neither conjoined nor dispersed.
Eye-contact is neither conjoined nor dispersed; ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact are likewise neither conjoined nor dispersed.

The various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition are neither conjoined nor dissociated; the various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions are likewise neither conjoined nor dissociated.
The earth element is neither conjoined nor dissociated; the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are likewise neither conjoined nor dissociated.

Ignorance is neither conjoined nor dissociated; volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are likewise neither conjoined nor dissociated.

The perfection of generosity is neither conjoined nor disjoined; the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are likewise neither conjoined nor disjoined.

Inner emptiness is neither conjoined nor disjoined; outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are likewise neither conjoined nor disjoined.

Suchness is neither conjoined nor disjoined; the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the nature free from birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm are likewise neither conjoined nor disjoined.
The noble truth of suffering is neither conjoined nor disjoined; the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are likewise neither conjoined nor disjoined.
The four meditative concentrations are neither conjoined nor disjoined; the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are likewise neither conjoined nor disjoined.

The eight liberations are neither conjoined nor dispersed; the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases are likewise neither conjoined nor dispersed.

The four applications of mindfulness are neither conjoined nor dispersed; the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eight branches of the noble path are likewise neither conjoined nor dispersed.
The gate of liberation of emptiness is neither conjoined nor dispersed; the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are likewise neither conjoined nor dispersed.
The five eyes are neither conjoined nor dispersed; the six supernormal powers are also neither conjoined nor dispersed.

The ten powers of a Buddha are neither conjoined nor dispersed; the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are also neither conjoined nor dispersed.
The quality of non-forgetfulness is neither conjoined nor dispersed; the nature of constant abiding in equanimity is also neither conjoined nor dispersed.
All-knowledge is neither conjoined nor dispersed; the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are likewise neither conjoined nor dispersed.
All dhāraṇī-doors are neither conjoined nor dispersed; all samādhi-doors are likewise neither conjoined nor dispersed.
The fruit of stream-entry is neither conjoined nor dispersed; the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are likewise neither conjoined nor dispersed.
The enlightenment of the pratyekabuddhas is neither conjoined nor dispersed;
all the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are neither conjoined nor dispersed;
and the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas is neither conjoined nor dispersed.
The conditioned realm is neither conjoined nor dispersed; the unconditioned realm is likewise neither conjoined nor dispersed.
Why is this? "Subhūti!..."
Thus, all these phenomena lack intrinsic nature; if they lack intrinsic nature, they do not exist; and if they do not exist, it cannot be said that they have either conjunction or disjunction.
"When all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas understand all phenomena in this way, they are then able to understand their concise and extensive characteristics.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
This is called the brief summary of the six perfections; if bodhisattva mahāsattvas train in them, they will be able to accomplish much.
World-Honored One!

Thus, these perfections, summarized in brief, are what a bodhisattva mahāsattva who is newly engaged in the practice should constantly train in, and even a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwelling on the tenth stage should likewise train in them.
“World-Honored One!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva studies this concise summary of the pāramitās, they will know the abbreviated and extensive characteristics of all phenomena.
The Buddha said:
“Excellent, Subhūti! It is so, it is so!”
"It is as you have said,
Subhūti! Such a Dharma-gate can be entered by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of sharp faculties, and it can also be entered by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of middling faculties."
"Subhūti! This Dharma gate can be entered by Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas with fixed faculties, and it can also be entered by Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas with unfixed faculties."
"Subhūti! This Dharma-gate is unobstructed and unhindered; if a bodhisattva mahāsattva applies themselves single-mindedly to its study, there is nothing they cannot enter. Subhūti!"

This Dharma gate cannot be entered by those who are indolent, those whose diligence is inferior, those who have lost right mindfulness, those with distracted minds, or those who habitually practice false wisdom.

"Subhūti! This Dharma gate can be entered only by those who are not indolent, who possess superior diligence, who abide in right mindfulness, who have well-restrained their minds, and who cultivate sublime wisdom."

"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to abide in the stage of non-retrogression, wishes to abide in the tenth stage, and wishes to abide in the stage of the knowledge of all modes, they should diligently apply skillful means to enter this Dharma-gate."
“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in accordance with what is taught in this perfection of wisdom,
that bodhisattva mahāsattva will be able to progressively realize generosity, ethical discipline, patience, and diligence.”
...the dhyāna-pāramitā, and the prajñā-pāramitā, as well as the realization of internal emptiness,
external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness,
conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersal emptiness, and non-alteration emptiness, from their very origin...
The emptiness of nature, the emptiness of self-characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility,
the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence;
furthermore, they accordingly realize suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, immutability, and equality.
The nature of phenomena, the nature of detachment from birth, the fixed order of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm;
furthermore, they accordingly realize the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path;
they accordingly realize the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, the four formless absorptions, and the eight [liberations].
They also successively realize the liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities;

they also successively realize the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eight branches of the noble path;
and they also successively realize the liberations of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness.
They also successively realize the doors of liberation; they also successively realize the five eyes and the six supernormal powers;

they also successively realize the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; and they also successively realize the quality of non-forgetfulness.
They also constantly abide in equanimity, and accordingly realize all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*);
they also accordingly realize all doors of dhāraṇī and all doors of samādhi.

“Subhūti! To the extent that a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in accordance with what is taught in this profound perfection of wisdom, to that same extent that bodhisattva mahāsattva draws closer to the omniscience they seek.”

"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in accordance with what is taught in this perfection of wisdom, then whatever māra-activities may arise for that bodhisattva mahāsattva will be extinguished as soon as they occur."
Therefore, Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to swiftly eliminate all karmic obstructions and wishes to correctly embrace skillful means, they should study the perfection of wisdom.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices this perfection of wisdom, cultivates this perfection of wisdom, and trains in this perfection of wisdom, at that time all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas currently dwelling and maintaining themselves while preaching the true Dharma in the immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless worlds of the ten directions will together protect and mindfully attend to that bodhisattva mahāsattva."
Why is this? Because all Buddhas of the past, future, and present have, without exception, been born from this very Prajñāpāramitā.
Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to practice the perfection of wisdom, they should form this thought:
"The dharmas realized by all Buddhas of the past, future, and present, I too shall realize."

"In this way, Subhūti, all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should diligently train in this perfection of wisdom. If they diligently train in this perfection of wisdom, these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas will swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
Therefore, Subhūti, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should always practice the perfection of wisdom without being separated from the mental engagement associated with the knowledge of all modes.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices this perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) according to reality for even the duration of a finger-snap, the mass of merit obtained by that bodhisattva mahāsattva will be exceedingly great."

Suppose there were someone who taught all sentient beings throughout the trichiliocosm, causing them all to dwell securely in generosity, pure ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; or caused them to dwell in liberation and the knowledge and vision of liberation; or caused them to dwell in the fruits of stream-entry, once-returning, non-returning, or arhatship; or caused them to dwell in the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha. Although such a person would acquire an immeasurable mass of merit, it would still not equal that of a bodhisattva mahāsattva who practices this perfection of wisdom as it truly is for even the duration of a finger-snap.
Why is this? Subhūti!
