This perfection of wisdom can give rise to all generosity, pure ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; it can give rise to all liberations and the knowledge and vision of liberation; it can give rise to the fruits of stream-entry, once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship; it can give rise to the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha; and it can give rise to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

All the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas currently existing in the infinite, countless, and boundless worlds of the ten directions have all appeared by means of this very Prajñāpāramitā; all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past have all appeared by means of this very Prajñāpāramitā; and all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the future will all appear by means of this very Prajñāpāramitā.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to practice the perfection of wisdom without being separated from mental attention associated with the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), whether for a brief moment, or half a day, or for one..."
Whether for a day, or a month, or a year, or a hundred years, or an eon (*kalpa*), or a hundred eons,
or even for incalculable eons, the mass of merit obtained by this bodhisattva mahāsattva is exceedingly vast,
surpassing that of one who teaches and transforms beings in each of the ten directions.

Suppose all sentient beings in worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges were each established in generosity, pure ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; or were established in liberation and the knowledge and vision of liberation;
or were established in the stages of stream-entry, once-returning, non-returning, or arhatship.
Or the mass of merit obtained by causing others to abide in the fruit of arhatship, or in the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha.
Why is this so? Subhūti!

Because it is from this perfection of wisdom that all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past, future, and present arise; because they, for the sake of all sentient beings, truly establish the practices of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; because they, for the sake of all sentient beings, truly establish liberation and the knowledge and vision of liberation; because they, for the sake of all sentient beings, truly establish the fruits of stream-entry, once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship; and because they, for the sake of all sentient beings, truly establish the enlightenment of pratyekabuddhas and the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas—this accumulation of merit surpasses the former.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva abides in accordance with what is taught in this perfection of wisdom, you should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva is no longer subject to regression. They are constantly protected and remembered by all Buddhas; they have accomplished the most supreme skill in means; they have already approached, attended upon, and made offerings to immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of Buddhas; and they have already planted immeasurable, distinguished roots of goodness in the presence of those Buddhas."
"You should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has already been sustained by immeasurable true spiritual friends;
they have long practiced the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom;
and they have long dwelt in internal emptiness, external emptiness, and internal-and-external emptiness."
Emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of the conditioned, the emptiness of the unconditioned,
absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of specific characteristics,
the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, and the emptiness of non-existence.
They have long been established in emptiness, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence;
they abide in suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the state of non-falsity, the state of immutability, equality, the state beyond birth,
the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm.
For a long time they have dwelt securely in the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path;
for a long time they have practiced the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments;

for a long time they have practiced the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative absorptions, and the ten totalities; and for a long time they have practiced the four foundations of mindfulness.
...the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path;
they have long practiced the gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness;
they have long practiced the five eyes and the six supernormal powers; they have long practiced the ten powers of a Buddha and the four [assurances]...
The fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity;
the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; the quality of non-forgetfulness long cultivated, and the state of constant abiding in equanimity;
and all the doors of dhāraṇī and all the doors of samādhi long cultivated.
They have long cultivated all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).

It should be known that this bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in the stage of a youth (*kumārabhūmi*); none of their aspirations remain unfulfilled. They constantly behold the Buddhas without ever abandoning them for a moment; they never forsake any roots of goodness (*kuśalamūla*); they are always able to bring all sentient beings to maturity and constantly adorn and purify all Buddha-fields. From one Buddha-field they proceed to another Buddha-field, reverently making offerings to the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, and listening to and practicing the teachings of the Unsurpassed Dharma.

"You should know that this bodhisattva-mahāsattva has already attained uninterrupted and inexhaustible eloquence; has already attained the dharma of the most excellent dhāraṇīs; has accomplished the most supreme and subtle form-body; has already received the perfect prediction from all Buddhas; and has already attained mastery over assuming various forms of existence as he pleases for the sake of liberating sentient beings."
"You should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva is skilled in knowing the gate of the object of focus, skilled in knowing the gate of the mode of activity;
skilled in knowing the gate of syllables, skilled in knowing the gate of non-syllables;
skilled in knowing speech, and skilled in knowing non-speech."
He is skilled in knowing the single designation, skilled in knowing the dual designation, and skilled in knowing the plural designation;
he is skilled in knowing the feminine designation, skilled in knowing the masculine designation, and skilled in knowing the designation that is neither feminine nor masculine;
he is skilled in knowing the past designation, skilled in knowing the future designation, and skilled in knowing the present designation.
He is well-versed in all literary expressions and well-versed in all meanings.

It should be known that this bodhisattva mahāsattva is well-versed in form (*rūpa*), well-versed in sensation (*vedanā*), well-versed in perception (*saṃjñā*), well-versed in mental formations (*saṃskāra*), and well-versed in consciousness (*vijñāna*);
he is well-versed in the aggregates (*skandha*), well-versed in the elements (*dhātu*), and well-versed in the sense bases (*āyatana*).
He skillfully understands dependent origination and skillfully understands the factors of dependent origination;
he skillfully understands the nature of the world and skillfully understands the nature of nirvana;

he skillfully understands the characteristics of the dharma-realm, skillfully understands the characteristics of conditioned formations, and skillfully understands the characteristics of the unconditioned.

They skillfully know the characteristics of the conditioned, they skillfully know the characteristics of the unconditioned, and they skillfully know the characteristics of both the conditioned and the unconditioned;
they skillfully know the characteristic of characteristics, and they skillfully know the characteristic of non-characteristics;
they skillfully know existence, and they skillfully know non-existence.
They skillfully know their own nature and skillfully know the nature of others;
they skillfully know conjunction and skillfully know dispersion, and skillfully know both conjunction and dispersion;
they skillfully know association and skillfully know non-association, and skillfully know both association and non-association.

He is skilled in knowing suchness; skilled in knowing the nature of non-falsity; skilled in knowing the nature of non-alteration; skilled in knowing the dharma-nature; skilled in knowing the dharma-realm; skilled in knowing the fixedness of dharmas; skilled in knowing the abiding of dharmas;
skilled in knowing the nature of conditions; skilled in knowing the nature of non-conditions;
and skilled in knowing all the noble truths.
He is skilled in knowing the meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*), skilled in knowing the immeasurables (*apramāṇa*), and skilled in knowing the formless attainments (*ārūpyasamāpatti*);
he is skilled in knowing the six perfections (*ṣaṭpāramitā*);

he is skilled in knowing the four foundations of mindfulness (*smṛtyupasthāna*), skilled in knowing the four right endeavors (*samyakprahāṇa*), skilled in knowing the four bases of power (*ṛddhipāda*), skilled in knowing the five faculties (*indriya*), skilled in knowing the five powers (*bala*), skilled in knowing the seven factors of enlightenment (*bodhyaṅga*), and skilled in knowing the eightfold noble path (*āryāṣṭāṅgamārga*).

They skillfully know the eight liberations; they skillfully know the eight bases of mastery; they skillfully know the nine successive meditative attainments; they skillfully know the ten spheres of totality;
they skillfully know the doors of dhāraṇī; they skillfully know the doors of samādhi;
they skillfully know the liberation door of emptiness, the liberation door of signlessness, and the liberation door of wishlessness.
They skillfully know all dharmas of emptiness;
they skillfully know the five eyes and skillfully know the six supernormal powers;

they skillfully know the ten powers of a Buddha, skillfully know the four fearlessnesses, and skillfully know the four analytical knowledges; they skillfully know great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, and great equanimity; and they skillfully know the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
They are skilled in knowing the quality of non-forgetfulness; they are skilled in knowing the state of constant abiding in equanimity;

they are skilled in knowing all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), skilled in knowing the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and skilled in knowing the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*);
they are skilled in knowing the conditioned realm (*saṃskṛtadhātu*) and skilled in knowing the unconditioned realm (*asaṃskṛtadhātu*).
They skillfully know the elements and skillfully know what is not an element.

"It should be known that this bodhisattva mahāsattva skillfully knows the mental attention toward form, and skillfully knows the mental attention toward feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness;
they skillfully know the mental attention toward the sense-base of the eye, and skillfully know the mental attention toward the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind."
He is skilled in the mental attention to the sphere of forms; he is skilled in the mental attention to the spheres of sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, and mental phenomena.
He is skilled in the mental attention to the eye constituent; he is skilled in the mental attention to the constituents of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.
He is skilled in the mental attention to the form constituent; he is skilled in the mental attention to the constituents of sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, and mental phenomena.

He skillfully understands the mental attention regarding the eye-consciousness element; he skillfully understands the mental attention regarding the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements.
He skillfully understands the mental attention regarding eye-contact; he skillfully understands the mental attention regarding ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact.

He skillfully understands the mental attention regarding all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition; he skillfully understands the mental attention regarding all feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as condition.
He is skilled in the mental attention to the earth element; he is skilled in the mental attention to the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements;

he is skilled in the mental attention to ignorance; he is skilled in the mental attention to volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair;

he is skilled in the mental attention to the perfection of generosity; and he is skilled in the mental attention to the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.

He is skilled in the mental engagement with internal emptiness; he is skilled in the mental engagement with external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, emptiness of dispersion, emptiness of non-alteration, essential emptiness, emptiness of self-characteristic, emptiness of common characteristic, emptiness of all phenomena, emptiness of non-apprehensibility, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, and emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.

He is skilled in the mental engagement with suchness; he is skilled in the mental engagement with the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, non-alteration, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm.
He is skilled in the mental attention to the noble truth of suffering; he is skilled in the mental attention to the noble truths of its origin, its cessation, and the path;

he is skilled in the mental attention to the four foundations of mindfulness; he is skilled in the mental attention to the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path;
he is skilled in the mental attention to the four dhyānas; and he is skilled in the mental attention to the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments.

They are skilled in the mental attention to the eight liberations; they are skilled in the mental attention to the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases;
they are skilled in the mental attention to all doors of dhāraṇī; they are skilled in the mental attention to all doors of samādhi;
they are skilled in the mental attention to the door of liberation that is emptiness; and they are skilled in the mental attention to the doors of liberation that are signlessness and wishlessness.
He is skilled in the mental engagement with the five eyes; he is skilled in the mental engagement with the six supernormal powers;

he is skilled in the mental engagement with the ten powers of a Buddha; he is skilled in the mental engagement with the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
he is skilled in the mental engagement with the quality of non-forgetfulness; and he is skilled in the mental engagement with the nature of constant abiding in equanimity.

They skillfully understand the mental engagement with omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), and they skillfully understand the mental engagements with the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).

"It should be known that this bodhisattva mahāsattva skillfully understands that form (*rūpa*) is empty of the characteristic of form, and skillfully understands that feeling (*vedanā*), perception (*saṃjñā*), formations (*saṃskāra*), and consciousness (*vijñāna*) are empty of the characteristics of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness;

he skillfully understands that the eye-base (*cakṣur-āyatana*) is empty of the characteristic of the eye-base, and skillfully understands that the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-bases (*śrotra-ghrāṇa-jihvā-kāya-manas-āyatana*) are empty of the characteristics of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-bases."

He skillfully knows that the sphere of form is empty of the characteristics of the sphere of form; he skillfully knows that the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental objects are empty of the characteristics of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental objects.

He skillfully knows that the eye-element is empty of the characteristics of the eye-element; he skillfully knows that the elements of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are empty of the characteristics of the elements of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.

He skillfully knows that the element of forms is empty of the characteristics of the element of forms; he skillfully knows that the elements of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental objects are empty of the characteristics of the elements of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental objects.

He skillfully knows that the eye-consciousness element is empty of the characteristics of the eye-consciousness element; he skillfully knows that the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements are empty of the characteristics of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements.

He skillfully knows that eye-contact is empty of the characteristics of eye-contact; he skillfully knows that ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact are empty of the characteristics of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact.

He skillfully knows that all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are empty of the characteristics of all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition; he skillfully knows that all feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions are empty of the characteristics of all feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions.

They skillfully know that the earth element is empty of the characteristics of the earth element; they skillfully know that the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are empty of the characteristics of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements.

They skillfully know that ignorance is empty of the characteristics of ignorance; they skillfully know that volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are empty of the characteristics of volitional formations through to old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.

They skillfully know that the perfection of generosity is empty of the characteristics of the perfection of generosity; they skillfully know that the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are empty of the characteristics of ethical discipline through to wisdom.

They skillfully know that internal emptiness is empty of the characteristic of internal emptiness; they skillfully know that external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—from external emptiness up to the emptiness of the characteristic of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—are likewise empty.

They skillfully know that suchness is empty of the characteristic of suchness; they skillfully know that the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-falsity, the non-alteration, the equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm are all empty of the characteristics of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm.

They skillfully know that the noble truth of suffering is empty of the characteristic of the noble truth of suffering; they skillfully know that the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are empty of the characteristics of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path.

They skillfully know that the four foundations of mindfulness are empty of the characteristics of the four foundations of mindfulness; they skillfully know that the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are all empty of the characteristics of the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path.

They skillfully know that the four dhyānas are empty of the characteristics of the four dhyānas; they skillfully know that the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are empty of the characteristics of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions;

they skillfully know that the eight liberations are empty of the characteristics of the eight liberations; they skillfully know that the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are empty of the characteristics of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities;

they skillfully know that all doors of dhāraṇī are empty of the characteristics of all doors of dhāraṇī; and they skillfully know that all doors of samādhi are empty of the characteristics of all doors of samādhi.

He skillfully knows that the gate of liberation of emptiness is empty of the characteristics of the gate of liberation of emptiness; he skillfully knows that the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are empty of the characteristics of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.

He skillfully knows that the five eyes are empty of the characteristics of the five eyes; he skillfully knows that the six supernormal powers are empty of the characteristics of the six supernormal powers.

He skillfully knows that the ten powers of a Buddha are empty of the characteristics of the ten powers of a Buddha; he skillfully knows that the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha—from the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha—are empty of the characteristics of the four fearlessnesses through to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.

They skillfully know that the quality of non-forgetfulness is empty of the characteristic of non-forgetfulness; they skillfully know that the state of constant abiding in equanimity is empty of the characteristic of constant abiding in equanimity.

They skillfully know that all-knowledge is empty of the characteristic of all-knowledge; they skillfully know that the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are empty of the characteristics of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects.

They skillfully know that the fruit of stream-entry is empty of the characteristic of the fruit of stream-entry; they skillfully know that the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship are empty of the characteristics of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship.
They skillfully know that the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is empty of the characteristics of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha;
they skillfully know that all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are empty of the characteristics of the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas;

and they skillfully know that the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas is empty of the characteristics of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas.
"You should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva well understands the path of cessation and well understands the path of non-cessation;
he well understands arising, well understands cessation, and well understands abiding and change;
he well understands greed, hatred, and delusion, and well understands non-greed, non-hatred, and non-delusion."
He skillfully knows views and skillfully knows non-views;
he skillfully knows wrong views and skillfully knows non-wrong views;

he skillfully knows all views, obsessions (*paryavasthāna*), latent tendencies (*anuśaya*), and fetters (*bandhana*), and he skillfully knows the abandonment of all views, obsessions, latent tendencies, and fetters.
He skillfully knows name, skillfully knows form, and skillfully knows both name and form;

he skillfully knows the causal condition (*hetu-pratyaya*), skillfully knows the immediately preceding condition (*samanantara-pratyaya*), skillfully knows the object condition (*ālambana-pratyaya*), and skillfully knows the dominant condition (*adhipati-pratyaya*);
he skillfully knows conduct (*caryā*) and skillfully knows liberation (*vimukti*).
He is skilled in knowing characteristics and skilled in knowing signs;
he is skilled in knowing suffering, skilled in knowing its origin, skilled in knowing its cessation, and skilled in knowing the path;
he is skilled in knowing the hells and skilled in knowing the path to the hells.
He is skilled in knowing the animal realm and skilled in knowing the path to the animal realm;
he is skilled in knowing the realm of hungry ghosts and skilled in knowing the path to the realm of hungry ghosts;
he is skilled in knowing human beings and skilled in knowing the path to the human realm.
He well knows the devas and well knows the path to the devas;
he well knows the stream-enterer, well knows the fruit of stream-entry, and well knows the path of stream-entry;
he well knows the once-returner, well knows the fruit of once-returning, and well knows the path of once-returning.
He skillfully knows the non-returner, skillfully knows the fruit of non-returning, and skillfully knows the path of the non-returner;
he skillfully knows the arhat, skillfully knows the fruit of arhatship, and skillfully knows the path of the arhat;
he skillfully knows the pratyekabuddha, skillfully knows the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, and skillfully knows the path of the pratyekabuddha.
They are skilled in knowing bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; they are skilled in knowing the conduct of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas;
they are skilled in knowing the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas;
and they are skilled in knowing unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
He skillfully knows all-knowledge and skillfully knows the path to all-knowledge;
he skillfully knows the knowledge of the aspects of the path and skillfully knows the path to the knowledge of the aspects of the path;
he skillfully knows the knowledge of all aspects and skillfully knows the path to the knowledge of all aspects.
He is skilled in knowing the faculties; he is skilled in knowing the perfection of the faculties; he is skilled in knowing the superiority and inferiority of the faculties.

He is skilled in knowing wisdom; he is skilled in knowing swift wisdom; he is skilled in knowing powerful wisdom; he is skilled in knowing sharp wisdom; he is skilled in knowing rapid wisdom; he is skilled in knowing penetrating wisdom; he is skilled in knowing expansive wisdom; he is skilled in knowing profound wisdom; he is skilled in knowing great wisdom; he is skilled in knowing incomparable wisdom; he is skilled in knowing true wisdom; he is skilled in knowing jewel-like wisdom.
He is skilled in knowing the past world, skilled in knowing the future world, and skilled in knowing the present world.
He is skilled in knowing skillful means;
he is skilled in knowing intentions, skilled in knowing resolute intentions;
and he is skilled in knowing how to regard sentient beings.
He is skilled in knowing the characteristics of words and their meanings;
he is skilled in knowing all the noble dharmas;
and he is skilled in knowing the skillful means for establishing the three vehicles.

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, draws forth the perfection of wisdom, and cultivates the perfection of wisdom, they will obtain such meritorious benefits as these.”
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
how should a bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the perfection of wisdom?”
"How should one draw forth the perfection of wisdom?
How should one cultivate the perfection of wisdom?
The Buddha said:
“Subhūti! Because they perceive that form is quiescent, destructible, lacking self-mastery, illusory in essence, and unsubstantial, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should practice the perfection of wisdom;

because they perceive that feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are quiescent, destructible, lacking self-mastery, illusory in essence, and unsubstantial, they should practice the perfection of wisdom.”
“Subhūti! Because the sphere of the eye is quiescent, destructible, lacking self-mastery, illusory in essence, and unsubstantial, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should practice the perfection of wisdom;
because the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are quiescent, destructible, lacking self-mastery, illusory in essence, and unsubstantial, he should practice the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! Because the sphere of form (*rūpāyatana*) is quiescent, destructible, lacking self-mastery, illusory in essence, and unsubstantial, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should practice the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).

Because the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena (*dharmāyatana*) are quiescent, destructible, lacking self-mastery, illusory in essence, and unsubstantial, one should practice the perfection of wisdom.”
“Subhūti! Because the eye-element is quiescent, destructible, lacking self-mastery, illusory in essence, and unsubstantial, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should practice the perfection of wisdom;
because the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements are quiescent, destructible, lacking self-mastery, illusory in essence, and unsubstantial, he should practice the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! Because the realm of form (*rūpadhātu*) is quiescent, destructible, lacking sovereignty, illusory in essence, and unsubstantial, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should practice the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).

Because the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) are quiescent, destructible, lacking sovereignty, illusory in essence, and unsubstantial, they should practice the perfection of wisdom.”

"Subhūti! Because the eye-consciousness element is quiescent, destructible, lacking self-mastery, illusory in essence, and unsubstantial, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should practice the perfection of wisdom;

because the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements are quiescent, destructible, lacking self-mastery, illusory in essence, and unsubstantial, they should practice the perfection of wisdom."
“Subhūti! Because the contact of the eye is quiescent, destructible, lacking self-mastery, illusory in essence, and unsubstantial, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should practice the perfection of wisdom;

because the contacts of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are quiescent, destructible, lacking self-mastery, illusory in essence, and unsubstantial, they should practice the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! A bodhisattva mahāsattva should practice the perfection of wisdom by contemplating that all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are quiescent, destructible, lacking self-mastery, illusory in essence, and unsubstantial;

and by contemplating that all feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions are quiescent, destructible, lacking self-mastery, illusory in essence, and unsubstantial, he should practice the perfection of wisdom.”
“Subhūti! Because the earth element is quiescent, destructible, lacking autonomy, illusory in nature, and unsubstantial, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should practice the perfection of wisdom;
because the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are quiescent, destructible, lacking autonomy, illusory in nature, and unsubstantial, they should practice the perfection of wisdom.”
“Subhūti! A bodhisattva mahāsattva should practice the perfection of wisdom by contemplating that ignorance is quiescent, destructible, lacking self-mastery, illusory in essence, and unsubstantial;

and they should practice the perfection of wisdom by contemplating that volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are quiescent, destructible, lacking self-mastery, illusory in essence, and unsubstantial.”

“Subhūti! Regarding your question as to how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should draw forth the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), a bodhisattva mahāsattva should draw forth the perfection of wisdom just as one draws forth the emptiness of emptiness.”

"Subhūti! As for your question regarding how a bodhisattva mahāsattva should cultivate the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā): a bodhisattva mahāsattva should cultivate the perfection of wisdom in the same manner as they cultivate the emptiness of emptiness (śūnyatā-śūnyatā)."
The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
for how long must a bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the perfection of wisdom, draw forth the perfection of wisdom, and cultivate the perfection of wisdom?”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

From the first generation of the mind of awakening until sitting upon the seat of sublime enlightenment, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should practice the perfection of wisdom, should draw forth the perfection of wisdom, and should cultivate the perfection of wisdom.”
The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
abiding in what kind of mind without interruption should a bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the perfection of wisdom, draw forth the perfection of wisdom, and cultivate the perfection of wisdom?”
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

From the first generation of the mind of awakening until sitting upon the seat of sublime enlightenment, a bodhisattva mahāsattva must not allow any other mental engagements to arise; rather, constantly abiding in mental engagement associated with the knowledge of all modes, they should practice the perfection of wisdom, draw forth the perfection of wisdom, and cultivate the perfection of wisdom.”

This bodhisattva mahāsattva should practice the perfection of wisdom in this way, should draw forth the perfection of wisdom in this way, and should cultivate the perfection of wisdom in this way, until they are able to prevent the mind and mental factors from turning toward objects.
“World-Honored One!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, draws forth the perfection of wisdom, and cultivates the perfection of wisdom, will they attain the knowledge of all modes?”
"No, World-Honored One!
[It is not so], Subhūti.
"World-Honored One!"

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not practice the perfection of wisdom, does not bring forth the perfection of wisdom, and does not cultivate the perfection of wisdom, will they attain the knowledge of all modes?
"No, World-Honored One!
Subhūti, [it is not so].
"World-Honored One! [Subhūti replied.]

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva neither practices nor does not practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), neither brings forth nor does not bring forth the perfection of wisdom, and neither cultivates nor does not cultivate the perfection of wisdom, will they attain the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna)?
"No, World-Honored One!
Subhūti, [it is not so]. World-Honored One!"

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva neither practices nor does not practice the perfection of wisdom, neither draws toward nor does not draw toward the perfection of wisdom, and neither cultivates nor does not cultivate the perfection of wisdom, will they attain the knowledge of all modes?
"No, World-Honored One!
Subhūti, [it is not so]. World-Honored One!"
"If that is so, how shall a bodhisattva mahāsattva attain the knowledge of all modes? "Subhūti,
a bodhisattva mahāsattva shall attain the knowledge of all modes in the manner of suchness."
“World-Honored One!
What is suchness? “Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [Listen.]”
"It is like the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi). “World-Honored One,
what is the limit of reality?”
“Subhūti, it is like the dharma-realm.
“World-Honored One!”
"What is the dharma-realm? "Subhūti,

it is like the realm of the self, the realm of sentient beings, the realm of the life-principle, the realm of the born, the realm of the nourisher, the realm of the person, and the realm of the individual."
“World-Honored One!

What are the realm of the self, the realm of sentient beings, the realm of the life-principle, the realm of the born, the realm of the nourisher, the realm of the person, and the realm of the individual?”
The Buddha said to Subhūti: "What do you think?
Can a self, a sentient being, a life-force, a living being, a nourisher, a person, or an individual be apprehended?"
Subhūti replied, “No, World-Honored One!”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti! Since a self,

a sentient being, a life-principle, a living being, a nourisher, a person, or an individual cannot be apprehended, how could I designate a realm of self, a realm of sentient beings, a realm of life-principles, a realm of living beings, a realm of nourishers, a realm of persons, or a realm of individuals?
Thus it is, Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not designate the perfection of wisdom, nor does he designate omniscience or any phenomena, that bodhisattva mahāsattva will certainly realize omniscience.
Then, the Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha,
saying: “World-Honored One,

is it only the perfection of wisdom that cannot be designated, or are the perfections of meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity also incapable of being designated?”
The Buddha said: “Subhūti!
It is not only the perfection of wisdom that cannot be designated; the perfections of concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity likewise cannot be designated.”

"Subhūti! Whether they be the dharmas of śrāvakas, the dharmas of pratyekabuddhas, the dharmas of bodhisattvas, the dharmas of buddhas, or conditioned dharmas or unconditioned dharmas—all such dharmas are ultimately incapable of being designated."
The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

If all dharmas are entirely incapable of being designated, how can one designate: ‘this is hell,’ ‘this is the animal realm,’ ‘this is the realm of hungry ghosts,’ ‘this is a human,’ ‘this is a deva,’ ‘this is a stream-enterer,’ ‘this is a once-returner,’ ‘this is a non-returner,’ ‘this is an arhat,’ ‘this is a pratyekabuddha,’ ‘this is a bodhisattva,’ ‘these are the Buddhas,’ or ‘these are all dharmas’?”
The Buddha said,
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin, what do you think?”
"Can the designation of sentient beings and the designation of phenomena be truly apprehended? Subhūti replied, "No!"
“World-Honored One!
The Buddha said, “Sudhana!”

The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they should train by not giving rise to any conditioned formations regarding form as being either existent or non-existent; they should likewise train by not giving rise to any conditioned formations regarding feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness as being either existent or non-existent.”

“Subhūti! The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:

The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they should train by contemplating that form is empty of the characteristic of form; they should train by contemplating that feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are empty of the characteristics of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness.”
Thus it is, Subhūti!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they should train by observing that the self-characteristics of all phenomena are empty.

Thus it is, Subhūti!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they should train by contemplating that the self-characteristics of all phenomena are empty.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they should train by contemplating that the sphere of form is empty of the characteristic of the sphere of form; they should train by contemplating that the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are empty of the characteristics of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena.”

when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they should train by contemplating that the self-characteristics of all phenomena are empty.
