In this way, Subhūti,
when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they should train by observing that the specific characteristics of all phenomena are empty.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they should train by contemplating that all bodhisattva mahāsattvas and all aspects of the conduct of bodhisattva mahāsattvas are empty.”
Thus it is, Subhūti!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they should train by contemplating that the self-characteristics of all phenomena are empty.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they should train by contemplating that the unexcelled, perfect enlightenment of all buddhas is empty of the characteristics of the unexcelled, perfect enlightenment of all buddhas.”
Thus it is, Subhūti!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they should train by contemplating that the self-characteristics of all phenomena are empty.
The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying: “World-Honored One,

if form is empty of the characteristic of form, and feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are empty of the characteristics of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, how should a bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the perfection of wisdom?”
“World-Honored One!

If the eye-base is empty of the characteristic of the eye-base, and the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases are empty of the characteristics of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases, how should a bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the perfection of wisdom?”
“World-Honored One!

If the sphere of form is empty of the characteristic of the sphere of form, and if the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena are empty of the characteristics of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena, how should a bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the perfection of wisdom?”
“World-Honored One!

If the eye-element is empty of the characteristics of the eye-element, and if the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements are empty of the characteristics of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements, how should a bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the perfection of wisdom?”
“World-Honored One!

If the form realm is empty of the characteristics of the form realm, and if the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and phenomena are empty of the characteristics of the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and phenomena, how should a bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the perfection of wisdom?”
“World-Honored One!

If the eye-consciousness element is empty of the characteristics of the eye-consciousness element, and if the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements are empty of the characteristics of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements, how should a bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the perfection of wisdom?”
“World-Honored One!

If eye-contact is empty of the characteristic of eye-contact, and if ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact are empty of the characteristics of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact, how should a bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the perfection of wisdom?”
“World-Honored One!

If the various feelings arising with eye-contact as condition are empty of the characteristics of feelings arising with eye-contact as condition, and if the various feelings arising with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions are empty of the characteristics of feelings arising with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions, how should a bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the perfection of wisdom?”
“World-Honored One!

If the earth element is empty of the characteristic of the earth element, and the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are each empty of the characteristics of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements, how should a bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the perfection of wisdom?”
“World-Honored One!

If ignorance is empty of the characteristic of ignorance, and if volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are likewise empty of the characteristics of old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair, how then should a bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the perfection of wisdom?”
“World-Honored One!

If the perfection of giving is empty of the characteristic of the perfection of giving, and if the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are empty of the characteristics of the perfections of ethical discipline through to wisdom, how should a bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the perfection of wisdom?”
“World-Honored One!

If internal emptiness is empty of the characteristic of internal emptiness, and if external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—down to the emptiness of the characteristic of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—are likewise empty, how should a bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the perfection of wisdom?”
“World-Honored One!

If true thusness (tathatā) is empty of the characteristic of true thusness, and if the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the dharma-nature (dharmatā), the non-erroneous nature, the unchanging nature, the nature of equality, the nature of being free from arising, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm—from the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm—are empty of the characteristics of the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm, how should a bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā)?”
“World-Honored One!

If the noble truth of suffering is empty of the characteristic of the noble truth of suffering, and if the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are empty of the characteristics of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path, how should a bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the perfection of wisdom?”
“World-Honored One!

If the four foundations of mindfulness are empty of the characteristic of the four foundations of mindfulness, and if the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path—from the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path—are empty of the characteristics of the four right endeavors through to the eightfold noble path, how should a bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the perfection of wisdom?”
“World-Honored One!

If the four dhyānas are empty of the characteristics of the four dhyānas, and the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are empty of the characteristics of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, how should a bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the perfection of wisdom?”
“World-Honored One!

If the eight liberations are empty of the characteristics of the eight liberations, and if the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are empty of the characteristics of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities, how should a bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the perfection of wisdom?”
“World-Honored One!

If all doors of samādhi are empty of the characteristics of all doors of samādhi, and all doors of dhāraṇī are empty of the characteristics of all doors of dhāraṇī, how should a bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the perfection of wisdom?”
“World-Honored One!

If the gate of liberation of emptiness is empty of the characteristics of the gate of liberation of emptiness, and if the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are empty of the characteristics of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, how should a bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the perfection of wisdom?”
“World-Honored One!

If the five eyes are empty of the characteristics of the five eyes, and the six supernormal powers are empty of the characteristics of the six supernormal powers, how should a bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the perfection of wisdom?”
“World-Honored One!

If the ten powers of a Buddha are empty of the characteristics of the ten powers of a Buddha, and if the four fearlessnesses, the four unhindered understandings, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha—from the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha—are empty of the characteristics of those [qualities], how should a bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the perfection of wisdom?”
“World-Honored One!

If the quality of non-forgetfulness is empty of the characteristic of non-forgetfulness, and the state of constant equanimity is empty of the characteristic of constant equanimity, how should a bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the perfection of wisdom?”
“World-Honored One!

If all-knowledge is empty of the characteristic of all-knowledge, and the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are empty of the characteristics of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects, how should a bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the perfection of wisdom?”
“World-Honored One!

If the fruit of stream-entry is empty of the characteristics of the fruit of stream-entry, and if the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are empty of the characteristics of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship, how should a bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the perfection of wisdom?”
“World-Honored One!
If the awakening of a pratyekabuddha is empty of the characteristics of the awakening of a pratyekabuddha, how should a bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the perfection of wisdom?”
“World-Honored One!
If all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the signs of all bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices which are empty, how should a bodhisattva-mahāsattva practice the perfection of wisdom?”
“World-Honored One!

If the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas is empty of the characteristics of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas, how should a bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the perfection of wisdom?”
The Buddha said,
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices nothing at all, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
for what reason is it that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva has no practice at all, this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom?”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Because this *prajñāpāramitā* cannot be apprehended, the bodhisattva mahāsattva also cannot be apprehended; the practice cannot be apprehended, nor can the one who practices, that by which one practices, or the locus where one practices—all these are unapprehendable.”
Therefore, Subhūti, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva has no practice whatsoever, this is practicing the perfection of wisdom, because within it all conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*) is unfindable.
The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,

if a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom by practicing nothing at all, how should a bodhisattva mahāsattva who is a beginner in their practice cultivate the perfection of wisdom?”
The Buddha said,
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
From the first production of the thought of awakening, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should always train in the non-apprehension of all phenomena.”
“Subhūti! When this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices generosity, he should practice generosity by means of non-apprehension;
when he practices ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, he should practice ethical discipline up to wisdom by means of non-apprehension.”
“Subhūti! When this bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in internal emptiness, he should dwell in internal emptiness by means of non-apprehension as his skillful method;

when he dwells in external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, he should dwell in external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence by means of non-apprehension as his skillful method.”
“Subhūti! When this bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in suchness (*tathatā*), he should dwell in suchness by means of non-apprehension as his skillful method;

when he dwells in the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), non-falsity, non-alteration, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*), he should dwell in the realm of phenomena up to the inconceivable realm by means of non-apprehension as his skillful method.”
“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the four foundations of mindfulness, he should practice them by means of non-apprehension;

when he practices the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path, he should practice the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path by means of non-apprehension.”
“Subhūti! When this bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in the noble truth of suffering, he should dwell in the noble truth of suffering by means of non-apprehension as his expedient;
when he dwells in the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, he should dwell in the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path by means of non-apprehension as his expedient.”
“Subhūti! When these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the four dhyānas, they should practice the four dhyānas by means of non-apprehension as their skillful method;

when they practice the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, they should practice the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments by means of non-apprehension as their skillful method.”
"Subhūti! When this bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the gate of liberation of emptiness, he should cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness by means of non-apprehension as the skillful method;

when cultivating the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, he should cultivate the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness by means of non-apprehension as the skillful method."
"Subhūti! When this bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the eight liberations, they should cultivate the eight liberations by means of non-apprehension as the skillful method;

when cultivating the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities, they should cultivate the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities by means of non-apprehension as the skillful method."
“Subhūti! When this bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the gateways of samādhi, he should cultivate the gateways of samādhi by means of non-apprehension as the skillful method;
when he cultivates the gateways of dhāraṇī, he should cultivate the gateways of dhāraṇī by means of non-apprehension as the skillful method.”
“Subhūti! When these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas cultivate the five eyes, they should cultivate the five eyes by means of non-apprehension as their skillful method;
when they cultivate the six supernormal powers, they should cultivate the six supernormal powers by means of non-apprehension as their skillful method.”
“Subhūti! When this bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the ten powers of a buddha, he should cultivate the ten powers of a buddha by means of non-apprehension as his skillful method;

when he cultivates the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, he should cultivate the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha by means of non-apprehension as his skillful method.”
“Subhūti! When this bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the quality of non-forgetfulness, he should cultivate that quality of non-forgetfulness by means of non-apprehension;
when he cultivates the nature of constant equanimity, he should cultivate that nature of constant equanimity by means of non-apprehension.”
"Subhūti! When this bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), they should cultivate all-knowledge by means of non-apprehension as their skillful method;

when cultivating the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), they should cultivate the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects by means of non-apprehension as their skillful method."
The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
to what extent is one said to have ‘attainment’?”
“By what standard, Subhūti, is it called ‘non-attainment’? The Buddha said, “Subhūti!”
"Whatever exists as duality is called 'having something to be apprehended'; whatever is non-dual is called 'having nothing to be apprehended.
World-Honored One, to what extent is there duality?"
“In what sense are they called ‘non-dual’?
“Subhūti! The various eyes and various forms constitute duality; the various ears and various sounds constitute duality; the various noses and various odors constitute duality.”
The various tongues and various tastes are two; the various bodies and various tangibles are two; the various minds and various phenomena are two.
Form and formlessness are two; the visible and the invisible are two; the resistant and the non-resistant are two; the outflowing and the non-outflowing are two;
the conditioned and the unconditioned are two; the mundane and the supramundane...
The world is dualistic; birth-and-death and nirvāṇa are dualistic. The phenomena of ordinary beings and ordinary beings are dualistic;
the phenomena of stream-enterers and stream-enterers are dualistic; the phenomena of once-returners and once-returners are dualistic; the phenomena of non-returners and non-returners are dualistic;
the phenomena of arhats and arhats are dualistic; and solitary awakening and solitary buddhas are dualistic.
To posit "two" is dualistic: for a bodhisattva mahāsattva to practice as a bodhisattva mahāsattva is dualistic;
for the Buddhas to have unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is dualistic. In this way, all such things involving conceptual proliferation are termed "dualistic."
"Subhūti! It is not that the eye and forms are non-dual; it is not that the ear and sounds are non-dual; it is not that the nose and odors are non-dual;
it is not that the tongue and tastes are non-dual; it is not that the body and tangibles are non-dual."
That which is neither mind nor dharma is non-dual; that which is neither with form nor without form is non-dual;
that which is neither visible nor invisible is non-dual; that which is neither resistant nor non-resistant is non-dual;
that which is neither with outflows nor without outflows is non-dual; that which is neither conditioned nor unconditioned is non-dual; that which is not of the world...
The mundane is not distinct from the supramundane, thus they are non-dual; saṃsāra is not distinct from nirvāṇa, thus they are non-dual;
the dharmas of ordinary beings are not distinct from ordinary beings, thus they are non-dual; the dharmas of stream-enterers are not distinct from stream-enterers, thus they are non-dual;
the dharmas of once-returners are not distinct from once-returners, thus they are non-dual; the dharmas of non-returners are not distinct from non-returners, thus they are non-dual.
Non-duality is not the dharma of an arhat, nor is it the arhat; this is non-duality. It is not the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, nor is it the pratyekabuddha; this is non-duality.
It is not the practice of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, nor is it the bodhisattva mahāsattva; this is non-duality.
It is not the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas, nor is it the buddhas; this is non-duality.
“Thus, all those who are free from conceptual proliferation are called ‘non-dual.
The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”
"Is it because of having something to attain that there is non-attainment?
Or is it because of having nothing to attain that there is non-attainment?
The Buddha said:

“Subhūti! It is not that there is non-apprehension because of apprehension, nor is it that there is non-apprehension because of non-apprehension; rather, the sameness of apprehension and non-apprehension is what is called ‘non-apprehension.’”
Thus it is, Subhūti!
A bodhisattva mahāsattva should diligently train in the equality of that which is apprehended and that which is non-apprehended. Subhūti!
"When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, it is called training in the meaning of the non-apprehensibility of the perfection of wisdom, remaining free from all faults.
The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), does not cling to anything that can be apprehended, nor cling to anything that cannot be apprehended, how does this bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, gradually fulfill the stages from one ground to the next?
"If there were no gradual fulfillment from one stage to the next, how could one attain the sought-after unsurpassed, perfect,
and complete enlightenment? The Buddha said, "Subhūti!"

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not attain the gradual fulfillment from one stage to the next and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment by dwelling in the state of apprehending something;
nor do they attain the gradual fulfillment from one stage to the next and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment by dwelling in the state of non-apprehension.
Why is this? Subhūti!

Because the perfection of wisdom is non-apprehendable; because unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is non-apprehendable; because when one who practices the perfection of wisdom practices within its sphere of activity, there is non-apprehension; and because even this dharma of non-apprehension is itself non-apprehendable.
"Subhūti! A bodhisattva mahāsattva should practice the perfection of wisdom in this manner.
The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:

“Bhagavān, if the *prajñāpāramitā* is unapprehendable, and unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is unapprehendable, and if the one who practices the *prajñāpāramitā*, the locus of practice, and the time of practice are also unapprehendable, how does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the *prajñāpāramitā*, constantly delight in the discernment of all phenomena?”
That is to say: "This is form; this is feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness;
this is the eye base; these are the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind bases;
this is the form base; these are the sound, odor, taste, tangible, and mental-object bases."
This is the eye-element; this is the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-element.
This is the form-element; this is the sound, odor, taste, tangible, and mental-object-element.
This is the eye-consciousness-element; this is the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness-element.
"This is eye-contact; this is ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact.
This is the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition; these are the various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions.
This is the earth element; these are the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements."

This is ignorance; these are volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, existence, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair;
this is the perfection of generosity; these are the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.

This is internal emptiness; this is external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence;

this is suchness; this is the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-falsity, the non-alteration, the equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of dharma, the stability of dharma, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm.

These are the four foundations of mindfulness; these are the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path;
this is the noble truth of suffering, these are the noble truths of its origin, its cessation, and the path;
these are the four dhyānas, these are the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.
This is the gate of liberation of emptiness; this is the gate of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness;
these are the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities;
these are the gates of samādhi and the gates of dhāraṇī.
These are the five eyes; these are the six supernormal powers;

these are the ten powers of a Buddha; these are the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
this is the quality of non-forgetfulness; this is the nature of constant abiding in equanimity.
This is omniscience; this is the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects;
this is the fruit of stream-entry; this is the fruit of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship;
this is the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha.
“This is the practice of all Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas;
this is the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas.

Thus ends the three-hundred-and-sixty-first fascicle of the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by imperial decree, from the first division, the sixty-first chapter, “The Many Questions on Non-duality,” part twelve. The Buddha said:

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, although they always delight in the discernment of all phenomena, they do not apprehend form, nor do they apprehend feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness;
they do not apprehend the sense base of the eye, nor do they apprehend the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind.”
One does not apprehend the sphere of form, nor does one apprehend the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental objects;
one does not apprehend the eye-element, nor does one apprehend the elements of ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind;
one does not apprehend the element of form, nor does one apprehend the elements of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental objects.
One does not apprehend the eye-consciousness element, nor does one apprehend the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-consciousness elements;
one does not apprehend eye-contact, nor does one apprehend ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact;

one does not apprehend the various sensations produced with eye-contact as condition, nor does one apprehend the various sensations produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as condition.
One does not apprehend the earth element, nor does one apprehend the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements;

one does not apprehend ignorance, nor does one apprehend volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, or old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair;
one does not apprehend the perfection of generosity, nor does one apprehend the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom.

One does not apprehend internal emptiness, nor external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self-characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature;

one does not apprehend suchness, nor the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-falsity, the non-alteration, the equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the reality-limit, the realm of space, or the inconceivable realm.

One does not apprehend the four foundations of mindfulness, nor does one apprehend the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path;
one does not apprehend the noble truth of suffering, nor does one apprehend the noble truths of origin, cessation, or the path;
one does not apprehend the four dhyānas, nor does one apprehend the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments.
They do not attain the gate of liberation through emptiness, nor do they attain the gates of liberation through signlessness and wishlessness;
they do not attain the eight liberations, nor the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative concentrations, or the ten totalities;
they do not attain the gates of samādhi, nor do they attain the gates of dhāraṇī.
One does not attain the five eyes, nor does one attain the six supernormal powers;

one does not attain the ten powers of a Buddha, nor does one attain the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
one does not attain the quality of non-forgetfulness, nor does one attain the nature of constant abiding in equanimity.
One does not attain all-knowledge, nor does one attain the knowledge of the aspects of the path or the knowledge of all aspects;
one does not attain the fruit of stream-entry, nor does one attain the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, or arhatship;
one does not attain the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha.
"One cannot attain any of the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva;
one cannot attain the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas.
The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:

“Bhagavān! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), if they do not apprehend form (rūpa), they likewise do not apprehend feeling (vedanā), perception (saṃjñā), formations (saṃskāra), or consciousness (vijñāna);
if they do not apprehend the sense-base of the eye (cakṣur-āyatana), they likewise do not apprehend the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind.”
If one does not apprehend the sphere of form, one also does not apprehend the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena;
if one does not apprehend the eye-element, one also does not apprehend the elements of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind;
if one does not apprehend the form-element, one also does not apprehend the elements of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena.
If one does not apprehend the eye-consciousness element, one also does not apprehend the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-consciousness elements;
if one does not apprehend eye-contact, one also does not apprehend ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact;

if one does not apprehend the various sensations produced with eye-contact as condition, one also does not apprehend the various sensations produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as condition.
If one does not apprehend the earth element, one likewise does not apprehend the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements;

if one does not apprehend ignorance, one likewise does not apprehend volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, or old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair;
if one does not apprehend the perfection of generosity, one likewise does not apprehend the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom.

If one does not apprehend internal emptiness, nor external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature;

and if one does not apprehend suchness, nor the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, non-alteration, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, or the inconceivable realm; [then one does not apprehend the perfection of wisdom].

If one does not attain the four foundations of mindfulness, one also does not attain the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path;
if one does not attain the noble truth of suffering, one also does not attain the noble truths of origin, cessation, or the path;
if one does not attain the four dhyānas, one also does not attain the four immeasurables or the four formless absorptions.
If one does not attain the gate of liberation of emptiness, one also does not attain the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness;
if one does not attain the eight liberations, one also does not attain the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative concentrations, or the ten totalities;
if one does not attain the gates of samādhi, one also does not attain the gates of dhāraṇī.
If one does not attain the five eyes, one also does not attain the six supernormal powers;

if one does not attain the ten powers of a Buddha, one also does not attain the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
if one does not attain the quality of non-forgetfulness, one also does not attain the nature of constant abiding in equanimity.
If one does not attain all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), one also does not attain the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) or the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*);

if one does not attain the fruit of stream-entry (*srotāpattiphala*), one also does not attain the fruits of once-returning (*sakṛdāgāmiphala*), non-returning (*anāgāmiphala*), or arhatship (*arhattvaphala*);
and if one does not attain the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha (*pratyekabodhi*).
If one does not attain the practice of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas,

and if one does not attain the unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas, how could one fulfill the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom?

If one cannot bring to perfection the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, how could one enter the bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s stage of correct determination and departure from birth?
If one cannot enter the bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s stage of rightness and departure from birth, how can one purify buddha-fields?
If one cannot purify buddha-fields, how can one bring sentient beings to maturity?
If one cannot bring sentient beings to maturity, how can one attain the knowledge of all modes?
If one cannot attain the knowledge of all modes, how can one turn the wheel of the true Dharma and perform the deeds of a Buddha?

If one cannot turn the wheel of the sublime Dharma and perform the deeds of a Buddha, how could one liberate immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of sentient beings from the manifold sufferings of birth and death, and cause them to realize the eternal bliss of nirvāṇa?
The Buddha said,
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

A bodhisattva mahāsattva does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of form, nor does he practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.”

"Subhūti! A bodhisattva mahāsattva does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the sense base of the eye, nor does he practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind."

“Subhūti! A bodhisattva mahāsattva does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the sphere of form, nor does he practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena.”

“Subhūti! A bodhisattva mahāsattva does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the eye-element, nor does he practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-element.”

“Subhūti! A bodhisattva mahāsattva does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the realm of form, nor does he practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena.”

"Subhūti! A bodhisattva mahāsattva does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the eye-consciousness element, nor does he practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-consciousness elements."

“Subhūti! A bodhisattva mahāsattva does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of eye-contact, nor does he practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact.”

“Subhūti! A bodhisattva mahāsattva does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the feelings produced with eye-contact as condition, nor does he practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact as conditions.”

“Subhūti! A bodhisattva mahāsattva does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the earth element, nor does he practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements.”

“Subhūti! A bodhisattva mahāsattva does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of ignorance, nor does he practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, or old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.”

“Subhūti! A bodhisattva mahāsattva does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the perfection of giving, nor do they practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom.”

“Subhūti! A bodhisattva mahāsattva does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of internal emptiness; nor does he practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.”

“Subhūti! A bodhisattva mahāsattva does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of suchness; nor do they practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, or the inconceivable realm.”

“Subhūti! A bodhisattva mahāsattva does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the four foundations of mindfulness, nor does he practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path.”

“Subhūti! A bodhisattva mahāsattva does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the noble truth of suffering, nor does he practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the noble truths of origination, cessation, or the path.”

"Subhūti! A bodhisattva mahāsattva does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the four dhyānas, nor does he practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the four immeasurables or the four formless absorptions."

“Subhūti! A bodhisattva mahāsattva does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the liberation door of emptiness, nor do they practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness.”

“Subhūti! A bodhisattva mahāsattva does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the eight liberations, nor does he practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, or the ten totalities.”

"Subhūti! A bodhisattva mahāsattva does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the gateways of samādhi, nor does he practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the gateways of dhāraṇī."
“Subhūti! A bodhisattva mahāsattva does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the five eyes, nor do they practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the six supernormal powers.”

“Subhūti! A bodhisattva mahāsattva does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the ten powers of a buddha, nor does he practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha.”

“Subhūti! A bodhisattva mahāsattva does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the quality of non-forgetfulness, nor do they practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the state of constant equanimity.”

“Subhūti! A bodhisattva mahāsattva does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of all-knowledge (sarvajñatā), nor does he practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the knowledge of the paths (mārgajñatā) or the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā).”

“Subhūti! A bodhisattva mahāsattva does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the fruit of a stream-enterer, nor does he practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the fruits of a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat.”
"Subhūti! A bodhisattva mahāsattva does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha. Subhūti!"
A bodhisattva mahāsattva does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of all the practices of bodhisattva mahāsattvas. "Subhūti!
A bodhisattva mahāsattva does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas."
The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
for what purpose does a bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the perfection of wisdom?”
The Buddha said,
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
A bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom because there is nothing for which it is done.”
Why is this so? Subhūti!

All dharmas are without purpose and without action; the perfection of wisdom is also without purpose and without action; unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is also without purpose and without action; and the bodhisattva mahāsattva is likewise without purpose and without action.
In this way, Subhūti,
a bodhisattva mahāsattva should practice the perfection of wisdom by means of non-action and non-activity as the skillful method.
The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

If all dharmas are without purpose and without activity, then one should not establish the distinctions of the three vehicles—namely, the Śrāvaka vehicle, the Pratyekabuddha vehicle, or the Unsurpassed Vehicle.”
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
No establishment of dharmas that are without purpose or without activity can be found; it is only through having a purpose and having activity that the establishment of dharmas can be found.”
Why is this so? Subhūti!
There are certain foolish, unlearned worldlings who cling to form, and likewise cling to feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.
They are attached to the sense base of the eye, and likewise attached to the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind;
they are attached to the sense base of forms, and likewise attached to the sense bases of sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, and mental phenomena;
they are attached to the eye element, and likewise attached to the elements of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.
They cling to the realm of form, and likewise cling to the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena;
they cling to the realm of eye-consciousness, and likewise cling to the realms of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness;
they cling to eye-contact, and likewise cling to ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact.
They cling to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition, and likewise cling to the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions;
they cling to the earth element, and likewise cling to the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements;

they cling to ignorance, and likewise cling to volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.
They cling to the perfection of generosity, and likewise cling to the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom;

they cling to internal emptiness, and likewise cling to external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.

They cling to suchness, and likewise cling to the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, immutability, equanimity, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm;

they cling to the four foundations of mindfulness, and likewise cling to the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path;
they cling to the noble truth of suffering, and likewise cling to the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path.
They are attached to the four dhyānas, and likewise attached to the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments;
they are attached to the liberation door of emptiness, and likewise attached to the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness;
they are attached to the eight liberations, and likewise attached to the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities.
They are attached to the gateways of samādhi and also attached to the gateways of dhāraṇī;
they are attached to the five eyes and also attached to the six supernormal powers;

they are attached to the ten powers of a Buddha and also attached to the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
They cling to the quality of non-forgetfulness, and they also cling to the nature of constant equanimity;
they cling to all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), and they also cling to the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*);
they cling to the fruit of stream-entry (*srotāpattiphala*), and they also cling to the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship.
They cling to the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha;
they cling to all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas;
they cling to the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas.

“Subhūti! These foolish, unlearned worldlings, through their attachment, conceive of form and apprehend form; they conceive of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness and apprehend feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness;
they conceive of the eye-base and apprehend the eye-base; they conceive of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases and apprehend the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases.”

Mindfulness of the sphere of form attains the sphere of form; mindfulness of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena attains the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena.
Mindfulness of the eye-element attains the eye-element; mindfulness of the elements of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind attains the elements of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.

Mindfulness of the element of forms attains the element of forms; mindfulness of the elements of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena attains the elements of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena.

He attends to the eye-consciousness element and attains the eye-consciousness element; he attends to the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements and attains the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements.
He attends to eye-contact and attains eye-contact; he attends to ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact and attains ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact.

He attends to the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition and attains the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition; he attends to the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions and attains the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions.

Mindfulness of the earth element results in the attainment of the earth element; mindfulness of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements results in the attainment of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements;

mindfulness of ignorance results in the attainment of ignorance; mindfulness of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair results in the attainment of volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair;

mindfulness of the perfection of generosity results in the attainment of the perfection of generosity; mindfulness of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom results in the attainment of ethical discipline through to wisdom.

By recollecting internal emptiness, one attains internal emptiness; by recollecting external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, one attains external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.

By recollecting true thusness (*tathatā*), one attains true thusness; by recollecting the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the non-falsity, the immutability, the equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*), one attains the dharma-realm up to the inconceivable realm.

By recollecting the noble truth of suffering (*duḥkha-āryasatya*), one attains the noble truth of suffering; by recollecting the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, one attains the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path.

By recollecting the four foundations of mindfulness (*smṛtyupasthāna*), one attains the four foundations of mindfulness; by recollecting the four right endeavors (*samyakprahāṇa*), the four bases of power (*ṛddhipāda*), the five faculties (*indriya*), the five powers (*bala*), the seven factors of enlightenment (*bodhyaṅga*), and the eightfold noble path (*āryāṣṭāṅgamārga*), one attains the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path.

By recollecting the four dhyānas, one attains the four dhyānas; by recollecting the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, one attains the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments;

by recollecting the eight liberations, one attains the eight liberations; by recollecting the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities, one attains the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities;
by recollecting all doors of samādhi, one attains all doors of samādhi; by recollecting all doors of dhāraṇī, one attains all doors of dhāraṇī.

By recollecting the liberation door of emptiness, one attains the liberation door of emptiness; by recollecting the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness, one attains the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness;
by recollecting the five eyes, one attains the five eyes; by recollecting the six supernormal powers, one attains the six supernormal powers;

by recollecting the ten powers of a Buddha, one attains the ten powers of a Buddha; by recollecting the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, one attains the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
By recollecting the quality of non-forgetfulness, one attains the quality of non-forgetfulness; by recollecting the constant abiding in equanimity, one attains the constant abiding in equanimity;

by recollecting all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), one attains all-knowledge; by recollecting the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), one attains the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects;

by recollecting the fruit of stream-entry (*srotāpattiphala*), one attains the fruit of stream-entry; by recollecting the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship, one attains the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship.
By recollecting the awakening of a pratyekabuddha, one attains the awakening of a pratyekabuddha;
by recollecting all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, one attains all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas;
and by recollecting the unexcelled, perfect, and complete awakening of all buddhas, one attains the unexcelled, perfect, and complete awakening of all buddhas.
“Subhūti! These foolish, unlearned worldlings conceive such thoughts as these:

‘Form is truly obtainable; feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are also truly obtainable. I shall definitively realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, liberate all sentient beings from the manifold sufferings of birth and death, and cause them to attain ultimate, eternal bliss in nirvāṇa.’”

The sense-base of the eye is truly obtainable; the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are also truly obtainable. I shall certainly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, liberate all sentient beings from the manifold sufferings of birth and death, and cause them to attain ultimate, eternal bliss in nirvāṇa.

The sphere of visible forms is truly obtainable; the spheres of sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, and mental phenomena are also truly obtainable. I shall certainly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, liberate all sentient beings from the manifold sufferings of birth and death, and cause them to attain ultimate, eternal bliss in *nirvāṇa*.

The eye-element can indeed be apprehended; the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements can likewise be apprehended. I shall certainly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, liberate all sentient beings from the manifold sufferings of birth and death, and cause them to attain ultimate, eternal bliss in nirvāṇa.

The realm of form can truly be apprehended; the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena can also truly be apprehended. I shall certainly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, liberate all sentient beings from the manifold sufferings of birth and death, and cause them to attain ultimate, eternal bliss in nirvāṇa.

The eye-consciousness element can truly be apprehended; the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements can likewise truly be apprehended. I shall certainly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, liberate all sentient beings from the manifold sufferings of birth and death, and cause them to attain ultimate, eternal bliss in *nirvāṇa*.

Visual contact is truly obtainable; auditory, olfactory, gustatory, tactile, and mental contact are also truly obtainable. I shall certainly realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, liberate all sentient beings from the manifold sufferings of birth and death, and cause them to attain ultimate, eternal bliss in nirvāṇa.

The various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are truly obtainable; the various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions are also truly obtainable. I shall certainly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, liberate all sentient beings from the manifold sufferings of birth and death, and cause them to attain ultimate, eternal bliss in nirvāṇa.

The earth element can indeed be apprehended, and the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements can likewise be apprehended; I shall certainly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, liberate all sentient beings from the manifold sufferings of birth and death, and cause them to attain ultimate, eternal bliss in nirvāṇa.

Ignorance can indeed be apprehended in reality; likewise, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair can also be apprehended in reality. I shall certainly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, liberate all sentient beings from the manifold sufferings of birth and death, and cause them to attain ultimate, eternal bliss in nirvana.

The perfection of generosity can truly be attained; the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom can also truly be attained. I shall certainly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, liberate all sentient beings from the manifold sufferings of birth and death, and cause them to obtain ultimate, eternal bliss in nirvāṇa.

Inner emptiness can truly be apprehended; outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self-characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence can also truly be apprehended. I shall certainly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, liberate all sentient beings from the manifold sufferings of birth and death, and cause them to attain the ultimate, eternal bliss of *nirvāṇa*.

True Suchness is truly attainable; the Dharma-realm, the Dharma-nature, the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm are also truly attainable. I shall certainly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, liberate all sentient beings from the manifold sufferings of birth and death, and cause them to attain ultimate, eternal bliss in Nirvana.

The noble truth of suffering can indeed be realized; the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path can also indeed be realized. I shall certainly attain unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, liberate all sentient beings from the manifold sufferings of birth and death, and cause them to obtain ultimate, eternal bliss in nirvana.

The four foundations of mindfulness can truly be attained; the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path can likewise truly be attained. The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

If all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas cannot find form when seeking it with the five eyes, and likewise cannot find feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness when seeking them;”
One cannot find the sense-base of the eye; one likewise cannot find the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind.
One cannot find the sense-base of forms; one likewise cannot find the sense-bases of sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, or mental phenomena.
One cannot find the eye-element; one likewise cannot find the elements of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind.
One cannot find the realm of form; one cannot find the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, or mental phenomena.
One cannot find the realm of eye-consciousness; one cannot find the realms of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-consciousness.
One cannot find eye-contact; one cannot find ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact.
One cannot find the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition; one likewise cannot find the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as conditions.
One cannot find the earth element; one likewise cannot find the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements. One cannot find ignorance;

one likewise cannot find volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, or old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.

One cannot find the perfection of generosity; one likewise cannot find the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom. One cannot find inner emptiness;

nor can one find outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self-characteristic, the emptiness of common characteristic, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

Seeking true suchness, it cannot be found; seeking the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, non-illusory nature, unchanging nature, equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of empty space, and the inconceivable realm, these also cannot be found.

Seeking the four foundations of mindfulness, they cannot be found; seeking the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path, these also cannot be found.
Seeking the noble truth of suffering, it cannot be found; seeking the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, these also cannot be found.
One cannot find the four dhyānas when seeking them; one likewise cannot find the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments when seeking them.
One cannot find the gate of liberation of emptiness when seeking it; one likewise cannot find the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness when seeking them.
One cannot find the eight liberations when seeking them; one likewise cannot find the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities when seeking them.
One cannot find the gates of samādhi when seeking them; one cannot find the gates of dhāraṇī when seeking them either.
One cannot find the five eyes when seeking them; one cannot find the six supernormal powers when seeking them either.

One cannot find the ten powers of a Buddha when seeking them; nor can one find the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha when seeking them.
One cannot find the quality of non-forgetfulness when sought; one also cannot find the nature of constant equanimity when sought.
One cannot find omniscience when sought; one also cannot find the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects when sought.
One cannot find the fruit of stream-entry when sought; one also cannot find the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, or arhatship when sought.
The solitary awakening of a pratyekabuddha cannot be found; the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas also cannot be found;

and because the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening of all Buddhas cannot be found, sentient beings likewise cannot be found. If this is so, then there would certainly be no one who realizes unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, nor anyone who liberates sentient beings from the manifold sufferings of birth and death to enable them to attain ultimate, eternal bliss in nirvāṇa. How then, World-Honored One, did you realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, and establish the distinctions among the three categories of sentient beings—namely, the group fixed in the right nature, the group fixed in the wrong nature, and the group that is not fixed?
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

With my five eyes, I observe according to reality that there is definitely no ‘self’ that can realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, nor any that establishes the distinctions among the three categories of sentient beings—namely, those fixed in the right nature, those fixed in the wrong nature, and those who are not fixed. Yet, because sentient beings are deluded and inverted, they give rise to the notion of real dharmas regarding what are not real dharmas, and they give rise to the notion of real sentient beings regarding what are not real sentient beings. To eliminate their false attachments, I speak according to worldly convention and not according to ultimate truth.”
