Because the noble truth of suffering, the noble truth of its origin, the noble truth of its cessation, and the noble truth of the path lack an inherent nature of synthesis, whatever dharma lacks an inherent nature of synthesis has non-existence as its very nature.
“World-Honored One!
For what reason do all the gateways of samādhi and all the gateways of dhāraṇī lack intrinsic nature? “Subhūti!
Because all doors of samādhi and all doors of dhāraṇī lack a nature of synthesis, if a phenomenon lacks a nature of synthesis, that phenomenon takes non-existence as its nature.
“World-Honored One!
For what reason are the nature of the Buddha’s ten powers, the four fearlessnesses, the four unhindered understandings, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha non-existent?”

“Subhūti! Because the ten powers of a Buddha, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, lack a nature of synthesis, any dharma that lacks a nature of synthesis has non-existence as its nature.”
“World-Honored One!
For what reason do great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity lack intrinsic nature?
“Suvīra! [The Buddha replied: “Suvīra!”

Because great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity lack an inherent nature of combination, if a dharma lacks an inherent nature of combination, that dharma takes the absence of nature as its nature.
“World-Honored One!
For what reason do the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant dwelling in equanimity lack intrinsic nature? “Subhūti!

Because the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant abiding in equanimity lack an inherent nature of synthesis, any dharma that lacks an inherent nature of synthesis has non-existence as its very nature.
“World-Honored One!
For what reason do omniscience and the knowledge of the aspects of the path lack intrinsic nature? “Subhūti!

Because omniscience (*sarvajñatā*) and the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) lack an inherent nature of synthesis, whatever dharma lacks an inherent nature of synthesis has non-existence as its very nature.
“World-Honored One!
For what reason do the first eye, the second, the third, the fourth, and the fifth eye lack intrinsic nature?
“Subhūti! [The Buddha replied.]

Because the first eye, the second, the third, the fourth, and the fifth eyes lack an inherent nature of combination, if a phenomenon lacks an inherent nature of combination, that phenomenon has non-existence as its very nature.
“World-Honored One!
For what reason do the first supernormal power, the second, the third, the fourth, the fifth, and the sixth supernormal power lack intrinsic nature?”

“Subhūti! Because the first supernormal power, the second, the third, the fourth, the fifth, and the sixth supernormal powers have no nature of synthesis, if a dharma has no nature of synthesis, that dharma takes non-existence as its nature.”
“World-Honored One!
For what reason do the conditioned realm and the unconditioned realm lack intrinsic nature? “Subhūti!

Because the conditioned realm and the unconditioned realm lack an inherent nature of synthesis, if a phenomenon lacks an inherent nature of synthesis, that phenomenon takes non-existence as its nature.
“Subhūti! For this reason, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should know that all dharmas have non-existence as their intrinsic nature.
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 364, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree, Part One, Chapter Sixty-two (iii): ‘Furthermore, Subhūti!’”
All phenomena have emptiness as their intrinsic nature; all phenomena have signlessness as their intrinsic nature; all phenomena have wishlessness as their intrinsic nature.
"Subhūti! For this reason, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should know that all phenomena have non-existence as their intrinsic nature.
Furthermore, Subhūti!"

All phenomena have *tathatā* (suchness) as their intrinsic nature; all phenomena have the *dharmadhātu* (dharma-realm) as their intrinsic nature; all phenomena have *dharmatā* (dharma-nature) as their intrinsic nature; all phenomena have the nature of non-falsity as their intrinsic nature; all phenomena have the nature of immutability as their intrinsic nature; all phenomena have the nature of equality as their intrinsic nature; all phenomena have the nature of being free from birth as their intrinsic nature; all phenomena have the nature of the fixedness of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*) as their intrinsic nature; all phenomena have the nature of the stability of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*) as their intrinsic nature; all phenomena have the nature of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) as their intrinsic nature; all phenomena have the nature of the realm of empty space (*ākāśadhātu*) as their intrinsic nature; and all phenomena have the nature of the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*) as their intrinsic nature.
"Subhūti! For this reason, all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should know that all phenomena have non-existence as their intrinsic nature.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

If all dharmas have non-existence as their intrinsic nature, by what skillful means does a bodhisattva mahāsattva who has first resolved to attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment accomplish the perfection of giving, thereby maturing sentient beings and purifying buddha-fields?”
Can one practice the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; ripen sentient beings; and purify buddha-fields?
By accomplishing what skillful means (*upāyakauśalya*) is one able to abide in internal emptiness (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*) while maturing sentient beings and purifying the Buddha-fields?

By abiding in external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, emptiness of own-marks, emptiness of common marks, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of own-nature, and the emptiness of the own-nature of non-existence, how does one mature sentient beings and purify the Buddha-fields?
What kind of skillful means must one accomplish to be able to abide in *tathatā* (suchness), while maturing sentient beings and purifying Buddha-fields?

What kind of skillful means must one accomplish to be able to abide in the *dharmadhātu* (dharma-realm), the *dharmatā* (dharma-nature), the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the nature free from birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm, while maturing sentient beings and purifying Buddha-fields?
What kind of skillful means must one accomplish to be able to practice the four foundations of mindfulness, thereby maturing sentient beings and purifying buddha-fields?

What kind of skillful means must one accomplish to be able to practice the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path, thereby maturing sentient beings and purifying buddha-fields?
What kind of skillful means must one accomplish to be able to abide in the noble truth of suffering, maturing sentient beings and purifying buddha-fields?
What kind [of skillful means] must one accomplish to be able to abide in the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, maturing sentient beings and purifying buddha-fields?
What kind of skillful means must one accomplish to be able to practice the first dhyāna, maturing sentient beings and purifying Buddha-fields?
What kind of skillful means must one accomplish to be able to practice the second, third, and fourth dhyānas, maturing sentient beings and purifying Buddha-fields?
What kind of skillful means must be accomplished to be able to practice the immeasurable of loving-kindness (*maitrī*) so as to mature sentient beings and purify Buddha-fields?

What kind [of skillful means] is required to be able to practice the immeasurables of compassion (*karuṇā*), sympathetic joy (*muditā*), and equanimity (*upekṣā*) so as to mature sentient beings and purify Buddha-fields?
What skillful means must be accomplished to be able to practice the meditative concentration of the sphere of infinite space, thereby maturing sentient beings and purifying buddha-fields?

What skillful means must be accomplished to be able to practice the meditative concentrations of the sphere of infinite consciousness, the sphere of nothingness, and the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, thereby maturing sentient beings and purifying buddha-fields?
What kind of skillful means must be accomplished to be able to practice the eight liberations, to mature sentient beings, and to adorn and purify Buddha-fields?

What kind [of skillful means] must be accomplished to be able to practice the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities, to mature sentient beings, and to adorn and purify Buddha-fields?
What kind of skillful means must be accomplished to be able to practice all gateways of samādhi, to ripen sentient beings, and to purify buddha-fields?
What kind [of skillful means] must be accomplished to be able to practice all gateways of dhāraṇī, to ripen sentient beings, and to purify buddha-fields?
What kind of skillful means must one accomplish to be able to practice the gate of liberation of emptiness, maturing sentient beings and purifying buddha-fields?
What kind [of skillful means] must one accomplish to be able to practice the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, maturing sentient beings and purifying buddha-fields?
What kind of skillful means must be accomplished to be able to exercise the five eyes, maturing sentient beings and purifying Buddha-fields?
What kind of skillful means must be accomplished to be able to exercise the six supernormal powers, maturing sentient beings and purifying Buddha-fields?
What kind of skillful means must be accomplished to be able to practice the ten powers of a Buddha, to mature sentient beings, and to purify Buddha-fields?

What kind [of skillful means] must be accomplished to be able to practice the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, to mature sentient beings, and to purify Buddha-fields?
What kind of skillful means must be accomplished to practice great loving-kindness, maturing sentient beings and purifying buddha-fields?
What must be accomplished to practice great compassion, great joy, and great equanimity, maturing sentient beings and purifying buddha-fields?
What kind of skillful means must one accomplish to be able to practice the dharma of non-forgetfulness, to bring sentient beings to maturity, and to adorn and purify buddha-fields?
What kind [of skillful means] must one accomplish to be able to practice the nature of constant equanimity, to bring sentient beings to maturity, and to adorn and purify buddha-fields?
What kind of skillful means must be accomplished to be able to practice all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), to bring sentient beings to maturity, and to purify Buddha-fields?

What kind of knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) and knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) must be accomplished to be able to bring sentient beings to maturity and purify Buddha-fields?
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

This bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes such skillful means that, although he practices and studies with the knowledge that all phenomena have non-existence as their intrinsic nature, he constantly and diligently matures sentient beings and purifies buddha-fields; and although he constantly and diligently matures sentient beings and purifies buddha-fields, he diligently practices and studies with the knowledge that both sentient beings and all buddha-fields have non-existence as their intrinsic nature.”

"Subhūti! Although this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of generosity while training in the path to enlightenment, he knows that the path to enlightenment has non-existence as its intrinsic nature;

although he practices the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom while training in the path to enlightenment, he knows that the path to enlightenment has non-existence as its intrinsic nature."
Although they dwell in the emptiness of the internal while training in the path to enlightenment, they know that the path to enlightenment has the absence of intrinsic nature as its own nature;

although they dwell in the emptiness of the external, the emptiness of the internal and external, the emptiness of emptiness, the great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate, the emptiness of the conditioned, the emptiness of the unconditioned, the absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of essential nature, the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of the absence of nature, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the absence of intrinsic nature in the absence of nature while training in the path to enlightenment, they know that the path to enlightenment has the absence of intrinsic nature as its own nature.
Although they dwell in *tathatā* while training in the path to enlightenment, they know that the nature of the path to enlightenment is the absence of intrinsic nature;

although they dwell in the *dharmadhātu*, the *dharmatā*, the non-falsity, the immutability, the equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm while training in the path to enlightenment, they know that the nature of the path to enlightenment is the absence of intrinsic nature.
Although they practice the four foundations of mindfulness while training in the path to awakening, they know that the path to awakening has non-substantiality as its intrinsic nature;

although they practice the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path while training in the path to awakening, they know that the path to awakening has non-substantiality as its intrinsic nature.
Although they abide in the noble truth of suffering while training in the path to enlightenment, they know that the nature of the path to enlightenment is the absence of intrinsic nature;

although they abide in the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path while training in the path to enlightenment, they know that the nature of the path to enlightenment is the absence of intrinsic nature.
Although they practice the path to awakening by training in the first dhyāna, they know that the nature of the path to awakening has non-substantiality as its intrinsic nature;
although they practice the path to awakening by training in the second, third, and fourth dhyānas, they know that the nature of the path to awakening has non-substantiality as its intrinsic nature.
Although they practice the immeasurable loving-kindness and train in the path to enlightenment, they know that the nature of the path to enlightenment is its lack of intrinsic nature;

although they practice the immeasurable compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity and train in the path to enlightenment, they know that the nature of the path to enlightenment is its lack of intrinsic nature.

Although they practice the meditative absorption of the sphere of infinite space while training in the path to enlightenment, they know that the path to enlightenment has non-substantiality as its intrinsic nature;

although they practice the meditative absorptions of the sphere of infinite consciousness, the sphere of nothingness, and the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception while training in the path to enlightenment, they know that the path to enlightenment has non-substantiality as its intrinsic nature.
Although they practice the eight liberations and train in the path to enlightenment, they know that the path to enlightenment has non-substantiality as its intrinsic nature;

although they practice the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten pervasive bases and train in the path to enlightenment, they know that the path to enlightenment has non-substantiality as its intrinsic nature.
Although they practice all gateways of samādhi to train in the path to enlightenment, they know that the path to enlightenment has the absence of intrinsic nature as its own nature;
although they practice all gateways of dhāraṇī to train in the path to enlightenment, they know that the path to enlightenment has the absence of intrinsic nature as its own nature.

Although they practice the gate of liberation of emptiness and train in the path to enlightenment, they know that the nature of the path to enlightenment has non-substantiality as its intrinsic nature;

although they practice the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness and train in the path to enlightenment, they know that the nature of the path to enlightenment has non-substantiality as its intrinsic nature.
Although they practice the five eyes while training in the path to enlightenment, they know that the nature of the path to enlightenment is to have no intrinsic nature as its own essence;

although they practice the six supernormal powers while training in the path to enlightenment, they know that the nature of the path to enlightenment is to have no intrinsic nature as its own essence.

Although they practice the ten powers of a Buddha and train in the path to enlightenment, they know that the path to enlightenment has non-substantiality as its intrinsic nature; although they practice the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha and train in the path to enlightenment, they know that the path to enlightenment has non-substantiality as its intrinsic nature.
Although they practice great loving-kindness and train in the path to enlightenment, they know that the nature of the path to enlightenment is the absence of intrinsic nature;

although they practice great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity and train in the path to enlightenment, they know that the nature of the path to enlightenment is the absence of intrinsic nature.

Although they practice the training of the quality of non-forgetfulness while learning the path to enlightenment, they know that the nature of the path to enlightenment has the absence of intrinsic nature as its own nature;

although they practice the training of the constant abiding in equanimity while learning the path to enlightenment, they know that the nature of the path to enlightenment has the absence of intrinsic nature as its own nature.
Although they practice the path of awakening by training in all-knowledge, they know that the path of awakening has non-substantiality as its intrinsic nature;

although they practice the path of awakening by training in the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, they know that the path of awakening has non-substantiality as its intrinsic nature.
"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva thus practices the perfection of generosity while training in the path to enlightenment;
likewise, they practice the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom."
The *pāramitā* practitioner studies the path to enlightenment; likewise, they dwell in internal emptiness while studying the path to enlightenment;

likewise, they dwell in external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, beginningless-and-endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, and non-existence... [emptiness].
One trains in the path to enlightenment by means of the emptiness of change, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of specific characteristics,

the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence; likewise,
one trains in the path to enlightenment by abiding thus in suchness, and likewise, one trains in the path to enlightenment by abiding thus in the Dharma.
One trains in the path to awakening by training in the elements, the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth,
the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm;
one trains in the path to awakening by thus practicing the four foundations of mindfulness, and thus practices.

One trains in the path to enlightenment by practicing the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path;

likewise, one trains in the path to enlightenment by abiding thus in the noble truth of suffering, and likewise trains in the path to enlightenment by abiding thus in the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path; in this way one cultivates.
One practices the path of awakening by training in the first dhyāna; likewise, one practices the path of awakening by training in the second, third, and fourth dhyānas;
likewise, one practices the path of awakening by training in the immeasurable state of loving-kindness (*maitrī*);
likewise, one practices the path of awakening by training in the immeasurable states of compassion (*karuṇā*), sympathetic joy (*muditā*), and equanimity (*upekṣā*). Thus one practices.
One trains in the path to enlightenment through the meditative absorption of the sphere of infinite space;

likewise, one trains in the path to enlightenment by practicing the meditative absorptions of the sphere of infinite consciousness, the sphere of nothingness, and the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.

Likewise, one trains in the path to enlightenment by practicing the eight liberations, and likewise, one trains in the path to enlightenment by practicing the eight bases of mastery and the nine successive absorptions.
...the ten totalities (*daśakṛtsnāyatana*) as the path of training for awakening; likewise, practicing all doors of meditative concentration (*samādhi-mukha*) as the path of training for awakening;
likewise, practicing all doors of dhāraṇī (*dhāraṇī-mukha*) as the path of training for awakening;

likewise, practicing the door of liberation of emptiness (*śūnyatā-vimokṣa-mukha*) as the path of training for awakening; likewise, practicing the signless (*animitta*) and the wishless (*apraṇihita*)...
One trains in the path to enlightenment by means of the gates of liberation; one trains in the path to enlightenment by thus practicing the five eyes;
one trains in the path to enlightenment by thus practicing the six supernormal powers; one trains in the path to enlightenment by thus practicing the ten powers of a Buddha;
and one trains in the path to enlightenment by thus practicing the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen [unique qualities of a Buddha].
One trains in the path to enlightenment by practicing the unique qualities of a Buddha; one trains in the path to enlightenment by thus practicing great loving-kindness;
one trains in the path to enlightenment by thus practicing great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity;
one trains in the path to enlightenment by thus practicing the quality of non-forgetfulness; one trains in the path to enlightenment by thus practicing the state of constant abiding in equanimity.
Subhūti, it is thus that one practices the path of awakening by training in all-knowledge;
it is thus that one practices the path of awakening by training in the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects;
and so on, until one has not yet attained the Tathāgata’s ten powers, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and great compassion.
Great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the quality of non-forgetfulness, the constant abiding in equanimity,
all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects— all these are called training in the path to enlightenment that has not yet reached fulfillment.
If one has already attained perfection in this path, then one has also attained perfection in all the pāramitās.
Because the pāramitās have been perfected, one realizes the omniscience of a Tathāgata (sarvākārajñatā) through a single moment of associated sublime wisdom.

At that time, because the continuity of all subtle habitual tendencies of affliction never arises again, it is called "complete abandonment without remainder. One is then named a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who, with the unobstructed and pure Buddha-eye, universally observes all phenomena throughout the ten directions and the triple world; since even non-existence cannot be apprehended, how much less could existence possibly exist!
"So it is, Subhūti!
All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should practice the perfection of wisdom, contemplating that all phenomena have non-existence as their intrinsic nature."

“Subhūti! This is called the most supreme skillful means of a bodhisattva mahāsattva: namely, when practicing the perfection of wisdom and contemplating all phenomena, one does not even apprehend their non-existence, let alone their existence!”

“Subhūti! When this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of generosity, he does not even perceive the non-existence of this giving—the giver, the recipient, the objects given, and the mind of enlightenment—let alone perceive them as existing!”

When practicing the perfection of pure ethical discipline, one does not even perceive the non-existence of this purity of ethical discipline, the locus of protecting ethical discipline, the one who maintains ethical discipline, or the mind that guards ethical discipline; how much less would one perceive them as existing!

When practicing the perfection of patience, one does not even perceive the non-existence of this patience, the object of patience, the one who practices patience, or the mind that practices patience; how much less could one perceive them as existing!

When practicing the perfection of diligence, one does not even perceive the non-existence of this diligence—the locus of diligence, the one who is diligent, and the mind that practices diligence—let alone perceive them as existing!

When practicing the perfection of meditative concentration, one does not even perceive the non-existence of this meditative concentration, the locus where it is practiced, the practitioner who meditates, or the mind that practices meditation; how much less could one perceive them as existing!

When practicing the perfection of wisdom, one does not even perceive the non-existence of this wisdom, the locus where wisdom is practiced, the practitioner of wisdom, or the mind that practices wisdom; how much less would one perceive them as existing!

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—at that time, regarding this dwelling in internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, one who is able to dwell therein, by virtue of such dwelling, and while practicing that state of dwelling, does not even perceive ‘non-existence,’ let alone perceive it as ‘existence’!”

"Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in suchness, the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), non-illusoriness, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm—at that time, regarding this dwelling in suchness up to the inconceivable realm, the one who can dwell therein, the means by which they dwell, and the place of dwelling they cultivate, they do not even perceive them as non-existent, let alone perceive them as existent!"

“Subhūti! When these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path, they do not even perceive the non-existence of the one who practices these—from the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path—the practice itself, or the locus of the practice; how much less would they perceive them as existing!”

“Subhūti! When this bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in the noble truth of suffering, the noble truth of its origin, the noble truth of its cessation, and the noble truth of the path, he does not even perceive the non-existence of those who can dwell in these noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and path, nor the basis upon which they dwell or the state of dwelling itself; how much less would he perceive them as existing!”

“Subhūti! When this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions, regarding those who are able to practice these four dhyānas, four immeasurables, and four formless absorptions, by virtue of this practice and the locus of practice, they do not even perceive them as non-existent, let alone perceive them as existent!”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities, they do not even perceive the non-existence of these eight liberations, eight bases of mastery, nine successive attainments, and ten totalities—nor the one who practices them, nor the act of practicing, nor the locus of practice—let alone perceiving them as existent!”

“Subhūti! When this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices all the gateways of samādhi and all the gateways of dhāraṇī, regarding these gateways of samādhi and dhāraṇī—the one who is able to practice them, the act of practicing by means of them, and the locus of practice—he does not even perceive them as non-existent, much less perceives them as existent!”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the gate of liberation of emptiness, the signless, and the wishless, they do not even perceive the non-existence of the one who can practice these gates of liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, nor the means by which they practice, nor the locus of their practice; how much less would they perceive them as existing!”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the five eyes and the six supernormal powers, they do not even perceive the non-existence of the one who practices these five eyes and six supernormal powers, the means by which they practice, or the locus of their practice; how much less would they perceive them as existing!”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the ten powers of a buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, they do not even perceive the non-existence of these—the ten powers up to the eighteen unique qualities—of the one who practices them, of the practice itself, or of the locus of that practice; how much less could they perceive them as existing!”

“Subhūti! When this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the dharma of non-forgetfulness and dwells constantly in equanimity, regarding this dharma of non-forgetfulness and constant dwelling in equanimity—both the one who can practice it, the means by which they practice, and the locus of that practice—he does not even perceive them as non-existent, let alone perceive them as existent!”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), they do not even perceive these—all-knowledge, knowledge of the paths, and knowledge of all aspects—as non-existent, let alone as existent; nor do they perceive the one who practices them, the means by which they practice, or the locus in which they practice.

“Subhūti! When this bodhisattva mahāsattva realizes all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna), regarding that which realizes it, that by which it is realized, and the locus of its realization, he does not even perceive them as non-existent, much less as existent!”
"Why is that? Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly reflects thus:"

"All phenomena have non-existence as their nature; such non-existence is the very nature of things, existing inherently from the beginning. It was not made by a Buddha, nor by a Pratyekabuddha, nor by a Śrāvaka, nor was it made by anyone else."
"Because all phenomena are without an agent, being devoid of an agent.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
“Is it not the case, Subhūti, that all phenomena are devoid of the intrinsic nature of phenomena?
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!”
"So it is! So it is! Just as you have said, there are no phenomena that are not devoid of the nature of phenomena."
The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
If all dharmas are detached from the nature of dharmas (dharmatā), how can that which is detached know whether that which is detached exists or does not exist?”
Why is this? World-Honored One!

A non-existent dharma cannot know a non-existent dharma; an existent dharma cannot know an existent dharma; a non-existent dharma cannot know an existent dharma; and an existent dharma cannot know a non-existent dharma.

"Bhagavān! Since all these phenomena have non-cognition as their intrinsic nature, how does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing the perfection of wisdom, manifest whether phenomena exist or do not exist?"
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they manifest whether phenomena exist or do not exist in accordance with worldly convention, not in accordance with the ultimate truth.”
“World-Honored One!
Are the conventional and the ultimate truth different? “No.”
"Subhūti! There is no ultimate truth that exists separately from the conventional. Why is this?

"Subhūti! The suchness of the conventional is itself the ultimate. Yet sentient beings, through their inverted and deluded attachments, neither know nor see this suchness. Out of compassion for them, the bodhisattva mahāsattva displays the existence or non-existence of all phenomena in accordance with conventional signs."
Furthermore, Subhūti!

Sentient beings give rise to the notion that the phenomena of the aggregates and so forth are substantially real, not knowing they are non-existent. Out of compassion for them, the bodhisattva mahāsattva discriminates whether these phenomena exist or do not exist, thinking: "How may I cause those sentient beings to know that the phenomena of the aggregates and so forth are all not substantially real?"
“Subhūti! All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should practice this profound perfection of wisdom in this manner.
Chapter Sixty-Three: Skillful Means in Practice, Part One At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
The Tathāgata has often said that a bodhisattva practices the bodhisattva path. What is called the ‘bodhisattva path’?
The Buddha replied:
“Subhūti! A bodhisattva practitioner practices for the sake of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; this is called the bodhisattva practice.
The Venerable Subhūti then addressed the Buddha again, saying:
“World-Honored One,
in what place should a bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the bodhisattva path?
The Buddha said:

“Subhūti! A bodhisattva mahāsattva should practice the bodhisattva conduct within the emptiness of form; they should practice the bodhisattva conduct within the emptiness of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.”

A bodhisattva mahāsattva should practice the bodhisattva conduct within the emptiness of the sense base of the eye; they should practice the bodhisattva conduct within the emptiness of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva should practice the bodhisattva conduct by dwelling in the emptiness of the sphere of form; they should practice the bodhisattva conduct by dwelling in the emptiness of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva should practice the bodhisattva conduct within the emptiness of the eye-element; they should practice the bodhisattva conduct within the emptiness of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva should practice the bodhisattva conduct within the emptiness of the realm of form; they should practice the bodhisattva conduct within the emptiness of the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva should practice the bodhisattva conduct by dwelling in the emptiness of the visual consciousness element; they should practice the bodhisattva conduct by dwelling in the emptiness of the auditory, olfactory, gustatory, tactile, and mental consciousness elements.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva should practice the bodhisattva conduct within the emptiness of eye-contact; they should practice the bodhisattva conduct within the emptiness of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva should practice the bodhisattva conduct by dwelling in the emptiness of all feelings arising conditioned by eye-contact; they should practice the bodhisattva conduct by dwelling in the emptiness of all feelings arising conditioned by ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva should practice the bodhisattva path by way of the emptiness of the earth element; they should practice the bodhisattva path by way of the emptiness of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva should practice the bodhisattva conduct by dwelling in the emptiness of ignorance; they should practice the bodhisattva conduct by dwelling in the emptiness of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.
A bodhisattva mahāsattva should practice the bodhisattva conduct within the emptiness of internal phenomena; they should practice the bodhisattva conduct within the emptiness of external phenomena.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva should practice the bodhisattva conduct within the emptiness of the perfection of generosity; they should practice the bodhisattva conduct within the emptiness of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva should practice the conduct of a bodhisattva by means of the emptiness of the internal; they should practice the conduct of a bodhisattva by means of the emptiness of the external, the emptiness of the internal and external, the emptiness of emptiness, the great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of the conditioned, the emptiness of the unconditioned, the emptiness of the absolute, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of essential nature, the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva should practice the bodhisattva conduct by way of emptiness within the first dhyāna; they should practice the bodhisattva conduct by way of emptiness within the second, third, and fourth dhyānas.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva should practice the bodhisattva conduct of the immeasurable emptiness of loving-kindness; they should practice the bodhisattva conduct of the immeasurable emptiness of compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva should practice the bodhisattva conduct within the emptiness of the concentration on the sphere of infinite space; they should practice the bodhisattva conduct within the concentration on the sphere of infinite consciousness, the concentration on the sphere of nothingness, and the concentration on the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva should practice the bodhisattva conduct by way of the emptiness of the four foundations of mindfulness; they should practice the bodhisattva conduct by way of the emptiness of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should practice the bodhisattva conduct within the emptiness of conjunction; they should practice the bodhisattva conduct within the emptiness of non-conjunction.

Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should practice the bodhisattva conduct within the emptiness of the gate of liberation of emptiness; they should practice the bodhisattva conduct within the emptiness of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva should practice the bodhisattva path within the emptiness of the eight liberations; they should practice the bodhisattva path within the emptiness of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva should practice the bodhisattva conduct within the emptiness of the noble truth of suffering; they should practice the bodhisattva conduct within the emptiness of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path.

Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should practice the bodhisattva conduct within the emptiness of the ten powers of a Buddha; they should practice the bodhisattva conduct within the emptiness of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.

Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should practice the bodhisattva conduct within the emptiness of great loving-kindness; they should practice the bodhisattva conduct within the emptiness of great compassion, great joy, and great equanimity.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva should practice the bodhisattva conduct within the emptiness of the five eyes; they should practice the bodhisattva conduct within the emptiness of the six supernormal powers.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva should practice the bodhisattva conduct within the emptiness of all doors of samādhi; they should practice the bodhisattva conduct within the emptiness of all doors of dhāraṇī.

Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should practice the bodhisattva conduct within the emptiness of the purification of buddha-fields; they should practice the bodhisattva conduct within the emptiness of the maturation of sentient beings.

Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should practice the bodhisattva conduct within the emptiness of the elicitation of the dharani of eloquence; they should practice the bodhisattva conduct within the emptiness of the elicitation of the dharani of syllables.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva should practice the bodhisattva conduct that enters into the emptiness of the dharani of syllables, and should practice the bodhisattva conduct that enters into the emptiness of the dharani of no-syllables.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva should practice the bodhisattva conduct within the emptiness of the conditioned realm, and should practice the bodhisattva conduct within the emptiness of the unconditioned realm.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the bodhisattva conduct in this manner, they do not conceive of dualistic characteristics regarding all phenomena, just as in the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of a Buddha.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this manner, it is called practicing the conduct of a bodhisattva for the sake of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
The Tathāgata constantly speaks of the 'Buddha. For what reason is he called a 'Buddha'?"
The Buddha said:
"Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
One is called a Buddha because of awakening to the true meaning."
Furthermore, Subhūti!
One is called a Buddha because of having realized the true Dharma.
Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because he has thoroughly realized the true meaning,
he is named Buddha. Furthermore, Subhūti,
because he has awakened to all phenomena as they truly are, he is named Buddha.
Furthermore, Subhūti!

One is called a Buddha because they spontaneously awaken to the specific characteristics, the common characteristics, the characteristics of existence, and the characteristics of non-existence of all phenomena.
Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because unobstructed knowledge operates with respect to all aspects of the phenomena of the three times and unconditioned phenomena, he is called a Buddha.
Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because he awakens all sentient beings to reality as it is, causing them to leave behind inverted views, evil karma, and manifold sufferings,
he is called a Buddha. Furthermore, Subhūti,
because he can awaken to the characteristics of all phenomena as they truly are— namely, that they are signless— he is called a Buddha.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One, the Tathāgata constantly speaks of ‘bodhi. For what reason is it called ‘bodhi’?”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

The meaning of realizing the emptiness of phenomena is the meaning of bodhi; the meaning of realizing suchness is the meaning of bodhi; the meaning of realizing the limit of reality is the meaning of bodhi; the meaning of realizing the nature of phenomena is the meaning of bodhi; the meaning of realizing the dharma-realm is the meaning of bodhi.”
Furthermore, Subhūti!

It is called *bodhi* because it is the supreme, most excellent, and sublime true awakening, established through the provisional designation of names and signs and expressed through conventional speech.
Furthermore, Subhūti,
it is called bodhi because it is indestructible and beyond conceptual differentiation.
Furthermore, Subhūti, [it is called bodhi...]
Because it is the true suchness of phenomena, its non-falsity, its immutability, and its absence of inversion, it is called bodhi.
Furthermore, Subhūti!

It is merely by way of conventional designation that we speak of "enlightenment" (*bodhi*); yet, no real name or characteristic can be apprehended therein, and for this reason it is called enlightenment.
Furthermore, Subhūti, that which constitutes the true, pure, and wondrous awakening of all Buddhas is therefore called enlightenment.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Because the Buddhas have realized all aspects of all phenomena through this, it is called 'awakening' (bodhi).
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom for the sake of awakening, with respect to what phenomena do they bring benefit or harm, increase or decrease, arise or cease, or become defiled or purified?”

“Bhagavān, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva, for the sake of awakening, dwells in internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence— toward what phenomena does he experience benefit or harm, increase or decrease, arising or cessation, or defilement or purification?”
“World-Honored One!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva, for the sake of awakening, abides in suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, non-alteration, equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the reality-limit, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm—at what dharma would there be benefit or harm, increase or decrease, arising or ceasing, or defilement or purification?”
“World-Honored One, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva,

for the sake of awakening, cultivates the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path, in what dharma do they find benefit or harm, increase or decrease, arising or ceasing, or defilement or purification?”
“World-Honored One!

When a bodhisattva-mahāsattva dwells in the noble truth of suffering, the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path for the sake of awakening, in what dharma does he find benefit or harm, increase or decrease, arising or ceasing, or defilement or purification?”

“World-Honored One, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments for the sake of bodhi, in what dharmas do they bring benefit or harm, increase or decrease, arising or ceasing, or defilement or purity?”
“World-Honored One!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva, for the sake of awakening, cultivates the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities, in what dharma do they find benefit or harm, increase or decrease, arising or ceasing, or defilement or purification?”
“World-Honored One!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the gates of samādhi and the gates of dhāraṇī for the sake of bodhi, with respect to what phenomena do they bring benefit or harm, increase or decrease, arising or ceasing, or defilement or purity?”
“World-Honored One!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva, for the sake of awakening, cultivates the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of signlessness, and the gate of wishlessness, with respect to what phenomena do they bring benefit or harm, increase or decrease, arise or cease, or become defiled or purified?”
“World-Honored One!

When a bodhisattva-mahāsattva, for the sake of awakening, cultivates the five eyes and the six supernormal powers, with respect to what phenomena do they act as benefit or harm, increase or decrease, arising or ceasing, defilement or purification?”
“World-Honored One!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva, for the sake of awakening, cultivates the ten powers of a buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, in what dharma is there benefit or harm, increase or decrease, arising or ceasing, or defilement or purification?”
“World-Honored One!

When a bodhisattva-mahāsattva cultivates great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity for the sake of awakening, with respect to what dharmas do they bring benefit or harm, increase or decrease, arise or cease, or become defiled or purified?”
“World-Honored One!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva, for the sake of awakening, cultivates the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity, in what dharmas does there exist benefit or harm, increase or decrease, arising or ceasing, or defilement or purification?”
“World-Honored One!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva, for the sake of awakening, cultivates all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), in what dharmas does there exist benefit or harm, increase or decrease, arising or ceasing, or defilement or purification?”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom for the sake of awakening, they neither benefit nor harm, neither increase nor decrease, neither arise nor cease, and neither defile nor purify any phenomena.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva, for the sake of awakening, dwells in internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, he neither benefits nor harms any phenomenon; there is no increase and no decrease, no arising and no ceasing, and no defilement and no purification.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva, for the sake of awakening, abides in suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, non-alteration, equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm, he neither benefits nor harms any dharma; there is no increase and no decrease, no arising and no ceasing, and no defilement and no purification.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva, for the sake of awakening, cultivates the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path, they neither benefit nor harm, neither increase nor decrease, neither arise nor cease, and neither defile nor purify any phenomena.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in the noble truth of suffering, the noble truth of its origin, its cessation, and the path for the sake of awakening, they neither benefit nor harm, neither increase nor decrease, neither arise nor cease, and neither defile nor purify any phenomena.”

“Subhūti! When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, for the sake of awakening, cultivate the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments, they neither benefit nor harm any phenomena; there is no increase and no decrease, no arising and no ceasing, and no defilement and no purification.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva, for the sake of awakening, cultivates the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive concentrations, and the ten totalities, they neither benefit nor harm, neither increase nor decrease, neither arise nor cease, and neither defile nor purify any phenomena.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva, for the sake of awakening, cultivates the gateways of samādhi and the gateways of dhāraṇī, they neither benefit nor harm, neither increase nor decrease, neither arise nor cease, and neither defile nor purify any phenomena.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva, for the sake of awakening, cultivates the gate of liberation of emptiness, the gate of liberation of signlessness, and the gate of liberation of wishlessness, they neither benefit nor harm any phenomena; there is no increase and no decrease, no arising and no ceasing, and no defilement and no purification.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the five eyes and the six supernormal powers for the sake of awakening, regarding all phenomena they neither benefit nor harm them; there is no increase and no decrease, no arising and no ceasing, and no defilement and no purification.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva, for the sake of awakening, cultivates the ten powers of a buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, he neither benefits nor harms any dharma; there is no increase or decrease, no arising or ceasing, and no defilement or purification.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity for the sake of awakening, they neither benefit nor harm, neither increase nor decrease, neither arise nor cease, and neither defile nor purify any phenomena.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva, for the sake of awakening, cultivates the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity, they neither benefit nor harm, neither increase nor decrease, neither arise nor cease, and neither defile nor purify any phenomena.”

“Subhūti! When bodhisattva mahāsattvas, for the sake of awakening, cultivate all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), they neither benefit nor harm, neither increase nor decrease, neither produce nor extinguish, and neither defile nor purify any phenomena.”
"Why is this? Subhūti!

Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom for the sake of awakening, employing as a skillful means the fact that there is no objective referent whatsoever in any phenomenon; thus, neither benefit nor harm, neither increase nor decrease, neither arising nor ceasing, nor defilement nor purity, manifest before them."
The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying: “World-Honored One, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva, for the sake of awakening,

practices the profound perfection of wisdom by means of non-apprehension regarding all phenomena— neither for the sake of benefit nor harm, neither for increase nor decrease, neither for arising nor ceasing, and neither for defilement nor purification— how then does that bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, embrace the perfection of giving, and embrace the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom?”

How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, embrace internal emptiness, and embrace external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature?

How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, embrace true thusness (tathatā), embrace the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), non-illusoriness, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm?

How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, take up the four foundations of mindfulness, and take up the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path?
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, embrace the noble truth of suffering, and embrace the noble truths of its origin, its cessation, and the path?
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, embrace the four dhyānas, embrace the four immeasurables, and embrace the four formless attainments?

How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, take up the eight liberations, take up the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities?
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, embrace the gateways of samādhi and embrace the gateways of dhāraṇī?

How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, embrace the gate of liberation of emptiness, and embrace the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness?
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, take up the five eyes and take up the six supernormal powers?

How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, take up the ten powers of a buddha, take up the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha?
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, embrace great loving-kindness, embrace great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity?
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, embrace the quality of non-forgetfulness and embrace the nature of constant equanimity?

How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, embrace all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), embrace the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and embrace the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*)?

How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, transcend the stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, enter the bodhisattva’s state of rightness and departure from birth, cultivate the correct practice of the ten bodhisattva stages, and realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment?

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 365. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter Sixty-three, Part Two, "Skillful Means in Practice. The Buddha said, "Suvikrāntavikrāmin! "

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not, by means of duality, take up the perfection of generosity; nor do they, by means of duality, take up the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not, by way of duality, grasp at internal emptiness; nor do they, by way of duality, grasp at external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not apprehend suchness by way of duality; nor do they apprehend the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), non-illusory nature, unchanging nature, equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space, or the inconceivable realm by way of duality.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not, by way of duality, take up the four foundations of mindfulness; nor do they, by way of duality, take up the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not apprehend the noble truth of suffering by means of duality, nor do they apprehend the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path by means of duality.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not, by means of duality, take up the four dhyānas; nor do they, by means of duality, take up the four immeasurables or the four formless absorptions.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not, by means of duality, grasp at the eight liberations; nor do they, by means of duality, grasp at the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not grasp at the gateways of samādhi by means of duality, nor do they grasp at the gateways of dhāraṇī by means of duality.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not, by way of duality, take up the gate of liberation of emptiness, nor do they, by way of duality, take up the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not grasp at the five eyes by way of duality, nor do they grasp at the six supernormal powers by way of duality.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not, by way of duality, grasp at the ten powers of a buddha; nor do they, by way of duality, grasp at the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, or the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not embrace great loving-kindness by means of duality, nor do they embrace great compassion, great sympathetic joy, or great equanimity by means of duality.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not, by means of duality, grasp at the quality of non-forgetfulness, nor do they, by means of duality, grasp at the state of constant equanimity.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not grasp at all-knowledge by means of duality; they do not grasp at the knowledge of the aspects of the path or the knowledge of all aspects by means of duality.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not transcend the stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas by means of duality; they do not enter the bodhisattva’s state of right determination (*samyaktvaniyāma*) by means of duality; they do not practice the correct conduct of the ten bodhisattva stages by means of duality; and they do not realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment by means of duality.
The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:

“World-Honored One, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not, by way of duality, grasp at the perfection of giving; nor do they, by way of duality, grasp at the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom.”

One does not, by means of duality, grasp at internal emptiness; nor does one, by means of duality, grasp at external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

One does not, by means of duality, grasp at suchness; nor does one, by means of duality, grasp at the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-falsity, the non-alteration, the equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of dharma, the stability of dharma, the reality-limit, the realm of space, or the inconceivable realm.

One does not, by way of duality, embrace the four foundations of mindfulness; one does not, by way of duality, embrace the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path;
one does not, by way of duality, embrace the noble truth of suffering, nor does one, by way of duality, embrace the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path;
one does not, by way of duality, embrace the four dhyānas, nor does one, by way of duality, embrace the four immeasurables or the four formless absorptions.
One does not, by means of duality, grasp at the eight liberations; one does not, by means of duality, grasp at the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive absorptions, or the ten totalities;
one does not, by means of duality, grasp at the doors of samādhi, nor does one, by means of duality, grasp at the doors of dhāraṇī;
one does not, by means of duality, grasp at the door of the liberation of emptiness, nor does one, by means of duality, grasp at the doors of the liberations of signlessness and wishlessness.
One does not grasp at the five eyes by way of duality; one does not grasp at the six supernormal powers by way of duality.

One does not grasp at the ten powers of a Buddha by way of duality; one does not grasp at the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha by way of duality.
One does not grasp at great loving-kindness by way of duality; one does not grasp at great compassion, great sympathetic joy, or great equanimity by way of duality.

If one does not, by way of non-duality, embrace the quality of non-forgetfulness; if one does not, by way of non-duality, embrace the state of constant equanimity; if one does not, by way of non-duality, embrace all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*);
if one does not, by way of non-duality, embrace the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*);

if one does not, by way of non-duality, transcend the stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; if one does not, by way of non-duality, enter the bodhisattva’s state of rightness and departure from birth (*samyaktvaniyāma*); if one does not, by way of non-duality, practice the correct conduct of the ten bodhisattva stages; and if one does not, by way of non-duality, realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment—then how is it that a bodhisattva mahāsattva, from the first generation of the mind of awakening until the final moment of thought, increases in wholesome qualities at all times?
The Buddha said,
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices by means of duality, then all wholesome dharmas will not increase.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
Because all foolish ordinary beings rely on duality, the various wholesome dharmas they give rise to do not increase.
Because Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice non-duality, from the first generation of the mind of awakening until the arising of the final thought, wholesome dharmas increase at all times.

"Therefore, Subhūti, the roots of goodness of all bodhisattva mahāsattvas are firm and indomitable; the gods, humans, and asuras of the world cannot destroy them so as to cause them to fall to the level of a śrāvaka or a pratyekabuddha. Various evil and unwholesome dharmas of the world cannot overpower them such that the wholesome dharmas arising when they practice the perfection of giving do not increase, nor can they overpower them such that the wholesome dharmas arising when they practice the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom do not increase."

When one is unable to subdue [the mind] so that it abides in internal emptiness, the wholesome dharmas arising at that time cannot increase; when one is unable to subdue [the mind] so that it abides in external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, the wholesome dharmas arising at those times cannot increase.

They cannot subdue [the mind] so that the wholesome dharmas arising when one abides in *tathatā* (suchness) do not increase; they cannot subdue [the mind] so that the wholesome dharmas arising when one abides in the *dharmadhātu*, *dharmatā*, non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the reality-limit (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm do not increase;

they cannot subdue [the mind] so that the wholesome dharmas arising when one cultivates the four foundations of mindfulness do not increase; and they cannot subdue [the mind] so that the wholesome dharmas arising when one cultivates the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path do not increase.

They cannot be subdued such that the wholesome dharmas arising when abiding in the noble truth of suffering do not increase; they cannot be subdued such that the wholesome dharmas arising when abiding in the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path do not increase;

they cannot be subdued such that the wholesome dharmas arising when practicing the four dhyānas do not increase; they cannot be subdued such that the wholesome dharmas arising when practicing the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions do not increase;

they cannot be subdued such that the wholesome dharmas arising when practicing the gateways of samādhi do not increase; and they cannot be subdued such that the wholesome dharmas arising when practicing the gateways of dhāraṇī do not increase.

They cannot be subdued such that the wholesome dharmas arising when practicing the gate of liberation of emptiness do not increase; they cannot be subdued such that the wholesome dharmas arising when practicing the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness do not increase;

they cannot be subdued such that the wholesome dharmas arising when practicing the five eyes do not increase; they cannot be subdued such that the wholesome dharmas arising when practicing the six supernormal powers do not increase;

they cannot be subdued such that the wholesome dharmas arising when practicing the ten powers of a Buddha do not increase; and they cannot be subdued such that the wholesome dharmas arising when practicing the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha do not increase.

They cannot be subdued such that the wholesome dharmas arising when practicing great loving-kindness (*mahāmaitrī*) do not increase; they cannot be subdued such that the wholesome dharmas arising when practicing great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*), great sympathetic joy (*mahāmuditā*), and great equanimity (*mahopekṣā*) do not increase;

they cannot be subdued such that the wholesome dharmas arising when practicing the quality of non-forgetfulness (*asaṃpramoṣadharma*) do not increase; they cannot be subdued such that the wholesome dharmas arising when practicing the nature of constant abiding in equanimity (*upekṣāsthiti*) do not increase;

they cannot be subdued such that the wholesome dharmas arising when practicing all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) do not increase; and they cannot be subdued such that the wholesome dharmas arising when practicing the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) do not increase.
"Therefore, Subhūti, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should practice the profound perfection of wisdom in this manner.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
does a bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the profound perfection of wisdom for the sake of roots of goodness?
The Buddha said:

"No, Subhūti! A bodhisattva mahāsattva does not practice the profound perfection of wisdom for the sake of roots of virtue, nor does he practice the profound perfection of wisdom for the sake of unwholesome roots."
Why is this? Subhūti!

It is the natural law for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that if they have not yet reverently made offerings to the Buddhas, if they have not yet perfected their sublime roots of virtue, and if they have not been extensively sustained by true spiritual friends, they will ultimately be unable to attain the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva reverently make offerings to the Buddhas, fulfill sublime roots of goodness, and receive the extensive guidance of true spiritual friends, so as to be able to realize the knowledge of all modes?”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!
From their first production of the thought of awakening, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas reverently make offerings to immeasurable Tathāgatas, Arhats...”
Having heard from the various Buddhas the discourses (*sūtra*), verses (*geya*), prophecies (*vyākaraṇa*), stanzas (*gāthā*), spontaneous utterances (*udāna*),

past events (*itivṛttaka*), birth stories (*jātaka*), extensive teachings (*vaipulya*), marvelous accounts (*adbhutadharma*), parables (*avadāna*), and expositions (*upadeśa*)— the perfectly awakened ones—
he retains them all in his memory; having retained them, he honors them with body and speech and recites them.
One should rehearse them until they are thoroughly mastered; having mastered them, one observes them well with the mind;

having observed them well, one deeply perceives their underlying intent; having perceived the intent, one further attains thorough penetration; having attained thorough penetration, one acquires *dhāraṇī*;
having acquired *dhāraṇī*, one gives rise to unimpeded analytical knowledge (*pratisaṃvid*); and having given rise to unimpeded analytical knowledge, [one proceeds] even unto...
