one should know, as they truly are, the causes and effects of the paths of the Āsaṃjñika heavens. One should know, as they truly are...
One should know, as they truly are, the causes and effects of the paths to the Heaven Free from Affliction (Avṛha), the Heaven Free from Heat (Atapa), the Heaven of Excellent Appearance (Sudṛśa),

the Heaven of Good Vision (Sudarśana), and the Heaven of Ultimate Form (Akaniṣṭha); and one should likewise know, as they truly are, the causes and effects of the paths to the Sphere of Infinite Space (Ākāśānantyāyatana),
the Sphere of Infinite Consciousness (Vijñānānantyāyatana), the Sphere of Nothingness (Ākiṃcanyāyatana), and the Sphere of Neither Perception nor Non-perception (Naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana).
Having known this, one employs skillful means as appropriate to obstruct those paths along with their causes and effects,
or to encourage the adoption and cultivation of wholesome dharmas;
one should know, in accordance with reality, the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, and the five faculties.
One should know, as they truly are, the powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, the eightfold noble path, and their causes and fruits;
one should know, as they truly are, the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—and their causes and fruits;
one should know, as they truly are, the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path, and their causes and fruits. One should...
One should know the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, and their causes and fruits as they truly are;
one should know the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, the ten totalities, and their causes and fruits as they truly are;
and one should know generosity, pure ethical discipline, patience, and diligence as they truly are.
One should know, as they truly are, the perfections of dhyāna and prajñā,
along with their causes and fruits, as well as internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness,
great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, and unchanging emptiness.
One should know, as they truly are, the emptiness of the other, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics,
the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature,
and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature— along with their causes and effects— as well as suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, and the non-falsity of reality.

...the unchanging nature, the state of equality, the nature of being free from arising, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*), and their causes and fruits;
one should know all gateways of samādhi and all gateways of dhāraṇī, as well as their causes and fruits, exactly as they are. One should [know]...
One should truly know the five eyes and the six supernormal powers, as well as their causes and results; one should truly know the ten stages of a bodhisattva and their causes and results;

one should truly know the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and their causes and results; one should truly know the Great [Vehicle].
One should know as they truly are loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, and great equanimity, along with their causes and results;
one should know as they truly are the quality of non-forgetfulness, the state of constant abiding in equanimity, and their causes and results;

one should know as they truly are all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), along with their causes and results; and one should know as they truly are all sounds.
They hear of the path of the śrāvakas, the path of the pratyekabuddhas, the path of the bodhisattvas, and their respective causes and fruits. "Subhūti!
By means of such paths, these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas establish sentient beings."
If there are classes of sentient beings who are destined to attain the fruit of stream-entry, he establishes them by means of the dharmas of stream-entry;
those destined to attain the fruit of once-returning, he establishes them by means of the dharmas of once-returning;
and those destined to attain the fruit of non-returning, he establishes them by means of the dharmas of non-returning.
Those who are destined to attain the fruit of arhatship, he establishes them in the dharmas of the fruit of arhatship;
those who are destined to attain the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, he establishes them in the dharmas of the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha;
and those who are destined to attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, he establishes them in the dharmas of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
“Subhūti! This is called the knowledge of the aspects of all paths that a bodhisattva mahāsattva should initiate.

Having trained in this knowledge of the aspects of all paths, the bodhisattva mahāsattva thoroughly penetrates the various elements and natures of sentient beings, their various latent tendencies, and their various inclinations.”
Having thus attained realization, he teaches the True Dharma according to what is appropriate for each, causing all to obtain benefit and peace, so that none pass by in vain. Why is this?

"Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva skillfully penetrates the superior and inferior faculties of sentient beings, and knows as they truly are the distinctions in the inclinations of the minds and mental factors of all classes of sentient beings as they wander through birth and death."
“Subhūti! All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should practice the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) in this way regarding all these paths. Why is that?

"Subhūti! All paths that should be studied by all śrāvakas, all paths that should be studied by all pratyekabuddhas, and all paths that should be studied by all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas—all such factors of enlightenment (bodhipakṣadharma) are subsumed within the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā)."

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 369. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One, Chapter Sixty-four, "The Path of Universal Training," Section Five. At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"

If all factors conducive to enlightenment (*bodhipakṣadharma*) and all forms of enlightenment are in every respect neither associated nor dissociated, without conjunction, without dispersion, formless, invisible, non-obstructive, and of a single characteristic—namely, the characteristic of being signless (*animitta*)—how can such factors conducive to enlightenment apprehend enlightenment?
World-Honored One!

All these are neither associated nor dissociated; they are without conjunction, without dispersion, without form, without visibility, and without resistance. They are of a single characteristic, namely the characteristicless dharma (animitta-dharma), which is able to engage in taking up and discarding with respect to other dharmas.
World-Honored One!

For example, just as space neither grasps nor abandons any phenomena because its own characteristic is empty, so too are all phenomena: their own characteristics are all empty, and they neither grasp nor abandon other phenomena. How, then, can it be said that the factors of enlightenment (bodhipakṣa-dharmas) are able to grasp bodhi?
The Buddha said, “So it is, Subhūti!”
"So it is! It is just as you have said.

Because all phenomena are empty of their own characteristics (*svalakṣaṇa*), there is neither grasping nor abandoning; yet sentient beings are unable to comprehend this meaning of the emptiness of the own-characteristics of all phenomena. Out of compassion for them, I skillfully teach the factors of enlightenment (*bodhipākṣikadharma*) which can bring about the attainment of bodhi."
"Furthermore, Subhūti! Whether it be form, or feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness;
whether it be the eye base, or the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind base;
Whether it be the sphere of form, or the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental phenomena;
whether it be the eye-element, or the elements of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind;
or whether it be the element of forms, or the elements of sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, and mental phenomena.
Whether it be the eye-consciousness element, or the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements;
whether it be eye-contact, or ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact;
or whether it be the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition, or the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as condition.
Whether it be the earth element, or the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements;

whether it be ignorance, or volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair;
or whether it be the perfection of generosity, or the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.

Whether it be internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence;

whether it be suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-falsity, the non-alteration, the equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the reality-limit, the realm of space, or the inconceivable realm;
whether it be the first dhyāna, or the second, third, or fourth dhyānas.
Whether it be the immeasurable of loving-kindness, or the immeasurables of compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity;
whether it be the sphere of infinite space, the sphere of infinite consciousness, the sphere of nothingness, or the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception;

or whether it be the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path.
Whether it be the noble truth of suffering, or the noble truths of the origin, cessation, and the path;
whether it be the gate of liberation of emptiness, or the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness;
whether it be the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities.
Whether it be all the gateways of samādhi, or all the gateways of dhāraṇī;

whether it be the Ground of Extreme Joy, the Ground of Purity, the Ground of Radiant Light, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Difficult to Conquer, the Ground of Presence, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, or the Ground of the Dharma Cloud;
or whether it be the five eyes, or the six supernormal powers;
Whether it be the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
whether it be great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, or great equanimity;
whether it be the quality of non-forgetfulness or the state of constant abiding in equanimity.
Whether it be all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), or the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*);
whether it be the fruit of stream-entry (*srotāpattiphala*), or the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, or arhatship; or the awakening of a pratyekabuddha;

whether it be all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, or the permanent severance of the continuity of all habitual tendencies (*vāsanā*), or the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening of the Buddhas (*anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi*).

Whether it be the conditioned realm or the unconditioned realm—all such phenomena within this noble Dharma and Vinaya are neither associated nor dissociated; they are without conjunction, without dispersion, without form, invisible, and non-obstructive, possessing a single characteristic, namely, the characteristicless. It is for the benefit of all sentient beings, so that they may attain correct understanding and enter into the true reality of phenomena, that the Buddha speaks by way of conventional truth, not by way of ultimate truth.
"Subhūti! All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should train in knowledge and vision regarding all these phenomena. Having trained in knowledge and vision, they should realize them as they truly are:
'Such phenomena are to be grasped; such phenomena are not to be grasped.'"
“World-Honored One!
Regarding which dharmas should a bodhisattva-mahāsattva, having studied them with wisdom and vision and having realized them as they truly are, not take up?
And regarding which dharmas should he, having studied them with wisdom and vision and having realized them as they truly are, take up?”

“Subhūti! Having trained in the knowledge and vision regarding the dharmas of the stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should realize them as they truly are and not grasp at them;
having trained in the knowledge and vision regarding all dharmas associated with the knowledge of all aspects, he should realize them as they truly are and grasp at them in every respect.”
"Subhūti! Within this noble Dharma and Vinaya, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should train in the profound perfection of wisdom in this manner."
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
Regarding what the Buddha calls the ‘Noble Dharma and Vinaya,’ what is meant by the ‘Noble Dharma and Vinaya’?”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

Whether they be śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, or tathāgatas, arhats, samyaksaṃbuddhas—all such as these are neither associated nor dissociated with greed, hatred, and delusion; they are neither conjoined nor dispersed.”

All are neither associated nor dissociated with the view of a self-identity (*satkāyadṛṣṭi*), the grasping at precepts and observances (*śīlavrataparāmarśa*), and doubt; they are neither conjoined nor dispersed with them.
All are neither associated nor dissociated with sensual desire (*kāmarāga*) and ill will (*vyāpāda*); they are neither conjoined nor dispersed with them.

All are neither associated nor dissociated with attachment to the realm of form (*rūparāga*), attachment to the formless realm (*ārūpyarāga*), restlessness (*auddhatya*), conceit (*māna*), and ignorance (*avidyā*); they are neither conjoined nor dispersed with them.
All are neither associated nor dissociated with the first dhyāna; they are neither conjoined nor dispersed;
all are neither associated nor dissociated with the second, third, and fourth dhyānas; they are neither conjoined nor dispersed;
all are neither associated nor dissociated with the immeasurable of loving-kindness (*maitrī*); they are neither conjoined nor dispersed.
All are neither associated nor dissociated with the immeasurables of compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity; they are neither conjoined nor dispersed from them.
All are neither associated nor dissociated with the concentration of the sphere of infinite space; they are neither conjoined nor dispersed from it.

All are neither associated nor dissociated with the concentrations of the sphere of infinite consciousness, the sphere of nothingness, and the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception; they are neither conjoined nor dispersed from them.
They are all neither associated nor dissociated with the four foundations of mindfulness; they are neither conjoined nor dispersed with them.

They are all neither associated nor dissociated with the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path; they are neither conjoined nor dispersed with them.
They are all neither associated nor dissociated with the noble truth of suffering; they are neither conjoined nor dispersed with it.
They are all neither associated nor dissociated with the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path;
they are all neither associated nor dissociated with the gate of liberation of emptiness;
they are all neither associated nor dissociated with the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness; they are neither conjoined nor dispersed.
All are neither associated nor dissociated with the eight liberations; they are neither conjoined nor dispersed with them.
All are neither associated nor dissociated with the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities; they are neither conjoined nor dispersed with them.
All are neither associated nor dissociated with the five eyes; they are neither conjoined nor dispersed with them.
All are neither associated nor dissociated with the six superknowledges; they are neither conjoined nor dispersed with them.
All are neither associated nor dissociated with the perfection of generosity; they are neither conjoined nor dispersed with it.
All are neither associated nor dissociated with the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; they are neither conjoined nor dispersed with them.
All are neither associated nor dissociated with internal emptiness; they are neither conjoined nor dispersed.

All are neither associated nor dissociated, neither conjoined nor dispersed, with external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, emptiness of all phenomena, unapprehendable emptiness, non-existence emptiness, self-nature emptiness, and non-existence-of-self-nature emptiness.
All are neither associated nor dissociated, neither conjoined nor dispersed, with suchness.

They are all neither associated nor dissociated with the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, the non-falsity, the immutability, the equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of empty space, and the inconceivable realm;
they are neither associated nor dissociated with the Stage of Extreme Joy, neither conjoined nor dispersed;

they are neither associated nor dissociated with the Stage of Purity, the Stage of Radiance, the Stage of Blazing Wisdom, the Stage of Supreme Difficulty to Conquer, the Stage of Presence, the Stage of Far-Going, the Stage of Immovability, the Stage of Excellent Intelligence, and the Stage of the Cloud of Dharma, neither conjoined nor dispersed.
All are neither associated nor dissociated with all samādhi-doors; they are neither conjoined nor dispersed;
all are neither associated nor dissociated with all dhāraṇī-doors; they are neither conjoined nor dispersed;
all are neither associated nor dissociated with the ten powers of a Buddha; they are neither conjoined nor dispersed.

They are neither associated nor dissociated with the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; they are neither conjoined nor dispersed with them.
They are neither associated nor dissociated with great loving-kindness; they are neither conjoined nor dispersed with it.
They are neither associated nor dissociated with great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity; they are neither conjoined nor dispersed with them.
All are neither associated nor dissociated with the quality of non-forgetfulness; they are neither conjoined nor dispersed with it;
all are neither associated nor dissociated with the nature of constant equanimity; they are neither conjoined nor dispersed with it;
all are neither associated nor dissociated with omniscience; they are neither conjoined nor dispersed with it.
All of them are neither associated nor dissociated with the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects; they are neither conjoined nor dispersed with them.
All of them are neither associated nor dissociated with the realm of the conditioned; they are neither conjoined nor dispersed with it.
All of them are neither associated nor dissociated with the realm of the unconditioned; they are neither conjoined nor dispersed with it.
“Subhūti! They are called ‘noble ones’ (ārya), and this is their noble Dharma-Vinaya; therefore it is called the ‘Noble Dharma-Vinaya. Why is that?

"Subhūti! All these phenomena are formless, invisible, non-obstructive, and of a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of being without characteristics; those noble ones perceive them as they truly are."
"Subhūti! Formlessness and formlessness are neither associated nor dissociated; they are neither conjoined nor dispersed.

Likewise, the invisible and the invisible, the non-obstructive and the non-obstructive, the single-characteristic and the single-characteristic, and the signless and the signless are also neither associated nor dissociated; they are neither conjoined nor dispersed."

"Subhūti! Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should constantly study this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, which is formless, invisible, non-obstructive, of a single characteristic, and signless; having studied it, they do not apprehend the characteristics of any phenomena."
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha,
saying: “World-Honored One,
should a bodhisattva mahāsattva not train in the characteristics of form, and should they also train in the characteristics of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness?”
Should one not train in the characteristics of the sense-base of the eye? Should one also train in the characteristics of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind?
Should one not train in the characteristics of the sense-base of forms? Should one also train in the characteristics of the sense-bases of sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, and mental phenomena?
Should one not train in the characteristics of the eye-element, and likewise train in the characteristics of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-elements?
Should one not train in the characteristics of the form-element, and likewise train in the characteristics of the sound, odor, taste, tangible, and mental-object elements?
Should one not train in the characteristics of the eye-consciousness element, and likewise train in the characteristics of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements?
Should one not train in the characteristics of eye-contact, and likewise train in the characteristics of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact?

Should one not train in the characteristics of all feelings arising conditioned by eye-contact, and likewise train in the characteristics of all feelings arising conditioned by ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact?
Should one not study the characteristics of the earth element? Should one also study the characteristics of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements?

Should one not study the characteristic of ignorance? Should one also study the characteristics of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair?

Should one not train in the characteristics of the perfection of generosity, and likewise train in the characteristics of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom?

Should one not train in the characteristic of internal emptiness? Should one also train in the characteristics of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence?

Should one not train in the characteristics of *tathatā* (suchness), and should one also train in the characteristics of the *dharmadhātu* (dharma-realm), *dharmatā* (dharma-nature), non-illusoriness, immutability, equality, the nature of being free from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm?
Should one not train in the characteristics of the first dhyāna? Should one also train in the characteristics of the second, third, and fourth dhyānas?

Should one not train in the characteristic of the immeasurable state of loving-kindness (maitrī)? Should one also train in the characteristics of the immeasurable states of compassion (karuṇā), sympathetic joy (muditā), and equanimity (upekṣā)?

Should one not train in the sign of the sphere of infinite space? Should one also train in the signs of the sphere of infinite consciousness, the sphere of nothingness, and the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception?

Should one not train in the characteristics of the four foundations of mindfulness? Should one also train in the characteristics of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path?
Should one not train in the characteristics of the gate of liberation of emptiness, and likewise train in the characteristics of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness?
Should one not train in the characteristics of the noble truth of suffering, and likewise train in the characteristics of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path?

Should one not train in the characteristics of the eight liberations? Should one also train in the characteristics of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities?
Should one not train in the characteristics of the five eyes? And should one also train in the characteristics of the six supernormal powers?
Should one not train in the characteristics of all samādhi-gates, and should one also train in the characteristics of all dhāraṇī-gates?

Should one not train in the characteristics of the Ground of Extreme Joy, and should one also train in the characteristics of the Ground of Purity, the Ground of Luminous Radiance, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Difficult to Conquer, the Ground of Manifestation, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, and the Ground of the Dharma Cloud?

Should one not study the characteristics of the ten powers of a Buddha? Should one also study the characteristics of the four fearlessnesses, the four unhindered analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?
Should one not train in the characteristics of great loving-kindness? Should one also train in the characteristics of great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity?
Should one not train in the characteristics of the quality of non-forgetfulness? And should one also train in the characteristics of the state of constant abiding in equanimity?

Should one not train in the characteristics of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), and should one also train in the characteristics of the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*)?

Should one not train in the characteristics of the fruit of stream-entry (*srotāpattiphala*), and should one also train in the characteristics of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, arhatship, and the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha?

Should one not train in the characteristics of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas’ practices, and should one also train in the characteristics of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas?

Should one not train in the characteristics of knowing suffering, abandoning its origin, realizing its cessation, and cultivating the path? Should one also train in the characteristics of the contemplation of dependent origination in both forward and reverse order?
Should one not train in the characteristics of all noble ones, and should one also train in the characteristics of all noble dharmas?
Should one not train in the characteristics of the conditioned realm, and should one also train in the characteristics of the unconditioned realm?
“World-Honored One!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train in the characteristics of these dharmas, nor should they train in the characteristics of conditioned formations (*saṃskāra*).
Since bodhisattva mahāsattvas cannot train in the characteristics of dharmas or the characteristics of formations, how can they transcend the stages of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas?”
If one cannot transcend the stages of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, how can one enter the bodhisattva’s state of rightness and departure from birth?
If one cannot enter the bodhisattva’s state of rightness and departure from birth, how can one attain the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna)?
If one cannot attain the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), how can one turn the wheel of the true Dharma?

If one cannot turn the wheel of the true Dharma, how can one establish sentient beings in the vehicle of the śrāvakas, or the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas, or the unsurpassed vehicle, thereby causing them to escape the manifold sufferings of boundless birth and death?
The Buddha said,
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
If all phenomena possessed real characteristics, bodhisattva mahāsattvas should train within them.”

Because all dharmas are in reality without marks—being formless, invisible, non-resistant, and of a single mark, namely, the markless—therefore, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva does not train in dharmas with marks, nor does he train in dharmas without marks.
Why is this? Subhūti!

Whether a Tathāgata appears in the world or does not appear, the dharma-realm remains eternally constant; all phenomena possess a single characteristic, namely, the absence of characteristics (*animitta*). Thus, this absence of characteristics is neither a presence of characteristics nor an absence of characteristics.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

If all dharmas are neither characterized by existence nor characterized by non-existence, they should be neither of a single characteristic nor of diverse characteristics. If this is so, how can a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivate the perfection of wisdom?”
If one cannot cultivate the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), how can one transcend the stages of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas?
If one cannot transcend the stages of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, how can one enter the bodhisattva’s state of rightness and departure from birth (*samyaktvaniyāma*)?
If one cannot enter the bodhisattva’s state of right determination and departure from birth, how can one give rise to the bodhisattva’s patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena?
If one cannot give rise to the bodhisattva’s patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena, how can one manifest the bodhisattva’s supernormal powers?
If one cannot manifest the supernormal powers of a bodhisattva, how can one bring sentient beings to maturity and purify buddha-fields?
If one cannot bring sentient beings to maturity and purify buddha-fields, how can one attain the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna)?
If one cannot attain the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), how can one turn the wheel of the true Dharma?

If one cannot turn the wheel of the true Dharma, then one should be unable to establish sentient beings so that they attain the fruits of stream-entry, once-returning, non-returning, or arhatship; nor should one be able to establish sentient beings so that they attain the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, nor establish sentient beings so that they attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; nor should one be able to establish sentient beings so that they abide in meritorious actions consisting of giving, or abide in meritorious actions consisting of ethical discipline, or abide in meritorious actions consisting of cultivation, thereby attaining the sovereignty of wealth and happiness among gods and humans.
The Buddha said, “So it is, Subhūti!”
"So it is! It is just as you have said.

All dharmas have no marks, no absence of marks, no single mark, and no diverse marks. If a bodhisattva mahāsattva knows that all dharmas—whether they have marks, lack marks, possess a single mark, or possess diverse marks—are all of one and the same mark, namely, the markless (animitta), then cultivating this marklessness is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā)."
The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
how is it that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates this signlessness, he is cultivating the perfection of wisdom?”
The Buddha said,
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the dispatching of all phenomena, this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.”
“World-Honored One!
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the dispatching of all dharmas; how is this the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [The Buddha replied:]”
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the relinquishing of form and also relinquishes this cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;
if they cultivate the relinquishing of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, and also relinquish this cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.
"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the relinquishing of the sense-base of the eye and also relinquishes this very practice, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;
if they practice the relinquishing of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind and also relinquish this very practice, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom."
"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the relinquishing of the sphere of form and also relinquishes this very practice, that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;

if they practice the relinquishing of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, and also relinquish this very practice, that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom."
“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the dispatching of the eye-element and also dispatches that cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;
if they cultivate the dispatching of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements and also dispatch that cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.”
“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the dispatching of the form realm and also dispatches this cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;

if they cultivate the dispatching of the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, and also dispatch this cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.”

"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the dispatching of the eye-consciousness element and also dispatches that practice itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom. To practice the dispatching of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements and also dispatch that practice itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom."
“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the relinquishing of eye-contact and also relinquishes that cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;
if they cultivate the relinquishing of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact and also relinquish that cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.”

"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the dispatching of all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition, and also dispatches that cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;

if they cultivate the dispatching of all feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions, and also dispatch that cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom."
“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the dispatching of the earth element and also dispatches this very practice, that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;
if they practice the dispatching of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements and also dispatch this very practice, that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the dispatching of the causal condition (*hetu-pratyaya*) and also dispatches this very practice, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).

To practice the dispatching of the immediately preceding condition (*samanantara-pratyaya*), the object-condition (*ālambana-pratyaya*), and the dominant condition (*adhipati-pratyaya*), and also to dispatch this very practice, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.”
“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the dispatching of ignorance and also the dispatching of this cultivation, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.

If they cultivate the dispatching of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair, and also the dispatching of this cultivation, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the dispatching of *āyuha* and *nirāyuha*, and also dispatches that cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).
If they cultivate the dispatching of the contemplation of impurity (*aśubhabhāvanā*), and also dispatches that cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.”
“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the dispatching of the first dhyāna and also dispatches that cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;
if they cultivate the dispatching of the second, third, and fourth dhyānas and also dispatch those cultivations themselves, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.”
“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the cultivation of the immeasurable loving-kindness while also relinquishing that cultivation, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;
if they cultivate the cultivation of the immeasurable compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity while also relinquishing those cultivations, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the meditative absorption of the sphere of infinite space and then relinquishes even that cultivation, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;

if they cultivate the meditative absorptions of the sphere of infinite consciousness, the sphere of nothingness, and the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, and then relinquish even those cultivations, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.”
“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the recollection of the Buddha while also relinquishing that cultivation, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;

if they cultivate the recollection of the Dharma, the recollection of the Saṅgha, the recollection of ethical discipline, the recollection of generosity, the recollection of the devas, the recollection with skillful means, the recollection without skillful means, the recollection of tranquility, and the recollection of mindfulness of inhalation and exhalation while also relinquishing that cultivation, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the relinquishing of the perception of impermanence and also relinquishes this cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.

To cultivate the relinquishing of the perception of impermanence and suffering, the perception of suffering and non-self, the perception of impurity, the perception of revulsion toward food, the perception that all worlds are not worth delighting in, the perception of death, the perception of abandonment, the perception of detachment, and the perception of cessation—and also to relinquish this cultivation itself—this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.”
“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the dispatching of the notion of a self and also dispatches this very practice, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.

To practice the dispatching of the notion of a sentient being, the notion of a life-principle, the notion of a living being, the notion of a nourisher, the notion of a spirit, the notion of a person, the notion of a mind-born, the notion of a youth, the notion of an agent, the notion of one who causes to act, the notion of an experiencer, the notion of one who causes to experience, the notion of a knower, the notion of one who causes to know, and the notion of a seer, and also to dispatch this very practice—this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the cultivation of the dispatching of the notion of permanence and impermanence, and also dispatches that very cultivation, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.

To practice the cultivation of the dispatching of the notion of pleasure and suffering, the notion of self and non-self, the notion of purity and impurity, the notion of remoteness and non-remoteness, and the notion of tranquility and non-tranquility, and also to dispatch that very cultivation, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the dispatching of the four foundations of mindfulness and also dispatches that cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;

if they cultivate the dispatching of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path, and also dispatch that cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the dispatching of the gate of liberation of emptiness and also dispatches this cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;
if they cultivate the dispatching of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness and also dispatch this cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.”
“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the dispatching of the eight liberations and also dispatches this cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;

if they cultivate the dispatching of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities and also dispatch this cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the cultivation of the samādhi with directed thought and sustained investigation while also relinquishing that very cultivation, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;

if they practice the cultivation of the samādhi without directed thought and with only sustained investigation, and the samādhi without directed thought and without sustained investigation, while also relinquishing those very cultivations, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.”
“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the relinquishing of the noble truth of suffering and also relinquishes this cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;
if they cultivate the relinquishing of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path and also relinquish this cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.”
“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the dispatching of the knowledge of suffering and also dispatches this cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.

To cultivate the dispatching of the knowledge of origin, the knowledge of cessation, the knowledge of the path, the knowledge of exhaustion, the knowledge of non-arising, the knowledge of phenomena, the subsequent knowledge, conventional knowledge, the knowledge of others’ minds, and the knowledge of things as they truly are—and also to dispatch this cultivation itself—is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.”
“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the dispatching of the perfection of generosity and also dispatches that practice itself, this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom;

if they practice the dispatching of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, and also dispatch those practices themselves, this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the cultivation of the emptiness of the internal and also cultivates the relinquishing of this practice, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.

To cultivate the relinquishing of the emptiness of the external, the emptiness of the internal and external, the emptiness of emptiness, the great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate, the emptiness of the conditioned, the emptiness of the unconditioned, the absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature—and also to cultivate the relinquishing of these practices—this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.”
“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the dispatching of the Stage of Extreme Joy and also dispatches this very practice, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.

To practice the dispatching of the Stage of Freedom from Defilement, the Radiant Stage, the Blazing Wisdom Stage, the Extremely Difficult to Conquer Stage, the Manifest Stage, the Far-Reaching Stage, the Immovable Stage, the Stage of Excellent Intelligence, and the Cloud of Dharma Stage—and also to dispatch this very practice—is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.”
“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the dispatching of the five eyes and also dispatches this very practice, that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;
if they practice the dispatching of the six superknowledges and also dispatch this very practice, that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.”
“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the dispatching of the ten powers of a buddha and also dispatches this cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;

if they cultivate the dispatching of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha and also dispatch this cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.”
“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the dispatching of great loving-kindness and also dispatches that cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;

if they cultivate the dispatching of great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity, and also dispatch those cultivations themselves, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.”
“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the dispatching of the quality of non-forgetfulness and also dispatches that practice itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;
if they practice the dispatching of the state of constant equanimity and also dispatch that practice itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.”
“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the dispatching of all samādhi-gates and also dispatches this cultivation itself, that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;
if they cultivate the dispatching of all dhāraṇī-gates and also dispatch this cultivation itself, that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the dispatching of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) while also dispatching that very cultivation, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).

If they cultivate the dispatching of the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), while also dispatching that very cultivation, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.”
“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the relinquishing of the fruit of a stream-enterer and also relinquishes this practice itself, that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;

if they practice the relinquishing of the fruits of a once-returner, a non-returner, and an arhat, as well as the awakening of a pratyekabuddha, and also relinquish this practice itself, that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.”
“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the dispatching of all bodhisattva mahāsattva practices and also dispatches this very practice, that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;
if they practice the dispatching of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas and also dispatch this very practice, that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.”

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the dispatching of all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna) while also dispatching that very practice, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

If they practice the dispatching of the perpetual severance of the continuity of all afflictions (kleśa) along with their habitual tendencies (vāsanā), while also dispatching that very practice, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.”
“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the dispatching of the conditioned realm and also dispatches this very practice, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;
if he practices the dispatching of the unconditioned realm and also dispatches this very practice, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.”
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha,
saying: “World-Honored One,
how is it that a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s cultivation of the elimination of form, while also eliminating this very cultivation, constitutes the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom?”

“If one cultivates the relinquishing of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, and furthermore relinquishes this very cultivation— is this the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom?
The Buddha said, “Excellent, Subhūti!”

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), if they conceive of form as existing and practice with the intent to eliminate it, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom;
if they conceive of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness as existing and practice with the intent to eliminate them, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Why is this? Subhūti!
One who possesses conceptualization is not able to cultivate the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the dispatching of form and also dispatches this practice itself, that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;
if they practice the dispatching of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, and also dispatch this practice itself, that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.
“World-Honored One!
How is it that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the relinquishing of the sense-base of the eye and also relinquishes this very practice, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;
and when they practice the relinquishing of the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind and also relinquish this very practice, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom?”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, if they conceive of the sphere of the eye as something to be abandoned through this cultivation, they are not cultivating the perfection of wisdom;
if they conceive of the spheres of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind as things to be abandoned through this cultivation, they are not cultivating the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
One who possesses conceptualization is not able to cultivate the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the relinquishing of the sense base of the eye and also relinquishes this cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;
if they cultivate the relinquishing of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind and also relinquish this cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How is it that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the relinquishing of the sphere of form (*rūpāyatana*) and also relinquishes this very practice, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*);

and when they practice the relinquishing of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena (*dharmāyatana*) and also relinquish this very practice, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom?”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, if they conceive of the sphere of forms as something to be eliminated through this cultivation, they are not cultivating the perfection of wisdom;
if they conceive of the spheres of sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, or mental phenomena as something to be eliminated through this cultivation, they are not cultivating the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
One who possesses conceptualization is not able to cultivate the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the relinquishing of the sphere of form and also relinquishes that cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;

if they cultivate the relinquishing of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena and also relinquish that cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.
“World-Honored One!
How is it that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the relinquishing of the eye-element and also relinquishes this very practice, he is practicing the perfection of wisdom;
and when he practices the relinquishing of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements and also relinquishes this very practice, he is practicing the perfection of wisdom?”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, if they conceive of the existence of the eye-element and practice with the intent of its removal, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom;
if they conceive of the existence of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-element and practice with the intent of their removal, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
One who possesses conceptualization is not able to cultivate the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the relinquishing of the eye-element and also relinquishes that cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;
if they cultivate the relinquishing of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements and also relinquish that cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.
“World-Honored One!
How is it that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the dispatching of the realm of form and also dispatches this very practice, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;
and when they practice the dispatching of the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena and also dispatch this very practice, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom?”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, if they think that there is a realm of form and that there is a cultivation which dispels it, they are not cultivating the perfection of wisdom;
if they think that there are realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena and that there is a cultivation which dispels them, they are not cultivating the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
One who possesses conceptualization is not able to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.
Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the dispatching of the realm of form and also dispatches this very practice, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;
if they practice the dispatching of the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, and also dispatch this very practice, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How is it that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the relinquishing of the eye-consciousness element and also relinquishes this very practice, that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;
and when they practice the relinquishing of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements and also relinquish this very practice, that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom?”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, if they think that there is an element of visual consciousness and that there is a cultivation involving its removal, they are not cultivating the perfection of wisdom;

if they think that there are elements of auditory, olfactory, gustatory, tactile, or mental consciousness and that there is a cultivation involving their removal, they are not cultivating the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
One who possesses conceptualization is not able to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.

Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the relinquishment of the eye-consciousness element and also relinquishes this cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;

if they cultivate the relinquishment of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements and also relinquish this cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.
“World-Honored One!
How is it that a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the dispatching of eye-contact and also the dispatching of this practice—that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom?
How is it that they practice the dispatching of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact and also the dispatching of this practice—that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom?”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, if they think that there is eye-contact and that there is the cultivation of its removal, they are not cultivating the perfection of wisdom;
if they think that there is ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact and that there is the cultivation of their removal, they are not cultivating the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
One who possesses conceptualization is not able to cultivate the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the relinquishing of eye-contact and also relinquishes that practice itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;
if they practice the relinquishing of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact and also relinquish that practice itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivate the dispatching of all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition, and also dispatch this very cultivation—this being the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;

and how does he cultivate the dispatching of all feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions, and also dispatch this very cultivation—this being the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom?”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, if they think that there is a cultivation involving the removal of those feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, they are not cultivating the perfection of wisdom;

if they think that there is a cultivation involving the removal of those feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as conditions, they are not cultivating the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
One who possesses conceptualization is not able to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.

Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the relinquishing of all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition, and also cultivates the relinquishing of that cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;

if they cultivate the relinquishing of all feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions, and also cultivate the relinquishing of that cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.
“World-Honored One!
How is it that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the dispatching of the earth element and also dispatches this very practice, they are practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā);
and how is it that when they practice the dispatching of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements and also dispatch this very practice, they are practicing the perfection of wisdom?”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, if they conceive of the earth element as something to be dispelled through this cultivation, they are not cultivating the perfection of wisdom;
if they conceive of the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements as something to be dispelled through this cultivation, they are not cultivating the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
One who possesses conceptualization is not able to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.
Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the relinquishing of the earth element and also relinquishes that cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;
if they cultivate the relinquishing of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements and also relinquish that cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How is it that a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the dispatching of causal conditions (*hetu-pratyaya*) and also dispatches this very practice—this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*)?

How is it that they practice the dispatching of the immediately preceding condition (*samanantara-pratyaya*), the object-condition (*ālambana-pratyaya*), and the dominant condition (*adhipati-pratyaya*), and also dispatch this very practice—this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom?”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, if they conceive of there being a causal condition (hetu-pratyaya) that involves the rejection of this cultivation, they are not cultivating the perfection of wisdom;

if they conceive of there being an immediately preceding condition (samanantara-pratyaya), an object-condition (ālambana-pratyaya), or a dominant condition (adhipati-pratyaya) that involves the rejection of this cultivation, they are not cultivating the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
One who possesses conceptualization is not able to cultivate the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the relinquishing of the causal condition (*hetu-pratyaya*) while also relinquishing that very practice, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).

If they practice the relinquishing of the equal-and-immediate condition (*samanantara-pratyaya*), the object-condition (*ālambana-pratyaya*), and the dominant condition (*adhipati-pratyaya*), while also relinquishing that very practice, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 373. Translated by the Dharma Master Xuanzang under Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter Sixty-four, "The Path of Universal Training," Section Six. "World-Honored One!..."
How is it that a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the dispatching of ignorance and also the dispatching of this cultivation—that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom?

How is it that they cultivate the dispatching of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair, and also the dispatching of this cultivation—that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom?

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, if they think that there is ignorance which can be dispelled through this cultivation, they are not cultivating the perfection of wisdom;

if they think that there are formative forces up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair which can be dispelled through this cultivation, they are not cultivating the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
One who possesses conceptualization is not able to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.
Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the dispatching of ignorance and also the dispatching of this cultivation, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;

if they cultivate the dispatching of formative factors up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, and also the dispatching of this cultivation, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How is it that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the cultivation of the dispatching of *ayūha* and *niryūha*, and further dispatches this very cultivation, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*)?

And how is it that when they practice the cultivation of the dispatching of the contemplation of impurity (*aśubhabhāvanā*), and further dispatch this very cultivation, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom?”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, if they think that there is an *ayuta* or a *nayuta* [of moments] through which this cultivation is dispelled, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom;
if they think that there is the meditation on impurity (*aśubha-bhāvanā*) through which this cultivation is dispelled, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
One who possesses conceptualization is not able to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.
Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the dispatching of *ayogha* and *nayogha*, and further dispatches that very practice, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;
if they practice the dispatching of the meditation on impurity (*aśubhabhāvanā*), and further dispatches that very practice, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.
“World-Honored One!
How is it that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the cultivation of the first dhyāna and also abandons this cultivation, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā);
and when they practice the cultivation of the second, third, and fourth dhyānas and also abandon this cultivation, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom?”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, if they conceive of the first dhyāna as something to be abandoned through this cultivation, they are not cultivating the perfection of wisdom;
if they conceive of the second, third, or fourth dhyānas as things to be abandoned through this cultivation, they are not cultivating the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
One who possesses conceptualization is not able to cultivate the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the relinquishing of the first dhyāna and also relinquishes that cultivation, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;
if they cultivate the relinquishing of the second, third, and fourth dhyānas and also relinquish that cultivation, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How is it that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the dispatching of the immeasurable loving-kindness and also dispatches this cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;

and when they cultivate the dispatching of the immeasurable compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity and also dispatch these cultivations themselves, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom?”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, if they conceive of the immeasurable loving-kindness as something to be dispatched while practicing it, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom;
if they conceive of the immeasurable compassion, sympathetic joy, or equanimity as things to be dispatched while practicing them, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
One who possesses conceptualization is not able to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.

Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the dispatching of the immeasurable loving-kindness and also dispatches that cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;
if they cultivate the dispatching of the immeasurable compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity and also dispatch those cultivations themselves, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How is it that a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the meditative concentration of the sphere of infinite space and then relinquishes even this cultivation—that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom?

How is it that they cultivate the meditative concentrations of the sphere of infinite consciousness, the sphere of nothingness, and the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, and then relinquish even these cultivations—that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom?”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, if they think that there is the meditative absorption of the sphere of infinite space and that there is the cultivation of its relinquishment, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom;

if they think that there is the meditative absorption of the sphere of infinite consciousness, the sphere of nothingness, or the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception and that there is the cultivation of their relinquishment, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
One who possesses conceptualization is not able to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.

Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the meditative absorption of the sphere of infinite space while also relinquishing that cultivation, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;

if they cultivate the meditative absorptions of the sphere of infinite consciousness, the sphere of nothingness, and the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception while also relinquishing those cultivations, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.
“World-Honored One!
How is it that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the cultivation of the recollection of the Buddha and also relinquishes this cultivation, that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;

and how is it that when they practice the cultivation of the recollection of the Dharma, the recollection of the Saṅgha, the recollection of ethical discipline, the recollection of generosity, the recollection of the devas, the recollection with skillful means, the recollection without skillful means, the recollection of tranquility, and the recollection of mindfulness of inhalation and exhalation, and also relinquish these cultivations, that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom?”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, if they maintain mindfulness of a Buddha or maintain mindfulness accompanied by the conceptualization of that mindfulness, this is not the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;

if they maintain mindfulness of dharmas, or even mindfulness of the inhalation and exhalation of breath accompanied by the conceptualization of that mindfulness, this is not the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
One who possesses conceptualization is not able to cultivate the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the recollection of the Buddha while also relinquishing that cultivation, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;

if they cultivate the recollection of the Dharma, up to and including the recollection of mindfulness of inhalation and exhalation, while also relinquishing those cultivations, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.
“World-Honored One!
How is it that a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the dispatching of the perception of impermanence and also dispatches this cultivation itself—that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom?

How is it that they cultivate the dispatching of the perception of suffering in the impermanent, the perception of non-self in suffering, the perception of impurity, the perception of revulsion toward food, the perception that all worlds are not worth delighting in, the perception of death, the perception of abandonment, the perception of detachment, and the perception of cessation—and also dispatch this cultivation itself—that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom?”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, if they think there is the perception of impermanence and that there is a cultivation which dispels it, they are not cultivating the perfection of wisdom;

if they think there is the perception of suffering in impermanence, up to the perception of cessation, and that there is a cultivation which dispels it, they are not cultivating the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
One who possesses conceptualization is not able to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.

Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the relinquishing of the perception of impermanence and also relinquishes that cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;

if they cultivate the relinquishing of the perception of suffering in impermanence, up to the perception of cessation, and also relinquish that cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.
“World-Honored One!
How is it that a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the dispatching of the notion of a self (*ātma-saṃjñā*) and also the dispatching of this very practice;

how is it that practicing the dispatching of the notion of a sentient being (*sattva-saṃjñā*), the notion of a life-principle (*jīva-saṃjñā*), the notion of a living being (*jantu-saṃjñā*), the notion of a nourisher (*poṣa-saṃjñā*), the notion of a person (*puruṣa-saṃjñā*), the notion of an individual (*pudgala-saṃjñā*), the notion of a mind-born (*manuja-saṃjñā*), the notion of a human (*mānava-saṃjñā*), the notion of an agent (*kāraka-saṃjñā*), the notion of an experiencer (*vedaka-saṃjñā*), the notion of one who causes to experience (*janayitṛ-vedaka-saṃjñā*), the notion of a knower (*jñātṛ-saṃjñā*), the notion of one who causes to know (*janayitṛ-jñātṛ-saṃjñā*), the notion of a seer (*draṣṭṛ-saṃjñā*), and the notion of one who causes to see (*janayitṛ-draṣṭṛ-saṃjñā*)—and also the dispatching of this very practice—is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*)?”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, if they conceive the notion of a self and practice with the intent to dispel it, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom;
if they conceive the notion of a sentient being, and so forth, up to the notion of a seer, and practice with the intent to dispel it, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
One who possesses conceptualization is unable to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.
Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the relinquishing of the notion of a self and also relinquishes that very practice, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;

if they practice the relinquishing of the notion of a sentient being, up to and including the notion of a seer, and also relinquish that very practice, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivate the relinquishing of the perception of permanence and impermanence, and furthermore relinquish that very cultivation—this being the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;

how does he cultivate the relinquishing of the perception of pleasure and non-pleasure, self and non-self, purity and impurity, detachment and non-detachment, and tranquility and non-tranquility, and furthermore relinquish that very cultivation—this being the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom?”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, if they entertain the notion that there is permanence and cultivate the removal of the notion of impermanence, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom;
