if they entertain the notion that there is pleasure and the notion of non-pleasure, up to the notion of tranquility and the notion of non-tranquility, and cultivate the removal of these, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
One who possesses conceptualization is not able to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.

Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the relinquishing of the perception of permanence and impermanence, and also relinquishes that cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;

if they cultivate the relinquishing of the perception of pleasure and non-pleasure, up to the perception of tranquility and non-tranquility, and also relinquish that cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How is it that a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the relinquishing of the four foundations of mindfulness and also relinquishes this very practice—this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom?

How is it that they practice the relinquishing of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path, and also relinquish this very practice—this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom?”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, if they conceive of the four foundations of mindfulness as something to be abandoned through this cultivation, they are not cultivating the perfection of wisdom;
if they conceive of the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path as something to be abandoned through this cultivation, they are not cultivating the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
One who possesses conceptualization is not able to cultivate the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the relinquishing of the four foundations of mindfulness and also relinquishes this very practice, that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;
if they practice the relinquishing of the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path and also relinquish this very practice, that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How is it that a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the dispatching of the gate of liberation of emptiness and also dispatches this cultivation itself—that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom?

How is it that they cultivate the dispatching of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness and also dispatch these cultivations themselves—that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom?”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, if they conceive of the liberation door of emptiness as something to be abandoned through cultivation, they are not cultivating the perfection of wisdom;
if they conceive of the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness as things to be abandoned through cultivation, they are not cultivating the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti,
one who possesses conceptualization is not able to cultivate the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the dispatching of the gate of liberation of emptiness and also dispatches that cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;
if they cultivate the dispatching of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness and also dispatch that cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.
“World-Honored One!
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivate the dispatching of the eight liberations and also dispatch this very cultivation—this being the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;

and how does he cultivate the dispatching of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities and also dispatch this very cultivation—this being the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom?”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, if they conceive of the eight liberations as something to be abandoned through this cultivation, they are not cultivating the perfection of wisdom;

if they conceive of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities as something to be abandoned through this cultivation, they are not cultivating the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
One who possesses conceptualization is not able to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.

Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the relinquishing of the eight liberations and also relinquishes that cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;

if they cultivate the relinquishing of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities and also relinquish that cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How is it that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the cultivation of the samādhi with vitarka and vicāra, and yet abandons even this cultivation, they are practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā);

and how is it that when they practice the cultivation of the samādhi without vitarka and with only vicāra, and the samādhi without vitarka and without vicāra, and yet abandon even these cultivations, they are practicing the perfection of wisdom?”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, if they conceive of the samādhi with directed thought and sustained investigation as something to be cultivated through its removal, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom;

if they conceive of the samādhi without directed thought and with only sustained investigation, or the samādhi without directed thought or sustained investigation, as something to be cultivated through their removal, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
One who possesses conceptualization is unable to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.

Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the dispatching of the samādhi with directed thought and sustained evaluation, and also dispatches that cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;

if they cultivate the dispatching of the samādhi without directed thought and with only sustained evaluation, and the samādhi without directed thought and without sustained evaluation, and also dispatch those cultivations themselves, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.
“World-Honored One!
How is it that a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the cultivation of the noble truth of suffering and also abandons this cultivation—that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;
how is it that they practice the cultivation of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path and also abandon this cultivation—that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom?”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, if they conceive of the noble truth of suffering as something to be abandoned through cultivation, they are not cultivating the perfection of wisdom;
if they conceive of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as things to be abandoned through cultivation, they are not cultivating the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
One who possesses conceptualization is not able to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.

Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the relinquishing of the noble truth of suffering and also relinquishes this practice itself, that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;
if they practice the relinquishing of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, and also relinquish this practice itself, that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How is it that a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s cultivation of the dispatching of the knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-jñāna*), and the dispatching of this very cultivation, is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*)?

How is it that the cultivation of the dispatching of the knowledge of origin (*samudaya-jñāna*), the knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-jñāna*), the knowledge of the path (*mārga-jñāna*), the knowledge of exhaustion (*kṣaya-jñāna*), the knowledge of non-arising (*anutpāda-jñāna*), the knowledge of phenomena (*dharma-jñāna*), subsequent knowledge (*anvaya-jñāna*), conventional knowledge (*saṃvṛti-jñāna*), the knowledge of others’ minds (*paracitta-jñāna*), and the knowledge of things as they truly are (*yathābhūta-jñāna*), and the dispatching of this very cultivation, is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom?”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, if they conceive of the knowledge of suffering as something to be abandoned through cultivation, they are not cultivating the perfection of wisdom;

if they conceive of the knowledge of origination, up to the knowledge of things as they truly are, as something to be abandoned through cultivation, they are not cultivating the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
One who possesses conceptualization is not able to cultivate the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the dispatching of the knowledge of suffering and also dispatches that cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;

if they cultivate the dispatching of the knowledge of origination up to the knowledge of things as they truly are and also dispatch that cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How is it that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the cultivation of the perfection of giving and also cultivates the relinquishing of this cultivation, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;

and when they practice the cultivation of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, and also cultivate the relinquishing of these cultivations, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom?”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, if they conceive of the existence of the perfection of giving and practice with a sense of rejection, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom;
if they conceive of the existence of the perfection of ethical discipline up to the perfection of wisdom and practice with a sense of rejection, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
One who possesses conceptualization is not able to cultivate the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the relinquishment of the perfection of generosity and also relinquishes that practice, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;
if they practice the relinquishment of the perfections from ethical discipline up to the perfection of wisdom and also relinquish that practice, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.
“World-Honored One!
How is it that a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the dispatching of internal emptiness and also the dispatching of this cultivation—this being the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;

and how is it that they cultivate the dispatching of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersal emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, emptiness of all dharmas, unapprehendable emptiness, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, and emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, while also dispatching this cultivation—this being the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom?”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, if they conceive of internal emptiness as having a cultivation that involves its rejection, they are not cultivating the perfection of wisdom;

if they conceive of external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, as having a cultivation that involves their rejection, they are not cultivating the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
One who possesses conceptualization is not able to cultivate the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the relinquishment of internal emptiness and also relinquishes that practice itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;

if they practice the relinquishment of external emptiness up to the emptiness of non-existence and intrinsic nature and also relinquish that practice itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How is it that a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the dispatching of the Stage of Extreme Joy (*pramuditā-bhūmi*) and also the dispatching of this very cultivation—that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*)?

How is it that they cultivate the dispatching of the Stage of Purity (*vimalā-bhūmi*), the Stage of Radiance (*prabhākārī-bhūmi*), the Stage of Blazing Wisdom (*arciṣmatī-bhūmi*), the Stage of Utmost Difficulty to Conquer (*sudurjayā-bhūmi*), the Stage of Presence (*abhimukhī-bhūmi*), the Stage of Far-Going (*dūraṅgamā-bhūmi*), the Immovable Stage (*acalā-bhūmi*), the Stage of Excellent Intelligence (*sādhumatī-bhūmi*), and the Stage of the Cloud of Dharma (*dharmameghā-bhūmi*), and also the dispatching of this very cultivation—that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom?”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, if they think that there is the Stage of Extreme Joy (pramuditā-bhūmi) which involves the cultivation of rejection, they are not cultivating the perfection of wisdom;

if they think that there is the Stage of Freedom from Defilement (vimalā-bhūmi) up to the Stage of the Dharma Cloud (dharmameghā-bhūmi) which involves the cultivation of rejection, they are not cultivating the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti,
one who possesses conceptualization is not able to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.
Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the relinquishing of the Stage of Extreme Joy and also relinquishes this very practice, that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;

if they practice the relinquishing of the Stage of Freedom from Defilement up to the Stage of the Dharma Cloud and also relinquish this very practice, that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.
“World-Honored One!
How is it that a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the dispatching of the five eyes and also dispatches this very practice—that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;
how is it that they practice the dispatching of the six supernormal powers and also dispatches this very practice—that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom?”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, if they conceive of the five eyes as having something to be discarded through this cultivation, they are not cultivating the perfection of wisdom;
if they conceive of the six supernormal powers as having something to be discarded through this cultivation, they are not cultivating the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
One who possesses conceptualization cannot cultivate the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the relinquishing of the five eyes and also relinquishes this very practice, that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;
if they practice the relinquishing of the six supernormal powers and also relinquish this very practice, that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.
“World-Honored One!
How is it that a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the dispatching of the Buddha’s ten powers and also dispatches this very practice;

how is it that they practice the dispatching of the four fearlessnesses, the four unhindered understandings, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, and also dispatches this very practice—this being the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom?”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), if they think that the ten powers of a Buddha exist and involve a removal [of conceptualization] in this cultivation, they are not cultivating the perfection of wisdom;

if they think that the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha exist and involve a removal [of conceptualization] in this cultivation, they are not cultivating the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
One who possesses conceptualization is not able to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.

Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the dispatching of the ten powers of a buddha and also dispatches this cultivation itself, that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;

if they cultivate the dispatching of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha and also dispatch this cultivation itself, that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.
“World-Honored One!
How is it that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the dispatching of great loving-kindness and also dispatches this very practice, they are practicing the perfection of wisdom;
and when they practice the dispatching of great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity, and also dispatch these very practices, they are practicing the perfection of wisdom?”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, if they think that there is great loving-kindness and that there is a cultivation involving its rejection, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom;
if they think that there is great compassion, great sympathetic joy, or great equanimity and that there is a cultivation involving their rejection, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
One who possesses conceptualization is not able to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.
Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the dispatching of great loving-kindness and also dispatches that cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;

if they cultivate the dispatching of great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity and also dispatch those cultivations themselves, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How is it that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the dispatching of the quality of non-forgetfulness and also dispatches this cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;
and when they cultivate the dispatching of the nature of constant equanimity and also dispatch this cultivation itself, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom?”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, if they conceive of the ‘dharmas of non-forgetfulness’ as something to be abandoned through this cultivation, they are not cultivating the perfection of wisdom;
if they conceive of the ‘nature of constant equanimity’ as something to be abandoned through this cultivation, they are not cultivating the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
One who possesses conceptualization is unable to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.

Therefore, Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the relinquishment of the quality of non-forgetfulness and also relinquishes this practice itself, that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;
if they practice the relinquishment of the state of constant equanimity and also relinquish this practice itself, that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.
“World-Honored One!
How is it that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the relinquishing of all samādhi-doors and also relinquishes this very practice, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;
and when they practice the relinquishing of all dhāraṇī-doors and also relinquish this very practice, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom?”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, if they conceive of any samādhi door as having this cultivation as something to be discarded, they are not cultivating the perfection of wisdom;
if they conceive of any dhāraṇī door as having this cultivation as something to be discarded, they are not cultivating the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
One who possesses conceptualization is not able to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.
Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the relinquishing of all samādhi doors and also relinquishes this cultivation itself, that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;
if they cultivate the relinquishing of all dhāraṇī doors and also relinquish this cultivation itself, that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivate the dispatching of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) while also dispatching this very cultivation—this being the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*)?

How does he cultivate the dispatching of the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), while also dispatching this very cultivation—this being the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom?”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, if they conceive of all-knowledge as something to be abandoned through this cultivation, they are not cultivating the perfection of wisdom;
if they conceive of the knowledge of the paths or the knowledge of all aspects as something to be abandoned through this cultivation, they are not cultivating the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
One who possesses conceptualization is not able to cultivate the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the relinquishing of all-knowledge and also relinquishes this very practice, that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;
if they practice the relinquishing of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects, and also relinquish this very practice, that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.
“World-Honored One!
How is it that a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the dispatching of the fruit of stream-entry and also the dispatching of this cultivation—that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom?

How is it that they cultivate the dispatching of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship, as well as the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, and also the dispatching of this cultivation—that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom?”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, if they think that there is the fruit of a stream-enterer and that this practice involves its rejection, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom;

if they think that there is the fruit of a once-returner, a non-returner, an arhat, or the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha and that this practice involves their rejection, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
One who possesses conceptualization is unable to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.
Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the dispatching of the fruit of stream-entry and also dispatches this very practice, that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;

if they practice the dispatching of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, arhatship, and pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, and also dispatch this very practice, that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.
“World-Honored One!
How is it that a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the dispatching of all bodhisattva mahāsattva practices and also dispatches this very practice—this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;

how is it that they practice the dispatching of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas and also dispatches this very practice—this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom?”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), if they conceive of there being any bodhisattva mahāsattva practice that involves the rejection of this cultivation, they are not cultivating the perfection of wisdom;

if they conceive of there being any unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas that involves the rejection of this cultivation, they are not cultivating the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
One who possesses conceptualization is not able to cultivate the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

Therefore, Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the relinquishing of all bodhisattva mahāsattva practices and also relinquishes this very practice, that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;
if they practice the relinquishing of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas and also relinquish this very practice, that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How is it that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the dispatching of all-knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) and also dispatches this very practice, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*);

and when they practice the dispatching of the permanent severance of the continuity of all afflictions (*kleśa*) along with their habitual tendencies (*vāsanā*), and also dispatches this very practice, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom?”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, if they conceive of the existence of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), this practice involves a rejection [of true cultivation] and is not the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;

if they conceive of the existence of the continuity of all afflictive habitual tendencies (*vāsanā*), or if they conceive of the permanent severance of the continuity of all afflictive habitual tendencies, this practice involves a rejection [of true cultivation] and is not the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
One who possesses conceptualization is not able to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.

Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the relinquishing of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) while also relinquishing that very cultivation, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*);

if they cultivate the relinquishing of the complete severance of the continuity of the habitual tendencies (*vāsanā*) of all afflictions while also relinquishing that very cultivation, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.
“World-Honored One!

How is it that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the dispatching of the conditioned realm (*saṃskṛtadhātu*) and also dispatches this very practice, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*);
and when they practice the dispatching of the unconditioned realm (*asaṃskṛtadhātu*) and also dispatch this very practice, this is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom?”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, if they conceive of a conditioned realm and practice its rejection, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom;
if they conceive of an unconditioned realm and practice its rejection, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.”
Why is this? Subhūti!
One who possesses conceptualization is not able to cultivate the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
Therefore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the dispatching of the conditioned realm and also dispatches this cultivation itself, that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;
if he cultivates the dispatching of the unconditioned realm and also dispatches this cultivation itself, that is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Those who dwell in the perception of existence are certainly unable to cultivate the perfection of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom."
Why is this? Subhūti!

One who dwells in the perception of existence, if they practice giving up to wisdom, will inevitably grasp at a self and what belongs to a self. Because of this grasping, they become attached to the two extremes; because they are attached to the two extremes, they are not liberated from birth and death, and there is neither the Path nor Nirvāṇa. How, then, could they truly practice the perfection of giving up to the perfection of wisdom?

“Subhūti! One who dwells in the perception of existence is certainly unable to cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path.”
Why is this? Subhūti!

One who dwells in the perception of existence, if they cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path, will necessarily grasp at a self and what belongs to a self. Because of this grasping, they become attached to the two extremes; because they are attached to the two extremes, they are not liberated from birth and death. For them there is no path and no nirvāṇa. How, then, could they truly cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path?

“Subhūti! One who dwells in the perception of existence can certainly not dwell in internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self-characteristic, the emptiness of common characteristic, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.”
Why is this? Subhūti!

One who dwells in the perception of existence, even if they dwell in internal emptiness up to the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature, will inevitably grasp at a self and what belongs to a self. Because of this grasping, they become attached to the two extremes; because of attachment to the two extremes, they are not liberated from birth and death, and for them there is no path and no nirvāṇa. How, then, could such a person truly dwell in internal emptiness up to the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature?

"Subhūti! Those who dwell in the perception of existence can certainly not abide in suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-illusory nature, non-alteration, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, or the inconceivable realm."
Why is this? Subhūti!

One who dwells in conceptualization, even if they dwell in suchness up to the inconceivable realm, will inevitably grasp at a self and what belongs to a self. Because of this grasping, they become attached to the two extremes; because they are attached to the two extremes, they are not liberated from birth and death, and for them there is neither the Path nor Nirvāṇa. How, then, could they truly dwell in suchness up to the inconceivable realm?
"Subhūti! One who dwells in the perception of existence can certainly not dwell in the Noble Truth of Suffering, nor in the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path. Why is this?

"Subhūti! Those who dwell in the perception of existence will inevitably grasp at a self and what belongs to a self. Because of this grasping, they become attached to the two extremes; because they are attached to the two extremes, they are not liberated from birth and death, and for them there is no path and no nirvāṇa. How, then, could they truly abide in the Noble Truth of Suffering, or in the Noble Truths of its Origin, its Cessation, and the Path?"
“Subhūti! Those who dwell in the perception of existence can certainly not cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness, nor the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness. Why is this?

"Subhūti! Those who dwell in the perception of existence will inevitably grasp at a self and what belongs to a self (*ātman* and *ātmīya*). Because of this grasping, they become attached to the two extremes; because they are attached to the two extremes, they are not liberated from birth and death, and for them there is neither the Path nor Nirvāṇa. How, then, could they truly cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness, or the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness?"
"Subhūti! Those who dwell in the perception of existence are certainly unable to cultivate the four sublime dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments. Why is that?

"Subhūti! Those who dwell in the perception of existence will inevitably grasp at a self and what belongs to a self. Because of this grasping, they become attached to the two extremes; because they are attached to the two extremes, they are not liberated from birth and death, and for them there is no path and no nirvāṇa. How, then, could they truly cultivate the four sublime dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments?"

“Subhūti! Those who dwell in the perception of existence can certainly not cultivate the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities. Why is this?

"Subhūti! Those who dwell in the perception of existence will inevitably grasp at a self and what belongs to a self (*ātman* and *ātmīya*). Because of this grasping, they become attached to the two extremes; because they are attached to the two extremes, they are not liberated from birth and death, and for them there is no Path and no Nirvāṇa. How, then, could they truly cultivate the eight liberations (*aṣṭavimokṣa*), the eight bases of mastery (*aṣṭābhibhvāyatana*), the nine successive meditative attainments (*navānupūrvavihārasamāpatti*), and the ten spheres of totality (*daśakṛtsnāyatana*)?"
“Subhūti! Those who dwell in the perception of existence are certainly unable to cultivate all the gateways of samādhi and all the gateways of dhāraṇī. Why is this?

"Subhūti! One who dwells in the perception of existence will inevitably grasp at a self and what belongs to a self (*ātman* and *ātmīya*). Because of this grasping, one becomes attached to the two extremes; because of attachment to the two extremes, one is not liberated from birth and death, and there is neither the Path nor Nirvāṇa. How, then, could such a person truly cultivate all the gateways of samādhi and all the gateways of dhāraṇī?"

“Subhūti! Those who dwell in the perception of existence can certainly not cultivate the Stage of Extreme Joy, the Stage of Purity, the Stage of Radiant Light, the Stage of Blazing Wisdom, the Stage of Utmost Difficulty to Conquer, the Stage of Presence, the Stage of Far-Going, the Immovable Stage, the Stage of Excellent Intelligence, or the Stage of the Dharma Cloud.”
Why is this? Subhūti!

Those who dwell in the perception of existence will inevitably grasp at a self and what belongs to a self (*ātman* and *ātmīya*). Because of this grasping, they become attached to the two extremes; because they are attached to the two extremes, they are not liberated from birth and death, and for them there is neither the Path nor Nirvāṇa. How, then, could they truly cultivate the stages from the Stage of Extreme Joy (*pramuditā-bhūmi*) up to the Cloud of Dharma (*dharmameghā-bhūmi*)?
“Subhūti! Those who dwell in the perception of existence can certainly not cultivate the five eyes or the six supernormal powers. Why is this?

"Subhūti! Those who dwell in the perception of existence will inevitably grasp at a self and what belongs to a self (*ātman* and *ātmīya*). Because of this grasping, they become attached to the two extremes; because they are attached to the two extremes, they are not liberated from birth and death, and for them there is neither the Path nor Nirvāṇa. How, then, could they truly cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers?"

“Subhūti! Those who dwell in the perception of existence can certainly not cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.”
Why is this? Subhūti!

Those who dwell in the perception of existence will inevitably grasp at a self and what belongs to a self (*ātman* and *ātmīya*). Because of this grasping, they become attached to the two extremes; because of attachment to the two extremes, they are not liberated from birth and death, and for them there is neither the Path nor Nirvāṇa. How, then, could they truly cultivate the Buddha’s ten powers, the four fearlessnesses, the four unhindered understandings, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?
"Subhūti! One who dwells in the perception of existence can certainly not cultivate great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, or great equanimity. Why is this?

Subhūti! Those who dwell in the perception of existence will inevitably grasp at a self and what belongs to a self. Because of this grasping, they become attached to the two extremes; because they are attached to the two extremes, they are not liberated from birth and death, and for them there is neither the Path nor Nirvāṇa. How, then, could they truly cultivate great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity?
“Subhūti! Those who dwell in the perception of existence can certainly not cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness or the state of constant equanimity. Why is this?

"Subhūti! Those who dwell in the perception of existence will inevitably grasp at a self and what belongs to a self. Because of this grasping, they become attached to the two extremes; because they are attached to the two extremes, they are not liberated from birth and death, and for them there is no path and no nirvāṇa. How, then, could they truly cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness or the state of constant equanimity?"
“Subhūti! One who dwells in the perception of existence can certainly not cultivate all-knowledge, the knowledge of the aspects of the path, or the knowledge of all aspects. Why is this?

"Subhūti! Those who dwell in the perception of existence will inevitably grasp at a self and what belongs to a self. Because of this grasping, they become attached to the two extremes; because they are attached to the two extremes, they are not liberated from birth and death, and for them there is no path and no nirvāṇa. How, then, could they truly cultivate all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects?"
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
what is existence?”
“What, then, is that which does not exist?
The Buddha said,
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
"Duality is existence; non-duality is non-existence.
"World-Honored One, what constitutes duality?"
"What is non-duality? "Subhūti!
The perception of form is duality; the emptiness of the perception of form is non-duality."
The perception of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness constitutes duality; the emptiness of the perception of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness is non-duality.
"Subhūti! The perception of the eye-base constitutes duality; the emptiness of the perception of the eye-base is non-duality."
To conceive of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind as dual is duality; to conceive of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind as empty is non-duality.
“Subhūti! The perception of the sphere of form is duality; the emptiness of the perception of the sphere of form is non-duality.

The perception of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is duality; the emptiness of the perceptions of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is non-duality.”
“Subhūti! The perception of the eye-element is duality; the emptiness of the perception of the eye-element is non-duality.
The perception of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements is duality; the emptiness of the perception of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements is non-duality.”
“Subhūti! The perception of the realm of form is duality; the emptiness of the perception of the realm of form is non-duality.

The perception of the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is duality; the emptiness of the perceptions of the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena is non-duality.”
“Subhūti! The conceptualization of the eye-consciousness element is duality; the emptiness of the conceptualization of the eye-consciousness element is non-duality.

The conceptualization of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements is duality; the emptiness of the conceptualization of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements is non-duality.”
"Subhūti! The perception of eye-contact is duality; the emptiness of the perception of eye-contact is non-duality.
The perceptions of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact are duality; the emptiness of the perceptions of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact is non-duality."
“Subhūti! The perceptions and feelings arising conditioned by eye-contact are duality; the emptiness of the perceptions and feelings arising conditioned by eye-contact is non-duality.

The perceptions and feelings arising conditioned by ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact are duality; the emptiness of the perceptions and feelings arising conditioned by ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact is non-duality.”
“Subhūti! The perception of the earth element is duality; the emptiness of the perception of the earth element is non-duality.
The perceptions of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are duality; the emptiness of the perceptions of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements is non-duality.”
“Subhūti! The perception of causal conditions is duality; the emptiness of the perception of causal conditions is non-duality.

The perception of the immediately preceding condition, the perceived-object condition, and the dominant condition is duality; the emptiness of the perceptions of the immediately preceding condition, the perceived-object condition, and the dominant condition is non-duality.”
“Subhūti! The perception of ignorance is duality; the emptiness of the perception of ignorance is non-duality.

The perceptions of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are duality; the emptiness of the perceptions of volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair is non-duality.”
“Subhūti! To conceive of the perfection of generosity as dual is one thing; to conceive of the perfection of generosity as empty is non-dual.

To conceive of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom as dual is one thing; to conceive of these perfections, from ethical discipline up to wisdom, as empty is non-dual.”
"Subhūti! To conceive of internal emptiness as dual is one thing; to conceive of internal emptiness as empty is non-dual.

To conceive of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature as dual is one thing; to conceive of these—from external emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature—as empty is non-dual."
“Subhūti! The perception of the four foundations of mindfulness is duality; the emptiness of the perception of the four foundations of mindfulness is non-duality.

The perception of the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path is duality; the emptiness of the perception of the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path is non-duality.”
“Subhūti! The perception of the noble truth of suffering is duality; the emptiness of the perception of the noble truth of suffering is non-duality.
The perception of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path is duality; the emptiness of the perceptions of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path is non-duality.”
“Subhūti! The perception of the four dhyānas is duality; the emptiness of the perception of the four dhyānas is non-duality.
The perception of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is duality; the emptiness of the perception of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments is non-duality.”
"Subhūti! The perception of the eight liberations is duality; the emptiness of the perception of the eight liberations is non-duality.

The perception of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities is duality; the emptiness of the perception of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities is non-duality."
“Subhūti! The conceptualization of all samādhi-gates is duality; the emptiness of the conceptualization of all samādhi-gates is non-duality.
The conceptualization of all dhāraṇī-gates is duality; the emptiness of the conceptualization of all dhāraṇī-gates is non-duality.”
“Subhūti! The perception of the gate of liberation of emptiness is duality; the emptiness of the perception of the gate of liberation of emptiness is non-duality.
The perception of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness is duality; the emptiness of the perceptions of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness is non-duality.”
“Subhūti! The perception of the Stage of Extreme Joy is duality; the emptiness of the perception of the Stage of Extreme Joy is non-duality.

The perceptions of the Stage of Stainless, the Radiant, the Blazing Wisdom, the Difficult to Conquer, the Manifest, the Far-Reaching, the Immovable, the Good Intelligence, and the Cloud of Dharma are duality; the emptiness of the perceptions from the Stage of Stainless up to the Cloud of Dharma is non-duality.”
"Subhūti! The perception of the five eyes is duality; the emptiness of the perception of the five eyes is non-duality.
The perception of the six supernormal powers is duality; the emptiness of the perception of the six supernormal powers is non-duality."
“Subhūti! The conceptualization of the ten powers of a Buddha is duality; the emptiness of the conceptualization of the ten powers of a Buddha is non-duality.

The conceptualization of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is duality; the emptiness of the conceptualization of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is non-duality.”
“Subhūti! The perception of great loving-kindness is duality; the emptiness of the perception of great loving-kindness is non-duality.

The perceptions of great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity are duality; the emptiness of the perceptions of great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity is non-duality.”
“Subhūti! The perception of the quality of non-forgetfulness is duality; the emptiness of the perception of the quality of non-forgetfulness is non-duality.
The perception of the state of constant equanimity is duality; the emptiness of the perception of the state of constant equanimity is non-duality.”
“Subhūti! The conceptualization of ‘all-knowledge’ is duality; the emptiness of the conceptualization of ‘all-knowledge’ is non-duality.

The conceptualization of ‘knowledge of the paths’ and ‘knowledge of all aspects’ is duality; the emptiness of the conceptualization of ‘knowledge of the paths’ and ‘knowledge of all aspects’ is non-duality.”
“Subhūti! The notion of a stream-enterer is duality; the emptiness of the notion of a stream-enterer is non-duality.

The notions of a once-returner, a non-returner, an arhat, and a pratyekabuddha are duality; the emptiness of the notions of a once-returner, a non-returner, an arhat, and a pratyekabuddha is non-duality.”
“Subhūti! The perception of the fruit of stream-entry is duality; the emptiness of the perception of the fruit of stream-entry is non-duality.

The perception of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, arhatship, and pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is duality; the emptiness of the perceptions of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, arhatship, and pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is non-duality.”
“Subhūti! The perception of a bodhisattva mahāsattva is duality; the emptiness of the perception of a bodhisattva mahāsattva is non-duality.
The perception of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha is duality; the emptiness of the perception of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha is non-duality.”
“Subhūti! The conceptualization of a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing is duality; the emptiness of the conceptualization of a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing is non-duality.
The conceptualization of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is duality; the emptiness of the conceptualization of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is non-duality.”
“Subhūti! The perception of the conditioned realm is duality; the emptiness of the perception of the conditioned realm is non-duality.
The perception of the unconditioned realm is duality; the emptiness of the perception of the unconditioned realm is non-duality.”

“Subhūti! All perceptions whatsoever constitute duality; all dualities whatsoever are existence; and all forms of existence involve birth and death. Those who possess birth and death cannot be liberated from birth, old age, sickness, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair.”

"Subhūti! Those for whom all perceptions are empty are non-dual; those who are non-dual are non-existent; those who are non-existent have neither birth nor death; and those who have neither birth nor death are able to be liberated from birth, old age, sickness, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair."

By this causal connection, one should know that for all those who possess the perception of duality, there is certainly no perfection of generosity, nor the perfection of ethical discipline, nor the perfection of patience, nor the perfection of diligence, nor the perfection of meditative concentration, nor the perfection of wisdom; there is no path, no fruit, and no clear realization.
Even for one who has attained the patience of conformity (*anulomikī kṣānti*), such a thing does not exist; how much less could there be full knowledge of form!
How much less could there be full knowledge of feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness!
How much less could there be full knowledge of the sense base of the eye!

Chapter Sixty-Five: The Three Gradual Stages, Part One. At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!..."

For those who dwell in the state of having perceptions, if they lack patient acceptance (*kṣānti*), they will have no path, no fruit, and no clear realization (*abhisamaya*). How could those who dwell in the state of having no perceptions possess patient acceptance?

Whether it be the stage of pure observation (*śuklavidarśanā-bhūmi*), the stage of the spiritual lineage (*gotra-bhūmi*), the eighth stage (*aṣṭamaka-bhūmi*), the stage of seeing (*darśana-bhūmi*), the stage of refinement (*tanu-bhūmi*), the stage of freedom from desire (*vītarāga-bhūmi*), the stage of completion (*kṛtāvī-bhūmi*), the stage of the solitary realizer (*pratyekabuddha-bhūmi*), or the stage of the bodhisattva (*bodhisattva-bhūmi*)—if one cultivates the noble path and, by cultivating the noble path, abandons all afflictions (*kleśa*), whether associated with the śrāvakas or associated with the solitary realizers—then, because they are obscured and obstructed by these very afflictions, how could the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas ever enter the bodhisattva’s state of rightness and departure from birth (*samyaktva-nyāma*)?
If one cannot enter the bodhisattva’s state of correct determination and transcendence, how could one possibly realize the knowledge of all aspects?
If one cannot realize the knowledge of all aspects, how could one possibly forever sever the continuity of all afflictions and their habitual tendencies?
“World-Honored One!

If all dharmas are entirely non-existent, without arising, without ceasing, without defilement, and without purity, then since such dharmas do not arise at all, how could one possibly realize the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna)?”
The Buddha said:
“So it is, Subhūti! It is just so.”

It is so! It is as you have said. For one who dwells in non-conceptualization (*asaṃjñin*), there is no acquiescence (*kṣānti*), no stage of pure observation (*śuklavidarśanā-bhūmi*), no stage of the lineage (*gotra-bhūmi*), no eighth stage (*aṣṭamaka-bhūmi*), no stage of vision (*darśana-bhūmi*), no stage of refinement (*tanu-bhūmi*), no stage of freedom from desire (*vītarāga-bhūmi*), no stage of completion (*kṛtāvi-bhūmi*), no stage of the solitary realizer (*pratyekabuddha-bhūmi*), and no stage of the bodhisattva (*bodhisattva-bhūmi*). Nor is there the stage of the Tathāgata; nor is there the cultivation of the noble path, nor the abandonment of all afflictions through the cultivation of the noble path—whether associated with the śrāvaka or associated with the pratyekabuddha.
Because they are obscured and hindered by these afflictions, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas would be unable to enter the bodhisattva’s state of rightness and departure from birth (*samyaktva-niyāma*).
If they cannot enter the bodhisattva’s state of rightness and departure from birth, they would be unable to realize the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).
If one cannot realize the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), one will be unable to eternally sever the continuity of the habitual tendencies (*vāsanā*) of all afflictions. Subhūti!

If all phenomena are entirely non-existent, without arising, without cessation, without defilement, and without purity, then since such phenomena do not arise at all, how could one possibly realize the knowledge of all-knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*)?
The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, does he have the perception of existence, or does he have the perception of non-existence?”
Is there the perception of form, and the perception of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness?
Is there the perception of the sense base of the eye, and the perceptions of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind?
Do you have the perception of the sphere of visible forms? Do you have the perceptions of the spheres of sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, and mental phenomena?
Do you have the perception of the eye-element? Do you have the perceptions of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements?
Is there the perception of the realm of form? Is there the perception of the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena?
Is there the perception of the realm of eye-consciousness? Is there the perception of the realms of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness?
Is there the perception of eye-contact? Is there the perception of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact?

Is there the various feelings and perceptions produced with eye-contact as condition? Are there the various feelings and perceptions produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions?
Is there the perception of the earth element, and the perceptions of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements?
Is there the perception of causes and conditions, and the perceptions of the immediately preceding condition, the object-condition, and the dominant condition?
Is there the perception of greed? Is there the perception of hatred and delusion?

Is there the perception of ignorance? Is there the perception of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair?
Do you have the notion that there is a perfection of giving, or the notion that there are perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom?

"Do you have the notion of internal emptiness, or the notions of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence?"

Do you have the notion that there are the four foundations of mindfulness, or the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, or the eight branches of the noble path?
Do you have the perception of the noble truth of suffering, and do you have the perceptions of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path?
Do you have the perception of the four dhyānas, and do you have the perceptions of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments?
Do you have the notion of the eight liberations? Do you have the notions of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities?
Do you have the notion of the gateways to meditative concentration, and the notion of the gateways to dhāraṇī?
Do you have the perception of the gate of liberation of emptiness? Do you have the perceptions of the gate of liberation of signlessness and the gate of liberation of wishlessness?

Do you have the perception of the Ground of Great Joy, and the perceptions of the Ground of Purity, the Ground of Radiance, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Difficult to Conquer, the Ground of Presence, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Good Intelligence, and the Ground of the Dharma Cloud?
Do you have the notion of the five eyes? Do you have the notion of the six supernormal powers?
Do you have the notion of the Buddha’s ten powers, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?
Do you have the perception of great loving-kindness, and the perceptions of great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity?
Do you have the perception of the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the perception of the nature of constant abiding in equanimity?
Is there the notion of "all-knowledge," or the notion of "knowledge of the aspects of the path" and "knowledge of all aspects"?
Is there the notion of the fruit of stream-entry, or the notions of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, arhatship, and pratyekabuddha-enlightenment?
Do you have the notion that there is a bodhisattva mahāsattva who practices, or the notion that there is the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas?
Do you have the notion that there is the knowledge of all modes?
"Do you have the notion that there is a permanent severance of the continuity of all afflictions and their habitual tendencies?
Do you have the notion of form, and the notion of the severance of form?
Do you have the notion of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, and the notion of the severance of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness?"
Is there a perception of the eye-base, and is there a perception of the cessation of the eye-base?
Is there a perception of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases, and is there a perception of the cessation of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases?
Is there a perception of the sphere of visible forms, and is there a perception of the cessation of the sphere of visible forms?

Is there a perception of the spheres of sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, and mental phenomena, and is there a perception of the cessation of the spheres of sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, and mental phenomena?
Is there the perception of the eye-element, and is there the perception of the cessation of the eye-element?
Is there the perception of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements, and is there the perception of the cessation of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements?
Is there a perception of the realm of form, and is there a perception of the cessation of the realm of form?
Is there a perception of the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena, and is there a perception of the cessation of the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena?
Is there the notion of the eye-consciousness element, and is there the notion of the cessation of the eye-consciousness element?
Is there the notion of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements, and is there the notion of the cessation of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements?
Is there a perception of eye-contact, and is there a perception of the cessation of eye-contact?
Is there a perception of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact, and is there a perception of the cessation of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact?
Is there a perception of the cessation of those feelings produced with eye-contact as condition?
Is there a perception of the cessation of those feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions?
Is there the perception of the earth element, and is there the perception of the cessation of the earth element?
Is there the perception of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements, and is there the perception of the cessation of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements?
Is there a perception of conditions as having causes, and is there a perception of conditions as being severed from their causes?

Is there a perception of the equal-and-immediate condition, the object-condition, and the predominant condition, and is there a perception of the equal-and-immediate condition, the object-condition, and the predominant condition as being severed?
Is there a perception of greed, and is there a perception of the abandonment of greed?
Is there a perception of hatred and delusion, and is there a perception of the abandonment of hatred and delusion?
Is there a perception of ignorance, and is there a perception of the abandonment of ignorance?

Is there the perception of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair; and is there the perception of the cessation of volitional formations up to the cessation of old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair?
Is there a perception of the perfection of generosity, or a perception of the cessation of the perfection of generosity?

Is there a perception of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, or a perception of the cessation of ethical discipline up to and including the perfection of wisdom?
Is there a perception of internal emptiness? Is there a perception of the abandonment of internal emptiness?

Is there a perception of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence? Is there a perception of the abandonment of external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence?
Is there the perception of the four foundations of mindfulness, and is there the perception of the abandonment of the four foundations of mindfulness?

Is there the perception of the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path, and is there the perception of the abandonment of the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path?
Is there the perception of the noble truth of suffering, and is there the perception of the abandonment of the noble truth of suffering?
Is there the perception of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path, and is there the perception of the abandonment of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path?
Are there perceptions of the four dhyānas, and are there perceptions of the abandonment of the four dhyānas?
Are there perceptions of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, and are there perceptions of the abandonment of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments?
Is there the perception of the eight liberations, and is there the perception of the abandonment of the eight liberations?

Is there the perception of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities, and is there the perception of the abandonment of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities?
Is there a perception of the doors of samādhi, or is there a perception of the cessation of the doors of samādhi?
Is there a perception of the dhāraṇī-doors, or is there a perception of the cessation of the dhāraṇī-doors?
Is there a perception of the emptiness liberation door, and is there a perception of the abandonment of the emptiness liberation door?
Is there a perception of the signlessness and wishlessness liberation doors, and is there a perception of the abandonment of the signlessness and wishlessness liberation doors?
Is there a perception of the Ground of Utmost Joy, and is there a perception of the abandonment of the Ground of Utmost Joy?

Is there a perception of the Ground of Freedom from Defilement, the Ground of Radiance, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Difficult Victory, the Ground of Presence, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, and the Ground of the Dharma-Cloud; and is there a perception of the abandonment of the Ground of Freedom from Defilement, up to and including the Ground of the Dharma-Cloud?
Is there a perception of the five eyes and a perception of the severance of the five eyes?
Is there a perception of the six supernormal powers and a perception of the severance of the six supernormal powers?
Is there a perception of the ten powers of a Buddha and a perception of the severance of the ten powers of a Buddha?

Is there a perception of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha? Is there a perception of the abandonment of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?
Is there a perception of great loving-kindness, and is there a perception of the abandonment of great loving-kindness?
Is there a perception of great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity, and is there a perception of the abandonment of great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity?
Is there a perception of the non-forgetfulness of dharmas, and is there a perception of the abandonment of the non-forgetfulness of dharmas?
Is there a perception of the nature of constant equanimity, and is there a perception of the abandonment of the nature of constant equanimity?
Is there a notion of omniscience, and is there a notion of the abandonment of omniscience?
Is there a notion of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects, and is there a notion of the abandonment of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects?
Is there a perception of the fruit of stream-entry, and is there a perception of the abandonment of the fruit of stream-entry?

Is there a perception of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, and arhatship, as well as the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, and is there a perception of the abandonment of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, arhatship, and the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha?
Is there for a bodhisattva mahāsattva the notion of practicing the bodhisattva path, or the notion of abandoning the bodhisattva path?
Is there the notion of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas, or the notion of abandoning the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas?
Is there the notion that there is the wisdom of all-knowledge, or the notion that there is the abandonment of the wisdom of all-knowledge?

Is there the notion that there are the habitual tendencies and continuities of all afflictions to be abandoned, or the notion that there is the abandonment of the habitual tendencies and continuities of all afflictions?
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they have neither any perception nor any non-perception regarding all phenomena.”
"Subhūti! If there is neither perception nor non-perception, you should know that this is the bodhisattva’s compliance with patience (anulomikī kṣānti);
if there is neither perception nor non-perception, this is the cultivation of the path."
If there is neither perception nor non-perception, that is the attainment of the fruit.
Subhūti, you should know this:
the absence of intrinsic nature (*niḥsvabhāva*) is the path of the bodhisattva mahāsattva; the absence of intrinsic nature is the clear realization (*abhisamaya*) of the bodhisattva mahāsattva.
"Subhūti! By this causal condition, you should know that all phenomena have non-existence as their intrinsic nature.
The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

If all dharmas have non-existence as their intrinsic nature, how is it that the Tathāgata has attained manifest, perfect enlightenment regarding the fact that all dharmas have non-existence as their nature? Having attained manifest, perfect enlightenment, how does he attain mastery over all dharmas and all objective spheres?”
The Buddha said,
"So it is, Subhūti! It is just so."

It is so! All phenomena have the absence of intrinsic nature as their very nature. When I was originally practicing the bodhisattva path, I practiced the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom without error; I dwelt having fully entered the first dhyāna, which is accompanied by applied and sustained thought, born of seclusion, and characterized by joy and bliss, being free from sensual desires and unwholesome states;

and I dwelt having fully entered the second dhyāna, which is free from applied and sustained thought, characterized by internal serenity and mental unification, born of concentration, and characterized by joy and bliss.

Detached from joy, he dwells in equanimity, mindful and clearly aware; experiencing happiness with the body, of which the Noble Ones say, "One who dwells in equanimity is mindful," he enters and abides in the third dhyāna.

With the abandoning of pleasure and pain, and with the prior disappearance of joy and grief, he enters and abides in the fourth dhyāna, which is neither painful nor pleasant and possesses purity of mindfulness through equanimity.

At that time, although I skillfully grasped the signs of the various meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*) and their constituent factors (*dhyānāṅga*), I harbored no attachment to them; I felt no relish for the various meditative concentrations and their constituent factors, nor did I perceive any objective reality in them at all.
At that time, I dwelt fully established in the various meditative absorptions (dhyāna), endowed with pure modes of practice and free from conceptual discrimination.

At that time, having become thoroughly matured in those meditative absorptions and their constituent factors (dhyānāṅga), I caused the mind to give rise to the supernormal power of the realization of the knowledge of psychic travel (ṛddhividhi-jñānasākṣātkriyābhijñā); I also caused the mind to give rise to the supernormal power of the realization of the knowledge of the divine ear (divyaśrotra-jñānasākṣātkriyābhijñā); I also caused the mind to give rise to the supernormal power of the realization of the knowledge of others' minds (paracitta-jñānasākṣātkriyābhijñā); I also caused the mind to give rise to the supernormal power of the realization of the knowledge of recollecting past lives (pūrvanivāsānusmṛti-jñānasākṣātkriyābhijñā); and I also caused the mind to give rise to the supernormal power of the realization of the knowledge of the divine eye (divyacakṣus-jñānasākṣātkriyābhijñā).

At that time, although I skillfully grasped the characteristics of the various knowledges and supernormal powers I had aroused, I harbored no attachment to them; I felt no relish for the various knowledges and supernormal powers I had aroused, and I apprehended nothing at all within those various knowledges and supernormal powers I had aroused.
"At that time, regarding all the wisdoms and supernormal knowledges I had aroused, I dwelt fully established in the vision of them as being non-conceptual, like space. Subhūti!..."

At that time, through a single moment of corresponding sublime wisdom, I realized unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment—namely, the full awakening that this is the Noble Truth of Suffering, this is the Noble Truth of the Origin, this is the Noble Truth of Cessation, and this is the Noble Truth of the Path—and that none of these possess any inherent existence whatsoever. I accomplished the ten powers, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and other boundless merits; I established the distinctions among sentient beings according to the three categories, and through appropriate skillful means, I instructed them, enabling them to attain supreme benefit and peace.
The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying: “World-Honored One, how is it that the Tathāgata, Arhat,

Samyaksaṃbuddha can give rise to the four dhyānas which have non-existence as their intrinsic nature, can manifest the five supernormal powers which have non-existence as their intrinsic nature, can realize unsurpassed perfect enlightenment which has non-existence as its intrinsic nature, and can establish non-existence as the intrinsic nature [of all things], so that after sentient beings have been categorized into the three groups, he may teach and guide them through appropriate skillful means, causing them to obtain supreme benefit and peace?”
The Buddha said: “Subhūti!

If all those desires, unwholesome states, and unvirtuous dharmas possessed even the slightest intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*) or a nature consisting of something other (*parabhāva*), then when I was formerly practicing the bodhisattva path, I would not have been able to penetrate the fact that all desires, unwholesome states, and unvirtuous dharmas have non-existence as their intrinsic nature, and thereby enter and dwell fully in the first dhyāna, and enter and dwell fully in the second, third, and fourth dhyānas. This is because all desires, unwholesome states, and unvirtuous dharmas lack both an intrinsic and an extrinsic nature, having only non-existence as their intrinsic nature.”

When I was originally practicing the bodhisattva path, having realized that desire, unwholesome states, and other such factors all have non-existence as their intrinsic nature, I was able to leave behind desire, unwholesome states, and evil qualities; with directed thought and sustained thought, born of seclusion, joyful and blissful, I entered and dwelt in the first dhyāna in its full perfection.

With the subsiding of directed thought and sustained thought, through internal serenity and the unification of the mind, free from directed thought and sustained thought, born of concentration, joyful and blissful, I entered and dwelt in the second dhyāna in its full perfection.

Free from joy, dwelling in equanimity, mindful and clearly aware, experiencing with the body that bliss of which the Noble Ones say, "One who is equanimous and mindful dwells in bliss," I entered and dwelt in the third dhyāna in its full perfection.

"With the abandoning of pleasure and the abandoning of pain, and with the prior disappearance of joy and sorrow, one enters and dwells in the fourth dhyāna, which is neither painful nor pleasant and is purified by equanimity and mindfulness. Subhūti!"

If the various supernormal powers possessed even the slightest intrinsic nature, or if another nature were their intrinsic nature, then when I was originally practicing the bodhisattva path, I should not have attained mastery over all supernormal powers. It is because they all take the absence of nature as their intrinsic nature that I have manifested these various sovereign supernormal powers; for since these supernormal powers possess neither an intrinsic nature nor a nature of another, they take only the absence of nature as their intrinsic nature.
