How can it be that a bodhisattva mahāsattva, dwelling in such dharmas born of maturation (*vipākaja*), matures sentient beings and purifies buddha-fields; and how is it that the roots of goodness obtained from reverently making offerings to the Buddhas—exquisite food and drink, clothing, flower garlands, powdered and incense perfumes, vehicles, necklaces, jeweled banners, flags and canopies, dwellings, bedding, music, lamps, and various other requisites for humans and devas—remain inexhaustible until the fruit of unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment is attained? Furthermore, how is it that even after their final *parinirvāṇa*, their own *śarīra* relics and their disciples continue to receive various offerings and reverence, the power of those roots of goodness still not having perished?
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

Because all dharmas are unattainable, there exists for the bodhisattva mahāsattva the Stage of Extreme Joy, the Stage of Freedom from Defilement, the Radiant Stage, the Stage of Blazing Wisdom, the Stage Difficult to Conquer, the Manifest Stage, the Far-Reaching Stage, the Immovable Stage, the Stage of Excellent Intelligence, and the Stage of the Dharma Cloud. It is precisely because of this that there exists for the bodhisattva mahāsattva the patient acceptance of the non-arising of dharmas; it is precisely because of this that there exist the supernormal powers born of karmic maturation; and it is precisely because of this that there exist the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom born of karmic maturation.”

It is precisely because of this that a bodhisattva mahāsattva can abide in such dharmas born of maturation (*vipākaja*), bringing sentient beings to maturity and purifying buddha-fields. At the abodes of all Buddhas, they reverently make offerings of exquisite food and drink, clothing, flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, vehicles, necklaces, precious banners, pennants and canopies, dwellings, bedding, music, lamps, and various other requisites for humans and devas; even until their unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment, the roots of goodness they have acquired and their fruits remain inexhaustible. This continues through successive stages until after their parinirvāṇa, when their own *śarīra* relics and their disciples still receive various forms of offering and reverence, the power of those roots of goodness not yet having been extinguished.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

If all dharmas are entirely unapprehendable, what difference is there between the perfections of giving, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, as well as the various supernormal powers?”
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

For one who has nothing to apprehend, there is no distinction between the perfection of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, nor among the various supernormal powers.”

In order to cause those who grasp at attainments to become free from defiled attachment, he skillfully teaches the distinct characteristics of the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, as well as the various supernormal powers.
The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One,

for what reason is there no distinction between the non-apprehension [of phenomena] and the perfection of giving, the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of patience, the perfection of diligence, the perfection of meditative concentration, the perfection of wisdom, and the various supernormal powers?"
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they do not apprehend giving, they do not apprehend the giver, they do not apprehend the recipient, and they do not apprehend that which is given while practicing giving; they do not apprehend pure ethical discipline while guarding pure ethical discipline; they do not apprehend patience while cultivating patience; they do not apprehend diligence while cultivating diligence; they do not apprehend meditative concentration while cultivating meditative concentration; they do not apprehend wisdom while cultivating wisdom; and they do not apprehend the supernormal powers while cultivating the supernormal powers.”

Without apprehending the four foundations of mindfulness, one cultivates the four foundations of mindfulness; without apprehending the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path, one cultivates the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path;

without apprehending the gate of liberation of emptiness, one cultivates the gate of liberation of emptiness; without apprehending the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, one cultivates the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness;

without apprehending the four dhyānas, one cultivates the four dhyānas; without apprehending the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments, one cultivates the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments.

Without attaining the eight liberations, one cultivates the eight liberations; without attaining the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive absorptions, or the ten totalities, one cultivates the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive absorptions, or the ten totalities;
without attaining any of the gateways of samādhi, one cultivates all the gateways of samādhi; without attaining any of the gateways of dhāraṇī, one cultivates all the gateways of dhāraṇī;
and without attaining the ten stages of a bodhisattva, one cultivates the ten stages of a bodhisattva.
Without attaining the five eyes, one cultivates the five eyes;

without attaining the ten powers of a Buddha, one cultivates the ten powers of a Buddha; without attaining the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, one cultivates the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;

without attaining great loving-kindness, one cultivates great loving-kindness; and without attaining great compassion, great joy, and great equanimity, one cultivates great compassion, great joy, and great equanimity.

One cannot attain the quality of non-forgetfulness while cultivating the quality of non-forgetfulness; one cannot attain the state of constant equanimity while cultivating the state of constant equanimity.

One cannot attain all-knowledge while cultivating all-knowledge; one cannot attain the knowledge of the aspects of the path or the knowledge of all aspects while cultivating the knowledge of the aspects of the path or the knowledge of all aspects.
One cannot attain sentient beings while maturing sentient beings; one cannot attain buddha-fields while purifying buddha-fields.
Without attaining any of the Buddha-dharmas, one realizes unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. "Subhūti!
A bodhisattva mahāsattva should practice this *prajñāpāramitā* of non-apprehension."
Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can practice such prajñāpāramitā of non-apprehension, no evil Māras or their retinues will be able to destroy them.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha,
saying: “World-Honored One,
how does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the perfection of wisdom, single-mindedly possess...”
It encompasses the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom;
it also fully encompasses the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments,
as well as the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, and the five faculties.
It also fully encompasses the powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eight branches of the noble path;
it also fully encompasses the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; it also fully encompasses the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path;
and it also fully encompasses the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities.
Furthermore, it can fully encompass all gateways of samādhi and all gateways of dhāraṇī;
it can also fully encompass internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness,
great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, and boundless emptiness.
The emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self-characteristics,
the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature,
and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence; these also fully encompass suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, and non-erroneousness.
It also fully encompasses intrinsic nature, immutability, equanimity, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena,
the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm; it also fully encompasses the five eyes, the six supernormal powers,
the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, and the four analytical knowledges.
It understands the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and is likewise able to fully encompass great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity;
it is likewise able to fully encompass the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant abiding in equanimity;
it is likewise able to fully encompass all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects; and it is likewise able to fully encompass...
“The thirty-two marks of a great man and the eighty secondary signs?
The Buddha told Subhūti:

“When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, the practice of the perfection of giving is not separate from the perfection of wisdom; it is entirely embraced by the perfection of wisdom.”

The practices of the perfection of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are not separate from the perfection of wisdom; they are all embraced by the perfection of wisdom.
The four dhyānas that are practiced, not being apart from the perfection of wisdom, are all embraced by the perfection of wisdom;
the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions that are practiced, not being apart from the perfection of wisdom, are all embraced by the perfection of wisdom.
The four foundations of mindfulness that one cultivates do not depart from the perfection of wisdom; they are all embraced by the perfection of wisdom.

The four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path that one cultivates do not depart from the perfection of wisdom; they are all embraced by the perfection of wisdom.
The gate of liberation of emptiness that is practiced does not depart from the perfection of wisdom; it is entirely embraced by the perfection of wisdom.
The gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness that are practiced do not depart from the perfection of wisdom; they are all embraced by the perfection of wisdom.
Whatever dwells in the Noble Truth of Suffering does not depart from the Perfection of Wisdom and is entirely embraced by the Perfection of Wisdom;
whatever dwells in the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path does not depart from the Perfection of Wisdom and is entirely embraced by the Perfection of Wisdom.
The eight liberations that are cultivated do not depart from the perfection of wisdom; they are all embraced by the perfection of wisdom.

The eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities that are cultivated do not depart from the perfection of wisdom; they are all embraced by the perfection of wisdom.
All samādhi-gates that are cultivated do not depart from the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), for they are all embraced by the perfection of wisdom;
all dhāraṇī-gates that are cultivated do not depart from the perfection of wisdom, for they are all embraced by the perfection of wisdom.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 373. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter Sixty-six, Part Two, "The Signless and the Non-attainment. "The inner emptiness in which they abide is not separate from the Prajñāpāramitā; all are embraced by the Prajñāpāramitā."

The emptiness of the external, the emptiness of the internal and external, the emptiness of emptiness, the great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, the absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—none of these depart from the *prajñāpāramitā*; they are all encompassed within the *prajñāpāramitā*.
The suchness in which they abide does not depart from the perfection of wisdom and is entirely embraced by the perfection of wisdom;

likewise, the dharmadhātu, the dharma-nature, the non-falsity, the unchanging nature, the equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the reality-limit, the realm of empty space, and the inconceivable realm—in which they abide—do not depart from the perfection of wisdom and are all embraced by the perfection of wisdom.
The five eyes that are cultivated do not depart from the perfection of wisdom; they are all embraced by the perfection of wisdom.
The six supernormal powers that are cultivated do not depart from the perfection of wisdom; they are all embraced by the perfection of wisdom.
The ten powers of a Buddha that are cultivated do not depart from the perfection of wisdom; they are all embraced by the perfection of wisdom.

The four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha that are cultivated do not depart from the perfection of wisdom; they are all embraced by the perfection of wisdom.
The great loving-kindness they cultivate does not depart from the perfection of wisdom and is entirely embraced by the perfection of wisdom;
the great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity they cultivate do not depart from the perfection of wisdom and are entirely embraced by the perfection of wisdom.
The cultivation of the quality of non-forgetfulness does not depart from the perfection of wisdom; it is entirely embraced by the perfection of wisdom.
The cultivation of the constant abiding in equanimity does not depart from the perfection of wisdom; it is entirely embraced by the perfection of wisdom.
All the omniscience that is cultivated does not depart from the perfection of wisdom and is entirely embraced by the perfection of wisdom;
all the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects that are cultivated do not depart from the perfection of wisdom and are entirely embraced by the perfection of wisdom.
The thirty-two marks of a great man that are brought forth do not depart from the perfection of wisdom; they are all embraced by the perfection of wisdom.
The eighty secondary signs that are brought forth do not depart from the perfection of wisdom; they are all embraced by the perfection of wisdom.
“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom in this way, in a single moment of mind,
they are able to fully encompass generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and— ”
The perfection of wisdom is also able to fully encompass the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments;

it is also able to fully encompass the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path; it is also able to fully encompass—
The gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—likewise fully encompass the Noble Truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path;
they likewise fully encompass the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities;
and they likewise fully encompass all gateways of samādhi and all dhāraṇīs.
The *dhāraṇī* gateways can also fully encompass internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness,
the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness,
absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersal emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, and self-characteristic emptiness.
The emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable,
the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence;
these also fully encompass suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-falsity, the non-alteration, equality, the state beyond birth, and the dharma.
It also fully encompasses meditative concentration, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm;

it also fully encompasses the five eyes and the six supernormal powers; it also fully encompasses the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; and it also fully encompasses great compassion.
Great compassion, great joy, and great equanimity can also fully encompass the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant abiding in equanimity;
they can also fully encompass all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects;
and they can also fully encompass the thirty-two marks of a great man and the eighty secondary signs.
The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
how does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the perfection of wisdom, [regard] all that exists?”
Because they act without departing from the *prajñāpāramitā* and are constantly sustained by the *prajñāpāramitā*,
a single moment of mind is able to fully encompass the *pāramitās* of generosity, ethical discipline,
patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, and is likewise able to fully encompass the four dhyānas.

...the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions; it can also fully encompass the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path;
it can also fully encompass the gateways to liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; it can also fully [encompass...]
It encompasses the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path;
it also fully encompasses the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases;
it further fully encompasses all doors of samādhi and all doors of dhāraṇī, as well as internal emptiness and external emptiness.
Internal and external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena,
the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration,
the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self-characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, and the emptiness of the unapprehendable.
The emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence also fully encompass suchness,
the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-illusory nature, unchanging nature, equality,
the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable.
The sphere of deliberation can also fully encompass the five eyes and the six supernormal powers;
it can also fully encompass the Buddha’s ten powers, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
it can also fully encompass great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity; it can also fully encompass the absence of...
Do the dharmas of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity also fully encompass all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*),

and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), as well as fully encompass the thirty-two marks of a great man (*dvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa*) and the eighty secondary signs (*aśītyanuvyañjana*)?
The Buddha told Subhūti:

"When bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, the perfection of giving they practice is all embraced by the perfection of wisdom, and thus they remain free from dualistic conceptions;

the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom that they practice are all embraced by the perfection of wisdom, and thus they remain free from dualistic conceptions."
Because the four dhyānas they cultivate are all embraced by the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they are free from dualistic conceptions;
because the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions they cultivate are all embraced by the perfection of wisdom, they are free from dualistic conceptions.
Because the four applications of mindfulness that are practiced are all embraced by the perfection of wisdom, they are free from dualistic conceptions;

because the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path that are practiced are all embraced by the perfection of wisdom, they are free from dualistic conceptions.
Because all cultivated gateways to liberation through emptiness are embraced by the perfection of wisdom, they are free from dualistic conceptions;
because all cultivated gateways to liberation through signlessness and wishlessness are embraced by the perfection of wisdom, they are free from dualistic conceptions.
Because all that they abide in—the Noble Truth of Suffering—is embraced by the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they remain free from dualistic conceptions;
because all that they abide in—the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path—are embraced by the perfection of wisdom, they remain free from dualistic conceptions.
Because the eight liberations they cultivate are all embraced by the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), they are free from dualistic conceptions;

because the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities they cultivate are all embraced by the perfection of wisdom, they are free from dualistic conceptions.
Because all the gateways of samādhi that are cultivated are embraced by the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they are free from dualistic conceptions;
because all the gateways of dhāraṇī that are cultivated are embraced by the perfection of wisdom, they are free from dualistic conceptions.
Because that which abides in internal emptiness is embraced by the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), one is far removed from dualistic conceptions;

because that which abides in external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is embraced by the perfection of wisdom, one is far removed from dualistic conceptions.
Because the suchness in which they abide is embraced by the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), they are free from dualistic conceptions;

because the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), the dharma-nature (*dharmatā*), the non-falsity, the unchanging nature, the equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of dharma, the stability of dharma, the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm are all embraced by the perfection of wisdom, they are free from dualistic conceptions.
Because the five eyes they cultivate are all embraced by the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they remain free from dualistic conceptions;
because the six supernormal powers (ṣaḍabhijñā) they cultivate are all embraced by the perfection of wisdom, they remain free from dualistic conceptions.
Because all the ten powers of a Buddha that are cultivated are embraced by the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), one remains far removed from dualistic conceptions;

because all the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha that are cultivated are embraced by the perfection of wisdom, one remains far removed from dualistic conceptions.
The great loving-kindness they cultivate is entirely embraced by the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), and thus they remain free from dualistic conceptions;
the great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity they cultivate are all embraced by the perfection of wisdom, and thus they remain free from dualistic conceptions.
Because all the qualities of non-forgetfulness that they cultivate are embraced by the perfection of wisdom, they remain free from dualistic conceptions;
because all the qualities of the constant abiding in equanimity that they cultivate are embraced by the perfection of wisdom, they remain free from dualistic conceptions.
Because all the omniscience that is cultivated is embraced by the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), one remains free from dualistic conceptions;
because the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are both embraced by the perfection of wisdom, one remains free from dualistic conceptions.
The thirty-two marks of a great man that are brought forth are all embraced by the perfection of wisdom, and thus they are free from dualistic conceptions;
the eighty minor marks that are brought forth are all embraced by the perfection of wisdom, and thus they are free from dualistic conceptions.
The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying: “World-Honored One,

how is it that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they practice the perfection of generosity without dualistic thought, and likewise practice the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom without dualistic thought?”

Although they cultivate the four dhyānas, they are without the notion of duality; although they cultivate the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, they are without the notion of duality?

Although they cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, they are without the notion of duality; although they cultivate the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path, they are without the notion of duality?

Although they cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness, they have no dualistic conception; although they cultivate the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, they have no dualistic conception?
Although they abide in the noble truth of suffering, they have no dualistic conception; although they abide in the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, they have no dualistic conception?

Although they cultivate the eight liberations, they have no notion of duality; although they cultivate the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative concentrations, and the ten universal bases, they have no notion of duality?
Although they cultivate all doors of samādhi, they have no notion of duality; although they cultivate all doors of dhāraṇī, they have no notion of duality?

While dwelling in internal emptiness, one has no notion of duality; while dwelling in external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, one likewise has no notion of duality.

Although they abide in suchness, they have no notion of duality; although they abide in the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (dharmatā-sthiti), the stability of phenomena (dharma-vyavasthāna), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of empty space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm, they have no notion of duality?
Although they cultivate the five eyes, they have no notion of duality; although they cultivate the six supernormal powers, they have no notion of duality?

Although they cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha, they have no notion of duality; although they cultivate the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, they have no notion of duality?
Although they cultivate great loving-kindness, they are free from dualistic thought; although they cultivate great compassion, great joy, and great equanimity, they are free from dualistic thought?

Although they cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness, they are free from dualistic thought; although they cultivate the nature of constant abiding in equanimity, they are free from dualistic thought?

Although they cultivate all-knowledge, they have no notion of duality; although they cultivate the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, they have no notion of duality?
Although they manifest the thirty-two marks of a great man, they have no notion of duality; although they manifest the eighty secondary signs, they have no notion of duality?
The Buddha told Subhūti:
“When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom,
for the sake of fulfilling the perfection of generosity, they embrace it within that very perfection of generosity.”
They practice giving by means of all the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom;
they practice giving while embracing all four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments;
and they embrace all four foundations of mindfulness and the four right efforts.
...practicing generosity while embracing the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path;
practicing generosity while embracing all the gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness;
and practicing generosity while embracing all the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path.
They practice giving while embracing all eight liberations, eight bases of mastery, nine successive meditative attainments, and ten totalities;
they practice giving while embracing all gateways of samādhi and gateways of dhāraṇī;
they practice giving while embracing internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, and emptiness...
Emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness,
emptiness of dispersion, emptiness of non-alteration, emptiness of intrinsic nature, emptiness of self-characteristics,
emptiness of common characteristics, emptiness of all phenomena, emptiness of non-apprehensibility, emptiness of non-existence, and emptiness of self-...
They practice giving while abiding in the emptiness of intrinsic nature and the emptiness of the self-nature of non-existence;
they embrace all suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth,
the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable.
They practice giving while encompassing all five eyes and six supernormal powers;
they practice giving while encompassing all the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
they practice giving while encompassing all great loving-kindness and great compassion.
They practice giving with great joy and great equanimity; they practice giving while embracing all dharmas of non-forgetfulness and the constant abiding in equanimity;
they practice giving while embracing all-knowledge (*sarvajñā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñā*);
and they practice giving while embracing all thirty-two marks of a Great Being.
He practices giving with the eighty minor marks; by reason of this, he is free from dualistic thought. "Subhūti!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, it is because he wishes to fulfill purity..."
By means of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration,
and wisdom, one embraces all the perfections from generosity up to wisdom within those very perfections of ethical discipline up to wisdom, and thus practices ethical discipline up to wisdom.
Embracing all four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments,
they practice the perfection of ethical discipline up to the perfection of wisdom; embracing all four foundations of mindfulness,
the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
They practice the perfection of ethical discipline up to the perfection of wisdom;
they embrace all the doors of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—and practice the perfection of ethical discipline up to the perfection of wisdom;
they embrace all the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path, and practice the perfection of ethical discipline up to the perfection of wisdom.
If, through the perfection of wisdom, one practices the perfection of ethical discipline up to the perfection of wisdom while embracing all eight liberations,
eight bases of mastery, nine successive meditative attainments, and ten totalities; and if, through the perfection of wisdom,
one practices the perfection of ethical discipline up to the perfection of wisdom while embracing all doors of samādhi and all doors of dhāraṇī.
The *pāramitās* encompass all forms of emptiness: internal emptiness, external emptiness,
internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness,
absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, and the emptiness of self-characteristics.

...practicing the perfection of ethical discipline up to the perfection of wisdom through the emptiness of mutual [dependence], the emptiness of all phenomena (*sarvadharma-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of the unapprehendable (*anupalambha-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of non-existence (*abhāva-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of intrinsic nature (*svabhāva-śūnyatā*), and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence (*abhāvasvabhāva-śūnyatā*),
thereby embracing all suchness (*tathatā*), the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), non-falsity (*avitathatā*), and non-alteration (*ananyathā*)...
They practice the perfection of ethical discipline up to the perfection of wisdom by way of mutability, sameness, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*),
the stability of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*);
they practice the perfection of ethical discipline up to the perfection of wisdom while embracing all five eyes and six supernormal powers.
The *pāramitās*, by encompassing all the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges,
and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, practice the precepts up to the *prajñāpāramitā*;
and by encompassing all great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity, they practice the precepts.

From the perfection of ethical discipline up to the perfection of wisdom, they practice the perfection of ethical discipline up to the perfection of wisdom while embracing all the qualities of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity;

they practice the perfection of ethical discipline up to the perfection of wisdom while embracing all-encompassing knowledge, the knowledge of the aspects of the path, and the knowledge of all aspects.
The *pāramitās* embrace all thirty-two marks of a great man and eighty secondary signs; thus,
one practices from the perfection of ethical discipline up to the perfection of wisdom, and by virtue of these causes and conditions, there is no dualistic conception.
“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, for the sake of fulfilling the four dhyānas,
they embrace all generosity and pure ethical discipline within those very four dhyānas.”
...practices the four dhyānas through the perfections of patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom;
practices the four dhyānas while embracing all four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments;
and practices the four dhyānas while embracing all four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, and the four bases of power.
They cultivate the four dhyānas by means of the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path;
they cultivate the four dhyānas while embracing all the gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness;
they cultivate the four dhyānas while embracing all the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path.
They cultivate the four dhyānas while embracing all eight liberations, eight bases of mastery, nine successive attainments, and ten totalities;
they cultivate the four dhyānas while embracing all doors of samādhi and all doors of dhāraṇī;
they [cultivate the four dhyānas] while embracing all internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, and emptiness...
Emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness,
emptiness of dispersion, emptiness of non-alteration, emptiness of intrinsic nature, emptiness of specific characteristics,
emptiness of common characteristics, emptiness of all phenomena, emptiness of non-apprehensibility, emptiness of non-existence, and self-...
They practice the four dhyānas through the emptiness of nature and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-nature,
thereby embracing all suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth,
the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable.
They cultivate the four dhyānas while discerning the realms; they cultivate the four dhyānas while embracing all five eyes and six supernormal powers;

they cultivate the four dhyānas while embracing all the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; and they cultivate the four dhyānas while embracing great loving-kindness.
...practicing the four dhyānas while embracing great compassion, great joy, and great equanimity;
practicing the four dhyānas while embracing all the qualities of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant abiding in equanimity;
practicing the four dhyānas while embracing all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*); embracing all...
While cultivating the thirty-two marks of a great man and the eighty minor signs through the four dhyānas, one does not,
by reason of these causes and conditions, give rise to dualistic conceptions. "Subhūti!..."
When a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, for the sake of fulfilling the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions,
they embrace all generosity, pure ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and [wisdom] within those very four immeasurables and four formless absorptions.
While practicing the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions through the perfection of wisdom,
one embraces all four dhyānas, four immeasurables, and four formless absorptions while practicing the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions;
one embraces all four foundations of mindfulness, four right efforts, and four bases of psychic power.
They cultivate the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions by means of the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path;
they cultivate the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions while embracing all the gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness;
they [cultivate them] while embracing all suffering, its origin, and its cessation.
Practicing the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions by means of the Noble Truth of the Path;

embracing all eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities while practicing the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions; and embracing all doors of samādhi and dhāraṇī...
They cultivate the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, and they embrace all forms of emptiness: internal emptiness, external emptiness,
internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness,
absolute emptiness, limitless emptiness, emptiness of dispersion, unchanging emptiness, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature.

They cultivate the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions through the emptiness of space, the emptiness of self-characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature,
and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, thereby embracing all suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, and non-falsity.
By means of nature, immutability, equality, the state of being free from birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the stability of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*),

the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*), one cultivates the four immeasurables (*apramāṇa*) and the four formless attainments (*ārūpyasamāpatti*);
and by encompassing all five eyes (*pañcacakṣus*) and six supernormal powers (*ṣaḍabhijñā*), one cultivates the four immeasurables and the four...
In the formless absorptions, they embrace all the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges,
and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha while practicing the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions;
they embrace all great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity while practicing the four immeasurables.
They cultivate the four formless absorptions while embracing all the qualities of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity;
they cultivate the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions while embracing all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects; they embrace everything.
While cultivating the thirty-two marks of a great man and the eighty minor marks, as well as the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions,
one does not, by reason of these causes and conditions, give rise to dualistic conceptions.
“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, for the sake of fulfilling the four foundations of mindfulness,
they embrace all generosity and pure ethical discipline within those very four foundations of mindfulness.”
...cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness through the perfections of patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom;
cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness while encompassing all four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments;
and encompass all four foundations of mindfulness, the four right endeavors, and the four bases of psychic power...
One cultivates the four foundations of mindfulness by means of the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path;
one cultivates the four foundations of mindfulness while embracing all the doors of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness;
and one cultivates the four foundations of mindfulness while embracing all the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path.
One cultivates the four foundations of mindfulness while embracing all eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities;
one cultivates the four foundations of mindfulness while embracing all doors of samādhi and all doors of dhāraṇī;
one [cultivates the four foundations of mindfulness] while embracing all internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, and emptiness...
Emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness,
emptiness of dispersion, emptiness of non-alteration, emptiness of intrinsic nature, emptiness of specific characteristics,
emptiness of common characteristics, emptiness of all phenomena, emptiness of non-apprehensibility, emptiness of non-existence, and self-...
They cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness through the emptiness of intrinsic nature and the emptiness of the self-nature of non-existence,
thereby embracing all suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth,
the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable.
One cultivates the four foundations of mindfulness by deliberating upon the realms; one cultivates the four foundations of mindfulness while embracing all five eyes and six supernormal powers;

one cultivates the four foundations of mindfulness while embracing all the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; and one embraces all great loving-kindness while cultivating the four foundations of mindfulness.
...practicing the four foundations of mindfulness by embracing great compassion, great joy, and great equanimity;
practicing the four foundations of mindfulness by embracing all qualities of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant abiding in equanimity;
practicing the four foundations of mindfulness by embracing all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*); and embracing all...
While cultivating the thirty-two marks of a great man and the eighty minor marks, one dwells in the four foundations of mindfulness;
by reason of this, there is no dualistic perception. "Subhūti!..."
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, desiring to fulfill the four right efforts,
the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path,
they embrace one [of these] within the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path.
Having practiced all the perfections of giving, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom,
they cultivate the four right endeavors up to the eight branches of the noble path; having embraced all the four dhyānas,
the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments, they cultivate the four right endeavors up to the eight branches of the noble path.
Śāriputra, he practices the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path, while embracing all the four foundations of mindfulness,
the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path;
and he embraces all the doors of liberation— emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness— while...

One cultivates the four right endeavors up to the eight branches of the noble path; one cultivates the four right endeavors up to the eight branches of the noble path by embracing all the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path;
and one cultivates the four right endeavors by embracing all the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities.
Having abandoned [the afflictions] up to the eight branches of the noble path,
they cultivate the four right endeavors up to the eight branches of the noble path while embracing all gateways of samādhi and dhāraṇī;
they embrace internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, and the emptiness of conditioned phenomena.
...and by practicing the four right efforts through the emptiness of the unconditioned, the emptiness of the ultimate, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion,
the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics,
the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
Abandoning [the afflictions] up to the eightfold noble path, one cultivates the four right efforts while embracing all suchness,
the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena,
the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm.
They cultivate the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path by abandoning [the hindrances] and embracing all five eyes and six supernormal powers;
they cultivate the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path by embracing all the ten powers of a Buddha,
the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.

Up to the eightfold noble path, they practice the four right endeavors through to the eightfold noble path while embracing all great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity;
they practice the four right endeavors through to the eightfold noble path while embracing all-knowledge, the knowledge of the aspects of the path, and the knowledge of all aspects.
Embracing all thirty-two marks of a great man and eighty secondary signs while cultivating the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path,
one thereby gives rise to no dualistic perception.
“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, for the sake of fulfilling the gate of liberation of emptiness,
they embrace all forms of giving within that very gate of liberation of emptiness.”
They cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness through the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom;
they cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness while embracing all four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments;
and they embrace all four foundations of mindfulness and the four right efforts.
They cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness by means of the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path;
they cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness while embracing all the gates of liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness;
and they embrace all the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path.

And they practice the gate of liberation of emptiness; they embrace all eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities while practicing the gate of liberation of emptiness;
they embrace all doors of samādhi and all doors of dhāraṇī while practicing the gate of liberation of emptiness; they embrace all internal emptiness.
...external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena,
the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration,
the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, and the [emptiness of non-]...
One may cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness by means of the emptiness of obtainability, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature,
and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, thereby embracing all suchness, the dharma-realm,
the dharma-nature, non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state of being free from birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, and the stability of dharmas.
They cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness by means of the reality-limit (*bhūtakoṭi*) and the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*);
they cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness while embracing all five eyes and six supernormal powers;

and they cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness while embracing all the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
And they cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness while embracing all great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity;
they cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness while embracing all the qualities of non-forgetfulness and the constant abiding in equanimity;
they cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness while embracing all-knowledge and the knowledge of the aspects of the path.
They cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness through the knowledge of all aspects,

and they cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness while embracing all thirty-two marks of a great man and eighty minor marks; by these causes and conditions, they are free from dualistic conceptions.
“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, for the sake of fulfilling the gateways to liberation that are signless and wishless,
they [practice] within those very signless and wishless gateways to liberation.”
They embrace all the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration,
and wisdom while cultivating the signless and wishless doors of liberation;
they embrace all the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments while cultivating the signless and wishless.
They embrace all the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power,
the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path to cultivate the signless and wishless doors of liberation;
they embrace all the doors of liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness.

They cultivate the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness; they embrace all the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path while cultivating the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness;
and they embrace all eight liberations, eight bases of mastery, nine successive meditative attainments, and ten totalities while cultivating signlessness.
The wishless door of liberation encompasses all doors of samādhi and dhāraṇī,
and one cultivates the signless and wishless doors of liberation; it encompasses all internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness,
the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, and unconditioned [emptiness].
One cultivates the signless and the wishless through emptiness, ultimate emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness,
essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, all-dharmas emptiness, unobtainable emptiness,
non-existence emptiness, intrinsic nature emptiness, and the non-existence of intrinsic nature emptiness.
The gate of liberation consists of practicing the signless and the wishless while embracing all suchness, the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena,
non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena,
the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm.
Entering the doors of liberation, they embrace all five eyes and six supernormal powers while practicing the signless and wishless doors of liberation;

they embrace all the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha while practicing the signless and wishless doors of liberation; they embrace...
Having embraced all great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity, they cultivate the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness;
having embraced all qualities of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant abiding in equanimity, they cultivate the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness;
and having embraced all aspects of omniscience and the knowledge of the paths.
They cultivate the gate of liberation of signlessness and the gate of liberation of wishlessness through all-aspect omniscience;
they cultivate the gate of liberation of signlessness and the gate of liberation of wishlessness while embracing all thirty-two marks of a great man and eighty minor marks;
by these causes and conditions, they are free from dualistic conceptions.
“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, for the sake of fulfilling the noble truth of suffering,
they embrace all generosity and pure ethical discipline within that very noble truth of suffering.”
...abiding in the noble truth of suffering through the perfections of patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom;
embracing all four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments while abiding in the noble truth of suffering;
and embracing all four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, and the four bases of psychic power...
Abiding in the Noble Truth of Suffering by means of the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path;
abiding in the Noble Truth of Suffering while embracing all the gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness;
and abiding in the Noble Truth of Suffering while embracing all the Noble Truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path.
They embrace all eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities while abiding in the noble truth of suffering;
they embrace all gateways of samādhi and gateways of dhāraṇī while abiding in the noble truth of suffering;
they embrace all internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, and emptiness...
emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness,
emptiness of dispersion, emptiness of non-alteration, emptiness of intrinsic nature, emptiness of specific characteristics,
emptiness of common characteristics, emptiness of all phenomena, emptiness of non-apprehensibility, emptiness of non-existence, and self-...
Abiding in the noble truth of suffering through the emptiness of intrinsic nature and the emptiness of the self-nature of non-existence,
one embraces all suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth,
the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable.
Abiding in the Noble Truth of Suffering by discerning the realms; abiding in the Noble Truth of Suffering while embracing all five eyes and six supernormal powers;

abiding in the Noble Truth of Suffering while embracing all the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; and embracing all great loving-kindness.
...abiding in the noble truth of suffering through great compassion, great joy, and great equanimity;
abiding in the noble truth of suffering while embracing all the qualities of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity;
abiding in the noble truth of suffering while embracing all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*), and knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*); and embracing all...
With the thirty-two marks of a great man and the eighty secondary signs, one dwells in the Noble Truth of Suffering;
by reason of this, there is no dualistic conception. "Subhūti!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, for the sake of fulfilling the noble truths of origin,
cessation, and the path, they embrace all generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom within those very noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path.

They cultivate all-knowledge by way of the nature of detachment from birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm;
they cultivate all-knowledge by embracing all five eyes and six supernormal powers;
and they cultivate all-knowledge by embracing all the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, and the four analytical knowledges.
One cultivates all-knowledge by understanding the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
one cultivates all-knowledge by embracing all great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity;
one cultivates all-knowledge by embracing all the qualities of non-forgetfulness and the constant abiding in equanimity; one embraces all and all... [cultivates] all-knowledge.
One cultivates all-knowledge through the knowledge of all modes, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects;
one cultivates all-knowledge by embracing all thirty-two marks of a great man and the eighty minor marks.
By these causes and conditions, there is no dualistic conception.
“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, for the sake of fulfilling the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects,
they [apply themselves] within that very knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects.”

They embrace all the perfections of giving, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom while cultivating the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects;
they embrace all the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments while cultivating the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects. One...
The knowledge of all aspects encompasses all four foundations of mindfulness, four right efforts, four bases of power,
five faculties, five powers, seven factors of enlightenment, and eight branches of the noble path, thereby cultivating the knowledge of the path and the knowledge of all aspects;
the knowledge of all aspects encompasses all the doors of liberation— emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness.

One cultivates the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects; one cultivates the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects by encompassing all the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path;

and one cultivates the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects by encompassing all the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities.
...the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), which encompasses all doors of meditative concentration (*samādhi*) and doors of dhāraṇī while cultivating the knowledge of paths (*mārgajñatā*);
and the knowledge of all aspects, which encompasses all internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness,
emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, emptiness of the ultimate (*paramārthaśūnyatā*), emptiness of the conditioned (*saṃskṛtaśūnyatā*), and emptiness of the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā*)...
One cultivates the knowledge of the aspects of the path by means of emptiness, ultimate emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential emptiness,
self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, emptiness of all phenomena, non-apprehendable emptiness,
absence-of-nature emptiness, intrinsic-nature emptiness, and absence-of-nature-intrinsic-nature emptiness. One.
The wisdom of all aspects encompasses all suchness, the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, non-falsity, immutability, equality,
the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space,
and the inconceivable realm; it is through this that one cultivates the wisdom of the aspects of the path and all [other wisdoms].

The knowledge of characteristics (*lakṣaṇajñāna*) encompasses all five eyes and six supernormal powers while cultivating the knowledge of characteristics and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*);

it encompasses all ten powers of a Buddha, four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, and eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha while cultivating the knowledge of characteristics and the knowledge of all aspects; it encompasses...
Having embraced all great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity, one cultivates the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects;
having embraced all the qualities of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant abiding in equanimity, one cultivates the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects;
and having embraced all the knowledge of all things and the knowledge of the aspects of the path.
One cultivates the knowledge of the aspects of the path by means of the knowledge of all aspects;
one cultivates the knowledge of the aspects of the path by means of the knowledge of all aspects as it encompasses all thirty-two marks of a great man and eighty minor marks;
for these reasons, there is no dualistic conception.
“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, for the sake of fulfilling the thirty-two marks of a great man,
they embrace one [mark] within those very thirty-two marks of a great man.”
All the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration,
and wisdom lead to the thirty-two marks of a Great Being; the mastery of all four dhyānas, the four immeasurables,
and the four formless attainments leads to the thirty-two marks of a Great Being, encompassing them all.

The four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path lead to the thirty-two marks of a great man;
the encompassing of all the gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—leads to the thirty-two marks of a great man. This encompasses...
By realizing the Noble Truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path, one brings forth the thirty-two marks of a Great Man;

by embracing all eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities, one brings forth the thirty-two marks of a Great Man; by embracing all gateways of samādhi and dhāraṇīs...
From the gate of dhāraṇī, one draws forth the thirty-two marks of a great being and embraces all forms of emptiness:
internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena,
the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, the emptiness of dispersion, and the emptiness of non-alteration.

By means of the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility,
the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence,
one brings forth the thirty-two marks of a great man and fully embraces all suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, and non-falsity.
By means of intrinsic nature, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena,
the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm, one brings forth the thirty-two marks of a great man;
by encompassing all five eyes and six supernormal powers, one brings forth the thirty-two marks of a great man.

He embraces all the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, thereby drawing forth the thirty-two marks of a Great Man;
he embraces all great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity, thereby drawing forth the thirty-two marks of a Great Man; he embraces the one...
By means of the quality of never forgetting and the constant abiding in equanimity, one brings forth the thirty-two marks of a Great Being;
by means of embracing all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), one brings forth the thirty-two marks of a Great Being;
and by means of embracing all thirty-two marks of a Great Being and the eighty secondary signs (*anuvyañjana*).
They manifest the thirty-two marks of a great man; by reason of these causes and conditions, they are free from dualistic conceptions. "Subhūti!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, it is for the sake of fulfilling the eight..."
By means of the ten secondary marks, one gathers all the perfections of generosity,
ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom within the eighty secondary marks,
thereby inducing the eighty secondary marks; and one likewise gathers all the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.

Through meditative concentration, one brings forth the eighty minor marks; by embracing all the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path, one brings forth the eighty minor marks;
and by embracing all the gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—one brings forth the eighty minor marks.
And they induce the eighty minor marks; they embrace all the Noble Truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path while inducing the eighty minor marks;
they embrace all the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities while inducing the eighty minor marks; they embrace all samādhis...
The gateways of the stages and the gateways of dhāraṇī lead to the eighty minor marks and encompass all forms of emptiness:
internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena,
the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, the emptiness of limits, the emptiness of dispersion, and the emptiness of non-alteration.
By means of emptiness, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self-characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics,
the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence,
one brings forth the eighty minor marks and fully embraces all suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, and that which is non-erroneous.
Through nature, immutability, equanimity, the state of being free from birth, the fixedness of phenomena, the stability of phenomena,
the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm, he draws forth the eighty minor marks;
through the inclusion of all five eyes and six supernormal powers, he draws forth the eighty minor marks and includes them all.
The ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha lead to the eighty minor marks;
the embrace of all great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity leads to the eighty minor marks;
and the embrace of all the quality of non-forgetfulness and constant abiding [in mindfulness] leads to the eighty minor marks.

Abandoning the nature [of form] while drawing forth the eighty minor marks; embracing all-knowledge (*sarvajñā*), knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) while drawing forth the eighty minor marks;

and embracing all thirty-two marks of a great man (*mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa*) and the eighty minor marks while drawing forth the eighty minor marks—it is by these causes and conditions that there is no [obstruction].
Second, regarding perception: "Furthermore, Subhūti,

because this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, when practicing the perfection of generosity, he dwells in an uncontaminated mind while practicing the perfection of generosity."
When practicing the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, one dwells in an untainted mind while practicing ethical discipline up to wisdom.
Therefore, although they practice from generosity up to the perfection of wisdom, they maintain no notion of duality. "Subhūti!
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, when they cultivate the four dhyānas, they do so while abiding in an untainted mind."
When practicing the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions, one dwells in an untainted mind while practicing the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions.
Therefore, although one practices the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions, there is no dualistic perception.

“Subhūti! Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, when practicing the four foundations of mindfulness, he dwells in an uncontaminated mind while practicing the four foundations of mindfulness;

when practicing the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path, he dwells in an uncontaminated mind while practicing the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path.”
Therefore, although they cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eight branches of the noble path, they remain free from the perception of duality. "Subhūti!

Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, when they cultivate the gate of liberation of emptiness, they dwell in an uncontaminated mind while cultivating the gate of liberation of emptiness;
When practicing the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, one dwells in an untainted mind while practicing these gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.
Therefore, although one practices the gateways of liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, there is no dualistic conception.
“Subhūti! Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, when he dwells in the noble truth of suffering, he dwells in the noble truth of suffering with an untainted mind;
when he dwells in the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, he dwells in those noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path with an untainted mind.”
Therefore, although they dwell in the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path, they do not harbor dualistic conceptions. Subhūti!
Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, when they cultivate the eight liberations, they do so while abiding in an untainted mind.

When practicing the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities, one dwells in an untainted mind while practicing the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities.
Therefore, although one cultivates the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities, there is no dualistic conception. "Subhūti!..."
Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, when practicing any of the doors of samādhi, they dwell in an untainted mind while practicing all the doors of samādhi;
when practicing any of the doors of dhāraṇī, they dwell in an untainted mind while practicing all the doors of dhāraṇī.
Therefore, although one cultivates all doors of samādhi and dhāraṇī, there is no notion of duality.
