The causal condition is empty and has no abode; likewise, the immediately preceding condition, the object-condition, and the dominant condition are also empty and have no abode.”
Why is this? Subhūti!

Causes and conditions lack intrinsic nature and cannot be apprehended; likewise, the immediately preceding condition, the object-condition, and the dominant condition also lack intrinsic nature and cannot be apprehended. Causes and conditions are empty, lacking intrinsic nature and being unapprehendable; the immediately preceding condition, the object-condition, and the dominant condition are also empty, lacking intrinsic nature and being unapprehendable. This is because that which lacks intrinsic nature and is unapprehendable has no place to abide.
“Subhūti! Phenomena produced from conditions have no place of abiding; the emptiness of phenomena produced from conditions likewise has no place of abiding. Why is this?

"Subhūti! Phenomena produced from conditions have no intrinsic nature and cannot be apprehended; the emptiness of phenomena produced from conditions likewise has no intrinsic nature and cannot be apprehended, for that which is an unapprehendable lack of intrinsic nature does not abide anywhere."

“Subhūti! Ignorance has no place of abiding; formative forces, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair likewise have no place of abiding.
Ignorance is empty and has no place of abiding; from formative forces up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, they too are empty and have no place of abiding.”
Why is this? Subhūti!

Ignorance has no intrinsic nature and is unapprehendable; the formative forces, up to and including old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, likewise have no intrinsic nature and are unapprehendable. Ignorance is empty, lacks intrinsic nature, and is unapprehendable; the formative forces, up to and including old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, are also empty, lack intrinsic nature, and are unapprehendable. This is because that which lacks intrinsic nature and is unapprehendable cannot have any place of abiding.
“Subhūti! The perfection of generosity has no abiding; the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom likewise have no abiding.

The emptiness of the perfection of generosity has no abiding; the emptiness of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom likewise has no abiding.”
Why is this so? Subhūti!

The perfection of generosity has no intrinsic nature and is unapprehendable; the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom likewise have no intrinsic nature and are unapprehendable. The emptiness of the perfection of generosity has no intrinsic nature and is unapprehendable; the emptiness of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom likewise has no intrinsic nature and is unapprehendable. This is because a dharma that is without intrinsic nature and unapprehendable cannot have any place of abiding.
"Subhūti! The four dhyānas have no abode; the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions likewise have no abode.
The emptiness of the four dhyānas has no abode; the emptiness of the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions likewise has no abode."
Why is this? Subhūti!

The four dhyānas lack intrinsic nature and cannot be apprehended; the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments likewise lack intrinsic nature and cannot be apprehended. The emptiness of the four dhyānas lacks intrinsic nature and cannot be apprehended; the emptiness of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments likewise lacks intrinsic nature and cannot be apprehended. This is because that which lacks intrinsic nature and cannot be apprehended has no place in which to abide.

“Subhūti! The four foundations of mindfulness have no place of abiding; the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eight branches of the noble path likewise have no place of abiding.

The four foundations of mindfulness are empty and have no place of abiding; the emptiness of the four right efforts, up to and including the eight branches of the noble path, also has no place of abiding.”
Why is this? Subhūti!

The four foundations of mindfulness lack intrinsic nature and are unapprehendable; the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path, likewise lack intrinsic nature and are unapprehendable. The four foundations of mindfulness are empty, lack intrinsic nature, and are unapprehendable; the emptiness of the four right efforts, up to and including the eightfold noble path, also lacks intrinsic nature and is unapprehendable. This is because a dharma that lacks intrinsic nature and is unapprehendable has no place in which to abide.
"Subhūti! The gate of liberation of emptiness has no abiding place; the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness likewise have no abiding place.
The gate of liberation of emptiness is empty and has no abiding place; the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are also empty and have no abiding place."
Why is this? Subhūti!

The gate of liberation of emptiness has no intrinsic nature and is unapprehendable; the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness likewise have no intrinsic nature and are unapprehendable. The emptiness of the gate of liberation of emptiness has no intrinsic nature and is unapprehendable; the emptiness of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness also has no intrinsic nature and is unapprehendable. This is because a dharma that is unapprehendable due to having no intrinsic nature cannot have any place of abiding.

“Subhūti! Inner emptiness has no place of abiding; outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, emptiness of the ultimate, emptiness of the conditioned, emptiness of the unconditioned, absolute emptiness, emptiness of the limitless, emptiness of dispersion, emptiness of non-alteration, emptiness of intrinsic nature, emptiness of self-characteristic, emptiness of common characteristic, emptiness of all phenomena, emptiness of the unapprehendable, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, and emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence likewise have no place of abiding.

The emptiness of inner emptiness has no place of abiding, and the emptiness of outer emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, likewise has no place of abiding.”
Why is this? Subhūti!

Internal emptiness has no intrinsic nature and is unapprehendable; external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, also has no intrinsic nature and is unapprehendable. The emptiness of internal emptiness has no intrinsic nature and is unapprehendable; the emptiness of external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, also has no intrinsic nature and is unapprehendable. This is because that which is unapprehendable due to the absence of intrinsic nature does not abide anywhere.
“Subhūti! The noble truth of suffering has no abiding place; the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path likewise have no abiding place.
The noble truth of suffering is empty and has no abiding place; the emptiness of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path likewise has no abiding place.”
Why is this? Subhūti!

The noble truth of suffering has no intrinsic nature and is unapprehendable; the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path likewise have no intrinsic nature and are unapprehendable. The noble truth of suffering is empty, lacks intrinsic nature, and is unapprehendable; the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path are also empty, lack intrinsic nature, and are unapprehendable. This is because that which lacks intrinsic nature and is unapprehendable cannot abide anywhere.
“Subhūti! The eight liberations have no abiding place; the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities likewise have no abiding place.
The emptiness of the eight liberations has no abiding place; the emptiness of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities likewise has no abiding place.”
Why is this? Subhūti!

The eight liberations lack intrinsic nature and cannot be apprehended; the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases likewise lack intrinsic nature and cannot be apprehended. The emptiness of the eight liberations lacks intrinsic nature and cannot be apprehended; the emptiness of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases likewise lacks intrinsic nature and cannot be apprehended. This is because a dharma that lacks intrinsic nature and cannot be apprehended has no place to abide.
“Subhūti! All dhāraṇī-doors have no place of abiding; all samādhi-doors likewise have no place of abiding.
All dhāraṇī-doors are empty and have no place of abiding; all samādhi-doors are also empty and have no place of abiding.”
Why is this? Subhūti!

All dhāraṇī-doors lack intrinsic nature and are unapprehendable; all samādhi-doors likewise lack intrinsic nature and are unapprehendable. All dhāraṇī-doors are empty, lacking intrinsic nature, and are unapprehendable; all samādhi-doors are also empty, lacking intrinsic nature, and are unapprehendable. This is because that which lacks intrinsic nature and is unapprehendable has no place to abide.

“Subhūti! The Ground of Supreme Joy has no abiding; the Ground of Freedom from Defilement, the Ground of Radiant Light, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Utmost Difficulty to Conquer, the Ground of Manifestation, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, and the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma likewise have no abiding.
The Ground of Supreme Joy is empty and has no abiding; the emptiness of the Ground of Freedom from Defilement, up to and including the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma, also has no abiding.”
Why is this? Subhūti!

The Ground of Extreme Joy has no intrinsic nature and is unapprehendable; from the Ground Free from Defilement up to the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma, these also have no intrinsic nature and are unapprehendable. The Ground of Extreme Joy is empty, lacks intrinsic nature, and is unapprehendable; from the Ground Free from Defilement up to the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma, their emptiness likewise lacks intrinsic nature and is unapprehendable. This is because that which is unapprehendable due to the absence of intrinsic nature cannot have any place of abiding.
“Subhūti! The five eyes have no place of abiding, and the six supernormal powers likewise have no place of abiding;
the five eyes are empty and have no place of abiding, and the six supernormal powers are empty and likewise have no place of abiding.”
Why is this? Subhūti!

The five eyes have no intrinsic nature and are unapprehendable; the six supernormal powers likewise have no intrinsic nature and are unapprehendable. The five eyes are empty, lack intrinsic nature, and are unapprehendable; the six supernormal powers are also empty, lack intrinsic nature, and are unapprehendable. This is because that which lacks intrinsic nature and is unapprehendable has no place in which to abide.
“Subhūti! The ten powers of a Buddha abide nowhere; the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha also abide nowhere.
The ten powers of a Buddha are empty and abide nowhere; the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are also empty and abide nowhere.”
Why is this? Subhūti!

The ten powers of a Buddha lack intrinsic nature and cannot be apprehended; the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha likewise lack intrinsic nature and cannot be apprehended. The emptiness of the ten powers of a Buddha lacks intrinsic nature and cannot be apprehended; the emptiness of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha also lacks intrinsic nature and cannot be apprehended. This is because that which lacks intrinsic nature and cannot be apprehended has no place in which to abide.
“Subhūti! Great loving-kindness has no abode; great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity likewise have no abode.
Great loving-kindness is empty and has no abode; great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity are also empty and have no abode.”
Why is this? Subhūti!

Great loving-kindness has no intrinsic nature and is unapprehendable; great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity likewise have no intrinsic nature and are unapprehendable. Great loving-kindness is empty, lacks intrinsic nature, and is unapprehendable; great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity are also empty, lack intrinsic nature, and are unapprehendable. This is because a dharma that lacks intrinsic nature and is unapprehendable cannot have any place of abiding.
“Subhūti! The quality of non-forgetfulness has no abode, and the state of constant dwelling in equanimity likewise has no abode;
the emptiness of the quality of non-forgetfulness has no abode, and the emptiness of the state of constant dwelling in equanimity likewise has no abode.”
Why is this? Subhūti!

The quality of non-forgetfulness has no intrinsic nature and is unapprehendable; the state of constant equanimity likewise has no intrinsic nature and is unapprehendable. The quality of non-forgetfulness is empty, lacks intrinsic nature, and is unapprehendable; the state of constant equanimity is also empty, lacks intrinsic nature, and is unapprehendable. This is because a dharma that lacks intrinsic nature and is unapprehendable cannot have any place of abiding.
“Subhūti! All-knowledge has no abiding place; the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects likewise have no abiding place.
All-knowledge is empty and has no abiding place; the emptiness of the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects likewise has no abiding place.”
Why is this? Subhūti!

All-knowledge (sarvajñatā) has no intrinsic nature (niḥsvabhāva) and is unapprehendable; the knowledge of the paths (mārgākārajñatā) and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā) likewise have no intrinsic nature and are unapprehendable. All-knowledge is empty, lacks intrinsic nature, and is unapprehendable; the emptiness of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects also lacks intrinsic nature and is unapprehendable. This is because that which lacks intrinsic nature and is unapprehendable cannot abide anywhere.
“Subhūti! The thirty-two marks of a great man have no abiding place; the eighty minor marks likewise have no abiding place.
The thirty-two marks of a great man are empty and have no abiding place; the eighty minor marks are also empty and have no abiding place.”
Why is this? Subhūti!

The thirty-two marks of a great man have no intrinsic nature and are unattainable; the eighty secondary characteristics also have no intrinsic nature and are unattainable. The thirty-two marks of a great man are empty, lack intrinsic nature, and are unattainable; the eighty secondary characteristics are also empty, lack intrinsic nature, and are unattainable. This is because that which lacks intrinsic nature and is unattainable has no place to abide.
“Subhūti! The fruit of stream-entry has no abiding; the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship, as well as pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, likewise have no abiding.
The fruit of stream-entry is empty and has no abiding; the emptiness of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, arhatship, and pratyekabuddha-enlightenment likewise has no abiding.”
Why is this? Subhūti!

The fruit of stream-entry has no intrinsic nature and is unapprehendable; the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship, as well as the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, likewise have no intrinsic nature and are unapprehendable. The fruit of stream-entry is empty, lacks intrinsic nature, and is unapprehendable; the emptiness of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, arhatship, and the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha also lacks intrinsic nature and is unapprehendable. This is because there is no dharma that lacks intrinsic nature and yet can abide anywhere.
“Subhūti! All practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas abide nowhere; the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas likewise abides nowhere.
All practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are empty and abide nowhere; the emptiness of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas likewise abides nowhere.”
Why is this? Subhūti!

All the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas lack intrinsic nature and cannot be apprehended; the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas likewise lacks intrinsic nature and cannot be apprehended. All the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are empty, lack intrinsic nature, and cannot be apprehended; the emptiness of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas also lacks intrinsic nature and cannot be apprehended. This is because a dharma that lacks intrinsic nature and cannot be apprehended has no place to abide.
“Subhūti! Worldly dharmas have no place of abiding; supramundane dharmas likewise have no place of abiding.
Worldly dharmas are empty and have no place of abiding; supramundane dharmas are also empty and have no place of abiding.”
Why is this? Subhūti!

Worldly phenomena lack intrinsic nature and cannot be apprehended; supramundane phenomena likewise lack intrinsic nature and cannot be apprehended. Worldly phenomena are empty, lacking intrinsic nature and cannot be apprehended; supramundane phenomena are also empty, lacking intrinsic nature and cannot be apprehended. This is because that which lacks intrinsic nature and cannot be apprehended has no place to abide.
“Subhūti! Contaminated phenomena have no place of abiding, and uncontaminated phenomena likewise have no place of abiding;
contaminated phenomena are empty and have no place of abiding, and uncontaminated phenomena are empty and likewise have no place of abiding.”
Why is this? Subhūti!

Contaminated phenomena (sāsrava-dharma) lack intrinsic nature (svabhāva) and are unapprehendable; uncontaminated phenomena (anāsrava-dharma) likewise lack intrinsic nature and are unapprehendable. Contaminated phenomena are empty, lacking intrinsic nature, and unapprehendable; uncontaminated phenomena are also empty, lacking intrinsic nature, and unapprehendable. This is because that which lacks intrinsic nature and is unapprehendable has no place in which to abide.
“Subhūti! Conditioned phenomena have no place of abiding, and unconditioned phenomena likewise have no place of abiding;
conditioned phenomena are empty and have no place of abiding, and the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena likewise has no place of abiding.”
Why is this? Subhūti!

Conditioned phenomena (saṃskṛtadharma) lack intrinsic nature (svabhāva) and are unapprehendable; unconditioned phenomena (asaṃskṛtadharma) likewise lack intrinsic nature and are unapprehendable. Conditioned phenomena are empty, lacking intrinsic nature and being unapprehendable; unconditioned phenomena are also empty, lacking intrinsic nature and being unapprehendable. This is because there is no place for a phenomenon that lacks intrinsic nature and is unapprehendable to abide.

“Subhūti! A phenomenon that lacks intrinsic nature does not abide in a phenomenon that lacks intrinsic nature; a phenomenon that possesses intrinsic nature does not abide in a phenomenon that possesses intrinsic nature; a phenomenon that lacks intrinsic nature does not abide in a phenomenon that possesses intrinsic nature; and a phenomenon that possesses intrinsic nature does not abide in a phenomenon that lacks intrinsic nature.

A phenomenon that is self-nature does not abide in a phenomenon that is self-nature; a phenomenon that is other-nature does not abide in a phenomenon that is other-nature; a phenomenon that is self-nature does not abide in a phenomenon that is other-nature; and a phenomenon that is other-nature does not abide in a phenomenon that is self-nature.”
Why is this? Because all these dharmas are unattainable; how could that which is unattainable have any place of abiding?
Thus it is, Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they employ these various emptinesses to cultivate and dispel all phenomena, and are also able to teach and reveal them to sentient beings as they truly are.

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can practice the profound perfection of wisdom in this manner, they will be free from all faults before the Buddha, the bodhisattvas, the pratyekabuddhas, the śrāvakas, and the entire assembly of noble ones.”

Why is this? Because all the holy multitudes—the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Pratyekabuddhas, and Śrāvakas—are able to awaken to this dharmatā accordingly; having awakened to it accordingly, they proclaim it without error for the sake of all sentient beings. Although they proclaim various dharmas for the sake of sentient beings, they neither deviate from nor transcend the dharmatā.
Why is this? Subhūti!
The true nature of all phenomena is precisely the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality; for such a dharma-realm, suchness, and limit of reality are all unalterable and unsurpassable.

Why is this? It is because such things as the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), true thusness (*tathatā*), and the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) are all devoid of intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*) and cannot be transcended.

*The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, Fascicle 382, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One, Chapter Sixty-eight, Section Five: "The Characteristics of All Merits. At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
If the true dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality do not undergo transmigration or transcendence, is form different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality?”
Are feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality?
“World-Honored One!
Are the eye-base different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality?”
Are the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality?
“World-Honored One,
are the sense base of form different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality?”
Are the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality?
“World-Honored One!
Is the eye-element different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality?”
"Are the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind elements different from the dharma-element, suchness, and the limit of reality?
"World-Honored One,
are the form element and the dharma-element, suchness, and the limit of reality different?"
Are the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena distinct from the sphere of mental phenomena, suchness, and the limit of reality?
“World-Honored One,
are the sphere of visual consciousness distinct from the sphere of mental phenomena, suchness, and the limit of reality?”
Are the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements different from the dharma-element, suchness, and the limit of reality?
“World-Honored One!
Is eye-contact different from the dharma-element, suchness, and the limit of reality?”
Are the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact, as well as the dharma-element, suchness, and the limit of reality, different from one another?
“World-Honored One!
Are the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition different from the dharma-element, suchness, and the limit of reality?”
Are the various sensations produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality?
“World-Honored One!
Is the earth element different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality?
Are the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality?”
“World-Honored One!
Are causes and conditions different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality?
Are the immediately preceding condition, the object-condition, and the dominant condition different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality?”
“World-Honored One!
Are the dharmas produced from various conditions different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality?
World-Honored One!”
Is ignorance different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality?

Are volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality?
“Bhagavān, is the perfection of generosity different from the dharmadhātu, suchness, and the limit of reality?
Are the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom different from the dharmadhātu, suchness, and the limit of reality?”
“World-Honored One!
Are the four dhyānas different from the dharma-dhātu, suchness, and the limit of reality?
Are the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments different from the dharma-dhātu, suchness, and the limit of reality?”
“World-Honored One!
Are the four foundations of mindfulness different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality?

Are the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality?”
“World-Honored One!
Is the gate of liberation of emptiness different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality?
Are the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality?”
“World-Honored One!
Is inner emptiness different from the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), suchness (*tathatā*), and the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*)?

Are outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, emptiness of all dharmas, unapprehendable emptiness, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, and emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality?”
“World-Honored One!
Is the noble truth of suffering different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the reality-limit?
Are the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the reality-limit?”
“World-Honored One!
Are the eight liberations different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality?
Are the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality?”
“World-Honored One!
Are all the gateways of dhāraṇī different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality?
Are all the gateways of samādhi different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality?”
“World-Honored One!
Is the Stage of Extreme Joy different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality?

Are the Stage Free from Defilement, the Radiant Stage, the Stage of Blazing Wisdom, the Stage Difficult to Conquer, the Manifest Stage, the Far-Reaching Stage, the Immovable Stage, the Stage of Excellent Intelligence, and the Dharma-Cloud Stage different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality?”
“World-Honored One!
Are the five eyes different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality?
Are the six supernormal powers different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality?”
“World-Honored One!
Are the ten powers of a Buddha different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality?
Are the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality?”
“World-Honored One!
Is great loving-kindness different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality?
Are great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality?”
“World-Honored One!
Is the quality of non-forgetfulness different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality?
Is the nature of constant dwelling in equanimity different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality?”
“Bhagavān, is all-knowledge (sarvajñatā) different from the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), suchness (tathatā), and the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi)?
Is the knowledge of the aspects of the path (mārgākārajñatā) and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā) different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality?”
“World-Honored One!
Are the thirty-two marks of a great man different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality?
Are the eighty secondary signs different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality?”
“Bhagavān, is the fruit of stream-entry different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality?
Are the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, arhatship, and the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality?”
“World-Honored One!
Are all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas different from the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), suchness (*tathatā*), and the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*)?
Is the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*) of all Buddhas different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality?”
“World-Honored One!
Are mundane phenomena different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality?
Are supramundane phenomena different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality?”
“World-Honored One!
Are contaminated phenomena different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality?
Are uncontaminated phenomena different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality?”
“World-Honored One!
Are conditioned phenomena different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality?
Are unconditioned phenomena different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality?”
The Buddha said, “No, Subhūti!”

Form is not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality; feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are likewise not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality.

“Subhūti! The sense base of the eye is not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality; the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are likewise not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality.”

“Subhūti! The sphere of form is not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality; the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are likewise not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality.”

“Subhūti! The eye-element is not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality; the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements are likewise not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality.”

"Subhūti! The realm of form is not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality; the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena are likewise not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality."

"Subhūti! The eye-consciousness element is not different from the dharma-element, suchness, and the limit of reality; likewise, the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements are also not different from the dharma-element, suchness, and the limit of reality."

“Subhūti! Eye-contact is not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality; likewise, ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact are also not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality.”

"Subhūti! The various sensations produced with eye-contact as a condition are not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality; the various sensations produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions are likewise not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality."

“Subhūti! The earth element is not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality; likewise, the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are also not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality.”

“Subhūti! The causal condition (*hetu-pratyaya*) is not different from the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), suchness (*tathatā*), and the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*); likewise, the immediately preceding condition (*samanantara-pratyaya*), the object-condition (*ālambana-pratyaya*), and the dominant condition (*adhipati-pratyaya*) are also not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality.”
"Subhūti! The phenomena produced from conditions are not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality. Subhūti!"

Ignorance is not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality; likewise, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are also not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality.

“Subhūti! The perfection of generosity is not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality; the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are likewise not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality.”

“Subhūti! The four dhyānas are not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality; the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are likewise not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality.”

“Subhūti! The four foundations of mindfulness are not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality; the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are likewise not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality.”

"Subhūti! The gate of liberation of emptiness is not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality; the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are likewise not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality."

“Subhūti! Internal emptiness is not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality. External emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate meaning, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self-characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are likewise not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality.”

"Subhūti! The noble truth of suffering is not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality; the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are likewise not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality."

“Subhūti! The eight liberations are not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality; the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases are likewise not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality.”

“Subhūti! All dhāraṇī-doors are not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality; all samādhi-doors as well are not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality.”

“Subhūti! The Ground of Extreme Joy is not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality; the Ground of Freedom from Defilement, the Ground of Radiant Light, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Utmost Difficulty to Conquer, the Ground of Manifestation, the Ground of Far-reaching Travel, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, and the Ground of the Dharma Cloud are likewise not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality.”

“Subhūti! The five eyes are not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality; the six supernormal powers, likewise, are not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality.”

“Subhūti! The ten powers of a Buddha are not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality; the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are likewise not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality.”

“Subhūti! Great loving-kindness is not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality; great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity are likewise not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality.”

“Subhūti! The quality of non-forgetfulness is not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality; the state of constant abiding in equanimity is also not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality.”

“Subhūti! All-knowledge is not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality; the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are likewise not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality.”

“Subhūti! The thirty-two marks of a great man are not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality; the eighty minor marks are likewise not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality.”

“Subhūti! The fruit of stream-entry is not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality; the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship, as well as the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, are likewise not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality.”

“Subhūti! All the practices of bodhisattva mahāsattvas do not differ from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality; the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas likewise does not differ from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality.”

“Subhūti! Worldly dharmas are not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality; supramundane dharmas, likewise, are not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality.”

"Subhūti! Contaminated phenomena (*sāsravadharma*) are not different from the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), suchness (*tathatā*), and the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*); uncontaminated phenomena (*anāsravadharma*) likewise are not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality."

"Subhūti! Conditioned phenomena are not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the reality-limit; unconditioned phenomena, likewise, are not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the reality-limit."
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

If form is not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality, and if feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are likewise not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality;”

"Bhagavān, if the eye-base is not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the reality-limit, then the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases are likewise not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the reality-limit; Bhagavān!"

If the sphere of form is not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality, then the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are likewise not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality;
O World-Honored One!

If the eye-element is not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the reality-limit, then the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements are likewise not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the reality-limit;
O Bhagavat!

If the realm of form is not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality, then the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena are likewise not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality;
World-Honored One!

If the eye-consciousness element is not different from the dharma-element, suchness, and the reality-limit, then the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements are likewise not different from the dharma-element, suchness, and the reality-limit;
O World-Honored One!

If eye-contact is not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the reality-limit, then ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact are likewise not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the reality-limit;
O Bhagavan!

If the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality, then the various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions are likewise not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality;
O Bhagavān!

If the earth element is not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the reality-limit, then the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are likewise not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the reality-limit;
O World-Honored One!

If the causal condition is not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality, then the equal-and-immediate condition, the object-condition, and the dominant condition are likewise not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality;
O Bhagavān!
If the phenomena produced from various conditions are not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality; O Bhagavan,

if ignorance is not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality, then volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, sensation, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are likewise not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality.
Blessed One!

If the perfection of generosity is not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality, then the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are likewise not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality;
Blessed One!

If the four dhyānas are not different from the dharma-dhātu, suchness, and the limit of reality, then the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are likewise not different from the dharma-dhātu, suchness, and the limit of reality;
O Bhagavān!

If the four foundations of mindfulness are not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality, then the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are likewise not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality;
O Bhagavan!

If the gate of liberation of emptiness is not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality, then the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are likewise not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality;
O World-Honored One!

If inner emptiness is not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the reality-limit, then outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate meaning, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of essential nature, the emptiness of self-characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are likewise not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the reality-limit;
O Bhagavān!

If the noble truth of suffering is not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality, then the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are likewise not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality;
O World-Honored One!

If the eight liberations are not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality, then the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are likewise not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality;
O World-Honored One!

If all dharani-doors are not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality, then all samadhi-doors as well are not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality;
World-Honored One!

If the Stage of Utmost Joy is not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality, then the Stage Free from Defilement, the Radiant Stage, the Stage of Blazing Wisdom, the Stage Difficult to Conquer, the Manifest Stage, the Far-Reaching Stage, the Immovable Stage, the Stage of Excellent Intelligence, and the Cloud of Dharma Stage are likewise not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality;
O World-Honored One!

If the five eyes are not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality, then the six supernormal powers are likewise not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality;
O World-Honored One!

If the ten powers of a Buddha are not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality, then the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are likewise not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality;
O World-Honored One!

If great loving-kindness is not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality, then great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity are likewise not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality;
World-Honored One!

If the quality of non-forgetfulness is not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality, then the state of constant abiding in equanimity is likewise not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality;
O Bhagavān!

If all-knowledge is not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality, then the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are likewise not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality;
O Bhagavan!

If the thirty-two marks of a great man are not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality, then the eighty secondary signs are likewise not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality;
O World-Honored One!

If the fruit of stream-entry is not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality, then the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship, as well as the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, are likewise not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality;
O Bhagavan!

If the practice of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality, and if the unexcelled, perfect enlightenment of all buddhas is likewise not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality;
O Bhagavān!

World-Honored One! If worldly phenomena are not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality, then supramundane phenomena likewise are not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality.

"World-Honored One, if contaminated phenomena are not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality, then uncontaminated phenomena likewise are not different from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality."

If conditioned phenomena are not distinct from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality, and if unconditioned phenomena are likewise not distinct from the dharma-realm, suchness, and the limit of reality, how is it that the Blessed One establishes the black dharmas as resulting in black maturation—namely, the realms of hell-beings, animals, and hungry ghosts?
How is it established that pure phenomena (*śukladharma*) produce a white maturation, namely as humans or gods?
And how is it established that black-and-white phenomena produce a black-and-white maturation, namely as certain classes of animals, the realm of hungry ghosts (*preta*), and certain humans?

How is it established that non-black, non-white dharmas bring about a non-black, non-white maturation—namely, the fruit of stream-entry, or the fruit of once-returning, or the fruit of non-returning, or the fruit of arhatship, or the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, or even unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?
The Buddha said: "Subhūti!

Such distinctions between cause and effect are established based on conventional truth (saṃvṛti-satya), not based on the ultimate truth (paramārtha). Within the ultimate truth, it cannot be said that there are distinctions between cause and effect."
Why is this so? Subhūti!

Within the ultimate truth (*paramārtha-satya*), the nature of all phenomena (*dharma*) is beyond conceptual differentiation; it is without expression and without demonstration. How, then, could there be any distinction between cause and effect?

“Subhūti! In the ultimate truth (*paramārthasatya*), form (*rūpa*) is without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purification; feeling (*vedanā*), perception (*saṃjñā*), formations (*saṃskāra*), and consciousness (*vijñāna*) are likewise without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purification, because they are ultimately empty (*atyantaśūnyatā*) and boundlessly empty (*anavakāraśūnyatā*).”

“Subhūti! Within the ultimate truth (*paramārthasatya*), the sense base of the eye is without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purification; the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are likewise without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purification, because they are ultimately empty and boundlessly empty.”

"Subhūti! Within the ultimate truth (*paramārthasatya*), the sphere of form (*rūpāyatana*) is without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purification; the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena (*dharmāyatana*) are likewise without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purification, because they are ultimately empty and boundlessly empty."

"Subhūti! Within the ultimate truth (paramārtha-satya), the eye-element (cakṣurdhātu) is without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purification; the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements (śrotra-, ghrāṇa-, jihvā-, kāya-, and manodhātu) are likewise without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purification, because they are ultimately empty (atyanta-śūnyatā) and boundlessly empty (anavara-śūnyatā)."

“Subhūti! In the ultimate truth (*paramārthasatya*), the realm of form (*rūpadhātu*) is without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purification; the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) are likewise without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purification, because they are ultimately empty (*atyantaśūnyatā*) and boundlessly empty (*anavakāraśūnyatā*).”

“Subhūti! Within the ultimate truth (*paramārthasatya*), the eye-consciousness element (*cakṣurvijñānadhātu*) is without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purification; likewise, the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements are also without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purification, because they are ultimately empty and boundlessly empty.”

“Subhūti! Within the ultimate truth (*paramārthasatya*), eye-contact is neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure; likewise, ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact are also neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure, because they are ultimately empty and boundlessly empty.”

“Subhūti! Within the ultimate truth (*paramārthasatya*), all feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor purified; likewise, all feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions are also neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor purified, because they are ultimately empty and boundlessly empty.”

"Subhūti! Within the ultimate truth (*paramārtha-satya*), the earth element is without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purification; likewise, the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are also without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purification, because they are ultimately empty and boundlessly empty."

“Subhūti! Within the ultimate truth (*paramārthasatya*), causes and conditions are without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purification; likewise, the immediately preceding condition (*samanantarapratyaya*), the objective condition (*ālambanapratyaya*), and the dominant condition (*adhipatipratyaya*) are also without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purification, because they are ultimately empty (*atyantaśūnyatā*) and boundlessly empty (*anavarāgraśūnyatā*).”

“Subhūti! Within the ultimate truth (*paramārthasatya*), phenomena produced from conditions are neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified, because they are characterized by absolute emptiness (*atyantaśūnyatā*) and the emptiness of limits (*anavarāgraśūnyatā*).”

“Subhūti! Within the ultimate truth (*paramārtha-satya*), ignorance is neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified; likewise, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, existence, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are also neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified, because they are ultimately empty and boundlessly empty.”

"Subhūti! Within the ultimate truth (*paramārthasatya*), the perfection of generosity (*dānapāramitā*) is without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purification; likewise, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are also without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purification, because they are ultimately empty and boundlessly empty."

“Subhūti! Within the ultimate truth (*paramārthasatya*), the four dhyānas are without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purification; the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions likewise are without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purification, because they are ultimately empty and boundlessly empty.”

"Subhūti! Within the ultimate truth (*paramārtha-satya*), the four foundations of mindfulness are without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purification; the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are likewise without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purification, because they are ultimately empty and boundlessly empty."

"Subhūti! Within the ultimate truth (*paramārtha-satya*), the gate of liberation of emptiness (*śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha*) is without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purification; the gates of liberation of signlessness (*animitta*) and wishlessness (*apraṇihita*) are likewise without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purification, because they are the emptiness of the ultimate (*atyanta-śūnyatā*) and the emptiness of the limitless (*anavara-agra-śūnyatā*)."

“Subhūti! Within the ultimate truth (*paramārthasatya*), internal emptiness (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*) is without arising and without cessation, and without defilement or purification. External emptiness (*bahirdhā-śūnyatā*), internal-and-external emptiness (*adhyātma-bahirdhā-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of emptiness (*śūnyatā-śūnyatā*), great emptiness (*mahā-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of the ultimate (*paramārtha-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of the conditioned (*saṃskṛta-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta-śūnyatā*), absolute emptiness (*atyanta-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of the limitless (*anavarāgra-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of dispersion (*anavakāra-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of non-alteration (*anavakāra-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of intrinsic nature (*prakṛti-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of specific characteristics (*svalakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of common characteristics (*sāmānya-lakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of all phenomena (*sarvadharma-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of the unapprehendable (*anupalambha-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of non-existence (*abhāva-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of intrinsic nature (*svabhāva-śūnyatā*), and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence (*abhāvasvabhāva-śūnyatā*) are likewise without arising and without cessation, and without defilement or purification, because of the emptiness of the absolute (*atyanta-śūnyatā*) and the emptiness of the limitless (*anavarāgra-śūnyatā*).”

“Subhūti! Within the ultimate truth (*paramārthasatya*), the noble truth of suffering is without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purification; the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are likewise without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purification, because they are ultimately empty and boundlessly empty.”

“Subhūti! Within the ultimate truth (*paramārtha-satya*), the eight liberations (*aṣṭa-vimokṣa*) are without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purification; the eight bases of mastery (*aṣṭābhibhv-āyatana*), the nine successive attainments (*navānupūrva-vihāra-samāpatti*), and the ten totalities (*daśa-kṛtsnāyatana*) are likewise without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purification, because they are ultimately empty and boundlessly empty.”

“Subhūti! Within the ultimate truth (*paramārthasatya*), all doors of dhāraṇī are without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purity; likewise, all doors of samādhi are without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purity, because they are ultimately empty and boundlessly empty.”

“Subhūti! Within the ultimate truth (*paramārtha-satya*), the Stage of Extreme Joy (*pramuditā-bhūmi*) is without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purification; the Stage of Purity (*vimalā-bhūmi*), the Stage of Radiance (*prabhākārī-bhūmi*), the Stage of Blazing Wisdom (*arciṣmatī-bhūmi*), the Stage Difficult to Conquer (*sudurjayā-bhūmi*), the Stage of Presence (*abhimukhī-bhūmi*), the Stage of Far-Going (*dūraṅgamā-bhūmi*), the Immovable Stage (*acalā-bhūmi*), the Stage of Good Intelligence (*sādhumatī-bhūmi*), and the Stage of the Dharma Cloud (*dharmameghā-bhūmi*) are likewise without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purification, because they are ultimately empty and boundlessly empty.”

“Subhūti! Within the ultimate truth (*paramārtha-satya*), the five eyes are without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purification; the six supernormal powers (*abhijñā*) likewise are without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purification, because they are ultimately empty and boundlessly empty.”

“Subhūti! Within the ultimate truth (*paramārtha-satya*), the ten powers (*daśabala*) of a Buddha are without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purification; the four fearlessnesses (*vaiśāradya*), the four analytical knowledges (*pratisamvid*), and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇika-buddhadharma*) are likewise without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purification, because they are ultimately empty and boundlessly empty.”

“Subhūti! Within the ultimate truth (*paramārthasatya*), great loving-kindness (*maitrī*) is without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purification; great compassion (*karuṇā*), great sympathetic joy (*muditā*), and great equanimity (*upekṣā*) are likewise without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purification, because they are ultimately empty and boundlessly empty.”

“Subhūti! Within the ultimate truth (*paramārthasatya*), the quality of non-forgetfulness is without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purification; the state of constant equanimity (*upekṣā*) is likewise without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purification, because of its absolute emptiness (*atyanta-śūnyatā*) and the emptiness of the limitless (*anavarāgra-śūnyatā*).”

“Subhūti! Within the ultimate truth (*paramārtha-satya*), all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) is neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor purified; the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are likewise neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor purified, because they are ultimately empty (*atyanta-śūnyatā*) and boundlessly empty (*anavara-agra-śūnyatā*).”

“Subhūti! Within the ultimate truth (*paramārtha-satya*), the thirty-two marks of a great man are without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purity; the eighty secondary characteristics (*anuvyañjana*) are likewise without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purity, because they are ultimately empty (*atyanta-śūnyatā*) and boundlessly empty (*anavara-grāma-śūnyatā*).”

“Subhūti! Within the ultimate truth (*paramārthasatya*), the fruit of stream-entry is without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purification; likewise, the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship, as well as the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, are also without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purification, because they are ultimately empty and boundlessly empty.”

“Subhūti! Within the ultimate truth (*paramārthasatya*), all practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purification; the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*) of all Buddhas is likewise without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purification, because of the emptiness of the ultimate (*atyanta-śūnyatā*) and the emptiness of the limitless (*anavara-agra-śūnyatā*).”

"Subhūti! Within the ultimate truth (*paramārthasatya*), worldly phenomena are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure; supramundane phenomena likewise are neither arising nor ceasing, neither defiled nor pure, because they are characterized by absolute emptiness (*atyanta-śūnyatā*) and the emptiness of the limitless (*anavarāgra-śūnyatā*)."

“Subhūti! Within the ultimate truth (*paramārthasatya*), contaminated phenomena (*sāsravadharma*) are neither produced nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified; uncontaminated phenomena (*anāsravadharma*) likewise are neither produced nor extinguished, neither defiled nor purified, because they are ultimately empty (*atyantaśūnyatā*) and boundlessly empty (*anavarāgraśūnyatā*).”

“Subhūti! In the ultimate truth (*paramārthasatya*), conditioned phenomena (*saṃskṛtadharma*) are without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purification; unconditioned phenomena (*asaṃskṛtadharma*) likewise are without arising and without cessation, without defilement and without purification, because they are ultimately empty (*atyantaśūnyatā*) and boundlessly empty (*anavarāgraśūnyatā*).”
Then, the Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

If the distinctions between cause and effect are established based on conventional truth (*saṃvṛti-satya*) and not based on ultimate truth (*paramārtha-satya*), then would it not follow that all foolish ordinary beings (*bāla-pṛthagjana*) should possess the fruit of a stream-enterer (*srotāpanna-phala*), or the fruit of a once-returner (*sakṛdāgāmi-phala*), or the fruit of a non-returner (*anāgāmi-phala*), or the fruit of an arhat (*arhat-phala*), or the enlightenment of a solitary buddha (*pratyekabuddha-bodhi*), or even unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*)?”
The Buddha said to Subhūti: "What do you think?
Do all foolish ordinary beings know the conventional truth and the ultimate truth as they truly are?"

If one knows it as it truly is, one should attain the fruit of stream-entry, or the fruit of once-returning, or the fruit of non-returning, or the fruit of arhatship, or the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, or unsurpassed perfect complete enlightenment.

However, since foolish ordinary beings do not know the conventional truth and the ultimate truth as they truly are, and lack the noble path and the cultivation of the noble path, how could there be any distinction of noble fruits for them?

Only the noble ones (ārya) are able to know the conventional truth (saṃvṛti-satya) and the ultimate truth (paramārtha-satya) as they truly are; because there is the noble path and the cultivation of the noble path, there exists the distinction of the noble fruits (ārya-phala).
The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
if one cultivates the Noble Path, does one attain the fruit of the Noble Ones?”
The Buddha said, “No, Subhūti!”

One cannot attain the fruit of the noble ones by practicing the noble path, nor can one attain the fruit of the noble ones without practicing the noble path; one cannot attain the fruit of the noble ones apart from the noble path, nor can one attain the fruit of the noble ones while dwelling within the noble path.
Why is this? Subhūti,
because within the ultimate truth (paramārthasatya), neither the path nor the fruit of the path can be apprehended.
Thus it is, Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, although they establish various distinctions among the noble fruits for the sake of sentient beings, they do not discriminate as to whether such noble fruits are established within the realm of the conditioned or the realm of the unconditioned.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying: “World-Honored One!

If one does not conceptually differentiate such noble fruits as being established within the realm of the conditioned or the realm of the unconditioned, how is it that the World-Honored One says that the severance of the three fetters is called the fruit of stream-entry; the attenuation of desire and hatred is called the fruit of once-returning; the permanent exhaustion of the five lower-tier fetters is called the fruit of non-returning; the permanent exhaustion of the five upper-tier fetters is called the fruit of arhatship; the transformation of all phenomena that arise into phenomena that cease is called the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha; and the permanent severance of the continuity of all habitual tendencies is called unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?”

"Bhagavān! How am I to understand the meaning of what the Buddha has taught—that one does not conceptually differentiate such noble fruits by establishing distinctions between the conditioned realm or the unconditioned realm?"
The Buddha said to Subhūti: "What do you think?

Are these noble fruits—the fruit of stream-entry, once-returning, non-returning, arhatship, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, and the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas—conditioned or unconditioned?"
Subhūti replied, “Such noble fruits are all unconditioned; they are not conditioned.
The Buddha told Subhūti:
“Is there any conceptual differentiation within unconditioned phenomena? Subhūti replied, “No!”
"No, World-Honored One! No, Sugata!"
The Buddha said to Subhūti: "What do you think?

If a son of good family or a daughter of good family thoroughly realizes that all conditioned and unconditioned phenomena share one single characteristic—namely, the characteristic of being signless—at that time, would they have any conceptual differentiation among phenomena, thinking 'this is conditioned' or 'this is unconditioned'?"
Subhūti replied, “No, World-Honored One!”
"No, Sugata! The Buddha said to Subhūti:
“The bodhisattva mahāsattva is also like this: when practicing the profound perfection of wisdom,
although they proclaim all dharmas for the sake of sentient beings, they do not discriminate the characteristics of the dharmas being taught—
whether by way of internal emptiness, or external emptiness, or internal-and-external emptiness, or the emptiness of emptiness.”
Whether it be because of the emptiness of the great, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of the conditioned,
the emptiness of the unconditioned, the emptiness of the absolute, the emptiness of the beginningless and endless,
the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of specific characteristics; or...
Because of the emptiness of common characteristics, or because of the emptiness of all phenomena, or because of the emptiness of the unapprehendable,
or because of the emptiness of non-existence, or because of the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or because of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva is himself without attachment to any phenomena, and is also able to teach others to be without attachment to any phenomena—
namely, regarding generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, [meditative concentration, and wisdom].”
The perfection of diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; whether it be the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, or the four formless attainments;

whether it be the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, or the eightfold noble path; or within the internal...
Emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena,
the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration,
the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self-characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, and the emptiness of all phenomena.
The emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence;
whether it be regarding suchness up to the inconceivable realm; or regarding the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path;
or regarding the doors of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; or regarding the eight liberations.
the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities;
whether it be regarding all doors of dhāraṇī and doors of samādhi, or the ten stages of a bodhisattva, or the five eyes and six supernormal powers,
or the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, and the four analytical knowledges—
Regarding great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity; regarding the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
whether it be the quality of non-forgetfulness or the state of constant abiding in equanimity;

or regarding omniscience (*sarvajñā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*)—in all these, there is no attachment. Because there is no attachment, in all places...
They attain non-obstruction.

"Just as those who are emanated by the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, although they practice the perfections of giving, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, do not accept or cling to their fruits, doing so solely for the sake of the parinirvāṇa of sentient beings;

and although they practice the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions, they do not accept or cling to their fruits, doing so solely for the sake of the parinirvāṇa of sentient beings;"

Although they practice the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of miraculous power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path, they do not accept or cling to those fruits, doing so solely for the sake of the parinirvāṇa of sentient beings;

although they practice internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersal emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, they do not accept or cling to those fruits, doing so solely for the sake of the parinirvāṇa of sentient beings.
Although they practice true thusness up to the inconceivable realm, they do not accept or cling to those fruits, doing so solely for the sake of bringing sentient beings to parinirvāṇa;

although they practice the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path, they do not accept or cling to those fruits, doing so solely for the sake of bringing sentient beings to parinirvāṇa;

although they practice the gates of liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, they do not accept or cling to those fruits, doing so solely for the sake of bringing sentient beings to parinirvāṇa.

Although they practice the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive absorptions, and the ten universal bases, they neither accept nor cling to those fruits, doing so solely for the sake of leading sentient beings to parinirvāṇa;
although they practice all the doors of dhāraṇī and all the doors of samādhi, they neither accept nor cling to those fruits, doing so solely for the sake of leading sentient beings to parinirvāṇa;
although they practice the ten stages of the bodhisattva, they neither accept nor cling to those fruits, doing so solely for the sake of leading sentient beings to parinirvāṇa.
Although they practice the five eyes and the six supernormal powers, they do not accept or cling to those fruits, doing so solely for the sake of bringing sentient beings to parinirvāṇa;

although they practice the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, they do not accept or cling to those fruits, doing so solely for the sake of bringing sentient beings to parinirvāṇa;

although they practice the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant dwelling in equanimity, they do not accept or cling to those fruits, doing so solely for the sake of bringing sentient beings to parinirvāṇa.

Although they practice all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*), and knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), they do not accept or cling to those fruits, acting solely for the sake of bringing sentient beings to parinirvāṇa.

Subhūti! It is the same for a bodhisattva mahāsattva: when practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, they abide in nothing whatsoever—whether among all phenomena that are mundane or supramundane, with outflows or without outflows, conditioned or unconditioned—and they encounter no obstruction.
Why is this? Because they have skillfully realized the true nature (*yathābhūtalakṣaṇa*) of all phenomena.
Chapter Sixty-nine: The Equality of All Phenomena, Part One. At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, thoroughly penetrate the true reality of all phenomena?”
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
Just as those who are emanated by the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas do not engage in greed, do not engage in hatred, and do not engage in delusion;”
One does not course in form, nor does one course in feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness;
