Why is this? Because the dharma-realm is non-dual and without differentiation.
"Is it not the case that the dharma-realm is destroyed by the sphere of form, and likewise destroyed by the spheres of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena?"
Why is this? Because the dharma-realm is non-dual and without differentiation.

"Is it not the case that the eye-element destroys the dharma-realm, and likewise that the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, eye-contact, and the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition destroy the dharma-realm?"
Why is this? Because the dharma-realm is non-dual and without differentiation.

"Is it not the case that the ear-element destroys the dharma-realm, and likewise do the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, as well as ear-contact and the various feelings produced with ear-contact as a condition, destroy the dharma-realm?"
Why is this? Because the dharma-realm is non-dual and without differentiation.

"Is it not the case that the nose-element destroys the dharma-realm, and likewise do the fragrance-element, the nose-consciousness-element, as well as nose-contact and the various feelings produced with nose-contact as a condition, destroy the dharma-realm?"
Why is this? Because the dharma-realm is non-dual and without differentiation.

"Is it not the case that the tongue-element destroys the dharma-realm, and likewise do the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, tongue-contact, and all sensations produced with tongue-contact as a condition destroy the dharma-realm?"
Why is this? Because the dharma-realm is non-dual and without differentiation.

"Is it not the case that the body-realm destroys the dharma-realm, and do the touch-realm, the body-consciousness-realm, as well as body-contact and the various feelings produced with body-contact as a condition, also destroy the dharma-realm?"
Why is this? Because the dharma-realm is non-dual and without differentiation.

"Is it not the case that the mind-realm destroys the dharma-realm, and that the dharma-realm, the mental-consciousness-realm, as well as mental contact and the various feelings produced with mental contact as a condition, also destroy the dharma-realm?"
Why is this? Because the dharma-realm is non-dual and without differentiation.
"Is it not the case that the earth-element destroys the dharma-realm, and likewise do the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness-elements destroy the dharma-realm?"
Why is this? Because the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu) is non-dual and without differentiation.
"Is it not the case that the noble truth of suffering destroys the dharma-realm, and likewise that the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path destroy the dharma-realm?"
Why is this? Because the dharma-realm is non-dual and without differentiation.

"Is it not the case that the dharma-realm is destroyed by the causal condition (*hetu-pratyaya*), and likewise by the immediately preceding condition (*samanantara-pratyaya*), the object-condition (*ālambana-pratyaya*), and the dominant condition (*adhipati-pratyaya*)?"
Why is this? Because the dharma-realm is non-dual and without differentiation.
[Objection: "Does not the destruction of the various phenomena produced from conditions destroy the dharma-realm?"
Why is this? Because the dharma-realm is non-dual and without differentiation.

[One might ask: "Is it not the case that the dharma-realm is destroyed by ignorance, and likewise destroyed by volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair?"
Why is this? Because the dharma-realm is non-dual and without differentiation. [One might ask:

"Does not the dharma-realm also perish through internal emptiness, as well as through external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersal emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature?"
Why is this? Because the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu) is non-dual and without differentiation.

"Is it not the case that the dharma-realm is destroyed by True Suchness (tathatā), and likewise by the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature (dharmatā), the non-falsity (avitathatā), the unchanging nature (ananyathābhāvatā), the sameness (samatā), the nature free from arising (anabhibhūtatā), the fixedness of dharma (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of dharma (dharmasthititā), the reality-limit (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu)?"
Why is this? Because the dharma-realm is non-dual and without differentiation. [One might ask:

"Is it not the case that the perfection of generosity destroys the dharma-realm, and likewise that the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, wisdom, skillful means, sublime aspiration, power, and knowledge destroy the dharma-realm?"
Why is this? Because the dharma-realm is non-dual and without differentiation.

"Is it not the case that the dharma-realm is destroyed by the Stage of Utmost Joy, and likewise by the Stage of Purity, the Stage of Radiance, the Stage of Blazing Wisdom, the Stage of Difficult Victory, the Stage of Presence, the Stage of Far-Going, the Stage of Immovability, the Stage of Excellent Intelligence, and the Stage of Dharma-Cloud?"
Why is this? Because the dharma-realm is non-dual and without differentiation.

"Is it not the case that the dharma-realm is destroyed by the four foundations of mindfulness? Is it also not the case that the dharma-realm is destroyed by the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path?"
Why is this? Because the dharma-realm is non-dual and without differentiation. [One might ask:
"Is it not the case that the dharma-realm is destroyed by the four dhyānas, and likewise destroyed by the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments?"
Why is this? Because the dharma-realm is non-dual and without differentiation.
"Is it not the case that the dharma-realm is destroyed by the eight liberations, and likewise destroyed by the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities?"
Why is this? Because the dharma-realm is non-dual and without differentiation.
"Is it not the case that all dhāraṇī-doors destroy the dharma-realm, and likewise all samādhi-doors destroy the dharma-realm?"
Why is this? Because the dharma-realm is non-dual and without differentiation. [One might ask:
"Does one not destroy the dharma-realm by means of the liberation door of emptiness, and likewise destroy the dharma-realm by means of the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness?"
Why is this? Because the dharma-realm is non-dual and without differentiation.
"Is it not the case that the dharma-realm is destroyed by the five eyes, and likewise destroyed by the six supernormal powers?"
Why is this? Because the dharma-realm is non-dual and without differentiation.

"Is it not the case that the Tathāgata’s ten powers destroy the dharma-realm, and likewise that the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha destroy the dharma-realm?"
Why is this? Because the dharma-realm is non-dual and without differentiation.
"Is it not the case that the dharma-realm is destroyed by great loving-kindness, and likewise destroyed by great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity?"
Why is this? Because the dharma-realm is non-dual and without differentiation.
"Is it not the case that the dharma-realm is destroyed by the absence of forgetfulness, and likewise destroyed by the nature of constant equanimity?"
Why is this? Because the dharma-realm is non-dual and without differentiation.
"Is it not the case that adorning and purifying buddha-fields destroys the dharma-realm, and likewise that maturing sentient beings destroys the dharma-realm?"
Why is this? Because the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu) is non-dual and without differentiation.
[Objection: "Does it not follow that the other immeasurable and boundless Buddha-dharmas destroy the dharma-realm?"
"Why is this? Because the dharma-realm is non-dual and without differentiation.
The Buddha told Subhūti:
"If there were any dharma obtainable apart from the dharmadhātu, one could say that such a dharma might destroy the dharmadhātu;
however, since no dharma can be obtained apart from the dharmadhātu, there is no other dharma capable of destroying the dharmadhātu."
Why is this so? Subhūti!

All Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, as well as Bodhisattvas, Pratyekabuddhas, and Śrāvakas, know that apart from the dharmadhātu, no dharma can be apprehended. Since they know that no dharma exists apart from the dharmadhātu, they do not establish or proclaim it for others. Therefore, the dharmadhātu cannot be destroyed by anything.
Thus it is, Subhūti!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they should train in the characteristic of the dharmadhātu as non-dual, undifferentiated, and indestructible.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
if a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to study the dharma-realm, in what should they train?”
The Buddha told Subhūti:
"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to study the dharma-realm, they should study all dharmas. Why is this?"
"Subhūti! It is because all phenomena enter into the dharmadhātu.
The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
For what reason do you say that all dharmas enter the dharma-realm?
The Buddha said:

“Subhūti! Whether a Tathāgata appears in the world or does not appear in the world, all phenomena are by their very nature (dharmatā) such that they enter the dharmadhātu with undifferentiated characteristics; this does not depend upon the teaching of a Buddha.”
Why is this so? Subhūti!

All wholesome dharmas—whether they be unwholesome dharmas, dharmas with a definite outcome or indeterminate dharmas, dharmas with outflows or without outflows, mundane dharmas or supramundane dharmas, conditioned dharmas or unconditioned dharmas—all of them without exception enter into the signless, unconditioned, and empty-natured realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*).

Therefore, Subhūti, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they wish to study the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), they should study all dharmas; for if they study all dharmas, they are studying the dharma-realm.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

If all dharmas enter the dharma-realm as non-dual and undifferentiated, how should a bodhisattva mahāsattva train in the perfection of wisdom, and likewise train in the perfections of meditative concentration, diligence, patience, ethical discipline, and generosity?”
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva train in the first dhyāna, and also train in the second, third, and fourth dhyānas?
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva train in the immeasurable state of loving-kindness, and also train in the immeasurable states of compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity?

How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva train in the meditative concentration of the sphere of infinite space, and likewise train in the meditative concentrations of the sphere of infinite consciousness, the sphere of nothingness, and the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception?

How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva train in the four foundations of mindfulness, and likewise train in the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path?
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva train in the gate of liberation of emptiness, and also train in the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness?
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva train in the eight liberations, and also train in the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities?
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva train in all the gateways of dhāraṇī and also train in all the gateways of samādhi?

How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva train in internal emptiness, and also train in external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature?

How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva train in suchness (tathatā), and likewise train in the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), the non-erroneous nature, the unchanging nature, equality, the nature free from birth, the fixed nature of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the stability of phenomena (dharmasthititā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and the inconceivable realm?
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva train in the noble truth of suffering, and likewise train in the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path?
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva train in the five eyes, and likewise train in the six supernormal powers?
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva train in the ten powers of a buddha, and likewise train in the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha?
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva train in great loving-kindness, and likewise train in great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity?
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva train in the quality of non-forgetfulness, and likewise train in the nature of constant abiding in equanimity?

How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva train in all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), and also train in the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*)?

How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva train in the perfection of the thirty-two marks of a great man (*dvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa*), and also train in the perfection of the eighty secondary signs (*aśītyanuvyañjana*)?
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva train to be born into the great clans of kṣatriyas, the great clans of brahmins, the great clans of householders, and the great clans of lay merchants?
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva train to become a deva among the Cāturmahārājakāyika, Trāyastriṃśa, Yāma, Tuṣita, Nirmāṇarati, and Paranirmitavaśavartin devas?
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva train to be born among the gods of the Brahmā-kāyika, Brahma-purohita, Brahma-pārṣadya, and Mahābrahmā heavens?
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva train to be born among the Ābhāsvara, Parīttābhā, Apramāṇābhā, and Ābhāsvara-sudṛśa heavens?
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva train to be born among the Śuddhāvāsa devas, the Parīttaśubha devas, the Apramāṇaśubha devas, and the Śubhakṛtsna devas?
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva train to be born among the Bṛhatphala devas, the Parīttabṛhatphala devas, the Apramāṇabṛhatphala devas, and the Bṛhatphala devas?
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva train in the dharmas of being born among the non-percipient beings (asaṃjñisattva) yet not take pleasure in being born there?

How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva train in the dharmas of being born among the heavens of No-Contention (avṛha), No-Heat (atapā), Good Appearance (sudṛśa), Good Vision (sudarśana), and the Ultimate of Form (akaniṣṭha), yet not take pleasure in being born there?

How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva train in the dharmas of the devas of the Sphere of Infinite Space, the Sphere of Infinite Consciousness, the Sphere of Nothingness, and the Sphere of Neither-Perception-nor-Non-Perception, yet not take delight in being born there?

How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva train in the initial arousal of the mind of enlightenment, and likewise train in the second, third, fourth, fifth, sixth, seventh, eighth, ninth, and tenth arousal of the mind of enlightenment?
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva train in the first bodhisattva stage, and likewise train in the second, third, fourth, fifth, sixth, seventh, eighth, ninth, and tenth bodhisattva stages?
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva train in the stage of the śrāvaka without realizing it, and likewise train in the stage of the pratyekabuddha without realizing it?
How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva train in the bodhisattva’s entry into the state of certainty (samyaktvaniyāma), and likewise train in maturing sentient beings and purifying the buddha-field?

How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva train in the dhāraṇīs and unimpeded eloquence, and also train in the path of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas and the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas?
“Having trained in this way, one attains the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and knows all phenomena in all their aspects?
World-Honored One,
it is not that within the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu) there are such various conceptual distinctions.”
World-Honored One!
Will not bodhisattvas, by means of this discrimination, practice in perversion and give rise to various conceptual proliferations within that which is free from conceptual proliferation? Why is this?
“World-Honored One!
Within the true dharma-realm, there are no phenomena of conceptual discrimination or frivolous proliferation.
World-Honored One!”
The dharma-realm is not form, yet it is not separate from form;
the dharma-realm is not feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, yet it is not separate from feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.
The dharma-realm is form, and form is the dharma-realm;
the dharma-realm is feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, and feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are the dharma-realm.
“World-Honored One!
The dharma-realm is not the eye-base, yet it is not apart from the eye-base;
the dharma-realm is not the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-base, yet it is not apart from the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-base.”
The dharma-realm is the eye-base, and the eye-base is the dharma-realm;
the dharma-realm is the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-bases, and the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-bases are the dharma-realm.
“World-Honored One!
The dharma-realm is not the sense-base of form, yet it is not separate from the sense-base of form;
the dharma-realm is not the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena, yet it is not separate from the sense-bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena.”
The dharma-realm is the sphere of form, and the sphere of form is the dharma-realm;
the dharma-realm is the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, and the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are the dharma-realm.
“World-Honored One!
The dharma-realm is not the eye-element, yet it is not separate from the eye-element;
the dharma-realm is not the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-element, yet it is not separate from the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-element.”
The dharma-realm is the eye-realm, and the eye-realm is the dharma-realm;
the dharma-realm is the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-realm, and the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-realm is the dharma-realm.
“World-Honored One!
The dharma-realm is not the realm of form, yet it is not separate from the realm of form;
the dharma-realm is not the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, or mental phenomena, yet it is not separate from the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, or mental phenomena.”
The dharma-realm is the realm of form; the realm of form is the dharma-realm.
The dharma-realm is the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena; the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena are the dharma-realm.
“World-Honored One!
The dharma-realm is not the eye-consciousness realm, yet it is not separate from the eye-consciousness realm;
the dharma-realm is not the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-consciousness realms, yet it is not separate from the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-consciousness realms.”
The dharma-dhātu is the eye-consciousness-dhātu, and the eye-consciousness-dhātu is the dharma-dhātu;
the dharma-dhātu is the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness-dhātus, and the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness-dhātus are the dharma-dhātu.
“World-Honored One!
The dharma-realm is not eye-contact, yet it is not separate from eye-contact;
the dharma-realm is not ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact, yet it is not separate from ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact.”
The dharma-realm is eye-contact, and eye-contact is the dharma-realm;
the dharma-realm is ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact, and ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact is the dharma-realm.
“World-Honored One!
The dharma-realm is not the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, nor is it apart from the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition;

the dharma-realm is not the various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact as conditions, nor is it apart from the various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact as conditions.”
The dharma-realm is precisely the various sensations produced with eye-contact as condition; the various sensations produced with eye-contact as condition are precisely the dharma-realm.

The dharma-realm is precisely the various sensations produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions; the various sensations produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions are precisely the dharma-realm.
“World-Honored One!
The dharma-realm is not the earth-element, yet it is not separate from the earth-element;
the dharma-realm is not the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness-elements, yet it is not separate from the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness-elements.”
The dharma-realm is the earth-element, and the earth-element is the dharma-realm;
the dharma-realm is the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness-elements, and the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness-elements are the dharma-realm.
“World-Honored One!
The dharma-realm is not a causal condition, yet it is not apart from causal conditions;

the dharma-realm is not an equal-and-immediate condition, an object-condition, or a dominant condition, yet it is not apart from the equal-and-immediate condition, the object-condition, or the dominant condition.”
The dharma-realm is itself the causal condition, and the causal condition is itself the dharma-realm;

the dharma-realm is itself the equal-and-immediate condition, the object-condition, and the dominant condition, and the equal-and-immediate condition, the object-condition, and the dominant condition are themselves the dharma-realm.
“World-Honored One!
The dharma-realm is not produced from conditions by way of those dharmas that arise from conditions, nor is it separate from those dharmas that arise from conditions;
the dharma-realm is precisely those dharmas that arise from conditions, and those dharmas that arise from conditions are precisely the dharma-realm.”
“World-Honored One!
The dharma-realm is not ignorance, yet it is not separate from ignorance;

the dharma-realm is not volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, or old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, yet it is not separate from volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair.”
The dharma-realm is ignorance, and ignorance is the dharma-realm;

the dharma-realm is the formative forces up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, and these formative forces up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are the dharma-realm.
“Bhagavān, the dharmadhātu is not the perfection of generosity, yet it is not separate from the perfection of generosity;

the dharmadhātu is not the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom, yet it is not separate from the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom.”
The dharma-realm is itself the perfection of generosity, and the perfection of generosity is itself the dharma-realm;

the dharma-realm is itself the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, and the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are themselves the dharma-realm.
“World-Honored One!
The dharma-realm is not the four dhyānas, yet it is not apart from the four dhyānas;
the dharma-realm is not the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments, yet it is not apart from the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments.”
The dharma-realm is the four dhyānas, and the four dhyānas are the dharma-realm;
the dharma-realm is the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, and the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are the dharma-realm.
“World-Honored One!
The dharma-realm is not the four foundations of mindfulness, yet it is not separate from the four foundations of mindfulness;

the dharma-realm is not the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path, yet it is not separate from the four right efforts up to and including the eightfold noble path.”
The dharma-realm is the four foundations of mindfulness, and the four foundations of mindfulness are the dharma-realm;
the dharma-realm is the four right efforts up to the eight factors of the noble path, and the four right efforts up to the eight factors of the noble path are the dharma-realm.
“World-Honored One!
The dharma-realm is neither the liberation gate of emptiness, nor is it apart from the liberation gate of emptiness;
the dharma-realm is neither the liberation gates of signlessness or wishlessness, nor is it apart from the liberation gates of signlessness and wishlessness.”
The dharma-realm is itself the gate of liberation of emptiness, and the gate of liberation of emptiness is itself the dharma-realm;
the dharma-realm is itself the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, and the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are themselves the dharma-realm.
“Bhagavān, the dharma-realm is not internal emptiness, nor is it apart from internal emptiness; the dharma-realm is not external emptiness,

internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, nor is it apart from external emptiness up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.”
The dharma-realm is internal emptiness, and internal emptiness is the dharma-realm;
the dharma-realm is external emptiness up to the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature, and external emptiness up to the emptiness of non-existence of intrinsic nature is the dharma-realm.
“World-Honored One!
The dharma-realm is not the noble truth of suffering, yet it is not apart from the noble truth of suffering;
the dharma-realm is not the noble truths of origin, cessation, or the path, yet it is not apart from the noble truths of origin, cessation, or the path.”
The dharma-realm is itself the noble truth of suffering, and the noble truth of suffering is itself the dharma-realm;
the dharma-realm is itself the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, and the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are themselves the dharma-realm.
“World-Honored One!
The dharma-realm is not the eight liberations, yet it is not separate from the eight liberations;

the dharma-realm is not the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive concentrations, or the ten universal bases, yet it is not separate from the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive concentrations, or the ten universal bases.”
The dharma-realm is the eight liberations, and the eight liberations are the dharma-realm;

the dharma-realm is the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities, and the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities are the dharma-realm.
“World-Honored One!
The dharma-realm is not all the gates of dhāraṇī, yet it is not separate from all the gates of dhāraṇī;
the dharma-realm is not all the gates of samādhi, yet it is not separate from all the gates of samādhi.”
The dharma-realm is all the gates of dhāraṇī, and all the gates of dhāraṇī are the dharma-realm;
the dharma-realm is all the gates of samādhi, and all the gates of samādhi are the dharma-realm.
“World-Honored One!
The dharma-realm is not the Ground of Extreme Joy, nor is it apart from the Ground of Extreme Joy;

the dharma-realm is not the Ground of Freedom from Defilement, the Ground of Radiance, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Utmost Difficulty to Conquer, the Ground of Presence, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, or the Ground of the Dharma Cloud, nor is it apart from the Ground of Freedom from Defilement up to the Ground of the Dharma Cloud.”
The dharma-realm is the Ground of Utmost Joy, and the Ground of Utmost Joy is the dharma-realm;
the dharma-realm is the Ground of Freedom from Defilement up to the Ground of the Dharma-Cloud, and the Ground of Freedom from Defilement up to the Ground of the Dharma-Cloud is the dharma-realm.
“World-Honored One!
The dharma-realm is not the five eyes, yet it is not separate from the five eyes;
the dharma-realm is not the six supernormal powers, yet it is not separate from the six supernormal powers.”
The dharma-realm is the five eyes, and the five eyes are the dharma-realm;
the dharma-realm is the six supernormal powers, and the six supernormal powers are the dharma-realm.
"World-Honored One!
The dharma-realm is not the ten powers of a Buddha, yet it is not separate from the ten powers of a Buddha;

the dharma-realm is not the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, yet it is not separate from the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
The dharma-realm is the ten powers of the Buddha, and the ten powers of the Buddha are the dharma-realm;

the dharma-realm is the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are the dharma-realm.
“World-Honored One!
The dharma-realm is not great loving-kindness, yet it is not apart from great loving-kindness;
the dharma-realm is not great compassion, great joy, or great equanimity, yet it is not apart from great compassion, great joy, or great equanimity.”
The dharma-realm is great loving-kindness, and great loving-kindness is the dharma-realm;
the dharma-realm is great compassion, great joy, and great equanimity, and great compassion, great joy, and great equanimity are the dharma-realm.
“World-Honored One!
The dharma-realm is not the state of non-forgetfulness, nor is it separate from the state of non-forgetfulness;
the dharma-realm is not the state of constant equanimity, nor is it separate from the state of constant equanimity.”
The dharma-realm is itself the quality of non-forgetfulness, and the quality of non-forgetfulness is itself the dharma-realm;
the dharma-realm is itself the state of constant equanimity, and the state of constant equanimity is itself the dharma-realm.
“World-Honored One!
The dharma-realm is not omniscience, nor is it apart from omniscience;
the dharma-realm is not the knowledge of the paths or the knowledge of all aspects, nor is it apart from the knowledge of the paths or the knowledge of all aspects.”
The dharma-realm is omniscience, and omniscience is the dharma-realm;
the dharma-realm is the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects, and the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are the dharma-realm.
“World-Honored One!
The dharma-realm is not the thirty-two marks of a great man, nor is it separate from the thirty-two marks of a great man;
the dharma-realm is not the eighty secondary signs, nor is it separate from the eighty secondary signs.”
The dharma-realm is the thirty-two marks of a great man, and the thirty-two marks of a great man are the dharma-realm;
the dharma-realm is the eighty secondary signs, and the eighty secondary signs are the dharma-realm.
“World-Honored One!
The dharma-realm is not the fruit of stream-entry, nor is it apart from the fruit of stream-entry;

the dharma-realm is not the fruit of once-returning, non-returning, arhatship, or pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, nor is it apart from the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, arhatship, or pratyekabuddha-enlightenment.”
The dharma-realm is the fruit of stream-entry, and the fruit of stream-entry is the dharma-realm;

the dharma-realm is the fruit of once-returning, non-returning, arhatship, and pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, and the fruit of once-returning, non-returning, arhatship, and pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is the dharma-realm.
“World-Honored One!
The dharma-realm is not the practice of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, yet it is not apart from the practice of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas;
the dharma-realm is not the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas, yet it is not apart from the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas.”
The dharma-realm is itself all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are themselves the dharma-realm;
the dharma-realm is itself the unexcelled, perfect enlightenment of all buddhas, and the unexcelled, perfect enlightenment of all buddhas is itself the dharma-realm.
“World-Honored One!
The dharma-realm is not a mundane dharma, yet it is not separate from mundane dharmas;
the dharma-realm is not a supramundane dharma, yet it is not separate from supramundane dharmas.”
“The dharma-realm is itself mundane phenomena, and mundane phenomena are themselves the dharma-realm;
the dharma-realm is itself supramundane phenomena, and supramundane phenomena are themselves the dharma-realm.
“World-Honored One!”
The dharma-realm is not a contaminated dharma, yet it is not separate from contaminated dharmas;
the dharma-realm is not an uncontaminated dharma, yet it is not separate from uncontaminated dharmas.
The dharma-realm is itself contaminated dharmas, and contaminated dharmas are themselves the dharma-realm.
The dharma-realm is itself the untainted dharmas, and the untainted dharmas are themselves the dharma-realm.
"World-Honored One!
The dharma-realm is not a conditioned dharma, nor is it separate from conditioned dharmas;
The dharma-realm is not an unconditioned phenomenon, nor is it separate from unconditioned phenomena.
The dharma-realm is itself conditioned phenomena, and conditioned phenomena are themselves the dharma-realm;
the dharma-realm is itself unconditioned phenomena, and unconditioned phenomena are themselves the dharma-realm.
The Buddha told Subhūti: "So it is! So it is!"
"It is as you have said.
Within the true dharma-realm, there are no conceptual proliferations of any kind. Subhūti!..."
Form is not the dharma-realm, yet there is no dharma-realm apart from form;
feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are not the dharma-realm, yet there is no dharma-realm apart from feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.
Form is the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is form;
feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.
"Subhūti! The eye-base is not the dharma-realm, yet there is no dharma-realm apart from the eye-base;
the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases are not the dharma-realm, yet there is no dharma-realm apart from the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases."
The sense-base of the eye is the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is the sense-base of the eye;
the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.
“Subhūti! The sphere of form is not the dharma-realm, nor is there a dharma-realm existing apart from the sphere of form;

the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are not the dharma-realm, nor is there a dharma-realm existing apart from the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena.”
The sphere of form is the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is the sphere of form;
the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena.
"Subhūti! The eye-element is not the dharma-realm, nor is there a dharma-realm existing apart from the eye-element;
the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements are not the dharma-realm, nor is there a dharma-realm existing apart from the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements."
The eye-element is the dharma-element, and the dharma-element is the eye-element;
the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements are the dharma-element, and the dharma-element is the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements.
“Subhūti! The realm of form is not the dharma-realm, nor is there a dharma-realm that exists apart from the realm of form.

The realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are not the dharma-realm, nor is there a dharma-realm that exists apart from the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena.”
The realm of form is itself the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is itself the realm of form;
the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena are themselves the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is itself the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, and mental phenomena.
“Subhūti! The eye-consciousness element is not the dharma-element, yet there is no dharma-element apart from the eye-consciousness element;

the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements are not the dharma-element, yet there is no dharma-element apart from the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements.”
The eye-consciousness element is the dharma-element, and the dharma-element is the eye-consciousness element;
the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements are the dharma-element, and the dharma-element is the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements.
"Subhūti! Eye-contact is not the dharma-realm, nor is there a dharma-realm apart from eye-contact;
ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact are not the dharma-realm, nor is there a dharma-realm apart from ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact."
Eye-contact is the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is eye-contact;
ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact are the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact.

“Subhūti! The various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are not the dharma-realm, yet there is no dharma-realm apart from the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.

The various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions are not the dharma-realm, yet there is no dharma-realm apart from the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions.”
The various sensations produced with eye-contact as a condition are themselves the dharma-realm; the dharma-realm is itself the various sensations produced with eye-contact as a condition.

The various sensations produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions are themselves the dharma-realm; the dharma-realm is itself the various sensations produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions.
“Subhūti! The earth element is not the dharma-element, nor is there a dharma-element existing apart from the earth element;
the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are not the dharma-element, nor is there a dharma-element existing apart from the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements.”
The earth element is the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is the earth element;
the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements.
“Subhūti! Conditions are not the dharma-realm, yet the dharma-realm does not exist apart from conditions;

the immediately preceding condition, the object-condition, and the dominant condition are not the dharma-realm, yet the dharma-realm does not exist apart from the immediately preceding condition, the object-condition, and the dominant condition.”
Dependent origination is the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is dependent origination;

the immediately preceding condition, the object-condition, and the dominant condition are the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is the immediately preceding condition, the object-condition, and the dominant condition.
“Subhūti! The phenomena produced from conditions are not the dharma-realm, nor is there a dharma-realm existing apart from the phenomena produced from conditions;
the phenomena produced from conditions are themselves the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is itself the phenomena produced from conditions.”
"Subhūti! Ignorance is not the dharma-realm, nor is there a dharma-realm apart from ignorance.

Volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are not the dharma-realm, nor is there a dharma-realm apart from volitional formations up to old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair."
Ignorance is the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is ignorance;

the formative forces up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is the formative forces up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair.
“Subhūti! The perfection of generosity is not the dharma-realm, nor is there a dharma-realm apart from the perfection of generosity;

the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are not the dharma-realm, nor is there a dharma-realm apart from the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.”
The perfection of generosity is the dharmadhātu, and the dharmadhātu is the perfection of generosity;

the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are the dharmadhātu, and the dharmadhātu is the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
“Subhūti! The four dhyānas are not the dharmadhātu, yet there is no dharmadhātu apart from the four dhyānas;
the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are not the dharmadhātu, yet there is no dharmadhātu apart from the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions.”
The four dhyānas are the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is the four dhyānas;
the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions.
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 385. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter Sixty-nine, "The Equality of All Dharmas," Section Four. "Subhūti!
The four foundations of mindfulness are not the dharma-realm, yet there is no dharma-realm apart from the four foundations of mindfulness;

the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are not the dharma-realm, yet there is no dharma-realm apart from the four right efforts up to and including the eightfold noble path.
The four foundations of mindfulness are the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is the four foundations of mindfulness;
the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path are the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path.
“Subhūti! The gate of liberation of emptiness is not the dharma-realm, yet apart from the gate of liberation of emptiness there is no separate dharma-realm;
the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are not the dharma-realm, yet apart from the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness there is no separate dharma-realm.”
The gate of liberation of emptiness is the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is the gate of liberation of emptiness;
the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.
“Subhūti! Internal emptiness is not the dharma-realm, nor is there a dharma-realm existing apart from internal emptiness.

External emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, emptiness of all dharmas, unapprehendable emptiness, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, and emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are not the dharma-realm, nor is there a dharma-realm existing apart from external emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.”
Internal emptiness is the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is internal emptiness;

external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, is the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
“Subhūti! The noble truth of suffering is not the dharma-realm, nor is there a dharma-realm existing apart from the noble truth of suffering;
the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are not the dharma-realm, nor is there a dharma-realm existing apart from the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path.”
The noble truth of suffering is the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is the noble truth of suffering;
the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path.
“Subhūti! The eight liberations are not the dharma-realm, yet there is no dharma-realm apart from the eight liberations;

the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities are not the dharma-realm, yet there is no dharma-realm apart from the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities.”
The eight liberations are the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is the eight liberations;

the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities are the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities.
“Subhūti! All dhāraṇī-doors are not the dharma-realm, nor is there a dharma-realm existing apart from all dhāraṇī-doors;
all samādhi-doors are not the dharma-realm, nor is there a dharma-realm existing apart from all samādhi-doors.”
All dharanī-gates are the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is all dharanī-gates;
all samādhi-gates are the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is all samādhi-gates.
“Subhūti! The Ground of Extreme Joy is not the dharma-realm, yet there is no dharma-realm apart from the Ground of Extreme Joy.

The Ground of Purity, the Ground of Radiance, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Supreme Difficulty to Conquer, the Ground of Manifestation, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, and the Ground of the Dharma Cloud are not the dharma-realm, yet there is no dharma-realm apart from these grounds, from the Ground of Purity up to the Ground of the Dharma Cloud.”
The Ground of Utmost Joy is the Dharma-realm, and the Dharma-realm is the Ground of Utmost Joy;
from the Ground of Purity up to the Ground of the Dharma-Cloud is the Dharma-realm, and the Dharma-realm is from the Ground of Purity up to the Ground of the Dharma-Cloud.
“Subhūti! The five eyes are not the dharma-realm, yet there is no dharma-realm apart from the five eyes;
the six supernormal powers are not the dharma-realm, yet there is no dharma-realm apart from the six supernormal powers.”
The five eyes are the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is the five eyes;
the six supernormal powers are the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is the six supernormal powers.
"Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
The ten powers of a Buddha are not the dharma-realm, yet there is no dharma-realm apart from the ten powers of a Buddha;

the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are not the dharma-realm, yet there is no dharma-realm apart from the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
The ten powers of a Buddha are the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is the ten powers of a Buddha;

the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
“Subhūti! Great loving-kindness is not the dharmadhātu, yet apart from great loving-kindness there is no separate dharmadhātu;
great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity are not the dharmadhātu, yet apart from great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity there is no separate dharmadhātu.”
Great loving-kindness is the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is great loving-kindness;
great compassion, great joy, and great equanimity are the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is great compassion, great joy, and great equanimity.
“Subhūti! The quality of non-forgetfulness is not the dharma-realm, nor is there a dharma-realm existing apart from the quality of non-forgetfulness;
the state of constant equanimity is not the dharma-realm, nor is there a dharma-realm existing apart from the state of constant equanimity.”
The quality of non-forgetfulness is the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is the quality of non-forgetfulness;
the state of constant abiding in equanimity is the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is the state of constant abiding in equanimity.
“Subhūti! All-knowledge is not the dharma-realm, yet there is no dharma-realm apart from all-knowledge;

the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are not the dharma-realm, yet there is no dharma-realm apart from the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects.”
All-knowledge is the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is all-knowledge;
the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects.
“Subhūti! The thirty-two marks of a great man are not the dharma-realm, yet there is no dharma-realm apart from the thirty-two marks of a great man;
the eighty secondary signs are not the dharma-realm, yet there is no dharma-realm apart from the eighty secondary signs.”
The thirty-two marks of a great man are the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is the thirty-two marks of a great man;
the eighty secondary signs are the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is the eighty secondary signs.
“Subhūti! The fruit of stream-entry is not the dharma-realm, yet there is no dharma-realm apart from the fruit of stream-entry;

the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, arhatship, and pratyekabuddha enlightenment are not the dharma-realm, yet there is no dharma-realm apart from the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, arhatship, and pratyekabuddha enlightenment.”
The fruit of stream-entry is the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is the fruit of stream-entry;

the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, arhatship, and pratyekabuddha-enlightenment are the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is the fruit of once-returning, non-returning, arhatship, and pratyekabuddha-enlightenment.
“Subhūti! All the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are not the dharma-realm, yet there is no dharma-realm apart from all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas;

the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas is not the dharma-realm, yet there is no dharma-realm apart from the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas.”
The practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas;
the unexcelled, perfect enlightenment of all buddhas is the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is the unexcelled, perfect enlightenment of all buddhas.
"Subhūti! Mundane phenomena are not the dharma-realm, yet there is no dharma-realm apart from mundane phenomena;
supramundane phenomena are not the dharma-realm, yet there is no dharma-realm apart from supramundane phenomena."
"Mundane phenomena are the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is mundane phenomena;
supramundane phenomena are the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is supramundane phenomena. Subhūti!..."
Contaminated phenomena (*sāsravadharma*) are not the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), yet there is no dharma-realm apart from contaminated phenomena;
uncontaminated phenomena (*anāsravadharma*) are not the dharma-realm, yet there is no dharma-realm apart from uncontaminated phenomena.
"Defiled phenomena are the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is defiled phenomena;
undefiled phenomena are the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is undefiled phenomena. Subhūti!..."
Conditioned phenomena are not the dharma-realm, yet there is no dharma-realm apart from conditioned phenomena;
unconditioned phenomena are not the dharma-realm, yet there is no dharma-realm apart from unconditioned phenomena.
Conditioned phenomena are the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is conditioned phenomena;
unconditioned phenomena are the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is unconditioned phenomena. "Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, if they perceive any phenomenon as being separate from the dharma-realm, they are not correctly proceeding toward the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment they seek.
"Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they know that all phenomena do not depart from the dharma-realm. Subhūti!"

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they know that all phenomena are the dharma-realm. Through skillful means, they provisionally teach by means of names and signs—though phenomena are devoid of names and signs—for the sake of sentient beings, saying: "This is form; this is feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness;
this is the eye-base; these are the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases;
this is the form-base; these are the sound, odor, taste, tangible, and phenomena-bases."
This is the eye-element; this is the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-element.
This is the form-element; this is the sound-, odor-, taste-, tangible-, and mental-object-element.
This is the eye-consciousness-element; this is the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness-element.
"This is eye-contact; this is ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact.
This is the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition; these are the various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions.
This is the earth element; these are the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements."
This is the causal condition; this is the immediately preceding condition, the object condition, and the dominant condition;
these are the phenomena produced from conditions;

this is ignorance; and these are volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.
"This is a worldly dharma; this is a supramundane dharma;
this is a material dharma; this is an immaterial dharma;
this is a visible dharma; this is an invisible dharma."
"This is a contaminated dharma; this is an uncontaminated dharma.
This is a conditioned dharma; this is an unconditioned dharma.
This is the perfection of generosity; these are the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom."
These are the four dhyānas; these are the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments;

these are the four foundations of mindfulness; these are the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path;
these are the gate of liberation of emptiness, and these are the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.

This is internal emptiness; this is external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of self-nature, and the emptiness of the self-nature of non-existence.

This is suchness; this is the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-falsity, the non-alteration, the equality, the state beyond birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the reality-limit, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm.
This is the noble truth of suffering; these are the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path.
These are the eight liberations; these are the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases;
these are all the doors of dhāraṇī; these are all the doors of samādhi;

these are the Ground of Extreme Joy, the Ground of Purity, the Ground of Radiance, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Difficult Victory, the Ground of Presence, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, and the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma.
These are the five eyes; these are the six supernormal powers;
these are the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
these are great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity.
This is the quality of non-forgetfulness; this is the nature of constant equanimity;
this is all-knowledge; this is the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects;
these are the thirty-two marks of a great man; these are the eighty secondary signs.
"This is the fruit of stream-entry; this is the fruit of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship; this is the awakening of a pratyekabuddha;
this is the practice of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; and this is the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening of all buddhas."
“Subhūti! It is like a skilled illusionist or his apprentice who, holding a small object before a crowd, conjures various kinds of diverse forms and appearances through illusion.”
That is to say, they may manifest through illusion various men and women, large and small, as well as elephants, horses, oxen, sheep, camels, donkeys, chickens, and other diverse birds and beasts;
or they may further manifest through illusion cities, towns, villages, gardens, groves, ponds, and pools, all exquisitely adorned and most delightful;
or they may further manifest through illusion clothing, food and drink, houses, bedding, incense, flowers, necklaces, and various kinds of precious jewels.
Or again, they may magically create immeasurable varieties of music, performers, and entertainers to cause countless people to rejoice and enjoy themselves;

or they may magically manifest various forms to cause them to practice giving, or to observe the precepts, or to cultivate patience, or to exert diligence, or to cultivate meditative concentration, or to cultivate wisdom;
or they may manifest birth into great kṣatriya clans, or manifest birth into great brahmin clans, or manifest birth into great householder clans, or manifest birth into great merchant clans.
Or again, they may magically create various mountains, great oceans, Sumeru, the king of mountains, and the Cakravāḍa mountain ranges;
or they may manifest birth among the gods of the Four Great Kings, the Heaven of the Thirty-three, the Yāma heaven, the Tuṣita heaven, the Nirmāṇarati heaven, and the Paranirmita-vaśavartin heaven;
or they may manifest birth among the Brahmakāyika, Brahmapurohita, Brahmakāyika-parṣad, and Mahābrahmā heavens.
Or again, they manifest birth in the Heaven of Light, the Heaven of Limited Light, the Heaven of Immeasurable Light, and the Heaven of Utmost Purity of Light;
or again, they manifest birth in the Heaven of Purity, the Heaven of Limited Purity, the Heaven of Immeasurable Purity, and the Heaven of Universal Purity;
or again, they manifest birth in the Vast Heaven, the Heaven of Limited Vastness, the Heaven of Immeasurable Vastness, and the Heaven of Vast Results.
Or again, they manifest birth in the Heaven of No-Thought;
or they are born in the Heaven of No-Strife, the Heaven of No-Heat, the Heaven of Excellent Appearance, the Heaven of Good Vision, or the Heaven of Ultimate Form;
or again, they manifest birth in the Heaven of Infinite Space, the Heaven of Infinite Consciousness, the Heaven of Nothingness, or the Heaven of Neither Perception nor Non-Perception.
Or again, they manifest as stream-enterers, once-returners, non-returners, arhats, or pratyekabuddhas; or again,
they manifest as bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, practicing from the first generation of the mind of awakening the pāramitās of generosity,
ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
The four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments;

the cultivation of the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path;
the cultivation of the gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; and training in abiding in internal emptiness.
...external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness,
conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness,
essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, and non-...
One may attain the emptiness of obtainability, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence;
one studies and dwells in suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, equality,
the nature of transcendence from birth, the fixedness of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, and the realm of empty space.
Within the inconceivable realm, they train in and abide by the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path;
they enter the bodhisattva’s state of rightness and departure from birth, and practice the stages of the Joyous,
the Stainless, the Luminous, the Radiant, the Difficult to Conquer, the Manifest, the Far-Reaching, and the Immovable.

The Stage of Excellent Intelligence and the Stage of the Cloud of Dharma; they sport in the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases; they sport in all doors of dhāraṇī and all doors of samādhi;
they manifest various extraordinary supernormal powers and radiate great light that illuminates all worlds.
They purify Buddha-fields and mature sentient beings, practicing the various merits of all Buddhas; or else they manifest as Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas,

endowed with the thirty-two marks of a Great Man and fully adorned with the eighty secondary signs, having accomplished the ten powers, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, and great equanimity, the quality of non-forgetfulness, the nature of constant dwelling in equanimity, omniscience, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects— immeasurable, boundless, inconceivable, and rare qualities.

"Subhūti! Thus, a magician or his apprentice, in order to delude others, performs these various magical illusions before a great multitude. When the ignorant men and women, both young and old, see these things, they all exclaim in wonder:
'How marvelous! "

This person was skilled in all arts and capable of performing various most rare feats, even to the extent of manifesting the body of a Tathāgata, adorned with the primary and secondary marks and endowed with all merits, thereby bringing joy to the multitude and displaying his own artistic talents.
Among them, one who possessed wisdom and insight, having perceived this matter, reflected thus:
"How truly extraordinary!

How can this person manifest such a thing? There is no real substance to be found herein, yet he causes the multitude to be deluded and delighted, giving rise to the perception of a real object where no real object exists."
“Subhūti! It is the same for a bodhisattva mahāsattva.

When practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), although they do not perceive any phenomenon that exists apart from the true dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), nor do they perceive the dharma-realm as existing apart from all phenomena; and although they do not perceive sentient beings or the substantial entities designated as such, they are nonetheless able, through various skillful means, to personally practice the perfection of generosity (dānapāramitā), to encourage others to practice the perfection of generosity, to unerringly praise the method of practicing the perfection of generosity, and to joyfully extol those who practice the perfection of generosity.”

They personally practice the perfection of ethical discipline and also encourage others to practice the perfection of ethical discipline; they correctly extol the method of practicing the perfection of ethical discipline and joyfully praise those who practice the perfection of ethical discipline.

They personally practice the perfection of patience and also encourage others to practice the perfection of patience; they correctly extol the method of practicing the perfection of patience and joyfully praise those who practice the perfection of patience.

They personally practice the perfection of diligence and also encourage others to practice the perfection of diligence; they correctly extol the method of practicing the perfection of diligence and joyfully praise those who practice the perfection of diligence.

They personally practice the perfection of meditative concentration (*dhyāna-pāramitā*), and also encourage others to practice the perfection of meditative concentration; they correctly praise the method of practicing the perfection of meditative concentration and joyfully extol those who practice it.

They personally practice the perfection of wisdom (*prajñā-pāramitā*), and also encourage others to practice the perfection of wisdom; they correctly praise the method of practicing the perfection of wisdom and joyfully extol those who practice it.

They personally uphold the ten paths of wholesome action (*daśa-kuśala-karmapatha*), and also encourage others to uphold the ten paths of wholesome action; they correctly praise the method of upholding the ten paths of wholesome action and joyfully extol those who uphold them.

They personally uphold the five precepts and also encourage others to uphold the five precepts; they unerringly praise the dharma of upholding the five precepts and joyfully extol those who uphold them.

They personally uphold the eight precepts and also encourage others to uphold the eight precepts; they unerringly praise the dharma of upholding the eight precepts and joyfully extol those who uphold them.

They personally uphold the monastic precepts and also encourage others to uphold the monastic precepts; they unerringly praise the dharma of upholding the monastic precepts and joyfully extol those who uphold them.

They personally cultivate the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments, and also encourage others to cultivate the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments; they unerringly praise the practice of the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments, and joyfully extol those who cultivate the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.

They personally cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path, and also encourage others to cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path; they unerringly praise the practice of the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path, and joyfully extol those who cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path.

They personally cultivate the gates of liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; they also exhort others to cultivate the gates of liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; they unerringly praise the dharma of cultivating the gates of liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; and they joyfully extol those who cultivate the gates of liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness.

They themselves abide in internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of essential nature, the emptiness of self-characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence; they also encourage others to abide in internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence; they unerringly extol the dharma of abiding in internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence; and they joyfully praise those who abide in internal emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.

They themselves abide in suchness, the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm; they also encourage others to abide in suchness up to the inconceivable realm, unerringly extol the teachings on abiding in suchness up to the inconceivable realm, and joyfully praise those who abide in suchness up to the inconceivable realm.

They themselves abide in the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path; they also encourage others to abide in the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path, unerringly extol the teachings on abiding in the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path, and joyfully praise those who abide in the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path.

They personally cultivate the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities, and they also exhort others to cultivate the eight liberations up to the ten totalities; they unerringly extol the dharmas of cultivating the eight liberations up to the ten totalities, and they joyfully praise those who cultivate the eight liberations up to the ten totalities.

They personally cultivate all doors of dhāraṇī and all doors of samādhi, and they also exhort others to cultivate all doors of dhāraṇī and all doors of samādhi; they unerringly extol the dharmas of cultivating all doors of dhāraṇī and all doors of samādhi, and they joyfully praise those who cultivate all doors of dhāraṇī and all doors of samādhi.

They personally cultivate the ten stages of a bodhisattva and also encourage others to cultivate the ten stages of a bodhisattva; they unerringly extol the dharma of cultivating the ten stages of a bodhisattva and joyfully praise those who cultivate the ten stages of a bodhisattva.

They personally cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers and also encourage others to cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers; they unerringly extol the dharma of cultivating the five eyes and the six supernormal powers and joyfully praise those who cultivate the five eyes and the six supernormal powers.

They personally cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; they also encourage others to cultivate these from the ten powers up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; they unerringly praise the Dharma of cultivating these from the ten powers up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; and they rejoice in and extol those who cultivate these from the ten powers up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.

They themselves fulfill the thirty-two marks of a great man and the eighty secondary signs, and they also encourage others to fulfill the thirty-two marks of a great man and the eighty secondary signs; they unerringly praise the dharma of fulfilling the thirty-two marks of a great man and the eighty secondary signs, and they joyfully extol those who fulfill the thirty-two marks of a great man and the eighty secondary signs.

They themselves cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity, and they also encourage others to cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity; they unerringly praise the dharma of cultivating the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity, and they joyfully extol those who cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity.

They personally cultivate all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*); they also encourage others to cultivate all-knowledge, knowledge of the paths, and knowledge of all aspects; they unerringly extol the practice of all-knowledge, knowledge of the paths, and knowledge of all aspects; and they joyfully praise those who cultivate all-knowledge, knowledge of the paths, and knowledge of all aspects.

“Subhūti! If the true dharma-realm were subject to distinctions between its initial, middle, and final stages, then bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, would not be able to skillfully employ expedient means to explain the true dharma-realm, to bring sentient beings to maturity, to adorn and purify buddha-fields, to cultivate the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and to realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”

Because the true dharma-realm is eternally without distinction across its initial, middle, and final stages, when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), they are able, through skillful means (*upāyakauśalya*), to expound the true dharma-realm, thereby maturing sentient beings, purifying buddha-fields, cultivating the various practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and realizing unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*).
Chapter 70: The Inconceivable (Acintya), Part One: The First Subdivision of the Inconceivable, Chapter Seventy. At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
If all sentient beings and even the designation of "sentient being" are ultimately unfindable, for whose sake do the bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom?
The Buddha told Subhūti: “Subhūti,
it is because they take the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) as their measure that bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom.”

If the limit of sentient beings were different from the limit of reality, then the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas would not practice the perfection of wisdom; because the limit of sentient beings is not different from the limit of reality, the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of all sentient beings.
Furthermore, Subhūti,
when bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they establish sentient beings within the reality-limit (bhūtakoṭi) by means of the non-disruption of the reality-limit.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
