they also cause them to be liberated from the notion of the four dhyānas regarding that which are not the four dhyānas, and from the notions of the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, regarding that which are not the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments;

they also cause them to be liberated from the notion of the eight liberations regarding that which are not the eight liberations, and from the notions of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities regarding that which are not the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities.

They also cause them to be liberated from the absence of the gateways of dhāraṇī and the conceptualization of "gateways of dhāraṇī," and from the absence of the gateways of samādhi and the conceptualization of "gateways of samādhi.

They also cause them to be liberated from the absence of the gateway of emptiness and the conceptualization of "gateway of emptiness," and from the absence of the gateways of signlessness and wishlessness and the conceptualization of "gateways of signlessness and wishlessness.

They also cause them to be liberated from the absence of the Ground of Great Joy and the conceptualization of "Ground of Great Joy," and from the absence of the Ground of Purity, the Ground of Radiance, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Difficult Victory, the Ground of Presence, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Good Intelligence, and the Ground of Dharma Clouds—ranging from the Ground of Purity up to the Ground of Dharma Clouds—and the conceptualization thereof.
They also cause them to be liberated from the absence of the five eyes and the notion of the five eyes; from the absence of the six supernormal powers and the notion of the six supernormal powers.

They also cause them to be liberated from the absence of the Buddha’s ten powers and the notion of the Buddha’s ten powers; from the absence of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha—and from the notions of these, from the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.

They also cause them to be liberated from the absence of the quality of non-forgetfulness and the notion of the quality of non-forgetfulness; from the absence of the nature of constant abiding in equanimity and the notion of the nature of constant abiding in equanimity.

They also cause them to be liberated from the absence of all-knowledge and the notion of all-knowledge; from the absence of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects, and the notions of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects;

they also cause them to be liberated from the absence of the fruit of stream-entry and the notion of the fruit of stream-entry; from the absence of the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, arhatship, and pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, and the notions of once-returner, non-returner, arhatship, and pratyekabuddha-enlightenment;

they also cause them to be liberated from the absence of all bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices and the notion of all bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices; and from the absence of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas and the notion of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas.

He also causes them to be liberated from the notion of formless and non-form dharmas as being form or non-form; he causes them to be liberated from the notions of seeing and non-seeing, resistance and non-resistance, outflows and no-outflows, and conditioned and unconditioned dharmas, including all such notions from seeing and non-seeing up to conditioned and unconditioned dharmas.

He also causes them to be liberated from the notion of the thirty-two marks of a Great Man as being the thirty-two marks of a Great Man, and from the notion of the eighty secondary signs as being the eighty secondary signs.

He also causes them to be liberated from the five aggregates of clinging and other such outflowing dharmas, and he causes them to be liberated from the four foundations of mindfulness and other such non-outflowing dharmas.
Why is this? Subhūti!

The various untainted dharmas, such as the four foundations of mindfulness, are likewise not—as they are in the ultimate truth—unborn and unceasing, signless, unconditioned, beyond conceptual proliferation, and non-discriminative; nor would they need to be liberated. The ultimate truth is intrinsic emptiness (*prakṛti-śūnyatā*), and this intrinsic emptiness is precisely the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment realized by all Buddhas.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll Three Hundred and Eighty-Seven. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter Seventy, "The Immovable," Section Three. "Subhūti, you should know this!

Within this, no self can be found, nor can a sentient being, a life-principle, a living being, a nourisher, a person, an individual, a mind-born, a youth, an agent, an instigator of action, an originator, an instigator of origination, an experiencer, an instigator of experience, a knower, or a seer be found;
no form can be found, nor can feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness be found;
no eye-base can be found, nor can the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind be found.
The sphere of formlessness cannot be apprehended, nor can the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental objects;
the eye-element cannot be apprehended, nor can the elements of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind;
the form-element cannot be apprehended, nor can the elements of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental objects.
The eye-consciousness element is not to be found, nor are the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-consciousness elements to be found;
the eye-contact is not to be found, nor are the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contacts to be found;
the various sensations produced with eye-contact as condition are not to be found, nor are the various sensations produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as conditions to be found.
The earth element cannot be apprehended, nor can the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements be apprehended;
no causes and conditions can be apprehended, nor can the immediately preceding condition, the object-condition, or the dominant condition be apprehended;
and no phenomena produced from conditions can be apprehended.

Ignorance cannot be apprehended, nor can volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, existence, birth, or old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair be apprehended;
the perfection of generosity cannot be apprehended, nor can the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom be apprehended.

There is no internal emptiness to be apprehended, nor can external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, all-dharmas emptiness, non-apprehensibility emptiness, non-existence emptiness, self-nature emptiness, or the non-existence-of-self-nature emptiness be apprehended;

there is no four applications of mindfulness to be apprehended, nor can the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path be apprehended;
there is no noble truth of suffering to be apprehended, nor can the noble truths of origin, cessation, or the path be apprehended.
The four dhyānas are not to be found, nor are the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments to be found;
the eight liberations are not to be found, nor are the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities to be found;
all dhāraṇī-doors are not to be found, nor are all samādhi-doors to be found.
The liberation door of emptiness cannot be apprehended, nor can the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness;

the Ground of Extreme Joy cannot be apprehended, nor can the Ground of Purity, the Ground of Radiance, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Difficult Victory, the Ground of Presence, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Good Intelligence, or the Ground of Dharma Clouds;
the five eyes cannot be apprehended, nor can the six supernormal powers.

The ten powers of a Buddha cannot be apprehended, nor can the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha be apprehended;
the quality of non-forgetfulness cannot be apprehended, nor can the nature of constant dwelling in equanimity be apprehended;
omniscience cannot be apprehended, nor can the knowledge of the aspects of the path or the knowledge of all aspects be apprehended.
There is no fruit of stream-entry to be attained, nor are the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, or arhatship, or the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha to be attained;
there is no bodhisattva-mahāsattva practice to be attained, nor is the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas to be attained;

there are no phenomena that are form or non-form to be attained, nor are any phenomena with visibility or invisibility, with resistance or non-resistance, with outflows or without outflows, or conditioned or unconditioned to be attained.
The thirty-two marks of a great man cannot be apprehended, nor can the eighty secondary signs be apprehended. "Subhūti!

Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do not seek to attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment for the sake of a path to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; rather, they seek to attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment solely for the sake of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of all phenomena."
“Subhūti! This intrinsic nature is empty of its own nature in the past, future, and present limits; it has never not been empty.

Abiding in the perfection of the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the knowledge of the aspects of the path for the sake of liberating all sentient beings from their attachment to the notion of a sentient being and the notion of phenomena.”

When this bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices the knowledge of the aspects of the path, they practice all paths—namely, the path of the śrāvaka, the path of the pratyekabuddha, the path of the bodhisattva, and the path of the Tathāgata.

“Subhūti! Once this bodhisattva mahāsattva has attained perfection in all paths, he is then able to bring the sentient beings to be converted to maturity, and is also able to purify the Buddha-field he seeks; he maintains his life-force in order to proceed toward the realization of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”
Having realized unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, one is able to ensure that the Buddha-eye is forever uninterrupted and indestructible.
What is called the Buddha-eye?
It is intrinsic emptiness that is named the Buddha-eye.
"Subhūti! All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past have all taken the emptiness of intrinsic nature as their Buddha-eye;
all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the future will all take the emptiness of intrinsic nature as their Buddha-eye."
All the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas currently residing in the infinite worlds of the ten directions all take the emptiness of intrinsic nature as their Buddha-eye.

"Subhūti! There is certainly no Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha who appears in the world apart from the emptiness of intrinsic nature. Among all Buddhas appearing in the world, there are none who do not expound the meaning of the emptiness of intrinsic nature. Sentient beings to be converted must hear the Buddha’s teaching on the principle of the emptiness of intrinsic nature before they can enter the Noble Path and realize the fruits of the Noble Path; apart from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, there is no other expedient means."

"Therefore, Subhūti, bodhisattva mahāsattvas who wish to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment should correctly abide in the principle of the emptiness of intrinsic nature and practice the perfection of wisdom and the other practices of bodhisattva mahāsattvas."

If one correctly abides in the principle of the emptiness of intrinsic nature and practices the perfection of wisdom and other bodhisattva-mahāsattva deeds, one will never fall away from the knowledge of all modes.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

It is truly rare for bodhisattva-mahāsattvas to practice all dharmas while they are all empty by their very nature, yet never to lose or impair that emptiness of intrinsic nature—meaning they do not grasp at form as being different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, nor do they grasp at feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness as being different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature.”

One does not grasp that the sense base of the eye is other than its own-nature emptiness, nor does one grasp that the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are other than their own-nature emptiness;

one does not grasp that the sense base of forms is other than its own-nature emptiness, nor does one grasp that the sense bases of sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, and mental phenomena are other than their own-nature emptiness;

one does not grasp that the eye element is other than its own-nature emptiness, nor does one grasp that the elements of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are other than their own-nature emptiness.

One does not grasp that the form realm is other than the emptiness of its own intrinsic nature, nor does one grasp that the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are other than the emptiness of their own intrinsic nature;

one does not grasp that the eye-consciousness realm is other than the emptiness of its own intrinsic nature, nor does one grasp that the realms of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness are other than the emptiness of their own intrinsic nature;

one does not grasp that eye-contact is other than the emptiness of its own intrinsic nature, nor does one grasp that ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact are other than the emptiness of their own intrinsic nature.

One does not grasp that the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition are other than emptiness of their own nature, nor does one grasp that the various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact as condition are other than emptiness of their own nature;

one does not grasp that the earth element is other than emptiness of its own nature, nor does one grasp that the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements are other than emptiness of their own nature;

one does not grasp that the causal condition is other than emptiness of its own nature, nor does one grasp that the immediately preceding condition, the object-condition, or the dominant condition are other than emptiness of their own nature.
One does not grasp that the phenomena arising from conditions are other than their own-being emptiness;

one does not grasp that ignorance is other than its own-being emptiness, nor does one grasp that volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, or old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are other than their own-being emptiness;

one does not grasp that the perfection of generosity is other than its own-being emptiness, nor does one grasp that the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are other than their own-being emptiness.

One does not grasp internal emptiness as being distinct from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, nor does one grasp external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, emptiness of specific characteristics, emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature as being distinct from the emptiness of intrinsic nature;

one does not grasp the four foundations of mindfulness as being distinct from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, nor does one grasp the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path as being distinct from the emptiness of intrinsic nature.

One does not grasp the Noble Truth of Suffering as being other than intrinsic emptiness, nor does one grasp the Noble Truths of Origination, Cessation, and the Path as being other than intrinsic emptiness;
one does not grasp the four dhyānas as being other than intrinsic emptiness, nor does one grasp the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments as being other than intrinsic emptiness;

one does not grasp the eight liberations as being other than intrinsic emptiness, nor does one grasp the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities as being other than intrinsic emptiness.
One does not grasp at all *dhāraṇī* gates as being other than emptiness of intrinsic nature, nor does one grasp at all *samādhi* gates as being other than emptiness of intrinsic nature;

one does not grasp at the gate of liberation of emptiness as being other than emptiness of intrinsic nature, nor does one grasp at the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness as being other than emptiness of intrinsic nature;

one does not grasp at the Ground of Extreme Joy as being other than emptiness of intrinsic nature, nor does one grasp at the Ground of Purity, the Ground of Radiance, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Difficult to Conquer, the Ground of Presence, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Good Intelligence, or the Ground of Dharma Clouds as being other than emptiness of intrinsic nature.
One does not grasp at the five eyes as being other than the emptiness of their own nature, nor does one grasp at the six supernormal powers as being other than the emptiness of their own nature;

one does not grasp at the ten powers of a Buddha as being other than the emptiness of their own nature, nor does one grasp at the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha as being other than the emptiness of their own nature;

one does not grasp at the thirty-two marks of a Great Man as being other than the emptiness of their own nature, nor does one grasp at the eighty minor marks as being other than the emptiness of their own nature.

One does not grasp the quality of non-forgetfulness as being different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, nor does one grasp the state of constant equanimity as being different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature;

one does not grasp all-knowledge as being different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, nor does one grasp the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects as being different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature;

one does not grasp the fruit of stream-entry as being different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, nor does one grasp the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, arhatship, or the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha as being different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature.

One does not grasp at the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas as being different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, nor does one grasp at the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas as being different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature.
“World-Honored One!
Form is itself the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself form.

Feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.”
The sense base of the eye is itself intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is itself the sense base of the eye;
the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are themselves intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is itself the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.
The sphere of form is itself intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is itself the sphere of form;

the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are themselves intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is itself the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena.
The eye-element is itself intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is itself the eye-element;
the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements are themselves intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is itself the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements.
The realm of form is itself the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the realm of form.

The realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena.
The eye-consciousness element is itself the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the eye-consciousness element.

The ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements.
Eye-contact is itself intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is itself eye-contact;
ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact are themselves intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is itself ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact.
The various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are themselves intrinsic emptiness; intrinsic emptiness is itself the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition.

The various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions are themselves intrinsic emptiness; intrinsic emptiness is itself the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions.
The earth element is itself the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the earth element;

the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements.
Dependent origination is itself the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself dependent origination;

the immediately preceding condition, the object-condition, and the dominant condition are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the immediately preceding condition, the object-condition, and the dominant condition.
All phenomena produced from conditions are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself all phenomena produced from conditions.
Ignorance is itself the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself ignorance.

Volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself volitional formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.
The perfection of generosity is intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is the perfection of generosity;

the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
Inner emptiness is itself the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself inner emptiness.

Outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of self-characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself outer emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
The four foundations of mindfulness are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the four foundations of mindfulness;

the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the four right efforts up to and including the eightfold noble path.
The noble truth of suffering is itself the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the noble truth of suffering;

the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path.
The four dhyānas are themselves intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is itself the four dhyānas;
the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are themselves intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is itself the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments.
The eight liberations are themselves intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is itself the eight liberations;

the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities are themselves intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is itself the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities.
All dharani-gates are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself all dharani-gates;
all samadhi-gates are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself all samadhi-gates.
The gate of liberation of emptiness is itself intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is itself the gate of liberation of emptiness;
the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are themselves intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is itself the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.
The Ground of Utmost Joy is itself intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is itself the Ground of Utmost Joy;

the Ground of Purity, the Ground of Radiance, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Supreme Difficulty to Conquer, the Ground of Presence, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, and the Ground of the Dharma Cloud are themselves intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is itself the Ground of Purity through to the Ground of the Dharma Cloud.
The five eyes are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the five eyes;
the six supernormal powers are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the six supernormal powers.
The ten powers of a Buddha are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the ten powers of a Buddha.

The four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the four fearlessnesses up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
The thirty-two marks of a great man are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the thirty-two marks of a great man.
The eighty secondary characteristics are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the eighty secondary characteristics.
The quality of non-forgetfulness is itself the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the quality of non-forgetfulness.
The state of constant abiding in equanimity is itself the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the state of constant abiding in equanimity.
All-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) is itself the emptiness of intrinsic nature (*prakṛti-śūnyatā*), and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself all-knowledge;

the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects.
The fruit of stream-entry is itself intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is itself the fruit of stream-entry;

the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, arhatship, and pratyekabuddha enlightenment are themselves intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is itself the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, arhatship, and pratyekabuddha enlightenment.
All the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.

The unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas is itself the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas.
The Buddha told Subhūti: “So it is! So it is!”
It is as you have said.
These bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are truly rare and marvelous; although they practice all dharmas, which are all empty by their very nature, they never lose or impair that emptiness of intrinsic nature.

“Subhūti! Form is not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from form. Form itself is the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature itself is form.

Feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness. Feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness themselves are the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature itself is feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.”

"Subhūti! The eye-base is not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from the eye-base. The eye-base is itself the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the eye-base.

The ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases are not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases. The ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases."

“Subhūti! The sphere of form is not different from intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is not different from the sphere of form; the sphere of form is itself intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is itself the sphere of form.

The spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are not different from intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is not different from the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena; the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are themselves intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is itself the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena.”

“Subhūti! The eye-element is not different from intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is not different from the eye-element; the eye-element is itself intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is itself the eye-element.

The ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements are not different from intrinsic emptiness; intrinsic emptiness is not different from the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements. The various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions are themselves intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is itself the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions.”

“Subhūti! The earth element is not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from the earth element. The earth element is itself the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the earth element.

The water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements. The water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements.”

“Subhūti! Conditions are not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from conditions. Conditions are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself conditions.

The immediately preceding condition, the object-condition, and the dominant condition are not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from the immediately preceding condition, the object-condition, and the dominant condition. The immediately preceding condition, the object-condition, and the dominant condition are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the immediately preceding condition, the object-condition, and the dominant condition.”

“Subhūti! All phenomena produced from conditions are not different from the emptiness of their intrinsic nature; the emptiness of their intrinsic nature is not different from all phenomena produced from conditions. All phenomena produced from conditions are themselves the emptiness of their intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of their intrinsic nature is itself all phenomena produced from conditions.”

“Subhūti! Ignorance is not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from ignorance. Ignorance is itself the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself ignorance.

Formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, existence, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair. Formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, existence, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself formations through to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.”

"Subhūti! The perfection of generosity is not different from intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is not different from the perfection of generosity; the perfection of generosity is itself intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is itself the perfection of generosity.

The perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are not different from intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is not different from the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are themselves intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is itself the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom."

“Subhūti! Inner emptiness is not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from inner emptiness. Inner emptiness is itself the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself inner emptiness.
This is also true for outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate, and the emptiness of conditioned phenomena.”

...the emptiness of the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of the ultimate (*atyanta-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of the limitless (*anavara-agra-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of dispersion (*anavakāra-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of non-alteration (*ananyathā-śūnyatā*),

the emptiness of specific characteristics (*svalakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of common characteristics (*sāmānya-lakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of all phenomena (*sarvadharma-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of the unapprehendable (*anupalambha-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of non-existence (*abhāva-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of intrinsic nature (*svabhāva-śūnyatā*),
and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence (*abhāvasvabhāva-śūnyatā*) are not different from the emptiness of original nature (*prakṛti-śūnyatā*); [they are] the original nature.
Emptiness is not different from external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the nature of non-existence; [it is] external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness,
the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness,
dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, the emptiness of self-characteristics, and the emptiness of common characteristics.
Emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature,

and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are themselves the emptiness of essential nature; the emptiness of essential nature is itself the emptiness of the external, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.

"Subhūti! The four foundations of mindfulness are not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from the four foundations of mindfulness. The four foundations of mindfulness are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the four foundations of mindfulness.

The four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path. The four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path."

"Subhūti! The noble truth of suffering is not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from the noble truth of suffering. The noble truth of suffering is itself the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the noble truth of suffering.

The noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path. The noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path."

“Subhūti! The four dhyānas are not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from the four dhyānas; the four dhyānas are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the four dhyānas.

The four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions; the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions.”

“Subhūti! The eight liberations are not different from intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is not different from the eight liberations; the eight liberations are themselves intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is itself the eight liberations.

The eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities are not different from intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is not different from the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities; the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities are themselves intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is itself the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities.”

“Subhūti! The gateways of dhāraṇī are not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from the gateways of dhāraṇī. The gateways of dhāraṇī are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the gateways of dhāraṇī.

The gateways of samādhi are not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from the gateways of samādhi. The gateways of samādhi are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the gateways of samādhi.”

"Subhūti! The gate of liberation of emptiness is not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from the gate of liberation of emptiness. The gate of liberation of emptiness is itself the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the gate of liberation of emptiness.

The gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness. The gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness."

“Subhūti! The Ground of Supreme Joy is not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from the Ground of Supreme Joy. The Ground of Supreme Joy is itself the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the Ground of Supreme Joy.

The Stainless Ground, the Radiant Ground, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Ultimate Difficulty to Conquer, the Ground of Manifestation, the Ground of Far-Going, the Immovable Ground, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, and the Ground of the Dharma Cloud are not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from the Stainless Ground up to the Ground of the Dharma Cloud. The Stainless Ground, the Radiant Ground, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Ultimate Difficulty to Conquer, the Ground of Manifestation, the Ground of Far-Going, the Immovable Ground, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, and the Ground of the Dharma Cloud are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the Stainless Ground up to the Ground of the Dharma Cloud.

“Subhūti! The five eyes are not different from intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is not different from the five eyes; the five eyes are themselves intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is itself the five eyes.

The six supernormal powers are not different from intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is not different from the six supernormal powers; the six supernormal powers are themselves intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is itself the six supernormal powers.”

“Subhūti! The ten powers of a Buddha are not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from the ten powers of a Buddha. The ten powers of a Buddha are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the ten powers of a Buddha.

The four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha. The four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.”

“Subhūti! The thirty-two marks of a great man are not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from the thirty-two marks of a great man. The thirty-two marks of a great man are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the thirty-two marks of a great man.

The eighty secondary signs are not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from the eighty secondary signs. The eighty secondary signs are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the eighty secondary signs.”

“Subhūti! The quality of non-forgetfulness is not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from the quality of non-forgetfulness. The quality of non-forgetfulness is itself the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the quality of non-forgetfulness.

The state of constant abiding in equanimity is not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from the state of constant abiding in equanimity. The state of constant abiding in equanimity is itself the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the state of constant abiding in equanimity.”

“Subhūti! All-knowledge (sarvajñatā) is not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature (prakṛti-śūnyatā), and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from all-knowledge; all-knowledge is itself the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself all-knowledge.

The knowledge of the paths (mārgākārajñatā) and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā) are not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects; the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects.”

“Subhūti! The fruit of stream-entry is not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from the fruit of stream-entry. The fruit of stream-entry is itself the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the fruit of stream-entry.

The fruits of once-returning, non-returning, arhatship, and pratyekabuddha enlightenment are not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, arhatship, and pratyekabuddha enlightenment. The fruits of once-returning, non-returning, arhatship, and pratyekabuddha enlightenment are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, arhatship, and pratyekabuddha enlightenment.”

“Subhūti! All the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. All the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.

The unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas is not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas. The unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas is itself the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas.”

"Furthermore, Subhūti! If form were different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or if the emptiness of intrinsic nature were different from form; if form were not the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or if the emptiness of intrinsic nature were not form;

and if feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness were different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or if the emptiness of intrinsic nature were different from feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness; if feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness were not the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or if the emptiness of intrinsic nature were not feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness."

"Subhūti! If the eye-base were different from intrinsic emptiness, or if intrinsic emptiness were different from the eye-base—such that the eye-base were not intrinsic emptiness and intrinsic emptiness were not the eye-base;

and if the ear-base, nose-base, tongue-base, body-base, and mind-base were different from intrinsic emptiness, or if intrinsic emptiness were different from the ear-base, nose-base, tongue-base, body-base, and mind-base—such that the ear-base, nose-base, tongue-base, body-base, and mind-base were not intrinsic emptiness and intrinsic emptiness were not the ear-base, nose-base, tongue-base, body-base, and mind-base."

“Subhūti! If the sphere of form were different from intrinsic emptiness, or if intrinsic emptiness were different from the sphere of form; if the sphere of form were not intrinsic emptiness, or if intrinsic emptiness were not the sphere of form;

if the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena were different from intrinsic emptiness, or if intrinsic emptiness were different from the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena; if the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena were not intrinsic emptiness, or if intrinsic emptiness were not the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena.”

“Subhūti! If the eye-element were different from intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness were different from the eye-element; if the eye-element were not intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness were not the eye-element;

if the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements were different from intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness were different from the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements; if the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements were not intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness were not the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements. [They are not so.]”

“Subhūti! If the realm of form were different from intrinsic emptiness, or if intrinsic emptiness were different from the realm of form, then the realm of form would not be intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness would not be the realm of form.

If the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena were different from intrinsic emptiness, or if intrinsic emptiness were different from the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, then the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena would not be intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness would not be the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena.”

"Subhūti! If the eye-consciousness element were different from intrinsic emptiness, or if intrinsic emptiness were different from the eye-consciousness element; if the eye-consciousness element were not intrinsic emptiness, or if intrinsic emptiness were not the eye-consciousness element;

and if the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements were different from intrinsic emptiness, or if intrinsic emptiness were different from the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements; if the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements were not intrinsic emptiness, or if intrinsic emptiness were not the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements..."

“Subhūti! If eye-contact were different from intrinsic emptiness, or if intrinsic emptiness were different from eye-contact; if eye-contact were not intrinsic emptiness, or if intrinsic emptiness were not eye-contact;

and if ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact were different from intrinsic emptiness, or if intrinsic emptiness were different from ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact; if ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact were not intrinsic emptiness, or if intrinsic emptiness were not ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact—[then it would not be so].”

“Subhūti! If the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition were different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or if the emptiness of intrinsic nature were different from the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition; if the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition were not the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or if the emptiness of intrinsic nature were not the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition;

[and if] the various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact as conditions were different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or if the emptiness of intrinsic nature were different from the various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact as conditions; if the various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact as conditions were not the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or if the emptiness of intrinsic nature were not the various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact as conditions.”

“Subhūti! If the earth element were different from intrinsic emptiness, or if intrinsic emptiness were different from the earth element; if the earth element were not intrinsic emptiness, or if intrinsic emptiness were not the earth element;

if the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements were different from intrinsic emptiness, or if intrinsic emptiness were different from the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements; if the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements were not intrinsic emptiness, or if intrinsic emptiness were not the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements—[then it would not be so].”

“Subhūti! If causes and conditions were different from intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness were different from causes and conditions; if causes and conditions were not intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness were not causes and conditions;

if the immediately preceding condition, the object-condition, and the dominant condition were different from intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness were different from the immediately preceding condition, the object-condition, and the dominant condition; if the immediately preceding condition, the object-condition, and the dominant condition were not intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness were not the immediately preceding condition, the object-condition, and the dominant condition—[then it would not be so].”

“Subhūti! If the phenomena produced from conditions were different from intrinsic emptiness, or if intrinsic emptiness were different from the phenomena produced from conditions, then the phenomena produced from conditions would not be intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness would not be the phenomena produced from conditions.

“Subhūti! If ignorance were different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or if the emptiness of intrinsic nature were different from ignorance; if ignorance were not the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or if the emptiness of intrinsic nature were not ignorance;

if formative forces, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair were different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or if the emptiness of intrinsic nature were different from formative forces up to old age, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair; if formative forces, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair were not the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or if the emptiness of intrinsic nature were not formative forces up to old age, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair—[then it would not be so].”

“Subhūti! If the perfection of generosity were different from intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness were different from the perfection of generosity; if the perfection of generosity were not intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness were not the perfection of generosity;

if the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom were different from intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness were different from the perfections of ethical discipline up to wisdom; if the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom were not intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness were not the perfections of ethical discipline up to wisdom—[then it would not be so].”

“Subhūti! If internal emptiness were different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or if the emptiness of intrinsic nature were different from internal emptiness; if internal emptiness were not the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or if the emptiness of intrinsic nature were not internal emptiness;

[and if] external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate, and the emptiness of conditioned phenomena [were likewise different]...”

...the emptiness of the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of the ultimate (*atyanta-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of the limitless (*anavara-agra-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of dispersion (*anavakāra-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of non-alteration (*anavakāra-śūnyatā*),

the emptiness of specific characteristics (*svalakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of common characteristics (*sāmānya-lakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of all phenomena (*sarvadharma-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of the unapprehendable (*anupalambha-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of non-existence (*abhāva-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of intrinsic nature (*svabhāva-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence (*abhāva-svabhāva-śūnyatā*), and the emptiness of other-nature (*parabhāva-śūnyatā*). This is the emptiness of intrinsic nature (*prakṛti-śūnyatā*).
From the emptiness of the external up to the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature— namely: the emptiness of the external, the internal-and-external emptiness,

the emptiness of emptiness, the great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate, the emptiness of the conditioned, the emptiness of the unconditioned, the absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless,
the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of self-characteristics, and the emptiness of common characteristics.

The emptiness of all phenomena (*sarvadharma-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of the unapprehendable (*anupalambha-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of non-existence (*abhāva-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of intrinsic nature (*svabhāva-śūnyatā*),

and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence (*abhāvasvabhāva-śūnyatā*) are not the emptiness of essential nature (*prakṛti-śūnyatā*); nor is the emptiness of essential nature the emptiness of the external (*bahirdhā-śūnyatā*) up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.

“Subhūti! If the four foundations of mindfulness were different from intrinsic emptiness, or if intrinsic emptiness were different from the four foundations of mindfulness; if the four foundations of mindfulness were not intrinsic emptiness, or if intrinsic emptiness were not the four foundations of mindfulness;

if the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path were different from intrinsic emptiness, or if intrinsic emptiness were different from the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path; if the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path were not intrinsic emptiness, or if intrinsic emptiness were not the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path—[then they would not be so].”

"Subhūti! If the noble truth of suffering were different from intrinsic emptiness, or if intrinsic emptiness were different from the noble truth of suffering; if the noble truth of suffering were not intrinsic emptiness, or if intrinsic emptiness were not the noble truth of suffering;

and if the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path were different from intrinsic emptiness, or if intrinsic emptiness were different from the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path; if the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path were not intrinsic emptiness, or if intrinsic emptiness were not the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path."

“Subhūti! If the four dhyānas were different from intrinsic emptiness, or if intrinsic emptiness were different from the four dhyānas; if the four dhyānas were not intrinsic emptiness, or if intrinsic emptiness were not the four dhyānas;

if the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions were different from intrinsic emptiness, or if intrinsic emptiness were different from the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions; if the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions were not intrinsic emptiness, or if intrinsic emptiness were not the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions.”

“Subhūti! If the eight liberations were different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or if the emptiness of intrinsic nature were different from the eight liberations; if the eight liberations were not the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or if the emptiness of intrinsic nature were not the eight liberations;

if the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities were different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or if the emptiness of intrinsic nature were different from the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities; if the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities were not the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or if the emptiness of intrinsic nature were not the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities...”

“Subhūti! If the gateways of dhāraṇī were different from intrinsic emptiness, or if intrinsic emptiness were different from the gateways of dhāraṇī; if the gateways of dhāraṇī were not intrinsic emptiness, or if intrinsic emptiness were not the gateways of dhāraṇī;

if the gateways of samādhi were different from intrinsic emptiness, or if intrinsic emptiness were different from the gateways of samādhi; if the gateways of samādhi were not intrinsic emptiness, or if intrinsic emptiness were not the gateways of samādhi.

“Subhūti! If the Ground of Extreme Joy were different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or if the emptiness of intrinsic nature were different from the Ground of Extreme Joy; if the Ground of Extreme Joy were not the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or if the emptiness of intrinsic nature were not the Ground of Extreme Joy;

if the Ground of Stainless, the Ground of Radiance, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Supreme Difficulty to Conquer, the Ground of Manifestation, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Good Intelligence, and the Ground of Dharma Clouds were different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or if the emptiness of intrinsic nature were different from the Ground of Stainless up to the Ground of Dharma Clouds; if the Ground of Stainless, the Ground of Radiance, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Supreme Difficulty to Conquer, the Ground of Manifestation, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Good Intelligence, and the Ground of Dharma Clouds were not the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or if the emptiness of intrinsic nature were not the Ground of Stainless up to the Ground of Dharma Clouds.”

“Subhūti! If the five eyes were different from intrinsic emptiness, or if intrinsic emptiness were different from the five eyes; if the five eyes were not intrinsic emptiness, or if intrinsic emptiness were not the five eyes;

if the six supernormal powers were different from intrinsic emptiness, or if intrinsic emptiness were different from the six supernormal powers; if the six supernormal powers were not intrinsic emptiness, or if intrinsic emptiness were not the six supernormal powers—[then they would not be so].”

“Subhūti! If the ten powers of a Buddha were different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or if the emptiness of intrinsic nature were different from the ten powers of a Buddha; if the ten powers of a Buddha were not the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or if the emptiness of intrinsic nature were not the ten powers of a Buddha;

if the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha were different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or if the emptiness of intrinsic nature were different from the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; if the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha were not the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or if the emptiness of intrinsic nature were not the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha...”

“Subhūti! If the thirty-two marks of a great man were different from intrinsic emptiness, or if intrinsic emptiness were different from the thirty-two marks of a great man; if the thirty-two marks of a great man were not intrinsic emptiness, or if intrinsic emptiness were not the thirty-two marks of a great man;

if the eighty secondary signs were different from intrinsic emptiness, or if intrinsic emptiness were different from the eighty secondary signs; if the eighty secondary signs were not intrinsic emptiness, or if intrinsic emptiness were not the eighty secondary signs—[then it would not be so].”

“Subhūti! If the quality of non-forgetfulness were different from intrinsic emptiness, or if intrinsic emptiness were different from the quality of non-forgetfulness; if the quality of non-forgetfulness were not intrinsic emptiness, or if intrinsic emptiness were not the quality of non-forgetfulness;

if the state of constant abiding in equanimity were different from intrinsic emptiness, or if intrinsic emptiness were different from the state of constant abiding in equanimity; if the state of constant abiding in equanimity were not intrinsic emptiness, or if intrinsic emptiness were not the state of constant abiding in equanimity—[then these would not be so].”

“Subhūti! If all-knowledge were different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or if the emptiness of intrinsic nature were different from all-knowledge; if all-knowledge were not the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or if the emptiness of intrinsic nature were not all-knowledge;

if the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects were different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or if the emptiness of intrinsic nature were different from the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects; if the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects were not the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or if the emptiness of intrinsic nature were not the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects—[then it would not be so].”

“Subhūti! If the fruit of stream-entry were different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or if the emptiness of intrinsic nature were different from the fruit of stream-entry; if the fruit of stream-entry were not the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or if the emptiness of intrinsic nature were not the fruit of stream-entry;

if the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, arhat, and pratyekabuddha awakening were different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or if the emptiness of intrinsic nature were different from the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, arhat, and pratyekabuddha awakening; if the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, arhat, and pratyekabuddha awakening were not the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or if the emptiness of intrinsic nature were not the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, arhat, and pratyekabuddha awakening.”

“Subhūti! If the practice of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas were different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or if the emptiness of intrinsic nature were different from the practice of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; if the practice of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas were not the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or if the emptiness of intrinsic nature were not the practice of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas;

or if the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas were different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or if the emptiness of intrinsic nature were different from the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas; or if the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas were not the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or if the emptiness of intrinsic nature were not the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas—then when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they would not contemplate all phenomena as being empty of intrinsic nature, nor would they realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll Three Hundred and Eighty-Eight. Translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter Seventy, "The Immovable," Section Four. "Subhūti!

Because form is not different from the emptiness of its own nature, and the emptiness of its own nature is not different from form; form itself is the emptiness of its own nature, and the emptiness of its own nature is itself form.

Feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are not different from the emptiness of their own nature, and the emptiness of their own nature is not different from feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness; feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness themselves are the emptiness of their own nature, and the emptiness of their own nature is itself feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.

“Subhūti! Because the eye-base is not different from intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is not different from the eye-base; the eye-base is itself intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is itself the eye-base.

The ear-base, nose-base, tongue-base, body-base, and mind-base are not different from intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is not different from the ear-base, nose-base, tongue-base, body-base, and mind-base; the ear-base, nose-base, tongue-base, body-base, and mind-base are themselves intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is itself the ear-base, nose-base, tongue-base, body-base, and mind-base.”

“Subhūti! Because the eye-element is not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from the eye-element; the eye-element is itself the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the eye-element.

The ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements are not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements; the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements.”

"Subhūti! Because the realm of form is not different from intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is not different from the realm of form; the realm of form is itself intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is itself the realm of form.

The realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are not different from intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is not different from the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena; the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are themselves intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is itself the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena."

“Subhūti! Because the eye-consciousness element is not different from intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is not different from the eye-consciousness element; the eye-consciousness element is itself intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is itself the eye-consciousness element.

The ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements are not different from intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is not different from the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements; the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements are themselves intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is itself the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness elements.”

"Subhūti! Because eye-contact is not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from eye-contact; eye-contact itself is the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature itself is eye-contact.

Ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact are not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact; ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact themselves are the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature itself is ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact."

“Subhūti! The various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition are not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition. The various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition.

The various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions are not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from the various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions. The various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions.”

“Subhūti! Because the earth element is not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from the earth element; the earth element is itself the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the earth element.
