The water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements; the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements.”

“Subhūti! Because conditions are not different from intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is not different from conditions; conditions are themselves intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is itself conditions.

The immediately preceding condition, the object-condition, and the dominant condition are not different from intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is not different from the immediately preceding condition, the object-condition, and the dominant condition; the immediately preceding condition, the object-condition, and the dominant condition are themselves intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is itself the immediately preceding condition, the object-condition, and the dominant condition.”

“Subhūti! All phenomena produced from conditions are not different from the emptiness of their intrinsic nature; the emptiness of their intrinsic nature is not different from all phenomena produced from conditions. All phenomena produced from conditions are themselves the emptiness of their intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of their intrinsic nature is itself all phenomena produced from conditions.”

“Subhūti! Ignorance is not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from ignorance; ignorance itself is the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself ignorance.

Volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from volitional formations up to old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair; volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself volitional formations up to old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.”

“Subhūti! Because the perfection of generosity is not other than intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is not other than the perfection of generosity; the perfection of generosity is itself intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is itself the perfection of generosity.

The perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are not other than intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is not other than the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are themselves intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is itself the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.”

“Subhūti! Because inner emptiness is not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from inner emptiness; inner emptiness is itself the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself inner emptiness;
[and likewise] outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate, and the emptiness of conditioned phenomena...”

...the emptiness of the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of the ultimate (*atyanta-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of the limitless (*anavara-agra-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of dispersion (*anavakāra-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of non-alteration (*ananyathā-śūnyatā*),

the emptiness of self-characteristics (*svalakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of common characteristics (*sāmānya-lakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of all phenomena (*sarvadharma-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of the unapprehendable (*anupalambha-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of non-existence (*abhāva-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of intrinsic nature (*svabhāva-śūnyatā*),
and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence (*abhāvasvabhāva-śūnyatā*) are not different from the emptiness of original nature (*prakṛti-śūnyatā*); [they are] original nature...
Emptiness is not different from external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the nature of non-existence; [it is] external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness,
the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness,
dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, the emptiness of self-characteristics, and the emptiness of common characteristics.
Emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature,

and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are themselves the emptiness of essential nature; the emptiness of essential nature is itself the emptiness of the external up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.

“Subhūti! Because the four foundations of mindfulness are not different from intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is not different from the four foundations of mindfulness; the four foundations of mindfulness are themselves intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is itself the four foundations of mindfulness.

The four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are not different from intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is not different from the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path; the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are themselves intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is itself the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path.”

“Subhūti! The noble truth of suffering is not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from the noble truth of suffering; the noble truth of suffering is itself the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the noble truth of suffering.

The noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path; the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path.”

“Subhūti! Because the four dhyānas are not different from intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is not different from the four dhyānas; the four dhyānas are themselves intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is itself the four dhyānas.

The four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are not different from intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is not different from the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions; the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are themselves intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is itself the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions.”

“Subhūti! The eight liberations are not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from the eight liberations; the eight liberations are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the eight liberations.

The eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities; the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities.”

“Subhūti! Because the gateways of dhāraṇī are not different from intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is not different from the gateways of dhāraṇī; the gateways of dhāraṇī are themselves intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is itself the gateways of dhāraṇī.

The gateways of samādhi are not different from intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is not different from the gateways of samādhi; the gateways of samādhi are themselves intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is itself the gateways of samādhi.”

“Subhūti! The gate of liberation of emptiness is not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from the gate of liberation of emptiness. The gate of liberation of emptiness is itself the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the gate of liberation of emptiness.

The gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness. The gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.”

“Subhūti! The Ground of Extreme Joy is not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from the Ground of Extreme Joy. The Ground of Extreme Joy is itself the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the Ground of Extreme Joy.”

The Stainless Ground, the Radiant Ground, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Supreme Difficulty to Conquer, the Ground of Manifestation, the Ground of Far-Going, the Immovable Ground, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, and the Ground of the Dharma Cloud are not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from the Stainless Ground up to the Ground of the Dharma Cloud. The Stainless Ground, the Radiant Ground, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Supreme Difficulty to Conquer, the Ground of Manifestation, the Ground of Far-Going, the Immovable Ground, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, and the Ground of the Dharma Cloud are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the Stainless Ground up to the Ground of the Dharma Cloud.

“Subhūti! Because the five eyes are not different from intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is not different from the five eyes; the five eyes are themselves intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is itself the five eyes.

The six supernormal powers are not different from intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is not different from the six supernormal powers; the six supernormal powers are themselves intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is itself the six supernormal powers.”

“Subhūti! Because the ten powers of a Buddha are not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from the ten powers of a Buddha; the ten powers of a Buddha are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the ten powers of a Buddha.

The four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.”

“Subhūti! The thirty-two marks of a great man are not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from the thirty-two marks of a great man. The thirty-two marks of a great man are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the thirty-two marks of a great man.

The eighty minor marks are not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from the eighty minor marks. The eighty minor marks are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the eighty minor marks.”

“Subhūti! Because the quality of non-forgetfulness is not different from intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is not different from the quality of non-forgetfulness; the quality of non-forgetfulness is itself intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is itself the quality of non-forgetfulness.

The state of constant abiding in equanimity is not different from intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is not different from the state of constant abiding in equanimity; the state of constant abiding in equanimity is itself intrinsic emptiness, and intrinsic emptiness is itself the state of constant abiding in equanimity.”

“Subhūti! All-knowledge is not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from all-knowledge; all-knowledge is itself the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself all-knowledge.

The knowledge of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from the knowledge of the path and the knowledge of all aspects; the knowledge of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the knowledge of the path and the knowledge of all aspects.”

“Subhūti! Because the fruit of stream-entry is not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from the fruit of stream-entry; the fruit of stream-entry is itself the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the fruit of stream-entry.

The fruits of once-returning, non-returning, arhatship, and the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha are not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, arhatship, and the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha. The fruits of once-returning, non-returning, arhatship, and the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, arhatship, and the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha.”

“Subhūti! Because all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are themselves the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.”

The unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment of all Buddhas is not different from the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not different from the unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment of all Buddhas. Because the unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment of all Buddhas is itself the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature is itself the unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment of all Buddhas, when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they contemplate all phenomena as being empty of intrinsic nature and thereby realize unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.
"Why is this so? Subhūti!

Apart from intrinsic emptiness (*prakṛti-śūnyatā*), there is not a single dharma that is real, permanent, destructible, or subject to cessation. Within intrinsic emptiness, likewise, there is not a single dharma that is real, permanent, destructible, or subject to cessation. It is only because of the delusions, errors, and inversions of foolish worldlings that they give rise to notions of differentiation, such as clinging to form as being different from intrinsic emptiness, or clinging to feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness as being different from intrinsic emptiness."

Some may grasp that the sense base of the eye is distinct from its intrinsic emptiness; or they may grasp that the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are distinct from their intrinsic emptiness.

Some may grasp that the sense base of form is distinct from its intrinsic emptiness; or they may grasp that the sense bases of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are distinct from their intrinsic emptiness.

Some may grasp that the eye constituent is distinct from its intrinsic emptiness; or they may grasp that the constituents of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are distinct from their intrinsic emptiness.

Some hold that the form realm is distinct from the emptiness of its own nature; some hold that the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are distinct from the emptiness of their own nature.

Some hold that the eye-consciousness realm is distinct from the emptiness of its own nature; some hold that the realms of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness are distinct from the emptiness of their own nature.
Some hold that eye-contact is distinct from the emptiness of its own nature; some hold that the contacts of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind are distinct from the emptiness of their own nature.

Some may grasp that the various feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition are different from their own-being emptiness; or they may grasp that the various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact as a condition are different from their own-being emptiness.

Some may grasp that the earth element is different from its own-being emptiness; or they may grasp that the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements are different from their own-being emptiness.

Some may grasp that the causal condition is different from its own-being emptiness; or they may grasp that the immediately preceding condition, the object-condition, and the dominant condition are different from their own-being emptiness.
Some hold that the various phenomena produced from conditions are distinct from their intrinsic emptiness;

some hold that ignorance is distinct from its intrinsic emptiness; or they hold that volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are distinct from their intrinsic emptiness;

or they hold that the perfection of generosity is distinct from its intrinsic emptiness; or they hold that the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are distinct from their intrinsic emptiness.

Or they may hold that internal emptiness is distinct from the emptiness of intrinsic nature; or they may hold that external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are each distinct from the emptiness of intrinsic nature;

or they may hold that the four foundations of mindfulness are distinct from the emptiness of intrinsic nature; or they may hold that the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are distinct from the emptiness of intrinsic nature.

Some may hold that the noble truth of suffering is distinct from the emptiness of intrinsic nature; some may hold that the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are distinct from the emptiness of intrinsic nature.

Some may hold that the four dhyānas are distinct from the emptiness of intrinsic nature; some may hold that the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions are distinct from the emptiness of intrinsic nature.

Some may hold that the eight liberations are distinct from the emptiness of intrinsic nature; some may hold that the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive absorptions, and the ten totalities are distinct from the emptiness of intrinsic nature.
Some may grasp that the gateways of dhāraṇī are distinct from the emptiness of intrinsic nature; some may grasp that the gateways of samādhi are distinct from the emptiness of intrinsic nature;

some may grasp that the gateway of the emptiness liberation is distinct from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or grasp that the gateways of signlessness and wishlessness liberations are distinct from the emptiness of intrinsic nature;

some may grasp that the Ground of Extreme Joy is distinct from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or grasp that the Ground of Purity, the Ground of Radiance, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Difficult Victory, the Ground of Manifestation, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, and the Ground of Dharma Clouds are distinct from the emptiness of intrinsic nature.
Some may grasp that the five eyes are distinct from the emptiness of their own nature; some may grasp that the six supernormal powers are distinct from the emptiness of their own nature;

some may grasp that the ten powers of a Buddha are distinct from the emptiness of their own nature; some may grasp that the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are distinct from the emptiness of their own nature;

some may grasp that the thirty-two marks of a Great Man are distinct from the emptiness of their own nature; or some may grasp that the eighty secondary signs are distinct from the emptiness of their own nature.
Some may hold that the quality of non-forgetfulness is distinct from intrinsic emptiness; or they may hold that the nature of constant equanimity is distinct from intrinsic emptiness.
Some may hold that all-knowledge is distinct from intrinsic emptiness; or they may hold that the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects are distinct from intrinsic emptiness.

Some may hold that the fruit of stream-entry is distinct from intrinsic emptiness; or they may hold that the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, arhatship, and the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha are distinct from intrinsic emptiness.

Some may hold that all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are distinct from the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or they may hold that the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas is distinct from the emptiness of intrinsic nature.

"Subhūti! These foolish commoners, having grasped at phenomena as being different from their own intrinsic emptiness, do not know form as it truly is; they do not know feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness as they truly are."
Due to ignorance, one becomes attached to form, and becomes attached to feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.
Due to this attachment, one conceives of form as "I" and "mine," and conceives of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness as "I" and "mine."

Due to false conceptualization, one becomes attached to internal and external things, thereby undergoing the aggregates of form, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness in future bodies. Consequently, one is unable to attain liberation from birth, old age, sickness, death, grief, lamentation, suffering, and distress within the various realms of existence, wandering endlessly through the cycle of the three states of being.

"For this reason, when bodhisattva mahāsattvas dwell in the perfection of emptiness of intrinsic nature and practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not grasp at form, nor do they destroy form as being either empty or non-empty;
they do not grasp at feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, nor do they destroy feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness as being either empty or non-empty."
They do not grasp at the sense base of the eye, nor do they destroy the sense base of the eye as being either empty or non-empty;
they do not grasp at the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, nor do they destroy the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind as being either empty or non-empty.
One does not grasp at the sphere of form, nor does one destroy the sphere of form as being either empty or non-empty;

one does not grasp at the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena, nor does one destroy the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena as being either empty or non-empty.
One does not grasp at the eye-element, nor does one destroy the eye-element as being either empty or non-empty;
one does not grasp at the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-element, nor does one destroy the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-element as being either empty or non-empty.
One does not grasp at the realm of form, nor does one destroy the realm of form as being either empty or non-empty;

one does not grasp at the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, or mental phenomena, nor does one destroy the realms of sound, odor, taste, touch, or mental phenomena as being either empty or non-empty.
One does not grasp at the eye-consciousness element, nor does one destroy the eye-consciousness element as being either empty or non-empty;
one does not grasp at the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-consciousness elements, nor does one destroy the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-consciousness elements as being either empty or non-empty.
One does not grasp at eye-contact, nor does one destroy eye-contact as being either empty or non-empty;
one does not grasp at ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact, nor does one destroy ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact as being either empty or non-empty.

One does not grasp at the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition, nor does one destroy those various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition, whether they be empty or non-empty;

one does not grasp at the various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact as condition, nor does one destroy those various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact as condition, whether they be empty or non-empty.
One does not grasp at the earth element, nor does one destroy the earth element as being either empty or non-empty;
one does not grasp at the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements, nor does one destroy the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements as being either empty or non-empty.
One does not grasp at the causal condition (*hetu-pratyaya*), nor does one destroy the causal condition as being either empty or non-empty;

one does not grasp at the immediately preceding condition (*samanantara-pratyaya*), the object condition (*ālambana-pratyaya*), or the dominant condition (*adhipati-pratyaya*), nor does one destroy these conditions as being either empty or non-empty.
One does not grasp at the phenomena arising from conditions, nor does one destroy those phenomena arising from conditions as being either empty or non-empty.
One does not grasp at ignorance, nor does one destroy ignorance as being either empty or non-empty;

one does not grasp at volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, or old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, nor does one destroy these—from volitional formations up to old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair—as being either empty or non-empty.

One does not grasp at the perfection of generosity, nor does one destroy the perfection of generosity as being either empty or non-empty; one does not grasp at the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, nor does one destroy the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom as being either empty or non-empty.
One does not grasp at internal emptiness, nor does one destroy internal emptiness—whether it be empty or not empty.

One does not grasp at external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence; nor does one destroy external emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—whether it be empty or not empty.
They do not grasp at the four foundations of mindfulness, nor do they disrupt the four foundations of mindfulness as being either empty or non-empty;

they do not grasp at the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, or the eightfold noble path, nor do they disrupt the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path as being either empty or non-empty.
One does not grasp at the noble truth of suffering, nor does one destroy the noble truth of suffering as being either empty or non-empty;
one does not grasp at the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, nor does one destroy the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path as being either empty or non-empty.
They do not grasp at the four dhyānas, nor do they destroy the four dhyānas as being either empty or non-empty;
they do not grasp at the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments, nor do they destroy the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments as being either empty or non-empty.
They do not grasp at the eight liberations, nor do they destroy the eight liberations as being either empty or non-empty;

they do not grasp at the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities, nor do they destroy the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities as being either empty or non-empty.
They do not grasp at the gateways of dhāraṇī, nor do they destroy the gateways of dhāraṇī, whether they are empty or not empty;
they do not grasp at the gateways of samādhi, nor do they destroy the gateways of samādhi, whether they are empty or not empty.
They do not grasp at the liberation door of emptiness, nor do they destroy the liberation door of emptiness as being either empty or non-empty;
they do not grasp at the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness, nor do they destroy the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness as being either empty or non-empty.
They do not grasp at the Ground of Utmost Joy, nor do they destroy the Ground of Utmost Joy as being either empty or non-empty;

they do not grasp at the Ground of Purity, the Ground of Radiance, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Supreme Difficulty to Conquer, the Ground of Presence, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, or the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma, nor do they destroy these grounds from the Ground of Purity up to the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma as being either empty or non-empty.
They do not grasp at the five eyes, nor do they destroy the five eyes as being either empty or non-empty;
they do not grasp at the six supernormal powers, nor do they destroy the six supernormal powers as being either empty or non-empty.
One does not grasp at the ten powers of a Buddha, nor does one destroy the ten powers of a Buddha as being either empty or non-empty;

one does not grasp at the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, nor does one destroy these from the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha as being either empty or non-empty.
They do not grasp at the thirty-two marks of a great man, nor do they destroy the thirty-two marks of a great man as being either empty or non-empty;
they do not grasp at the eighty secondary signs, nor do they destroy the eighty secondary signs as being either empty or non-empty.
One does not grasp at the quality of non-forgetfulness, nor does one destroy the quality of non-forgetfulness as being either empty or non-empty;
one does not grasp at the state of constant equanimity, nor does one destroy the state of constant equanimity as being either empty or non-empty.
They do not grasp at omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), nor do they destroy omniscience as being either empty or non-empty;

they do not grasp at the knowledge of the paths (*mārgākārajñatā*) or the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), nor do they destroy the knowledge of the paths or the knowledge of all aspects as being either empty or non-empty.
One does not grasp at the fruit of stream-entry, nor does one destroy the fruit of stream-entry as being either empty or non-empty;

one does not grasp at the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, or arhatship, nor the awakening of a pratyekabuddha, nor does one destroy the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, arhatship, or the awakening of a pratyekabuddha as being either empty or non-empty.
One does not grasp at any of the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, nor does one destroy any of the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva—whether they be empty or non-empty;

one does not grasp at the unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas, nor does one destroy the unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas—whether it be empty or non-empty.
"Why is that? Subhūti!
Form does not destroy emptiness, nor does emptiness destroy form; one does not say, 'This is form' and 'This is emptiness.'"

Feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness do not destroy emptiness, nor does emptiness destroy feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness; one does not say, "This is feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness," and "This is emptiness."
“Subhūti! The eye-base is not destroyed by emptiness, and emptiness is not destroyed by the eye-base; that is to say, ‘this is the eye-base’ and ‘this is emptiness.

The ear-base, nose-base, tongue-base, body-base, and mind-base are not destroyed by emptiness, and emptiness is not destroyed by the ear-base, nose-base, tongue-base, body-base, and mind-base; that is to say, ‘these are the ear-base, nose-base, tongue-base, body-base, and mind-base,’ and ‘this is emptiness.’”
“Subhūti! The sphere of form is not destroyed by emptiness, nor does emptiness destroy the sphere of form; one cannot say, ‘This is the sphere of form’ and ‘This is emptiness.

The spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena are not destroyed by emptiness, nor does emptiness destroy the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena; one cannot say, ‘These are the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena’ and ‘This is emptiness.’”
“Subhūti! The eye-element is not destroyed by emptiness, nor does emptiness destroy the eye-element; one cannot say, ‘This is the eye-element’ and ‘This is emptiness.

The ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements are not destroyed by emptiness, nor does emptiness destroy the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements; one cannot say, ‘These are the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements’ and ‘This is emptiness.’”
“Subhūti! The realm of form does not destroy emptiness, nor does emptiness destroy the realm of form; one does not say, ‘This is the realm of form’ and ‘This is emptiness.

The realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena do not destroy emptiness, nor does emptiness destroy the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena; one does not say, ‘These are the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena’ and ‘This is emptiness.’”

“Subhūti! The element of eye-consciousness does not destroy emptiness, nor does emptiness destroy the element of eye-consciousness; one cannot say, ‘This is the element of eye-consciousness’ and ‘This is emptiness.

The elements of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness do not destroy emptiness, nor does emptiness destroy the elements of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness; one cannot say, ‘These are the elements of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness’ and ‘This is emptiness.’”
“Subhūti! Eye-contact does not destroy emptiness, nor does emptiness destroy eye-contact; one cannot say, ‘This is eye-contact’ and ‘This is emptiness.

Ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, and mind-contact do not destroy emptiness, nor does emptiness destroy ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, and mind-contact; one cannot say, ‘This is ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact’ and ‘This is emptiness.’”

“Subhūti! The various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition are not destroyed by emptiness, nor does emptiness destroy the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition; one cannot say, ‘These are the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition,’ and ‘This is emptiness.

The various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions are not destroyed by emptiness, nor does emptiness destroy the various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions; one cannot say, ‘These are the various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions,’ and ‘This is emptiness.’”
“Subhūti! The earth element does not destroy emptiness, nor does emptiness destroy the earth element; one cannot say, ‘This is the earth element’ and ‘This is emptiness.

The water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements do not destroy emptiness, nor does emptiness destroy the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements; one cannot say, ‘These are the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements’ and ‘This is emptiness.’”
“Subhūti! Conditioned origination does not destroy emptiness, and emptiness does not destroy conditioned origination; that is to say, ‘this is conditioned origination’ and ‘this is emptiness.

The immediately preceding condition, the object condition, and the dominant condition do not destroy emptiness, and emptiness does not destroy the immediately preceding condition, the object condition, and the dominant condition; that is to say, ‘these are the immediately preceding condition, the object condition, and the dominant condition,’ and ‘this is emptiness.’”

“Subhūti! The phenomena produced from conditions do not destroy emptiness, and emptiness does not destroy the phenomena produced from conditions; that is to say, ‘these are the phenomena produced from conditions’ and ‘this is emptiness.’”
“Subhūti! Ignorance does not destroy emptiness, nor does emptiness destroy ignorance; one does not say, ‘This is ignorance’ and ‘This is emptiness.

Formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair do not destroy emptiness, nor does emptiness destroy formations through to old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair; one does not say, ‘These are formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair,’ and ‘This is emptiness.’”

“Subhūti! The perfection of generosity does not destroy emptiness, nor does emptiness destroy the perfection of generosity; one cannot say, ‘This is the perfection of generosity’ and ‘This is emptiness.

The perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom do not destroy emptiness, nor does emptiness destroy the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; one cannot say, ‘These are the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom’ and ‘This is emptiness.’”
“Subhūti! Internal emptiness does not destroy emptiness, nor does emptiness destroy internal emptiness; that is to say, ‘this is internal emptiness’ and ‘this is emptiness.

This applies likewise to external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, and the emptiness of conditioned phenomena.”
emptiness of the unconditioned, emptiness of the ultimate, emptiness of the limitless, emptiness of dispersion, emptiness of non-alteration, emptiness of intrinsic nature,
emptiness of specific characteristics, emptiness of common characteristics, emptiness of all phenomena, emptiness of the unapprehendable,
emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of self-nature, emptiness of the self-nature of non-existence, and the indestructible emptiness.
Emptiness does not destroy outer emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the essential nature of non-entities;
that is to say, this is outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness,
absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature.
The emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility,
the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence— these are emptiness.

“Subhūti! The four foundations of mindfulness are not destroyed by emptiness, nor does emptiness destroy the four foundations of mindfulness; that is to say, ‘this is the four foundations of mindfulness’ and ‘this is emptiness.

The four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path are not destroyed by emptiness, nor does emptiness destroy the four right efforts up to the eightfold noble path; that is to say, ‘these are the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path,’ and ‘this is emptiness.’”

“Subhūti! The noble truth of suffering does not destroy emptiness, nor does emptiness destroy the noble truth of suffering; that is to say, ‘this is the noble truth of suffering’ and ‘this is emptiness.

The noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path do not destroy emptiness, nor does emptiness destroy the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path; that is to say, ‘these are the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path’ and ‘this is emptiness.’”
“Subhūti! The four dhyānas do not destroy emptiness, nor does emptiness destroy the four dhyānas; that is to say, ‘these are the four dhyānas’ and ‘this is emptiness.

The four immeasurables and the four formless attainments do not destroy emptiness, nor does emptiness destroy the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments; that is to say, ‘these are the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments’ and ‘this is emptiness.’”
“Subhūti! The eight liberations do not undermine emptiness, and emptiness does not undermine the eight liberations; that is to say, ‘these are the eight liberations’ and ‘this is emptiness.

The eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities do not undermine emptiness, and emptiness does not undermine the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities; that is to say, ‘these are the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities,’ and ‘this is emptiness.’”
“Subhūti! The gateways of dhāraṇī do not destroy emptiness, and emptiness does not destroy the gateways of dhāraṇī; one cannot say, ‘This is the gateway of dhāraṇī’ and ‘This is emptiness.
The gateways of samādhi do not destroy emptiness, and emptiness does not destroy the gateways of samādhi; one cannot say, ‘This is the gateway of samādhi’ and ‘This is emptiness.’”

“Subhūti! The gate of liberation of emptiness does not destroy emptiness, nor does emptiness destroy the gate of liberation of emptiness; one cannot say, ‘This is the gate of liberation of emptiness’ and ‘This is emptiness.

The gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness do not destroy emptiness, nor does emptiness destroy the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness; one cannot say, ‘These are the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness’ and ‘This is emptiness.’”
“Subhūti! The Ground of Extreme Joy is not destroyed by emptiness, nor does emptiness destroy the Ground of Extreme Joy; one cannot say, ‘This is the Ground of Extreme Joy’ and ‘This is emptiness.

The Ground of Stainless Purity, the Ground of Radiant Light, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Utmost Difficulty to Conquer, the Ground of Manifest Presence, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, and the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma are not destroyed by emptiness, nor does emptiness destroy these grounds from the Ground of Stainless Purity up to the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma; one cannot say, ‘This is the Ground of Stainless Purity, the Ground of Radiant Light, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Utmost Difficulty to Conquer, the Ground of Manifest Presence, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, or the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma,’ nor can one say, ‘This is emptiness.’”
“Subhūti! The five eyes do not destroy emptiness, nor does emptiness destroy the five eyes; one cannot say, ‘These are the five eyes’ and ‘This is emptiness.
The six supernormal powers do not destroy emptiness, nor does emptiness destroy the six supernormal powers; one cannot say, ‘These are the six supernormal powers’ and ‘This is emptiness.’”
“Subhūti! The ten powers of a Buddha do not destroy emptiness, nor does emptiness destroy the ten powers of a Buddha; one cannot say, ‘These are the ten powers of a Buddha’ and ‘This is emptiness.

The four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha do not destroy emptiness, nor does emptiness destroy the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; one cannot say, ‘These are the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha,’ and ‘This is emptiness.’”

“Subhūti! The thirty-two marks of a great man do not undermine emptiness, nor does emptiness undermine the thirty-two marks of a great man; one cannot say, ‘These are the thirty-two marks of a great man’ and ‘This is emptiness.
The eighty minor marks do not undermine emptiness, nor does emptiness undermine the eighty minor marks; one cannot say, ‘These are the eighty minor marks’ and ‘This is emptiness.’”

“Subhūti! The quality of non-forgetfulness does not destroy emptiness, and emptiness does not destroy the quality of non-forgetfulness; one cannot say, ‘This is the quality of non-forgetfulness’ and ‘This is emptiness.

The nature of constant equanimity does not destroy emptiness, and emptiness does not destroy the nature of constant equanimity; one cannot say, ‘This is the nature of constant equanimity’ and ‘This is emptiness.’”
“Subhūti! All-knowledge does not destroy emptiness, and emptiness does not destroy all-knowledge; that is to say, ‘this is all-knowledge’ and ‘this is emptiness.

Path-knowledge and all-aspect-knowledge do not destroy emptiness, and emptiness does not destroy path-knowledge and all-aspect-knowledge; that is to say, ‘this is path-knowledge and all-aspect-knowledge’ and ‘this is emptiness.’”
“Subhūti! The fruit of stream-entry does not destroy emptiness, nor does emptiness destroy the fruit of stream-entry; one cannot say, ‘This is the fruit of stream-entry’ and ‘This is emptiness.

The fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship, as well as the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, do not destroy emptiness, nor does emptiness destroy the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, arhatship, and the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha; one cannot say, ‘This is the fruit of once-returning, non-returning, arhatship, or the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha,’ and ‘This is emptiness.’”

“Subhūti! All the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do not destroy emptiness, and emptiness does not destroy all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; that is to say, ‘this is all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas’ and ‘this is emptiness.

The unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas does not destroy emptiness, and emptiness does not destroy the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas; that is to say, ‘this is the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas’ and ‘this is emptiness.’”

“Subhūti! For example, space does not destroy space; the internal realm of space does not destroy the external realm of space, and the external realm of space does not destroy the internal realm of space.”
"In this way, Subhūti! Form does not destroy emptiness, and emptiness does not destroy form;
feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness do not destroy emptiness, and emptiness does not destroy feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness."
Why is this? Because all such phenomena are equally devoid of intrinsic nature and cannot be characterized as being either "empty" or "not empty. "Subhūti!..."
The eye-base does not destroy emptiness, and emptiness does not destroy the eye-base;
the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases do not destroy emptiness, and emptiness does not destroy the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases.

Why is this? Because all such phenomena are equally devoid of intrinsic nature and cannot be characterized as being destroyed; that is to say, one cannot designate "this is empty" or "this is not empty. "Subhūti!..."
The sphere of form does not destroy emptiness, and emptiness does not destroy the sphere of form;
the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena do not destroy emptiness, and emptiness does not destroy the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena.

Why is this? Because all such phenomena are equally devoid of intrinsic nature and cannot be characterized as being either destroyed or otherwise; that is to say, "this is empty" and "this is not empty. "Subhūti!..."
The eye-element does not destroy emptiness, and emptiness does not destroy the eye-element;
the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements do not destroy emptiness, and emptiness does not destroy the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements.
Why is this? Because all such phenomena are equally devoid of intrinsic nature and cannot be characterized as being destroyed; that is to say, "this is empty" and "this is not empty. "Subhūti!..."

The eye-consciousness element does not destroy emptiness, and emptiness does not destroy the eye-consciousness element;
the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements do not destroy emptiness, and emptiness does not destroy the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements.
Why is this? Because all such dharmas are equally devoid of intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*) and cannot be characterized as being either "this is empty" or "this is not empty. "Subhūti!..."

the various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions are not destroyed by emptiness, and emptiness is not destroyed by the various feelings produced with ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact as conditions.

The earth element does not destroy emptiness, and emptiness does not destroy the earth element;
the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements do not destroy emptiness, and emptiness does not destroy the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements.
Why is this? Because all such phenomena are equally devoid of intrinsic nature and cannot be characterized as being destroyed; that is to say, "this is empty" and "this is not empty.
"Suvikrāntavikrāmin! [It is thus.]”

the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments do not destroy emptiness, and emptiness does not destroy the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments.
Why is this? Because all such phenomena are equally devoid of intrinsic nature and cannot be characterized as being destructible; that is to say, "this is empty" and "this is not empty. "Subhūti!..."
The eight liberations do not destroy emptiness, and emptiness does not destroy the eight liberations;

the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities do not destroy emptiness, and emptiness does not destroy the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, or the ten totalities.
Why is this? Because all such phenomena are equally devoid of intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*) and cannot be characterized as being either "this is empty" or "this is not empty. "Subhūti!..."
The gateways of dhāraṇī do not destroy emptiness, and emptiness does not destroy the gateways of dhāraṇī;
the gateways of samādhi do not destroy emptiness, and emptiness does not destroy the gateways of samādhi.
Why is this? Because all such dharmas are equally devoid of intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*) and cannot be characterized as being either "this is empty" or "this is not empty. "Subhūti!..."
The liberation door of emptiness does not destroy emptiness, and emptiness does not destroy the liberation door of emptiness;
the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness do not destroy emptiness, and emptiness does not destroy the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness.

Why is this? Because all such phenomena are equally devoid of intrinsic nature and cannot be characterized as being either destroyed or otherwise; that is to say, one cannot designate "this is empty" or "this is not empty. "Subhūti!..."
The emptiness that does not destroy the Ground of Utmost Joy does not destroy the Ground of Utmost Joy;

the emptiness that does not destroy the Ground of Stainless, the Ground of Radiant Light, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Supreme Difficulty to Conquer, the Ground of Manifestation, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, and the Ground of the Dharma Cloud does not destroy the Ground of Stainless up to the Ground of the Dharma Cloud.

Why is this? Because all such phenomena are equally devoid of intrinsic nature and cannot be characterized as being either destroyed or otherwise; that is to say, one cannot designate "this is empty" or "this is not empty. "Subhūti!..."
The five eyes do not destroy emptiness, and emptiness does not destroy the five eyes;
the six supernormal powers do not destroy emptiness, and emptiness does not destroy the six supernormal powers. Why is this?
In this way, all these phenomena are equally devoid of intrinsic nature and cannot be characterized as being either "this is empty" or "this is not empty. Subhūti!
The Buddha’s ten powers do not destroy emptiness, and emptiness does not destroy the Buddha’s ten powers.

The four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are not destroyed by emptiness; emptiness is not destroyed by the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
Why is this? Because all such phenomena are equally devoid of intrinsic nature and cannot be characterized as being either "empty" or "not empty. "Subhūti!..."
The thirty-two marks of a great man do not destroy emptiness, and emptiness does not destroy the thirty-two marks of a great man;
the eighty secondary characteristics do not destroy emptiness, and emptiness does not destroy the eighty secondary characteristics.
Why is this? Because all such phenomena are equally devoid of intrinsic nature and cannot be characterized as being destroyed; that is to say, "this is empty" and "this is not empty. "Subhūti!..."
The quality of non-forgetfulness does not destroy emptiness, and emptiness does not destroy the quality of non-forgetfulness;
the nature of constant abiding in equanimity does not destroy emptiness, and emptiness does not destroy the nature of constant abiding in equanimity.

Why is this? Because all such phenomena are equally devoid of intrinsic nature and cannot be characterized as being destructible; that is to say, one cannot designate "this is empty" or "this is not empty. "Subhūti!..."
All-knowledge does not destroy emptiness, and emptiness does not destroy all-knowledge;

the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects do not destroy emptiness, and emptiness does not destroy the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects.

Why is this? Because all such phenomena are equally devoid of intrinsic nature and cannot be characterized as being either destroyed or otherwise; that is to say, one cannot designate "this is empty" or "this is not empty. "Subhūti!..."
The fruit of stream-entry does not destroy emptiness, and emptiness does not destroy the fruit of stream-entry;

the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, arhatship, and pratyekabuddha-enlightenment do not destroy emptiness, and emptiness does not destroy the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, arhatship, and pratyekabuddha-enlightenment.

Why is this? Because all such phenomena are equally devoid of intrinsic nature and cannot be characterized by destruction, such that one could say, "this is empty" and "this is not empty. "Subhūti!..."
The practice of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas does not destroy emptiness, and emptiness does not destroy the practice of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas;
the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas does not destroy emptiness, and emptiness does not destroy the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas.
Why is this? Because all such phenomena are equally devoid of intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*) and cannot be mutually subverted by saying, "This is empty" or "This is not empty.

*The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, Fascicle 389, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree, Part One, Chapter Seventy, Section Five: "The Chapter on the Immovable. At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

If all dharmas are empty of intrinsic nature, and within the emptiness of intrinsic nature there is no distinction whatsoever, for what purpose do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dwell when they resolve their minds upon unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, making this vow:
‘I shall proceed toward and realize vast, unexcelled, perfect, and complete bodhi’?”
"World-Honored One!

The unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas has no dualistic mode of activity; one cannot realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment through a dualistic mode of activity."
The Buddha told Subhūti: “So it is! So it is!”
It is as you have said:
the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas has no dualistic aspect, and one cannot realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment through a dualistic aspect.
Why is this? Subhūti!
Awakening is non-dual and without discrimination; if one practices with respect to awakening by means of dualistic marks or engages in discrimination, one will certainly be unable to realize it.

“Subhūti! Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do not practice toward awakening by means of dualistic signs, nor do they engage in conceptual discrimination; abiding nowhere at all, they give rise to the mind of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”

When Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do not engage with the dualistic characteristics of any phenomena, nor do they engage in conceptual discrimination, being entirely without such engagement, they are then able to proceed toward the realization of vast, unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
“Subhūti! The unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment sought by bodhisattva mahāsattvas cannot be realized by practicing with dualistic characteristics. Subhūti!”

The enlightenment of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas has no sphere of activity whatsoever; that is to say, they do not engage with form, nor do they engage with feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness;
they do not engage with the sense-base of the eye, nor do they engage with the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind;
they do not engage with the sense-base of forms, nor do they engage with the sense-bases of sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, or mental phenomena.
They do not course in the eye-element, nor do they course in the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-element;
they do not course in the form-element, nor do they course in the sound, odor, taste, tangible, or mental-object-element;
they do not course in the eye-consciousness-element, nor do they course in the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-consciousness-element.
They do not practice with respect to the activity of eye-contact, nor with respect to the activities of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact;
they do not practice with respect to the feelings produced conditioned by eye-contact, nor with respect to the feelings produced conditioned by ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact;
they do not practice with respect to the earth element, nor with respect to the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements.
He does not course in conditions; nor does he course in the immediately preceding condition, the object-condition, or the dominant condition.
He does not course in the various phenomena produced from conditions.

He does not course in ignorance, nor does he course in volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, or old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.
They do not practice the perfection of generosity, nor do they practice the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom;

they do not practice inner emptiness, nor do they practice outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

They do not course in the four foundations of mindfulness, nor do they course in the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path;
they do not course in the noble truth of suffering, nor do they course in the noble truths of origin, cessation, or the path;
they do not course in the four dhyānas, nor do they course in the four immeasurables or the four formless absorptions.
They do not practice in the eight liberations, nor do they practice in the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities;
they do not practice in the doors of dhāraṇī, nor do they practice in the doors of samādhi;
they do not practice in the door of the emptiness liberation, nor do they practice in the doors of the signless and wishless liberations.

He does not course in the Ground of Extreme Joy, nor does he course in the Ground of Purity, the Ground of Radiance, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Difficult Victory, the Ground of Presence, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, or the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma;
he does not course in the five eyes, nor does he course in the six supernormal powers;

he does not course in the ten powers of a Buddha, nor does he course in the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
They do not course in the thirty-two marks of a great man, nor do they course in the eighty secondary signs;
they do not course in the quality of non-forgetfulness, nor do they course in the nature of constant equanimity;
they do not course in all-knowledge, nor do they course in the knowledge of the paths or the knowledge of all aspects.
They do not course in the fruit of a stream-enterer, nor do they course in the fruits of a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat, nor in the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha;
they do not course in any of the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, nor do they course in the unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas.
"Why is this? Subhūti!
All the awakening of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas does not take name and fame as a basis for grasping at 'self' and 'what belongs to self'; that is to say, they do not form such thoughts:"
"I practice with regard to form; I practice with regard to feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.
Nor does he form such a thought:
"I practice with regard to the sense-base of the eye; I practice with regard to the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind."
Nor does he form such thoughts as:
"I am practicing in the sphere of forms," or "I am practicing in the spheres of sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, or mental phenomena.
Nor does he form such thoughts:
"I practice within the eye-element; I practice within the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-elements.
Nor does one form such a thought:
"I practice within the form-element; I practice within the sound, odor, taste, tangible, and mental-object elements."
Nor does one form this thought:
"I am practicing within the sphere of eye-consciousness; I am practicing within the spheres of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness."
Nor does one form this thought:
"I am practicing eye-contact; I am practicing ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact.
Nor does one form this thought:
"I course in the various feelings produced with eye-contact as condition; I course in the various feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions."
Nor does he form this thought:
"I am practicing within the earth element; I am practicing within the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements.
Nor does he form this thought:
"I practice in dependence on causes and conditions; I practice in dependence on the immediately preceding condition, the object condition, and the dominant condition.
Nor does he form this thought:
"I practice regarding those phenomena that arise from conditions."
Nor does one form such a thought:

"I am practicing ignorance; I am practicing volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair."
Nor does he form this thought:
"I am practicing the perfection of generosity; I am practicing the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom."
Nor does he form this thought: "I practice inner emptiness;

I practice outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence."
Nor does he form this thought:

"I am practicing the four foundations of mindfulness; I am practicing the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path."
Nor does he form this thought:
"I am practicing the noble truth of suffering; I am practicing the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path.
Nor does he form this thought:
"I practice the four dhyānas; I practice the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments.
Nor does he form such thoughts as:
"I practice the eight liberations; I practice the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities."
Nor does he form this thought:
"I am practicing the gateways of dhāraṇī; I am practicing the gateways of samādhi.
Nor does he form this thought:
"I practice the gate of liberation of emptiness; I practice the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.
Nor does one form such thoughts as:

"I practice the Ground of Extreme Joy; I practice the Ground of Purity, the Ground of Radiant Light, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Difficult to Conquer, the Ground of Manifestation, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Good Intelligence, and the Ground of the Dharma Cloud."
Nor does he form this thought:
"I practice the five eyes; I practice the six supernormal powers.
Nor does he form this thought:

"I practice the ten powers of a Buddha; I practice the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha."
Nor does he form this thought:
"I am practicing the thirty-two marks of a great man; I am practicing the eighty secondary characteristics.
Nor does he form this thought:
"I practice the dharma of non-forgetfulness; I practice the state of constant equanimity.
Nor does he form such thoughts as:
"I practice all-knowledge; I practice the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects."
Nor does one form such thoughts as:
"I am practicing for the fruit of stream-entry; I am practicing for the fruit of once-returning, non-returning, arhatship, or the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha."
Nor does he form this thought:
"I am practicing all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; I am practicing for the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas."
"Furthermore, Subhūti! The bodhi of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is practiced neither for the sake of grasping nor for the sake of relinquishing.
The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
If the bodhi of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is practiced neither by way of grasping nor by way of relinquishing, then in what place should the bodhi of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas be practiced?”
The Buddha said to Subhūti: "What do you think?
Where would the bodhi of all the emanations of the Buddhas proceed?"
"Do you practice for the sake of grasping,
or do you practice for the sake of relinquishing? Subhūti replied:
"No, World-Honored One! No!"
"Sugata! Since the emanation bodies of all Buddhas are in reality non-existent, how can it be said that there is any enlightenment, any sphere of activity, or anything to be grasped or abandoned?"
The Buddha said to Subhūti: "What do you think?
Where would the awakening of the various arhats travel within a dream?"
"Do you practice for the sake of grasping,
or do you practice for the sake of relinquishing? Subhūti replied:
"No, World-Honored One! No!"

"Sugata! Since all Arhats have eternally exhausted all outflows (*āsrava*), and both the hindrances of torpor and drowsiness (*styāna-middha-nīvaraṇa*) have been extinguished, they ultimately have no dreams. How, then, could there be any place for the practice of awakening within a dream, whether involving grasping or relinquishing?"
The Buddha said, “Subhūti!

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, all their awakening is likewise: they do not practice by way of grasping, nor do they practice by way of relinquishing; there is no place of practice at all, because its intrinsic nature is empty.”
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, whatever awakening they possess is practiced neither by way of grasping nor by way of relinquishing; it is entirely without a locus of practice—meaning one does not practice with respect to form, nor does one practice with respect to feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.”
They do not course in the sense-base of the eye, nor do they course in the sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind;
they do not course in the sense-base of forms, nor do they course in the sense-bases of sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, or mental phenomena;
they do not course in the element of the eye, nor do they course in the elements of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind.
They do not course in the realm of form, nor do they course in the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena;
they do not course in the realm of eye-consciousness, nor do they course in the realms of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-consciousness;
they do not course in eye-contact, nor do they course in ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact.
They do not engage with the various feelings produced conditioned by eye-contact, nor do they engage with the various feelings produced conditioned by ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact;

they do not engage with the causal condition (*hetu-pratyaya*), nor do they engage with the immediately preceding condition (*samanantara-pratyaya*), the object-condition (*ālambana-pratyaya*), or the dominant condition (*adhipati-pratyaya*);
they do not engage with the phenomena produced from conditions.

One does not practice with regard to ignorance, nor does one practice with regard to volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, existence, birth, or old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair;

one does not practice with regard to the perfection of generosity, nor does one practice with regard to the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom.

They do not practice in internal emptiness, nor do they practice in external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature;

they do not practice in the four foundations of mindfulness, nor do they practice in the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path;
they do not practice in the noble truth of suffering, nor do they practice in the noble truths of the origin, cessation, or the path.
They do not practice the four dhyānas, nor do they practice the four immeasurables or the four formless absorptions;
they do not practice the eight liberations, nor do they practice the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive absorptions, or the ten totalities;
they do not practice the doors of dhāraṇī, nor do they practice the doors of samādhi.
They do not practice the liberation door of emptiness, nor do they practice the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness;

they do not practice the Ground of Extreme Joy, nor do they practice the Ground of Purity, the Ground of Radiance, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Difficult Victory, the Ground of Presence, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Good Intelligence, or the Ground of Dharma Clouds;
they do not practice the five eyes, nor do they practice the six supernormal powers.

They do not practice the ten powers of a Buddha, nor do they practice the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
they do not practice the thirty-two marks of a great man, nor do they practice the eighty secondary signs;
they do not practice the quality of non-forgetfulness, nor do they practice the state of constant abiding in equanimity.
They do not course in all-knowledge, nor do they course in the knowledge of the paths or the knowledge of all aspects;
they do not course in the fruit of stream-entry, nor do they course in the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, arhatship, or pratyekabuddha-enlightenment;
