they do not course in any of the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, nor do they course in the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Buddhas.

“Blessed One, would it not be that a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not practice the perfection of generosity, nor practices the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom;

does not practice inner emptiness, nor practices outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature?”

They do not practice the four foundations of mindfulness; they do not practice the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path;
they do not practice the noble truth of suffering, nor the noble truths of origin, cessation, or the path;
they do not practice the four dhyānas, nor the four immeasurables, nor the four formless absorptions.
They do not practice the eight liberations; they do not practice the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities;
they do not practice any of the doors of dhāraṇī, nor any of the doors of samādhi;
they do not practice the liberation door of emptiness, nor the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness.
They do not enter the bodhisattva’s state of certainty;

they do not practice the Ground of Extreme Joy, nor the Ground of Purity, the Ground of Radiant Light, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Difficult Victory, the Ground of Presence, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, or the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma;
they do not practice the five eyes, nor the six supernormal powers.

They do not practice the ten powers of a Buddha; they do not practice the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
they do not practice the thirty-two marks of a Great Man, nor the eighty minor marks;
they do not practice the quality of non-forgetfulness, nor the nature of constant abiding in equanimity.
Without practicing all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), without practicing the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) or the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*);

and without abiding in the sublime supernormal powers of a bodhisattva, in the ripening of sentient beings, and in the purification of Buddha-fields—how could one attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?
The Buddha said, “No, Subhūti!”
Although the bodhi of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas has no sphere of activity, nevertheless, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas must practice the perfections of giving,
ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; they must practice internal emptiness,
external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, and the emptiness of emptiness.
Great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, emptiness of dispersion, emptiness of non-alteration,
emptiness of intrinsic nature, emptiness of self-characteristic, emptiness of common characteristic,
emptiness of all phenomena, emptiness of non-apprehensibility, emptiness of non-existence, and emptiness of intrinsic nature.

Emptiness and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence; one must practice the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path;
one must practice the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path; one must practice the four dhyānas and the four immeasurables.

One must practice the four formless absorptions; one must practice the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten universal bases; one must practice all doors of dhāraṇī and all doors of samādhi;
one must practice the gate of liberation of emptiness, the signless, and the wishless; and one must enter the bodhisattva [path].
To enter the state of certainty beyond regression (samyaktva-niyāma), one must practice the ten stages:

the Stage of Extreme Joy, the Stage of Purity, the Stage of Radiance, the Stage of Blazing Wisdom, the Stage of Difficult Victory, the Stage of Presence, the Stage of Far-Going, the Immovable Stage, the Stage of Excellent Intelligence, and the Stage of the Cloud of Dharma;
one must practice the five eyes and the six supernormal powers; one must practice the Buddha[-nature].

The ten powers, the four fearlessnesses, the four unhindered analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; the essential practice of the thirty-two marks of a great man and the eighty secondary signs;
the essential practice of the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant abiding in equanimity; the essential practice.
All-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects must be attained by abiding in the sublime supernormal powers of a bodhisattva,
maturing sentient beings, and purifying buddha-fields, before one can attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Then, the Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying: “World-Honored One,

if the bodhi of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas has no sphere of activity, will it not be the case that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do not dwell in the perfection of giving, and do not dwell in the perfections of pure ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom for a long time, cultivating them until they are fulfilled?”

They do not dwell in internal emptiness, nor do they dwell in external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, having cultivated them for a long time until they are fulfilled;

they do not dwell in the four foundations of mindfulness, nor do they dwell in the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path, having cultivated them for a long time until they are fulfilled;
they do not dwell in the noble truth of suffering, nor do they dwell in the noble truths of the origin, cessation, or the path, having cultivated them for a long time until they are fulfilled.
They do not abide in the four dhyānas, nor do they abide in the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments, yet they cultivate them for a long time until they are perfected;

they do not abide in the eight liberations, nor do they abide in the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities, yet they cultivate them for a long time until they are perfected;
they do not abide in any of the doors of dhāraṇī, nor do they abide in any of the doors of samādhi, yet they cultivate them for a long time until they are perfected.
They do not abide in the liberation door of emptiness, nor do they abide in the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness, yet they cultivate them for a long time until they are fulfilled;

they do not enter the bodhisattva’s state of right determination (*samyaktva-niyāma*), nor do they abide in the Ground of Extreme Joy, nor do they abide in the Ground of Purity, the Ground of Radiance, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Difficult Victory, the Ground of Presence, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Good Intelligence, or the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma, yet they cultivate them for a long time until they are fulfilled;
they do not abide in the five eyes, nor do they abide in the six supernormal powers, yet they cultivate them for a long time until they are fulfilled.

They do not abide in the ten powers of a Buddha, nor do they abide in the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, while cultivating them for a long time to bring them to fulfillment;
they do not abide in the thirty-two marks of a Great Being, nor do they abide in the eighty minor marks, while cultivating them for a long time to bring them to fulfillment;
they do not abide in the quality of non-forgetfulness, nor do they abide in the nature of constant equanimity, while cultivating them for a long time to bring them to fulfillment.

Without dwelling in all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), without dwelling in the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) or the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), and having long cultivated them until they are fulfilled;

and without dwelling in the sublime supernormal powers of a bodhisattva, the maturing of sentient beings, or the purification of buddha-fields, how does one long cultivate these until they are fulfilled and attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?
The Buddha said, “No, Subhūti!”
Although the bodhi of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas has no sphere of activity,
those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas must dwell for a long time in the perfection of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence,
meditative concentration, and wisdom until they are fulfilled; they must dwell in internal emptiness, external emptiness, and internal-external emptiness...
Emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of the conditioned, the emptiness of the unconditioned,
absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of specific characteristics,
the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, and the emptiness of non-existence.
Having long cultivated and brought to fulfillment the emptiness of space, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence;

having long cultivated and brought to fulfillment the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path;
one must abide in the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path.

To bring the truths to fulfillment through long-term cultivation, one must dwell in the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments, cultivating them for a long time until they are fulfilled;

one must dwell in the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative absorptions, and the ten totalities, cultivating them for a long time until they are fulfilled; and one must dwell in all the doors of dhāraṇī and all the [samādhis]...

One must long cultivate and bring to fulfillment the gateways of meditative concentration (*samādhi*); one must dwell in and long cultivate to fulfillment the gates of liberation of emptiness (*śūnyatā*), signlessness (*animitta*), and wishlessness (*apraṇihita*);
one must enter the bodhisattva’s state of rightness and departure from birth (*samyaktva-niyāma*);

and one must dwell in the Ground of Utmost Joy (*pramuditā-bhūmi*), the Ground of Purity (*vimalā-bhūmi*), the Ground of Radiance (*prabhākārī-bhūmi*), the Ground of Blazing Wisdom (*arciṣmatī-bhūmi*), and the Ground Difficult to Conquer (*sudurjayā-bhūmi*).

Having long cultivated and brought to fulfillment the Ground of Presence (*abhimukhī*), the Ground of Far-Going (*dūraṃgamā*), the Ground of Immovability (*acalā*), the Ground of Excellent Intelligence (*sādhumatī*), and the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma (*dharmameghā*);
having necessarily dwelt in and long cultivated to fulfillment the five eyes (*pañca-cakṣus*) and the six superknowledges (*ṣaḍ-abhijñā*);

and having necessarily dwelt in the ten powers of a Buddha (*daśa-tathāgatabala*), the four fearlessnesses (*catvāri vaiśāradyāni*), the four analytical knowledges (*catasraḥ pratisamvidah*), great loving-kindness (*mahāmaitrī*), and great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*).

Having long cultivated and brought to fulfillment joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, one must abide in the thirty-two marks of a Great Being and the eighty minor marks, long cultivating them until they are fulfilled;

one must abide in the quality of non-forgetfulness and the nature of constant equanimity, long cultivating them until they are fulfilled; and one must abide in all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) and the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*).
Having long cultivated and brought to fulfillment the knowledge of all aspects, and having long cultivated and brought to fulfillment the sublime supernormal powers of a bodhisattva—
thereby maturing sentient beings and purifying buddha-fields— one then attains unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva has not yet brought the cultivation of all roots of goodness to ultimate perfection, they will ultimately be unable to attain the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment they seek."

"Furthermore, Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, they should abide in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of form; they should abide in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness;

they should abide in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the sense base of the eye; and they should abide in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind."

One should dwell in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the sphere of form; one should dwell in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena.

One should dwell in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the eye constituent; one should dwell in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the constituents of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.

One should dwell in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the form constituent; one should dwell in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the constituents of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, and mental phenomena.

One should abide in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the eye-consciousness element; one should abide in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements.
One should abide in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of eye-contact; one should abide in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact.

One should abide in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition; one should abide in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of all feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions.
One should dwell in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the earth element; one should dwell in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements;

one should dwell in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of causes and conditions; one should dwell in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the immediately preceding condition, the object-condition, and the dominant condition;
and one should dwell in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of all phenomena produced from conditions.

One should abide in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of ignorance; one should abide in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair;

one should abide in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the perfection of generosity; and one should abide in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.

One should abide in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of internal emptiness; one should abide in the emptiness of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, emptiness of intrinsic nature, emptiness of specific characteristics, emptiness of common characteristics, emptiness of all phenomena, emptiness of the unapprehendable, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of self-nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the non-existence of self-nature.

One should abide in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the four foundations of mindfulness; one should abide in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.

One should abide in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the noble truth of suffering; one should abide in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path.
One should dwell in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the four dhyānas; one should dwell in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments;

one should dwell in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the eight liberations; one should dwell in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities; one should dwell in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the doors of dhāraṇī; one should dwell in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the doors of samādhi;

one should dwell in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the gate of liberation through emptiness; and one should dwell in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the gates of liberation through signlessness and wishlessness.

One should dwell in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the Ground of Utmost Joy; one should dwell in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the Ground of Freedom from Defilement, the Ground of Radiance, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Extreme Difficulty to Conquer, the Ground of Presence, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, and the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma;
one should dwell in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the five eyes; one should dwell in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the six supernormal powers;

one should dwell in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the ten powers of a Buddha; and one should dwell in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
One should abide in the emptiness of the essential nature of the thirty-two marks of a great man; one should abide in the emptiness of the essential nature of the eighty minor marks;
one should abide in the emptiness of the essential nature of the quality of non-forgetfulness; one should abide in the emptiness of the essential nature of the state of constant equanimity;

one should abide in the emptiness of the essential nature of all-knowledge; and one should abide in the emptiness of the essential nature of the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects.

One should dwell in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the fruit of stream-entry; one should dwell in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship, as well as in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment;

one should dwell in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of all bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices, and one should dwell in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas;

one should dwell in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of all phenomena and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of all sentient beings. Having cultivated all meritorious qualities until they are perfected, one then realizes unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

“Subhūti! This intrinsic emptiness of all phenomena and the intrinsic emptiness of sentient beings are utterly quiescent; there is not the slightest phenomenon that can increase or decrease, arise or cease, be annihilated or eternal, be defiled or purified, or attain a fruit or realize clear observation.”
“Subhūti, you should know this:

it is by relying on the conventional designations of dharmas that a bodhisattva mahāsattva is said to cultivate the perfection of wisdom; having realized the emptiness of intrinsic nature as it truly is, they attain unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment—this is not, however, the ultimate truth.”
Why is this? Because within true ultimate reality, form cannot be apprehended, nor can feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness be apprehended;
the eye-base cannot be apprehended, nor can the bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind be apprehended.
The sphere of formlessness cannot be apprehended, nor can the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena be apprehended;
the eye-element cannot be apprehended, nor can the elements of the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind be apprehended;
the form-element cannot be apprehended, nor can the elements of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena be apprehended.
The eye-consciousness element cannot be apprehended, nor can the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-consciousness elements be apprehended;
eye-contact cannot be apprehended, nor can ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact be apprehended;

and the various sensations produced with eye-contact as a condition cannot be apprehended, nor can the various sensations produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as a condition be apprehended.
The earth element cannot be apprehended, nor can the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements be apprehended;
no causal conditions can be apprehended, nor can the immediately preceding condition, the object-condition, or the dominant condition be apprehended;
and no phenomena produced from conditions can be apprehended.

Ignorance cannot be apprehended, nor can volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, existence, birth, or old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair be apprehended;
neither can the perfection of generosity be apprehended, nor can the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom be apprehended.

One cannot apprehend internal emptiness, nor can one apprehend external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature;

one cannot apprehend the four foundations of mindfulness, nor can one apprehend the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path;
one cannot apprehend the noble truth of suffering, nor can one apprehend the noble truths of origination, cessation, or the path.
The four dhyānas are not to be found, nor are the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments to be found;
the eight liberations are not to be found, nor are the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities to be found;
the doors of dhāraṇī are not to be found, nor are the doors of samādhi to be found.
The liberation door of emptiness cannot be apprehended, nor can the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness;

the Ground of Utmost Joy cannot be apprehended, nor can the Ground of Purity, the Ground of Radiance, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Difficult Victory, the Ground of Presence, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Good Intelligence, or the Ground of the Dharma Cloud;
the five eyes cannot be apprehended, nor can the six supernormal powers.

The ten powers of a Buddha cannot be apprehended, nor can the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
the thirty-two marks of a Great Man cannot be apprehended, nor can the eighty secondary signs;
the quality of non-forgetfulness cannot be apprehended, nor can the nature of constant abiding in equanimity.
There is no omniscience (sarvajñatā) to be attained, nor is there any knowledge of the paths (mārgajñatā) or knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā) to be attained;
there is no fruit of stream-entry (srotāpattiphala) to be attained, nor are there the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, arhatship, or the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha to be attained;
there is no conduct of any bodhisattva mahāsattva to be attained, nor is there the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi) of any buddha to be attained.
No practitioner of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva path can be apprehended, nor can one who practices for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment be apprehended.
Subhūti! Thus all these phenomena are established by means of conventional designations; they do not depend on the ultimate truth.

“Subhūti! When bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, although from their first production of the thought of enlightenment they engage in the conduct of awakening for the sake of all sentient beings with extreme vigor, they do not apprehend this mind at all; they do not apprehend sentient beings; they do not apprehend great awakening; and they do not apprehend Buddhas or bodhisattvas.”
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
If all dharmas are entirely non-existent and all are unobtainable, how does a bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the conduct of enlightenment?"
"How can one attain unsurpassed enlightenment?
The Buddha told Subhūti: "What do you think?"

In the past, by relying on the realm of abandonment, you severed all afflictions and attained the untainted faculties; dwelling in the concentration of immediate succession, you attained the fruit of stream-entry, or the fruit of once-returning, or the fruit of non-returning, or the fruit of arhatship. At that time, did you perceive any sentient being—whether their mind, their path, or the fruits of the various paths—as something that could be apprehended?
Subhūti replied, “No, World-Honored One!”
"No, Sugata," he replied. The Buddha said:
“Subhūti! If at that time you had not apprehended anything at all, how could you say that you attained the fruit of arhatship? Subhūti replied:
"It is spoken according to conventional truth, not according to ultimate truth.
The Buddha told Subhūti: "So it is!"
So it is! It is just as you have said.

All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas likewise rely on conventional discourse to practice the conduct of awakening and to attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, rather than relying on the ultimate truth.
“Subhūti! It is by way of worldly convention that there is the designation of ‘form,’ and the designation of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness;
it is by way of worldly convention that there is the designation of the eye-base, and the designation of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-bases.”
Based on worldly convention, there is the designation of the form base; based on worldly convention, there is the designation of the sound, odor, taste, tangible, and mental-object bases.
Based on worldly convention, there is the designation of the eye constituent; based on worldly convention, there is the designation of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind constituents.
Based on worldly convention, there is the designation of the form element; based on worldly convention, there is the designation of the sound, odor, taste, tangible, and mental-object elements.

Based on worldly convention, there is the designation of the eye-consciousness element; based on worldly convention, there are the designations of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-consciousness elements.
Based on worldly convention, there is the designation of eye-contact; based on worldly convention, there are the designations of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact.

Based on worldly convention, there is the designation of all feelings produced with eye-contact as condition; based on worldly convention, there are the designations of all feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact as conditions.
Based on worldly convention, there is the designation of the earth element; based on worldly convention, there are the designations of the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements.

Based on worldly convention, there is the designation of causes and conditions; based on worldly convention, there are the designations of the immediately preceding condition, the object condition, and the dominant condition.
Based on worldly convention, there are the designations of all phenomena that arise from conditions.

Based on worldly convention, there is the designation of ignorance; there is the designation of volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.

Based on worldly convention, there is the designation of the perfection of generosity; there is the designation of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.

Based on worldly convention, there is the designation of internal emptiness; there is the designation of external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

Based on worldly convention, there is the designation of the four foundations of mindfulness; there is the designation of the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.

Based on worldly convention, there is the designation of the noble truth of suffering; based on worldly convention, there is the designation of the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path.
Based on worldly convention, there is the designation of the four dhyānas; based on worldly convention, there is the designation of the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments.

Based on worldly convention, there is the designation of the eight liberations; based on worldly convention, there is the designation of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities.
Based on worldly convention, there is the designation of the gateways of dhāraṇī; based on worldly convention, there is the designation of the gateways of samādhi.
Based on worldly convention, there is the designation of the emptiness liberation gateway; based on worldly convention, there is the designation of the signless and wishless liberation gateways.

Based on worldly convention, there is the designation of the Ground of Utmost Joy; based on worldly convention, there is the designation of the Ground of Purity, the Ground of Radiance, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Difficult to Conquer, the Ground of Manifestation, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, and the Ground of Dharma Clouds.
Based on worldly convention, the five eyes are provisionally established; based on worldly convention, the six supernormal powers are provisionally established.

Based on worldly convention, the ten powers of a Buddha are provisionally established; based on worldly convention, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are provisionally established.
Based on worldly convention, the thirty-two marks of a Great Man are provisionally established; based on worldly convention, the eighty secondary signs are provisionally established.
Based on worldly convention, one designates the "qualities of non-forgetfulness" and designates the "nature of constant equanimity";
based on worldly convention, one designates "omniscience," designates "knowledge of the aspects of the path," and designates "knowledge of all aspects";
based on worldly convention, one designates the "fruit of stream-entry," and designates the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, arhatship, and the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha.
It is by relying on worldly convention that one designates the existence of all the practices of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and designates the unexcelled, perfect enlightenment of all buddhas;
it is by relying on worldly convention that one designates sentient beings, and designates bodhisattvas and the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones—it is not by relying on the ultimate truth.

“Subhūti! Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do not perceive any dharma that can increase or decrease, benefit or harm, in regard to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, because all dharmas are empty by their very nature.”
"Subhūti! Since even the intrinsic emptiness of all phenomena cannot be apprehended by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, how much less can an initial resolve to attain enlightenment be apprehended!"
How much less could there be anything to be obtained through the cultivation of the perfection of generosity!
How much less could there be anything to be obtained through the cultivation of the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom!
How much less could there be anything to be apprehended while dwelling in internal emptiness!

How much less could there be anything to be apprehended while dwelling in external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, the emptiness of dispersion, the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self-characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of self-nature, or the emptiness of the self-nature of non-existence!
How much less could there be anything to be attained through the cultivation of the four foundations of mindfulness!

How much less could there be anything to be attained through the cultivation of the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path!
How much less can there be anything to be attained by abiding in the noble truth of suffering!
How much less can there be anything to be attained by abiding in the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path!
How much less can there be anything to be attained by practicing the four dhyānas!
How much less could there be anything to be attained through the cultivation of the four immeasurables or the four formless absorptions!
How much less could there be anything to be attained through the cultivation of the eight liberations!
How much less could there be anything to be attained through the cultivation of the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive absorptions, or the ten totalities!
How much less can there be anything to be attained by practicing the gateways of dhāraṇī!
How much less can there be anything to be attained by practicing the gateways of samādhi!
How much less can there be anything to be attained by practicing the gateway of the liberation of emptiness!
How much less could there be anything to be attained in the cultivation of the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness!
How much less could there be anything to be attained in the cultivation of the Ground of Utmost Joy!

How much less could there be anything to be attained in the cultivation of the Ground of Purity, the Ground of Radiance, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Utmost Difficulty to Conquer, the Ground of Presence, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, or the Ground of the Dharma Cloud!
How much less could there be anything to be attained through the cultivation of the five eyes!
How much less could there be anything to be attained through the cultivation of the six supernormal powers!
How much less could there be anything to be attained through the cultivation of the ten powers of a Buddha!

How much less could there be anything to be attained through the cultivation of the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha!
How much less could there be anything to be attained by cultivating the thirty-two marks of a great man!
How much less could there be anything to be attained by cultivating the eighty secondary signs!
How much less could there be anything to be attained by cultivating the quality of non-forgetfulness!
How much less can there be anything to be attained by cultivating the nature of constant equanimity!
How much less can there be anything to be attained by cultivating omniscience!
How much less can there be anything to be attained by cultivating the knowledge of the aspects of the path or the knowledge of all aspects!
How much less can there be anything to be attained when practicing all the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva!
How much less can there be anything to be attained when practicing the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas!
“Subhūti! It is impossible for bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, while dwelling in the cultivation of any of the Buddha-dharmas, to have any apprehension of them.
Thus it is, Subhūti!”

All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; having realized unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, they constantly and uninterruptedly benefit sentient beings.
Chapter 71: Maturing Sentient Beings, Part One. At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of generosity, and practices the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom;

and abides in internal emptiness, abides in external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature;

They practice the four foundations of mindfulness; they practice the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path;
they abide in the noble truth of suffering, and they abide in the noble truths of the origin, cessation, and the path;
they practice the four dhyānas, and they practice the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions.
They practice the eight liberations; they practice the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive concentrations, and the ten totalities;
they practice the gates of dhāraṇī, and they practice the gates of samādhi;
they practice the gate of the liberation of emptiness, and they practice the gates of the liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.

They practice the Ground of Perfect Joy; they practice the Ground of Purity, the Ground of Radiance, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Difficult Victory, the Ground of Presence, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Good Intelligence, and the Ground of the Dharma Cloud.
They practice the five eyes; they practice the six supernormal powers.

They practice the ten powers of a Buddha; they practice the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
They cultivate the thirty-two marks of a great man and the eighty minor marks;
they cultivate the quality of non-forgetfulness and cultivate the state of constant abiding in equanimity;
they cultivate all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects.
One practices all the deeds of a bodhisattva mahāsattva and practices the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas;
yet if one does not fully complete the practice of the bodhisattva path, one cannot realize the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment that is sought.
“World-Honored One!
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivate the bodhisattva path so as to bring it to full completion and be able to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?
The Buddha told Subhūti:

“If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, practices the perfection of generosity through skillful means, does not apprehend the gift, does not apprehend the giver, does not apprehend that which is given, and does not apprehend the purpose for which it is given—and yet does not practice the perfection of generosity by remaining apart from these phenomena—then this bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to fulfill the cultivation of the bodhisattva path.”

"Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, and through skillful means practices the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, they do not apprehend ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or wisdom; they do not apprehend the one who practices, nor that which is practiced, nor the purpose for which it is practiced. Furthermore, they do not practice the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom while remaining apart from these dharmas. It is in this way that a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to bring the cultivation of the bodhisattva path to fulfillment."
Thus it is, Subhūti!

When bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they cultivate the bodhisattva path through skillful means until it is brought to fulfillment, and are thus able to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom and, through skillful means, abides in internal emptiness, yet does not apprehend internal emptiness, does not apprehend that which abides, does not apprehend that wherein one abides, does not apprehend that for which it is done, and furthermore does not abide in internal emptiness by being separated from these dharmas—then this bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to fulfill the cultivation of the bodhisattva path.”
"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they skillfully employ means to abide in external emptiness,
internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, and conditioned emptiness..."
When [one contemplates] emptiness, the emptiness of the unconditioned, ultimate emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersal emptiness, the emptiness of non-alteration,
the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of common characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility,
the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, one does not...
Having attained the emptiness of the external up to the emptiness of the nature of non-entities, they do not apprehend that which abides, nor that in which one abides, nor that for which it is done;
yet they do not dwell apart from these dharmas while dwelling in the emptiness of the external up to the emptiness of the nature of non-entities.
Such a bodhisattva mahāsattva is then able to fulfill the cultivation of the bodhisattva path.

In this way, Subhūti, bodhisattva mahāsattvas practicing the perfection of wisdom, through skillful means, cultivate the bodhisattva path until it is brought to fulfillment, and are thus able to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

"Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom and, through skillful means, practices the four applications of mindfulness, they do not apprehend the four applications of mindfulness, they do not apprehend the one who practices, they do not apprehend that which is practiced, nor do they apprehend the purpose for which it is practiced. Furthermore, they practice the four applications of mindfulness without being separated from these dharmas; in this way, that bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to fulfill the cultivation of the bodhisattva path."

"Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, skillfully practicing the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path, they do not apprehend the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path; they do not apprehend the one who practices, they do not apprehend that which is practiced, and they do not apprehend that for which it is practiced. Furthermore, they do not practice the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path by remaining apart from these dharmas. It is in this way that a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to fulfill the cultivation of the bodhisattva path."
Thus it is, Subhūti!

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they cultivate the bodhisattva path through skillful means until it is brought to fulfillment, and are thereby able to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle Three Hundred and Ninety-Three. Translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One: Chapter Seventy-One, "Maturing Sentient Beings," Section Two. "Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, skillfully abides in the noble truth of suffering, yet does not apprehend the noble truth of suffering, does not apprehend that which abides, does not apprehend that in which one abides, and does not apprehend that for which it is done—and furthermore, does not abide in the noble truth of suffering by being separated from such dharmas—then this bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to fulfill the cultivation of the bodhisattva path.

"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, dwells through skillful means in the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path, yet does not apprehend the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path; does not apprehend that which dwells, does not apprehend that wherein one dwells, and does not apprehend that for which one acts; and furthermore, does not dwell in the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path by being separated from these dharmas—then this bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to fulfill the cultivation of the bodhisattva path."
Thus it is, Subhūti!

When bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they cultivate the bodhisattva path through skillful means until it is brought to fulfillment, and are thereby able to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom and, through skillful means, practices the four dhyānas, they do not apprehend the four dhyānas, they do not apprehend the one who practices, they do not apprehend that which is practiced, nor do they apprehend the purpose for which it is practiced; furthermore, they practice the four dhyānas without being separated from these dharmas. In this way, that bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to bring the cultivation of the bodhisattva path to fulfillment.”

"Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, practicing the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions through skillful means, they do not apprehend the four immeasurables or the four formless absorptions; they do not apprehend the one who practices, nor that which is practiced, nor the purpose for which it is practiced. Furthermore, they do not practice the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions by remaining apart from these dharmas. It is in this way that a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to fulfill the cultivation of the bodhisattva path."
Thus it is, Subhūti!

When bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they cultivate the bodhisattva path through skillful means until it is brought to fulfillment, and are thereby able to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom and, through skillful means, practices the eight liberations while not apprehending the eight liberations, not apprehending that which practices them, not apprehending that which is practiced, and not apprehending that for which it is practiced—and yet does not practice the eight liberations by being separated from such dharmas—then this bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to fulfill the cultivation of the bodhisattva path.”

Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, practicing the eight bases of mastery (*aṣṭau abhibhvāyatanāni*), the nine successive attainments (*navānupūrvavihārasamāpattayaḥ*), and the ten totalities (*daśa kṛtsnāyatanāni*) through skillful means, they do not apprehend the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities; they do not apprehend the one who practices, the practice itself, or the purpose for which it is practiced. Furthermore, they do not practice the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities by remaining apart from these dharmas. It is in this way that the bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to fulfill the cultivation of the bodhisattva path.
Thus it is, Subhūti!

When bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they cultivate the path of a bodhisattva through skillful means until it is brought to fulfillment, thereby enabling them to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom and, through skillful means, practices all the gateways of dhāraṇī, they do not apprehend any gateway of dhāraṇī; they do not apprehend that which practices, they do not apprehend that which is practiced, nor do they apprehend that for which it is practiced. Furthermore, they practice all the gateways of dhāraṇī without being separated from these very dharmas. It is in this way that a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to fulfill the cultivation of the bodhisattva path.”

"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom and, through skillful means, practices all the gateways of samādhi while not apprehending any of those gateways of samādhi, not apprehending that which practices, not apprehending that which is practiced, and not apprehending that for which it is practiced—and yet does not practice the gateways of samādhi by being separated from these dharmas—then this bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to fulfill the cultivation of the bodhisattva path."
Thus it is, Subhūti!

When bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they cultivate the bodhisattva path through skillful means until it is brought to fulfillment, and are thereby able to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom and, through skillful means, practices the gate of liberation that is emptiness, they do not apprehend the gate of liberation that is emptiness, they do not apprehend the one who practices, they do not apprehend that which is practiced, nor do they apprehend the purpose for which it is practiced; furthermore, they do not practice the gate of liberation that is emptiness by remaining apart from these dharmas. It is in this way that a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to bring the cultivation of the bodhisattva path to fulfillment.”

"Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom and, through skillful means, practices the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, they do not apprehend the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness; they do not apprehend that which practices, they do not apprehend that which is practiced, and they do not apprehend that for which it is practiced. Furthermore, they do not practice the gateways of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness by remaining apart from these phenomena. It is in this way that a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to fulfill the cultivation of the bodhisattva path."
Thus it is, Subhūti!

When bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they cultivate the bodhisattva path through skillful means until it is brought to fulfillment, and are thereby able to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom and, through skillful means, practices the Stage of Extreme Joy (*pramuditā-bhūmi*), they do not apprehend the Stage of Extreme Joy, they do not apprehend that which practices it, they do not apprehend that which is practiced, nor do they apprehend the purpose for which it is practiced. Furthermore, they practice the Stage of Extreme Joy without being separated from these dharmas; in this way, that bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to bring the cultivation of the bodhisattva path to fulfillment.”

"Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, skillfully practicing the Ground of Freedom from Defilement, the Ground of Radiance, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Utmost Difficulty to Conquer, the Ground of Manifestation, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, and the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma—at that time, they do not apprehend the Ground of Freedom from Defilement up to the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma; they do not apprehend the one who practices, they do not apprehend that which is practiced, and they do not apprehend that for which it is practiced. Furthermore, they do not practice the Ground of Freedom from Defilement up to the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma by being separated from these dharmas. It is in this way that a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to fulfill the cultivation of the bodhisattva path."
Thus it is, Subhūti!

When bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they cultivate the bodhisattva path through skillful means until it is brought to fulfillment, and are thereby able to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

“Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom and, through skillful means, practices the five eyes, they do not apprehend the five eyes, they do not apprehend that which can practice them, they do not apprehend that which is practiced, nor do they apprehend that for which it is practiced; furthermore, they do not practice the five eyes by being detached from these dharmas. It is in this way that a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to fulfill the cultivation of the bodhisattva path.”

"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom and, through skillful means, practices the six supernormal powers (*ṣaḍabhijñā*), yet does not apprehend the six supernormal powers, does not apprehend that which practices them, does not apprehend that which is practiced, and does not apprehend that for which they are practiced—and furthermore, does not practice the six supernormal powers by being separated from these dharmas—then this bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to fulfill the cultivation of the bodhisattva path."
Thus it is, Subhūti!

When bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they cultivate the bodhisattva path through skillful means until it is brought to fulfillment, and are thereby able to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom and, through skillful means, practices the ten powers of a buddha, they do not apprehend the ten powers of a buddha; they do not apprehend that which practices them, nor that which is practiced, nor that for which it is done. Furthermore, they practice the ten powers of a buddha without being separated from these dharmas. In this way, that bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to bring the cultivation of the bodhisattva path to fulfillment.”

Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, skillfully employing means to practice the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, they do not apprehend the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha; they do not apprehend that which practices, they do not apprehend that which is practiced, and they do not apprehend that for which it is done. Furthermore, they do not practice the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha while remaining apart from these dharmas. It is in this way that a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to fulfill the cultivation of the bodhisattva path.
Thus it is, Subhūti!

When bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they cultivate the bodhisattva path through skillful means until it is brought to fulfillment, and are thereby able to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom and, through skillful means, practices the thirty-two marks of a great man, they do not apprehend the thirty-two marks of a great man; they do not apprehend that which practices, they do not apprehend that which is practiced, and they do not apprehend that for which it is practiced. Furthermore, they do not practice the thirty-two marks of a great man by remaining apart from these dharmas. It is in this way that a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to fulfill the practice of the bodhisattva path.”

"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom and, through skillful means, practices the eighty minor marks while not apprehending the eighty minor marks, not apprehending that which practices, not apprehending that which is practiced, and not apprehending that for which it is practiced—yet without being separated from these dharmas—practices the eighty minor marks, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to fulfill the cultivation of the bodhisattva path."
Thus it is, Subhūti!

When bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they cultivate the bodhisattva path through skillful means until it is brought to fulfillment, and are thereby able to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom and, through skillful means, practices the dharma of non-forgetfulness, they do not apprehend the dharma of non-forgetfulness, they do not apprehend that which practices it, they do not apprehend that which is practiced, nor do they apprehend that for which it is done; furthermore, they practice the dharma of non-forgetfulness without being separated from these dharmas. It is in this way that a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to fulfill the cultivation of the bodhisattva path.”

"Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom and, through skillful means, practices the state of constant equanimity (upekṣā-vihāra), they do not apprehend the state of constant equanimity, they do not apprehend the one who practices, they do not apprehend that which is practiced, and they do not apprehend that for which it is practiced; yet, they do not practice the state of constant equanimity by remaining apart from these dharmas. It is in this way that a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to bring the cultivation of the bodhisattva path to fulfillment."
Thus it is, Subhūti!

When bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they cultivate the path of a bodhisattva through skillful means until it is brought to fulfillment, and are thereby able to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom and, through skillful means, practices for the sake of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), they do not apprehend all-knowledge, they do not apprehend that which practices, they do not apprehend that which is practiced, and they do not apprehend that for which it is practiced; yet, they do not practice for all-knowledge by remaining apart from these dharmas. It is in this way that a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to fulfill the cultivation of the bodhisattva path.”

"Subhūti! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom and, through skillful means, practices the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects, yet does not apprehend the knowledge of the aspects of the path or the knowledge of all aspects; does not apprehend that which practices, does not apprehend that which is practiced, and does not apprehend that for which it is practiced; and furthermore, does not practice the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects while remaining apart from these dharmas—then this bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to fulfill the cultivation of the bodhisattva path."
Thus it is, Subhūti!

When bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they cultivate the bodhisattva path through skillful means until it is brought to fulfillment, thereby enabling them to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom and, through skillful means, practices all the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, they do not apprehend any practice of a bodhisattva mahāsattva; they do not apprehend that which can practice, they do not apprehend that which is practiced, and they do not apprehend that for which it is done. Furthermore, they do not practice the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva while remaining apart from these dharmas. It is in this way that a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to fulfill the cultivation of the bodhisattva path.”

“Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom and, through skillful means, practices the unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas, they do not apprehend unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment; they do not apprehend that which can practice it, nor that which is practiced, nor that for which it is practiced. Furthermore, they do not practice the unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas by remaining apart from these dharmas. It is in this way that a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to fulfill the cultivation of the bodhisattva path.”
Thus it is, Subhūti!

When bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they cultivate the bodhisattva path through skillful means until it is brought to fulfillment, thereby enabling them to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra addressed the Buddha,
saying: “World-Honored One,
how does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the perfection of wisdom, cultivate the path to enlightenment with courageous and correct diligence?”
The Buddha said,
“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom through skillful means, they do not conjoin form, nor do they disperse form;”
One does not unite with feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, nor does one separate from feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.
Why is this? Because all such phenomena lack an intrinsic nature that could be joined or separated.
“Śāriputra! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom through skillful means, they do not conjoin the sense base of the eye, nor do they disperse the sense base of the eye;
they do not conjoin the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, nor do they disperse the sense bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.”
Why is this? Because all such phenomena lack any intrinsic nature that could be joined or separated. "Śāriputra!..."
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom through skillful means, they do not combine the sphere of form, nor do they disperse the sphere of form;
they do not combine the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena, nor do they disperse the spheres of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena.
Why is this? Because all such phenomena lack an intrinsic nature that could be joined or separated. "Śāriputra!..."
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom through skillful means, they do not conjoin the eye-element, nor do they disperse the eye-element;
they do not conjoin the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-element, nor do they disperse the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-element.
Why is this? Because all such phenomena lack an intrinsic nature that could be joined or separated. "Śāriputra!..."
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom through skillful means, they do not conjoin with the realm of form, nor do they disperse the realm of form;
they do not conjoin with the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena, nor do they disperse the realms of sound, odor, taste, tangibility, or mental phenomena.
Why is this? Because all such phenomena lack an intrinsic nature that could either be joined or separated. "Śāriputra!..."
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom with skillful means, they do not conjoin the eye-consciousness element, nor do they disperse the eye-consciousness element;
they do not conjoin the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-consciousness elements, nor do they disperse the ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-consciousness elements.
Why is this? Because all such phenomena lack any intrinsic nature that could be joined or separated. "Śāriputra!..."
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom through skillful means, they do not conjoin eye-contact, nor do they disperse eye-contact;
they do not conjoin ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact, nor do they disperse ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact.
Why is this? Because all such phenomena lack any intrinsic nature that could be joined or separated. "Śāriputra!..."

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom with skillful means, they do not conjoin the feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition, nor do they disperse the feelings produced with eye-contact as a condition;

they do not conjoin the feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as a condition, nor do they disperse the feelings produced with ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind-contact as a condition.
Why is this? Because all such phenomena lack an intrinsic nature that can be joined or separated. "Śāriputra!..."
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom through skillful means, they do not combine the earth element nor do they disperse the earth element;
they do not combine the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements, nor do they disperse the water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness elements.
Why is this? Because all such phenomena lack an intrinsic nature that could either be joined or separated. "Śāriputra!..."
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they employ skillful means such that they do not conjoin causal conditions, nor do they disperse them;

they do not conjoin the equal-and-immediate condition, the object-condition, or the dominant condition, nor do they disperse the equal-and-immediate condition, the object-condition, or the dominant condition.
Why is this? Because all such phenomena lack any intrinsic nature that could be joined or separated. "Śāriputra!..."
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they employ skillful means such that they neither conjoin nor disperse the phenomena that arise from conditions.
Why is this? Because all such phenomena lack an intrinsic nature that could be joined or separated. "Śāriputra!..."
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom through skillful means, they do not conjoin ignorance, nor do they disperse ignorance;

they do not conjoin volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, or aging, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair, nor do they disperse these factors from volitional formations up to aging, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.
Why is this? Because all such phenomena lack an intrinsic nature that could be joined or separated. "Śāriputra!..."
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they employ skillful means such that they do not conjoin the perfection of giving, nor do they disperse the perfection of giving;

they do not conjoin the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, nor do they disperse the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
Why is this? Because all such phenomena lack any intrinsic nature that could be joined or separated. "Śāriputra!..."
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom through skillful means, they do not conjoin inner emptiness, nor do they disperse inner emptiness;

they do not conjoin outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, emptiness of all phenomena, unapprehendable emptiness, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of intrinsic nature, or emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, nor do they disperse outer emptiness up to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
Why is this? Because all such phenomena lack any intrinsic nature that could be joined or separated. "Śāriputra!..."

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom through skillful means, they do not conjoin the four foundations of mindfulness, nor do they disperse the four foundations of mindfulness;

they do not conjoin the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path, nor do they disperse the four right endeavors up to the eightfold noble path.
Why is this? Because all such phenomena lack any intrinsic nature that could be joined or separated. "Śāriputra!..."
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom through skillful means, they do not conjoin the noble truth of suffering, nor do they disperse the noble truth of suffering;
they do not conjoin the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path, nor do they disperse the noble truths of origination, cessation, and the path.
Why is this? Because all such phenomena lack an intrinsic nature that could be joined or separated. "Śāriputra!..."
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, through skillful means, they do not combine the four dhyānas nor do they disperse the four dhyānas;
they do not combine the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments, nor do they disperse the four immeasurables or the four formless attainments.
Why is this? Because all such phenomena lack any intrinsic nature that could be joined or separated. "Śāriputra!..."
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they employ skillful means such that they do not conjoin with the eight liberations, nor do they disperse the eight liberations;

they do not conjoin with the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities, nor do they disperse the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities.
Why is this? Because all such phenomena lack an intrinsic nature that could either be joined or separated. "Śāriputra!..."
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom through skillful means, they do not conjoin the gateways of dhāraṇī, nor do they disperse the gateways of dhāraṇī;
they do not conjoin the gateways of samādhi, nor do they disperse the gateways of samādhi.
Why is this? Because all such phenomena lack an intrinsic nature that could be joined or separated. "Śāriputra!..."

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom with skillful means, they do not conjoin with the gate of liberation of emptiness, nor do they disperse the gate of liberation of emptiness;
they do not conjoin with the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness, nor do they disperse the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.
Why is this? Because all such phenomena lack any intrinsic nature that could be joined or separated. "Śāriputra!..."
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom with skillful means, they do not combine with the Stage of Extreme Joy, nor do they separate from the Stage of Extreme Joy;

they do not combine with the Stage of Purity, the Stage of Radiance, the Stage of Blazing Wisdom, the Stage of Difficult Victory, the Stage of Presence, the Stage of Far-Going, the Immovable Stage, the Stage of Good Intelligence, or the Stage of the Cloud of Dharma, nor do they separate from these stages from the Stage of Purity up to the Stage of the Cloud of Dharma.
Why is this? Because all such phenomena lack an intrinsic nature that could either be joined or separated. "Śāriputra!..."
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom through skillful means, they do not conjoin the five eyes nor do they disperse them;
they do not conjoin the six supernormal powers nor do they disperse them.
Why is this? Because all such phenomena lack any intrinsic nature that could be joined or separated. "Śāriputra!..."
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom through skillful means, they do not conjoin the ten powers of a buddha, nor do they disperse the ten powers of a buddha;

they do not conjoin the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, nor do they disperse these qualities from the four fearlessnesses up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha.
Why is this? Because all such phenomena lack an intrinsic nature that could be joined or separated. "Śāriputra!..."

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom through skillful means, they do not combine the thirty-two marks of a great man, nor do they disperse the thirty-two marks of a great man;
they do not combine the eighty secondary signs, nor do they disperse the eighty secondary signs.
Why is this? Because all such phenomena lack an intrinsic nature that could be joined or separated. "Śāriputra!..."
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom through skillful means, they do not conjoin the quality of non-forgetfulness, nor do they disperse it;
they do not conjoin the state of constant abiding in equanimity, nor do they disperse it.
Why is this? Because all such phenomena lack any intrinsic nature that could be joined or separated. "Śāriputra!..."
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom through skillful means, they do not conjoin with all-knowledge, nor do they disperse all-knowledge;
they do not conjoin with the knowledge of the aspects of the path or the knowledge of all aspects, nor do they disperse the knowledge of the aspects of the path or the knowledge of all aspects.
Why is this? Because all such phenomena lack any intrinsic nature that could be joined or separated. "Śāriputra!..."
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom with skillful means, they do not conjoin with the fruit of stream-entry, nor do they disperse from the fruit of stream-entry;

they do not conjoin with the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, arhatship, or pratyekabuddha enlightenment, nor do they disperse from the fruits of once-returner, non-returner, arhatship, or pratyekabuddha enlightenment.
Why is this? Because all such phenomena lack an intrinsic nature that could be joined or separated. "Śāriputra!..."
