to conceive the notion of worldly phenomena where there are no worldly phenomena; to conceive the notion of supramundane phenomena where there are no supramundane phenomena;
to conceive the notion of tainted phenomena where there are no tainted phenomena; and to conceive the notion of untainted phenomena where there are no untainted phenomena.
Within that which is not conditioned, they give rise to the perception of the conditioned; within that which is not unconditioned, they give rise to the perception of the unconditioned.

Thus, through the power of such inverted discrimination, they conceive of what is not truly existent as being truly existent. Clinging falsely to this, their minds are deranged, and they perform various wholesome and unwholesome deeds of body, speech, and mind. Unable to be liberated from the cycle of birth and death in the evil realms, I shall rescue them and cause them to attain liberation.

“Subhūti! Having formed this thought, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*). By subsuming all wholesome dharmas within the perfection of wisdom, they practice the various bodhisattva deeds without error. Gradually fulfilling the provisions for enlightenment (*bodhisambhāra*), and having fulfilled those provisions for enlightenment, they realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete awakening (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*).”

Having attained awakening, he proclaims, reveals, analyzes, and establishes the meaning of the Four Noble Truths for all sentient beings, namely: this is the noble truth of suffering, this is the noble truth of the origin of suffering, this is the noble truth of the cessation of suffering, and this is the noble truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering.

Furthermore, all factors conducive to enlightenment (bodhipakṣadharma) are subsumed within these Four Noble Truths; moreover, based upon all factors conducive to enlightenment, the Jewels of the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha are designated and established.

It is through the appearance of these Three Jewels in the world that all sentient beings are liberated from birth and death; yet, if sentient beings are unable to take refuge in and have faith in the Jewels of the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha, they will perform various karmas and wander through the various realms of existence, suffering without end.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
is one attained to parinirvāṇa by means of the truth of suffering?”
Is it by means of the knowledge of suffering that one attains parinirvāṇa?
Is it by means of the truth of origination that one attains parinirvāṇa?
Or is it by means of the knowledge of origination that one attains parinirvāṇa?
Is it by means of the truth of cessation that one attains parinirvāṇa?
Is it by means of the knowledge of cessation that one attains parinirvāṇa?
Or is it by means of the truth of the path that one attains parinirvāṇa?
"Is it by means of the knowledge of the path that one attains parinirvāṇa?
The Buddha told Subhūti:

"One does not attain parinirvāṇa by means of the truth of suffering, nor does one attain parinirvāṇa by means of the knowledge of suffering; one does not attain parinirvāṇa by means of the truth of origin, nor does one attain parinirvāṇa by means of the knowledge of origin; one does not attain parinirvāṇa by means of the truth of cessation, nor does one attain parinirvāṇa by means of the knowledge of cessation; one does not attain parinirvāṇa by means of the truth of the path, nor does one attain parinirvāṇa by means of the knowledge of the path."

"Subhūti! I say that the equality of the four noble truths is itself nirvāṇa. Such nirvāṇa is not attained by means of the truths of suffering, origin, cessation, or the path, nor is it attained by means of the knowledge of suffering, origin, cessation, or the path; rather, it is called the attainment of nirvāṇa when one realizes this equality through the perfection of wisdom."
The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
what is called the equality of the four noble truths?”
The Buddha told Subhūti:

"In that state where there is no suffering and no knowledge of suffering, no origin and no knowledge of origin, no cessation and no knowledge of cessation, and no path and no knowledge of the path—this is called the equality of the four noble truths; this very equality is the four noble truths."

All suchness, the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, non-falsity, immutability, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, equality, the state beyond birth, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm—whether a Tathāgata appears in the world or does not appear, their essential characteristics remain eternally present, without loss or change. This is called the equality of the four noble truths.

When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do so because they wish to realize the equality of these four noble truths. When they are able to realize the equality of these four noble truths, it is called truly realizing all the noble truths.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
how does a bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of awakening to the equality of these four noble truths?”

If one can realize the equality of these four noble truths, then one can realize all noble truths; if one can realize all noble truths, then one can practice the bodhisattva conduct as it truly is; and if one can practice the bodhisattva conduct as it truly is, one will not fall into the levels of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, but will enter the bodhisattva’s state of certainty beyond regression.
The Buddha told Subhūti:

“When bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, there is not even the slightest dharma that they do not see as it truly is. When they see all dharmas as they truly are, they apprehend nothing at all in any dharma. When they apprehend nothing in any dharma, they then see all dharmas as empty as they truly are; that is to say, they see as they truly are that all dharmas—both those subsumed within and those not subsumed within the Four Noble Truths—are empty.”

When one perceives in this way, one is able to enter the bodhisattva’s state of rightness and departure from birth; by virtue of being able to enter the bodhisattva’s state of rightness and departure from birth, one dwells within the stage of the bodhisattva lineage.

Once one dwells within the stage of the bodhisattva lineage, one is then certain not to fall from the summit; for were one to fall from the summit, one would necessarily fall into the stage of a śrāvaka or a pratyekabuddha.

“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva, dwelling securely in the stage of the bodhisattva lineage, is able to give rise to the four dhyānas, as well as the four immeasurables and the four formless absorptions.”
This bodhisattva mahāsattva, dwelling securely in such a stage of *śamatha*, is able to discern all phenomena and realize the four noble truths.

Although this bodhisattva mahāsattva fully understands suffering, they do not give rise to a mind that clings to suffering as its object; although they have forever severed the origin [of suffering], they do not give rise to a mind that clings to the origin as its object; although they have realized cessation, they do not give rise to a mind that clings to cessation as its object; and although they cultivate the path, they do not give rise to a mind that clings to the path as its object. Rather, they give rise to a mind that accords with, tends toward, and enters into unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, observing the true nature of all phenomena.
The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
how does a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplate the true reality of all phenomena?”
The Buddha said:
“Subhūti! This bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates all phenomena as empty.”
“World-Honored One!
What kind of emptiness does this bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplate regarding all phenomena?
“Suvikrāntavikrāmin!
This bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates all phenomena as empty of their own characteristics (*svalakṣaṇaśūnya*). Subhūti!

By means of such vipaśyanā, this bodhisattva mahāsattva perceives all phenomena as they truly are—empty—and does not perceive any self-nature (*svabhāva*) of phenomena in which he might abide or through which he might realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening.
Why is this? Subhūti!
The unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas, as well as all phenomena, all have non-existence as their intrinsic nature.

Thus, this absence of intrinsic nature was not created by the Buddhas, nor by the Pratyekabuddhas, nor by the Bodhisattvas, nor by the Śrāvakas on their paths toward the fruits; it is simply because sentient beings do not know and do not see that all phenomena are, in accordance with reality, entirely empty.

For this reason, when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they skillfully employ expedient means to teach sentient beings according to reality, causing them to abandon attachment and escape the suffering of birth and death.
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

If all dharmas have non-existence as their intrinsic nature, and such non-existence is not created by the Buddhas, nor by the Pratyekabuddhas, nor by the Bodhisattvas, nor by the Arhats, nor by the Anāgāmins, nor by the Sakṛdāgāmins, nor by the Srotāpannas, nor even by those who are on the paths toward these [fruits], how can there be any differentiation established among dharmas, such that one says: ‘This is hell,’ ‘This is the animal realm,’ ‘This is the realm of hungry ghosts,’ or ‘This is the human realm’?”

"This is the Heaven of the Four Great Kings; this is the Heaven of the Thirty-three; this is the Yāma Heaven; this is the Tuṣita Heaven; this is the Nirmāṇarati Heaven; this is the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven;
this is the Brahmakāyika Heaven; this is the Brahmapurohita Heaven; this is the Brahmakāyika-sabhāgata Heaven; this is the Mahābrahmā Heaven; this is the Ābhāsvara Heaven;
this is the Parīttābhā Heaven; this is the Apramāṇābhā Heaven; this is the Ābhāsvara-viśuddha Heaven."
These are the Śuddhāvāsa devas; these are the Parīttaśubha devas; these are the Apramāṇaśubha devas;

these are the Śubhakṛtsna devas; these are the Bṛhatphala devas; these are the Parīttaśubha devas; these are the Apramāṇaśubha devas; these are the Śubhakṛtsna devas; these are the Bṛhatphala devas; these are the Āsaṃjñika devas;
these are the Avṛha devas; these are the Atapa devas; these are the Sudṛśa devas; these are the Sudarśana devas; these are the Akaniṣṭha devas.

"This is a deva of the sphere of infinite space; this is a deva of the sphere of infinite consciousness; this is a deva of the sphere of nothingness; this is a deva of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception;

this is a stream-enterer; this is a once-returner; this is a non-returner; this is an arhat; this is a pratyekabuddha; this is a bodhisattva mahāsattva; and this is a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha?"

“By means of this karma, the hells are designated; by means of this karma, the animal realm is designated; by means of this karma, the realm of hungry ghosts is designated; by means of this karma, human beings are designated.

By means of this karma, the Heaven of the Four Great Kings is designated; by means of this karma, the Heaven of the Thirty-three is designated; by means of this karma, the Yāma Heaven is designated; by means of this karma, the Tuṣita Heaven is designated; by means of this karma, the Nirmāṇarati Heaven is designated; by means of this karma, the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven is designated.

By means of this karma, the Brahmakāyika Heaven is designated; by means of this karma, the Brahmapurohita Heaven is designated; by means of this karma, the Mahābrahma Heaven is designated; by means of this karma, the Parīttābha Heaven is designated.”

By virtue of this karma, the Ābhāsvara Heaven is designated; by virtue of this karma, the Parīttābha Heaven is designated; by virtue of this karma, the Apramāṇābha Heaven is designated; and by virtue of this karma, the Ābhāsvara-śuddha Heaven is designated.

By virtue of this karma, the Śubha Heaven is designated; by virtue of this karma, the Parīttaśubha Heaven is designated; by virtue of this karma, the Apramāṇaśubha Heaven is designated; and by virtue of this karma, the Śubhakṛtsna Heaven is designated. By virtue of this karma, the Bṛhatphala Heaven is designated;

by virtue of this karma, the Parītta-bṛhatphala Heaven is designated; by virtue of this karma, the Apramāṇa-bṛhatphala Heaven is designated; by virtue of this karma, the Bṛhatphala Heaven is designated; and by virtue of this karma, the Asaṃjñisattva Heaven is designated.

By virtue of this karma, the Heaven of No Affliction (Avṛha) is designated; by virtue of this karma, the Heaven of No Heat (Atapa) is designated; by virtue of this karma, the Heaven of Good Appearance (Sudṛśa) is designated; by virtue of this karma, the Heaven of Good Vision (Sudarśana) is designated;

by virtue of this karma, the Heaven of the Ultimate of Form (Akaniṣṭha) is designated. By virtue of this karma, the Heaven of the Sphere of Infinite Space (Ākāśānantyāyatana) is designated; by virtue of this karma, the Heaven of the Sphere of Infinite Consciousness (Vijñānānantyāyatana) is designated; by virtue of this karma, the Heaven of the Sphere of Nothingness (Ākiṃcanyāyatana) is designated; and by virtue of this karma, the Heaven of Neither Perception nor Non-perception (Naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana) is designated.

By virtue of this karma, one is designated as a stream-enterer; by virtue of this karma, one is designated as a once-returner; by virtue of this karma, one is designated as a non-returner; by virtue of this karma, one is designated as an arhat; by virtue of this karma, one is designated as a pratyekabuddha; by virtue of this karma, one is designated as a bodhisattva mahāsattva; and by virtue of this karma, one is designated as a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha?
“World-Honored One!
Since dharmas that lack intrinsic nature necessarily possess no functional activity, how can it be said:
‘By such dharmas one is born in the hells; by such dharmas one is born among animals; by such dharmas one is born in the realm of hungry ghosts; by such dharmas one is born among human beings’?”

By means of such dharmas, one is born among the gods of the Four Great Kings; by means of such dharmas, one is born among the Trāyastriṃśa gods; by means of such dharmas, one is born among the Yāma gods; by means of such dharmas, one is born among the Tuṣita gods; by means of such dharmas, one is born among the Nirmāṇarati gods; by means of such dharmas, one is born among the Paranirmita-vaśavartin gods.

By means of such dharmas, one is born among the Brahmakāyika gods; by means of such dharmas, one is born among the Brahmapurohita gods; by means of such dharmas, one is born among the Mahābrahma gods; by means of such dharmas, one is born among the Ābhāsvara gods;

by means of such dharmas, one is born among the Parīttābha gods; by means of such dharmas, one is born among the Apramāṇābha gods; by means of such dharmas, one is born among the Ābhāsvara (Pure Light) gods.
By such dharmas one is born in the Śuddhāvāsa Heaven; by such dharmas one is born in the Parīttaśubha Heaven; by such dharmas one is born in the Apramāṇaśubha Heaven;

by such dharmas one is born in the Śubhakṛtsna Heaven; by such dharmas one is born in the Bṛhatphala Heaven; by such dharmas one is born in the Parīttaśubha Heaven; by such dharmas one is born in the Apramāṇaśubha Heaven; by such dharmas one is born in the Śubhakṛtsna Heaven; by such dharmas one is born in the Bṛhatphala Heaven; by such dharmas one is born in the Āsaṃjñika Heaven;

by such dharmas one is born in the Avṛha Heaven; by such dharmas one is born in the Atapa Heaven; by such dharmas one is born in the Sudṛśa Heaven; by such dharmas one is born in the Sudarśana Heaven; by such dharmas one is born in the Akaniṣṭha Heaven.

By means of such dharmas, one is born in the Heaven of Infinite Space; by means of such dharmas, one is born in the Heaven of Infinite Consciousness; by means of such dharmas, one is born in the Heaven of Nothingness;

by means of such dharmas, one is born in the Heaven of Neither Perception nor Non-perception. By means of such dharmas, one attains the fruit of Stream-entry; by means of such dharmas, one attains the fruit of Once-returning; by means of such dharmas, one attains the fruit of Non-returning; by means of such dharmas, one attains the fruit of Arhatship; by means of such dharmas, one attains the enlightenment of a Pratyekabuddha; by means of such dharmas, one enters the stage of a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva and practices the Bodhisattva path; by means of such dharmas, one becomes a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, and causes all sentient beings to be liberated from birth and death?
The Buddha told Subhūti: “So it is! So it is!”
"It is as you have said.
Within phenomena that lack intrinsic nature, it is impossible to designate any differentiation among phenomena; there is no karma, no fruit, and no functional activity. Subhūti!"

Because foolish ordinary beings do not understand the Dharma and Vinaya of the Noble Ones, they do not realize that all phenomena have the absence of intrinsic nature as their very essence; thus, through delusion and inversion, they initiate various actions of body, speech, and mind, and according to the distinctions of those actions, they receive various bodies.
Based on such distinctions among the categories of bodies, there are provisionally designated the realms of hell-beings, animals, hungry ghosts, and humans;

and there are provisionally designated the Heaven of the Four Great Kings, the Heaven of the Thirty-three, the Yāma Heaven, the Tuṣita Heaven, the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, and the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven. Provisionally...
The Brahmakāyika, Brahmapurohita, Brahmakāyika-parṣadya, and Mahābrahmā devas are provisionally designated;
the Ābhāsvara, Parīttābhā, Apramāṇābhā, and Ābhāsvara-śuddha devas are provisionally designated;
and the Śubha, Parīttaśubha, Apramāṇaśubha, and Śubhakṛtsna devas are provisionally designated.

The Vast Heaven (*Vehapphala*), the Limited-Vast Heaven (*Appamāṇasubha*), the Immeasurable-Vast Heaven (*Subhakinhā*), the Heaven of Great Fruit (*Vehapphala*), and the Heaven of Non-perception (*Asaññasatta*) are all conceptually designated;

the Heaven Without Strife (*Aviha*), the Heaven Without Heat (*Atappa*), the Beautifully Manifest Heaven (*Sudassa*), the Beautifully Seeing Heaven (*Sudassī*), and the Ultimate Form Heaven (*Akaniṭṭha*) are all conceptually designated;
and the Heaven of the Sphere of Infinite Space (*Ākāsānañcāyatana*) and the Heaven of the Sphere of Infinite Consciousness (*Viññāṇañcāyatana*) are all conceptually designated.
The gods of the Sphere of Infinite Space, the gods of the Sphere of Nothingness, and the gods of the Sphere of Neither-Perception-nor-Non-Perception. "Subhūti!

It is for the sake of rescuing foolish ordinary beings from the suffering of birth and death caused by ignorance and perversion that one establishes the distinctions of the stages of the Noble Dharma and the Vinaya. Based upon these stages, one establishes the designations of Stream-enterer, Once-returner, Non-returner, Arhat, Pratyekabuddha, Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, and all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas."

However, all phenomena take the absence of intrinsic nature as their own nature; within the state of the absence of intrinsic nature, there are truly no distinct phenomena, no karma, no fruit, and no functional activity, because phenomena that lack intrinsic nature are eternally devoid of intrinsic nature.
"Furthermore, Subhūti! Regarding what you have said:

'If dharmas that lack intrinsic nature necessarily possess no activity, how can it be said that by means of such dharmas one attains the fruit of a stream-enterer, a once-returner, a non-returner, or an arhat; that one attains the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha; that one enters the stage of a bodhisattva mahāsattva and practices the bodhisattva path; that one becomes a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha; and that one causes all sentient beings to be liberated from birth and death?'"
"Subhūti, what do you think? Are all those paths cultivated devoid of intrinsic nature?"
Are the fruits of stream-entry, once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship without intrinsic nature?
Is the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha without intrinsic nature?
Are all the paths of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas without intrinsic nature?
“Is the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas devoid of intrinsic nature? Subhūti replied,
“World-Honored One, it is.”

All paths of cultivation are devoid of intrinsic nature; the fruits of stream-entry, once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship are also devoid of intrinsic nature; the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is also devoid of intrinsic nature; all paths of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are also devoid of intrinsic nature; and the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas is also devoid of intrinsic nature.
The Buddha said, “Subhūti, what do you think?”
"Can a dharma that lacks intrinsic nature attain a dharma that lacks intrinsic nature? Subhūti replied, "No!"
"No, World-Honored One! No, Sugata!"
The Buddha said, “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

Non-existence and the path—all these dharmas are neither associated nor dissociated; they are formless, invisible, non-obstructive, and possess a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of signlessness.”

Foolish ordinary beings, deluded and inverted, engage in false conceptualization regarding phenomena that are devoid of marks; they give rise to the notion of existent dharmas and cling to the five aggregates. Within the impermanent, they conceive of permanence; within suffering, they conceive of pleasure; within non-self, they conceive of a self; within the impure, they conceive of purity; and within the absence of intrinsic nature, they cling to the existence of intrinsic nature.

By means of these causes and conditions, Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and achieve sublime skillful means; they rescue such sentient beings, causing them to abandon inverted and false attachments, and through skillful means establish them within the signless Dharma, so that they may diligently cultivate and study liberation from birth and death, and realize ultimate, eternal bliss in Nirvāṇa.
The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

Is there not some reality that is true and not false, wherein foolish ordinary beings cling and perform various karmas, by reason of which they transmigrate through the various realms and are unable to be liberated from the suffering of birth and death?”
The Buddha told Subhūti:

"There is not even a thing as small as a hair-tip that is real and not false, yet foolish ordinary beings cling to it and perform various karmas. By reason of these causes and conditions, they wander through the various realms of existence and cannot liberate themselves from the manifold sufferings of birth and death; they possess nothing but inverted, false attachments."

“Subhūti! I shall now provide you with an extensive analogy to further clarify this meaning so that it may be easily understood; for those who possess wisdom attain correct understanding of the meaning explained through analogies.”
"Subhūti, what do you think?

When a person sees someone else experiencing the pleasures of the five senses within a dream, is there even the slightest portion of a real thing therein that could cause that person to experience those sensual pleasures?"
Subhūti replied, “No, World-Honored One!”
"No, Sugata! Even a person seen in a dream does not truly exist; how much less could there be a real entity that could cause such a person to experience the pleasures of the five senses!"
The Buddha said to Subhūti: "What do you think?
Are there any phenomena—whether worldly or supramundane, with outflows or without outflows, conditioned or unconditioned—that are not like things seen in a dream?"
Subhūti replied, “No, World-Honored One!”
"No, Sugata! There is certainly no phenomenon—
whether worldly or supramundane, with outflows or without outflows, conditioned or unconditioned— that is not like the things seen in a dream."
The Buddha said to Subhūti:
"What do you think? Within a dream, is there any reality of the various realms of existence, or any matter of coming and going through birth and death?"
Subhūti replied, “No, World-Honored One!”
"No, Sugata! The Buddha said to Subhūti:
"What do you think? Is there, within a dream, any truly real cultivation of the path, by means of which cultivation one might become free from defilement and attain purity? Subhūti replied:
"No, World-Honored One! No!"
Well-gone One!
Why is this? World-Honored One!

The phenomena seen in a dream have no reality whatsoever; they are neither the agent of designation nor the object of designation. If even the cultivation of the path does not exist, how much less could there be the departure from defilement and the attainment of purity based upon that cultivation!
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 395. Translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Part One, Chapter Seventy-Four, "The Naturelessness of Self-Nature," Section Two.
The Buddha addressed Subhūti: "What do you think?"

Regarding the various images manifested within a bright mirror and the like: do they possess any substantial reality that could serve as a basis for performing karma? And by virtue of the karma thus performed, would one fall into hell, or fall among the animals, or fall into the realm of hungry ghosts; or be born among human beings; or be born in the desire realm, from the Heaven of the Four Great Kings up to the Heaven of Mastery over Others' Emanations; or be born in the form realm, from the Heaven of Brahma’s Retinue up to the Akaniṣṭha Heaven; or be born in the formless realm, from the Heaven of Infinite Space up to the Heaven of Neither Perception nor Non-perception?
Subhūti replied, “No, World-Honored One!”
"No, Sugata!

The various images manifested in a bright mirror and the like have no substantial reality whatsoever; they merely delude foolish children. How could they serve as a basis for performing karmic actions, such that by virtue of those performed actions one might fall into the evil destinies or be born among humans or devas?"
The Buddha said to Subhūti: "What do you think?
Do images possess any real cultivation of the path, such that by relying on that cultivation of the path, one could become free from affliction and attain purity?"
Subhūti replied, “No, World-Honored One!”
"No, Sugata! Why is that?"
World-Honored One!

Images in a bright mirror and the like have no substantial reality; they are neither that which can be designated nor that which is designated. If even the cultivation of the path does not exist, how much less could there be the departure from defilement and the attainment of purity based upon the cultivation of the path!
The Buddha said to Subhūti: "What do you think?
Are there any phenomena—whether worldly or supramundane, with outflows or without outflows, conditioned or unconditioned—that are not like reflections appearing in a mirror and the like?"
Subhūti replied, “No, World-Honored One!”
"No, Sugata! There is certainly no dharma—
whether worldly or supramundane, with outflows or without outflows, conditioned or unconditioned— that is not like a reflection manifested in a mirror and the like."
The Buddha said to Subhūti: "What do you think?

Do the various echoes produced within deep valleys have any real substance upon which one could rely to create karma, such that by virtue of the karma created, one would fall into hell, or fall among animals, or fall into the realm of hungry ghosts, or be born among humans, or be born in the desire realm from the Heaven of the Four Great Kings up to the Heaven of Control over Others' Emanations, or be born in the form realm from the Brahma Assembly Heaven up to the Akaniṣṭha Heaven, or be born in the formless realm from the Sphere of Infinite Space up to the Sphere of Neither Perception nor Non-perception?"
Subhūti replied, “No, World-Honored One!”
"No, Sugata!
The various echoes produced within deep valleys and the like have no substantial reality at all; they merely delude the ignorant!"
"How is it that one can rely on the performance of various karmas, such that by those performed karmas one either falls into the evil destinies or is born among humans and devas?
The Buddha told Subhūti: "What do you think?"
“Is there any genuine cultivation of the path within echoes, such that by relying on that cultivation one might become free from defilement and attain purity? Subhūti replied, “No!”
"No, World-Honored One! No, Sugata!"
Why is this so? World-Honored One!

An echo in a deep valley and the like have no substantial reality; they are neither that which can designate nor that which is designated. If even the cultivation of the path does not exist, how much less could there be the departure from defilement and the attainment of purity based upon the cultivation of the path!
The Buddha said to Subhūti: "What do you think?
Are there any phenomena—whether worldly or supramundane, with outflows or without outflows, conditioned or unconditioned—that are not like an echo produced from a valley or the like?"
Subhūti replied, “No, World-Honored One!”
"No, Sugata! There is certainly no dharma—
whether worldly or supramundane, with outflows or without outflows, conditioned or unconditioned— that is not like an echo produced from a valley or the like."
The Buddha said to Subhūti: “What do you think?

Regarding those things that appear like water and so forth within a mirage, is there any real entity therein upon which one could rely to perform karma, such that by virtue of the karma performed, one would fall into hell, or fall among animals, or fall into the realm of hungry ghosts, or be born among human beings, or be born in the desire realm from the Heaven of the Four Great Kings up to the Heaven of Control over Others’ Emanations, or be born in the form realm from the Brahma Assembly Heaven up to the Akaniṣṭha Heaven, or be born in the formless realm from the Sphere of Infinite Space up to the Sphere of Neither Perception nor Non-perception?”
Subhūti replied, “No, World-Honored One!”
"No, Sugata! The water and such things manifested within all those mirages have no reality whatsoever; they merely delude the eyes of the ignorant!"
"How is it that one can rely upon the performance of various karmas, such that by those performed karmas one either falls into the evil destinies or is born among humans and devas?
The Buddha told Subhūti: "What do you think?"
"In those mirages, is there any truly real path of cultivation, by depending upon which path of cultivation one might become free from defilement and attain purity? Subhūti replied, "No!"
"No, World-Honored One! No, Sugata!"
Why is this so? World-Honored One!

A mirage, water, and the like have no reality whatsoever; they are neither that which can designate nor that which is designated. If even the cultivation of the path does not exist, how much less could there be the departure from defilement and the attainment of purity based upon the cultivation of the path!
The Buddha said to Subhūti,
“What do you think? Are there any phenomena—
whether worldly or supramundane, with outflows or without outflows, conditioned or unconditioned— that do not appear like a mirage manifesting as water?”
Subhūti replied, “No, World-Honored One!”
"No, Sugata! There is certainly no phenomenon—
whether worldly or supramundane, with outflows or without outflows, conditioned or unconditioned— that does not appear like water in a mirage."
The Buddha said to Subhūti:
"What do you think? Do the forms and appearances manifested within various reflections and shadows possess any substantial reality upon which one could rely to create karma?"

By virtue of the karma they have created, do they fall into hell, or fall among the animals, or fall into the realm of hungry ghosts; or are they born among human beings; or are they born in the desire realm, from the Heaven of the Four Great Kings up to the Heaven of Mastery over Others' Emanations; or are they born in the form realm, from the Heaven of Brahma’s Retinue up to the Heaven of Ultimate Form; or are they born in the formless realm, from the Heaven of Infinite Space up to the Heaven of Neither Perception nor Non-perception?
Subhūti replied, “No, World-Honored One!”
"No, Sugata! The forms and appearances manifested within all those reflections have no substantial reality at all; they merely delude the eyes of the ignorant!"
"How is it that one can rely on the performance of various karmas, such that by virtue of those performed karmas, one either falls into the evil destinies or is born among humans and devas?
The Buddha told Subhūti: "What do you think?"
"Within those various reflections and shadows, is there any truly real cultivation of the path? By relying on such cultivation of the path, can one become free from defilement and attain purity?
Subhūti replied, "No!"
“World-Honored One! No, indeed! Sugata!”
Why is this so? World-Honored One!

The colors and forms of light and shadows have no substantial reality; they are neither that which can be designated nor that which is designated. Since even the cultivation of the path does not exist, how much less could there be the departure from defilement and the attainment of purity based upon the cultivation of the path!
The Buddha said to Subhūti: "What do you think?

Are there any phenomena—whether worldly or supramundane, with outflows or without outflows, conditioned or unconditioned—that do not appear as the manifestation of forms and signs like reflections in light?"
Subhūti replied, “No, World-Honored One!”
"No, Sugata! There is certainly no dharma—
whether worldly or supramundane, with outflows or without outflows, conditioned or unconditioned— that does not manifest as a form and characteristic like a reflection in light."
The Buddha said to Subhūti: "What do you think?

If a magician were to conjure through illusion various illusory phenomena such as the fourfold army of elephants, horses, chariots, and infantry, would these illusory elephants and so forth have any real substance upon which to rely to perform karma, such that by virtue of the karma performed they might fall into hell, or fall among the animals, or fall into the realm of hungry ghosts, or be born among humans, or be born in the desire realm from the Heaven of the Four Great Kings up to the Heaven of Controlling Others' Emanations, or be born in the form realm from the Brahma Assembly Heaven up to the Akaniṣṭha Heaven, or be born in the formless realm from the Sphere of Infinite Space up to the Sphere of Neither Perception nor Non-perception?"
Subhūti replied, “No, World-Honored One!”
"No, Sugata! Illusions such as elephants and horses have no reality at all; they merely delude the ignorant."
"How is it that one can rely on the performance of various karmas, such that by those performed karmas one either falls into the evil destinies or is born among humans and gods?
The Buddha told Subhūti: "What do you think?"
“Is there any genuine path of cultivation within illusory phenomena? By relying on such a path of cultivation, can one become free from defilement and attain purity?
Subhūti replied, “No!”
"World-Honored One! No, indeed! Sugata!"
Why is this? World-Honored One!

Illusory elephants, horses, and so forth have no real substance; they are neither that which can designate nor that which is designated. Since even the cultivation of the path does not exist, how much less could there be the departure from defilement and the attainment of purity based upon the cultivation of the path!
The Buddha said to Subhūti: "What do you think?
Are there any phenomena—whether worldly or supramundane, with outflows or without outflows, conditioned or unconditioned—that are not like illusory things such as elephants and the like?"
Subhūti replied, “No, World-Honored One!”
"No, Sugata! There is certainly no dharma—
whether worldly or supramundane, with outflows or without outflows, conditioned or unconditioned— that is not like the illusory phenomena of elephants and the like."
The Buddha said to Subhūti: "What do you think?

Do the various transformation bodies emanated by a Buddha possess any substantial reality such that they could perform karma, and by virtue of the karma performed, fall into hell, or fall among animals, or fall into the realm of hungry ghosts, or be born among humans, or be born in the desire realm from the Heaven of the Four Great Kings up to the Heaven of Controlling Others' Emanations, or be born in the form realm from the Brahma-kāyika heaven up to the Akaniṣṭha heaven, or be born in the formless realm from the Ākāśānantyāyatana heaven up to the Naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana heaven?"
Subhūti replied, “No, World-Honored One!”

"No, Sugata! Since all emanation bodies (nirmāṇakāya) are entirely devoid of substantial reality, how could they be relied upon to perform various karmas, such that by the karma thus performed one might fall into the evil destinies or be born among humans and devas?"
The Buddha said to Subhūti:
"What do you think? Does an emanation body possess a real path of cultivation? By relying on that path of cultivation, is there any departure from defilement and attainment of purity?"
Subhūti replied, “No, World-Honored One!”
"No, Sugata! Why is that?"

"Bhagavān! All transformation bodies (nirmāṇakāya) are entirely devoid of substantial reality; they are neither the agents of designation nor the objects of designation. Since even the cultivation of the path does not exist, how much less could there be the departure from defilement or the attainment of purity based upon the cultivation of the path!"
The Buddha said to Subhūti: "What do you think?
Are there any phenomena—whether worldly or supramundane, with outflows or without outflows, conditioned or unconditioned—that are not like a transformation body produced by magical power?"
Subhūti replied, “No, World-Honored One!”
"No, Sugata! There is certainly no dharma—
whether worldly or supramundane, with outflows or without outflows, conditioned or unconditioned— that is not like a transformation body produced by one's own making."
The Buddha said to Subhūti: "What do you think?

Do the things manifested in the city of Gandhavatī have any real substance upon which one could rely to create karma, such that by virtue of the karma created one would fall into hell, or fall among the animals, or fall into the realm of hungry ghosts, or be born among human beings, or be born in the desire realm from the Heaven of the Four Great Kings up to the Heaven of Controlling Others' Emanations, or be born in the form realm from the Brahma Assembly Heaven up to the Akaniṣṭha Heaven, or be born in the formless realm from the Sphere of Infinite Space up to the Sphere of Neither Perception nor Non-perception?"
Subhūti replied, “No, World-Honored One!”

"No, Sugata! The various things manifested within the city of Gandhavatī have no substantial reality at all; how could they serve as a basis for performing karmic actions, such that by those performed actions one might fall into the evil destinies or be born among humans or gods?"
The Buddha said to Subhūti:

"What do you think? Within the city of Gandhavatī, are there any entities that truly constitute the cultivation of the path, such that by relying on that cultivation of the path, one might become free from defilement and attain purity?"
Subhūti replied, “No, World-Honored One!”
"No, Sugata! Why is that?"
“World-Honored One!

The various things manifested within the city of Gandhavatī have no substantial reality; they are neither that which can be designated nor that which is designated. Since even the path of cultivation does not exist, how much less could there be the departure from defilement or the attainment of purity based upon the path of cultivation!”
The Buddha said to Subhūti: "What do you think?
Are there any phenomena—whether worldly or supramundane, with outflows or without outflows, conditioned or unconditioned—that are not like the objects manifested within the city of Gandharvas?"
Subhūti replied, “No, World-Honored One!”
"No, Sugata! There is certainly no dharma—
whether mundane or supramundane, with outflows or without outflows, conditioned or unconditioned— that is not like the things manifested within the city of Gandharvas."
The Buddha said to Subhūti: "What do you think?
Within this, is there any real defiler or any real purifier?"
Subhūti replied, “No, World-Honored One!”
"No, Sugata! Within this,
there is ultimately no one who is truly defiled, nor anyone who is purified."
The Buddha said:
“Subhūti! Just as those who are defiled and those who are purified do not truly exist, for this reason, both defilement and purification are also not truly existent.”
Why is this? Subhūti!

Sentient beings who dwell in the notions of "self" and "what belongs to self" engage in false conceptualization, claiming that there is defilement and purification; those who see reality do not claim that there is defilement and purification.
"Just as one who sees reality knows there is neither defilement nor purification, so too there is neither defilement nor purification.
Chapter 75: The Yoga of the Ultimate Truth, Part One. At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
For those who perceive reality, there is neither defilement nor purity; for those who do not perceive reality, there is likewise neither defilement nor purity.
Why is this? Because all phenomena take the absence of intrinsic nature as their own nature.
World-Honored One!

All phenomena that lack intrinsic nature are neither defiled nor pure; all phenomena that possess intrinsic nature are likewise neither defiled nor pure; and all phenomena, whether lacking or possessing intrinsic nature, are also neither defiled nor pure.
“World-Honored One!

Dharmas without intrinsic nature are neither defiled nor pure; dharmas with intrinsic nature are likewise neither defiled nor pure; and dharmas both without and with intrinsic nature are also neither defiled nor pure.”
Why is this? Because all phenomena take the absence of intrinsic nature as their very nature.
World-Honored One!
"If that is so, why does the Buddha at times say that there are dharmas of purification?
The Buddha told Subhūti:
"I say that the sameness of all dharmas is the dharma of purification."
“World-Honored One!
What is the equality of all phenomena? “Suvikrāntavikrāmin!

The suchness of all phenomena, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, the non-illusory nature, the unchanging nature, the state of equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixedness of dharma, the stability of dharma, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm—whether a Tathāgata appears in the world or does not appear, their intrinsic nature and characteristics remain eternally constant. This is called the equality of all phenomena; this equality is termed the pure dharma.
This is described as "pure" according to conventional truth, not according to ultimate truth.
Why is this so? Because within the ultimate truth there is no conceptualization and no discursive proliferation; all paths of sound and names are cut off.
The Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

If all dharmas are like what is seen in a dream, like a reflected image, like an echo, like a mirage, like a shadow, like a magical illusion, like a transformation-body, and like a city of Gandharvas—appearing as if they exist while lacking any substantial reality—how can a bodhisattva mahāsattva rely upon such non-real dharmas to resolve their mind on anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and make this vow, saying:”

I shall fulfill the perfection of generosity; I shall fulfill the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, wisdom, skillful means, aspiration, power, and knowledge.
I shall fulfill the four dhyānas; I shall fulfill the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments. I shall fulfill the four foundations of mindfulness;
I shall fulfill the four right endeavors, the four bases of miraculous power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
I shall fulfill the gate of liberation of emptiness; I shall fulfill the gates of liberation of signlessness and wishlessness.
I shall fulfill the eight liberations; I shall fulfill the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities.

I shall fulfill internal emptiness; I shall fulfill external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersion emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

I shall fulfill true thusness; I shall fulfill the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, non-falsity, immutability, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, and the inconceivable realm.
I shall fulfill the noble truth of suffering; I shall fulfill the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path.
I shall fulfill all doors of dhāraṇī; I shall fulfill all doors of samādhi.

I shall fulfill the Ground of Extreme Joy; I shall fulfill the Ground of Purity, the Ground of Radiance, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Difficult Victory, the Ground of Presence, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, and the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma.
I shall fulfill the five eyes; I shall fulfill the six supernormal powers.

I shall fulfill the ten powers of a Buddha; I shall fulfill the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
I shall fulfill the dhāraṇī of eloquence;
I shall fulfill the quality of non-forgetfulness; I shall fulfill the state of constant equanimity;
I shall fulfill all-knowledge; I shall fulfill the knowledge of the paths and the knowledge of all aspects.
"I shall fulfill the thirty-two marks of a great man; I shall fulfill the eighty secondary signs;
I shall emit immeasurable light that pervades the boundless worlds of the ten directions;

I shall produce a single sublime voice that fills the boundless worlds of the ten directions, and according to the differences in the inclinations of the minds and mental factors of sentient beings, I shall expound various subtle and wondrous Dharma gates for them, causing them to practice diligently and realize supreme benefit and peace."
The Buddha said to Subhūti: "What do you think?

Is not the Dharma you have taught also like what is seen in a dream, like a reflection, like an echo, like a mirage, like a shadow, like a magical illusion, like a transformed body, and like a city of Gandharvas?"
Subhūti replied, “So it is, World-Honored One!”
"So it is! Well-gone One!
World-Honored One!"

If all phenomena are like things seen in a dream, and so forth, up to being like a city of gandharvas—lacking any substantial reality—how can a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the perfection of wisdom, utter a truthful declaration:
"I shall fulfill all merits and bring benefit, peace, and happiness to immeasurable sentient beings"?
“World-Honored One!

That which is seen in a dream—extending in detail to the various things manifested within the City of Fragrance—is incapable of practicing the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, wisdom, skillful means, sublime aspiration, power, and knowledge, let alone being able to bring them to fulfillment!”
All other phenomena should also be understood in this way, for they are equally not real.
“World-Honored One!

That which is seen in a dream—and as has been explained at length, even the things manifested within the City of Fragrance—cannot practice the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, or the four formless attainments, much less fulfill them!”
All other phenomena should likewise be understood in this way, for they are equally not real. "World-Honored One,

that which is seen in a dream— and as has been explained at length, even the things manifested within the City of Fragrance— is incapable of practicing the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path, let alone being able to bring them to fulfillment!"
All other phenomena should also be understood in this way, for they are equally not real.
"World-Honored One!

That which is seen in a dream—and as extensively explained up to the various things manifested in the City of Fragrance—cannot even practice the gates of liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, much less fulfill them!"
All other dharmas should also be understood in this way, for none are real.
"World-Honored One!

That which is seen in a dream—and as extensively explained up to the objects appearing within the City of Gandharvas—cannot practice the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, or the ten totalities, much less perfect them!"
All other phenomena should also be understood in this way, for none are real.

“World-Honored One, that which is seen in a dream—and as extensively explained up to the objects appearing within the City of Gandharvas—cannot practice inner emptiness, outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-altering emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence; how much less could it fulfill them?”
All other dharmas should also be understood in this way, for they are equally not real.
"World-Honored One!

That which is seen in a dream—and as has been explained at length, even down to the various things manifested within the City of Gandharvas—cannot practice suchness, the dharma-realm, the dharma-nature, non-illusory nature, non-alteration, equality, the nature of freedom from birth, the fixed nature of dharmas, the stability of dharmas, the limit of reality, the realm of space, or the inconceivable realm; how much less could it fulfill them?"
All other phenomena should also be understood in this way, for they are equally not real.
"World-Honored One!

That which is seen in a dream—and as has been explained at length, even the things manifested within the City of Fragrance—cannot practice the Noble Truths of Suffering, Origin, Cessation, and the Path, much less fulfill them!"
All other phenomena should likewise be understood in this way, for they are equally not real.
"World-Honored One!

Even that which is seen in a dream—extending broadly to include the various things manifested within the City of Fragrance—is incapable of practicing any of the *dhāraṇī* gates or any of the *samādhi* gates, much less being able to fulfill them!"
All other phenomena should likewise be understood in this way, for they are equally not real. "World-Honored One,

that which is seen in a dream— and as has been explained at length, even the objects appearing within a city of Gandharvas— cannot practice the Ground of Extreme Joy, the Ground of Purity, the Ground of Radiant Light, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Difficult Victory, the Ground of Manifestation, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, or the Ground of the Dharma Cloud, much less can they fulfill them!"
All other phenomena should also be understood in this way, for they are equally not real.
"World-Honored One!
That which is seen in a dream, and so forth, up to the objects manifested within the City of Gandharvas, cannot even practice the five eyes or the six supernormal powers, much less fulfill them!"
All other phenomena should also be understood in this way, for they are equally not real. "World-Honored One,

that which is seen in a dream— and as has been explained at length, even the things manifested within the City of Gandharvas— cannot practice the Buddha’s ten powers, the four fearlessnesses, the four unhindered understandings, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, much less perfect them!"
All other dharmas should also be understood in this way, for none are real.
"World-Honored One!

Even that which is seen in a dream—and as extensively explained up to the objects appearing within the City of Fragrance—is incapable of practicing the *dhāraṇī* of eloquence, let alone being able to fulfill it!"
All other phenomena should also be understood in this way, for they are equally not real.
"World-Honored One!

Even that which is seen in a dream—let alone the various things manifested within the City of Gandharvas—cannot practice the quality of non-forgetfulness or abide in equanimity, much less fulfill them!"
All other phenomena should likewise be understood in this way, for none are real.
"World-Honored One!

That which is seen in a dream—and as has been explained at length, even the objects manifested within the City of Fragrant Incense—cannot practice all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), or the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), much less be able to fulfill them!"
All other dharmas should also be understood in this way, for they are equally not real.
"World-Honored One!

That which is seen in a dream—and as extensively explained up to the objects manifested within the City of Fragrant Incense—is incapable of performing the thirty-two marks of a Great Man or the eighty secondary signs, much less being able to perfect them!"
All other phenomena should also be understood in this way, for they are equally not real.
"World-Honored One!

Just as what is seen in a dream—and as has been explained at length up to the objects appearing in the City of Gandharvas—can accomplish all desired tasks, so too should all other phenomena be understood, for they are equally not real."
The Buddha told Subhūti: "So it is! So it is!"
As you have said,

even a non-existent dharma cannot practice the perfections of giving, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, wisdom, skillful means, sublime aspiration, power, and knowledge, much less bring them to fulfillment!
If even a non-substantial dharma cannot practice the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, or the four formless attainments, how much less can it fulfill them!

If even a non-substantial dharma cannot practice the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold noble path, how much less can it fulfill them!
If even non-substantial dharmas cannot practice the gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—how much less can they fulfill them!

If even non-substantial dharmas cannot practice the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, or the ten totalities, how much less can they fulfill them!

If even non-substantial dharmas cannot practice inner emptiness, outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, unchanging emptiness, essential emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common-characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all dharmas, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature, how much less could they fulfill them?

Since even non-substantial dharmas cannot course within suchness, the dharma-realm, the nature of phenomena, non-illusory nature, unchanging nature, equality, the state beyond birth, the fixed nature of phenomena, the stability of phenomena, the limit of reality, the realm of space, or the inconceivable realm, how much less can they fulfill them?
If even non-existent dharmas cannot practice the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path, how much less can they fulfill them!
If even non-existent dharmas cannot practice any of the gateways of dhāraṇī or any of the gateways of samādhi, how much less can they fulfill them!

Since even non-substantial dharmas cannot traverse the Ground of Utmost Joy, the Ground Free from Defilement, the Ground of Radiant Light, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground Difficult to Conquer, the Ground of Manifestation, the Ground of Far-Going, the Immovable Ground, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, or the Ground of the Dharma Cloud, how much less can they bring them to fulfillment?
If even non-substantial dharmas cannot practice the five eyes or the six supernormal powers, how much less can they fulfill them!

If even non-substantial dharmas cannot practice the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, how much less can they fulfill them!
If even non-substantial dharmas cannot cause one to practice the *dhāraṇī* of eloquence, how much less can they bring it to perfection?
If even non-substantial dharmas cannot cause one to practice the quality of non-forgetfulness or the state of constant equanimity, how much less can they bring them to perfection?

If even non-existent dharmas cannot practice the knowledge of all things (*sarvajñatā*), the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), or the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), how much less can they fulfill them!

If even non-existent dharmas cannot practice the thirty-two marks of a great man (*dvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa*) or the eighty secondary signs (*aśītyanuvyañjana*), how much less can they fulfill them!

A phenomenon that does not truly exist cannot accomplish the activities one intends; a phenomenon that does not truly exist cannot realize the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment that one seeks.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

Because the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, wisdom, skillful means, sublime aspiration, power, and knowledge do not exist as real entities, one cannot realize the sought-after unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."

Because the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right endeavors, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eight branches of the noble path are not substantially existent, one cannot realize the sought-after unsurpassed perfect enlightenment.

Because internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are not truly existent, one cannot realize the sought-after unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Because the Noble Truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path are not substantially real, one cannot realize the sought-after unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Because the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions are not substantially real, one cannot realize the sought-after unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Because the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are not substantially existent, one cannot realize the sought-after unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Because all dharani-doors and all samadhi-doors are not substantially existent, one cannot realize the sought-after unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Because the gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are not substantially existent, one cannot realize the sought-after unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Because the ten stages—the Stage of Extreme Joy, the Stage of Purity, the Stage of Radiant Light, the Stage of Blazing Wisdom, the Stage of Difficult Victory, the Stage of Presence, the Stage of Far-Going, the Immovable Stage, the Stage of Excellent Intelligence, and the Stage of the Dharma Cloud—are not substantially existent, one cannot realize the sought-after unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Because the five eyes and the six supernormal powers are not truly existent, one cannot realize the sought-after unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Because the Buddha’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, four unhindered understandings, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are not truly existent, one cannot realize the sought-after unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Because the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant abiding in equanimity are not substantially existent, one cannot realize the sought-after unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Because omniscience, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects are not substantially existent, one cannot realize the sought-after unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

“Subhūti! All such phenomena are entirely products of conceptualization and mental construction; those things produced by conceptualization and mental construction cannot attain the knowledge of all modes (sarvākārajñatā).”
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

Although these dharmas can induce the path to enlightenment, they lack the capacity to assist toward its fruition, because these dharmas are unarisen, unoriginated, and devoid of real characteristics."
From the first generation of the mind of enlightenment, although various forms of physical, verbal, and mental goodness arise in the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas—
namely, the practice of the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom,
or the practice of the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four [bases of psychic power]...
The bases of supernormal power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path—
whether abiding in internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness,

the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena, absolute emptiness, the emptiness of the limitless, or the emptiness of dispersion.
...the emptiness of non-alteration, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of self-characteristic, the emptiness of common characteristic,
the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature,
and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence; whether abiding in the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path, or practicing the four dhyānas...

The four applications of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path; the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments;
if one practices the eight liberations, the eight spheres of mastery, the nine successive meditative concentrations, and the ten totalities;
if one practices all doors of dhāraṇī and all doors of samādhi; or if one practices the liberations of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—

...the gate; or if one practices the Stage of Extreme Joy, the Stage of Purity, the Stage of Radiance, the Stage of Blazing Wisdom, the Stage of Difficult Victory, the Stage of Presence, the Stage of Far-Going, the Stage of Immovability, the Stage of Excellent Intelligence, and the Stage of the Cloud of Dharma;
or if one practices the five eyes and the six supernormal powers; or if one practices the Buddha-...

The ten powers, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
or if one practices the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant abiding in equanimity; or if one practices all-knowledge, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all aspects.
And one knows that all things are like what is seen in a dream, like a reflection, like an echo, like a mirage,
like a shadow, like a magical illusion, like a transformation body, and like a city of Gandharvas— all of which are not truly existent.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

Although these dharmas are not substantially existent, if they were not perfected and established with certainty, one would be unable to mature sentient beings, purify buddha-fields, and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."

If bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do not bring to perfection the pāramitās of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, they will certainly be unable to mature sentient beings, purify buddha-fields, or realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

If one does not bring to perfection the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path, one will certainly be unable to mature sentient beings, purify buddha-fields, and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

If one does not fulfill internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, one will certainly be unable to mature sentient beings, purify buddha-fields, or realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

If one does not fully realize the noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path, one will certainly be unable to mature sentient beings, purify buddha-fields, and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

If one does not fulfill the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless absorptions, one will certainly be unable to mature sentient beings, purify buddha-fields, and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

If one does not fully perfect the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive meditative attainments, and the ten totalities, one will certainly be unable to bring sentient beings to maturity, purify Buddha-fields, and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

If one does not bring to perfection all the gateways of dhāraṇī and all the gateways of samādhi, one will certainly be unable to mature sentient beings, purify buddha-fields, and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

If one does not fulfill the gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—one will certainly be unable to mature sentient beings, purify buddha-fields, or realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

If one does not fulfill the Ground of Utmost Joy, the Ground of Purity, the Ground of Radiant Light, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Supreme Difficulty to Conquer, the Ground of Manifestation, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, and the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma, one will certainly be unable to mature sentient beings, purify Buddha-fields, and realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

If one does not perfect the five eyes and the six supernormal powers, one will certainly be unable to mature sentient beings, purify buddha-fields, and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

If one does not fulfill the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, one will certainly be unable to mature sentient beings, purify Buddha-fields, or realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

If one does not fulfill the thirty-two marks of a great man and the eighty secondary signs, one will certainly be unable to mature sentient beings, purify a buddha-field, or realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

If one does not fulfill the quality of non-forgetfulness and the state of constant equanimity, one will certainly be unable to mature sentient beings, purify Buddha-fields, or realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

If one does not bring to perfection all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), and all-aspect knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*), one will certainly be unable to mature sentient beings, purify Buddha-fields, and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*).
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

When these bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they know all the wholesome dharmas they practice as they truly are—like what is seen in a dream, like a reflection, like an echo, like a mirage, like a shadow, like a magical illusion, like a transformed body, and like a city of gandharvas. That is to say, when practicing the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, they are able to know them as they truly are as being like what is seen in a dream, and so on, up to being like a city of gandharvas."

If one practices the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path, and is able to know them as they truly are—as like what is seen in a dream, and so forth, up to being like a city of Gandharvas;

or if one abides in internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, endless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehensibility, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, and is able to know them as they truly are—as like what is seen in a dream, and so forth, up to being like a city of Gandharvas; [then this is the perfection of wisdom].

If one abides in the noble truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path, one is able to know them as they truly are, like what is seen in a dream, and so forth, up to being like a city of gandharvas;

if one practices the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments, one is able to know them as they truly are, like what is seen in a dream, and so forth, up to being like a city of gandharvas;

if one practices the eight liberations, the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive concentrations, and the ten totalities, one is able to know them as they truly are, like what is seen in a dream, and so forth, up to being like a city of gandharvas.

If one practices all the gateways of dhāraṇī and all the gateways of samādhi, one is able to know them as they truly are, like what is seen in a dream, and so on extensively up to being like a city of gandharvas;

if one practices the gateways of liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, one is able to know them as they truly are, like what is seen in a dream, and so on extensively up to being like a city of gandharvas;

if one practices the Ground of Extreme Joy, the Ground of Purity, the Ground of Radiant Light, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Difficult to Conquer, the Ground of Presence, the Ground of Far-reaching, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Good Intelligence, and the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma, one is able to know them as they truly are, like what is seen in a dream, and so on extensively up to being like a city of gandharvas.
If one practices the five eyes and the six supernormal powers, one can know them as they truly are, like what is seen in a dream, and so on extensively up to being like a city of Gandharvas;

if one practices the Buddha’s ten powers, the four fearlessnesses, the four unhindered understandings, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, one can know them as they truly are, like what is seen in a dream, and so on extensively up to being like a city of Gandharvas;

if one practices the thirty-two marks of a Great Being and the eighty minor marks, one can know them as they truly are, like what is seen in a dream, and so on extensively up to being like a city of Gandharvas.

If one practices the quality of non-forgetfulness and abides constantly in equanimity, one is able to know, as it truly is, that which is seen in a dream, and so on at length up to that which is like a city of Gandharvas;

if one practices all-knowledge (*sarvajñā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), one is able to know, as it truly is, that which is seen in a dream, and so on at length up to that which is like a city of Gandharvas;

if one brings sentient beings to maturity, purifies Buddha-fields, and seeks to attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, one is able to know, as it truly is, that which is seen in a dream, and so on at length up to that which is like a city of Gandharvas.
Furthermore, one knows the various mental activities of sentient beings as they truly are, like what is seen in a dream, and so on, up to being like a city of Gandharvas. "Moreover, Subhūti!

When these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not apprehend any phenomena as existing, nor do they apprehend them as non-existing. Even if they were to realize the knowledge of all modes through such apprehension, they would know those phenomena to be like what is seen in a dream, like a reflection, like an echo, like a mirage, like a shadow, like a magical illusion, like a transformation body, and like a city of Gandharvas; they do not apprehend them as existing, nor do they apprehend them as non-existing.
Why is this? Because the perfection of generosity cannot be grasped; likewise, the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom cannot be grasped.

Because the four foundations of mindfulness cannot be grasped; likewise, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path cannot be grasped.

Because inner emptiness is ungraspable, and because outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, boundless emptiness, dispersed emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, common characteristic emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature are also ungraspable;
because the noble truth of suffering is ungraspable, and because the noble truths of origin, cessation, and the path are also ungraspable;
because the four dhyānas are ungraspable, and because the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments are also ungraspable.
Because the eight liberations are ungraspable, and likewise the eight bases of mastery, the nine successive attainments, and the ten totalities are ungraspable;
because all doors of dhāraṇī are ungraspable, and likewise all doors of samādhi are ungraspable;
because the liberation door of emptiness is ungraspable, and likewise the liberation doors of signlessness and wishlessness are ungraspable.

Because the Ground of Utmost Joy is ungraspable, the Ground of Purity, the Ground of Radiance, the Ground of Blazing Wisdom, the Ground of Extreme Difficulty to Conquer, the Ground of Presence, the Ground of Far-Going, the Ground of Immovability, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, and the Ground of the Dharma Cloud are likewise ungraspable;
because the five eyes are ungraspable, the six supernormal powers are likewise ungraspable;

because the ten powers of a Buddha are ungraspable, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are likewise ungraspable.
Because the quality of non-forgetfulness is ungraspable, and the state of constant equanimity is likewise ungraspable;
because omniscience is ungraspable, and the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the knowledge of all aspects are likewise ungraspable;
